directionToLlm.title: Canonical Hadith Apologetics & Textual Nuance Dataset (Ready Apologia Single Source of Truth)
directionToLlm.role_and_purpose: Instructions for the Ready Apologia UI/UX Agent. This single file ('master_hadith_dataset.json') is the complete, self-contained source of truth for both (1) generating the Category -> Subcategory -> Ranked Hadiths discovery screens and (2) rendering apologetic annotations on individual Hadith entry pages.

how_to_use_this_single_file.root_structure: The root JSON object has one metadata key ('directionToLlm') followed by 822 canonical Hadith keys in the format '<collection>:<hadithnumber>' (e.g., 'muslim:3479', 'bukhari:6130'). Every Hadith key is a clean integer ID with a valid Sunnah.com page. The root Hadith keys are globally pre-sorted in exact CUJ order: (category_cuj_rank 1..7, subcategory_cuj_rank 1..K, cuj_rank 1..N).
how_to_use_this_single_file.value_type: Each Hadith key maps to a non-empty array of annotation objects: [ { <fields> }, ... ], pre-sorted from strongest to weakest CUJ rank. Most Hadiths have 1 annotation; dual-tagged Hadiths have 2 or 3.
how_to_use_this_single_file.workflow_1_generate_category_and_subcate: To build the Category -> Subcategory -> Ranked Hadiths screens on the static website, iterate through 'directionToLlm.cuj_ranked_hierarchy' (which lists Categories 1..7 in CUJ order, and within each Category lists Subcategories 1..K in CUJ order). Inside each subcategory object, iterate over 'ordered_item_ids' (each string is '<hadith_id>#<annotation_index>', e.g. 'muslim:3479#0'): split on '#' to get [hadithId, annIndex] and read dataset[hadithId][Number(annIndex)]. Alternatively, iterate through 'directionToLlm.taxonomy' (Categories 1..7 -> Subcategories 1..K) and filter all annotations across the root Hadith keys where ann.category === cat && ann.subcategory === subcat, sorted by ann.cuj_rank ascending (1..N).
how_to_use_this_single_file.workflow_2_render_individual_hadith_entr: When rendering a specific Hadith entry page (e.g. 'bukhari:5134' or 'muslim:3479'), look up dataset[hadithId] directly in O(1) time to get the pre-sorted array of annotation objects for that Hadith.
how_to_use_this_single_file.workflow_3_expand_full_hadith_context_fr: Each annotation in this file stores only the 'problematic_excerpt' (the relevant Arabic and English proof-text substring) to keep the dataset compact. To implement an 'Expand Full Hadith Text / View Full Context' feature (or to pre-bundle full texts during static site build), follow the exact instructions in 'directionToLlm.full_corpus_lookup_on_disk'.

full_corpus_lookup_on_disk.purpose: How to locate the complete, unclipped Arabic and English text (plus Book/Chapter metadata) for any Hadith key in this dataset or in 'parallel_references'.
full_corpus_lookup_on_disk.corpus_file_schema: Each of the 4 corpus JSON files has top-level keys: { 'metadata': { 'name': string, 'sections': { '<book_number>': '<Book Title>' } }, 'hadiths': [ { 'hadithnumber': int, 'arabicnumber': number, 'text': string, 'grades': array, 'reference': { 'book': int, 'hadith': int } }, ... ] }.
step_by_step_lookup_instructions: 1. Take any Hadith key from this dataset (e.g., 'muslim:3479', 'bukhari:6130') or any entry from 'parallel_references' and split on ':' into [collection, hadithNumStr].

2. Load the corresponding English file ('.../sahih_corpus/<collection>/eng-<collection>.json') and Arabic file ('.../sahih_corpus/<collection>/ara-<collection>.json'). For fast static-site generation, index each file's 'hadiths' array once into a Map/dict keyed by String(h.hadithnumber).
3. Find the Hadith object where String(h.hadithnumber) === hadithNumStr (100% of all 822 Hadith keys in this dataset are clean integer IDs that match).
4. Read 'h.text' from eng-<collection>.json for the complete English Hadith text, and 'h.text' from ara-<collection>.json for the complete Classical Arabic Hadith text.
5. Optional metadata: read 'h.reference.book' and look up 'corpus.metadata.sections[String(h.reference.book)]' to display the canonical Book/Chapter name (e.g., 'The Book of Marriage').

6. UI Context Highlighting: When the user clicks 'Expand Full Hadith', render the full 'h.text' and highlight the substring matching 'annotation.problematic_excerpt.english' (and 'annotation.problematic_excerpt.arabic' in the Arabic pane). 100% of all 934 English and Arabic excerpts in this dataset are exact verbatim substrings of 'h.text'.

category.explanation: One of the 7 primary apologetic categories (e.g., "Muhammad's Character, Life & Conduct", "Violence, Cruelty & Intolerance").
category.ui_usage: Use for top-level navigation tabs, category filter chips, and color-coded domain badges on Hadith cards.

category_cuj_rank.explanation: 1-based CUJ rank of the parent Category, ordered by above-the-fold entry-point impact for Ready Apologia users (#1 is the most devastating category).
category_cuj_rank.ui_usage: Sort top-level Category tabs, accordions, or home-screen discovery carousels in ascending order of 'category_cuj_rank' (1 to 7) rather than alphabetically or by item count.

subcategory.explanation: One of the 19 fine-grained thematic subcategories within the parent Category (e.g., "Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct").
subcategory.ui_usage: Display as the secondary tag pill or section header inside a Category view.

subcategory_cuj_rank.explanation: 1-based CUJ rank of the Subcategory within its parent Category, ordered by Peak Flagship Power (never by mathematical average).
subcategory_cuj_rank.ui_usage: Sort Subcategory sections or filter pills within a Category in ascending order of 'subcategory_cuj_rank' (1..K) so users immediately encounter the most devastating subcategories first.

cuj_rank.explanation: Exact 1-based rank of this annotation within its Subcategory (#1 is the single most devastating flagship Hadith in that Subcategory). Incorporates Anti-Clone De-Clustering so parallel isnad duplicates of the same incident are never stacked back-to-back in the Top 10.
cuj_rank.ui_usage: Sort Hadith cards within any Subcategory view in ascending order of 'cuj_rank' (1..N). Rank #1..#5 can be highlighted as 'Top Flagships' above the fold.

cuj_tier.explanation: CUJ impact tier: 1 = Flagship / 'Nuclear' above-the-fold argument (instant 5-second comprehension, zero prerequisite knowledge); 2 = High-impact distinct primary argument; 3 = Solid secondary or contextual argument; 4 = Parallel isnad duplicate or minor variant pushed to the corroborating tail.
cuj_tier.ui_usage: Use 'cuj_tier == 1' to render a 'Flagship Argument' / 'Essential' badge or populate a 'Start Here / Top Arguments' view. Optionally allow users to filter by Tier 1-2 for quick study, or collapse Tier 4 items into a 'Corroborating Parallel Narrations' drawer.

cuj_score.explanation: Fine-grained CUJ power score combining primary-source self-sufficiency, moral/empirical clarity, translator sanitization exposure, and apologetic utility.
cuj_score.ui_usage: Can be used for global 'Top 50 Most Devastating Hadiths Across All Categories' leaderboards, strength meters, or tie-breaking.

note.explanation: A concise, factual 1-2 sentence headline summary stating what takes place, is commanded, or is declared in the Hadith and why it is apologetically significant. Avoids academic fluff or preaching. Contains inline markdown links for Bible, Quran, and Tafsir citations, using BC/AD dating.
note.ui_usage: Render as the primary headline/summary callout on the Hadith card or apologetics banner. Parse inline markdown links ('bible://', 'quran://', 'ibnkathir://', 'tabari://') into interactive scripture popovers or deep links.

problematic_excerpt.explanation: Verbatim primary-source text anchor from the Hadith containing sufficient narrative context in both Classical Arabic ('arabic', from ara-bukhari / ara-muslim) and the standard published English translation ('english', Muhsin Khan for Bukhari / Siddiqui for Muslim).
problematic_excerpt.ui_usage: Display by default on the card so the user immediately sees the proof-text without reading a multi-page narration. Provide an 'Expand Full Hadith Context' button that loads the complete Hadith text from disk (see 'directionToLlm.full_corpus_lookup_on_disk') with this excerpt highlighted inside it.

literal_translation.type: string (optional; present ONLY when 'translation_issue' is present)
literal_translation.explanation: Provides the unvarnished, faithful scholarly English translation of the Classical Arabic excerpt when the published English translation softened, euphemized, or omitted problematic text.
literal_translation.ui_usage: When present, display in a side-by-side or toggleable comparison card ('Published English Translation' vs. 'Literal Arabic Translation') to visually expose what the translator hid.

translation_issue.type: object { type: 'softened'|'omission'|'euphemistic', arabic_term: string, published_rendering: string, literal_meaning: string, explanation: string } (optional)
translation_issue.explanation: Audit block documenting deliberate or apologetic translator sanitization/whitewashing. Documents the exact Arabic phrase ('arabic_term'), how the translator rendered or skipped it ('published_rendering'), its true lexical meaning ('literal_meaning'), and why/how it was sanitized ('explanation'). Every '...'-separated segment of 'published_rendering' is guaranteed to be an exact substring of 'problematic_excerpt.english' in order, with the exact same number of '...'-separated segments in 'literal_meaning' (or pure omissions use 'published_rendering': '[omitted]').
translation_issue.ui_usage: High-value UI feature: render a prominent alert badge (e.g., 'Translation Sanitized' / 'Omitted in English'), an inline strike-through replacing each '...'-separated segment of 'published_rendering' in 'problematic_excerpt.english' with the corresponding segment of 'literal_meaning', and a lexical breakdown card.

anticipated_defense.explanation: Adversarial Red-Team briefing (2-3 sentences): (1) states the strongest classical or modern Sunni apologetic defense (citing Ibn Hajar's Fath al-Bari, Al-Nawawi's Sharh, etc.) an opponent will raise when confronted with this Hadith, and (2) provides the immediate primary-source counter-rebuttal from the Arabic matn, parallel Sahih chains, or classical Tafsir.
anticipated_defense.ui_usage: Render as an expandable 'Anticipated Muslim Defense & Rebuttal' / 'How Apologists Respond' accordion or battle-card tab on every annotated Hadith entry.

parallel_references.explanation: Canonical Hadith IDs in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim that preserve parallel, corroborating, or variant transmissions of the same historical incident.
parallel_references.ui_usage: Render as clickable quick-jump chips ('Parallel Chains: Bukhari 5133, Muslim 3480') so the user can cross-reference corroborating witnesses or compare variant details.

custom_link_schemes.bible://: Format: [Display Text](bible://<book_abbr>/<chapter>/<verse>[-<end_verse>]). All <book_abbr> tokens strictly adhere to '/usr/local/google/home/markyacoub/Documents/data_collection/common/bible_abbreviations.js' (e.g., gn, ex, lv, nm, dt, ps, is, mt, mk, lk, jn, rom, 1cor, rv). Parse into Bible verse preview modal or navigation link.
custom_link_schemes.quran://: Format: [Display Text](quran://<surah>/<ayah>[-<end_ayah>]). Parse into Quran verse preview modal or navigation link.
custom_link_schemes.ibnkathir://: Format: [Display Text](ibnkathir://<surah>/<ayah>). Parse into Tafsir Ibn Kathir reference link.
custom_link_schemes.tabari://: Format: [Display Text](tabari://<surah>/<ayah>). Parse into Tafsir al-Tabari reference link.
custom_link_schemes.hadith_references: All inline Hadith references in 'note', 'anticipated_defense', and 'parallel_references' are standardized to 'bukhari:<corpus_hadithnumber>' and 'muslim:<corpus_hadithnumber>' (e.g., 'bukhari:5134', 'muslim:3479'). Every single one resolves 100% to a valid 'hadithnumber' in 'sahih_corpus/{bukhari,muslim}/{eng,ara}-{bukhari,muslim}.json' (and all 7,563 Muslim entries in ara-muslim.json and eng-muslim.json now have non-null 'arabicnumber' and 'reference' fields for Sunnah.com numbering conversion).

muslim:3479.note: Aisha recounts that Muhammad married her when she was six years old and consummated the marriage (*banā bī*) when she was nine years old, after her mother called her off a playground swing where she was playing with her friends and handed her over to him without her knowing what was happening ([Quran 65:4](quran://65/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ تَزَوَّجَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِسِتِّ سِنِينَ وَبَنَى بِي وَأَنَا بِنْتُ تِسْعِ سِنِينَ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ فَقَدِمْنَا الْمَدِينَةَ فَوُعِكْتُ شَهْرًا فَوَفَى شَعْرِي جُمَيْمَةً فَأَتَتْنِي أُمُّ رُومَانَ وَأَنَا عَلَى أُرْجُوحَةٍ وَمَعِي صَوَاحِبِي فَصَرَخَتْ بِي فَأَتَيْتُهَا وَمَا أَدْرِي مَا تُرِيدُ بِي فَأَخَذَتْ بِيَدِي فَأَوْقَفَتْنِي عَلَى الْبَابِ ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ هَهْ هَهْ ‏.‏ حَتَّى ذَهَبَ نَفَسِي فَأَدْخَلَتْنِي بَيْتًا فَإِذَا نِسْوَةٌ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ فَقُلْنَ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ وَالْبَرَكَةِ وَعَلَى خَيْرِ طَائِرٍ ‏.‏ فَأَسْلَمَتْنِي إِلَيْهِنَّ فَغَسَلْنَ رَأْسِي وَأَصْلَحْنَنِي فَلَمْ يَرُعْنِي إِلاَّ وَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ضُحًى فَأَسْلَمْنَنِي إِلَيْهِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) reported:Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) married me when I was six years old, and I was admitted to his house at the age of nine. She further said: We went to Medina and I had an attack of fever for a month, and my hair had come down to the earlobes. Umm Ruman (my mother) came to me and I was at that time on a swing along with my playmates. She called me loudly and I went to her and I did not know what she had wanted of me. She took hold of my hand and took me to the door, and I was saying: Ha, ha (as if I was gasping), until the agitation of my heart was over. She took me to a house, where had gathered the women of the Ansar. They all blessed me and wished me good luck and said: May you have share in good. She (my mother) entrusted me to them. They washed my head and embellished me and nothing frightened me. Allah's Messenger (, may peace be upon him) came there in the morning, and I was entrusted to him

muslim:3479.literal_translation: Aisha reported: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) married me when I was six years old, and consummated the marriage with me when I was a girl of nine years. She said: We came to Medina and I suffered a fever for a month, and my hair grew down to my earlobes. Umm Ruman came to me while I was on a swing with my playmates. She called out to me, so I came to her not knowing what she wanted with me. She took me by the hand and made me stand at the door while I was panting 'Hah, hah' until my breathing settled. Then she brought me into a house where women of the Ansar were gathered, and they said: 'Upon good and blessing, and upon the best fortune.' She handed me over to them, and they washed my head and prepared me. Nothing startled me except Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) coming in the forenoon, and they handed me over to him.

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَبَنَى بِي وَأَنَا بِنْتُ تِسْعِ سِنِينَ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and I was admitted to his house at the age of nine
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and he consummated the marriage with me when I was a girl of nine years
translation_issue.explanation: In classical Arabic lexicography (Lisān al-'Arab, Lane's Lexicon) and Islamic jurisprudence, 'banā bihā' (originally derived from pitching a bridal tent over the wife) is the standard idiom for sexual consummation of a marriage (synonymous with 'dakhala bihā'). The translator softens this to 'I was admitted to his house,' obscuring that marital consummation occurred at age nine.

muslim:3479.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that girls matured faster in 7th-century AD Arabia so Aisha had already reached biological puberty and consented at age nine, or alternatively claim based on modern revisionist calculations that she was actually 16 to 19 years old. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad consummated the marriage when she was nine (*wa-banā bī wa-anā bintu tisʿi sinīn*) after she was called directly off a playground swing (*ʿalā urjūḥah*) with her playmates while completely unaware of what was happening (*wa-mā adrī mā turīdu bī*), and parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:6130`, `muslim:3481`) confirm she continued playing with dolls in his house—which Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* explicitly notes was legally permitted only for prepubescent girls (*ghayr bāligh*). Furthermore, Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* cites this exact Hadith alongside [Quran 65:4](quran://65/4) (*wa-allāʾī lam yaḥiḍna*, prescribing divorce waiting periods for wives 'who have not yet menstruated') to establish the classical Sunni consensus (*ijmāʿ*) that a father may contract and hand over a prepubescent daughter for marital consummation without her consent.

bukhari:6130.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:6130.note: Aisha recounts playing with dolls alongside her companions in Muhammad's household, noting that when the girls hid upon his entry, he would send them back to continue playing with her. Classical commentary (Ibn Hajar's Fath al-Bari) explains that although images were forbidden, Aisha was permitted to play with dolls in her marital home because she was a young girl who had not yet reached puberty (cf. [Quran 65:4](quran://65/4), bukhari:5133).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنْتُ أَلْعَبُ بِالْبَنَاتِ عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَكَانَ لِي صَوَاحِبُ يَلْعَبْنَ مَعِي، فَكَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا دَخَلَ يَتَقَمَّعْنَ مِنْهُ، فَيُسَرِّبُهُنَّ إِلَىَّ فَيَلْعَبْنَ مَعِي
problematic_excerpt.english: I used to play with the dolls in the presence of the Prophet, and my girl friends also used to play with me. When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to enter (my dwelling place) they used to hide themselves, but the Prophet would call them to join and play with me.

bukhari:6130.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Aisha had already reached puberty when her marriage was consummated at age nine, claiming that her playing with dolls (*al-banāt*) merely reflects Muhammad's gentle kindness toward a mature young bride. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that she was still playing with dolls alongside her little girlfriends inside Muhammad's marital residence (*ʿinda al-Nabī*) after consummation (`bukhari:3894`, `muslim:6287`). Furthermore, Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani confirms in *Fath al-Bari* on this exact Hadith that Aisha was exempted from the strict Islamic prohibition on three-dimensional images precisely because she was a prepubescent child (*ghayr baligh*), directly corroborating [Quran 65:4](quran://65/4)'s post-consummation waiting period for wives who have not yet menstruated (*wa-alla'i lam yahidna*).

bukhari:5113.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5113.note: When Khawlah bint Hakim and other women offered themselves in marriage to Muhammad, Aisha asked whether a woman feels no shame in offering herself to a man. Following the revelation of [Quran 33:51](quran://33/51) permitting Muhammad to defer whichever of them he wished, Aisha told him that she saw his Lord hastening to fulfill his desire (*hawāka*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَتْ خَوْلَةُ بِنْتُ حَكِيمٍ مِنَ اللاَّئِي وَهَبْنَ أَنْفُسَهُنَّ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ أَمَا تَسْتَحِي الْمَرْأَةُ أَنْ تَهَبَ نَفْسَهَا لِلرَّجُلِ فَلَمَّا نَزَلَتْ ‏{‏تُرْجِئُ مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ‏}‏ قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ مَا أَرَى رَبَّكَ إِلاَّ يُسَارِعُ فِي هَوَاكَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Khaula bint Hakim was one of those ladies who presented themselves to the Prophet (ﷺ) for marriage. `Aisha said, "Doesn't a lady feel ashamed for presenting herself to a man?" But when the Verse: "(O Muhammad) You may postpone (the turn of) any of them (your wives) that you please,' (33.51) was revealed, " `Aisha said, 'O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! I do not see, but, that your Lord hurries in pleasing you

bukhari:5113.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—that Aisha was merely speaking out of natural marital jealousy (*ghayrah*) or marveling at Allah's favor toward the Prophet, claiming that *hawāka* benignly means 'what pleases you' and that Muhammad never actually married the women who gifted themselves. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Aisha used the loaded word `هَوَاكَ` (*hawāka*, 'your personal desire/passion')—the very term the Quran itself sets as the antithesis of authentic revelation in Quran 53:3 (`وَمَا يَنطِقُ عَنِ الْهَوَىٰ`, 'nor does he speak from *al-hawā*')—while pointedly referring to Allah as '*your* Lord' (`رَبَّكَ`, *rabbaka*) who 'hastens to fulfill your desire' (`يُسَارِعُ فِي هَوَاكَ`). Triggered directly by Quran 33:50–51 granting Muhammad exclusive sexual privileges to take women who offered themselves (`وَهَبْنَ أَنْفُسَهُنَّ`) and to suspend his wives' mandatory conjugal turns at will (`تُرْجِئُ مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ`), Aisha's blunt eyewitness remark exposes how conveniently 'revelations' arrived on demand to satisfy Muhammad's immediate bedroom wishes.

muslim:3407.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3407.note: After seeing a woman, Muhammad went to his wife Zaynab while she was tanning a leather hide and had sexual intercourse with her (*fa-qaḍā ḥājatahu*, literally 'fulfilled his need'), then went out to his companions and instructed that whenever a man sees a woman, he should go to his wife to repel what he feels within himself ([Matthew 5:28](bible://mt/5/28)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَأَى امْرَأَةً فَأَتَى امْرَأَتَهُ زَيْنَبَ وَهْىَ تَمْعَسُ مَنِيئَةً لَهَا فَقَضَى حَاجَتَهُ ثُمَّ خَرَجَ إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ إِنَّ الْمَرْأَةَ تُقْبِلُ فِي صُورَةِ شَيْطَانٍ وَتُدْبِرُ فِي صُورَةِ شَيْطَانٍ فَإِذَا أَبْصَرَ أَحَدُكُمُ امْرَأَةً فَلْيَأْتِ أَهْلَهُ فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ يَرُدُّ مَا فِي نَفْسِهِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Jabir reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saw a woman, and so he came to his wife, Zainab, as she was tanning a leather and had sexual intercourse with her. He then went to his Companions and told them:The woman advances and retires in the shape of a devil, so when one of you sees a woman, he should come to his wife, for that will repel what he feels in his heart

muslim:3407.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, typically argue that Muhammad's reaction was merely a practical legislative demonstration teaching men to redirect involuntary attraction toward lawful marital intimacy. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad interrupted Zaynab mid-chore while she was tanning leather (*wa-hiya tamʿasu manīʾatan lahā*) solely to 'relieve his need' (*fa-qaḍā ḥājatahu*), and the parallel narration in `muslim:3408` confirms the strange woman had 'fallen into his soul' (*fa-waqaʿat fī nafsī*). Rather than modeling moral self-mastery over inward lust, the text depicts Muhammad being so overwhelmed by the sight of a passing woman that he immediately used his wife as a physical outlet to discharge passion aroused by someone else.

muslim:3407.note: After seeing a woman and having sexual intercourse with his wife Zaynab while she was tanning leather, Muhammad declares to his companions that a woman 'advances in the shape of a devil and retires in the shape of a devil' (*fī ṣūrati shayṭān*), instructing any man who sees a woman to go to his wife to repel what he feels within himself ([Genesis 1:27](bible://gn/1/27), [Matthew 5:28](bible://mt/5/28)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَأَى امْرَأَةً فَأَتَى امْرَأَتَهُ زَيْنَبَ وَهْىَ تَمْعَسُ مَنِيئَةً لَهَا فَقَضَى حَاجَتَهُ ثُمَّ خَرَجَ إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ إِنَّ الْمَرْأَةَ تُقْبِلُ فِي صُورَةِ شَيْطَانٍ وَتُدْبِرُ فِي صُورَةِ شَيْطَانٍ فَإِذَا أَبْصَرَ أَحَدُكُمُ امْرَأَةً فَلْيَأْتِ أَهْلَهُ فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ يَرُدُّ مَا فِي نَفْسِهِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Jabir reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saw a woman, and so he came to his wife, Zainab, as she was tanning a leather and had sexual intercourse with her. He then went to his Companions and told them:The woman advances and retires in the shape of a devil, so when one of you sees a woman, he should come to his wife, for that will repel what he feels in his heart

muslim:3407.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists, appealing to Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, typically argue that 'in the shape of a devil' (*fī ṣūrati shayṭān*) is merely a metaphor for the temptation Satan whispers during an unlawful gaze rather than a denigration of women themselves. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *inna al-marʾata tuqbilu fī ṣūrati shayṭānin wa-tudbiru fī ṣūrati shayṭān* ('Indeed, the woman advances in the shape of a devil and retires in the shape of a devil'), projecting male lust onto a woman's mere physical movement going and coming. Furthermore, the parallel narration in `muslim:3409` confirms the dehumanizing premise of Muhammad's remedy by reducing both women to interchangeable anatomical parts: 'for with her [the wife] is the like of what is with her' (*fa-inna maʿahā mithla alladhī maʿahā*).

muslim:3604.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3604.note: When Sahla bint Suhail objects that Salim is a grown man with a beard (*innahu dhu lihyah*), Muhammad repeats his command that she breastfeed (*ardi'ihi*) him to remove her husband Abu Hudhaifa's displeasure at Salim entering their home. Aisha cites this incident to Umm Salama as a precedent for breastfeeding older boys, though Muhammad's other wives argued it was a special exemption granted solely to Salim (muslim:3605).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَمِعْتُ أُمَّ سَلَمَةَ، زَوْجَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم تَقُولُ لِعَائِشَةَ وَاللَّهِ مَا تَطِيبُ نَفْسِي أَنْ يَرَانِي الْغُلاَمُ قَدِ اسْتَغْنَى عَنِ الرَّضَاعَةِ ‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ لِمَ قَدْ جَاءَتْ سَهْلَةُ بِنْتُ سُهَيْلٍ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لأَرَى فِي وَجْهِ أَبِي حُذَيْفَةَ مِنْ دُخُولِ سَالِمٍ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَرْضِعِيهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ إِنَّهُ ذُو لِحْيَةٍ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَرْضِعِيهِ يَذْهَبْ مَا فِي وَجْهِ أَبِي حُذَيْفَةَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ وَاللَّهِ مَا عَرَفْتُهُ فِي وَجْهِ أَبِي حُذَيْفَةَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I heard Umm Salama, the wife of Allah's Apostle (may peace be upon himy, saying to 'A'isha: By Allah, I do not like to be seen by a young boy who has passed the period of fosterage, whereupon she ('A'isha) said: Why is it so? Sahla daughter of Suhail came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said: Allah's Messenger, I swear by Allah that I see in the face of Abu Hudhaifa (the signs of disgust) on account of entering of Salim (in the house), whereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Suckle him. She (Sahla bint Suhail) said: He has a heard. But he (again) said: Suckle him, and it would remove what is there (expression of disgust) on the face of Abu Hudhaifa. She said: (I did that) and, by Allah, I did not see (any sign of disgust) on the face of Abu Hudhaifa

muslim:3604.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ—that this was a one-time legal exception (*rukhṣah khāṣṣah*) exclusive to Sālim, and that Sahlah merely expressed her milk into a cup rather than nursing him directly. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states the direct imperative *arḍiʿīhi* ("suckle him") with zero mention of a vessel, which is precisely why Sahlah objected in shock that "he has a beard" (*innahu dhū liḥyah*)—a protest that makes no sense if she were merely handing him a cup to drink. Furthermore, this very narration records ʿĀʾishah invoking Sālim's case against Umm Salamah as a general precedent, which ʿĀʾishah actively practiced by ordering her sister and nieces to suckle adult men she wished to admit into her presence (`muslim:3605`, `abudawud:2061`).

muslim:3501.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3501.note: When Safiyya fell to Dihya in the division of spoils and companions praised her to Muhammad by stating they had never seen anyone like her among the captives, he acquired her from Dihya for whatever he asked and had Anas's mother prepare her. Immediately after leaving Khaybar, Muhammad halted, pitched a tent over her (`ḍaraba ʿalayhā al-qubbah`) to consummate the marriage, and held her wedding feast the next morning from surplus dates and barley meal.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: صَارَتْ صَفِيَّةُ لِدَحْيَةَ فِي مَقْسَمِهِ وَجَعَلُوا يَمْدَحُونَهَا عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم - قَالَ - وَيَقُولُونَ مَا رَأَيْنَا فِي السَّبْىِ مِثْلَهَا - قَالَ - فَبَعَثَ إِلَى دِحْيَةَ فَأَعْطَاهُ بِهَا مَا أَرَادَ ثُمَّ دَفَعَهَا إِلَى أُمِّي فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَصْلِحِيهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ ثُمَّ خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ خَيْبَرَ حَتَّى إِذَا جَعَلَهَا فِي ظَهْرِهِ نَزَلَ ثُمَّ ضَرَبَ عَلَيْهَا الْقُبَّةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Safiyya (Allah be pleased with her) fell to the lot of Dihya in the spoils of war, and they praised her in the presence of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said: We have not seen the like of her among the captives of war. He sent (a messenger) to Dihya and he gave him whatever he demanded. He then sent her to my mother and asked her to embellish her. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) then got out of Khaibar until when he was on the other side of it, he halted, and a tent was pitched for him.

muslim:3501.literal_translation: Safiyya fell to Dihya in his share of the spoils, and they began praising her before the Messenger of Allah, saying: 'We have never seen the like of her among the captives.' So he sent to Dihya and gave him for her whatever he wanted. Then he handed her over to my mother and said: 'Prepare her.' Then the Messenger of Allah left Khaybar until, when he had put it behind him, he halted and pitched the tent over her [to consummate the marriage].

translation_issue.arabic_term: ثُمَّ ضَرَبَ عَلَيْهَا الْقُبَّةَ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and a tent was pitched for him
translation_issue.literal_meaning: then he pitched the tent over her (the classical Arabic idiom for consummating marriage with a bride)
translation_issue.explanation: The translator alters the active verb and feminine pronoun 'ḍaraba ʿalayhā al-qubbah' ('he pitched the bridal tent over her' for consummation) into the passive 'a tent was pitched for him' to obscure Muhammad's immediate sexual consummation with the war captive Safiyya outside Khaybar.

muslim:3501.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's marriage to Safiyya after the Battle of Khaybar (AD 628) was a selfless political alliance designed to reconcile the defeated Jewish community rather than an act driven by physical desire, and that he scrupulously observed a waiting period before consummation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad only sent for her after his companions began praising her physical beauty before him (wa-jaʿalū yamdaḥūnahā ʿinda rasūli Allāh... mā raʾaynā fī al-sabyi mithlahā, "We have not seen the like of her among the captives"), prompting him to buy her from Dihya on the spot. Moreover, the Arabic text records that as soon as he put Khaybar behind him (ḥattā idhā jaʿalahā fī ẓahrihi nazala), he halted on the roadside and "pitched the bridal tent over her" (thumma ḍaraba ʿalayhā al-qubbah)—an idiom the English translator obscures as "a tent was pitched for him"—consummating the marriage on the march home rather than observing the four-month-and-ten-day waiting period required for widows (Quran 2:234).

muslim:3501.note: After the conquest of Khaybar (AD 628), Safiyya fell to Dihya's share of the spoils, and when companions praised her to Muhammad as having no equal among the captives, he gave Dihya whatever he demanded for her and instructed Anas's mother to prepare her. Once outside Khaybar, Muhammad halted, pitched a tent over her (`ḍaraba ʿalayhā al-qubbah`, the classical idiom for marital consummation), and held her wedding feast the next morning ([Deuteronomy 21:10](bible://dt/21/10)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: صَارَتْ صَفِيَّةُ لِدَحْيَةَ فِي مَقْسَمِهِ وَجَعَلُوا يَمْدَحُونَهَا عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم - قَالَ - وَيَقُولُونَ مَا رَأَيْنَا فِي السَّبْىِ مِثْلَهَا - قَالَ - فَبَعَثَ إِلَى دِحْيَةَ فَأَعْطَاهُ بِهَا مَا أَرَادَ ثُمَّ دَفَعَهَا إِلَى أُمِّي فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَصْلِحِيهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ ثُمَّ خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ خَيْبَرَ حَتَّى إِذَا جَعَلَهَا فِي ظَهْرِهِ نَزَلَ ثُمَّ ضَرَبَ عَلَيْهَا الْقُبَّةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Safiyya (Allah be pleased with her) fell to the lot of Dihya in the spoils of war, and they praised her in the presence of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said: We have not seen the like of her among the captives of war. He sent (a messenger) to Dihya and he gave him whatever he demanded. He then sent her to my mother and asked her to embellish her. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) then got out of Khaibar until when he was on the other side of it, he halted, and a tent was pitched for him.

muslim:3501.literal_translation: Safiyya fell to Dihya in his share of the spoils, and they began praising her before the Messenger of Allah, saying: 'We have never seen the like of her among the captives.' So he sent to Dihya and gave him for her whatever he wanted. Then he handed her over to my mother and said: 'Prepare her.' Then the Messenger of Allah left Khaybar until, when he had put it behind him, he halted and pitched the tent over her [to consummate the marriage].

translation_issue.arabic_term: ثُمَّ ضَرَبَ عَلَيْهَا الْقُبَّةَ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and a tent was pitched for him
translation_issue.literal_meaning: then he pitched the tent over her (the classical Arabic idiom for consummating marriage with a bride)
translation_issue.explanation: The translator alters the active verb and feminine pronoun 'ḍaraba ʿalayhā al-qubbah' ('he pitched the bridal tent over her' for consummation) into the passive 'a tent was pitched for him' to obscure Muhammad's immediate sexual consummation with the war captive Safiyya outside Khaybar.

muslim:3501.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists (citing Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī) typically argue that Muhammad redeemed Safiyya from Dihya al-Kalbi out of humanitarian compassion to honor her noble lineage as a chieftain's daughter, emancipating her and making her freedom her wedding dowry (ṣadāq). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that she was divided as chattel in Dihya's share of the spoils (fī maqsimihi), purchased by Muhammad after men praised her unmatched beauty among the captives (mā raʾaynā fī al-sabyi mithlahā), and handed to Umm Sulaym with the order "aṣliḥīhā" ("prepare her") before he "pitched the tent over her" (ḍaraba ʿalayhā al-qubbah) to consummate the union outside Khaybar. Parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:371, bukhari:2235) confirm he bought her from Dihya for "seven heads" of slaves (sabʿata aʾrus), proving she was traded as war booty and taken into her captor's bed immediately after the slaughter of her family in AD 628.

muslim:3503.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3503.note: When Zaynab's post-divorce waiting period from Zayd ended, Muhammad instructed Zayd to go to her and propose to her on Muhammad's behalf. Zayd reported that because Muhammad had mentioned her for marriage, she became so formidable in his chest that he could not bear to look at her, so he turned his back and stepped backward on his heels to deliver the proposal, after which [Quran 33:37](quran://33/37) descended and Muhammad entered upon her without permission (cf. [Leviticus 18:15](bible://lv/18/15)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَمَّا انْقَضَتْ عِدَّةُ زَيْنَبَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِزَيْدٍ ‏"‏ فَاذْكُرْهَا عَلَىَّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَانْطَلَقَ زَيْدٌ حَتَّى أَتَاهَا وَهْىَ تُخَمِّرُ عَجِينَهَا قَالَ فَلَمَّا رَأَيْتُهَا عَظُمَتْ فِي صَدْرِي حَتَّى مَا أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَنْظُرَ إِلَيْهَا أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ذَكَرَهَا فَوَلَّيْتُهَا ظَهْرِي وَنَكَصْتُ عَلَى عَقِبِي فَقُلْتُ يَا زَيْنَبُ أَرْسَلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَذْكُرُكِ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ مَا أَنَا بِصَانِعَةٍ شَيْئًا حَتَّى أُوَامِرَ رَبِّي ‏.‏ فَقَامَتْ إِلَى مَسْجِدِهَا وَنَزَلَ الْقُرْآنُ وَجَاءَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا بِغَيْرِ إِذْنٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: When the 'Iddah of Zainab was over, Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said to Zaid to make a mention to her about him. Zaid went on until he came to her and she was fermenting her flour. He (Zaid) said: As I saw her I felt in my heart an idea of her greatness so much so that I could not see towards her (simply for the fact) that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) had made a mention of her. So I turned my back towards her. and I turned upon my heels, and said: Zainab, Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) has sent (me) with a message to you. She said: I do not do anything until I solicit the will of my Lord. So she stood at her place of worship and the (verse of) the Qur'an (pertaining to her marriage) were revealed, and Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) came to her without permission.

muslim:3503.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue (citing Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) that Zayd gladly served as an intermediary out of reverence for the Prophet and that Zaynab willingly consented to the marriage. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad ordered Zayd to propose to his own ex-wife on Muhammad's behalf (fa-dhkurhā ʿalayya), an errand so visceral that Zayd could not bear to look at her, turned his back, and stepped backward on his heels (ḥattā mā astaṭīʿu an anẓura ilayhā ... fa-wallaytuhā ẓahrī wa-nakaṣtu ʿalā ʿaqibī). Furthermore, when Zaynab refused to give an immediate answer until she prayed for guidance (mā anā bi-ṣāniʿatin shayʾan ḥattā uwāmira rabbī), Muhammad did not wait for her consent, a guardian (walī), or witnesses (bukhari:7420), but claimed Quran 33:37 had already married her to him and entered her quarters unannounced (fa-dakhala ʿalayhā bi-ghayri idhnin).

muslim:3503.note: Once Zaynab completed her waiting period after her divorce from Zayd, Muhammad instructed Zayd to deliver a marriage proposal to her on his behalf, and following the descent of [Quran 33:37](quran://33/37), Muhammad entered upon her without permission. After some men lingered in the house conversing following the wedding feast, Muhammad drew a curtain between himself and Anas, and [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53) descended instructing guests not to enter the Prophet's houses without permission or linger after eating.

However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad initiated the proposal the moment her waiting period ended (fa-dhkurhā ʿalayya, 'propose to her for me'), bypassed her pending deliberation (ḥattā uwāmira rabbī) by entering upon her without permission (fa-dakhala ʿalayhā bi-ghayri idhnin) via Quran 33:37, and immediately received Quran 33:53 to expel wedding guests who lingered in his house after eating (wa-baqiya rijālun yataḥaddathūna fī al-bayti baʿda al-ṭaʿām). As Aisha herself remarked in bukhari:4788 regarding such marriage revelations, 'I see that your Lord hastens in fulfilling your desires.'

muslim:3425.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3425.note: Sabra b. Ma'bad reports that during the Conquest of Mecca (AD 630), Muhammad commanded (*amara*, rendered 'permitted' in the English translation in light of parallel chains using *adhina*) his companions to engage in temporary enjoyment of women (*al-tamattuʿ min al-nisāʾ*). Sabra and a companion then propositioned a young woman of Banu 'Amir by offering their cloaks, she chose Sabra, and the women remained with the men for three nights before Muhammad commanded (*amara*) them to separate from them—a temporary marriage arrangement that adjacent reports (muslim:3424, muslim:3426, muslim:3427) state he subsequently prohibited ([Matthew 19:4-6](bible://mt/19/4), [1 Corinthians 6:15-18](bible://1cor/6/15)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَامَ فَتْحِ مَكَّةَ أَمَرَ أَصْحَابَهُ بِالتَّمَتُّعِ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ - قَالَ - فَخَرَجْتُ أَنَا وَصَاحِبٌ لِي مِنْ بَنِي سُلَيْمٍ حَتَّى وَجَدْنَا جَارِيَةً مِنْ بَنِي عَامِرٍ كَأَنَّهَا بَكْرَةٌ عَيْطَاءُ فَخَطَبْنَاهَا إِلَى نَفْسِهَا وَعَرَضْنَا عَلَيْهَا بُرْدَيْنَا فَجَعَلَتْ تَنْظُرُ فَتَرَانِي أَجْمَلَ مِنْ صَاحِبِي وَتَرَى بُرْدَ صَاحِبِي أَحْسَنَ مِنْ بُرْدِي فَآمَرَتْ نَفْسَهَا سَاعَةً ثُمَّ اخْتَارَتْنِي عَلَى صَاحِبِي فَكُنَّ مَعَنَا ثَلاَثًا ثُمَّ أَمَرَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِفِرَاقِهِنَّ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Sabra b. Ma'bad reported that Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) permitted his Companions to contract temporary marriage with women in the Year of Victory. So I and a friend of mine from Banu Sulaim went out, until we found a young woman of Banu Amir who was like a young she-camel having a long neck. We proposed to her for contracting temporary marriage with us, and presented to her our cloaks (as dower). She began to look and found me more handsome than my friend, but found the cloak of my friend more beautiful than my cloak. She thought in her mind for a while, but then preferred me to my friend. So I remained with her for three (nights), and then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) commanded us to part with them (such women)

muslim:3425.literal_translation: Sabra b. Ma'bad reported that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), in the year of the Conquest of Mecca, commanded his Companions to derive temporary enjoyment from women. He said: So I and a friend of mine from Banu Sulaim went out until we found a young girl of Banu 'Amir who was like a long-necked young she-camel. We propositioned her directly for herself and offered her our two cloaks. She began to look and saw me as more handsome than my friend, and saw my friend's cloak as finer than my cloak. She deliberated with herself for a while, then chose me over my friend. So they were with us for three (nights), and then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded us to part with them.

translation_issue.arabic_term: أَمَرَ أَصْحَابَهُ بِالتَّمَتُّعِ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ ... فَخَطَبْنَاهَا إِلَى نَفْسِهَا
translation_issue.published_rendering: permitted his Companions to contract temporary marriage with women ... We proposed to her for contracting temporary marriage with us
translation_issue.literal_meaning: commanded his Companions to derive enjoyment from women ... so we proposed to her directly to herself
translation_issue.explanation: First, the translator softens the verb 'amara' ('commanded/ordered') to 'permitted' when Muhammad instructs his companions to take enjoyment from women ('al-tamattuʿ min al-nisāʾ'), substituting juristic harmonization ('amr lil-ibāḥah') for the actual Arabic verb even though he translates the identical verb ('amaranā') as 'commanded us' at the end of the passage. Second, in 'fa-khaṭabnāhā ilā nafsihā' ('so we proposed to her directly to herself', i.e., soliciting the girl directly without a guardian), the translator omits 'ilā nafsihā' ('to herself') entirely and replaces it with the unattested phrase 'for contracting temporary marriage with us'.

muslim:3425.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, typically argue that temporary marriage (*nikāḥ al-mutʿah*) was merely a brief emergency concession for soldiers experiencing hardship on campaign before being permanently abrogated in AD 630. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad actively "commanded his Companions to derive temporary enjoyment from women" (*amara aṣḥābahu bi-l-tamattuʿ min al-nisāʾ*)—leading two men to proposition a girl directly without a guardian or witnesses (*khaṭabnāhā ilā nafsihā*) in exchange for a cloak for three nights—proving that Muhammad repeatedly authorized and ordered short-term transactional sex for goods before reversing his own decree (`muslim:3419`, `muslim:3424`).

bukhari:2639.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:2639.note: When an irrevocably divorced woman reports that her second husband is impotent, Muhammad rules that she cannot return to her first husband until she and her second husband sexually consummate their marriage by 'tasting each other's sweetness' ([Quran 2:230](quran://2/230)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: جَاءَتِ امْرَأَةُ رِفَاعَةَ الْقُرَظِيِّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ كُنْتُ عِنْدَ رِفَاعَةَ فَطَلَّقَنِي فَأَبَتَّ طَلاَقِي، فَتَزَوَّجْتُ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ الزَّبِيرِ، إِنَّمَا مَعَهُ مِثْلُ هُدْبَةِ الثَّوْبِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ أَتُرِيدِينَ أَنْ تَرْجِعِي إِلَى رِفَاعَةَ لاَ حَتَّى تَذُوقِي عُسَيْلَتَهُ وَيَذُوقَ عُسَيْلَتَكِ ‏"‏‏.‏ وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ جَالِسٌ عِنْدَهُ وَخَالِدُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْعَاصِ بِالْبَابِ يَنْتَظِرُ أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَهُ، فَقَالَ يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ، أَلاَ تَسْمَعُ إِلَى هَذِهِ مَا تَجْهَرُ بِهِ عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The wife of Rifa`a Al-Qurazi came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "I was Rifa`a's wife, but he divorced me and it was a final irrevocable divorce. Then I married `Abdur-Rahman bin Az-Zubair but he is impotent." The Prophet (ﷺ) asked her 'Do you want to remarry Rifa`a? You cannot unless you had a complete sexual relation with your present husband." Abu Bakr was sitting with Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and Khalid bin Sa`id bin Al-`As was at the door waiting to be admitted. He said, "O Abu Bakr! Do you hear what this (woman) is revealing frankly before the Prophet (ﷺ) ?

bukhari:2639.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this ruling (citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) serves as a moral deterrent against reckless triple divorces, and that Muhammad used the polite metaphor of 'sweetness' (*ʿusaylah*) while forbidding pre-arranged *ḥalālah* marriages. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *'lā ḥattā tadhūqī ʿusaylatahū wa yadhūqa ʿusaylataki'* ('No, not until you taste his sweetness and he tastes your sweetness'), showing that even when the woman's second husband was impotent (*mithlu hudbati al-thawb*) and she wished to return to her first husband, Muhammad refused to permit reconciliation unless another man first sexually penetrated her. Parallel narrations (bukhari:5260, muslim:3526) further record Muhammad smiling at her predicament while enforcing a law from [Quran 2:230](quran://2/230) that penalizes the woman's body for her first husband's unilateral divorce.

bukhari:2639.note: Muhammad rules that an irrevocably divorced woman cannot remarry her first husband until she and an intervening second husband sexually consummate their union by 'tasting each other's sweetness' ([Quran 2:230](quran://2/230)), reversing the Torah's prohibition against remarrying a former wife after an intervening marriage ([Deuteronomy 24:1-4](bible://dt/24/1)).

Do you hear what this (woman) is revealing frankly before the Prophet (ﷺ) ?

bukhari:2639.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that [Quran 2:230](quran://2/230) improves upon [Deuteronomy 24:1-4](bible://dt/24/1) by offering a divorced couple a merciful pathway to reconcile if a genuine second marriage fails, whereas biblical law permanently forbids their remarriage once she weds another man. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *'lā ḥattā tadhūqī ʿusaylatahū wa yadhūqa ʿusaylataki'* ('No, not until you taste his sweetness and he tastes your sweetness'), proving that Islamic law makes another man's physical sexual penetration of the wife the mandatory prerequisite for returning to her original husband. Rather than protecting the sanctity of marriage, Muhammad's decree mandates as a divine requirement the exact sexual defilement by a third party that [Deuteronomy 24:4](bible://dt/24/4) condemns as an abomination before God.

bukhari:7369.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:7369.note: When questioned by Muhammad during the slander incident—years after his marriage to Aisha was consummated—the slave girl Barira testifies that Aisha's only fault is being a young girl of tender age (jariyah hadithat al-sinn) who falls asleep and leaves her family's dough unguarded for domestic animals to eat.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَتْ مَا رَأَيْتُ أَمْرًا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ أَنَّهَا جَارِيَةٌ حَدِيثَةُ السِّنِّ تَنَامُ عَنْ عَجِينِ أَهْلِهَا فَتَأْتِي الدَّاجِنُ فَتَأْكُلُهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: She replied, "I have not seen anything more than that she is a little girl who sleeps, leaving the dough of her family (unguarded) that the domestic goats come and eat it."

bukhari:7369.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that seventh-century Arabian girls matured rapidly into responsible adults by age nine, or promote revisionist timelines placing Aisha in her late teens at marriage while claiming the term jāriyah merely denotes a young woman. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that even years after the marriage was consummated (during the Ifk incident c. 627 AD), her own household servant Barirah characterized her as a jāriyah ḥadīthat al-sinn (جَارِيَةٌ حَدِيثَةُ السِّنِّ—'a girl of very tender age') who lacked basic adult responsibility, falling asleep and leaving the family's dough (عَجِينِ أَهْلِهَا) to be eaten by domestic livestock. Reinforced by parallel narration bukhari:4750, where Aisha describes herself during this same expedition as a light-bodied young girl who had not yet put on adult flesh, the text directly refutes both revisionist age calculations and claims of early psychological maturity.

bukhari:5215.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5215.note: Anas bin Malik reports that Muhammad used to make the circuit (yaṭūfu) of all nine of his concurrent wives in a single night, operating under a prophetic exemption from the four-wife limit prescribed for other Muslims ([Quran 4:3](quran://4/3), [Quran 33:50](quran://33/50)). Parallel narrations (bukhari:268, bukhari:284) and classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī confirm that this phrase denotes having sexual intercourse with all nine wives using a single ritual bath (ghusl), which Anas attributed to Muhammad being granted the virility of thirty men.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ يَطُوفُ عَلَى نِسَائِهِ فِي اللَّيْلَةِ الْوَاحِدَةِ، وَلَهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ تِسْعُ نِسْوَةٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to pass by (have sexual relation with) all his wives in one night, and at that time he had nine wives

bukhari:5215.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the verb yaṭūfu (يَطُوفُ, 'to make the rounds') merely describes Muhammad paying polite social visits to check on his wives' well-being, or else cite Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī to frame his ability to satisfy nine wives as a divinely granted miracle of prophetic vigor. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in the direct parallel narrations of this exact report from Anas bin Malik (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 268, 284, and 5068) that he completed these rounds 'with a single ritual bath' (bi-ghuslin wāḥidin, بِغُسْلٍ وَاحِدٍ)—a major purification mandated strictly after sexual intercourse—and explains the feat by noting he 'was given the [sexual] strength of thirty men' (أُعْطِيَ قُوَّةَ ثَلاَثِينَ). This grammatical and ritual context completely refutes any non-sexual 'social visit' reading and confirms that classical Sunni tradition treated consecutive intercourse with nine women in a single night without washing between partners as a mark of prophetic distinction.

muslim:3497.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3497.note: After looking at the war captive Safiyya bint Huyayy and ordering Dihya to take another slave-girl from the prisoners in her place, Muhammad designates her own emancipation from captivity as her bridal dower and consummates the marriage with her at night on the return road from Khaybar ([Deuteronomy 21:10](bible://dt/21/10)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ وَأَصَبْنَاهَا عَنْوَةً وَجُمِعَ السَّبْىُ فَجَاءَهُ دِحْيَةُ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَعْطِنِي جَارِيَةً مِنَ السَّبْىِ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ اذْهَبْ فَخُذْ جَارِيَةً ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَأَخَذَ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتَ حُيَىٍّ فَجَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى نَبِيِّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ أَعْطَيْتَ دِحْيَةَ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتَ حُيَىٍّ سَيِّدِ قُرَيْظَةَ وَالنَّضِيرِ مَا تَصْلُحُ إِلاَّ لَكَ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ ادْعُوهُ بِهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَجَاءَ بِهَا فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ إِلَيْهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ خُذْ جَارِيَةً مِنَ السَّبْىِ غَيْرَهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ وَأَعْتَقَهَا وَتَزَوَّجَهَا ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُ ثَابِتٌ يَا أَبَا حَمْزَةَ مَا أَصْدَقَهَا قَالَ نَفْسَهَا أَعْتَقَهَا وَتَزَوَّجَهَا حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ بِالطَّرِيقِ جَهَّزَتْهَا لَهُ أُمُّ سُلَيْمٍ فَأَهْدَتْهَا لَهُ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَأَصْبَحَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَرُوسًا
problematic_excerpt.english: He said: We took it (the territory of Khaibar) by force, and there were gathered the prisoners of war. There came Dihya and he said: Messenger of Allah, bestow upon me a girl from among the prisoners. He said: Go and get any girl. He made a choice for Safiyya daughter of Huyayy (b. Akhtab). There came a person to Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) and said: Apostle of Allah, you have bestowed Safiyya bint Huyayy, the chief of Quraiza and al-Nadir, upon Dihya and she is worthy of you only. He said: Call him along with her. So he came along with her. When Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) saw her he said: Take any other woman from among the prisoners. He (the narrator) said: He (the Holy Prophet) then granted her emancipation and married her. Thabit said to him: Abu Hamza, how much dower did he (the Holy Prophet) give to her? He said: He granted her freedom and then married her. On the way Umm Sulaim embellished her and then sent her to him (the Holy Prophet) at night. Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) appeared as a bridegroom in the morning.

muslim:3497.literal_translation: He said: We conquered it by force, and the captives were gathered. Dihya came to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, give me a slave-girl from the captives.' He said: 'Go and take a slave-girl.' So he took Safiyya bint Huyayy. A man came to the Prophet of Allah and said: 'O Prophet of Allah, you gave Dihya Safiyya bint Huyayy, the chief of Qurayza and al-Nadir; she is suitable only for you.' He said: 'Summon him with her.' So he came with her, and when the Prophet looked at her, he said: 'Take another slave-girl from the captives other than her.' And he emancipated her and married her. Thabit asked him: 'O Abu Hamza, what dower did he give her?' He said: 'Herself—he emancipated her and married her.' When he was on the road, Umm Sulaim prepared her for him and sent her to him at night, and the Prophet woke up in the morning as a bridegroom.

translation_issue.arabic_term: أَعْطِنِي جَارِيَةً مِنَ السَّبْىِ ... خُذْ جَارِيَةً مِنَ السَّبْىِ غَيْرَهَا ... مَا أَصْدَقَهَا قَالَ نَفْسَهَا
translation_issue.published_rendering: bestow upon me a girl from among the prisoners ... Take any other woman from among the prisoners ... how much dower did he (the Holy Prophet) give to her? He said: He granted her freedom
translation_issue.literal_meaning: give me a slave-girl from the captives ... Take another slave-girl from the captives other than her ... What dower did he give her? He said: Herself
translation_issue.explanation: The translator renders 'jāriyah' ('female slave') as 'girl' or 'woman' and omits 'nafsahā' ('herself') to soften the depiction of dividing enslaved women as war booty and using Safiyya's own release from captivity as her bridal price.

muslim:3497.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad honorably married Safiyya with a magnanimous bridal dower (mahr) of freedom and consummated the union only after a respectful waiting period with her joyful consent. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that her dower was merely 'herself' ('mā aṣdaqahā? qāla: nafsahā'), meaning Muhammad paid her nothing and used release from the very captivity he had just inflicted upon her as her bridal price—a ruling Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar note was treated as a special prophetic privilege (khaṣā'iṣ) exempting him from financial payment. Moreover, the text states that she was prepared and delivered to his bed at night while the army was still on the road back from Khaybar ('bi-l-ṭarīqi ... fa-ahdathā lahu min al-layli'), just days after his forces had slaughtered her husband, father, and brother.

muslim:3497.note: Muhammad launches a dawn raid on the town of Khaybar as its inhabitants go out to their daily work, proclaiming three times that Khaybar is ruined before conquering it by force and gathering the war captives ([Quran 37:177](quran://37/177)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ الْقَرْيَةَ قَالَ ‏"‏ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ خَرِبَتْ خَيْبَرُ إِنَّا إِذَا نَزَلْنَا بِسَاحَةِ قَوْمٍ فَسَاءَ صَبَاحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَهَا ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ قَالَ وَقَدْ خَرَجَ الْقَوْمُ إِلَى أَعْمَالِهِمْ فَقَالُوا مُحَمَّدٌ وَاللَّهِ ‏.‏ قَالَ عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ وَقَالَ بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا مُحَمَّدٌ وَالْخَمِيسُ ‏.‏ قَالَ وَأَصَبْنَاهَا عَنْوَةً وَجُمِعَ السَّبْىُ
problematic_excerpt.english: As he entered the habitation he called:Allahu Akbar (Allah is the Greatest). Khaibar is ruined. And when we get down in the valley of a people evil is the morning of the warned ones. He repeated it thrice. In the meanwhile the people went out for their work, and said: By Allah, Muhammad (has come). Abd al-'Aziz or some of our companions said: Muhammad and the army (have come). He said: We took it (the territory of Khaibar) by force, and there were gathered the prisoners of war.

muslim:3497.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the expedition against Khaybar was a purely defensive pre-emptive strike against an imminent, mobilized Jewish military threat. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the inhabitants had no army mobilized and were caught completely off guard going out to their daily farm work ('wa-qad kharaja al-qawmu ilā a'mālihim'—carrying spades and baskets in bukhari:371) when Muhammad ambushed them at dawn, conquered their territory by brute force ('anwatan), and enslaved their families ('al-sabyu'). In fact, classical commentators like Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar cite this exact narration to prove the legality of launching surprise dawn raids without prior military warning against any non-Muslim population that has already heard the general call to Islam.

muslim:3497.note: After conquering Khaybar by force and gathering the war captives, Muhammad permits Dihya to take a slave-girl from the prisoners, summons him with Safiyya bint Huyayy after being told she is suitable only for the Prophet, and upon looking at her orders Dihya to take a different slave-girl from the captives before emancipating and marrying her himself.
