translation_issue.published_rendering: bestow upon me a girl from among the prisoners ... Take any other woman from among the prisoners ... how much dower did he (the Holy Prophet) give to her? He said: He granted her freedom
translation_issue.literal_meaning: give me a slave-girl from the captives ... Take another slave-girl from the captives other than her ... What dower did he give her? He said: Herself
translation_issue.explanation: The translator renders 'jāriyah' ('female slave') as 'girl' or 'woman' and omits 'nafsahā' ('herself') to soften the depiction of dividing enslaved women as war booty and using Safiyya's own release from captivity as her bridal price.

muslim:3497.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad took Safiyya from Dihya out of noble compassion to rescue a chief's daughter from the indignity of slavery by emancipating and marrying her. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad himself ordered the enslavement of the women ('jumi'a al-sabyu'), only reclaimed Safiyya after summoning and physically inspecting her ('falammā naẓara ilayhā'), and immediately commanded Dihya to take a different female captive into concubinage instead ('khudh jāriyatan min al-sabyi ghayrahā'). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (muslim:3500) record that Muhammad bought Safiyya from Dihya for the price of seven human captives ('bi-sab'ati ar'usin'), confirming that the entire exchange operated as chattel slave trading.

bukhari:3894.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:3894.note: Aisha recounts that Muhammad married her when she was six years old, and that when she was nine, her mother called her from playing on a swing with her friends, had Ansar women prepare her, and handed her over to him to consummate the marriage (bukhari:5133; [Quran 65:4](quran://65/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: تَزَوَّجَنِي النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَنَا بِنْتُ سِتِّ سِنِينَ، فَقَدِمْنَا الْمَدِينَةَ فَنَزَلْنَا فِي بَنِي الْحَارِثِ بْنِ خَزْرَجٍ، فَوُعِكْتُ فَتَمَرَّقَ شَعَرِي فَوَفَى جُمَيْمَةً، فَأَتَتْنِي أُمِّي أُمُّ رُومَانَ وَإِنِّي لَفِي أُرْجُوحَةٍ وَمَعِي صَوَاحِبُ لِي، فَصَرَخَتْ بِي فَأَتَيْتُهَا لاَ أَدْرِي مَا تُرِيدُ بِي فَأَخَذَتْ بِيَدِي حَتَّى أَوْقَفَتْنِي عَلَى باب الدَّارِ، وَإِنِّي لأَنْهَجُ، حَتَّى سَكَنَ بَعْضُ نَفَسِي، ثُمَّ أَخَذَتْ شَيْئًا مِنْ مَاءٍ فَمَسَحَتْ بِهِ وَجْهِي وَرَأْسِي ثُمَّ أَدْخَلَتْنِي الدَّارَ فَإِذَا نِسْوَةٌ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ فِي الْبَيْتِ فَقُلْنَ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ وَالْبَرَكَةِ، وَعَلَى خَيْرِ طَائِرٍ‏.‏ فَأَسْلَمَتْنِي إِلَيْهِنَّ فَأَصْلَحْنَ مِنْ شَأْنِي، فَلَمْ يَرُعْنِي إِلاَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ضُحًى، فَأَسْلَمَتْنِي إِلَيْهِ، وَأَنَا يَوْمَئِذٍ بِنْتُ تِسْعِ سِنِينَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) engaged me when I was a girl of six (years). We went to Medina and stayed at the home of Bani-al-Harith bin Khazraj. Then I got ill and my hair fell down. Later on my hair grew (again) and my mother, Um Ruman, came to me while I was playing in a swing with some of my girl friends. She called me, and I went to her, not knowing what she wanted to do to me. She caught me by the hand and made me stand at the door of the house. I was breathless then, and when my breathing became alright, she took some water and rubbed my face and head with it. Then she took me into the house. There in the house I saw some Ansari women who said, "Best wishes and Allah's Blessing and a good luck." Then she entrusted me to them and they prepared me (for the marriage). Unexpectedly Allah's Apostle came to me in the forenoon and my mother handed me over to him, and at that time I was a girl of nine years of age

bukhari:3894.literal_translation: The Prophet (ﷺ) married me when I was a girl of six years. We came to Medina and stayed among the Banu al-Harith bin Khazraj. Then I became ill and my hair fell out, then it grew back to shoulder-length. My mother, Umm Ruman, came to me while I was on a swing with some of my girlfriends. She shouted for me, so I came to her, not knowing what she wanted with me. She took me by the hand until she made me stand at the door of the house, and I was gasping for breath until my breath calmed down. Then she took some water and wiped my face and head with it, then brought me into the house. There were women of the Ansar in the house, and they said, 'Upon the good, the blessing, and the best fortune.' She handed me over to them and they prepared me. Nothing startled me except the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arriving in the forenoon, and she handed me over to him, and at that time I was a girl of nine years of age.

translation_issue.arabic_term: تَزَوَّجَنِي
translation_issue.published_rendering: engaged me
translation_issue.literal_meaning: married me
translation_issue.explanation: The translator renders 'tazawwajanī' ('married me / contracted marriage with me') as 'engaged me' to give modern English readers the impression of a betrothal rather than a completed marriage contract at age six.

bukhari:3894.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Aisha was either much older based on revisionist historical timelines, or already a mature adult at age nine under 7th-century AD Arabian norms, citing classical commentators like Ibn Hajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) and Al-Nawawī who claim the three-year delay after the marriage contract (tazawwajanī) ensured her physical readiness. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states she was six (bintu sitti sinīna) at marriage and nine (bintu tisʿi sinīna) at consummation, depicting a breathless child pulled straight off a swing (urjūḥah) who had no idea what was being done to her (lā adrī mā turīdu bī) until Muhammad suddenly startled her (falam yaruʿnī). Furthermore, Ibn Hajar himself acknowledges under bukhari:6130 that Aisha continued playing with dolls after consummation—a concession reserved in Islamic law strictly for prepubescent children (ghayr bāligh)—while Quran 65:4 explicitly legislates post-consummation divorce waiting periods for girls who have not yet menstruated (wa-allāʾī lam yaḥiḍna).

bukhari:4788.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:4788.note: Aisha recounts feeling jealous of the women who offered themselves to Muhammad and questioning how a woman could do so, until the revelation of [Quran 33:51](quran://33/51) permitted him to defer or receive whichever of them he wished without blame. Upon hearing this verse, Aisha remarked to Muhammad that she saw his Lord hastening to fulfill his desires (hawāka).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنْتُ أَغَارُ عَلَى اللاَّتِي وَهَبْنَ أَنْفُسَهُنَّ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَقُولُ أَتَهَبُ الْمَرْأَةُ نَفْسَهَا فَلَمَّا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ‏{‏تُرْجِئُ مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ وَتُؤْوِي إِلَيْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَمَنِ ابْتَغَيْتَ مِمَّنْ عَزَلْتَ فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكَ‏}‏ قُلْتُ مَا أُرَى رَبَّكَ إِلاَّ يُسَارِعُ فِي هَوَاكَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I used to look down upon those ladies who had given themselves to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and I used to say, "Can a lady give herself (to a man)?" But when Allah revealed: "You (O Muhammad) can postpone (the turn of) whom you will of them (your wives), and you may receive any of them whom you will; and there is no blame on you if you invite one whose turn you have set aside (temporarily).' (33.51) I said (to the Prophet), "I feel that your Lord hastens in fulfilling your wishes and desires

bukhari:4788.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that—as claimed in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—Aisha's remark was merely affectionate praise of Muhammad's favored station with Allah or playful marital coquetry (*idlāl*), and that his marriages served socio-political alliances rather than personal gratification. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Aisha was driven by intense jealousy (`كُنْتُ أَغَارُ`, *kuntu aghāru*, disguised in English translations as "I used to look down upon") over women offering themselves to Muhammad (`وَهَبْنَ أَنْفُسَهُنَّ`), and she pointedly used the noun `هَوَاكَ` (*hawāka*—personal desire, passion, or caprice) in declaring, "I see nothing except that your Lord hastens to fulfill your desire" (`مَا أُرَى رَبَّكَ إِلاَّ يُسَارِعُ فِي هَوَاكَ`). Furthermore, her observation was triggered directly by Quran 33:50–51 granting Muhammad an exclusive privilege (`خَالِصَةً لَكَ`) to take women who offered themselves without a dowry and to suspend his wives' mandatory nightly turns at will (`تُرْجِئُ مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ وَتُؤْوِي إِلَيْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ`), proving that revelations were conveniently arriving to satisfy his immediate domestic and sexual preferences.

bukhari:5133.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5133.note: Aisha narrates that Muhammad married her when she was six years old and consummated the marriage when she was nine years old, after which she remained with him for nine years until his death. Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi affirm these literal ages and cite this report alongside [Quran 65:4](quran://65/4) to establish the legal permissibility of contracting and consummating marriage with a minor.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم تَزَوَّجَهَا وَهْىَ بِنْتُ سِتِّ سِنِينَ، وَأُدْخِلَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَهْىَ بِنْتُ تِسْعٍ، وَمَكَثَتْ عِنْدَهُ تِسْعًا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: that the Prophet (ﷺ) married her when she was six years old and he consummated his marriage when she was nine years old, and then she remained with him for nine years (i.e., till his death)

bukhari:5133.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue either that girls reached puberty much earlier in 7th-century AD Arabia—making Aisha a mature adult at nine—or that the narrator Hishām ibn ʿUrwah suffered memory loss in Iraq and miscalculated her age. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states she was six (`بِنْتُ سِتِّ سِنِينَ`) at the marriage contract and nine (`بِنْتُ تِسْعٍ`) when delivered for consummation (`وَأُدْخِلَتْ عَلَيْهِ`), a fact corroborated by independent non-Hishām chains (muslim:3481) and by bukhari:6130, where she was still playing with dolls—an allowance Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* admits was strictly reserved for a prepubescent girl (`غَيْرُ بَالِغٍ`). Furthermore, Al-Bukhārī uses this exact narration to anchored his legal chapter on [Quran 65:4](quran://65/4), which prescribes a post-consummation waiting period (`عِدَّة`) for wives who have not yet menstruated (`وَاللَّائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ`), proving that consummating marriage with prepubescent girls is a timeless Quranic institution rather than a historical miscalculation.

bukhari:5134.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5134.note: Aisha narrates that Muhammad married her when she was six years old and consummated the marriage when she was nine years old, remaining with her for nine years until his death ([Quran 65:4](quran://65/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم تَزَوَّجَهَا وَهْىَ بِنْتُ سِتِّ سِنِينَ، وَبَنَى بِهَا وَهْىَ بِنْتُ تِسْعِ سِنِينَ‏.‏ قَالَ هِشَامٌ وَأُنْبِئْتُ أَنَّهَا كَانَتْ عِنْدَهُ تِسْعَ سِنِينَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: that the Prophet (ﷺ) married her when she was six years old and he consummated his marriage when she was nine years old. Hisham said: I have been informed that `Aisha remained with the Prophet (ﷺ) for nine years (i.e. till his death)

bukhari:5134.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that 7th-century AD cultural norms and rapid desert puberty made Aisha physically mature at nine, or claim that the narrator Hishām ibn ʿUrwah suffered memory loss in Iraq and misstated her age. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad consummated the marriage (wa-banā bihā) when she was a girl of nine years (bintu tisʿi sinīn), a fact corroborated independently of Hishām through Al-Zuhrī (Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:3481) and confirmed by Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6130, which records Aisha still playing with dolls (al-banāt)—an exemption Ibn Ḥajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) notes was strictly reserved for prepubescent girls (ghayr bāligh). Furthermore, classical Sunni authorities including Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) and Ibn Ḥajar cite this exact narration alongside Quran 65:4 (wa-allāʾī lam yaḥiḍna, 'those who have not yet menstruated') not as a bygone cultural custom, but to codify the permanent Islamic legal permissibility of contracting and consummating marriage with prepubescent minors.

bukhari:5158.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5158.note: Muhammad married Aisha when she was six years old, consummated the marriage with her when she was nine years old, and she remained with him for nine years ([Quran 65:4](quran://65/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: تَزَوَّجَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَائِشَةَ وَهْىَ ابْنَةُ سِتٍّ وَبَنَى بِهَا وَهْىَ ابْنَةُ تِسْعٍ وَمَكَثَتْ عِنْدَهُ تِسْعًا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) wrote the (marriage contract) with `Aisha while she was six years old and consummated his marriage with her while she was nine years old and she remained with him for nine years (i.e. till his death)

bukhari:5158.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that girls matured faster in 7th-century AD Arabia so Aisha had already reached puberty at age nine, or they attempt to impugn the narrator Hisham ibn Urwah to claim she was actually in her late teens. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad married her as a girl of six (ابْنَةُ سِتٍّ) and consummated the marriage with her at nine (وَبَنَى بِهَا وَهْىَ ابْنَةُ تِسْعٍ)—a fact confirmed by independent chains outside Hisham's Iraqi period (Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:3481) and by Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6130, where Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī admits Aisha was still playing with dolls because she was prepubescent (لَمْ تَكُنْ بَلَغَتْ). Furthermore, Quran 65:4 explicitly legislates the post-consummation divorce waiting period ('iddah) for girls who have not yet menstruated (وَاللَّائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ), proving that prepubescent marital consummation is entrenched in Islamic law itself.

muslim:3481.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3481.note: Transmitted via al-Zuhri from 'Urwah (independently of Hisham ibn 'Urwah), Aisha reports that Muhammad married her when she was seven years old, she was brought to his home as a bride at the age of nine with her dolls still with her, and he died when she was eighteen.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم تَزَوَّجَهَا وَهْىَ بِنْتُ سَبْعِ سِنِينَ وَزُفَّتْ إِلَيْهِ وَهِيَ بِنْتُ تِسْعِ سِنِينَ وَلُعَبُهَا مَعَهَا وَمَاتَ عَنْهَا وَهِيَ بِنْتُ ثَمَانَ عَشْرَةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) reported that Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) married her when she was seven years old, and he was taken to his house as a bride when she was nine, and her dolls were with her; and when he (the Holy Prophet) died she was eighteen years old

muslim:3481.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that girls in 7th-century AD Arabia matured rapidly and that Aisha had already reached biological puberty and adulthood when her marriage was consummated at age nine. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that she was brought to Muhammad as a bride at nine while "her dolls were with her" (وَلُعَبُهَا مَعَهَا, wa-luʿabuhā maʿahā)—a detail that classical authorities like Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī (Fatḥ al-Bārī on bukhari:6130) and Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) explicitly cite as proof that she was still a prepubescent child (lam tablugh), since playing with dolls was forbidden for anyone who had reached puberty. Furthermore, this practice is enshrined in Quran 65:4, which explicitly legislates the post-consummation divorce waiting period (ʿiddah) for girls "who have not yet menstruated" (وَاللَّائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ).

bukhari:4211.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:4211.note: Upon hearing of the beauty of the newlywed Safiyya bint Huyayy after her husband was killed at Khaybar in AD 628, Muhammad selected her for himself and departed with her. On the return march at Sadd al-Sahba, as soon as she became lawful (*ḥallat*) by completing a single menstrual cycle, Muhammad consummated the marriage (*banā bihā*) and held a wedding banquet.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا فَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْحِصْنَ ذُكِرَ لَهُ جَمَالُ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتِ حُيَىِّ بْنِ أَخْطَبَ، وَقَدْ قُتِلَ زَوْجُهَا وَكَانَتْ عَرُوسًا، فَاصْطَفَاهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِنَفْسِهِ، فَخَرَجَ بِهَا، حَتَّى بَلَغْنَا سَدَّ الصَّهْبَاءِ حَلَّتْ، فَبَنَى بِهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم
problematic_excerpt.english: when Allah helped His Apostle to open the fort, the beauty of Safiya bint Huyai bin Akhtaq whose husband had been killed while she was a bride, was mentioned to Allah's Apostle. The Prophet (ﷺ) selected her for himself, and set out with her, and when we reached a place called Sidd-as-Sahba,' Safiya became clean from her menses. Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) married her.

bukhari:4211.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's observance of Safiyya's waiting period before consummation and his gentle gesture of offering his knee for her to mount the camel demonstrate a respectful, consensual marriage rather than wartime coercion. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that he consummated the union with her (fa-banā bihā) on the return march from Khaybar at Sadd al-Sahba' immediately after a single menstrual cycle ended (ḥallat), only days after his forces killed her newlywed husband (wa-qad qutila zawjuhā wa-kānat ʿarūsan). As classical commentators like Al-Nawawī and Ibn Hajar explain, she was subjected to the expedited one-cycle clearance required for female war captives (istibrāʾ al-sabiyyah) rather than the four-month-and-ten-day mourning period granted to free widows (Q 2:234), proving her legal status as a conquered captive taken on the way home from battle.

bukhari:4211.note: After the conquest of Khaybar in AD 628, Muhammad was informed of the beauty of the newlywed Safiyya bint Huyayy—whose husband had just been killed—and selected her for himself (*iṣṭafāhā li-nafsih*) from the war captives before emancipating her as her own marriage dower (bukhari:371, bukhari:2235).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا فَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْحِصْنَ ذُكِرَ لَهُ جَمَالُ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتِ حُيَىِّ بْنِ أَخْطَبَ، وَقَدْ قُتِلَ زَوْجُهَا وَكَانَتْ عَرُوسًا، فَاصْطَفَاهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِنَفْسِهِ، فَخَرَجَ بِهَا، حَتَّى بَلَغْنَا سَدَّ الصَّهْبَاءِ حَلَّتْ، فَبَنَى بِهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم
problematic_excerpt.english: when Allah helped His Apostle to open the fort, the beauty of Safiya bint Huyai bin Akhtaq whose husband had been killed while she was a bride, was mentioned to Allah's Apostle. The Prophet (ﷺ) selected her for himself, and set out with her, and when we reached a place called Sidd-as-Sahba,' Safiya became clean from her menses. Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) married her.

bukhari:4211.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī, that Muhammad took Safiyya bint Huyayy out of chivalry to rescue a chief's daughter from the humiliation of slavery under Dihya al-Kalbi, emancipating her as her dowry (ṣadāq) and elevating her to a Mother of the Believers. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad only selected her as his personal share of the war booty (fa-ṣṭafāhā al-nabī li-nafsihi) after her physical beauty was reported to him (dhukira lahu jamālu Ṣafiyyah) right after her husband was killed while she was a newlywed bride (wa-qad qutila zawjuhā wa-kānat ʿarūsan). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:371, bukhari:2235) confirm she was rounded up in the captive haul (al-sabī), traded for other captives, and taken away while the Companions debated whether he would use her as a slave concubine (mā malakat yamīnuhu) or a wife.

bukhari:2235.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:2235.note: Upon conquering the fortress at Khaybar (AD 628), Muhammad was informed of the beauty of Safiyya bint Huyayy—a newlywed bride (*ʿarūs*) whose husband had been killed—and selected her for himself (*iṣṭafāhā li-nafsihi*). As soon as she completed a single menstrual cycle (*ḥallat*) at Sadd al-Rawha' during the return journey to Medina, he consummated the marriage with her (*banā bihā*) and held a wedding banquet of *ḥays* on a small leather sheet.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَدِمَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم خَيْبَرَ، فَلَمَّا فَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْحِصْنَ ذُكِرَ لَهُ جَمَالُ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتِ حُيَىِّ بْنِ أَخْطَبَ، وَقَدْ قُتِلَ زَوْجُهَا، وَكَانَتْ عَرُوسًا، فَاصْطَفَاهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِنَفْسِهِ فَخَرَجَ بِهَا، حَتَّى بَلَغْنَا سَدَّ الرَّوْحَاءِ حَلَّتْ، فَبَنَى بِهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) came to Khaibar and when Allah made him victorious and he conquered the town by breaking the enemy's defense, the beauty of Safiya bint Huyai bin Akhtab was mentioned to him and her husband had been killed while she was a bride. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) selected her for himself and he set out in her company till he reached Sadd-ar-Rawha' where her menses were over and he married her.

bukhari:2235.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad observed a respectful waiting period (*ʿiddah*) after the death of Safiyya's husband so she could grieve and freely consent to marriage in Medina. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that her husband had just been killed while she was a newlywed bride (*wa-qad qutila zawjuhā wa-kānat ʿarūsan*) and that Muhammad consummated the union (*fa-banā bihā*) on the roadside at Sadd al-Rawha' the instant she finished a single menstrual bleed (*ḥallat*). As Ibn Hajar notes in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, this applied the expedited *istibrāʾ* rule for newly enslaved war captives (checking only for pregnancy via one menses) rather than the four-month-and-ten-day mourning period mandated for free widows in Quran 2:234.

bukhari:2235.note: Following the conquest of the fortress at Khaybar (AD 628), after the beauty of the newlywed bride (*ʿarūs*) Safiyya bint Huyayy was mentioned to him and her husband had been killed, Muhammad selected her for himself (*iṣṭafāhā li-nafsihi*) as his personal share. He then took her with him until she completed a single menstrual waiting period (*ḥallat*) at Sadd al-Rawha', where he consummated the union with her (*banā bihā*) on the return march to Medina.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَدِمَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم خَيْبَرَ، فَلَمَّا فَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْحِصْنَ ذُكِرَ لَهُ جَمَالُ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتِ حُيَىِّ بْنِ أَخْطَبَ، وَقَدْ قُتِلَ زَوْجُهَا، وَكَانَتْ عَرُوسًا، فَاصْطَفَاهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِنَفْسِهِ فَخَرَجَ بِهَا، حَتَّى بَلَغْنَا سَدَّ الرَّوْحَاءِ حَلَّتْ، فَبَنَى بِهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) came to Khaibar and when Allah made him victorious and he conquered the town by breaking the enemy's defense, the beauty of Safiya bint Huyai bin Akhtab was mentioned to him and her husband had been killed while she was a bride. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) selected her for himself and he set out in her company till he reached Sadd-ar-Rawha' where her menses were over and he married her.

bukhari:2235.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad emancipated and married Safiyya bint Huyayy out of humanitarian compassion to preserve her noble status as a chief's daughter rather than claiming her as war booty. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that he claimed her only after her physical beauty was reported to him (*dhukira lahu jamālu Ṣafiyyata*) and that he exercised the commander's *ṣafī* prerogative to select her for himself (*fa-ṣṭafāhā... li-nafsihi*). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (such as `bukhari:371` and `muslim:3499`) record that she was initially awarded as a slave to Dihya al-Kalbi until companions told Muhammad she was too beautiful for anyone else, prompting him to purchase her for seven slaves and substitute her manumission for a bridal dowry (*mahr*).

muslim:3482.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3482.note: Transmitted via the Kufan chain of al-A'mash, Ibrāhīm al-Nakha'ī, and al-Aswad (independent of Hishām ibn 'Urwah), Aisha reports that Muhammad married her when she was six years old, consummated the marriage with her (*banā bihā*) when she was nine, and died when she was eighteen.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ تَزَوَّجَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهْىَ بِنْتُ سِتٍّ وَبَنَى بِهَا وَهْىَ بِنْتُ تِسْعٍ وَمَاتَ عَنْهَا وَهْىَ بِنْتُ ثَمَانَ عَشْرَةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) reported that Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) married her when she was six years old, and he (the Holy Prophet) took her to his house when she was nine, and when he (the Holy Prophet) died she was eighteen years old

muslim:3482.literal_translation: From Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married her when she was a girl of six, and consummated the marriage with her (bana biha) when she was a girl of nine, and died leaving her when she was a girl of eighteen.

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَبَنَى بِهَا وَهْىَ بِنْتُ تِسْعٍ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and he (the Holy Prophet) took her to his house when she was nine
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and he consummated the marriage with her (idiomatically; lit., 'set up the bridal tent/dwelling with her') when she was a girl of nine
translation_issue.explanation: In classical Arabic lexicography (Ibn Manzur's Lisan al-'Arab, Lane's Lexicon, s.v. b-n-y) and Islamic jurisprudence (al-Nawawi's Sharh Sahih Muslim), 'bana biha' (originating from pitching a bridal tent over a new wife) is the standard legal and hadith term for consummating a marriage ('dakhala biha'). While standard translations of parallel narrations (e.g., Muhsin Khan in Bukhari 5133 and Darussalam's Sahih Muslim) render 'bana biha' directly as 'consummated the marriage with her,' Siddiqui softens it to 'took her to his house,' which can mislead English readers into thinking she merely moved into his household without sexual consummation.

muslim:3482.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Aisha had already reached full adult maturity in 7th-century AD Arabia, or that reports of her age are unreliable because they allegedly rely solely on the Medinan narrator Hisham ibn 'Urwah in old age. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *wa-banā bihā wa-hiya bintu tisʿin* ('and he consummated the marriage with her when she was a girl of nine') through an entirely independent Kufan chain via Al-Aswad and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i directly from Aisha, demolishing the single-narrator excuse. Moreover, parallel narrations (*Sahih Muslim* 3480; *Sahih al-Bukhari* 6130) record that she was still playing with dolls—which Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* confirms was only permitted for prepubescent girls—and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* cites this exact Hadith alongside Quran 65:4 to establish the Sunni legal consensus permitting a father to marry off his prepubescent daughter.

bukhari:3896.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:3896.note: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr reports that two years after Khadijah's death, Muhammad contracted marriage with Aisha when she was six years old and consummated the marriage when she was nine years old ([Quran 65:4](quran://65/4)). Classical commentators including Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi affirm these literal ages and cite this narration as legal proof for the permissibility of marrying and consummating marriage with prepubescent girls.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: تُوُفِّيَتْ خَدِيجَةُ قَبْلَ مَخْرَجِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ بِثَلاَثِ سِنِينَ، فَلَبِثَ سَنَتَيْنِ أَوْ قَرِيبًا مِنْ ذَلِكَ، وَنَكَحَ عَائِشَةَ وَهْىَ بِنْتُ سِتِّ سِنِينَ، ثُمَّ بَنَى بِهَا وَهْىَ بِنْتُ تِسْعِ سِنِينَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Khadija died three years before the Prophet (ﷺ) departed to Medina. He stayed there for two years or so and then he married `Aisha when she was a girl of six years of age, and he consummated that marriage when she was nine years old

bukhari:3896.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that marriage at nine was a harmless 7th-century AD cultural norm once a girl reached puberty, or else claim that the narrator Hishām ibn ʿUrwah erred in his old age and that Aisha was actually a teenager. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad contracted the marriage when she was 'a girl of six years' (بِنْتُ سِتِّ سِنِينَ) and consummated it when she was 'a girl of nine years' (بِنْتُ تِسْعِ سِنِينَ)—a fact corroborated by independent *Ṣaḥīḥ* chains (such as al-Zuhrī and al-Aʿmash) and by Aisha's admission that she still played with dolls (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 6130), which Ibn Ḥajar confirms in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* was only permitted for prepubescent girls (*ghayr bāligh*). Furthermore, because Muhammad is Islam's timeless moral exemplar (Quran 33:21) and Quran 65:4 legislates post-consummation divorce waiting periods for girls who 'have not yet menstruated' (وَاللَّائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ), classical jurists like al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar cite this exact Hadith to codify the permanent permissibility of marrying and consummating with minor girls.

muslim:3500.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3500.note: When a 'beautiful slave-girl' (*jāriyah jamīlah*)—Safiyya bint Huyayy—falls into Dihya's share of the Khaybar war booty, Muhammad purchases her for seven slaves ('seven heads,' *sabʿati ar'us*) and entrusts her to Umm Sulaim to beautify and prepare her for him (with the sub-narrator adding that he thinks he said she also observed her waiting period in Umm Sulaim's house) before holding their wedding feast.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ وَهَزَمَهُمُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَوَقَعَتْ فِي سَهْمِ دَحْيَةَ جَارِيَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ فَاشْتَرَاهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِسَبْعَةِ أَرْؤُسٍ ثُمَّ دَفَعَهَا إِلَى أُمِّ سُلَيْمٍ تُصَنِّعُهَا لَهُ وَتُهَيِّئُهَا - قَالَ وَأَحْسِبُهُ قَالَ - وَتَعْتَدُّ فِي بَيْتِهَا وَهِيَ صَفِيَّةُ بِنْتُ حُيَىٍّ - قَالَ - وَجَعَلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَلِيمَتَهَا التَّمْرَ وَالأَقِطَ وَالسَّمْنَ فُحِصَتِ الأَرْضُ أَفَاحِيصَ وَجِيءَ بِالأَنْطَاعِ فَوُضِعَتْ فِيهَا وَجِيءَ بِالأَقِطِ وَالسَّمْنِ فَشَبِعَ النَّاسُ - قَالَ - وَقَالَ النَّاسُ لاَ نَدْرِي أَتَزَوَّجَهَا أَمِ اتَّخَذَهَا أُمَّ وَلَدٍ ‏.‏ قَالُوا إِنْ حَجَبَهَا فَهْىَ امْرَأَتُهُ وَإِنْ لَمْ يَحْجُبْهَا فَهْىَ أُمُّ وَلَدٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah, the Majestic and the Glorious, defeated them (the inhabitants of Khaibar), and there fell to the lot of Dihya a beautiful girl, and Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) got her in exchange of seven heads, and then entrusted her to Umm Sulaim so that she might embellish her and prepare her (for marriage) with him. He (the narrator) said: He had been under the impression that he had said that so that she might spend her period of 'Iddah in her (Umm Sulaim's) house. (The woman) was Safiyya daughter of Huyayy. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) arranged the wedding feast consisting of dates, cheese, and refined butter, and pits were dug and tiers were set in them dining cloths, and there was brought cheese and refined butter, and these were placed there. And the people ate to their fill, and they said: We do not know whether he (the Holy Prophet) had married her (as a free woman), or as a slave woman. They said: If he (the Holy Prophet) would make her wear the veil, then she would be a (free married) woman, and if he would not make her wear the veil, then she should be a slave woman.

muslim:3500.literal_translation: And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, defeated them, and a beautiful slave-girl fell into the booty share of Dihya, so the Messenger of Allah bought her for seven heads [of slaves], then handed her over to Umm Sulaim to beautify her and prepare her for him—the narrator said: and I think he said: and to observe her waiting period in her house—and she was Safiyya bint Huyayy. And the Messenger of Allah made her wedding feast of dates, dried curd, and clarified butter... And the people said: 'We do not know whether he married her or took her as a concubine (*umm walad*).' They said: 'If he veils her, she is his wife, and if he does not veil her, she is a concubine (*umm walad*).'

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَوَقَعَتْ فِي سَهْمِ دَحْيَةَ جَارِيَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ فَاشْتَرَاهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِسَبْعَةِ أَرْؤُسٍ ثُمَّ دَفَعَهَا إِلَى أُمِّ سُلَيْمٍ تُصَنِّعُهَا لَهُ وَتُهَيِّئُهَا
translation_issue.published_rendering: and there fell to the lot of Dihya a beautiful girl, and Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) got her in exchange of seven heads, and then entrusted her to Umm Sulaim so that she might embellish her and prepare her (for marriage) with him.
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and a beautiful slave-girl fell into the booty share of Dihya, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) bought her for seven heads [of slaves], then handed her over to Umm Sulaim to beautify her for him and prepare her.
translation_issue.explanation: The translator softens 'jāriyah' ('slave-girl' in the context of war spoils) to 'girl,' softens 'ishtarāhā' ('bought her') to 'got her in exchange' to avoid explicitly stating that Muhammad purchased a human being, and interpolates the unattested parenthetical '(for marriage)' into 'tuhayyi'uhā' ('prepare her') even though the Hadith immediately notes that the companions did not know whether he married her or took her as a concubine ('umm walad').

muslim:3500.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad married Safiyya purely out of political statesmanship because her noble lineage as the chief's daughter made her unsuitable for Dihya, and that he respectfully observed a waiting period (*ʿiddah*) before consummating the union. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the transaction was triggered when 'a beautiful slave-girl fell into the booty share of Dihya' (*وَقَعَتْ فِي سَهْمِ دَحْيَةَ جَارِيَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ*), after which Muhammad bought her and immediately handed her to Umm Sulaim to 'beautify her and prepare her for him' (*تُصَنِّعُهَا لَهُ وَتُهَيِّئُهَا*). Moreover, the sub-narrator's explicit doubt regarding any waiting period ('I think he said: and to observe her *ʿiddah* in her house,' *وَأَحْسِبُهُ قَالَ وَتَعْتَدُّ فِي بَيْتِهَا*) aligns with parallel Sahih narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4211, *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 3497) confirming he consummated the union on the march back from Khaybar right after her single menstrual clearance (*istibrā'*) as a newly acquired slave, rather than the four-month-and-ten-day mourning period mandated for free widows in Qur'an 2:234.

muslim:3500.note: After defeating the people of Khaybar, Muhammad buys the captive Safiyya bint Huyayy from Dihya's share of the war booty in exchange for seven enslaved captives ('seven heads,' *sabʿati ar'us*). His companions then wait to see whether he veils her to determine if he took her as a concubine (*umm walad*) or married her, concluding he married her when he places the veil on her for the return journey.

He (the narrator) said: He had been under the impression that he had said that so that she might spend her period of 'Iddah in her (Umm Sulaim's) house. (The woman) was Safiyya daughter of Huyayy. They said: If he (the Holy Prophet) would make her wear the veil, then she would be a (free married) woman, and if he would not make her wear the veil, then she should be a slave woman.

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَوَقَعَتْ فِي سَهْمِ دَحْيَةَ جَارِيَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ فَاشْتَرَاهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِسَبْعَةِ أَرْؤُسٍ ثُمَّ دَفَعَهَا إِلَى أُمِّ سُلَيْمٍ تُصَنِّعُهَا لَهُ وَتُهَيِّئُهَا

translation_issue.literal_meaning: and a beautiful slave-girl fell into the booty share of Dihya, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) bought her for seven heads [of slaves], then handed her over to Umm Sulaim to beautify her for him and prepare her.
translation_issue.explanation: The translator softens 'jāriyah' ('slave-girl' in the context of war spoils) to 'girl,' softens 'ishtarāhā' ('bought her') to 'got her in exchange' to avoid explicitly stating that Muhammad purchased a human being, and interpolates the unattested parenthetical '(for marriage)' into 'tuhayyi'uhā' ('prepare her') even though the Hadith immediately notes that the companions did not know whether he married her or took her as a concubine ('umm walad').

muslim:3500.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists (citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*) typically argue that Muhammad rescued Safiyya from the humiliation of bondage by manumitting her, making her emancipation her bridal dower (*ṣadāq*), and elevating her to the honored status of a free wife. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad 'bought her for seven heads [of slaves]' (*fa-shtarāhā... bi-sabʿati ar'us*), proving he traded seven other enslaved human beings as chattel currency to acquire her while withholding any financial dower in exchange for her release (cf. *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 371, *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 3497). Furthermore, his companions' open debate over whether he had married her or taken her as a sexual concubine (*umm walad*) based solely on whether he veiled her (*إن حجبها فهي امرأته وإن لم يحجبها فهي أم ولد*) proves that using female war captives for sex without marriage was routine among Muhammad and his army.

muslim:3602.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3602.note: When Sahla bint Suhail reports that Abu Hudhaifa's freed slave Salim is living in their house after having attained the maturity and knowledge of men, Muhammad commands her to suckle him so that she becomes unlawful for him in marriage. The sub-narrator Ibn Abi Mulaika states that he refrained from transmitting this hadith for nearly a year out of fear until al-Qasim bin Muhammad bin Abi Bakr instructed him to narrate it on his authority from Aisha.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ سَهْلَةَ بِنْتَ سُهَيْلِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو جَاءَتِ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ سَالِمًا - لِسَالِمٍ مَوْلَى أَبِي حُذَيْفَةَ - مَعَنَا فِي بَيْتِنَا وَقَدْ بَلَغَ مَا يَبْلُغُ الرِّجَالُ وَعَلِمَ مَا يَعْلَمُ الرِّجَالُ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏ "‏ أَرْضِعِيهِ تَحْرُمِي عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَمَكَثْتُ سَنَةً أَوْ قَرِيبًا مِنْهَا لاَ أُحَدِّثُ بِهِ وَهِبْتُهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Sahla bint Suhail b. 'Amr came to Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) and said:Messenger of Allah, Salim (the freed slave of Abu Hudhaifa) is living with us in our house, and he has attained (puberty) as men attain it and has acquired knowledge (of the sex problems) as men acquire, whereupon he said: Suckle him so that he may become unlawful (in regard to marriage) for you He (Ibn Abu Mulaika) said: I refrained from (narrating this hadith) for a year or so on account of fear.

muslim:3602.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ—that this was a one-time legal exception (rukhṣah khāṣṣah) unique to Salim after the abolition of adoption, and that Sahla merely expressed her breast milk into a cup rather than nursing him directly. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Salim had reached full male puberty and sexual awareness (wa-qad balagha mā yablughu al-rijāl wa-ʿalima mā yaʿlamu al-rijāl) when Muhammad commanded "Suckle him" (arḍiʿīhi) with zero mention of a vessel in the Sahih matn—a ruling so scandalous that the narrator Ibn Abi Mulaika admitted, "I refrained from narrating it for a year or nearly so out of fear" (lā uḥaddithu bihi wa-hibtuhu). Furthermore, immediately adjacent narrations in Sahih Muslim (muslim:3605, muslim:3607) prove that Aisha herself rejected the "unique exception" claim, actively applying this ruling as a general legal precedent by having her nieces and sisters breastfeed adult men so they could enter her private quarters.

bukhari:2893.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:2893.note: After conquering the fortress of Khaybar (AD 628) and hearing of the beauty of Safiyya bint Huyayy—whose husband had been killed while she was a bride (*wa-qad qutila zawjuhā wa-kānat 'arūsan*)—Muhammad selected her for himself. On the return journey toward Medina, he consummated the marriage with her (*banā bihā*) at Sadd al-Sahba' as soon as she completed a menstrual cycle (*ḥallat*) and held a wedding banquet (*walīma*) of *ḥays*.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا فَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْحِصْنَ ذُكِرَ لَهُ جَمَالُ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتِ حُيَىِّ بْنِ أَخْطَبَ، وَقَدْ قُتِلَ زَوْجُهَا وَكَانَتْ عَرُوسًا، فَاصْطَفَاهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِنَفْسِهِ، فَخَرَجَ بِهَا حَتَّى بَلَغْنَا سَدَّ الصَّهْبَاءِ حَلَّتْ، فَبَنَى بِهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: when Allah enabled him to conquer the Fort (of Khaibar), the beauty of Safiya bint Huyai bin Akhtab was described to him. Her husband had been killed while she was a bride. So Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) selected her for himself and took her along with him till we reached a place called Sa`d-As-Sahba,' where her menses were over and he took her for his wife.

bukhari:2893.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that Muhammad waited for Safiyya's legal purification period before consummating the marriage and demonstrated exemplary gentleness by letting her step on his knee to mount his camel. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that after her husband was killed while she was a newlywed bride (`wa-qad qutila zawjuhā wa-kānat 'arūsan`), Muhammad consummated the union (`fa-banā bihā`) at a roadside camp (`Sadd al-Ṣahbā'`) on the march back from Khaybar in AD 628 immediately after a single menstrual cycle ended (`ḥallat`). By applying the one-cycle clearance rule (*istibrā'*) for enslaved captives rather than the four-month-and-ten-day mourning period (*'iddah*) required for free widows in Quran 2:234, the text proves she was subjected to sexual intercourse within days of her family's slaughter.

bukhari:2893.note: Following the conquest of the fortress of Khaybar (AD 628), Muhammad was informed of the beauty of the newlywed Safiyya bint Huyayy—whose husband had been killed—and selected her for himself (*iṣṭafāhā li-nafsihi*) before taking her as his wife at Sadd al-Sahba' once her menstruation ended (cf. bukhari:371, where her manumission from captivity served as her dowry).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا فَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْحِصْنَ ذُكِرَ لَهُ جَمَالُ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتِ حُيَىِّ بْنِ أَخْطَبَ، وَقَدْ قُتِلَ زَوْجُهَا وَكَانَتْ عَرُوسًا، فَاصْطَفَاهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِنَفْسِهِ، فَخَرَجَ بِهَا حَتَّى بَلَغْنَا سَدَّ الصَّهْبَاءِ حَلَّتْ، فَبَنَى بِهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: when Allah enabled him to conquer the Fort (of Khaibar), the beauty of Safiya bint Huyai bin Akhtab was described to him. Her husband had been killed while she was a bride. So Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) selected her for himself and took her along with him till we reached a place called Sa`d-As-Sahba,' where her menses were over and he took her for his wife.

bukhari:2893.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad took Safiyya bint Huyayy solely as a humanitarian gesture to rescue a chief's daughter from humiliation, granting her freedom and an honorable marriage rather than treating her as war spoils. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that he claimed her for himself (`fa-ṣṭafāhā... li-nafsihi`) as his exclusive war-booty prerogative (*ṣafiyy*) only after her physical beauty was described to him (`dhukira lahu jamālu Ṣafiyyata`) right after her newlywed husband was killed (`wa-qad qutila zawjuhā wa-kānat 'arūsan`). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:371`, `bukhari:2235`) confirm she was initially handed over as a captive slave to Dihya al-Kalbi before Muhammad purchased her for seven slaves and the companions openly debated whether he kept her as a wife or a right-hand-possessed concubine (`mā malakat yamīnuhu`).

bukhari:371.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:371.note: After conquering Khaybar by force in AD 628 and claiming the captive Safiyya bint Huyayy from Dihya, Muhammad manumitted and married her, designating her release from captivity itself as her bridal dowry (mahr). While still on the return journey from Khaybar, Umm Sulaym prepared Safiyya and sent her to Muhammad at night to consummate the marriage.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَصَبْنَاهَا عَنْوَةً، فَجُمِعَ السَّبْىُ، فَجَاءَ دِحْيَةُ فَقَالَ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، أَعْطِنِي جَارِيَةً مِنَ السَّبْىِ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ اذْهَبْ فَخُذْ جَارِيَةً ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأَخَذَ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتَ حُيَىٍّ، فَجَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، أَعْطَيْتَ دِحْيَةَ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتَ حُيَىٍّ سَيِّدَةَ قُرَيْظَةَ وَالنَّضِيرِ، لاَ تَصْلُحُ إِلاَّ لَكَ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ ادْعُوهُ بِهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَجَاءَ بِهَا، فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ إِلَيْهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ خُذْ جَارِيَةً مِنَ السَّبْىِ غَيْرَهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَعْتَقَهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَتَزَوَّجَهَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُ ثَابِتٌ يَا أَبَا حَمْزَةَ، مَا أَصْدَقَهَا قَالَ نَفْسَهَا، أَعْتَقَهَا وَتَزَوَّجَهَا، حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ بِالطَّرِيقِ جَهَّزَتْهَا لَهُ أُمُّ سُلَيْمٍ فَأَهْدَتْهَا لَهُ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ، فَأَصْبَحَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَرُوسًا
problematic_excerpt.english: We conquered Khaibar, took the captives, and the booty was collected. Dihya came and said, 'O Allah's Prophet! Give me a slave girl from the captives.' The Prophet said, 'Go and take any slave girl.' He took Safiya bint Huyai. A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, 'O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! You gave Safiya bint Huyai to Dihya and she is the chief mistress of the tribes of Quraidha and An-Nadir and she befits none but you.' So the Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'Bring him along with her.' So Dihya came with her and when the Prophet (ﷺ) saw her, he said to Dihya, 'Take any slave girl other than her from the captives.' Anas added: The Prophet (ﷺ) then manumitted her and married her." Thabit asked Anas, "O Abu Hamza! What did the Prophet (ﷺ) pay her (as Mahr)?" He said, "Her self was her Mahr for he manumitted her and then married her." Anas added, "While on the way, Um Sulaim dressed her for marriage (ceremony) and at night she sent her as a bride to the Prophet (ﷺ) . So the Prophet was a bridegroom

bukhari:371.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī and Ibn Hajar, that Safiyya freely consented to marry Muhammad after he generously granted her freedom and waited for her post-captivity purification period (istibrā') following the AD 628 battle of Khaybar. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad gave her no bridal dowry other than release from the very enslavement he had just imposed upon her (مَا أَصْدَقَهَا قَالَ نَفْسَهَا، أَعْتَقَهَا وَتَزَوَّجَهَا), and that she was prepared and brought to his bed at night while the army was still on the road returning from the battlefield (حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ بِالطَّرِيقِ جَهَّزَتْهَا لَهُ أُمُّ سُلَيْمٍ فَأَهْدَتْهَا لَهُ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ). Because her community had just been subjugated by force (عَنْوَةً) and her family slain by his troops, any claim of uncoerced marital consent is refuted by the immediate duress of wartime captivity.

bukhari:371.note: After conquering Khaybar by force in AD 628, Muhammad permitted Dihya to take a female slave from the gathered captives, but upon being told that Dihya had selected Safiyya bint Huyayy—the chief mistress of Qurayza and an-Nadir—Muhammad summoned them, looked at her, and instructed Dihya to take a different slave girl from the captives instead.

problematic_excerpt.english: We conquered Khaibar, took the captives, and the booty was collected. Dihya came and said, 'O Allah's Prophet! Give me a slave girl from the captives.' The Prophet said, 'Go and take any slave girl.' He took Safiya bint Huyai. A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, 'O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! You gave Safiya bint Huyai to Dihya and she is the chief mistress of the tribes of Quraidha and An-Nadir and she befits none but you.' So the Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'Bring him along with her.' So Dihya came with her and when the Prophet (ﷺ) saw her, he said to Dihya, 'Take any slave girl other than her from the captives.' Anas added: The Prophet (ﷺ) then manumitted her and married her." Thabit asked Anas, "O Abu Hamza! What did the Prophet (ﷺ) pay her (as Mahr)?" He said, "Her self was her Mahr for he manumitted her and then married her." Anas added, "While on the way, Um Sulaim dressed her for marriage (ceremony) and at night she sent her as a bride to the Prophet (ﷺ) . So the Prophet was a bridegroom

bukhari:371.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī, that Muhammad took Safiyya bint Huyayy from Dihya and manumitted her solely to honor her noble status as a tribal chief's daughter rather than leave her as a regular soldier's slave. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad first enslaved the women of Khaybar by military force (فَأَصَبْنَاهَا عَنْوَةً، فَجُمِعَ السَّبْىُ), inspected Safiyya before claiming her (فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ إِلَيْهَا), and ordered Dihya to simply take any other captive slave girl in her place (خُذْ جَارِيَةً مِنَ السَّبْىِ غَيْرَهَا). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:2235) confirm that Muhammad purchased her from Dihya for seven heads of slaves (اشْتَرَاهَا بِسَبْعَةِ أَرْؤُسٍ), proving that captured women were bartered and reassigned as interchangeable chattel.

muslim:3600.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3600.note: When Sahlah bint Suhayl told Muhammad that she noticed disapproval on Abu Hudhayfah's face over his ally Salim—a veteran of the Battle of Badr—entering their home, Muhammad commanded her to breastfeed him. When she asked how she could breastfeed a grown man, Muhammad smiled (or in Ibn Abi Umar's narration, laughed) and replied that he already knew Salim was a grown man.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: جَاءَتْ سَهْلَةُ بِنْتُ سُهَيْلٍ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي أَرَى فِي وَجْهِ أَبِي حُذَيْفَةَ مِنْ دُخُولِ سَالِمٍ - وَهُوَ حَلِيفُهُ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَرْضِعِيهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ وَكَيْفَ أُرْضِعُهُ وَهُوَ رَجُلٌ كَبِيرٌ فَتَبَسَّمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَقَالَ ‏"‏ قَدْ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّهُ رَجُلٌ كَبِيرٌ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ زَادَ عَمْرٌو فِي حَدِيثِهِ وَكَانَ قَدْ شَهِدَ بَدْرًا ‏.‏ وَفِي رِوَايَةِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَرَ فَضَحِكَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Sahla bint Suhail came to Allah's Apostle (may peace be eupon him) and said:Messengerof Allah, I see on the face of Abu Hudhaifa (signs of disgust) on entering of Salim (who is an ally) into (our house), whereupon Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) said: Suckle him. She said: How can I suckle him as he is a grown-up man? Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) smiled and said: I already know that he is a young man 'Amr has made this addition in his narration that he participated in the Battle of Badr and in the narration of Ibn 'Umar (the words are): Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) laughed

muslim:3600.literal_translation: Sahlah bint Suhayl came to the Prophet and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I see [dislike] on the face of Abu Hudhayfah from the entering of Salim—and he is his ally.' The Prophet said: 'Suckle him.' She said: 'And how can I suckle him while he is a grown-up man?' The Messenger of Allah smiled and said: 'I already know that he is a grown-up man.' Amr added in his narration that he had participated in Badr, and in the narration of Ibn Abi Umar, the Messenger of Allah laughed.

translation_issue.arabic_term: قَدْ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّهُ رَجُلٌ كَبِيرٌ
translation_issue.published_rendering: I already know that he is a young man
translation_issue.literal_meaning: I already know that he is a grown-up man
translation_issue.explanation: The translator renders 'rajulun kabīrun' as 'a grown-up man' in Sahlah's question, yet softens the identical Arabic phrase to 'a young man' in Muhammad's reply.

muslim:3600.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Sahlah expressed her milk into a vessel rather than nursing Salim directly, and that this command was a one-time exception restricted to Salim alone. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states the unqualified imperative *arḍiʿīhi* ('suckle him') with no mention of any container, and when Sahlah protested, 'How can I suckle him when he is a grown-up man (*rajulun kabīrun*)?', Muhammad laughed and replied, 'I already know that he is a grown-up man,' without correcting her understanding. Moreover, calling the order a special concession does not alter the fact that Muhammad resolved the domestic complication of abolishing adoption ([Quran 33:4](quran://33/4)) by commanding a married woman to breastfeed an adult man who had fought at Badr (`muslim:3601`, `muslim:3602`, `muslim:3604`).

bukhari:4200.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:4200.note: Following the killing of Khaybar's fighting men and the enslavement of its women and offspring in AD 628, the captive Safiyya first went to Dihya al-Kalbi before being acquired by Muhammad, who designated her release from captivity as her bridal dower (mahr; cf. bukhari:371, bukhari:2235).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَتَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْمُقَاتِلَةَ، وَسَبَى الذُّرِّيَّةَ، وَكَانَ فِي السَّبْىِ صَفِيَّةُ، فَصَارَتْ إِلَى دِحْيَةَ الْكَلْبِيِّ، ثُمَّ صَارَتْ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَجَعَلَ عِتْقَهَا صَدَاقَهَا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) had their warriors killed, their offspring and women taken as captives. Safiya was amongst the captives, She first came in the share of Dihya Al-Kalbi but later on she belonged to the Prophet . The Prophet (ﷺ) made her manumission as her 'Mahr

bukhari:4200.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's marriage to Safiyya bint Huyayy in AD 628 was a compassionate, consensual political union intended to honor her noble status and reconcile her tribe. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that she was seized among the war captives (`وَكَانَ فِي السَّبْىِ صَفِيَّةُ`) immediately after Muhammad slaughtered Khaybar's men (`فَقَتَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْمُقَاتِلَةَ`)—including her husband, father, and brother—and was passed from one captor (`دِحْيَةَ الْكَلْبِيِّ`) to Muhammad, who used her release from captivity as her bridal price (`فَجَعَلَ عِتْقَهَا صَدَاقَهَا`). Parallel narrations (bukhari:371, bukhari:4211) further document that Muhammad consummated the marriage with the bereaved seventeen-year-old bride in an army tent on the road back from Khaybar (`فَزَفَّتْهَا إِلَيْهِ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَكَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَرُوسًا`) just days after executing her husband.

bukhari:4200.note: In AD 628, Muhammad prayed the dawn prayer in the dark near Khaybar, declared the settlement's ruin as its inhabitants came out onto the roads (with their agricultural spades; cf. bukhari:4198), and had their fighting men killed and their women and offspring taken captive ([Quran 48:20](quran://48/20)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: صَلَّى النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الصُّبْحَ قَرِيبًا مِنْ خَيْبَرَ بِغَلَسٍ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏ "‏ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ خَرِبَتْ خَيْبَرُ، إِنَّا إِذَا نَزَلْنَا بِسَاحَةِ قَوْمٍ، فَسَاءَ صَبَاحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَخَرَجُوا يَسْعَوْنَ فِي السِّكَكِ، فَقَتَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْمُقَاتِلَةَ، وَسَبَى الذُّرِّيَّةَ، وَكَانَ فِي السَّبْىِ صَفِيَّةُ، فَصَارَتْ إِلَى دِحْيَةَ الْكَلْبِيِّ، ثُمَّ صَارَتْ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَجَعَلَ عِتْقَهَا صَدَاقَهَا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) offered the Fajr Prayer near Khaibar when it was still dark and then said, "Allahu-Akbar! Khaibar is destroyed, for whenever we approach a (hostile) nation (to fight), then evil will be the morning for those who have been warned." Then the inhabitants of Khaibar came out running on the roads. The Prophet (ﷺ) had their warriors killed, their offspring and women taken as captives. Safiya was amongst the captives, She first came in the share of Dihya Al-Kalbi but later on she belonged to the Prophet . The Prophet (ﷺ) made her manumission as her 'Mahr

bukhari:4200.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the AD 628 expedition against Khaybar was a pre-emptive defensive strike against a mobilized military fortress actively preparing to invade Medina. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad attacked at dawn while it was still dark (`بِغَلَسٍ`) as the inhabitants came out running into the roads (`فَخَرَجُوا يَسْعَوْنَ فِي السِّكَكِ`), which parallel narrations (bukhari:371, bukhari:2945) clarify was an unwarned surprise assault on farmers heading to their fields with spades and baskets (`بِمَسَاحِيهِمْ وَمَكَاتِلِهِمْ`). Furthermore, Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* confirms that Muhammad's battle cry—"evil is the morning for those who have been warned" (`فَسَاءَ صَبَاحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ`)—established the legal rule that any non-Muslim population that has heard the general call to Islam may be attacked without prior military notice.

bukhari:4200.note: After having the fighting men of Khaybar killed in AD 628, Muhammad took their women and offspring captive, with Safiyya initially falling into the share of Dihya al-Kalbi before passing to Muhammad, who designated her manumission as her bridal dower (mahr).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَتَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْمُقَاتِلَةَ، وَسَبَى الذُّرِّيَّةَ، وَكَانَ فِي السَّبْىِ صَفِيَّةُ، فَصَارَتْ إِلَى دِحْيَةَ الْكَلْبِيِّ، ثُمَّ صَارَتْ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَجَعَلَ عِتْقَهَا صَدَاقَهَا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) had their warriors killed, their offspring and women taken as captives. Safiya was amongst the captives, She first came in the share of Dihya Al-Kalbi but later on she belonged to the Prophet . The Prophet (ﷺ) made her manumission as her 'Mahr

bukhari:4200.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that taking the women and children of Khaybar was a protective humanitarian measure for displaced non-combatants rather than chattel slavery, and that freeing Safiyya as her dowry (`فَجَعَلَ عِتْقَهَا صَدَاقَهَا`) proves Muhammad's emancipatory ethic. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad enslaved the women and offspring (`وَسَبَى الذُّرِّيَّةَ`) as war booty and distributed Safiyya as property to Dihya al-Kalbi (`فَصَارَتْ إِلَى دِحْيَةَ الْكَلْبِيِّ`) before taking her for himself. Parallel narrations (bukhari:371, muslim:3499) and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* confirm that Muhammad purchased her from Dihya in exchange for seven other human slaves (`بِسَبْعَةِ أَرْؤُسٍ`) and paid her no wealth or property for her marriage beyond revoking the bondage he had just inflicted upon her.

bukhari:4201.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:4201.note: When asked what bridal dowry (*mahr*) Muhammad gave Safiyya after taking her captive at Khaybar (AD 628), Anas ibn Malik stated that he made her own person her dowry by manumitting her to marry her.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَبَى النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم صَفِيَّةَ، فَأَعْتَقَهَا وَتَزَوَّجَهَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ ثَابِتٌ لأَنَسٍ مَا أَصْدَقَهَا قَالَ أَصْدَقَهَا نَفْسَهَا فَأَعْتَقَهَا‏.‏

bukhari:4201.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that Muhammad's marriage to Safiyya in AD 628 was a consensual political union that honored her status and legally substituted her emancipation for a monetary dowry. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *sabā al-nabīyu Ṣafīyata* ("the Prophet enslaved Safiyya as a captive") and *aṣdaqahā nafsahā* ("he gave her herself as her dowry"), demonstrating that her release from slavery was contingent upon marrying the commander whose forces had just conquered her people and executed her husband and father. Parallel accounts in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 371 and 4200 confirm that Muhammad consummated the marriage immediately on the return march from Khaybar before even reaching Medina, underscoring the coercive nature of taking a newly bereaved war captive into his bed.

bukhari:4201.note: Anas ibn Malik reports that Muhammad took Safiyya as a war captive (*saba*), manumitted her, and married her, designating her emancipation itself as her obligatory bridal gift (*mahr*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَبَى النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم صَفِيَّةَ، فَأَعْتَقَهَا وَتَزَوَّجَهَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ ثَابِتٌ لأَنَسٍ مَا أَصْدَقَهَا قَالَ أَصْدَقَهَا نَفْسَهَا فَأَعْتَقَهَا‏.‏

bukhari:4201.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that freeing Safiyya bint Huyayy and marrying her after the Battle of Khaybar in AD 628 was an act of noble charity that rescued a defeated chieftain's daughter from bondage and elevated her to a Mother of the Believers. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *sabā al-nabīyu Ṣafīyata* ("the Prophet took Safiyya as a war captive") and *aṣdaqahā nafsahā fa-aʿtaqahā* ("he made her own self her bridal gift and manumitted her"), proving that Muhammad first reduced her to owned chattel property and then used her own liberation as payment to acquire her as a bride without giving her any financial *mahr*. Furthermore, parallel narrations in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 371 and 4200 reveal that she was initially handed to Dihya al-Kalbi as war booty before Muhammad claimed her for himself upon hearing of her beauty, leaving his companions unsure whether she was a wife or an enslaved concubine (*mā malakat yamīnuhu*) until he veiled her.

bukhari:947.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:947.note: After killing the fighting men of Khaybar and taking its women and children as captives in AD 628, Muhammad acquired the captive Safiyya from Dihya al-Kalbi and married her, setting her emancipation from captivity as her bridal dower.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَظَهَرَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَتَلَ الْمُقَاتِلَةَ وَسَبَى الذَّرَارِيَّ، فَصَارَتْ صَفِيَّةُ لِدِحْيَةَ الْكَلْبِيِّ، وَصَارَتْ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ تَزَوَّجَهَا وَجَعَلَ صَدَاقَهَا عِتْقَهَا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) vanquished them by force and their warriors were killed; the children and women were taken as captives. Safiya was taken by Dihya Al-Kalbi and later she belonged to Allah's Apostle, who married her and her Mahr was her manumission

bukhari:947.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Safiyya eagerly consented to marry Muhammad out of genuine affection and that the union was a dignified, mutually desired marriage. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that she became his property (`وَصَارَتْ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ`) immediately after his army slaughtered her community's men and enslaved their families (`فَقَتَلَ الْمُقَاتِلَةَ وَسَبَى الذَّرَارِيَّ`), with her release from bondage serving as her only dowry (`أَمْهَرَهَا نَفْسَهَا`). Parallel narrations (bukhari:371, bukhari:4211) further establish that Muhammad only confiscated her from Dihya after a companion praised her beauty as chief mistress of Qurayza and al-Nadir, and that he consummated the marriage in a tent on the march back from Khaybar right after her father, brother, and husband had been executed.

bukhari:947.note: After offering the dawn prayer in the dark, Muhammad rode against Khaybar in AD 628, killed its fighting men, and took its women and children as captives ([Quran 48:20](quran://48/20)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم صَلَّى الصُّبْحَ بِغَلَسٍ ثُمَّ رَكِبَ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ خَرِبَتْ خَيْبَرُ، إِنَّا إِذَا نَزَلْنَا بِسَاحَةِ قَوْمٍ فَسَاءَ صَبَاحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَخَرَجُوا يَسْعَوْنَ فِي السِّكَكِ وَيَقُولُونَ مُحَمَّدٌ وَالْخَمِيسُ ـ قَالَ وَالْخَمِيسُ الْجَيْشُ ـ فَظَهَرَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَتَلَ الْمُقَاتِلَةَ وَسَبَى الذَّرَارِيَّ، فَصَارَتْ صَفِيَّةُ لِدِحْيَةَ الْكَلْبِيِّ، وَصَارَتْ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ تَزَوَّجَهَا وَجَعَلَ صَدَاقَهَا عِتْقَهَا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) offered the Fajr prayer when it was still dark, then he rode and said, 'Allahu Akbar! Khaibar is ruined. When we approach near to a nation, the most unfortunate is the morning of those who have been warned." The people came out into the streets saying, "Muhammad and his army." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) vanquished them by force and their warriors were killed; the children and women were taken as captives. Safiya was taken by Dihya Al-Kalbi and later she belonged to Allah's Apostle, who married her and her Mahr was her manumission

bukhari:947.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the AD 628 expedition against Khaybar was a defensive pre-emptive strike against an imminent military threat and that its inhabitants had been given formal prior warning. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the residents were caught completely by surprise as they came out into the streets (`فَخَرَجُوا يَسْعَوْنَ فِي السِّكَكِ`)—which parallel narrations (bukhari:371, bukhari:2945) clarify meant walking to their fields with agricultural spades and baskets (`وَمَعَهُمُ الْمَسَاحِي وَالْمَكَاتِلُ`)—before Muhammad overpowered them, killed their fighting-age men (`فَقَتَلَ الْمُقَاتِلَةَ`), and enslaved their women and children (`وَسَبَى الذَّرَارِيَّ`).

bukhari:947.note: Following the conquest of Khaybar in AD 628, Muhammad took the women and children as captives and acquired Safiyya after she had initially fallen to Dihya al-Kalbi, marrying her and designating her manumission as her bridal dower.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَظَهَرَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَتَلَ الْمُقَاتِلَةَ وَسَبَى الذَّرَارِيَّ، فَصَارَتْ صَفِيَّةُ لِدِحْيَةَ الْكَلْبِيِّ، وَصَارَتْ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ تَزَوَّجَهَا وَجَعَلَ صَدَاقَهَا عِتْقَهَا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) vanquished them by force and their warriors were killed; the children and women were taken as captives. Safiya was taken by Dihya Al-Kalbi and later she belonged to Allah's Apostle, who married her and her Mahr was her manumission

bukhari:947.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad acquired and married Safiyya bint Huyayy out of humanitarian compassion to honor her status as a chief's daughter and rescue her from slavery. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad himself enslaved the women and children (`وَسَبَى الذَّرَارِيَّ`), reassigned Safiyya from Dihya al-Kalbi after she had already been distributed as war booty (`فَصَارَتْ صَفِيَّةُ لِدِحْيَةَ الْكَلْبِيِّ`), and substituted her emancipation for her mandatory bridal dower (`وَجَعَلَ صَدَاقَهَا عِتْقَهَا`) so that he paid her nothing (`أَمْهَرَهَا نَفْسَهَا`). Furthermore, parallel narrations (bukhari:371, muslim:3499) confirm that Muhammad bought her from Dihya in exchange for other human captives, trading her female cousins or seven enslaved souls (`سَبْعَةَ أَرْؤُسٍ`) as chattel.

muslim:3419.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3419.note: Muhammad permits his companions to contract temporary marriage (*mutʿah*), under which Sabrah al-Juhani gives his cloak to a woman of Banu 'Amir to stay with her for three nights before Muhammad reverses his permission and orders the men to release the women (cf. muslim:3417, where companions continue practicing *mutʿah* until Umar forbids it; [1 Corinthians 6:18](bible://1cor/6/18), [Hebrews 13:4](bible://heb/13/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَذِنَ لَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِالْمُتْعَةِ فَانْطَلَقْتُ أَنَا وَرَجُلٌ إِلَى امْرَأَةٍ مِنْ بَنِي عَامِرٍ كَأَنَّهَا بَكْرَةٌ عَيْطَاءُ فَعَرَضْنَا عَلَيْهَا أَنْفُسَنَا فَقَالَتْ مَا تُعْطِي فَقُلْتُ رِدَائِي ‏.‏ وَقَالَ صَاحِبِي رِدَائِي ‏.‏ وَكَانَ رِدَاءُ صَاحِبِي أَجْوَدَ مِنْ رِدَائِي وَ كُنْتُ أَشَبَّ مِنْهُ فَإِذَا نَظَرَتْ إِلَى رِدَاءِ صَاحِبِي أَعْجَبَهَا وَإِذَا نَظَرَتْ إِلَىَّ أَعْجَبْتُهَا ثُمَّ قَالَتْ أَنْتَ وَرِدَاؤُكَ يَكْفِينِي ‏.‏ فَمَكَثْتُ مَعَهَا ثَلاَثًا ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ مَنْ كَانَ عِنْدَهُ شَىْءٌ مِنْ هَذِهِ النِّسَاءِ الَّتِي يَتَمَتَّعُ فَلْيُخَلِّ سَبِيلَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) permitted temporary marriage for us. So I and another person went out and saw a woman of Bana 'Amir, who was like a young long-necked she-camel. We presented ourselves to her (for contracting temporary marriage), whereupon she said: What dower would you give me? I said: My cloak. And my companion also said: My cloak. And the cloak of-my companion was superior to my cloak, but I was younger than he. So when she looked at the cloak of my companion she liked it, and when she cast a glance at me I looked more attractive to her. She then said: Well, you and your cloak are sufficient for me. I remained with her for three nights, and then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: He who has any such woman with whom he had contracted temporary marriage, he should let her off

muslim:3419.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that *mutʿah* was merely a pre-Islamic remnant temporarily tolerated under extreme military hardship (*ḍarūrah*) before being gradually abrogated like alcohol. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *adhina lanā rasūlu llāhi... bi-l-mutʿati* ('Allah's Messenger permitted enjoyment [*mutʿah*] for us'), proving Muhammad actively authorized his men to barter a cloak for three nights of sex (*famakathtu maʿahā thalāthan*). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 3416, 3418) document that Muhammad prohibited and then re-authorized *mutʿah* across multiple expeditions through the Conquest of Mecca (630 AD), showing that sexual ethics were repeatedly suspended as a military incentive.

muslim:3419.note: With Muhammad's permission for temporary marriage (*mutʿah*), Sabrah al-Juhani and a companion offer their cloaks to a woman of Banu 'Amir—whom Sabrah compares to 'a young long-necked she-camel' (*bakrah ʿayṭāʾ*)—and Sabrah stays with her for three nights. Muhammad then orders any man who has 'anything of these women whom he is enjoying' (*shayʾun min hādhihi al-nisāʾ allatī yatamattaʿu*) to release her, abrogating the permission he had granted ([Matthew 19:4](bible://mt/19/4)).

We presented ourselves to her (for contracting temporary marriage), whereupon she said: What dower would you give me? I said: My cloak. And my companion also said: My cloak. And the cloak of-my companion was superior to my cloak, but I was younger than he. So when she looked at the cloak of my companion she liked it, and when she cast a glance at me I looked more attractive to her. She then said: Well, you and your cloak are sufficient for me. muslim:3419.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that comparing the woman to a *bakrah ʿayṭāʾ* ('a young, long-necked she-camel') was a classical Arabic compliment for tall, graceful beauty, and that the exchange of a cloak constituted a legitimate bridal dower (*mahr*) within a recognized marriage contract. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that two men approached her together to bid their cloaks after she asked simply *mā tuʿṭī* ('What do you give?'—with no mention of *mahr*, a guardian, or witnesses), and quotes Muhammad referring to such a woman as an objectified possession (*shayʾ*, 'a thing/anything'): *man kāna ʿindahu shayʾun min hādhihi al-nisāʾi allatī yatamattaʿu falyukhalli sabīlahā* ('Whoever has with him anything of these women whom he is enjoying, let him release her').

bukhari:302.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:302.note: Aisha reports that whenever Muhammad wanted to fondle (*yubāshir*) one of his menstruating wives, he ordered her to tie on a waist-wrapper (*izār*) at the initial peak and heaviest flow of her menses (*fī fawri ḥayḍatihā*—a phrase omitted from the published English translation) and then fondled her. She adds the remark: 'And which of you can control his sexual desire (*irbahu*) as the Prophet could control his sexual desire?'

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَتْ إِحْدَانَا إِذَا كَانَتْ حَائِضًا، فَأَرَادَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ يُبَاشِرَهَا، أَمَرَهَا أَنْ تَتَّزِرَ فِي فَوْرِ حَيْضَتِهَا ثُمَّ يُبَاشِرُهَا‏.‏ قَالَتْ وَأَيُّكُمْ يَمْلِكُ إِرْبَهُ كَمَا كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَمْلِكُ إِرْبَهُ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Whenever Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) wanted to fondle anyone of us during her periods (menses), he used to order her to put on an Izar and start fondling her." `Aisha added, "None of you could control his sexual desires as the Prophet (ﷺ) could

bukhari:302.literal_translation: Aisha said: Whenever one of us was menstruating and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to fondle her, he would order her to tie on a waist-wrapper at the height of her menses, and then he would fondle her. She added: 'And which of you can control his sexual desire as the Prophet (ﷺ) could control his sexual desire?'

translation_issue.arabic_term: فِي فَوْرِ حَيْضَتِهَا
translation_issue.published_rendering: [omitted]
translation_issue.literal_meaning: at the height / most intense flow of her menses
translation_issue.explanation: The translator omitted 'fī fawri ḥayḍatihā' to obscure that Muhammad engaged in intimate fondling even during the peak, heaviest flow of his wives' menstruation.

bukhari:302.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists, citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, typically argue that this narration demonstrates Muhammad's exemplary self-restraint and progressive kindness toward menstruating women—maintaining marital affection without violating Quran 2:222's prohibition of vaginal intercourse. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that he ordered his wives to tie on a waist-wrapper specifically *fī fawri ḥayḍatihā* (فِي فَوْرِ حَيْضَتِهَا—'at the peak and heaviest flow of her menses,' a phrase deliberately omitted from the standard English translation) so he could engage in direct skin-to-skin fondling (*yubāshirahā*). Far from demonstrating ascetic self-mastery, this admission reveals that even with nine concurrent wives available to him, Muhammad would not temporarily abstain from seeking sexual gratification from a wife enduring the heaviest, most uncomfortable days of her menstrual bleeding.

muslim:3420.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3420.note: During the Conquest of Mecca (AD 630), Muhammad permitted his companions to practice temporary pleasure marriage (*mutʿat al-nisāʾ*), under which Sabra b. Maʿbad contracted temporary sexual enjoyment with a young woman in exchange for his worn-out cloak (*burd khalaq*) before Muhammad subsequently abrogated and forbade the practice (cf. muslim:3422; [1 Corinthians 6:18](bible://1cor/6/18), [Hebrews 13:4](bible://heb/13/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَذِنَ لَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي مُتْعَةِ النِّسَاءِ فَخَرَجْتُ أَنَا وَرَجُلٌ مِنْ قَوْمِي وَلِي عَلَيْهِ فَضْلٌ فِي الْجَمَالِ وَهُوَ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الدَّمَامَةِ مَعَ كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنَّا بُرْدٌ فَبُرْدِي خَلَقٌ وَأَمَّا بُرْدُ ابْنِ عَمِّي فَبُرْدٌ جَدِيدٌ غَضٌّ حَتَّى إِذَا كُنَّا بِأَسْفَلِ مَكَّةَ أَوْ بِأَعْلاَهَا فَتَلَقَّتْنَا فَتَاةٌ مِثْلُ الْبَكْرَةِ الْعَنَطْنَطَةِ فَقُلْنَا هَلْ لَكِ أَنْ يَسْتَمْتِعَ مِنْكِ أَحَدُنَا قَالَتْ وَمَاذَا تَبْذُلاَنِ فَنَشَرَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنَّا بُرْدَهُ فَجَعَلَتْ تَنْظُرُ إِلَى الرَّجُلَيْنِ وَيَرَاهَا صَاحِبِي تَنْظُرُ إِلَى عِطْفِهَا فَقَالَ إِنَّ بُرْدَ هَذَا خَلَقٌ وَبُرْدِي جَدِيدٌ غَضٌّ ‏.‏ فَتَقُولُ بُرْدُ هَذَا لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ ‏.‏ ثَلاَثَ مِرَارٍ أَوْ مَرَّتَيْنِ ثُمَّ اسْتَمْتَعْتُ مِنْهَا فَلَمْ أَخْرُجْ حَتَّى حَرَّمَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: and Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) permitted us to contract temporary marriage with women. So I and another person of my tribe went out, and I was more handsome than he, whereas he was almost ugly. Each one of us had a cloaks, My cloak was worn out, whereas the cloak of my cousin was quite new. As we reached the lower or the upper side of Mecca, we came across a young woman like a young smart long-necked she-camel.
