Maʿbad and his cousin to proposition a young woman likened to a 'long-necked young she-camel' (*al-bakrah al-ʿanaṭnaṭah*) by spreading out their cloaks, after which Sabra enjoyed her (*istamtaʿtu minhā*) in exchange for his worn-out garment until Muhammad forbade the practice (cf. muslim:3422; [Matthew 19:4](bible://mt/19/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: غَزَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَتْحَ مَكَّةَ قَالَ فَأَقَمْنَا بِهَا خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ - ثَلاَثِينَ بَيْنَ لَيْلَةٍ وَيَوْمٍ - فَأَذِنَ لَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي مُتْعَةِ النِّسَاءِ فَخَرَجْتُ أَنَا وَرَجُلٌ مِنْ قَوْمِي وَلِي عَلَيْهِ فَضْلٌ فِي الْجَمَالِ وَهُوَ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الدَّمَامَةِ مَعَ كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنَّا بُرْدٌ فَبُرْدِي خَلَقٌ وَأَمَّا بُرْدُ ابْنِ عَمِّي فَبُرْدٌ جَدِيدٌ غَضٌّ حَتَّى إِذَا كُنَّا بِأَسْفَلِ مَكَّةَ أَوْ بِأَعْلاَهَا فَتَلَقَّتْنَا فَتَاةٌ مِثْلُ الْبَكْرَةِ الْعَنَطْنَطَةِ فَقُلْنَا هَلْ لَكِ أَنْ يَسْتَمْتِعَ مِنْكِ أَحَدُنَا قَالَتْ وَمَاذَا تَبْذُلاَنِ فَنَشَرَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنَّا بُرْدَهُ فَجَعَلَتْ تَنْظُرُ إِلَى الرَّجُلَيْنِ وَيَرَاهَا صَاحِبِي تَنْظُرُ إِلَى عِطْفِهَا فَقَالَ إِنَّ بُرْدَ هَذَا خَلَقٌ وَبُرْدِي جَدِيدٌ غَضٌّ ‏.‏ فَتَقُولُ بُرْدُ هَذَا لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ ‏.‏ ثَلاَثَ مِرَارٍ أَوْ مَرَّتَيْنِ ثُمَّ اسْتَمْتَعْتُ مِنْهَا فَلَمْ أَخْرُجْ حَتَّى حَرَّمَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Rabi' b. Sabra reported that his father went on an expedition with Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) during the Victory of Mecca, and we stayed there for fifteen days (i. e. for thirteen full days and a day and a night), and Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) permitted us to contract temporary marriage with women. So I and another person of my tribe went out, and I was more handsome than he, whereas he was almost ugly. Each one of us had a cloaks, My cloak was worn out, whereas the cloak of my cousin was quite new. As we reached the lower or the upper side of Mecca, we came across a young woman like a young smart long-necked she-camel. We said:Is it possible that one of us may contract temporary marriage with you? She said: What will you give me as a dower? Each one of us spread his cloak. She began to cast a glance on both the persons. My companion also looked at her when she was casting a glance at her side and he said: This cloak of his is worn out, whereas my cloak is quite new. She, however, said twice or thrice: There is no harm in (accepting) this cloak (the old one). So I contracted temporary marriage with her, and I did not come out (of this) until Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) declared it forbidden

muslim:3420.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *mutʿat al-nisāʾ* was a legitimate, dignified marital contract with a formal dower (*mahr*) temporarily tolerated before abrogation, and that likening the woman to a 'young long-necked she-camel' (*al-bakrah al-ʿanaṭnaṭah*) was merely a classical Arabic idiom praising her tall stature. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the two soldiers accosted her on the road without a guardian (*walī*) or witnesses by asking, *'hal laki an yastamtiʿa minki aḥadunā'* ('Would you like one of us to enjoy sexual pleasure from you?'), to which she replied, *'wa-mādhā tabdhulāni'* ('And what will you two offer?'). Far from a sacred marriage covenant, the narration records two men spreading out their garments on the street to bid for short-term sexual access (*istimtāʿ*) in exchange for a worn-out cloak (*burd khalaq*).

muslim:3416.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3416.note: Jabir ibn Abdullah reports that during the lifetime of Muhammad and the caliphate of Abu Bakr, Muslim men practiced temporary pleasure marriage (*nikāḥ al-mutʿah*), contracting women for a few days (*al-ayyām*) in exchange for a handful of dates or flour ([Quran 4:24](quran://4/24), [Matthew 19:4](bible://mt/19/4), [Hebrews 13:4](bible://heb/13/4)). Although Sunni jurisprudence holds that Muhammad ultimately abrogated the practice (muslim:3418), this narration states that it continued until Caliph Umar forbade it in the case of Amr ibn Huraith.

While Sunni jurisprudence considers temporary marriage (*mutʿah*) subsequently abrogated, this report records that prophetic law permitted the practice and that it remained in use until Umar prohibited it.

However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *"kunnā nastamtiʿu bi-l-qubḍati mina l-tamri wa-l-daqīqi l-ayyāma"* ("we used to enjoy [women sexually] for a handful of dates and flour for a few days"), containing no word for marriage or dower that English translators artificially insert. Classical commentators reconcile these conflicting timelines by proposing that the practice was prohibited and re-permitted multiple times and that companions such as Jabir remained unaware of the final prophetic ban until Umar's reign.

However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that they openly practiced it throughout the era of the Prophet and Abu Bakr until Umar forbade it (*ʿalā ʿahdi rasūli llāhi ... wa-Abī Bakr ḥattā nahā ʿanhu ʿUmar*), and in `muslim:3415` Jabir directly attributes its prohibition to Umar despite being fully aware of the earlier rulings. It is historically absurd that prominent Medinan Companions and Caliph Abu Bakr himself remained ignorant of a supposed public ban "until the Day of Resurrection" (`muslim:3421`), exposing irreconcilable contradictions across the Sahih canon over whether *mutʿah* was banned at Khaybar (`bukhari:5115`), Mecca (`muslim:3420`), Awtas (`muslim:3418`), or by Umar.

bukhari:5075.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5075.note: When his fighters lack wives on military expeditions, Muhammad forbids them from castrating themselves and instead permits them to contract temporary marriages (*nikāḥ al-mutʿah*) with women in exchange for a garment (*bi-l-thawb*, omitted in the published English translation), reciting [Quran 5:87](quran://5/87) to classify the practice among the 'good things' made lawful by Allah. While Sunni jurisprudence holds that Muhammad later abrogated temporary marriage (e.g. bukhari:5115)—whereas Twelver Shi'ism maintains its permissibility—this report records his initial prophetic sanction of the practice under Quranic revelation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنَّا نَغْزُو مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَلَيْسَ لَنَا شَىْءٌ فَقُلْنَا أَلاَ نَسْتَخْصِي فَنَهَانَا عَنْ ذَلِكَ ثُمَّ رَخَّصَ لَنَا أَنْ نَنْكِحَ الْمَرْأَةَ بِالثَّوْبِ، ثُمَّ قَرَأَ عَلَيْنَا ‏{‏يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لاَ تُحَرِّمُوا طَيِّبَاتِ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَلاَ تَعْتَدُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ‏}‏

bukhari:4615.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:4615.note: When his fighters on military campaigns without women ask whether they should castrate themselves, Muhammad forbids it, grants them permission to marry a woman in exchange for a garment—explicitly specified as temporary marriage (*nikāḥ al-mutʿah*) for a fixed term in parallel reports (bukhari:5075)—and recites [Quran 5:87](quran://5/87). Although Sunni jurisprudence holds that he later abrogated this practice permanently (bukhari:5115, muslim:3419) while Shia Islam maintains its permissibility, the report records Muhammad initially licensing temporary marriage and invoking Quranic revelation to justify it.

However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad licensed his fighters to take a woman in exchange for a single garment (*an natazawwaja al-marʾata bi-th-thawbi*—specified as 'for a fixed term,' *ilā ajalin*, in the parallel narration bukhari:5075) and justified the practice by reciting [Quran 5:87](quran://5/87), thereby classifying transactional sex for clothing as one of the 'good and pure things which Allah has made lawful' (*ṭayyibāti mā aḥalla Allāhu lakum*). Because a holy God cannot sanction temporary prostitution as 'pure' (*ṭayyibāt*) simply to relieve soldiers' sexual frustration—and because Sūrat al-Māʾidah is among the final Medinan revelations, leading senior Companions like Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās (as noted in Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*) to uphold its permissibility long after Muhammad's death—appealing to abrogation only underscores the moral opportunism of Muhammad's rulings.

muslim:3414.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3414.note: Salama ibn al-Akwa' and Jabir ibn 'Abdullah report that Muhammad came to them and permitted them to practice *al-mutʿah* (temporary marriage) ([Quran 4:24](quran://4/24), [Matthew 19:4](bible://mt/19/4)). Although Sunni commentators maintain that Muhammad later abrogated this permission, adjacent narrations (muslim:3415, muslim:3416) record companions continuing the practice for a handful of dates or flour throughout the lifetimes of Muhammad and Abu Bakr until Caliph 'Umar prohibited it, while Twelver Shi'ism still permits it.

muslim:3414.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that *nikāḥ al-mutʿah* (temporary marriage) was merely a brief wartime concession (*rukhṣah*) for soldiers enduring hardship on military campaigns before being permanently abrogated (*mansūkh*) by Muhammad. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad personally came to his men and authorized *al-mutʿah* (*atānā fa-adhina lanā fī al-mutʿah* — literally 'pleasure/enjoyment'), which the immediate parallel narrations from the exact same companions (`bukhari:5115`, `muslim:3413`, `muslim:3415`) define as hiring a woman for three nights in exchange for a single cloak (*burd*) or a handful of dates and flour (*al-qabḍah min al-tamr wa-al-daqīq*). Moreover, Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh explicitly testifies in the adjacent narration (`muslim:3415`) that the companions continued practicing *mutʿah* throughout the lifetimes of Muhammad and Abū Bakr until Caliph ʿUmar personally prohibited it (*ḥattā nahā ʿanhā ʿUmar*), proving that Muhammad himself sanctioned transactional, short-term prostitution as divine law without ever conclusively abolishing it.

bukhari:268.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:268.note: Recorded in the book of ritual bathing after sexual intercourse (Kitab al-Ghusl), Anas bin Malik reports that Muhammad would go round having marital relations with all eleven (or, in Sa'id's transmission, nine) of his wives within a single hour of the day or night. When asked how Muhammad had the stamina for this, Anas states that the companions said he had been given the strength of thirty men (cf. bukhari:284, bukhari:5068).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَدُورُ عَلَى نِسَائِهِ فِي السَّاعَةِ الْوَاحِدَةِ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ، وَهُنَّ إِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ لأَنَسٍ أَوَكَانَ يُطِيقُهُ قَالَ كُنَّا نَتَحَدَّثُ أَنَّهُ أُعْطِيَ قُوَّةَ ثَلاَثِينَ‏.‏ وَقَالَ سَعِيدٌ عَنْ قَتَادَةَ إِنَّ أَنَسًا حَدَّثَهُمْ تِسْعُ نِسْوَةٍ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to visit all his wives in a round, during the day and night and they were eleven in number." I asked Anas, "Had the Prophet (ﷺ) the strength for it?" Anas replied, "We used to say that the Prophet (ﷺ) was given the strength of thirty (men)." And Sa`id said on the authority of Qatada that Anas had told him about nine wives only (not eleven)

bukhari:268.literal_translation: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to go round to his wives [for sexual intercourse] in a single hour of the night and the day, and they were eleven. I said to Anas, "Could he endure it?" He said, "We used to say that he was given the strength of thirty [men]." And Sa`id said on the authority of Qatada that Anas narrated to them: "Nine wives."

translation_issue.arabic_term: فِي السَّاعَةِ الْوَاحِدَةِ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ
translation_issue.published_rendering: during the day and night
translation_issue.literal_meaning: in a single hour of the night and the day
translation_issue.explanation: While 'yadūru ʿalā nisāʾihi' ('used to go round to his wives') is itself an Arabic idiom for making the rounds of one's wives for intercourse (as confirmed by Bukhari placing it under the chapter on repeating sexual intercourse with a single ghusl), the translator completely omits the explicit temporal phrase 'fī al-sāʿati al-wāḥidati' ('in a single hour'), rendering 'in a single hour of the night and the day' merely as 'during the day and night' to soften the claim that he visited all eleven wives within one hour.

bukhari:268.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that 'visiting his wives' merely refers to non-sexual social check-ins, or follow Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī in claiming that the 'strength of thirty men' was a divine prophetic miracle enabling Muhammad to fulfill his marital duties equitably without detracting from his worship. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Qatada asked 'अوَكَانَ يُطِيقُهُ' (awakāna yuṭīquhu — 'Could he physically endure that?') in reference to a single hour (fī al-sā'ati al-wāḥidati), and parallel narrations (bukhari:284, bukhari:5215) confirm this was sequential sexual intercourse performed 'with a single ritual bath' (bi-ghuslin wāḥidin) at the very end. Furthermore, the narrator's own admission of confusion over whether there were nine or eleven wives exposes the account as locker-room folklore among the Companions (kunnā nataḥaddathu — 'we used to talk among ourselves') that reduces prophetic credentials to unbridled carnal hyper-virility.

bukhari:284.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:284.note: Anas bin Malik reports that Muhammad had nine wives at one time and used to go round having sexual intercourse (*yatufu*) with all nine during a single night. Recorded in the Book of Ghusl (ritual bathing after sexual impurity) alongside parallel reports where Anas states that Muhammad was given the sexual strength of thirty men (bukhari:268), classical commentators like Ibn Hajar confirm that the Arabic idiom denotes marital relations rather than a social visit.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ يَطُوفُ عَلَى نِسَائِهِ فِي اللَّيْلَةِ الْوَاحِدَةِ، وَلَهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ تِسْعُ نِسْوَةٍ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to visit all his wives in one night and he had nine wives at that time

bukhari:284.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the English rendering 'used to visit' merely describes Muhammad making brief pastoral rounds to check on his wives' welfare, or else cite Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī to frame his serial intercourse as a miraculous prophetic distinction (khaṣīṣah) demonstrating divinely granted vigor. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states kāna yaṭūfu ʿalā nisāʾihi ('he used to go round unto his wives'), an established idiom for sexual intercourse placed directly inside Al-Bukhari's Book of Ghusl (ritual bath after sexual defilement). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:268, bukhari:5068) specify that he completed this circuit 'with a single ritual bath' (bi-ghuslin wāḥidin) because he was purportedly given the sexual strength of thirty men (quwwata thalāthīna), completely refuting the 'social visit' euphemism and reducing prophetic distinction to carnal hyper-virility.

bukhari:5068.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5068.note: Anas ibn Malik reports that Muhammad had nine wives simultaneously—exempt from the four-wife limit imposed on other Muslims ([Quran 4:3](quran://4/3))—and used to go round (`yatufu`) to all nine in a single night. Parallel transmissions (bukhari:268) and classical commentators like Ibn Hajar confirm that `yatufu` denotes sexual intercourse (`al-jima'`), as evidenced by the report's placement in the chapters on post-coital ritual bathing (`ghusl`) and Anas's accompanying statement that Muhammad was given the sexual strength of thirty men.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ يَطُوفُ عَلَى نِسَائِهِ فِي لَيْلَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ، وَلَهُ تِسْعُ نِسْوَةٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to go round (have sexual relations with) all his wives in one night, and he had nine wives

bukhari:5068.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase 'used to go round' (yaṭūfu ʿalā nisāʾihi) merely describes non-sexual social visits to check on his wives' well-being, or they cite Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī to frame the act as a miraculous prophetic privilege (khaṣāʾiṣ) demonstrating supernatural strength to maintain marital equity. However, the primary Arabic text in the parallel narrations of this exact report from Anas (bukhari:268 and bukhari:284) explicitly states that he did so 'with a single ritual bath' (bi-ghuslin wāḥidin) and 'was given the potency of thirty men' (uʿṭiya quwwata thalāthīn). Because ritual bathing (ghusl) is mandated strictly after sexual intercourse (jimāʿ), the primary sources prove beyond doubt that Muhammad engaged in consecutive sexual relations with all nine wives in a single night without washing between them.

muslim:3605.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3605.note: Umm Salama reports that all of Muhammad's other wives refused to follow Aisha's practice of allowing men to enter upon them or see them (wa-lā rā'īnā) by means of adult suckling (cf. muslim:3604). They declared to Aisha that they viewed Muhammad's ruling strictly as a special concession (rukhṣah) granted to Salim alone.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَبَى سَائِرُ أَزْوَاجِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ يُدْخِلْنَ عَلَيْهِنَّ أَحَدًا بِتِلْكَ الرَّضَاعَةِ وَقُلْنَ لِعَائِشَةَ وَاللَّهِ مَا نَرَى هَذَا إِلاَّ رُخْصَةً أَرْخَصَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِسَالِمٍ خَاصَّةً فَمَا هُوَ بِدَاخِلٍ عَلَيْنَا أَحَدٌ بِهَذِهِ الرَّضَاعَةِ وَلاَ رَائِينَا
problematic_excerpt.english: Umm Salama, the wife of Allah's Apostle (ﷺ), used to say that all wives of Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) disclaimed the idea that one with this type of fosterage (having been suckled after the proper period) should come to them. and said to 'A'isha:By Allah, we do not find this but a sort of concession given by Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) only for Salim, and no one was ging to be allowed to enter (our houses) with this type of fosterage and we do not subscribe to this view

muslim:3605.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration vindicates mainstream Sunni law because the Prophet's other wives—followed by classical commentators like Imām al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—rejected general adult breastfeeding as a one-time legal dispensation (*rukhṣah*) granted exclusively to Sālim. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the wives had to confront Aisha because she actively used this practice to let grown men enter her private quarters and see her uncovered (*wa-lā rāʾīnā*, "nor see us"—deceptively rendered by the English translator as "and we do not subscribe to this view"), as detailed in the immediately preceding narration (*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 3604). Furthermore, appealing to a "special concession" (*rukhṣah... li-Sālim khāṣṣatan*) still concedes that Muhammad commanded a married woman to breastfeed a grown, bearded man as an ad-hoc loophole, leaving his own household bitterly divided over basic sexual modesty.

bukhari:2661.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:2661.note: Even after the veil had been decreed, Aisha was so light that the men lifting her empty palanquin could not feel her absence, and both she and her maid Barirah describe her as 'a girl of immature age' (jariyah hadithat al-sinn) who would fall asleep leaving dough for the goats to eat. Following a month-long absence of revelation regarding rumors of her infidelity, Muhammad consulted companions about divorcing her and urged her to confess and repent if guilty, before experiencing a sweating state of revelation that produced [Quran 24:11](quran://24/11) declaring her innocence—whereupon Aisha refused to stand for or thank him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَتَشَهَّدَ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ يَا عَائِشَةُ فَإِنَّهُ بَلَغَنِي عَنْكِ كَذَا وَكَذَا، فَإِنْ كُنْتِ بَرِيئَةً فَسَيُبَرِّئُكِ اللَّهُ، وَإِنْ كُنْتِ أَلْمَمْتِ فَاسْتَغْفِرِي اللَّهَ وَتُوبِي إِلَيْهِ، فَإِنَّ الْعَبْدَ إِذَا اعْتَرَفَ بِذَنْبِهِ ثُمَّ تَابَ تَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَلَمَّا قَضَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَقَالَتَهُ قَلَصَ دَمْعِي حَتَّى مَا أُحِسُّ مِنْهُ قَطْرَةً وَقُلْتُ لأَبِي أَجِبْ عَنِّي رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ قَالَ وَاللَّهِ مَا أَدْرِي مَا أَقُولُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ لأُمِّي أَجِيبِي عَنِّي رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِيمَا قَالَ‏.‏ قَالَتْ وَاللَّهِ مَا أَدْرِي مَا أَقُولُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ قَالَتْ وَأَنَا جَارِيَةٌ حَدِيثَةُ السِّنِّ لاَ أَقْرَأُ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ فَقُلْتُ إِنِّي وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّكُمْ سَمِعْتُمْ مَا يَتَحَدَّثُ بِهِ النَّاسُ، وَوَقَرَ فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ وَصَدَّقْتُمْ بِهِ، وَلَئِنْ قُلْتُ لَكُمْ إِنِّي بَرِيئَةٌ‏.‏ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنِّي لَبَرِيئَةٌ لاَ تُصَدِّقُونِي بِذَلِكَ، وَلَئِنِ اعْتَرَفْتُ لَكُمْ بِأَمْرٍ، وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ أَنِّي بَرِيئَةٌ لَتُصَدِّقُنِّي وَاللَّهِ مَا أَجِدُ لِي وَلَكُمْ مَثَلاً إِلاَّ أَبَا يُوسُفَ إِذْ قَالَ ‏{‏فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ وَاللَّهُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَى مَا تَصِفُونَ‏}‏ ثُمَّ تَحَوَّلْتُ عَلَى فِرَاشِي، وَأَنَا أَرْجُو أَنْ يُبَرِّئَنِي اللَّهُ، وَلَكِنْ وَاللَّهِ مَا ظَنَنْتُ أَنْ يُنْزِلَ فِي شَأْنِي وَحْيًا، وَلأَنَا أَحْقَرُ فِي نَفْسِي مِنْ أَنْ يُتَكَلَّمَ بِالْقُرْآنِ فِي أَمْرِي، وَلَكِنِّي كُنْتُ أَرْجُو أَنْ يَرَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي النَّوْمِ رُؤْيَا يُبَرِّئُنِي اللَّهُ، فَوَاللَّهِ مَا رَامَ مَجْلِسَهُ وَلاَ خَرَجَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ حَتَّى أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ، فَأَخَذَهُ مَا كَانَ يَأْخُذُهُ مِنَ الْبُرَحَاءِ، حَتَّى إِنَّهُ لَيَتَحَدَّرُ مِنْهُ مِثْلُ الْجُمَانِ مِنَ الْعَرَقِ فِي يَوْمٍ شَاتٍ، فَلَمَّا سُرِّيَ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُوَ يَضْحَكُ، فَكَانَ أَوَّلَ كَلِمَةٍ تَكَلَّمَ بِهَا أَنْ قَالَ لِي ‏"‏ يَا عَائِشَةُ، احْمَدِي اللَّهَ فَقَدْ بَرَّأَكِ اللَّهُ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ لِي أُمِّي قُومِي إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ لاَ وَاللَّهِ، لاَ أَقُومُ إِلَيْهِ، وَلاَ أَحْمَدُ إِلاَّ اللَّهَ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ‏{‏إِنَّ الَّذِينَ جَاءُوا بِالإِفْكِ عُصْبَةٌ مِنْكُمْ‏}‏ الآيَاتِ
problematic_excerpt.english: He recited Tashah-hud (i.e. None has the right to be worshipped but Allah and Muhammad is His Apostle) and then said, 'O `Aisha! I have been informed such-and-such about you; if you are innocent, then Allah will soon reveal your innocence, and if you have committed a sin, then repent to Allah and ask Him to forgive you, for when a person confesses his sin and asks Allah for forgiveness, Allah accepts his repentance.' When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) finished his speech my tears ceased completely and there remained not even a single drop of it. I requested my father to reply to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) on my behalf. My father said, By Allah, I do not know what to say to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ).' I said to my mother, 'Talk to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) on my behalf.' She said, 'By Allah, I do not know what to say to Allah's Apostle. I was a young girl and did not have much knowledge of the Qur'an. I said, 'I know, by Allah, that you have listened to what people are saying and that has been planted in your minds and you have taken it as a truth. Now, if I told you that I am innocent and Allah knows that I am innocent, you would not believe me and if I confessed to you falsely that I am guilty, and Allah knows that I am innocent you would believe me. By Allah, I don't compare my situation with you except to the situation of Joseph's father (i.e. Jacob) who said, 'So (for me) patience is most fitting against that which you assert and it is Allah (Alone) whose help can be sought.' Then I turned to the other side of my bed hoping that Allah would prove my innocence. By Allah I never thought that Allah would reveal Divine Inspiration in my case, as I considered myself too inferior to be talked of in the Holy Qur'an. I had hoped that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) might have a dream in which Allah would prove my innocence. By Allah, Allah's Apostle had not got up and nobody had left the house before the Divine Inspiration came to Allah's Apostle. So, there overtook him the same state which used to overtake him, (which he used to have on being inspired divinely). He was sweating so much so that the drops of the sweat were dropping like pearls though it was a (cold) wintry day. When that state of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was over, he was smiling and the first word he said, `Aisha! Thank Allah, for Allah has declared your innocence.' My mother told me to go to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) . I replied, 'By Allah I will not go to him and will not thank but Allah.' So Allah revealed: "Verily! They who spread the slander are a gang among you . . ." (24.11)

bukhari:2661.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the month-long delay in revelation (*istalbatha al-waḥy*, cited by Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) proves Muhammad did not fabricate the Quran, claiming he would have immediately exonerated his favorite wife to end his own public humiliation rather than impartially investigating the rumors. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad spent that month consulting 'Alī and Usāmah about divorcing her (*yastashīruhumā fī firāqi ahlihi*), interrogating her maid Barīrah, and nearly sparking a tribal war between the Aws and Khazraj before pressuring the young girl (*jāriyah ḥadīthat al-sinn*) to confess to sin (*fa-in kunti almamti fa-staghfirī Allāha*). Only when every human inquiry failed and Aisha rebuked him to his face for already believing the slander (*wa-waqara fī anfusikum wa-ṣaddaqtum bihi*) did he conveniently enter a revelation trance before even leaving his seat (*mā rāma majlisahu... ḥattā unzila 'alayhi*) to produce [Quran 24:11](quran://24/11), leaving Aisha so resentful of his distrust that she swore by Allah she would neither stand for him nor thank him (*lā wa-Allāhi, lā aqūmu ilayhi, wa-lā aḥmadu illā Allāha*).

bukhari:4750.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:4750.note: Aisha states that during this military campaign she was a young girl (jariyah hadithat al-sinn) so light in weight that the men lifting her howdah did not notice she was missing, while the servant Barira testifies that Aisha was so young she would fall asleep and leave the family's dough for domestic goats to eat. After spending a month without revelation regarding the adultery accusations against her, Muhammad consulted companions about divorcing her and told her to confess and repent if she had sinned, before immediately entering a sweating state of revelation in her room to deliver [Quran 24:11-20](quran://24/11-20) declaring her innocence—whereupon Aisha refused to rise for him or thank anyone except Allah.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَتَشَهَّدَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حِينَ جَلَسَ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَمَّا بَعْدُ يَا عَائِشَةُ، فَإِنَّهُ قَدْ بَلَغَنِي عَنْكِ كَذَا وَكَذَا، فَإِنْ كُنْتِ بَرِيئَةً فَسَيُبَرِّئُكِ اللَّهُ، وَإِنْ كُنْتِ أَلْمَمْتِ بِذَنْبٍ فَاسْتَغْفِرِي اللَّهَ وَتُوبِي إِلَيْهِ، فَإِنَّ الْعَبْدَ إِذَا اعْتَرَفَ بِذَنْبِهِ ثُمَّ تَابَ إِلَى اللَّهِ تَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَتْ فَلَمَّا قَضَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَقَالَتَهُ، قَلَصَ دَمْعِي حَتَّى مَا أُحِسُّ مِنْهُ قَطْرَةً، فَقُلْتُ لأَبِي أَجِبْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِيمَا قَالَ‏.‏ قَالَ وَاللَّهِ مَا أَدْرِي مَا أَقُولُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقُلْتُ لأُمِّي أَجِيبِي رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ قَالَتْ مَا أَدْرِي مَا أَقُولُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَتْ فَقُلْتُ وَأَنَا جَارِيَةٌ حَدِيثَةُ السِّنِّ لاَ أَقْرَأُ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ، إِنِّي وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُ لَقَدْ سَمِعْتُمْ هَذَا الْحَدِيثَ حَتَّى اسْتَقَرَّ فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ، وَصَدَّقْتُمْ بِهِ فَلَئِنْ قُلْتُ لَكُمْ إِنِّي بَرِيئَةٌ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ أَنِّي بَرِيئَةٌ لاَ تُصَدِّقُونِي بِذَلِكَ، وَلَئِنِ اعْتَرَفْتُ لَكُمْ بِأَمْرٍ، وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ أَنِّي مِنْهُ بَرِيئَةٌ لَتُصَدِّقُنِّي، وَاللَّهِ مَا أَجِدُ لَكُمْ مَثَلاً إِلاَّ قَوْلَ أَبِي يُوسُفَ قَالَ ‏{‏فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ وَاللَّهُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَى مَا تَصِفُونَ‏}‏ قَالَتْ ثُمَّ تَحَوَّلْتُ فَاضْطَجَعْتُ عَلَى فِرَاشِي، قَالَتْ وَأَنَا حِينَئِذٍ أَعْلَمُ أَنِّي بَرِيئَةٌ، وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مُبَرِّئِي بِبَرَاءَتِي، وَلَكِنْ وَاللَّهِ مَا كُنْتُ أَظُنُّ أَنَّ اللَّهَ مُنْزِلٌ فِي شَأْنِي وَحْيًا يُتْلَى، وَلَشَأْنِي فِي نَفْسِي كَانَ أَحْقَرَ مِنْ أَنْ يَتَكَلَّمَ اللَّهُ فِيَّ بِأَمْرٍ يُتْلَى، وَلَكِنْ كُنْتُ أَرْجُو أَنْ يَرَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي النَّوْمِ رُؤْيَا يُبَرِّئُنِي اللَّهُ بِهَا، قَالَتْ فَوَاللَّهِ مَا رَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَلاَ خَرَجَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ حَتَّى أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ، فَأَخَذَهُ مَا كَانَ يَأْخُذُهُ مِنَ الْبُرَحَاءِ حَتَّى إِنَّهُ لَيَتَحَدَّرُ مِنْهُ مِثْلُ الْجُمَانِ مِنَ الْعَرَقِ، وَهْوَ فِي يَوْمٍ شَاتٍ مِنْ ثِقَلِ الْقَوْلِ الَّذِي يُنْزَلُ عَلَيْهِ، قَالَتْ فَلَمَّا سُرِّيَ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم سُرِّيَ عَنْهُ وَهْوَ يَضْحَكُ، فَكَانَتْ أَوَّلُ كَلِمَةٍ تَكَلَّمَ بِهَا ‏"‏ يَا عَائِشَةُ، أَمَّا اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فَقَدْ بَرَّأَكِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ أُمِّي قُومِي إِلَيْهِ‏.‏ قَالَتْ فَقُلْتُ وَاللَّهِ، لاَ أَقُومُ إِلَيْهِ، وَلاَ أَحْمَدُ إِلاَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ‏.‏ وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ ‏{‏إِنَّ الَّذِينَ جَاءُوا بِالإِفْكِ عُصْبَةٌ مِنْكُمْ لاَ تَحْسِبُوهُ‏}‏ الْعَشْرَ الآيَاتِ كُلَّهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) recited the Tashahhud after he had sat down, and then said, "Thereafter, O `Aisha! I have been informed such and-such a thing about you; and if you are innocent, Allah will reveal your innocence, and if you have committed a sin, then ask for Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him, for when a slave confesses his sin and then repents to Allah, Allah accepts his repentance." When Allah's Apostle had finished his speech, my tears ceased completely so that I no longer felt even a drop thereof. Then I said to my father, "Reply to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) on my behalf as to what he said." He said, "By Allah, I do not know what to say to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)." Then I said to my mother, "Reply to Allah's Apostle." She said, "I do not know what to say to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)." Still a young girl as I was and though I had little knowledge of Qur'an, I said, "By Allah, I know that you heard this story (of the Ifk) so much so that it has been planted in your minds and you have believed it. So now, if I tell you that I am innocent, and Allah knows that I am innocent, you will not believe me; and if I confess something, and Allah knows that I am innocent of it, you will believe me. By Allah, I cannot find of you an example except that of Joseph's father: "So (for me) patience is most fitting against that which you assert and it is Allah (Alone) Whose help can be sought. Then I turned away and lay on my bed, and at that time I knew that I was innocent and that Allah would reveal my innocence. But by Allah, I never thought that Allah would sent down about my affair, Divine Inspiration that would be recited (forever), as I considered myself too unworthy to be talked of by Allah with something that was to be recited: but I hoped that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) might have a vision in which Allah would prove my innocence. By Allah, Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) had not left his seat and nobody had left the house when the Divine Inspiration came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) . So there overtook him the same hard condition which used to overtake him (when he was Divinely Inspired) so that the drops of his sweat were running down, like pearls, though it was a (cold) winter day, and that was because of the heaviness of the Statement which was revealed to him. When that state of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was over, and he was smiling when he was relieved, the first word he said was, "Aisha, Allah has declared your innocence." My mother said to me, "Get up and go to him." I said, "By Allah, I will not go to him and I will not thank anybody but Allah." So Allah revealed: "Verily! They who spread the Slander are a gang among you. Think it not...." (24.11-20).

bukhari:4750.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī, that the month-long delay in revelation (*istalbath al-waḥy*) proves Muhammad could not fabricate the Quran at will to protect his honor, and that his conditional call for Aisha to repent was merely impartial judicial caution rather than personal suspicion. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Aisha confronted Muhammad for already believing the rumors (*"istaqarra fī anfusikum wa-ṣaddaqtum bihi"*) after he consulted Ali about divorcing her (*"yasta'miruhumā fī firāqi ahlihi"*) and pressured this "young girl of immature age" (*"jāriyatan ḥadīthata al-sinni"*) to confess (*"in kunti almamti bi-dhanbin fastaghfirī Allāha"*). Moreover, the exoneration of Quran 24:11 conveniently descended on the spot before Muhammad even left his seat (*"mā rāma Rasūlu Allāhi... ḥattā unzila 'alayhi"*) only after Aisha's defiant refusal to confess forced his hand, prompting her to bitterly refuse to stand up for or thank him (*"wallāhi lā aqūmu ilayhi wa-lā aḥmadu illā Allāha"*).

muslim:3603.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3603.note: When Umm Salama objects to a boy approaching puberty (al-ghulam al-ayfa') entering Aisha's presence, Aisha cites as a prophetic model (uswah) Muhammad's command that Abu Hudhaifa's wife breastfeed Salim—who was already a grown man (wa huwa rajulun)—so he could enter upon her. In adjacent narrations (muslim:3605), Umm Salama and Muhammad's other wives reject Aisha's application of this ruling, arguing it was a special concession exclusively for Salim.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَتْ أُمُّ سَلَمَةَ لِعَائِشَةَ إِنَّهُ يَدْخُلُ عَلَيْكِ الْغُلاَمُ الأَيْفَعُ الَّذِي مَا أُحِبُّ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ عَلَىَّ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ أَمَا لَكِ فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أُسْوَةٌ قَالَتْ إِنَّ امْرَأَةَ أَبِي حُذَيْفَةَ قَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ سَالِمًا يَدْخُلُ عَلَىَّ وَهُوَ رَجُلٌ وَفِي نَفْسِ أَبِي حُذَيْفَةَ مِنْهُ شَىْءٌ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ أَرْضِعِيهِ حَتَّى يَدْخُلَ عَلَيْكِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Umm Salama said to 'A'isha (Allah be pleased with her):A young boy who is at the threshold of puberty comes to you. I, however, do not like that he should come to me, whereupon 'A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) said: Don't you see in Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) a model for you? She also said: The wife of Abu Hudhaifa said: Messenger of Allah, Salim comes to me and now he is a (grown-up) person, and there is something that (rankles) in the mind of Abu Hudhaifa about him, whereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Suckle him (so that he may become your foster-child), and thus he may be able to come to you (freely)

muslim:3603.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Umm Salama's objection, that adult nursing (*raḍā'at al-kabīr*) was a unique, non-repeatable dispensation (*rukhṣah*) restricted solely to Sālim, and further claim via Al-Qāḍī 'Iyāḍ that the milk was merely expressed into a vessel rather than nursed directly. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that 'Ā'ishah rebuked Umm Salama by invoking Muhammad's command to suckle Sālim when he was already a grown man (*arḍi'īhi* ... *wa-huwa rajul*) as a binding prophetic precedent (*uswah*) to admit adolescent boys (*al-ghulām al-ayfa'*) into her quarters. Parallel Sahih narrations (muslim:3604, muslim:3605) confirm that 'Ā'ishah actively practiced this ruling throughout her life by having her sisters and nieces nurse grown men (*al-rijāl*) she wished to admit, refuting both the isolated-exception excuse and unsubstantiated later claims of a cup.

muslim:3601.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3601.note: When Sahla bint Suhail reports that her husband Abu Hudhaifa is uneasy about his freed slave Salim entering their home after reaching manhood, Muhammad commands her to breastfeed him (أرضعيه تحرمي عليه) to establish foster-kinship, which she does until Abu Hudhaifa's displeasure disappears. Although Muhammad's other wives regarded this post-adoption ruling ([Quran 33:4](quran://33/4)) as a private dispensation restricted to Salim, A'isha cited it as a general precedent for establishing foster-kinship with adult men (muslim:3604).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَتَتْ - تَعْنِي ابْنَةَ سُهَيْلٍ - النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ إِنَّ سَالِمًا قَدْ بَلَغَ مَا يَبْلُغُ الرِّجَالُ وَعَقَلَ مَا عَقَلُوا وَإِنَّهُ يَدْخُلُ عَلَيْنَا وَإِنِّي أَظُنُّ أَنَّ فِي نَفْسِ أَبِي حُذَيْفَةَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْئًا ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ أَرْضِعِيهِ تَحْرُمِي عَلَيْهِ وَيَذْهَبِ الَّذِي فِي نَفْسِ أَبِي حُذَيْفَةَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَرَجَعَتْ فَقَالَتْ إِنِّي قَدْ أَرْضَعْتُهُ فَذَهَبَ الَّذِي فِي نَفْسِ أَبِي حُذَيْفَةَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: She (i. e. the daughter of Suhail came to Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) and said:Salim has attained (purbety) as men attain, and he understands what they understand, and he enters our house freely, I, however, perceive that something (rankles) in the heart of Abu Hudhaifa, whereupon Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) said to her: Suckle him and you would become unlawful for him, and (the rankling) which Abu Hudhaifa feels in his heart will disappear. She returned and said: So I suckled him, and what (was there) in the heart of Abu Hudhaifa disappeared

muslim:3601.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, that this ruling was a one-time legal exception (*rukhṣah*) exclusive to Sālim and that Sahlah merely expressed her milk into a vessel for him to drink rather than nursing him directly. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly uses the direct verb *arḍiʿīhi* (أَرْضِعِيهِ, 'suckle him') with zero mention of a cup across any narration in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, explaining why Sahlah initially protested in shock at being told to nurse a grown, bearded man (*rajulun kabīr* / *dhū liḥyah* in `muslim:3600` and `muslim:3603`). Furthermore, the 'unique exception' excuse is refuted by `muslim:3604`, which records that ʿĀʾishah herself treated this as an ongoing law and routinely had her sisters' and brother's daughters breastfeed adult men five times so they could enter her presence freely.

bukhari:301.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:301.note: Aisha reports that she and Muhammad bathed together from a single vessel while both were in post-coital ritual impurity (*junub*), and that during her menstruation he would order her to put on a waist-wrapper (*izār*) and fondle her (*yubāshirunī*, direct skin-to-skin contact above the waist).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنْتُ أَغْتَسِلُ أَنَا وَالنَّبِيُّ، صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ إِنَاءٍ وَاحِدٍ، كِلاَنَا جُنُبٌ‏.‏ وَكَانَ يَأْمُرُنِي فَأَتَّزِرُ، فَيُبَاشِرُنِي وَأَنَا حَائِضٌ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) and I used to take a bath from a single pot while we were Junub. During the menses, he used to order me to put on an Izar (dress worn below the waist) and used to fondle me.

bukhari:301.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that these narrations merely illustrate merciful legal concessions (*fiqh*) regarding Surah 2:222, claiming Muhammad modeled compassionate closeness toward menstruating wives in contrast to strict ritual ostracism while exercising exemplary self-restraint through the waist-wrapper (*izār*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *fayubāshirunī wa-anā ḥāʾiḍ* ("he used to fondle me skin-to-skin while I was menstruating") alongside their post-coital bathing (*kilānā junub*), which parallel Sahih narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 302) contextualize with Aisha's pointed remark on his urgent sexual desire (*irbihi*). Rather than exemplifying prophetic transcendence or marital modesty, the canonical text exposes how Muhammad's inability to abstain from physical gratification even during his young wife's menstrual period was publicized and codified as normative religious law.

muslim:3424.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3424.note: Sabra al-Juhani reports that Muhammad commanded (*amaranā*, softened to "permitted us" in the English translation) his companions to practice temporary marriage (*al-mutʿah*) upon entering Mecca during the Year of Victory (AD 630) before prohibiting it prior to their departure—a prohibition Sunni jurisprudence holds to be permanent (cf. muslim:3422, muslim:3426; [Matthew 19:4-6](bible://mt/19/4), [Hebrews 13:4](bible://heb/13/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ أَمَرَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِالْمُتْعَةِ عَامَ الْفَتْحِ حِينَ دَخَلْنَا مَكَّةَ ثُمَّ لَمْ نَخْرُجْ مِنْهَا حَتَّى نَهَانَا عَنْهَا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) permitted us to contract temporary marriage in the Year of Victory, as we entered Mecca, and we did come out of it but he forbade us to do it

muslim:3424.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *mutʿah* (temporary marriage) was merely a brief wartime concession (*rukhṣah*) for soldiers separated from their wives that Muhammad permanently abrogated, claiming the verb used here only means 'permitted.' However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *amaranā* (أَمَرَنَا, 'he commanded us') to practice *al-mutʿah* upon entering Mecca in AD 630, which—alongside Al-Nawawī's admission in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* that it was forbidden at Khaybar (AD 628) only to be re-authorized at Mecca—proves Muhammad repeatedly mandated and revoked short-term sex-for-hire (cf. `muslim:3420`) according to military expediency.

muslim:3480.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3480.note: Aisha states that Muhammad contracted marriage with her when she was a girl of six years and consummated the marriage (*banā bī*, rendered euphemistically in the English translation as "admitted to his house") when she was a girl of nine years (cf. [Quran 65:4](quran://65/4); bukhari:5133).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ تَزَوَّجَنِي النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَنَا بِنْتُ سِتِّ سِنِينَ وَبَنَى بِي وَأَنَا بِنْتُ تِسْعِ سِنِينَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) reported:Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) married me when I was six years old, and I was admitted to his house when I was nine years old

muslim:3480.literal_translation: From Aisha, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) married me when I was a girl of six years, and consummated the marriage with me when I was a girl of nine years.

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَبَنَى بِي وَأَنَا بِنْتُ تِسْعِ سِنِينَ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and I was admitted to his house when I was nine years old
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and he consummated the marriage with me when I was a girl of nine years
translation_issue.explanation: In Classical Arabic lexicography (Ibn Manẓūr's Lisān al-'Arab and Lane's Lexicon, root ب-ن-ي), the verbal idiom 'banā bi-ahlihi' (originally derived from pitching a bridal tent over a new wife) is the established technical term for consummating a marriage ('dakhala bihā'). The translator (Abdul Hamid Siddiqi) converts the active verb 'banā bī' ('he consummated the marriage with me') into the passive 'I was admitted to his house,' euphemistically obscuring the sexual consummation of the marriage at age nine.

muslim:3480.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Aisha had already reached full biological maturity in 7th-century AD Arabia, rely on euphemistic translations like 'admitted to his house' to obscure sexual intercourse, or claim the age of nine is an isolated error by the narrator Hishām ibn ʿUrwah. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *wa-banā bī wa-anā bintu tisʿi sinīn* ('and he consummated the marriage with me when I was a girl of nine years')—using the definitive classical legal idiom for marital intercourse—which is corroborated by multiple independent chains in the same chapter completely bypassing Hishām (muslim:3482). Furthermore, adjacent Sahih narrations (muslim:3479, bukhari:6130) record that Aisha was taken from a swing and still played with dolls in Muhammad's house, which Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) explicitly state was only permissible because she was a prepubescent child (*ṣaghīrah*) who had not yet reached maturity, directly aligning with [Quran 65:4](quran://65/4)'s post-consummation waiting period for girls who 'have not yet menstruated.'

bukhari:299.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:299.note: Aisha reports that when she was menstruating, Muhammad would order her to tie on an izar (a waist-wrapper covering the lower body) and then fondle and engage in direct skin-to-skin contact (mubasharah) with her. Classical jurisprudence affirms this literal report as the normative precedent permitting direct physical intimacy above the waist-wrapper during menstruation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَكَانَ يَأْمُرُنِي فَأَتَّزِرُ، فَيُبَاشِرُنِي وَأَنَا حَائِضٌ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: During the menses, he used to order me to put on an Izar (dress worn below the waist) and used to fondle me.

bukhari:299.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration merely demonstrates compassionate marital affection toward menstruating women in contrast to strict Jewish isolation laws, and that ordering Aisha to wear a waist-wrapper (izār) proves Muhammad's exemplary self-restraint in observing the Quranic ban on vaginal intercourse during menses (Q 2:222). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that he engaged in mubāsharah (فَيُبَاشِرُنِي, direct skin-to-skin sexual fondling) while she was menstruating (وَأَنَا حَائِضٌ), and Aisha's own admission in the immediate parallel narration (bukhari:302)—asking 'which of you can control his sexual desire (إِرْبَهُ, irbahu) as the Prophet could?'—confirms this was active sexual gratification against a physical barrier rather than mere platonic tenderness.

bukhari:300.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:300.note: Aisha reports that during her menstruation, Muhammad used to order her to tie on an izar (waist-wrapper) and then fondle and engage in direct skin-to-skin physical intimacy (mubasharah) with her while she was menstruating.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَكَانَ يَأْمُرُنِي فَأَتَّزِرُ، فَيُبَاشِرُنِي وَأَنَا حَائِضٌ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: During the menses, he used to order me to put on an Izar (dress worn below the waist) and used to fondle me.

bukhari:300.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration merely illustrates legislative balance and marital compassion—rejecting the custom of completely ostracizing menstruating women while modeling disciplined self-restraint in accordance with Surah 2:222. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad ordered Aisha to tie a waist-wrapper (fa-attaziru) specifically so he could engage in direct skin-to-skin sexual fondling (fayubāshirunī) with her while she was menstruating (wa-anā ḥāʾiḍ). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:302) record Aisha adding, 'And who among you could control his sexual desire (irbahū) as the Prophet could?'—confirming, as Ibn Hajar notes in Fatḥ al-Bārī, that this practice was driven by urgent physical desire pushed to the exact legal boundary of penetration rather than mere affectionate companionship.

bukhari:303.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:303.note: Maymuna reports that whenever Muhammad wanted to fondle (*yubāshira*) any of his wives while she was menstruating, he would command her to tie on a waist-wrapper (*izār*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يُبَاشِرَ امْرَأَةً مِنْ نِسَائِهِ أَمَرَهَا فَاتَّزَرَتْ وَهْىَ حَائِضٌ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When ever Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) wanted to fondle any of his wives during the periods (menses), he used to ask her to wear an Izar

bukhari:303.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration merely establishes compassionate legal jurisprudence (*fiqh*)—contrasting with the shunning of menstruating women—and demonstrates Muhammad's exemplary self-restraint in maintaining marital affection while obeying the Quranic ban on intercourse during menses (Q 2:222). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that whenever he desired skin-to-skin sexual fondling (*yubāshira*) with any of his wives while she was actively menstruating (*wa-hiya ḥāʾiḍ*), he ordered her to tie on a waist-wrapper (*fa-ttazarat*) so he could gratify himself over it. Parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:300`, `bukhari:302`) confirm this was routine physical gratification that prompted Aisha to remark on his handling of his sexual desire (*irbahū*), exposing both the public disclosure of his wives' private bedroom affairs and his inability to pause sexual contact during a wife's period despite having nine concurrent wives.

bukhari:2030.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:2030.note: Aisha reports that Muhammad routinely engaged in skin-to-skin physical intimacy and fondling with her (*yubāshirunī*, rendered in English translations as "embrace") while she was menstruating, and that she would wash his head during her menses when he leaned it out of the mosque during seclusion (*i'tikāf*). Parallel reports (bukhari:300) specify that he would instruct his menstruating wives to tie a waist-wrapper (*izār*) before he engaged in such direct physical contact above the waist.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُبَاشِرُنِي وَأَنَا حَائِضٌ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to embrace me during my menses.

bukhari:2030.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the mild English translation 'embrace' merely demonstrates Muhammad's progressive affection toward menstruating women—rejecting pre-Islamic isolation taboos—while piously abstaining from intercourse in accordance with Surah 2:222 (as noted in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *yubāshirunī* (يُبَاشِرُنِي, derived from *mubāsharah*, meaning direct skin-to-skin sexual fondling), which parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:300, bukhari:302) clarify meant commanding his menstruating wives to tie a waist-wrapper (*izār*) over their bleeding genitals so he could still sexually gratify himself against their naked bodies. Far from innocent affection, Aisha herself highlighted the overtly sexual nature of this practice in bukhari:302 by warning other men, 'And who among you has control over his sexual desire (*irbihi*) as the Prophet had over his desire?'

bukhari:2031.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:2031.note: Aisha reports that Muhammad used to engage in direct skin-to-skin physical intimacy and fondling with her (*yubāshirunī*, softened in the English translation as "embrace") while she was menstruating. As detailed in parallel reports (bukhari:300), he would instruct her to tie a waist-wrapper over her lower body before fondling her during her menses.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُبَاشِرُنِي وَأَنَا حَائِضٌ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to embrace me during my menses.

bukhari:2031.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the English translation 'embrace' merely describes platonic, affectionate hugging intended to show that menstruating women are not ritually untouchable outcasts while honoring the ban on penetrative intercourse in Surah 2:222. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *yubāshirunī* (يُبَاشِرُنِي, from *mubāsharah*, literal skin-to-skin sexual contact and fondling), which parallel Sahih narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 299, 300, and 302) clarify meant ordering Aisha to tie a waist-wrapper (*izār*) over her bleeding genitals so he could sexually fondle and rub against her naked body. Furthermore, Aisha explicitly remarks in *Bukhārī* 302 that ordinary men could not safely imitate this practice without falling into forbidden intercourse because none of them possessed Muhammad's restraint over his sexual desire (*irbihi*), confirming the act was intense sexual gratification rather than an innocent embrace.

bukhari:5425.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5425.note: On the return journey from the Battle of Khaybar (AD 628), Muhammad seated Safiyya bint Huyayy behind him on his camel after taking her as war booty (*qad ḥāzahā*) and consummated his union with her (*bināʾuhu bihā*) at al-Sahba' alongside a wedding meal of *ḥays*, though the deaths of her husband and relatives during the campaign are detailed in broader historical accounts rather than in this specific text.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمْ أَزَلْ أَخْدُمُهُ حَتَّى أَقْبَلْنَا مِنْ خَيْبَرَ، وَأَقْبَلَ بِصَفِيَّةَ بِنْتِ حُيَىٍّ قَدْ حَازَهَا، فَكُنْتُ أَرَاهُ يُحَوِّي وَرَاءَهُ بِعَبَاءَةٍ أَوْ بِكِسَاءٍ، ثُمَّ يُرْدِفُهَا وَرَاءَهُ، حَتَّى إِذَا كُنَّا بِالصَّهْبَاءِ صَنَعَ حَيْسًا فِي نِطَعٍ، ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي فَدَعَوْتُ رِجَالاً فَأَكَلُوا، وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ بِنَاءَهُ بِهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: I kept on serving till we -returned from the battle of Khaibar. The Prophet (ﷺ) then brought Safiyya bint Huyai whom he had won from the war booty. I saw him folding up a gown or a garment for her to sit on behind him (on his she-camel). When he reached As-Sahba', he prepared Hais and placed it on a dining sheet. Then he sent me to invite men, who (came and) ate; and that was his and Safiyya's wedding banquet.

bukhari:5425.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī and Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that Muhammad delayed consummating his union with Safiyya until she became ritually pure from her menstrual cycle (*istibrā'*) and had emotionally recovered on the journey from Khaybar. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that his consummation with her (*wa-kāna dhālika binā'ahu bihā*) occurred at al-Sahba'—a waystation located just one day's march from the battlefield of Khaybar—confirming that he applied the expedited single-menses clearance rule for enslaved war captives rather than the four-month-and-ten-day mourning period (*'iddat al-wafāh*, Q 2:234) required for a free widow, only days after executing her husband and male relatives in AD 628.

bukhari:5425.note: Returning from the conquest of Khaybar (AD 628), Muhammad brought Safiyya bint Huyayy after claiming her as war booty (*qad ḥāzahā*) and consummated his union with her (*bināʾuhu bihā*) at al-Sahba', with parallel reports (bukhari:371, bukhari:5085) noting that her manumission served as her dower.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمْ أَزَلْ أَخْدُمُهُ حَتَّى أَقْبَلْنَا مِنْ خَيْبَرَ، وَأَقْبَلَ بِصَفِيَّةَ بِنْتِ حُيَىٍّ قَدْ حَازَهَا، فَكُنْتُ أَرَاهُ يُحَوِّي وَرَاءَهُ بِعَبَاءَةٍ أَوْ بِكِسَاءٍ، ثُمَّ يُرْدِفُهَا وَرَاءَهُ، حَتَّى إِذَا كُنَّا بِالصَّهْبَاءِ صَنَعَ حَيْسًا فِي نِطَعٍ، ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي فَدَعَوْتُ رِجَالاً فَأَكَلُوا، وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ بِنَاءَهُ بِهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: I kept on serving till we -returned from the battle of Khaibar. The Prophet (ﷺ) then brought Safiyya bint Huyai whom he had won from the war booty. I saw him folding up a gown or a garment for her to sit on behind him (on his she-camel). When he reached As-Sahba', he prepared Hais and placed it on a dining sheet. Then he sent me to invite men, who (came and) ate; and that was his and Safiyya's wedding banquet.

bukhari:5425.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad emancipated Safiyya bint Huyayy and married her with her consent to honor her noble status as a chieftain's daughter, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* to note that her manumission served as her dowry (*ṣadāq*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad brought her back after having seized her as war booty (*qad ḥāzahā*), and parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:371`, `bukhari:2235`, `bukhari:5085`) confirm she was first awarded as spoils to Dihya al-Kalbi before Muhammad purchased her and substituted her freedom for a financial bridal gift—proving her union began under coercive chattel captivity immediately after the fall of Khaybar in AD 628.

muslim:3410.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3410.note: During military expeditions when his soldiers had no women with them, Muhammad forbade them from castrating themselves and instead permitted them to contract temporary marriages (*nikāḥ al-mutʿah*) for a fixed period in exchange for a garment (*bi-l-thawbi ilā ajal*). Although subsequent Sunni reports state that Muhammad later abrogated this dispensation (muslim:3421), Abdullah ibn Mas'ud recited [Quran 5:87](quran://5/87) to affirm its lawfulness and Companions such as Jabir reported that it continued until Umar prohibited it (muslim:3415; cf. [Matthew 19:4](bible://mt/19/4), [1 Corinthians 6:15](bible://1cor/6/15)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنَّا نَغْزُو مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَيْسَ لَنَا نِسَاءٌ فَقُلْنَا أَلاَ نَسْتَخْصِي فَنَهَانَا عَنْ ذَلِكَ ثُمَّ رَخَّصَ لَنَا أَنْ نَنْكِحَ الْمَرْأَةَ بِالثَّوْبِ إِلَى أَجَلٍ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ ‏{‏ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لاَ تُحَرِّمُوا طَيِّبَاتِ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَلاَ تَعْتَدُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ‏}‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: We were on an expedition with Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and we had no women with us. We said: Should we not have ourselves castrated? He (the Holy Prophet) forbade us to do so He then granted us permission that we should contract temporary marriage for a stipulated period giving her a garment, and 'Abdullah then recited this verse: 'Those who believe do not make unlawful the good things which Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Allah does not like trangressers" (al-Qur'an, v)

muslim:3410.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that temporary marriage (*nikāḥ al-mutʿah*) was merely a transitional wartime concession (*rukhṣah*) that Muhammad later permanently abrogated (*mansūkh*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad actively licensed (*rakhkhaṣa lanā*) his soldiers to contract women for a fixed period in exchange for a garment (*an nankiḥa al-marʾata bi-l-thawbi ilā ajal*), proving that he endorsed short-term transactional sex as a morally permissible divine provision. Furthermore, the narration records senior companion ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd reciting a late Medinan verse (Quran 5:87, *lā tuḥarrimū ṭayyibāti mā aḥalla Allāhu lakum*) after Muhammad's death to rebuke those who banned the practice, demonstrating that the Prophet's own inner circle regarded this arrangement as an enduring, God-given 'good thing' (*ṭayyibāt*).

muslim:3410.note: When Muhammad's soldiers lacked women on military campaigns, he granted them permission to marry a woman for a stipulated period in exchange for a single garment (*an nankiḥa al-marʾata bi-l-thawbi ilā ajal*). While Sunni jurisprudence holds that this wartime concession was later abrogated, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud cited [Quran 5:87](quran://5/87) in support of the practice ([Matthew 19:4](bible://mt/19/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنَّا نَغْزُو مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَيْسَ لَنَا نِسَاءٌ فَقُلْنَا أَلاَ نَسْتَخْصِي فَنَهَانَا عَنْ ذَلِكَ ثُمَّ رَخَّصَ لَنَا أَنْ نَنْكِحَ الْمَرْأَةَ بِالثَّوْبِ إِلَى أَجَلٍ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ ‏{‏ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لاَ تُحَرِّمُوا طَيِّبَاتِ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَلاَ تَعْتَدُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ‏}‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: We were on an expedition with Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and we had no women with us. We said: Should we not have ourselves castrated? He (the Holy Prophet) forbade us to do so He then granted us permission that we should contract temporary marriage for a stipulated period giving her a garment, and 'Abdullah then recited this verse: 'Those who believe do not make unlawful the good things which Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Allah does not like trangressers" (al-Qur'an, v)

muslim:3410.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this practice was not sexual exploitation or prostitution, but a legitimate marriage contract with a modest dowry (*mahr*) permitted under military necessity (*ḍarūrah*) to keep soldiers from fornication (*zinā*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that because the fighters had no women with them on campaign (*laysa lanā nisāʾ*) and asked to castrate themselves (*nastakhṣī*), Muhammad authorized them to take a woman for a single piece of clothing for a stipulated expiration period (*an nankiḥa al-marʾata bi-l-thawbi ilā ajal*) strictly as a physical outlet for male lust. Parallel Sahih narrations (muslim:3413, muslim:3419) confirm that these contracts lasted as little as three nights with no ongoing maintenance or inheritance rights, reducing women to disposable instruments of temporary gratification.

muslim:3415.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3415.note: Jabir ibn 'Abdullah testifies that the companions practiced temporary pleasure-marriage (*mutʿah*) during the lifetime of Muhammad, the caliphate of Abu Bakr, and into the rule of 'Umar ([Quran 4:24](quran://4/24), [Matthew 19:4](bible://mt/19/4)). Although neighboring reports state that 'Umar later prohibited the practice (muslim:3416, muslim:3417) and Sunni jurisprudence holds it was abrogated, Jabir's account affirms that temporary marriage for sexual enjoyment (*istimtāʿ*) was practiced with prophetic permission during Muhammad's era (bukhari:5115, muslim:3413).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَدِمَ جَابِرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ مُعْتَمِرًا فَجِئْنَاهُ فِي مَنْزِلِهِ فَسَأَلَهُ الْقَوْمُ عَنْ أَشْيَاءَ ثُمَّ ذَكَرُوا الْمُتْعَةَ فَقَالَ نَعَمِ اسْتَمْتَعْنَا عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَبِي بَكْرٍ وَعُمَرَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: 'Ati' reported that jibir b. Abdullah came to perform 'Umra, and we came to his abode, and the people asked him about different things, and then they made a mention of temporary marriage, whereupon he said: Yes, we had been benefiting ourselves by this temporary marriage during the lifetime of the Prophet (ﷺ) and during the time of Abu Bakr and 'Umar

muslim:3415.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *mutʿah* was only a brief, emergency wartime concession (*ḍarūrah*) for soldiers on distant expeditions and functioned as a regulated marriage rather than transactional prostitution. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *"istamtaʿnā ʿalā ʿahdi Rasūli llāhi... wa-Abī Bakrin wa-ʿUmara"* ("we enjoyed [women in pleasure-marriage] during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr, and 'Umar"), and Jabir's parallel testimony in `muslim:3416` specifies that they contracted it for *"a handful of dates and flour for a few days"* (*al-qabḍatu min al-tamr wa-l-daqīq al-ayyām*), confirming that short-term sex-for-hire was practiced long after Muhammad's military campaigns ended.

muslim:3415.note: Jabir ibn 'Abdullah testifies that Muslims practiced temporary pleasure-marriage (*mutʿah*) during the lifetime of Muhammad, the caliphate of Abu Bakr, and into the rule of 'Umar, who subsequently forbade it himself (muslim:3416, muslim:3417). This directly contradicts rival canonical narrations claiming that Muhammad permanently outlawed *mutʿah* at Khaybar in AD 628 (bukhari:4216) or at the conquest of Mecca in AD 630 (muslim:3420).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَدِمَ جَابِرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ مُعْتَمِرًا فَجِئْنَاهُ فِي مَنْزِلِهِ فَسَأَلَهُ الْقَوْمُ عَنْ أَشْيَاءَ ثُمَّ ذَكَرُوا الْمُتْعَةَ فَقَالَ نَعَمِ اسْتَمْتَعْنَا عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَبِي بَكْرٍ وَعُمَرَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: 'Ati' reported that jibir b. Abdullah came to perform 'Umra, and we came to his abode, and the people asked him about different things, and then they made a mention of temporary marriage, whereupon he said: Yes, we had been benefiting ourselves by this temporary marriage during the lifetime of the Prophet (ﷺ) and during the time of Abu Bakr and 'Umar

muslim:3415.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, following Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*), that Muhammad permanently abolished *mutʿah* at the Conquest of Mecca in AD 630 and that Jabir and a few others simply continued practicing it because news of the prophetic abrogation had not yet reached them (*lam yablughhum al-nāsikh*) until 'Umar publicized it. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in the collective plural *"istamtaʿnā ʿalā ʿahdi Rasūli llāhi... wa-Abī Bakrin wa-ʿUmara"* ("we practiced pleasure-marriage during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr, and 'Umar"), and its immediate sequel (`muslim:3416`) adds *"ḥattā nahā ʿanhā ʿUmaru"* ("until 'Umar forbade it"), proving that an inner-circle Companion present with Muhammad at both Khaybar and Mecca knew of no prophetic ban throughout Abu Bakr's entire caliphate.

muslim:3417.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3417.note: Addressing a dispute between Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr, Jabir ibn Abdullah affirms that the companions practiced temporary marriage (*mutʿah*) with women during Muhammad's lifetime (*maʿa Rasūli Llāh*, i.e., with his sanction) and only stopped when Caliph Umar forbade it. Although Sunni jurisprudence cites adjacent reports (muslim:3418, bukhari:5115) to hold that Muhammad later abrogated the practice, this narration confirms that Muhammad authorized temporary marriage and that senior companions disputed its continued permissibility after his death ([Matthew 19:4](bible://mt/19/4), [1 Corinthians 6:18](bible://1cor/6/18)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ فَأَتَاهُ آتٍ فَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ وَابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ اخْتَلَفَا فِي الْمُتْعَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ جَابِرٌ فَعَلْنَاهُمَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ نَهَانَا عَنْهُمَا عُمَرُ فَلَمْ نَعُدْ لَهُمَا ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: While I was in the company of Jabir b. Abdullah, a person came to him and said that Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Zubair differed on the two types of Mut'as (Tamattu' of Hajj 1846 and Tamattu' with women), whereupon Jabir said: We used to do these two during the lifetime of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ). Umar then forbade us to do them, and so we did not revert to them

muslim:3417.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *mutʿah* (temporary marriage) was merely a brief, transitional concession granted under extreme wartime hardship for soldiers away from their wives before Islamic marital law was fully established. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Companions practiced it alongside Allah's Messenger (*faʿalnāhumā maʿa rasūli llāhi*) and only stopped when Caliph Umar banned it (*thumma nahānā ʿanhumā ʿUmaru falam naʿud lahumā*), while parallel narrations (`muslim:3416`, `muslim:3419`) prove that men continued contracting women for a few days in exchange for a handful of dates or flour throughout the peacetime caliphate of Abu Bakr and that Ibn Abbas still defended its permissibility decades later. By sanctioning time-limited sexual contracts for material compensation and leaving his own Companions divided over whether the practice was lawful or fornication, Muhammad's example directly subverts the permanence and sanctity of marriage.

muslim:3417.note: Jabir ibn Abdullah states that the companions practiced both the *tamattuʿ* of Hajj and temporary marriage (*mutʿah*) with women during Muhammad's lifetime (*maʿa Rasūli Llāh*) and only ceased when Caliph Umar forbade them. While classical commentators attempt to harmonize this report with rival traditions claiming Muhammad himself banned *mutʿah* at Khaybar (bukhari:5115), Awtas (muslim:3418), or Mecca (muslim:3420) by arguing that Jabir remained unaware of the prophetic abrogation, Jabir's testimony here attributes the prohibition to Umar.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ فَأَتَاهُ آتٍ فَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ وَابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ اخْتَلَفَا فِي الْمُتْعَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ جَابِرٌ فَعَلْنَاهُمَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ نَهَانَا عَنْهُمَا عُمَرُ فَلَمْ نَعُدْ لَهُمَا ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: While I was in the company of Jabir b. Abdullah, a person came to him and said that Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Zubair differed on the two types of Mut'as (Tamattu' of Hajj 1846 and Tamattu' with women), whereupon Jabir said: We used to do these two during the lifetime of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ). Umar then forbade us to do them, and so we did not revert to them

muslim:3417.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that *mutʿah* was permitted and abrogated multiple times until Muhammad permanently forbade it before his death, claiming Jabir was simply unaware of the final prophetic ban until Umar publicly enforced it. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that they practiced both forms alongside Allah's Messenger and that it was Umar who subsequently forbade them (*thumma nahānā ʿanhumā ʿUmaru*), which parallel *Ṣaḥīḥ* testimony (`muslim:3416`) confirms by recording that the Companions openly practiced *mutʿah* throughout Muhammad's lifetime, the entire caliphate of Abu Bakr, and into Umar's reign (*ʿalā ʿahdi rasūli llāhi... wa-Abī Bakrin*). This timeline collapses the claim of a known prophetic prohibition and exposes irreconcilable contradictions across the *Ṣaḥīḥ* canon, which variously places the final ban at Khaybar in 628 AD (`bukhari:5115`), the Conquest of Mecca in 630 AD (`muslim:3420`), or Awṭās (`muslim:3418`).

muslim:2947.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:2947.note: Responding to the dispute between Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr over *al-mut'ah*, Jabir ibn Abdullah testifies that the Companions practiced it with Muhammad before Caliph Umar commanded completing Hajj and 'Umra separately and making marriages permanent, threatening to stone any man who marries a woman for an appointed duration (*nikāḥ ilā ajal*, cf. [Quran 4:24](quran://4/24); [Matthew 19:4–6](bible://mt/19/4-6)). Although the English translation inserts an unbracketed interpolation restricting the opening statement to the pilgrimage ritual and Sunni jurisprudence holds that Umar was enforcing Muhammad's later abrogation of temporary marriage (*mut'at al-nisā'*, cf. muslim:3416), Umar's explicit ruling in the Arabic text addresses both pilgrimage *tamattu'* and temporary sexual marriage.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ يَأْمُرُ بِالْمُتْعَةِ وَكَانَ ابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ يَنْهَى عَنْهَا قَالَ فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِجَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ فَقَالَ عَلَى يَدَىَّ دَارَ الْحَدِيثُ تَمَتَّعْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏ فَلَمَّا قَامَ عُمَرُ قَالَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ يُحِلُّ لِرَسُولِهِ مَا شَاءَ بِمَا شَاءَ وَإِنَّ الْقُرْآنَ قَدْ نَزَلَ مَنَازِلَهُ فَأَتِمُّوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ لِلَّهِ كَمَا أَمَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ وَأَبِتُّوا نِكَاحَ هَذِهِ النِّسَاءِ فَلَنْ أُوتَى بِرَجُلٍ نَكَحَ امْرَأَةً إِلَى أَجَلٍ إِلاَّ رَجَمْتُهُ بِالْحِجَارَةِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: (Abu Nadra reported:Ibn 'Abbas commanded the performance of Mut'a putting ihram for 'Umra during the months of Dhul-Hijja and after completing it. then putting on Ihram for Hajj), but Ibn Zubair forbade to do it. I made a mention of it to Jabir b. Abdullih and he said: It is through me that this hadith has been circulated. We entered into the state of Ihram as Tamattu' with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When 'Umar was Installed as Caliph, he said: Verily Allah made permissible for His Messenger (ﷺ) whatever He liked and as Re liked. And (every command) of the Holy Qur'an has been revealed for every occasion. So accomplish Hajj and Umra for Allah as Allah has commanded you; and confirm by (proper conditions) the marriage of those women (with whom you have performed Mut'a). And any person would come to me with a marriage of appointed duration (Mut'a), I would stone him (to death)

muslim:2947.literal_translation: Abu Nadra reported: Ibn 'Abbas used to command al-Mut'ah, while Ibn al-Zubayr used to forbid it. I mentioned that to Jabir b. 'Abdullah and he said: 'It is through me that this hadith has circulated; we practiced mut'ah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When 'Umar rose (as Caliph), he said: Verily Allah used to make permissible for His Messenger whatever He wished by whatever means He wished, and the Qur'an has been revealed in its places. So complete the Hajj and 'Umra for Allah as Allah has commanded you, and make permanent the marriage of these women, for no man who married a woman for an appointed duration will be brought to me except that I will stone him with stones.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: كَانَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ يَأْمُرُ بِالْمُتْعَةِ وَكَانَ ابْنُ الزُّبَيْرِ يَنْهَى عَنْهَا ... تَمَتَّعْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم
translation_issue.published_rendering: Ibn 'Abbas commanded the performance of Mut'a putting ihram for 'Umra during the months of Dhul-Hijja and after completing it. then putting on Ihram for Hajj), but Ibn Zubair forbade to do it. ... We entered into the state of Ihram as Tamattu' with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).
translation_issue.literal_meaning: Ibn 'Abbas used to command al-Mut'ah, while Ibn al-Zubayr used to forbid it. ... We practiced mut'ah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).
translation_issue.explanation: The translator inserts an unbracketed interpolation restricting Ibn 'Abbas's command and Jabir's testimony solely to the pilgrimage ritual (Tamattu'), obscuring that the Arabic term al-mut'ah here encompasses both pilgrimage mut'ah and temporary sexual marriage (mut'at al-nisa') addressed by Umar in the following sentence.

muslim:2947.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that Muhammad permanently abrogated temporary marriage (*mut'at al-nisā'*) before his death and that Caliph 'Umar was merely publicizing an existing prophetic ban, while English translators interpolate the opening lines to restrict *al-mut'ah* to the pilgrimage ritual (*tamattu'*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that 'Umar justified his decree by declaring that 'Allah used to make permissible for His Messenger whatever He wished' (*inna Allāha kāna yuḥillu li-rasūlihi mā shā'a*), before ordering men to 'make permanent the marriage of these women' (*wa-abittū nikāḥa hādhihi al-nisā'*) and threatening to stone anyone who 'married a woman for an appointed duration' (*nakaḥa imra'atan ilā ajal*). Furthermore, in direct parallel narrations (*Sahih Muslim* 3416–3417), Jābir ibn 'Abdullāh confirms that the Companions practiced temporary sexual marriage for a handful of dates or flour throughout the entire lifetime of Muhammad and the caliphate of Abū Bakr until 'Umar personally outlawed it.

muslim:3025.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3025.note: When informed that Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr differed over the two *mutʿahs* (Hajj *Tamattuʿ* and temporary marriage with women, *mutʿat al-nisāʾ*), Jabir ibn Abdullah testifies that the companions practiced both with Muhammad and only stopped after Caliph Umar forbade them ([Quran 4:24](quran://4/24)). Although Sunni jurisprudence holds that Muhammad abrogated temporary marriage before his death (muslim:3422) and that Umar merely enforced an existing ban, this report directly establishes that Muhammad sanctioned the practice during his prophetic ministry ([Matthew 19:4](bible://mt/19/4), [Hebrews 13:4](bible://heb/13/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ فَأَتَاهُ آتٍ فَقَالَ إِنَّ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ وَابْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ اخْتَلَفَا فِي الْمُتْعَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ جَابِرٌ فَعَلْنَاهُمَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ نَهَانَا عَنْهُمَا عُمَرُ فَلَمْ نَعُدْ لَهُمَا
problematic_excerpt.english: While I was in the company of Jibir, a person came and said: There is difference of opinion amomg Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zubair about two Mut'as (benefits, Tamattul in Hajj and temporary marriage with women), whereupon jibir said: We have been doing this during the lifetime of Allah's Messenger (way peace be upon him), and then 'Umar forbade us to do so, and we never resorted to them

muslim:3025.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that temporary pleasure-marriage (*mutʿat al-nisāʾ*) was only a brief emergency concession during military campaigns that Muhammad himself permanently abrogated at Khaybar or the Conquest of Mecca (`muslim:3422`), claiming, as Al-Nawawī argues in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that Jabir was simply unaware of the prophetic ban until Caliph Umar publicized it. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *faʿalnāhumā maʿa rasūli llāhi... thumma nahānā ʿanhumā ʿumaru* ('we practiced both of them with the Messenger of Allah... then Umar forbade us from them'), directly attributing the ban to Umar rather than Muhammad. Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations from Jabir (`muslim:3416`, `bukhari:4518`) confirm that the Companions openly practiced *mutʿah* throughout Muhammad's entire lifetime, Abu Bakr's caliphate, and into Umar's reign, proving that Muhammad died leaving temporary sexual contracts intact.

muslim:3025.note: Addressing the dispute between Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr over the two *mutʿahs* (Hajj *Tamattuʿ* and *mutʿat al-nisāʾ*, temporary marriage with women for a specified term and dower), Jabir ibn Abdullah states that the companions practiced both alongside Muhammad until Caliph Umar prohibited them ([Quran 4:24](quran://4/24)). Even under the Sunni doctrine that Muhammad later abrogated temporary marriage (muslim:3422) before Umar publicized the prohibition, the primary text confirms that temporary marriage was practiced with prophetic approval ([Matthew 19:4](bible://mt/19/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ فَأَتَاهُ آتٍ فَقَالَ إِنَّ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ وَابْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ اخْتَلَفَا فِي الْمُتْعَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ جَابِرٌ فَعَلْنَاهُمَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ نَهَانَا عَنْهُمَا عُمَرُ فَلَمْ نَعُدْ لَهُمَا
problematic_excerpt.english: While I was in the company of Jibir, a person came and said: There is difference of opinion amomg Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zubair about two Mut'as (benefits, Tamattul in Hajj and temporary marriage with women), whereupon jibir said: We have been doing this during the lifetime of Allah's Messenger (way peace be upon him), and then 'Umar forbade us to do so, and we never resorted to them
