muslim:3025.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *mutʿah* was a legitimate, protective marital contract rather than religious prostitution, permitted only under extreme hardship before Islamic law established permanent marriage norms. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly groups the practice under *al-mutʿatayn* ('the two enjoyments/pleasures') practiced alongside Muhammad (*faʿalnāhumā maʿa rasūli llāhi*), and parallel Sahih narrations (`muslim:3416`, `muslim:3417`, `bukhari:5117`) record that Muslim men contracted women for a few days in exchange for 'a handful of dates or flour' (*qabḍatin min tamrin wa-daqīqin*) or a single garment. Grounded in [Quran 4:24](quran://4/24) (*fa-mā stamtaʿtum bihi minhunna fa-ātūhunna ujūrahunna*, 'for what you have enjoyed of them, give them their compensation'), this prophetic practice reduced women to short-term commodities for male sexual gratification without lifelong marital commitment.

muslim:3025.note: Jabir ibn Abdullah states that the companions practiced both *mutʿahs* (temporary marriage and Hajj *Tamattuʿ*) with Muhammad and ceased only when Caliph Umar forbade them, which stands in tension with canonical reports stating that Muhammad himself permanently abolished temporary marriage (bukhari:5115, muslim:3422) and decreed Hajj *Tamattuʿ* valid forever (muslim:2951, muslim:2972). Sunni commentators harmonize these accounts by arguing that companions like Jabir remained unaware of Muhammad's final ban on temporary marriage until Umar enforced it, and that Umar restricted Hajj *Tamattuʿ* through personal juristic reasoning (*ijtihād*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ فَأَتَاهُ آتٍ فَقَالَ إِنَّ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ وَابْنَ الزُّبَيْرِ اخْتَلَفَا فِي الْمُتْعَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ جَابِرٌ فَعَلْنَاهُمَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ نَهَانَا عَنْهُمَا عُمَرُ فَلَمْ نَعُدْ لَهُمَا
problematic_excerpt.english: While I was in the company of Jibir, a person came and said: There is difference of opinion amomg Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zubair about two Mut'as (benefits, Tamattul in Hajj and temporary marriage with women), whereupon jibir said: We have been doing this during the lifetime of Allah's Messenger (way peace be upon him), and then 'Umar forbade us to do so, and we never resorted to them

muslim:3025.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that no contradiction exists in the Sahih corpus because, according to Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, Umar did not legislate against Muhammad's Sunnah on his own authority, but merely enforced Muhammad's prior abrogation of temporary marriage (`bukhari:5115`, `muslim:3422`) and issued an administrative preference regarding Hajj *Tamattuʿ*. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *faʿalnāhumā maʿa rasūli llāhi... thumma nahānā ʿanhumā ʿumaru* ('we practiced both of them with the Messenger of Allah... then Umar forbade us from them'), placing both practices on identical legal footing as prophetic customs terminated solely by Umar's decree. Because canonical Hadith simultaneously claim that Muhammad himself forbade *mutʿat al-nisāʾ* forever (`muslim:3422`) while declaring Hajj *Tamattuʿ* valid 'until the Day of Resurrection' (`muslim:2951`, `muslim:2972`), the Sahih tradition is caught in an irreconcilable contradiction over whether Muhammad or Umar abolished these practices.

muslim:3418.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3418.note: Salama ibn al-Akwaʿ reports that Muhammad granted dispensation (*rakhkhaṣa*) for three-night temporary marriage (*mutʿah*) during the year of the campaign of Awtas (AD 630) before prohibiting it ([Matthew 19:4](bible://mt/19/4), [Hebrews 13:4](bible://heb/13/4)). While Sunni jurisprudence holds that this permission was permanently abrogated (*mansūkh*)—contrasting with Shia Islam's continued allowance and neighboring reports stating the practice persisted until ʿUmar's caliphate (muslim:3416, muslim:3417)—the text explicitly records Muhammad sanctioning three-day marital contracts before reversing the ruling.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: رَخَّصَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَامَ أَوْطَاسٍ فِي الْمُتْعَةِ ثَلاَثًا ثُمَّ نَهَى عَنْهَا ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) gave sanction for contracting temporary marriage for three nights in the year of Autas 1847 and then forbade it

muslim:3418.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that—as Al-Nawawī explains in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—temporary marriage (*mutʿah*) was merely a pre-Islamic custom briefly tolerated under gradual legislation (*tadrīj*) for soldiers enduring hardship away from their wives, and that its final prohibition proves Islam's high view of marital sanctity. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad actively granted a fresh dispensation (`رَخَّصَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ... عَامَ أَوْطَاسٍ فِي الْمُتْعَةِ ثَلاَثًا`) in the Year of Awṭās (AD 630)—two years *after* he had already forbidden it at Khaybar (AD 628, cf. `muslim:3432`)—proving he repeatedly legalized and banned the practice according to military convenience. Furthermore, immediate parallel narrations (`muslim:3419`, `muslim:3420`) confirm that this prophetic license allowed men to contract a woman for just three nights of sexual enjoyment in exchange for a single garment, reducing divine moral law to state-sanctioned, transactional prostitution.

bukhari:5117.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5117.note: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ report that Muhammad came to his troops during a military campaign and declared that they were permitted to contract temporary marriages (*mutʿah*), instructing them to do so ([Matthew 19:4-6](bible://mt/19/4); [Hebrews 13:4](bible://heb/13/4)). While adjacent chapter reports state that Muhammad later prohibited *mutʿah* at Khaybar (bukhari:5115, bukhari:5119) and that Ibn ʿAbbās still permitted it under severe necessity (bukhari:5116), this narration confirms that Muhammad authorized temporary marriage for his soldiers.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنَّا فِي جَيْشٍ فَأَتَانَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ إِنَّهُ قَدْ أُذِنَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَسْتَمْتِعُوا فَاسْتَمْتِعُوا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: While we were in an army, Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) came to us and said, "You have been allowed to do the Mut'a (marriage), so do it

bukhari:5117.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that *nikāḥ al-mutʿah* (temporary marriage) was merely a brief wartime concession for soldiers enduring severe hardship away from home, which Muhammad subsequently and permanently abrogated (*naskh*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad personally approached the troops to announce a divine permission and direct imperative—*"innahu qad udhina lakum an tastamtiʿū fa-stamtiʿū"* (إِنَّهُ قَدْ أُذِنَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَسْتَمْتِعُوا فَاسْتَمْتِعُوا, 'You have been allowed to do *mutʿah*, so do it')—which the immediately following narration (`bukhari:5118`) reveals meant contracting a woman for a few days in exchange for a mere handful of dates or flour. Even on the Sunni claim of later abrogation, a prophet sanctioning short-term, pay-for-pleasure sexual arrangements to appease his army proves that Islamic sexual morality was treated as utilitarian and malleable, while parallel Sahih texts (`bukhari:4518`, `muslim:3415`) expose that Companions like Jābir and Ibn ʿAbbās maintained the practice was never abrogated by Allah but was only outlawed later by Caliph ʿUmar.

bukhari:5118.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5118.note: While on a military campaign, Muhammad came to his soldiers, announced that temporary marriage (*nikāḥ al-mutʿah*) had been permitted for them, and instructed them to practice it—an authorization that Sunni jurisprudence maintains he later abrogated (bukhari:5119; cf. [Hebrews 13:4](bible://heb/13/4); [Matthew 19:4-6](bible://mt/19/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنَّا فِي جَيْشٍ فَأَتَانَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ إِنَّهُ قَدْ أُذِنَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَسْتَمْتِعُوا فَاسْتَمْتِعُوا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: While we were in an army, Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) came to us and said, "You have been allowed to do the Mut'a (marriage), so do it

bukhari:5118.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that temporary marriage (*nikāḥ al-mutʿah*) was merely a brief wartime concession (*rukhṣah*) granted under extreme necessity, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī to claim that Muhammad later permanently abrogated (*naskh*) the practice. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad approached his army and commanded, "Indeed, you have been permitted to enjoy [women temporarily], so enjoy [them]" (*innahu qad udhina lakum an tastamtiʿū fastamtiʿū*), which parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:5075) confirm allowed soldiers to contract a woman for a fixed period in exchange for a mere garment (*thawb*). By sanctioning short-term, transactional sex for material goods before allegedly revoking it—while the immediately preceding narration (bukhari:5117) testifies that no Quranic verse ever prohibited it before Muhammad died—Islam reduces sexual morality to shifting military expediency rather than an unchanging divine standard.

bukhari:5119.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5119.note: Muhammad authorized temporary marriage (*nikāḥ al-mutʿah*) by declaring that an agreeing man and woman have a three-night term of companionship (*ʿishrah*) after which they may either extend the arrangement or separate at will, though Al-Bukhārī appends ʿAlī's report that the Prophet subsequently abrogated (*mansūkh*) the practice ([Hebrews 13:4](bible://heb/13/4); [1 Corinthians 7:2](bible://1cor/7/2)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ أَيُّمَا رَجُلٍ وَامْرَأَةٍ تَوَافَقَا فَعِشْرَةُ مَا بَيْنَهُمَا ثَلاَثُ لَيَالٍ فَإِنْ أَحَبَّا أَنْ يَتَزَايَدَا أَوْ يَتَتَارَكَا تَتَارَكَا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَمَا أَدْرِي أَشَىْءٌ كَانَ لَنَا خَاصَّةً أَمْ لِلنَّاسِ عَامَّةً‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "If a man and a woman agree (to marry temporarily), their marriage should last for three nights, and if they like to continue, they can do so; and if they want to separate, they can do so." I do not know whether that was only for us or for all the people in general.

bukhari:5119.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that temporary marriage (*nikāḥ al-mutʿah*) was merely a transitional wartime concession during early military expeditions that was later permanently abrogated (*mansūkh*), citing Al-Bukhārī's appended editorial note and classical commentaries like Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad himself legislated a three-night sexual arrangement (*fa-ʿishratu mā baynahumā thalāthu layālin*) that couples could extend or dissolve at will (*yatazāyadā aw yatatārakā*), meaning he actively sanctioned as divine law a transactional practice—contracted for as little as a single garment (`bukhari:5117`) or a handful of dates (`muslim:3416`)—that Sunni orthodoxy now condemns as fornication. Furthermore, parallel *Ṣaḥīḥ* narrations (`bukhari:4518`, `muslim:3415`) confirm that senior companions maintained that the Qur'anic verse of *mutʿah* (Surah 4:24) was never abrogated and continued practicing it throughout the lifetimes of Muhammad and Abū Bakr until ʿUmar personally prohibited it.

muslim:3422.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3422.note: Muhammad states that he had previously permitted his followers to derive temporary sexual enjoyment from women (*al-istimtāʿ min al-nisāʾ*)—a license neighboring reports place during the Conquest of Mecca (muslim:3420)—before declaring that Allah has forbidden it until the Day of Resurrection and ordering men to release the women in their possession without reclaiming what they had given them ([Matthew 19:4-6](bible://mt/19/4), [Hebrews 13:4](bible://heb/13/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّهُ، كَانَ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنِّي قَدْ كُنْتُ أَذِنْتُ لَكُمْ فِي الاِسْتِمْتَاعِ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ حَرَّمَ ذَلِكَ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ فَمَنْ كَانَ عِنْدَهُ مِنْهُنَّ شَىْءٌ فَلْيُخَلِّ سَبِيلَهُ وَلاَ تَأْخُذُوا مِمَّا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ شَيْئًا‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Sabra al-Juhani reported on the authority of his father that while he was with Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) he said:O people, I had permitted you to contract temporary marriage with women, but Allah has forbidden it (now) until the Day of Resurrection. So he who has any (woman with this type of marriage contract) he should let her off, and do not take back anything you have given to them (as dower)

muslim:3422.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that temporary marriage (*mutʿah*) was merely a brief wartime concession (*rukhṣah*) under gradual legislation (*tadarruj*) to spare soldiers from hardship before being permanently abrogated. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad personally licensed "deriving sexual enjoyment from women" (*al-istimtāʿ min al-nisāʾ*) for payment and refers to the women held in these contracts with the neuter noun "a thing" (*shayʾ*), while parallel narrations (`muslim:3419`, `muslim:3425`, `muslim:3430`) prove the practice was permitted, forbidden, and re-permitted multiple times, sanctioning paid, short-term sexual transactions.

muslim:3413.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:3413.note: Muhammad's public herald announces to Jabir ibn Abdullah and Salamah ibn al-Akwa that Muhammad has granted them permission to engage in temporary pleasure-marriage (*mutʿat al-nisāʾ*) with women ([Quran 4:24](quran://4/24), [Matthew 19:4](bible://mt/19/4)). Although subsequent reports in this chapter state that Muhammad later prohibited the practice (e.g., muslim:3419)—while muslim:3415 records that companions continued practicing it until Umar banned it—this narration establishes his initial prophetic authorization of temporary sexual contracts.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: خَرَجَ عَلَيْنَا مُنَادِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَدْ أَذِنَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَسْتَمْتِعُوا ‏.‏ يَعْنِي مُتْعَةَ النِّسَاءِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Jabir b. 'Abdullah and Salama b. al-Akwa' said:There came to us the proclaimer of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) has granted you permission to benefit yourselves, i. e. to contract temporary marriage with women

muslim:3413.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that temporary pleasure-marriage (*mutʿat al-nisāʾ*) was merely a brief, transitional concession for soldiers under extreme hardship that Muhammad permanently abrogated at Khaybar or the Conquest of Mecca (as argued in Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad dispatched his official herald to publicly authorize his army "to enjoy yourselves sexually" (*an tastamtiʿū*), proving that an supposedly eternal moral prophet actively sanctioned transactional sex-for-hire to appease his troops. Furthermore, adjacent Sahih Muslim narrations (`muslim:3410`, `muslim:3414`) record the narrator Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh testifying that the companions continued practicing *mutʿah* for a handful of dates throughout Muhammad's entire lifetime and Abū Bakr's caliphate until ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb unilaterally prohibited it.

muslim:3413.note: Muhammad dispatches his herald to publicly grant his followers permission to contract temporary pleasure-marriage (*mutʿat al-nisāʾ*) with women ([Quran 4:24](quran://4/24), [1 Corinthians 6:18](bible://1cor/6/18)). While Sunni jurisprudence holds that Muhammad later abrogated this permission (as recorded in muslim:3419, though complicated by muslim:3415 attributing the ban to Umar and disputed in Shia jurisprudence), this text confirms that he actively sanctioned temporary marriage contracts.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: خَرَجَ عَلَيْنَا مُنَادِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَدْ أَذِنَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَسْتَمْتِعُوا ‏.‏ يَعْنِي مُتْعَةَ النِّسَاءِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Jabir b. 'Abdullah and Salama b. al-Akwa' said:There came to us the proclaimer of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) has granted you permission to benefit yourselves, i. e. to contract temporary marriage with women

muslim:3413.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *mutʿah* was a dignified, consensual marital contract that protected women rather than exploiting them, and that it was gradually phased out just like the prohibition of alcohol. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that men were granted permission "to enjoy yourselves sexually—meaning the pleasure-use of women" (*an tastamtiʿū yaʿnī mutʿata al-nisāʾ*), framing women strictly as instruments of male gratification rather than lifelong covenant partners. Parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:5115`, `muslim:3414`, `muslim:3416`) confirm that soldiers contracted women for as little as a single cloak or a handful of flour for three nights with automatic termination and zero long-term maintenance or inheritance rights, reducing women to disposable sexual commodities.

muslim:4934.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:4934.note: Muhammad regularly enters upon Umm Haram bint Milhan, the wife of 'Ubada ibn al-Samit, where she feeds him, picks lice from his head (*taflī ra'sahu*), and he sleeps in her presence. The published English translation renders *taflī ra'sahu* as "rub his head" and inserts a parenthetical foster-kinship claim that is absent from the Arabic text.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ يَدْخُلُ عَلَى أُمِّ حَرَامٍ بِنْتِ مِلْحَانَ فَتُطْعِمُهُ وَكَانَتْ أُمُّ حَرَامٍ تَحْتَ عُبَادَةَ بْنِ الصَّامِتِ فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَوْمًا فَأَطْعَمَتْهُ ثُمَّ جَلَسَتْ تَفْلِي رَأْسَهُ فَنَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم
problematic_excerpt.english: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to visit Umm Haram daughter of Milhan (who was the sister of his foster-mother or his father's aunt). She was the wife of 'Ubada b. Samit, One day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) paid her a visit. She entertained him with food and then sat down to rub his head. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dozed off

muslim:4934.literal_translation: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to enter upon Umm Haram daughter of Milhan and she would feed him, while Umm Haram was the wife of 'Ubada b. al-Samit. One day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon her, so she fed him and then sat down picking lice from his head, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell asleep.

translation_issue.arabic_term: ثُمَّ جَلَسَتْ تَفْلِي رَأْسَهُ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and then sat down to rub his head
translation_issue.literal_meaning: then she sat down searching his head for lice
translation_issue.explanation: The translator euphemizes 'taflī ra'sahu' ('searching his head for lice' or 'delousing his head') as 'rub his head' and interpolates a parenthetical kinship claim ('who was the sister of his foster-mother or his father's aunt') that is absent from the Arabic text.

muslim:4934.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Umm Haram bint Milhan was an unmarriageable relative—relying on the English translator's parenthetical gloss ('the sister of his foster-mother or his father's aunt')—and that she merely 'rub[bed] his head' during an innocent family visit. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states only that she was the married wife of 'Ubada ibn al-Samit (تَحْتَ عُبَادَةَ بْنِ الصَّامِتِ) with no foster or blood kinship mentioned anywhere in the Arabic matn, and that she sat picking lice from Muhammad's head (ثُمَّ جَلَسَتْ تَفْلِي رَأْسَهُ, taflī ra'sahu) before he fell asleep (فَنَامَ) in her home. The English translator had to insert an unstated parenthetical claim of kinship absent from the Arabic text of muslim:4934 and euphemize taflī ra'sahu as 'rub his head' to conceal that Muhammad had head lice and was being deloused by another man's wife.

muslim:6288.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:6288.note: In Jarir's narration, Aisha states that she used to play with dolls—defined in the Arabic text as toys (*al-luʿab*)—inside Muhammad's house (*fī baytihi*), a clause the published English translation omits by summarizing the report as 'a slight variation of wording' (bukhari:6130, muslim:6287, [Quran 65:4](quran://65/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُلُّهُمْ عَنْ هِشَامٍ، بِهَذَا الإِسْنَادِ وَقَالَ فِي حَدِيثِ جَرِيرٍ كُنْتُ أَلْعَبُ بِالْبَنَاتِ فِي بَيْتِهِ وَهُنَّ اللُّعَبُ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: This hadith has been narrated on the authority of Hisham with the same chain of transmitters with a slight variation of wording

muslim:6288.literal_translation: All of them narrated from Hisham with this chain of transmitters, and he said in the hadith of Jarir: 'I used to play with dolls in his house, and they are toys.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَقَالَ فِي حَدِيثِ جَرِيرٍ كُنْتُ أَلْعَبُ بِالْبَنَاتِ فِي بَيْتِهِ وَهُنَّ اللُّعَبُ
translation_issue.published_rendering: with a slight variation of wording
translation_issue.literal_meaning: And he said in the hadith of Jarir: 'I used to play with dolls in his house, and they are toys'
translation_issue.explanation: The published English translation omits the entire Arabic clause quoting Aisha's statement in Jarir's narration—that she played with dolls (explicitly defined as toys, al-lu'ab) inside Muhammad's house (fi baytihi)—and replaces it with the unattested summary phrase 'with a slight variation of wording.'

muslim:6288.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Aisha was already a mature woman when living with Muhammad, or that the Arabic word *al-banāt* refers to young female companions rather than children's dolls. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in Jarir's narration—omitted by the English summary 'with a slight variation of wording'—*kuntu alʿabu bi-l-banāti fī baytihi wa-hunna al-luʿab* ('I used to play with dolls in his house, and they are toys'), defining *al-banāt* directly as toys (*al-luʿab*) inside his marital home (`bukhari:6130`, `muslim:3481`, `muslim:6287`, [Quran 65:4](quran://65/4)).

muslim:6287.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:6287.note: Aisha reports that she used to play with dolls (*talʿabu bi-l-banāt*) in the presence of Muhammad, and that when her playmates (*ṣawāḥibī*) came to her and withdrew out of shyness from him, he would send them in to her (bukhari:6130; muslim:3481; muslim:6288; see [Quran 65:4](quran://65/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، أَنَّهَا كَانَتْ تَلْعَبُ بِالْبَنَاتِ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَتْ وَكَانَتْ تَأْتِينِي صَوَاحِبِي فَكُنَّ يَنْقَمِعْنَ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَتْ فَكَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُسَرِّبُهُنَّ إِلَىَّ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha reported that she used to play with dolls in the presence of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and when her playmates came to her they left (the house) because they felt shy of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), whereas Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) sent them to her

muslim:6287.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Aisha was already a mature, post-pubescent woman when living with Muhammad, or that this narration merely illustrates his kindness toward his household. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Aisha was playing with dolls (*talʿabu bi-l-banāt*) in Muhammad's home (*ʿinda rasūli llāhi*) while her young playmates (*ṣawāḥibī*) hid from him out of shyness (*yanqamiʿna*), prompting him to send them in to play with her (*yusarribuhunna ilayya*). Alongside parallel Sahih reports (`bukhari:6130`, `muslim:3481`, `muslim:6288`) and the waiting-period legislation for wives who have not yet menstruated ([Quran 65:4](quran://65/4)), the text confirms she was still a child playing with dolls while living as his wife.

muslim:7021.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:7021.note: While accompanying Muhammad as his wife on a military campaign after the revelation of the veil, Aisha states that she was a young girl (*jāriyah ḥadīthat al-sinn*) who had not read much of the Quran, and that camel drivers lifted her empty howdah without noticing her absence because women then ate little and she was a young girl. When Muhammad questions the maidservant Barira about Aisha's conduct, Barira likewise testifies that the only fault she ever saw in her was that she was a young girl (*jāriyah ḥadīthat al-sinn*) who would fall asleep and leave her family's kneaded dough for a domestic animal to eat.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَدَعَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَرِيرَةَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَىْ بَرِيرَةُ هَلْ رَأَيْتِ مِنْ شَىْءٍ يَرِيبُكِ مِنْ عَائِشَةَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ لَهُ بَرِيرَةُ وَالَّذِي بَعَثَكَ بِالْحَقِّ إِنْ رَأَيْتُ عَلَيْهَا أَمْرًا قَطُّ أَغْمِصُهُ عَلَيْهَا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ أَنَّهَا جَارِيَةٌ حَدِيثَةُ السِّنِّ تَنَامُ عَنْ عَجِينِ أَهْلِهَا فَتَأْتِي الدَّاجِنُ فَتَأْكُلُهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: So, Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) called Bailra and said: Barira, did you see anything in 'A'isha which can cause doubt about her? Barira said: By Him Who sent thee with the truth, I have seen nothing objectionable in her but only this much that she is a young girl and she goes to sleep while kneading the flour and the lamb eats that.

muslim:7021.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Aisha was a fully mature woman at the time of her marriage and that women in that environment matured much faster than in modern times. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that even years into the marriage during this military campaign, both Aisha and her maidservant Barira describe her as a young girl of tender age (*jāriyah ḥadīthat al-sinn*) who was light in weight because women had not put on flesh (*lam yaghshahunna al-laḥm*) and who had not read much of the Quran (*lā aqra'u kathīran min al-Qur'ān*). Furthermore, Barira testifies under oath that Aisha's only fault was being a young girl who would fall asleep and leave her family's kneaded dough for the domestic animal to eat (*tanāmu 'an 'ajīni ahlihā fa-ta'tī al-dājinu fa-ta'kuluhu*), confirming her ongoing developmental youth (`bukhari:2661`, `bukhari:4750`).

muslim:7021.note: During a month in which nothing is revealed to him regarding the accusation against Aisha, Muhammad consults Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usama ibn Zaid about separating from his wife, questions the maidservant Barira, and tells Aisha that Allah will exonerate her if she is innocent but that she should confess and repent if she has committed a sin. Before leaving his seat, Muhammad receives the revelation of [Quran 24:11](quran://24/11) and ten verses exonerating her, and when Aisha's mother tells her to rise for him, Aisha refuses and vows to praise only Allah.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا سُرِّيَ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُوَ يَضْحَكُ فَكَانَ أَوَّلَ كَلِمَةٍ تَكَلَّمَ بِهَا أَنْ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَبْشِرِي يَا عَائِشَةُ أَمَّا اللَّهُ فَقَدْ بَرَّأَكِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ لِي أُمِّي قُومِي إِلَيْهِ فَقُلْتُ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أَقُومُ إِلَيْهِ وَلاَ أَحْمَدُ إِلاَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ بَرَاءَتِي - قَالَتْ - فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ‏{‏ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ جَاءُوا بِالإِفْكِ عُصْبَةٌ مِنْكُمْ‏}‏ عَشْرَ آيَاتٍ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ هَؤُلاَءِ الآيَاتِ بَرَاءَتِي
problematic_excerpt.english: When this state of receiving revelation was over, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled and the first words which he spoke to me were that he said: 'A'isha, there is glad tidings for you. Verily, Allah has vindicated your honour, and my mother who had been standing by me said: Get up (and thank him, i. e. the Holy Prophet). I said: By Allah, I shall not thank him and laud him but Allah Who has descended revelation vindicating my honour. She ('A'isha) said: Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, revealed:" 'Verily, those who spread the slander are a gang among you" (and) ten (subsequent) verses in regard to my innocence.

muslim:7021.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the month-long delay in revelation (*wa-qad labitha shahran lā yūḥā ilayhi fī sha'nī bi-shay'*) proves Muhammad could not produce verses at will, claiming he would have exonerated Aisha immediately if the revelation were his own. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that throughout that month Muhammad lacked certainty about her innocence and actively investigated the accusation—consulting Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usama ibn Zaid about separating from his wife (*yastashīruhumā fī firāqi ahlihi*), questioning her maidservant Barira for any suspicious behavior (*hal ra'ayti min shay'in yarībuki min 'Ā'ishah*), and urging Aisha to confess and repent if she had committed a sin (*wa-in kunti almamti bi-dhanbin fa-staghfirī Allāha wa-tūbī ilayhi*). Only after Aisha refused to confess in front of her parents and invoked [Quran 12:18](quran://12/18) did revelation descend on the spot before Muhammad even moved from his seat (*mā rāma Rasūlu Allāhi majlisahu*) to deliver [Quran 24:11](quran://24/11), prompting an alienated Aisha to refuse her mother's command to rise and thank him (`wāllāhi lā aqūmu ilayhi wa-lā aḥmadu illā Allāha`).

muslim:7021.note: When revelation descends upon Muhammad while he is sitting with Aisha and her parents, he is seized by the severe feverish distress (*al-buraḥā'*) that regularly overtook him at the time of revelation, causing sweat to pour from him like pearls on a wintry day from the heaviness of the speech sent down upon him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَوَاللَّهِ مَا رَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَجْلِسَهُ وَلاَ خَرَجَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ أَحَدٌ حَتَّى أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ عَلَى نَبِيِّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَخَذَهُ مَا كَانَ يَأْخُذُهُ مِنَ الْبُرَحَاءِ عِنْدَ الْوَحْىِ حَتَّى إِنَّهُ لَيَتَحَدَّرُ مِنْهُ مِثْلُ الْجُمَانِ مِنَ الْعَرَقِ فِي الْيَوْمِ الشَّاتِ مِنْ ثِقَلِ الْقَوْلِ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: And, by Allah, Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) had not moved an inch from where he had been sitting and none from the members of my family had gone that Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, descended revelation upon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) there and then and he felt the burden which he used to feel at the time of receiving revelation. He began to perspire because of the burden of words of Allah as they descended upon him even during the winter season and there fell the drops of his sweat like silvery beads.

muslim:7021.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's physical reaction during revelation was a calm spiritual concentration reflecting the weighty responsibility of receiving divine words. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that revelation seized him with his habitual feverish agony and paroxysms (*fa-akhadhahu mā kāna ya'khudhuhu min al-buraḥā'i 'inda al-waḥy*) until sweat poured down from him like pearls on a cold winter day (*fī al-yawm al-shāt*) from the heaviness of the speech descending upon him (`bukhari:2661`, `bukhari:4750`). The classical noun *al-buraḥā'* denotes intense feverish distress and physical paroxysm—a detail obscured in the English rendering as merely feeling "the burden."

muslim:6056.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:6056.note: Muhammad habitually enters the house of Umm Sulaim and sleeps on her bed while she is not in it. When she returns and finds his sweat pooled on a piece of leather on her bed, she wipes up the sweat and squeezes it into her scent bottles hoping for its blessing for their children, which Muhammad approves by telling her she has done right.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَدْخُلُ بَيْتَ أُمِّ سُلَيْمٍ فَيَنَامُ عَلَى فِرَاشِهَا وَلَيْسَتْ فِيهِ - قَالَ - فَجَاءَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ فَنَامَ عَلَى فِرَاشِهَا فَأُتِيَتْ فَقِيلَ لَهَا هَذَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَامَ فِي بَيْتِكِ عَلَى فِرَاشِكِ - قَالَ - فَجَاءَتْ وَقَدْ عَرِقَ وَاسْتَنْقَعَ عَرَقُهُ عَلَى قِطْعَةِ أَدِيمٍ عَلَى الْفِرَاشِ فَفَتَحَتْ عَتِيدَتَهَا فَجَعَلَتْ تُنَشِّفُ ذَلِكَ الْعَرَقَ فَتَعْصِرُهُ فِي قَوَارِيرِهَا فَفَزِعَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَا تَصْنَعِينَ يَا أُمَّ سُلَيْمٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ نَرْجُو بَرَكَتَهُ لِصِبْيَانِنَا قَالَ ‏"‏ أَصَبْتِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Anas b. Malik reported that Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) came to the house of Umm Sulaim and slept in her bed while she was away from her house. On the other day too he slept in her bed. She came and it was said to her:It is Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) who is having siesta in your house, lying in your bed. She came and found him sweating and his sweat falling on the leather cloth spread on her bed. She opened her scent-bag and began to fill the bottles with it. Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) was startled and woke up and said: Umm Sulaim, what are you doing? She said: Allah's Messenger, we seek blessings for our children through it. Thereupon he said: You have done something right

muslim:6056.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Umm Sulaim was treated like a close family member and that no impropriety occurred because Muhammad lay down on her bed while she was away from the house. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that he habitually entered her home to sleep on her bed (`yadkhulu bayta Ummi Sulaymin fa-yanāmu ʿalā firāshihā`), and that she returned while he was still sleeping on her bed (`nāma fī baytiki ʿalā firāshiki`), where she wiped up his pooled sweat (`istanqaʿa ʿaraquhu`) and squeezed it into her bottles (`fa-taʿṣiruhu fī qawārīrihā`) with his explicit approval (`aṣabti`). This physical access to the bed of a woman who was not his wife directly contrasts with the strict household entry and seclusion rules imposed on others in [Quran 24:27](quran://24/27) and [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53).

bukhari:5825.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5825.note: Although the woman seeks to leave a second husband who bruised her skin greener than her garment and whom she accuses of impotence, Muhammad rules that she cannot lawfully return to her first husband, Rifa'a, until the second husband 'tastes of her sweetness' (`yadhūqa min 'usaylatiki`), a binding stipulation requiring sexual consummation with the intervening husband ([Quran 2:230](quran://2/230)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَتْ وَاللَّهِ مَا لِي إِلَيْهِ مِنْ ذَنْبٍ، إِلاَّ أَنَّ مَا مَعَهُ لَيْسَ بِأَغْنَى عَنِّي مِنْ هَذِهِ‏.‏ وَأَخَذَتْ هُدْبَةً مِنْ ثَوْبِهَا، فَقَالَ كَذَبَتْ وَاللَّهِ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنِّي لأَنْفُضُهَا نَفْضَ الأَدِيمِ، وَلَكِنَّهَا نَاشِزٌ تُرِيدُ رِفَاعَةَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَإِنْ كَانَ ذَلِكَ لَمْ تَحِلِّي لَهُ ـ أَوْ لَمْ تَصْلُحِي لَهُ ـ حَتَّى يَذُوقَ مِنْ عُسَيْلَتِكِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: She said, "By Allah! I have done no wrong to him but he is impotent and is as useless to me as this," holding and showing the fringe of her garment, `Abdur-Rahman said, "By Allah, O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! She has told a lie! I am very strong and can satisfy her but she is disobedient and wants to go back to Rifa`a." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, to her, "If that is your intention, then know that it is unlawful for you to remarry Rifa`a unless `Abdur-Rahman has had sexual intercourse with you."

bukhari:5825.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the requirement of an intervening marriage in Quran 2:230 was instituted purely as a protective legal deterrent against reckless triple divorces, and that Muhammad employed modest, figurative phrasing (`عُسَيْلَتِكِ`, "your little honey") to explain a clinical legal condition. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad told a visibly battered, unwilling wife (`أَشَدُّ خُضْرَةً مِنْ ثَوْبِهَا`) that she was barred from returning to her first husband "until he tastes of your sweetness" (`حَتَّى يَذُوقَ مِنْ عُسَيْلَتِكِ`). As both Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) establish, this idiom legally mandates actual vaginal penetration of the glans (`تَغْيِيبُ الْحَشَفَةِ فِي الْفَرْجِ`), thereby forcing an abused woman to submit to sexual intercourse with the man who beat her as the price of her marital freedom.

bukhari:5825.note: After a divorced woman who remarried 'Abdur-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr complains to Aisha and shows her skin bruised greener than her green veil, Aisha tells Muhammad that she has never seen any women suffer as much as the believing women ([Quran 4:34](quran://4/34)). Rather than rebuking the husband for the beating, Muhammad hears his counter-claim that his wife is recalcitrant (`nāshiz`) and wishes to return to her first husband.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ وَعَلَيْهَا خِمَارٌ أَخْضَرُ‏.‏ فَشَكَتْ إِلَيْهَا، وَأَرَتْهَا خُضْرَةً بِجِلْدِهَا، فَلَمَّا جَاءَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَالنِّسَاءُ يَنْصُرُ بَعْضُهُنَّ بَعْضًا قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ مَا رَأَيْتُ مِثْلَ مَا يَلْقَى الْمُؤْمِنَاتُ، لَجِلْدُهَا أَشَدُّ خُضْرَةً مِنْ ثَوْبِهَا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: `Aisha said that the lady (came), wearing a green veil (and complained to her (Aisha) of her husband and showed her a green spot on her skin caused by beating). It was the habit of ladies to support each other, so when Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) came, `Aisha said, "I have not seen any woman suffering as much as the believing women. Look! Her skin is greener than her clothes!"

bukhari:5825.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islam strictly forbids domestic abuse and claim the wife in this narration either fabricated her injuries out of bias to return to her ex-husband—citing the narrator's remark that women support one another (`وَالنِّسَاءُ يَنْصُرُ بَعْضُهُنَّ بَعْضًا`)—or represented an isolated transgression condemned by Aisha. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that she physically displayed skin bruised greener than her garment (`وَأَرَتْهَا خُضْرَةً بِجِلْدِهَا`), which Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* confirms resulted from her husband beating her due to her marital recalcitrance (`نَاشِزٌ`) under Quran 4:34. Furthermore, Aisha's sweeping indictment—"I have not seen anything like what the believing women suffer" (`مَا رَأَيْتُ مِثْلَ مَا يَلْقَى الْمُؤْمِنَاتُ`)—proves such battery was systemic among Muslim wives, and Muhammad neither reprimanded nor punished the husband despite his open boast of shaking her like tanned leather (`إِنِّي لأَنْفُضُهَا نَفْضَ الأَدِيمِ`).

bukhari:5825.note: Enforcing [Quran 2:230](quran://2/230), Muhammad rules that a divorced woman is unlawful for her first husband until her intervening second husband has sexually consummated their marriage ('tastes of her sweetness'), directly inverting [Deuteronomy 24:1-4](bible://dt/24/1), which prohibits a first husband from ever remarrying his divorced wife after she has married another man.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَتْ وَاللَّهِ مَا لِي إِلَيْهِ مِنْ ذَنْبٍ، إِلاَّ أَنَّ مَا مَعَهُ لَيْسَ بِأَغْنَى عَنِّي مِنْ هَذِهِ‏.‏ وَأَخَذَتْ هُدْبَةً مِنْ ثَوْبِهَا، فَقَالَ كَذَبَتْ وَاللَّهِ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنِّي لأَنْفُضُهَا نَفْضَ الأَدِيمِ، وَلَكِنَّهَا نَاشِزٌ تُرِيدُ رِفَاعَةَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَإِنْ كَانَ ذَلِكَ لَمْ تَحِلِّي لَهُ ـ أَوْ لَمْ تَصْلُحِي لَهُ ـ حَتَّى يَذُوقَ مِنْ عُسَيْلَتِكِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: She said, "By Allah! I have done no wrong to him but he is impotent and is as useless to me as this," holding and showing the fringe of her garment, `Abdur-Rahman said, "By Allah, O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! She has told a lie! I am very strong and can satisfy her but she is disobedient and wants to go back to Rifa`a." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, to her, "If that is your intention, then know that it is unlawful for you to remarry Rifa`a unless `Abdur-Rahman has had sexual intercourse with you."

bukhari:5825.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Quran 2:230 upholds the sanctity of marriage in continuity with biblical revelation by preventing men from endlessly divorcing and recalling their wives, insisting that Islam forbids pre-arranged sham marriages (*nikāḥ al-taḥlīl*) and only permits remarriage after a genuine second union fails. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that a thrice-divorced woman is unlawful for her first husband until a second man sexually penetrates her (`لَمْ تَحِلِّي لَهُ ... حَتَّى يَذُوقَ مِنْ عُسَيْلَتِكِ`), which Sunni jurists like Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawī confirm makes carnal consummation by an intervening husband the indispensable prerequisite for lawful remarriage. By elevating a second man's sexual penetration into the very mechanism that purifies a woman for her original husband, Muhammad's decree directly inverts Deuteronomy 24:1-4, which declares remarrying an ex-wife after she has been with another man to be a defiling abomination before God.

bukhari:5260.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5260.note: When the irrevocably divorced wife of Rifa'a al-Qurazi complains that her second husband is impotent ('only has like the fringe of a garment'), Muhammad rules that she cannot return to Rifa'a until she and her new husband 'taste each other's sweetness' ([Quran 2:230](quran://2/230)). Classical Sunni jurisprudence upholds this ruling as requiring actual sexual penetration by an intervening husband before a thrice-divorced woman may remarry her first spouse.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: امْرَأَةَ رِفَاعَةَ الْقُرَظِيِّ جَاءَتْ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ رِفَاعَةَ طَلَّقَنِي فَبَتَّ طَلاَقِي، وَإِنِّي نَكَحْتُ بَعْدَهُ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ الزَّبِيرِ الْقُرَظِيَّ، وَإِنَّمَا مَعَهُ مِثْلُ الْهُدْبَةِ‏.‏ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ لَعَلَّكِ تُرِيدِينَ أَنْ تَرْجِعِي إِلَى رِفَاعَةَ، لاَ، حَتَّى يَذُوقَ عُسَيْلَتَكِ وَتَذُوقِي عُسَيْلَتَهُ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The wife of Rifa`a Al-Qurazi came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Rifa`a divorced me irrevocably. After him I married `Abdur-Rahman bin Az-Zubair Al-Qurazi who proved to be impotent." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said to her, "Perhaps you want to return to Rifa`a? Nay (you cannot return to Rifa`a) until you and `Abdur-Rahman consummate your marriage

bukhari:5260.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the requirement of consummating an intervening marriage in Quran 2:230 was instituted as a protective deterrent to stop men from recklessly pronouncing irrevocable divorce, noting that pre-arranged halala marriages are condemned in other hadiths. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad refused to let Rifa'a's former wife return to him unless her impotent second husband physically penetrated her—demanding that "he tastes your sweetness and you taste his sweetness" (ḥattā yadhūqa ʿusaylataki wa-tadhūqī ʿusaylatahu), which Ibn Hajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī in Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim define as the insertion of the glans into the vagina. Instead of punishing the impulsive husband, Muhammad's decree penalizes the woman by making her body the instrument of her ex-husband's penalty, requiring her to endure unwanted sexual intercourse with another man as the sole legal price of reconciling her original marriage.

bukhari:5260.note: Applying [Quran 2:230](quran://2/230), Muhammad rules that Rifa'a's irrevocably divorced wife cannot return to him unless her impotent second husband first sexually consummates their marriage ('tastes your sweetness and you taste his sweetness'). This requirement of an intervening sexual union directly inverts the Torah's law, which forbids a divorced woman from returning to her first husband after marrying another man ([Deuteronomy 24:1-4](bible://dt/24/1)).

After him I married `Abdur-Rahman bin Az-Zubair Al-Qurazi who proved to be impotent." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said to her, "Perhaps you want to return to Rifa`a? Nay (you cannot return to Rifa`a) until you and `Abdur-Rahman consummate your marriage

bukhari:5260.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Quran 2:230 and this ruling represent a compassionate legal reform that abrogates earlier Mosaic restrictions by permitting a divorced couple to eventually reunite if a subsequent marriage genuinely fails. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the woman is barred from returning to Rifa'a "until he [the second husband] tastes your sweetness and you taste his sweetness" (ḥattā yadhūqa ʿusaylataki wa-tadhūqī ʿusaylatahu), making sexual penetration by a second man the mandatory prerequisite for marital reconciliation. This directly inverts the moral law of Deuteronomy 24:1–4—which declares a woman's return to her first husband after being sexually joined to another man an abomination (tōʿēḇāh) that defiles the land—by turning what Scripture condemns as moral defilement into a divine requirement.

bukhari:5261.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5261.note: Muhammad rules that a thrice-divorced woman who marries and is divorced by a second man cannot lawfully remarry her first husband until the second husband "tastes her sweetness"—a metaphor classical commentators define as actual sexual penetration ([Quran 2:230](quran://2/230)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَجُلاً، طَلَّقَ امْرَأَتَهُ ثَلاَثًا، فَتَزَوَّجَتْ فَطَلَّقَ فَسُئِلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَتَحِلُّ لِلأَوَّلِ قَالَ ‏ "‏ لاَ، حَتَّى يَذُوقَ عُسَيْلَتَهَا كَمَا ذَاقَ الأَوَّلُ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A man divorced his wife thrice (by expressing his decision to divorce her thrice), then she married another man who also divorced her. The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked if she could legally marry the first husband (or not). The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, "No, she cannot marry the first husband unless the second husband consummates his marriage with her, just as the first husband had done

bukhari:5261.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the intervening marriage rule in [Quran 2:230](quran://2/230) was designed as a protective deterrent to stop men from recklessly pronouncing triple divorce, claiming that pre-arranged *ḥalālah* marriages are forbidden and that Muhammad's wording is merely a modest idiom. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the woman remains unlawful to her first husband *ḥattā yadhūqa 'usaylatahā* ("until he tastes her sweetness"), which Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* define from parallel narrations (bukhari:2639, bukhari:5260) as requiring the literal insertion of the second man's glans into her vagina—penalizing the wife with mandatory sexual submission to another man for her first husband's rashness.

bukhari:5261.note: Muhammad rules that an irrevocably divorced woman cannot return to her first husband unless an intervening husband marries her and consummates the marriage by "tasting her sweetness" ([Quran 2:230](quran://2/230)), directly inverting the Mosaic law that forbids a divorced wife from ever returning to her first husband after marrying another man ([Deuteronomy 24:1-4](bible://dt/24/1)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَجُلاً، طَلَّقَ امْرَأَتَهُ ثَلاَثًا، فَتَزَوَّجَتْ فَطَلَّقَ فَسُئِلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَتَحِلُّ لِلأَوَّلِ قَالَ ‏ "‏ لاَ، حَتَّى يَذُوقَ عُسَيْلَتَهَا كَمَا ذَاقَ الأَوَّلُ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A man divorced his wife thrice (by expressing his decision to divorce her thrice), then she married another man who also divorced her. The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked if she could legally marry the first husband (or not). The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, "No, she cannot marry the first husband unless the second husband consummates his marriage with her, just as the first husband had done

bukhari:5261.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that [Quran 2:230](quran://2/230) and this prophetic ruling improve upon the Mosaic Law by providing a realistic path for a remorseful couple to reconcile if a genuine second marriage naturally ends, rather than permanently barring them as in [Deuteronomy 24:1-4](bible://dt/24/1). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *lā, ḥattā yadhūqa 'usaylatahā kamā dhāqa al-awwal* ("No, not until he tastes her sweetness just as the first husband tasted it"), making carnal penetration by an intervening man the mandatory legal prerequisite for remarriage and thereby institutionalizing the exact sexual defilement and wife-trading that Biblical law condemns as an abomination before God ([Deuteronomy 24:4](bible://dt/24/4); [Jeremiah 3:1](bible://jer/3/1)).

bukhari:5265.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5265.note: When a divorced woman reports that her second husband was impotent—comparing his organ to the fringe of a garment—and divorced her without achieving intercourse, Muhammad rules she remains unlawful for her first husband until the second husband 'tastes her sweetness and she tastes his sweetness' ([Quran 2:230](quran://2/230)). Classical Sunni jurists confirm this idiom stipulates actual sexual penetration with the intervening husband before an irrevocably divorced woman may remarry her first husband.

She came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said that her new husband did not approach her, and that he was completely impotent. The Prophet (ﷺ) said (to her), "No (you cannot remarry your first husband) till you taste the second husband and he tastes you (i.e. till he consummates his marriage with you)

bukhari:5317.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the requirement of an intervening marriage (Quran 2:230) was instituted purely as a noble legal deterrent to stop men from impulsively pronouncing triple divorce, and that Muhammad forbade pre-arranged halala schemes. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "lā ḥattā tadhūqī ʿusaylatahu wa yadhūqa ʿusaylataki" ("No, not until you taste his sweetness and he tastes your sweetness"), while parallel narrations (bukhari:2639, 5260) record Muhammad smiling at her predicament after she complained that her new husband's penis was flaccid "like the fringe of a garment" ("mithlu hudbah"). As both Ibn Hajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī in Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim confirm, this ruling makes physical vaginal penetration by a second man the mandatory prerequisite for reconciliation, penalizing the woman for her first husband's divorce by requiring her to be sexually used by another man.

bukhari:5317.note: Specifying [Quran 2:230](quran://2/230), Muhammad rules that a divorced woman cannot return to her first husband until she and her second husband consummate their marriage by 'tasting each other's sweetness,' requiring as a prerequisite for reconciliation the very intervening marital union that [Deuteronomy 24:1-4](bible://dt/24/1) declares permanently bars a woman from returning to her former husband.

However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "lā ḥattā tadhūqī ʿusaylatahu wa yadhūqa ʿusaylataki" ("No, not until you taste his sweetness and he tastes your sweetness"), establishing actual sexual intercourse with an intervening husband as the non-negotiable condition to make the woman lawful again for her first husband. bukhari:5792.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
bukhari:5792.note: When the irrevocably divorced wife of Rifa'a al-Qurazi complains that her new husband is impotent, Muhammad smiles and rules that she cannot return to Rifa'a until she and her second husband "taste each other's sweetness" ([Quran 2:230](quran://2/230))—an idiom classical commentators (Ibn Hajar, Al-Nawawi) define as actual vaginal penetration.

problematic_excerpt.english: The wife of Rifa`a Al-Qurazi came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) while I was sitting, and Abu Bakr was also there. She said, 'O Allah's Apostle! I was the wife of Rifa`a and he divorced me irrevocably. Then I married `AbdurRahman bin Az-Zubair who, by Allah, O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), has only something like a fringe of a garment, Showing the fringe of her veil. Khalid bin Sa`id, who was standing at the door, for he had not been admitted, heard her statement and said, "O Abu Bakr! Why do you not stop this lady from saying such things openly before Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)?" No, by Allah, Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) did nothing but smiled. Then he said to the lady, "Perhaps you want to return to Rifa`a? That is impossible unless `Abdur-Rahman consummates his marriage with you." That became the tradition after him

bukhari:5792.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad used a polite, modest metaphor ('tasting sweetness') to deter men from rashly pronouncing triple divorce and to protect women's marital dignity. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that when Rifa'a's former wife complained of her new husband's impotence (`مَا مَعَهُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِلَّا مِثْلُ هَذِهِ الْهُدْبَةِ` — 'what he has is only like this fringe'), Muhammad merely smiled (`مَا يَزِيدُ ... عَلَى التَّبَسُّمِ`) and refused to let her leave the loveless marriage until she underwent physical sexual intercourse: `حَتَّى يَذُوقَ عُسَيْلَتَكِ وَتَذُوقِي عُسَيْلَتَهُ` ('until he tastes your sweetness and you taste his sweetness'). As Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) and Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) confirm, this ruling established the permanent Sunni legal precedent (`فَصَارَ سُنَّةً بَعْدُ`) that an irrevocably divorced woman must experience actual vaginal penetration (*taghyīb al-ḥashafah*) by another man to pay for her first husband's impulsive divorce.

bukhari:5792.note: Whereas biblical law forbids a divorced woman from returning to her first husband after marrying another man as an abomination ([Deuteronomy 24:1-4](bible://dt/24/1)), Muhammad establishes as binding sunnah that an irrevocably divorced woman cannot return to her first husband until her second husband consummates the marriage by "tasting her sweetness" ([Quran 2:230](quran://2/230)). Sunni consensus (ijma') cited by Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawi upholds this requirement of actual sexual penetration by an intervening husband as mandatory law.

bukhari:6084.note: When a thrice-divorced woman complains that her subsequent husband possesses nothing with him except like the fringe of her garment, Muhammad smiles and rules that she cannot return to her first husband until she and her second husband "taste each other's sweetness" through sexual consummation ([Quran 2:230](quran://2/230)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رِفَاعَةَ، الْقُرَظِيَّ طَلَّقَ امْرَأَتَهُ فَبَتَّ طَلاَقَهَا، فَتَزَوَّجَهَا بَعْدَهُ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ الزَّبِيرِ، فَجَاءَتِ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ عِنْدَ رِفَاعَةَ فَطَلَّقَهَا آخِرَ ثَلاَثِ تَطْلِيقَاتٍ، فَتَزَوَّجَهَا بَعْدَهُ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ الزَّبِيرِ، وَإِنَّهُ وَاللَّهِ مَا مَعَهُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِلاَّ مِثْلُ هَذِهِ الْهُدْبَةِ، لِهُدْبَةٍ أَخَذَتْهَا مِنْ جِلْبَابِهَا‏.‏ قَالَ وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ جَالِسٌ عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَابْنُ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْعَاصِ جَالِسٌ بِبَابِ الْحُجْرَةِ لِيُؤْذَنَ لَهُ، فَطَفِقَ خَالِدٌ يُنَادِي أَبَا بَكْرٍ، يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ أَلاَ تَزْجُرُ هَذِهِ عَمَّا تَجْهَرُ بِهِ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَمَا يَزِيدُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى التَّبَسُّمِ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏ "‏ لَعَلَّكِ تُرِيدِينَ أَنْ تَرْجِعِي إِلَى رِفَاعَةَ، لاَ، حَتَّى تَذُوقِي عُسَيْلَتَهُ، وَيَذُوقَ عُسَيْلَتَكِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Rifa`a Al-Qurazi divorced his wife irrevocably (i.e. that divorce was the final). Later on `Abdur- Rahman bin Az-Zubair married her after him. She came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! I was Rifa`a's wife and he divorced me thrice, and then I was married to `Abdur-Rahman bin Az-Zubair, who, by Allah has nothing with him except something like this fringe, O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)," showing a fringe she had taken from her covering sheet. Abu Bakr was sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ) while Khalid Ibn Sa`id bin Al-As was sitting at the gate of the room waiting for admission. Khalid started calling Abu Bakr, "O Abu Bakr! Why don't you reprove this lady from what she is openly saying before Allah's Apostle?" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) did nothing except smiling, and then said (to the lady), "Perhaps you want to go back to Rifa`a? No, (it is not possible), unless and until you enjoy the sexual relation with him (`Abdur Rahman), and he enjoys the sexual relation with you

bukhari:6084.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this ruling on Quran 2:230 was instituted as a protective deterrent against reckless triple divorces, and they cite Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī to claim that Muhammad used a polite metaphor ('little honey') out of prophetic modesty. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that while Khalid bin Sa'id demanded the woman be rebuked for her graphic complaint, Muhammad merely smiled (wa-mā yazīdu... ʿalā al-tabassumi) and declared she could not return to her husband 'until you taste his sweetness and he tastes your sweetness' (ḥattā tadhūqī ʿusaylatahu wa-yadhūqa ʿusaylataki). As Al-Nawawī and Ibn Hajar confirm, this bedchamber idiom legally mandates actual vaginal penetration (īlāj al-ḥashafah) by the second husband, forcing the woman to submit to intercourse with another man to pay for her first husband's rash divorce.

bukhari:6084.note: Muhammad rules that a thrice-divorced woman cannot lawfully return to her first husband until an intervening husband marries her and consummates the marriage by "tasting her sweetness" ([Quran 2:230](quran://2/230)). This mandate reverses Torah law, which prohibits a divorced woman from ever returning to her first husband after marrying another man and declares such a remarriage an abomination ([Deuteronomy 24:1-4](bible://dt/24/1)).

bukhari:6084.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Quran 2:230 improves upon earlier biblical law by allowing a divorced couple a conditional path back to marriage while preventing men from abusing women through endless cycles of divorce. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that reconciliation is unlawful 'until you taste his sweetness and he tastes your sweetness' (ḥattā tadhūqī ʿusaylatahu wa-yadhūqa ʿusaylataki), directly inverting Deuteronomy 24:1–4 by taking the exact intervening sexual union that Yahweh condemns as a defiling abomination and making it a mandatory divine prerequisite. Rather than protecting Rifa'a's former wife, Muhammad's decree traps her in a marriage to an impotent man and requires her to be sexually penetrated by him before she can ever lawfully return to her first spouse.

muslim:679.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:679.note: Aisha reports that whenever one of Muhammad's wives was menstruating, he would command her to tie on a waist-wrapper (*izār*) and then engage in direct skin-to-skin sexual fondling (*yubāshiruhā*) with her above the wrapper (bukhari:300, [Quran 2:222](quran://2/222), [Leviticus 18:19](bible://lv/18/19)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ كَانَ إِحْدَانَا إِذَا كَانَتْ حَائِضًا أَمَرَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَتَأْتَزِرُ بِإِزَارٍ ثُمَّ يُبَاشِرُهَا ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha reported:When anyone amongst us (amongst the wives of the Holy Prophet) menstruated, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked her to tie a waist-wrapper over her (body) and then embraced her

muslim:679.literal_translation: Aisha reported: When one of us was menstruating, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would order her to tie on a waist-wrapper, and then he would fondle her (engage in direct skin-to-skin sexual contact with her).

translation_issue.arabic_term: ثُمَّ يُبَاشِرُهَا
translation_issue.published_rendering: and then embraced her
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and then he would fondle her / engage in direct skin-to-skin sexual contact with her
translation_issue.explanation: Derived from 'basharah' (outer skin), the Form III verb 'yubāshiruhā' ('mubāsharah') denotes direct skin-to-skin sexual contact, fondling, or lying together naked above the waist-wrapper—not a mere hug or embrace ('mu'ānaqah'). Rendering it as 'embraced her' euphemistically softens intimate sexual fondling during menstruation into an ordinary embrace.

muslim:679.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—that this narration merely shows Muhammad's compassionate rejection of the custom of isolating menstruating women by offering affectionate 'embraces' while honoring [Quran 2:222](quran://2/222). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *yubāshiruhā* (يُبَاشِرُهَا, direct skin-to-skin sexual fondling rather than a platonic embrace), which clashes with [Quran 2:222](quran://2/222)'s explicit command to 'keep away from women during menstruation' (*faʿtazilū al-nisāʾa fī al-maḥīḍi*). Furthermore, the immediate parallel in muslim:680 specifies that he ordered his wives to do this during the heaviest onset of menstrual bleeding (*fī fawrati al-ḥayḍati*), proving this was about satisfying urgent sexual desire rather than emotional comfort.

muslim:680.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:680.note: Aisha recounts that when one of Muhammad's wives was menstruating, he would command her to tie on a waist-wrapper (*taʾtazira*) at the initial peak of her menstrual flow (*fī fawri ḥayḍatihā*) and then engage in direct skin-to-skin sexual fondling with her (*yubāshiruhā*), adding that none of her listeners could control his sexual member or desire (*irbahū*) as Muhammad could (bukhari:302; cf. [Quran 2:222](quran://2/222), [Leviticus 18:19](bible://lv/18/19)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ كَانَ إِحْدَانَا إِذَا كَانَتْ حَائِضًا أَمَرَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ تَأْتَزِرَ فِي فَوْرِ حَيْضَتِهَا ثُمَّ يُبَاشِرُهَا ‏.‏ قَالَتْ وَأَيُّكُمْ يَمْلِكُ إِرْبَهُ كَمَا كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَمْلِكُ إِرْبَهُ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha reported:When anyone amongst us was menstruating the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked her to tie waist-wrapper daring the time when the menstrual blood profusely flowed and then embraced her; and she ('A'isha) observed: And who amongst you can have control over his desires as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had over his desires

muslim:680.literal_translation: Aisha reported: When one of us was menstruating, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would order her to tie on a waist-wrapper at the height of her menstrual flow, and then he would fondle her (engage in direct skin-to-skin sexual contact with her). She said: 'And which of you can control his sexual desire/member (irbahū) as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to control his sexual desire/member?'

translation_issue.arabic_term: ثُمَّ يُبَاشِرُهَا
translation_issue.published_rendering: and then embraced her
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and then he would fondle her / engage in direct skin-to-skin sexual contact with her
translation_issue.explanation: The translator renders 'yubāshiruhā' (Form III of b-sh-r, 'mubāsharah', derived from 'basharah' [skin], denoting direct skin-to-skin sexual contact or fondling short of vaginal penetration) as 'embraced her,' softening the explicit sexual contact during the peak flow of menstruation into a benign-sounding hug.

muslim:680.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration highlights Muhammad's progressive compassion in rejecting ancient taboos that isolated menstruating women, claiming he merely offered affectionate companionship while exercising supreme self-restraint (*yamliku irbahū*) to obey [Quran 2:222](quran://2/222). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that he commanded his wives to tie a waist-wrapper during the heaviest gush of their menstrual blood (*fī fawri ḥayḍatihā*) specifically to engage in *mubāsharah* (*yubāshiruhā*—direct skin-to-skin sexual fondling rather than a platonic 'embrace'), aligning with his ruling in muslim:682 to 'do everything except actual sexual intercourse (*iṣnaʿū kulla shayʾin illā an-nikāḥ*)' with a menstruating woman. Furthermore, as Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) document, *irbahū* literally denotes his sexual need or male member (*ʿuḍwahū*), meaning Aisha herself had to warn other men that imitating Muhammad's bedroom conduct during peak menstruation would cause them to lose control and violate the prohibition of intercourse.

muslim:681.subcategory: Sexual Ethics, Child Marriage & Bedroom Conduct
muslim:681.note: Maymuna reports that Muhammad used to fondle and engage in direct skin-to-skin sexual intimacy (*yubāshiru*) with his wives above a waist-wrapper (*izār*) while they were menstruating (cf. [Quran 2:222](quran://2/222); bukhari:302; muslim:679).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ مَيْمُونَةَ، قَالَتْ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُبَاشِرُ نِسَاءَهُ فَوْقَ الإِزَارِ وَهُنَّ حُيَّضٌ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Maimuna (the wife of the Holy Prophet) reported:The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) contacted and embraced his wives over the waist-wrapper when they were menstruating

muslim:681.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration (as explained in Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) merely demonstrates Muhammad's progressive compassion toward menstruating women in contrast to strict Jewish purity laws, claiming he only showed gentle affection while honoring the prohibition of intercourse in [Quran 2:222](quran://2/222). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *yubāshiru nisāʾahu fawqa al-izār* (يُبَاشِرُ نِسَاءَهُ فَوْقَ الإِزَارِ)—meaning direct skin-to-skin sexual fondling over a waist-wrapper—which parallel Sahih narrations (muslim:682, bukhari:302) confirm was a method to gratify his sexual urges (*irbihi*) with everything short of vaginal penetration (*illā al-nikāḥ*).

muslim:3631.note: Expressing jealousy over the women who offered themselves to Muhammad, Aisha questioned how a woman could give herself away. When [Quran 33:51](quran://33/51) was revealed permitting him to defer or receive whichever of them he wished, she told him that she saw his Lord only hastening to fulfill his desire.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنْتُ أَغَارُ عَلَى اللاَّتِي وَهَبْنَ أَنْفُسَهُنَّ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَقُولُ وَتَهَبُ الْمَرْأَةُ نَفْسَهَا فَلَمَّا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ‏{‏ تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ وَتُؤْوِي إِلَيْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَمَنِ ابْتَغَيْتَ مِمَّنْ عَزَلْتَ‏}‏ قَالَتْ قُلْتُ وَاللَّهِ مَا أَرَى رَبَّكَ إِلاَّ يُسَارِعُ لَكَ فِي هَوَاكَ
problematic_excerpt.english: I felt jealous of the women who offered themselves to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said: Then when Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, revealed this:" You may defer any one of them you wish, and take to yourself any you wish; and if you desire any you have set aside (no sin is chargeable to you)" (xxxiii. 51), I ('A'isha.) said: It seems to me that your Lord hastens to satisfy your desire

muslim:3631.literal_translation: I used to feel jealous of the women who offered themselves to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), and I would say: 'Does a woman offer herself?!' Then when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {You may defer whom you will of them and take to yourself whom you will, and whomever you desire of those you had set aside} ([Quran 33:51](quran://33/51)), she said: I said: 'By Allah, I do not see your Lord except hastening for you in your desire!'

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَأَقُولُ وَتَهَبُ الْمَرْأَةُ نَفْسَهَا ... قُلْتُ وَاللَّهِ مَا أَرَى رَبَّكَ إِلاَّ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and said: Then when Allah ... I ('A'isha.) said: It seems to me that your Lord
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and I would say: 'Does a woman offer herself?!' Then when Allah ... I said: 'By Allah, I do not see your Lord except
translation_issue.explanation: The published translation completely omits Aisha's indignant question ('wa-tahabu al-mar'atu nafsahā' — 'Does a woman offer herself?!') after the dangling 'and said:', as well as her explicit oath ('wa-Allāhi' — 'By Allah') before her concluding remark.

muslim:3631.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Aisha's remark was an expression of praise or light marital teasing about how Allah honored and pleased His Prophet, rather than a critique of convenient revelations. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that she spoke out of jealousy (كُنْتُ أَغَارُ) over women offering themselves to him and protested, 'Does a woman offer herself?!' (وَتَهَبُ الْمَرْأَةُ نَفْسَهَا)—a clause omitted from the published English translation—before swearing by Allah (وَاللَّهِ) upon the revelation of [Quran 33:51](quran://33/51) that she sees his Lord only hastening to fulfill his personal desire (فِي هَوَاكَ).

bukhari:4782.note: Abdullah ibn Umar reports that the companions exclusively called Zaid bin Haritha 'Zaid bin Muhammad' until the revelation of [Quran 33:5](quran://33/5) commanded that adopted sons be named after their biological fathers. This abolition of adoptive lineage is linked later in the same chapter ([Quran 33:37](quran://33/37); bukhari:4787) to permitting Muhammad's marriage to Zaid's divorced wife, Zaynab.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ زَيْدَ بْنَ حَارِثَةَ، مَوْلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَا كُنَّا نَدْعُوهُ إِلاَّ زَيْدَ ابْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ حَتَّى نَزَلَ الْقُرْآنُ ‏{‏ادْعُوهُمْ لآبَائِهِمْ هُوَ أَقْسَطُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: We used not to call Zaid bin Haritha the freed slave of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) except Zaid bin Muhammad till the Qur'anic Verse was revealed: "Call them (adopted sons) by (the names of) their fathers. That is more than just in the Sight of Allah

bukhari:4782.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the abolition of legal adoption (al-tabannī) in Surah 33:5—as explained in Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī—was an objective social reform meant to preserve biological lineage (nasab) and inheritance rights rather than a self-serving measure for Muhammad. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the community universally recognized Zaid as Muhammad's own son (مَا كُنَّا نَدْعُوهُ إِلاَّ زَيْدَ ابْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ — 'We used not to call him except Zaid bin Muhammad') until this verse abruptly stripped his filial status, a legal reversal that Surah 33:37 and parallel narrations (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4787; Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:3503) directly tie to legitimizing Muhammad's marriage to Zaid's wife, Zaynab bint Jahsh, after Muhammad concealed his desire for her in his heart (وَتُخْفِي فِي نَفْسِكَ مَا اللَّهُ مُبْدِيهِ). Rather than simply regulating inheritance while keeping adoptive family bonds intact, this convenient revelation permanently deprived orphans of full legal filiation solely to dissolve the incest taboo obstructing Muhammad's personal marriage.

bukhari:2831.note: When [Quran 4:95](quran://4/95) is initially revealed and written down by Zayd ibn Thabit on a shoulder-blade without an exemption, Ibn Umm Maktum complains about his blindness, whereupon the verse is immediately revealed again with the added clause 'except those who are disabled' (`ghayru uli al-darar`; cf. bukhari:2832).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَشَكَا ابْنُ أُمِّ مَكْتُومٍ ضَرَارَتَهُ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لاَ يَسْتَوِي الْقَاعِدُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ ‏}‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Ibn Um-Maktum complained about his blindness and on that the following revelation came: "Not equal are those believers who sit (at home) except those who are disabled

bukhari:2831.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, following Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī, that this delayed exemption was not an oversight corrected by human complaint, but deliberate gradual legislation (tadrīj) designed to test the sincerity of the believers before granting relief to the disabled. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad had already summoned Zayd ibn Thābit and had the absolute, unqualified verse written down on a shoulder-blade (fajā'a bi-katifin fa-katabahā), and that the exception (ghayru ulī al-ḍarar) was only revealed as an immediate causal reaction (fa-nazalat) after Ibn Umm Maktūm complained about his blindness (wa-shakā Ibn Umm Maktūm ḍarāratahu). An eternal, uncreated scripture preserved on a heavenly tablet (Quran 85:22) would not be dictated into finalized written form with a glaring omission, only to be patched seconds later in real time (cf. bukhari:2832, 4593) because a blind bystander pointed out the oversight.

muslim:3611.note: When Muslim soldiers hesitated to have sexual intercourse with married women captured at Awtas (AD 630), [Quran 4:24](quran://4/24) was sent down in direct response to their fear (takhawwuf), authorizing sexual access to married captives as 'those whom your right hands possess' (cf. muslim:3608, muslim:3609).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَصَابُوا سَبْيًا يَوْمَ أَوْطَاسٍ لَهُنَّ أَزْوَاجٌ فَتَخَوَّفُوا فَأُنْزِلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ ‏{‏ وَالْمُحْصَنَاتُ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ إِلاَّ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ‏}‏
problematic_excerpt.english: They took captives (women) on the day of Autas who had their husbands. They were afraid (to have sexual intercourse with them) when this verse was revealed:" And women already married except those whom you right hands posses" (iv)

muslim:3611.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the revelation of Quran 4:24 after the Battle of Awtas (AD 630) was an objective divine legislation meant to clarify the legal status of war captives rather than an opportunistic concession to the desires of Muhammad's soldiers. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states via the direct causal sequence (fa-takhawwafū fa-unzilat hādhihi al-āyah) that the verse was revealed specifically because the troops were afraid to sleep with married captives (sabyan... lahunna azwāj), immediately granting them the exact sexual license they craved. Instead of upholding the moral prohibition against violating married women (wal-muḥṣanātu mina al-nisā'), the revelation conveniently carved out a military exemption (illā mā malakat aymānukum) to reward Muhammad's army with sexual access to their enemies' wives.

muslim:3611.note: After Muslim forces captured married women on the Day of Awtas (AD 630) and feared having sexual intercourse with them because they had living husbands, [Quran 4:24](quran://4/24) was revealed to exempt enslaved female captives from the prohibition on married women ([Deuteronomy 21:10](bible://dt/21/10), [Exodus 20:14](bible://ex/20/14)). Classical commentators such as al-Nawawi affirm this incident as the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) establishing the legal ruling that capture annuls a captive woman's existing marriage and renders her sexually lawful to her captor.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَصَابُوا سَبْيًا يَوْمَ أَوْطَاسٍ لَهُنَّ أَزْوَاجٌ فَتَخَوَّفُوا فَأُنْزِلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ ‏{‏ وَالْمُحْصَنَاتُ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ إِلاَّ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ‏}‏
problematic_excerpt.english: They took captives (women) on the day of Autas who had their husbands. They were afraid (to have sexual intercourse with them) when this verse was revealed:" And women already married except those whom you right hands posses" (iv)

muslim:3611.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Quran 4:24 merely regulated ancient warfare by legally dissolving prior pagan marriages upon capture (saby) and requiring a waiting period (istibrā') or formal marriage before any relations occurred. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that these women had living husbands (lahunna azwāj) and that the exception 'except what your right hands possess' (illā mā malakat aymānukum) was revealed specifically to remove the soldiers' hesitation (fa-takhawwafū) and permit sexual intercourse with them as enslaved concubines rather than wives. Parallel narrations in Sahih Muslim (muslim:3608) further confirm that the troops used this verse to legitimate sleeping with these married captives at Awtas (AD 630) without their consent while their husbands were still alive.

muslim:3502.note: After two guests lingered in conversation inside Muhammad's house following his wedding feast with Zaynab, Muhammad drew a curtain between himself and Anas ibn Malik upon their departure, and Allah revealed [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53) forbidding believers from entering the Prophet's houses without permission or staying to talk after a meal.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ الْبَابَ إِذَا هُوَ بِالرَّجُلَيْنِ قَدِ اسْتَأْنَسَ بِهِمَا الْحَدِيثُ فَلَمَّا رَأَيَاهُ قَدْ رَجَعَ قَامَا فَخَرَجَا فَوَاللَّهِ مَا أَدْرِي أَنَا أَخْبَرْتُهُ أَمْ أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ الْوَحْىُ بِأَنَّهُمَا قَدْ خَرَجَا فَرَجَعَ وَرَجَعْتُ مَعَهُ فَلَمَّا وَضَعَ رِجْلَهُ فِي أُسْكُفَّةِ الْبَابِ أَرْخَى الْحِجَابَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى هَذِهِ الآيَةَ ‏{‏ لاَ تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ‏}‏ الآيَةَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: And as he reached the door, (he found) that the two men were still busy in talking. And when they saw him having returned, they stood up and went out; and by Allah! I do not know whether I had informed him, or there was a revelation to him (to the affect) that they had gone. He (the Holy Prophet) then came back and I also returned along with him, and as he put his step on the threshold of his door he hung a curtain between me and him, and (it was on this occasion) that Allah revealed this verse: (" O you who believe), do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to 'you" (xxxiii)

muslim:3502.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar—that [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53) was revealed to establish universal household etiquette (*ādāb al-isti'dhān*) for the Muslim community, and that Allah intervened only because Muhammad's extraordinary modesty (*ḥayā'*) prevented him from asking his guests to leave. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that this eternal scripture was triggered on the exact spot when two men lingered in conversation (`اسْتَأْنَسَ بِهِمَا الْحَدِيثُ`) while Muhammad was waiting to consummate his marriage with Zaynab, prompting him to drop the curtain (`أَرْخَى الْحِجَابَ`) and immediately receive a verse (`لاَ تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ`) functioning as his personal domestic bouncer. Using the supposedly uncreated speech of God to clear out dinner guests—while the very same verse simultaneously bans anyone from ever marrying Muhammad's widows—exemplifies why Aisha famously remarked in bukhari:4788, 'I see that your Lord hastens in fulfilling your desires.'
