muslim:5668.note: After the Hijab had been imposed on her, Sawda went out to relieve her need—which the narrator Hisham clarifies meant defecation (*al-barāz*), a clause omitted from the published English translation—and Umar ibn al-Khattab recognized her large stature and warned her to watch how she went out because she was not hidden from them. When she returned and reported Umar's words to Muhammad while he was eating supper in Aisha's house, revelation came to him and was lifted while the meat-bone (*al-'arq*) remained in his hand without being set down, declaring that the women were permitted to go out for their needs.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: خَرَجَتْ سَوْدَةُ بَعْدَ مَا ضُرِبَ عَلَيْهَا الْحِجَابُ لِتَقْضِيَ حَاجَتَهَا وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَةً جَسِيمَةً تَفْرَعُ النِّسَاءَ جِسْمًا لاَ تَخْفَى عَلَى مَنْ يَعْرِفُهَا فَرَآهَا عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ فَقَالَ يَا سَوْدَةُ وَاللَّهِ مَا تَخْفَيْنَ عَلَيْنَا فَانْظُرِي كَيْفَ تَخْرُجِينَ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ فَانْكَفَأَتْ رَاجِعَةً وَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي بَيْتِي وَإِنَّهُ لَيَتَعَشَّى وَفِي يَدِهِ عَرْقٌ فَدَخَلَتْ فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي خَرَجْتُ فَقَالَ لِي عُمَرُ كَذَا وَكَذَا ‏.‏ قَالَتْ فَأُوحِيَ إِلَيْهِ ثُمَّ رُفِعَ عَنْهُ وَإِنَّ الْعَرْقَ فِي يَدِهِ مَا وَضَعَهُ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ إِنَّهُ قَدْ أُذِنَ لَكُنَّ أَنْ تَخْرُجْنَ لِحَاجَتِكُنَّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَفِي رِوَايَةِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ يَفْرَعُ النِّسَاءَ جِسْمُهَا ‏.‏ زَادَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ فِي حَدِيثِهِ فَقَالَ هِشَامٌ يَعْنِي الْبَرَازَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha reported that Sauda (Allah he pleated with her) went out (in the fields) in order to answer the call of nature even after the time when veil had been prescribed for women. She had been a bulky lady, significant in height amongst the women, and she could not conceal herself from him who had known her. 'Umar b. Khattab saw her and said:Sauda, by Allah, you cannot conceal from us. Therefore, be careful when you go out. She ('A'isha) said: She turned back. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was at that time in my house having his evening meal and there was a bone in his hand. She (Sauda) cline and said: Allah's Messenger. I went out and 'Umar said to me so and so. She ('A'isha) reported: There came the revelation to him and then it was over; the bone was then in his hand and he had not thrown it and he said:" Permission has been granted to you that you may go out for your needs

muslim:5668.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration demonstrates divine mercy in clarifying the scope of the Hijab ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53)) to remove hardship for Muhammad's wives, and that Umar ibn al-Khattab was merely expressing protective concern. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that after the Hijab was imposed on Sawda (*baʿda mā ḍuriba ʿalayhā al-ḥijāb*), Umar accosted her when she went out for defecation (*al-barāz*)—warning her, 'By Allah, you are not hidden from us, so watch how you go out!' (*wallāhi mā takhfayna ʿalaynā fanẓurī kayfa takhrujīna*)—which forced her to turn back (*fankafaʾat rājiʿatan*) and complain to Muhammad. Rather than rebuking Umar for policing his wife's basic bodily needs, Muhammad received an instantaneous revelation while still holding his supper meat-bone in his hand (*wa-inna al-ʿarqa fī yadihi mā waḍaʿahu*) just to grant his wives permission to go outside to relieve themselves (*qad udhina lakunna an takhrujna li-ḥājatikunna*).

muslim:3302.note: On the day of the conquest of Mecca in AD 630, Muhammad declares that Allah made Mecca sacred from the creation of the heavens and the earth until the Day of Resurrection—forbidding warfare in it to anyone before him while permitting it exclusively for him for a single hour of one day—and prohibits cutting its thorns or fresh herbage. When his uncle al-'Abbas immediately asks to exempt rush (*al-idhkhir*) for their blacksmiths and houses, Muhammad amends the prohibition on the spot by stating, "Except *al-idhkhir*" (which classical commentators like al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar explain by positing instantaneous unrecited revelation or prophetic *ijtihad* mid-speech).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَقَالَ يَوْمَ الْفَتْحِ فَتْحِ مَكَّةَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ هَذَا الْبَلَدَ حَرَّمَهُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ خَلَقَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضَ فَهُوَ حَرَامٌ بِحُرْمَةِ اللَّهِ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ وَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يَحِلَّ الْقِتَالُ فِيهِ لأَحَدٍ قَبْلِي وَلَمْ يَحِلَّ لِي إِلاَّ سَاعَةً مِنْ نَهَارٍ فَهُوَ حَرَامٌ بِحُرْمَةِ اللَّهِ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ لاَ يُعْضَدُ شَوْكُهُ وَلاَ يُنَفَّرُ صَيْدُهُ وَلاَ يَلْتَقِطُ إِلاَّ مَنْ عَرَّفَهَا وَلاَ يُخْتَلَى خَلاَهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ الْعَبَّاسُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِلاَّ الإِذْخِرَ فَإِنَّهُ لِقَيْنِهِمْ وَلِبُيُوتِهِمْ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِلاَّ الإِذْخِرَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He also said on the Day of Victory over Mecca: Allah made this town sacred on the day He created the earth and the heavens; so it is -sacred by the sacred- ness conferred on it by Allah until the Day of Resurrection and fighting in it was not lawful to anyone before me, and it was made lawful for me only during an hour on one day, for it is sacred by the sacredness conferred on it by Allah until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorns are not to be cut, its game is not to be molested, and the things dropped are to be picked up only by one who makes a public announcement of it, and its fresh herbage is not to be cut. Abbas (Allah be pleased with him) said: Messenger of Allah, exception may be made in case of rush, for it is useful for their blacksmiths and for their houses. He (the Holy Prophet) conceding the suggestion of 'Abbas) said: Except rush

muslim:3302.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's brief military exemption in Mecca was a unique divine dispensation (*khaṣīṣah*) to purge idolatry, and—citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—claim that his sudden exemption of rush (*al-idhkhir*) was authorized by instantaneous, unrecited revelation (*waḥy*) descending at the exact second his uncle al-'Abbās spoke. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Mecca's sanctity and the blanket ban on cutting its herbage (*وَلاَ يُخْتَلَى خَلاَهَا*) were unalterably decreed by Allah on the day He created the heavens and the earth until the Day of Resurrection (*حَرَّمَهُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ خَلَقَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضَ ... إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ*), only for Muhammad to immediately repeat his uncle's exact words (*فَقَالَ «إِلاَّ الإِذْخِرَ»*) without any pause or mention of revelation as soon as al-'Abbās raised a mundane economic objection regarding their blacksmiths and houses. This sequence exposes how supposedly eternal decrees established at creation were conveniently suspended for Muhammad's AD 630 military conquest (*وَلَمْ يَحِلَّ لِي إِلاَّ سَاعَةً مِنْ نَهَارٍ*) and modified in real time through human lobbying.

muslim:3678.note: After Aisha and Hafsa agreed to tell Muhammad that they noticed the odor of maghafir (mimosa gum) on him, he stated that he had drunk honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh and would never do so again, prompting the revelation of [Quran 66:1-4](quran://66/1) asking why he forbade what Allah made lawful for him and calling on Aisha and Hafsa to repent.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ يَمْكُثُ عِنْدَ زَيْنَبَ بِنْتِ جَحْشٍ فَيَشْرَبُ عِنْدَهَا عَسَلاً قَالَتْ فَتَوَاطَأْتُ أَنَا وَحَفْصَةُ أَنَّ أَيَّتَنَا مَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلْتَقُلْ إِنِّي أَجِدُ مِنْكَ رِيحَ مَغَافِيرَ أَكَلْتَ مَغَافِيرَ فَدَخَلَ عَلَى إِحْدَاهُمَا فَقَالَتْ ذَلِكَ لَهُ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ بَلْ شَرِبْتُ عَسَلاً عِنْدَ زَيْنَبَ بِنْتِ جَحْشٍ وَلَنْ أَعُودَ لَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَنَزَلَ ‏{‏ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏{‏ إِنْ تَتُوبَا‏}‏ لِعَائِشَةَ وَحَفْصَةَ ‏{‏ وَإِذْ أَسَرَّ النَّبِيُّ إِلَى بَعْضِ أَزْوَاجِهِ حَدِيثًا‏}‏ لِقَوْلِهِ ‏"‏ بَلْ شَرِبْتُ عَسَلاً ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) narrated that Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) used to spend time with Zainab daughter of Jahsh and drank honey at her house. She ('A'isha further) said:I and Hafsa agreed that one whom Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) would visit first should say: I notice that you have an odour of the Maghafir (gum of mimosa). He (the Holy Prophet) visited one of them and she said to him like this, whereupon he said: I have taken honey in the house of Zainab bint Jabsh and I will never do it again. It was at this (that the following verse was revealed): 'Why do you hold to be forbidden what Allah has made lawful for you... (up to). If you both ('A'isha and Hafsa) turn to Allah" up to:" And when the Prophet confided an information to one of his wives" (lxvi. 3). This refers to his saying: But I have taken honey

muslim:3678.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that [Quran 66:1-4](quran://66/1) demonstrates prophetic independence from Muhammad's own wishes by rebuking his decision to abstain from something lawful and establishing a general legal ruling. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that these verses descended (`فَنَزَلَ`) in direct response to a domestic agreement between Aisha and Hafsa (`فَتَوَاطَأْتُ أَنَا وَحَفْصَةُ`) after they told him he smelled of *maghafir* gum to stop him from drinking honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh. Instead of penalizing Muhammad, the revelation released him from his vow never to drink it again (`بَلْ شَرِبْتُ عَسَلاً عِنْدَ زَيْنَبَ بِنْتِ جَحْشٍ وَلَنْ أَعُودَ لَهُ`) and called on Aisha and Hafsa to repent (`إِنْ تَتُوبَا`) for their scheme (`bukhari:5267`, `muslim:3679`).

muslim:3487.note: A woman comes to Muhammad to gift herself to him in marriage (*ahabu laka nafsī*) under the exclusive prophetic exemption from paying a dower ([Quran 33:50](quran://33/50)), whereupon he raises and lowers his gaze upon her before lowering his head without making a decision. When a destitute companion asks to marry her if Muhammad has no need of her (*ḥājah*), Muhammad requires him to provide a dower—ultimately granting her to him (*mallaktukahā*) for the chapters of the Quran he has memorized—since marriage by gift without a dower was restricted to the Prophet alone.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: جَاءَتِ امْرَأَةٌ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ جِئْتُ أَهَبُ لَكَ نَفْسِي ‏.‏ فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَصَعَّدَ النَّظَرَ فِيهَا وَصَوَّبَهُ ثُمَّ طَأْطَأَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَأْسَهُ فَلَمَّا رَأَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَقْضِ فِيهَا شَيْئًا جَلَسَتْ فَقَامَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَكَ بِهَا حَاجَةٌ فَزَوِّجْنِيهَا ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A woman came to Allah's Messenger. (ﷺ) and said: Messenger of Allah, I have come to you to entrust myself to you (you may contract my marriage with anyone at your discretion). Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saw her and cast a glance at her from head to foot. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) then lowered his head. When the woman saw that he had made no decision in regard to her, she sat down. There stood up a person from amongst his companions and said: Messenger of Allah, marry her to me if you have no need of her.

muslim:3487.literal_translation: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have come to gift myself to you.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at her, raising his gaze upon her and lowering it, and then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lowered his head. When the woman saw that he had made no decision regarding her, she sat down. A man among his companions stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if you have no desire/need for her, marry her to me.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ جِئْتُ أَهَبُ لَكَ نَفْسِي
translation_issue.published_rendering: Messenger of Allah, I have come to you to entrust myself to you (you may contract my marriage with anyone at your discretion).
translation_issue.literal_meaning: O Messenger of Allah, I have come to gift myself to you.
translation_issue.explanation: The translator replaces 'ji'tu ahabu laka nafsī' ('I have come to gift myself to you' under the prophetic marriage exemption of Quran 33:50) with 'to entrust myself to you (you may contract my marriage with anyone at your discretion)' to conceal that the woman was offering herself as a bride to Muhammad before he looked her up and down and silently declined her.

muslim:3487.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the woman was merely entrusting her marriage guardianship to the Prophet (as Abdul Hamid Siddiqi's English translation interpolates), or that as Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar explain, looking her up and down was simply a lawful pre-marital inspection (*al-naẓar ilā al-makhṭūbah*) followed by polite silence to spare her embarrassment. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *ji'tu ahabu laka nafsī* ("I have come to gift myself to you")—directly invoking Muhammad's exclusive exemption from paying a dower in Quran 33:50 (*in wahabat nafsahā lil-nabiyy*)—and the companion's immediate plea (*in lam yakun laka bihā ḥājah fa-zawwijnīhā*, "if you have no desire for her, marry her to me") confirms she offered herself as a bride to Muhammad personally. Only after visually appraising her from head to foot (*ṣaʿʿada al-naẓara fīhā wa-ṣawwabahu*) and declining her for himself did Muhammad enforce upon his destitute follower the strict dower requirement that Quran 33:50 waived for the Prophet alone.

muslim:6307.note: While polygyny is permitted for Muslim men ([Quran 4:3](quran://4/3)) and expanded for Muhammad himself ([Quran 33:50](quran://33/50)), Muhammad declares from the pulpit three times that he will not permit the sons of Hisham ibn al-Mughira to marry their daughter to Ali ibn Abi Talib unless Ali first divorces Muhammad's daughter. Although parallel reports such as muslim:6309 note that the prospective bride was the daughter of Abu Jahl, Muhammad here grounds his prohibition in the declaration that his daughter is a part of him and that whatever disturbs or harms her disturbs and harms him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَمِعَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ إِنَّ بَنِي هِشَامِ بْنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ اسْتَأْذَنُونِي أَنْ يُنْكِحُوا ابْنَتَهُمْ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ فَلاَ آذَنُ لَهُمْ ثُمَّ لاَ آذَنُ لَهُمْ ثُمَّ لاَ آذَنُ لَهُمْ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُحِبَّ ابْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ أَنْ يُطَلِّقَ ابْنَتِي وَيَنْكِحَ ابْنَتَهُمْ فَإِنَّمَا ابْنَتِي بَضْعَةٌ مِنِّي يَرِيبُنِي مَا رَابَهَا وَيُؤْذِينِي مَا آذَاهَا ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Miswar b. Makhramali reported that he heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) say, as he sat on the pulpit:The sons of Hisham b. Mughira have asked my permission to marry their daughter with 'Ali b. Abi Talib (that refers to the daughter of Abu Jahl for whom 'All had sent a proposal for marriage). But I would not allow them, I would not allow them, I would not allow them (and the only alternative possible is) that 'Ali should divorce my daughter (and then marry their daughter), for my daughter is part of me. He who disturbs her in fact disturbs me and he who offends her offends me

muslim:6307.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad only objected because the prospective bride was the daughter of Abu Jahl, or to protect Fatima from jealousy that might cause her to offend the Prophet's unique status. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Ali was permitted to marry Abu Jahl's daughter if he divorced Muhammad's daughter first (illā an yuḥibba ibnu Abī Ṭālibin an yuṭalliqa ibnatī wa-yankiḥa ibnatahum), proving the prohibition was not due to the bride's lineage. Furthermore, by grounding his thrice-repeated refusal (fa-lā ādhanu lahum) in the fact that a co-wife would disturb and harm his daughter (yarībunī mā rābahā wa-yuʾdhīnī mā ādhāhā), Muhammad acknowledged that polygyny harms a wife while shielding only his own daughter from the practice permitted to other men in [Quran 4:3](quran://4/3).

muslim:6622.note: Muhammad declares that he is a mortal who gets angry like other mortals (*yaghḍabu kamā yaghḍabu al-bashar*) and claims an unbreakable covenant (*ʿahdan*) with Allah whereby any believer he harms (*ādhaytuhu*), reviles (*sababtuhu*), or flogs (*jaladtuhu*) receives that treatment as an expiation (*kaffāratan*) and a means of nearness to Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّمَا مُحَمَّدٌ بَشَرٌ يَغْضَبُ كَمَا يَغْضَبُ الْبَشَرُ وَإِنِّي قَدِ اتَّخَذْتُ عِنْدَكَ عَهْدًا لَنْ تُخْلِفَنِيهِ فَأَيُّمَا مُؤْمِنٍ آذَيْتُهُ أَوْ سَبَبْتُهُ أَوْ جَلَدْتُهُ فَاجْعَلْهَا لَهُ كَفَّارَةً وَقُرْبَةً تُقَرِّبُهُ بِهَا إِلَيْكَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: he heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying: O Allah, Muhammad is a human being. I lose my temper just as human beings lose temper, and I have held a covenant with Thee which Thou wouldst not break: For a believer whom I give any trouble or invoke curse or beat, make that an expiation (of his sins and a source of) his nearness to Thee on the Day of Resurrection

muslim:6622.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this supplication reflects prophetic humility and mercy, intended to compensate believers if an apparent legal judgment or colloquial Arabic figure of speech was ever misapplied. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that these acts occur because Muhammad loses his temper just as mortals lose their temper (*yaghḍabu kamā yaghḍabu al-bashar*) and specifically includes harming (*ādhaytuhu*), reviling (*sababtuhu*), or whipping (*jaladtuhu*) a believer (*muʾmin*). Rather than offering earthly restitution for actions committed in anger, Muhammad invokes a personal covenant (*ʿahdan*) with Allah to reclassify the harm, insults, and flogging he inflicts as afterlife expiation (*kaffārah*) and nearness (*qurbah*) on the Day of Resurrection.

muslim:3632.note: Aisha used to ask whether a woman feels no shame in offering herself to a man, until the revelation of [Quran 33:51](quran://33/51) permitted Muhammad to defer or take to himself whichever of them he wished, prompting her to remark that his Lord hastens to fulfill his desires.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّهَا كَانَتْ تَقُولُ أَمَا تَسْتَحْيِي امْرَأَةٌ تَهَبُ نَفْسَهَا لِرَجُلٍ حَتَّى أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ‏{‏ تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ وَتُؤْوِي إِلَيْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ‏}‏ فَقُلْتُ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيُسَارِعُ لَكَ فِي هَوَاكَ
problematic_excerpt.english: 'A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) used to say:Does the woman not feel shy of offering herself to a man? Then Allah the Exalted and Glorious revealed this verse:" You may defer any of them you wish and take to yourself any you wish." I ('A'isha said): It seems to me that your Lord hastens to satisfy your desire

muslim:3632.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Aisha's remark was merely an expression of pious admiration for Allah's favor toward Muhammad or a harmless comment born of marital jealousy rather than a critique of convenient revelation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Aisha questioned the modesty of a woman offering herself to a man (`أَمَا تَسْتَحْيِي امْرَأَةٌ تَهَبُ نَفْسَهَا لِرَجُلٍ`) until [Quran 33:51](quran://33/51) was sent down permitting him to defer or receive whichever women he wished (`تُرْجِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ مِنْهُنَّ وَتُؤْوِي إِلَيْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ`). Her immediate reply uses the emphatic construction `إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيُسَارِعُ لَكَ فِي هَوَاكَ` ("Indeed, your Lord surely hastens for you in your desires"), directly connecting the descent of the verse to the satisfaction of his personal desire (`هَوَاكَ`).

muslim:440.note: Arguing that Muhammad concealed no revelation (cf. muslim:439), Aisha states that if he had hidden anything, it would have been [Quran 33:37](quran://33/37), which rebukes him for telling his adopted son Zayd to keep his wife while concealing in his heart what Allah would disclose out of fear of people—referring to his subsequent marriage to Zayd's wife Zaynab bint Jahsh.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَتْ وَلَوْ كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَاتِمًا شَيْئًا مِمَّا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ لَكَتَمَ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ ‏{‏ وَإِذْ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِي أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ أَمْسِكْ عَلَيْكَ زَوْجَكَ وَاتَّقِ اللَّهَ وَتُخْفِي فِي نَفْسِكَ مَا اللَّهُ مُبْدِيهِ وَتَخْشَى النَّاسَ وَاللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ تَخْشَاهُ‏}‏
problematic_excerpt.english: She ('A'isha) said: If Muhammad were to conceal anything which was sent to him, he would have certainly concealed this verse:" And when thou saidst to him on whom Allah had conferred favour and thou too had conferred favour: Keep thy wife to thyself and fear Allah, and thou wast concealing in thy heart that which Allah was going to disclose, and thou wast fearing men while Allah has a better right that thou shouldst fear Him

muslim:440.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Aisha's remark proves Muhammad's prophetic integrity because an impostor would never fabricate a verse that publicly rebukes him, claiming (via Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar) that what he concealed in his heart (wa-tukhfī fī nafsika) was merely Allah's prior notification that Zayd would divorce Zaynab rather than any personal desire for her. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad commanded Zayd to 'keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah' (amsik ʿalayka zawjaka wa-ttaqi Allāh) while hiding his true motive out of 'fear of the people' (wa-takhshā al-nās)—a moral reproach that is incoherent if he were simply guarding a divine secret rather than hiding his desire for his adopted son's wife, as early Sunni exegetes like Al-Ṭabarī openly recorded on Quran 33:37. Ultimately, this mild rhetorical rebuke functioned as a masterstroke of self-serving deflection, neutralizing public scandal in Medina by framing his marriage to his former daughter-in-law as an inescapable heavenly decree (zawwajnākahā) enacted without a guardian or witnesses (bukhari:7420).

muslim:3506.note: After three wedding guests lingered in conversation following Muhammad's marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh—delaying him from entering his apartment until Anas ibn Malik reported their departure—Muhammad entered, drew a curtain (*hijab*) between himself and Anas, and Allah revealed [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53) commanding believers not to linger in the Prophet's homes after meals, requiring them to address his wives from behind a partition, and forbidding anyone from ever marrying his widows.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَمَّا تَزَوَّجَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم زَيْنَبَ بِنْتَ جَحْشٍ دَعَا الْقَوْمَ فَطَعِمُوا ثُمَّ جَلَسُوا يَتَحَدَّثُونَ - قَالَ - فَأَخَذَ كَأَنَّهُ يَتَهَيَّأُ لِلْقِيَامِ فَلَمْ يَقُومُوا فَلَمَّا رَأَى ذَلِكَ قَامَ فَلَمَّا قَامَ قَامَ مَنْ قَامَ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ ‏.‏ زَادَ عَاصِمٌ وَابْنُ عَبْدِ الأَعْلَى فِي حَدِيثِهِمَا قَالَ فَقَعَدَ ثَلاَثَةٌ وَإِنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم جَاءَ لِيَدْخُلَ فَإِذَا الْقَوْمُ جُلُوسٌ ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ قَامُوا فَانْطَلَقُوا - قَالَ - فَجِئْتُ فَأَخْبَرْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُمْ قَدِ انْطَلَقُوا - قَالَ - فَجَاءَ حَتَّى دَخَلَ فَذَهَبْتُ أَدْخُلُ فَأَلْقَى الْحِجَابَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ - قَالَ - وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ‏{‏ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لاَ تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلَى طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ نَاظِرِينَ إِنَاهُ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏{‏ إِنَّ ذَلِكُمْ كَانَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَظِيمًا‏}‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) married Zainab bint jahsh, he invited people (to the wedding feast) and they ate food. They then sat there and entered into conversation. He (the Holy Prophet) made a stir as if he was preparing to stand up, but (the persons busy in talking) did not stand up. When he (the Holy Prophet) saw it, he stood up and when he did so, some other persons stood up. 'Asim and Abd al-A'la in their narrations made this addition: Three (persons) sat there, and Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) came there to enter (the apartment) but he found the people sitting there. Then they stood up and went away. He said: Then I came and informed Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) that they had gone away. He (the Holy Prophet) then came there until he entered (the apartment). I also went and was about to enter, when he hung a curtain between me and him (and it was on this occasion that) Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, revealed this verse:" O you who believe, enter not the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you for a meal, not waiting for its cooking being finished to the (words)" Surely this is serious in the sight of Allah" (xxxiii)

muslim:3506.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53) was revealed to legislate universal social etiquette (*ādāb al-istiʾdhān*), claiming—as Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar note—that Muhammad's noble shyness (*ḥayāʾ*) prevented him from dismissing inconsiderate guests himself. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah sent down this eternal revelation at the exact moment Muhammad grew frustrated waiting for three lingering guests to leave (`فَقَعَدَ ثَلاَثَةٌ ... فَأَلْقَى الْحِجَابَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ`) so he could enter his bridal apartment with Zaynab. Far from establishing a general rule for all Muslim homes, the verse specifically targets 'the houses of the Prophet' (`بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ`) and concludes by forbidding anyone from ever marrying his widows (`إِنَّ ذَلِكُمْ كَانَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَظِيمًا`), exemplifying the exact pattern Aisha critiqued in bukhari:4788: 'I see that your Lord hastens in fulfilling your desires (`هَوَاكَ`).'

bukhari:4990.note: As Muhammad was dictating [Surah 4:95](quran://4/95) to his scribe Zayd without qualification—declaring that believers who sit at home are not equal to those who fight—the blind companion 'Amr ibn Umm Maktum sitting behind him asked how the command applied to his blindness. Immediately 'in its place' (fa-nazalat makanaha), the verse was revealed with the added exemption 'other than the disabled' (ghayru uli al-darar), recording an on-the-spot textual amendment prompted by a bystander's question that commentators categorize as legislative specification (takhsis) (cf. bukhari:4594).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ اكْتُبْ لاَ يَسْتَوِي الْقَاعِدُونَ ‏"‏ وَخَلْفَ ظَهْرِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَمْرُو بْنُ أُمِّ مَكْتُومٍ الأَعْمَى قَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَمَا تَأْمُرُنِي فَإِنِّي رَجُلٌ ضَرِيرُ الْبَصَرِ فَنَزَلَتْ مَكَانَهَا ‏{‏لاَ يَسْتَوِي الْقَاعِدُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ‏}‏ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ‏{‏غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ‏}‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Then he said, "Write: 'Not equal are those Believers who sit..", and at that time `Amr bin Um Maktum, the blind man was sitting behind the Prophet (ﷺ) . He said, "O Allah's Apostle! What is your order For me (as regards the above Verse) as I am a blind man?" So, instead of the above Verse, the following Verse was revealed: 'Not equal are those believers who sit (at home) except those who are disabled

bukhari:4990.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that Allah intentionally revealed Surah 4:95 in stages as a test of sincerity and mercifully sent down the exemption in response to 'Amr ibn Umm Maktum's plea, while the complete verse remained eternally fixed in the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the amended wording came down 'in its place' (فَنَزَلَتْ مَكَانَهَا, *fa-nazalat makānahā*) only after Muhammad had already ordered Zayd to write down the unqualified decree (اكْتُبْ لاَ يَسْتَوِي الْقَاعِدُونَ) and the blind man sitting right behind him pointed out the oversight (فَمَا تَأْمُرُنِي فَإِنِّي رَجُلٌ ضَرِيرُ الْبَصَرِ). Together with Zayd ibn Thabit's parallel account (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4594), this sequence exposes Quranic text being patched in real time on the spot to fix an obvious practical omission only after a human bystander objected.

muslim:5671.note: A'isha reported that Umar ibn al-Khattab told Muhammad to veil his wives, but Muhammad did not do so. When Muhammad's wife Sauda bint Zam'a went out at night to the open fields to relieve herself, Umar called out that they recognized her in the hope that the veil (Hijab) would be revealed, after which Allah revealed the verses of the veil.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ أَزْوَاجَ، رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كُنَّ يَخْرُجْنَ بِاللَّيْلِ إِذَا تَبَرَّزْنَ إِلَى الْمَنَاصِعِ وَهُوَ صَعِيدٌ أَفْيَحُ وَكَانَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ يَقُولُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم احْجُبْ نِسَاءَكَ ‏.‏ فَلَمْ يَكُنْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَفْعَلُ فَخَرَجَتْ سَوْدَةُ بِنْتُ زَمْعَةَ زَوْجُ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَيْلَةً مِنَ اللَّيَالِي عِشَاءً وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَةً طَوِيلَةً فَنَادَاهَا عُمَرُ أَلاَ قَدْ عَرَفْنَاكِ يَا سَوْدَةُ ‏.‏ حِرْصًا عَلَى أَنْ يُنْزِلَ الْحِجَابَ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ الْحِجَابَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha reported that the wives of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to go out in the cover of night when they went to open fields (in the outskirts of Medina) for easing themselves. 'Umar b Khattab used to say:Allah's Messenger, ask your ladies to observe veil, but Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) did not do that. So there went out Sauda, daughter of Zarn'a, the wife of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), during one of the nights when it was dark. She was a tall statured lady. 'Umar called her saying: Sauda, we recognise you. (He did this with the hope that the verses pertaining to veil would be revealed.) 'A'isha said: Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, then revealed the verses pertaining to veil

muslim:5671.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Umar ibn al-Khattab was merely expressing protective concern for the honor of Muhammad's wives and that the revelation of the Hijab verses ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53), [Quran 33:59](quran://33/59)) was an independent divine decree that coincided with Umar's insight. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that after Muhammad did not comply with Umar's demand to veil his wives (`احْجُبْ نِسَاءَكَ . فَلَمْ يَكُنْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَفْعَلُ`), Umar called out to Sauda bint Zam'a (`أَلاَ قَدْ عَرَفْنَاكِ يَا سَوْدَةُ`) when the wives went out at night to relieve themselves (`إِذَا تَبَرَّزْنَ إِلَى الْمَنَاصِعِ`) specifically with the desire that the Hijab would be revealed (`حِرْصًا عَلَى أَنْ يُنْزِلَ الْحِجَابَ`). Rather than rebuking Umar for calling out to Muhammad's wife in the dark to force a change in policy, the narration states that Allah subsequently revealed the Hijab (`فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ الْحِجَابَ`), a sequence also recorded in `bukhari:146`, `bukhari:4790`, and `muslim:5670`.

bukhari:7011.note: Muhammad told Aisha that she was shown to him twice in a dream carried in a piece of silk by a man declaring her to be his wife, to which Muhammad responded that Allah would bring it to pass if the vision was from Him. Because prophetic dreams constitute divine revelation (wahy) in Sunni theology, this narration presents his marriage to Aisha—contracted at age six and consummated at age nine (bukhari:5133)—as divinely ordained.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُرِيتُكِ فِي الْمَنَامِ مَرَّتَيْنِ، إِذَا رَجُلٌ يَحْمِلُكِ فِي سَرَقَةِ حَرِيرٍ فَيَقُولُ هَذِهِ امْرَأَتُكَ‏.‏ فَأَكْشِفُهَا فَإِذَا هِيَ أَنْتِ فَأَقُولُ إِنْ يَكُنْ هَذَا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ يُمْضِهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: You were shown to me twice in (my) dream. Behold, a man was carrying you in a silken piece of cloth and said to me, "She is your wife, so uncover her,' and behold, it was you. I would then say (to myself), 'If this is from Allah, then it must happen

bukhari:7011.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that because the dreams of prophets constitute divine revelation (*waḥy*), this vision proves Muhammad's marriage to Aisha was a heavenly decree rather than a personal desire, and that his conditional response reflects pious submission to God's will. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that an unidentified "man" (*rajul*, `رَجُلٌ`) presented her and records Muhammad himself questioning whether the dream was even from God (`إِنْ يَكُنْ هَذَا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ يُمْضِهِ` — "If this is from Allah, He will bring it to pass"), forcing commentators like Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* to awkwardly explain away how a prophet could doubt supposedly infallible revelation. Moreover, invoking a private, unverifiable dream to divinely sanction marrying his chief companion's young daughter exemplifies the exact pattern of convenient revelations that Aisha herself criticized in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4788: "I see that your Lord hastens to fulfill your desires."

bukhari:6238.note: Following his wedding meal with Zainab bint Jahsh, a group of guests lingered at length, prompting Muhammad to repeatedly walk out to Aisha's threshold and return until they finally departed. Upon their departure, the Verse of the Hijab ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53)) was revealed and Muhammad drew a curtain between himself and Anas bin Malik—though a neighboring report in the same chapter (bukhari:6240) attributes the revelation of the Hijab to Umar bin Al-Khattab urging Muhammad to veil his wives and calling out to Sauda at night.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَكَانَ أَوَّلَ مَا نَزَلَ فِي مُبْتَنَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِزَيْنَبَ ابْنَةِ جَحْشٍ، أَصْبَحَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِهَا عَرُوسًا فَدَعَا الْقَوْمَ، فَأَصَابُوا مِنَ الطَّعَامِ ثُمَّ خَرَجُوا، وَبَقِيَ مِنْهُمْ رَهْطٌ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَطَالُوا الْمُكْثَ فَقَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَخَرَجَ وَخَرَجْتُ مَعَهُ كَىْ يَخْرُجُوا، فَمَشَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَمَشَيْتُ مَعَهُ حَتَّى جَاءَ عَتَبَةَ حُجْرَةِ عَائِشَةَ، ثُمَّ ظَنَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُمْ خَرَجُوا فَرَجَعَ وَرَجَعْتُ مَعَهُ، حَتَّى دَخَلَ عَلَى زَيْنَبَ فَإِذَا هُمْ جُلُوسٌ لَمْ يَتَفَرَّقُوا، فَرَجَعَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَرَجَعْتُ مَعَهُ، حَتَّى بَلَغَ عَتَبَةَ حُجْرَةِ عَائِشَةَ، فَظَنَّ أَنْ قَدْ خَرَجُوا، فَرَجَعَ وَرَجَعْتُ مَعَهُ، فَإِذَا هُمْ قَدْ خَرَجُوا، فَأُنْزِلَ آيَةُ الْحِجَابِ، فَضَرَبَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ سِتْرًا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: It was revealed (for the first time) during the marriage of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) with Zainab bint Jahsh. In the morning, the Prophet (ﷺ) was a bride-groom of her and he Invited the people, who took their meals and went away, but a group of them remained with Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and they prolonged their stay. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) got up and went out, and I too, went out along with him till he came to the lintel of `Aisha's dwelling place. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) thought that those people had left by then, so he returned, and I too, returned with him till he entered upon Zainab and found that they were still sitting there and had not yet gone. The Prophet (ﷺ) went out again, and so did I with him till he reached the lintel of `Aisha's dwelling place, and then he thought that those people must have left by then, so he returned, and so did I with him, and found those people had gone. At that time the Divine Verse of Al-Hijab was revealed, and the Prophet (ﷺ) set a screen between me and him (his family)

bukhari:6238.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the revelation of the Hijab verse on the morning of Muhammad's wedding to Zainab bint Jahsh—as explained in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—merely highlights the Prophet's extraordinary bashfulness (*ḥayā'*) in not wanting to rudely dismiss lingering guests, prompting Allah to establish timeless communal etiquette (*adab*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the verse descended directly in response to Muhammad's acute domestic impatience as a new bridegroom (*ʿarūsan*) when guests 'prolonged their stay' (*fa-aṭālū al-muktha*) and forced him to repeatedly pace out to Aisha's lintel 'so that they would leave' (*kay yakhrujū*), whereupon he immediately dropped a physical curtain (*fa-ḍaraba baynī wa-baynahu sitran*). Indeed, Quran 33:53 itself openly codifies Muhammad's personal irritation into eternal divine law—declaring that lingering 'annoys the Prophet' (*yu'dhī al-nabiyya*), mandating that his wives be spoken to only from behind a screen (*min warā'i ḥijābin*), and forbidding anyone from ever marrying his widows—a pattern of convenient revelations regarding his marriages that led Aisha to dryly remark in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4788, 'I see that your Lord hastens in fulfilling your desires' (*mā arā rabbaka illā yusāriʿu fī hawāka*).

muslim:4911.note: After Muhammad orders Zaid ibn Thabit to inscribe [Quran 4:95](quran://4/95)—declaring that believers who sit at home and those who wage jihad in the way of Allah are not equal—on a shoulder-blade without an exception clause, Ibn Umm Maktum complains to him of his blindness, whereupon the revelation descends with the added exemption for the disabled (`ghayru uli al-darar`).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ الْبَرَاءَ، يَقُولُ فِي هَذِهِ الآيَةِ لاَ يَسْتَوِي الْقَاعِدُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُجَاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَأَمَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم زَيْدًا فَجَاءَ بِكَتِفٍ يَكْتُبُهَا فَشَكَا إِلَيْهِ ابْنُ أُمِّ مَكْتُومٍ ضَرَارَتَهُ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏ لاَ يَسْتَوِي الْقَاعِدُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ‏}‏
problematic_excerpt.english: that he heard Bara' talking about the Qur'anic verse:" Those who sit (at home) from among the believers and those who go out for Jihad in the way of Allah are not aqual" (iv. 95). (He said that) the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered Zaid (to write the verse). He brought a shoulder-blade (of a slaughtered camel) and inscribed it (the verse) thereon. The son of Umm Maktum complained of his blindness to the Prophet (ﷺ). (At this) descended the revelation:" Those of the believers who sit (at home) without any trouble (illness, incapacity, disability)" (iv. 95).

muslim:4911.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the exemption for the disabled in [Quran 4:95](quran://4/95) reflects gradual legislation and divine mercy responding to a companion's inquiry rather than an oversight in the initial revelation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad had already ordered Zaid ibn Thabit to write down the unqualified verse on a shoulder-blade (`فَأَمَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم زَيْدًا فَجَاءَ بِكَتِفٍ يَكْتُبُهَا`) before the son of Umm Maktum complained of his blindness (`فَشَكَا إِلَيْهِ ابْنُ أُمِّ مَكْتُومٍ ضَرَارَتَهُ`), which immediately triggered the descent of the exception (`فَنَزَلَتْ ... غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ`). As confirmed in parallel narrations (`bukhari:2831`, `bukhari:4593`, `muslim:4912`), the revelation was dictated without accounting for physical incapacity until a blind man pointed out the omission while the scribe was actively recording the text.

bukhari:5267.note: After Aisha and Hafsa agreed to tell Muhammad that they detected the odor of *maghāfīr* (a foul-smelling gum) on him because he stayed with his wife Zaynab bint Jahsh and drank honey at her house, Muhammad declared he would never drink it again, prompting the revelation of [Quran 66:1](quran://66/1)-[4](quran://66/4) addressing his self-imposed prohibition and calling Aisha and Hafsa to repent to Allah.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ يَمْكُثُ عِنْدَ زَيْنَبَ ابْنَةِ جَحْشٍ، وَيَشْرَبُ عِنْدَهَا عَسَلاً، فَتَوَاصَيْتُ أَنَا وَحَفْصَةُ أَنَّ أَيَّتَنَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلْتَقُلْ إِنِّي أَجِدُ مِنْكَ رِيحَ مَغَافِيرَ، أَكَلْتَ مَغَافِيرَ فَدَخَلَ عَلَى إِحْدَاهُمَا فَقَالَتْ لَهُ ذَلِكَ، فَقَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ بَلْ شَرِبْتُ عَسَلاً عِنْدَ زَيْنَبَ ابْنَةِ جَحْشٍ وَلَنْ أَعُودَ لَهُ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ‏}‏ إِلَى ‏{‏إِنْ تَتُوبَا إِلَى اللَّهِ‏}‏ لِعَائِشَةَ وَحَفْصَةَ ‏{‏وَإِذْ أَسَرَّ النَّبِيُّ إِلَى بَعْضِ أَزْوَاجِهِ‏}‏ لِقَوْلِهِ ‏"‏ بَلْ شَرِبْتُ عَسَلاً ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to stay for a long while with Zanab bint Jahsh and drink honey at her house. So Hafsa and I decided that if the Prophet (ﷺ) came to anyone of us, she should say him, "I detect the smell of Maghafir (a nasty smelling gum) in you. Have you eaten Maghafir?' " So the Prophet (ﷺ) visited one of them and she said to him similarly. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Never mind, I have taken some honey at the house of Zainab bint Jahsh, but I shall never drink of it anymore." So there was revealed: 'O Prophet ! Why do you ban (for you) that which Allah has made lawful for you . . . If you two (wives of Prophet) turn in repentance to Allah,' (66.1-4) addressing Aisha and Hafsa. 'When the Prophet (ﷺ) disclosed a matter in confidence to some of his wives.' (66.3) namely his saying: But I have taken some honey

bukhari:5267.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that [Quran 66:1](quran://66/1) proves Muhammad did not author the Quran because it rebukes him over a harmless vow to stop drinking honey, and they use this narration to dismiss reports about him being caught with his concubine Mariyah the Copt. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that once Aisha and Hafsa conspired (`فَتَوَاصَيْتُ أَنَا وَحَفْصَةُ`) and Muhammad vowed never to drink the honey again (`وَلَنْ أَعُودَ لَهُ`), revelation immediately descended (`فَنَزَلَتْ`) to release him from his oath ([Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)) while commanding his wives to repent (`إِنْ تَتُوبَا إِلَى اللَّهِ`) under the threat of Allah, Gabriel, and the angels backing him against them ([Quran 66:4](quran://66/4)) and replacing them in divorce ([Quran 66:5](quran://66/5)). Moreover, Ibn Hajar affirms in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* that authentic (*ṣaḥīḥ*) chains in *Sunan al-Nasāʾī* (3959) and *Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī* also link these verses to Hafsa catching Muhammad with Mariyah on her bed, showing that a mild opening question to the Prophet served to nullify his sworn restriction and silence his wives' domestic grievances.

muslim:6206.note: Through Ibn Umar, Umar ibn al-Khattab declares that he and his Lord concurred (wafaqtu rabbi) on three matters: the Station of Abraham ([Quran 2:125](quran://2/125)), the observance of the veil ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53)), and the captives of Badr ([Quran 8:67](quran://8/67)). While this concise report lists the three occasions without the underlying dialogues, parallel narrations (bukhari:402, bukhari:4483) record the episodes in which Umar's proposals preceded the corresponding revelations.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ عُمَرُ وَافَقْتُ رَبِّي فِي ثَلاَثٍ فِي مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَفِي الْحِجَابِ وَفِي أُسَارَى بَدْرٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: Ibn Umar reported Umar as saying:My lord concorded with (my judgments) on three occasions. In case of the Station of Ibrahim, in case of the observance of veil and in case of the prisoners of Badr

muslim:6206.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrasing wāfaqtu rabbī ("I agreed with my Lord") means Umar's personal judgment merely coincided with divine wisdom, denying that human demands prompted Quranic revelation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states وَافَقْتُ رَبِّي فِي ثَلاَثٍ ("My lord concorded with (my judgments) on three occasions") specifically regarding the Station of Ibrahim ([Quran 2:125](quran://2/125)), the observance of the veil ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53)), and the prisoners of Badr ([Quran 8:67](quran://8/67)). Corroborated by parallel narrations in bukhari:402 and bukhari:4483, the text establishes that Umar's stated judgments preceded and were subsequently ratified by the descent of those three Quranic verses.

muslim:3690.note: After his wives ask him for household maintenance (*al-nafaqah*) and swear not to ask for what he does not possess, Muhammad withdraws from them for a month (or twenty-nine days) until [Quran 33:28](quran://33/28) is revealed in response to the domestic dispute. Muhammad then begins with Aisha, reciting the verse to her and advising her to consult her parents before deciding, whereupon she replies that she chooses Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقُلْنَ وَاللَّهِ لاَ نَسْأَلُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم شَيْئًا أَبَدًا لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ ثُمَّ اعْتَزَلَهُنَّ شَهْرًا أَوْ تِسْعًا وَعِشْرِينَ ثُمَّ نَزَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ ‏{‏ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ قُلْ لأَزْوَاجِكَ‏}‏ حَتَّى بَلَغَ ‏{‏ لِلْمُحْسِنَاتِ مِنْكُنَّ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا‏}‏ قَالَ فَبَدَأَ بِعَائِشَةَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا عَائِشَةُ إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَعْرِضَ عَلَيْكَ أَمْرًا أُحِبُّ أَنْ لاَ تَعْجَلِي فِيهِ حَتَّى تَسْتَشِيرِي أَبَوَيْكِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ وَمَا هُوَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَتَلاَ عَلَيْهَا الآيَةَ قَالَتْ أَفِيكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَسْتَشِيرُ أَبَوَىَّ بَلْ أَخْتَارُ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَالدَّارَ الآخِرَةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: They said: By Allah, we do not ask Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) for anything he does not possess. Then he withdrew from them for a month or for twenty-nine days. Then this verse was revealed to him:" Prophet: Say to thy wives... for a mighty reward" (xxxiii. 28). He then went first to 'A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) and said: I want to propound something to you, 'A'isha, but wish no hasty reply before you consult your parents. She said: Messenger of Allah, what is that? He (the Holy Prophet) recited to her the verse, whereupon she said: Is it about you that I should consult my parents, Messenger of Allah? Nay, I choose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode

muslim:3690.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the revelation of [Quran 33:28](quran://33/28) offered the wives a dignified, uncoerced choice between worldly wealth and the hereafter, noting that Muhammad advised Aisha not to rush before consulting her parents (`حَتَّى تَسْتَشِيرِي أَبَوَيْكِ`). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that this verse descended (`نَزَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ`) only after Abu Bakr and Umar struck Aisha and Hafsa on their necks (`يَجَأُ عُنُقَهَا`) for requesting maintenance (`النَّفَقَةَ`) and after Muhammad boycotted all his wives for twenty-nine days or a month (`ثُمَّ اعْتَزَلَهُنَّ شَهْرًا أَوْ تِسْعًا وَعِشْرِينَ`). Instructing Aisha to consult her parents (`أَبَوَيْكِ`) meant referring her back to Abu Bakr, who had just struck her on the neck in Muhammad's presence to stop her from asking for maintenance.

muslim:3690.note: To make a silent, dejected Muhammad laugh, Umar recounts that he struck his wife (the daughter of Kharijah) on the neck (*fawaja'tu 'unuqaha*) when she asked him for household maintenance (*al-nafaqah*). Muhammad laughs and remarks that his own wives are surrounding him asking for maintenance, whereupon Abu Bakr and Umar rise in his presence and strike Aisha and Hafsa on their necks until the wives swear never to ask Muhammad for anything he does not possess.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَوَجَدَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم جَالِسًا حَوْلَهُ نِسَاؤُهُ وَاجِمًا سَاكِتًا - قَالَ - فَقَالَ لأَقُولَنَّ شَيْئًا أُضْحِكُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوْ رَأَيْتَ بِنْتَ خَارِجَةَ سَأَلَتْنِي النَّفَقَةَ فَقُمْتُ إِلَيْهَا فَوَجَأْتُ عُنُقَهَا ‏.‏ فَضَحِكَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَقَالَ ‏"‏ هُنَّ حَوْلِي كَمَا تَرَى يَسْأَلْنَنِي النَّفَقَةَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَامَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ إِلَى عَائِشَةَ يَجَأُ عُنُقَهَا فَقَامَ عُمَرُ إِلَى حَفْصَةَ يَجَأُ عُنُقَهَا كِلاَهُمَا يَقُولُ تَسْأَلْنَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَا لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ ‏.‏ فَقُلْنَ وَاللَّهِ لاَ نَسْأَلُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم شَيْئًا أَبَدًا لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: he found Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) sitting sad and silent with his wives around him. He (Hadrat 'Umar) said: I would say something which would make the Prophet (ﷺ) laugh, so he said: Messenger of Allah, I wish you had seen (the treatment meted out to) the daughter ofKhadija when you asked me some money, and I got up and slapped her on her neck. Allah's Messenger (mav peace be upon him) laughed and said: They are around me as you see, asking for extra money. Abu Bakr (Allah be pleased with him) then got up went to 'A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) and slapped her on the neck, and 'Umar stood up before Hafsa and slapped her saying: You ask Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) which he does not possess. They said: By Allah, we do not ask Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) for anything he does not possess.

muslim:3690.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad never personally struck his wives—pointing to his closing statement that he was sent as an easygoing teacher (`مُعَلِّمًا مُيَسِّرًا`)—and claim that Abu Bakr and Umar only gave their daughters a light paternal tap for demanding extravagant luxuries. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the wives requested basic maintenance (`النَّفَقَةَ`, *al-nafaqah*) rather than "extra money," and uses the forceful verb *waja'a* (`فَوَجَأْتُ عُنُقَهَا` / `يَجَأُ عُنُقَهَا`), meaning to punch or strike on the neck. Furthermore, the narration records that Muhammad laughed (`فَضَحِكَ`) at Umar's account of striking his own wife on the neck and then watched without objection as Abu Bakr and Umar struck Aisha and Hafsa on their necks until they swore by Allah never to ask again (`فَقُلْنَ وَاللَّهِ لاَ نَسْأَلُ`).

muslim:6309.note: When Ali ibn Abi Talib proposed marriage to the daughter of Abu Jahl while married to Fatima, Muhammad addressed the people from the pulpit and declared that Fatima was a part of him and that he feared she would be put to trial in her religion. While stating that he was not forbidding what is generally lawful ([Quran 4:3](quran://4/3)), he swore by Allah that the daughter of Allah's Messenger and the daughter of the enemy of Allah would never be combined in one place.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ خَطَبَ بِنْتَ أَبِي جَهْلٍ عَلَى فَاطِمَةَ فَسَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُوَ يَخْطُبُ النَّاسَ فِي ذَلِكَ عَلَى مِنْبَرِهِ هَذَا وَأَنَا يَوْمَئِذٍ مُحْتَلِمٌ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ فَاطِمَةَ مِنِّي وَإِنِّي أَتَخَوَّفُ أَنْ تُفْتَنَ فِي دِينِهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ صِهْرًا لَهُ مِنْ بَنِي عَبْدِ شَمْسٍ فَأَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ فِي مُصَاهَرَتِهِ إِيَّاهُ فَأَحْسَنَ قَالَ ‏"‏ حَدَّثَنِي فَصَدَقَنِي وَوَعَدَنِي فَأَوْفَى لِي وَإِنِّي لَسْتُ أُحَرِّمُ حَلاَلاً وَلاَ أُحِلُّ حَرَامًا وَلَكِنْ وَاللَّهِ لاَ تَجْتَمِعُ بِنْتُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ وَبِنْتُ عَدُوِّ اللَّهِ مَكَانًا وَاحِدًا أَبَدًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Verily 'Ali b. Abi Talib sent a proposal of marriage to the daughter of Abu Jahl in spite of (the fact that his wife) Fatima (had been living in his house). Thereupon I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) say while addressing the people on the pulpit. I was adolescing in those days. He said: Fatima is a part of me and I fear that she may be put to trial in regard to religion. He then made a mention of his son-in law who had been from the tribe of 'Abd Shams and praised his behaviour as a son-in-law and said: Whatever he said to me he told the truth and whatever he promised he fulfilled it for me. I am not going to declare forbidden what is lawful and make lawful what is forbidden, but, by Allah, the daaghter of Allah's Messenger and the daughter of the enemy of Allah can never be combined at one place

muslim:6309.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was not exempting his daughter from the law of polygyny in [Quran 4:3](quran://4/3), claiming he affirmed that he did not forbid what is lawful and objected only because the proposed bride was the daughter of Abu Jahl, the enemy of Allah. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad feared Fatima would be put to trial in her religion (`أَتَخَوَّفُ أَنْ تُفْتَنَ فِي دِينِهَا`) by Ali's proposal (`خَطَبَ بِنْتَ أَبِي جَهْلٍ عَلَى فَاطِمَةَ`) and immediately followed his disclaimer (`لَسْتُ أُحَرِّمُ حَلاَلاً`) with a public oath (`وَاللَّهِ لاَ تَجْتَمِعُ بِنْتُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ وَبِنْتُ عَدُوِّ اللَّهِ مَكَانًا وَاحِدًا أَبَدًا`) prohibiting the union. By recognizing that polygyny threatens a wife's religious stability while praising his son-in-law from Banu 'Abd Shams for fulfilling his promise (`وَوَعَدَنِي فَأَوْفَى لِي`), the text demonstrates that Muhammad used his pulpit authority to protect his own daughter from a trial that his law permits for other women.

muslim:4552.note: After Muhammad burned and cut down the date-palms of Banu Nadir at Buwaira, [Quran 59:5](quran://59/5) was subsequently revealed to declare that cutting down the trees or leaving them standing occurred "with the permission of Allah so that He may disgrace the evil-doers."

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَرَّقَ نَخْلَ بَنِي النَّضِيرِ وَقَطَعَ وَهِيَ الْبُوَيْرَةُ ‏.‏ زَادَ قُتَيْبَةُ وَابْنُ رُمْحٍ فِي حَدِيثِهِمَا فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ‏{‏ مَا قَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ لِينَةٍ أَوْ تَرَكْتُمُوهَا قَائِمَةً عَلَى أُصُولِهَا فَبِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَلِيُخْزِيَ الْفَاسِقِينَ‏}‏
problematic_excerpt.english: It is narrated on the authority of 'Abdullah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the date-palms of Banu Nadir to be burnt and cut. These palms were at Buwaira. Qutaibah and Ibn Rumh in their versions of the tradition have added:So Allah, the Glorious and Exalted, revealed the verse:" Whatever trees you have cut down or left standing on their trunks, it was with the permission of Allah so that He may disgrace the evil-doers" (lix)

muslim:4552.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islamic rules of warfare prohibit destroying trees and crops, claiming the cutting of the date-palms at Buwaira was a restrained tactical measure enacted under prior divine directive. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Messenger of Allah first burned and cut down the date-palms of Banu Nadir (حَرَّقَ نَخْلَ بَنِي النَّضِيرِ وَقَطَعَ), and subsequently (فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ) Allah revealed [Quran 59:5](quran://59/5) declaring that whatever trees were cut down or left standing on their trunks was "with the permission of Allah so that He may disgrace the evil-doers." This chronological sequence in the narration—corroborated by parallel reports in bukhari:4031, bukhari:4884, and muslim:4553—demonstrates that the verse was revealed after the destruction had already occurred to validate the burning and cutting of the palms.

muslim:6262.note: Abdullah ibn Umar reports that they called Zaid bin Haritha solely by the name 'Zaid bin Muhammad' until [Quran 33:5](quran://33/5) was revealed commanding that individuals be called by their fathers' names instead, revoking his adoptive attribution to Muhammad (bukhari:4782, muslim:6263).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: مَا كُنَّا نَدْعُو زَيْدَ بْنَ حَارِثَةَ إِلاَّ زَيْدَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ حَتَّى نَزَلَ الْقُرْآنُ ‏{‏ ادْعُوهُمْ لآبَائِهِمْ هُوَ أَقْسَطُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ‏}‏
problematic_excerpt.english: We were in the habit of calling Zaid b. Harith as Zaid b. Muhammad until it was revealed in the Qur'an:" Call them by the names of their fathers. This is more equitable with Allah"

muslim:6262.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that [Quran 33:5](quran://33/5) was revealed to preserve biological lineage and truth in genealogical attribution while still permitting the care of orphans. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the community knew him solely as Muhammad's son—*mā kunnā nadʿū Zayda bna Ḥārithata illā Zayda bna Muḥammadin* ("We were not in the habit of calling Zaid bin Haritha anything except Zaid bin Muhammad")—until the verse nullified his adoptive name ([Quran 33:5](quran://33/5); cf. `bukhari:4782`, `muslim:6263`). Rather than merely recording genealogy, this revocation of legal adoption provided the exact legal mechanism in [Quran 33:37](quran://33/37) for Muhammad to marry Zaid's divorced wife, Zaynab bint Jahsh, in contrast to the New Testament elevation of adoption as true filial standing ([Romans 8:15](bible://rom/8/15)).

muslim:6207.note: When Muhammad stands up to pray over the deceased Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Umar grabs his garment and objects that Allah forbade praying over him, to which Muhammad replies that [Quran 9:80](quran://9/80) gave him a choice and states that he will ask forgiveness more than seventy times. Despite Umar repeating that the man was a hypocrite, Muhammad performs the funeral prayer over him, after which [Quran 9:84](quran://9/84) is revealed prohibiting him from ever praying over deceased hypocrites or standing at their graves (bukhari:4671; muslim:6208).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِيُصَلِّيَ عَلَيْهِ فَقَامَ عُمَرُ فَأَخَذَ بِثَوْبِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَتُصَلِّي عَلَيْهِ وَقَدْ نَهَاكَ اللَّهُ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّمَا خَيَّرَنِيَ اللَّهُ فَقَالَ ‏{‏ اسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ أَوْ لاَ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ إِنْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً‏}‏ وَسَأَزِيدُ عَلَى سَبْعِينَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ إِنَّهُ مُنَافِقٌ ‏.‏ فَصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ‏{‏ وَلاَ تُصَلِّ عَلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ مَاتَ أَبَدًا وَلاَ تَقُمْ عَلَى قَبْرِهِ‏}‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) stood up to say prayer over him Thereupon I Umar caught hold of the clothe of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said:Allah's Messenger, are you going to offer prayer, whereas Allah has forbidden to offer prayer for him, whereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Allah has given me a choice saying: Ask forgiveness for them or you may not ask for them; even if you ask for them seventy times, I will make an addition to the seventy. He was a hypocrite and Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said prayer over him that Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, revealed the verse:" And never pray over any one of them that has died and never should you stand by his grave" (ix)

muslim:6207.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was exercising prophetic mercy and permissible discretion before a final prohibition was revealed, claiming [Quran 9:80](quran://9/80) initially granted him the option to intercede for Abdullah ibn Ubayy. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Umar grabbed Muhammad's garment (فَأَخَذَ بِثَوْبِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ) and protested that Allah had already forbidden the prayer (وَقَدْ نَهَاكَ اللَّهُ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَيْهِ), whereas Muhammad treated the seventy-times clause in [Quran 9:80](quran://9/80) as a literal threshold he could bypass by adding to seventy (وَسَأَزِيدُ عَلَى سَبْعِينَ). After Muhammad prayed over him despite Umar's warning that the man was a hypocrite (إِنَّهُ مُنَافِقٌ), [Quran 9:84](quran://9/84) (وَلاَ تُصَلِّ عَلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ مَاتَ أَبَدًا) was revealed to overrule Muhammad's choice and codify Umar's exact objection into scripture (see also bukhari:4671).

bukhari:5237.note: When Umar recognized Muhammad's wife Sawda bint Zam'a going out at night and told her she was not hidden from them, she reported it to Muhammad while he was eating supper with a meat-covered bone in his hand, whereupon he immediately received a revelation declaring that Allah permitted women to go out for their needs. While parallel reports specify that this confrontation occurred after the veil was instituted (bukhari:4795; muslim:5668) and others state it prompted the verse of the veil itself ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53); bukhari:146), classical commentators harmonize the accounts by positing that Umar confronted Sawda on two separate occasions.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: خَرَجَتْ سَوْدَةُ بِنْتُ زَمْعَةَ لَيْلاً فَرَآهَا عُمَرُ فَعَرَفَهَا فَقَالَ إِنَّكِ وَاللَّهِ يَا سَوْدَةُ مَا تَخْفَيْنَ عَلَيْنَا، فَرَجَعَتْ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَذَكَرَتْ ذَلِكَ لَهُ، وَهْوَ فِي حُجْرَتِي يَتَعَشَّى، وَإِنَّ فِي يَدِهِ لَعَرْقًا، فَأُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ فَرُفِعَ عَنْهُ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ قَدْ أَذِنَ لَكُنَّ أَنْ تَخْرُجْنَ لِحَوَائِجِكُنَّ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Once Sa`da bint Zam`a went out at night for some need, and `Umar saw her, and recognizing her, he said (to her), "By Allah, O Sa`da! You cannot hide yourself from us." So she returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him while he was sitting in my dwelling taking his supper and holding a bone covered with meat in his hand. Then the Divine Inspiration was revealed to him and when that state was over, he (the Prophet (ﷺ) was saying: "O women! You have been allowed by Allah to go out for your needs

bukhari:5237.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Umar was merely expressing protective concern for the Prophet's wives, and that the ensuing revelation demonstrates divine mercy in safeguarding women's practical needs against overzealous strictness. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Umar accosted Sawda at night by declaring, 'By Allah, O Sawda, you cannot hide yourself from us' (إِنَّكِ وَاللَّهِ يَا سَوْدَةُ مَا تَخْفَيْنَ عَلَيْنَا)—which parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:146, 4795; muslim:5668) confirm occurred after the veil was already imposed (وَكَانَ حُجِبَ النِّسَاءُ) as Umar continued policing the wives on their way to the outdoor latrines. Instead of rebuking Umar for stalking and shaming his wife, Muhammad entered an immediate trance while still clutching his supper bone (وَإِنَّ فِي يَدِهِ لَعَرْقًا، فَأُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ) to deliver an ad-hoc divine decree merely permitting women to go out to relieve themselves (قَدْ أَذِنَ لَكُنَّ أَنْ تَخْرُجْنَ لِحَوَائِجِكُنَّ).

muslim:1167.note: Muhammad declares that among the six distinctions granting him superiority over previous prophets is that war spoils (*al-ghanāʾim*) were made lawful for him ([Quran 8:1](quran://8/1), [Quran 8:69](quran://8/69); cf. muslim:1163; contrast [Exodus 20:15](bible://ex/20/15), [Exodus 20:17](bible://ex/20/17)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فُضِّلْتُ عَلَى الأَنْبِيَاءِ بِسِتٍّ أُعْطِيتُ جَوَامِعَ الْكَلِمِ وَنُصِرْتُ بِالرُّعْبِ وَأُحِلَّتْ لِيَ الْغَنَائِمُ وَجُعِلَتْ لِيَ الأَرْضُ طَهُورًا وَمَسْجِدًا وَأُرْسِلْتُ إِلَى الْخَلْقِ كَافَّةً وَخُتِمَ بِيَ النَّبِيُّونَ
problematic_excerpt.english: I have been given superiority over the other prophets in six respects: I have been given words which are concise but comprehensive in meaning; I have been helped by terror (in the hearts of enemies): spoils have been made lawful to me: the earth has been made for me clean and a place of worship; I have been sent to all mankind and the line of prophets is closed with me

muslim:1167.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that permitting war spoils (*al-ghanāʾim*) was a merciful divine concession (*rukhṣah*) granted due to the early Muslim community's poverty and weakness rather than a financial incentive for conquest. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *'fuḍḍiltu ʿalā al-anbiyāʾi bi-sittin... wa uḥillat liya al-ghanāʾim'* ('I have been given superiority over the prophets in six respects... and spoils have been made lawful to me'), framing the confiscation of enemy wealth and captives as a mark of prophetic superiority (*tafḍīl*) over previous prophets, for whom taking plunder was strictly forbidden (bukhari:3122). Furthermore, [Quran 8:1](quran://8/1) and [Quran 8:41](quran://8/41) institutionalized this privilege by vesting ownership of the spoils in Muhammad and granting him a permanent one-fifth (*khums*) share of all conquered booty.

muslim:1167.note: Muhammad declares that he was given superiority over the other prophets in six respects, including being aided by terror (*nuṣirtu bi-l-ruʿb*) and being sent to all creation ([Quran 3:151](quran://3/151), [Quran 8:12](quran://8/12); contrast [Matthew 5:9](bible://mt/5/9), [John 18:36](bible://jn/18/36)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فُضِّلْتُ عَلَى الأَنْبِيَاءِ بِسِتٍّ أُعْطِيتُ جَوَامِعَ الْكَلِمِ وَنُصِرْتُ بِالرُّعْبِ وَأُحِلَّتْ لِيَ الْغَنَائِمُ وَجُعِلَتْ لِيَ الأَرْضُ طَهُورًا وَمَسْجِدًا وَأُرْسِلْتُ إِلَى الْخَلْقِ كَافَّةً وَخُتِمَ بِيَ النَّبِيُّونَ
problematic_excerpt.english: I have been given superiority over the other prophets in six respects: I have been given words which are concise but comprehensive in meaning; I have been helped by terror (in the hearts of enemies): spoils have been made lawful to me: the earth has been made for me clean and a place of worship; I have been sent to all mankind and the line of prophets is closed with me

muslim:1167.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *al-ruʿb* ('terror') refers merely to a bloodless psychological awe cast into hostile armies to deter attacks and prevent bloodshed during defensive warfare. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *'nuṣirtu bi-l-ruʿb wa uḥillat liya al-ghanāʾim... wa ursiltu ilā al-khalqi kāffatan'* ('I have been helped by terror, spoils have been made lawful to me... and I have been sent to all mankind'), linking this terror directly to the seizure of war plunder and universal expansion rather than local self-defense. Parallel narrations (bukhari:335; muslim:1163) and classical commentators like Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) confirm that this terror projected a full month's journey ahead of Muhammad's advancing armies against distant populations, matching [Quran 8:12](quran://8/12) where casting *al-ruʿb* is immediately coupled with the command to strike off heads and fingertips.

muslim:480.note: Declaring himself the leader of mankind on Resurrection Day, Muhammad states that while Adam, Noah, Abraham, and Moses each decline to intercede due to specific sins, Jesus—addressed as Allah's Word and a Spirit from Him—mentions no sin of his own (وَلَمْ يَذْكُرْ لَهُ ذَنْبًا; cf. [1 Peter 2:22](bible://1pt/2/22)) yet still says 'Myself, myself!' and directs humanity to Muhammad. Humanity then approaches Muhammad—whose past and future sins required Allah's forgiveness ([Quran 48:2](quran://48/2))—so that the supreme station of intercession (al-Maqām al-Maḥmūd) remains reserved for him rather than the sinless Messiah (contrast [1 John 2:1](bible://1jn/2/1), [Hebrews 7:25](bible://heb/7/25)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَيَقُولُ لَهُمْ عِيسَى صلى الله عليه وسلم إِنَّ رَبِّي قَدْ غَضِبَ الْيَوْمَ غَضَبًا لَمْ يَغْضَبْ قَبْلَهُ مِثْلَهُ وَلَنْ يَغْضَبَ بَعْدَهُ مِثْلَهُ - وَلَمْ يَذْكُرْ لَهُ ذَنْبًا - نَفْسِي نَفْسِي اذْهَبُوا إِلَى غَيْرِي اذْهَبُوا إِلَى مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَيَأْتُونِّي فَيَقُولُونَ يَا مُحَمَّدُ أَنْتَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَخَاتَمُ الأَنْبِيَاءِ وَغَفَرَ اللَّهُ لَكَ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ اشْفَعْ لَنَا إِلَى رَبِّكَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Jesus (peace be upon him) would say: Verily, my Lord is angry today as He had never been angry before or would ever be angry afterwards. He mentioned no sin of his. (He simply said: ) I am concerned with myself, I am concerned with myself; you go to someone else: better go to Muhammad (ﷺ). They would come to me and say: O Mahammad, thou art the messenger of Allah and the last of the apostles. Allah has pardoned thee all thy previous and later sins. Intercede for us with thy Lord

muslim:480.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that the Great Intercession (*al-Shafāʿah al-ʿUẓmā*) is simply a divinely decreed station (*al-Maqām al-Maḥmūd*, Quran 17:79) reserved exclusively for Muhammad, and that the prophets' cited faults were merely minor slips (*zallāt*) expressed out of humility rather than real sins violating prophetic infallibility (*ʿiṣmah*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the other prophets committed concrete transgressions—Adam's disobedience (*fa-ʿaṣaytuhu*), Abraham's lies (*kadhabātihi*), and Moses's uncommanded killing (*qataltu nafsan*)—while uniquely exempting Jesus with the words *'and he mentioned no sin'* (*wa-lam yadhkur lahu dhanban*). This exposes a glaring theological inversion within the narration itself: the sinless *'Word'* and *'Spirit'* from Allah (*kalimatun minhu... wa-rūḥun minhu*) is made to cry *'Myself, myself!'* (*nafsī nafsī*) in terror and send humanity to an intercessor who explicitly needed Allah to forgive *'what preceded of your sin and what followed'* (*mā taqaddama min dhanbika wa-mā taʾakhkhara*, cf. Quran 48:2).

bukhari:7420.note: [Quran 33:37](quran://33/37) is revealed concerning Zaynab and Zayd ibn Harithah, about which Aisha remarks that if the Prophet were to conceal anything of the revelation, he would have concealed this verse. Zaynab subsequently boasts to the Prophet's other wives that while their families gave them in marriage, Allah married her to him from above the seven heavens.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَكَانَتْ زَيْنَبُ تَفْخَرُ عَلَى أَزْوَاجِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم تَقُولُ زَوَّجَكُنَّ أَهَالِيكُنَّ، وَزَوَّجَنِي اللَّهُ تَعَالَى مِنْ فَوْقِ سَبْعِ سَمَوَاتٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: Zainab used to boast before the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) and used to say, "You were given in marriage by your families, while I was married (to the Prophet) by Allah from over seven Heavens."

bukhari:7420.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad had no personal desire for Zainab and that what he 'hid in his heart' (Quran 33:37) was merely divine foreknowledge of a reluctant legal duty to abolish the pre-Islamic taboo against marrying an adopted son's ex-wife. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states via Aisha that if Muhammad were to conceal anything of the Quran, he would have concealed this verse (لَوْ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَاتِمًا شَيْئًا لَكَتَمَ هَذِهِ)—an admission that makes no sense if the verse merely praised his reluctant obedience to a legal reform rather than exposing a personally embarrassing desire that made him 'fear the people' (وَتَخْشَى النَّاسَ). Moreover, as Ibn Hajar acknowledges in Fatḥ al-Bārī alongside early exegetes like Al-Ṭabarī, the episode culminated in Allah conveniently bypassing all earthly marriage requirements to contract Muhammad's marriage to his adopted son's ex-wife directly 'from over seven Heavens' (مِنْ فَوْقِ سَبْعِ سَمَوَاتٍ).

muslim:3507.note: After several men remained seated following the wedding feast for Zaynab bint Jahsh—leading Muhammad to walk twice to the door of Aisha's apartment thinking they had left—he drew a curtain between himself and Anas bin Malik once they departed, and Allah revealed the verse of the Hijab ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ أَنَسَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ قَالَ أَنَا أَعْلَمُ النَّاسِ، بِالْحِجَابِ لَقَدْ كَانَ أُبَىُّ بْنُ كَعْبٍ يَسْأَلُنِي عَنْهُ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَنَسٌ أَصْبَحَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَرُوسًا بِزَيْنَبَ بِنْتِ جَحْشٍ - قَالَ - وَكَانَ تَزَوَّجَهَا بِالْمَدِينَةِ فَدَعَا النَّاسَ لِلطَّعَامِ بَعْدَ ارْتِفَاعِ النَّهَارِ فَجَلَسَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَجَلَسَ مَعَهُ رِجَالٌ بَعْدَ مَا قَامَ الْقَوْمُ حَتَّى قَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَمَشَى فَمَشَيْتُ مَعَهُ حَتَّى بَلَغَ بَابَ حُجْرَةِ عَائِشَةَ ثُمَّ ظَنَّ أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ خَرَجُوا فَرَجَعَ وَرَجَعْتُ مَعَهُ فَإِذَا هُمْ جُلُوسٌ مَكَانَهُمْ فَرَجَعَ فَرَجَعْتُ الثَّانِيَةَ حَتَّى بَلَغَ حُجْرَةَ عَائِشَةَ فَرَجَعَ فَرَجَعْتُ فَإِذَا هُمْ قَدْ قَامُوا فَضَرَبَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ بِالسِّتْرِ وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ آيَةَ الْحِجَابِ.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I was the best informed among the people pertaining to Hijab (veil and seclusion). Ubayy b. Ka'b used to ask me about it. Anas (Allah be pleased with him) thus narrated: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) got up in the morning as a bridegroom of Zainab bint jahsh (Allah be pleased witt her) as he had married her at Medina. He invited people to the wedding feast after the day had well risen. There sat Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and there kept sitting along with him some persons after the people had stood up (for departure) ; then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) stood up and walked on and I also walked along with him until he reached the door of the apartment of 'A'isha (Allah be pleased with her). He then thought that they (those who had been sitting there after meal) had gone away. So he returned and I also returned with him, but they were still sitting at their places. So he returned for the second time and I also returned until he reached the apartment of 'A'isha. He again returned and I also returned and they had (by that time) stood up, and he hung a curtain between me and him (at the door of the apartment of Hadrat Zainab, where he had to stay), and Allah revealed the verse pertaining to veil

muslim:3507.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that this incident merely highlights Muhammad's extreme shyness (*ḥayā'*) and that [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53) was revealed to teach universal social etiquette and female modesty rather than to serve his personal convenience. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the verse descended on the exact morning he became a bridegroom to Zaynab bint Jahsh (`أَصْبَحَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَرُوسًا بِزَيْنَبَ بِنْتِ جَحْشٍ`) immediately after he paced back and forth twice waiting for lingering male guests to vacate his bridal chamber (`فَرَجَعَ فَرَجَعْتُ فَإِذَا هُمْ قَدْ قَامُوا فَضَرَبَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ بِالسِّتْرِ وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ آيَةَ الْحِجَابِ`). Furthermore, [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53) itself explicitly states it was revealed because lingering visitors 'annoyed the Prophet, and he is shy of dismissing you' (`إِنَّ ذَٰلِكُمْ كَانَ يُؤْذِي النَّبِيَّ فَيَسْتَحْيِي مِنكُمْ`), turning Muhammad's wedding-day frustration into eternal divine law that secluded his wives behind a curtain (`السِّتْرِ`) and forbade anyone from ever marrying his widows.

muslim:3508.note: After wedding guests lingered talking in Muhammad's house while his bride sat facing the wall—weighing heavily upon him until they realized it and departed—Muhammad entered behind a curtain for a brief while before coming out to recite the newly revealed [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53), which commands believers to disperse promptly after meals without lingering for conversation and instituted the seclusion (*hijab*) of his wives.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَجَلَسَ طَوَائِفُ مِنْهُمْ يَتَحَدَّثُونَ فِي بَيْتِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم جَالِسٌ وَزَوْجَتُهُ مُوَلِّيَةٌ وَجْهَهَا إِلَى الْحَائِطِ فَثَقُلُوا عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَخَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَسَلَّمَ عَلَى نِسَائِهِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَدْ رَجَعَ ظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ ثَقُلُوا عَلَيْهِ - قَالَ - فَابْتَدَرُوا الْبَابَ فَخَرَجُوا كُلُّهُمْ وَجَاءَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم َتَّى أَرْخَى السِّتْرَ وَدَخَلَ وَأَنَا جَالِسٌ فِي الْحُجْرَةِ فَلَمْ يَلْبَثْ إِلاَّ يَسِيرًا حَتَّى خَرَجَ عَلَىَّ ‏.‏ وَأُنْزِلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ فَخَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَقَرَأَهُنَّ عَلَى النَّاسِ ‏{‏ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لاَ تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلَى طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ نَاظِرِينَ إِنَاهُ وَلَكِنْ إِذَا دُعِيتُمْ فَادْخُلُوا فَإِذَا طَعِمْتُمْ فَانْتَشِرُوا وَلاَ مُسْتَأْنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍ إِنَّ ذَلِكُمْ كَانَ يُؤْذِي النَّبِيَّ‏}‏ إِلَى آخِرِ الآيَةِ ‏.‏ قَالَ الْجَعْدُ قَالَ أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ أَنَا أَحْدَثُ النَّاسِ عَهْدًا بِهَذِهِ الآيَاتِ وَحُجِبْنَ نِسَاءُ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A group among them (the guests) began to talk in the house of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting and his wife had been sitting with her face turned towards the wall. It was troublesome for Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), so Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) went out and greeted his wives. He then returned. When they (the guests) saw that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) had returned they thought that it (their overstay) was something troublesome for him. He (the narrator) said: They hastened towards the door and all of them went out. And there came Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and he hung a curtain and went in, and I was sitting in his apartment and he did not stay but for a short while. He then came to me and these verses were revealed. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) came out and recited them to the people:" O you who believe, enter not the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you for a meal, not waiting for its cooking being finished-but when you are invited, enter, and when you have taken food, disperse not seeking to listen to talk. Surely this gives the Prophet trouble", to the end of verse (xxxiii. 53). (Al-Ja'd said that Anas [b. Malik] stated: I am the first amongst the people to hear these verses), and henceforth the wives of the Apostle (ﷺ) began to observe seclusion (al-hijab)

muslim:3508.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists (citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*) typically argue that [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53) was revealed not for Muhammad's personal convenience, but to teach an uncouth society general Islamic social etiquette (*ādāb*) because Muhammad's extreme shyness (*ḥayāʾ*) prevented him from dismissing his guests. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the verse descended immediately (`فَلَمْ يَلْبَثْ إِلاَّ يَسِيرًا`) after the lingering guests burdened Muhammad (`فَثَقُلُوا عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ`) while his bride sat facing the wall (`وَزَوْجَتُهُ مُوَلِّيَةٌ وَجْهَهَا إِلَى الْحَائِطِ`), and the verse itself specifically targets the "houses of the Prophet" (`بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ`), imposes seclusion exclusively on his wives (`وَحُجِبْنَ نِسَاءُ النَّبِيِّ`), and concludes by forbidding believers from ever marrying his widows—proving that eternal divine revelation was deployed on the spot to resolve Muhammad's domestic irritation and secure his exclusive marital privileges.

bukhari:6239.note: When guests remained sitting and conversing after a meal celebrating Muhammad's marriage to Zainab despite his signaling to rise, he exited and returned only after they departed, lowering a screen (hijab) between himself and Anas as [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53) was revealed instructing believers not to enter the Prophet's houses.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَمَّا تَزَوَّجَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم زَيْنَبَ دَخَلَ الْقَوْمُ فَطَعِمُوا، ثُمَّ جَلَسُوا يَتَحَدَّثُونَ فَأَخَذَ كَأَنَّهُ يَتَهَيَّأُ لِلْقِيَامِ فَلَمْ يَقُومُوا، فَلَمَّا رَأَى ذَلِكَ قَامَ، فَلَمَّا قَامَ قَامَ مَنْ قَامَ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ وَقَعَدَ بَقِيَّةُ الْقَوْمِ، وَإِنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم جَاءَ لِيَدْخُلَ، فَإِذَا الْقَوْمُ جُلُوسٌ، ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ قَامُوا فَانْطَلَقُوا فَأَخْبَرْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَجَاءَ حَتَّى دَخَلَ، فَذَهَبْتُ أَدْخُلُ فَأَلْقَى الْحِجَابَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ، وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ‏{‏يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لاَ تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ‏}‏ الآيَةَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When the Prophet (ﷺ) married Zainab, the people came and were offered a meal, and then they sat down (after finishing their meals) and started chatting.
