The Prophet (ﷺ) showed as if he wanted to get up, but they did not get up. When he noticed that, he got up, and some of the people also got up and went away, while some others kept on sitting. When the Prophet (ﷺ) returned to enter, he found the people still sitting, but then they got up and left. So I told the Prophet (ﷺ) of their departure and he came and went in. I intended to go in but the Prophet (ﷺ) put a screen between me and him, for Allah revealed:-- 'O you who believe! Enter not the Prophet's houses

bukhari:6239.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Quran 33:53 (as framed in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*) demonstrates Muhammad's extraordinary prophetic modesty (*ḥayā'*), claiming that because he was too polite to dismiss lingering guests, God intervened on his behalf to teach the community general social etiquette. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that right after Muhammad paced out and back waiting for the wedding guests with Zainab to leave (`فَأَخَذَ كَأَنَّهُ يَتَهَيَّأُ لِلْقِيَامِ فَلَمْ يَقُومُوا`) and they finally departed, he immediately dropped the curtain (`فَأَلْقَى الْحِجَابَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ`) and announced the revelation of Quran 33:53 (`لاَ تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ`). Enshrining an awkward wedding-night inconvenience into the eternal, uncreated speech of God—while using the exact same verse to permanently ban all men from ever marrying Muhammad's widows—directly corroborates Aisha's observation in `bukhari:4788` that his Lord always hastened to fulfill his personal desires.

muslim:4912.note: When the opening of [Quran 4:95](quran://4/95) declaring that believers who sit at home are not equal is initially revealed, Ibn Umm Maktum speaks to Muhammad—complaining of his blindness as detailed in the parallel report muslim:4911—whereupon the exception clause exempting the disabled is revealed.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَمَّا نَزَلَتْ ‏{‏ لاَ يَسْتَوِي الْقَاعِدُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ‏}‏ كَلَّمَهُ ابْنُ أُمِّ مَكْتُومٍ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏ غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ‏}‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When the Qur'anic verse:" Those who sit (at home) from among mu'min" (iv. 94) was revealed, the son of Umm Maktum spoke to him (the Holy Prophet). (At this). the words:" other than those who have a trouble (illness)" were revealed

muslim:4912.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the exemption in [Quran 4:95](quran://4/95) was eternally decreed, and that revealing it in stages after Ibn Umm Maktum's inquiry merely reflects divine wisdom in addressing the community's needs progressively. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the initial verse was revealed (`لَمَّا نَزَلَتْ { لاَ يَسْتَوِي الْقَاعِدُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ}`) without any exception, and only after Ibn Umm Maktum spoke to him (`كَلَّمَهُ ابْنُ أُمِّ مَكْتُومٍ`) did the qualifying clause (`فَنَزَلَتْ { غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ}`) come down as a direct, immediate consequence (`فَـ`). This chronological cause-and-effect sequence shows the text of [Quran 4:95](quran://4/95) being modified in real time only after a human companion raised a concern about the initial unqualified statement.

muslim:6614.note: When two visitors anger Muhammad (*fa-aghḍabāhu*), he curses and insults them both (*fa-laʿanahumā wa-sabbahumā*), prompting Aisha to state that they will never attain any good. Despite declaring in the immediately preceding reports that cursers cannot be witnesses or intercessors on the Day of Resurrection (muslim:6612) and that he was not sent as a curser (muslim:6613), Muhammad tells Aisha that he has stipulated a condition with Allah (*shāraṭtu ʿalayhi rabbī*) converting any curse or insult he utters against a Muslim as a human being into purification and reward (cf. bukhari:6361, muslim:6615, muslim:6616).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: دَخَلَ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَجُلاَنِ فَكَلَّمَاهُ بِشَىْءٍ لاَ أَدْرِي مَا هُوَ فَأَغْضَبَاهُ فَلَعَنَهُمَا وَسَبَّهُمَا فَلَمَّا خَرَجَا قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ مَنْ أَصَابَ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ شَيْئًا مَا أَصَابَهُ هَذَانِ قَالَ ‏"‏ وَمَا ذَاكِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ قُلْتُ لَعَنْتَهُمَا وَسَبَبْتَهُمَا قَالَ ‏"‏ أَوَمَا عَلِمْتِ مَا شَارَطْتُ عَلَيْهِ رَبِّي قُلْتُ اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّمَا أَنَا بَشَرٌ فَأَىُّ الْمُسْلِمِينَ لَعَنْتُهُ أَوْ سَبَبْتُهُ فَاجْعَلْهُ لَهُ زَكَاةً وَأَجْرًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha reported that two persons visited Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and both of them talked about a thing, of which I am not aware, but that annoyed him and he invoked curse upon both of them and hurled malediction, and when they went out I said:Allah's Messenger, the good would reach everyone but it would not reach these two. He said: Why so? I said: Because you have invoked curse and hurled malediction upon both of them. He said: Don't you know that I have made condition with my Lord saying thus: O Allah, I am a human being and that for a Muslim upon whom I invoke curse or hurl malediction make it a source of purity and reward

muslim:6614.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's words were either harmless Arabic idioms not meant as literal curses, a justified rebuke of deserving offenders, or a display of humility in acknowledging his human nature (*innamā anā bashar*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the two visitors angered him so he cursed them and insulted them (*fa-aghḍabāhu fa-laʿanahumā wa-sabbahumā*), and Aisha immediately understood his outburst as a literal malediction that would deprive them of all good by protesting, 'whoever attains any good, these two will never attain it' (*man aṣāba min al-khayri shayʾan mā aṣābahu hādhāni*). Rather than claiming the men deserved the abuse or that his words were merely idiomatic, Muhammad invokes a special stipulation with his Lord (*mā shāraṭtu ʿalayhi rabbī*) covering 'whichever of the Muslims I have cursed or insulted' (*fa-ayyu al-muslimīna laʿantuhu aw sababtuhu*), confirming that he directed real curses and verbal insults at fellow Muslims in anger and relied on a prophetic exemption to reclassify them as 'purification and a reward' (*zakātan wa-ajran*).

bukhari:4791.note: At the wedding feast of Muhammad and Zaynab bint Jahsh (AD 627), three guests remained sitting and conversing even after Muhammad signaled to rise and stepped out, prompting him upon their departure to draw a curtain (`hijab`) between himself and Anas ibn Malik. Immediately thereafter, [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53) was revealed forbidding believers from entering the Prophet's houses without permission or lingering after a meal and instituting the seclusion of his wives.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَمَّا تَزَوَّجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم زَيْنَبَ ابْنَةَ جَحْشٍ دَعَا الْقَوْمَ، فَطَعِمُوا ثُمَّ جَلَسُوا يَتَحَدَّثُونَ وَإِذَا هُوَ كَأَنَّهُ يَتَهَيَّأُ لِلْقِيَامِ فَلَمْ يَقُومُوا، فَلَمَّا رَأَى ذَلِكَ قَامَ، فَلَمَّا قَامَ قَامَ مَنْ قَامَ، وَقَعَدَ ثَلاَثَةُ نَفَرٍ فَجَاءَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِيَدْخُلَ فَإِذَا الْقَوْمُ جُلُوسٌ ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ قَامُوا، فَانْطَلَقْتُ فَجِئْتُ فَأَخْبَرْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُمْ قَدِ انْطَلَقُوا، فَجَاءَ حَتَّى دَخَلَ، فَذَهَبْتُ أَدْخُلُ فَأَلْقَى الْحِجَابَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ ‏{‏يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لاَ تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ‏}‏ الآيَةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) married Zainab bint Jahsh, he invited the people to a meal. They took the meal and remained sitting and talking. Then the Prophet (showed them) as if he is ready to get up, yet they did not get up. When he noticed that (there was no response to his movement), he got up, and the others too, got up except three persons who kept on sitting. The Prophet (ﷺ) came back in order to enter his house, but he went away again. Then they left, whereupon I set out and went to the Prophet (ﷺ) to tell him that they had departed, so he came and entered his house. I wanted to enter along with him, but he put a screen between me and him. Then Allah revealed: 'O you who believe! Do not enter the houses of the Prophet

bukhari:4791.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Quran 33:53 was not a self-serving convenience, but a broader communal lesson in domestic etiquette revealed because Muhammad's extraordinary shyness (ḥayāʾ), as noted by Ibn Hajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī, prevented him from dismissing the lingering wedding guests himself. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the revelation descended at the exact moment Muhammad dropped the curtain to shut out even his own servant Anas and be alone with his new bride Zainab (فَأَلْقَى الْحِجَابَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ — 'he put a screen between me and him, and then Allah revealed...'), directly resolving his immediate personal frustration. Moreover, [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53) goes far beyond general manners by explicitly centering on what personally annoyed Muhammad (إِنَّ ذَٰلِكُمْ كَانَ يُؤْذِي النَّبِيَّ) and coupling the dismissal of his guests with permanent, exclusive prophetic privileges—secluding his wives behind a physical partition (حِجَابٍ) and forbidding anyone from ever marrying his widows after his death.

bukhari:4792.note: When wedding guests remained sitting and conversing in Muhammad's house while his newlywed wife Zainab bint Jahsh was inside, Muhammad repeatedly went out and returned while they continued talking. Allah then revealed [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53)—forbidding believers from entering the Prophet's houses for a meal without permission and mandating that his wives be addressed from behind a screen (*hijab*)—whereupon the screen was set up and the guests departed.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَمَّا أُهْدِيَتْ زَيْنَبُ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَتْ مَعَهُ فِي الْبَيْتِ، صَنَعَ طَعَامًا، وَدَعَا الْقَوْمَ، فَقَعَدُوا يَتَحَدَّثُونَ، فَجَعَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَخْرُجُ، ثُمَّ يَرْجِعُ، وَهُمْ قُعُودٌ يَتَحَدَّثُونَ، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ‏{‏يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لاَ تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلَى طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ نَاظِرِينَ إِنَاهُ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏{‏مِنْ وَرَاءِ حِجَابٍ‏}‏ فَضُرِبَ الْحِجَابُ، وَقَامَ الْقَوْمُ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) married Zainab bint Jahsh she was with him in the house and he prepared a meal and invited the people (to it). They sat down (after finishing their meal) and started chatting. So the Prophet (ﷺ) went out and then returned several times while they were still sitting and talking. So Allah revealed the Verse: 'O you who believe! Enter not the Prophet's houses until leave is given to you for a meal, (and then) not (so early as) to wait for its preparation .....ask them from behind a screen.' (33.53) So the screen was set up and the people went away

bukhari:4792.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists, citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī, typically argue that Quran 33:53 was revealed to establish universal Islamic visiting etiquette because Muhammad's profound modesty (ḥayā') prevented him from rudely asking lingering guests to leave his home. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah delivered this supposedly eternal, uncreated legislation (فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى... لاَ تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ) on the spot solely because Muhammad kept pacing in and out (يَخْرُجُ، ثُمَّ يَرْجِعُ) waiting for chatting dinner guests (وَهُمْ قُعُودٌ يَتَحَدَّثُونَ) to vacate the chamber where his newlywed bride—his adopted son's former wife, Zainab bint Jahsh (لَمَّا أُهْدِيَتْ زَيْنَبُ)—was waiting inside. Far from general hospitality laws, the revelation exclusively regulates the 'houses of the Prophet' (بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ), immediately clears the room behind a drawn curtain (فَضُرِبَ الْحِجَابُ، وَقَامَ الْقَوْمُ), and bans anyone from ever marrying his widows after his death, reducing divine revelation to a personal domestic convenience that famously prompted Aisha to remark in bukhari:4788, 'I see that your Lord hastens in fulfilling your desires.'

bukhari:4793.note: Following his wedding banquet with Zainab bint Jahsh, three guests lingered in the house chatting while Muhammad—described as intensely shy (`شَدِيدَ الْحَيَاءِ`)—repeatedly left to visit his other wives' apartments rather than ask them to leave. Once the men departed, Muhammad returned, drew a curtain between himself and Anas, and the Verse of Hijab ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53)) was immediately revealed to reprimand lingering guests and mandate speaking to his wives from behind a partition.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: بُنِيَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِزَيْنَبَ ابْنَةِ جَحْشٍ بِخُبْزٍ وَلَحْمٍ فَأُرْسِلْتُ عَلَى الطَّعَامِ دَاعِيًا فَيَجِيءُ قَوْمٌ فَيَأْكُلُونَ وَيَخْرُجُونَ، ثُمَّ يَجِيءُ قَوْمٌ فَيَأْكُلُونَ وَيَخْرُجُونَ، فَدَعَوْتُ حَتَّى مَا أَجِدُ أَحَدًا أَدْعُو فَقُلْتُ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ مَا أَجِدُ أَحَدًا أَدْعُوهُ قَالَ ارْفَعُوا طَعَامَكُمْ، وَبَقِيَ ثَلاَثَةُ رَهْطٍ يَتَحَدَّثُونَ فِي الْبَيْتِ، فَخَرَجَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَانْطَلَقَ إِلَى حُجْرَةِ عَائِشَةَ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ وَعَلَيْكَ السَّلاَمُ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ، كَيْفَ وَجَدْتَ أَهْلَكَ بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكَ فَتَقَرَّى حُجَرَ نِسَائِهِ كُلِّهِنَّ، يَقُولُ لَهُنَّ كَمَا يَقُولُ لِعَائِشَةَ، وَيَقُلْنَ لَهُ كَمَا قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ، ثُمَّ رَجَعَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَإِذَا ثَلاَثَةُ رَهْطٍ فِي الْبَيْتِ يَتَحَدَّثُونَ، وَكَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم شَدِيدَ الْحَيَاءِ، فَخَرَجَ مُنْطَلِقًا نَحْوَ حُجْرَةِ عَائِشَةَ فَمَا أَدْرِي آخْبَرْتُهُ أَوْ أُخْبِرَ أَنَّ الْقَوْمَ خَرَجُوا، فَرَجَعَ حَتَّى إِذَا وَضَعَ رِجْلَهُ فِي أُسْكُفَّةِ الْبَابِ دَاخِلَةً وَأُخْرَى خَارِجَةً أَرْخَى السِّتْرَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ، وَأُنْزِلَتْ آيَةُ الْحِجَابِ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A banquet of bread and meat was held on the occasion of the marriage of the Prophet (ﷺ) to Zainab bint Jahsh. I was sent to invite the people (to the banquet), and so the people started coming (in groups); They would eat and then leave. Another batch would come, eat and leave. So I kept on inviting the people till I found nobody to invite. Then I said, "O Allah's Prophet! I do not find anybody to invite." He said, "Carry away the remaining food." Then a batch of three persons stayed in the house chatting. The Prophet (ﷺ) left and went towards the dwelling place of Aisha and said, "Peace and Allah's Mercy be on you, O the people of the house!" She replied, "Peace and the mercy of Allah be on you too. How did you find your wife? May Allah bless you. Then he went to the dwelling places of all his other wives and said to them the same as he said to Aisha and they said to him the same as Aisha had said to him. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) returned and found a group of three persons still in the house chatting. The Prophet was a very shy person, so he went out (for the second time) and went towards the dwelling place of `Aisha. I do not remember whether I informed him that the people have gone away. So he returned and as soon as he entered the gate, he drew the curtain between me and him, and then the Verse of Al-Hijab was revealed

bukhari:4793.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this incident—as framed in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's commentary—merely highlights Muhammad's noble shyness (*shadīd al-ḥayā'*) and that Quran 33:53 was revealed to institute general social etiquette (*adab*) rather than to serve his personal convenience. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Verse of Hijab was revealed (*وَأُنْزِلَتْ آيَةُ الْحِجَابِ*) at the exact moment Muhammad grew frustrated waiting to consummate his marriage with Zainab bint Jahsh because three dinner guests lingered chatting in the room (*ثَلاَثَةُ رَهْطٍ يَتَحَدَّثُونَ فِي الْبَيْتِ*), right as he stepped across the threshold and drew the curtain between himself and Anas (*أَرْخَى السِّتْرَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ*). Thus, an eternal Quranic statute mandating the seclusion of women behind a barrier (*ḥijāb*) and ordering guests to disperse immediately after eating (Quran 33:53) was triggered on the spot as a convenient divine intervention to clear Muhammad's bridal chamber in AD 627.

bukhari:4794.note: After hosting the wedding banquet for his marriage to Zainab bint Jahsh and visiting his other wives' chambers, Muhammad returned home to find two men still conversing and turned back outside until they hurriedly departed. Upon re-entering, he lowered a curtain between himself and Anas ibn Malik, marking the occasion of revelation for the Verse of the Hijab ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53)) instructing guests to disperse after eating and to address his wives from behind a partition.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَوْلَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حِينَ بَنَى بِزَيْنَبَ ابْنَةِ جَحْشٍ فَأَشْبَعَ النَّاسَ خُبْزًا وَلَحْمًا ثُمَّ خَرَجَ إِلَى حُجَرِ أُمَّهَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كَمَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ صَبِيحَةَ بِنَائِهِ فَيُسَلِّمُ عَلَيْهِنَّ وَيَدْعُو لَهُنَّ وَيُسَلِّمْنَ عَلَيْهِ وَيَدْعُونَ لَهُ فَلَمَّا رَجَعَ إِلَى بَيْتِهِ رَأَى رَجُلَيْنِ جَرَى بِهِمَا الْحَدِيثُ، فَلَمَّا رَآهُمَا رَجَعَ عَنْ بَيْتِهِ، فَلَمَّا رَأَى الرَّجُلاَنِ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَجَعَ عَنْ بَيْتِهِ وَثَبَا مُسْرِعَيْنِ، فَمَا أَدْرِي أَنَا أَخْبَرْتُهُ بِخُرُوجِهِمَا أَمْ أُخْبِرَ فَرَجَعَ حَتَّى دَخَلَ الْبَيْتَ، وَأَرْخَى السِّتْرَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ وَأُنْزِلَتْ آيَةُ الْحِجَابِ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) married Zainab bint Jahsh, he made the people eat meat and bread to their fill (by giving a Walima banquet). Then he went out to the dwelling places of the mothers of the believers (his wives), as he used to do in the morning of his marriage. He would greet them and invoke good on them, and they (too) would return his greeting and invoke good on him. When he returned to his house, he found two men talking to each other; and when he saw them, he went out of his house again. When those two men saw Allah's Messenger (ﷺ): going out of his house, they quickly got up (and departed). I do not remember whether I informed him of their departure, or he was informed (by somebody else). So he returned, and when he entered the house, he lowered the curtain between me and him. Then the Verse of Al-Hijab was revealed

bukhari:4794.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the Verse of the Hijab (Quran 33:53) was a timeless, objective legislation revealed to establish communal etiquette (adab) and protect domestic modesty, rather than a self-serving reaction to Muhammad's personal annoyance. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that only after two wedding guests lingered in conversation (جَرَى بِهِمَا الْحَدِيثُ)—causing Muhammad to repeatedly step out of his house until they hurriedly departed and he physically dropped the curtain (وَأَرْخَى السِّتْرَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ)—was the verse immediately revealed (وَأُنْزِلَتْ آيَةُ الْحِجَابِ). Crucially, Quran 33:53 verbatim codifies this exact domestic irritation by ordering dinner guests to disperse without lingering for conversation (وَلَا مُسْتَأْنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍ) because 'that was troubling the Prophet, and he is shy of dismissing you,' demonstrating how supposedly eternal divine revelation functioned to clear out Muhammad's house on his wedding day.

bukhari:5163.note: Following Muhammad's wedding feast with Zainab, after guests who had remained behind talking finally departed, Muhammad returned to his chamber, let the curtain fall, and recited [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53)—commanding believers not to enter his houses for a meal without permission and to disperse immediately after eating without lingering for conversation, as such behavior annoys the Prophet though he is shy to dismiss them.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَخَرَجْتُ فِي إِثْرِهِ فَقُلْتُ إِنَّهُمْ قَدْ ذَهَبُوا‏.‏ فَرَجَعَ فَدَخَلَ الْبَيْتَ، وَأَرْخَى السِّتْرَ، وَإِنِّي لَفِي الْحُجْرَةِ، وَهْوَ يَقُولُ ‏{‏يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لاَ تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلَى طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ نَاظِرِينَ إِنَاهُ وَلَكِنْ إِذَا دُعِيتُمْ فَادْخُلُوا فَإِذَا طَعِمْتُمْ فَانْتَشِرُوا وَلاَ مُسْتَأْنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍ إِنَّ ذَلِكُمْ كَانَ يُؤْذِي النَّبِيَّ فَيَسْتَحْيِي مِنْكُمْ وَاللَّهُ لاَ يَسْتَحْيِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ‏}‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I too, went out after him and told him that those people had left. Then he returned and entered his dwelling place and let the curtains fall while I was in (his) dwelling place, and he was reciting the Verses:-- 'O you who believe! Enter not the Prophet's house until leave is given you for a meal, (and then) not (as early as) to what for its preparation. But when you are invited, enter, and when you have taken your meals, disperse without sitting for a talk. Verily such (behavior) annoys the Prophet; and he would be shy of (asking) you (to go), but Allah is not shy of (telling you) the Truth.' (33-53)

bukhari:5163.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Quran 33:53 (as framed in Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī) was revealed to establish universal social etiquette (ādāb) and protect household privacy rather than to serve Muhammad's immediate personal convenience, often deflecting to the feeding of the crowd from a single dish of ḥaysa as proof of prophethood. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that this eternal Quranic legislation materialized at the exact moment Anas informed the bridegroom Muhammad ('arūsan bi-Zaynab) that the lingering guests had finally left (innahum qad dhahabū), whereupon he immediately dropped the curtain (wa-arkhā al-sitr) and recited a verse scolding visitors because their conversation 'annoyed the Prophet, and he would be shy of asking you to leave' (inna dhālikum kāna yuʾdhī al-nabiyya fa-yastaḥyī minkum). Parallel narrations in bukhari:4791–bukhari:4792 confirm that Muhammad's impatience to be alone with Zainab bint Jahsh on his wedding night was the direct sabab al-nuzūl (occasion of revelation) for the Verse of the Hijab, exposing how supposedly eternal divine scripture was instantaneously deployed as a domestic eviction notice to spare Muhammad social awkwardness.

bukhari:5166.note: Following his wedding banquet with Zainab bint Jahsh, a group of guests lingered at length, prompting Muhammad to twice walk out to the threshold of Aisha's quarters so that they would leave. Once they finally departed, he drew a curtain between himself and his servant Anas, and the verse of the Hijab ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53)) was revealed.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَكَانَ أَوَّلَ مَا أُنْزِلَ فِي مُبْتَنَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِزَيْنَبَ ابْنَةِ جَحْشٍ، أَصْبَحَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِهَا عَرُوسًا، فَدَعَا الْقَوْمَ فَأَصَابُوا مِنَ الطَّعَامِ، ثُمَّ خَرَجُوا وَبَقِيَ رَهْطٌ مِنْهُمْ عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَطَالُوا الْمُكْثَ، فَقَامَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَخَرَجَ وَخَرَجْتُ مَعَهُ لِكَىْ يَخْرُجُوا، فَمَشَى النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَمَشَيْتُ، حَتَّى جَاءَ عَتَبَةَ حُجْرَةِ عَائِشَةَ، ثُمَّ ظَنَّ أَنَّهُمْ خَرَجُوا فَرَجَعَ وَرَجَعْتُ مَعَهُ، حَتَّى إِذَا دَخَلَ عَلَى زَيْنَبَ فَإِذَا هُمْ جُلُوسٌ لَمْ يَقُومُوا، فَرَجَعَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَرَجَعْتُ مَعَهُ، حَتَّى إِذَا بَلَغَ عَتَبَةَ حُجْرَةِ عَائِشَةَ، وَظَنَّ أَنَّهُمْ خَرَجُوا، فَرَجَعَ وَرَجَعْتُ مَعَهُ فَإِذَا هُمْ قَدْ خَرَجُوا فَضَرَبَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ بِالسِّتْرِ، وَأُنْزِلَ الْحِجَابُ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: It was revealed for the first time when Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) had consummated his marriage with Zainab bint Jahsh. When the day dawned, the Prophet (ﷺ) was a bridegroom and he invited the people to a banquet, so they came, ate, and then all left except a few who remained with the Prophet (ﷺ) for a long time. The Prophet (ﷺ) got up and went out, and I too went out with him so that those people might leave too. The Prophet (ﷺ) proceeded and so did I, till he came to the threshold of `Aisha's dwelling place. Then thinking that these people have left by then, he returned and so did I along with him till he entered upon Zainab and behold, they were still sitting and had not gone. So the Prophet (ﷺ) again went away and I went away along with him. When we reached the threshold of `Aisha's dwelling place, he thought that they had left, and so he returned and I too, returned along with him and found those people had left. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) drew a curtain between me and him, and the Verses of Al-Hijab were revealed

bukhari:5166.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists (citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī) typically argue that the revelation of the Hijab verse (Quran 33:53) on this occasion merely showcased Muhammad's extraordinary shyness (ḥayā') in not wanting to dismiss lingering guests himself, while establishing timeless communal etiquette and modesty laws. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the revelation occurred directly because guests prolonged their stay (fa-aṭālū al-mukth) while Muhammad was a newlywed bridegroom ('arūsan) eager for privacy with Zainab bint Jahsh, causing him to pace back and forth until they left and immediately draw a physical curtain (fa-ḍaraba... bi-l-sitr) as the verse descended. Rather than addressing a universal spiritual crisis, Quran 33:53 intervened on the spot to resolve Muhammad's personal domestic annoyance at his wedding banquet, reprimanding his dinner guests for lingering while simultaneously forbidding anyone from ever marrying his wives after him.

bukhari:5466.note: Following his wedding meal with Zaynab bint Jahsh in Medina (AD 627), after several male guests remained sitting in his house, Muhammad twice walked out to the door of Aisha's room and back until they finally departed. Once they left, he hung a curtain between himself and Anas ibn Malik, and the verse of the Hijab ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53))—instructing guests to disperse after eating and to speak to his wives from behind a screen—was revealed.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَصْبَحَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَرُوسًا بِزَيْنَبَ ابْنَةِ جَحْشٍ وَكَانَ تَزَوَّجَهَا بِالْمَدِينَةِ، فَدَعَا النَّاسَ لِلطَّعَامِ بَعْدَ ارْتِفَاعِ النَّهَارِ، فَجَلَسَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَجَلَسَ مَعَهُ رِجَالٌ بَعْدَ مَا قَامَ الْقَوْمُ، حَتَّى قَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَمَشَى وَمَشَيْتُ مَعَهُ، حَتَّى بَلَغَ باب حُجْرَةِ عَائِشَةَ، ثُمَّ ظَنَّ أَنَّهُمْ خَرَجُوا فَرَجَعْتُ مَعَهُ، فَإِذَا هُمْ جُلُوسٌ مَكَانَهُمْ، فَرَجَعَ وَرَجَعْتُ مَعَهُ الثَّانِيَةَ، حَتَّى بَلَغَ باب حُجْرَةِ عَائِشَةَ فَرَجَعَ وَرَجَعْتُ مَعَهُ، فَإِذَا هُمْ قَامُوا، فَضَرَبَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ سِتْرًا، وَأُنْزِلَ الْحِجَابُ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) became the bridegroom of Zainab bint Jahsh whom he married at Medina. After the sun had risen high in the sky, the Prophet (ﷺ) invited the people to a meal. Allah's Apostle remained sitting and some people remained sitting with him after the other guests had left. Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) got up and went away, and I too, followed him till he reached the door of `Aisha's room. Then he thought that the people must have left the place by then, so he returned and I also returned with him. Behold, the people were still sitting at their places. So he went back again for the second time, and I went along with him too. When we reached the door of `Aisha's room, he returned and I also returned with him to see that the people had left. Thereupon the Prophet (ﷺ) hung a curtain between me and him and the Verse regarding the order for (veiling of women) Hijab was revealed

bukhari:5466.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Quran 33:53 (framed by Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* as a lesson in communal etiquette) was revealed merely to teach general manners because Muhammad was too modest (*ḥayā'*) to dismiss lingering guests himself, insisting the Hijab mandate was a timeless divine decree rather than a self-serving reaction to his personal frustration. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the revelation descended at the exact moment the men finally departed (*fa-idhā hum qāmū*) after Muhammad had twice paced out to Aisha's door waiting to be alone as a bridegroom with Zainab (*'arūsan bi-Zaynab*), whereupon he immediately dropped a curtain between himself and Anas (*fa-ḍaraba baynī wa-baynahu sitran wa-unzila al-ḥijāb*). Furthermore, Quran 33:53 itself exposes the immediate personal utility of the revelation by elevating Muhammad's domestic annoyance (*yu'dhī al-nabiyya*) into eternal cosmic law—simultaneously evicting his wedding guests, secluding his wives behind a physical barrier, and forbidding any man from ever marrying them after his death.

bukhari:6271.note: At Muhammad's wedding feast with Zainab bint Jahsh (AD 627), three guests remained sitting and talking in his house after eating even after he signaled to rise and stepped out, delaying his entry until they finally departed. Upon returning and entering, Muhammad dropped a curtain (*hijab*) between himself and Anas ibn Malik, at which point [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53) was revealed prohibiting believers from entering the Prophet's houses without permission and establishing the *hijab* partition.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَمَّا تَزَوَّجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم زَيْنَبَ ابْنَةَ جَحْشٍ دَعَا النَّاسَ طَعِمُوا ثُمَّ جَلَسُوا يَتَحَدَّثُونَ ـ قَالَ ـ فَأَخَذَ كَأَنَّهُ يَتَهَيَّأُ لِلْقِيَامِ فَلَمْ يَقُومُوا، فَلَمَّا رَأَى ذَلِكَ قَامَ، فَلَمَّا قَامَ قَامَ مَنْ قَامَ مَعَهُ مِنَ النَّاسِ، وَبَقِيَ ثَلاَثَةٌ، وَإِنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم جَاءَ لِيَدْخُلَ فَإِذَا الْقَوْمُ جُلُوسٌ، ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ قَامُوا فَانْطَلَقُوا ـ قَالَ ـ فَجِئْتُ فَأَخْبَرْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُمْ قَدِ انْطَلَقُوا، فَجَاءَ حَتَّى دَخَلَ فَذَهَبْتُ أَدْخُلُ، فَأَرْخَى الْحِجَابَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ، وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ‏{‏يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لاَ تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏{‏إِنَّ ذَلِكُمْ كَانَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَظِيمًا‏}‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) married Zainab bint Jahsh, he invited the people who took their meals and then remained sitting and talking. The Prophet (ﷺ) pretended to be ready to get up, but the people did not get up. When he noticed that, he got up, and when he had got up, some of those people got up along with him and there remained three (who kept on sitting). Then the Prophet (ﷺ) came back and found those people still sitting. Later on those people got up and went away. So I went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him that they had left. The Prophet (ﷺ) came, and entered (his house). I wanted to enter(along with him) but he dropped a curtain between me and him. Allah then revealed: 'O you who believe! Do not enter the Prophet's Houses until leave is given... (to His statement)... Verily! That shall be an enormity, in Allah's sight

bukhari:6271.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that this incident demonstrates Muhammad's exemplary modesty (*ḥayā'*) in being too polite to dismiss lingering guests and merely served as the occasion to legislate general household etiquette and privacy in [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that as soon as the three guests departed (`ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ قَامُوا فَانْطَلَقُوا`) so Muhammad could consummate his AD 627 marriage to Zainab bint Jahsh, he personally dropped the curtain against his servant Anas (`فَأَرْخَى الْحِجَابَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُ`), and Allah immediately sent down [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53) (`وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى`) to turn his private annoyance into eternal scripture. Far from mere universal etiquette, the revelation directly resolved Muhammad's personal domestic inconvenience while coupling the *ḥijāb* mandate with an exclusive prophetic privilege forbidding anyone from ever marrying his wives after his death as an 'enormity in Allah's sight' (`إِنَّ ذَلِكُمْ كَانَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَظِيمًا`).

bukhari:4912.note: After Aisha and Hafsa agreed to tell Muhammad that he smelled of *maghafir* resin because he stayed with Zaynab bint Jahsh to drink honey, Muhammad swore an oath never to drink it again and ordered that no one be told. Recorded in al-Bukhari's Book of Tafsir as the occasion of revelation (*sabab al-nuzul*) for [Quran 66:1](quran://66/1)-[4](quran://66/4), this domestic incident prompted verses releasing Muhammad from his oath and rebuking his wives (bukhari:5267, bukhari:6691).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَوَاطَيْتُ أَنَا وَحَفْصَةُ عَنْ أَيَّتُنَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا فَلْتَقُلْ لَهُ أَكَلْتَ مَغَافِيرَ إِنِّي أَجِدُ مِنْكَ رِيحَ مَغَافِيرَ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏ "‏ لاَ وَلَكِنِّي كُنْتُ أَشْرَبُ عَسَلاً عِنْدَ زَيْنَبَ ابْنَةِ جَحْشٍ فَلَنْ أَعُودَ لَهُ وَقَدْ حَلَفْتُ لاَ تُخْبِرِي بِذَلِكِ أَحَدًا ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: So Hafsa and I agreed secretly that, if he come to either of us, she would say to him. "It seems you have eaten Maghafir (a kind of bad-smelling resin), for I smell in you the smell of Maghafir," (We did so) and he replied. "No, but I was drinking honey in the house of Zainab, the daughter of Jahsh, and I shall never take it again. I have taken an oath as to that, and you should not tell anybody about it

bukhari:4912.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this incident—cited by Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* as the primary occasion for [Quran 66:1](quran://66/1)—proves Muhammad did not fabricate the Quran, claiming the opening verse rebukes him for prohibiting lawful honey merely to please his wives and avoid an unpleasant odor. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad bound himself by a rash oath (*wa-qad ḥalaftu*, وَقَدْ حَلَفْتُ) and demanded strict secrecy (*lā tukhbirī bi-dhālika aḥadan*, لاَ تُخْبِرِي بِذَلِكِ أَحَدًا) to navigate a domestic rivalry, only for the subsequent revelation ([Quran 66:1](quran://66/1)–[5](quran://66/5)) to conveniently absolve him of his own regretted vow while mobilizing Allah, Gabriel, and the angels to threaten Aisha and Hafsa with divorce and replacement by more submissive wives.

bukhari:6691.note: After Aisha and Hafsa agreed to tell Muhammad that they smelled maghafir on him because he drank honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh, he swore an oath in confidence never to drink it again. In response, [Quran 66:1](quran://66/1)-[4](quran://66/4) was revealed, questioning why he forbade what Allah had made lawful for him and calling Aisha and Hafsa to repentance.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ يَمْكُثُ عِنْدَ زَيْنَبَ بِنْتِ جَحْشٍ، وَيَشْرَبُ عِنْدَهَا عَسَلاً، فَتَوَاصَيْتُ أَنَا وَحَفْصَةُ أَنَّ أَيَّتَنَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلْتَقُلْ إِنِّي أَجِدُ مِنْكَ رِيحَ مَغَافِيرَ، أَكَلْتَ مَغَافِيرَ فَدَخَلَ عَلَى إِحْدَاهُمَا فَقَالَتْ ذَلِكَ لَهُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ بَلْ شَرِبْتُ عَسَلاً عِنْدَ زَيْنَبَ بِنْتِ جَحْشٍ، وَلَنْ أَعُودَ لَهُ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ‏}‏، ‏{‏إِنْ تَتُوبَا إِلَى اللَّهِ‏}‏، لِعَائِشَةَ وَحَفْصَةَ، ‏{‏وَإِذْ أَسَرَّ النَّبِيُّ إِلَى بَعْضِ أَزْوَاجِهِ حَدِيثًا‏}‏ لِقَوْلِهِ ‏"‏ بَلْ شَرِبْتُ عَسَلاً ‏"‏‏.‏ وَقَالَ لِي إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ مُوسَى عَنْ هِشَامٍ، ‏"‏ وَلَنْ أَعُودَ لَهُ، وَقَدْ حَلَفْتُ، فَلاَ تُخْبِرِي بِذَلِكَ أَحَدًا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to stay (for a period) in the house of Zainab bint Jahsh (one of the wives of the Prophet ) and he used to drink honey in her house. Hafsa and I decided that when the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon either of us, she would say, "I smell in you the bad smell of Maghafir (a bad smelling raisin). Have you eaten Maghafir?" When he entered upon one of us, she said that to him. He replied (to her), "No, but I have drunk honey in the house of Zainab bint Jahsh, and I will never drink it again." Then the following verse was revealed: 'O Prophet ! Why do you ban (for you) that which Allah has made lawful for you?. ..(up to) If you two (wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) turn in repentance to Allah.' (66.1-4) The two were `Aisha and Hafsa And also the Statement of Allah: 'And (Remember) when the Prophet (ﷺ) disclosed a matter in confidence to one of his wives!' (66.3) i.e., his saying, "But I have drunk honey." Hisham said: It also meant his saying, "I will not drink anymore, and I have taken an oath, so do not inform anybody of that

bukhari:6691.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that [Quran 66:1](quran://66/1)–[4](quran://66/4) proves Muhammad did not author the Quran because the opening verse mildly reproves him, and they cite Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* to insist the occasion of revelation was merely drinking honey rather than the parallel reports of Hafsa catching him with his concubine Mariyah the Copt. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that after Aisha and Hafsa tricked him into swearing a secret oath (`وَلَنْ أَعُودَ لَهُ، وَقَدْ حَلَفْتُ، فَلاَ تُخْبِرِي بِذَلِكَ أَحَدًا`) over foul breath (`رِيحَ مَغَافِيرَ`), divine revelation immediately descended (`فَنَزَلَتْ`) to release Muhammad from his own binding vow (`لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ`) while demanding that his wives repent to Allah (`إِنْ تَتُوبَا إِلَى اللَّهِ`). Thus, even under the sanitized honey narration, the eternal word of Allah is deployed to nullify Muhammad's rash domestic oath, expose his wives' private confidences, and rally Allah, Gabriel, and the angels against two wives ([Quran 66:4](quran://66/4)) over a trivial household prank.

muslim:3691.note: During Muhammad's twenty-nine-day separation from his wives, Umar tells him that if he divorces them, Allah, His angels, Gabriel, Michael, Umar, Abu Bakr, and the believers are with him, and states that he hoped Allah would confirm the words he spoke. Immediately thereafter, [Quran 66:4](quran://66/4) and [Quran 66:5](quran://66/5) are revealed, declaring that if his wives back one another against him, Allah, Gabriel, the righteous believers, and the angels are his helpers, and that his Lord may replace them with better wives if he divorces them.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ مَا يَشُقُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ شَأْنِ النِّسَاءِ فَإِنْ كُنْتَ طَلَّقْتَهُنَّ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَكَ وَمَلاَئِكَتَهُ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَائِيلَ وَأَنَا وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ مَعَكَ وَقَلَّمَا تَكَلَّمْتُ وَأَحْمَدُ اللَّهَ بِكَلاَمٍ إِلاَّ رَجَوْتُ أَنْ يَكُونَ اللَّهُ يُصَدِّقُ قَوْلِي الَّذِي أَقُولُ وَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ آيَةُ التَّخْيِيرِ ‏{‏ عَسَى رَبُّهُ إِنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ أَنْ يُبْدِلَهُ أَزْوَاجًا خَيْرًا مِنْكُنَّ‏}‏ ‏{‏ وَإِنْ تَظَاهَرَا عَلَيْهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ مَوْلاَهُ وَجِبْرِيلُ وَصَالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمَلاَئِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ‏}
problematic_excerpt.english: Messenger of Allah, what trouble do you feel from your wives, and if youhave divorced them, verily Allah is with you, His angels, Gabriel, Mika'il, I and Abu Bakr and the believers are with you. And seldom I talked and (which I uttered on that day) I hoped that Allah would testify to my words that I uttered. And so the verse of option (Ayat al-Takhyir) was revealed. Maybe his Lord, if he divorce you, will give him in your place wives better than you..." (Ixv. 5). And if you back up one another against him, then surely Allah is his Patron, and Gabriel and the righteous believers, and the angels after that are the aidera (lvi. 4).

muslim:3691.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the alignment between Umar's speech and the Quran reflects Umar's spiritual insight matching eternal divine truth, and that the verses simply upheld Muhammad's austere lifestyle against worldly demands. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Umar first proposed his own partisan coalition to comfort an angry Muhammad (`فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَكَ وَمَلاَئِكَتَهُ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَائِيلَ وَأَنَا وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ مَعَكَ`) while hoping Allah would validate the exact words he spoke (`يُصَدِّقُ قَوْلِي الَّذِي أَقُولُ`). Immediately afterward, [Quran 66:4](quran://66/4) and [Quran 66:5](quran://66/5) were revealed reproducing Umar's roster of divine and human allies (`فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ مَوْلاَهُ وَجِبْرِيلُ وَصَالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمَلاَئِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ`) and threatening Aisha, Hafsa, and the other wives with divorce and replacement (`إِنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ أَنْ يُبْدِلَهُ أَزْوَاجًا خَيْرًا مِنْكُنَّ`).

muslim:3695.note: Umar identifies Hafsa and Aisha as the two wives addressed in [Quran 66:4](quran://66/4) following a domestic dispute in which Muhammad swore an oath not to visit his wives for a month out of severe anger until Allah reproved him. After twenty-nine nights, Muhammad returned to Aisha and recited [Quran 33:28](quran://33/28), instructing her to consult her parents before choosing between remaining with Allah and His Messenger or separating from him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَكَانَ أَقْسَمَ أَنْ لاَ يَدْخُلَ عَلَيْهِنَّ شَهْرًا مِنْ شِدَّةِ مَوْجِدَتِهِ عَلَيْهِنَّ ‏.‏ حَتَّى عَاتَبَهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ‏.‏ قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ فَأَخْبَرَنِي عُرْوَةُ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ لَمَّا مَضَى تِسْعٌ وَعِشْرُونَ لَيْلَةً دَخَلَ عَلَىَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَدَأَ بِي فَقُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّكَ أَقْسَمْتَ أَنْ لاَ تَدْخُلَ عَلَيْنَا شَهْرًا وَإِنَّكَ دَخَلْتَ مِنْ تِسْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ أَعُدُّهُنَّ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ الشَّهْرَ تِسْعٌ وَعِشْرُونَ - ثُمَّ قَالَ - يَا عَائِشَةُ إِنِّي ذَاكِرٌ لَكِ أَمْرًا فَلاَ عَلَيْكِ أَنْ لاَ تَعْجَلِي فِيهِ حَتَّى تَسْتَأْمِرِي أَبَوَيْكِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ عَلَىَّ الآيَةَ ‏{‏ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ قُلْ لأَزْوَاجِكَ‏}‏ حَتَّى بَلَغَ ‏{‏ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا‏}‏ قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ قَدْ عَلِمَ وَاللَّهِ أَنَّ أَبَوَىَّ لَمْ يَكُونَا لِيَأْمُرَانِي بِفِرَاقِهِ قَالَتْ فَقُلْتُ أَوَفِي هَذَا أَسْتَأْمِرُ أَبَوَىَّ فَإِنِّي أُرِيدُ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَالدَّارَ الآخِرَةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: And he (Allah's Messenger) had taken an oath that he would not visit them for a month due to extreme annoyance with them until Allah showed His displeasure to him (Allah's Messenger). Zuhri said: 'Urwa informed me that 'A'Isha (Allah be pleased with her) said: When twenty-nine nights were over, Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) visited me, and he began (his visit) with me. I said: Messenger of Allah, you had taken an oath that you would not visit us for a month, while you have visited after I have counted only twenty-nine (nights). Thereupon he said: The month may also be of twenty-nine (days). He then said: 'A'isha, I am going to talk to you about a matter, and you should not be hasty in it (and do not give your final decision) until you have consulted your parents. He then recited this verse to me:" O Prophet, say to your wives" till he reached" mighty reward" (xxxiii. 28). 'A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) said: By Allah, he knew that my parents would not allow me to separate from him. I said: Is there any need to consult my parents in this matter? I in fact choose Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) and the abode in the Hereafter.

muslim:3695.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the revelation of [Quran 33:28](quran://33/28) and [Quran 66:4](quran://66/4) was not a self-serving intervention in Muhammad's domestic disputes, claiming it merely offered his wives a fair, uncoerced choice between worldly wealth and ascetic devotion after Allah reproved him (`عَاتَبَهُ اللَّهُ`). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad boycotted his wives for a month out of his extreme anger toward them (`مِنْ شِدَّةِ مَوْجِدَتِهِ عَلَيْهِنَّ`) because they retorted against him (`لَيُرَاجِعْنَهُ`) and shunned him until night (`وَتَهْجُرُهُ إِحْدَاهُنَّ الْيَوْمَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ`), which triggered both Allah's demand that Hafsa and Aisha repent (`{إِنْ تَتُوبَا إِلَى اللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا}`) and the divorce ultimatum of [Quran 33:28](quran://33/28). Furthermore, when Muhammad told Aisha to consult her parents before answering the verse (`حَتَّى تَسْتَأْمِرِي أَبَوَيْكِ`), Aisha testified under oath that he already knew her parents would never instruct her to separate from him (`قَدْ عَلِمَ وَاللَّهِ أَنَّ أَبَوَىَّ لَمْ يَكُونَا لِيَأْمُرَانِي بِفِرَاقِهِ`), while Umar warned Hafsa that provoking the Messenger's anger brings Allah's wrath and ruin (`أَنْ يَغْضَبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهَا لِغَضَبِ رَسُولِهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَإِذَا هِيَ قَدْ هَلَكَتْ`).

muslim:3696.note: Umar identifies Hafsa and Aisha as the two wives addressed in [Quran 66:4](quran://66/4) after the Prophet's wives retorted against him and shunned him from day until night. After swearing an oath not to enter upon his wives for a month out of severe anger with them until Allah rebuked him, Muhammad returned to Aisha on the twenty-ninth night and recited [Quran 33:28](quran://33/28), instructing her to consult her parents before choosing between separation or Allah, His Messenger, and the Hereafter.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَكَانَ أَقْسَمَ أَنْ لاَ يَدْخُلَ عَلَيْهِنَّ شَهْرًا مِنْ شِدَّةِ مَوْجِدَتِهِ عَلَيْهِنَّ ‏.‏ حَتَّى عَاتَبَهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ‏.‏ قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ فَأَخْبَرَنِي عُرْوَةُ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، قَالَتْ لَمَّا مَضَى تِسْعٌ وَعِشْرُونَ لَيْلَةً دَخَلَ عَلَىَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَدَأَ بِي فَقُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّكَ أَقْسَمْتَ أَنْ لاَ تَدْخُلَ عَلَيْنَا شَهْرًا وَإِنَّكَ دَخَلْتَ مِنْ تِسْعٍ وَعِشْرِينَ أَعُدُّهُنَّ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ الشَّهْرَ تِسْعٌ وَعِشْرُونَ - ثُمَّ قَالَ - يَا عَائِشَةُ إِنِّي ذَاكِرٌ لَكِ أَمْرًا فَلاَ عَلَيْكِ أَنْ لاَ تَعْجَلِي فِيهِ حَتَّى تَسْتَأْمِرِي أَبَوَيْكِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ عَلَىَّ الآيَةَ ‏{‏ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ قُلْ لأَزْوَاجِكَ‏}‏ حَتَّى بَلَغَ ‏{‏ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا‏}‏ قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ قَدْ عَلِمَ وَاللَّهِ أَنَّ أَبَوَىَّ لَمْ يَكُونَا لِيَأْمُرَانِي بِفِرَاقِهِ قَالَتْ فَقُلْتُ أَوَفِي هَذَا أَسْتَأْمِرُ أَبَوَىَّ فَإِنِّي أُرِيدُ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَالدَّارَ الآخِرَةَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: And he (Allah's Messenger) had taken an oath that he would not visit them for a month due to extreme annoyance with them until Allah showed His displeasure to him (Allah's Messenger). Zuhri said: 'Urwa informed me that 'A'Isha (Allah be pleased with her) said: When twenty-nine nights were over, Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) visited me, and he began (his visit) with me. I said: Messenger of Allah, you had taken an oath that you would not visit us for a month, while you have visited after I have counted only twenty-nine (nights). Thereupon he said: The month may also be of twenty-nine (days). He then said: 'A'isha, I am going to talk to you about a matter, and you should not be hasty in it (and do not give your final decision) until you have consulted your parents. He then recited this verse to me:" O Prophet, say to your wives" till he reached" mighty reward" (xxxiii. 28). 'A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) said: By Allah, he knew that my parents would not allow me to separate from him. I said: Is there any need to consult my parents in this matter? I in fact choose Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) and the abode in the Hereafter.

muslim:3696.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the month-long separation and the verse of choice in [Quran 33:28](quran://33/28) were gentle, egalitarian measures granting Muhammad's wives free agency to choose between asceticism and worldly comfort rather than leveraging revelation to settle domestic disputes. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad boycotted his wives for a month out of extreme anger with them (*min shiddati mawjidatihi 'alayhinna*) after they retorted upon him (*yurāji'nahu*), while [Quran 66:4](quran://66/4) intervened against Hafsa and Aisha by commanding them to repent (*in tatūbā ilā Allāhi faqad ṣaghat qulūbukumā*). Furthermore, Muhammad smiled (*fa-tabassama*) when Umar recounted warning the wives that angering the Messenger brings the wrath of Allah and leads to destruction (*an yaghḍaba Allāhu 'alayhā li-ghaḍabi rasūlihi fa-idhā hiya qad halakat*), and Aisha noted regarding his instruction to consult her parents over the divorce ultimatum that he already knew her parents would never order her to separate from him (*qad 'alima wallāhi anna abawayya lam yakūnā li-ya'murānī bi-firāqihi*).

muslim:6310.note: When Fatima complained to Muhammad that her husband Ali ibn Abi Talib had proposed marriage to the daughter of Abu Jahl, Muhammad publicly declared that Fatima is a part of him, that he dislikes her being put to trial, and swore by Allah that the daughter of Allah's Messenger and the daughter of Allah's enemy would never be joined under one man, prompting Ali to abandon the proposal.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ خَطَبَ بِنْتَ أَبِي جَهْلٍ وَعِنْدَهُ فَاطِمَةُ بِنْتُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ بِذَلِكَ فَاطِمَةُ أَتَتِ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنَّ قَوْمَكَ يَتَحَدَّثُونَ أَنَّكَ لاَ تَغْضَبُ لِبَنَاتِكَ وَهَذَا عَلِيٌّ نَاكِحًا ابْنَةَ أَبِي جَهْلٍ ‏.‏ قَالَ الْمِسْوَرُ فَقَامَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَسَمِعْتُهُ حِينَ تَشَهَّدَ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏ "‏ أَمَّا بَعْدُ فَإِنِّي أَنْكَحْتُ أَبَا الْعَاصِ بْنَ الرَّبِيعِ فَحَدَّثَنِي فَصَدَقَنِي وَإِنَّ فَاطِمَةَ بِنْتَ مُحَمَّدٍ مُضْغَةٌ مِنِّي وَإِنَّمَا أَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَفْتِنُوهَا وَإِنَّهَا وَاللَّهِ لاَ تَجْتَمِعُ بِنْتُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ وَبِنْتُ عَدُوِّ اللَّهِ عِنْدَ رَجُلٍ وَاحِدٍ أَبَدًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَتَرَكَ عَلِيٌّ الْخِطْبَةَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Ali b. Husain reported that Miswar b. Makhramah informed him that 'Ali b. Abi Talib sent the proposal of marriage to the daughter of Abu Jahl as he had Fatima, the daughter of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), (as his wife). When Fatima heard about it, she came to Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) and said:The people say that you never feel angry on account of your daughters and now 'Ali is going to marry the daughter of Abu Jahl. Makhramah said: Thereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) rose up and I heard him reciting Tashahhud and say: Now to the point. I gave a daughter of mine (Zainab) to Abu'l-'As b. Rabi, and he spoke to me and spoke the truth. Verily Fatima, the daughter of Muhammad, is a part of me and I do not approve that she may be put to any trial and by Allah, the daughter of Allah's Messenger cannot be combined with the daughter of God's enemy (as the co-wives) of one person. Thereupon 'Ali gave up (the idea of his intended) marriage

muslim:6310.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was not applying a double standard regarding polygamy, but only preventing his daughter from being joined in marriage with the daughter of Allah's enemy, Abu Jahl, lest jealousy subject Fatima's faith to a trial. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad grounded his objection in his personal bond with his daughter—declaring, "Verily Fatima, the daughter of Muhammad, is a part of me, and I dislike that they should put her to trial" (wa-inna Fāṭimata binta Muḥammadin muḍghatun minnī wa-innamā akrahu an yaftinūhā)—right after praising his other son-in-law, Abu'l-'As b. Rabi, husband of Zainab, because "he spoke to me and spoke the truth" (fa-ḥaddathanī fa-ṣadaqanī). By acknowledging that a co-wife marriage would put Fatima to trial (an yaftinūhā) and compelling Ali to abandon the proposal (bukhari:3110, muslim:6307, muslim:6309), Muhammad exempted his own daughter from the marital distress that his own co-wives were required to endure ([Quran 33:50](quran://33/50)).

muslim:4553.note: Ibn Umar narrates that after Muhammad cut down and burned the date-palms of Banu Nadir at al-Buwaira, [Quran 59:5](quran://59/5) was revealed regarding the event, declaring (as quoted more fully in muslim:4552) that cutting down the trees or leaving them standing was done with Allah's permission to disgrace the evil-doers.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَطَعَ نَخْلَ بَنِي النَّضِيرِ وَحَرَّقَ وَلَهَا يَقُولُ حَسَّانُ وَهَانَ عَلَى سَرَاةِ بَنِي لُؤَىٍّ حَرِيقٌ بِالْبُوَيْرَةِ مُسْتَطِيرُ وَفِي ذَلِكَ نَزَلَتْ ‏{‏ مَا قَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ لِينَةٍ أَوْ تَرَكْتُمُوهَا قَائِمَةً عَلَى أُصُولِهَا‏}‏ الآيَةَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: It is narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) caused the date-palms of Banu Nadir to be cut down and burnt. It is in this connection that Hassan (the poet) said:It was easy for the nobles of Quraish to burn Buwaira whose sparks were flying in all directions, in the same connection was revealed the Qur'anic verse:" Whatever trees you have cut down or left standing on their trunks

muslim:4553.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that cutting down and burning the date-palms of Banu Nadir at al-Buwaira was a pre-authorized military measure rather than an action requiring retroactive justification. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Messenger of Allah first cut down and burned the date-palms of Banu Nadir (qaṭaʿa nakhla Banī al-Naḍīr wa-ḥarraqa)—a widespread fire at al-Buwaira (ḥarīqun bi-al-Buwayrati mustaṭīr) recounted by the poet Hassan—and that in connection with this completed act [Quran 59:5](quran://59/5) was subsequently revealed (wa-fī dhālika nazalat). As recorded across the parallel narrations in bukhari:4032, bukhari:4884, and muslim:4552, the verse ("Whatever trees you have cut down or left standing on their trunks") descended after the destruction of the orchards to sanction what had already taken place.

muslim:6624.note: Muhammad declares to Allah that he holds an unbreakable covenant (*ʿahdan*) whereby any believer he reviles (*sababtuhu*) or whips (*jaladtuhu*) has that act made an expiation for him on the Day of Resurrection. The parallel report in muslim:6622 states that he does this when losing his temper as a human being.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي اتَّخَذْتُ عِنْدَكَ عَهْدًا لَنْ تُخْلِفَنِيهِ فَأَيُّمَا مُؤْمِنٍ سَبَبْتُهُ أَوْ جَلَدْتُهُ فَاجْعَلْ ذَلِكَ كَفَّارَةً لَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:I have held covenant with Thee which Thou wouldst not break, so for any believer whom I curse or beat, make that an expiation on the Day of Resurrection

muslim:6624.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this supplication demonstrates prophetic mercy and humility by ensuring that any believer affected by Muhammad's human reactions receives spiritual expiation (*kaffāratan lahu*) on the Day of Resurrection. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad reviled (*sababtuhu*) and whipped (*jaladtuhu*) believers (*muʾminin*), and rather than offering repentance or restitution to those he harmed, he invokes an unbreakable personal covenant (*ʿahdan*) with Allah that reframes his own verbal and physical mistreatment as a posthumous benefit.

muslim:6625.note: Muhammad declares that because he is only a mortal (*innamā anā bashar*), he has made a stipulation with his Lord (*ishtaraṭtu ʿalā rabbī*) that whenever he reviles (*sababtuhu*) or insults (*shatamtuhu*) any Muslim, it shall be counted as purification (*zakātan*) and a reward (*ajran*) for that person.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ إِنَّمَا أَنَا بَشَرٌ وَإِنِّي اشْتَرَطْتُ عَلَى رَبِّي عَزَّ وَجَلَّ أَىُّ عَبْدٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ سَبَبْتُهُ أَوْ شَتَمْتُهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ ذَلِكَ لَهُ زَكَاةً وَأَجْرًا ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Jabir b. Abdullah reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:I am a human being and I have made this term with my Lord, the Exalted and Glorious: For any servant amongst Muslims whom I curse or scold, make that a source of purity and reward.

muslim:6625.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's words were merely righteous prophetic discipline or harmless figures of speech that Allah mercifully turned into a spiritual blessing for believers. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *sababtuhu aw shatamtuhu* ('whom I revile or insult')—terms denoting direct verbal abuse—and attributes this conduct to his mortal human nature (*innamā anā bashar*, 'I am only a mortal') rather than divine instruction. By claiming a personal stipulation with his Lord (*ishtaraṭtu ʿalā rabbī*) that converts his insults against any Muslim into purification and reward (*zakātan wa-ajran*), the narration establishes a special prophetic privilege that exempts his verbal mistreatment from fault (see also bukhari:6361, muslim:6614, muslim:6622).

muslim:1163.note: Muhammad declares that he was granted five things not given to anyone before him, including that the spoils of war (*al-ghanāʾim*) were made lawful for him despite never being made lawful for any previous prophet ([Quran 8:41](quran://8/41), [Quran 8:69](quran://8/69)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُعْطِيتُ خَمْسًا لَمْ يُعْطَهُنَّ أَحَدٌ قَبْلِي كَانَ كُلُّ نَبِيٍّ يُبْعَثُ إِلَى قَوْمِهِ خَاصَّةً وَبُعِثْتُ إِلَى كُلِّ أَحْمَرَ وَأَسْوَدَ وَأُحِلَّتْ لِيَ الْغَنَائِمُ وَلَمْ تُحَلَّ لأَحَدٍ قَبْلِي
problematic_excerpt.english: I have been conferred upon five (things) which were not granted to anyone before me (and these are): Every apostle wassent particularly to his own people, whereas I have been sent to all the red and the black the spoils of war have been made lawful for me, and these were never made lawful to anyone before me

muslim:1163.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that earlier prophets were forbidden from keeping war booty because fire from heaven consumed it as an offering, whereas Allah permitted spoils to Muhammad's community out of mercy for their material weakness. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *uḥillat liya al-ghanāʾim wa-lam tuḥalla li-aḥadin qablī* ("the spoils of war have been made lawful for me, and they were never made lawful for anyone before me"), framing the legalization of plunder directly as a personal prophetic privilege granted to Muhammad. Furthermore, this claim commits a glaring historical anachronism—since Biblical prophets like Moses, Joshua, and David routinely took and divided war spoils centuries before 7th-century AD Arabia (Numbers 31:26–27, 1 Samuel 30:22–26)—while conveniently institutionalizing a personal one-fifth share (*khumus*) of all captured wealth, land, and captives for Muhammad himself (Quran 8:41, 8:69).

muslim:1163.note: Muhammad declares that he was made victorious by terror (*bi-l-ruʿb*) across the distance of a month's journey ahead of him and that the spoils of war (*al-ghanāʾim*) were made lawful for him ([Quran 8:12](quran://8/12), [Quran 8:69](quran://8/69)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُعْطِيتُ خَمْسًا لَمْ يُعْطَهُنَّ أَحَدٌ قَبْلِي كَانَ كُلُّ نَبِيٍّ يُبْعَثُ إِلَى قَوْمِهِ خَاصَّةً وَبُعِثْتُ إِلَى كُلِّ أَحْمَرَ وَأَسْوَدَ وَأُحِلَّتْ لِيَ الْغَنَائِمُ وَلَمْ تُحَلَّ لأَحَدٍ قَبْلِي وَجُعِلَتْ لِيَ الأَرْضُ طَيِّبَةً طَهُورًا وَمَسْجِدًا فَأَيُّمَا رَجُلٍ أَدْرَكَتْهُ الصَّلاَةُ صَلَّى حَيْثُ كَانَ وَنُصِرْتُ بِالرُّعْبِ بَيْنَ يَدَىْ مَسِيرَةِ شَهْرٍ وَأُعْطِيتُ الشَّفَاعَةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: I have been conferred upon five (things) which were not granted to anyone before me (and these are): Every apostle wassent particularly to his own people, whereas I have been sent to all the red and the black the spoils of war have been made lawful for me, and these were never made lawful to anyone before me, and the earth has been made sacred and pure and mosque for me, so whenever the time of prayer comes for any one of you he should pray whenever he is, and I have been supported by awe (by which the enemy is overwhelmed) from the distance (which one takes) one month to cover and I have been granted intercession

muslim:1163.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *al-ruʿb* merely refers to a non-violent "psychological awe" or defensive deterrent that prevented bloodshed by causing hostile armies to surrender without fighting. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *nuṣirtu bi-l-ruʿb bayna yaday masīrati shahr* ("I have been made victorious by terror ahead of me for the distance of a month's journey") directly alongside *uḥillat liya al-ghanāʾim* ("the spoils of war have been made lawful for me"), linking this terror directly to offensive military campaigning and plunder. Both Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī* on bukhari:335) confirm that this *ruʿb* was the casting of panic into distant nations as Muslim armies advanced to subjugate them, matching the Quranic mandate to cast terror (*al-ruʿb*) into the hearts of unbelievers while striking their necks and seizing their property (Quran 8:12, 33:26–27).

bukhari:6982.note: In Aisha's narration of the first revelation in the cave of Hira, the angel seizes and presses (ghaṭṭanī) Muhammad three times to the limit of his endurance, leaving his neck muscles trembling in terror (al-rawʿ) and prompting him to tell Khadija, 'I feared for myself.' After Waraqa's death and a pause in revelation, the report adds—prefaced by the narrator al-Zuhrī's phrase 'as has reached us' (fīmā balaghanā)—that Muhammad grew so grieved he repeatedly went to the peaks of high mountains to throw himself down, returning home each time Gabriel appeared to affirm his prophethood.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَخَذَنِي فَغَطَّنِي حَتَّى بَلَغَ مِنِّي الْجَهْدَ ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي‏.‏ فَقَالَ اقْرَأْ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ مَا أَنَا بِقَارِئٍ‏.‏ فَأَخَذَنِي فَغَطَّنِي الثَّانِيَةَ حَتَّى بَلَغَ مِنِّي الْجَهْدَ، ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي فَقَالَ اقْرَأْ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ مَا أَنَا بِقَارِئٍ‏.‏ فَغَطَّنِي الثَّالِثَةَ حَتَّى بَلَغَ مِنِّي الْجَهْدُ، ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي فَقَالَ اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ ‏"‏‏.‏ حَتَّى بَلَغَ ‏{‏مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ‏}‏ فَرَجَعَ بِهَا تَرْجُفُ بَوَادِرُهُ حَتَّى دَخَلَ عَلَى خَدِيجَةَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ زَمِّلُونِي زَمِّلُونِي ‏"‏‏.‏ فَزَمَّلُوهُ حَتَّى ذَهَبَ عَنْهُ الرَّوْعُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا خَدِيجَةُ مَا لِي ‏"‏‏.‏ وَأَخْبَرَهَا الْخَبَرَ وَقَالَ ‏"‏ قَدْ خَشِيتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ لَهُ كَلاَّ أَبْشِرْ، فَوَاللَّهِ لاَ يُخْزِيكَ اللَّهُ أَبَدًا، إِنَّكَ لَتَصِلُ الرَّحِمَ، وَتَصْدُقُ الْحَدِيثَ، وَتَحْمِلُ الْكَلَّ، وَتَقْرِي الضَّيْفَ، وَتُعِينُ عَلَى نَوَائِبِ الْحَقِّ‏.‏ ثُمَّ انْطَلَقَتْ بِهِ خَدِيجَةُ حَتَّى أَتَتْ بِهِ وَرَقَةَ بْنَ نَوْفَلِ بْنِ أَسَدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْعُزَّى بْنِ قُصَىٍّ ـ وَهْوَ ابْنُ عَمِّ خَدِيجَةَ أَخُو أَبِيهَا، وَكَانَ امْرَأً تَنَصَّرَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، وَكَانَ يَكْتُبُ الْكِتَابَ الْعَرَبِيَّ فَيَكْتُبُ بِالْعَرَبِيَّةِ مِنَ الإِنْجِيلِ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَكْتُبَ، وَكَانَ شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا قَدْ عَمِيَ ـ فَقَالَتْ لَهُ خَدِيجَةُ أَىِ ابْنَ عَمِّ اسْمَعْ مِنِ ابْنِ أَخِيكَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ وَرَقَةُ ابْنَ أَخِي مَاذَا تَرَى فَأَخْبَرَهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَا رَأَى فَقَالَ وَرَقَةُ هَذَا النَّامُوسُ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ عَلَى مُوسَى، يَا لَيْتَنِي فِيهَا جَذَعًا أَكُونُ حَيًّا، حِينَ يُخْرِجُكَ قَوْمُكَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَوَمُخْرِجِيَّ هُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ وَرَقَةُ نَعَمْ، لَمْ يَأْتِ رَجُلٌ قَطُّ بِمَا جِئْتَ بِهِ إِلاَّ عُودِيَ، وَإِنْ يُدْرِكْنِي يَوْمُكَ أَنْصُرْكَ نَصْرًا مُؤَزَّرًا‏.‏ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَنْشَبْ وَرَقَةُ أَنْ تُوُفِّيَ، وَفَتَرَ الْوَحْىُ فَتْرَةً حَتَّى حَزِنَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِيمَا بَلَغَنَا حُزْنًا غَدَا مِنْهُ مِرَارًا كَىْ يَتَرَدَّى مِنْ رُءُوسِ شَوَاهِقِ الْجِبَالِ، فَكُلَّمَا أَوْفَى بِذِرْوَةِ جَبَلٍ لِكَىْ يُلْقِيَ مِنْهُ نَفْسَهُ، تَبَدَّى لَهُ جِبْرِيلُ فَقَالَ يَا مُحَمَّدُ إِنَّكَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ حَقًّا‏.‏ فَيَسْكُنُ لِذَلِكَ جَأْشُهُ وَتَقِرُّ نَفْسُهُ فَيَرْجِعُ
problematic_excerpt.english: The angel caught me (forcefully) and pressed me so hard that I could not bear it anymore. He then released me and again asked me to read, and I replied, "I do not know how to read," whereupon he caught me again and pressed me a second time till I could not bear it anymore. He then released me and asked me again to read, but again I replied, "I do not know how to read (or, what shall I read?)." Thereupon he caught me for the third time and pressed me and then released me and said, "Read: In the Name of your Lord, Who has created (all that exists). Has created man from a clot. Read and Your Lord is Most Generous...up to..... ..that which he knew not." (96.15) Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) returned with the Inspiration, his neck muscles twitching with terror till he entered upon Khadija and said, "Cover me! Cover me!" They covered him till his fear was over and then he said, "O Khadija, what is wrong with me?" Then he told her everything that had happened and said, 'I fear that something may happen to me." Khadija said, 'Never! But have the glad tidings, for by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you as you keep good reactions with your Kith and kin, speak the truth, help the poor and the destitute, serve your guest generously and assist the deserving, calamityafflicted ones." Khadija then accompanied him to (her cousin) Waraqa bin Naufal bin Asad bin `Abdul `Uzza bin Qusai. Waraqa was the son of her paternal uncle, i.e., her father's brother, who during the Pre-Islamic Period became a Christian and used to write the Arabic writing and used to write of the Gospels in Arabic as much as Allah wished him to write. He was an old man and had lost his eyesight. Khadija said to him, "O my cousin! Listen to the story of your nephew." Waraqa asked, "O my nephew! What have you seen?" The Prophet (ﷺ) described whatever he had seen. Waraqa said, "This is the same Namus (i.e., Gabriel, the Angel who keeps the secrets) whom Allah had sent to Moses. I wish I were young and could live up to the time when your people would turn you out." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) asked, "Will they turn me out?" Waraqa replied in the affirmative and said: "Never did a man come with something similar to what you have brought but was treated with hostility. If I should remain alive till the day when you will be turned out then I would support you strongly." But after a few days Waraqa died and the Divine Inspiration was also paused for a while and the Prophet (ﷺ) became so sad as we have heard that he intended several times to throw himself from the tops of high mountains and every time he went up the top of a mountain in order to throw himself down, Gabriel would appear before him and say, "O Muhammad! You are indeed Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) in truth" whereupon his heart would become quiet and he would calm down and would return home.

bukhari:6982.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the angel's squeezing was merely a firm embrace to focus Muhammad's attention, and they cite Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī to dismiss the suicide attempts as an unverified remark (balāgh) inserted by the narrator Al-Zuhri (fīmā balaghanā, 'as has reached us'). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states within the unbroken chain that the spirit violently choked or crushed him to the point of utter exhaustion (fa-ghaṭṭanī ḥattā balagha minnī al-jahd) three times without a single word of comfort, leaving his neck muscles spasming in terror (tarjufu bawādiruhu) as he cried out, 'I fear for myself' (qad khashītu ʿalā nafsī). Furthermore, Al-Bukhari himself canonized the account of Muhammad repeatedly climbing mountain peaks 'in order to throw himself down' (likay yulqiya minhu nafsahu) in his Sahih collection, a suicidal despair corroborated across early Sunni sources (such as Tārīkh al-Ṭabarī) where Muhammad explicitly feared he had become demon-possessed (majnūn).

bukhari:3175.note: Aisha reports that Muhammad was bewitched (suhira) to the point that he imagined doing things he had not actually done. Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawi affirm the literal authenticity of this report, arguing that the magic-induced delusions only affected his worldly and marital perceptions rather than his prophetic legislation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم سُحِرَ حَتَّى كَانَ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ صَنَعَ شَيْئًا وَلَمْ يَصْنَعْهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: the Prophet (ﷺ) was bewitched so that he began to imagine that he had done a thing which in fact he had not done

bukhari:3175.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*), and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*), that Labīd ibn al-Aʿṣam's spell only affected Muhammad's worldly physical senses—specifically imagining he had been intimate with his wives—without compromising his intellect or his infallibility in conveying divine revelation (*tablīgh al-waḥy*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `سُحِرَ حَتَّى كَانَ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ صَنَعَ شَيْئًا وَلَمْ يَصْنَعْهُ` ('he was bewitched so that he began to imagine [`yukhayyalu ilayhi`] that he had done a thing [`shayʾan`, unrestricted] which in fact he had not done'), describing a direct cognitive delusion of memory and perception using the exact verb the Quran employs for demonic magical illusions (Q 20:66). Conceding that occult magic hijacked Muhammad's mind into hallucinating false memories directly vindicates his contemporaries' Quranic charge that he was 'a bewitched man' (`رَجُلًا مَسْحُورًا`, Q 17:47, 25:8) and fatally undermines the epistemological reliability of his prophetic consciousness.

muslim:5548.note: Abu Huraira reports Muhammad's declaration that the bell (*al-jaras*) is the musical instrument of Satan (*mazāmīr al-shayṭān*)—an object that repels angels (muslim:5546)—even though Muhammad describes his own revelation as arriving like the ringing of a bell (*ṣalṣalat al-jaras*, bukhari:2).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ الْجَرَسُ مَزَامِيرُ الشَّيْطَانِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:The bell is the musical instrument of the Satan

muslim:5548.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this condemnation applies only to literal bells, whereas the ringing sound during Muhammad's revelation in bukhari:2 was merely an acoustic metaphor for the intensity of the experience. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states as an unqualified rule that the bell is the musical instrument of Satan (*al-jaras mazāmīr al-shayṭān*), using the exact same noun (*al-jaras*) used to describe his revelation arriving like the ringing of a bell (*ṣalṣalat al-jaras* in bukhari:2). Rather than comparing divine revelation to something pure or angelic, Muhammad's own terminology directly equates the auditory signature of his revelation with the instrument of Satan (muslim:5546, muslim:5548).

muslim:7108.note: Muhammad declares that every person—including himself—has an assigned jinn companion (*qarīn*, explicitly termed a devil, *shayṭān*, in muslim:7110) attached to him. When asked by his Companions if this applies to him as well, he confirms that it does, stating that Allah helped him against his companion so that it became a Muslim (*fa-aslama*, or under the alternative vocalization *fa-aslamu*, so that he is safe from it) and now commands him (*ya'murunī*) only to do good.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ مَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلاَّ وَقَدْ وُكِّلَ بِهِ قَرِينُهُ مِنَ الْجِنِّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا وَإِيَّاكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ وَإِيَّاىَ إِلاَّ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَعَانَنِي عَلَيْهِ فَأَسْلَمَ فَلاَ يَأْمُرُنِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said:There is none amongst you with whom is not an attache from amongst the jinn (devil). They (the Companions) said: Allah's Messenger, with you too? Thereupon he said: Yes, but Allah helps me against him and so I am safe from his hand and he does not command me but for good

muslim:7108.literal_translation: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: 'There is none amongst you who does not have his companion from the jinn assigned to him.' They said: 'Even you, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Even me, except that Allah helped me against him so he became a Muslim, and he does not command me except to do good.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَأَسْلَمَ فَلاَ يَأْمُرُنِي إِلاَّ بِخَيْرٍ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and so I am safe from his hand and he does not command me but for good
translation_issue.literal_meaning: so he became a Muslim (submitted), and he does not command me except with good
translation_issue.explanation: Rather than translating the vocalized past-tense verb fa-aslama ('so he became a Muslim/submitted') printed in the Arabic text, the translator follows the alternative vocalization fa-aslamu ('so I am safe') and interpolates 'from his hand' to soften the statement that Muhammad's jinn companion converted to Islam.

muslim:7108.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase should be read as 'so I am safe from him' (*fa-aslamu*) rather than 'so he became a Muslim' (*fa-aslama*), claiming this narration illustrates Allah's protection of Muhammad from demonic whispering. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *fa-aslama fa-lā ya'murunī illā bi-khayrin* ('so he became a Muslim, and he does not command me except with good'), vocalizing the verb in the third-person past tense (*fa-aslama*) to state that Muhammad's assigned jinn-companion (*qarīnuhu min al-jinni*) converted to Islam. Even if the alternate vocalization is asserted, Muhammad still concedes that an attached jinn-devil is assigned to him (*wa-iyyāya*) and issues commands to him (*ya'murunī*), placing him under the direction of an attached *qarīn* ([Quran 43:36](quran://43/36)).

muslim:413.note: While playing with other boys, Muhammad was seized and thrown to the ground (*fasara'ahu*) by Gabriel, who split open his chest, extracted a blood-clot from his heart declared to be 'the share of Satan in you' (*hadha hazzu al-shaytani minka*), and washed his heart with Zamzam water in a golden basin before restoring it. His playmates ran to his wet-nurse declaring that Muhammad had been murdered, and they found him pale and drained of color (*muntaqa'u al-lawn*), with Anas ibn Malik noting that he later saw the needle marks on Muhammad's chest.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَتَاهُ جِبْرِيلُ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُوَ يَلْعَبُ مَعَ الْغِلْمَانِ فَأَخَذَهُ فَصَرَعَهُ فَشَقَّ عَنْ قَلْبِهِ فَاسْتَخْرَجَ الْقَلْبَ فَاسْتَخْرَجَ مِنْهُ عَلَقَةً فَقَالَ هَذَا حَظُّ الشَّيْطَانِ مِنْكَ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ غَسَلَهُ فِي طَسْتٍ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ بِمَاءِ زَمْزَمَ ثُمَّ لأَمَهُ ثُمَّ أَعَادَهُ فِي مَكَانِهِ وَجَاءَ الْغِلْمَانُ يَسْعَوْنَ إِلَى أُمِّهِ - يَعْنِي ظِئْرَهُ - فَقَالُوا إِنَّ مُحَمَّدًا قَدْ قُتِلَ ‏.‏ فَاسْتَقْبَلُوهُ وَهُوَ مُنْتَقَعُ اللَّوْنِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Anas b. Malik reported that Gabriel came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was playing with his playmates. He took hold of him and lay him prostrate on the ground and tore open his breast and took out the heart from it and then extracted a blood-clot out of it and said:That was the part of Satan in thee. And then he washed it with the water of Zamzam in a golden basin and then it was joined together and restored to it place. The boys came running to his mother, i. e. his nurse, and said: Verily Muhammad has been murdered. They all rushed toward him (and found him all right) His color was changed

muslim:413.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the splitting of the chest (*shaqqu al-ṣadr*), as defended by Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, was either a spiritual metaphor or a miraculous angelic surgery that permanently removed all satanic susceptibility and established Muhammad's prophetic infallibility (*ʿiṣmah*) from childhood. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the entity violently threw him down (*fa-ṣaraʿahu*, from the root *ṣarʿ* used for epileptic or demonic seizure), extracted an actual 'portion of Satan in you' (*hādhā ḥaẓẓu al-shayṭāni minka*), and left him ghastly pale (*muntaqaʿu al-lawn*) with physical needle-scars (*athara dhālika al-mikhyaṭ*) witnessed by Anas ibn Mālik, refuting any metaphorical reading. Moreover, this childhood procedure failed to immunize him against later satanic and occult affliction: Sahih narrations record that his chest had to be cut open again in adulthood (`bukhari:349`, `muslim:415`), while canonical texts confirm Satan later cast false verses into his recitation (Quran 22:52) and dark magic bewitched his mind for months (`bukhari:5765`).

bukhari:6391.note: Aisha reports that Muhammad was bewitched by Labid bin al-A'sam using a comb, hair, and a date-palm spathe placed in the well of Dharwan, causing him to imagine that he had done things he had not actually done. Classical commentators maintain that this bewitchment only affected his worldly and marital perceptions rather than his prophetic revelation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم طُبَّ حَتَّى إِنَّهُ لَيُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ قَدْ صَنَعَ الشَّىْءَ وَمَا صَنَعَهُ، وَإِنَّهُ دَعَا رَبَّهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَشَعَرْتِ أَنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَفْتَانِي فِيمَا اسْتَفْتَيْتُهُ فِيهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ فَمَا ذَاكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ جَاءَنِي رَجُلاَنِ فَجَلَسَ أَحَدُهُمَا عِنْدَ رَأْسِي، وَالآخَرُ عِنْدَ رِجْلَىَّ فَقَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا لِصَاحِبِهِ مَا وَجَعُ الرَّجُلِ قَالَ مَطْبُوبٌ‏.‏ قَالَ مَنْ طَبَّهُ قَالَ لَبِيدُ بْنُ الأَعْصَمِ‏.‏ قَالَ فِيمَا ذَا قَالَ فِي مُشْطٍ وَمُشَاطَةٍ وَجُفِّ طَلْعَةٍ‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَيْنَ هُوَ قَالَ فِي ذَرْوَانَ، وَذَرْوَانُ بِئْرٌ فِي بَنِي زُرَيْقٍ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was affected by magic, so much that he used to think that he had done something which in fact, he did not do, and he invoked his Lord (for a remedy). Then (one day) he said, "O `Aisha!) Do you know that Allah has advised me as to the problem I consulted Him about?" `Aisha said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! What's that?" He said, "Two men came to me and one of them sat at my head and the other at my feet, and one of them asked his companion, 'What is wrong with this man?' The latter replied, 'He is under the effect of magic.' The former asked, 'Who has worked magic on him?' The latter replied, 'Labid bin Al-A'sam.' The former asked, 'With what did he work the magic?' The latter replied, 'With a comb and the hair, which are stuck to the comb, and the skin of pollen of a date-palm tree.' The former asked, 'Where is that?' The latter replied, 'It is in Dharwan.' Dharwan was a well in the dwelling place of the (tribe of) Bani Zuraiq.

bukhari:6391.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ and Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī, that Labīd bin al-Aʿṣam's spell was merely an external bodily affliction restricted to worldly marital relations (as noted in bukhari:5765) that never compromised Muhammad's intellect or prophetic revelation (waḥy). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Prophet was bewitched (ṭubba and suḥira) to the point of cognitive delusion—layukhayyalu ilayhi qad ṣanaʿa al-shayʾa wa-mā ṣanaʿahu ('he used to imagine that he had done a thing which in fact he did not do')—demonstrating that demonic magic directly hijacked his mental perception and memory rather than just his physical limbs.
