Moreover, this Sahih admission confirms the exact theological disqualifier raised by Muhammad's critics in the Quran (Q 17:47, 25:8), who warned against following a 'bewitched man' (rajulan masḥūran).

bukhari:3268.note: Aisha reports that Muhammad was bewitched by Labid bin al-A'sam—using a comb, hair combings, and the spathe of a male date-palm hidden in the well of Dharwan—causing him to imagine doing things he had not actually done until two men in a dream revealed the spell's location. Although classical commentators argue this bewitchment only affected his worldly and marital perception (cf. bukhari:5765) rather than prophetic revelation, the text explicitly states that magic caused him to imagine performing actions he had not done.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سُحِرَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى كَانَ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ يَفْعَلُ الشَّىْءَ وَمَا يَفْعَلُهُ، حَتَّى كَانَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ دَعَا وَدَعَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَشَعَرْتِ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَفْتَانِي فِيمَا فِيهِ شِفَائِي أَتَانِي رَجُلاَنِ، فَقَعَدَ أَحَدُهُمَا عِنْدَ رَأْسِي وَالآخَرُ عِنْدَ رِجْلَىَّ، فَقَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا لِلآخَرِ مَا وَجَعُ الرَّجُلِ قَالَ مَطْبُوبٌ‏.‏ قَالَ وَمَنْ طَبَّهُ قَالَ لَبِيدُ بْنُ الأَعْصَمِ‏.‏ قَالَ فِي مَاذَا قَالَ فِي مُشُطٍ وَمُشَاقَةٍ وَجُفِّ طَلْعَةٍ ذَكَرٍ‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَيْنَ هُوَ قَالَ فِي بِئْرِ ذَرْوَانَ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Magic was worked on the Prophet (ﷺ) so that he began to fancy that he was doing a thing which he was not actually doing. One day he invoked (Allah) for a long period and then said, "I feel that Allah has inspired me as how to cure myself. Two persons came to me (in my dream) and sat, one by my head and the other by my feet. One of them asked the other, "What is the ailment of this man?" The other replied, 'He has been bewitched" The first asked, 'Who has bewitched him?' The other replied, 'Labid bin Al-A'sam.' The first one asked, 'What material has he used?' The other replied, 'A comb, the hair gathered on it, and the outer skin of the pollen of the male date-palm.' The first asked, 'Where is that?' The other replied, 'It is in the well of Dharwan.' "

bukhari:3268.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, that Labid bin al-A'sam's spell was merely an external bodily ailment restricted to worldly affairs—such as imagining he had been intimate with his wives (bukhari:5765)—that never compromised his prophetic intellect or divine revelation (waḥy). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Prophet was bewitched (suḥira al-nabī) and under a magical curse (maṭbūb) to the point of cognitive delusion where 'he began to imagine that he was doing a thing which he was not actually doing' (yukhayyalu ilayhi annahu yafʿalu al-shayʾa wa-mā yafʿaluhu). By conceding that occult magic successfully hijacked Muhammad's mind and perception of reality, this narration directly validates the exact objection recorded in Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:47 and Sūrat al-Furqān 25:8—that he was 'a bewitched man' (rajulan masḥūran).

bukhari:5763.note: Aisha narrates that Labid bin al-A'sam of Banu Zurayq bewitched Muhammad using a comb, hair combings, and a male date-palm spathe hidden in the well of Dharwan, causing Muhammad to imagine (yukhayyalu ilayhi) that he had done things he had not actually done. After two visitors diagnosed his condition, Muhammad stated that Allah had cured him and ordered the well buried—an episode Sunni commentators restrict to his worldly perceptions (such as imagining intimacy with his wives in bukhari:5765) rather than his prophetic revelation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَحَرَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَجُلٌ مِنْ بَنِي زُرَيْقٍ يُقَالُ لَهُ لَبِيدُ بْنُ الأَعْصَمِ، حَتَّى كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ يَفْعَلُ الشَّىْءَ وَمَا فَعَلَهُ، حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ أَوْ ذَاتَ لَيْلَةٍ وَهْوَ عِنْدِي لَكِنَّهُ دَعَا وَدَعَا ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ يَا عَائِشَةُ، أَشَعَرْتِ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَفْتَانِي فِيمَا اسْتَفْتَيْتُهُ فِيهِ، أَتَانِي رَجُلاَنِ فَقَعَدَ أَحَدُهُمَا عِنْدَ رَأْسِي، وَالآخَرُ عِنْدَ رِجْلَىَّ، فَقَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا لِصَاحِبِهِ مَا وَجَعُ الرَّجُلِ فَقَالَ مَطْبُوبٌ‏.‏ قَالَ مَنْ طَبَّهُ قَالَ لَبِيدُ بْنُ الأَعْصَمِ‏.‏ قَالَ فِي أَىِّ شَىْءٍ قَالَ فِي مُشْطٍ وَمُشَاطَةٍ، وَجُفِّ طَلْعِ نَخْلَةٍ ذَكَرٍ‏.‏ قَالَ وَأَيْنَ هُوَ قَالَ فِي بِئْرِ ذَرْوَانَ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A man called Labid bin al-A'sam from the tribe of Bani Zaraiq worked magic on Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) till Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) started imagining that he had done a thing that he had not really done. One day or one night he was with us, he invoked Allah and invoked for a long period, and then said, "O `Aisha! Do you know that Allah has instructed me concerning the matter I have asked him about? Two men came to me and one of them sat near my head and the other near my feet. One of them said to his companion, "What is the disease of this man?" The other replied, "He is under the effect of magic.' The first one asked, 'Who has worked the magic on him?' The other replied, "Labid bin Al-A'sam.' The first one asked, 'What material did he use?' The other replied, 'A comb and the hairs stuck to it and the skin of pollen of a male date palm.' The first one asked, 'Where is that?' The other replied, '(That is) in the well of Dharwan;' "

bukhari:5763.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that—per Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ and Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī—this bewitchment was merely an external, physical ailment restricted to Muhammad's worldly marital life (imagining he had visited his wives, as in bukhari:5765) that never compromised his intellect or prophetic infallibility ('iṣmah) in conveying revelation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in unrestricted terms that Labīd 'bewitched Allah's Messenger' (سَحَرَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ) and left him 'spellbound' (مَطْبُوبٌ) until 'it was made to appear to him that he was doing a thing when he had not done it' (يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ يَفْعَلُ الشَّىْءَ وَمَا فَعَلَهُ), directly confirming the very pagan accusation the Qur'an furiously denies—that Muhammad was 'a man bewitched' (رَجُلًا مَسْحُورًا, Qur'an 17:47, 25:8). Conceding that occult magic successfully hijacked the Prophet's mind and implanted false memories of actions he never performed (bukhari:3175, bukhari:5765) fatally collapses the epistemic reliability of his cognitive faculties.

bukhari:5765.note: Aisha narrates that Labid bin al-A'sam bewitched Muhammad using a comb and hair hidden in the well of Dharwan, causing him to think he had sexual relations with his wives when he had not—an effect the sub-narrator Sufyan ibn Uyaynah describes as the severest kind of magic. While classical commentators argue that this bewitchment affected only his worldly perception and not his prophetic revelation, the text explicitly records that the spell altered his perception until two men came to him and disclosed its source.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم سُحِرَ حَتَّى كَانَ يَرَى أَنَّهُ يَأْتِي النِّسَاءَ وَلاَ يَأْتِيهِنَّ‏.‏ قَالَ سُفْيَانُ وَهَذَا أَشَدُّ مَا يَكُونُ مِنَ السِّحْرِ إِذَا كَانَ كَذَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا عَائِشَةُ أَعَلِمْتِ أَنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَفْتَانِي فِيمَا اسْتَفْتَيْتُهُ فِيهِ، أَتَانِي رَجُلاَنِ فَقَعَدَ أَحَدُهُمَا عِنْدَ رَأْسِي، وَالآخَرُ عِنْدَ رِجْلَىَّ، فَقَالَ الَّذِي عِنْدَ رَأْسِي لِلآخَرِ مَا بَالُ الرَّجُلِ قَالَ مَطْبُوبٌ‏.‏ قَالَ وَمَنْ طَبَّهُ قَالَ لَبِيدُ بْنُ أَعْصَمَ، رَجُلٌ مِنْ بَنِي زُرَيْقٍ حَلِيفٌ لِيَهُودَ، كَانَ مُنَافِقًا‏.‏ قَالَ وَفِيمَ قَالَ فِي مُشْطٍ وَمُشَاقَةٍ‏.‏ قَالَ وَأَيْنَ قَالَ فِي جُفِّ طَلْعَةٍ ذَكَرٍ، تَحْتَ رَعُوفَةٍ، فِي بِئْرِ ذَرْوَانَ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Magic was worked on Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) so that he used to think that he had sexual relations with his wives while he actually had not (Sufyan said: That is the hardest kind of magic as it has such an effect). Then one day he said, "O `Aisha do you know that Allah has instructed me concerning the matter I asked Him about? Two men came to me and one of them sat near my head and the other sat near my feet. The one near my head asked the other. What is wrong with this man?' The latter replied the is under the effect of magic The first one asked, Who has worked magic on him?' The other replied Labid bin Al-A'sam, a man from Bani Zuraiq who was an ally of the Jews and was a hypocrite.' The first one asked, What material did he use)?' The other replied, 'A comb and the hair stuck to it.' The first one asked, 'Where (is that)?' The other replied. 'In a skin of pollen of a male date palm tree kept under a stone in the well of Dharwan' ''

bukhari:5765.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, following Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ and Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that Labīd ibn al-Aʿṣam's spell merely affected Muhammad's physical body in worldly matters without ever impairing his mind, memory, or prophetic infallibility (*ʿiṣmah*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the magic hijacked his cognitive perception of reality—*kāna yarā annahu yaʾtī al-nisāʾa wa-lā yaʾtīhinna* ('he used to think that he had sexual relations with his wives while he actually had not')—which Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah identifies in the text as 'the most severe kind of magic' (*ashaddu mā yakūnu mina al-siḥr*), while parallel narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3175) confirm he broadly hallucinated doing things he never did (*yukhayyalu ilayhi annahu yafʿalu al-shayʾa wa-mā faʿalahu*). Furthermore, by conceding that Muhammad was 'bewitched' (*suḥira* / *maṭbūb*), the Hadith directly vindicates his Meccan critics whom the Qur'an condemns as liars for calling him 'a bewitched man' (*rajulan masḥūran*, Q 17:47; 25:8).

bukhari:6063.note: Aisha reports that Labid bin al-A'sam bewitched Muhammad (`matbub` / `mas'hur`) using a comb, hair, and a male date-palm spathe hidden under a stone in the well of Dharwan, causing him for a period to imagine that he had sexual relations with his wives when he had not (cf. [Quran 17:47](quran://17/47); bukhari:3175, bukhari:5765).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: مَكَثَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَذَا وَكَذَا يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ يَأْتِي أَهْلَهُ وَلاَ يَأْتِي، قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ فَقَالَ لِي ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ ‏"‏ يَا عَائِشَةُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ أَفْتَانِي فِي أَمْرٍ اسْتَفْتَيْتُهُ فِيهِ، أَتَانِي رَجُلاَنِ، فَجَلَسَ أَحَدُهُمَا عِنْدَ رِجْلَىَّ وَالآخَرُ عِنْدَ رَأْسِي، فَقَالَ الَّذِي عِنْدَ رِجْلَىَّ لِلَّذِي عِنْدَ رَأْسِي مَا بَالُ الرَّجُلِ قَالَ مَطْبُوبٌ‏.‏ يَعْنِي مَسْحُورًا‏.‏ قَالَ وَمَنْ طَبَّهُ قَالَ لَبِيدُ بْنُ أَعْصَمَ‏.‏ قَالَ وَفِيمَ قَالَ فِي جُفِّ طَلْعَةٍ ذَكَرٍ فِي مُشْطٍ وَمُشَاقَةٍ، تَحْتَ رَعُوفَةٍ فِي بِئْرِ ذَرْوَانَ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) continued for such-and-such period imagining that he has slept (had sexual relations) with his wives, and in fact he did not. One day he said, to me, "O `Aisha! Allah has instructed me regarding a matter about which I had asked Him. There came to me two men, one of them sat near my feet and the other near my head. The one near my feet, asked the one near my head (pointing at me), 'What is wrong with this man? The latter replied, 'He is under the effect of magic.' The first one asked, 'Who had worked magic on him?' The other replied, 'Lubaid bin Asam.' The first one asked, 'What material (did he use)?' The other replied, 'The skin of the pollen of a male date tree with a comb and the hair stuck to it, kept under a stone in the well of Dharwan."'

bukhari:6063.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ—that Labīd ibn al-Aʿṣam's spell was a purely physical ailment restricted to worldly marital relations that never impaired Muhammad's intellect (*ʿaql*), memory, or prophetic infallibility (*ʿiṣmah*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that he was `مَسْحُورًا` (*masḥūran*, "bewitched"—the exact condition Quran 17:47 and 25:8 condemn unbelievers as "wrongdoers" for attributing to him) and suffered prolonged delusions where `يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ يَأْتِي أَهْلَهُ وَلاَ يَأْتِي` ("it was made to appear to him that he had sexual relations with his wives when he had not"). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:3175, 5765) generalize this cognitive failure to `يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ يَفْعَلُ الشَّىْءَ وَمَا يَفْعَلُهُ` ("he used to imagine that he had done a thing when he had not done it"), proving that occult magic directly compromised his mind and perception of reality rather than merely his body.

muslim:403.note: During Muhammad's first revelation in the cave of Hira, the angel seizes and chokes/presses him (ghaṭṭanī) three times to the limit of exhaustion (balagha minnī al-jahd) before reciting [Quran 96:1-5](quran://96/1-5). Muhammad returns to Khadija with trembling neck muscles (tarjufu bawādiruhu), asks to be wrapped up until his terror (al-rawʿ) subsides, and states, 'I truly feared for myself,' before Khadija and her Christian cousin Waraqa b. Nawfal reassure him (cf. bukhari:3; contrast [Luke 1:13](bible://lk/1/13), [Luke 1:30](bible://lk/1/30)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَجَاءَهُ الْمَلَكُ فَقَالَ اقْرَأْ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ مَا أَنَا بِقَارِئٍ - قَالَ - فَأَخَذَنِي فَغَطَّنِي حَتَّى بَلَغَ مِنِّي الْجَهْدَ ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي فَقَالَ اقْرَأْ ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ مَ�� أَنَا بِقَارِئٍ - قَالَ - فَأَخَذَنِي فَغَطَّنِي الثَّانِيَةَ حَتَّى بَلَغَ مِنِّي الْجَهْدَ ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي فَقَالَ اقْرَأْ ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ مَا أَنَا بِقَارِئٍ فَأَخَذَنِي فَغَطَّنِي الثَّالِثَةَ حَتَّى بَلَغَ مِنِّي الْجَهْدَ ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏{‏ اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ * خَلَقَ الإِنْسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ * اقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الأَكْرَمُ * الَّذِي عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ * عَلَّمَ الإِنْسَانَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ‏}‏ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَرَجَعَ بِهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم تَرْجُفُ بَوَادِرُهُ حَتَّى دَخَلَ عَلَى خَدِيجَةَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ زَمِّلُونِي زَمِّلُونِي ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَزَمَّلُوهُ حَتَّى ذَهَبَ عَنْهُ الرَّوْعُ ثُمَّ قَالَ لِخَدِيجَةَ ‏"‏ أَىْ خَدِيجَةُ مَا لِي ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَأَخْبَرَهَا الْخَبَرَ قَالَ ‏"‏ لَقَدْ خَشِيتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: There came to him the angel and said: Recite, to which he replied: I am not lettered. He took hold of me [the Apostle said] and pressed me, till I was hard pressed; thereafter he let me off and said: Recite. I said: I am not lettered. He then again took hold of me and pressed me for the second time till I was hard pressed and then let me off and said: Recite, to which I replied: I am not lettered. He took hold of me and pressed me for the third time, till I was hard pressed and then let me go and said: Recite in the name of your Lord Who created, created man from a clot of blood. Recite. And your most bountiful Lord is He Who taught the use of pen, taught man what he knew not (al-Qur'an, xcvi. 1-4). Then the Prophet returned therewith, his heart was trembling, and he went to Khadija and said: Wrap me up, wrap me up! So they wrapped him till the fear had left him. He then said to Khadija: O Khadija! what has happened to me? and he informed her of the happening, saying: I fear for myself.

muslim:403.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Gabriel's three-fold squeeze was merely a firm, reassuring embrace meant to focus Muhammad's attention and prove he was awake, claiming his admission 'I feared for myself' (khashītu 'alā nafsī) only reflected natural awe at the weight of divine revelation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the entity violently choked or suffocated him to the point of utter physical exhaustion (fa-akhadhanī fa-ghaṭṭanī ḥattā balagha minnī al-jahd) three times, leaving him fleeing in sheer terror (al-raw') with visibly trembling neck muscles (tarjufu bawādiruhu) while asking Khadija, 'What is wrong with me?' (mā lī). Furthermore, both Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) and Ibn Hajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) explicitly acknowledge that khashītu 'alā nafsī includes the fear of insanity (al-junūn) or demonic possession—a trauma that parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:6982) confirm drove Muhammad to repeatedly attempt suicide by throwing himself off mountain cliffs.

muslim:5703.note: Aisha reports that Labid b. al-A'sam, a Jew of Banu Zuraiq, bewitched (*saḥara*) Muhammad using a comb, hair from the comb (*mushāṭah*), and the spathe of a male date-palm placed in the well of Dhi Arwan, causing him to imagine (*yukhayyalu ilayhi*) that he was doing things he had not done. The report describes him as bewitched (*maṭbūb*) without drawing any textual boundary between worldly actions and prophetic revelation, standing in tension with the Quran's condemnation of critics who called him 'a bewitched man' ([Quran 17:47](quran://17/47), [Quran 25:8](quran://25/8)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَحَرَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَهُودِيٌّ مِنْ يَهُودِ بَنِي زُرَيْقٍ يُقَالُ لَهُ لَبِيدُ بْنُ الأَعْصَمِ - قَالَتْ - حَتَّى كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ يَفْعَلُ الشَّىْءَ وَمَا يَفْعَلُهُ حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ أَوْ ذَاتَ لَيْلَةٍ دَعَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ دَعَا ثُمَّ دَعَا ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ يَا عَائِشَةُ أَشَعَرْتِ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَفْتَانِي فِيمَا اسْتَفْتَيْتُهُ فِيهِ جَاءَنِي رَجُلاَنِ فَقَعَدَ أَحَدُهُمَا عِنْدَ رَأْسِي وَالآخَرُ عِنْدَ رِجْلَىَّ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ الَّذِي عِنْدَ رَأْسِي لِلَّذِي عِنْدَ رِجْلَىَّ أَوِ الَّذِي عِنْدَ رِجْلَىَّ لِلَّذِي عِنْدَ رَأْسِي مَا وَجَعُ الرَّجُلِ قَالَ مَطْبُوبٌ ‏.‏ قَالَ مَنْ طَبَّهُ قَالَ لَبِيدُ بْنُ الأَعْصَمِ ‏.‏ قَالَ فِي أَىِّ شَىْءٍ قَالَ فِي مُشْطٍ وَمُشَاطَةٍ ‏.‏ قَالَ وَجُبِّ طَلْعَةِ ذَكَرٍ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَيْنَ هُوَ قَالَ فِي بِئْرِ ذِي أَرْوَانَ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: a Jew from among the Jews of Banu Zuraiq who was called Labid b. al-A'sam cast a spell upon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) with the result that he (under the influence of the spell) felt that he had been doing something whereas in fact he had not been doing that. (This state of affairs lasted) until one day or during one night Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) made supplication (to dispel its effects). He again made a supplication and he again did this and said to 'A'isha: "Do you know that Allah has told me what I had asked Him? There came to me two men and one amongst them sat near my head and the other one near my feet and he who sat near my head said to one who sat near my feet or one who sat near my feet said to one who sat near my head: What is the trouble with the man? He said: The spell has affected him. He said: Who has cast that? He (the other one) said: It was Labid b. A'sam (who has done it). He said: What is the thing by which he transmitted its effect? He said: By the comb and by the hair stuck to the comb and the spathe of the date-palm. He said: Where is that? He replied: In the well of Dhi Arwan."

muslim:5703.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the spell cast by Labid b. al-A'sam only caused a temporary physical ailment or minor worldly delusion without impairing Muhammad's cognitive faculties or his infallibility in conveying revelation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in unqualified terms that Muhammad was bewitched (*saḥara* / *maṭbūb*) so that 'he was made to imagine that he was doing a thing when he was not doing it' (*yukhayyalu ilayhi annahu yafʿalu al-shayʾa wa-mā yafʿaluhu*), demonstrating that occult magic directly altered his perception of reality until two men informed him of the spell in the well of Dhi Arwan. Furthermore, this admission across `muslim:5703`, `muslim:5704`, `bukhari:3175`, and `bukhari:5763` directly concedes the exact charge that [Quran 17:47](quran://17/47) and [Quran 25:8](quran://25/8) denounce as the slander of wrongdoers: that his followers were obeying 'a bewitched man' (*rajulan masḥūran*).

bukhari:3.note: During his first revelation in the cave of Hira, the angel seized and pressed Muhammad three times until he reached his limit of endurance (فَغَطَّنِي حَتَّى بَلَغَ مِنِّي الْجَهْدَ) before delivering [Quran 96:1-3](quran://96/1-3). Muhammad returned to Khadija with a trembling heart, asked to be covered until his fear subsided, and declared, 'I feared for myself' (لَقَدْ خَشِيتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي), whereupon Khadija and her Christian cousin Waraqa bin Naufal reassured him that the visitor was the angel sent to Moses.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَخَذَنِي فَغَطَّنِي حَتَّى بَلَغَ مِنِّي الْجَهْدَ، ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي فَقَالَ اقْرَأْ‏.‏ قُلْتُ مَا أَنَا بِقَارِئٍ‏.‏ فَأَخَذَنِي فَغَطَّنِي الثَّانِيَةَ حَتَّى بَلَغَ مِنِّي الْجَهْدَ، ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي فَقَالَ اقْرَأْ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ مَا أَنَا بِقَارِئٍ‏.‏ فَأَخَذَنِي فَغَطَّنِي الثَّالِثَةَ، ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي فَقَالَ ‏{‏اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ * خَلَقَ الإِنْسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ * اقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الأَكْرَمُ‏}‏ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَرَجَعَ بِهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَرْجُفُ فُؤَادُهُ، فَدَخَلَ عَلَى خَدِيجَةَ بِنْتِ خُوَيْلِدٍ رضى الله عنها فَقَالَ ‏"‏ زَمِّلُونِي زَمِّلُونِي ‏"‏‏.‏ فَزَمَّلُوهُ حَتَّى ذَهَبَ عَنْهُ الرَّوْعُ، فَقَالَ لِخَدِيجَةَ وَأَخْبَرَهَا الْخَبَرَ ‏"‏ لَقَدْ خَشِيتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي
problematic_excerpt.english: The angel caught me (forcefully) and pressed me so hard that I could not bear it any more. He then released me and again asked me to read and I replied, 'I do not know how to read.' Thereupon he caught me again and pressed me a second time till I could not bear it any more. He then released me and again asked me to read but again I replied, 'I do not know how to read (or what shall I read)?' Thereupon he caught me for the third time and pressed me, and then released me and said, 'Read in the name of your Lord, who has created (all that exists), created man from a clot. Read! And your Lord is the Most Generous." (96.1, 96.2, 96.3) Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) returned with the Inspiration and with his heart beating severely. Then he went to Khadija bint Khuwailid and said, "Cover me! Cover me!" They covered him till his fear was over and after that he told her everything that had happened and said, "I fear that something may happen to me."

bukhari:3.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as explained in Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Gabriel's forceful pressing was merely a pedagogical embrace to focus Muhammad's mind and prepare his human frame for the heavy weight of revelation, while his terror was simply natural human shock upon seeing an angel in his true form. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the spirit violently crushed or suffocated him (fa-ghaṭṭanī) three times to the point of utter physical exhaustion (ḥattā balagha minnī al-jahd) without offering any identification or reassurance, leaving his heart trembling in dread (al-raw') as he cried, 'laqad khashītu 'alā nafsī' ('I feared for myself'). Moreover, Ibn Ḥajar himself admits in Fatḥ al-Bārī that commentators interpreted 'khashītu 'alā nafsī' to mean Muhammad feared he had been struck with madness (al-junūn) or jinn possession—a trauma confirmed in the parallel narration of Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6982, where the aftermath of this encounter drove him to repeatedly attempt suicide by throwing himself from mountain cliffs.

bukhari:4953.note: Recounting his first revelation in the cave of Hira, Muhammad states that when he replied he could not read, the angel seized and pressed him three times until he reached exhaustion before reciting Surah 96:1–5. He returned to Khadija with his neck and shoulder muscles trembling in fear, asked to be covered, and told her, 'I feared for myself,' prompting Khadija and her Christian cousin Waraqa bin Nawfal to reassure him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَخَذَنِي فَغَطَّنِي حَتَّى بَلَغَ مِنِّي الْجُهْدُ ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي‏.‏ فَقَالَ اقْرَأْ‏.‏ قُلْتُ مَا أَنَا بِقَارِئٍ‏.‏ فَأَخَذَنِي فَغَطَّنِي الثَّانِيِةَ حَتَّى بَلَغَ مِنِّي الْجُهْدُ، ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي‏.‏ فَقَالَ اقْرَأْ‏.‏ قُلْتُ مَا أَنَا بِقَارِئٍ‏.‏ فَأَخَذَنِي فَغَطَّنِي الثَّالِثَةَ حَتَّى بَلَغَ مِنِّي الْجُهْدُ ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَنِي‏.
problematic_excerpt.english: Then the Angel held me (forcibly) and pressed me so hard that I felt distressed. Then he released me and again asked me to read, and I replied, 'I do not know how to read.' Thereupon he held me again and pressed me for the second time till I felt distressed. He then released me and asked me to read, but again I replied. 'I do not know how to read.' Thereupon he held me for the third time and pressed me till I got distressed, and then he released me

bukhari:4953.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī—that Gabriel's three-time squeezing was merely a pedagogical embrace meant to focus Muhammad's spiritual attention and prepare his human frame for the heavy weight of revelation (Quran 73:5), and that his subsequent panic was simply natural human awe. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the entity violently throttled or suffocated him (*faghaṭṭanī*) to the point of utter physical exhaustion (*balagha minnī al-juhd*), leaving his neck muscles spasming in terror (*tarjufu bawādiruhu*) and crying, 'I feared for myself' (*laqad khashītu ʿalā nafsī*)—a phrase Ibn Hajar himself admits classical commentators interpreted as fear of madness (*al-junūn*) or demonic touch (*al-lamam*). Furthermore, the parallel narration in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 6982 reveals that the aftermath of this encounter drove Muhammad to repeatedly attempt suicide by throwing himself off mountain cliffs, standing in total antithesis to the biblical Gabriel who immediately comforts God's messengers with 'Fear not!' (Daniel 10:12; Luke 1:13, 30) rather than choking them into suicidal despair.

muslim:7110.note: When Aisha asks whether a devil (*shayṭān*) is attached to every human being and to him as well, Muhammad confirms that a devil is with him too, stating that his Lord helped him against it until it became a Muslim (*ḥattā aslama*, rendered in the published English translation as being safe from its mischief).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَوَمَعِيَ شَيْطَانٌ قَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ وَمَعَ كُلِّ إِنْسَانٍ قَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ وَمَعَكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ وَلَكِنْ رَبِّي أَعَانَنِي عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى أَسْلَمَ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: she said: Allah's Messenger, is there along with me a devil? He said: Yes. I said: Is a devil attached to everyone? He said: Yes. I (Aisha) again said: Allah's Messenger, is it with you also? He said: Yes, but my Lord has helped me against him and as such I am absolutely safe from his mischief

muslim:7110.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this passage merely means Muhammad was protected from temptation—relying on softened English renderings such as 'I am absolutely safe from his mischief'—or that his personal devil's submission proves his prophetic immunity. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that when Aisha asked if a devil (*shayṭān*) was attached to him (`وَمَعَكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ`), Muhammad answered 'Yes' (`نَعَمْ`) and declared `حَتَّى أَسْلَمَ` (*ḥattā aslama*), vocalized in the third-person past tense meaning 'until he became a Muslim' (as also recorded in `muslim:7108` and `muslim:7109`). Rather than casting out demons by the Spirit of God ([Matthew 12:28](bible://mt/12/28)), Muhammad retains an attached *shayṭān* that allegedly converted to Islam.

muslim:5546.note: Muhammad declares that angels do not accompany a group of travelers who have a dog or a bell (*jaras*) with them, and in muslim:5548 he states that the bell is the musical instrument of Satan (*mazāmīr al-shayṭān*). Yet in bukhari:2, Muhammad claims that angelic revelation came to him sounding like the ringing of a bell (*ṣalṣalat al-jaras*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ لاَ تَصْحَبُ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ رُفْقَةً فِيهَا كَلْبٌ وَلاَ جَرَسٌ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:Angels do not accompany the travellers who have with them a dog and a bell

muslim:5546.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the ringing of a bell (*ṣalṣalat al-jaras*) in `bukhari:2` is merely an acoustic simile for the intensity of revelation rather than a literal bell, or that the restriction in `muslim:5546` applies only to travelers rather than prophetic revelation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in unqualified terms that "the angels do not accompany" (*lā taṣḥabu al-malāʾikatu*) a group in which there is a bell (*jaras*). Employing the exact same item (*jaras*) that repels angels (`muslim:5546`, `muslim:5548`) as the defining auditory description of Muhammad's revelations (`bukhari:2`) establishes a direct tension within the Sahih texts over the nature of his spiritual encounters.

muslim:4664.note: Muhammad asks who will kill Ka'b b. al-Ashraf for maligning Allah and His Messenger and grants Muhammad b. Maslama permission to say whatever he wishes in order to kill him. Feigning hardship over Muhammad's demand for charity and offering to pledge weapons for a loan, Muhammad b. Maslama and his companions call Ka'b down at night, seize his head under the pretense of smelling his perfume, and kill him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ مَنْ لِكَعْبِ بْنِ الأَشْرَفِ فَإِنَّهُ قَدْ آذَى اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَتُحِبُّ أَنْ أَقْتُلَهُ قَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ ائْذَنْ لِي فَلأَقُلْ قَالَ ‏"‏ قُلْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَأَتَاهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ وَذَكَرَ مَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَقَالَ إِنَّ هَذَا الرَّجُلَ قَدْ أَرَادَ صَدَقَةً وَقَدْ عَنَّانَا ‏.‏ فَلَمَّا سَمِعَهُ قَالَ وَأَيْضًا وَاللَّهِ لَتَمَلُّنَّهُ ‏.‏ قَالَ إِنَّا قَدِ اتَّبَعْنَاهُ الآنَ وَنَكْرَهُ أَنْ نَدَعَهُ حَتَّى نَنْظُرَ إِلَى أَىِّ شَىْءٍ يَصِيرُ أَمْرُهُ - قَالَ - وَقَدْ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ تُسْلِفَنِي سَلَفًا قَالَ فَمَا تَرْهَنُنِي قَالَ مَا تُرِيدُ ‏.‏ قَالَ تَرْهَنُنِي نِسَاءَكُمْ قَالَ أَنْتَ أَجْمَلُ الْعَرَبِ أَنَرْهَنُكَ نِسَاءَنَا قَالَ لَهُ تَرْهَنُونِي أَوْلاَدَكُمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ يُسَبُّ ابْنُ أَحَدِنَا فَيُقَالُ رُهِنَ فِي وَسْقَيْنِ مِنْ تَمْرٍ ‏.‏ وَلَكِنْ نَرْهَنُكَ اللأْمَةَ - يَعْنِي السِّلاَحَ - قَالَ فَنَعَمْ ‏.‏ وَوَاعَدَهُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُ بِالْحَارِثِ وَأَبِي عَبْسِ بْنِ جَبْرٍ وَعَبَّادِ بْنِ بِشْرٍ قَالَ فَجَاءُوا فَدَعَوْهُ لَيْلاً فَنَزَلَ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ سُفْيَانُ قَالَ غَيْرُ عَمْرٍو قَالَتْ لَهُ امْرَأَتُهُ إِنِّي لأَسْمَعُ صَوْتًا كَأَنَّهُ صَوْتُ دَمٍ قَالَ إِنَّمَا هَذَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ وَرَضِيعُهُ وَأَبُو نَائِلَةَ إِنَّ الْكَرِيمَ لَوْ دُعِيَ إِلَى طَعْنَةٍ لَيْلاً لأَجَابَ ‏.‏ قَالَ مُحَمَّدٌ إِنِّي إِذَا جَاءَ فَسَوْفَ أَمُدُّ يَدِي إِلَى رَأْسِهِ فَإِذَا اسْتَمْكَنْتُ مِنْهُ فَدُونَكُمْ قَالَ فَلَمَّا نَزَلَ نَزَلَ وَهُوَ مُتَوَشِّحٌ فَقَالُوا نَجِدُ مِنْكَ رِيحَ الطِّيبِ قَالَ نَعَمْ تَحْتِي فُلاَنَةُ هِيَ أَعْطَرُ نِسَاءِ الْعَرَبِ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَتَأْذَنُ لِي أَنْ أَشُمَّ مِنْهُ قَالَ نَعَمْ فَشُمَّ ‏.‏ فَتَنَاوَلَ فَشَمَّ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَتَأْذَنُ لِي أَنْ أَعُودَ قَالَ فَاسْتَمْكَنَ مِنْ رَأْسِهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ دُونَكُمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَتَلُوهُ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:Who will kill Ka'b b. Ashraf? He has maligned Allah, the Exalted, and His Messenger. Muhammad b. Maslama said: Messenger of Allah, do you wish that I should kill him? He said: Yes. He said: Permit me to talk (to him in the way I deem fit). He said: Talk (as you like). So, Muhammad b. Maslama came to Ka'b and talked to him, referred to the old friendship between them and said: This man (i. e. the Holy Prophet) has made up his mind to collect charity (from us) and this has put us to a great hardship. When be heard this, Ka'b said: By God, you will be put to more trouble by him. Muhammad b. Maslama said: No doubt, now we have become his followers and we do not like to forsake him until we see what turn his affairs will take. I want that you should give me a loan. He said: What will you mortgage? He said: What do you want? He said: Pledge me your women. He said: You are the most handsome of the Arabs; should we pledge our women to you? He said: Pledge me your children. He said: The son of one of us may abuse us saying that he was pledged for two wasqs of dates, but we can pledge you (cur) weapons. He said: All right. Then Muhammad b. Maslama promised that he would come to him with Harith, Abu 'Abs b. Jabr and Abbad b. Bishr. So they came and called upon him at night. He came down to them. Sufyan says that all the narrators except 'Amr have stated that his wife said: I hear a voice which sounds like the voice of murder. He said: It is only Muhammad b. Maslama and his foster-brother, Abu Na'ila. When a gentleman is called at night even it to be pierced with a spear, he should respond to the call. Muhammad said to his companions: As he comes down, I will extend my hands towards his head and when I hold him fast, you should do your job. So when he came down and he was holding his cloak under his arm, they said to him: We sense from you a very fine smell. He said: Yes, I have with me a mistress who is the most scented of the women of Arabia. He said: Allow me to smell (the scent on your head). He said: Yes, you may smell. So he caught it and smelt. Then he said: Allow me to do so (once again). He then held his head fast and said to his companions: Do your job. And they killed him

muslim:4664.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Ka'b b. al-Ashraf was executed as an active military combatant for treason and that Muhammad b. Maslama merely used permissible wartime ambiguity rather than outright deceit. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad solicited his killing because 'he has maligned Allah and His Messenger' (*fainnahu qad ādhā Allāha wa-rasūlahu*), and directly authorized Muhammad b. Maslama's request to speak falsehood (*i'dhan lī fala-aqul* — *qul*). Furthermore, the narration records a nighttime ambush (*fajā'ū fada'awhu laylan*) in which the assassins feigned disaffection over charity (*qad arāda ṣadaqatan wa-qad 'annānā*), fabricated a loan pledge to bring weapons (*narhanuka al-la'mata — ya'nī al-silāḥa*), and asked twice to smell Ka'b's perfumed head (*fata'dhanu lī an ashumma minhu*) solely to restrain and kill him, standing in direct contrast to the New Testament command to love one's enemies and abstain from deceit ([Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44), [Romans 12:19](bible://rom/12/19)).

bukhari:4040.note: Muhammad sent 'Abdullah ibn 'Atik, 'Abdullah ibn 'Utba, and a group of men to Abu Rafi', whereupon 'Abdullah ibn 'Atik infiltrated his fortress at night, locked the residents' doors from the outside, repeatedly altered his voice in the dark to feign coming to Abu Rafi's aid between sword strikes, and drove his sword into his belly until he heard the sound of bone, before returning to deliver the good news of his death to Muhammad.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: بَعَثَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى أَبِي رَافِعٍ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَتِيكٍ وَعَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُتْبَةَ فِي نَاسٍ مَعَهُمْ، فَانْطَلَقُوا حَتَّى دَنَوْا مِنَ الْحِصْنِ، فَقَالَ لَهُمْ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَتِيكٍ امْكُثُوا أَنْتُمْ حَتَّى أَنْطَلِقَ أَنَا فَأَنْظُرَ‏.‏ قَالَ فَتَلَطَّفْتُ أَنْ أَدْخُلَ الْحِصْنَ، فَفَقَدُوا حِمَارًا لَهُمْ ـ قَالَ ـ فَخَرَجُوا بِقَبَسٍ يَطْلُبُونَهُ ـ قَالَ ـ فَخَشِيتُ أَنْ أُعْرَفَ ـ قَالَ ـ فَغَطَّيْتُ رَأْسِي كَأَنِّي أَقْضِي حَاجَةً، ثُمَّ نَادَى صَاحِبُ الْبَابِ مَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ فَلْيَدْخُلْ قَبْلَ أَنْ أُغْلِقَهُ‏.‏ فَدَخَلْتُ ثُمَّ اخْتَبَأْتُ فِي مَرْبِطِ حِمَارٍ عِنْدَ باب الْحِصْنِ، فَتَعَشَّوْا عِنْدَ أَبِي رَافِعٍ وَتَحَدَّثُوا حَتَّى ذَهَبَتْ سَاعَةٌ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ، ثُمَّ رَجَعُوا إِلَى بُيُوتِهِمْ، فَلَمَّا هَدَأَتِ الأَصْوَاتُ وَلاَ أَسْمَعُ حَرَكَةً خَرَجْتُ ـ قَالَ ـ وَرَأَيْتُ صَاحِبَ الْبَابِ حَيْثُ وَضَعَ مِفْتَاحَ الْحِصْنِ، فِي كَوَّةٍ فَأَخَذْتُهُ فَفَتَحْتُ بِهِ باب الْحِصْنِ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ إِنْ نَذِرَ بِي الْقَوْمُ انْطَلَقْتُ عَلَى مَهَلٍ، ثُمَّ عَمَدْتُ إِلَى أَبْوَابِ بُيُوتِهِمْ، فَغَلَّقْتُهَا عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ ظَاهِرٍ، ثُمَّ صَعِدْتُ إِلَى أَبِي رَافِعٍ فِي سُلَّمٍ، فَإِذَا الْبَيْتُ مُظْلِمٌ قَدْ طَفِئَ سِرَاجُهُ، فَلَمْ أَدْرِ أَيْنَ الرَّجُلُ، فَقُلْتُ يَا أَبَا رَافِعٍ‏.‏ قَالَ مَنْ هَذَا قَالَ فَعَمَدْتُ نَحْوَ الصَّوْتِ فَأَضْرِبُهُ، وَصَاحَ فَلَمْ تُغْنِ شَيْئًا ـ قَالَ ـ ثُمَّ جِئْتُ كَأَنِّي أُغِيثُهُ فَقُلْتُ مَا لَكَ يَا أَبَا رَافِعٍ وَغَيَّرْتُ صَوْتِي‏.‏ فَقَالَ أَلاَ أُعْجِبُكَ لأُمِّكَ الْوَيْلُ، دَخَلَ عَلَىَّ رَجُلٌ فَضَرَبَنِي بِالسَّيْفِ‏.‏ قَالَ فَعَمَدْتُ لَهُ أَيْضًا فَأَضْرِبُهُ أُخْرَى فَلَمْ تُغْنِ شَيْئًا، فَصَاحَ وَقَامَ أَهْلُهُ، قَالَ ثُمَّ جِئْتُ وَغَيَّرْتُ صَوْتِي كَهَيْئَةِ الْمُغِيثِ، فَإِذَا هُوَ مُسْتَلْقٍ عَلَى ظَهْرِهِ، فَأَضَعُ السَّيْفَ فِي بَطْنِهِ ثُمَّ أَنْكَفِئُ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى سَمِعْتُ صَوْتَ الْعَظْمِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) sent `Abdullah bin 'Atik and `Abdullah bin `Utba with a group of men to Abu Rafi` (to kill him). They proceeded till they approached his castle, whereupon `Abdullah bin Atik said to them, "Wait (here), and in the meantime I will go and see." `Abdullah said later on, "I played a trick in order to enter the castle. By chance, they lost a donkey of theirs and came out carrying a flaming light to search for it. I was afraid that they would recognize me, so I covered my head and legs and pretended to answer the call to nature. The gatekeeper called, 'Whoever wants to come in, should come in before I close the gate.' So I went in and hid myself in a stall of a donkey near the gate of the castle. They took their supper with Abu Rafi` and had a chat till late at night. Then they went back to their homes. When the voices vanished and I no longer detected any movement, I came out. I had seen where the gate-keeper had kept the key of the castle in a hole in the wall. I took it and unlocked the gate of the castle, saying to myself, 'If these people should notice me, I will run away easily.' Then I locked all the doors of their houses from outside while they were inside, and ascended to Abu Rafi` by a staircase. I saw the house in complete darkness with its light off, and I could not know where the man was. So I called, 'O Abu Rafi`!' He replied, 'Who is it?' I proceeded towards the voice and hit him. He cried loudly but my blow was futile. Then I came to him, pretending to help him, saying with a different tone of my voice, ' What is wrong with you, O Abu Rafi`?' He said, 'Are you not surprised? Woe on your mother! A man has come to me and hit me with a sword!' So again I aimed at him and hit him, but the blow proved futile again, and on that Abu Rafi` cried loudly and his wife got up. I came again and changed my voice as if I were a helper, and found Abu Rafi` lying straight on his back, so I drove the sword into his belly and bent on it till I heard the sound of a bone break.

bukhari:4040.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Abu Rafi (Sallam bin Abi Al-Huqaiq) was a hostile war financier who incited pagan tribes against Medina, making his covert killing a legitimate military operation where tactical deception is permissible. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the assassin infiltrated a sleeping household and murdered an unarmed man in the dark by repeatedly feigning the voice of a sympathetic rescuer (ji'tu ka-annī ughīthuhu... wa-ghayyartu ṣawtī ka-hay'ati l-mughīth) until he could drive his sword through Abu Rafi's belly in front of his terrified wife. Furthermore, the adjacent narration in bukhari:4039 admits that Muhammad authorized this hit so the Khazraj tribe could match the prestige of the Aws after they assassinated Ka'b bin Al-Ashraf, and Ibn Hajar cites bukhari:4040 in Fatḥ al-Bārī as normative legal proof permitting the stealth assassination (ightiyāl) of unbelievers without warning.

bukhari:1846.note: During the Conquest of Mecca in AD 630, when informed that Ibn Khatal was clinging to the curtains of the Ka'ba for refuge, Muhammad commanded his followers, "Kill him." Classical commentators (such as Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi) explain that he was denied the Ka'ba's customary sanctuary (Quran 3:97) because he was accused of apostasy, killing a Muslim servant, and having singing girls recite satirical poetry against Muhammad.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم دَخَلَ عَامَ الْفَتْحِ، وَعَلَى رَأْسِهِ الْمِغْفَرُ، فَلَمَّا نَزَعَهُ جَاءَ رَجُلٌ، فَقَالَ إِنَّ ابْنَ خَطَلٍ مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِأَسْتَارِ الْكَعْبَةِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ اقْتُلُوهُ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) entered Mecca in the year of its Conquest wearing an Arabian helmet on his head and when the Prophet (ﷺ) took it off, a person came and said, "Ibn Khatal is holding the covering of the Ka`ba (taking refuge in the Ka`ba)." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Kill him

bukhari:1846.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Ibn Khatal was executed not for political dissent or apostasy, but as retributive justice (*qiṣāṣ*) for murdering a Muslim servant before fleeing to Mecca, carried out during a temporary one-hour prophetic suspension of Mecca's sanctuary (`bukhari:1834`). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad ordered his summary execution (`اقْتُلُوهُ`) while he was unarmed and clinging to the curtains of the Ka'ba (`مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِأَسْتَارِ الْكَعْبَةِ`), directly violating the Quran's unconditional sanctuary guarantee in Surah 3:97 (`وَمَن دَخَلَهُ كَانَ آمِنًا`—'whoever enters it shall be safe'). Furthermore, as Ibn Hajar documents in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* (on `bukhari:1846` and `bukhari:4286`), Muhammad simultaneously ordered the execution of Ibn Khatal's two singing slave girls—who had committed no murder—solely for chanting satirical poetry mocking him (`يُغَنِّيَانِ بِهِجَاءِ النَّبِيِّ`), proving the death warrants targeted verbal insult rather than homicide.

muslim:6634.note: In Salih's transmission, Umm Kulthum directly attributes to Muhammad himself the concession to lie in three cases—enumerated in the cross-referenced report (muslim:6633) as war, reconciling people, and spouses speaking to one another—rather than recording that specification as a statement of Ibn Shihab as in Yunus's transmission. The published English translation omits this entire Arabic clause, summarizing it only as 'a slight variation of wording.'

problematic_excerpt.arabic: مِثْلَهُ غَيْرَ أَنَّفِي حَدِيثِ صَالِحٍ وَقَالَتْ وَلَمْ أَسْمَعْهُ يُرَخِّصُ فِي شَىْءٍ مِمَّا يَقُولُ النَّاسُ إِلاَّ فِي ثَلاَثٍ ‏.‏ بِمِثْلِ مَا جَعَلَهُ يُونُسُ مِنْ قَوْلِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: This hadith has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab with the same chain of transmitters but with a slight variation of wording

muslim:6634.literal_translation: The like of it, except that in the narration of Salih she [Umm Kulthum] said: 'And I did not hear him [the Prophet] grant concession in anything of what people speak except in three,' just like what Yunus made the statement of Ibn Shihab.

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَقَالَتْ وَلَمْ أَسْمَعْهُ يُرَخِّصُ فِي شَىْءٍ مِمَّا يَقُولُ النَّاسُ إِلاَّ فِي ثَلاَثٍ ‏.‏ بِمِثْلِ مَا جَعَلَهُ يُونُسُ مِنْ قَوْلِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ
translation_issue.published_rendering: but with a slight variation of wording
translation_issue.literal_meaning: And she said: 'And I did not hear him grant concession in anything of what people speak except in three,' just like what Yunus made the statement of Ibn Shihab.
translation_issue.explanation: The translator omits the Arabic clause in which Umm Kulthum explicitly attributes the permission to lie in three cases directly to Muhammad himself ('I did not hear him grant concession') rather than to the later jurist Ibn Shihab, summarizing it away as 'a slight variation of wording.'

muslim:6634.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the three exceptions permitting falsehood—in war, reconciling people, and spouses speaking to one another—were merely an explanatory addition by the narrator Ibn Shihab rather than a directive from Muhammad himself. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in Salih's transmission that Umm Kulthum said, 'And I did not hear him grant concession in anything of what people speak except in three' (وَقَالَتْ وَلَمْ أَسْمَعْهُ يُرَخِّصُ فِي شَىْءٍ مِمَّا يَقُولُ النَّاسُ إِلاَّ فِي ثَلاَثٍ), directly attributing the three exemptions to Muhammad rather than to the statement of Ibn Shihab (بِمِثْلِ مَا جَعَلَهُ يُونُسُ مِنْ قَوْلِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ). Moreover, the published English translation conceals this direct prophetic attribution from English readers by omitting the entire Arabic clause and summarizing it away as 'a slight variation of wording.'

bukhari:6721.note: While angry, Muhammad swore by Allah not to give Abu Musa and the Ash'ariyyin mounts, yet after camels from war spoils arrived he gave them five camels. When his companions returned fearing that he had forgotten his oath, Muhammad declared that whenever he swears an oath and later sees a better alternative, he does what is better and absolves himself of the oath through expiation ([Matthew 5:33-37](bible://mt/5/33-37); [Numbers 30:2](bible://nm/30/2); cf. [Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَتَيْنَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي رَهْطٍ مِنَ الأَشْعَرِيِّينَ أَسْتَحْمِلُهُ، وَهْوَ يُقْسِمُ نَعَمًا مِنْ نَعَمِ الصَّدَقَةِ ـ قَالَ أَيُّوبُ أَحْسِبُهُ قَالَ وَهْوَ غَضْبَانُ ـ قَالَ ‏"‏ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أَحْمِلُكُمْ، وَمَا عِنْدِي مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَانْطَلَقْنَا فَأُتِيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِنَهْبِ إِبِلٍ، فَقِيلَ أَيْنَ هَؤُلاَءِ الأَشْعَرِيُّونَ فَأَتَيْنَا فَأَمَرَ لَنَا بِخَمْسِ ذَوْدٍ غُرِّ الذُّرَى، قَالَ فَانْدَفَعْنَا فَقُلْتُ لأَصْحَابِي أَتَيْنَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَسْتَحْمِلُهُ، فَحَلَفَ أَنْ لاَ يَحْمِلَنَا، ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَ إِلَيْنَا فَحَمَلَنَا، نَسِيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَمِينَهُ، وَاللَّهِ لَئِنْ تَغَفَّلْنَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَمِينَهُ لاَ نُفْلِحُ أَبَدًا، ارْجِعُوا بِنَا إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلْنُذَكِّرْهُ يَمِينَهُ‏.‏ فَرَجَعْنَا فَقُلْنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَتَيْنَاكَ نَسْتَحْمِلُكَ، فَحَلَفْتَ أَنْ لاَ تَحْمِلَنَا ثُمَّ حَمَلْتَنَا فَظَنَنَّا ـ أَوْ فَعَرَفْنَا ـ أَنَّكَ نَسِيتَ يَمِينَكَ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ انْطَلِقُوا، فَإِنَّمَا حَمَلَكُمُ اللَّهُ، إِنِّي وَاللَّهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لاَ أَحْلِفُ عَلَى يَمِينٍ، فَأَرَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا، إِلاَّ أَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ وَتَحَلَّلْتُهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Once we went to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) in company with a group of Ash'airiyin, asking him for mounts while he was distributing some camels from the camels of Zakat. (Aiyub said, "I think he said that the Prophet was in an angry mood at the time.") The Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'By Allah! I will not give you mounts, and I have nothing to mount you on.' After we had left, some camels of booty were brought to Allah's Apostle and he said, "Where are those Ash`ariyin? Where are those Ash`ariyin?" So we went (to him) and he gave us five very fat good-looking camels. We mounted them and went away, and then I said to my companions, 'We went to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) to give us mounts, but he took an oath that he would not give us mounts, and then later on he sent for us and gave us mounts, perhaps Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) forgot his oath. By Allah, we will never be successful, for we have taken advantage of the fact that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) forgot to fulfill his oath. So let us return to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) to remind him of his oath.' We returned and said, 'O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! We came to you and asked you for mounts, but you took an oath that you would not give us mounts) but later on you gave us mounts, and we thought or considered that you have forgotten your oath.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'Depart, for Allah has given you Mounts. By Allah, Allah willing, if I take an oath and then later find another thing better than that, I do what is better, and make expiation for the oath.' "

bukhari:6721.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that breaking a vow to perform a greater good—such as providing mounts to needy companions—and paying legal expiation (*kaffārah*, per Quran 5:89 and 66:2) is an act of piety rather than dishonesty, or that his initial refusal merely reflected a temporary lack of animals (Ibn Hajar, *Fatḥ al-Bārī*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore a categorical oath in a fit of anger (*wa-huwa ghaḍbān*) while actively distributing Zakat camels (*wa-huwa yuqsimu naʿaman min naʿami al-ṣadaqah*), declaring, 'By Allah, I will not mount you, and I have nothing on which to mount you' (*wa-Allāhi lā aḥmilukum wa-mā ʿindī mā aḥmilukum*). Even his own companions recognized the moral gravity of violating a solemn vow sworn in God's name—fearing they would 'never prosper' (*lā nufliḥu abadan*) if he broke it—yet Muhammad codified a rule allowing oaths by Allah to be dissolved (*wa-taḥallaltuhā*) whenever a more advantageous option arises (*fa-arā ghayrahā khayran minhā*).

muslim:4273.note: Muhammad instructs that whoever swears an oath and later sees another course of action as better should do what is better and perform expiation for his broken oath (cf. [Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)). Although neighboring reports apply this ruling to retracting rash personal vows (muslim:4271, muslim:4272), the directive itself is stated as a general principle whenever an alternative is judged superior.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ مَنْ حَلَفَ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَرَأَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا فَلْيَأْتِ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ وَلْيُكَفِّرْ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:He who took an oath and (later on) found another thing better than that, he should do that which is better, and expiate for the vow (broken by him)

muslim:4273.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this ruling only permits breaking rash personal vows that prevent a person from performing a pious deed, rather than allowing someone to abandon solemn oaths whenever a more advantageous option appears. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an unrestricted condition—"whoever swears an oath and then sees something else as better than it" (*man ḥalafa ʿalā yamīnin fa-raʾā ghayrahā khayran minhā*)—instructing the swearer to do what is better and expiate for his oath (*wa-lyukaffir ʿan yamīnihi*). Grounded in [Quran 5:89](quran://5/89) and [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2), this framework makes sworn oaths revocable based on the swearer's own subsequent judgment (*fa-raʾā*), contrasting with the binding requirement to keep one's word in [Matthew 5:33](bible://mt/5/33).

muslim:2451.note: Muhammad distributed unrefined gold sent by Ali from Yemen among four Najdi tribal chiefs, angering the Quraish who complained that he gave to the chiefs of Najd while leaving them out. Muhammad stated that he did so only to win them over, and a man then confronted him saying, 'Fear Allah, O Muhammad.'

problematic_excerpt.arabic: بَعَثَ عَلِيٌّ - رضى الله عنه - وَهُوَ بِالْيَمَنِ بِذَهَبَةٍ فِي تُرْبَتِهَا إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَسَمَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَيْنَ أَرْبَعَةِ نَفَرٍ الأَقْرَعُ بْنُ حَابِسٍ الْحَنْظَلِيُّ وَعُيَيْنَةُ بْنُ بَدْرٍ الْفَزَارِيُّ وَعَلْقَمَةُ بْنُ عُلاَثَةَ الْعَامِرِيُّ ثُمَّ أَحَدُ بَنِي كِلاَبٍ وَزَيْدُ الْخَيْرِ الطَّائِيُّ ثُمَّ أَحَدُ بَنِي نَبْهَانَ - قَالَ - فَغَضِبَتْ قُرَيْشٌ فَقَالُوا أَتُعْطِي صَنَادِيدَ نَجْدٍ وَتَدَعُنَا فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنِّي إِنَّمَا فَعَلْتُ ذَلِكَ لأَتَأَلَّفَهُمْ ‏"‏ فَجَاءَ رَجُلٌ كَثُّ اللِّحْيَةِ مُشْرِفُ الْوَجْنَتَيْنِ غَائِرُ الْعَيْنَيْنِ نَاتِئُ الْجَبِينِ مَحْلُوقُ الرَّأْسِ فَقَالَ اتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَا مُحَمَّدُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Said Khudri reported that 'Ali (Allah be pleased with him) sent some gold alloyed with dust to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) distributed that among four men, al-Aqra b. Habis Hanzali and Uyaina b. Badr al-Fazari and 'Alqama b. 'Ulatha al-'Amiri, then to one person of the tribe of Kilab and to Zaid al-Khair al-Ta'l, and then to one person of the tribe of Nabhan. Upon this the people of Quraish felt angry and said:He (the Holy Prophet) gave to the chiefs of Najd and ignored us. Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: I have done it with a view to conciliating between them. Then there came a person with thick beard, prominent cheeks, deep sunken eyes and protruding forehead and shaven head. He said: Muhammad, fear Allah.

muslim:2451.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar explain under the Quranic principle of *al-mu'allafati qulūbuhum* (Quran 9:60), Muhammad's distribution of Yemeni gold was a wise, divinely sanctioned diplomatic strategy to solidify the faith of newly converted tribal leaders, while dismissing his critic as an insolent hypocrite who fathered the extremist Khawārij sect. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad's own Quraishī companions were outraged (*fa-ghaḍibat Quraysh*) because he bypassed faithful believers to lavish state plunder exclusively upon four powerful Najdī warlords (*ṣanādīd Najd*), forcing Muhammad to openly admit he was using war booty as political patronage to buy their loyalty (*li-ata'allafahum*). Furthermore, in the immediate parallel narration (*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2452), the objector directly exposes this transactional bribery as a division 'by which Allah's countenance was not sought' (*mā urīda bihā wajhu Allāh*), and rather than demonstrating how buying religious allegiance with gold is spiritually righteous, Muhammad demands unquestioning submission to his personal authority and vows to exterminate the critic's ideological descendants 'like the killing of ʿĀd' (*qatla ʿĀd*).

bukhari:2731.note: During the al-Hudaibiya negotiations (AD 628), Abu Bakr tells the Quraish envoy Urwa bin Mas'ud in Muhammad's presence without rebuke to "suck the clitoris of al-Lat" (imsus bazr al-Lat), an anatomical phrase affirmed literally by classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar that the published English translation renders as "abused him." Later in the same narration, after the convert Abu Basir tricks a Quraish envoy into handing over his sword and kills him, Muhammad remarks that he would be a war-kindler if he had supporters, prompting Abu Basir to form an armed band that kills Quraish caravan members and seizes their property.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ امْصُصْ بَظْرَ اللاَّتِ، أَنَحْنُ نَفِرُّ عَنْهُ وَنَدَعُهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Hearing that, Abu Bakr abused him and said, "Do you say we would run and leave the Prophet (ﷺ) alone?"

bukhari:2731.literal_translation: Abu Bakr said to him: "Suck the clitoris of al-Lat! Would we flee from him and leave him?"

translation_issue.arabic_term: امْصُصْ بَظْرَ اللاَّتِ
translation_issue.published_rendering: abused him and said
translation_issue.literal_meaning: suck the clitoris of al-Lat
translation_issue.explanation: The translator omitted the vulgar anatomical profanity uttered by Abu Bakr, replacing it with the vague phrase "abused him and said".

bukhari:2731.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī, that Abu Bakr merely redirected a customary Arab idiom against the pagan idol al-Lāt to humiliate polytheism and defend the Muslims' honor during tense negotiations. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Abu Bakr shouted the graphic anatomical obscenity 'imṣuṣ baẓra al-Lāt' ('suck the clitoris of al-Lāt') in Muhammad's immediate presence without receiving any rebuke, directly violating both the Quranic ban on reviling pagan deities (Surah 6:108) and Muhammad's own dictum that a believer is never foul-mouthed (fāḥish or badhī', Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1977). Furthermore, the fact that standard Sunni English translations deliberately conceal the exact words behind the sanitized phrase 'abused him' proves that modern Islamic scholars recognize the indefensible vulgarity of the original Arabic.

bukhari:2731.note: While observing the Muslim camp at al-Hudaibiya, the Quraish envoy Urwa bin Mas'ud reports that whenever Muhammad expectorates spittle (nukhamah), one of his companions catches it in his palm to rub over his own face and skin, and that his followers nearly fight one another over his used ablution water. Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar cite this account as a legal proof-text for the ritual purity of Muhammad's bodily secretions and the practice of seeking blessing (tabarruk) through them.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَوَاللَّهِ مَا تَنَخَّمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نُخَامَةً إِلاَّ وَقَعَتْ فِي كَفِّ رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ فَدَلَكَ بِهَا وَجْهَهُ وَجِلْدَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: By Allah, whenever Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) spat, the spittle would fall in the hand of one of them (i.e. the Prophet's companions) who would rub it on his face and skin

bukhari:2731.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī, that the Companions either staged this behavior at al-Hudaibiya as a strategic spectacle to intimidate the Quraysh envoy `Urwa ibn Mas`ud, or that seeking physical blessing (tabarruk) from Muhammad's bodily secretions was a uniquely pure prophetic privilege. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that whenever Muhammad coughed up phlegm (tanakhkhama... nukhāmatan—thick mucus expelled from the chest, not mere saliva), his followers caught it in their palms to rub over their faces and skin (dalka bihā wajhahu wa-jildahu) and nearly fought one another (kādū yaqtatilūna) over his used ablution water. Parallel Sahih narrations confirm that this was not a one-time diplomatic act but routine relic-veneration—such as Companions harvesting his sweat in bottles (muslim:6055) and fighting over his shaved hair (muslim:6043)—exposing a superstitious cult of a mortal man's bodily waste that contradicts Islam's claim of strict, anti-idolatrous monotheism.

bukhari:3110.note: Although [Quran 4:3](quran://4/3) permits Muslim men to marry up to four wives, Muhammad spoke from the pulpit when Ali proposed to Abu Jahl's daughter, stating he feared his daughter Fatima would be tried in her religion and swearing the two women would never be joined in marriage. While Muhammad states here that he is not prohibiting what is lawful, parallel reports record his ultimatum that Ali must divorce Fatima first (bukhari:5230), an intervention classical commentators explain as a special prophetic exemption (khususiyyah) to spare Fatima from co-wife jealousy.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ خَطَبَ ابْنَةَ أَبِي جَهْلٍ عَلَى فَاطِمَةَ ـ عَلَيْهَا السَّلاَمُ ـ فَسَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَخْطُبُ النَّاسَ فِي ذَلِكَ عَلَى مِنْبَرِهِ هَذَا وَأَنَا يَوْمَئِذٍ مُحْتَلِمٌ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ فَاطِمَةَ مِنِّي، وَأَنَا أَتَخَوَّفُ أَنْ تُفْتَنَ فِي دِينِهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ صِهْرًا لَهُ مِنْ بَنِي عَبْدِ شَمْسٍ، فَأَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ فِي مُصَاهَرَتِهِ إِيَّاهُ قَالَ ‏"‏ حَدَّثَنِي فَصَدَقَنِي، وَوَعَدَنِي فَوَفَى لِي، وَإِنِّي لَسْتُ أُحَرِّمُ حَلاَلاً وَلاَ أُحِلُّ حَرَامًا، وَلَكِنْ وَاللَّهِ لاَ تَجْتَمِعُ بِنْتُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَبِنْتُ عَدُوِّ اللَّهِ أَبَدًا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When `Ali bin Abu Talib demanded the hand of the daughter of Abi Jahal to be his wife besides Fatima, I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) on his pulpit delivering a sermon in this connection before the people, and I had then attained my age of puberty. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Fatima is from me, and I am afraid she will be subjected to trials in her religion (because of jealousy)." The Prophet (ﷺ) then mentioned one of his son-in-law who was from the tribe of 'Abdi Shams, and he praised him as a good son-in-law, saying, "Whatever he said was the truth, and he promised me and fulfilled his promise. I do not make a legal thing illegal, nor do I make an illegal thing legal, but by Allah, the daughter of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and the daughter of the enemy of Allah, (i.e. Abu Jahl) can never get together (as the wives of one man)

bukhari:3110.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was not exempting his family from polygamy—citing his disclaimer 'I do not make a lawful thing unlawful' (wa-innī lastu uḥarrimu ḥalālan)—but, as Ibn Ḥajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) and Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) explain, was only preventing the dishonorable pairing of the Prophet's daughter with the daughter of God's enemy (Abu Jahl) and sparing Ali the sin of hurting the Prophet. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad feared co-wife jealousy would subject Fatima to trials in her religion (wa-anā atakhauwwafu an tuftana fī dīnihā) and praises his other son-in-law for remaining monogamous, while parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:5230; muslim:6310) record his universal objection: 'My daughter is a part of me; whatever troubles her troubles me, and whatever harms her harms me' (yurībunī mā rābahā wa-yuʾdhīnī mā ādhāhā). By admitting from the pulpit that polygamy inflicts severe emotional harm (adhā) and spiritual trial (fitnah) on a wife while simultaneously legislating up to four wives for Muslim men (Quran 4:3) and maintaining nine wives himself, Muhammad enforced a blatant double standard that shielded his own daughter from the very distress his law imposed on all other women.

muslim:6619.note: Declaring that he is only a human being (*innamā anā bashar*), Muhammad claims an unbreakable covenant with Allah that whichever believer he harms (*ādhaytuhu*), reviles (*shatamtuhu*), curses (*laʿantuhu*), or whips (*jaladtuhu*), Allah will make it for him a blessing, purification, and means of nearness to Him on the Day of Resurrection.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَتَّخِذُ عِنْدَكَ عَهْدًا لَنْ تُخْلِفَنِيهِ فَإِنَّمَا أَنَا بَشَرٌ فَأَىُّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ آذَيْتُهُ شَتَمْتُهُ لَعَنْتُهُ جَلَدْتُهُ فَاجْعَلْهَا لَهُ صَلاَةً وَزَكَاةً وَقُرْبَةً تُقَرِّبُهُ بِهَا إِلَيْكَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) as saying:O Allah, I make a covenant with Thee against which Thou wouldst never go. I am a human being and thus for a Muslim whom I give any harm or whom I scold or upon whom I invoke curse or whom I beat, make this a source of blessing, purification and nearness to Thee on the Day of Resurrection

muslim:6619.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this supplication reflects prophetic humility and mercy, claiming that Muhammad only administered deserved discipline or used harmless idiomatic expressions of rebuke. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that because he is only a human being (*fa-innamā anā bashar*), he harms (*ādhaytuhu*), reviles (*shatamtuhu*), curses (*laʿantuhu*), and whips (*jaladtuhu*) believers (`bukhari:6361`, `muslim:6616`, `muslim:6622`), asking Allah to compensate the victims on the Day of Resurrection rather than refraining from mistreating them ([1 Peter 2:23](bible://1pt/2/23)).

muslim:6633.note: Muhammad declares that one who reconciles between people and speaks or conveys good is not a liar. Ibn Shihab adds—in a clause that muslim:6634 attributes through Umm Kulthum directly to Muhammad—that no concession was granted in anything people call a lie except in three cases: war, reconciling between people, and a husband and wife speaking to one another.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّهَا سَمِعَتْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُوَ يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ لَيْسَ الْكَذَّابُ الَّذِي يُصْلِحُ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ وَيَقُولُ خَيْرًا وَيَنْمِي خَيْرًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ شِهَابٍ وَلَمْ أَسْمَعْ يُرَخَّصُ فِي شَىْءٍ مِمَّا يَقُولُ النَّاسُ كَذِبٌ إِلاَّ فِي ثَلاَثٍ الْحَرْبُ وَالإِصْلاَحُ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ وَحَدِيثُ الرَّجُلِ امْرَأَتَهُ وَحَدِيثُ الْمَرْأَةِ زَوْجَهَا ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: she heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:A liar is not one who tries to bring reconciliation amongst people and speaks good (in order to avert dispute), or he conveys good. Ibn Shihab said he did not hear that exemption was granted in anything what the people speak as lie but in three cases: in battle, for bringing reconciliation amongst persons and the narration of the words of the husband to his wife, and the narration of the words of a wife to her husband (in a twisted form in order to bring reconciliation between them)

muslim:6633.literal_translation: she heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying: 'A liar is not one who reconciles between people and speaks good and conveys good.' Ibn Shihab said: And I did not hear any concession granted in anything that people call a lie except in three: war, reconciling between people, and a man's speaking to his wife, and a woman's speaking to her husband.

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَحَدِيثُ الرَّجُلِ امْرَأَتَهُ وَحَدِيثُ الْمَرْأَةِ زَوْجَهَا
translation_issue.published_rendering: and the narration of the words of the husband to his wife, and the narration of the words of a wife to her husband (in a twisted form in order to bring reconciliation between them)
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and a man's speaking to his wife, and a woman's speaking to her husband
translation_issue.explanation: The translator reframes direct speech between spouses as 'the narration of the words' and interpolates an unattested parenthetical gloss ('in a twisted form in order to bring reconciliation between them') to soften the permission for husbands and wives to lie to one another.

muslim:6633.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration only permits harmless ambiguity rather than actual falsehood, or that the three exemptions are merely an appended remark by Ibn Shihab rather than Muhammad's own ruling. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the concession (yurakhkhasu) applies directly to "what the people call a lie" (mimma yaqulu al-nasu kadhibun) in war (al-harb), reconciling people (al-islahu bayna al-nas), and a husband's and wife's speech to one another (hadithu al-rajuli imra'atahu wa-hadithu al-mar'ati zawjaha), which the English translator had to soften by inserting the unattested parenthetical gloss "(in a twisted form in order to bring reconciliation between them)". Furthermore, Muhammad's own statement (corroborated in bukhari:2692 and muslim:6634) redefines one who conveys fabricated good reports (yaqulu khayran wa-yanmi khayran) as "not a liar" (laysa al-kadhdhab), directly contradicting the New Testament command not to lie to one another ([Colossians 3:9](bible://col/3/9)).

bukhari:2732.note: During the al-Hudaibiya negotiations, Abu Bakr told the Quraysh emissary 'Urwa bin Mas'ud to 'suck the clitoris of al-Lat' (imsus bazr al-Lat) in Muhammad's presence without rebuke, a phrase the English translation renders as 'abused him.' In Sunni jurisprudence, Muhammad's silence constitutes tacit approval (taqrir), which classical commentators like Ibn Hajar cite when discussing the permissibility of using such expressions against polytheists.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ امْصُصْ بَظْرَ اللاَّتِ، أَنَحْنُ نَفِرُّ عَنْهُ وَنَدَعُهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Hearing that, Abu Bakr abused him and said, "Do you say we would run and leave the Prophet (ﷺ) alone?"

bukhari:2732.literal_translation: Abu Bakr said to him: "Suck the clitoris of al-Lat! Would we flee from him and leave him?"

translation_issue.arabic_term: امْصُصْ بَظْرَ اللاَّتِ
translation_issue.published_rendering: abused him and said
translation_issue.literal_meaning: suck the clitoris of al-Lat
translation_issue.explanation: The translator omitted the vulgar anatomical profanity uttered by Abu Bakr, replacing it with the vague phrase "abused him and said".

bukhari:2732.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī, that Abu Bakr merely adapted a common Arab idiom to humiliate the pagan idol al-Lāt after 'Urwa provoked the Muslims by calling them a mob of cowards. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Abu Bakr shouted the graphic anatomical obscenity 'imṣuṣ baẓra al-Lāt' ('suck the clitoris of al-Lāt') during a formal diplomatic negotiation while Muhammad sat silently and approved it without rebuke. This directly contradicts Quran 6:108—which forbids reviling pagan deities—and exposes a vulgarity so embarrassing that modern English translators deliberately whitewash the Arabic into the generic phrase 'abused him.'

bukhari:2732.note: Whenever Muhammad expectorated mucus or spittle (nukhamah) at al-Hudaibiya, his companions caught it in their palms to rub over their faces and skin, and they nearly fought one another over his used ablution water. Classical commentators affirm this account literally as a practice of seeking blessing (tabarruk) from Muhammad's bodily remnants.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَوَاللَّهِ مَا تَنَخَّمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نُخَامَةً إِلاَّ وَقَعَتْ فِي كَفِّ رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ فَدَلَكَ بِهَا وَجْهَهُ وَجِلْدَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: By Allah, whenever Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) spat, the spittle would fall in the hand of one of them (i.e. the Prophet's companions) who would rub it on his face and skin

bukhari:2732.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, following Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī, that seeking physical blessing (tabarruk) from Muhammad's bodily fluids was uniquely permissible because his body was divinely pure, and that the Companions amplified this display to intimidate the Quraysh envoy 'Urwa ibn Mas'ud. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that whenever Muhammad coughed up 'nukhāmah'—thick phlegm or mucus from the chest, not mere saliva—his followers caught it in their palms and rubbed it over their faces and skin ('fadallaka bihā wajhahu wa-jildahu') while nearly fighting one another ('kādū yaqtatilūna') over his used ablution water. By encouraging his followers to smear his expelled respiratory mucus on their bodies in cultic devotion, Muhammad presided over the very sort of extreme creature-veneration that Islamic theology otherwise condemns in other religions.

muslim:3308.note: Upon entering Mecca wearing a helmet during the conquest in AD 630, Muhammad is informed that Ibn Khatal is clinging to the curtains of the Ka'ba and commands, 'Kill him' ([Quran 3:97](quran://3/97), [Exodus 20:13](bible://ex/20/13)). Classical commentators such as al-Nawawī and Ibn Hajar harmonize this execution inside the sacred precinct with Mecca's sanctuary inviolability by citing a temporary prophetic exemption granted on the day of conquest (cf. bukhari:1846, bukhari:3044).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم دَخَلَ مَكَّةَ عَامَ الْفَتْحِ وَعَلَى رَأْسِهِ مِغْفَرٌ فَلَمَّا نَزَعَهُ جَاءَهُ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ ابْنُ خَطَلٍ مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِأَسْتَارِ الْكَعْبَةِ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ اقْتُلُوهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Anas b. Malik (Allah be pleased with them) reported that Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) entered Mecca in the Year of Victory with a helmet on his head; and when he took it off, a man came to him and said:Ibn Khatal is hanging on to the curtains of the Ka'ba, whereupon he said: Kill him.

muslim:3308.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue (citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*) that Abdullah ibn Khatal was executed as lawful retribution (*qiṣāṣ*) for murdering a servant before defecting, and that Allah temporarily suspended Mecca's sanctuary laws for Muhammad for one hour during the conquest in AD 630. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that he was clinging to the curtains of the Ka'ba (*mutaʿalliqun bi-astāri al-Kaʿbah*) when Muhammad summarily ordered *"uqtulūhu"* ("Kill him"), flatly contradicting the unconditional Quranic guarantee that whoever enters the Sacred Mosque is safe (*wa-man dakhalahu kāna āminan*, Quran 3:97). Moreover, Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī* 4/60) admits that Muhammad simultaneously ordered the execution of Ibn Khatal's two singing slave-girls (*qaynatān*) solely for chanting satirical verses mocking him, proving the purge targeted political dissidents rather than enforcing a neutral murder trial.

muslim:4265.note: Muhammad swore by Allah not to provide mounts (*wa-llāhi lā aḥmilukum*, softened in translation to 'I cannot provide you with riding animals') to Abu Musa and a group of Ash'arites, then broke his oath by giving them five white-humped camels after war booty arrived. When reminded of his oath, he declared that he never swears an oath and later sees another option as better without doing what is better and making atonement to dissolve his oath ([Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنِّي أَتَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي رَهْطٍ مِنَ الأَشْعَرِيِّينَ نَسْتَحْمِلُهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أَحْمِلُكُمْ وَمَا عِنْدِي مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَلَبِثْنَا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ فَأُتِيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِنَهْبِ إِبِلٍ فَدَعَا بِنَا فَأَمَرَ لَنَا بِخَمْسِ ذَوْدٍ غُرِّ الذُّرَى قَالَ فَلَمَّا انْطَلَقْنَا قَالَ بَعْضُنَا لِبَعْضٍ أَغْفَلْنَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَمِينَهُ لاَ يُبَارَكُ لَنَا ‏.‏ فَرَجَعْنَا إِلَيْهِ فَقُلْنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّا أَتَيْنَاكَ نَسْتَحْمِلُكَ وَإِنَّكَ حَلَفْتَ أَنْ لاَ تَحْمِلَنَا ثُمَّ حَمَلْتَنَا أَفَنَسِيتَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنِّي وَاللَّهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لاَ أَحْلِفُ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَأَرَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا إِلاَّ أَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ وَتَحَلَّلْتُهَا فَانْطَلِقُوا فَإِنَّمَا حَمَلَكُمُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) along with a group of people belonging to the tribe of Ash'ari, asking him to provide us with riding camels. He (the Holy Prophet) said: By Allah, I cannot provide you with riding animals. And there is nothing with me with which I can provide you a mount. We stayed (for some time) there as Allah willed, and there was brought to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) booty of camels. He called us and commanded that we should be given five white humped camels. As we were about to go back, some of us said to the other: As we made Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) forget oath, there would be no blessing for us (in his gift). We went back to him and said: Allah's Messenger, we came to you to provide us with riding animals and you took an oath that you would never equip us with mounts and then you have provided us with the riding beasts Allah's Messenger, have you forgotten? Thereupon he said: I swear by Allah that if Allah so wills, I shall not swear an oath, and then consider something else to be better than it without making atonement for my oath and doing the thing that is better. So you go; Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, has given you riding animals

muslim:4265.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad merely stated he lacked mounts at that moment, or that breaking an oath to perform a charitable act through expiation ([Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)) is a virtuous legal principle rather than a moral breach. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that he swore a categorical negative oath—*wallāhi lā aḥmilukum* ('By Allah, I will not provide you with mounts')—which his own companions recognized as a violated vow (*ḥalafta an lā taḥmilanā thumma ḥamaltanā*) that risked stripping their gift of blessing (*lā yubāraku lanā*). By declaring that he never swears an oath (*lā aḥlifu ʿalā yamīnin*) without breaking and absolving it (*taḥallaltuhā*) whenever he sees another option as better (*khayran minhā*), Muhammad treated solemn oaths in God's name as revocable conveniences, directly contradicting the biblical command that vows to the Lord must not be broken ([Numbers 30:2](bible://nm/30/2), [Matthew 5:33](bible://mt/5/33)).

muslim:6022.note: Following the conquest of Mecca and the fighting at Hunayn, Muhammad gave Safwan ibn Umayya one hundred camels three consecutive times—consistent with reconciling hearts through material wealth ([Quran 9:60](quran://9/60); cf. muslim:6021). Safwan swore by Allah that Muhammad was the most detested of people to him when those gifts began, yet Muhammad continued giving to him until he became the dearest of people to him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: غَزَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم غَزْوَةَ الْفَتْحِ فَتْحِ مَكَّةَ ثُمَّ خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِمَنْ مَعَهُ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَاقْتَتَلُوا بِحُنَيْنٍ فَنَصَرَ اللَّهُ دِينَهُ وَالْمُسْلِمِينَ وَأَعْطَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَوْمَئِذٍ صَفْوَانَ بْنَ أُمَيَّةَ مِائَةً مِنَ النَّعَمِ ثُمَّ مِائَةً ثُمَّ مِائَةً ‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ شِهَابٍ حَدَّثَنِي سَعِيدُ بْنُ الْمُسَيَّبِ أَنَّ صَفْوَانَ قَالَ وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ أَعْطَانِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَا أَعْطَانِي وَإِنَّهُ لأَبْغَضُ النَّاسِ إِلَىَّ فَمَا بَرِحَ يُعْطِينِي حَتَّى إِنَّهُ لأَحَبُّ النَّاسِ إِلَىَّ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) went on the expedition of Victory, i. e. the Victory of Mecca, and then he went out along with the Muslims and they fought at Hunain, and Allah granted victory to his religion and to the Muslims, and Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) gave one hundred camels to Safwan b. Umayya. He again gave him one hundred camels, and then again gave him one hundred camels. Sa'id b. Musayyib said that Safwan told him:(By Allah) Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) gave me what he gave me (and my state of mind at that time was) that he was the most detested person amongst people in my eyes. But he continued giving to me until now he is the dearest of people to me

muslim:6022.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that giving war spoils to Safwan ibn Umayya to reconcile hearts ([Quran 9:60](quran://9/60)) merely demonstrated detachment from worldly wealth that inspired genuine spiritual conviction. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in Safwan's own oath that Muhammad was the most detested of people to him (وَإِنَّهُ لأَبْغَضُ النَّاسِ إِلَىَّ) and that it was the continuous material handouts (فَمَا بَرِحَ يُعْطِينِي) of three hundred camels (مِائَةً مِنَ النَّعَمِ ثُمَّ مِائَةً ثُمَّ مِائَةً) after the battle of Hunayn that made Muhammad the dearest of people to him (حَتَّى إِنَّهُ لأَحَبُّ النَّاسِ إِلَىَّ). The narration records no theological teaching or spiritual proof, attributing the change in Safwan's attitude strictly to repeated transfers of livestock from the war spoils (muslim:6292, muslim:6021, bukhari:3147).

bukhari:6718.note: Muhammad swore by Allah not to provide Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and his companions with mounts, yet subsequently gave them three camels after camels were brought to him. When reminded of his oath, he stated that Allah had mounted them rather than him and declared that whenever he swears an oath and later sees a better option, he breaks his oath and performs expiation (*kaffārah*) ([Matthew 5:33-37](bible://mt/5/33-37); [Numbers 30:2](bible://nm/30/2); cf. [Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)).
