problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَتَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي رَهْطٍ مِنَ الأَشْعَرِيِّينَ أَسْتَحْمِلُهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أَحْمِلُكُمْ، مَا عِنْدِي مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ لَبِثْنَا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ، فَأُتِيَ بِإِبِلٍ فَأَمَرَ لَنَا بِثَلاَثَةِ ذَوْدٍ، فَلَمَّا انْطَلَقْنَا قَالَ بَعْضُنَا لِبَعْضٍ لاَ يُبَارِكُ اللَّهُ لَنَا، أَتَيْنَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَسْتَحْمِلُهُ فَحَلَفَ أَنْ لاَ يَحْمِلَنَا فَحَمَلَنَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ أَبُو مُوسَى فَأَتَيْنَا النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَذَكَرْنَا ذَلِكَ لَهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَا أَنَا حَمَلْتُكُمْ بَلِ اللَّهُ حَمَلَكُمْ، إِنِّي وَاللَّهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لاَ أَحْلِفُ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَأَرَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا، إِلاَّ كَفَّرْتُ عَنْ يَمِينِي، وَأَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ وَكَفَّرْتُ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I went to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) along with a group of people from (the tribe of) Al-Ash`ari, asking for mounts. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "By Allah, I will not give you anything to ride, and I have nothing to mount you on." We stayed there as long as Allah wished, and after that, some camels were brought to the Prophet and he ordered that we be given three camels. When we set out, some of us said to others, "Allah will not bless us, as we all went to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) asking him for mounts, and although he had sworn that he would not give us mounts, he did give us." So we returned to the Prophet; and mentioned that to him. He said, "I have not provided you with mounts, but Allah has. By Allah, Allah willing, if I ever take an oath, and then see that another is better than the first, I make expiation for my (dissolved) oath, and do what is better and make expiation

bukhari:6718.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī—that Muhammad merely lacked mounts at that moment and that Islamic jurisprudence (Quran 5:89; 66:2) commends dissolving an oath via expiation (kaffārah) whenever a better moral alternative arises. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore an unconditional vow by God's name (وَاللَّهِ لاَ أَحْمِلُكُمْ — "By Allah, I will not give you anything to ride") and then deflected personal responsibility onto God (مَا أَنَا حَمَلْتُكُمْ بَلِ اللَّهُ حَمَلَكُمْ — "I have not provided you with mounts, but Allah has") only after his own companions feared losing divine blessing (لاَ يُبَارِكُ اللَّهُ لَنَا) over his broken word. Furthermore, the parallel narration in bukhari:4385 admits he rashly swore this oath during a fit of anger (وَافَقَ ذَلِكَ غَضَبًا), codifying a utilitarian standard where solemn vows in God's name are disposable whenever a more convenient option appears (وَأَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ وَكَفَّرْتُ).

muslim:2436.note: After the Battle of Hunain (AD 630), Muhammad distributed 100 camels each from the spoils of Hawazin to men of the Quraysh, prompting young men among the Ansar to object that they were left out while their swords were still dripping with blood. Gathering the Ansar, Muhammad stated that he gives to men recently in unbelief in order to win them over (`ata'allafuhum`, cf. [Quran 9:60](quran://9/60); rendered with the unattested addition 'to truth' in the English translation), and asked if they were not pleased to return to their dwellings with him while others leave with the wealth.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَطَفِقَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُعْطِي رِجَالاً مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ الْمِائَةَ مِنَ الإِبِلِ فَقَالُوا يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ يُعْطِي قُرَيْشًا وَيَتْرُكُنَا وَسُيُوفُنَا تَقْطُرُ مِنْ دِمَائِهِمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ فَحُدِّثَ ذَلِكَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ قَوْلِهِمْ فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَى الأَنْصَارِ فَجَمَعَهُمْ فِي قُبَّةٍ مِنْ أَدَمٍ فَلَمَّا اجْتَمَعُوا جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَا حَدِيثٌ بَلَغَنِي عَنْكُمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُ فُقَهَاءُ الأَنْصَارِ أَمَّا ذَوُو رَأْيِنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَلَمْ يَقُولُوا شَيْئًا وَأَمَّا أُنَاسٌ مِنَّا حَدِيثَةٌ أَسْنَانُهُمْ قَالُوا يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لِرَسُولِهِ يُعْطِي قُرَيْشًا وَيَتْرُكُنَا وَسُيُوفُنَا تَقْطُرُ مِنْ دِمَائِهِمْ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَإِنِّي أُعْطِي رِجَالاً حَدِيثِي عَهْدٍ بِكُفْرٍ أَتَأَلَّفُهُمْ أَفَلاَ تَرْضَوْنَ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ النَّاسُ بِالأَمْوَالِ وَتَرْجِعُونَ إِلَى رِحَالِكُمْ بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ فَوَاللَّهِ لَمَا تَنْقَلِبُونَ بِهِ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَنْقَلِبُونَ بِهِ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set about distributing to some persons of Quraish one hundred camels Upon this they (the young people from the Ansar) said:May Allah grant pardon to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he bestowed (these camels) upon the people of Quraish, and he ignored us, whereas our swords are still dripping blood. Anas b. Malik said: Their statement was conveyed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he sent (someone) to the Ansar and gathered them under a tent of leather. When they had assembled, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to them and said: What is this news that has reached me from you? The wise people of the Ansar said: Messenger of Allah, so far as the sagacious amongst us are concerned they have said nothing, but we have amongst us persons of immature age; they said: May Allah grant pardon to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he gave to the Quraish and ignored us (despite the fact) that our swords are besmeared with their blood. Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: I give (at times material gifts) to persons who were quite recently in the state of unbelief, so that I may incline them to truth Don't you feel delighted that people should go with riches, and you should go back to your places with the Messenger of Allah? By Allah, that with which you would return is better than that with which they would return.

muslim:2436.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that withholding the Hunain war booty from the Ansar—as framed in Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—was a supreme spiritual honor recognizing their unshakeable faith, whereas gifting 100 camels each to Quraysh elites (*al-mu'allafatu qulūbuhum* under [Quran 9:60](quran://9/60)) was a benevolent measure to gently incline their hearts toward spiritual truth. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad handed out this massive plunder merely 'to win them over' (*ata'allafuhum*—with the words 'to truth' entirely fabricated by the English translator), proving that loyalty to Islam was openly purchased with captured wealth rather than won by moral conviction. Meanwhile, the Ansar who actually bled in combat recognized this as blatant tribal nepotism—protesting that 'he gives to the Quraysh and leaves us out, while our swords are still dripping with their blood' (*yu'ṭī Qurayshan wa-yatrukunā wa-suyūfunā taqṭuru min dimā'ihim*)—only for Muhammad to pacify the fighters he exploited with rhetorical flattery and a cold admission that they would suffer 'severe preferential treatment against you' (*atharatan shadīdatan*) going forward.

muslim:2447.note: After the Battle of Hunayn, Muhammad gave preferential shares (athara) of the war spoils—including 100 camels each to Arab elites al-Aqra' ibn Habis and 'Uyaynah—a distribution classical commentators categorize under reconciling hearts ([Quran 9:60](quran://9/60)). When a man objected that the division was neither just nor done for Allah's sake, Muhammad's face turned deep red (ka-al-sirf) and he replied, "Who will be just if Allah and His Messenger are not just?"

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَمَّا كَانَ يَوْمُ حُنَيْنٍ آثَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَاسًا فِي الْقِسْمَةِ فَأَعْطَى الأَقْرَعَ بْنَ حَابِسٍ مِائَةً مِنَ الإِبِلِ وَأَعْطَى عُيَيْنَةَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ وَأَعْطَى أُنَاسًا مِنْ أَشْرَافِ الْعَرَبِ وَآثَرَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ فِي الْقِسْمَةِ فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ هَذِهِ لَقِسْمَةٌ مَا عُدِلَ فِيهَا وَمَا أُرِيدَ فِيهَا وَجْهُ اللَّهِ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقُلْتُ وَاللَّهِ لأُخْبِرَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم - قَالَ - فَأَتَيْتُهُ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ بِمَا قَالَ - قَالَ - فَتَغَيَّرَ وَجْهُهُ حَتَّى كَانَ كَالصِّرْفِ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَمَنْ يَعْدِلُ إِنْ لَمْ يَعْدِلِ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: On the day of Hunain, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) showed preference (to some) people in the distribution of the spoils. He bestowed on Aqra' b. Habis one hundred camels, and bestowed an equal (number) upon 'Uyaina, and bestowed on people among the elites of Arabia, and preferred them (to others) on that day, in the distribution (of spoils). Upon this a person said: By Allah, neither justice has been done in this distribution (of spoils), nor has the pleasure of Allah been sought in it. I (the narrator ) said: By Allah, I will certainly inform the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it. I came to him and informed him about what he had said. The colour of his (the Prophet's) face changed red like blood and he then said: "Who would do justice, if Allah and His Messenger do not do justice?"

muslim:2447.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as explained in Al-Nawawī’s Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and Ibn Ḥajar’s Fatḥ al-Bārī, Muhammad was merely exercising strategic statesmanship under Quran 9:60 (al-muʾallafatu qulūbuhum) by using his discretionary share of the spoils to reconcile wavering tribal leaders, and that the critic was a proto-Khārijī hypocrite. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states twice that Muhammad practiced unequal favoritism in the division (āthara... fī al-qismah) specifically toward the powerful 'elites of the Arabs' (ashrāf al-ʿarab) with massive payouts of 100 camels each (miʾatan min al-ibil)—a distribution that even the loyal Anṣār protested in parallel narrations (bukhari:4330, muslim:2436) while their swords were still dripping with blood. Rather than offering a transparent accounting of the plunder, Muhammad's face turned blood-red with rage (ka-al-ṣirf) and he insulated his political patronage from moral scrutiny by equating his personal favoritism with God's own justice ('fa-man yaʿdilu in lam yaʿdili Allāhu wa-rasūluh').

muslim:6021.note: After Muhammad gave a requester a flock of sheep filling the valley between two mountains, the recipient returned to his tribe urging them to embrace Islam because Muhammad gives like one who does not fear poverty (muslim:6020, muslim:6022). Anas ibn Malik adds that although a man would initially convert to Islam desiring nothing but worldly wealth, Islam would subsequently become dearer to him than the world and all it contains.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَجُلاً، سَأَلَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم غَنَمًا بَيْنَ جَبَلَيْنِ فَأَعْطَاهُ إِيَّاهُ فَأَتَى قَوْمَهُ فَقَالَ أَىْ قَوْمِ أَسْلِمُوا فَوَاللَّهِ إِنَّ مُحَمَّدًا لَيُعْطِي عَطَاءً مَا يَخَافُ الْفَقْرَ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ أَنَسٌ إِنْ كَانَ الرَّجُلُ لَيُسْلِمُ مَا يُرِيدُ إِلاَّ الدُّنْيَا فَمَا يُسْلِمُ حَتَّى يَكُونَ الإِسْلاَمُ أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا وَمَا عَلَيْهَا ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Anas 'b. Malik reported that a person requested Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) to give him a very large flock and he gave that to him. He came to his tribe and said:O people, embrace Islam. By Allah, Muhammad donates so much as if he did not fear want. Anas said that the person embraced Islam for the sake of the world but later he became Muslim until Islam became dearer to him than the world and what it contains

muslim:6021.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration illustrates Muhammad's generosity and that because such converts later came to love Islam more than worldly possessions, the initial material gifts served only to reconcile their hearts toward sincere faith ([Quran 9:60](quran://9/60)). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that after receiving 'sheep between two mountains' (غَنَمًا بَيْنَ جَبَلَيْنِ), the man summoned his tribe by saying, 'O my people, embrace Islam! For by Allah, Muhammad gives a gift as one who does not fear poverty' (أَىْ قَوْمِ أَسْلِمُوا فَوَاللَّهِ إِنَّ مُحَمَّدًا لَيُعْطِي عَطَاءً مَا يَخَافُ الْفَقْرَ), making material enrichment the direct appeal for tribal conversion. Furthermore, Anas ibn Malik's habitual statement—'Indeed, a man would embrace Islam desiring nothing but this world' (إِنْ كَانَ الرَّجُلُ لَيُسْلِمُ مَا يُرِيدُ إِلاَّ الدُّنْيَا)—confirms that professing Islam solely for worldly wealth was an established pattern rather than an isolated case (cf. muslim:6020, muslim:6022, [Acts 8:20](bible://acts/8/20), [1 Timothy 6:5](bible://1tm/6/5)).

muslim:2446.note: After the conquest of Hunayn (AD 630), Muhammad distributed the war spoils to those whose allegiance to Islam he sought to win through material incentives (*al-mu'allafatu qulūbuhum*, [Quran 9:60](quran://9/60)). When it reached him that the Ansar wished to receive a share like the others, he reminded them that Allah had guided, enriched, and united them through him, asking if they were not satisfied that others left with sheep and camels while they returned home with the Messenger of Allah.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَمَّا فَتَحَ حُنَيْنًا قَسَمَ الْغَنَائِمَ فَأَعْطَى الْمُؤَلَّفَةَ قُلُوبُهُمْ فَبَلَغَهُ أَنَّ الأَنْصَارَ يُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يُصِيبُوا مَا أَصَابَ النَّاسُ فَقَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَخَطَبَهُمْ فَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ وَأَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ يَا مَعْشَرَ الأَنْصَارِ أَلَمْ أَجِدْكُمْ ضُلاَّلاً فَهَدَاكُمُ اللَّهُ بِي وَعَالَةً فَأَغْنَاكُمُ اللَّهُ بِي وَمُتَفَرِّقِينَ فَجَمَعَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِي ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَيَقُولُونَ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمَنُّ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَلاَ تُجِيبُونِي ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالُوا اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمَنُّ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَمَا إِنَّكُمْ لَوْ شِئْتُمْ أَنْ تَقُولُوا كَذَا وَكَذَا وَكَانَ مِنَ الأَمْرِ كَذَا وَكَذَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ لأَشْيَاءَ عَدَّدَهَا ‏.‏ زَعَمَ عَمْرٌو أَنْ لاَ يَحْفَظُهَا فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَلاَ تَرْضَوْنَ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ النَّاسُ بِالشَّاءِ وَالإِبِلِ وَتَذْهَبُونَ بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ إِلَى رِحَالِكُمُ
problematic_excerpt.english: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Hunain he distributed the booty, and he bestowed upon those whose hearts it was intended to win. It was conveyed to him (the Holy Prophet) that the Ansar cherished a desire that they should be given (that very portion) which the people (of Quraish) had got. Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and, after having praised Allah and lauded Him, addressed them thus:O people of Ansar, did I not find you erring and Allah guided you aright through me, and (in the state of) being destitute and Allah made you free from want through me, and in a state of disunity and Allah united you through me, and they (the Ansar) said: Allah and His Messenger are most benevolent. He (again) said: Why do you not answer me? They said: Allah and His Messenger are the most benevolent. He said, If you wish you should say so and so, and the event (should take) such and such course (and in this connection he made a mention) of so many things. 'Amr is under the impression that he has not been able to remember them. He (the Holy Prophet) further said: Don't you feel happy (over this state of affairs) that the people should go away with goats and camels, and you go to your places along with the Messenger of Allah?

muslim:2446.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that withholding the spoils of Hunayn from the Ansar was an honor recognizing their unshakeable faith, whereas newly conquered Meccan elites needed material generosity to soften their hearts toward Islam. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad handed the war plunder (*qasama al-ghanāʾim*) to *al-muʾallafati qulūbuhum*—institutionalizing financial inducements to buy political loyalty and conversion ([Quran 9:60](quran://9/60))—while deflecting the protests of the Ansar who fought the battle by claiming, 'Did I not find you destitute and Allah enriched you through me?' (*wa-ʿālatan fa-aghnākumu Allāhu bī*). Rather than winning converts through spiritual truth, Muhammad bought off hostile Quraysh chiefs with 'sheep and camels' (*bi-al-shāʾi wa-al-ibil*) while pacifying his loyal Medinan soldiers with rhetoric that they should be content taking him home and enduring future material deprivation (*atharah*).

muslim:4263.note: Muhammad swore by Allah that he would not provide mounts to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and his companions because he had nothing on which to mount them, then gave them three white-humped camels after camels were brought to him. When they noted that he had sworn not to mount them, he stated that Allah had provided the mounts and declared that whenever he swears an oath and later sees something better, he expiates his oath and does what is better ([Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَتَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي رَهْطٍ مِنَ الأَشْعَرِيِّينَ نَسْتَحْمِلُهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أَحْمِلُكُمْ وَمَا عِنْدِي مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَلَبِثْنَا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ أُتِيَ بِإِبِلٍ فَأَمَرَ لَنَا بِثَلاَثِ ذَوْدٍ غُرِّ الذُّرَى فَلَمَّا انْطَلَقْنَا قُلْنَا - أَوْ قَالَ بَعْضُنَا لِبَعْضٍ - لاَ يُبَارِكُ اللَّهُ لَنَا أَتَيْنَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَسْتَحْمِلُهُ فَحَلَفَ أَنْ لاَ يَحْمِلَنَا ثُمَّ حَمَلَنَا ‏.‏ فَأَتَوْهُ فَأَخْبَرُوهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَا أَنَا حَمَلْتُكُمْ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَمَلَكُمْ وَإِنِّي وَاللَّهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لاَ أَحْلِفُ عَلَى يَمِينٍ ثُمَّ أَرَى خَيْرًا مِنْهَا إِلاَّ كَفَّرْتُ عَنْ يَمِينِي وَأَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I came to Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) along with a group of Ash'arites requesting to give us a mount. He (the Holy Prophet) said: By Allah, I cannot provide you with a mount, and there is nothing with me which I should give you as a ride. He (the narrator) said: We stayed there as long as Allah willed. Then there were brought to him (to the Holy Prophet) camels. He (the Holy Prophet) then ordered to give us three white humped camels, We started and said (or some of us said to the others): Allah will not bless us. We came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) begging him to provide us with riding camels. He swore that he could not provide us with a mount, but later on he provided us with that. They (some of the Prophet's Companions) came and informed him about this (rankling of theirs), whereupon he said: It was not I who provided you with a mount, but Allah has provided you with that. So far as I am concerned, by Allah, if He so wills, I would not swear, but if, later on, I would see better than it, I (would break the vow) and expiate it and do that which is better

muslim:4263.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad merely stated his present inability to provide mounts, and that breaking an oath to perform a better deed through expiation (kaffārah) is a virtuous legal provision ([Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore a categorical oath of refusal in Allah's name (wallāhi lā aḥmilukum, 'By Allah, I will not provide you with mounts'), which troubled his own companions so much that they said Allah would not bless them because he swore not to mount them and then did so (ḥalafa an lā yaḥmilanā thumma ḥamalanā). Rather than honoring the binding nature of oaths sworn in God's name ([Numbers 30:2](bible://nm/30/2), [Matthew 5:33](bible://mt/5/33)), Muhammad attributed the act to Allah (mā anā ḥamaltukum walākinna Allāha ḥamalakum) and institutionalized breaking his sworn vows whenever he later saw something better (kaffartu ʿan yamīnī wa-ataytu alladhī huwa khayr).

bukhari:7555.note: After swearing by Allah not to provide mounts to a group of Ash'ariyyin and subsequently giving them five camels from the war booty, Muhammad tells them that Allah provided the mounts rather than him. He then declares that whenever he swears an oath and later sees a better alternative, he does what is better and dissolves (`tahallaltuha`) the oath.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنِّي وَاللَّهِ لاَ أَحْلِفُ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَأَرَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا، إِلاَّ أَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ، وَتَحَلَّلْتُهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: By Allah, I may take an oath to do something, but on finding something else which is better, I do that which is better and make the expiation for my oath

bukhari:7555.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and Quran 5:89, that this ruling is not deceitful oath-breaking, but a merciful legal mechanism (kaffārat al-yamīn) that prevents rash personal vows from obstructing charitable deeds or a greater moral good. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore a categorical oath in God's name (وَاللَّهِ لاَ أَحْمِلُكُمْ—'By Allah, I will not mount you'), deflected personal responsibility when his companions feared ruin over his broken vow (لَسْتُ أَنَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ، وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَمَلَكُمْ), and declared that he unilaterally 'dissolves' (وَتَحَلَّلْتُهَا) any oath whenever a more advantageous option (خَيْرًا مِنْهَا) appears. Coupled with Quran 66:1–2—which legislated the 'dissolution of oaths' (تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمَانِكُمْ) specifically to absolve Muhammad for breaking his sworn vow to his wives—this doctrine reduces solemn oaths in God's name into provisional promises revocable at convenience.

muslim:4269.note: After swearing an oath by Allah that he would not provide Abu Musa al-Ash'ari's group with riding camels, Muhammad sends them three camels and declares that whenever he swears an oath and sees another course as better, he does what is better ([Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)). Parallel reports such as muslim:4271 add that breaking a sworn oath in this manner is accompanied by expiation (kaffarah).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَتَيْنَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَسْتَحْمِلُهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَا عِنْدِي مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ وَاللَّهِ مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ بَعَثَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِثَلاَثَةِ ذَوْدٍ بُقْعِ الذُّرَى فَقُلْنَا إِنَّا أَتَيْنَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَسْتَحْمِلُهُ فَحَلَفَ أَنْ لاَ يَحْمِلَنَا فَأَتَيْنَاهُ فَأَخْبَرْنَاهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنِّي لاَ أَحْلِفُ عَلَى يَمِينٍ أَرَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا إِلاَّ أَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: We came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) requesting him to provide us with riding camels. He (the Holy Prophet) said: There is nothing with me with which I should equip you. By Allah, I would not provide you with (riding camels). Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) sent to us three camels with spotted bumps. We said: We came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) asking him to equip us with riding animals. He took an oath that he could not equip us. We came to him and informed him. He said: By Allah, I do not take an oath, but when I find the other thing better than that, I do that which is better

muslim:4269.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that breaking a sworn oath for a perceived greater good is a commendable act permitted under [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2) rather than a breach of integrity. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore by Allah not to provide camels (wa-Allāhi mā aḥmilukum) and then declared a standing rule that he never swears an oath (lā aḥlifu ʿalā yamīnin) without abandoning it whenever he sees something else as better (arā ghayrahā khayran minhā illā ataytu alladhī huwa khayr). By treating solemn oaths invoked in God's name as revocable whenever a preferable alternative arises (see bukhari:5518, muslim:4263, and muslim:4265), this practice directly contradicts the biblical command in [Numbers 30:2](bible://nm/30/2) and [Matthew 5:33](bible://mt/5/33) that a person must not break their word but fulfill every oath sworn to the Lord.

muslim:4281.note: Muhammad instructs 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samura not to ask for political authority, and directs that whenever he swears an oath and subsequently sees another course of action as better, he should pay expiation for breaking his oath and do what is better ([Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2); cf. bukhari:6622, muslim:4275). Although neighboring reports apply this ruling to retracting rash oaths such as refusing charity (muslim:4279), Muhammad here states the permission to dissolve a sworn oath through expiation as a general rule whenever a more advantageous option arises.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ لِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ يَا عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ سَمُرَةَ لاَ تَسْأَلِ الإِمَارَةَ فَإِنَّكَ إِنْ أُعْطِيتَهَا عَنْ مَسْأَلَةٍ وُكِلْتَ إِلَيْهَا وَإِنْ أُعْطِيتَهَا عَنْ غَيْرِ مَسْأَلَةٍ أُعِنْتَ عَلَيْهَا وَإِذَا حَلَفْتَ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَرَأَيْتَ غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا فَكَفِّرْ عَنْ يَمِينِكَ وَائْتِ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Abd al-Rahman b. Samura reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said to me:Abd al-Rahman b. Samura, don't ask for authority for if it is granted to you for asking for it, you would be commissioned for it (without having the support of Allah), but if you are granted it without your asking for it. You would be helped (by Allah) in it. And when you take an oath and find something else better than that, expiate for (breaking) your oath, and do that which is better.

muslim:4281.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this instruction only applies to rash or sinful personal vows where keeping the oath would prevent a righteous deed, rather than permitting general oath-breaking. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in unrestricted terms, 'when you take an oath and see something else better than it, expiate for your oath and do that which is better' (wa-idhā ḥalafta ʿalā yamīnin fa-raʾayta ghayrahā khayran minhā fa-kaffir ʿan yamīnika wa-ʾti alladhī huwa khayr), conditioning the dissolution of an oath solely on the swearer's own judgment (fa-raʾayta) that another course of action is more advantageous. Together with [Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2), and parallel reports (bukhari:6622, bukhari:6722, muslim:4275), this institutionalizes a legal mechanism for nullifying sworn commitments through expiation, in direct contrast to the biblical command that a person who swears an oath must not break their word ([Numbers 30:2](bible://nm/30/2); [Matthew 5:33](bible://mt/5/33)).

muslim:4276.note: Muhammad decrees that whoever swears an oath and subsequently sees another course of action as better should do what is better and abandon his oath ([Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)). Parallel narrations specify that rescinding such an oath—illustrated by retracting an oath made in anger to withhold charity—is accomplished by offering legal expiation (muslim:4274, muslim:4277, bukhari:6622).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ مَنْ حَلَفَ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَرَأَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا فَلْيَأْتِ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ وَلْيَتْرُكْ يَمِينَهُ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Adi b. Hatim reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:He who took an oath, but he found something else better than that, should do that which is better and break his oath

muslim:4276.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this ruling applies only to rash personal vows to abstain from good deeds and merely prevents an oath from obstructing piety. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in unrestricted terms—*man ḥalafa ʿalā yamīnin fa-raʾā ghayrahā khayran minhā fa-l-yaʾti alladhī huwa khayrun wa-l-yatruk yamīnahu* ('He who took an oath, but he found something else better than that, should do that which is better and break his oath')—making the binding force of any sworn oath contingent on whether the oath-taker subsequently perceives a preferable alternative. Rather than limiting the exception to sinful vows, this unqualified directive authorizes abandoning a solemn oath whenever a better option is seen, matching the oath-dissolution provisions of [Quran 5:89](quran://5/89) and [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2) (cf. `bukhari:6622`, `muslim:4277`; contrast [Matthew 5:33-37](bible://mt/5/33-37)).

muslim:4277.note: Muhammad instructs his followers that whenever anyone swears an oath (*al-yamin*) and later sees something better (*khayran*), he should expiate the oath and do what is better ([Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2); bukhari:6622, muslim:4276). Although the narrator 'Adi applies this ruling in neighboring reports (muslim:4275, muslim:4279) to retract a rash oath refusing charity, Muhammad states the command as a general rule permitting sworn oaths to be broken through expiation whenever a better course of action is found.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ إِذَا حَلَفَ أَحَدُكُمْ عَلَى الْيَمِينِ فَرَأَى خَيْرًا مِنْهَا فَلْيُكَفِّرْهَا وَلْيَأْتِ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Adi reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:When anyone amongst you takes an oath, but he finds (something) better than that he should expiate (the breaking of the oath), and do that which is better

muslim:4277.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this instruction applies only when a person rashly swears to commit a sin or neglect a religious duty, framing expiation as a moral corrective rather than a license to break solemn pledges. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states without restriction that whenever anyone swears an oath and sees something better than it (فَرَأَى خَيْرًا مِنْهَا), he is to expiate it and do what is better (فَلْيُكَفِّرْهَا وَلْيَأْتِ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ), codifying the dissolution of oaths ([Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)) whenever a more advantageous option appears. This stands in direct contrast to the New Testament command to let one's 'Yes' simply be 'Yes' ([Matthew 5:37](bible://mt/5/37)) and the biblical requirement to keep an oath even to one's own hurt ([Psalm 15:4](bible://ps/15/4)).

bukhari:6722.note: Muhammad instructs 'Abdur-Rahman bin Samura that if he swears an oath (yamin) and later sees a better alternative, he should do what is better and make expiation (kaffarah) for dissolving the oath. Even when applied to personal oaths in neighboring reports (bukhari:6721), this normative rule—paired with [Quran 66:1-2](quran://66/1-2)—explicitly permits breaking sworn oaths via expiation whenever a preferable option is found, contrasting with the biblical command to fulfill all vows and oaths ([Numbers 30:2](bible://nm/30/2)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَإِذَا حَلَفْتَ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَرَأَيْتَ غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا، فَأْتِ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ، وَكَفِّرْ عَنْ يَمِينِكَ
problematic_excerpt.english: And if you take an oath to do something and later on find another thing, better than that, then do what is better and make expiation for (the dissolution of) your oath

bukhari:6722.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī, that this ruling merely prevents a believer from persisting in a rash oath to commit a sin or neglect a religious obligation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "fa-ra'ayta ghayrahā khayran minhā" ("and you see something else better than it"), making a person's subjective assessment of a more advantageous alternative sufficient grounds to break a solemn oath sworn in Allah's name. Furthermore, as demonstrated in Quran 66:1–2 and bukhari:6622, Muhammad used this exact expiation mechanism (kaffārat al-yamīn) to dissolve his own sworn vows to his wives for personal convenience, reducing sacred oaths to transactional commitments that can be voided whenever a better option arises.

bukhari:7146.note: Muhammad instructs 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah that if he swears an oath and later sees a better alternative, he should expiate his oath and do what is better, contrasting with the biblical command to fulfill sworn vows even to one's own hurt ([Psalm 15:4](bible://ps/15/4); [Numbers 30:2](bible://nm/30/2)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَإِذَا حَلَفْتَ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَرَأَيْتَ غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا، فَكَفِّرْ يَمِينَكَ، وَأْتِ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ
problematic_excerpt.english: If you ever take an oath to do something and later on you find that something else is better, then you should expiate your oath and do what is better

bukhari:7146.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that—as framed in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—this instruction merely prevents a person from remaining bound to a rash, sinful oath, such as swearing in anger to sever family ties or abstain from a good deed. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *wa-idhā ḥalafta ʿalā yamīnin fa-raʾayta ghayrahā khayran minhā* ('if you swear an oath and see something else better than it'), employing an unrestricted subjective comparative (*khayran*, 'better' or 'more advantageous') with no limitation to sinful vows. Paired with Quran 66:2 (*qad faraḍa Allāhu lakum taḥillata aymānikum*), this institutionalizes a transactional legal loophole (*kaffārah*) whereby any solemn oath sworn in Allah's name can be bought out and broken whenever a more expedient option arises.

bukhari:7147.note: Muhammad instructs Abdur-Rahman ibn Samura that if he swears an oath and subsequently sees another course of action as better (khayran minha), he should break the oath by doing what is better and offer expiation (kaffarat al-yamin) for his oath.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَإِذَا حَلَفْتَ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَرَأَيْتَ غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا، فَأْتِ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ، وَكَفِّرْ عَنْ يَمِينِكَ
problematic_excerpt.english: If you ever take an oath to do something and later on you find that something else is better, then do what is better and make expiation for your oath

bukhari:7147.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that this ruling only applies to rash personal vows to commit a sin or abstain from a righteous deed, rather than permitting opportunistic oath-breaking. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in sweeping, unqualified terms that whenever you swear an oath and subsequently judge another option to be more advantageous (*fara'ayta ghayrahā khayran minhā*), you should break your word and simply pay the expiation (*wa-kaffir 'an yamīnika*). Grounded in Quran 66:2 and 5:89, this doctrine reduces a solemn oath sworn in God's name from an inviolable moral covenant into a disposable transaction that can be bought out whenever a more favorable alternative arises.

bukhari:4039.note: Muhammad dispatched a group of Ansar led by Abdullah ibn Atik to kill the Jewish merchant Abu Rafi, who had harmed Muhammad and aided his enemies against him. Abdullah deceived the gatekeeper to infiltrate the fortress at night, located Abu Rafi in a dark room among his family by calling out his name, and drove a sword through his abdomen until it reached his back ([Exodus 20:13](bible://ex/20/13)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: بَعَثَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى أَبِي رَافِعٍ الْيَهُودِيِّ رِجَالاً مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ، فَأَمَّرَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَتِيكٍ، وَكَانَ أَبُو رَافِعٍ يُؤْذِي رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَيُعِينُ عَلَيْهِ، وَكَانَ فِي حِصْنٍ لَهُ بِأَرْضِ الْحِجَازِ، فَلَمَّا دَنَوْا مِنْهُ، وَقَدْ غَرَبَتِ الشَّمْسُ، وَرَاحَ النَّاسُ بِسَرْحِهِمْ فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ لأَصْحَابِهِ اجْلِسُوا مَكَانَكُمْ، فَإِنِّي مُنْطَلِقٌ، وَمُتَلَطِّفٌ لِلْبَوَّابِ، لَعَلِّي أَنْ أَدْخُلَ‏.‏ فَأَقْبَلَ حَتَّى دَنَا مِنَ الْبَابِ ثُمَّ تَقَنَّعَ بِثَوْبِهِ كَأَنَّهُ يَقْضِي حَاجَةً، وَقَدْ دَخَلَ النَّاسُ، فَهَتَفَ بِهِ الْبَوَّابُ يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَدْخُلَ فَادْخُلْ، فَإِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُغْلِقَ الْبَابَ‏.‏ فَدَخَلْتُ فَكَمَنْتُ، فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ النَّاسُ أَغْلَقَ الْبَابَ، ثُمَّ عَلَّقَ الأَغَالِيقَ عَلَى وَتَدٍ قَالَ فَقُمْتُ إِلَى الأَقَالِيدِ، فَأَخَذْتُهَا فَفَتَحْتُ الْبَابَ، وَكَانَ أَبُو رَافِعٍ يُسْمَرُ عِنْدَهُ، وَكَانَ فِي عَلاَلِيَّ لَهُ، فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنْهُ أَهْلُ سَمَرِهِ صَعِدْتُ إِلَيْهِ، فَجَعَلْتُ كُلَّمَا فَتَحْتُ بَابًا أَغْلَقْتُ عَلَىَّ مِنْ دَاخِلٍ، قُلْتُ إِنِ الْقَوْمُ نَذِرُوا بِي لَمْ يَخْلُصُوا إِلَىَّ حَتَّى أَقْتُلَهُ‏.‏ فَانْتَهَيْتُ إِلَيْهِ، فَإِذَا هُوَ فِي بَيْتٍ مُظْلِمٍ وَسْطَ عِيَالِهِ، لاَ أَدْرِي أَيْنَ هُوَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ فَقُلْتُ يَا أَبَا رَافِعٍ‏.‏ قَالَ مَنْ هَذَا فَأَهْوَيْتُ نَحْوَ الصَّوْتِ، فَأَضْرِبُهُ ضَرْبَةً بِالسَّيْفِ، وَأَنَا دَهِشٌ فَمَا أَغْنَيْتُ شَيْئًا، وَصَاحَ فَخَرَجْتُ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ، فَأَمْكُثُ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ ثُمَّ دَخَلْتُ إِلَيْهِ فَقُلْتُ مَا هَذَا الصَّوْتُ يَا أَبَا رَافِعٍ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لأُمِّكَ الْوَيْلُ، إِنَّ رَجُلاً فِي الْبَيْتِ ضَرَبَنِي قَبْلُ بِالسَّيْفِ، قَالَ فَأَضْرِبُهُ ضَرْبَةً أَثْخَنَتْهُ وَلَمْ أَقْتُلْهُ، ثُمَّ وَضَعْتُ ظُبَةَ السَّيْفِ فِي بَطْنِهِ حَتَّى أَخَذَ فِي ظَهْرِهِ، فَعَرَفْتُ أَنِّي قَتَلْتُهُ، فَجَعَلْتُ أَفْتَحُ الأَبْوَابَ بَابًا بَابًا حَتَّى انْتَهَيْتُ إِلَى دَرَجَةٍ لَهُ، فَوَضَعْتُ رِجْلِي وَأَنَا أُرَى أَنِّي قَدِ انْتَهَيْتُ إِلَى الأَرْضِ فَوَقَعْتُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُقْمِرَةٍ، فَانْكَسَرَتْ سَاقِي، فَعَصَبْتُهَا بِعِمَامَةٍ، ثُمَّ انْطَلَقْتُ حَتَّى جَلَسْتُ عَلَى الْبَابِ فَقُلْتُ لاَ أَخْرُجُ اللَّيْلَةَ حَتَّى أَعْلَمَ أَقَتَلْتُهُ فَلَمَّا صَاحَ الدِّيكُ قَامَ النَّاعِي عَلَى السُّورِ فَقَالَ أَنْعَى أَبَا رَافِعٍ تَاجِرَ أَهْلِ الْحِجَازِ‏.‏ فَانْطَلَقْتُ إِلَى أَصْحَابِي فَقُلْتُ النَّجَاءَ، فَقَدْ قَتَلَ اللَّهُ أَبَا رَافِعٍ‏.‏ فَانْتَهَيْتُ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَحَدَّثْتُهُ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ ابْسُطْ رِجْلَكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَبَسَطْتُ رِجْلِي، فَمَسَحَهَا، فَكَأَنَّهَا لَمْ أَشْتَكِهَا قَطُّ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) sent some men from the Ansar to ((kill) Abu Rafi`, the Jew, and appointed `Abdullah bin Atik as their leader. Abu Rafi` used to hurt Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and help his enemies against him. He lived in his castle in the land of Hijaz. When those men approached (the castle) after the sun had set and the people had brought back their livestock to their homes. `Abdullah (bin Atik) said to his companions, "Sit down at your places. I am going, and I will try to play a trick on the gate-keeper so that I may enter (the castle)." So `Abdullah proceeded towards the castle, and when he approached the gate, he covered himself with his clothes, pretending to answer the call of nature. The people had gone in, and the gate-keeper (considered `Abdullah as one of the castle's servants) addressing him saying, "O Allah's Servant! Enter if you wish, for I want to close the gate." `Abdullah added in his story, "So I went in (the castle) and hid myself. When the people got inside, the gate-keeper closed the gate and hung the keys on a fixed wooden peg. I got up and took the keys and opened the gate. Some people were staying late at night with Abu Rafi` for a pleasant night chat in a room of his. When his companions of nightly entertainment went away, I ascended to him, and whenever I opened a door, I closed it from inside. I said to myself, 'Should these people discover my presence, they will not be able to catch me till I have killed him.' So I reached him and found him sleeping in a dark house amidst his family, I could not recognize his location in the house. So I shouted, 'O Abu Rafi`!' Abu Rafi` said, 'Who is it?' I proceeded towards the source of the voice and hit him with the sword, and because of my perplexity, I could not kill him. He cried loudly, and I came out of the house and waited for a while, and then went to him again and said, 'What is this voice, O Abu Rafi`?' He said, 'Woe to your mother! A man in my house has hit me with a sword! I again hit him severely but I did not kill him. Then I drove the point of the sword into his belly (and pressed it through) till it touched his back, and I realized that I have killed him. I then opened the doors one by one till I reached the staircase, and thinking that I had reached the ground, I stepped out and fell down and got my leg broken in a moonlit night. I tied my leg with a turban and proceeded on till I sat at the gate, and said, 'I will not go out tonight till I know that I have killed him.' So, when (early in the morning) the cock crowed, the announcer of the casualty stood on the wall saying, 'I announce the death of Abu Rafi`, the merchant of Hijaz. Thereupon I went to my companions and said, 'Let us save ourselves, for Allah has killed Abu Rafi`,' So I (along with my companions proceeded and) went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and described the whole story to him. "He said, 'Stretch out your (broken) leg. I stretched it out and he rubbed it and it became All right as if I had never had any ailment whatsoever

bukhari:4039.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Abu Rafi' (Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq) financed and incited hostile tribes against Medina—as detailed in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—making his killing a legitimate wartime covert operation where tactical ruse is permissible. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad's operative used deceit (*mutalaṭṭifun lil-bawwāb*) to infiltrate a private residence at night, ambushed the unarmed merchant in a dark room amidst his family (*fī baytin muẓlimin wasṭa 'iyālihi*), and even disguised his voice to feign concern as a rescuer before driving his sword through Abu Rafi's belly (*waḍa'tu ẓubata al-sayfi fī baṭnihi ḥattā akhadha fī ẓahrihi*). Furthermore, the adjacent Sahih narration (`bukhari:4038`) admits this assassination was authorized so the Khazraj tribe could rival the Aws tribe's credit for the earlier treacherous murder of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, proving it was a competitive political hit rather than honorable battlefield combat.

bukhari:4037.note: Declaring that Ka'b bin al-Ashraf had harmed Allah and His Messenger ([Quran 33:57](quran://33/57)), Muhammad commissioned Muhammad bin Maslama to kill him and granted permission to speak deceptively to lure Ka'b from his fortress at night, where the operatives seized his head under the pretext of smelling his perfume and killed him ([Exodus 20:13](bible://ex/20/13)). Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi cite this report as a primary legal proof-text for the permissibility of covert assassination (ightiyal) and lying to deceive targets in warfare.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ مَنْ لِكَعْبِ بْنِ الأَشْرَفِ فَإِنَّهُ قَدْ آذَى اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَامَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَتُحِبُّ أَنْ أَقْتُلَهُ قَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَأْذَنْ لِي أَنْ أَقُولَ شَيْئًا‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ قُلْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأَتَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ فَقَالَ إِنَّ هَذَا الرَّجُلَ قَدْ سَأَلَنَا صَدَقَةً، وَإِنَّهُ قَدْ عَنَّانَا، وَإِنِّي قَدْ أَتَيْتُكَ أَسْتَسْلِفُكَ‏.‏ قَالَ وَأَيْضًا وَاللَّهِ لَتَمَلُّنَّهُ قَالَ إِنَّا قَدِ اتَّبَعْنَاهُ فَلاَ نُحِبُّ أَنْ نَدَعَهُ حَتَّى نَنْظُرَ إِلَى أَىِّ شَىْءٍ يَصِيرُ شَأْنُهُ، وَقَدْ أَرَدْنَا أَنْ تُسْلِفَنَا وَسْقًا، أَوْ وَسْقَيْنِ ـ وَحَدَّثَنَا عَمْرٌو غَيْرَ مَرَّةٍ، فَلَمْ يَذْكُرْ وَسْقًا أَوْ وَسْقَيْنِ أَوْ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ فِيهِ وَسْقًا أَوْ وَسْقَيْنِ فَقَالَ أُرَى فِيهِ وَسْقًا أَوْ وَسْقَيْنِ ـ فَقَالَ نَعَمِ ارْهَنُونِي‏.‏ قَالُوا أَىَّ شَىْءٍ تُرِيدُ قَالَ فَارْهَنُونِي نِسَاءَكُمْ‏.‏ قَالُوا كَيْفَ نَرْهَنُكَ نِسَاءَنَا وَأَنْتَ أَجْمَلُ الْعَرَبِ قَالَ فَارْهَنُونِي أَبْنَاءَكُمْ‏.‏ قَالُوا كَيْفَ نَرْهَنُكَ أَبْنَاءَنَا فَيُسَبُّ أَحَدُهُمْ، فَيُقَالُ رُهِنَ بِوَسْقٍ أَوْ وَسْقَيْنِ‏.‏ هَذَا عَارٌ عَلَيْنَا، وَلَكِنَّا نَرْهَنُكَ اللأْمَةَ ـ قَالَ سُفْيَانُ يَعْنِي السِّلاَحَ ـ فَوَاعَدَهُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُ، فَجَاءَهُ لَيْلاً وَمَعَهُ أَبُو نَائِلَةَ وَهْوَ أَخُو كَعْبٍ مِنَ الرَّضَاعَةِ، فَدَعَاهُمْ إِلَى الْحِصْنِ، فَنَزَلَ إِلَيْهِمْ فَقَالَتْ لَهُ امْرَأَتُهُ أَيْنَ تَخْرُجُ هَذِهِ السَّاعَةَ فَقَالَ إِنَّمَا هُوَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ، وَأَخِي أَبُو نَائِلَةَ ـ وَقَالَ غَيْرُ عَمْرٍو قَالَتْ أَسْمَعُ صَوْتًا كَأَنَّهُ يَقْطُرُ مِنْهُ الدَّمُ‏.‏ قَالَ إِنَّمَا هُوَ أَخِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ وَرَضِيعِي أَبُو نَائِلَةَ ـ إِنَّ الْكَرِيمَ لَوْ دُعِيَ إِلَى طَعْنَةٍ بِلَيْلٍ لأَجَابَ قَالَ وَيُدْخِلُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ مَعَهُ رَجُلَيْنِ ـ قِيلَ لِسُفْيَانَ سَمَّاهُمْ عَمْرٌو قَالَ سَمَّى بَعْضَهُمْ قَالَ عَمْرٌو جَاءَ مَعَهُ بِرَجُلَيْنِ وَقَالَ غَيْرُ عَمْرٍو أَبُو عَبْسِ بْنُ جَبْرٍ، وَالْحَارِثُ بْنُ أَوْسٍ وَعَبَّادُ بْنُ بِشْرٍ قَالَ عَمْرٌو وَجَاءَ مَعَهُ بِرَجُلَيْنِ ـ فَقَالَ إِذَا مَا جَاءَ فَإِنِّي قَائِلٌ بِشَعَرِهِ فَأَشَمُّهُ، فَإِذَا رَأَيْتُمُونِي اسْتَمْكَنْتُ مِنْ رَأْسِهِ فَدُونَكُمْ فَاضْرِبُوهُ‏.‏ وَقَالَ مَرَّةً ثُمَّ أُشِمُّكُمْ‏.‏ فَنَزَلَ إِلَيْهِمْ مُتَوَشِّحًا وَهْوَ يَنْفَحُ مِنْهُ رِيحُ الطِّيبِ، فَقَالَ مَا رَأَيْتُ كَالْيَوْمِ رِيحًا ـ أَىْ أَطْيَبَ ـ وَقَالَ غَيْرُ عَمْرٍو قَالَ عِنْدِي أَعْطَرُ نِسَاءِ الْعَرَبِ وَأَكْمَلُ الْعَرَبِ قَالَ عَمْرٌو فَقَالَ أَتَأْذَنُ لِي أَنْ أَشَمَّ رَأْسَكَ قَالَ نَعَمْ، فَشَمَّهُ، ثُمَّ أَشَمَّ أَصْحَابَهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَتَأْذَنُ لِي قَالَ نَعَمْ‏.‏ فَلَمَّا اسْتَمْكَنَ مِنْهُ قَالَ دُونَكُمْ‏.‏ فَقَتَلُوهُ ثُمَّ أَتَوُا النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَخْبَرُوهُ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Who is willing to kill Ka`b bin Al-Ashraf who has hurt Allah and His Apostle?" Thereupon Muhammad bin Maslama got up saying, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Would you like that I kill him?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Yes," Muhammad bin Maslama said, "Then allow me to say a (false) thing (i.e. to deceive Ka`b). "The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "You may say it." Then Muhammad bin Maslama went to Ka`b and said, "That man (i.e. Muhammad demands Sadaqa (i.e. Zakat) from us, and he has troubled us, and I have come to borrow something from you." On that, Ka`b said, "By Allah, you will get tired of him!" Muhammad bin Maslama said, "Now as we have followed him, we do not want to leave him unless and until we see how his end is going to be. Now we want you to lend us a camel load or two of food." (Some difference between narrators about a camel load or two.) Ka`b said, "Yes, (I will lend you), but you should mortgage something to me." Muhammad bin Mas-lama and his companion said, "What do you want?" Ka`b replied, "Mortgage your women to me." They said, "How can we mortgage our women to you and you are the most handsome of the 'Arabs?" Ka`b said, "Then mortgage your sons to me." They said, "How can we mortgage our sons to you? Later they would be abused by the people's saying that so-and-so has been mortgaged for a camel load of food. That would cause us great disgrace, but we will mortgage our arms to you." Muhammad bin Maslama and his companion promised Ka`b that Muhammad would return to him. He came to Ka`b at night along with Ka`b's foster brother, Abu Na'ila. Ka`b invited them to come into his fort, and then he went down to them. His wife asked him, "Where are you going at this time?" Ka`b replied, "None but Muhammad bin Maslama and my (foster) brother Abu Na'ila have come." His wife said, "I hear a voice as if dropping blood is from him, Ka`b said, "They are none but my brother Muhammad bin Maslama and my foster brother Abu Naila. A generous man should respond to a call at night even if invited to be killed." Muhammad bin Maslama went with two men. (Some narrators mention the men as 'Abu bin Jabr. Al Harith bin Aus and `Abbad bin Bishr). So Muhammad bin Maslama went in together with two men, and said to them, "When Ka`b comes, I will touch his hair and smell it, and when you see that I have got hold of his head, strike him. I will let you smell his head." Ka`b bin Al-Ashraf came down to them wrapped in his clothes, and diffusing perfume. Muhammad bin Maslama said, "I have never smelt a better scent than this." Ka`b replied, "I have got the best 'Arab women who know how to use the high class of perfume." Muhammad bin Maslama requested Ka`b "Will you allow me to smell your head?" Ka`b said, "Yes." Muhammad smelt it and made his companions smell it as well. Then he requested Ka`b again, "Will you let me (smell your head)?" Ka`b said, "Yes." When Muhammad got a strong hold of him, he said (to his companions), "Get at him!" So they killed him and went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him.

bukhari:4037.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists (citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) typically argue that Ka'b bin al-Ashraf was a treasonous combatant who violated a Medina pact by inciting the Meccan Quraysh after Badr in AD 624, making his killing a lawful wartime execution where tactical ruse (*al-ḥarb khud'ah*) is permitted. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad ordered his death solely because 'he has offended Allah and His Messenger' (*fainnahu qad ādhā Allāha wa-rasūlahu* — فَإِنَّهُ قَدْ آذَى اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ) with no mention of any treaty violation, and directly records Muhammad authorizing premeditated lying (*fa'dhan lī an aqūla shay'an. qāla: qul* — فَأْذَنْ لِي أَنْ أَقُولَ شَيْئًا. قَالَ قُلْ) so the assassins could feign apostasy and carry weapons undetected. Furthermore, the operatives exploited the sacred bond of foster-brotherhood (*أَخُو كَعْبٍ مِنَ الرَّضَاعَةِ*) and nighttime hospitality to lure an unarmed host from his fortress and murder him by treachery, establishing the canonical Sunni legal precedent (codified by Al-Nawawī and Ibn Hajar) that anyone who verbally insults Muhammad via poetry or speech may be assassinated without warning.

bukhari:3022.note: Muhammad sent a group of Ansari men to kill the Hijazi merchant Abu Rafi, and one of them infiltrated his fortress at night, struck him in the dark, and then returned altering his voice to pose as a helper before driving a sword through Abu Rafi's abdomen until it struck the bone.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: بَعَثَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَهْطًا مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ إِلَى أَبِي رَافِعٍ لِيَقْتُلُوهُ، فَانْطَلَقَ رَجُلٌ مِنْهُمْ فَدَخَلَ حِصْنَهُمْ قَالَ فَدَخَلْتُ فِي مَرْبِطِ دَوَابَّ لَهُمْ، قَالَ وَأَغْلَقُوا باب الْحِصْنِ، ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ فَقَدُوا حِمَارًا لَهُمْ، فَخَرَجُوا يَطْلُبُونَهُ، فَخَرَجْتُ فِيمَنْ خَرَجَ أُرِيهِمْ أَنَّنِي أَطْلُبُهُ مَعَهُمْ، فَوَجَدُوا الْحِمَارَ، فَدَخَلُوا وَدَخَلْتُ، وَأَغْلَقُوا باب الْحِصْنِ لَيْلاً، فَوَضَعُوا الْمَفَاتِيحَ فِي كَوَّةٍ حَيْثُ أَرَاهَا، فَلَمَّا نَامُوا أَخَذْتُ الْمَفَاتِيحَ، فَفَتَحْتُ باب الْحِصْنِ ثُمَّ دَخَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ فَقُلْتُ يَا أَبَا رَافِعٍ‏.‏ فَأَجَابَنِي، فَتَعَمَّدْتُ الصَّوْتَ، فَضَرَبْتُهُ فَصَاحَ، فَخَرَجْتُ ثُمَّ جِئْتُ، ثُمَّ رَجَعْتُ كَأَنِّي مُغِيثٌ فَقُلْتُ يَا أَبَا رَافِعٍ، وَغَيَّرْتُ صَوْتِي، فَقَالَ مَا لَكَ لأُمِّكَ الْوَيْلُ قُلْتُ مَا شَأْنُكَ قَالَ لاَ أَدْرِي مَنْ دَخَلَ عَلَىَّ فَضَرَبَنِي‏.‏ قَالَ فَوَضَعْتُ سَيْفِي فِي بَطْنِهِ، ثُمَّ تَحَامَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى قَرَعَ الْعَظْمَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) sent a group of Ansari men to kill Abu-Rafi`. One of them set out and entered their (i.e. the enemies) fort. That man said, "I hid myself in a stable for their animals. They closed the fort gate. Later they lost a donkey of theirs, so they went out in its search. I, too, went out along with them, pretending to look for it. They found the donkey and entered their fort. And I, too, entered along with them. They closed the gate of the fort at night, and kept its keys in a small window where I could see them. When those people slept, I took the keys and opened the gate of the fort and came upon Abu Rafi` and said, 'O Abu Rafi`. When he to replied me, I proceeded towards the voice and hit him. He shouted and I came out to come back, pretending to be a helper. I said, 'O Abu Rafi`,' changing the tone of my voice. He asked me, 'What do you want; woe to your mother?' I asked him, 'What has happened to you?' He said, 'I don't know who came to me and hit me.' Then I drove my sword into his belly and pushed it forcibly till it touched the bone.

bukhari:3022.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Abu Rafi (Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq) was a hostile financier who incited tribes against Medina, citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī to frame his killing as a legitimate wartime covert operation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the assassin waited until the household was asleep (فَلَمَّا نَامُوا), feigned being a rescuer coming to his aid (كَأَنِّي مُغِيثٌ) by disguising his voice (وَغَيَّرْتُ صَوْتِي), and drove his sword into the unarmed man's belly until it struck bone (فَوَضَعْتُ سَيْفِي فِي بَطْنِهِ، ثُمَّ تَحَامَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى قَرَعَ الْعَظْمَ), while identifying the victim simply as 'the merchant of the people of Hijaz' (تَاجِرِ أَهْلِ الْحِجَازِ). Moreover, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:4039) reveal that the Khazraj tribe requested this hit merely to rival the Aws tribe's murder of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, leading Ibn Hajar to cite this exact incident as the legal precedent permitting the stealth assassination (ightiyāl) of non-Muslims in their beds.

bukhari:3032.note: Muhammad asked who would deal with Ka'b bin al-Ashraf, confirmed that he wanted Muhammad bin Maslama to kill him, and granted him permission to say whatever he wished to carry out the killing—an authorization al-Bukhari places under the chapter 'Lying in War' ([Exodus 20:13](bible://ex/20/13)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏"‏ مَنْ لِكَعْبِ بْنِ الأَشْرَفِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ أَتُحِبُّ أَنْ أَقْتُلَهُ قَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَأْذَنْ لِي فَأَقُولَ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ قَدْ فَعَلْتُ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Who is ready to kill Ka`b bin Ashraf (i.e. a Jew)." Muhammad bin Maslama replied, "Do you like me to kill him?" The Prophet (ﷺ) replied in the affirmative. Muhammad bin Maslama said, "Then allow me to say what I like." The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, "I do (i.e. allow you)

bukhari:3032.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Ka'b bin al-Ashraf was a treasonous combatant who violated a Medinan pact by inciting the Quraysh, making his killing and the use of wartime stratagem (citing 'war is deceit' in bukhari:3030) a lawful military execution rather than a treacherous murder. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad granted blanket permission to speak falsehood (fa-'dhan lī fa-aqūla — 'allow me to say [what I like]') so his operatives could feign disaffection against Muhammad, exploit Ka'b's personal trust as a foster-brother, and lure an unarmed man out of his home at night under the pretense of smelling his perfume before slaughtering him (bukhari:4037). In fact, Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani explicitly cites this exact narration in Fatḥ al-Bārī as the foundational legal proof permitting covert assassination (al-ightiyāl) and deceptive betrayal of trust against non-Muslims who offend Islam.

bukhari:3031.note: Muhammad commissioned the killing of Ka'b bin al-Ashraf (AD 624) for having 'offended Allah and His Messenger' ([Quran 33:57](quran://33/57)), after which Muhammad bin Maslama feigned grievances over charity demands to gain Ka'b's trust until he was able to kill him (cf. [Exodus 20:13](bible://ex/20/13)). Al-Bukhari pairs this report with bukhari:3032—where Muhammad explicitly authorizes speaking falsehoods to facilitate the killing—and Sunni jurists cite it to codify the legal permissibility of wartime deceit and targeted assassination (*ightiyāl*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ مَنْ لِكَعْبِ بْنِ الأَشْرَفِ، فَإِنَّهُ قَدْ آذَى اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ أَتُحِبُّ أَنْ أَقْتُلَهُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَتَاهُ فَقَالَ إِنَّ هَذَا ـ يَعْنِي النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ قَدْ عَنَّانَا وَسَأَلَنَا الصَّدَقَةَ، قَالَ وَأَيْضًا وَاللَّهِ قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدِ اتَّبَعْنَاهُ فَنَكْرَهُ أَنْ نَدَعَهُ حَتَّى نَنْظُرَ إِلَى مَا يَصِيرُ أَمْرُهُ قَالَ فَلَمْ يَزَلْ يُكَلِّمُهُ حَتَّى اسْتَمْكَنَ مِنْهُ فَقَتَلَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Who is ready to kill Ka`b bin Al-Ashraf who has really hurt Allah and His Apostle?" Muhammad bin Maslama said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Do you like me to kill him?" He replied in the affirmative. So, Muhammad bin Maslama went to him (i.e. Ka`b) and said, "This person (i.e. the Prophet) has put us to task and asked us for charity." Ka`b replied, "By Allah, you will get tired of him." Muhammad said to him, "We have followed him, so we dislike to leave him till we see the end of his affair." Muhammad bin Maslama went on talking to him in this way till he got the chance to kill him

bukhari:3031.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Ka'b bin al-Ashraf was not assassinated merely for satirical poetry, but executed for treason as an enemy combatant after allegedly breaking the Medinan pact by inciting the Quraysh to war in AD 624 (as argued in Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad's sole indictment was that Ka'b 'has hurt Allah and His Messenger' (fa-innahu qad ādhā Allāha wa-rasūlahu, فَإِنَّهُ قَدْ آذَى اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ)—the standard Quranic idiom for verbal insult and mockery—with zero mention of any broken treaty or military conspiracy. Furthermore, the parallel narration in bukhari:4037 records that Muhammad bin Maslama explicitly requested permission to lie (fa-ʾdhan lī an aqūla shayʾan) and Muhammad authorized it (qul, قُلْ), directly sanctioning premeditated deceit and false pretenses of friendship to lure an unarmed man out at night and murder him.

bukhari:5230.note: Despite permitting Muslim men up to four wives ([Quran 4:3](quran://4/3)), Muhammad publicly forbade Ali ibn Abi Talib from marrying a daughter of Banu Hisham bin Al-Mughira unless he divorced Fatima first, declaring that Fatima is a part of him and that whatever troubles or hurts her hurts him. While fuller parallels (bukhari:3110, muslim:6307) identify the prospective co-wife as the daughter of Abu Jahl and add that Muhammad was not forbidding the lawful in general, his explicit reasoning here exempts his own daughter from the distress and harm of sharing a husband.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ بَنِي هِشَامِ بْنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ اسْتَأْذَنُوا فِي أَنْ يُنْكِحُوا ابْنَتَهُمْ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ فَلاَ آذَنُ، ثُمَّ لاَ آذَنُ، ثُمَّ لاَ آذَنُ، إِلاَّ أَنْ يُرِيدَ ابْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ أَنْ يُطَلِّقَ ابْنَتِي وَيَنْكِحَ ابْنَتَهُمْ، فَإِنَّمَا هِيَ بَضْعَةٌ مِنِّي، يُرِيبُنِي مَا أَرَابَهَا وَيُؤْذِينِي مَا آذَاهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: Banu Hisham bin Al-Mughira have requested me to allow them to marry their daughter to `Ali bin Abu Talib, but I don't give permission, and will not give permission unless `Ali bin Abi Talib divorces my daughter in order to marry their daughter, because Fatima is a part of my body, and I hate what she hates to see, and what hurts her, hurts me

bukhari:5230.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was not exempting his family from polygyny out of personal bias, citing Ibn Ḥajar and Al-Nawawī on parallel narrations (bukhari:3110) to claim he only objected to joining the daughter of Allah's Messenger with the daughter of 'Allah's enemy' (Abū Jahl) or feared Fatima would be tried in her religion. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Ali could marry their daughter if he divorced Fatima first (illā an yurīda ibnu Abī Ṭālibin an yuṭalliqa ibnatī wa yankiḥa ibnatahum), proving the bride's lineage was completely lawful for Ali. Instead, Muhammad grounds his triple refusal strictly in the emotional torment that co-wife jealousy would inflict on his own flesh and blood (fa-innamā hiya baḍʿatun minnī, yurībunī mā arābahā wa yuʾḏīnī mā āḏāhā—'she is a piece of me; what troubles her troubles me, and what hurts her hurts me'), openly conceding that polygyny harms a wife while sanctioning it for other women (Quran 4:3).

bukhari:2510.note: Muhammad asked who would deal with Ka'b bin al-Ashraf on the grounds that he had harmed Allah and His Messenger (cf. [Quran 33:57](quran://33/57)). Muhammad bin Maslama volunteered, arranged to bring weapons to Ka'b under the pretext of pledging them as collateral for a grain loan, and killed him with his companions before reporting the deed back to the Prophet (cf. bukhari:3031, bukhari:4037; [Exodus 20:13](bible://ex/20/13)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ مَنْ لِكَعْبِ بْنِ الأَشْرَفِ فَإِنَّهُ آذَى اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ أَنَا‏.‏ فَأَتَاهُ فَقَالَ أَرَدْنَا أَنْ تُسْلِفَنَا وَسْقًا أَوْ وَسْقَيْنِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ارْهَنُونِي نِسَاءَكُمْ‏.‏ قَالُوا كَيْفَ نَرْهَنُكَ نِسَاءَنَا، وَأَنْتَ أَجْمَلُ الْعَرَبِ قَالَ فَارْهَنُونِي أَبْنَاءَكُمْ‏.‏ قَالُوا كَيْفَ نَرْهَنُ أَبْنَاءَنَا فَيُسَبُّ أَحَدُهُمْ، فَيُقَالُ رُهِنَ بِوَسْقٍ أَوْ وَسْقَيْنِ هَذَا عَارٌ عَلَيْنَا وَلَكِنَّا نَرْهَنُكَ اللأْمَةَ ـ قَالَ سُفْيَانُ يَعْنِي السِّلاَحَ ـ فَوَعَدَهُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُ فَقَتَلُوهُ، ثُمَّ أَتَوُا النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَخْبَرُوهُ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Who would kill Ka`b bin Al-Ashraf as he has harmed Allah and His Apostle ?" Muhammad bin Maslama (got up and) said, "I will kill him." So, Muhammad bin Maslama went to Ka`b and said, "I want a loan of one or two Wasqs of food grains." Ka`b said, "Mortgage your women to me." Muhammad bin Maslama said, "How can we mortgage our women, and you are the most handsome among the Arabs?" He said, "Then mortgage your sons to me." Muhammad said, "How can we mortgage our sons, as the people will abuse them for being mortgaged for one or two Wasqs of food grains? It is shameful for us. But we will mortgage our arms to you." So, Muhammad bin Maslama promised him that he would come to him next time. They (Muhammad bin Maslama and his companions came to him as promised and murdered him. Then they went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him about it

bukhari:2510.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Ka'b bin al-Ashraf was executed for high treason and inciting war against Medina after the Battle of Badr in AD 624, claiming (alongside Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*) that the assassins' ruse was merely a permissible wartime stratagem. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states Muhammad's sole indictment was that "he has harmed Allah and His Messenger" (*fa-innahu ādhā Allāha wa-rasūlahu*), and the parallel narration in bukhari:4037 records Muhammad explicitly authorizing his hitmen to lie (*fa-qul*) so they could feign disaffection and request a food loan. By promising to mortgage their weapons (*narhanuka al-la'mah*) solely as a pretext to approach him armed without raising alarm, Muhammad's companions did not conduct a lawful military operation, but weaponized a fraudulent commercial pledge to murder an unsuspecting host.

bukhari:4038.note: Muhammad sent a group of men to Abu Rafi', and 'Abdullah bin 'Atik entered his house at night and killed him while he was sleeping—an account classical commentators like Ibn Hajar cite as a legal precedent permitting the stealth assassination (*ightiyal*) of enemy figures ([Exodus 20:13](bible://ex/20/13)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: بَعَثَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَهْطًا إِلَى أَبِي رَافِعٍ فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَتِيكٍ بَيْتَهُ لَيْلاً وَهْوَ نَائِمٌ فَقَتَلَهُ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) sent a group of persons to Abu Rafi`. `Abdullah bin Atik entered his house at night, while he was sleeping, and killed him

bukhari:4038.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Abu Rafi (Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq) was an active military belligerent who financed tribal coalitions against Medina, making his killing a legitimate wartime targeted strike rather than an assassination. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad's operative infiltrated his private home at night and slaughtered him unarmed in his sleep (dakhala 'alayhi... baytahu laylan wa-huwa nā'imun fa-qatalahu), while the immediate sequel narration (bukhari:4039) admits the raid was authorized so the Khazraj tribe could rival the Aws tribe's murder of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf for equal tribal prestige. Furthermore, rather than treating this as an exceptional military necessity, Imam Bukhari's own chapter headings (bukhari:3022–3023) and Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī codify this nocturnal killing as permanent Islamic legal precedent for using deceit and stealth assassination (ightiyāl) against unarmed non-Muslims without prior warning.

bukhari:3023.note: Muhammad dispatched a group of the Ansar to Abu Rafi, and Abdullah ibn Atik entered his house at night and killed him while he was sleeping (see also bukhari:3022, bukhari:4039). Classical jurists, including al-Bukhari in his chapter heading, cite this report to establish the legal permissibility of covertly killing an enemy while he is asleep.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: بَعَثَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَهْطًا مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ إِلَى أَبِي رَافِعٍ فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَتِيكٍ بَيْتَهُ لَيْلاً، فَقَتَلَهُ وَهْوَ نَائِمٌ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) sent a group of the Ansar to Abu Rafi`. `Abdullah bin Atik entered his house at night and killed him while he was sleeping

bukhari:3023.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Abu Rafi' was a legitimate military target who financed and incited hostile tribes against Medina, making his death a lawful wartime operation rather than a treacherous murder. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad's operative infiltrated his private residence at night and slaughtered him while he was unarmed and asleep in bed (فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَتِيكٍ بَيْتَهُ لَيْلاً، فَقَتَلَهُ وَهْوَ نَائِمٌ — 'entered his house at night and killed him while he was sleeping'). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:3022, 4039) and Ibn Hajar's Fath al-Bari confirm that the Khazraj undertook this hit squad mission merely to rival the Aws tribe's earlier assassination of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, and Sunni jurists explicitly classify this Hadith under chapters legalizing deceit in war (الكذب في الحرب) and assassinating a sleeping, unsuspecting non-Muslim without warning.

bukhari:6649.note: Muhammad swore an oath by Allah not to provide Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and his companions with mounts, then gave them five camels when war booty arrived. When his companions returned fearing he had forgotten his oath, Muhammad stated that Allah had provided the mounts and declared that whenever he swears an oath and sees a better alternative, he does what is better and makes expiation to dissolve the oath ([Matthew 5:33-37](bible://mt/5/33-37); [Numbers 30:2](bible://nm/30/2); cf. [Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنِّي أَتَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي نَفَرٍ مِنَ الأَشْعَرِيِّينَ نَسْتَحْمِلُهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أَحْمِلُكُمْ، وَمَا عِنْدِي مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأُتِيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِنَهْبِ إِبِلٍ فَسَأَلَ عَنَّا‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَيْنَ النَّفَرُ الأَشْعَرِيُّونَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأَمَرَ لَنَا بِخَمْسِ ذَوْدٍ غُرِّ الذُّرَى، فَلَمَّا انْطَلَقْنَا قُلْنَا مَا صَنَعْنَا حَلَفَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لاَ يَحْمِلُنَا وَمَا عِنْدَهُ مَا يَحْمِلُنَا ثُمَّ حَمَلَنَا، تَغَفَّلْنَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَمِينَهُ، وَاللَّهِ لاَ نُفْلِحُ أَبَدًا، فَرَجَعْنَا إِلَيْهِ فَقُلْنَا لَهُ إِنَّا أَتَيْنَاكَ لِتَحْمِلَنَا فَحَلَفْتَ أَنْ لاَ تَحْمِلَنَا، وَمَا عِنْدَكَ مَا تَحْمِلُنَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنِّي لَسْتُ أَنَا حَمَلْتُكُمْ، وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَمَلَكُمْ، وَاللَّهِ لاَ أَحْلِفُ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَأَرَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا، إِلاَّ أَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ وَتَحَلَّلْتُهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Once a group of the Ash`ariyin and I went to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and asked him to provide us with mounts; he said, 'By Allah, I will never give you any mounts nor do I have anything to mount you on.' Then a few camels of war booty were brought to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) , and he asked about us, saying, 'Where are the Ash-'ariyin?' He then ordered five nice camels to be given to us, and when we had departed, we said, 'What have we done? Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) had taken the oath not to give us any mounts, and that he had nothing to mount us on, and later he gave us that we might ride? Did we take advantage of the fact that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) had forgotten his oath? By Allah, we will never succeed.' So we went back to him and said to him, 'We came to you to give us mounts, and you took an oath that you would not give us any mounts and that you had nothing to mount us on.' On that he said, 'I did not provide you with mounts, but Allah did. By Allah, if I take an oath to do something, and then find something else better than it, I do that which is better and make expiation for the dissolution of the oath

bukhari:6649.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's refusal was merely an unintentional oath spoken in frustration (*laghw al-yamīn*), or that Islamic law (Quran 5:89; 66:2) virtuously permits breaking a vow through expiation (*kaffārah*) whenever a more charitable action becomes possible. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore a solemn, binding oath in God's name (*"wa-llāhi lā aḥmilukum"*) that his own companions recognized as inviolable (*"wa-llāhi lā nufliḥu abadan"*—'By Allah, we will never succeed'), and when confronted, he first attempted to dodge accountability with a semantic technicality (*"innī lastu anā ḥamaltukum, wa-lākinna llāha ḥamalakum"*—'It was not I who mounted you, but Allah'). By immediately swearing yet another oath (*"wa-llāhi"*) to establish the personal rule that he breaks any vow whenever a better alternative appears and simply absolves himself of it (*"wa-taḥallaltuhā"*), Muhammad reduced solemn oaths sworn by God's name to disposable, transactional conveniences.

bukhari:3044.note: During the Conquest of Mecca in AD 630, upon being informed that Ibn Khatal was clinging to the curtains of the Ka'bah, Muhammad ordered his followers to kill him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم دَخَلَ عَامَ الْفَتْحِ وَعَلَى رَأْسِهِ الْمِغْفَرُ، فَلَمَّا نَزَعَهُ جَاءَ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ إِنَّ ابْنَ خَطَلٍ مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِأَسْتَارِ الْكَعْبَةِ، فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ اقْتُلُوهُ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) entered (Makkah) in the year of the Conquest (of Makkah) wearing a helmet over his head. After he took it off, a man came and said, "Ibn Khatal is clinging to the curtains of the Ka'bah." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Kill him

bukhari:3044.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the AD 630 Conquest of Mecca was a bloodless general amnesty and that Ibn Khaṭal was only executed as a capital punishment for murdering a servant and apostatizing, rather than for political opposition. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that he was unarmed and seeking sacred asylum while "clinging to the curtains of the Ka'bah" (mutaʿalliqun bi-astāri al-Kaʿbah) when Muhammad summarily ordered, "Kill him" (uqtulūhu), bypassing the Quranic guarantee that whoever enters the Sacred Mosque is safe (Quran 3:97) through a convenient one-hour suspension of sanctuary (bukhari:1834). Furthermore, Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī admits that Muhammad simultaneously ordered the execution of Ibn Khaṭal's two female singers (qaynatān) solely for singing satirical poetry mocking him (bi-hijāʾi al-nabī), proving the purge targeted personal critics rather than strictly enforcing murder laws.

bukhari:6680.note: After swearing in anger not to provide mounts to the Ash'arites, Muhammad declares as a general rule that whenever he swears an oath and later sees a better alternative, he does what is better and dissolves his oath through expiation, contrasting with the biblical standard of keeping one's oath even when it hurts ([Ps 15:4](bible://ps/15/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَاللَّهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لاَ أَحْلِفُ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَأَرَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا، إِلاَّ أَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ وَتَحَلَّلْتُهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: if ever I take an oath (to do something) and later on I find something else better than the first, then I do the better one and give expiation for the dissolution of my oath

bukhari:6680.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists, citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, typically argue that breaking a rash oath in order to perform a more charitable deed—here, generously providing mounts to the needy Ash'arites—is a divinely sanctioned act of piety under Quran 5:89 rather than opportunistic deceit. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad initially swore a solemn oath in Allah's name simply because he was in an "angry mood" (*wa-huwa ghaḍbān*, وَهْوَ غَضْبَانُ), and then formulated the sweeping rule: *"I do not swear an oath and then see something else better than it, except that I do that which is better and dissolve my oath"* (لاَ أَحْلِفُ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَأَرَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا، إِلاَّ أَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ وَتَحَلَّلْتُهَا). Furthermore, parallel narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3133, 6622) admit he initially handed over the camels because he forgot his oath, and by codifying the subjective standard of "seeing something better" (*fa-arā ghayrahā khayran minhā*) paired with ritual expiation (*wa-taḥallaltuhā*), he reduced sacred vows in God's name to revocable conveniences whenever a more advantageous option arises.

bukhari:4331.note: After Muhammad distributed the Hawazin war spoils by giving 100 camels each to Qurayshi men while leaving out the Ansar, younger men among the Ansar protested that he was giving to the Quraysh while their swords were still dripping with Qurayshi blood. Summoning the Ansar privately, Muhammad stated that he gave the wealth to men who had recently left unbelief in order to win over their hearts ([Leviticus 19:15](bible://lv/19/15); [Quran 9:58-60](quran://9/58-60)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: حِينَ أَفَاءَ اللَّهُ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَا أَفَاءَ مِنْ أَمْوَالِ هَوَازِنَ، فَطَفِقَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُعْطِي رِجَالاً الْمِائَةَ مِنَ الإِبِلِ فَقَالُوا يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُعْطِي قُرَيْشًا وَيَتْرُكُنَا، وَسُيُوفُنَا تَقْطُرُ مِنْ دِمَائِهِمْ‏.‏ قَالَ أَنَسٌ فَحُدِّثَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِمَقَالَتِهِمْ، فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَى الأَنْصَارِ فَجَمَعَهُمْ فِي قُبَّةٍ مِنْ أَدَمٍ وَلَمْ يَدْعُ مَعَهُمْ غَيْرَهُمْ، فَلَمَّا اجْتَمَعُوا قَامَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَا حَدِيثٌ بَلَغَنِي عَنْكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ فُقَهَاءُ الأَنْصَارِ أَمَّا رُؤَسَاؤُنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَلَمْ يَقُولُوا شَيْئًا، وَأَمَّا نَاسٌ مِنَّا حَدِيثَةٌ أَسْنَانُهُمْ فَقَالُوا يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُعْطِي قُرَيْشًا وَيَتْرُكُنَا، وَسُيُوفُنَا تَقْطُرُ مِنْ دِمَائِهِمْ‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَإِنِّي أُعْطِي رِجَالاً حَدِيثِي عَهْدٍ بِكُفْرٍ، أَتَأَلَّفُهُمْ
problematic_excerpt.english: When Allah gave Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) what he gave of the properties of the Hawazin tribe as a war booty, the Prophet (ﷺ) started giving some men 100 camels each. The Ansar (then) said, "May Allah forgive Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as he gives to Quraish and leaves us although our swords are still dribbling with the blood of Quraish." Allah's Apostle was informed of their statement, so he sent for the Ansar and gathered them in a leather tent, and did not call anybody else along with them. When they all gathered, the Prophet (ﷺ) got up and said, "What is this talk being informed to me about you?" The learned men amongst the Ansar said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Our chiefs did not say anything, but some people amongst us who are younger in age said, 'May Allah forgive Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as he gives (of the booty) to Quraish and leaves us though our swords are still dribbling with their blood." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "I give to these men who have newly deserted heathenism (and embraced Islam) so as to attract their hearts.

bukhari:4331.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's distribution of the Hunayn spoils was not tribal nepotism toward his fellow Quraysh, but wise statesmanship under Quran 9:60 (*al-mu'allafatu qulūbuhum*)—defended by Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī as honoring the Ansar's firm faith while stabilizing fragile Meccan converts. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad used plundered war booty to buy the allegiance of recent polytheists with a hundred camels each (*'uʿṭī rijālan ḥadīthī ʿahdin bi-kufrin ata'allafuhum'*) while leaving the actual combatants whose swords were still dripping with blood (*'suyūfunā taqṭuru min dimā'ihim'*) empty-handed. Furthermore, parallel narration `bukhari:3147` confirms that Qurayshi elites like Safwan ibn Umayyah despised Muhammad until this windfall of plunder purchased their loyalty, and Anas ibn Malik concludes `bukhari:4331` by recording that when the Ansar subsequently suffered the 'severe favoritism' (*'uthratan shadīdatan'*) Muhammad predicted, 'they did not remain patient' (*'fa-lam yaṣbirū'*).

bukhari:6623.note: Muhammad swore by Allah that he would not provide Abu Musa and the Ash'ariyyin with mounts, yet gave them three she-camels when they arrived, prompting the group to return out of fear that they would not be blessed because he had broken his oath. Muhammad replied that it was Allah who gave them the mounts and declared that whenever he swears an oath and later sees a better course of action, he dissolves his vow through expiation (kaffārah) and does what is better ([Matthew 5:33-37](bible://mt/5/33-37); [Numbers 30:2](bible://nm/30/2); cf. [Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَتَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي رَهْطٍ مِنَ الأَشْعَرِيِّينَ أَسْتَحْمِلُهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أَحْمِلُكُمْ، وَمَا عِنْدِي مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ ثُمَّ لَبِثْنَا مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ أَنْ نَلْبَثَ، ثُمَّ أُتِيَ بِثَلاَثِ ذَوْدٍ غُرِّ الذُّرَى فَحَمَلَنَا عَلَيْهَا فَلَمَّا انْطَلَقْنَا قُلْنَا أَوْ قَالَ بَعْضُنَا وَاللَّهِ لاَ يُبَارَكُ لَنَا، أَتَيْنَا النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَسْتَحْمِلُهُ، فَحَلَفَ أَنْ لاَ يَحْمِلَنَا ثُمَّ حَمَلَنَا، فَارْجِعُوا بِنَا إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَنُذَكِّرُهُ، فَأَتَيْنَاهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَا أَنَا حَمَلْتُكُمْ، بَلِ اللَّهُ حَمَلَكُمْ، وَإِنِّي وَاللَّهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لاَ أَحْلِفُ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَأَرَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا، إِلاَّ كَفَّرْتُ عَنْ يَمِينِي، وَأَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I went to the Prophet (ﷺ) along with a group of Al-Ash`ariyin in order to request him to provide us with mounts. He said, "By Allah, I will not provide you with mounts and I haven't got anything to mount you on." Then we stayed there as long as Allah wished us to stay, and then three very nice looking she-camels were brought to him and he made us ride them. When we left, we, or some of us, said, "By Allah, we will not be blessed, as we came to the Prophet (ﷺ) asking him for mounts, and he swore that he would not give us any mounts but then he did give us. So let us go back to the Prophet (ﷺ) and remind him (of his oath)." When we returned to him (and reminded him of the fact), he said, "I did not give you mounts, but it is Allah Who gave you.
