By Allah, Allah willing, if I ever take an oath to do something and then I find something else than the first, I will make expiation for my oath and do the thing which is better

bukhari:6623.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—that Muhammad only meant he had no mounts at that immediate moment, forgot his vow when camels later arrived, and modeled the moral virtue of paying expiation (*kaffārah*) rather than letting an oath prevent an act of charity. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that his own companions recognized his action as a violated oath that would forfeit God's blessing (*Wallāhi lā yubāraku lanā... fa-ḥalafa an lā yaḥmilanā thumma ḥamalanā*), while parallel narrations (`bukhari:4385`) admit he rashly swore in Allah's name simply because he was angry (*ghadbān*). When confronted, Muhammad first deflected responsibility onto God (*mā anā ḥamaltukum, bal Allāhu ḥamalakum*) before institutionalizing a policy of breaking solemn vows whenever a preferable option appears (*illā kaffartu ʿan yamīnī wa-ataytu alladhī huwa khayr*)—the same theological loophole later invoked in Quran 66:1–2 to absolve him of breaking his sworn oath to his wives.

bukhari:4334.note: Muhammad told the Ansar that he gave the worldly spoils to the Quraysh—who had only recently left pre-Islamic paganism and suffered losses—in order to compensate them and win over their hearts (أَجْبُرَهُمْ وَأَتَأَلَّفَهُمْ), asking the Ansar to be content returning home with him rather than material wealth. Classical jurisprudence codifies this unequal distribution of wealth to secure loyalty to Islam under the legal category of al-mu'allafatu qulūbuhum (those whose hearts are to be reconciled; see [Quran 9:58](quran://9/58); [Quran 9:60](quran://9/60); cf. [Leviticus 19:15](bible://lv/19/15)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: جَمَعَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَاسًا مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ، فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ قُرَيْشًا حَدِيثُ عَهْدٍ بِجَاهِلِيَّةٍ وَمُصِيبَةٍ، وَإِنِّي أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَجْبُرَهُمْ وَأَتَأَلَّفَهُمْ أَمَا تَرْضَوْنَ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ النَّاسُ بِالدُّنْيَا، وَتَرْجِعُونَ بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى بُيُوتِكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالُوا بَلَى‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) gathered some people of Ansar and said, "The People of Quraish are still close to their Pre-Islamic period of ignorance and have suffered a lot, and I want to help them and attract their hearts (by giving them the war booty). Won't you be pleased that the people take the worldly things) and you take Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) with you to your homes?" They said, "Yes, (i.e. we are pleased with this distribution)."

bukhari:4334.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as Ibn Hajar explains in Fatḥ al-Bārī, giving the Hunayn war spoils to the Quraysh (al-mu'allafatu qulūbuhum in Quran 9:60) was not tribal favoritism or bribery, but wise statesmanship that honored the Ansar's superior, unshakeable faith while comforting fragile new converts. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad used worldly plunder (al-dunyā) to placate and win over (ajburahum wa ata'allafahum) people still steeped in pre-Islamic paganism (ḥadīthu 'ahdin bi-jāhiliyyatin), reducing religious allegiance to a material transaction. Moreover, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:4331, bukhari:3147) confirm that the Ansar themselves initially recognized and condemned this unequal payout as tribal nepotism that 'did not seek the Face of Allah' (mā urīda bihā wajhu Allāh).

bukhari:4667.note: Muhammad distributed goods sent to him among four men—identified in parallel reports (bukhari:3344, bukhari:4351) as four tribal chiefs given gold spoils—stating that he did so to win their hearts (ata'allafuhum; cf. [Quran 9:58](quran://9/58); [Leviticus 19:15](bible://lv/19/15)). When a man objected that he had not acted justly (ma 'adalta), Muhammad declared that people who abandon the religion would emerge from the critic's lineage.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: بُعِثَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِشَىْءٍ، فَقَسَمَهُ بَيْنَ أَرْبَعَةٍ وَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَتَأَلَّفُهُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مَا عَدَلْتَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ ضِئْضِئِ هَذَا قَوْمٌ يَمْرُقُونَ مِنَ الدِّينِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Something was sent to the Prophet (ﷺ) and he distributed it amongst four (men) and said, "I want to attract their hearts,(to Islam thereby)," A man said (to the Prophet (ﷺ) ), "You have not done justice." Thereupon the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "There will emerge from the offspring of this (man) some people who will renounce the religion

bukhari:4667.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that distributing wealth to 'reconcile hearts' (*al-mu'allafatu qulūbuhum* in Quran 9:60) was wise statesmanship rather than bribery, and that the critic (Dhū al-Khuwayṣirah) was an arrogant proto-Kharijite rightly rebuked in Quran 9:58. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad funnelled public tribute exclusively to four powerful tribal chiefs to 'attract their hearts' (`أَتَأَلَّفُهُمْ`, *ata'allafuhum*) to Islam—a practice parallel narrations (`bukhari:4351`, `bukhari:3344`) confirm outraged even his own loyal Quraysh and Anṣār companions over the blatant favoritism. Rather than refuting the charge of partiality (`مَا عَدَلْتَ`, 'You have not done justice') on its merits, Muhammad deflected the critique by cursing the whistleblower's future offspring (`يَخْرُجُ مِنْ ضِئْضِئِ هَذَا`) and codifying financial inducement as a permanent tool of conversion.

bukhari:5518.note: While angry, Muhammad swore an oath not to provide Abu Musa and the Ash'ariyyin with mounts, but after captured camels arrived he gave them five and declared that whenever he swears an oath and later sees a better alternative, he does what is better and expiates his oath ([Matthew 5:33-37](bible://mt/5/33-37); [Numbers 30:2](bible://nm/30/2); cf. [Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنِّي أَتَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي نَفَرٍ مِنَ الأَشْعَرِيِّينَ، فَوَافَقْتُهُ وَهْوَ غَضْبَانُ، وَهْوَ يَقْسِمُ نَعَمًا مِنْ نَعَمِ الصَّدَقَةِ فَاسْتَحْمَلْنَاهُ فَحَلَفَ أَنْ لاَ يَحْمِلَنَا، قَالَ ‏"‏ مَا عِنْدِي مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ أُتِيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِنَهْبٍ مِنْ إِبِلٍ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَيْنَ الأَشْعَرِيُّونَ أَيْنَ الأَشْعَرِيُّونَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَعْطَانَا خَمْسَ ذَوْدٍ غُرِّ الذُّرَى، فَلَبِثْنَا غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ، فَقُلْتُ لأَصْحَابِي نَسِيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَمِينَهُ، فَوَاللَّهِ لَئِنْ تَغَفَّلْنَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَمِينَهُ لاَ نُفْلِحُ أَبَدًا‏.‏ فَرَجَعْنَا إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقُلْنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّا اسْتَحْمَلْنَاكَ، فَحَلَفْتَ أَنْ لاَ تَحْمِلَنَا فَظَنَنَّا أَنَّكَ نَسِيتَ يَمِينَكَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ حَمَلَكُمْ، إِنِّي وَاللَّهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لاَ أَحْلِفُ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَأَرَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا إِلاَّ أَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ، وَتَحَلَّلْتُهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Once I went to Allah's Apostle with a group of Al-Ash`ariyin, and met him while he was angry, distributing some camels of rak`at. We asked for mounts but he took an oath that he would not give us any mounts, and added, 'I have nothing to mount you on' In the meantime some camels of booty were brought to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and he asked twice, 'Where are Al-Ash`ariyin?" So he gave us five white camels with big humps. We stayed for a short while (after we had covered a little distance), and then I said to my companions, "Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) has forgotten his oath. By Allah, if we do not remind Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) of his oath, we will never be successful." So we returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! We asked you for mounts, but you took an oath that you would not give us any mounts; we think that you have forgotten your oath.' He said, 'It is Allah Who has given you mounts. By Allah, and Allah willing, if I take an oath and later find something else better than that. then I do what is better and expiate my oath

bukhari:5518.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islamic law (citing Quran 5:89, 66:2, and Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī) commends breaking a vow to perform a more charitable deed via expiation (kaffārah), claiming Muhammad only swore because he temporarily lacked mounts. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore his categorical refusal in a state of anger (wa-huwa ghaḍbān, وَهْوَ غَضْبَانُ) and subsequently codified a utilitarian rule to dissolve his solemn oaths (wa-taḥallaltuhā, وَتَحَلَّلْتُهَا) whenever another option later seemed preferable (fa-arā ghayrahā khayran minhā). Even his own companions recognized the moral gravity of violating a vow sworn by Allah—warning that if they let him break his oath they would 'never be successful' (lā nufliḥu abadan, لاَ نُفْلِحُ أَبَدًا)—demonstrating how ritual expiation renders solemn divine oaths completely disposable whenever convenience dictates.

bukhari:3344.note: Muhammad divided a piece of gold sent by Ali among four tribal chiefs—Al-Aqra' bin Habis, 'Uyaina bin Badr, Zaid at-Ta'i, and 'Alqama bin 'Ulatha—explaining that he did so to win their hearts (*ta'lif al-qulub*). This distribution angered the Quraish and the Ansar, who objected that he gave to the chiefs of Najd while excluding them, and prompted a man to tell him to fear Allah.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: بَعَثَ عَلِيٌّ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِذُهَيْبَةٍ فَقَسَمَهَا بَيْنَ الأَرْبَعَةِ الأَقْرَعِ بْنِ حَابِسٍ الْحَنْظَلِيِّ ثُمَّ الْمُجَاشِعِيِّ، وَعُيَيْنَةَ بْنِ بَدْرٍ الْفَزَارِيِّ، وَزَيْدٍ الطَّائِيِّ ثُمَّ أَحَدِ بَنِي نَبْهَانَ، وَعَلْقَمَةَ بْنِ عُلاَثَةَ الْعَامِرِيِّ ثُمَّ أَحَدِ بَنِي كِلاَبٍ، فَغَضِبَتْ قُرَيْشٌ وَالأَنْصَارُ، قَالُوا يُعْطِي صَنَادِيدَ أَهْلِ نَجْدٍ وَيَدَعُنَا‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّمَا أَتَأَلَّفُهُمْ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: `Ali sent a piece of gold to the Prophet (ﷺ) who distributed it among four persons: Al-Aqra' bin H`Abis Al-Hanzali from the tribe of Mujashi, 'Uyaina bin Badr Al-Fazari, Zaid at-Ta'i who belonged to (the tribe of) Bani Nabhan, and 'Alqama bin Ulatha Al-`Amiri who belonged to (the tribe of) Bani Kilab. So the Quraish and the Ansar became angry and said, "He (i.e. the Prophet, ) gives the chief of Najd and does not give us." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "I give them) so as to attract their hearts (to Islam)."

bukhari:3344.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that distributing this gold exclusively to tribal leaders was wise statecraft under the Quranic category of al-mu'allafatu qulūbuhum (Surah 9:60), citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim to claim it softened wavering hearts and protected the community from hostility. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad bypassed his own devoted followers to enrich the powerful 'chieftains of the people of Najd' (صَنَادِيدَ أَهْلِ نَجْدٍ), provoking immediate anger from both the Quraysh and the Ansar (فَغَضِبَتْ قُرَيْشٌ وَالأَنْصَارُ) and a public rebuke to 'fear Allah' (اتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَا مُحَمَّدُ). By justifying this unequal distribution with the admission 'I only seek to win them over' (إِنَّمَا أَتَأَلَّفُهُمْ), Muhammad confirmed that he relied on material bribery of political elites rather than spiritual conviction to purchase tribal allegiance.

bukhari:4385.note: Muhammad swore an oath not to provide the Ash'ariyyin with mounts, but subsequently gave them five camels from captured war booty and declared that whenever he swears an oath and later sees a better alternative, he acts on the better option ([Matthew 5:33-37](bible://mt/5/33-37); [Numbers 30:2](bible://nm/30/2); cf. [Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)). While the English translation interpolates a parenthetical clause about paying expiation from parallel reports (e.g. bukhari:6623), the Arabic text of this narration records only his declaration that he sets aside his sworn oath whenever he sees something more advantageous.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّا أَتَيْنَا النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَفَرٌ مِنَ الأَشْعَرِيِّينَ، فَاسْتَحْمَلْنَاهُ فَأَبَى أَنْ يَحْمِلَنَا فَاسْتَحْمَلْنَاهُ، فَحَلَفَ أَنْ لاَ يَحْمِلَنَا، ثُمَّ لَمْ يَلْبَثِ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ أُتِيَ بِنَهْبِ إِبِلٍ، فَأَمَرَ لَنَا بِخَمْسِ ذَوْدٍ، فَلَمَّا قَبَضْنَاهَا قُلْنَا تَغَفَّلْنَا النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَمِينَهُ، لاَ نُفْلِحُ بَعْدَهَا أَبَدًا فَأَتَيْتُهُ فَقُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّكَ حَلَفْتَ أَنْ لاَ تَحْمِلَنَا وَقَدْ حَمَلْتَنَا‏.‏ قَالَ ‏ "‏ أَجَلْ، وَلَكِنْ لاَ أَحْلِفُ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَأَرَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا إِلاَّ أَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِنْهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: We, a group of Al-Ash`ariyin people went to the Prophet and asked him to give us something to ride, but the Prophet (ﷺ) refused. Then we asked him for the second time to give us something to ride, but the Prophet (ﷺ) took an oath that he would not give us anything to ride. After a while, some camels of booty were brought to the Prophet (ﷺ) and he ordered that five camels be given to us. When we took those camels we said, "We have made the Prophet (ﷺ) forget his oath, and we will not be successful after that." So I went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "O Allah's Apostle ! You took an oath that you would not give us anything to ride, but you have given us." He said, "Yes, for if I take an oath and later I see a better solution than that, I act on the later (and gave the expiation of that oath)

bukhari:4385.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—that Muhammad was modeling the legal mechanism of *kaffārat al-yamīn* (oath expiation under Quran 5:89), whereby a believer ought to set aside a rash vow if a more charitable deed presents itself. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore not to provide mounts (`فَحَلَفَ أَنْ لاَ يَحْمِلَنَا`) and reversed his vow only after war plunder arrived (`أُتِيَ بِنَهْبِ إِبِلٍ`), while the English translator's parenthetical gloss "(and gave the expiation of that oath)" is entirely absent from the Arabic text of this narration (`إِلاَّ أَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِنْهَا`). Furthermore, even when read alongside parallel narrations mentioning expiation (`bukhari:6623`), Muhammad's stated maxim (`لاَ أَحْلِفُ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَأَرَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا`) reduces a solemn oath in Allah's name to a disposable commitment that can be voided whenever a more advantageous outcome appears.

bukhari:3133.note: Muhammad swore an oath by Allah not to provide Abu Musa and the Ash'ariyyin with mounts, yet later gave them five camels from acquired war booty. When questioned about his oath, he stated that Allah had provided the mounts and declared that whenever he swears an oath and later sees a better alternative, he does what is better and expiates his oath ([Matthew 5:33-37](bible://mt/5/33-37); [Numbers 30:2](bible://nm/30/2); cf. [Quran 5:89](quran://5/89), [Quran 66:2](quran://66/2)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَرَجَعْنَا إِلَيْهِ فَقُلْنَا إِنَّا سَأَلْنَاكَ أَنْ تَحْمِلَنَا، فَحَلَفْتَ أَنْ لاَ تَحْمِلَنَا أَفَنَسِيتَ قَالَ ‏"‏ لَسْتُ أَنَا حَمَلْتُكُمْ، وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَمَلَكُمْ، وَإِنِّي وَاللَّهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لاَ أَحْلِفُ عَلَى يَمِينٍ فَأَرَى غَيْرَهَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا إِلاَّ أَتَيْتُ الَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ وَتَحَلَّلْتُهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: So, we returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, 'We asked you to provide us with means of conveyance, but you took an oath that you would not provide us with any means of conveyance. Did you forget (your oath when you gave us the camels)? He replied. 'I have not provided you with means of conveyance, but Allah has provided you with it, and by Allah, Allah willing, if ever I take an oath to do something, and later on I find that it is more beneficial to do something different, I will do the thing which is better, and give expiation for my oath

bukhari:3133.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—that Islamic jurisprudence virtuously prioritizes charitable outcomes over rigid vows by prescribing expiation (*kaffārah* per Quran 5:89) whenever a better deed arises, adding that Muhammad only swore initially because Abu Musa approached him while he was angry (`bukhari:4385`). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad first tried to deflect his oath-breaking through a semantic technicality (`لَسْتُ أَنَا حَمَلْتُكُمْ، وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَمَلَكُمْ` — "It is not I who provided you with mounts, but Allah provided you") before admitting that he voids his sworn oaths (`وَتَحَلَّلْتُهَا`) whenever a more advantageous option (`خَيْرًا مِنْهَا`) appears. This reduces swearing by God's name (`وَاللَّهِ لاَ أَحْمِلُكُمْ`) from an inviolable covenant into a revocable convenience, a breach so severe that Muhammad's own companions initially feared they would be cursed for accepting the camels (`مَا صَنَعْنَا لاَ يُبَارَكُ لَنَا` — "What have we done? We will never be blessed").

bukhari:6922.note: After Ali burned a group of apostates (`zanādiqah`), Ibn Abbas stated that while Muhammad forbade punishing with fire, he would have executed them in accordance with Muhammad's command: 'Whoever changes his religion, kill him' (cf. bukhari:3017). Classical Sunni jurisprudence cites this declaration (`man baddala dīnahu fa-qtulūhu`) as the foundational mandate for executing those who leave Islam.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لِقَوْلِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ مَنْ بَدَّلَ دِينَهُ فَاقْتُلُوهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: according to the statement of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), 'Whoever changed his Islamic religion, then kill him

bukhari:6922.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the command to execute apostates applied only to wartime political treason and armed rebellion against the early Islamic state, citing Quran 2:256 ('There is no compulsion in religion'). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an unconditional legal maxim—'man baddala dīnahu fa-qtulūhu' ('whoever changes his religion, then kill him')—which both 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas applied directly to theological heretics (zanādiqah) with zero mention of armed warfare. Furthermore, Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani in Fatḥ al-Bārī and consensus across all four Sunni legal schools confirm that mere religious apostasy (riddah) after accepting Islam mandates capital punishment by the sword.

bukhari:6824.note: When Ma'iz bin Malik confesses to illicit sexual relations, Muhammad first asks if he merely kissed, winked, or looked at the woman, and then uses the direct, un-euphemized Arabic term for intercourse (*aniktaha*) to eliminate legal ambiguity before ordering him stoned to death.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏"‏ أَنِكْتَهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ لاَ يَكْنِي‏.‏ قَالَ فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَمَرَ بِرَجْمِهِ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet said, using no euphemism, "Did you have sexual intercourse with her?" The narrator added: At that, (i.e. after his confession) the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that he be stoned (to death)

bukhari:6824.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad mercifully tried to give Ma'iz a legal exit by suggesting he only kissed or looked (لَعَلَّكَ قَبَّلْتَ أَوْ غَمَزْتَ أَوْ نَظَرْتَ), and claim—citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī—that he only used the explicit term أَنِكْتَهَا (anikta-hā) out of strict judicial necessity to verify penetration before acting on a voluntary confession. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad spoke without euphemism (لاَ يَكْنِي) by using the vulgar root n-y-k ('Did you fuck her?')—which English translators sanitize into clinical phrasing—before immediately ordering him stoned to death (أَمَرَ بِرَجْمِهِ). Furthermore, the adjacent Sahih narrations (bukhari:6820, bukhari:6825, bukhari:6826) collapse the 'voluntary purification' defense by recording that as soon as the stones struck Ma'iz, he fled in terror for his life (هَرَبَ), yet the Companions chased him down and bludgeoned him to death anyway.

bukhari:6829.note: Umar ibn al-Khattab declares that stoning to death (al-rajm) is a binding divine obligation upon any married person who commits unlawful sexual intercourse when established by witnesses, pregnancy, or confession. He testifies that Muhammad carried out the penalty of stoning and that the companions continued to enforce it after him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَلاَ وَإِنَّ الرَّجْمَ حَقٌّ عَلَى مَنْ زَنَى، وَقَدْ أَحْصَنَ، إِذَا قَامَتِ الْبَيِّنَةُ، أَوْ كَانَ الْحَمْلُ أَوْ الاِعْتِرَافُ ـ قَالَ سُفْيَانُ كَذَا حَفِظْتُ ـ أَلاَ وَقَدْ رَجَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَرَجَمْنَا بَعْدَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Lo! I confirm that the penalty of Rajam be inflicted on him who commits illegal sexual intercourse, if he is already married and the crime is proved by witnesses or pregnancy or confession." Sufyan added, "I have memorized this narration in this way." `Umar added, "Surely Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) carried out the penalty of Rajam, and so did we after him

bukhari:6829.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that stoning to death (*al-rajm*) is either un-Quranic—pointing to the 100 lashes in Surah 24:2—or a purely symbolic deterrent that is practically impossible to enforce due to the requirement of four eyewitnesses. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that stoning the married adulterer is a binding right (*al-rajma ḥaqqun ‘alā man zanā wa-qad aḥṣana*) established not merely by witnesses (*al-bayyinah*), but also by pregnancy (*al-ḥaml*)—which uniquely weaponizes biological evidence against women—or confession (*al-i‘tirāf*). Moreover, Umar refutes any claim that the punishment was merely theoretical by testifying that "the Messenger of Allah stoned, and we stoned after him" (*wa-qad rajama Rasūl Allāh... wa-rajamnā ba‘dahu*).

bukhari:6829.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:6829.note: Umar ibn al-Khattab warns that people will eventually say they do not find stoning (al-rajm) in the Book of Allah and go astray by abandoning an obligation that Allah sent down (anzalaha Allah). In the fuller report immediately following (bukhari:6830), Umar explicitly states that Allah revealed the Verse of Stoning (ayat al-rajm) which the companions recited and memorized—an absence from the extant Quranic text that classical commentators explain as the abrogation of the verse's wording while its legal ruling remains in force.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَقَدْ خَشِيتُ أَنْ يَطُولَ بِالنَّاسِ زَمَانٌ حَتَّى يَقُولَ قَائِلٌ لاَ نَجِدُ الرَّجْمَ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ‏.‏ فَيَضِلُّوا بِتَرْكِ فَرِيضَةٍ أَنْزَلَهَا اللَّهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: I am afraid that after a long time has passed, people may say, "We do not find the Verses of the Rajam (stoning to death) in the Holy Book," and consequently they may go astray by leaving an obligation that Allah has revealed.

bukhari:6829.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the stoning verse underwent *naskh al-tilāwah dūna al-ḥukm* (abrogation of its recitation while retaining its legal ruling), claiming its omission from the Quran was a deliberate divine decree rather than textual loss. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Umar feared future generations would go astray because they "do not find stoning in the Book of Allah" (*lā najidu al-rajma fī Kitāb Allāh*), despite it being "an obligation that Allah revealed" (*farīḍatin anzalahā Allāh*). Furthermore, in the immediate parallel narration (bukhari:6830), Umar admits he wanted to write the verse into the *Muṣḥaf* himself and only refrained out of fear that people would accuse him of adding to the Quran—proving its absence was a crisis of preservation rather than a settled theological doctrine.

bukhari:4341.note: Dispatched by Muhammad to govern Yemen with instructions to make things easy and give good tidings, Mu`adh bin Jabal visits Abu Musa, finds a man with his hands tied to his neck for disbelieving after embracing Islam, and refuses to dismount from his mule until Abu Musa orders the man killed. Parallel narrations specify that the prisoner was a Jewish convert who reverted to Judaism and record Mu`adh declaring his execution to be the judgment of Allah and His Messenger (bukhari:4344, bukhari:6923; cf. [Quran 4:89](quran://4/89)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَإِذَا رَجُلٌ عِنْدَهُ قَدْ جُمِعَتْ يَدَاهُ إِلَى عُنُقِهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ مُعَاذٌ يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ قَيْسٍ، أَيَّمَ هَذَا قَالَ هَذَا رَجُلٌ كَفَرَ بَعْدَ إِسْلاَمِهِ‏.‏ قَالَ لاَ أَنْزِلُ حَتَّى يُقْتَلَ‏.‏ قَالَ إِنَّمَا جِيءَ بِهِ لِذَلِكَ فَانْزِلْ‏.‏ قَالَ مَا أَنْزِلُ حَتَّى يُقْتَلَ فَأَمَرَ بِهِ فَقُتِلَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Behold! There was a man tied with his hands behind his neck. Mu`adh said to Abu Musa, "O `Abdullah bin Qais! What is this?" Abu Musa replied. "This man has reverted to Heathenism after embracing Islam." Mu`adh said, "I will not dismount till he is killed." Abu Musa replied, "He has been brought for this purpose, so come down." Mu`adh said, "I will not dismount till he is killed." So Abu Musa ordered that he be killed, and he was killed.

bukhari:4341.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that capital punishment for apostasy only applied to political treason or armed rebellion (*ḥirābah*), and cite Muhammad's opening command in this Hadith—'facilitate things and do not repulse people' (*yassirā wa lā tuʿassirā*)—as proof of religious tolerance. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the bound prisoner's sole offense was religious—'this is a man who disbelieved after his Islam' (*hādhā rajulun kafara baʿda islāmihi*)—which parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:4342, 6923) specify was merely reverting to Judaism (*kāna yahūdiyyan fa-aslama thumma tahawwada*) with zero mention of treason or sedition. Mu'adh's refusal to even dismount his mule until the man was executed on the spot (*lā anzilu ḥattā yuqtala*), upheld by Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī as the binding prophetic verdict (*qaḍāʾu Allāhi wa rasūlihi*), proves that prophetic 'lenience' never included freedom of conscience.

bukhari:6915.note: When asked if he possesses any written revelation outside the Quran, Ali states that his scroll (al-sahifah) records regulations on blood-money, the release of captives, and the decree that no Muslim is to be executed (la yuqtal muslimun bi-kafir) for killing a disbeliever. While adjacent traditions (such as bukhari:6914) warn of afterlife punishment for killing a treaty-protected non-Muslim, this text codifies the earthly legal exemption in majority Sunni jurisprudence that a Muslim is not subject to retaliatory capital punishment (qisas) for killing a non-Muslim.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَأَنْ لاَ يُقْتَلَ مُسْلِمٌ بِكَافِرٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: and the judgment that no Muslim should be killed in Qisas (equality in punishment) for killing a Kafir (disbeliever)

bukhari:6915.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the term kāfir in this decree refers exclusively to a hostile enemy combatant (ḥarbī) rather than a peaceful non-Muslim citizen (dhimmī), often appealing to a minority Hanafi legal opinion. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states lā yuqtala muslimun bi-kāfirin (لاَ يُقْتَلَ مُسْلِمٌ بِكَافِرٍ), employing an unrestricted indefinite noun (nakirah) under negation that grammatically encompasses every non-Muslim without exception. As Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani confirms in Fatḥ al-Bārī alongside the majority (jumhūr) of Sunni jurisprudence (the Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali schools), this foundational Prophetic statute categorically forbids executing a Muslim in retaliation (qiṣāṣ) for murdering any non-Muslim, including a protected dhimmī.

bukhari:4357.note: During the campaign commissioned by Muhammad to destroy Dhu-l-Khalasa, Jarir ordered a man casting divination arrows to break them and testify that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah or else have his neck struck off, upon which the man complied.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ يَضْرِبُ بِهَا إِذْ وَقَفَ عَلَيْهِ جَرِيرٌ فَقَالَ لَتَكْسِرَنَّهَا وَلَتَشْهَدَنَّ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ أَوْ لأَضْرِبَنَّ عُنُقَكَ‏.‏ قَالَ فَكَسَرَهَا وَشَهِدَ
problematic_excerpt.english: One day while he was using them (i.e. arrows of divination), Jarir stopped there and said to him, "Break them (i.e. the arrows) and testify that None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, or else I will chop off your neck." So the man broke those arrows and testified that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah.

bukhari:4357.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islam forbids forced conversion under Quran 2:256 ('There is no compulsion in religion') and claim Jarir was merely halting an unlawful public practice of pagan divination rather than compelling belief. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Jarir issued a literal ultimatum of conversion or immediate decapitation—'latashhadanna an lā ilāha illā Allāhu aw la-aḍribanna ʿunuqaka' ('you shall surely testify that there is no god but Allah, or else I will strike your neck')—forcing the diviner to recite the shahada at swordpoint ('fa-kasarahā wa-shahida'). Furthermore, as Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani explains in Fatḥ al-Bārī, Sunni jurisprudence ratifies this exact coercion because Quran 9:5 and Muhammad's command in bukhari:25 leave Arab polytheists no choice except embracing Islam or the sword.

bukhari:4357.note: Muhammad commissioned Jarir and 150 cavalrymen from the Ahmas tribe to relieve him of Dhu-l-Khalasa—a sanctuary in Yemen called the Ka'ba that housed worshipped idols—by burning and dismantling it, after which Muhammad blessed the riders and their horses five times. A parallel report (bukhari:4355) adds that Jarir's forces also killed everyone present at the sanctuary during the raid.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ لِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَلاَ تُرِيحُنِي مِنْ ذِي الْخَلَصَةِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ بَلَى‏.‏ فَانْطَلَقْتُ فِي خَمْسِينَ وَمِائَةِ فَارِسٍ مِنْ أَحْمَسَ وَكَانُوا أَصْحَابَ خَيْلٍ وَكُنْتُ لاَ أَثْبُتُ عَلَى الْخَيْلِ، فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَضَرَبَ يَدَهُ عَلَى صَدْرِي حَتَّى رَأَيْتُ أَثَرَ يَدِهِ فِي صَدْرِي وَقَالَ ‏"‏ اللَّهُمَّ ثَبِّتْهُ وَاجْعَلْهُ هَادِيًا مَهْدِيًّا ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَمَا وَقَعْتُ عَنْ فَرَسٍ بَعْدُ‏.‏ قَالَ وَكَانَ ذُو الْخَلَصَةِ بَيْتًا بِالْيَمَنِ لِخَثْعَمَ وَبَجِيلَةَ، فِيهِ نُصُبٌ تُعْبَدُ، يُقَالُ لَهُ الْكَعْبَةُ‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَتَاهَا فَحَرَّقَهَا بِالنَّارِ وَكَسَرَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: Jarir said "Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said to me, "Won't you relieve me from Dhul-Khalasa?" I replied, "Yes, (I will relieve you)." So I proceeded along with one-hundred and fifty cavalry from Ahmas tribe who were skillful in riding horses. I used not to sit firm over horses, so I informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of that, and he stroke my chest with his hand till I saw the marks of his hand over my chest and he said, O Allah! Make him firm and one who guides others and is guided (on the right path).' Since then I have never fallen from a horse. Dhul-l--Khulasa was a house in Yemen belonging to the tribe of Khatham and Bajila, and in it there were idols which were worshipped, and it was called Al-Ka`ba." Jarir went there, burnt it with fire and dismantled it.

bukhari:4357.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the expedition against Dhu-l-Khalasa was a defensive military operation against a hostile political stronghold in Yemen rather than an unprovoked attack on another religion's sanctuary. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad ordered the raid simply to rid himself of a rival sanctuary where idols were worshipped ('fīhi nuṣubun tuʿbadu, yuqālu lahu al-kaʿbah'), asking Jarir, 'alā turīḥunī min Dhī al-Khalaṣah' ('Won't you relieve me from Dhu-l-Khalasa?'), whereupon Jarir burned and demolished the temple ('fa-ḥarraqahā bi-l-nāri wa-kasarahā'). Moreover, parallel narrations (bukhari:4356) and Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī record that Jarir's cavalry slaughtered the temple's defenders—killing up to three hundred men—before Muhammad blessed the raiders and their horses five times.

bukhari:7543.note: After demanding that the Jews bring and recite their Torah scroll—where a reader physically covers the stoning verse with his hand rather than the text being altered—Muhammad orders a Jewish man and woman to be stoned to death for adultery, with Ibn Umar witnessing the man bending over the woman to shield her from the stones.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَمَرَ بِهِمَا فَرُجِمَا، فَرَأَيْتُهُ يُجَانِئُ عَلَيْهَا الْحِجَارَةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that the two sinners be stoned to death and, and they were stoned to death, and I saw the man protecting the woman from the stones.

bukhari:7543.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was merely arbitrating for the Jewish community using their own Mosaic law rather than enforcing an Islamic punishment, or that he was simply exposing their rabbinic hypocrisy. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad personally issued the lethal execution command (فَأَمَرَ بِهِمَا فَرُجِمَا, 'so he ordered regarding them both, and they were stoned') as the man died shielding the woman with his body (يُجَانِئُ عَلَيْهَا الْحِجَارَةَ). Furthermore, both Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim confirm that Muhammad executed them under binding Islamic law (ḥukm al-Islām)—which permanently mandates stoning for married adulterers—while his demand to read their physical 7th-century AD Torah scroll (فَأْتُوا بِالتَّوْرَاةِ فَاتْلُوهَا) to verify Divine Law (آيَةُ الرَّجْمِ تَلُوحُ) simultaneously collapses the modern apologetic claim that the Jewish scriptures had been textually corrupted.

bukhari:2314.note: Muhammad commands Unais to go to a man's wife and stone her to death (*farjumha*) if she confesses to adultery. Classical commentators like Ibn Hajar in *Fath al-Bari* affirm this report (detailed in bukhari:2315 and bukhari:6827, where she confesses and is stoned) as a binding prophetic judicial ruling establishing capital punishment by stoning (*rajm*) for married adulterers.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏ "‏ وَاغْدُ يَا أُنَيْسُ إِلَى امْرَأَةِ هَذَا، فَإِنِ اعْتَرَفَتْ فَارْجُمْهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "O Unais! Go to the wife of this (man) and if she confesses (that she has committed illegal sexual intercourse), then stone her to death

bukhari:2314.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that stoning (rajm) is absent from the Quran or that Islamic law requires four eyewitnesses or four unprompted court confessions, rendering the death penalty a virtually impossible theoretical deterrent. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad proactively sent Unais to interrogate the accused woman with the mandate, 'fa-in iʿtarafat fa-rjumhā' ('if she confesses, then stone her'), requiring neither four witnesses nor repeated voluntary appearances. Furthermore, the parallel narrations in bukhari:2315 and bukhari:6827 confirm that she confessed upon questioning and was immediately stoned to death (fa-rujimat) at Muhammad's command, proving that lethal stoning after a single solicited confession was actively enforced.

muslim:4375.note: Reported by 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Muhammad decrees that the blood of a Muslim who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that he is the Messenger of Allah may be lawfully shed in three cases: the married adulterer, a life for a life, and one who forsakes his religion (Islam) and abandons the community.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ لاَ يَحِلُّ دَمُ امْرِئٍ مُسْلِمٍ يَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَأَنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلاَّ بِإِحْدَى ثَلاَثٍ الثَّيِّبُ الزَّانِ وَالنَّفْسُ بِالنَّفْسِ وَالتَّارِكُ لِدِينِهِ الْمُفَارِقُ لِلْجَمَاعَةِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abdullah (b. Mas'ud) reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:It is not permissible to take the life of a Muslim who bears testimony (to the fact that there is no god but Allah, and I am the Messenger of Allah, but in one of the three cases: the married adulterer, a life for life, and the deserter of his Din (Islam), abandoning the community

muslim:4375.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase 'abandoning the community' (الْمُفَارِقُ لِلْجَمَاعَةِ) restricts the death penalty for apostasy to political treason or armed rebellion rather than peaceful religious conversion. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that a Muslim's blood is lawfully shed for 'the deserter of his Din (Islam), abandoning the community' (وَالتَّارِكُ لِدِينِهِ الْمُفَارِقُ لِلْجَمَاعَةِ), defining separation from the community through the act of leaving the religion (دِينِهِ) with no requirement of armed combat, consistent with bukhari:6878, muslim:4377, and bukhari:3017. Furthermore, the same ruling commands shedding the blood (دَمُ) of 'the married adulterer' (الثَّيِّبُ الزَّانِ) alongside 'a life for life' (وَالنَّفْسُ بِالنَّفْسِ), demonstrating that these three exceptions enforce capital religious penalties rather than wartime treason laws.

muslim:4408.note: Muhammad invokes the curse of Allah upon a thief who steals an egg or a rope and has his hand cut off ([Quran 5:38](quran://5/38)). To reconcile this declaration with reports setting a three-dirham threshold for amputation (muslim:4406), the sub-narrator Al-A'mash remarks in a parallel transmission that people reinterpreted the 'egg' as an iron helmet and the rope as one worth a few dirhams (bukhari:6783).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ لَعَنَ اللَّهُ السَّارِقَ يَسْرِقُ الْبَيْضَةَ فَتُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ وَيَسْرِقُ الْحَبْلَ فَتُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:Let there be the curse of Allah upon the thief who steals an egg and his hand is cut off, and steals a rope and his hand is cut off

muslim:4408.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *al-bayḍah* (the egg) metaphorically denotes an iron helmet and *al-ḥabl* (the rope) denotes a costly ship's cable, or that the saying merely warns how petty theft gradually escalates into larger crimes. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *yasriqu al-bayḍata fa-tuqṭaʿu yaduhu wa-yasriqu al-ḥabla fa-tuqṭaʿu yaduhu* ("he steals an egg and his hand is cut off, and steals a rope and his hand is cut off"), using the ordinary nouns for an egg and a rope and attaching the causal conjunction *fa-* ("and so") directly to the amputation of the hand ([Quran 5:38](quran://5/38); `bukhari:6783`, `muslim:4409`). Rather than qualifying the items as high-value goods, the declaration opens with *laʿana Allāhu al-sāriq* ("let there be the curse of Allah upon the thief") precisely because the offender forfeits his hand over such ordinary objects.

muslim:4432.note: After Ma'iz b. Malik confesses to adultery four times and his people confirm his sanity, Muhammad has a pit dug for him and orders him stoned to death. When a pregnant woman from Ghamid likewise insists on confessing to adultery, Muhammad delays her execution until she gives birth and weans her child, then hands the child to a Muslim, has a pit dug for her up to her chest, and commands the people to stone her, during which Khalid b. al-Walid flings a stone at her head that splatters blood onto his face.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا كَانَ الرَّابِعَةَ حَفَرَ لَهُ حُفْرَةً ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِهِ فَرُجِمَ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَجَاءَتِ الْغَامِدِيَّةُ فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي قَدْ زَنَيْتُ فَطَهِّرْنِي ‏.‏ وَإِنَّهُ رَدَّهَا فَلَمَّا كَانَ الْغَدُ قَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لِمَ تَرُدُّنِي لَعَلَّكَ أَنْ تَرُدَّنِي كَمَا رَدَدْتَ مَاعِزًا فَوَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لَحُبْلَى ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ إِمَّا لاَ فَاذْهَبِي حَتَّى تَلِدِي ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَلَمَّا وَلَدَتْ أَتَتْهُ بِالصَّبِيِّ فِي خِرْقَةٍ قَالَتْ هَذَا قَدْ وَلَدْتُهُ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ اذْهَبِي فَأَرْضِعِيهِ حَتَّى تَفْطِمِيهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَلَمَّا فَطَمَتْهُ أَتَتْهُ بِالصَّبِيِّ فِي يَدِهِ كِسْرَةُ خُبْزٍ فَقَالَتْ هَذَا يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ قَدْ فَطَمْتُهُ وَقَدْ أَكَلَ الطَّعَامَ ‏.‏ فَدَفَعَ الصَّبِيَّ إِلَى رَجُلٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِهَا فَحُفِرَ لَهَا إِلَى صَدْرِهَا وَأَمَرَ النَّاسَ فَرَجَمُوهَا فَيُقْبِلُ خَالِدُ بْنُ الْوَلِيدِ بِحَجَرٍ فَرَمَى رَأْسَهَا فَتَنَضَّحَ الدَّمُ عَلَى وَجْهِ خَالِدٍ فَسَبَّهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: When it was the fourth time, a ditch was dug for him and he (the Holy Prophet) pronounced judg- ment about him and he wis stoned. He (the narrator) said: There came to him (the Holy Prophet) a woman from Ghamid and said: Allah's Messenger, I have committed adultery, so purify me. He (the Holy Prophet) turned her away. On the following day she said: Allah's Messenger, Why do you turn me away? Perhaps, you turn me away as you turned away Ma'iz. By Allah, I have become pregnant. He said: Well, if you insist upon it, then go away until you give birth to (the child). When she was delivered she came with the child (wrapped) in a rag and said: Here is the child whom I have given birth to. He said: Go away and suckle him until you wean him. When she had weaned him, she came to him (the Holy Prophet) with the child who was holding a piece of bread in his hand. She said: Allah's Apostle, here is he as I have weaned him and he eats food. He (the Holy Prophet) entrusted the child to one of the Muslims and then pronounced punishment. And she was put in a ditch up to her chest and he commanded people and they stoned her. Khalid b Walid came forward with a stone which he flung at her head and there spurted blood on the face of Khalid and so he abused her.

muslim:4432.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's repeated dismissals of Ma'iz, his inquiries into Ma'iz's mental soundness, the postponement of the Ghamidiyyah woman's execution until she weaned her child, and his rebuke of Khalid b. al-Walid demonstrate that Islamic law prioritizes mercy, child welfare, and the avoidance of capital punishment. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that once Ma'iz's sanity was confirmed (`لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ وَلاَ بِعَقْلِهِ`), Muhammad dug a pit and ordered him stoned (`حَفَرَ لَهُ حُفْرَةً ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِهِ فَرُجِمَ`), and once the woman's child could eat bread (`فِي يَدِهِ كِسْرَةُ خُبْزٍ`), he took the weaned child from his mother, handed him to another man (`فَدَفَعَ الصَّبِيَّ إِلَى رَجُلٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ`), and ordered her buried up to her chest and stoned (`فَحُفِرَ لَهَا إِلَى صَدْرِهَا وَأَمَرَ النَّاسَ فَرَجَمُوهَا`). Furthermore, although both confessors pleaded for spiritual purification (`طَهِّرْنِي`) and Muhammad testified that the woman had made a sincere repentance (`لَقَدْ تَابَتْ تَوْبَةً`) before Khalid struck her head with a stone (`فَرَمَى رَأْسَهَا فَتَنَضَّحَ الدَّمُ عَلَى وَجْهِ خَالِدٍ`), he still enforced lethal stoning rather than granting forgiveness upon repentance.

muslim:4418.note: Umar ibn al-Khattab declares from Muhammad's pulpit that the Messenger of Allah executed married adulterers by stoning and that the Companions continued enforcing the punishment after him. He affirms that stoning to death remains a binding duty prescribed by Allah for any married man or woman when adultery is established by proof, pregnancy, or confession.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَرَجَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَرَجَمْنَا بَعْدَهُ فَأَخْشَى إِنْ طَالَ بِالنَّاسِ زَمَانٌ أَنْ يَقُولَ قَائِلٌ مَا نَجِدُ الرَّجْمَ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ فَيَضِلُّوا بِتَرْكِ فَرِيضَةٍ أَنْزَلَهَا اللَّهُ وَإِنَّ الرَّجْمَ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ عَلَى مَنْ زَنَى إِذَا أَحْصَنَ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ وَالنِّسَاءِ إِذَا قَامَتِ الْبَيِّنَةُ أَوْ كَانَ الْحَبَلُ أَوْ الاِعْتِرَافُ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) awarded the punishment of stoning to death (to the married adulterer and adulteress) and, after him, we also awarded the punishment of stoning, I am afraid that with the lapse of time, the people (may forget it) and may say: We do not find the punishment of stoning in the Book of Allah, and thus go astray by abandoning this duty prescribed by Allah. Stoning is a duty laid down in Allah's Book for married men and women who commit adultery when proof is established, or it there is pregnancy, or a confession

muslim:4418.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that stoning to death is absent from the Quran and serves only as a theoretical deterrent that cannot be enforced due to strict evidentiary standards. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah's Messenger carried out stoning (*fa-rajama Rasūlu Allāhi*) and the Companions stoned after him (*wa-rajamnā ba'dahu*), condemning anyone who abandons this obligation sent down by Allah (*bi-tarki farīḍatin anzalahā Allāh*). Moreover, Umar declares that stoning is a binding duty in the Book of Allah upon married men and women (*ḥaqqun 'alā man zanā idhā aḥṣana mina al-rijāli wa-al-nisā'*) whenever proof is established, or when there is pregnancy or a confession (*idhā qāmati al-bayyinatu aw kāna al-ḥabalu aw al-i'tirāf*).

muslim:4418.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:4418.note: Speaking from Muhammad's pulpit, Umar ibn al-Khattab testifies that the Verse of Stoning (*ayat al-rajm*) was sent down in the Book of Allah and that the Companions recited, memorized, and understood it ([Quran 15:9](quran://15/9)). He warns that with the lapse of time people will say they do not find stoning in the Book of Allah, going astray by abandoning an active obligation revealed by Allah whose recited text is absent from the written codex.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ وَهُوَ جَالِسٌ عَلَى مِنْبَرِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ بَعَثَ مُحَمَّدًا صلى الله عليه وسلم بِالْحَقِّ وَأَنْزَلَ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابَ فَكَانَ مِمَّا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةُ الرَّجْمِ قَرَأْنَاهَا وَوَعَيْنَاهَا وَعَقَلْنَاهَا فَرَجَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَرَجَمْنَا بَعْدَهُ فَأَخْشَى إِنْ طَالَ بِالنَّاسِ زَمَانٌ أَنْ يَقُولَ قَائِلٌ مَا نَجِدُ الرَّجْمَ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ فَيَضِلُّوا بِتَرْكِ فَرِيضَةٍ أَنْزَلَهَا اللَّهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: 'Umar b. Khattab sat on the pulpit of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said:Verily Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ) with truth and He sent down the Book upon him, and the verse of stoning was included in what was sent down to him. We recited it, retained it in our memory and understood it. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) awarded the punishment of stoning to death (to the married adulterer and adulteress) and, after him, we also awarded the punishment of stoning, I am afraid that with the lapse of time, the people (may forget it) and may say: We do not find the punishment of stoning in the Book of Allah, and thus go astray by abandoning this duty prescribed by Allah.

muslim:4418.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the Verse of Stoning represents an abrogation of recitation while its legal ruling remains in force (*naskh al-tilawah duna al-hukm*), claiming its removal from the written text does not compromise Quranic preservation ([Quran 15:9](quran://15/9)). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the verse of stoning was sent down upon Muhammad (*mimmā unzila 'alayhi āyatu al-rajm*) and that the Companions recited, memorized, and understood it (*qara'nāhā wa-wa'aynāhā wa-'aqalnāhā*), with no indication that its wording was ever revoked. Furthermore, Umar warns that future generations will go astray by saying 'We do not find stoning in the Book of Allah' (*mā najidu al-rajma fī kitābi Allāh*) and abandoning an obligation sent down by Allah (*farīḍatin anzalahā Allāh*), demonstrating that the absence of this verse from the written codex directly undermines scriptural completeness.

bukhari:4342.note: While serving as Muhammad's appointed governors in Yemen, Mu`adh bin Jabal refused to dismount from his mule until Abu Musa ordered the execution of a bound prisoner who had disbelieved after embracing Islam ([Quran 4:89](quran://4/89)). Parallel narrations identify the prisoner as a Jew who reverted to Judaism and record Mu`adh declaring his execution to be the judgment of Allah and His Messenger (bukhari:6923).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَإِذَا رَجُلٌ عِنْدَهُ قَدْ جُمِعَتْ يَدَاهُ إِلَى عُنُقِهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ مُعَاذٌ يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ قَيْسٍ، أَيَّمَ هَذَا قَالَ هَذَا رَجُلٌ كَفَرَ بَعْدَ إِسْلاَمِهِ‏.‏ قَالَ لاَ أَنْزِلُ حَتَّى يُقْتَلَ‏.‏ قَالَ إِنَّمَا جِيءَ بِهِ لِذَلِكَ فَانْزِلْ‏.‏ قَالَ مَا أَنْزِلُ حَتَّى يُقْتَلَ فَأَمَرَ بِهِ فَقُتِلَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Behold! There was a man tied with his hands behind his neck. Mu`adh said to Abu Musa, "O `Abdullah bin Qais! What is this?" Abu Musa replied. "This man has reverted to Heathenism after embracing Islam." Mu`adh said, "I will not dismount till he is killed." Abu Musa replied, "He has been brought for this purpose, so come down." Mu`adh said, "I will not dismount till he is killed." So Abu Musa ordered that he be killed, and he was killed.

bukhari:4342.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the death penalty for apostasy in early Islam applied only to armed political treason (*ḥirābah*), or cite Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* to claim that Abū Mūsā had already granted the prisoner a lengthy period to repent (*istitābah*) before Muʿādh arrived. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that his sole offense was religious conversion—*kafara baʿda islāmihi* (كَفَرَ بَعْدَ إِسْلاَمِهِ, "he disbelieved after his Islam")—which parallel *Ṣaḥīḥ* narrations (`bukhari:4341`, `bukhari:6923`) define simply as "a Jew who embraced Islam and then reverted to Judaism" (*kāna yahūdiyyan fa-aslama thumma tahawwada*), with zero mention of treason or rebellion. Furthermore, in those parallel accounts Muʿādh invokes "the judgment of Allah and His Messenger" (*qaḍāʾu Allāhi wa-rasūlihi*) to demand the bound prisoner's immediate execution before he would even dismount his mule (*lā anzilu ḥattā yuqtala*).

muslim:4428.note: After repeatedly turning Ma'iz b. Malik away and verifying his sanity with his tribe following his confession of sexual immorality, Muhammad commands his companions to stone him, leading them to pelt him with bones, clods, and potsherds before chasing him down as he flees and stoning him to death with boulders at al-Harrah. In an evening address afterward, Muhammad likens a man who stays behind from a military raid among the womenfolk and dependents to a rutting billy goat, vows to make a severe example of anyone brought to him for such an act, and neither seeks forgiveness for Ma'iz nor reviles him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَرَجَعَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَمَرَنَا أَنْ نَرْجُمَهُ - قَالَ - فَانْطَلَقْنَا بِهِ إِلَى بَقِيعِ الْغَرْقَدِ - قَالَ - فَمَا أَوْثَقْنَاهُ وَلاَ حَفَرْنَا لَهُ - قَالَ - فَرَمَيْنَاهُ بِالْعَظْمِ وَالْمَدَرِ وَالْخَزَفِ - قَالَ - فَاشْتَدَّ فَاشْتَدَدْنَا خَلْفَهُ حَتَّى أَتَى عُرْضَ الْحَرَّةِ فَانْتَصَبَ لَنَا فَرَمَيْنَاهُ بِجَلاَمِيدِ الْحَرَّةِ - يَعْنِي الْحِجَارَةَ - حَتَّى سَكَتَ - قَالَ - ثُمَّ قَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم خَطِيبًا مِنَ الْعَشِيِّ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ أَوَكُلَّمَا انْطَلَقْنَا غُزَاةً فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ تَخَلَّفَ رَجُلٌ فِي عِيَالِنَا لَهُ نَبِيبٌ كَنَبِيبِ التَّيْسِ عَلَىَّ أَنْ لاَ أُوتَى بِرَجُلٍ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ إِلاَّ نَكَّلْتُ بِهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَمَا اسْتَغْفَرَ لَهُ وَلاَ سَبَّهُ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He (Ma'iz) came back to Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) and he commanded us to stone him. We took him to the Baqi' al-Gharqad (the graveyard of Medina). We neither tied him nor dug any ditch for him. We attacked him with bones, with clods and pebbles. He ran away and we ran after him until he came upon the ston ground (al-Harra) and stopped there and we stoned him with heavy stones of the Harra until he became motionless (lie died). He (the Holy Prophet) then addressed (us) in the evening saying Whenever we set forth on an expedition in the cause of Allah, some one of those connected with us shrieked (under the pressure of sexual lust) as the bleating of a male goat. It is essential that if a person having committed such a deed is brought to me, I should punish him. He neither begged forgiveness for him nor cursed him

muslim:4428.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islamic stoning is designed to be nearly impossible to enforce and functions as a merciful purification, pointing out that Muhammad repeatedly turned Ma'iz away (faraddahu al-nabiyyu mirāran) and inquired into his mental state before accepting his confession. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad commanded his companions to stone him (fa-amaranā an narjumahu), after which they pelted him with bones, clods, and potsherds (bi-l-ʿaẓmi wa-l-madari wa-l-khazafi) and chased him down as he fled (fa-shtadda fa-shtadadnā khalfahu) until they killed him with the boulders of al-Harrah (bi-jalāmīdi al-ḥarrati). Rather than treating his execution as a merciful purification or reproaching the crowd for pursuing a fleeing penitent, Muhammad stood that evening to liken him to a rutting billy goat staying behind among the womenfolk during a military raid (takhallafa rajulun fī ʿiyālinā lahu nabībun ka-nabībi al-taysi), vowed to make an example of anyone brought to him for that deed (illā nakkaltu bihi), and refused to pray for his forgiveness (famā istaghfara lahu).

muslim:4718.note: After Muhammad dispatches Abu Musa and Mu'adh ibn Jabal to Yemen, Mu'adh arrives to find a bound prisoner whom Abu Musa identifies as a Jew who had converted to Islam and then reverted to Judaism, which Abu Musa calls 'the religion of evil' (din al-saw'). Mu'adh declares three times that he will not sit down until the man is killed in accordance with the judgment of Allah and His Messenger, whereupon Abu Musa orders his execution.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَبَعَثَهُ عَلَى الْيَمَنِ ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَهُ مُعَاذَ بْنَ جَبَلٍ فَلَمَّا قَدِمَ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ انْزِلْ وَأَلْقَى لَهُ وِسَادَةً وَإِذَا رَجُلٌ عِنْدَهُ مُوثَقٌ قَالَ مَا هَذَا قَالَ هَذَا كَانَ يَهُودِيًّا فَأَسْلَمَ ثُمَّ رَاجَعَ دِينَهُ دِينَ السَّوْءِ فَتَهَوَّدَ قَالَ لاَ أَجْلِسُ حَتَّى يُقْتَلَ قَضَاءُ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فَقَالَ اجْلِسْ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ لاَ أَجْلِسُ حَتَّى يُقْتَلَ قَضَاءُ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ ‏.‏ فَأَمَرَ بِهِ فَقُتِلَ
problematic_excerpt.english: He sent him to Yemen as governor. then he sent Mu'adh b. jabal in his wake (to help him in the discharge of duties). When Mu'adh reached the camp of Abu Musa, the latter (received him and) said: Please get yourself down; and he spread for him a mattress, while there was a man bound hand and foot as a prisoner. Mu'adh said: Who is this? Abu Musa said: He was a Jew. He embraced Islam. Then he reverted to his false religion and became a Jew. Mu'adh said: I won't sit until he is killed according to the decree of Allah and His Apostle (ﷺ) (in this case). Abu Musa said: Be seated. It will be done. He said: I won't sit unless he is killed in accordance with the decree of Allah and His Apostle (ﷺ). He repeated these words thrice. Then Abu Musa ordered him (to be killed) and he was kilied.

muslim:4718.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that [Quran 2:256](quran://2/256) guarantees freedom of religion and that capital punishment for apostasy in early Islam applied only to political treason or armed rebellion against the state. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the bound prisoner's sole offense was religious reversion (`كَانَ يَهُودِيًّا فَأَسْلَمَ ثُمَّ رَاجَعَ دِينَهُ دِينَ السَّوْءِ فَتَهَوَّدَ` — "he was a Jew who embraced Islam, then returned to his religion, the religion of evil, and became a Jew"), with no mention of treason or warfare. Furthermore, Mu'adh ibn Jabal thrice refuses even to sit down until the man is killed on the spot (`لاَ أَجْلِسُ حَتَّى يُقْتَلَ`), enforcing execution for leaving Islam as the binding "judgment of Allah and His Messenger" (`قَضَاءُ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ`, cf. `bukhari:4341`, `bukhari:6923`, `bukhari:7157`).

bukhari:6903.note: Ali ibn Abi Talib states that his written scroll (sahifah) contains the regulations on blood-money (al-'aql), the release of captives, and the ruling that a Muslim shall not be executed in retaliation (qisas) for killing a disbeliever (kafir). Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar affirm this as a prophetic legal decree that serves as the primary textual basis in majority Sunni jurisprudence (Shafi'i, Maliki, and Hanbali) for exempting Muslims from capital retaliation for killing non-Muslims.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَأَنْ لاَ يُقْتَلَ مُسْلِمٌ بِكَافِرٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: a Muslim should not be killed in Qisas (equality in punishment) for killing a disbeliever.

bukhari:6903.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, appealing to minority Hanafi legal reasoning, that the term kāfir (disbeliever) in this decree refers exclusively to a ḥarbī (a hostile enemy combatant at war with Islam) rather than a peaceful non-Muslim citizen (dhimmī). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "لاَ يُقْتَلَ مُسْلِمٌ بِكَافِرٍ" (lā yuqtalu muslimun bi-kāfirin), placing an indefinite noun (kāfirin) inside a negative clause, which by the rules of Classical Arabic grammar and legal theory (uṣūl al-fiqh) establishes absolute universality (ʿumūm) encompassing every non-Muslim without exception. As Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī demonstrates in Fatḥ al-Bārī, executing a Muslim for killing an active enemy combatant was never conceivable in Islamic law to begin with, proving that this constitutional decree specifically shields Muslims from retaliatory execution (qiṣāṣ) when they murder peaceful non-Muslim subjects—the formal ruling of the Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali schools.

bukhari:3017.note: Upon hearing that Ali burned a group of people, Ibn Abbas states that he would not have burned them—citing Muhammad's prohibition, "Do not punish with Allah's punishment"—but affirms he would have executed them in accordance with Muhammad's command, "Whoever changes his religion, kill him" ([Quran 4:89](quran://4/89)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ عَلِيًّا ـ رضى الله عنه ـ حَرَّقَ قَوْمًا، فَبَلَغَ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ فَقَالَ لَوْ كُنْتُ أَنَا لَمْ أُحَرِّقْهُمْ، لأَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ تُعَذِّبُوا بِعَذَابِ اللَّهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ وَلَقَتَلْتُهُمْ كَمَا قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ مَنْ بَدَّلَ دِينَهُ فَاقْتُلُوهُ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: `Ali burnt some people and this news reached Ibn `Abbas, who said, "Had I been in his place I would not have burnt them, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'Don't punish (anybody) with Allah's Punishment.' No doubt, I would have killed them, for the Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'If somebody (a Muslim) discards his religion, kill him

bukhari:3017.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's command only targeted political treason or armed rebellion (*ḥirābah*) against the Islamic state rather than peaceful freedom of conscience, or they deflect by emphasizing that Ibn Abbas condemned Ali's use of fire. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an unconditional religious decree—*man baddala dīnahu fa-qtulūhu* ("whoever changes his religion, kill him")—making the mere alteration of one's faith (*dīn*), with zero mention of military insurrection, the sole trigger for execution. Furthermore, the parallel narration in bukhari:6922 and Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* confirm that those executed were *zanādiqah* punished strictly for theological heresy rather than armed warfare, and Ibn Abbas objected only to the *method* of execution (burning instead of the sword) while affirming the classical Sunni consensus (*ijmāʿ*) that apostasy itself mandates death.

bukhari:6830.note: Umar ibn al-Khattab states that Muhammad and his successors carried out stoning to death (rajm), declaring it a binding obligation in Allah's Book upon any married man or woman who commits unlawful sexual intercourse when established by evidence, pregnancy, or confession.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَالرَّجْمُ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ عَلَى مَنْ زَنَى إِذَا أُحْصِنَ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ وَالنِّسَاءِ، إِذَا قَامَتِ الْبَيِّنَةُ أَوْ كَانَ الْحَبَلُ أَوْ الاِعْتِرَافُ
problematic_excerpt.english: And the punishment of the Rajam is to be inflicted to any married person (male & female), who commits illegal sexual intercourse, if the required evidence is available or there is conception or confession.

bukhari:6830.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the capital punishment of stoning (*rajm*) is merely a theoretical deterrent that is nearly impossible to carry out because Islamic law requires four eyewitnesses to the actual act of penetration. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that stoning is an obligatory right in Allah's Book (*فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ*) triggered not only by witnesses (*al-bayyinah*), but also by pregnancy (*أَوْ كَانَ الْحَبَلُ*) or confession (*أَوْ الاِعْتِرَافُ*). By making physical pregnancy standalone legal proof for execution alongside Umar's testimony that 'Allah's Messenger stoned and we stoned after him' (*رَجَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَرَجَمْنَا بَعْدَهُ*), the text proves this brutal penalty was actively enforced and placed women at unique lethal risk.

bukhari:6830.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:6830.note: Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab declares from the pulpit of Medina that the Verse of Stoning (Ayat al-Rajm) was revealed by Allah, recited, and memorized, warning that people might later abandon the obligation because they do not find the verse in Allah's Book. Classical Sunni commentators classify this missing passage as a revelation whose recitation was abrogated while its legal ruling remained in force (naskh al-tilawah duna al-hukm).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَكَانَ مِمَّا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ آيَةُ الرَّجْمِ، فَقَرَأْنَاهَا وَعَقَلْنَاهَا وَوَعَيْنَاهَا، رَجَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَرَجَمْنَا بَعْدَهُ، فَأَخْشَى إِنْ طَالَ بِالنَّاسِ زَمَانٌ أَنْ يَقُولَ قَائِلٌ وَاللَّهِ مَا نَجِدُ آيَةَ الرَّجْمِ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ، فَيَضِلُّوا بِتَرْكِ فَرِيضَةٍ أَنْزَلَهَا اللَّهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: and among what Allah revealed, was the Verse of the Rajam (the stoning of married person (male & female) who commits illegal sexual intercourse, and we did recite this Verse and understood and memorized it. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) did carry out the punishment of stoning and so did we after him. I am afraid that after a long time has passed, somebody will say, 'By Allah, we do not find the Verse of the Rajam in Allah's Book,' and thus they will go astray by leaving an obligation which Allah has revealed.

bukhari:6830.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the absence of the stoning verse from the Quran is a divinely intended case of *naskh al-tilāwah dūna al-ḥukm* (abrogation of the wording while the legal ruling remains), citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* to claim Allah purposely withdrew its recitation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Umar feared future generations would go astray precisely because they would say, 'By Allah, we do not find the Verse of Stoning in Allah's Book' (*mā najidu āyat al-rajm fī kitāb Allāh*), proving the omission created a theological crisis rather than a seamless divine abrogation. Furthermore, parallel narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 7171 and *Sunan Ibn Mājah* 1944) reveal that Umar wanted to write the verse back into the *muṣḥaf* with his own hands—refraining only out of fear of public accusation—while Aisha testified that the physical parchment containing the verse was eaten by a domestic animal after Muhammad's death.

bukhari:6830.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:6830.note: Umar ibn al-Khattab testifies that the Companions used to recite as part of Allah's Book a verse stating that claiming lineage to other than one's father is disbelief. Although absent from the canonical Quran, Sunni commentators classify this passage as a verse whose recitation was later abrogated (mansukh al-tilawah).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّا كُنَّا نَقْرَأُ فِيمَا نَقْرَأُ مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ أَنْ لاَ تَرْغَبُوا عَنْ آبَائِكُمْ، فَإِنَّهُ كُفْرٌ بِكُمْ أَنْ تَرْغَبُوا عَنْ آبَائِكُمْ
problematic_excerpt.english: And then we used to recite among the Verses in Allah's Book: 'O people! Do not claim to be the offspring of other than your fathers, as it is disbelief (unthankfulness) on your part that you claim to be the offspring of other than your real father.'

bukhari:6830.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the command not to disown one's fathers is merely a Prophetic Hadith (as recorded in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 6768) or another verse whose recitation was divinely abrogated (*mansūkh al-tilāwah*), as suggested in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *kunnā naqraʾu fīmā naqraʾu min kitāb Allāh* ('we used to recite among what we recited from the Book of Allah'), demonstrating that the senior Companions originally recited this passage as actual Quranic scripture before it disappeared from the written codex. Moreover, the narrator's recorded doubt over the exact wording of this lost verse (*فَإِنَّهُ كُفْرٌ بِكُمْ... أَوْ إِنَّ كُفْرًا بِكُمْ*) directly refutes the apologetic claim of flawless oral preservation among the Companions.

bukhari:6923.note: Upon arriving in Yemen after being sent by Muhammad, Mu'adh ibn Jabal finds a bound prisoner with Abu Musa who had converted from Judaism to Islam and then reverted to Judaism. Mu'adh refuses to sit down until the man is executed, declaring three times that this is the judgment of Allah and His Messenger, whereupon Abu Musa orders the man killed.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ يَهُودِيًّا فَأَسْلَمَ ثُمَّ تَهَوَّدَ‏.‏ قَالَ اجْلِسْ‏.‏ قَالَ لاَ أَجْلِسُ حَتَّى يُقْتَلَ‏.‏ قَضَاءُ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ‏.‏ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ، فَأَمَرَ بِهِ فَقُتِلَ
problematic_excerpt.english: He was a Jew and became a Muslim and then reverted back to Judaism." Then Abu Muisa requested Mu`adh to sit down but Mu`adh said, "I will not sit down till he has been killed. This is the judgment of Allah and His Apostle (for such cases) and repeated it thrice. Then Abu Musa ordered that the man be killed, and he was killed.

bukhari:6923.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that apostasy in early Islam was only a capital offense when coupled with violent political treason (ḥirābah) or armed rebellion against the state, claiming this prisoner must have been a seditious combatant. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that his sole offense was peaceful religious reversion—"he was a Jew, became a Muslim, and then reverted to Judaism" (kāna yahūdiyyan fa-aslama thumma tahawwada)—with zero mention of treason, espionage, or warfare. Furthermore, Mu'adh ibn Jabal thrice mandates his execution as "the judgment of Allah and His Messenger" (qaḍāʾu llāhi wa-rasūlihi), and both Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and the parallel narration in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 7157 confirm he was executed strictly for refusing to recant his return to Judaism after previously being pressured to repent (istitābah).

bukhari:6826.note: After confirming that a man who confessed four times to adultery is sane and married, Muhammad orders his companions to take him away and stone him to death. When the pain of the stones causes the man to flee, the companions overtake him at al-Harra and stone him to death—though in parallel narrations, Muhammad later remarks that they should have let him go when he fled since his conviction rested solely on self-confession.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏"‏ اذْهَبُوا فَارْجُمُوهُ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ شِهَابٍ أَخْبَرَنِي مَنْ، سَمِعَ جَابِرًا، قَالَ فَكُنْتُ فِيمَنْ رَجَمَهُ، فَرَجَمْنَاهُ بِالْمُصَلَّى، فَلَمَّا أَذْلَقَتْهُ الْحِجَارَةُ جَمَزَ حَتَّى أَدْرَكْنَاهُ بِالْحَرَّةِ فَرَجَمْنَاهُ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said (to the people), "Take him away and stone him to death." Ibn Shihab added, "I was told by one who heard Jabir, that Jabir said, 'I was among those who stoned the man, and we stoned him at the Musalla (`Id praying Place), and when the stones troubled him, he jumped quickly and ran away, but we overtook him at Al-Harra and stoned him to death (there)

bukhari:6826.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's repeated turning away (fa-aʿraḍa ʿanhu) and his remark in parallel narrations wishing the companions had let the fleeing man escape prove that Islam prioritizes mercy and makes stoning (rajm) nearly impossible to enforce. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that once the man confirmed he was sane and married (aḥṣanta), Muhammad himself issued the direct, binding lethal command, 'Idhhabū farjumūhu' ('Go and stone him'), personally ordering the brutal execution. When the piercing agony of the stones overwhelmed the victim (adhlaqathu al-ḥijārah—deceptively softened in English translations to 'the stones troubled him') and caused him to flee for his life, Muhammad's followers hunted him down at Al-Ḥarrah and bludgeoned him to death, enacting what Ibn Ḥajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī and unanimous Sunni consensus (ijmāʿ) affirm as an unrepealed, mandatory ḥadd punishment.

bukhari:2725.note: Swearing to judge by the Book of Allah (Kitab Allah), Muhammad ordered a ransom of a slave-girl and one hundred sheep returned, sentenced an unmarried laborer to one hundred lashes and one year of exile for adultery, and instructed Unais to stone the employer's wife to death if she confessed. After she confessed the next morning, she was stoned to death at Muhammad's command.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ لأَقْضِيَنَّ بَيْنَكُمَا بِكِتَابِ اللَّهِ، الْوَلِيدَةُ وَالْغَنَمُ رَدٌّ، وَعَلَى ابْنِكَ جَلْدُ مِائَةٍ وَتَغْرِيبُ عَامٍ، اغْدُ يَا أُنَيْسُ إِلَى امْرَأَةِ هَذَا فَإِنِ اعْتَرَفَتْ فَارْجُمْهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَغَدَا عَلَيْهَا فَاعْتَرَفَتْ، فَأَمَرَ بِهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَرُجِمَتْ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "By Him in Whose Hands my soul is, I will judge between you according to Allah's Laws. The slave-girl and the sheep are to be returned to you, your son is to receive a hundred lashes and be exiled for one year. You, Unais, go to the wife of this (man) and if she confesses her guilt, stone her to death." Unais went to that woman next morning and she confessed. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) ordered that she be stoned to death

bukhari:2725.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that stoning (*al-rajm*) is either foreign to the Quran—since Surah 24:2 prescribes only a hundred lashes—or a purely symbolic deterrent made practically impossible to enforce by the strict requirement of four eyewitnesses. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore an oath to judge 'by the Book of Allah' (`لأَقْضِيَنَّ بَيْنَكُمَا بِكِتَابِ اللَّهِ`) when sentencing the married woman to stoning (`فَأَمَرَ بِهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَرُجِمَتْ`), which Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) and Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) explain refers to Allah's binding legal decree and the abrogated Quranic 'verse of stoning' (*āyat al-rajm*). Moreover, far from treating the penalty as an unenforceable deterrent or requiring four witnesses, Muhammad proactively dispatched Unais (`اغْدُ يَا أُنَيْسُ إِلَى امْرَأَةِ هَذَا فَإِنِ اعْتَرَفَتْ فَارْجُمْهَا`) to interrogate the accused wife and executed her immediately upon her confession.

muslim:4377.note: Muhammad swears by Allah that the blood of a Muslim who testifies to the Islamic creed may be lawfully shed in three cases: one who abandons Islam and deserts the community, a married adulterer, and a life for a life.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَامَ فِينَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ وَالَّذِي لاَ إِلَهَ غَيْرُهُ لاَ يَحِلُّ دَمُ رَجُلٍ مُسْلِمٍ يَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَأَنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلاَّ ثَلاَثَةُ نَفَرٍ التَّارِكُ الإِسْلاَمَ الْمُفَارِقُ لِلْجَمَاعَةِ أَوِ الْجَمَاعَةَ - شَكَّ فِيهِ أَحْمَدُ - وَالثَّيِّبُ الزَّانِي وَالنَّفْسُ بِالنَّفْسِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) stood up and said: By Him besides Whom there is no god but He, the blood of a Muslim who bears the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and I am His Messenger, may be lawfully shed only in case of three persons: the one who abandons Islam, and deserts the community [Ahmad, one of the narrators, is doubtful whether the Prophet (ﷺ) used the word li'l-jama'ah or al-jama'ah), and the married adulterer, and life for life

muslim:4377.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase "deserts the community" (al-mufāriq li'l-jamā'ah) restricts capital punishment for apostasy to wartime political treason or armed rebellion against the state rather than peaceful departure from the faith. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that lawful bloodshed applies to "the one who abandons Islam, parting from the community" (al-tārik al-islām al-mufāriq li'l-jamā'ah), defining separation from the Muslim collective as the natural consequence of leaving the religion itself without any mention of armed warfare. Furthermore, grouping the abandonment of Islam alongside domestic capital offenses like married adultery (wa al-thayyib al-zānī) and murder (wa al-nafs bi'l-nafs)—as reinforced in muslim:4375 and bukhari:6878—establishes that renouncing the faith is a standalone capital crime.

bukhari:5270.note: After a man from Bani Aslam testified against himself four times to adultery and confirmed that he was sane and married, Muhammad ordered him to be stoned at the praying place; when the sharp edges of the stones struck him, he fled, but was caught at al-Harrah and killed.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَجُلاً، مِنْ أَسْلَمَ أَتَى النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهْوَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ فَقَالَ إِنَّهُ قَدْ زَنَى‏.‏ فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ، فَتَنَحَّى لِشِقِّهِ الَّذِي أَعْرَضَ فَشَهِدَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ أَرْبَعَ شَهَادَاتٍ، فَدَعَاهُ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ هَلْ بِكَ جُنُونٌ هَلْ أُحْصِنْتَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ نَعَمْ‏.‏ فَأَمَرَ بِهِ أَنْ يُرْجَمَ بِالْمُصَلَّى، فَلَمَّا أَذْلَقَتْهُ الْحِجَارَةُ جَمَزَ حَتَّى أُدْرِكَ بِالْحَرَّةِ فَقُتِلَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A man from the tribe of Bani Aslam came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was in the mosque and said, "I have committed illegal sexual intercourse." The Prophet (ﷺ) turned his face to the other side. The man turned towards the side towards which the Prophet (ﷺ) had turned his face, and gave four witnesses against himself. On that the Prophet (ﷺ) called him and said, "Are you insane?" (He added), "Are you married?" The man said, 'Yes." On that the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered him to be stoned to the death in the Musalla (a praying place). When the stones hit him with their sharp edges and he fled, but he was caught at Al- Harra and then killed

bukhari:5270.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad sought every avenue to avert the punishment—turning his face away four times (`فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ`), probing for insanity (`هَلْ بِكَ جُنُونٌ`), and later asking his companions in parallel narrations (`bukhari:6820`) why they did not let the man go when he fled—to prove that Islamic law prioritizes mercy and treats fleeing as a valid retraction of confession. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that once the man confirmed he was sane and married (`هَلْ أُحْصِنْتَ`), Muhammad himself issued the lethal execution order (`فَأَمَرَ بِهِ أَنْ يُرْجَمَ بِالْمُصَلَّى` — 'so he ordered him to be stoned at the praying place'), directly initiating the pelting with sharp stones (`أَذْلَقَتْهُ الْحِجَارَةُ`) that caused the man to flee in agony before being hunted down and killed (`فَقُتِلَ`). Furthermore, as Ibn Ḥajar documents in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, Muhammad neither penalized the companions for completing the killing nor abrogated the penalty, and all four Sunni *madhhabs* unanimously codified stoning to death (*al-rajm*) as permanent divine law.

muslim:4431.note: Muhammad orders both Ma'iz b. Malik and a woman from the tribe of Ghamid stoned to death (*rajm*) after they confess to adultery, executing the woman once she gives birth and an Ansari volunteers to take responsibility for nursing her newborn infant.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَزَنَيْتَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ فَأَمَرَ بِهِ فَرُجِمَ فَكَانَ النَّاسُ فِيهِ فِرْقَتَيْنِ قَائِلٌ يَقُولُ لَقَدْ هَلَكَ لَقَدْ أَحَاطَتْ بِهِ خَطِيئَتُهُ وَقَائِلٌ يَقُولُ مَا تَوْبَةٌ أَفْضَلَ مِنْ تَوْبَةِ مَاعِزٍ أَنَّهُ جَاءَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَوَضَعَ يَدَهُ فِي يَدِهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ اقْتُلْنِي بِالْحِجَارَةِ - قَالَ - فَلَبِثُوا بِذَلِكَ يَوْمَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلاَثَةً ثُمَّ جَاءَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُمْ جُلُوسٌ فَسَلَّمَ ثُمَّ جَلَسَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ اسْتَغْفِرُوا لِمَاعِزِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَالُوا غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لِمَاعِزِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ ‏.‏ - قَالَ - فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لَقَدْ تَابَ تَوْبَةً لَوْ قُسِمَتْ بَيْنَ أُمَّةٍ لَوَسِعَتْهُمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ ثُمَّ جَاءَتْهُ امْرَأَةٌ مِنْ غَامِدٍ مِنَ الأَزْدِ فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ طَهِّرْنِي ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ وَيْحَكِ ارْجِعِي فَاسْتَغْفِرِي اللَّهَ وَتُوبِي إِلَيْهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ أَرَاكَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تُرَدِّدَنِي كَمَا رَدَّدْتَ مَاعِزَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ وَمَا ذَاكِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ إِنَّهَا حُبْلَى مِنَ الزِّنَا ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ آنْتِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهَا ‏"‏ حَتَّى تَضَعِي مَا فِي بَطْنِكِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَكَفَلَهَا رَجُلٌ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ حَتَّى وَضَعَتْ قَالَ فَأَتَى النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ قَدْ وَضَعَتِ الْغَامِدِيَّةُ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِذًا لاَ نَرْجُمَهَا وَنَدَعَ وَلَدَهَا صَغِيرًا لَيْسَ لَهُ مَنْ يُرْضِعُهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَامَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ فَقَالَ إِلَىَّ رَضَاعُهُ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَرَجَمَهَا ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Thereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Have you committed adultery? He said: Yes. He made pronouncement about him and he was stoned to death. The people had been (divided) into two groups about him (Ma'iz). One of them said: He has been undone for his sins had encompassed him, whereas another said: There is no repentance more excellent than the repentance of Ma'iz, for he came to Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) and placing his hand in his (in the Holy Prophet's) hand said: Kill me with stones. (This controversy about Ma'iz) remained for two or three days. Then came Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) to them (his Companions) as they were sitting.
