However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore to judge by the 'Book of Allah' (*bi-kitābi llāh* — بِكِتَابِ اللَّهِ)—which Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) and Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) confirm refers to Allah's legal decree and the abrogated Quranic stoning verse (*Āyat al-Rajm*, cf. bukhari:6830)—and proactively dispatched Unays to interrogate the accused woman with an immediate execution order: 'Go in the morning to the wife of this man and ask her, and if she confesses, stone her' (*ughdu 'alā mra'ati hādhā fa-salhā, fa-in i'tarafat fa-rjumhā* — اغْدُ عَلَى امْرَأَةِ هَذَا فَسَلْهَا، فَإِنِ اعْتَرَفَتْ فَارْجُمْهَا). Far from discouraging her confession or requiring four separate court appearances, the text records her summary execution by a single delegated investigator upon a single confession: 'She confessed and he stoned her to death' (*fa-'tarafat fa-rajamahā* — فَاعْتَرَفَتْ فَرَجَمَهَا).

bukhari:6860.note: Swearing to judge 'by the Book of Allah' (*bi-kitāb Allāh*), Muhammad sentences an unmarried male laborer to one hundred lashes and a year's exile for fornication, and orders Unays to question the married woman involved and stone her to death if she confesses—which she does, and he stones her to death. While the one hundred lashes appear in [Surah 24:2](quran://24/2), neither the one-year exile nor the stoning penalty is found in the extant Quran.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَيَا أُنَيْسُ اغْدُ عَلَى امْرَأَةِ هَذَا فَسَلْهَا، فَإِنِ اعْتَرَفَتْ فَارْجُمْهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَاعْتَرَفَتْ فَرَجَمَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: And O Unais! Go in the morning to the wife of this man and ask her, and if she confesses, stone her to death." She confessed and he stoned her to death

bukhari:6860.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that stoning (al-rajm) is absent from the Quran—which prescribes only flogging in Surah 24:2—or that Islamic jurisprudence renders the penalty virtually impossible to enforce by requiring four eyewitnesses and discouraging self-incrimination. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore to judge "by the Book of Allah" (bi-Kitāb Allāh) and proactively dispatched Unais to interrogate the accused woman (ughdu ʿalā imraʾati hādhā fa-salhā), ordering her immediate execution upon a single confession (fa-in iʿtarafat fa-rjumhā). As Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī confirms in Fatḥ al-Bārī, this narration proves that the lethal ruling of the abrogated stoning verse (āyat al-rajm) remains legally binding in Sunni law and that the state actively investigates and executes based on a single confession.

bukhari:3635.note: After appealing to the physical Torah scroll brought by the Medinan Jews to verify its stoning verse, Muhammad ordered a Jewish man and woman who had committed unlawful sexual intercourse to be stoned to death. The narrator, 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, reports watching the man bend over the woman to shield her from the stones during the execution.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالُوا صَدَقَ يَا مُحَمَّدُ، فِيهَا آيَةُ الرَّجْمِ‏.‏ فَأَمَرَ بِهِمَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَرُجِمَا‏.‏ قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ فَرَأَيْتُ الرَّجُلَ يَجْنَأُ عَلَى الْمَرْأَةِ يَقِيهَا الْحِجَارَةَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: They said, "Muhammad has told the truth; the Torah has the Verse of Rajm. The Prophet (ﷺ) then gave the order that both of them should be stoned to death. (`Abdullah bin `Umar said, "I saw the man leaning over the woman to shelter her from the stones)

bukhari:3635.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was merely arbitrating a dispute for the Jewish community according to their own Mosaic Law rather than imposing an Islamic decree. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad personally issued the lethal command (`فَأَمَرَ بِهِمَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ... فَرُجِمَا`), and in the parallel Sahih narration (`muslim:4437`) he declares, "O Allah, I am the first to revive Your command when they had made it dead," enshrining stoning (`ar-rajm`) as binding Islamic law. Furthermore, by authenticating the physical 7th-century AD Torah scroll unrolled before him (`فَأَتَوْا بِالتَّوْرَاةِ فَنَشَرُوهَا`, cf. Q. 5:43), the narration simultaneously refutes the Islamic claim of biblical corruption (*taḥrīf*) and exposes Muhammad's regression from Christ's mercy to brutal execution.

bukhari:4556.note: After verifying the stoning verse in the physical Torah brought by the Jews, Muhammad ordered a Jewish man and woman who had committed adultery to be stoned to death near his mosque, while the man bent over the woman to shield her from the stones.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا ذَلِكَ قَالُوا هِيَ آيَةُ الرَّجْمِ‏.‏ فَأَمَرَ بِهِمَا فَرُجِمَا قَرِيبًا مِنْ حَيْثُ مَوْضِعُ الْجَنَائِزِ عِنْدَ الْمَسْجِدِ، فَرَأَيْتُ صَاحِبَهَا يَجْنَأُ عَلَيْهَا يَقِيهَا الْحِجَارَةَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: So when the Jews saw that Verse, they said, "This is the Verse of Ar-Rajm." So the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered the two adulterers to be stoned to death, and they were stoned to death near the place where biers used to be placed near the Mosque. I saw her companion (i.e. the adulterer) bowing over her so as to protect her from the stones

bukhari:4556.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was merely granting the Jewish community judicial autonomy by applying their own Mosaic law from the Torah rather than enforcing an Islamic punishment. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Jews sought to apply a non-lethal penalty (`نُحَمِّمُهُمَا وَنَضْرِبُهُمَا`—blackening their faces and flogging them), which Muhammad actively overruled before personally commanding their lethal stoning (`فَأَمَرَ بِهِمَا فَرُجِمَا`) beside his mosque as the man desperately shielded the woman with his body (`يَجْنَأُ عَلَيْهَا يَقِيهَا الْحِجَارَةَ`). Furthermore, both Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) and Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) confirm that Muhammad enforced this execution because *al-rajm* is the permanent, un-abrogated Islamic *ḥadd* penalty for married adulterers (`bukhari:6829`), while his verification of their physical Torah scroll (`فَأْتُوا بِالتَّوْرَاةِ`) in the 7th century AD simultaneously refutes modern Islamic claims that the Hebrew Bible had been textually corrupted.

muslim:4421.note: Continuing the account in muslim:4420 where Muhammad ordered the stoning (*rajm*) of an unnamed married Muslim who confessed four times to adultery, Jabir bin Abdullah recounts participating in the execution at the prayer ground (*al-Muṣallā*). When the pain of the stones caused the man to flee, the companions caught him in the lava field (*al-Ḥarrah*) and stoned him to death.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَكُنْتُ فِيمَنْ رَجَمَهُ فَرَجَمْنَاهُ بِالْمُصَلَّى فَلَمَّا أَذْلَقَتْهُ الْحِجَارَةُ هَرَبَ فَأَدْرَكْنَاهُ بِالْحَرَّةِ فَرَجَمْنَاهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: I was one of those who stoned him. We stoned him at the place of prayer (either that of 'Id or a funeral). When the stones hurt him, he ran away. We caught him in the Harra and stoned him (to death)

muslim:4421.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that stoning (*rajm*) was only applied to a willing penitent, or that the unnamed transmitter between Ibn Shihab and Jabir bin Abdullah in `muslim:4421` weakens the report. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that as soon as the stones hurt the man he fled (`فَلَمَّا أَذْلَقَتْهُ الْحِجَارَةُ هَرَبَ`), and Jabir and the others caught him in the Harra and stoned him to death (`فَأَدْرَكْنَاهُ بِالْحَرَّةِ فَرَجَمْنَاهُ`), an event corroborated in `bukhari:6820` and `muslim:4424`. Rather than a consensual punishment at the prayer ground (`بِالْمُصَلَّى`), the text records an execution from which the condemned man tried to escape once the stones injured him.

bukhari:6827.note: Swearing to judge by the 'Book of Allah' (*Kitāb Allāh*), Muhammad sentences an unmarried laborer to one hundred lashes and a one-year exile for fornication, and orders Unais to stone a married woman to death upon her confession, which Unais executes. Although neither stoning nor exile appears in the extant Quran ([Surah 24:2](quran://24/2)), Sunni jurisprudence upholds this ruling alongside the abrogated recitation of the Verse of Stoning (bukhari:6829) as the normative *ḥadd* penalty for married adulterers.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَاغْدُ يَا أُنَيْسُ عَلَى امْرَأَةِ هَذَا، فَإِنِ اعْتَرَفَتْ فَارْجُمْهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَغَدَا عَلَيْهَا فَاعْتَرَفَتْ فَرَجَمَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: O Unais! Go to the wife of this man, and if she confesses, then stone her to death." Unais went to her and she confessed. He then stoned her to death

bukhari:6827.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that capital stoning (rajm) is either absent from the Quran (Surah 24:2) or functions merely as a theoretical deterrent requiring four eyewitnesses or four separate court confessions, while citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī to claim the harsher penalty applied solely because the woman was married (muḥṣan). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore to judge 'by the Book of Allah' (لأَقْضِيَنَّ بَيْنَكُمَا بِكِتَابِ اللَّهِ) before ordering both exile and stoning—exposing the missing Quranic stoning verse (āyat al-rajm attested in bukhari:6829 and muslim:4418)—and instructed Unais, 'if she confesses, then stone her to death' (فَإِنِ اعْتَرَفَتْ فَارْجُمْهَا). Far from being an unreachable judicial deterrent requiring four court appearances, Unais went to her privately, took a single confession, and summarily stoned her to death on the spot (فَغَدَا عَلَيْهَا فَاعْتَرَفَتْ فَرَجَمَهَا).

bukhari:6828.note: Swearing to judge by the Book of Allah (bi-Kitabi Allah), Muhammad sentences an unmarried male laborer to one hundred lashes and one year's exile for committing adultery with his employer's wife, and orders Unais to stone the married woman to death if she confesses. Upon her confession, Unais stones her to death.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَاغْدُ يَا أُنَيْسُ عَلَى امْرَأَةِ هَذَا، فَإِنِ اعْتَرَفَتْ فَارْجُمْهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَغَدَا عَلَيْهَا فَاعْتَرَفَتْ فَرَجَمَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: O Unais! Go to the wife of this man, and if she confesses, then stone her to death." Unais went to her and she confessed. He then stoned her to death

bukhari:6828.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that stoning (rajm) is either un-Quranic or a purely theoretical deterrent that is virtually impossible to enforce without four eyewitnesses or four separate courtroom confessions that a judge actively discourages. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore an oath to judge by the "Book of Allah" (lāqḍiyanna baynakumā bi-kitābi Allāh) before ordering her execution—pointing directly to the abrogated Quranic "stoning verse" preserved in bukhari:6829—and he never summoned the woman to court or urged her to retract. Instead, he dispatched a single deputy with the summary command, "if she confesses, stone her" (fa-in iʿtarafat fa-rjumhā), and as Ibn Hajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) and Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) observe on this narration, Unais stoned her to death (fa-rajamahā) immediately upon a single admission without requiring a four-fold confession.

muslim:4425.note: After turning away a man who had committed adultery twice—or four times according to Sa'id b. Jubair—Muhammad orders him stoned to death (*fa-rujima*) and warns that he will make a deterrent example (*nakālan*) of any man who lags behind from military campaigns bleating like a rutting billy-goat (*yanibbu nabīb al-tays*) and giving one of the women (*iḥdāhunna*, rendered in the English translation as '(goats'') a small cup of milk (*al-kuthbah*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُتِيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِرَجُلٍ قَصِيرٍ أَشْعَثَ ذِي عَضَلاَتٍ عَلَيْهِ إِزَارٌ وَقَدْ زَنَى فَرَدَّهُ مَرَّتَيْنِ ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِهِ فَرُجِمَ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ كُلَّمَا نَفَرْنَا غَازِينَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ تَخَلَّفَ أَحَدُكُمْ يَنِبُّ نَبِيبَ التَّيْسِ يَمْنَحُ إِحْدَاهُنَّ الْكُثْبَةَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يُمْكِنِّي مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ إِلاَّ جَعَلْتُهُ نَكَالاً ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: there was brought to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) a short-statured person with thick uncombed hair, muscular body, having a mantle around him and he had committed adultery. He turned him away twice and then made pronouncement about him and he was stoned. Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said:We set out for Jihad in the cause of Allah and one of you lagged behind and shrieked like the bleating of a male goat and one of then (goats' gave a small quantity of milk. In case Allah gives me power over one of them, I will punish him (in such a way that it may have a deterrent effect upon others).

muslim:4425.literal_translation: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was brought a short, disheveled, muscular man wearing a waist-wrapper who had committed adultery. He turned him away twice and then ordered him to be stoned. Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: 'Whenever we set out campaigning in the way of Allah, one of you stays behind rutting like the mating cry of a billy-goat, giving one of them [the women] a small cup of milk [for illicit sex]. Allah will not give me power over any one of them except that I will make him a deterrent example!'

translation_issue.arabic_term: يَنِبُّ نَبِيبَ التَّيْسِ يَمْنَحُ إِحْدَاهُنَّ الْكُثْبَةَ
translation_issue.published_rendering: shrieked like the bleating of a male goat and one of then (goats' gave a small quantity of milk
translation_issue.literal_meaning: making the mating cry of a billy-goat, giving one of them [the women] a small cupful of milk
translation_issue.explanation: The translator obscures the masculine verb 'yamnaḥu' ('he gives') and the feminine object pronoun 'iḥdāhunna' ('one of them [the women]') by interpolating '(goats'' so the clause reads as if a goat gave milk rather than a man giving a woman milk for illicit relations.

muslim:4425.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad sought to avoid capital punishment by turning the confessing man away twice—or four times in Sa'id b. Jubair's narration—before reluctantly enforcing the law to protect the households of soldiers away on Jihad. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad ordered him stoned (*fa-amara bihi fa-rujima*) and then vowed that whenever Allah grants him power over any man who stays behind from campaigning (*ghāzīn fī sabīl Allāh*) rutting like a billy-goat (*yanibbu nabīb al-tays*) and giving one of the women a small cup of milk (*yamnaḥu iḥdāhunna al-kuthbah*), he will make him a deterrent example (*illā jaʿaltuhu nakālan*). Moreover, the published English rendering conceals this rebuke by inserting '(goats'' to mistranslate the feminine pronoun *iḥdāhunna* ('one of the women'), hiding the admission that women in the community were trading adultery for a small cup of milk while the men were at war.

bukhari:6835.note: Swearing to judge according to the Book of Allah, Muhammad sentences an unmarried male laborer to one hundred lashes and a year of exile for illicit sexual relations, and commands Unais to stone the married woman to death. While this chain via Ibn Abi Dhi'b omits the confession requirement that the English translator supplies in parentheses from parallel narrations (bukhari:2724, bukhari:6827), neither stoning nor a one-year exile appears in the canonical text of the Quran ([Quran 24:2](quran://24/2)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَعَلَى ابْنِكَ جَلْدُ مِائَةٍ وَتَغْرِيبُ عَامٍ، وَأَمَّا أَنْتَ يَا أُنَيْسُ فَاغْدُ عَلَى امْرَأَةِ هَذَا فَارْجُمْهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَغَدَا أُنَيْسٌ فَرَجَمَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: your son will be flogged one-hundred stripes and be exiled for one year. And you, O Unais! Go to the wife of this man (and if she confesses), stone her to death." So Unais went in the morning and stoned her to death (after she had confessed)

bukhari:6835.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the disparate punishment reflects marital status (*iḥṣān*) rather than gender inequality—flogging the unmarried son (*bikr*) while stoning the married woman (*muḥṣanah*)—and appeal to Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and parallel narrations (e.g., *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 2724) to claim her execution required a voluntary confession. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an unconditional imperative to execute her (`فَاغْدُ عَلَى امْرَأَةِ هَذَا فَارْجُمْهَا` — 'go to the wife of this man and stone her') with zero mention of any confession, proving that the English translator fabricated the parenthetical clause '(and if she confesses)' to sanitize the narration. Moreover, Muhammad swears to judge strictly 'by the Book of Allah' (`لأَقْضِيَنَّ بَيْنَكُمَا بِكِتَابِ اللَّهِ`) yet pronounces stoning (*rajm*) and year-long exile (*taghrīb*)—rulings completely absent from the extant Quran (Surah 24:2 mandates only 100 lashes), which forces the apologist to concede both the textual loss of the Quranic 'stoning verse' (*āyat al-rajm*, *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 6829) and the binding brutality of prophetic stoning.

bukhari:6836.note: Swearing to judge by the Book of Allah (*Kitab Allah*), Muhammad sentences a laborer to one hundred lashes and a year's exile for illicit sexual intercourse with his employer's wife, while commanding Unais to stone the woman to death. Although the Arabic of this specific narration omits the translator's parenthetical condition 'if she confesses,' fuller parallel reports of the same case (bukhari:2724, bukhari:6827) include that stipulation in the Arabic text.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَعَلَى ابْنِكَ جَلْدُ مِائَةٍ وَتَغْرِيبُ عَامٍ، وَأَمَّا أَنْتَ يَا أُنَيْسُ فَاغْدُ عَلَى امْرَأَةِ هَذَا فَارْجُمْهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَغَدَا أُنَيْسٌ فَرَجَمَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: your son will be flogged one-hundred stripes and be exiled for one year. And you, O Unais! Go to the wife of this man (and if she confesses), stone her to death." So Unais went in the morning and stoned her to death (after she had confessed)

bukhari:6836.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islamic ḥadd punishments like stoning are nearly impossible to enforce due to the four-witness requirement, or claim—citing Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and parallel narration bukhari:6835—that the woman was only executed after a voluntary confession while Quran 24:2 prescribes only flogging. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore to judge 'by the Book of Allah' (la-aqḍiyanna baynakumā bi-kitābi llāhi) and commanded Unais unconditionally in this chain, 'Go to the wife of this man and stone her' (fa-ghdu ʿalā mraʾati hādhā fa-rjumhā)—exposing the English translator's parenthetical insertion of '(and if she confesses)' as entirely absent from the Arabic of this narration. Even when harmonized with bukhari:6835, the ruling proves that lethal stoning (al-rajm) was actively enforced on the spot as 'Allah's Book' without four witnesses, simply by dispatching a single companion to question and execute the married woman while the unmarried man received lashes and exile.

bukhari:6843.note: Swearing to judge by the Book of Allah, Muhammad annuls a private ransom of a hundred sheep and a slave girl, sentences the unmarried male laborer to 100 lashes and one year of exile for illicit sexual intercourse, and orders Unais al-Aslami to stone the married woman to death upon her confession.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَجَلَدَ ابْنَهُ مِائَةً وَغَرَّبَهُ عَامًا، وَأَمَرَ أُنَيْسًا الأَسْلَمِيَّ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ امْرَأَةَ الآخَرِ، فَإِنِ اعْتَرَفَتْ فَارْجُمْهَا، فَاعْتَرَفَتْ فَرَجَمَهَا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) had the man's son flogged one hundred stripes and exiled for one year, and ordered Unais Al-Aslami to go to the wife of the other man, and if she confessed, stone her to death. She confessed and was stoned to death

bukhari:6843.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue either that stoning (rajm) is absent from the Quran (Surah 24:2) and therefore un-Islamic, or—citing classical commentators like Ibn Hajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī—that ḥadd executions functioned merely as theoretical deterrents due to strict four-witness requirements and judicial encouragement to retract confessions. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore to judge by the 'Book of Allah' (lā-aqḍiyanna baynakumā bi-Kitāb Allāh)—which classical jurists tie to the abrogated Quranic stoning verse (āyat al-rajm, cf. bukhari:6830)—and ordered Unays, 'if she confesses, stone her' (fa-in iʿtarafat fa-rjumhā), resulting in her immediate execution (fa-rajamahā). Far from treating stoning as a theoretical deterrent or encouraging retraction, Muhammad proactively dispatched an interrogator to secure the married woman's confession and stone her to death on the spot.

muslim:4416.note: Following an episode of revelation, Muhammad declares that Allah has ordained the punishment for unlawful sexual intercourse: married adulterers must receive one hundred lashes followed by stoning to death, while unmarried offenders receive one hundred lashes and one year of exile. Neighboring reports such as muslim:4418 record Umar affirming that Muhammad enforced this capital penalty of stoning to death based on a revealed stoning verse.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏ "‏ خُذُوا عَنِّي فَقَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَهُنَّ سَبِيلاً الثَّيِّبُ بِالثَّيِّبِ وَالْبِكْرُ بِالْبِكْرِ الثَّيِّبُ جَلْدُ مِائَةٍ ثُمَّ رَجْمٌ بِالْحِجَارَةِ وَالْبِكْرُ جَلْدُ مِائَةٍ ثُمَّ نَفْىُ سَنَةٍ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: he said:Take from me. Verily Allah has ordained a way for them (the women who commit fornication),: (When) a married man (commits adultery) with a married woman, and an unmarried male with an unmarried woman, then in case of married (persons) there is (a punishment) of one hundred lashes and then stoning (to death). And in case of unmarried persons, (the punishment) is one hundred lashes and exile for one year

muslim:4416.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that stoning to death is not a divinely revealed Islamic punishment or that it was merely a customary practice preceding the Quranic legal rulings. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that revelation descended directly upon Muhammad (`أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ`), causing his face to change complexion (`وَتَرَبَّدَ لَهُ وَجْهُهُ`), before he announced, 'Take from me, for Allah has ordained a way for them' (`خُذُوا عَنِّي فَقَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَهُنَّ سَبِيلاً`) as the ordained penalty promised in [Quran 4:15](quran://4/15). Grounded in this direct revelation and confirmed in parallel reports (`muslim:4417`, `muslim:4418`, `bukhari:6829`), Muhammad decrees one hundred lashes followed by stoning with stones (`جَلْدُ مِائَةٍ ثُمَّ رَجْمٌ بِالْحِجَارَةِ`) for married adulterers and one hundred lashes with a one-year exile (`جَلْدُ مِائَةٍ ثُمَّ نَفْىُ سَنَةٍ`) for unmarried fornicators.

bukhari:6841.note: After verifying the ruling of stoning (rajm) from a physical copy of the Torah brought by the Jews of Medina, Muhammad ordered a Jewish man and woman guilty of unlawful sexual intercourse (zina) to be stoned to death. The narrator, `Abdullah ibn `Umar, witnessed the execution and reported seeing the man bending over the woman to shield her from the stones.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَمَرَ بِهِمَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَرُجِمَا، فَرَأَيْتُ الرَّجُلَ يَحْنِي عَلَى الْمَرْأَةِ يَقِيهَا الْحِجَارَةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) ordered that the two persons (guilty of illegal sexual intercourse) be stoned to death, and so they were stoned, and I saw the man bending over the woman so as to protect her from the stones

bukhari:6841.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was merely arbitrating for the Jewish community according to their own Mosaic law in the Torah rather than instituting an Islamic punishment. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad personally commanded their execution (`فَأَمَرَ بِهِمَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ... فَرُجِمَا`), and as Ibn Ḥajar’s *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and parallel narrations (muslim:4440) confirm, he declared, 'O Allah, I am the first to revive Your command when they had made it dead'—enforcing brutal stoning (`الرَّجْمِ`) as binding Islamic law across his own community while inadvertently validating the textual integrity of the 7th-century AD Torah scroll opened before him.

muslim:4424.note: After Ma'iz bin Malik confesses four times to adultery and swears by Allah that he committed the act itself despite Muhammad asking 'Perhaps you [only kissed or embraced her]?', Muhammad has him stoned to death (*fa-rajamahu*). Muhammad then delivers a sermon declaring that whenever the Muslims set out campaigning in the way of Allah (*ghāzīn fī sabīlillāh*), a man stays behind making the mating cry of a rutting billy-goat (*nabīb al-tays*) while offering a small cup of milk (*al-kuthbah*), and vows by Allah to make an exemplary punishment (*la-unakkilannahu*) of anyone he catches doing so.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَشَهِدَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ أَرْبَعَ مَرَّاتٍ أَنَّهُ زَنَى فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَلَعَلَّكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ لاَ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ قَدْ زَنَى الأَخِرُ - قَالَ - فَرَجَمَهُ ثُمَّ خَطَبَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَلاَ كُلَّمَا نَفَرْنَا غَازِينَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ خَلَفَ أَحَدُهُمْ لَهُ نَبِيبٌ كَنَبِيبِ التَّيْسِ يَمْنَحُ أَحَدُهُمُ الْكُثْبَةَ أَمَا وَاللَّهِ إِنْ يُمْكِنِّي مِنْ أَحَدِهِمْ لأُنَكِّلَنَّهُ عَنْهُ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: He bore witness against his own self four times that he had committed adultery, whereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Perhaps (you kissed her or embraced her). He said: No. by God, one deviating (from the path of virtue) has committed adultery. He then got him stoned (to death), and then delivered the address: Behold, as we set out for Jihad in the cause of Allah, one of you lagged behind and shrieked like the bleating of a male goat, and gave a small quantity of milk. By Allah, in case I get hold of him, I shall certainly punish him

muslim:4424.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad sought to avoid capital punishment by suggesting Ma'iz bin Malik had merely kissed or embraced the woman (*fa-la'allaka*), claiming the legal process models restraint and dignified prophetic speech. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad stoned him to death (*fa-rajamahu*) and immediately delivered a sermon comparing men who stay behind from Jihad to solicit adultery for a small cup of milk (*al-kuthbah*) to the rutting cry of a billy-goat (*nabīb ka-nabīb al-tays*). Rather than discouraging punishment, Muhammad swore by Allah that if given power over any such offender, he would make an exemplary punishment of him (*la-unakkilannahu 'anhu*, cf. `muslim:4418`, `muslim:4425`).

bukhari:2420.note: Muhammad declared that he intended to order the congregational prayer to be established and then go to the homes of those who did not attend to burn their houses down over them (cf. bukhari:644, bukhari:657). Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar note that this warning targeted absentees or suspected hypocrites and remained unexecuted only because women and children not obligated to attend were inside the homes.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ أَنْ آمُرَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فَتُقَامَ ثُمَّ أُخَالِفَ إِلَى مَنَازِلِ قَوْمٍ لاَ يَشْهَدُونَ الصَّلاَةَ فَأُحَرِّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ
problematic_excerpt.english: No doubt, I intended to order somebody to pronounce the Iqama of the (compulsory congregational) prayer and then I would go to the houses of those who do not attend the prayer and burn their houses over them

bukhari:2420.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that Muhammad's statement was merely unexecuted hyperbolic deterrence (*zajr wa-tahdīd*) aimed at known hypocrites (*munāfiqūn*), which he refrained from carrying out only to spare innocent women and children inside the homes. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states his firm resolve (`لَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ`) to go to the homes of absentees and burn them down over their occupants (`فَأُحَرِّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ`), with parallel narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 644 and 657) adding that he planned to order men to gather bundles of firewood (`حَطَبٍ`) to incinerate them with fire (`بِالنَّارِ`). Furthermore, Ibn Ḥajar records in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* that classical Sunni jurists treated this threat not as empty rhetoric, but as binding legal proof that congregational prayer is strictly obligatory (*farḍ ʿayn*) and that the Islamic state is authorized to use violent coercion against those who fail to attend.

muslim:4427.note: Muhammad questions Ma'iz b. Malik about reports that he committed adultery with a family's slave-girl and, upon his fourfold confession, commands that he be stoned to death. Parallel report muslim:4428 notes that Ma'iz had initially confessed voluntarily and was turned away before his repeated testimony led to the execution order.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ لِمَاعِزِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ ‏"‏ أَحَقٌّ مَا بَلَغَنِي عَنْكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ وَمَا بَلَغَكَ عَنِّي قَالَ ‏"‏ بَلَغَنِي أَنَّكَ وَقَعْتَ بِجَارِيَةِ آلِ فُلاَنٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَشَهِدَ أَرْبَعَ شَهَادَاتٍ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِهِ فَرُجِمَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) said to Ma'iz b. Malik:Is it true what has reached me about you? He said: What has reached you about me? He said: It has reached me that you have committed (adultery) with the slave-girl of so and so? He said: Yes. He (the narrator) said: He testified four times. He (the Holy Prophet) then made pronouncement about him and he was stoned (to death)

muslim:4427.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that stoning in Islam is merely a theoretical deterrent requiring four eyewitnesses and that authorities do not interrogate individuals over reports of private sins. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad initiated the questioning of Ma'iz b. Malik over a report (`أَحَقٌّ مَا بَلَغَنِي عَنْكَ` — 'Is it true what has reached me about you?'), asked specifically whether he had committed adultery with a family's slave-girl (`بَلَغَنِي أَنَّكَ وَقَعْتَ بِجَارِيَةِ آلِ فُلاَنٍ`), and upon his fourfold confession (`فَشَهِدَ أَرْبَعَ شَهَادَاتٍ`) ordered him stoned to death (`ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِهِ فَرُجِمَ`).

muslim:4420.note: After a Muslim man in the mosque confesses four times to committing adultery despite Muhammad repeatedly turning away from him, Muhammad confirms that the man is sane and married, then commands that he be taken away and stoned. In the immediate continuation (muslim:4421), when the stones hurt the man and he tries to flee, the companions pursue him and stone him to death.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَتَى رَجُلٌ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُوَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ فَنَادَاهُ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي زَنَيْتُ ‏.‏ فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ فَتَنَحَّى تِلْقَاءَ وَجْهِهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي زَنَيْتُ ‏.‏ فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ حَتَّى ثَنَى ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِ أَرْبَعَ مَرَّاتٍ فَلَمَّا شَهِدَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ أَرْبَعَ شَهَادَاتٍ دَعَاهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَبِكَ جُنُونٌ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ لاَ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَهَلْ أَحْصَنْتَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ اذْهَبُوا بِهِ فَارْجُمُوهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: a person from amongst the Muslims came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) while he was in the mosque. He called him saying:Allah's Messenger. I have committed adultery. He (the Holy Prophet) turned away from him, He (again) came round facing him and said to him: Allah's Messenger, I have committed adultery. He (the Holy Prophet) turned away until he did that four times, and as he testified four times against his own self, Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) called him and said: Are you mad? He said: No. He (again) said: Are you married? He said: Yes. Thereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Take him and stone him

muslim:4420.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that stoning for adultery is merely a theoretical deterrent that is practically impossible to enforce, pointing to how Muhammad repeatedly turned away (فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ) when the man confessed in the mosque. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that once the man testified against himself four times (شَهِدَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ أَرْبَعَ شَهَادَاتٍ), denied madness (أَبِكَ جُنُونٌ), and confirmed that he was married (فَهَلْ أَحْصَنْتَ), Muhammad directly commanded, "Take him and stone him" (اذْهَبُوا بِهِ فَارْجُمُوهُ). Rather than treating capital punishment for adultery as an unenforceable formality, this report—alongside bukhari:6814, bukhari:6825, and muslim:4421—establishes that a fourfold confession by a sane, married Muslim legally mandates execution by stoning.

bukhari:7193.note: Judging according to Allah's Book, Muhammad sentences an unmarried male laborer to 100 lashes and a year of exile for adultery, and commands Unais to go to the married woman involved and stone her to death. Parallel narrations (bukhari:6827, bukhari:7194) specify that Muhammad instructed Unais to question her first and stone her upon her confession.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَأَمَّا أَنْتَ يَا أُنَيْسُ ـ لِرَجُلٍ ـ فَاغْدُ عَلَى امْرَأَةِ هَذَا فَارْجُمْهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَغَدَا عَلَيْهَا أُنَيْسٌ فَرَجَمَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) addressed some man, "Go in the morning to the wife of this man and stone her to death." So Unais went to her the next morning and stoned her to death

bukhari:7193.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists (citing Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī) typically argue that this narration merely abbreviates parallel reports (such as bukhari:2724) in which Muhammad conditioned the woman's execution on her confession (fa-in i'tarafat), and that stoning was the standard divine penalty for a married adulterer (muḥṣan) in contrast to the unmarried laborer. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore to judge strictly by the Book of Allah (la-aqḍiyanna baynakumā bi-kitābi Allāh) before ordering her stoned to death (farjumhā), even though stoning and exile are completely absent from the Quran (which mandates only 100 lashes in Surah 24:2). Furthermore, even taking the parallel narration into account, dispatching a single man (Unais) to extract a confession in private and immediately stone her to death bypasses the Quran's own four-witness requirement (Surah 24:4) and confirms the brutal reality of summary execution.

bukhari:7194.note: Declaring that he is judging according to the Book of Allah, Muhammad sentences an unmarried laborer to a hundred lashes and one year of exile for adultery, and orders a man named Unais to stone the married woman to death. While this abridged report omits the step of questioning her, fuller parallel narrations (e.g., bukhari:6827) specify that Unais was instructed to stone her if she confessed, which she did before being executed.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَأَمَّا أَنْتَ يَا أُنَيْسُ ـ لِرَجُلٍ ـ فَاغْدُ عَلَى امْرَأَةِ هَذَا فَارْجُمْهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَغَدَا عَلَيْهَا أُنَيْسٌ فَرَجَمَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) addressed some man, "Go in the morning to the wife of this man and stone her to death." So Unais went to her the next morning and stoned her to death

bukhari:7194.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as Ibn Hajar explains in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* citing parallel narrations like `bukhari:6827`, Unais was instructed to stone the woman only if she confessed (*fa-in i'tarafat*), and that capital punishment for married adulterers was a tightly regulated judicial procedure. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad swore to judge "by Allah's Book" (*la-aqḍiyanna baynakumā bi-kitābi Allāh*) and commanded Unais, "Go in the morning to the wife of this man and stone her" (*faghdu 'alā imra'ati hādhā farjumhā*), delegating both the morning interrogation and summary execution by stoning (*fa-rajamahā*) to a single emissary while the unmarried male offender received only lashes and exile. Furthermore, even with the confession clause in `bukhari:6827`, Muhammad's claim to enforce "Allah's Book" by stoning directly contradicts the canonical Quran—which prescribes only one hundred lashes in Surah 24:2—exposing the textual crisis of the missing "verse of stoning" (*āyat al-rajm*).

muslim:4400.note: Muhammad decrees that a thief's hand is to be cut off for stealing property valued at a quarter of a dinar and upwards ([Quran 5:38](quran://5/38); cf. muslim:4398).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ لاَ تُقْطَعُ يَدُ السَّارِقِ إِلاَّ فِي رُبْعِ دِينَارٍ فَصَاعِدًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:The hand of a thief should not be cut off but for a quarter of a dinar and upwards

muslim:4400.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that hand amputation under [Quran 5:38](quran://5/38) is reserved only for major, high-value thefts and sets a high threshold to prevent the punishment from being carried out for minor offenses. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that "the hand of a thief should not be cut off but for a quarter of a dinar and upwards" (لاَ تُقْطَعُ يَدُ السَّارِقِ إِلاَّ فِي رُبْعِ دِينَارٍ فَصَاعِدًا), fixing the threshold for amputation at any theft valued at a quarter of a dinar or more (muslim:4398, bukhari:6789, bukhari:6790). Instead of mandating restitution ([Exodus 22:1](bible://ex/22/1)) or rehabilitating the thief to work with his own hands to share with those in need ([Ephesians 4:28](bible://eph/4/28)), Muhammad's decree enforces permanent bodily amputation once that quarter-dinar threshold is met.

muslim:4401.note: Narrated by A'isha, Muhammad establishes the legal threshold for cutting off a thief's hand ([Quran 5:38](quran://5/38)), ruling that the hand is amputated for stealing a quarter of a dinar or more (bukhari:6789, muslim:4402).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّهَا سَمِعَتْ عَائِشَةَ، تُحَدِّثُ أَنَّهَا سَمِعَتْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ لاَ تُقْطَعُ الْيَدُ إِلاَّ فِي رُبْعِ دِينَارٍ فَمَا فَوْقَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha reported:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying: The hand (of a thief) should not be cut off but for a quarter of a dinar and what is above that

muslim:4401.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the Quranic mandate for amputating a thief's hand ([Quran 5:38](quran://5/38)) applies only to major heist-level crimes or functions as a theoretical deterrent rather than an active penalty for petty theft. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `لاَ تُقْطَعُ الْيَدُ إِلاَّ فِي رُبْعِ دِينَارٍ فَمَا فَوْقَهُ` ("The hand should not be cut off but for a quarter of a dinar and what is above that"), fixing a specific, low monetary threshold at which literal hand amputation (`تُقْطَعُ الْيَدُ`) is mandated (`bukhari:6789`, `bukhari:6790`, `muslim:4402`). Instead of requiring restitution or instructing the thief to labor with his own hands to share with those in need ([Ephesians 4:28](bible://eph/4/28)), Muhammad's legal ruling permanently severs the hand for taking a fraction of a single dinar.

muslim:4402.note: Muhammad decrees that a thief's hand is to be cut off for stealing a quarter of a dinar or more ([Quran 5:38](quran://5/38)), though A'isha elsewhere reports that during his lifetime a thief's hand was not amputated for less than the price of a shield or armour (muslim:4404).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، أَنَّهَا سَمِعَتِ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ لاَ تُقْطَعُ يَدُ السَّارِقِ إِلاَّ فِي رُبْعِ دِينَارٍ فَصَاعِدًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha reported that she heard Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) as saying:The hand of the thief may not be cut off but for a quarter of a dinar and upwards

muslim:4402.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that setting a minimum threshold for theft is a merciful legal safeguard designed to prevent punishment for trivial offenses and serve merely as a societal deterrent. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "لاَ تُقْطَعُ يَدُ السَّارِقِ إِلاَّ فِي رُبْعِ دِينَارٍ فَصَاعِدًا" ("The hand of the thief may not be cut off but for a quarter of a dinar and upwards"), enforcing the physical amputation mandated in [Quran 5:38](quran://5/38) as soon as a theft reaches the threshold of a quarter of a dinar (bukhari:6789, muslim:4398, muslim:4401). Rather than amputating a thief's hand, the New Testament commands that a thief stop stealing and work with his own hands to share with those in need ([Ephesians 4:28](bible://eph/4/28)).

bukhari:7167.note: After a man testifies against himself four times to committing unlawful sexual intercourse (zina) and confirms he is of sound mind, Muhammad orders his companions to take him away and stone him to death. Classical Sunni jurists identify the man as Ma'iz ibn Malik and cite this command as foundational legal proof for the mandatory execution by stoning (rajm) of married adulterers.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي زَنَيْتُ‏.‏ فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ‏.‏ فَلَمَّا شَهِدَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ أَرْبَعًا قَالَ ‏"‏ أَبِكَ جُنُونٌ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ لاَ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ اذْهَبُوا بِهِ فَارْجُمُوهُ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: "O Allah's Apostle! I have committed illegal sexual intercourse." The Prophet (ﷺ) turned his face to the other side, but when the man gave four witnesses against himself, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him, "Are you mad?" The man said, "No." So the Prophet (ﷺ) said (to his companions), "Take him away and stone him to death

bukhari:7167.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that stoning (rajm) in Islamic law is merely a theoretical deterrent and emphasize that Muhammad turned away (fa-aʿraḍa ʿanhu) and asked, 'Are you mad?' (abika junūn) to give the man every merciful opportunity to retract his voluntary confession. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad issued the binding, lethal imperative 'Idhhabū bihi farjumūhu' ('Take him away and stone him to death'), which Ibn Ḥajar’s Fatḥ al-Bārī confirms establishes the mandatory ḥadd execution for any married adulterer (muḥṣan) once four confessions or witnesses are met. Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:6820) record that when the stones actually struck the man and he fled in terror to escape the execution, Muhammad's companions chased him down and bludgeoned him to death anyway.

muslim:4437.note: When a Jewish man and woman are brought for adultery, Muhammad demands that the Jews bring their physical Torah scroll to verify its ruling, and once Abdullah ibn Salam exposes the stoning verse beneath the reader's hand, Muhammad orders them both stoned to death. Abdullah ibn Umar recounts participating in the stoning and watching the man shield the woman from the stones with his own body.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أُتِيَ بِيَهُودِيٍّ وَيَهُودِيَّةٍ قَدْ زَنَيَا فَانْطَلَقَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى جَاءَ يَهُودَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَا تَجِدُونَ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ عَلَى مَنْ زَنَى ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا نُسَوِّدُ وُجُوهَهُمَا وَنُحَمِّلُهُمَا وَنُخَالِفُ بَيْنَ وُجُوهِهِمَا وَيُطَافُ بِهِمَا ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَأْتُوا بِالتَّوْرَاةِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَجَاءُوا بِهَا فَقَرَءُوهَا حَتَّى إِذَا مَرُّوا بِآيَةِ الرَّجْمِ وَضَعَ الْفَتَى الَّذِي يَقْرَأُ يَدَهُ عَلَى آيَةِ الرَّجْمِ وَقَرَأَ مَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَمَا وَرَاءَهَا فَقَالَ لَهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ سَلاَمٍ وَهْوَ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مُرْهُ فَلْيَرْفَعْ يَدَهُ فَرَفَعَهَا فَإِذَا تَحْتَهَا آيَةُ الرَّجْمِ فَأَمَرَ بِهِمَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَرُجِمَا ‏.‏ قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ كُنْتُ فِيمَنْ رَجَمَهُمَا فَلَقَدْ رَأَيْتُهُ يَقِيهَا مِنَ الْحِجَارَةِ بِنَفْسِهِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abdullah b. 'Umar reported that a Jew and a Jewess were brought to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) who had committed adultery. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) came to the Jews and said:What do you find in Torah for one who commits adultery? They said: We darken their faces and make them ride on the donkey with their faces turned to the opposite direction (and their backs touching each other), and then they are taken round (the city). He said: Bring Torah if you are truthful. They brought it and recited it until when they came to the verse pertaining to stoning, the person who was reading placed his hand on the verse pertaining to stoning, and read (only that which was) between his hands and what was subsequent to that. Abdullah b. Salim who was at that time with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Command him (the reciter) to lift his hand. He lifted it and there was, underneath that, the verse pertaining to stoning. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) pronounced judgment about both of them and they were stoned. Abdullah b. 'Umar said: I was one of those who stoned them, and I saw him (the Jew) protecting her (the Jewess) with his body

muslim:4437.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this incident demonstrates the textual corruption of the Torah, or that Muhammad merely deferred to Jewish authorities rather than enforcing stoning himself. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad demanded their physical Torah scroll as the test of truth (فَأْتُوا بِالتَّوْرَاةِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ) and that when Abdullah b. Salam told Muhammad to make the reader lift his hand, the intact stoning verse was written directly underneath (فَإِذَا تَحْتَهَا آيَةُ الرَّجْمِ), proving the written text was preserved in Medina while the reader only attempted to cover it with his hand ([Quran 5:43](quran://5/43)). Furthermore, Muhammad personally issued the execution order (فَأَمَرَ بِهِمَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَرُجِمَا) and his companions, including Abdullah b. Umar, stoned the couple (كُنْتُ فِيمَنْ رَجَمَهُمَا) as the man shielded the woman from the stones with his own body (يَقِيهَا مِنَ الْحِجَارَةِ بِنَفْسِهِ).

bukhari:6924.note: Muhammad declares that he has been ordered to fight people until they testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah, making the protection of their lives and property conditional upon this profession and its accompanying legal obligations. Invoking this legal exception, Caliph Abu Bakr—with Umar's eventual agreement—wages war against Arab tribes who profess the creed but withhold the Zakat tax.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ‏.‏ فَمَنْ قَالَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ‏.‏ عَصَمَ مِنِّي مَالَهُ وَنَفْسَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, 'I have been ordered to fight the people till they say: 'None has the right to be worshipped but Allah, 'and whoever said, 'None has the right to be worshipped but Allah', Allah will save his property and his life from me

bukhari:6924.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that—citing Al-Khaṭṭābī via Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—the word 'the people' (*al-nās*) is a general term meant specifically (*ʿāmm urīda bihi al-khuṣūṣ*) for hostile Arab polytheists waging war, and that Abu Bakr was merely suppressing armed political rebellion. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the protection of a person's life and property (*ʿaṣama minnī mālahu wa-nafsahu*) is withheld 'until they say there is no god but Allah' (*ḥattā yaqūlū lā ilāha illā Allāh*) and fulfill its legal rights (*illā bi-ḥaqqihi*), making physical survival contingent on theological conversion rather than ceasing military aggression. Moreover, Abu Bakr and Umar apply this prophetic mandate to wage war against anyone who differentiates between ritual prayer and the alms tax (*man farraqa bayna al-ṣalāti wa-al-zakāti*), confirming alongside `bukhari:25` that this command enforces religious submission and ritual observance rather than defensive self-preservation.

muslim:4521.note: Muhammad instructs his military commanders to fight those who disbelieve in Allah—while prohibiting embezzlement, treachery, mutilation, and killing children—and to present polytheist enemies with an ultimatum: convert to Islam, submit and pay the *jizyah* tax ([Quran 9:29](quran://9/29)), or be fought. While this directive requires inviting the enemy before attacking, a neighboring report (muslim:4519) notes that Muhammad later raided the Banu Mustaliq without prior warning.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏ "‏ اغْزُوا بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ قَاتِلُوا مَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ اغْزُوا وَ لاَ تَغُلُّوا وَلاَ تَغْدِرُوا وَلاَ تَمْثُلُوا وَلاَ تَقْتُلُوا وَلِيدًا وَإِذَا لَقِيتَ عَدُوَّكَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ فَادْعُهُمْ إِلَى ثَلاَثِ خِصَالٍ - أَوْ خِلاَلٍ - فَأَيَّتُهُنَّ مَا أَجَابُوكَ فَاقْبَلْ مِنْهُمْ وَكُفَّ عَنْهُمْ ثُمَّ ادْعُهُمْ إِلَى الإِسْلاَمِ فَإِنْ أَجَابُوكَ فَاقْبَلْ مِنْهُمْ وَكُفَّ عَنْهُمْ ثُمَّ ادْعُهُمْ إِلَى التَّحَوُّلِ مِنْ دَارِهِمْ إِلَى دَارِ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَأَخْبِرْهُمْ أَنَّهُمْ إِنْ فَعَلُوا ذَلِكَ فَلَهُمْ مَا لِلْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَعَلَيْهِمْ مَا عَلَى الْمُهَاجِرِينَ فَإِنْ أَبَوْا أَنْ يَتَحَوَّلُوا مِنْهَا فَأَخْبِرْهُمْ أَنَّهُمْ يَكُونُونَ كَأَعْرَابِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ يَجْرِي عَلَيْهِمْ حُكْمُ اللَّهِ الَّذِي يَجْرِي عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلاَ يَكُونُ لَهُمْ فِي الْغَنِيمَةِ وَالْفَىْءِ شَىْءٌ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُجَاهِدُوا مَعَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَإِنْ هُمْ أَبَوْا فَسَلْهُمُ الْجِزْيَةَ فَإِنْ هُمْ أَجَابُوكَ فَاقْبَلْ مِنْهُمْ وَكُفَّ عَنْهُمْ فَإِنْ هُمْ أَبَوْا فَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَقَاتِلْهُمْ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He would say:Fight in the name of Allah and in the way of Allah. Fight against those who disbelieve in Allah. Make a holy war, do not embezzle the spoils; do not break your pledge; and do not mutilate (the dead) bodies; do not kill the children. When you meet your enemies who are polytheists, invite them to three courses of action. If they respond to any one of these, you also accept it and withhold yourself from doing them any harm. Invite them to (accept) Islam; if they respond to you, accept it from them and desist from fighting against them. Then invite them to migrate from their lands to the land of the Muhajireen and inform them that, if they do so, they shall have all the privileges and obligations of the Muhajireen. If they refuse to migrate, tell them that they will have the status of Bedouin Muslims and will be subjected to the Commands of Allah like other Muslims, but they will not get any share from the spoils of war or Fai' except when they actually fight with the Muslims (against the disbelievers). If they refuse to accept Islam, demand from them the Jizya. If they agree to pay, accept it from them and hold off your hands. If they refuse to pay the tax, seek Allah's help and fight them.

muslim:4521.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration establishes ethical rules for defensive warfare—pointing to the prohibitions against mutilation (`لاَ تَمْثُلُوا`) and killing children (`وَلاَ تَقْتُلُوا وَلِيدًا`)—and claim that the *jizyah* is merely a civic tax in exchange for military protection. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states the theological mandate for sending out raiding expeditions (`اغْزُوا`) and besieging enemy forts (`حِصْنٍ`): `قَاتِلُوا مَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ` ('Fight against those who disbelieve in Allah'). Rather than repelling an attack, the Muslim commander is instructed to withhold harm (`وَكُفَّ عَنْهُمْ`) only if the targets convert to Islam (`الإِسْلاَمِ`) or submit to paying the *jizyah* (`الْجِزْيَةَ`, cf. [Quran 9:29](quran://9/29)), and if they refuse both, to fight them (`فَإِنْ هُمْ أَبَوْا فَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَقَاتِلْهُمْ`).

bukhari:4121.note: After the people of Banu Qurayza surrendered to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, Sa'd decreed that their warriors and combatant-age men (*muqatilah*) be executed and their women and children (*dharari*) be taken as captives, a verdict Muhammad ratified as the judgment of Allah ([Quran 33:26](quran://33/26)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: نَزَلَ أَهْلُ قُرَيْظَةَ عَلَى حُكْمِ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ، فَأَرْسَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى سَعْدٍ، فَأَتَى عَلَى حِمَارٍ، فَلَمَّا دَنَا مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ قَالَ لِلأَنْصَارِ ‏"‏ قُومُوا إِلَى سَيِّدِكُمْ ـ أَوْ ـ خَيْرِكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ هَؤُلاَءِ نَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ تَقْتُلُ مُقَاتِلَتَهُمْ وَتَسْبِي ذَرَارِيَّهُمْ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ قَضَيْتَ بِحُكْمِ اللَّهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ وَرُبَّمَا قَالَ ‏"‏ بِحُكْمِ الْمَلِكِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The people of (Banu) Quraiza agreed to accept the verdict of Sa`d bin Mu`adh. So the Prophet (ﷺ) sent for Sa`d, and the latter came (riding) a donkey and when he approached the Mosque, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the Ansar, "Get up for your chief or for the best among you." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said (to Sa`d)." These (i.e. Banu Quraiza) have agreed to accept your verdict." Sa`d said, "Kill their (men) warriors and take their offspring as captives, "On that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "You have judged according to Allah's Judgment," or said, "according to the King's judgment

bukhari:4121.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the Banu Qurayza were executed for wartime treason by an arbitrator of their own choosing applying Torah law (Deuteronomy 20:10–14), and that the term *muqātilatahum* ('their fighters') restricted punishment solely to active combatants. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad ratified the massacre as Allah's own divine decree (*qaḍayta bi-ḥukmi Allāhi* — 'You have judged according to Allah's Judgment'), not Jewish law. Furthermore, as Ibn Hajar documents in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* alongside authentic narrations (e.g., Sunan Abi Dawud 4404), 'combatant' status was determined not by individual trials for treason, but by stripping adolescent boys to inspect them for pubic hair and beheading every male who had reached physical puberty.

bukhari:4121.note: Upon the surrender of Banu Qurayza, Muhammad endorsed Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's ruling to enslave their offspring and dependents (*saby al-dharari*) alongside executing their warriors, declaring the sentence to be the judgment of Allah ([Quran 33:26](quran://33/26)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: نَزَلَ أَهْلُ قُرَيْظَةَ عَلَى حُكْمِ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ، فَأَرْسَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى سَعْدٍ، فَأَتَى عَلَى حِمَارٍ، فَلَمَّا دَنَا مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ قَالَ لِلأَنْصَارِ ‏"‏ قُومُوا إِلَى سَيِّدِكُمْ ـ أَوْ ـ خَيْرِكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ هَؤُلاَءِ نَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ تَقْتُلُ مُقَاتِلَتَهُمْ وَتَسْبِي ذَرَارِيَّهُمْ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ قَضَيْتَ بِحُكْمِ اللَّهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ وَرُبَّمَا قَالَ ‏"‏ بِحُكْمِ الْمَلِكِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The people of (Banu) Quraiza agreed to accept the verdict of Sa`d bin Mu`adh. So the Prophet (ﷺ) sent for Sa`d, and the latter came (riding) a donkey and when he approached the Mosque, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the Ansar, "Get up for your chief or for the best among you." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said (to Sa`d)." These (i.e. Banu Quraiza) have agreed to accept your verdict." Sa`d said, "Kill their (men) warriors and take their offspring as captives, "On that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "You have judged according to Allah's Judgment," or said, "according to the King's judgment

bukhari:4121.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that taking the women and offspring (*dharārīyahum*) of Banu Qurayza was a merciful humanitarian measure to shelter and provide for dependents left behind after their men were executed, rather than true chattel slavery. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly uses the legal verb *tasbī* ('you enslave as war captives'), which Muhammad sanctified as 'the Judgment of Allah' (*bi-ḥukmi Allāhi*) in direct parallel with Quran 33:26 ('some you slew and some you took captive'). Classical sources, including Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and *Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr*, confirm these women and children were distributed as chattel property among the troops—with Muhammad taking Rayhana for himself—and that a portion of the captives were sent to Najd to be sold to pagans in exchange for horses and weapons.

muslim:4594.note: Umar ibn al-Khattab reports via Jabir ibn Abd Allah that Muhammad declared he would expel the Jews and Christians from the Arabian Peninsula until he left no one there except a Muslim (cf. muslim:4595, bukhari:3053, bukhari:3168).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَخْبَرَنِي عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ لأُخْرِجَنَّ الْيَهُودَ وَالنَّصَارَى مِنْ جَزِيرَةِ الْعَرَبِ حَتَّى لاَ أَدَعَ إِلاَّ مُسْلِمًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: It has been narrated by 'Umar b. al-Khattib that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say:I will expel the Jews and Christians from the Arabian Peninsula and will not leave any but Muslim

muslim:4594.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this expulsion was a political security measure directed only against specific tribes that had violated treaties rather than a blanket religious purge. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an emphatic oath—"la-ukhrijanna al-yahūda wa-l-naṣārā min jazīrati al-ʿarab" ("I will expel the Jews and Christians from the Arabian Peninsula")—and defines religious identity rather than treaty compliance as the sole criterion for remaining: "ḥattā lā adaʿa illā musliman" ("until I do not leave any but a Muslim"). This categorical religious exclusion is corroborated by parallel Sahih narrations (muslim:4595, bukhari:3053, bukhari:3168) without any qualification regarding political hostility.

bukhari:3012.note: When asked about raiding polytheist settlements by night in which some of their women and offspring are struck, Muhammad permitted the attacks by declaring, "They are of them." While Muhammad also prohibited the direct killing of women and children (bukhari:3014), classical Sunni jurists either reconcile the reports by permitting nocturnal raids and siege warfare in which non-combatants are struck alongside combatants, or hold that this allowance was abrogated.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَسُئِلَ عَنْ أَهْلِ الدَّارِ يُبَيَّتُونَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ، فَيُصَابُ مِنْ نِسَائِهِمْ وَذَرَارِيِّهِمْ قَالَ ‏"‏ هُمْ مِنْهُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: and was asked whether it was permissible to attack the pagan warriors at night with the probability of exposing their women and children to danger. The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, "They (i.e. women and children) are from them (i.e. pagans)."

bukhari:3012.literal_translation: and he was asked about the inhabitants of a settlement from among the polytheists being raided at night, whereby some of their women and offspring are struck [wounded or killed]. He said, "They are of them."

translation_issue.arabic_term: أَهْلِ الدَّارِ يُبَيَّتُونَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ، فَيُصَابُ مِنْ نِسَائِهِمْ وَذَرَارِيِّهِمْ
translation_issue.published_rendering: attack the pagan warriors at night with the probability of exposing their women and children to danger
translation_issue.literal_meaning: the inhabitants of a settlement from among the polytheists being raided at night, whereby some of their women and offspring are struck
translation_issue.explanation: The translator renders 'ahl ad-dār' (inhabitants of the dwelling/settlement) as 'warriors' and softens 'fa-yuṣābu min nisā'ihim wa-dharārīhim' (whereby some of their women and offspring are struck/hit) into 'with the probability of exposing their women and children to danger.'

bukhari:3012.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islam strictly forbids intentionally targeting non-combatants (citing bukhari:3015), claiming via Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī that this narration merely addresses unavoidable collateral damage during night raids (bayāt) when combatants cannot be distinguished from civilians in the dark. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the raid targets the inhabitants of the dwellings (أَهْلِ الدَّارِ يُبَيَّتُونَ, ahl al-dār yubayyatūna—not merely 'pagan warriors' as interpolated by the English translator) where women and children are inevitably struck and killed (فَيُصَابُ مِنْ نِسَائِهِمْ وَذَرَارِيِّهِمْ). Rather than prohibiting the raid or mandating precautions, Muhammad justifies their deaths by assigning them the collective status of their polytheist parents—declaring 'هُمْ مِنْهُمْ' ('They are of them,' and in muslim:4550, 'هُمْ مِنْ آبَائِهِمْ', 'They are of their fathers') to authorize surprise nocturnal attacks on family settlements.

bukhari:2926.note: Muhammad prophesies that the Last Hour will not be established until Muslims fight the Jews and stones call out to Muslims to kill Jews hiding behind them ([Romans 12:14](bible://rom/12/14); [Luke 6:27-28](bible://lk/6/27-28)). Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi affirm this as a literal end-times prophecy situated during the eschatological war against the Dajjal.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ لاَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ حَتَّى تُقَاتِلُوا الْيَهُودَ حَتَّى يَقُولَ الْحَجَرُ وَرَاءَهُ الْيَهُودِيُّ يَا مُسْلِمُ، هَذَا يَهُودِيٌّ وَرَائِي فَاقْتُلْهُ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "The Hour will not be established until you fight with the Jews, and the stone behind which a Jew will be hiding will say. "O Muslim! There is a Jew hiding behind me, so kill him

bukhari:2926.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration is merely a descriptive eschatological prophecy restricted to the end-times battle against the army of the false messiah (*al-Dajjāl*), rather than a general mandate for religious violence. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *hādhā yahūdiyyun warāʾī fa-qtulhu* ('this is a Jew behind me, so kill him'), commanding the execution of a fleeing person in hiding solely on the basis of his ethno-religious identity (*yahūdiyyun*) without any mention of the Dajjal or active combat. Furthermore, Imam al-Bukhari codified this narration directly inside the *Book of Jihad and Expeditions* under the chapter 'Fighting the Jews' (*Bāb Qitāl al-Yahūd*), treating it as part of normative Jihad jurisprudence rather than passive apocalyptic lore.

muslim:5661.note: Muhammad commands Muslims not to initiate the greeting of peace to Jews or Christians and orders that when meeting any of them on a road, Muslims must force him to its narrowest part.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ لاَ تَبْدَءُوا الْيَهُودَ وَلاَ النَّصَارَى بِالسَّلاَمِ فَإِذَا لَقِيتُمْ أَحَدَهُمْ فِي طَرِيقٍ فَاضْطَرُّوهُ إِلَى أَضْيَقِهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:Do not greet the Jews and the Christians before they greet you and when you meet any one of them on the roads force him to go to the narrowest part of it

muslim:5661.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this command was restricted to hostile combatants or merely meant declining to yield the center of a crowded path out of deference. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a general prohibition against initiating peace greetings to Jews and Christians (لاَ تَبْدَءُوا الْيَهُودَ وَلاَ النَّصَارَى بِالسَّلاَمِ) and issues the direct imperative to "force him to go to the narrowest part of it" (فَاضْطَرُّوهُ إِلَى أَضْيَقِهِ) whenever meeting any one of them on a road (فَإِذَا لَقِيتُمْ أَحَدَهُمْ فِي طَرِيقٍ), containing no condition of warfare or road congestion.

muslim:6365.note: Muhammad asks Jarir to rid him of the pre-Islamic sanctuary of Dhu al-Khalasah (the Yamanite or northern Ka'ba), and blesses Jarir and the men of Ahmas after they demolish it and kill everyone found there. The Arabic text specifies Jarir leading 150 men from Ahmas (confirmed in muslim:6366), whereas the English translation renders these as 'Jabir' and '350'.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ بَيْتٌ يُقَالُ لَهُ ذُو الْخَلَصَةِ وَكَانَ يُقَالُ لَهُ الْكَعْبَةُ الْيَمَانِيَةُ وَالْكَعْبَةُ الشَّامِيَّةُ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ هَلْ أَنْتَ مُرِيحِي مِنْ ذِي الْخَلَصَةِ وَالْكَعْبَةِ الْيَمَانِيَةِ وَالشَّامِيَّةِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَنَفَرْتُ إِلَيْهِ فِي مِائَةٍ وَخَمْسِينَ مِنْ أَحْمَسَ فَكَسَرْنَاهُ وَقَتَلْنَا مَنْ وَجَدْنَا عِنْدَهُ فَأَتَيْتُهُ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ - قَالَ - فَدَعَا لَنَا وَلأَحْمَسَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Jabir reported that there was in pre-Islamic days a temple called Dhu'l- Khalasah and it was called the Yamanite Ka'ba or the northern Ka'ba. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said unto me:Will you rid me of Dhu'l-Khalasah and so I went forth at the head of 350 horsemen of the tribe of Ahmas and we destroyed it and killed whomsoever we found there. Then we came back to him (to the Holy Prophet) and informed him and he blessed us and the tribe of Ahmas

muslim:6365.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's military campaigns were strictly defensive responses to political aggression and that places of worship and non-combatants were protected under Islamic rules of engagement. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad initiated the expedition solely to eliminate a rival religious sanctuary—asking Jarir, "Will you rid me of Dhu al-Khalasah and the Yamanite and Syrian Ka'ba?" (هَلْ أَنْتَ مُرِيحِي مِنْ ذِي الْخَلَصَةِ وَالْكَعْبَةِ الْيَمَانِيَةِ وَالشَّامِيَّةِ)—with no mention of any military provocation. Furthermore, Jarir reports that his force from the tribe of Ahmas made no distinction among those present, stating, "we demolished it and killed whomsoever we found there" (فَكَسَرْنَاهُ وَقَتَلْنَا مَنْ وَجَدْنَا عِنْدَهُ), a report for which Muhammad immediately blessed them (فَدَعَا لَنَا وَلأَحْمَسَ).

bukhari:6944.note: Muhammad goes to the Jewish study house (Bait al-Midras) and three times commands the assembly to embrace Islam in order to be safe (aslimū taslamū). When they respond only that he has conveyed his message, he declares that the earth belongs to Allah and His Messenger and orders their expulsion and the sale of their property (cf. bukhari:3167; contrast [John 18:36](bible://jn/18/36)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَامَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَنَادَاهُمْ ‏"‏ يَا مَعْشَرَ يَهُودَ أَسْلِمُوا تَسْلَمُوا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالُوا قَدْ بَلَّغْتَ يَا أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ ذَلِكَ أُرِيدُ ‏"‏، ثُمَّ قَالَهَا الثَّانِيَةَ‏.‏ فَقَالُوا قَدْ بَلَّغْتَ يَا أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ الثَّالِثَةَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ اعْلَمُوا أَنَّ الأَرْضَ لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ، وَإِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُجْلِيَكُمْ، فَمَنْ وَجَدَ مِنْكُمْ بِمَالِهِ شَيْئًا فَلْيَبِعْهُ، وَإِلاَّ فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا الأَرْضُ لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) stood up and addressed them, "O Assembly of Jews! Embrace Islam and you will be safe!" The Jews replied, "O Aba-l-Qasim! You have conveyed Allah's message to us." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "That is what I want (from you)." He repeated his first statement for the second time, and they said, "You have conveyed Allah's message, O Aba-l- Qasim." Then he said it for the third time and added, "You should Know that the earth belongs to Allah and His Apostle, and I want to exile you fro,,, this land, so whoever among you owns some property, can sell it, otherwise you should know that the Earth belongs to Allah and His Apostle."

bukhari:6944.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that this ultimatum was a purely political response to a breached treaty by the Medinan Jewish tribes rather than religious coercion. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad entered their Torah study house (*Bayt al-Midrās*) without mentioning any treaty violation and conditioned their safety and property rights solely on conversion (*"aslimū taslamū"* — "Embrace Islam and you will be safe") before ordering their exile (*"innī urīdu an ujliyakum"*) on the theological grounds that "the earth belongs to Allah and His Messenger" (*"al-arḍa lillāhi wa-rasūlihi"*). Moreover, Imam al-Bukhari himself categorized this narration under *Kitāb al-Ikrāh* (The Book of Coercion), and parallel Sahih narrations (`muslim:4594`) confirm Muhammad's blanket decree to expel all Jews and Christians from the Arabian Peninsula purely on the basis of their religion.

muslim:6222.note: On the Day of Khaybar, Muhammad gives the standard to Ali ibn Abi Talib and commands him to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His Messenger, declaring that their blood and property become inviolable only once they do so, except as justified by law.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَدَعَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ فَأَعْطَاهُ إِيَّاهَا وَقَالَ ‏"‏ امْشِ وَلاَ تَلْتَفِتْ حَتَّى يَفْتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَسَارَ عَلِيٌّ شَيْئًا ثُمَّ وَقَفَ وَلَمْ يَلْتَفِتْ فَصَرَخَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ عَلَى مَاذَا أُقَاتِلُ النَّاسَ قَالَ ‏"‏ قَاتِلْهُمْ حَتَّى يَشْهَدُوا أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ فَإِذَا فَعَلُوا ذَلِكَ فَقَدْ مَنَعُوا مِنْكَ دِمَاءَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ إِلاَّ بِحَقِّهَا وَحِسَابُهُمْ عَلَى اللَّهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) called 'Ali b. Abu Talib and he conferred (this honour) upon him and said: Proceed on and do not look about until Allah grants you victory, and 'Ali went a bit and then halted and did not look about and then said in a loud voice: Allah's Messenger, on what issue should I fight with the people? Thereupon he (the Prophet) said: Fight with them until they bear testimony to the fact that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is his Messenger, and when they do that then their blood and their riches are inviolable from your hands but what is justified by law and their reckoning is with Allah

muslim:6222.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the campaign at Khaybar was a purely defensive military measure rather than a war to compel religious conversion, or that the command to fight 'the people' (*al-nās*) applied only to Arab polytheists rather than the Jewish inhabitants of Khaybar. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that on the Day of Khaybar (*yawma Khaybar*), when Ali ibn Abi Talib asked on what basis he should fight the people (*'alā mādhā uqātilu al-nās*), Muhammad commanded, 'Fight with them until they bear testimony to the fact that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is his Messenger' (*qātilhum ḥattā yashhadū an lā ilāha illā Allāhu wa-anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh*). Furthermore, the narration states that only 'when they do that' (*fa-idhā fa'alū dhālika*) have they protected their blood and their riches from his hands (*mana'ū minka dimā'ahum wa-amwālahum*), making the inviolability of life and property during the Khaybar campaign directly conditional upon professing the Islamic creed (see also bukhari:25, bukhari:2942, and [Quran 9:29](quran://9/29)).

bukhari:4431.note: On his deathbed in AD 632—after his companions disputed his request to write a document to keep them from going astray and asked whether he was speaking deliriously (ahajara)—Muhammad commanded the expulsion of the polytheists (al-mushrikin) from the Arabian Peninsula, while the narrator forgot the third of his final instructions. Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawi affirm this as a binding Prophetic order to remove non-Muslims from the Arabian Peninsula (or the Hijaz), which parallel Sunni narrations explicitly extend to Jews and Christians.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: اشْتَدَّ بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَجَعُهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ ائْتُونِي أَكْتُبْ لَكُمْ كِتَابًا لَنْ تَضِلُّوا بَعْدَهُ أَبَدًا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَتَنَازَعُوا، وَلاَ يَنْبَغِي عِنْدَ نَبِيٍّ تَنَازُعٌ، فَقَالُوا مَا شَأْنُهُ أَهَجَرَ اسْتَفْهِمُوهُ فَذَهَبُوا يَرُدُّونَ عَلَيْهِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ دَعُونِي فَالَّذِي أَنَا فِيهِ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا تَدْعُونِي إِلَيْهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ وَأَوْصَاهُمْ بِثَلاَثٍ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَخْرِجُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ مِنْ جَزِيرَةِ الْعَرَبِ، وَأَجِيزُوا الْوَفْدَ بِنَحْوِ مَا كُنْتُ أُجِيزُهُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The ailment of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) became worse (on Thursday) and he said, "Fetch me something so that I may write to you something after which you will never go astray." The people (present there) differed in this matter, and it was not right to differ before a prophet. Some said, "What is wrong with him ? (Do you think ) he is delirious (seriously ill)? Ask him ( to understand his state )." So they went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him again. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Leave me, for my present state is better than what you call me for." Then he ordered them to do three things. He said, "Turn the pagans out of the 'Arabian Peninsula; respect and give gifts to the foreign delegations as you have seen me dealing with them."

bukhari:4431.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the term al-mushrikīn ('polytheists') applied only to hostile idolaters who violated treaties, or that Jazīrat al-‘Arab ('the Arabian Peninsula') referred strictly to the immediate sanctuary of Mecca rather than the broader region. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an unconditional, blanket imperative (أَخْرِجُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ مِنْ جَزِيرَةِ الْعَرَبِ — 'Expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula') with zero requirement of hostility or treaty breach, while parallel Sahih narrations (e.g., muslim:4594) explicitly clarify this mandate as: 'I will certainly expel the Jews and the Christians from the Arabian Peninsula until I leave none but a Muslim.' Furthermore, in Fatḥ al-Bārī, Ibn Ḥajar al-‘Asqalānī confirms that al-mushrikīn here encompasses Jews and Christians, and that Caliph ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb enforced this exact deathbed decree by deporting the peaceful Jews of Khaybar and Christians of Najrān despite their prior treaties.

bukhari:2541.note: Eyewitness participant Ibn 'Umar reported that Muhammad launched an unannounced raid against the Banu al-Mustaliq while they were heedless and watering their livestock, killing their fighting men, taking their women and children captive, and acquiring Juwayriyya on that day. Nafi' and classical jurists cite this account in parallel reports (muslim:4519) as legal precedent for attacking non-Muslim tribes without prior warning once the general call to Islam has reached them.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَغَارَ عَلَى بَنِي الْمُصْطَلِقِ وَهُمْ غَارُّونَ وَأَنْعَامُهُمْ تُسْقَى عَلَى الْمَاءِ، فَقَتَلَ مُقَاتِلَتَهُمْ، وَسَبَى ذَرَارِيَّهُمْ، وَأَصَابَ يَوْمَئِذٍ جُوَيْرِيَةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: the Prophet (ﷺ) had suddenly attacked Bani Mustaliq without warning while they were heedless and their cattle were being watered at the places of water. Their fighting men were killed and their women and children were taken as captives; the Prophet (ﷺ) got Juwairiya on that day

bukhari:2541.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the raid on the Banu al-Mustaliq was a defensive preemptive strike against a tribe mobilizing for war, and that Muhammad's taking of Juwayriyya was a compassionate political marriage meant to emancipate her people. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad launched a surprise attack against them (*aghāra 'alā Banī al-Muṣṭaliq*) while they were completely heedless and unawares (*wa-hum ghārrūn*) and peacefully watering their livestock (*wa-an'āmuhum tusqā 'alā al-mā'*), slaughtering their men and enslaving their women and children (*wa-sabā dharāriyyahum*). Furthermore, the parallel narration in `muslim:4519` (alongside Al-Nawawī's and Ibn Ḥajar's commentaries) cites this exact raid to establish the legal permissibility of attacking disbelievers without prior warning, while `bukhari:4138` records that Muhammad's soldiers immediately subjected the captive women to sexual slavery using coitus interruptus (*'azl*) so they could still be sold for ransom.

bukhari:6262.note: After the people of Qurayza surrendered to the judgment of Sa'd, he decreed that their fighting men (muqatilatuhum) be killed and their women and children (dharariyyuhum) be taken captive, which Muhammad ratified by declaring that Sa'd had judged according to the judgment of the King (Allah) ([Quran 33:26](quran://33/26)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ أَهْلَ، قُرَيْظَةَ نَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِ سَعْدٍ فَأَرْسَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَيْهِ فَجَاءَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ قُومُوا إِلَى سَيِّدِكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ أَوْ قَالَ ‏"‏ خَيْرِكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَعَدَ عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏"‏ هَؤُلاَءِ نَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَإِنِّي أَحْكُمُ أَنْ تُقْتَلَ مُقَاتِلَتُهُمْ، وَتُسْبَى ذَرَارِيُّهُمْ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ لَقَدْ حَكَمْتَ بِمَا حَكَمَ بِهِ الْمَلِكُ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The people of (the tribe of) Quraiza agreed upon to accept the verdict of Sa`d. The Prophet (ﷺ) sent for him (Sa`d) and he came. The Prophet (ﷺ) said (to those people), "Get up for your chief or the best among you!" Sa`d sat beside the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Prophet (ﷺ) said (to him), "These people have agreed to accept your verdict." Sa`d said, "So I give my judgment that their warriors should be killed and their women and children should be taken as captives." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "You have judged according to the King's (Allah's) judgment."

bukhari:6262.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Banu Qurayza voluntarily selected Sa'd bin Mu'adh as an independent arbitrator, that he merely applied Jewish Torah law (Deuteronomy 20:10–14) rather than Islamic law, and that only active combatants guilty of treason were executed. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad ratified the massacre as the direct decree of Allah (`laqad ḥakamta bimā ḥakama bihi al-Malik`—"You have judged according to what the King [Allah] has judged"), a divine sanction further confirmed in [Quran 33:26](quran://33/26). Furthermore, as Ibn Hajar explains in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* alongside parallel Sahih narrations (Sunan Abi Dawud 4404; Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1584), "warriors" (`muqātilatuhum`) was defined not by proving individual treason, but by forcibly inspecting surrendered boys for pubic hair (`man anbata`) and beheading every male who had reached biological puberty.

bukhari:6262.note: When the surrendered tribe of Qurayza submitted to Sa'd's verdict, he judged that their fighting men be killed and their women and offspring (dharariyyuhum) be enslaved as captives (tusba), a ruling Muhammad endorsed as the direct judgment of the King (Allah) ([Quran 33:26](quran://33/26)).
