problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ أَهْلَ، قُرَيْظَةَ نَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِ سَعْدٍ فَأَرْسَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَيْهِ فَجَاءَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ قُومُوا إِلَى سَيِّدِكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ أَوْ قَالَ ‏"‏ خَيْرِكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَعَدَ عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏"‏ هَؤُلاَءِ نَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَإِنِّي أَحْكُمُ أَنْ تُقْتَلَ مُقَاتِلَتُهُمْ، وَتُسْبَى ذَرَارِيُّهُمْ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ لَقَدْ حَكَمْتَ بِمَا حَكَمَ بِهِ الْمَلِكُ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The people of (the tribe of) Quraiza agreed upon to accept the verdict of Sa`d. The Prophet (ﷺ) sent for him (Sa`d) and he came. The Prophet (ﷺ) said (to those people), "Get up for your chief or the best among you!" Sa`d sat beside the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Prophet (ﷺ) said (to him), "These people have agreed to accept your verdict." Sa`d said, "So I give my judgment that their warriors should be killed and their women and children should be taken as captives." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "You have judged according to the King's (Allah's) judgment."

bukhari:6262.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that taking the women and children of Banu Qurayza was a merciful humanitarian measure to shelter and feed dependents left behind after their men were executed for treason, or that it simply followed Torah arbitration. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `wa-tusbā dharārīyuhum` (using the legal verb *tusbā*, meaning to seize women and offspring as chattel war-captives) and declares this enslavement to be the direct judgment of Allah (`ḥakama bihi al-Malik`). Moreover, as Ibn Hajar documents in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, these captive women and children were distributed as property (`ghanīmah`) among the Muslim soldiers for concubinage and labor—with a portion sent to Najd to be sold in exchange for horses and weapons—refuting any claim of humanitarian guardianship.

bukhari:25.note: Muhammad declares that he has been commanded to fight the people (`al-nās`) until they testify to the Islamic creed, establish prayer, and pay zakat, stating that only upon doing so do they protect their blood and property from him. Even where classical commentators like Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi qualify 'the people' as polytheists ([Quran 9:5](quran://9/5)) or exempt tribute-paying People of the Book ([Quran 9:29](quran://9/29)), the mandate explicitly makes the inviolability of non-Muslim life and property conditional upon either conversion to Islam or tributary subjugation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَشْهَدُوا أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ، وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلاَةَ، وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ، فَإِذَا فَعَلُوا ذَلِكَ عَصَمُوا مِنِّي دِمَاءَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ إِلاَّ بِحَقِّ الإِسْلاَمِ، وَحِسَابُهُمْ عَلَى اللَّهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: I have been ordered (by Allah) to fight against the people until they testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah and that Muhammad is Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), and offer the prayers perfectly and give the obligatory charity, so if they perform that, then they save their lives and property from me except for Islamic laws and then their reckoning (accounts) will be done by Allah

bukhari:25.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that 'the people' (*al-nās*) is a general term intended with a restricted meaning (*'āmm urīda bihi al-khuṣūṣ*) referring solely to hostile, treaty-breaking Arab polytheists, and that the verb *uqātila* implies reciprocal defensive combat. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the condition for sparing their blood and property (*'aṣamū minnī dimā'ahum wa-amwālahum*) is not a military ceasefire, but full religious conversion—testifying to the *Shahādah*, establishing prayer, and paying *zakāh* (*ḥattā yashhadū an lā ilāha illā Allāh... wa-yuqīmū al-ṣalāh wa-yu'tū al-zakāh*). Classical commentators like Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) and Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) confirm that this mandate parallels the Verse of the Sword ([Quran 9:5](quran://9/5)), leaving non-Muslims with no inviolability of life or wealth unless they embrace Islam or, if they are People of the Book, submit to paying the *jizyah* tribute ([Quran 9:29](quran://9/29)).

bukhari:4355.note: At Muhammad's request to be relieved of the rival sanctuary of Dhu al-Khalasa (the Yemeni Ka'ba), Jarir led 150 riders to demolish the structure and kill everyone they found there. Upon being informed of what they had done, Muhammad invoked blessings upon Jarir's raiders and the tribe of Ahmas.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ لِي النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ أَلاَ تُرِيحُنِي مِنْ ذِي الْخَلَصَةِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَنَفَرْتُ فِي مِائَةٍ وَخَمْسِينَ رَاكِبًا، فَكَسَرْنَاهُ وَقَتَلْنَا مَنْ وَجَدْنَا عِنْدَهُ، فَأَتَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ، فَدَعَا لَنَا وَلأَحْمَسَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me, "Won't you relieve me from Dhu-l- Khalasa?" So I set out with one-hundred-and-fifty riders, and we dismantled it and killed whoever was present there. Then I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and he invoked good upon us and Al- Ahmas (tribe)

bukhari:4355.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the expedition to Dhu-l-Khalasa was a defensive military operation against hostile tribes plotting against Medina, or that Jarir's forces only fought back after being attacked while peacefully dismantling an idol. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad initiated an unprovoked religious purge solely to eliminate a rival sanctuary—asking, "Won't you relieve me from Dhu-l-Khalasa?" (أَلاَ تُرِيحُنِي مِنْ ذِي الْخَلَصَةِ)—whereupon 150 horsemen rode out, burned and demolished the temple (فَحَرَّقْنَاهَا بِالنَّارِ وَكَسَرْنَاهَا in bukhari:4357), and indiscriminately slaughtered everyone at the site: "and we killed whoever we found near it" (وَقَتَلْنَا مَنْ وَجَدْنَا عِنْدَهُ). Rather than rebuking this massacre of worshippers and custodians at their own sanctuary, Muhammad celebrated the report by invoking blessings upon the Ahmas raiders and their horses five times (bukhari:4357; cf. Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī).

bukhari:3168.note: During his final illness in AD 632—after his companions disputed his request to write a guiding document and asked whether he was speaking deliriously—Muhammad commanded the expulsion of all polytheists (al-mushrikin) from the Arabian Peninsula, while his third dying injunction was forgotten by the narrator. Although this specific report uses the term polytheists, parallel narrations (such as bukhari:3167) and classical legal commentators extend the expulsion mandate to Jews and Christians as well.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: اشْتَدَّ بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَجَعُهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ ائْتُونِي بِكَتِفٍ أَكْتُبْ لَكُمْ كِتَابًا لاَ تَضِلُّوا بَعْدَهُ أَبَدًا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَتَنَازَعُوا وَلاَ يَنْبَغِي عِنْدَ نَبِيٍّ تَنَازُعٌ فَقَالُوا مَا لَهُ أَهَجَرَ اسْتَفْهِمُوهُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ ذَرُونِي، فَالَّذِي أَنَا فِيهِ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا تَدْعُونِي إِلَيْهِ ـ فَأَمَرَهُمْ بِثَلاَثٍ قَالَ ـ أَخْرِجُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ مِنْ جَزِيرَةِ الْعَرَبِ، وَأَجِيزُوا الْوَفْدَ بِنَحْوِ مَا كُنْتُ أُجِيزُهُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When the condition (i.e. health) of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) deteriorated, he said, 'Bring me a bone of scapula, so that I may write something for you after which you will never go astray.'The people differed in their opinions although it was improper to differ in front of a prophet, They said, 'What is wrong with him? Do you think he is delirious? Ask him (to understand). The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, 'Leave me as I am in a better state than what you are asking me to do.' Then the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered them to do three things saying, 'Turn out all the pagans from the Arabian Peninsula, show respect to all foreign delegates by giving them gifts as I used to do.' "

bukhari:3168.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the command to expel the *mushrikīn* (polytheists) applied only to hostile pagan idolaters who violated treaties, or was geographically restricted to the immediate sanctuary of Mecca and Medina while sparing peaceful Jews and Christians. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `أَخْرِجُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ مِنْ جَزِيرَةِ الْعَرَبِ` ("Expel the *mushrikīn* from the Arabian Peninsula"), which Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* explains is clarified by parallel *Ṣaḥīḥ* narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1767a) where Muhammad commands: "I will certainly expel the Jews and the Christians from the Arabian Peninsula until I leave none but a Muslim" (`لَأُخْرِجَنَّ الْيَهُودَ وَالنَّصَارَى مِنْ جَزِيرَةِ الْعَرَبِ حَتَّى لَا أَدَعَ إِلَّا مُسْلِمًا`). Furthermore, Caliph ‘Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb executed this exact deathbed mandate by forcibly deporting the peaceful, treaty-abiding Jewish and Christian communities of Khaybar and Najran based purely on their religious identity.

bukhari:3167.note: Muhammad went to the Jewish house of study (Bayt al-Midras) and told the Jews to embrace Islam in order to be safe, declaring that the earth belongs to Allah and His Messenger and that he intended to expel them from the land after permitting them to sell whatever property they could.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَسْلِمُوا تَسْلَمُوا، وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ الأَرْضَ لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ، وَإِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُجْلِيَكُمْ مِنْ هَذِهِ الأَرْضِ، فَمَنْ يَجِدْ مِنْكُمْ بِمَالِهِ شَيْئًا فَلْيَبِعْهُ، وَإِلاَّ فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ الأَرْضَ لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He said to them, "If you embrace Islam, you will be safe. You should know that the earth belongs to Allah and His Apostle, and I want to expel you from this land. So, if anyone amongst you owns some property, he is permitted to sell it, otherwise you should know that the Earth belongs to Allah and His Apostle

bukhari:3167.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this ultimatum was a localized political measure directed at a Medinan Jewish tribe (such as Banu Qaynuqa or Banu Nadir) for allegedly violating a treaty, claiming that permitting them to sell their property demonstrates benevolence. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states no treaty violation whatsoever, recording instead that Muhammad marched unprovoked into their synagogue (*Bayt al-Midrās*) and issued a purely religious ultimatum—"Submit to Islam and you will be safe" (*aslimū taslamū*)—justified solely by the supremacist claim that "the earth belongs to Allah and His Messenger" (*al-arḍa lillāhi wa-rasūlihi*). Furthermore, both Al-Bukhārī (citing this under *Kitāb al-Ikrāh* [Coercion] in `bukhari:6944`) and Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* on `muslim:4594`) treat this decree not as a penalty for treason, but as foundational legal proof for religious coercion and the permanent expulsion of Jews and Christians from the Arabian Peninsula.

muslim:4592.note: Muhammad expelled all the Jews of Medina, including Banu Nadir, Banu Qaynuqa (the tribe of Abdullah ibn Salam), the Jews of Banu Haritha, and every other Jew who was in the city.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَجْلَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَنِي النَّضِيرِ وَأَقَرَّ قُرَيْظَةَ وَمَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ حَتَّى حَارَبَتْ قُرَيْظَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَقَتَلَ رِجَالَهُمْ وَقَسَمَ نِسَاءَهُمْ وَأَوْلاَدَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ بَيْنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ إِلاَّ أَنَّ بَعْضَهُمْ لَحِقُوا بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَآمَنَهُمْ وَأَسْلَمُوا وَأَجْلَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَهُودَ الْمَدِينَةِ كُلَّهُمْ بَنِي قَيْنُقَاعَ - وَهُمْ قَوْمُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَلاَمٍ - وَيَهُودَ بَنِي حَارِثَةَ وَكُلَّ يَهُودِيٍّ كَانَ بِالْمَدِينَةِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: the Jews of Banu Nadir and Banu Quraiza fought against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who expelled Banu Nadir, and allowed Quraiza to stay on, and granted favour to them until they too fought against him Then he killed their men, and distributed their women, children and properties among the Muslims, except that some of them had joined the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who granted them security. They embraced Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned out all the Jews of Medina. Banu Qainuqa' (the tribe of 'Abdullah b. Salim) and the Jews of Banu Haritha and every other Jew who was in Medina

muslim:4592.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad only penalized specific tribes that engaged in military hostilities while allowing peaceful Jewish residents to remain in Medina. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad expelled all the Jews of Medina (`وَأَجْلَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَهُودَ الْمَدِينَةِ كُلَّهُمْ`), including Banu Nadir, Banu Qaynuqa, and the Jews of Banu Haritha. The narration concludes with the unqualified universal clause that he turned out every Jew who was in Medina (`وَكُلَّ يَهُودِيٍّ كَانَ بِالْمَدِينَةِ`), refuting the claim that expulsion was restricted to active combatants.

muslim:4592.note: After initially allowing the Jewish tribe of Banu Qurayza to remain in Medina and granting them favor, Muhammad killed their men when they later fought against him, sparing only those who joined him, received security, and embraced Islam.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَجْلَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَنِي النَّضِيرِ وَأَقَرَّ قُرَيْظَةَ وَمَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ حَتَّى حَارَبَتْ قُرَيْظَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَقَتَلَ رِجَالَهُمْ وَقَسَمَ نِسَاءَهُمْ وَأَوْلاَدَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ بَيْنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ إِلاَّ أَنَّ بَعْضَهُمْ لَحِقُوا بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَآمَنَهُمْ وَأَسْلَمُوا
problematic_excerpt.english: the Jews of Banu Nadir and Banu Quraiza fought against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who expelled Banu Nadir, and allowed Quraiza to stay on, and granted favour to them until they too fought against him Then he killed their men, and distributed their women, children and properties among the Muslims, except that some of them had joined the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who granted them security. They embraced Islam.

muslim:4592.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the execution of the men of Banu Qurayza was a targeted legal punishment for individual wartime treason rather than collective execution or religious coercion. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad killed their men (`فَقَتَلَ رِجَالَهُمْ`) as an entire group without distinguishing between combatants and non-combatants. Furthermore, the narration notes that the only men granted security (`فَآمَنَهُمْ`) were those who joined Muhammad and embraced Islam (`وَأَسْلَمُوا`), demonstrating that survival depended on defecting and converting rather than individual judicial exoneration.

muslim:4592.note: Following the conflict with Banu Qurayza and the killing of their men, Muhammad distributed their women, children, and properties among the Muslims, excluding those who had joined him, received security, and embraced Islam.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: حَتَّى حَارَبَتْ قُرَيْظَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَقَتَلَ رِجَالَهُمْ وَقَسَمَ نِسَاءَهُمْ وَأَوْلاَدَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ بَيْنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ إِلاَّ أَنَّ بَعْضَهُمْ لَحِقُوا بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَآمَنَهُمْ وَأَسْلَمُوا
problematic_excerpt.english: until they too fought against him Then he killed their men, and distributed their women, children and properties among the Muslims, except that some of them had joined the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who granted them security. They embraced Islam.

muslim:4592.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that taking the women and children of Banu Qurayza was a protective welfare arrangement to care for dependents left behind after the conflict. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad divided their women, their children, and their properties among the Muslims (`وَقَسَمَ نِسَاءَهُمْ وَأَوْلاَدَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ بَيْنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ`). By governing women, children, and material wealth (`أَمْوَالَهُمْ`) with the single verb of division (`قَسَمَ`), the text treats the surviving families as war plunder distributed to the very forces that had just executed their husbands and fathers (`فَقَتَلَ رِجَالَهُمْ`).

bukhari:3159.note: During Caliph Umar's invasion of Persia, the Companion Al-Mughira declares to the Persian envoy that Muhammad commanded Muslims to fight them until they either worship Allah alone or pay the Jizya tribute ([Quran 9:29](quran://9/29)), adding that slain Muslims enter Paradise while survivors become masters over the conquered.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَمَرَنَا نَبِيُّنَا رَسُولُ رَبِّنَا صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ نَقَاتِلَكُمْ حَتَّى تَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَحْدَهُ أَوْ تُؤَدُّوا الْجِزْيَةَ، وَأَخْبَرَنَا نَبِيُّنَا صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنْ رِسَالَةِ رَبِّنَا أَنَّهُ مَنْ قُتِلَ مِنَّا صَارَ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ فِي نَعِيمٍ لَمْ يَرَ مِثْلَهَا قَطُّ، وَمَنْ بَقِيَ مِنَّا مَلَكَ رِقَابَكُمْ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Our Prophet, the Messenger of our Lord, has ordered us to fight you till you worship Allah Alone or give Jizya (i.e. tribute); and our Prophet has informed us that our Lord says:-- "Whoever amongst us is killed (i.e. martyred), shall go to Paradise to lead such a luxurious life as he has never seen, and whoever amongst us remains alive, shall become your master."

bukhari:3159.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the early Islamic invasions of Persia and Byzantium were purely pre-emptive, defensive wars against imperial aggression, or that Al-Mughira was merely expressing personal military bravado rather than binding prophetic doctrine. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Caliph Umar personally planned and initiated these offensive invasions (*fī maghāziyya hādhihi*) and that Muhammad directly commanded Muslims to wage war strictly for religious and political subjugation until the conquered peoples worship Allah alone or pay the *jizya* tribute (*fa-amaranā nabiyyunā... an nuqātilakum ḥattā taʿbudū Allāha waḥdahu aw tuʾaddū al-jizyata*). Furthermore, far from being a defensive or humanitarian liberation, the divine message cited by Al-Mughira—enforcing Quran 9:29 and affirmed by Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—explicitly guarantees that surviving Muslim conquerors will literally 'own your necks' (*malaka riqābakum*) through enslavement and mastery.

muslim:4915.note: After sending Busaisah as a spy (`'aynan`) to track Abu Sufyan's caravan, Muhammad declares, 'Indeed, we have a target we are pursuing (`ṭalibah`)'—softened in the published translation to 'We are in need (of men)'—and orders only men with mounts immediately present to ride out to Badr without waiting for animals grazing in upper Medina. When the polytheists approach at Badr, Muhammad calls his men to 'rise up to a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth' and guarantees Umayr ibn al-Humam a place in it, prompting Umayr to declare that living long enough to finish eating his dates would be 'a long life,' throw them away, and fight until he is killed.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: بَعَثَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بُسَيْسَةَ عَيْنًا يَنْظُرُ مَا صَنَعَتْ عِيرُ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ فَجَاءَ وَمَا فِي الْبَيْتِ أَحَدٌ غَيْرِي وَغَيْرُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ لاَ أَدْرِي مَا اسْتَثْنَى بَعْضَ نِسَائِهِ قَالَ فَحَدَّثَهُ الْحَدِيثَ قَالَ فَخَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَتَكَلَّمَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ لَنَا طَلِبَةً فَمَنْ كَانَ ظَهْرُهُ حَاضِرًا فَلْيَرْكَبْ مَعَنَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَجَعَلَ رِجَالٌ يَسْتَأْذِنُونَهُ فِي ظُهْرَانِهِمْ فِي عُلْوِ الْمَدِينَةِ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ إِلاَّ مَنْ كَانَ ظَهْرُهُ حَاضِرًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَانْطَلَقَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَصْحَابُهُ حَتَّى سَبَقُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ إِلَى بَدْرٍ وَجَاءَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لاَ يُقَدِّمَنَّ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ إِلَى شَىْءٍ حَتَّى أَكُونَ أَنَا دُونَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَدَنَا الْمُشْرِكُونَ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ قُومُوا إِلَى جَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا السَّمَوَاتُ وَالأَرْضُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ يَقُولُ عُمَيْرُ بْنُ الْحُمَامِ الأَنْصَارِيُّ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ جَنَّةٌ عَرْضُهَا السَّمَوَاتُ وَالأَرْضُ قَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ بَخٍ بَخٍ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ مَا يَحْمِلُكَ عَلَى قَوْلِكَ بَخٍ بَخٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ لاَ وَاللَّهِ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِلاَّ رَجَاءَةَ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِنَّكَ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَأَخْرَجَ تَمَرَاتٍ مِنْ قَرْنِهِ فَجَعَلَ يَأْكُلُ مِنْهُنَّ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَئِنْ أَنَا حَيِيتُ حَتَّى آكُلَ تَمَرَاتِي هَذِهِ إِنَّهَا لَحَيَاةٌ طَوِيلَةٌ - قَالَ - فَرَمَى بِمَا كَانَ مَعَهُ مِنَ التَّمْرِ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَاتَلَهُمْ حَتَّى قُتِلَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Busaisah as a scout to see what the caravan of Abu Sufyan was doing. He came (back and met the Prophet in his house) where there was nobody except myself and the Messenger of Allah. I do not remember whether he (Hadrat Anas) made an exception of some wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) or not and told him the news of the caravan. (Having heard the news), the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out (hurriedly), spoke to the people and said: We are in need (of men) ; whoever has an animal to ride upon ready with him should ride with us. People began to ask him permission for bringing their riding animals which were grazing on the hillocks near Medina. He said: No. (I want) only those who have their riding animals ready. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions proceeded towards Badr and reached there forestalling the polytheists (of Mecca). When the polytheists (also) reached there, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: None of you should step forward to (do) anything unless I am ahead of him. The polytheists (now) advanced (towards us), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said. Get up to enter Paradise which is equal in width to the heavens and the earth. 'Umair b. al- Humam al-Ansari said: Messenger of Allah, is Paradise equal in extent to the heavens and the earth? He said: Yes. 'Umair said: My goodness! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked him: What prompted you to utter these words (i. e. my goodness! ')? He said: Messenger of Allah, nothing but the desire that I be among its residents. He said: Thou art (surely) amona its residents. He took out dates from his bag and began to eat them. Then he said: If I were to live until I have eaten all these dates of mine, it would be a long life. (The narrator said): He threw away all the dates he had with him. Then he fought the enemies until he was killed

muslim:4915.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the expedition to Badr was a defensive response to Meccan military aggression, often relying on the softened English rendering ('We are in need of men') to frame the mobilization as an emergency call for defense. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad first sent Busaisah as a scout ('aynan) to track Abu Sufyan's trade caravan ('īr Abī Sufyān) and hurriedly mobilized only men with ready mounts (man kāna ẓahruhu ḥāḍiran) by declaring, 'Indeed, we have a target we are pursuing' (inna lanā ṭalibatan), reaching Badr ahead of the polytheists (sabaqū al-mushrikīna ilā Badr). Once the Meccans arrived, Muhammad called his men to advance by promising immediate entry into Paradise (qūmū ilā jannatin), prompting Umayr ibn al-Humam to throw away his dates and fight until he was killed (qātalahum ḥattā qutila).

muslim:4519.note: Answering whether an invitation to Islam must precede combat, Nafi' states that this practice belonged only to early Islam. As proof, he cites the eyewitness report of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar—who fought in the army—recording that Muhammad raided Banu al-Mustaliq without warning while they were heedless and watering their livestock, killing their fighters and enslaving their captives ([Quran 9:5](quran://9/5)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى نَافِعٍ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ الدُّعَاءِ، قَبْلَ الْقِتَالِ قَالَ فَكَتَبَ إِلَىَّ إِنَّمَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ فِي أَوَّلِ الإِسْلاَمِ قَدْ أَغَارَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى بَنِي الْمُصْطَلِقِ وَهُمْ غَارُّونَ وَأَنْعَامُهُمْ تُسْقَى عَلَى الْمَاءِ فَقَتَلَ مُقَاتِلَتَهُمْ وَسَبَى سَبْيَهُمْ وَأَصَابَ يَوْمَئِذٍ - قَالَ يَحْيَى أَحْسِبُهُ قَالَ - جُوَيْرِيَةَ - أَوْ قَالَ الْبَتَّةَ - ابْنَةَ الْحَارِثِ
problematic_excerpt.english: I wrote to Nafi' inquiring from him whether it was necessary to extend (to the disbelievers) an invitation to accept (Islam) before meeting them in fight. He wrote (in reply) to me that it was necessary in the early days of Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a raid upon Banu Mustaliq while they were unaware and their cattle were having a drink at the water. He killed those who fought and imprisoned others. On that very day, he captured Juwairiya bint al-Harith.

muslim:4519.literal_translation: I wrote to Nafi' asking him about extending an invitation [to Islam] before fighting. He wrote to me: 'That was only in the early days of Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) raided Banu al-Mustaliq while they were heedless and their livestock were being watered at the watering place; he killed their fighters and enslaved their captives [women and children], and on that day he acquired Juwayriyya bint al-Harith.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَسَبَى سَبْيَهُمْ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and imprisoned others
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and took their captives [women and children] into slavery
translation_issue.explanation: In classical Arabic lexicography, 'sabā / saby' denotes taking women and children as war captives into slavery (in contrast to 'muqātilatahum', the male combatants who were killed), which the published rendering softens to 'and imprisoned others'.

muslim:4519.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islamic warfare is strictly defensive and requires formal warnings before hostilities, or that the Banu al-Mustaliq were actively mobilizing for war when attacked. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that extending an invitation to Islam before fighting (*al-duʿāʾ qabla al-qitāl*) was only required in the early days of Islam (*innamā kāna dhālika fī awwali al-islām*), and that Muhammad raided (*aghāra*) the Banu al-Mustaliq while they were heedless and watering their livestock (*wa-hum ghārrūna wa-anʿāmuhum tusqā ʿalā al-māʾ*). Rather than encountering a mobilized army, the narration records that the raiding troops caught the tribe unaware, killed their fighters (*fa-qatala muqātilatahum*), and enslaved their captives (*wa-sabā sabyahum*) in accordance with [Quran 9:5](quran://9/5) (see also bukhari:2541 and muslim:4520).

muslim:4519.note: According to the eyewitness 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, during the unwarned raid on Banu al-Mustaliq at their watering place, Muhammad killed their combatants, enslaved their women and children (*sabā sabyahum*, softened in translation as 'imprisoned others'; cf. bukhari:2541), and acquired Juwayriyya bint al-Harith as a war captive ([Quran 4:24](quran://4/24), [Quran 33:50](quran://33/50)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَدْ أَغَارَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلَى بَنِي الْمُصْطَلِقِ وَهُمْ غَارُّونَ وَأَنْعَامُهُمْ تُسْقَى عَلَى الْمَاءِ فَقَتَلَ مُقَاتِلَتَهُمْ وَسَبَى سَبْيَهُمْ وَأَصَابَ يَوْمَئِذٍ - قَالَ يَحْيَى أَحْسِبُهُ قَالَ - جُوَيْرِيَةَ - أَوْ قَالَ الْبَتَّةَ - ابْنَةَ الْحَارِثِ
problematic_excerpt.english: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a raid upon Banu Mustaliq while they were unaware and their cattle were having a drink at the water. He killed those who fought and imprisoned others. On that very day, he captured Juwairiya bint al-Harith.

muslim:4519.literal_translation: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) raided Banu al-Mustaliq while they were heedless and their livestock were being watered at the watering place; he killed their fighters and enslaved their captives [women and children], and on that day he acquired Juwayriyya bint al-Harith.

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَسَبَى سَبْيَهُمْ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and imprisoned others
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and took their captives [women and children] into slavery
translation_issue.explanation: In classical Arabic lexicography, 'sabā / saby' denotes taking women and children as war captives into slavery (in contrast to 'muqātilatahum', the male combatants who were killed), which the published rendering softens to 'and imprisoned others'.

muslim:4519.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad merely detained prisoners of war during this campaign, appealing to softened English translations that render the text as 'and imprisoned others.' However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *wa-sabā sabyahum* ('and he enslaved their captives'), which specifically denotes taking non-combatant women and children into chattel slavery after killing the male fighters (*fa-qatala muqātilatahum*). The narration further records that on that day he acquired (*aṣāba*) Juwayriyya bint al-Harith as a war captive, reflecting the enslavement of captured women permitted in [Quran 4:24](quran://4/24) and [Quran 33:50](quran://33/50) (see also bukhari:2541, bukhari:2542, and muslim:4520).

bukhari:4557.note: In his exegesis of [Quran 3:110](quran://3/110)—applying Muhammad's prophetic statement regarding people entering Paradise in chains (bukhari:3010)—Abu Huraira declares that Muslims are "the best of peoples for the people" because they bring people with chains on their necks until they enter Islam ([2 Corinthians 10:4](bible://2cor/10/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ‏{‏كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ‏}‏ قَالَ خَيْرَ النَّاسِ لِلنَّاسِ، تَأْتُونَ بِهِمْ فِي السَّلاَسِلِ فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ حَتَّى يَدْخُلُوا فِي الإِسْلاَمِ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Verse:--"You (true Muslims) are the best of peoples ever raised up for mankind." means, the best of peoples for the people, as you bring them with chains on their necks till they embrace Islam

bukhari:4557.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the 'chains' are merely a metaphor for spiritual guidance or refer strictly to defensive prisoners of war who later converted voluntarily after witnessing Muslim conduct. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *ta'tūna bihim fī al-salāsil fī a'nāqihim ḥattā yadkhulū fī al-islām* ('you bring them with chains on their necks until they enter Islam'), making physical captivity by the neck the direct condition (*ḥattā*, 'until') for their conversion. Furthermore, Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* (on bukhari:3010 and 4557) and Ibn Kathīr in his *Tafsīr* of Quran 3:110 explicitly confirm this refers to literal non-Muslims captured in Jihad and bound in fetters until they embrace Islam.

bukhari:4028.note: Ibn Umar reports that after Banu al-Nadir and Banu Qurayza fought against Muhammad, he exiled Banu al-Nadir and subsequently killed the men of Banu Qurayza—sparing only those who joined him and converted to Islam—while dividing their women, children, and property among the Muslims ([Quran 33:26](quran://33/26); [Quran 59:2](quran://59/2)). He also exiled all the Jews of Medina, including Banu Qaynuqa', the Jews of Banu Haritha, and every remaining Jew in the city.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: حَارَبَتِ النَّضِيرُ وَقُرَيْظَةُ، فَأَجْلَى بَنِي النَّضِيرِ، وَأَقَرَّ قُرَيْظَةَ وَمَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ، حَتَّى حَارَبَتْ قُرَيْظَةُ فَقَتَلَ رِجَالَهُمْ وَقَسَمَ نِسَاءَهُمْ وَأَوْلاَدَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ بَيْنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ إِلاَّ بَعْضَهُمْ لَحِقُوا بِالنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَآمَنَهُمْ وَأَسْلَمُوا، وَأَجْلَى يَهُودَ الْمَدِينَةِ كُلَّهُمْ بَنِي قَيْنُقَاعَ وَهُمْ رَهْطُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَلاَمٍ وَيَهُودَ بَنِي حَارِثَةَ، وَكُلَّ يَهُودِ الْمَدِينَةِ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Bani An-Nadir and Bani Quraiza fought (against the Prophet (ﷺ) violating their peace treaty), so the Prophet exiled Bani An-Nadir and allowed Bani Quraiza to remain at their places (in Medina) taking nothing from them till they fought against the Prophet (ﷺ) again) . He then killed their men and distributed their women, children and property among the Muslims, but some of them came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and he granted them safety, and they embraced Islam. He exiled all the Jews from Medina. They were the Jews of Bani Qainuqa', the tribe of `Abdullah bin Salam and the Jews of Bani Haritha and all the other Jews of Medina

bukhari:4028.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the execution of Banu Qurayza and the expulsion of Medina's Jews were strictly targeted military penalties for wartime treason rather than acts of collective punishment or religious intolerance. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad executed their men (*fa-qatala rijālahum*)—defined in parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:4121) by the physical inspection of pubic hair rather than individual trials—spared only those who converted to Islam (*wa-aslamū*), and subsequently expelled "all the Jews of Medina" (*kulla yahūdi l-madīnati*), including non-combatant tribes like Banu Haritha. As Ibn Hajar affirms in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, this total purge fulfilled the broader Islamic mandate to expel all non-Muslims from the Hijaz regardless of individual treaty compliance.

bukhari:4028.note: Ibn Umar reports that after Banu Qurayza fought against Muhammad and their men were killed, Muhammad divided and distributed their women, children, and property as spoils among the Muslims, sparing only those who joined him and converted to Islam ([Quran 33:26](quran://33/26)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: حَارَبَتِ النَّضِيرُ وَقُرَيْظَةُ، فَأَجْلَى بَنِي النَّضِيرِ، وَأَقَرَّ قُرَيْظَةَ وَمَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ، حَتَّى حَارَبَتْ قُرَيْظَةُ فَقَتَلَ رِجَالَهُمْ وَقَسَمَ نِسَاءَهُمْ وَأَوْلاَدَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ بَيْنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ إِلاَّ بَعْضَهُمْ لَحِقُوا بِالنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَآمَنَهُمْ وَأَسْلَمُوا، وَأَجْلَى يَهُودَ الْمَدِينَةِ كُلَّهُمْ بَنِي قَيْنُقَاعَ وَهُمْ رَهْطُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَلاَمٍ وَيَهُودَ بَنِي حَارِثَةَ، وَكُلَّ يَهُودِ الْمَدِينَةِ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Bani An-Nadir and Bani Quraiza fought (against the Prophet (ﷺ) violating their peace treaty), so the Prophet exiled Bani An-Nadir and allowed Bani Quraiza to remain at their places (in Medina) taking nothing from them till they fought against the Prophet (ﷺ) again) . He then killed their men and distributed their women, children and property among the Muslims, but some of them came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and he granted them safety, and they embraced Islam. He exiled all the Jews from Medina. They were the Jews of Bani Qainuqa', the tribe of `Abdullah bin Salam and the Jews of Bani Haritha and all the other Jews of Medina

bukhari:4028.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that distributing the women and children of Banu Qurayza was a merciful humanitarian measure to house and feed war widows and orphans, or merely the application of Jewish Torah law via Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's arbitration. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad divided their women and children directly alongside their confiscated wealth as chattel property (*wa-qasama nisāʾahum wa-awlādahum wa-amwālahum bayna l-muslimīna*), treating human beings and material plunder identically under the verb *qasama* (to partition war booty). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:3043, 4121) confirm that Muhammad ratified this mass enslavement (*wa-tusbā dhurriyyatuhum*) not as a concession to Jewish law, but as the direct judgment of Allah Himself revealed in Quran 33:26.

bukhari:1399.note: Umar quotes Muhammad declaring that he was ordered to fight people until they testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah, whereby they save their lives and property from him "except by its right" ([Quran 9:5](quran://9/5)). Following Muhammad's death in AD 632, Abu Bakr invoked this exception clause—stating that zakat is the compulsory right of property—to wage war against Arab tribes that apostatized or separated prayer from zakat, vowing to fight them even over a withheld young female goat, a ruling Umar accepted and classical commentators (such as Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawi) affirm as a binding obligation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَمَّا تُوُفِّيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَكَانَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ وَكَفَرَ مَنْ كَفَرَ مِنَ الْعَرَبِ فَقَالَ عُمَرُ ـ رضى الله عنه كَيْفَ تُقَاتِلُ النَّاسَ، وَقَدْ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ‏.‏ فَمَنْ قَالَهَا فَقَدْ عَصَمَ مِنِّي مَالَهُ وَنَفْسَهُ إِلاَّ بِحَقِّهِ، وَحِسَابُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ لأُقَاتِلَنَّ مَنْ فَرَّقَ بَيْنَ الصَّلاَةِ وَالزَّكَاةِ، فَإِنَّ الزَّكَاةَ حَقُّ الْمَالِ، وَاللَّهِ لَوْ مَنَعُونِي عَنَاقًا كَانُوا يُؤَدُّونَهَا إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَقَاتَلْتُهُمْ عَلَى مَنْعِهَا‏.‏ قَالَ عُمَرُ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ فَوَاللَّهِ مَا هُوَ إِلاَّ أَنْ قَدْ شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ فَعَرَفْتُ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) died and Abu Bakr became the caliph some Arabs renegade (reverted to disbelief) (Abu Bakr decided to declare war against them), `Umar, said to Abu Bakr, "How can you fight with these people although Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, 'I have been ordered (by Allah) to fight the people till they say: "None has the right to be worshipped but Allah, and whoever said it then he will save his life and property from me except on trespassing the law (rights and conditions for which he will be punished justly), and his accounts will be with Allah.' " Abu Bakr said, "By Allah! I will fight those who differentiate between the prayer and the Zakat as Zakat is the compulsory right to be taken from the property (according to Allah's orders) By Allah! If they refuse to pay me even a she-kid which they used to pay at the time of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) . I would fight with them for withholding it" Then `Umar said, "By Allah, it was nothing, but Allah opened Abu Bakr's chest towards the decision (to fight) and I came to know that his decision was right

bukhari:1399.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Abu Bakr's AD 632 Ridda campaigns were merely secular enforcement against treasonous tax evasion, and claim—via selective readings of Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that Muhammad's command to fight 'the people' (*al-nās*) targeted only hostile polytheist aggressors. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that a person's life and property only gain immunity (*ʿaṣama minnī mālahu wa-nafsahu*) by professing *lā ilāha illā Allāh* and fulfilling its statutory rights (*illā bi-ḥaqqihi*), which both Umar and Abu Bakr cited as a binding prophetic mandate to wage war (*uqātila al-nās*) over religious compliance. Furthermore, as Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Hajar confirm, Abu Bakr vowed to fight even confessing, praying Muslims (*man farraqa bayna al-ṣalāti wa-al-zakāh*) over a single young she-goat (*ʿanāqan*) or hobble-cord (*ʿiqālan* in `bukhari:1400`), proving that lethal force was used to compel religious obligations.

bukhari:3053.note: During his aggravated illness on Thursday, when Muhammad asked for writing materials to record a document after which his followers would never go astray, those present disputed and said he was speaking deliriously (hajara), prompting him to tell them to leave him alone. At his death, he issued three commands, including the order to expel the polytheists (al-mushrikin) from the Arabian Peninsula—defined in the report as Mecca, Medina, al-Yamama, and Yemen.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: اشْتَدَّ بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَجَعُهُ يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ ائْتُونِي بِكِتَابٍ أَكْتُبْ لَكُمْ كِتَابًا لَنْ تَضِلُّوا بَعْدَهُ أَبَدًا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَتَنَازَعُوا وَلاَ يَنْبَغِي عِنْدَ نَبِيٍّ تَنَازُعٌ فَقَالُوا هَجَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ دَعُونِي فَالَّذِي أَنَا فِيهِ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا تَدْعُونِي إِلَيْهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ وَأَوْصَى عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ بِثَلاَثٍ ‏"‏ أَخْرِجُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ مِنْ جَزِيرَةِ الْعَرَبِ، وَأَجِيزُوا الْوَفْدَ بِنَحْوِ مَا كُنْتُ أُجِيزُهُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ وَنَسِيتُ الثَّالِثَةَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: "On Thursday the illness of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was aggravated and he said, "Fetch me writing materials so that I may have something written to you after which you will never go astray." The people (present there) differed in this matter and people should not differ before a prophet. They said, "Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) is seriously sick.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Let me alone, as the state in which I am now, is better than what you are calling me for." The Prophet (ﷺ) on his death-bed, gave three orders saying, "Expel the pagans from the Arabian Peninsula, respect and give gifts to the foreign delegates as you have seen me dealing with them." I forgot the third (order)"

bukhari:3053.literal_translation: The pain of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intensified on Thursday, so he said: "Bring me writing material so that I may write for you a document after which you will never go astray." But they disputed, and there should be no disputing before a prophet, and they said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is speaking deliriously." He said: "Leave me, for that which I am in is better than what you call me to." And at his death he enjoined three things: "Expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula, and grant gifts to delegations just as I used to grant them." And I forgot the third.

translation_issue.arabic_term: هَجَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم
translation_issue.published_rendering: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) is seriously sick
translation_issue.literal_meaning: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is speaking deliriously / raving
translation_issue.explanation: In classical Arabic lexicons (e.g., Ibn al-Athīr's al-Nihāyah, Lisān al-'Arab, and Lane's Lexicon), hajara (verbal noun hujr) when said of a sick person means to speak deliriously, incoherently, or nonsensically (al-hadhayān) due to fever or pain. The translator replaced 'he is speaking deliriously' with the euphemism 'is seriously sick' to conceal the companions' suggestion that intense illness had caused Muhammad to speak incoherently.

bukhari:3053.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the deathbed command to expel the mushrikīn (الْمُشْرِكِينَ) only targeted hostile, treaty-breaking idolaters within the immediate sanctuary of Mecca and Medina, while claiming the companions' remark hajara (هَجَرَ) merely expressed concern that physical pain had overpowered him. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Jazīrat al-ʿArab (جَزِيرَةِ الْعَرَبِ) encompasses 'Mecca, Medina, Al-Yamama, and Yemen,' and records the companions' blunt charge that 'the Messenger of Allah is raving deliriously' (هَجَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ)—a dispute that caused Muhammad to abandon writing his promised guidance. Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3168; Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:4594) and Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī confirm that this unconditional religious cleansing explicitly targeted Jews and Christians ('I will certainly expel the Jews and the Christians from the Arabian Peninsula until I leave none but a Muslim'), which Caliph ʿUmar enforced by deporting the treaty-abiding communities of Khaybar and Najrān.

bukhari:392.note: Muhammad declares that he has been ordered to fight people until they testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah, pray the Islamic prayer, face the Islamic qibla, and slaughter as Muslims slaughter, stating that only then do their blood and property become inviolable ([Quran 9:5](quran://9/5)). Classical commentators like Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi affirm that this mandate conditions the sanctity of life and property upon adopting Islam and its outward rituals, with an exception only for those who submit to paying the jizyah under [Quran 9:29](quran://9/29) (cf. bukhari:25, muslim:125).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ‏.‏ فَإِذَا قَالُوهَا وَصَلَّوْا صَلاَتَنَا، وَاسْتَقْبَلُوا قِبْلَتَنَا، وَذَبَحُوا ذَبِيحَتَنَا، فَقَدْ حَرُمَتْ عَلَيْنَا دِمَاؤُهُمْ وَأَمْوَالُهُمْ إِلاَّ بِحَقِّهَا، وَحِسَابُهُمْ عَلَى اللَّهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: I have been ordered to fight the people till they say: 'None has the right to be worshipped but Allah.' And if they say so, pray like our prayers, face our Qibla and slaughter as we slaughter, then their blood and property will be sacred to us and we will not interfere with them except legally and their reckoning will be with Allah

bukhari:392.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim—that "the people" (al-nās) is a general term with a restricted meaning (ʿāmm urīda bihi al-khuṣūṣ) referring only to hostile Arabian polytheists, while Jews and Christians are exempted via the jizyah poll tax. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that human blood and property only become inviolable (faqad ḥarumat ʿalaynā dimāʾuhum wa-amwāluhum) on the strict condition (fa-idhā qālūhā) that they recite the shahādah, pray the Islamic prayer, face the qiblah, and perform Islamic slaughter—rendering non-Muslim life and property unprotected by default. Moreover, even under Ibn Ḥajar's classical qualification via Quran 9:5 and 9:29, this prophetic command still mandates offensive jihad to force polytheists into conversion or death and to violently subjugate Jews and Christians until they pay tribute in humiliation.

bukhari:610.note: When campaigning against a people, Muhammad waited until morning and raided them if he did not hear the Islamic call to prayer (adhan); arriving at Khaybar at night in AD 628, he rode out at dawn as its inhabitants came out with their baskets and spades and declared Khaybar's ruin ([Quran 37:177](quran://37/177)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ إِذَا غَزَا بِنَا قَوْمًا لَمْ يَكُنْ يَغْزُو بِنَا حَتَّى يُصْبِحَ وَيَنْظُرَ، فَإِنْ سَمِعَ أَذَانًا كَفَّ عَنْهُمْ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْمَعْ أَذَانًا أَغَارَ عَلَيْهِمْ، قَالَ فَخَرَجْنَا إِلَى خَيْبَرَ فَانْتَهَيْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ لَيْلاً، فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ وَلَمْ يَسْمَعْ أَذَانًا رَكِبَ وَرَكِبْتُ خَلْفَ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ، وَإِنَّ قَدَمِي لَتَمَسُّ قَدَمَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ قَالَ فَخَرَجُوا إِلَيْنَا بِمَكَاتِلِهِمْ وَمَسَاحِيهِمْ فَلَمَّا رَأَوُا النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالُوا مُحَمَّدٌ وَاللَّهِ، مُحَمَّدٌ وَالْخَمِيسُ‏.‏ قَالَ فَلَمَّا رَآهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، خَرِبَتْ خَيْبَرُ، إِنَّا إِذَا نَزَلْنَا بِسَاحَةِ قَوْمٍ فَسَاءَ صَبَاحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) went out with us to fight (in Allah's cause) against any nation, he never allowed us to attack till morning and he would wait and see: if he heard Adhan he would postpone the attack and if he did not hear Adhan he would attack them." Anas added, "We reached Khaibar at night and in the morning when he did not hear the Adhan for the prayer, he (the Prophet ) rode and I rode behind Abi Talha and my foot was touching that of the Prophet. The inhabitants of Khaibar came out with their baskets and spades and when they saw the Prophet (ﷺ) they shouted 'Muhammad! By Allah, Muhammad and his army.' When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saw them, he said, "Allahu-Akbar! Allahu-Akbar! Khaibar is ruined. Whenever we approach a (hostile) nation (to fight), then evil will be the morning of those who have been warned

bukhari:610.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the AD 628 expedition against Khaybar was a defensive strike against mobilized enemy combatants—even inserting the parenthetical word '(hostile)' into English translations—and that listening for the adhān was merely a precaution to avoid friendly fire. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad applied a purely religious litmus test to any people (قَوْمًا, qawman) he approached, launching a predatory dawn raid (أَغَارَ عَلَيْهِمْ, aghāra ʿalayhim) whenever he did not hear the Islamic call to prayer, while the residents of Khaybar emerged completely unmobilized carrying only farming baskets and spades (بِمَكَاتِلِهِمْ وَمَسَاحِيهِمْ). Furthermore, classical commentators like Ibn Hajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī cite Muhammad's invocation of [Quran 37:177](quran://37/177) (فَسَاءَ صَبَاحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ) in this narration to establish the legal ruling that any population that has previously heard the general invitation to Islam and refuses to adopt its rites may be raided by surprise without provocation.

bukhari:2946.note: Muhammad declares that he has been commanded to fight people until they testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah, stating that a person's life and property become protected from him only upon professing this creed (bukhari:25, muslim:125). While classical commentators (such as Ibn Ḥajar and al-Nawawī) apply juristic specification (takhṣīṣ) to exempt People of the Book who pay the jizyah ([Quran 9:29](quran://9/29)) from the unconditional mandate against idolaters ([Quran 9:5](quran://9/5)), the immunity of non-Muslim life and property remains contingent upon either conversion or tribute.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ‏.‏ فَمَنْ قَالَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ، فَقَدْ عَصَمَ مِنِّي نَفْسَهُ وَمَالَهُ، إِلاَّ بِحَقِّهِ، وَحِسَابُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: I have been ordered to fight with the people till they say, 'None has the right to be worshipped but Allah,' and whoever says, 'None has the right to be worshipped but Allah,' his life and property will be saved by me except for Islamic law, and his accounts will be with Allah, (either to punish him or to forgive him)

bukhari:2946.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase 'the people' (*al-nās*) is a general term intended for a specific group (*ʿāmm urīda bihi al-khuṣūṣ*), applying only to hostile 7th-century AD Arab polytheists who broke treaties rather than mandating universal offensive warfare. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that only whoever recites the Islamic creed 'has protected his life and property from me' (*عَصَمَ مِنِّي نَفْسَهُ وَمَالَهُ*), proving that non-Muslim blood and wealth possess no inherent inviolability (*ʿiṣmah*). Furthermore, parallel narrations (bukhari:25, bukhari:392) expand this military ultimatum to require testifying to Muhammad's prophethood, praying, and paying *zakāt*, while Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) and Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) confirm that the only exemption from conversion or death is the violent subjugation and *jizyah* tribute imposed on Jews and Christians under [Quran 9:29](quran://9/29).

bukhari:3823.note: After Muhammad asked Jarir ibn Abdullah to relieve him of the pre-Islamic sanctuary of Dhul-Khalasa (also known as the Yemeni or Syrian Ka'ba), Jarir led 150 cavalrymen from the tribe of Ahmas to demolish the structure and kill whoever they found there. Upon being informed of the demolition and killings, Muhammad invoked blessings upon the raiders and the tribe of Ahmas.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ بَيْتٌ يُقَالَ لَهُ ذُو الْخَلَصَةِ، وَكَانَ يُقَالُ لَهُ الْكَعْبَةُ الْيَمَانِيَةُ، أَوِ الْكَعْبَةُ الشَّأْمِيَّةُ، فَقَالَ لِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ هَلْ أَنْتَ مُرِيحِي مِنْ ذِي الْخَلَصَةِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَنَفَرْتُ إِلَيْهِ فِي خَمْسِينَ وَمِائَةِ فَارِسٍ مِنْ أَحْمَسَ ـ قَالَ ـ فَكَسَرْنَا، وَقَتَلْنَا مَنْ وَجَدْنَا عِنْدَهُ، فَأَتَيْنَاهُ، فَأَخْبَرْنَاهُ، فَدَعَا لَنَا وَلأَحْمَسَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: There was a house called Dhul-Khalasa in the Pre-Islamic Period and it was also called Al-Ka'ba Al-Yamaniya or Al-Ka'ba Ash-Shamiya. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said to me, "Will you relieve me from Dhul-Khalasa?" So I left for it with 150 cavalrymen from the tribe of Ahmas and then we destroyed it and killed whoever we found there. Then we came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him about it. He invoked good upon us and upon the tribe of Ahmas

bukhari:3823.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the expedition to Dhul-Khalasa in AD 632 was a defensive military operation against a hostile rebel stronghold, claiming that Jarir's forces only engaged armed combatants who resisted them. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad targeted the site solely because it was a rival religious sanctuary known as 'the Yemeni Ka'ba' (al-Ka'ba al-Yamāniyya), asking Jarir, 'Will you relieve me from Dhul-Khalasa?' (hal anta murīḥī min Dhī al-Khalaṣah), with zero mention of any prior military provocation. Furthermore, Jarir explicitly reports indiscriminate slaughter at the temple—'we destroyed it and killed whoever we found there' (fa-kasarnā wa-qatalnā man wajadnā 'indahu)—and parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:4355–4357) confirm that after they burned the sanctuary with fire, Muhammad blessed the raiders and their horses five times.

bukhari:2925.note: Muhammad declares that Muslims will fight the Jews until a Jew hides behind a stone, which will call out to the Muslim to come and kill him ([Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44); [Romans 12:14](bible://rom/12/14)). Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi affirm this as a literal eschatological battle in which Jews are pursued and killed even while fleeing and hiding.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ تُقَاتِلُونَ الْيَهُودَ حَتَّى يَخْتَبِيَ أَحَدُهُمْ وَرَاءَ الْحَجَرِ فَيَقُولُ يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ هَذَا يَهُودِيٌّ وَرَائِي فَاقْتُلْهُ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "You (i.e. Muslims) will fight with the Jews until some of them will hide behind stones. The stones will (betray them) saying, 'O `Abdullah (i.e. slave of Allah)! There is a Jew hiding behind me; so kill him

bukhari:2925.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration is purely a descriptive end-times prophecy restricted to a specific militant faction of Jews who will fight alongside the false Messiah (*al-Masīḥ al-Dajjāl*), rather than a normative command for violence against Jewish people. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *"hāḏā yahūdiyyun warāʾī fa-qtulhu"* ("There is a Jew behind me, so kill him"), ordering the execution of a non-combatant who is fleeing and hiding (*yaḫtabiʾa*) based solely on his ethno-religious identity as a Jew (*yahūdī*), which is why Imām al-Bukhārī codified it under the normative military rulings of the *Book of Jihād* (*Kitāb al-Jihād wa-l-Siyar*). Moreover, as Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī explains in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, this eschatological war takes place when Islam's version of Jesus abolishes the *jizyah* and leaves non-Muslims no option but conversion to Islam or death, thereby enshrining the total religious extermination of unrepentant Jews as a divinely mandated triumph.

bukhari:3043.note: After the tribe of Banu Qurayza surrendered to the arbitration of Sa'd bin Mu'adh, he decreed that their combatants be executed and their women and children be taken captive, a verdict Muhammad ratified as the judgment of the King (Allah) (cf. [Quran 33:26](quran://33/26)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ لَهُ ‏"‏ إِنَّ هَؤُلاَءِ نَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَإِنِّي أَحْكُمُ أَنْ تُقْتَلَ الْمُقَاتِلَةُ، وَأَنْ تُسْبَى الذُّرِّيَّةُ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ لَقَدْ حَكَمْتَ فِيهِمْ بِحُكْمِ الْمَلِكِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: who said to him. "These people are ready to accept your judgment." Sa`d said, "I give the judgment that their warriors should be killed and their children and women should be taken as prisoners." The Prophet (ﷺ) then remarked, "O Sa`d! You have judged amongst them with (or similar to) the judgment of the King Allah

bukhari:3043.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad merely honored Banu Qurayza's own choice of their former ally Sa'd bin Mu'adh as an independent arbitrator, and that only convicted wartime traitors were executed under a ruling mirroring the Torah (Deuteronomy 20:12–14). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad consecrated Sa'd's decree to slaughter the *al-muqātilah* (الْمُقَاتِلَةُ, fighting-age males) and enslave the *al-dhurriyyah* (الذُّرِّيَّةُ, women and children) as the direct 'judgment of the King [Allah]' (*bi-ḥukmi al-Maliki*, بِحُكْمِ الْمَلِكِ; cf. `bukhari:4121`). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (`abudawud:4404`, `tirmidhi:1584`) prove that guilt was not determined by individual trials for treason, but by physically inspecting every surrendered boy's groin and beheading anyone who had grown pubic hair (*man anbata*).

bukhari:3593.note: Muhammad declares that the Jews will fight the Muslims and the Muslims will be given mastery over them, to the point that a stone will call out to a Muslim to kill a Jew hiding behind it (cf. bukhari:2925; bukhari:2926; [Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44); [Romans 12:14](bible://rom/12/14)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ تُقَاتِلُكُمُ الْيَهُودُ فَتُسَلَّطُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ الْحَجَرُ يَا مُسْلِمُ، هَذَا يَهُودِيٌّ وَرَائِي فَاقْتُلْهُ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "The Jews will fight with you, and you will be given victory over them so that a stone will say, 'O Muslim! There is a Jew behind me; kill him

bukhari:3593.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the opening verb *tuqātilukum al-yahūd* ('the Jews will fight you') proves this is strictly a defensive conflict, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* to restrict the prophecy to an end-times battle against the army of the *Dajjāl* (Antichrist) rather than general hostility toward Jewish people. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the stone betrays a fleeing, hidden person based purely on his ethnoreligious identity (*hādhā yahūdiyyun warāʾī fa-qtulhu* — 'this is a Jew behind me, so kill him'), mandating the summary execution of a fugitive hiding for his life rather than an active combatant. Furthermore, the immediate parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:2925` and `bukhari:2926`) place the offensive initiative on the Muslims (*tuqātilūna al-yahūda* — 'you will fight the Jews') as a mandatory condition for the Hour to arrive, demonstrating that the tradition sanctifies total religious eradication rather than proportionate self-defense.

bukhari:3804.note: When the people of Banu Qurayza surrendered to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, he decreed that their fighting men (muqatilatuhum) be killed and their women and children (dharariyyuhum) be taken captive. Muhammad ratified this verdict by declaring that Sa'd had judged with the judgment of Allah, or the judgment of the King (cf. [Quran 33:26](quran://33/26), bukhari:3043, bukhari:4121).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ أُنَاسًا نَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ، فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَيْهِ فَجَاءَ عَلَى حِمَارٍ، فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ قَرِيبًا مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ قُومُوا إِلَى خَيْرِكُمْ أَوْ سَيِّدِكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا سَعْدُ، إِنَّ هَؤُلاَءِ نَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَإِنِّي أَحْكُمُ فِيهِمْ أَنْ تُقْتَلَ مُقَاتِلَتُهُمْ وَتُسْبَى ذَرَارِيُّهُمْ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ حَكَمْتَ بِحُكْمِ اللَّهِ، أَوْ بِحُكْمِ الْمَلِكِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Some people (i.e. the Jews of Bani Quraiza) agreed to accept the verdict of Sa`d bin Mu`adh so the Prophet (ﷺ) sent for him (i.e. Sa`d bin Mu`adh). He came riding a donkey, and when he approached the Mosque, the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Get up for the best amongst you." or said, "Get up for your chief." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "O Sa`d! These people have agreed to accept your verdict." Sa`d said, "I judge that their warriors should be killed and their children and women should be taken as captives." The Prophet said, "You have given a judgment similar to Allah's Judgment (or the King's judgment)

bukhari:3804.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the Banu Qurayza committed wartime treason, voluntarily chose their former ally Sa'd bin Mu'adh as an independent arbitrator, and were judged strictly according to their own Torah law (Deuteronomy 20:10–14) with only active fighters (*muqātilatuhum*) executed. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad ratified the mass execution and enslavement of women and children (*tusbā dharāriyyuhum*) as Allah's own supreme decree rather than a Mosaic concession, declaring, *'ḥakamta bi-ḥukmi Allāhi, aw bi-ḥukmi al-Maliki'* ('You have judged by the judgment of Allah, or by the judgment of the King,' which was also canonized in Quran 33:26). Furthermore, as Ibn Hajar explains in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and parallel authentic narrations confirm (Sunan Abi Dawud 4404, Jami` at-Tirmidhi 1584), 'combatants' (*muqātilah*) was not determined by proven individual guilt in treason, but by forcibly inspecting the captives' groins and beheading every male youth who had begun to grow pubic hair (*man anbata*).

bukhari:4122.note: Following the Battle of the Trench (AD 627), Gabriel directed Muhammad to march against Banu Qurayza, who surrendered to Muhammad's judgment. Muhammad delegated the verdict to Sa'd bin Mu'adh, who decreed that their combatants (`al-muqatilah`) be killed, their women and children taken captive (`tusba`), and their property divided—a ruling Muhammad ratified as the judgment of Allah in the immediately preceding report (bukhari:4121; cf. [Quran 33:26](quran://33/26)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا رَجَعَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنَ الْخَنْدَقِ وَضَعَ السِّلاَحَ وَاغْتَسَلَ، فَأَتَاهُ جِبْرِيلُ ـ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ ـ وَهْوَ يَنْفُضُ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ الْغُبَارِ فَقَالَ قَدْ وَضَعْتَ السِّلاَحَ وَاللَّهِ مَا وَضَعْتُهُ، اخْرُجْ إِلَيْهِمْ‏.‏ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ فَأَيْنَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأَشَارَ إِلَى بَنِي قُرَيْظَةَ، فَأَتَاهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَنَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِهِ، فَرَدَّ الْحُكْمَ إِلَى سَعْدٍ، قَالَ فَإِنِّي أَحْكُمُ فِيهِمْ أَنْ تُقْتَلَ الْمُقَاتِلَةُ، وَأَنْ تُسْبَى النِّسَاءُ وَالذُّرِّيَّةُ، وَأَنْ تُقْسَمَ أَمْوَالُهُمْ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When the Prophet returned from the (battle) of Al-Khandaq (i.e. Trench) and laid down his arms and took a bath Gabriel came to him while he (i.e. Gabriel) was shaking the dust off his head, and said, "You have laid down the arms?" By Allah, I have not laid them down. Go out to them (to attack them)." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Where?" Gabriel pointed towards Bani Quraiza. So Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) went to them (i.e. Banu Quraiza) (i.e. besieged them). They then surrendered to the Prophet's judgment but he directed them to Sa`d to give his verdict concerning them. Sa`d said, "I give my judgment that their warriors should be killed, their women and children should be taken as captives, and their properties distributed."

bukhari:4122.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the Banu Qurayza were punished solely for wartime treason by an independent arbitrator of their own choosing, Sa'd bin Mu'adh, who merely applied the Torah's war code rather than Islamic law. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the tribe surrendered to Muhammad's own judgment (فَنَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِهِ) after Gabriel ordered the attack (اخْرُجْ إِلَيْهِمْ), and that Muhammad himself delegated the verdict to Sa'd (فَرَدَّ الْحُكْمَ إِلَى سَعْدٍ). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:3804, bukhari:4028) confirm that Muhammad ratified this massacre as the direct decree of Allah (حُكْمِ اللَّهِ), and that the "combatants" (الْمُقَاتِلَةُ) marked for execution were determined not by trial for treason, but by inspecting captive boys for the growth of pubic hair.

bukhari:4122.note: When Banu Qurayza surrendered to Muhammad's judgment in AD 627, he delegated the verdict to Sa'd bin Mu'adh, who decreed that their women and children be enslaved as war captives (`tusba al-nisa' wa-al-dhurriyyah`) and their property distributed. In the immediately preceding narration (bukhari:4121), Muhammad explicitly endorsed this decree as the judgment of Allah (cf. [Quran 33:26](quran://33/26)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَتَاهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَنَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِهِ، فَرَدَّ الْحُكْمَ إِلَى سَعْدٍ، قَالَ فَإِنِّي أَحْكُمُ فِيهِمْ أَنْ تُقْتَلَ الْمُقَاتِلَةُ، وَأَنْ تُسْبَى النِّسَاءُ وَالذُّرِّيَّةُ، وَأَنْ تُقْسَمَ أَمْوَالُهُمْ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: So Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) went to them (i.e. Banu Quraiza) (i.e. besieged them). They then surrendered to the Prophet's judgment but he directed them to Sa`d to give his verdict concerning them. Sa`d said, "I give my judgment that their warriors should be killed, their women and children should be taken as captives, and their properties distributed."

bukhari:4122.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islam forbids punishing non-combatants and that taking the women and children of Banu Qurayza was a humanitarian measure to shelter destitute widows and orphans after the AD 627 siege. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the women and children were decreed to be enslaved as war captives (وَأَنْ تُسْبَى النِّسَاءُ وَالذُّرِّيَّةُ) alongside the confiscation and division of their property (وَأَنْ تُقْسَمَ أَمْوَالُهُمْ). Parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:3043, bukhari:3804) and classical tafsir on Quran 33:26 (such as Ibn Kathīr) confirm that Muhammad endorsed this enslavement as the judgment of Allah (بِحُكْمِ اللَّهِ), reducing the non-combatant women and children to chattel property distributed as war booty and sold to purchase horses and weapons.

bukhari:7285.note: Umar cites Muhammad's declaration that he was commanded to fight people until they testify that there is no deity but Allah, which alone protects their lives and property from him except by legal right. Invoking that exception clause after Muhammad's death, Caliph Abu Bakr rules that Zakat is the obligatory right on wealth and vows to wage war against anyone who separates prayer from Zakat by withholding even a camel-tether (or young female goat) previously paid to Muhammad.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ‏.‏ فَمَنْ قَالَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ‏.‏ عَصَمَ مِنِّي مَالَهُ وَنَفْسَهُ، إِلاَّ بِحَقِّهِ، وَحِسَابُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: I have been ordered to fight the people till they say 'None has the right to be worshipped but Allah' And whoever says: None has the right to be worshipped but Allah.' waves his wealth and his life from me unless he deserves a legal punishment lusty, and his account will be with Allah!

bukhari:7285.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase al-nās ('the people') is a general term restricted to hostile Arab polytheists who initiated military aggression against Medina, and that Abu Bakr was merely suppressing a violent political rebellion. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the sole condition for sparing a person's life and property is religious confession (ḥattā yaqūlū lā ilāha illā Allāh... ʿaṣama minnī mālahu wa-nafsahu—'until they say there is no god but Allah... [whereby] he protects his wealth and his life from me'), making ideological submission rather than a ceasefire the prerequisite for survival. Furthermore, classical authorities like Ibn Hajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) and Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) confirm that this Hadith mandates offensive war against all non-scriptuary polytheists until they convert, while Abu Bakr invoked its exception clause (illā bi-ḥaqqihi) to wage war even against praying Muslims whose only offense was withholding the zakāt tax (man farraqa bayna al-ṣalāti wa-al-zakāh).

muslim:124.note: Umar ibn al-Khattab quotes Muhammad's declaration that he was commanded to fight people until they testify that there is no god but Allah, making the protection of their lives and property contingent on professing Islam and fulfilling its legal rights. Caliph Abu Bakr invokes this 'except for its right' clause to wage war against Arab tribes that professed the testimony of faith but withheld the Zakat tax after Muhammad's death.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ فَمَنْ قَالَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ فَقَدْ عَصَمَ مِنِّي مَالَهُ وَنَفْسَهُ إِلاَّ بِحَقِّهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: I have been directed to fight against people so long as they do not say: There is no god but Allah, and he who professed it was granted full protection of his property and life on my behalf except for a right

muslim:124.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the word 'the people' (al-nās) is a general term restricted only to hostile Meccan treaty-breakers ('āmm urīda bihi al-khuṣūṣ), and that Abu Bakr was merely suppressing armed political treason rather than enforcing religious submission. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that a person's life and property are only protected ('aṣama minnī mālahu wa-nafsahu) once they profess lā ilāha illā Allāh and fulfill its statutory right (illā bi-ḥaqqihi), which Abu Bakr and 'Umar invoke to wage lethal war (la-uqātilanna) against tribes solely for withholding the religious alms tax (al-zakāt). In his Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Imam al-Nawawī confirms that this narration—grounded in Surah 9:5—mandates fighting idolaters until they accept Islam and waging war against anyone who refuses obligatory Islamic rituals like prayer or zakāt.

bukhari:7284.note: Muhammad declares that he has been ordered to fight people until they testify that there is no deity but Allah, making the protection of their lives and wealth contingent upon this profession and its legal obligations. Invoking the exception clause ('except by its right') in this decree, Caliph Abu Bakr overcomes Umar's initial objection and wages war against Arab tribes that profess Islam but withhold compulsory zakat.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ‏.‏ فَمَنْ قَالَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ‏.‏ عَصَمَ مِنِّي مَالَهُ وَنَفْسَهُ، إِلاَّ بِحَقِّهِ، وَحِسَابُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: I have been ordered to fight the people till they say 'None has the right to be worshipped but Allah' And whoever says: None has the right to be worshipped but Allah.' waves his wealth and his life from me unless he deserves a legal punishment lusty, and his account will be with Allah!

bukhari:7284.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the term al-nās ('the people') is a general expression intended in a restricted sense (ʿāmm urīda bihi al-khuṣūṣ), applying only to hostile 7th-century AD Arab polytheists who initiated war or to political rebels during the Ridda Wars. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that a person's life and wealth are only protected (ʿaṣama minnī mālahu wa-nafsahu) 'until they say there is no deity but Allah' (ḥattā yaqūlū lā ilāha illā Allāh), making theological confession—not a peace treaty or cessation of hostilities—the condition for sparing their blood. Furthermore, even when classical commentators like Ibn Hajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) and Al-Nawawī harmonize this with Surah 9:5 and 9:29, non-Muslims remain subject to offensive jihad until polytheists convert or People of the Book pay the jizyah in subjugation, while Abu Bakr invokes the exception clause illā bi-ḥaqqihi ('except by its right') to wage lethal war even against professing Muslims who withhold the religious zakāt tax.

muslim:125.note: Muhammad declares that he has been commanded to fight people until they profess that there is no god but Allah, granting protection of life and property from him only to those who make this declaration (except where legal right requires otherwise). Classical commentators such as al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar affirm that this ruling mandates fighting polytheists until they convert to Islam, while People of the Book are fought until they either convert or pay the jizya.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ فَمَنْ قَالَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ عَصَمَ مِنِّي مَالَهُ وَنَفْسَهُ إِلاَّ بِحَقِّهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: I have been commanded to fight against people so long as they do not declare that there is no god but Allah, and he who professed it was guaranteed the protection of his property and life on my behalf except for the right affairs rest with Allah

muslim:125.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the term *al-nās* ('the people') is a general word intended for a specific group (*ʿāmm urīda bihi al-khuṣūṣ*)—namely, hostile Arab polytheists who initiated war against Medina—while citing Al-Nawawī and Ibn Hajar to note that People of the Book are spared if they pay the *jizyah*. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that a person's property and life only become protected from Muhammad (*ʿaṣama minnī mālahu wa-nafsahu*) once they profess the Islamic creed ('حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ'), making theological submission or tributary subjugation—not the cessation of military aggression—the prerequisite for sparing their blood. Furthermore, in the immediately preceding narration (muslim:124), Caliph Abu Bakr invokes this exact command and its exception clause (*illā bi-ḥaqqihi*, 'except for its right') to wage war against tribes who merely withheld the *zakāt*, proving the Companions understood it as a mandate for coercive religious enforcement rather than mere self-defense.

bukhari:6925.note: Umar cites Muhammad's declaration that he was commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no deity but Allah, which alone protects their lives and property from him except by legal right. In response, Caliph Abu Bakr rules that obligatory alms (zakat) is part of the legal right due on property and vows to fight anyone who separates prayer from zakat by withholding even a young goat they previously paid to Muhammad.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ‏.‏ فَمَنْ قَالَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ‏.‏ عَصَمَ مِنِّي مَالَهُ وَنَفْسَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, 'I have been ordered to fight the people till they say: 'None has the right to be worshipped but Allah, 'and whoever said, 'None has the right to be worshipped but Allah', Allah will save his property and his life from me

bukhari:6925.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the general term al-nās ('the people') is a restricted generality (ʿāmm makhṣūṣ) referring only to hostile Arabian polytheists who initiated aggression against Medina, or that this narration merely reflects Abu Bakr enforcing civic tax obligations. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the condition for ceasing warfare is religious conversion—'حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ' ('until they say: None has the right to be worshipped but Allah')—rather than a peace treaty, and establishes that a person's life and wealth remain forfeit until they profess Islam ('عَصَمَ مِنِّي مَالَهُ وَنَفْسَهُ'). Moreover, both parallel bukhari:25 and classical commentators like Ibn Hajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) and Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) confirm that this command obligates warfare until idolaters convert and perform Islamic rituals ('إِلاَّ بِحَقِّهِ', defined here by Abu Bakr as prayer and Zakāh) or People of the Book submit to paying the Jizyah under Quran 9:29.

muslim:126.note: Muhammad declares that he has been commanded to fight people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and believe in him and his message, conditioning the protection of their blood and property upon this profession of faith (cf. bukhari:25). Classical commentators (such as al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar) note that while People of the Book may alternatively secure protection by paying the jizya, this declaration establishes the mandate to fight idolaters until they convert to Islam.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَشْهَدُوا أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَيُؤْمِنُوا بِي وَبِمَا جِئْتُ بِهِ فَإِذَا فَعَلُوا ذَلِكَ عَصَمُوا مِنِّي دِمَاءَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ إِلاَّ بِحَقِّهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: I have been commanded to fight against people, till they testify to the fact that there is no god but Allah, and believe in me (that) I am the messenger (from the Lord) and in all that I have brought. And when they do it, their blood and riches are guaranteed protection on my behalf except where it is justified by law

muslim:126.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar, that the word *al-nās* ('the people') is a general term with a restricted meaning (*ʿāmm urīda bihi al-khuṣūṣ*) targeting only hostile Arab idolaters, while People of the Book are spared upon paying the *jizyah*. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *fa-idhā faʿalū dhālika ʿaṣamū minnī dimāʾahum wa-amwālahum* ('when they do that, they protect from me their blood and their property'), making the basic sanctity of human life and wealth strictly conditional upon confessing Islam rather than peaceful non-aggression. Even when classical commentators harmonize this with Quran 9:29 for Jews and Christians, the only alternative to conversion or the sword is violent subjugation and paying tribute in humiliation (*wa-hum ṣāghirūn*), proving that unbelief itself—not military hostility—is the *casus belli*.

muslim:127.note: Muhammad declares that he has been commanded to fight people until they profess that there is no god but Allah, granting protection to their blood and property only upon this outward declaration (cf. bukhari:25). His concluding recitation of Quran 88:21-22 ('You are not a controller over them') is explained by classical commentators such as al-Nawawi as leaving people's inward sincerity to Allah's judgment once outward submission has been secured.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ فَإِذَا قَالُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ عَصَمُوا مِنِّي دِمَاءَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ إِلاَّ بِحَقِّهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: I have been commanded that I should fight against people till they declare that there is no god but Allah, and when they profess it that there is no god but Allah, their blood and riches are guaranteed protection on my behalf except where it is justified by law

muslim:127.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the general term al-nās ('the people') refers strictly to hostile Meccan treaty-breakers in self-defense, and that Muhammad's recitation of Quran 88:22 ('You are not a dictator over them') proves peaceful religious freedom. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that people's blood and property only gain protection ('aṣamū minnī dimā'ahum wa-amwālahum) once they utter the Islamic profession of faith (ḥattā yaqūlū lā ilāha illā Allāh), establishing that non-Muslim life and wealth are otherwise forfeit.
