Furthermore, Imām al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) explains that Quran 88:22 was either abrogated by the command to fight or simply means a ruler cannot control secret disbelief in the heart—which is left to Allah's reckoning (wa-ḥisābuhum 'alā Allāh)—once military force has compelled outward submission or the jizyah tribute (Quran 9:29).

muslim:129.note: Muhammad declares that he has been commanded to fight people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His messenger, establish prayer, and pay Zakat, stating that doing so protects their blood and property from him except where justified by law (cf. bukhari:25). Although classical jurists invoke external texts to add a jizya exception or limit 'the people' to polytheists, the declaration itself directly conditions the protection of life and property on conversion and religious practice.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَشْهَدُوا أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلاَةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ فَإِذَا فَعَلُوا عَصَمُوا مِنِّي دِمَاءَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ إِلاَّ بِحَقِّهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: I have been commanded to fight against people till they testify that there is no god but Allah, that Muhammad is the messenger of Allah, and they establish prayer, and pay Zakat and if they do it, their blood and property are guaranteed protection on my behalf except when justified by law

muslim:129.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ (uqātila al-nās, 'fight the people') is a general expression intended for a specific group (ʿāmm urīda bihi al-khāṣṣ), claiming it only targeted hostile Arab polytheists who initiated military aggression against Medina rather than mandating offensive religious warfare. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states فَإِذَا فَعَلُوا عَصَمُوا مِنِّي دِمَاءَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ ('then if they do that, they have protected from me their blood and their property'), making the inviolability (ʿiṣmah) of human life and wealth strictly conditional upon reciting the Shahādah, praying, and paying Zakāt rather than ceasing hostilities. Furthermore, Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) and Ibn Ḥajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī on bukhari:25) confirm that under Quran 9:5 idolaters are afforded no peaceful coexistence short of conversion or execution, and in the immediately preceding narration (muslim:124) Caliph Abū Bakr invokes this exact Hadith to wage war on tribes simply for withholding the Zakāt tax.

muslim:4232.note: During his severe illness on a Thursday, after his companions disputed his offer to write a document so they would not go astray and questioned whether he was speaking delirious nonsense, Muhammad told them to leave him and commanded them to expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: اشْتَدَّ بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَجَعُهُ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ ائْتُونِي أَكْتُبْ لَكُمْ كِتَابًا لاَ تَضِلُّوا بَعْدِي ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَتَنَازَعُوا وَمَا يَنْبَغِي عِنْدَ نَبِيٍّ تَنَازُعٌ ‏.‏ وَقَالُوا مَا شَأْنُهُ أَهَجَرَ اسْتَفْهِمُوهُ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ دَعُونِي فَالَّذِي أَنَا فِيهِ خَيْرٌ أُوصِيكُمْ بِثَلاَثٍ أَخْرِجُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ مِنْ جَزِيرَةِ الْعَرَبِ وَأَجِيزُوا الْوَفْدَ بِنَحْوِ مَا كُنْتُ أُجِيزُهُمْ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The illness of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) took a serious turn (on this day), and he said: Come to me, so that I should write for you a document that you may not go astray after me. They (the Companions around him) disputed, and it is not meet to dispute in the presence of the Apostle. They said: How is lie (Allah's Apostle)? Has he lost his consciousness? Try to learn from him (this point). He (the Holy Prophet) said: Leave me. I am better in the state (than the one in which you are engaged). I make a will about three things: Turn out the polytheists from the territory of Arabia; show hospitality to the (foreign) delegations as I used to show them hospitality.

muslim:4232.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the order to expel polytheists was a defensive measure limited to hostile combatants, and point to the accompanying instruction to show hospitality to foreign delegations as proof of religious tolerance. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an unconditional deathbed bequest (أُوصِيكُمْ بِثَلاَثٍ, ūṣīkum bi-thalāthin) commanding Muslims to "expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula" (أَخْرِجُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ مِنْ جَزِيرَةِ الْعَرَبِ, akhrijū al-mushrikīna min jazīrati al-ʿArab) based on their religious identity, with no qualification restricting it to combatants. Pairing this expulsion mandate with gifts for visiting delegations (الْوَفْدَ, al-wafd) confirms that non-Muslims were only permitted to enter the peninsula temporarily as foreign envoys while resident polytheists were permanently banished (bukhari:3053, bukhari:3168, bukhari:4431).

muslim:4522.note: Muhammad instructs his military commanders to fight those who disbelieve in Allah, presenting polytheist enemies with an ultimatum to convert to Islam, pay the *jizyah* tax ([Quran 9:29](quran://9/29)), or be fought. During sieges, he further directs commanders to grant only their own and their companions' guarantees of safety rather than the guarantee of Allah and His Prophet, stating that violating their own pledges is a lesser sin.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏ "‏ اغْزُوا بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ قَاتِلُوا مَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ اغْزُوا وَ لاَ تَغُلُّوا وَلاَ تَغْدِرُوا وَلاَ تَمْثُلُوا وَلاَ تَقْتُلُوا وَلِيدًا وَإِذَا لَقِيتَ عَدُوَّكَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ فَادْعُهُمْ إِلَى ثَلاَثِ خِصَالٍ - أَوْ خِلاَلٍ - فَأَيَّتُهُنَّ مَا أَجَابُوكَ فَاقْبَلْ مِنْهُمْ وَكُفَّ عَنْهُمْ ثُمَّ ادْعُهُمْ إِلَى الإِسْلاَمِ فَإِنْ أَجَابُوكَ فَاقْبَلْ مِنْهُمْ وَكُفَّ عَنْهُمْ ثُمَّ ادْعُهُمْ إِلَى التَّحَوُّلِ مِنْ دَارِهِمْ إِلَى دَارِ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَأَخْبِرْهُمْ أَنَّهُمْ إِنْ فَعَلُوا ذَلِكَ فَلَهُمْ مَا لِلْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَعَلَيْهِمْ مَا عَلَى الْمُهَاجِرِينَ فَإِنْ أَبَوْا أَنْ يَتَحَوَّلُوا مِنْهَا فَأَخْبِرْهُمْ أَنَّهُمْ يَكُونُونَ كَأَعْرَابِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ يَجْرِي عَلَيْهِمْ حُكْمُ اللَّهِ الَّذِي يَجْرِي عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلاَ يَكُونُ لَهُمْ فِي الْغَنِيمَةِ وَالْفَىْءِ شَىْءٌ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُجَاهِدُوا مَعَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَإِنْ هُمْ أَبَوْا فَسَلْهُمُ الْجِزْيَةَ فَإِنْ هُمْ أَجَابُوكَ فَاقْبَلْ مِنْهُمْ وَكُفَّ عَنْهُمْ فَإِنْ هُمْ أَبَوْا فَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَقَاتِلْهُمْ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He would say:Fight in the name of Allah and in the way of Allah. Fight against those who disbelieve in Allah. Make a holy war, do not embezzle the spoils; do not break your pledge; and do not mutilate (the dead) bodies; do not kill the children. When you meet your enemies who are polytheists, invite them to three courses of action. If they respond to any one of these, you also accept it and withhold yourself from doing them any harm. Invite them to (accept) Islam; if they respond to you, accept it from them and desist from fighting against them. Then invite them to migrate from their lands to the land of the Muhajireen and inform them that, if they do so, they shall have all the privileges and obligations of the Muhajireen. If they refuse to migrate, tell them that they will have the status of Bedouin Muslims and will be subjected to the Commands of Allah like other Muslims, but they will not get any share from the spoils of war or Fai' except when they actually fight with the Muslims (against the disbelievers). If they refuse to accept Islam, demand from them the Jizya. If they agree to pay, accept it from them and hold off your hands. If they refuse to pay the tax, seek Allah's help and fight them.

muslim:4522.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration establishes humane rules of engagement—such as prohibiting mutilation and the killing of children—and applies strictly to defensive warfare against military aggressors. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states the ideological command to "fight against those who disbelieve in Allah" (*qātilū man kafara bi-llāhi*) and directs Muslim armies to besiege non-Muslim strongholds (*wa-idhā ḥāṣarta ahla ḥiṣnin*) and fight them (*wa-qātilhum*) unless they either convert to Islam (*udʿuhum ilā l-islām*) or submit to paying the *jizyah* tribute (*fasalhumu l-jizyah*; cf. [Quran 9:29](quran://9/29)).

muslim:4591.note: Muhammad goes out from the mosque to the Jewish community and calls on them three times to accept Islam so that they will be safe (*aslimū taslamū*). When they reply only that he has conveyed his message, he declares that the earth belongs to Allah and His Messenger, announces his intention to expel them from the land, and instructs them to sell whatever property they can or else know that the land belongs to Allah and His Messenger.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَنَادَاهُمْ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا مَعْشَرَ يَهُودَ أَسْلِمُوا تَسْلَمُوا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالُوا قَدْ بَلَّغْتَ يَا أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ ذَلِكَ أُرِيدُ أَسْلِمُوا تَسْلَمُوا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالُوا قَدْ بَلَّغْتَ يَا أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ ذَلِكَ أُرِيدُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُمُ الثَّالِثَةَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ اعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا الأَرْضُ لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَأَنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُجْلِيَكُمْ مِنْ هَذِهِ الأَرْضِ فَمَنْ وَجَدَ مِنْكُمْ بِمَالِهِ شَيْئًا فَلْيَبِعْهُ وَإِلاَّ فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ الأَرْضَ لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and called out to them (saying): O ye assembly of Jews, accept Islam (and) you will be safe. They said: Abu'l-Qasim, you have communicated (God's Message to us). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: I want this (i. e. you should admit that God's Message has been communicated to you), accept Islam and you would be safe. They said: Abu'l-Qisim, you have communicated (Allah's Message). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: I want this... - He said to them (the same words) the third time (and on getting the same reply) he added: You should know that the earth belongs to Allah and His Apostle, and I wish that I should expel you from this land Those of you who have any property with them should sell it, otherwise they should know that the earth belongs to Allah and His Apostle (and they may have to go away leaving everything behind)

muslim:4591.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this expulsion was a defensive measure prompted by a treaty violation or military provocation rather than religious coercion. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad initiated the march directly from the mosque (*inṭaliqū ilā yahūda*) and conditioned their safety and residency solely on converting to Islam (*aslimū taslamū*—"accept Islam and you will be safe"). When they replied three times that he had communicated his message (*qad ballaghta yā Abā al-Qāsim*), he cited no breach of treaty, instead ordering their expulsion (*ujliyakum min hādhihi al-arḍ*) and property liquidation on the theological claim that the earth belongs to Allah and His Messenger (*annamā al-arḍu lillāhi wa-rasūlihi*), as also recorded in bukhari:3167, bukhari:6944, and bukhari:7348.

bukhari:7348.note: Muhammad goes to the Jewish house of study (Bait al-Midras) and three times tells the Jews to embrace Islam in order to be safe ('aslimu taslamu'). When they reply only that he has conveyed his message, he declares that the land belongs to Allah and His Messenger, announces his intention to expel them from it, and instructs them to sell whatever property they can.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: يَا مَعْشَرَ يَهُودَ أَسْلِمُوا تَسْلَمُوا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالُوا بَلَّغْتَ يَا أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ ذَلِكَ أُرِيدُ أَسْلِمُوا تَسْلَمُوا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالُوا قَدْ بَلَّغْتَ يَا أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ ذَلِكَ أُرِيدُ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَهَا الثَّالِثَةَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ اعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا الأَرْضُ لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُجْلِيَكُمْ مِنْ هَذِهِ الأَرْضِ، فَمَنْ وَجَدَ مِنْكُمْ بِمَالِهِ شَيْئًا فَلْيَبِعْهُ، وَإِلاَّ فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا الأَرْضُ لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: "O assembly of Jews! Surrender to Allah (embrace Islam) and you will be safe!" They said, "You have conveyed Allah's message, O Aba-al-Qasim" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) then said to them, "That is what I want; embrace Islam and you will be safe." They said, "You have conveyed the message, O Aba-al- Qasim." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) then said to them, "That is what I want," and repeated his words for the third time and added, "Know that the earth is for Allah and I want to exile you from this land, so whoever among you has property he should sell it, otherwise, know that the land is for Allah and His Apostle

bukhari:7348.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this ultimatum—as contextualized in Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī—was not religious coercion, but a defensive political measure against the Jewish tribe of Banū Qaynuqāʿ after they allegedly breached their peace treaty. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states no treaty violation or provocation whatsoever, recording instead that Muhammad marched directly from the mosque to their house of study (Bayt al-Midrās) and conditioned their safety solely on religious conversion: 'Embrace Islam and you will be safe' (aslimū taslamū). When they peacefully declined to convert, he justified their forced expulsion (ujliyakum min hādhihi al-arḍ) not by citing a broken pact, but by asserting absolute theological supremacy over their homeland: 'Know that the earth belongs only to Allah and His Messenger' (innamā al-arḍu lillāhi wa-rasūlihi).

bukhari:1400.note: Following Muhammad's death in AD 632, Umar cited Muhammad's mandate—"I have been ordered to fight the people until they say 'There is no god but Allah,' and whoever says it has protected his property and his life from me except by its right" ([Quran 9:5](quran://9/5))—when questioning Abu Bakr's campaign against Arab tribes. Abu Bakr replied that zakat is the compulsory "right of property" and swore to wage war against anyone who separates prayer from zakat, even for withholding a single young she-goat previously paid to Muhammad, a ruling Umar then endorsed.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَمَّا تُوُفِّيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَكَانَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ وَكَفَرَ مَنْ كَفَرَ مِنَ الْعَرَبِ فَقَالَ عُمَرُ ـ رضى الله عنه كَيْفَ تُقَاتِلُ النَّاسَ، وَقَدْ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ‏.‏ فَمَنْ قَالَهَا فَقَدْ عَصَمَ مِنِّي مَالَهُ وَنَفْسَهُ إِلاَّ بِحَقِّهِ، وَحِسَابُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ لأُقَاتِلَنَّ مَنْ فَرَّقَ بَيْنَ الصَّلاَةِ وَالزَّكَاةِ، فَإِنَّ الزَّكَاةَ حَقُّ الْمَالِ، وَاللَّهِ لَوْ مَنَعُونِي عَنَاقًا كَانُوا يُؤَدُّونَهَا إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَقَاتَلْتُهُمْ عَلَى مَنْعِهَا‏.‏ قَالَ عُمَرُ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ فَوَاللَّهِ مَا هُوَ إِلاَّ أَنْ قَدْ شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ فَعَرَفْتُ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) died and Abu Bakr became the caliph some Arabs renegade (reverted to disbelief) (Abu Bakr decided to declare war against them), `Umar, said to Abu Bakr, "How can you fight with these people although Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, 'I have been ordered (by Allah) to fight the people till they say: "None has the right to be worshipped but Allah, and whoever said it then he will save his life and property from me except on trespassing the law (rights and conditions for which he will be punished justly), and his accounts will be with Allah.' " Abu Bakr said, "By Allah! I will fight those who differentiate between the prayer and the Zakat as Zakat is the compulsory right to be taken from the property (according to Allah's orders) By Allah! If they refuse to pay me even a she-kid which they used to pay at the time of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) . I would fight with them for withholding it" Then `Umar said, "By Allah, it was nothing, but Allah opened Abu Bakr's chest towards the decision (to fight) and I came to know that his decision was right

bukhari:1400.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Abu Bakr's campaign was merely a secular crackdown on political treason and tax evasion rather than religious coercion, and that the term al-nās ('the people') in Muhammad's command to fight only targeted hostile polytheists who violated treaties. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad was ordered to fight people until they profess the Islamic creed (أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُقَاتِلَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَقُولُوا لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ), establishing that a person's life and property (مَالَهُ وَنَفْسَهُ) have no immunity (عَصَمَ) unless they submit to Islam and its religious laws (إِلاَّ بِحَقِّهِ). Furthermore, as Ibn Hajar confirms in Fatḥ al-Bārī, Abu Bakr explicitly waged war against those who separated ritual prayer from almsgiving (مَنْ فَرَّقَ بَيْنَ الصَّلاَةِ وَالزَّكَاةِ), proving that even professing Muslims in AD 632 faced lethal military force for withholding a single religious tithe (عَنَاقًا, a young female goat).

bukhari:3160.note: During Caliph Umar's invasion of Persia, the companion Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba declares to Khosrau's representative that Muhammad commanded Muslims to fight them until they worship Allah alone or pay the *jizya* tribute ([Quran 9:29](quran://9/29)). He adds that Muhammad conveyed Allah's promise that slain Muslim fighters enter Paradise while survivors become masters over the necks of the conquered.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَمَرَنَا نَبِيُّنَا رَسُولُ رَبِّنَا صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ نَقَاتِلَكُمْ حَتَّى تَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَحْدَهُ أَوْ تُؤَدُّوا الْجِزْيَةَ، وَأَخْبَرَنَا نَبِيُّنَا صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنْ رِسَالَةِ رَبِّنَا أَنَّهُ مَنْ قُتِلَ مِنَّا صَارَ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ فِي نَعِيمٍ لَمْ يَرَ مِثْلَهَا قَطُّ، وَمَنْ بَقِيَ مِنَّا مَلَكَ رِقَابَكُمْ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Our Prophet, the Messenger of our Lord, has ordered us to fight you till you worship Allah Alone or give Jizya (i.e. tribute); and our Prophet has informed us that our Lord says:-- "Whoever amongst us is killed (i.e. martyred), shall go to Paradise to lead such a luxurious life as he has never seen, and whoever amongst us remains alive, shall become your master."

bukhari:3160.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the early Islamic invasions of the Sassanid and Byzantine empires were strictly defensive or preemptive campaigns to liberate oppressed populations, claiming the jizya was merely a benign tax in exchange for military protection. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that `Umar initiated an offensive strategy to "crush the head" (شُدِخَ الرَّأْسُ) of Persia, and the Companion Al-Mughira bin Shu`ba openly declares to the Persians that Muhammad commanded Muslims "to fight you until you worship Allah alone or pay the jizya" (أَنْ نُقَاتِلَكُمْ حَتَّى تَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَحْدَهُ أَوْ تُؤَدُّوا الْجِزْيَةَ). Far from offering liberation, Al-Mughira proclaims the prophetic promise that any surviving Muslim conqueror "shall own your necks" (مَلَكَ رِقَابَكُمْ—"become your master"), confirming alongside Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and Quran 9:29 that these campaigns were waged for religious subjugation and imperial dominion.

bukhari:5685.note: After men whom Muhammad had sheltered and given camel milk recovered their health, killed his shepherd, and drove off his camels, he had them pursued, cut off their hands and feet, and branded their eyes with heated iron, with Anas ibn Malik witnessing one of them licking or biting the earth with his tongue until he died (cf. bukhari:233, bukhari:5686). In the untranslated Arabic addendum, Anas recounts this to the governor al-Hajjaj as the severest punishment Muhammad ever inflicted—prompting al-Hasan al-Basri to wish Anas had never told him—while classical commentators rationalize the mutilation as either exact retaliation (*qiṣāṣ*) or a ruling prior to the cross-amputation and crucifixion mandate of [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا صَحُّوا قَتَلُوا رَاعِيَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَاسْتَاقُوا ذَوْدَهُ، فَبَعَثَ فِي آثَارِهِمْ، فَقَطَعَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَأَرْجُلَهُمْ، وَسَمَرَ أَعْيُنَهُمْ، فَرَأَيْتُ الرَّجُلَ مِنْهُمْ يَكْدُمُ الأَرْضَ بِلِسَانِهِ حَتَّى يَمُوتَ
problematic_excerpt.english: But when they became healthy, they killed the shepherd of the Prophet (ﷺ) and drove away his camels. The Prophet (ﷺ) sent some people in their pursuit. Then he got their hands and feet cut and their eyes were branded with heated pieces of iron. I saw one of them licking the earth with his tongue till he died

bukhari:5685.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this was either strictly proportional retaliation (*qiṣāṣ*) for how the raiders killed the shepherd, or an early punishment later abrogated by the prohibition of mutilation (*muthlah*) and the revelation of [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that after amputating their hands and feet and branding their eyes (*wa-samara aʿyunahum*), Muhammad left them to die of exposure and dehydration in the volcanic stones until a man was seen biting the ground with his tongue until he died (*yakdumu al-arḍa bi-lisānihi ḥattā yamūta*), while [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33)—revealed specifically regarding this incident—permanently enshrined cross-amputation into Islamic law. Furthermore, the untranslated Arabic conclusion of this very narration records that Anas ibn Mālik cited this episode to the tyrant Al-Ḥajjāj as the 'severest punishment' (*bi-ashaddi ʿuqūbatin*) Muhammad ever inflicted, prompting Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī to lament that Anas had handed a ruthless governor a prophetic precedent for torture (*wadidtu annahu lam yuḥaddithhu bi-hādhā*).

muslim:7023.note: When a man is suspected (*kāna yuttahamu*) in connection with Muhammad's concubine-mother of his child (*umm walad*), Muhammad issues an unconditional command to Ali to 'go and strike his neck' (*idhhab fa-ḍrib ʿunuqahu*) without prior investigation or questioning. The execution is averted only when Ali pulls the man from a well where he was cooling himself and discovers that he is completely castrated and lacks a penis (*majbūb laysa lahu dhakar*), prompting Ali to refrain from killing him and report his condition to Muhammad.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَجُلاً، كَانَ يُتَّهَمُ بِأُمِّ وَلَدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِعَلِيٍّ ‏ "‏ اذْهَبْ فَاضْرِبْ عُنُقَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَأَتَاهُ عَلِيٌّ فَإِذَا هُوَ فِي رَكِيٍّ يَتَبَرَّدُ فِيهَا فَقَالَ لَهُ عَلِيٌّ اخْرُجْ ‏.‏ فَنَاوَلَهُ يَدَهُ فَأَخْرَجَهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ مَجْبُوبٌ لَيْسَ لَهُ ذَكَرٌ فَكَفَّ عَلِيٌّ عَنْهُ ثُمَّ أَتَى النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَمَجْبُوبٌ مَا لَهُ ذَكَرٌ
problematic_excerpt.english: Anas reported that a person was charged with fornication with the slavegirl of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ). Thereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said to 'Ali:Go and strike his neck. 'Ali came to him and he found him in a well making his body cool. 'Ali said to him: Come out, and as he took hold of his hand and brought him out, he found that his sexual organ had been cut. Hadrat 'Ali refrained from striking his neck. He came to Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) and said: Allah's Messenger, he has not even the sexual organ with him

muslim:7023.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad either issued the execution order as a calculated bluff while already knowing the man was a eunuch in order to publicly exonerate his concubine (*umm walad*), or intended for Ali to investigate the accusation before carrying out any punishment. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that upon mere suspicion (*kāna yuttahamu*), Muhammad gave the unconditional command, 'Go and strike his neck' (*idhhab fa-ḍrib ʿunuqahu*), without ordering an inquiry or demanding the four witnesses required by [Quran 24:4](quran://24/4). Furthermore, the particle of unexpected discovery (*fa-idhā*) in *fa-idhā huwa majbūbun laysa lahu dhakar* ('and behold, he was completely castrated, having no penis') and Ali's subsequent report back to the Prophet ('O Messenger of Allah, he is completely castrated; he has no penis') demonstrate that neither Ali nor Muhammad knew of his condition beforehand, and that Ali refrained (*fa-kaffa ʿAlīyun ʿanhu*) only because pulling the man from a well where he was cooling himself accidentally exposed his anatomy.

muslim:4596.note: After the people of Qurayza surrendered to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, he decreed that their fighters (*muqātilatahum*) be killed and their women and children enslaved (*tasbī dhurriyyatahum*). Muhammad ratified this sentence as the direct judgment of Allah, the Sovereign King (*al-Malik*) (bukhari:3043, bukhari:4121).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: نَزَلَ أَهْلُ قُرَيْظَةَ عَلَى حُكْمِ سَعْدِ بْنِ مُعَاذٍ فَأَرْسَلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى سَعْدٍ فَأَتَاهُ عَلَى حِمَارٍ فَلَمَّا دَنَا قَرِيبًا مِنَ الْمَسْجِدِ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِلأَنْصَارِ ‏"‏ قُومُوا إِلَى سَيِّدِكُمْ - أَوْ خَيْرِكُمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ هَؤُلاَءِ نَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ تَقْتُلُ مُقَاتِلَتَهُمْ وَتَسْبِي ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ قَضَيْتَ بِحُكْمِ اللَّهِ - وَرُبَّمَا قَالَ - قَضَيْتَ بِحُكْمِ الْمَلِكِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The people of Quraiza surrendered accepting the decision of Sa'd b. Mu'adh about them. Accordingly, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Sa'd who came to him riding a donkey. When he approached the mosque, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the Ansar: Stand up to receive your chieftain. Then he said (to Sa'd): These people have surrendered accepting your decision. He (Sa'd) said: You will kill their fighters and capture their women and children. (Hearing this), the Prophet (ﷺ) said: You have adjudged by the command of God. The narrator is reported to have said: Perhaps he said: You have adjudged by the decision of a king.

muslim:4596.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the punishment of Banu Qurayza was merely the independent tribal arbitration of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh—citing the English rendering 'the decision of a king'—and applied only to guilty combatants. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that after the tribe surrendered, Sa'd decreed both the mass execution of their fighting-age men and the enslavement of their women and children (*taqtulu muqātilatahum wa tasbī dhurriyyatahum*). Furthermore, Muhammad ratified this collective sentence as the direct decree of God, declaring, 'You have judged by the judgment of Allah' (*qaḍayta bi-ḥukmi Allāh*) and 'by the judgment of the Sovereign King' (*bi-ḥukmi al-Malik*), aligning with [Quran 33:26](quran://33/26) and `bukhari:3043`.

muslim:4596.note: When the people of Qurayza surrendered to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, he decreed the enslavement of their women and children (*tasbī dhurriyyatahum*) alongside the execution of their fighters. Muhammad endorsed this decree reducing their non-combatant women and children into chattel captivity (*saby*) as the judgment of Allah, the Sovereign King (*al-Malik*) (bukhari:3043, bukhari:4121).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ هَؤُلاَءِ نَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ تَقْتُلُ مُقَاتِلَتَهُمْ وَتَسْبِي ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ قَضَيْتَ بِحُكْمِ اللَّهِ - وَرُبَّمَا قَالَ - قَضَيْتَ بِحُكْمِ الْمَلِكِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Then he said (to Sa'd): These people have surrendered accepting your decision. He (Sa'd) said: You will kill their fighters and capture their women and children. (Hearing this), the Prophet (ﷺ) said: You have adjudged by the command of God. The narrator is reported to have said: Perhaps he said: You have adjudged by the decision of a king.

muslim:4596.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the non-combatant women and children of Banu Qurayza were merely detained in protective custody, relying on the euphemistic English translation 'capture their women and children.' However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *wa tasbī dhurriyyatahum* (`وَتَسْبِي ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ`), using the legal verb for reducing women and children into chattel slavery (*saby*) upon their surrender. Rather than exempting non-combatants, Muhammad endorsed their enslavement alongside the execution of the men as the judgment of Allah (`قَضَيْتَ بِحُكْمِ اللَّهِ`), as confirmed in [Quran 33:26](quran://33/26) and `bukhari:4121`.

muslim:4588.note: After the Muslims capture seventy prisoners at the Battle of Badr, Umar urges Muhammad to reject Abu Bakr's counsel of ransom and instead have the captives beheaded, with Ali striking off the neck of Aqil and Umar beheading his own relative. The next day, Muhammad and Abu Bakr weep because Allah brought the Muslims' punishment closer than a nearby tree for taking ransom and revealed [Quran 8:67](quran://8/67), declaring that a prophet may not take captives until he has committed extensive slaughter in the land.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا أَسَرُوا الأُسَارَى قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لأَبِي بَكْرٍ وَعُمَرَ ‏"‏ مَا تَرَوْنَ فِي هَؤُلاَءِ الأُسَارَى ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ هُمْ بَنُو الْعَمِّ وَالْعَشِيرَةِ أَرَى أَنْ تَأْخُذَ مِنْهُمْ فِدْيَةً فَتَكُونُ لَنَا قُوَّةً عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ فَعَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَهْدِيَهُمْ لِلإِسْلاَمِ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ مَا تَرَى يَا ابْنَ الْخَطَّابِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ لاَ وَاللَّهِ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ مَا أَرَى الَّذِي رَأَى أَبُو بَكْرٍ وَلَكِنِّي أَرَى أَنْ تُمَكِّنَّا فَنَضْرِبَ أَعْنَاقَهُمْ فَتُمَكِّنَ عَلِيًّا مِنْ عَقِيلٍ فَيَضْرِبَ عُنُقَهُ وَتُمَكِّنِّي مِنْ فُلاَنٍ - نَسِيبًا لِعُمَرَ - فَأَضْرِبَ عُنُقَهُ فَإِنَّ هَؤُلاَءِ أَئِمَّةُ الْكُفْرِ وَصَنَادِيدُهَا فَهَوِيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَا قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ وَلَمْ يَهْوَ مَا قُلْتُ فَلَمَّا كَانَ مِنَ الْغَدِ جِئْتُ فَإِذَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ قَاعِدَيْنِ يَبْكِيَانِ قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَخْبِرْنِي مِنْ أَىِّ شَىْءٍ تَبْكِي أَنْتَ وَصَاحِبُكَ فَإِنْ وَجَدْتُ بُكَاءً بَكَيْتُ وَإِنْ لَمْ أَجِدْ بُكَاءً تَبَاكَيْتُ لِبُكَائِكُمَا ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَبْكِي لِلَّذِي عَرَضَ عَلَىَّ أَصْحَابُكَ مِنْ أَخْذِهِمُ الْفِدَاءَ لَقَدْ عُرِضَ عَلَىَّ عَذَابُهُمْ أَدْنَى مِنْ هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ شَجَرَةٍ قَرِيبَةٍ مِنْ نَبِيِّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏ وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ‏{‏ مَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ أَسْرَى حَتَّى يُثْخِنَ فِي الأَرْضِ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏{‏ فَكُلُوا مِمَّا غَنِمْتُمْ حَلاَلاً طَيِّبًا‏}‏ فَأَحَلَّ اللَّهُ الْغَنِيمَةَ لَهُمْ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr and `Umar (Allah be pleased with them): What is your opinion about these captives? Abu Bakr said: They are our kith and kin. I think you should release them after getting from them a ransom. This will be a source of strength to us against the infidels. It is quite possible that Allah may guide them to Islam. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: What is your opinion, Ibn Khattab? He said: Messenger of Allah, I do not hold the same opinion as Abu Bakr. I am of the opinion that you should hand them over to us so that we may cut off their heads. Hand over `Aqil to `Ali that he may cut off his head, and hand over such and such relative to me that I may cut off his head. They are leaders of the disbelievers and veterans among them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) approved the opinion of Abu Bakr and did not approve what I said. The next day when I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I found that both he and Abu Bakr were sitting shedding tears. I said: Messenger of Allah, why are you and your Companion shedding tears? Tell me the reason. For I will weep, or I will at least pretend to weep in sympathy with you. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: I weep for what has happened to your companions for taking ransom (from the prisoners). I was shown the torture to which they were subjected. It was brought to me as close as this tree. (He pointed to a tree close to him.) Then God revealed the verse: "It is not befitting for a prophet that he should take prisoners until the force of the disbelievers has been crushed..." to the end of the verse: "so eat ye the spoils of war, (it is) lawful and pure. So Allah made booty lawful for them

muslim:4588.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's decision to ransom the seventy captives of Badr demonstrates prophetic mercy, and that [Quran 8:67](quran://8/67) merely addresses neutralizing enemy military power. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad wept because Allah presented the companions' punishment (`عَذَابُهُمْ`) closer than a nearby tree specifically for taking ransom (`مِنْ أَخْذِهِمُ الْفِدَاءَ`) rather than adopting Umar's proposal to strike off the prisoners' necks (`فَنَضْرِبَ أَعْنَاقَهُمْ`). Far from endorsing clemency, the revealed phrase `حَتَّى يُثْخِنَ فِي الأَرْضِ` rebukes the prophet for taking captives before inflicting heavy slaughter in the land.

muslim:4588.note: Muhammad weeps that his Companions' punishment was brought closer than a nearby tree because they proposed taking ransom from their captured relatives at Badr instead of beheading them as Umar urged. In the same revelation condemning the taking of captives before committing extensive slaughter in the land ([Quran 8:67](quran://8/67)), Allah concludes by making the war booty they collected 'lawful and pure' for them to consume ([Quran 8:69](quran://8/69)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَبْكِي لِلَّذِي عَرَضَ عَلَىَّ أَصْحَابُكَ مِنْ أَخْذِهِمُ الْفِدَاءَ لَقَدْ عُرِضَ عَلَىَّ عَذَابُهُمْ أَدْنَى مِنْ هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ شَجَرَةٍ قَرِيبَةٍ مِنْ نَبِيِّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏ وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ‏{‏ مَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ أَسْرَى حَتَّى يُثْخِنَ فِي الأَرْضِ‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏{‏ فَكُلُوا مِمَّا غَنِمْتُمْ حَلاَلاً طَيِّبًا‏}‏ فَأَحَلَّ اللَّهُ الْغَنِيمَةَ لَهُمْ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: I weep for what has happened to your companions for taking ransom (from the prisoners). I was shown the torture to which they were subjected. It was brought to me as close as this tree. (He pointed to a tree close to him.) Then God revealed the verse: "It is not befitting for a prophet that he should take prisoners until the force of the disbelievers has been crushed..." to the end of the verse: "so eat ye the spoils of war, (it is) lawful and pure. So Allah made booty lawful for them

muslim:4588.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the rebuke in [Quran 8:67](quran://8/67) only addressed a procedural error in taking ransom before receiving formal divine permission, which Allah then pardoned by legalizing war spoils in [Quran 8:69](quran://8/69). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah threatened the Muslims with imminent punishment (`عَذَابُهُمْ أَدْنَى مِنْ هَذِهِ الشَّجَرَةِ`) for choosing Abu Bakr's counsel of taking ransom (`أَخْذِهِمُ الْفِدَاءَ`) over Umar's demand to behead the prisoners (`فَنَضْرِبَ أَعْنَاقَهُمْ`). Threatening divine torment for sparing captives in exchange for ransom while immediately declaring that exact same ransom and war booty lawful and good (`فَكُلُوا مِمَّا غَنِمْتُمْ حَلاَلاً طَيِّبًا`) establishes a contradictory moral standard within a single revelation.

muslim:1481.note: When men fail to attend the night congregational prayer, Muhammad declares his intention to appoint a substitute prayer leader, go to those who stayed behind, and order their houses burned down over them ('alayhim) with bundles of firewood, remarking that any of them would have attended if promised a fat meaty bone ([Luke 9:54-55](bible://lk/9/54-55)). Although the published English translation omits 'alayhim ('over them') and classical commentators explain that carrying out the act was stayed due to women and children inside the homes, the Arabic text explicitly records his threat to burn men inside their houses for missing prayer (cf. bukhari:644, muslim:3718).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَدَ نَاسًا فِي بَعْضِ الصَّلَوَاتِ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ لَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ أَنْ آمُرَ رَجُلاً يُصَلِّي بِالنَّاسِ ثُمَّ أُخَالِفَ إِلَى رِجَالٍ يَتَخَلَّفُونَ عَنْهَا فَآمُرَ بِهِمْ فَيُحَرِّقُوا عَلَيْهِمْ بِحُزَمِ الْحَطَبِ بُيُوتَهُمْ وَلَوْ عَلِمَ أَحَدُهُمْ أَنَّهُ يَجِدُ عَظْمًا سَمِينًا لَشَهِدَهَا ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) found some people absenting from certain prayers and he said: I intend that I order (a) person to lead people in prayer, and then go to the persons who do not join the (congregational prayer) and then order their houses to be burnt by the bundles of fuel. If one amongst them were to know that he would find a fat fleshy bone he would attend the night prayer

muslim:1481.literal_translation: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) missed some people at certain prayers and said: 'I strongly intended to order a man to lead the people in prayer, then go behind to men who stay back from it and order concerning them that their houses be burned down over them with bundles of firewood. Yet if one of them knew that he would find a fat meaty bone, he would attend it.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَآمُرَ بِهِمْ فَيُحَرِّقُوا عَلَيْهِمْ بِحُزَمِ الْحَطَبِ بُيُوتَهُمْ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and then order their houses to be burnt by the bundles of fuel
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and order concerning them that they burn down their houses over them with bundles of firewood
translation_issue.explanation: The translator omits 'ʿalayhim' ('over them'), softening Muhammad's threat to burn men alive inside their homes into mere property destruction.

muslim:1481.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this was merely an unexecuted, hyperbolic deterrent directed at known hypocrites (*munāfiqūn*) rather than a literal command against ordinary Muslims. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *fayuḥarriqū ʿalayhim bi-ḥuzami al-ḥaṭabi buyūtahum* ('burn down their houses over them with bundles of firewood') for the offense of missing the night prayer (*ṣalāt al-ʿishāʾ*). Furthermore, parallel traditions (*Musnad Aḥmad* 8796) and classical commentators like Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar confirm that Muhammad only refrained from burning these men alive because exempt women and children were inside the homes, proving his intent to inflict lethal immolation was literal.

muslim:4549.note: When asked about polytheists being attacked in nighttime raids in which their women and children are struck and killed, Muhammad permitted the practice by declaring, "They are from them." While neighboring reports (muslim:4547, muslim:4548) forbid deliberately targeting women and children in battle, this ruling excuses their deaths during night raids on the grounds that they belong to the polytheists.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سُئِلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنِ الذَّرَارِيِّ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ يُبَيَّتُونَ فَيُصِيبُونَ مِنْ نِسَائِهِمْ وَذَرَارِيِّهِمْ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ هُمْ مِنْهُمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: It is reported on the authority of Sa'b b. Jaththama that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), when asked about the women and children of the polytheists being killed during the night raid, said:They are from them

muslim:4549.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islamic warfare protects non-combatants and that this report only addresses unintended collateral damage in the dark. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that when Muhammad was asked about conducting night raids (*yubayyatūna*) in which the women and children of the polytheists are struck (*fa-yuṣībūna min nisāʾihim wa-dharārīhim*), he did not prohibit the raids. Instead, he justified their deaths by grouping the women and children with the polytheists, declaring, "They are from them" (*hum minhum*), as also recorded in bukhari:3012, muslim:4550, and muslim:4551.

muslim:4622.note: During the Conquest of Mecca, Muhammad signals the Ansar with his hands to kill the followers of Quraysh until meeting him at al-Safa—a gesture explicitly verbalized in the adjacent narration as "Mow them down completely" (*uḥṣudūhum ḥaṣdan*, muslim:4623). Abu Huraira reports that the Muslims then killed whomever they wished while none of the Meccans directed any resistance against them (*wa-mā aḥadun minhum yuwajjihu ilaynā shay'an*), continuing until Abu Sufyan pleaded that the multitude of Quraysh was being exterminated (*ubīḥat khaḍrā'u Quraysh*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ تَرَوْنَ إِلَى أَوْبَاشِ قُرَيْشٍ وَأَتْبَاعِهِمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ بِيَدَيْهِ إِحْدَاهُمَا عَلَى الأُخْرَى ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ حَتَّى تُوَافُونِي بِالصَّفَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَانْطَلَقْنَا فَمَا شَاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنَّا أَنْ يَقْتُلَ أَحَدًا إِلاَّ قَتَلَهُ وَمَا أَحَدٌ مِنْهُمْ يُوَجِّهُ إِلَيْنَا شَيْئًا - قَالَ - فَجَاءَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أُبِيحَتْ خَضْرَاءُ قُرَيْشٍ لاَ قُرَيْشَ بَعْدَ الْيَوْمِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said (to the Ansar): You see the ruffians and the (lowly) followers of the Quraish. And he indicated by (striking) one of his hands over the other that they should be killed and said: Meet me at as-Safa. Then we went on (and) if any one of us wanted that a certain person should be killed, he was killed, and none could offer any resistance. Abu Huraira continued: Then came Abu Sufyan and said: Messenger of Allah, the blood of the Quraish has become very cheap. There will be no Quraish from this day on.

muslim:4622.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the Conquest of Mecca in AD 630 was a peaceful entry in which force was used only defensively after the Quraysh sent their ruffians (*awbāsh*) forward, and that Muhammad prioritized amnesty by declaring Abu Sufyan's house a sanctuary. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad personally signaled the Ansar with his hands to kill them until meeting him at al-Safa, and Abu Huraira testifies that the Muslims killed whomever they wished (*fa-mā shā'a aḥadun minnā an yaqtula aḥadan illā qatalahu*) while not a single Meccan directed any resistance against them (*wa-mā aḥadun minhum yuwajjihu ilaynā shay'an*). Furthermore, the sanctuary at Abu Sufyan's house was granted only after this unresisted killing was already underway and Abu Sufyan pleaded that the collective body of Quraysh had been exterminated (*ubīḥat khaḍrā'u Quraysh*).

bukhari:6799.note: Muhammad declares that Allah curses a thief whose hand is cut off for stealing an egg (*al-baydah*) or a rope (*al-habl*). To reconcile this literal wording with neighboring reports setting the minimum threshold for hand amputation at a quarter-dinar or three dirhams (bukhari:6797, bukhari:6798), classical commentators either argue that this statement preceded the fixed threshold or reinterpret the Arabic terms as an iron helmet and a ship's rope.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَعَنَ اللَّهُ السَّارِقَ، يَسْرِقُ الْبَيْضَةَ فَتُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ، وَيَسْرِقُ الْحَبْلَ فَتُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah curses the thief who steals an egg (or a helmet) for which his hand is to be cut off, or steals a rope, for which his hand is to be cut off

bukhari:6799.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that `al-bayḍah` refers to an expensive iron helmet rather than an egg and `al-ḥabl` refers to a costly ship's cable—or that the statement merely warns how petty theft escalates into crimes meeting the quarter-dinar threshold (*niṣāb*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `يَسْرِقُ الْبَيْضَةَ فَتُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ، وَيَسْرِقُ الْحَبْلَ فَتُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ` ('he steals an egg and so his hand is cut off, and he steals a rope and so his hand is cut off'), using the immediate causal particle `fa-` (`فَتُقْطَعُ`) to link amputation directly to these trivial items. Furthermore, the preceding narration (`bukhari:6798`) reveals that the 'iron helmet' gloss was a later scholarly conjecture (`kānū yarawna`) invented to harmonize conflicting traditions, and even the alternative threshold in `bukhari:6789` still mandates permanent physical mutilation (Quran 5:38) over a mere quarter-dinar (three dirhams).

muslim:5641.note: Anas ibn Malik reports that when a man looked into one of Muhammad's chambers, Muhammad rose toward him with a broad iron arrowhead (*mishqaṣ*) and crept up stealthily upon him (*yakhtiluhu*) to stab him. Parallel and neighboring reports (bukhari:6242, muslim:5639, muslim:5642) pair this incident with Muhammad's ruling that putting out the eye of an unpermitted onlooker incurs no liability.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، أَنَّ رَجُلاً، اطَّلَعَ مِنْ بَعْضِ حُجَرِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ بِمِشْقَصٍ أَوْ مَشَاقِصَ فَكَأَنِّي أَنْظُرُ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَخْتِلُهُ لِيَطْعُنَهُ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Anas b. Malik reported that a person peeped in some of the holes (in the doors) of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) (and he found him) standing up (lifting) an arrow or some arrows. The narrator said:I perceived as if Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was going to pierce (his eyes)

muslim:5641.literal_translation: From Anas b. Malik: that a man looked into some of the chambers of the Prophet (ﷺ), so he rose toward him with a broad iron arrowhead or arrowheads; and it is as though I am looking at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) creeping up stealthily upon him to stab him.

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ بِمِشْقَصٍ أَوْ مَشَاقِصَ فَكَأَنِّي أَنْظُرُ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَخْتِلُهُ لِيَطْعُنَهُ
translation_issue.published_rendering: (and he found him) standing up (lifting) an arrow or some arrows. The narrator said:I perceived as if Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was going to pierce (his eyes)
translation_issue.literal_meaning: so he rose toward him with a broad iron arrowhead or arrowheads, and it is as though I am looking at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) creeping up stealthily upon him to stab him
translation_issue.explanation: The translator omits 'yakhtiluhu' ('creeping up stealthily upon him by surprise') and alters 'fa-qāma ilayhi' ('so he rose toward him') into '(and he found him) standing up' to obscure Muhammad actively stalking the man to stab him with an arrowhead.

muslim:5641.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was merely protecting domestic privacy by making a deterrent gesture to scare away an intruder rather than attempting to maim him. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad "rose toward him with a broad iron arrowhead (*bi-mishqaṣin*)" and was "creeping up stealthily upon him to stab him (*yakhtiluhu li-yaṭʿanahu*)" (see also `bukhari:6242`, `muslim:5638`, and `muslim:5642`). Approaching by stealth (*yakhtiluhu*) rather than issuing a verbal warning prevents the person from retreating before being struck with the iron blade, contrasting with Jesus' rejection of physical retaliation ([Matthew 5:38](bible://mt/5/38)).

bukhari:6795.note: Muhammad cuts off a thief's hand for stealing a shield valued at three dirhams, establishing the canonical minimum property threshold (nisab) for the hadd punishment of hand amputation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَطَعَ فِي مِجَنٍّ ثَمَنُهُ ثَلاَثَةُ دَرَاهِمَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) cut off the hand of a thief for stealing a shield that was worth three Dirhams

bukhari:6795.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Quranic hand amputation (Quran 5:38) is a rare deterrent reserved strictly for grand larceny, claiming that the minimum legal threshold (niṣāb) of a quarter-dinar (three silver dirhams) represented substantial wealth in 7th-century AD Arabia. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad severed a hand (qaṭaʿa) for a single shield worth a mere three dirhams (fī mijannin thamanuhu thalāthatu darāhima), a sum so trivial that parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:6789; muslim:4408) record the amputation of thieves' hands for stealing items as cheap as an ordinary rope (ḥabl) or an egg (bayḍah).

muslim:1482.note: Declaring the night and dawn prayers heaviest for hypocrites, Muhammad states his intention to appoint a man to lead the people in prayer while he takes men carrying bundles of firewood to burn down the houses of congregational prayer absentees over them (`ʿalayhim`, omitted in the published English translation) with fire ([Luke 9:54](bible://lk/9/54)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ إِنَّ أَثْقَلَ صَلاَةٍ عَلَى الْمُنَافِقِينَ صَلاَةُ الْعِشَاءِ وَصَلاَةُ الْفَجْرِ وَلَوْ يَعْلَمُونَ مَا فِيهِمَا لأَتَوْهُمَا وَلَوْ حَبْوًا وَلَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ أَنْ آمُرَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فَتُقَامَ ثُمَّ آمُرَ رَجُلاً فَيُصَلِّيَ بِالنَّاسِ ثُمَّ أَنْطَلِقَ مَعِي بِرِجَالٍ مَعَهُمْ حُزَمٌ مِنْ حَطَبٍ إِلَى قَوْمٍ لاَ يَشْهَدُونَ الصَّلاَةَ فَأُحَرِّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ بُيُوتَهُمْ بِالنَّارِ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: The most burdensome prayers for the hypocrites are the night prayer and the morning prayer. If they were to know the blessings they have in store, they would have come to them, even though crawling, and I thought that I should order the prayer to be commenced and command a person to lead people in prayer, and I should then go along with some persons having a fagot of fuel with them to the people who have not attended the prayer (in congregation) and would burn their houses with fire

muslim:1482.literal_translation: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, the heaviest prayers for the hypocrites are the night prayer and the dawn prayer. Had they known what is in them, they would have come to them even if crawling. And I strongly intended to order the prayer to be established, then command a man to lead the people in prayer, and then set out with men carrying bundles of firewood with me to a people who do not attend the prayer, and burn down their houses over them with fire.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَأُحَرِّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ بُيُوتَهُمْ بِالنَّارِ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and would burn their houses with fire
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and burn down their houses over them with fire
translation_issue.explanation: The published translation omits 'ʿalayhim' ('over them / upon them'), obscuring that the threat is to burn the houses down over the absentees while they remain inside rather than merely burning empty structures.

muslim:1482.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this was merely an unexecuted rhetorical warning (`hamamtu`, 'I intended') directed solely at treasonous hypocrites, noting that commentators like Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar cite parallel narrations where Muhammad refrained from acting to spare the innocent women and children inside the homes. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `fa-uḥarriqa ʿalayhim buyūtahum bi-l-nār` ('and burn down their houses over them with fire'), proving that Islam's supreme moral exemplar genuinely desired to incinerate absentees alive for missing congregational prayer. Moreover, both Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) confirm that jurists cited this exact threat to establish the strict legal obligation (`farḍ ʿayn`) of congregational prayer for all Muslim men—demonstrating that only the logistical presence of dependents, rather than any moral objection to burning non-attendees alive, prevented him from carrying it out.

bukhari:3018.note: After eight men from 'Ukl killed a shepherd, drove away the camels, and apostatized, Muhammad had their hands and feet severed, ordered their eyes branded with heated iron nails, and left them in the rocky terrain of al-Harrah pleading for water until they died. The sub-narrator Abu Qilaba cites their murder, theft, and waging war against Allah and His Messenger ([Quran 5:33](quran://5/33)) as the basis for this punishment.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَمَا تَرَجَّلَ النَّهَارُ حَتَّى أُتِيَ بِهِمْ، فَقَطَّعَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَأَرْجُلَهُمْ، ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِمَسَامِيرَ فَأُحْمِيَتْ فَكَحَلَهُمْ بِهَا، وَطَرَحَهُمْ بِالْحَرَّةِ، يَسْتَسْقُونَ فَمَا يُسْقَوْنَ حَتَّى مَاتُوا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: before the sun rose high, they were brought, and he had their hands and feet cut off. Then he ordered for nails which were heated and passed over their eyes, and they were left in the Harra (i.e. rocky land in Medina). They asked for water, and nobody provided them with water till they died

bukhari:3018.literal_translation: before the day had fully advanced, they were brought, and he had their hands and feet severed. Then he ordered nails to be heated and seared their eyes with them, and cast them into al-Harrah; they kept pleading for water, but were not given any water until they died.

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَكَحَلَهُمْ بِهَا
translation_issue.published_rendering: passed over their eyes
translation_issue.literal_meaning: seared/pierced their eyes with them [like applying a kohl rod]
translation_issue.explanation: In classical Arabic usage and hadith commentary (e.g., Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī), 'kaḥalahum bihā' (lit. 'applied them to their eyes like kohl') denotes searing and blinding their eyes by drawing the red-hot iron nails directly into the eyes like a kohl probe—corresponding to 'fa-samala aʿyunahum' ('gouged out their eyes') in Bukhari's parallel narrations. Rendering this as 'passed over their eyes' softens direct ocular cauterization and blinding.

bukhari:3018.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this punishment was merely proportional retaliation (*qiṣāṣ*) for mutilating the shepherd, or that it occurred before Islamic law prohibited mutilation (*muthlah*) and established formal *ḥudūd* penalties. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states only that they killed the shepherd (`وَقَتَلُوا الرَّاعِيَ`) before Muhammad severed their hands and feet (`فَقَطَّعَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَأَرْجُلَهُمْ`), branded their eyes with heated iron nails (`فَكَحَلَهُمْ بِهَا`), and left them begging for water until they died (`يَسْتَسْقُونَ فَمَا يُسْقَوْنَ حَتَّى مَاتُوا`). Furthermore, the narration directly invokes the language of [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33) (`وَحَارَبُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ... وَسَعَوْا فِي الأَرْضِ فَسَادًا`), confirming that rather than abrogating this brutality, Allah revealed the *ḥirābah* verse on this exact occasion to permanently institutionalize cross-amputation as timeless divine law.

bukhari:3018.note: When eight men from 'Ukl fell ill from the climate of Medina and requested milk, Muhammad directed them to join the camel herd, where they drank the camels' urine and milk until they recovered and gained weight. While this abbreviated report simply states that the men drank the urine upon joining the herd, parallel narrations (bukhari:233, bukhari:5686, muslim:4353) explicitly record Muhammad commanding them to drink the camels' urine and milk as a remedy.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَهْطًا، مِنْ عُكْلٍ ثَمَانِيَةً قَدِمُوا عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَاجْتَوَوُا الْمَدِينَةَ فَقَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، ابْغِنَا رِسْلاً‏.‏ قَالَ ‏ "‏ مَا أَجِدُ لَكُمْ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَلْحَقُوا بِالذَّوْدِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَانْطَلَقُوا فَشَرِبُوا مِنْ أَبْوَالِهَا وَأَلْبَانِهَا حَتَّى صَحُّوا وَسَمِنُوا،
problematic_excerpt.english: A group of eight men from the tribe of 'Ukl came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and then they found the climate of Medina unsuitable for them. So, they said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Provide us with some milk." Allah's Apostle said, "I recommend that you should join the herd of camels." So they went and drank the urine and the milk of the camels (as a medicine) till they became healthy and fat.

bukhari:3018.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that prescribing camel urine was either non-binding, customary Bedouin folk medicine rather than divine revelation, or that modern studies validate camel urine's supposed therapeutic properties. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the men drank the camels' urine and milk (`فَشَرِبُوا مِنْ أَبْوَالِهَا وَأَلْبَانِهَا`) upon Muhammad's instruction—an explicit prophetic command (`فَأَمَرَهُمْ... فَيَشْرَبُوا مِنْ أَلْبَانِهَا وَأَبْوَالِهَا` in `bukhari:233`) that classical authorities like Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawī cite as binding *Sunnah* to rule the urine of edible animals ritually pure (*ṭāhir*) and medicinally lawful. Far from being a miraculous cure, ingesting camel urine and raw milk is scientifically documented by the World Health Organization (WHO) as a primary transmission vector for lethal Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS-CoV) and brucellosis.

bukhari:6805.note: After the recovered men kill the shepherd and drive away the camels, Muhammad orders their hands and feet cut off, their eyes branded with heated iron, and their bodies cast onto the stony ground of Al-Harra where their pleas for water are refused. The sub-narrator Abu Qilaba cites their theft, murder, apostasy, and waging war against Allah and His Messenger (cf. [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33)) as the basis for this punishment.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَمَرَ بِهِمْ فَقَطَعَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَأَرْجُلَهُمْ وَسَمَرَ أَعْيُنَهُمْ، فَأُلْقُوا بِالْحَرَّةِ يَسْتَسْقُونَ فَلاَ يُسْقَوْنَ
problematic_excerpt.english: He ordered to cut off their hands and legs and their eyes to be branded with heated iron pieces and they were thrown at Al-Harra, and when they asked for water to drink, they were not given water.

bukhari:6805.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim—that this punishment was strictly proportional retaliation (qiṣāṣ) because the men had mutilated the shepherd, or that such mutilation (muthlah) was later abrogated by the revelation of Quran 5:33. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states through Abū Qilābah's concluding legal ruling that these men were tortured because they 'waged war against Allah and His Messenger' (wa-ḥārabū Allāha wa-rasūlahu), directly invoking the exact wording of Quran 5:33—which classical Tafsir confirms was revealed about this very incident to codify cross-amputation and crucifixion as permanent law. Furthermore, the Arabic text records that Muhammad ordered heated iron nails driven into their eyes (wa-samara aʿyunahum) and left the amputees on the volcanic rocks of Al-Ḥarrah pleading for water while forbidding anyone from giving them a drink (yastasqūna fa-lā yusqawna), demonstrating that he personally authorized sadistic torture and death by dehydration.

bukhari:6805.note: When men from the Ukl or Uraina tribe arrive in Medina, Muhammad orders them to go to a herd of she-camels and drink their urine and milk until they recover from their illness.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَمَرَ لَهُمُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِلِقَاحٍ، وَأَمَرَهُمْ أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا فَيَشْرَبُوا مِنْ أَبْوَالِهَا وَأَلْبَانِهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered them to go to the herd of (Milch) she-camels and told them to go out and drink the camels' urine and milk (as a medicine).

bukhari:6805.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that prescribing camel urine was merely non-binding 7th-century AD Bedouin folk medicine for a localized abdominal ailment, or that modern studies validate its medicinal properties. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad directly commanded them to drink the animals' urine (fa-amarahum an yakhrujū fa-yashrabū min abwālihā), which led Al-Bukhārī to codify it in his Book of Medicine (bukhari:5686) and classical commentators like Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar to rule that the urine of edible animals is ritually pure (ṭāhir) and a normative Prophetic cure. Far from being divinely guided medicine, consuming raw camel excreta and unpasteurized milk is a documented vector for lethal zoonotic pathogens such as MERS-CoV and Brucella.

bukhari:7224.note: Muhammad swears an oath that he intended (`hamamtu`) to order firewood gathered, appoint a man to lead the congregational prayer, and go burn down the houses upon (`'alayhim`, omitted in the published English translation) the men who did not attend. Although he did not ultimately execute the act, the text explicitly records his sworn threat to burn men inside their homes for missing the congregational prayer.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ أَنْ آمُرَ بِحَطَبٍ يُحْتَطَبُ، ثُمَّ آمُرَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فَيُؤَذَّنَ لَهَا، ثُمَّ آمُرَ رَجُلاً فَيَؤُمَّ النَّاسَ، ثُمَّ أُخَالِفَ إِلَى رِجَالٍ فَأُحَرِّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ بُيُوتَهُمْ
problematic_excerpt.english: I was about to order for collecting fire wood and then order someone to pronounce the Adhan for the prayer and then order someone to lead the people in prayer and then I would go from behind and burn the houses of men who did not present themselves for the (compulsory congregational) prayer

bukhari:7224.literal_translation: I was about to order for firewood to be gathered, then order the prayer to be called, then order a man to lead the people in prayer, and then go behind to men and burn their houses down upon them.

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَأُحَرِّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ بُيُوتَهُمْ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and burn the houses of men
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and burn their houses down upon them
translation_issue.explanation: The published translation omits the prepositional phrase 'alayhim ('upon them' / 'over them'), reducing 'burn their houses down upon them' (while the men are inside) to merely 'burn the houses of men' (property destruction).

bukhari:7224.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this threat was merely unexecuted rhetorical hyperbole (*zajr*) directed exclusively at known hypocrites (*munāfiqūn*), citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* to claim Muhammad refrained out of mercy for the innocent women and children inside the homes. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states under a solemn divine oath (*wa-alladhī nafsī bi-yadihi*) that Muhammad seriously resolved (*la-qad hamamtu*) to burn their houses down "upon them" (*fa-uḥarriqa ʿalayhim buyūtahum*)—a crucial preposition omitted in the English translation—while parallel narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 644, *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 652) apply this threat broadly to men who fail to attend congregational prayer (*lā yashhadūna al-ṣalāt*). Rather than dismissing it as empty hyperbole, classical Sunni jurists cited this very narration as legal proof for physically punishing those who abandon congregational prayer, exposing how the text weaponizes the threat of burning men alive for religious coercion.

muslim:4354.note: After eight men from the tribe of Ukl kill the shepherd and drive off the camels, Muhammad sends men in pursuit to capture them and orders that their hands and feet be cut off, their eyes pierced and branded with heated iron nails (*sumira/summirat aʿyunuhum*), and that they be cast out in the sun until they die.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَتَلُوا الرَّاعِيَ وَطَرَدُوا الإِبِلَ فَبَلغَ ذَلِكَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَبَعَثَ فِي آثَارِهِمْ فَأُدْرِكُوا فَجِيءَ بِهِمْ فَأَمَرَ بِهِمْ فَقُطِعَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُمْ وَسُمِرَ أَعْيُنُهُمْ ثُمَّ نُبِذُوا فِي الشَّمْسِ حَتَّى مَاتُوا ‏.‏ وَقَالَ ابْنُ الصَّبَّاحِ فِي رِوَايَتِهِ وَاطَّرَدُوا النَّعَمَ ‏.‏ وَقَالَ وَسُمِّرَتْ أَعْيُنُهُمْ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: They killed the shepherd and drove away the camels. This (news) reached Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and he sent them on their track and they were caught and brought to him (the Holy Prophet). He commanded about them, and (thus) their hands and feet were cut off and their eyes were gouged and then they were thrown in the sun, until they died. This hadith has been narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Sabbah with a slight variation of words

muslim:4354.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the punishment inflicted on the eight men of 'Ukl was merely proportional retaliation for how they treated the shepherd, while relying on softened English translations that render the blinding simply as 'gouged.' However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states only that the men killed the shepherd and drove away the camels (fa-qatalū al-rāʿī wa-ṭaradū al-ibil), whereas Muhammad commanded (fa-amara bihim) that their hands and feet be cut off (fa-quṭiʿat aydīhim wa-arjuluhum), their eyes be branded with heated iron nails (wa-sumira aʿyunuhum, and in Ibn al-Sabbah's narration wa-summirat aʿyunuhum), and their bodies be cast out into the sun until they died (thumma nubidhū fī al-shams ḥattā mātū). This sequence of quadruple amputation, ocular branding with iron nails, and death by exposure in the sun goes beyond simple execution for murder and cattle theft as recorded across the parallel narrations (bukhari:233, bukhari:5685, muslim:4353, muslim:4355).

muslim:4354.note: When eight men from the tribe of Ukl find the climate of the land uncongenial and fall sick, Muhammad instructs them to go out with his shepherd to his camels and drink their urine and milk (*abwālihā wa-albānihā*) to regain their health.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ نَفَرًا، مِنْ عُكْلٍ ثَمَانِيَةً قَدِمُوا عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَبَايَعُوهُ عَلَى الإِسْلاَمِ فَاسْتَوْخَمُوا الأَرْضَ وَسَقُمَتْ أَجْسَامُهُمْ فَشَكَوْا ذَلِكَ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ أَلاَ تَخْرُجُونَ مَعَ رَاعِينَا فِي إِبِلِهِ فَتُصِيبُونَ مِنْ أَبْوَالِهَا وَأَلْبَانِهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالُوا بَلَى ‏.‏ فَخَرَجُوا فَشَرِبُوا مِنْ أَبْوَالِهَا وَأَلْبَانِهَا فَصَحُّوا
problematic_excerpt.english: Eight men of the tribe of 'Ukl came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and swore allegiance to him on Islam, but found the climate of that land uncogenial to their health and thus they became sick, and they made complaint of that to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), and he said: Why don't you go to (the fold) of our camels along with our shepherd, and make use of their milk and urine. They said: Yes. They set out and drank their (camels') milk and urine and regained their health.

muslim:4354.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that prescribing camel urine was merely an incidental desert custom rather than a prophetic medical remedy, or claim that the sick men primarily drank the camels' milk. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that when the eight men of 'Ukl complained of their illness to Muhammad (fa-shakaw dhālika ilā rasūli Allāh), he directly instructed them to go out with his shepherd and consume both the camels' urine and milk (fa-tuṣībūna min abwālihā wa-albānihā), placing the urine (abwālihā) first in the Arabic phrasing. Furthermore, the text directly attributes their recovery to drinking both substances (fa-sharibū min abwālihā wa-albānihā fa-ṣaḥḥū), presenting the ingestion of animal waste as an effective prophetic cure across the parallel reports (bukhari:233, bukhari:5686, muslim:4353, muslim:4355).

muslim:4357.note: In this abridged narration regarding the eight men from the tribe of 'Ukl (cf. muslim:4353, muslim:4354), Anas bin Malik adds the explicit detail that Muhammad did not cauterize (*wa-lam yaḥsimhum*) the wounds inflicted upon them during their punishment.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، قَالَ قَدِمَ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثَمَانِيَةُ نَفَرٍ مِنْ عُكْلٍ ‏.‏ بِنَحْوِ حَدِيثِهِمْ ‏.‏ وَزَادَ فِي الْحَدِيثِ وَلَمْ يَحْسِمْهُمْ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Anas b. Malik reported:There came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) eight persons from the tribe of 'Ukl, but with this addition that he did not cauterise (the wounds which hid been inflicted upon them while punishing them)

muslim:4357.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the punishment of the eight men from the tribe of Ukl was a standard legal execution and that Muhammad prohibited mutilation or prolonged suffering during capital punishment. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that he "did not cauterize them" (*wa-lam yaḥsimhum*), confirming that after their hands and feet were cut off, their stumps were left untreated to bleed to death (muslim:4353, muslim:4354, bukhari:6802).

muslim:4598.note: Upon Muhammad's return from the Battle of the Ditch, the angel Gabriel appears and orders him to march against Banu Qurayza, whom Muhammad fights until they surrender to his judgment. Muhammad then refers the ruling over them to Sa'd, who decrees that their fighting men (*al-muqātila*) be killed, their children and women be enslaved, and their property be distributed—a judgment Muhammad ratifies as the decree of Allah in parallel reports (muslim:4596, muslim:4597, muslim:4599).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا رَجَعَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنَ الْخَنْدَقِ وَضَعَ السِّلاَحَ فَاغْتَسَلَ فَأَتَاهُ جِبْرِيلُ وَهُوَ يَنْفُضُ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ الْغُبَارِ فَقَالَ وَضَعْتَ السِّلاَحَ وَاللَّهِ مَا وَضَعْنَاهُ اخْرُجْ إِلَيْهِمْ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ فَأَيْنَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَأَشَارَ إِلَى بَنِي قُرَيْظَةَ فَقَاتَلَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَنَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَرَدَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْحُكْمَ فِيهِمْ إِلَى سَعْدٍ قَالَ فَإِنِّي أَحْكُمُ فِيهِمْ أَنْ تُقْتَلَ الْمُقَاتِلَةُ وَأَنْ تُسْبَى الذُّرِّيَّةُ وَالنِّسَاءُ وَتُقْسَمَ أَمْوَالُهُمْ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When he returned from the Ditch and laid down his arms and took a bath, the angel Gabriel appeared to him and he was removing dust from his hair (as if he had just returned from the battle). The latter said: You have laid down arms. By God, we haven't (yet) laid them down. So march against them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked: Where? He pointed to Banu Quraiza. So the Messenger of Allah (may peace he upon him) fought against them. They surrendered at the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but he referred the decision about them to Sa'd who said: I decide about them that those of them who can fight be killed, their women and children taken prisoners and their properties distributed (among the Muslims)

muslim:4598.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the Banu Qurayza themselves selected Sa'd ibn Mu'adh as an independent arbitrator and that his decree to execute the men was a secular military verdict rather than a prophetic mandate from Muhammad. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the siege was launched at the direct command of the angel Gabriel (*ukhruj ilayhim*, 'Go out to them'), that the tribe surrendered directly to Muhammad's own judgment (*fanazalū ʿalā ḥukmi Rasūli Allāhi*), and that Muhammad personally referred their fate to Sa'd (*faradda Rasūlu Allāhi ... al-ḥukma fīhim ilā Saʿdin*). Furthermore, parallel narrations (`bukhari:4117`, `muslim:4596`) and [Quran 33:26](quran://33/26) confirm that the decree to kill the fighting men (*an tuqtala al-muqātilatu*) was endorsed as the judgment of Allah.

muslim:4598.note: When Banu Qurayza surrender to Muhammad's judgment, he delegates the decision concerning them to Sa'd, who decrees that their children and women be enslaved (*tusbā al-dhurriyyatu wa-l-nisā'*) and their wealth be divided among the Muslims. Although the English translation renders *tusbā* as 'taken prisoners,' the Arabic verb denotes captive enslavement, a ruling that Muhammad ratifies as the judgment of Allah in parallel reports (muslim:4596, muslim:4597, muslim:4599).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَنَزَلُوا عَلَى حُكْمِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَرَدَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْحُكْمَ فِيهِمْ إِلَى سَعْدٍ قَالَ فَإِنِّي أَحْكُمُ فِيهِمْ أَنْ تُقْتَلَ الْمُقَاتِلَةُ وَأَنْ تُسْبَى الذُّرِّيَّةُ وَالنِّسَاءُ وَتُقْسَمَ أَمْوَالُهُمْ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: They surrendered at the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but he referred the decision about them to Sa'd who said: I decide about them that those of them who can fight be killed, their women and children taken prisoners and their properties distributed (among the Muslims)

muslim:4598.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, relying on euphemistic English translations, that the women and children of Banu Qurayza were merely 'taken prisoners' for temporary protective custody and that non-combatants were spared from harm. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *wa-an tusbā al-dhurriyyatu wa-l-nisāʾu wa-tuqsama amwāluhum* ('and that the children and women be enslaved as captives, and that their wealth be divided'), employing the verb *tusbā* (from *sabā*), which denotes chattel enslavement rather than temporary detention. Because the tribe surrendered to Muhammad's judgment (*ḥukmi Rasūli Allāhi*), this collective enslavement of women and children and confiscation of their property was executed as a divinely sanctioned decree (`bukhari:2813`, `muslim:4596`, [Quran 33:26](quran://33/26)).

muslim:5642.note: Muhammad decrees that if someone looks into a people's house without their permission (*bi-ghayri idhnihim*), it is lawful (*ḥalla*) for the occupants to gouge out his eye (*yafqaʾū ʿaynahu*; cf. bukhari:6902, muslim:5641, muslim:5643).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ مَنِ اطَّلَعَ فِي بَيْتِ قَوْمٍ بِغَيْرِ إِذْنِهِمْ فَقَدْ حَلَّ لَهُمْ أَنْ يَفْقَئُوا عَيْنَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported having heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) say:He who peeped into the house of people without their consent, it is permissible for them to put out his eyes

muslim:5642.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this ruling is merely hyperbolic deterrence to protect domestic privacy or only covers accidental injury when driving a voyeur away. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *faqad ḥalla lahum an yafqaʾū ʿaynahu* ("it is permissible for them to put out his eyes"), directly granting homeowners lawful permission (*ḥalla*) to gouge out a person's eye (`muslim:5642`; cf. `bukhari:6902`, `muslim:5641`, `muslim:5643`). Rather than requiring a judicial process or prior warning, the decree authorizes summary blinding against anyone who looks (*iṭṭalaʿa*) into a house without consent (*bi-ghayri idhnihim*).

bukhari:6789.note: Unlike the biblical mandate of financial restitution for theft ([Exodus 22:1](bible://ex/22/1)), Muhammad decrees that a thief's hand must be amputated for stealing anything worth a quarter of a dinar or more, establishing the binding minimum monetary threshold (niṣāb) for the ḥadd punishment.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ تُقْطَعُ الْيَدُ فِي رُبُعِ دِينَارٍ فَصَاعِدًا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The hand should be cut off for stealing something that is worth a quarter of a Dinar or more

bukhari:6789.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the ḥadd punishment for theft ([Quran 5:38](quran://5/38)) functions primarily as a theoretical deterrent restricted by stringent legal conditions (such as safe custody, ḥirz, and the nisāb threshold), or that 'cutting off the hand' metaphorically means restraining the thief. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states 'tuqṭaʿu al-yadu fī rubʿi dīnārin fa-ṣāʿidan' ('the hand is cut off for a quarter of a dinar and upwards'), establishing a binding legal decree of literal physical amputation for a paltry sum. As Ibn Ḥajar confirms in Fatḥ al-Bārī alongside parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:6788, bukhari:6790, bukhari:6795), Muhammad strictly enforced this permanent mutilation in practice—amputating hands for a shield worth merely three dirhams and forbidding any intercession or restitution once a case reached him.

muslim:4624.note: During the Conquest of Mecca, Muhammad orders the Ansar to "mow down" (*taḥṣidūhum ḥaṣdan*) the rabble of Quraysh (*awbāsha qurayshin*), resulting in them putting to death everyone who came into their sight that day (*anāmūhu*). After Abu Sufyan pleads at Mount al-Safa that the Quraysh are being wiped out, Muhammad grants safety to anyone who enters Abu Sufyan's house, lays down his arms, or locks his door.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ ادْعُ لِي الأَنْصَارَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَدَعَوْتُهُمْ فَجَاءُوا يُهَرْوِلُونَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا مَعْشَرَ الأَنْصَارِ هَلْ تَرَوْنَ أَوْبَاشَ قُرَيْشٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ انْظُرُوا إِذَا لَقِيتُمُوهُمْ غَدًا أَنْ تَحْصِدُوهُمْ حَصْدًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَأَخْفَى بِيَدِهِ وَوَضَعَ يَمِينَهُ عَلَى شِمَالِهِ وَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَوْعِدُكُمُ الصَّفَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَمَا أَشْرَفَ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَهُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ أَنَامُوهُ - قَالَ - وَصَعِدَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم الصَّفَا وَجَاءَتِ الأَنْصَارُ فَأَطَافُوا بِالصَّفَا فَجَاءَ أَبُو سُفْيَانَ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أُبِيدَتْ خَضْرَاءُ قُرَيْشٍ لاَ قُرَيْشَ بَعْدَ الْيَوْمِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He (then) said: Abu Huraira, call the Ansar to me. So I called out to them and they came hurriedly. He said: O ye Assembly of the Ansaar, do you see the ruffians of the Quraish? They said: Yes. He said: See, when you meet them tomorrow, wipe them out. He hinted at this with his hand, placing his right hand on his left and said: You will meet us at as-Safa'. (Abu Huraira continued): Whoever was seen by them that day was put to death. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ascended the mount of as-Safa'. The Ansar also came there and surrounded the mount. Then came Abu Sufyan and said: Messenger ot Allah, the Quraish have perished. No member of the Quraish tribe will survive this day.

muslim:4624.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the Conquest of Mecca was a peaceful victory in which Muhammad granted general amnesty—promising safety to anyone who entered the house of Abu Sufyan, laid down his arms, or locked his door—and that force was only directed against a faction of Quraysh ruffians (*awbāsh Quraysh*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that before the advance, Muhammad summoned the Ansar and commanded them to 'mow them down' (*an taḥṣidūhum ḥaṣdan*), placing his right hand on his left to gesture wiping them out. Consequently, the narration records that 'no one came into their sight that day except that they put him to death' (*famā ashrafa yawma'idhin lahum aḥadun illā anāmūhu*), and Muhammad only announced the terms of safety at as-Safa after Abu Sufyan cried out that the Quraysh had perished (*ubīdat khaḍrā'u Quraysh*).

muslim:4355.note: Following their apostasy, murder of a shepherd, and theft of camels as detailed in the fuller parallel reports (muslim:4353, muslim:4354), the men of Ukl or Uraynah had their eyes pierced with heated iron (*sumirat aʿyunuhum*) and were cast onto the stony volcanic ground (*al-harrah*) on Muhammad's orders. There they begged for water, and none was given to them.
