problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ وَسُمِرَتْ أَعْيُنُهُمْ وَأُلْقُوا فِي الْحَرَّةِ يَسْتَسْقُونَ فَلاَ يُسْقَوْنَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Their eyes were pierced, and they were thrown on the stony ground. They were asking for water, but they were not given water

muslim:4355.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this punishment was strict reciprocal retribution (*qiṣāṣ*) for the tribesmen's crimes or a temporary measure before mutilation was prohibited. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that their eyes were pierced (*wa-sumirat aʿyunuhum*) and they were cast onto the stony volcanic ground (*fī al-ḥarrah*), where they kept begging for water while being denied any drink (*yastasqūna fa-lā yusqawna*). As the full parallel reports in muslim:4353, muslim:4354, and bukhari:233 confirm, Muhammad ordered their limbs amputated, their eyes branded with iron nails, and their bodies left exposed without water until they died, establishing that he directly commanded prolonged execution by torture and dehydration.

muslim:4355.note: When people from the tribe of Ukl or Uraynah find the climate of Medina uncongenial and fall ill, Muhammad provides them with milch she-camels and commands them to drink the camels' urine (*abwaliha*) and milk.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَدِمَ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَوْمٌ مِنْ عُكْلٍ أَوْ عُرَيْنَةَ فَاجْتَوَوُا الْمَدِينَةَ فَأَمَرَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِلِقَاحٍ وَأَمَرَهُمْ أَنْ يَشْرَبُوا مِنْ أَبْوَالِهَا وَأَلْبَانِهَا ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Anas b. Malik reported that some people of the tribe of 'Ukl or 'Uraina came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), and they found the climate of Medina uncogenial. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) commanded them to the milch she-camels and commanded them to drink their urine and their milk.

muslim:4355.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that prescribing camel urine was either a non-binding concession to Bedouin folk remedies or a prophetic medical insight with unacknowledged therapeutic benefits. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that when the tribesmen fell ill in Medina (*fajtawaw al-madīnah*), Muhammad personally commanded them to drink from the camels' urine and milk (*wa-amarahum an yashrabū min abwālihā wa-albānihā*). Canonical collections including bukhari:5686 and muslim:4353 codify this command as normative prophetic medicine, binding Islamic tradition to the ingestion of animal waste that carries dangerous zoonotic pathogens.

muslim:4550.note: When Sa'b b. Jaththama informed Muhammad that Muslim forces kill the children of polytheists during night raids, Muhammad answered, "They are from them." While the preceding report (muslim:4548) prohibits deliberately killing women and children in battle, this ruling permits their deaths during night raids on the grounds that the children share the status of their polytheist parents.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّا نُصِيبُ فِي الْبَيَاتِ مِنْ ذَرَارِيِّ الْمُشْرِكِينَ قَالَ ‏ "‏ هُمْ مِنْهُمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: It is narrated by Sa'b b. Jaththama that he said (to the Holy Prophet):Messenger of Allah, we kill the children of the polytheists during the night raids. He said: They are from them

muslim:4550.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islamic law prohibits harming non-combatants and that the deaths of children during night raids (`al-bayāt`) were merely regrettable collateral damage caused by darkness. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that when Sa'b ibn Jaththama reported killing the children of the polytheists (`dharāriyyi al-mushrikīn`), Muhammad neither expressed regret nor restricted night raids, instead justifying their deaths by declaring, "They are from them" (`hum minhum`). Rather than treating the children as protected individuals, Muhammad's ruling assigns them the collective status of their polytheist parents (`bukhari:3012`, `muslim:4549`, `muslim:4551`).

muslim:4551.note: When asked about cavalry launching a nighttime raid (*aghārat mina al-layl*) in which the children of polytheists are struck and killed, Muhammad replies, "They are of their fathers" (*hum min ābā'ihim*). Rather than prohibiting nighttime attacks that result in child casualties, he sanctions the raids by assigning the children the status of their polytheist fathers (cf. bukhari:3012, muslim:4549, muslim:4550).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قِيلَ لَهُ لَوْ أَنَّ خَيْلاً أَغَارَتْ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَأَصَابَتْ مِنْ أَبْنَاءِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ قَالَ ‏ "‏ هُمْ مِنْ آبَائِهِمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Sa'b b. Jaththama has narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) asked:What about the children of polytheists killed by the cavalry during the night raid? He said: They are from them

muslim:4551.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islamic military law forbids intentionally targeting children and that this ruling merely addresses unavoidable collateral casualties when darkness prevents cavalry from distinguishing non-combatants during a night raid. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that when asked about cavalry conducting a night raid (أَغَارَتْ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ, *aghārat min al-layl*) and striking the children of polytheists (فَأَصَابَتْ مِنْ أَبْنَاءِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ, *fa-aṣābat min abnā'i al-mushrikīn*), Muhammad permits the action by declaring, "They are from their fathers" (هُمْ مِنْ آبَائِهِمْ, *hum min ābā'ihim*). Rather than prohibiting night raids that kill children or treating the children as distinct innocents, his ruling subsumes their blood and legal status directly under their polytheist fathers (as also recorded in bukhari:3012, muslim:4549, and muslim:4550).

muslim:4360.note: Anas ibn Malik states that Muhammad pierced the eyes (*samala... aʿyuna*) of "those people" (*ulāʾika*—identified in the preceding and parallel narrations muslim:4353–muslim:4359 and bukhari:233 as the captured men of Ukl and Uraynah) because they had pierced the eyes of the shepherds.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ أَنَسٍ، قَالَ إِنَّمَا سَمَلَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَعْيُنَ أُولَئِكَ لأَنَّهُمْ سَمَلُوا أَعْيُنَ الرِّعَاءِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Anas reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) pierced their eyes because they had pierced the eyes of the shepherds

muslim:4360.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that piercing the captives' eyes was a justified act of proportionate legal reciprocation because the perpetrators had first committed the same act against the shepherds. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Prophet gouged out their eyes in direct retaliation (*innamā samala al-nabiyyu... aʿyuna ulāʾika li-annahum samalū aʿyuna al-riʿāʾ*), confirming that bodily mutilation was enacted as a prophetic punishment across parallel Sahih accounts (bukhari:233, muslim:4353, muslim:4354, muslim:4355). This practice of retaliatory blinding stands in direct contrast to the teaching of Jesus, who explicitly repudiated 'an eye for an eye' and commanded love for enemies ([Matthew 5:38](bible://mt/5/38), [Matthew 5:44](bible://mt/5/44)).

bukhari:657.note: Muhammad declared that the Fajr and Isha prayers are the heaviest upon the hypocrites, and stated his resolve to appoint a man to lead the congregation while he took torches of fire to burn upon those who had not come out to the prayer.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَيْسَ صَلاَةٌ أَثْقَلَ عَلَى الْمُنَافِقِينَ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ وَالْعِشَاءِ، وَلَوْ يَعْلَمُونَ مَا فِيهِمَا لأَتَوْهُمَا وَلَوْ حَبْوًا، لَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ أَنْ آمُرَ الْمُؤَذِّنَ فَيُقِيمَ، ثُمَّ آمُرَ رَجُلاً يَؤُمُّ النَّاسَ، ثُمَّ آخُذَ شُعَلاً مِنْ نَارٍ فَأُحَرِّقَ عَلَى مَنْ لاَ يَخْرُجُ إِلَى الصَّلاَةِ بَعْدُ
problematic_excerpt.english: No prayer is heavier upon the hypocrites than the Fajr and the `Isha' prayers and if they knew what is in them (in reward), they would have attended them, even if (it was) crawling. Certainly, I felt the urge to order the Mu'adh-dhin (call-maker) so that he would pronounce Iqama, then order a man to lead the people (in prayer), then take a flame of fire so that I burn (the houses) upon those who had not left for the prayer yet

bukhari:657.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's statement was merely rhetorical hyperbole (*zajr*) aimed solely at known hypocrites (*munāfiqūn*), noting that he never carried out the act and citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* (alongside *Musnad Aḥmad* 8796) that he refrained because women and children were inside the houses. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *"laqad hamamtu"* (لَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ — "I firmly resolved/intended") to take flames of fire and burn (*fa-uḥarriqa ʿalā*) the homes upon anyone who had not come out to the prayer (*man lā yakhruju ilā al-ṣalāh*), and parallel Sahih narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 644, 2420; *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 651) state he intended to burn their houses down upon them with bundles of firewood without restricting the threat to hypocrites. Furthermore, the very excuse cited in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that he held back solely to avoid collateral harm to exempt women and children—proves that burning the absent men alive was a literal, actionable intent rather than a figure of speech.

bukhari:233.note: After men from Ukl or Uraynah killed his shepherd, drove away his camels, and apostatized, Muhammad ordered their hands and feet cut off, their eyes branded with heated iron, and their bodies cast into the rocky plain of al-Harrah where they were denied water when they asked for it. The narrator Abu Qilaba cited their theft, murder, and apostasy as waging war against Allah and His Messenger ([Quran 5:33](quran://5/33)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَمَرَ فَقَطَعَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَأَرْجُلَهُمْ، وَسُمِرَتْ أَعْيُنُهُمْ، وَأُلْقُوا فِي الْحَرَّةِ يَسْتَسْقُونَ فَلاَ يُسْقَوْنَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He then ordered to cut their hands and feet (and it was done), and their eyes were branded with heated pieces of iron, They were put in 'Al-Harra' and when they asked for water, no water was given to them."

bukhari:233.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this punishment was either strict reciprocal retaliation (qisas) because the tribesmen had similarly mutilated the Prophet's shepherd (as recorded in muslim:4353), or that it occurred before the revelation of Quran 5:33 and the prophetic prohibition against mutilation (muthlah). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Abu Qilabah cited their crime of waging war against Allah and His Messenger (wa-harabu Allaha wa-rasulahu)—the exact phrasing of Quran 5:33, which classical tafsir confirms was revealed specifically regarding this incident to permanently institutionalize cross-amputation in Islamic law. Furthermore, the Arabic text records that after amputating their limbs and branding their eyes with heated iron (wa-sumirat a'yunuhum), Muhammad cast them onto the scorching volcanic rocks of al-Harrah begging for water while refusing to give them drink (yastasquna fala yusqawna), inflicting prolonged torture by dehydration that goes far beyond reciprocal execution.

bukhari:233.note: When people from the tribes of Ukl or Uraynah fell ill from the climate of Medina, Muhammad ordered them to go to a herd of milch camels and drink their urine and milk as a remedy.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَدِمَ أُنَاسٌ مِنْ عُكْلٍ أَوْ عُرَيْنَةَ، فَاجْتَوَوُا الْمَدِينَةَ، فَأَمَرَهُمُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِلِقَاحٍ، وَأَنْ يَشْرَبُوا مِنْ أَبْوَالِهَا وَأَلْبَانِهَا،
problematic_excerpt.english: Some people of `Ukl or `Uraina tribe came to Medina and its climate did not suit them. So the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered them to go to the herd of (Milch) camels and to drink their milk and urine (as a medicine).

bukhari:233.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that prescribing camel urine was either non-binding local Bedouin folk medicine rather than prophetic revelation, or conversely claim that modern scientific studies validate camel urine as a miraculous antimicrobial and anti-cancer therapy. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Prophet personally commanded them to drink the camels' urine alongside their milk (fa-amarahumu al-nabiyyu ... wa-an yashrabu min abwaliha wa-albaniha), leading Al-Bukhari (both here in the Book of Ablutions and in bukhari:5686 in the Book of Medicine), Al-Nawawi, and Ibn Hajar to codify this narration as binding proof of both the ritual purity (taharah) and divinely endorsed medicinal value of camel urine. Far from being a safe clinical remedy, modern infectious disease medicine confirms that consuming raw dromedary secretions and excretions exposes humans to lethal zoonotic pathogens such as MERS-CoV and brucellosis.

bukhari:1501.note: After tribesmen from Uraynah killed the shepherd and drove away the charity camels, Muhammad had them captured, cut off their hands and feet, branded their eyes with heated iron, and left them in the stony tract of al-Harrah biting the stones. Classical commentators debate whether this punishment constituted retaliation in kind (qisas), the statutory penalty for highway robbery ([Quran 5:33](quran://5/33)), or a ruling issued prior to the prohibition of mutilation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَتَلُوا الرَّاعِيَ وَاسْتَاقُوا الذَّوْدَ، فَأَرْسَلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأُتِيَ بِهِمْ، فَقَطَّعَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَأَرْجُلَهُمْ وَسَمَرَ أَعْيُنَهُمْ، وَتَرَكَهُمْ بِالْحَرَّةِ يَعَضُّونَ الْحِجَارَةَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: but they killed the shepherd and drove away all the camels. So Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) sent (men) in their pursuit to catch them, and they were brought, and he had their hands and feet cut, and their eyes were branded with heated pieces of iron and they were left in the Harra (a stony place at Medina) biting the stones.

bukhari:1501.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—that Muhammad only inflicted this punishment as strict *qiṣāṣ* (retaliation in kind) because the tribesmen had similarly mutilated the shepherd, or that such mutilation (*muthlah*) was subsequently abrogated. However, the primary Arabic text here explicitly states only that they killed the shepherd and stole the camels (`فَقَتَلُوا الرَّاعِيَ وَاسْتَاقُوا الذَّوْدَ`) before Muhammad cut off their hands and feet, branded their eyes (`وَسَمَرَ أَعْيُنَهُمْ`), and left them in the lava fields biting stones (`يَعَضُّونَ الْحِجَارَةَ`) while being denied water until death (bukhari:233). Furthermore, parallel narrations (bukhari:4192; muslim:4353) confirm that this very execution was the occasion of revelation (*sabab al-nuzūl*) for [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33), permanently codifying cross-amputation and crucifixion as binding Islamic law rather than an abrogated anomaly.

bukhari:1501.note: When visitors from the tribe of Uraynah fell ill from the climate of Medina, Muhammad directed them to the herd of charity camels to drink their milk and urine as a remedy (bukhari:233, bukhari:5686). Classical jurists cite this instruction either as legal proof for the ritual purity of camel urine or as a medical dispensation to consume impure substances.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ نَاسًا، مِنْ عُرَيْنَةَ اجْتَوَوُا الْمَدِينَةَ، فَرَخَّصَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ يَأْتُوا إِبِلَ الصَّدَقَةِ فَيَشْرَبُوا مِنْ أَلْبَانِهَا وَأَبْوَالِهَا،
problematic_excerpt.english: Some people from `Uraina tribe came to Medina and its climate did not suit them, so Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) allowed them to go to the herd of camels (given as Zakat) and they drank their milk and urine (as medicine)

bukhari:1501.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue either that camel urine possesses miraculous anti-microbial and anti-cancer properties, or—following Ḥanafī jurists cited in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that this was merely a localized, one-time concession rather than universal prophetic medicine. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad prescribed drinking camel urine alongside milk (`فَيَشْرَبُوا مِنْ أَلْبَانِهَا وَأَبْوَالِهَا`) to treat their illness, a practice Al-Bukhari formally canonized as normative prophetic medicine in his *Book of Medicine* under the chapter *"Medicine with Camel Urine"* (bukhari:5686). In reality, urine is toxic metabolic waste, and modern medical authorities including the World Health Organization explicitly warn against consuming camel excretions due to severe health hazards and lethal zoonotic pathogens such as MERS-CoV.

muslim:1483.note: Muhammad declares that he intended to command his young men to prepare bundles of firewood for him, appoint a man to lead the people in prayer, and then have houses burned down over those remaining inside instead of attending the congregation ([Luke 9:54](bible://lk/9/54)). Classical commentators such as al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar state that this threat targeted prayer absentees and hypocrites, and that Muhammad refrained from carrying it out because women, children, and excused individuals also lived inside those homes.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ لَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ أَنْ آمُرَ فِتْيَانِي أَنْ يَسْتَعِدُّوا لِي بِحُزَمٍ مِنْ حَطَبٍ ثُمَّ آمُرَ رَجُلاً يُصَلِّي بِالنَّاسِ ثُمَّ تُحَرَّقُ بُيُوتٌ عَلَى مَنْ فِيهَا ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: I intend that I should command my young men to gather bundles fuel for me, and then order a person to lead people in prayer, and then burn the houses with their inmates (who have not joined the congregation)

muslim:1483.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as discussed in Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, this was merely an unexecuted rhetorical threat (*tahdīd*) aimed at known hypocrites (*munāfiqūn*), which Muhammad refrained from carrying out only because innocent women and children were inside the homes. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad resolved to have the houses burned down indiscriminately over whoever was inside them (*tuḥarraqu buyūtun ʿalā man fīhā*), and in parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:644, muslim:3718) he swears an oath by Allah (*wa-alladhī nafsī bi-yadihi*) to burn the men alive with fire (*fa-uḥarriqa ʿalayhim buyūtahum bi-al-nār*) simply for missing congregational prayer. Moreover, because Sunni orthodoxy holds that a prophet cannot firmly resolve (*laqad hamamtu*) to commit a sin or injustice, classical commentators themselves concede that incinerating absentees alive was a morally legitimate prophetic punishment rather than empty hyperbole.

bukhari:4192.note: After men from 'Ukl and 'Uraynah apostatized, killed the Prophet's shepherd, and drove off his camels, Muhammad ordered their eyes branded with iron, their hands cut off (alongside their legs in bukhari:233), and them left in al-Harrah until they died. Although an untranslated remark by sub-narrator Qatadah notes a report that Muhammad later prohibited mutilation (*muthlah*), classical jurists debate whether this execution served as reciprocal retaliation (*qisas*) or was superseded by the *hirabah* penalties of cross-amputation and crucifixion in [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَبَلَغَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَبَعَثَ الطَّلَبَ فِي آثَارِهِمْ فَأَمَرَ بِهِمْ فَسَمَرُوا أَعْيُنَهُمْ، وَقَطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ، وَتُرِكُوا فِي نَاحِيَةِ الْحَرَّةِ حَتَّى مَاتُوا عَلَى حَالِهِمْ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When this news reached the Prophet, he sent some people in pursuit of them. (So they were caught and brought back to the Prophet (ﷺ) ). The Prophet (ﷺ) gave his orders in their concern. So their eyes were branded with pieces of iron and their hands and legs were cut off and they were left away in Harra till they died in that state of theirs.

bukhari:4192.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this punishment was strictly symmetrical retaliation (*qiṣāṣ*) because the tribesmen had blinded the shepherd first, and claim Qatādah's appended remark—that Muhammad later forbade mutilation (*wa-yanhā ʿan al-muthlah*)—proves the practice was abrogated. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states only that they killed the shepherd (*wa-qatalū rāʿiya al-nabī*) before Muhammad ordered their eyes branded with heated iron (*fa-samarū aʿyunahum*), their limbs amputated, and their bodies left in the volcanic wasteland until they died (*ḥattā mātū ʿalā ḥālihim*). Furthermore, Qatādah's remark is merely a disconnected report (*balaghanā*), whereas this exact incident was permanently enshrined into un-abrogated Islamic law as the occasion of revelation (*sabab al-nuzūl*) for Quran 5:33, which forever mandates crucifixion and cross-amputation of hands and feet.

bukhari:4192.note: When visitors from 'Ukl and 'Uraynah found the climate of Medina unhealthy, Muhammad ordered them to go out to a herd of milch camels and drink both their milk and their urine (*abwaliha*). Classical commentators and jurists treat this order as a literal prophetic medical prescription, citing it in *fiqh* as a primary proof-text regarding the ritual purity and permissibility of consuming the urine of edible livestock.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَاسْتَوْخَمُوا الْمَدِينَةَ، فَأَمَرَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِذَوْدٍ وَرَاعٍ، وَأَمَرَهُمْ أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا فِيهِ، فَيَشْرَبُوا مِنْ أَلْبَانِهَا وَأَبْوَالِهَا،
problematic_excerpt.english: They found the climate of Medina unsuitable for them. So Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) ordered that they should be provided with some milch camels and a shepherd and ordered them to go out of Medina and to drink the camels' milk and urine (as medicine)

bukhari:4192.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that prescribing camel urine was either non-binding 7th-century AD Bedouin folk advice rather than divine revelation, or a miraculous prophetic medicine (*al-ṭibb al-nabawī*) with hidden therapeutic benefits. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad directly commanded them to drink the camels' milk and urine (*fa-amarahum... fa-yashrabū min albānihā wa-abwālihā*), leading classical Sunni authorities like Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* to canonize camel urine as both ritually pure (*ṭāhir*) and divinely guided medicine. Modern medical science and the World Health Organization directly refute this prescription, confirming that consuming camel urine and raw camel milk is a primary transmission vector for lethal Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS-CoV) and brucellosis.

muslim:1485.note: Regarding people who stay behind from the Friday (Jumu'ah) prayer, Muhammad states that he intended to command a man to lead the people in prayer and then burn down the houses of the men who absent themselves over them ([Luke 9:54-55](bible://lk/9/54-55)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَخَلَّفُونَ عَنِ الْجُمُعَةِ ‏ "‏ لَقَدْ هَمَمْتُ أَنْ آمُرَ رَجُلاً يُصَلِّي بِالنَّاسِ ثُمَّ أُحَرِّقَ عَلَى رِجَالٍ يَتَخَلَّفُونَ عَنِ الْجُمُعَةِ بُيُوتَهُمْ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Abdullah reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying about people who are absent from Jumu'a prayer:I intend that I should command a person to lead people in prayer, and then burn those persons who absent themselves from Jumu'a prayer in their houses

muslim:1485.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this threat was merely rhetorical hyperbole (zajr) directed exclusively at seditious hypocrites (munāfiqūn), noting that Muhammad never actually carried it out because of innocent women and children inside the homes. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that his threat targeted men simply for staying behind from the Friday prayer (yatakhallafūna ʿani l-jumuʿah), expressing a concrete resolve (laqad hamamtu) to burn their houses down over them (uḥarriqa ʿalā rijālin... buyūtahum)—a threat reinforced in parallel Sahih narrations (muslim:1481, bukhari:644) where he specifies ordering bundles of firewood (ḥaṭab) to incinerate those who pray in their homes instead of the mosque. Furthermore, classical commentators like Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) and Ibn Ḥajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) emphasize that Muhammad would never intend (hamm) an unlawful act, proving that burning absentees in their homes was treated as a morally legitimate prophetic punishment in principle rather than harmless hyperbole.

bukhari:5686.note: After the men recovered, killed his shepherd, and drove off his camels, Muhammad had their hands and feet amputated and their eyes branded with heated iron. An appended statement in the Arabic text from Muhammad ibn Sirin notes that this took place before the revelation of the fixed legal punishments (hudud; compare [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَبَلَغَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَبَعَثَ فِي طَلَبِهِمْ، فَجِيءَ بِهِمْ فَقَطَعَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَأَرْجُلَهُمْ، وَسَمَرَ أَعْيُنَهُمْ
problematic_excerpt.english: When the news reached the Prophet (ﷺ) he sent some people in their pursuit. When they were brought, he cut their hands and feet and their eyes were branded with heated pieces of iron

bukhari:5686.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this punishment was either strict *qiṣāṣ* (retaliation in kind because the raiders had blinded the shepherd, as cited by Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar) or an early measure enacted before Islamic penal laws were revealed, pointing to Ibn Sīrīn's appended remark (*qabla an tanzila al-ḥudūd*). However, the primary Arabic text and parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:233`, `bukhari:6802`) explicitly state that after amputating their hands and feet and branding their eyes with heated iron (*fa-qaṭaʿa aydiyahum wa-arjulahum wa-samara aʿyunahum*), Muhammad cast them onto the scorching volcanic rocks of Medina begging for water while forbidding anyone to give them drink (*yastasqūna fa-lā yusqawna*) until they died. Furthermore, Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and classical *tafsīr* confirm that this very incident was the occasion of revelation (*sabab al-nuzūl*) for [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33), which permanently codified cross-amputation and crucifixion into Islamic law rather than abrogating it.

bukhari:5686.note: When visitors became unwell from the climate of Medina, Muhammad ordered them to join his shepherd and drink both the milk and urine of his camels as a remedy until their bodies recovered.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ نَاسًا، اجْتَوَوْا فِي الْمَدِينَةِ فَأَمَرَهُمُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ يَلْحَقُوا بِرَاعِيهِ ـ يَعْنِي الإِبِلَ ـ فَيَشْرَبُوا مِنْ أَلْبَانِهَا وَأَبْوَالِهَا، فَلَحِقُوا بِرَاعِيهِ فَشَرِبُوا مِنْ أَلْبَانِهَا وَأَبْوَالِهَا، حَتَّى صَلَحَتْ أَبْدَانُهُمْ
problematic_excerpt.english: The climate of Medina did not suit some people, so the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered them to follow his shepherd, i.e. his camels, and drink their milk and urine (as a medicine). So they followed the shepherd that is the camels and drank their milk and urine till their bodies became healthy.

bukhari:5686.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that prescribing camel urine was either a localized, one-time treatment for a specific abdominal ailment (*istisqā'*) among desert tribesmen or a prophetic 'scientific miracle' containing supposed antimicrobial and anti-cancer compounds. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad directly commanded (*fa-amarahum al-Nabī*) the sick men to drink the camels' urine (*fa-yashrabū min albānihā wa-abwālihā*), and Al-Bukhārī codified this narration as normative prophetic medicine in his *Kitāb al-Ṭibb* (*Book of Medicine*). Rather than being a miraculous cure, ingesting raw camel urine is a clinically documented vector for lethal zoonotic pathogens—including Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and brucellosis—prompting explicit World Health Organization advisories against the exact practice Muhammad prescribed.

bukhari:5727.note: After men from the tribes of Ukl and Uraynah apostatized, killed his shepherd, and drove away his camels, Muhammad ordered their eyes branded with heated iron, their hands cut off, and left them in al-Harrah until they died ([Quran 5:33](quran://5/33)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَبَلَغَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَبَعَثَ الطَّلَبَ فِي آثَارِهِمْ، وَأَمَرَ بِهِمْ فَسَمَرُوا أَعْيُنَهُمْ وَقَطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَتُرِكُوا فِي نَاحِيَةِ الْحَرَّةِ حَتَّى مَاتُوا عَلَى حَالِهِمْ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When this news reached the Prophet (ﷺ) he sent in their pursuit (and they were caught and brought). The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that their eyes be branded with heated iron bars and their hands be cut off, and they were left at Al-Harra till they died in that state

bukhari:5727.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this torture was merely proportional retaliation (qiṣāṣ) because the tribesmen had blinded the shepherd, or claim via discussions in Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī that such mutilation (muthlah) was later abrogated by Quran 5:33. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad personally ordered their eyes branded with heated iron (فَسَمَرُوا أَعْيُنَهُمْ), their hands cut off (وَقَطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُمْ), and their bodies left exposed at al-Ḥarrah until they died (وَتُرِكُوا فِي نَاحِيَةِ الْحَرَّةِ حَتَّى مَاتُوا عَلَى حَالِهِمْ), while parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:233, 6802) confirm he refused to cauterize their bleeding stumps (فَلَمْ يَحْسِمْهُمْ) or give them water as they begged in agony (يَسْتَسْقُونَ فَلاَ يُسْقَوْنَ). Furthermore, classical commentators like al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr confirm that Quran 5:33 was revealed specifically about the Uraynah incident to permanently codify—rather than abrogate—crucifixion and cross-amputation as binding Islamic law (ḥadd al-ḥirābah).

bukhari:5727.note: When men from the tribes of Ukl and Uraynah found the climate of Medina unsuitable, Muhammad ordered them to go out with a herd of camels and drink their milk and urine.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَاسْتَوْخَمُوا الْمَدِينَةَ فَأَمَرَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِذَوْدٍ وَبِرَاعٍ وَأَمَرَهُمْ، أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا فِيهِ فَيَشْرَبُوا مِنْ أَلْبَانِهَا وَأَبْوَالِهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: and they found the climate of Medina unsuitable for them. So Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) ordered that they be given some camels and a shepherd, and ordered them to go out with those camels and drink their milk and urine.

bukhari:5727.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that prescribing camel urine was either non-binding 7th-century AD Bedouin folk medicine for abdominal dropsy (istisqāʾ) or a scientifically miraculous remedy with purported antimicrobial and anti-cancer properties. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad issued a direct prophetic command for the sick men to drink the camels' urine alongside their milk (فَأَمَرَهُمْ أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا فِيهِ فَيَشْرَبُوا مِنْ أَلْبَانِهَا وَأَبْوَالِهَا), which al-Bukhārī codified in his Book of Medicine (Kitāb al-Ṭibb) and which classical jurists like al-Nawawī and Ibn Hajar cite to rule that camel urine is ritually pure (ṭāhir) and medicinally normative. Far from being a divinely inspired cure, ingesting raw camel excreta consumes toxic metabolic waste and is a primary vector for lethal zoonotic diseases such as MERS-CoV and brucellosis.

bukhari:6802.note: After the recovered tribesmen apostatize, kill the herdsmen, and steal the camels, Muhammad orders their hands and feet amputated, their eyes branded with heated iron, and their wounds left uncauterized until they die. Parallel reports (bukhari:6805) state the men had also blinded the shepherd, leading classical jurists to debate whether the ocular branding was strict retaliation (qisas) or subsequently abrogated by prohibitions on mutilation (muthla) and the punishments codified in [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَطَعَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَأَرْجُلَهُمْ وَسَمَلَ أَعْيُنَهُمْ، ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْسِمْهُمْ حَتَّى مَاتُوا
problematic_excerpt.english: the Prophets ordered that their hands and legs should be cut off and that their eyes should be branded with heated pieces of iron, and that their cut hands and legs should not be cauterized, till they die

bukhari:6802.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that Muhammad was merely applying proportional retaliation (*qiṣāṣ*) for what the renegades did to the shepherd, or that this torture was subsequently abrogated by the revelation of the *ḥirābah* verse (Surah 5:33) and prohibitions against mutilation (*muthlah*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states only that the men killed the shepherds (`وَقَتَلُوا رُعَاتَهَا`) before Muhammad ordered their limbs amputated, their eyes branded (`وَسَمَلَ أَعْيُنَهُمْ`), and their wounds left uncauterized (`ثُمَّ لَمْ يَحْسِمْهُمْ حَتَّى مَاتُوا`), while parallel narration `bukhari:6804` adds that they were thrown onto the scorching lava stones of *al-Ḥarrah* begging for water and denied it until they died. Furthermore, classical *tafsīr* authorities (including Al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr) and Bukhari's own chapter placement affirm that Surah 5:33—which permanently mandates opposite-limb amputation and crucifixion—was revealed specifically regarding these men to codify, rather than abrogate, their execution.

bukhari:6802.note: Muhammad orders men from the tribe of 'Ukl who fell ill from Medina's climate to drink the urine and milk of charity camels to recover. Classical commentators like Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawi affirm this command literally as the basis for the ritual purity and medicinal permissibility of camel urine.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَمَرَهُمْ أَنْ يَأْتُوا إِبِلَ الصَّدَقَةِ، فَيَشْرَبُوا مِنْ أَبْوَالِهَا وَأَلْبَانِهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered them to go to the (herd of milch) camels of charity and to drink, their milk and urine (as a medicine)

bukhari:6802.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this prescription was either a non-binding local desert custom for abdominal swelling (ascites) or a miraculous 'Prophetic Medicine' (*al-ṭibb al-nabawī*) with supposed antimicrobial properties. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad issued a direct command (`فَأَمَرَهُمْ ... فَيَشْرَبُوا مِنْ أَبْوَالِهَا`, 'he ordered them... to drink from their urine'), which classical commentators like Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* cite as binding legal proof that camel urine is ritually pure (*ṭāhir*) and medicinally beneficial. Far from being a divinely guided cure, consuming raw camel urine and unpasteurized milk is a documented medical hazard that transmits fatal pathogens such as MERS-CoV and causes severe renal toxicity.

bukhari:6803.note: Muhammad cuts off the hands and feet of men from the 'Uraina tribe and withholds cauterization until they bleed to death. Surrounding narrations (bukhari:6802, bukhari:6805) report that this punishment followed their apostasy, murder of his shepherd, and theft of his camels, an incident classical jurists connect to [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33) while debating whether the act was retaliatory (qisas), a prescribed hadd penalty, or later abrogated.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَطَعَ الْعُرَنِيِّينَ وَلَمْ يَحْسِمْهُمْ حَتَّى مَاتُوا
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) cut off the hands and feet of the men belonging to the tribe of `Uraina and did not cauterise (their bleeding limbs) till they died

bukhari:6803.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this punishment was merely proportional *qiṣāṣ* (lex talionis) because the men of 'Uraina had murdered and blinded Muhammad's shepherd, or that such mutilation (*muthla*) was later abrogated. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad amputated their limbs and deliberately refused to cauterize their wounds so they would slowly bleed to death (`قَطَعَ الْعُرَنِيِّينَ وَلَمْ يَحْسِمْهُمْ حَتَّى مَاتُوا`), while parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:6802`, `bukhari:6805`) add that he branded their eyes with heated irons and left them in the scorching lava fields begging for water in vain (`يَسْتَسْقُونَ فَلاَ يُسْقَوْنَ`). Furthermore, far from being an abrogated exception, classical Sunni jurisprudence and `bukhari:6802` cite this exact execution as the foundational precedent for the permanent Quranic mandate of cross-amputation and crucifixion in Surah 5:33.

bukhari:6804.note: After the men of 'Ukl murder a shepherd and steal the camels, Muhammad orders their eyes branded with heated iron nails, their hands and feet cut off without cauterization, and that they be cast onto the stony ground of Al-Harra where they ask for water and are given none until they die. Classical commentators explain this punishment either as retaliation in kind (qisas) or as having preceded the prohibition of mutilation and the revelation of Quran 5:33.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَمَرَ بِمَسَامِيرَ فَأُحْمِيَتْ فَكَحَلَهُمْ وَقَطَعَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَأَرْجُلَهُمْ، وَمَا حَسَمَهُمْ، ثُمَّ أُلْقُوا فِي الْحَرَّةِ يَسْتَسْقُونَ فَمَا سُقُوا حَتَّى مَاتُوا
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet ordered for some iron pieces to be made red hot, and their eyes were branded with them and their hands and feet were cut off and were not cauterized. Then they were put at a place called Al- Harra, and when they asked for water to drink they were not given till they died.

bukhari:6804.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists (citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) typically argue that this torture was strictly reciprocal lex talionis (*qiṣāṣ*) because the culprits had allegedly blinded the shepherd first, or claim that it was later abrogated by the revelation of Quran 5:33 forbidding mutilation (*muthlah*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states only that they killed the shepherd (`وَقَتَلُوا الرَّاعِيَ`) while Muhammad ordered heated iron spikes to brand their eyes (`فَأَمَرَ بِمَسَامِيرَ فَأُحْمِيَتْ فَكَحَلَهُمْ`), cut off their hands and feet without cauterizing the bleeding stumps (`وَقَطَعَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَأَرْجُلَهُمْ، وَمَا حَسَمَهُمْ`), and left them begging for water on the volcanic rocks until they died (`يَسْتَسْقُونَ فَمَا سُقُوا حَتَّى مَاتُوا`). Furthermore, the immediately following narration (`bukhari:6805`) explicitly states that Quran 5:33 (`إِنَّمَا جَزَاءُ الَّذِينَ يُحَارِبُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ`) was revealed to validate—not abrogate—this exact punishment of amputation and execution.

bukhari:6804.note: When men from the tribe of 'Ukl fall ill in Medina, Muhammad directs them to his camels, where they drink the camels' milk and urine to recover—an act explicitly commanded by Muhammad himself in parallel narrations (bukhari:6802, bukhari:6805).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ مَا أَجِدُ لَكُمْ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَلْحَقُوا بِإِبِلِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأَتَوْهَا فَشَرِبُوا مِنْ أَلْبَانِهَا وَأَبْوَالِهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, I see no other way for you than to use the camels of Allah's Apostle." So they went and drank the milk and urine of the camels, (as medicine)

bukhari:6804.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the tribesmen drank the camel urine on their own initiative without a prophetic command, or claim that camel urine possesses hidden medicinal properties that justify Ibn Hajar's defense of it as a prophetic remedy. However, the primary Arabic text of this narration (`فَشَرِبُوا مِنْ أَلْبَانِهَا وَأَبْوَالِهَا`) and its immediate Sahih parallel (`bukhari:6802`) explicitly state that Muhammad directly commanded them to drink both the milk and urine (`فَأَمَرَهُمْ أَنْ يَلْحَقُوا بِالرَّاعِي فَيَشْرَبُوا مِنْ أَلْبَانِهَا وَأَبْوَالِهَا`). Rather than being a divine cure, consuming raw dromedary camel secretions is medically recognized today as a toxic practice and a primary transmission vector for the lethal MERS-CoV coronavirus.

muslim:4353.note: After people from the tribe of Uraynah kill the shepherds, apostatize from Islam, and drive off the Prophet's camels, Muhammad has them captured, cuts off their hands and feet, puts out their eyes (*samala aʿyunahum*), and leaves them on the stony ground of the Harrah until they die (cf. [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ مَالُوا عَلَى الرِّعَاءِ فَقَتَلُوهُمْ وَارْتَدُّوا عَنِ الإِسْلاَمِ وَسَاقُوا ذَوْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَبَعَثَ فِي أَثْرِهِمْ فَأُتِيَ بِهِمْ فَقَطَعَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ وَأَرْجُلَهُمْ وَسَمَلَ أَعْيُنَهُمْ وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِي الْحَرَّةِ حَتَّى مَاتُوا
problematic_excerpt.english: They then fell upon the shepherds and killed them and turned apostates from Islam and drove off the camels of the Prophet (ﷺ). This news reached Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) and he sent (people) on their track and they were (brought) and handed over to him. He (the Holy Prophet) got their hands cut off, and their feet, and put out their eyes, and threw them on the stony ground until they died

muslim:4353.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this punishment was proportional retaliation (*qiṣāṣ*) matching what the offenders did to the shepherds, or a temporary measure prior to formal Islamic legislation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states only that the men killed the shepherds, apostatized, and drove off the camels (*faqatalūhum wa-rtaddū ʿan al-islām wa-sāqū dhawda rasūli llāh*), whereas Muhammad ordered their hands and feet cut off (*faqaṭaʿa aydiyahum wa-arjulahum*), their eyes put out (*wa-samala aʿyunahum*), and their bodies left on the stony ground of the Harrah until they died (*wa-tarakahum fī al-ḥarrah ḥattā mātū*). Furthermore, cross-amputation of hands and feet for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger remains a permanent prescription in [Quran 5:33](quran://5/33), and this account is corroborated across `bukhari:233`, `bukhari:5685`, `muslim:4354`, and `muslim:4355`.

muslim:4353.note: When people from the tribe of Uraynah find the climate of Medina uncongenial, Muhammad instructs them to go to the charity camels and drink their milk and urine (*albānihā wa-abwālihā*) to recover.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ نَاسًا، مِنْ عُرَيْنَةَ قَدِمُوا عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْمَدِينَةَ فَاجْتَوَوْهَا فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ إِنْ شِئْتُمْ أَنْ تَخْرُجُوا إِلَى إِبِلِ الصَّدَقَةِ فَتَشْرَبُوا مِنْ أَلْبَانِهَا وَأَبْوَالِهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَفَعَلُوا فَصَحُّوا
problematic_excerpt.english: Anas b. Malik reported that some people belonging (to the tribe) of 'Uraina came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) at Medina, but they found its climate uncogenial. So Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said to them:If you so like, you may go to the camels of Sadaqa and drink their milk and urine. They did so and were all right.

muslim:4353.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was offering non-binding local folk advice tailored to a specific climate illness rather than a prophetic medical prescription, or that camel urine contains unacknowledged medicinal benefits. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah's Messenger directed the sick men to the charity camels to drink from both their milk and their urine (*fatashrabū min albānihā wa-abwālihā*), recording that they did so and were cured (*fafaʿalū faṣaḥḥū*). By attributing their recovery directly to following Muhammad's instruction across `muslim:4353`, `bukhari:233`, `bukhari:5686`, `muslim:4354`, and `muslim:4355`, the text establishes the ingestion of animal excrement (*abwālihā*) as an endorsed prophetic remedy.

bukhari:6790.note: Muhammad rules that a thief's hand is to be cut off for stealing a quarter of a dinar—a minimum legal threshold (nisab) clarified in adjacent narrations as 'a quarter of a dinar or more' (bukhari:6789) and equated to the price of a shield (bukhari:6792). Whereas Mosaic law prescribes financial restitution for theft ([Exodus 22:1](bible://ex/22/1)), this decree establishes hand amputation as the mandatory punishment once that threshold is reached.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ تُقْطَعُ يَدُ السَّارِقِ فِي رُبُعِ دِينَارٍ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The hand of a thief should be cut off for stealing a quarter of a Dinar

bukhari:6790.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that hand amputation under Quran 5:38 is a rare deterrent reserved for grand larceny after strict conditions of secure storage (*ḥirz*) are met, or that the verb *qaṭaʿa* merely means restraining or marking the thief. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *"tuqṭaʿu yadu al-sāriq fī rubʿi dīnār"* (the hand of a thief is cut off for a quarter of a dinar—roughly one gram of gold), setting an exceptionally low monetary threshold (*niṣāb*) for permanent bodily mutilation. Furthermore, both Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* affirm that this decree mandates literal severance at the wrist joint, corroborated by parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:6789`, `bukhari:6799`) recording amputations for stealing a mere rope, an egg, or a three-dirham shield.

bukhari:6791.note: Muhammad decrees that a thief's hand is to be amputated for stealing a quarter of a dinar. Classical Sunni jurisprudence (such as Fath al-Bari) affirms this as a literal, binding hadd minimum threshold (nisab), harmonizing it with reports mentioning the value of a shield (bukhari:6792) by noting that a shield then cost a quarter of a gold dinar (three silver dirhams).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ يُقْطَعُ فِي رُبُعِ دِينَارٍ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The hand should be cut off for stealing a quarter of a Dinar

bukhari:6791.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the *ḥadd* amputation for theft is either a metaphorical 'cutting off' of a criminal's means or a rare deterrent reserved strictly for grand larceny under nearly impossible legal conditions. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `يُقْطَعُ فِي رُبُعِ دِينَارٍ` ('the hand is cut off for a quarter of a dinar'), fixing the mandatory legal threshold (*niṣāb*) at a petty sum equivalent to the value of a common shield (`bukhari:6795`). Furthermore, parallel *Ṣaḥīḥ* narrations (`bukhari:6788`, `bukhari:6799`) record Muhammad enforcing literal physical amputation on a Makhzumi woman and cursing the thief whose hand is severed (`فَتُقْطَعُ يَدُهُ`) over a mere egg or rope, which Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* confirms is permanent bodily severance at the wrist.

bukhari:6798.note: Muhammad cut off the hand of a thief for stealing a shield valued at three dirhams (bukhari:6796, bukhari:6797). Classical commentary, such as Ibn Hajar's *Fath al-Bari*, affirms this act as the foundational legal precedent establishing the three-dirham threshold (*nisab*) for mandatory hand amputation (*hadd al-sariqah*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَطَعَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَدَ سَارِقٍ فِي مِجَنٍّ ثَمَنُهُ ثَلاَثَةُ دَرَاهِمَ
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) cutoff the hand of a thief for stealing a shield that was worth three Dirhams

bukhari:6798.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the ḥudūd amputation in Quran 5:38 functions merely as a theoretical deterrent reserved for grand larceny, claiming that strict legal prerequisites (shurūṭ) and a high monetary threshold (niṣāb) prevented its execution for petty crimes. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad personally enforced the amputation (qaṭaʿa al-nabī ... yada sāriqin) for a single shield worth a mere three silver dirhams (fī mijannin thamanuhu thalāthatu darāhima, equivalent to a quarter-dinar in bukhari:6789). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations record Muhammad declaring that a thief's hand is severed even over the value of an egg or a rope (yasriqu al-bayḍata fatuqṭaʿu yaduhu, bukhari:6783) and angrily rebuking companions who tried to intercede to waive this permanent mutilation (bukhari:6788).

muslim:2256.note: Aisha reports that after she secretly followed Muhammad to the Baqi' cemetery at night, he struck her in the chest with a blow that caused her pain (*lahadanī fī ṣadrī lahdatan awjaʿatnī*; cf. [Quran 4:34](quran://4/34)). Although the published English translation softens the phrase to 'gave me a nudge on the chest which I felt,' the Arabic text explicitly states that the strike hurt her (*awjaʿatnī*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏"‏ فَأَنْتِ السَّوَادُ الَّذِي رَأَيْتُ أَمَامِي ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ فَلَهَدَنِي فِي صَدْرِي لَهْدَةً أَوْجَعَتْنِي ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَظَنَنْتِ أَنْ يَحِيفَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكِ وَرَسُولُهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He said: Was it the darkness (of your shadow) that I saw in front of me? I said: Yes. He gave me a nudge on the chest which I felt, and then said: Did you think that Allah and His Apostle would deal unjustly with you?

muslim:2256.literal_translation: He said: 'Then you were the dark figure that I saw in front of me?' I said: 'Yes.' So he struck/shoved me in the chest with a blow that caused me pain, then said: 'Did you think that Allah and His Messenger would deal unjustly with you?'

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَلَهَدَنِي فِي صَدْرِي لَهْدَةً أَوْجَعَتْنِي
translation_issue.published_rendering: He gave me a nudge on the chest which I felt
translation_issue.literal_meaning: So he struck/shoved me in the chest with a blow/thrust that caused me pain
translation_issue.explanation: The translator softens two explicit Arabic terms: 'lahada' (defined by Ibn al-Athīr and Lane's Lexicon specifically for this hadith as to strike on the chest or push/thrust violently, 'dafaʿahu dafʿan shadīdan') is minimized to 'gave me a nudge', and 'awjaʿatnī' (Form IV of w-j-ʿ, literally 'it caused me pain' or 'it hurt me') is sanitized into 'which I felt'.

muslim:2256.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad never struck a woman and claim this gesture—dishonestly softened in English translations to a 'nudge' that she 'felt'—was merely a playful or gentle poke to chide Aisha's jealousy. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states lahadanī fī ṣadrī lahdatan awjaʿatnī ('he struck me in the chest with a blow that caused me pain'), using the verb lahada (and lakaza, 'punched,' in the parallel Sunan an-Nasa'i 2037), which classical lexicographers and Al-Nawawī define as a forceful shove or strike to the chest. Aisha's explicit testimony that the blow physically hurt her (awjaʿatnī) collapses the apologetic claim that Muhammad never hit his wives and exemplifies the domestic battery sanctioned in Quran 4:34.

muslim:3540.note: Muhammad swears an oath that whenever a man calls his wife to bed and she refuses him, "the One Who is in heaven" remains wrathful against her until her husband is pleased with her ([1 Corinthians 7:3](bible://1cor/7/3), [1 Peter 3:7](bible://1pt/3/7)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ مَا مِنْ رَجُلٍ يَدْعُو امْرَأَتَهُ إِلَى فِرَاشِهَا فَتَأْبَى عَلَيْهِ إِلاَّ كَانَ الَّذِي فِي السَّمَاءِ سَاخِطًا عَلَيْهَا حَتَّى يَرْضَى عَنْهَا ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira (Allah be pleased with him) reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:By Him in Whose Hand is my life, when a man calls his wife to his bed, and she does not respond, the One Who is in the heaven is displeased with her until he (her husband) is pleased with her

muslim:3540.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this warning applies only when a wife maliciously withholds intimacy without a valid excuse, claiming that Islamic law upholds mutual sexual rights between spouses. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states unconditionally that whenever a man calls his wife to bed and she refuses him (*fa-taʾbā ʿalayhi*), 'the One Who is in heaven is wrathful against her (*sākhiṭan ʿalayhā*) until he is pleased with her (*ḥattā yarḍā ʿanhā*)'—tying God's own anger directly to the husband's sexual satisfaction with zero reciprocal threat ever issued against a husband who refuses his wife. Furthermore, commenting on this exact narration in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, Imam al-Nawawī confirms that emotional unwillingness or fatigue does not excuse her, ruling that unless she is menstruating or medically incapacitated, a wife is forbidden from declining her husband whenever he demands her.

bukhari:5204.note: Muhammad instructs men not to flog their wives as they flog a slave and then have sexual intercourse with them at the end of the day. Classical commentators like Ibn Hajar harmonize this with the permission to strike wives in [Quran 4:34](quran://4/34) by ruling that it restricts only severe, slave-like flogging while leaving non-severe beating permissible.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لاَ يَجْلِدُ أَحَدُكُمُ امْرَأَتَهُ جَلْدَ الْعَبْدِ، ثُمَّ يُجَامِعُهَا فِي آخِرِ الْيَوْمِ
problematic_excerpt.english: None of you should flog his wife as he flogs a slave and then have sexual intercourse with her in the last part of the day

bukhari:5204.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration proves Muhammad prohibited domestic abuse, or cite Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* to claim that any permissible striking is merely symbolic and discouraged out of compassion for women. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *lā yajlidu aḥadukum imra'atahu jalda al-ʿabdi, thumma yujāmiʿuhā fī ākhiri al-yawm* ('None of you should flog his wife like the flogging of a slave, and then have sexual intercourse with her at the end of the day'), which casually normalizes the brutal whipping of enslaved people while restricting only slave-level lashings of a wife. Furthermore, as Ibn Hajar himself notes in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, this specific qualification ('like the flogging of a slave') does not abrogate a husband's right to beat his wife ([Quran 4:34](quran://4/34)), but merely discourages severe flogging on the pragmatic grounds that it is awkward to brutally whip a woman and then demand sexual intercourse (*yujāmiʿuhā*) from her that same night.

bukhari:146.note: Around AD 627, Umar repeatedly told Muhammad to veil and seclude his wives (ihjub nisa'aka), which Muhammad did not do until Umar called out to Muhammad's wife Sauda bint Zam'a—saying, 'We have recognized you, O Sauda'—when she went out at night to the open plains of Al-Manasi where the women relieved themselves. The report states that Umar did so out of an eager desire for the veil mandate (al-hijab) to be sent down, whereupon Allah revealed the verse of the veil ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53), [Quran 33:59](quran://33/59); cf. bukhari:4795, muslim:5671).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَكَانَ عُمَرُ يَقُولُ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم احْجُبْ نِسَاءَكَ‏.‏ فَلَمْ يَكُنْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَفْعَلُ، فَخَرَجَتْ سَوْدَةُ بِنْتُ زَمْعَةَ زَوْجُ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَيْلَةً مِنَ اللَّيَالِي عِشَاءً، وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَةً طَوِيلَةً، فَنَادَاهَا عُمَرُ أَلاَ قَدْ عَرَفْنَاكِ يَا سَوْدَةُ‏.‏ حِرْصًا عَلَى أَنْ يَنْزِلَ الْحِجَابُ، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ آيَةَ الْحِجَابِ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: `Umar used to say to the Prophet (ﷺ) "Let your wives be veiled," but Allah's Apostle did not do so. One night Sauda bint Zam`a the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ) went out at `Isha' time and she was a tall lady. `Umar addressed her and said, "I have recognized you, O Sauda." He said so, as he desired eagerly that the verses of Al-Hijab (the observing of veils by the Muslim women) may be revealed. So Allah revealed the verses of "Al-Hijab" (A complete body cover excluding the eyes)

bukhari:146.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī on the 'Concordances of Umar' (Muwāfaqāt ʿUmar)—that Umar was merely acting out of protective jealousy (ghayrah) to shield the Prophet's wives from Medinan hypocrites and that his pious intuition (ilhām) simply anticipated Allah's eternal decree. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad refused Umar's demands (falam yakun Rasūlu Allāhi yafʿalu) until Umar staked out the nocturnal latrine fields (idhā tabarrazna) and publicly shamed Sauda specifically 'out of an eager desire that the veil be revealed' (ḥirṣan ʿalā an yanzila al-ḥijāb), exposing that calculated human intimidation—rather than divine initiative—triggered the revelation of Quran 33:53. Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:4795, muslim:5671) record that Umar continued to stalk and call out to Sauda at night even after the Hijab was revealed, forcing her to return home in humiliation to complain to Muhammad, who capitulated to Umar's surveillance rather than rebuking him.

bukhari:304.note: Muhammad tells a gathering of women that they form the majority of the inhabitants of Hell because they curse frequently and are ungrateful to their husbands (*takfurna al-ʿashīr*). He further declares women to be deficient in intelligence and religion (*nāqiṣāt ʿaql wa-dīn*), defining their intellectual deficiency by a woman's testimony being worth half that of a man ([Quran 2:282](quran://2/282)) and their religious deficiency by their inability to pray or fast during menstruation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا مَعْشَرَ النِّسَاءِ تَصَدَّقْنَ، فَإِنِّي أُرِيتُكُنَّ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِ النَّارِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقُلْنَ وَبِمَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ تُكْثِرْنَ اللَّعْنَ، وَتَكْفُرْنَ الْعَشِيرَ، مَا رَأَيْتُ مِنْ نَاقِصَاتِ عَقْلٍ وَدِينٍ أَذْهَبَ لِلُبِّ الرَّجُلِ الْحَازِمِ مِنْ إِحْدَاكُنَّ ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْنَ وَمَا نُقْصَانُ دِينِنَا وَعَقْلِنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَلَيْسَ شَهَادَةُ الْمَرْأَةِ مِثْلَ نِصْفِ شَهَادَةِ الرَّجُلِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْنَ بَلَى‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَذَلِكَ مِنْ نُقْصَانِ عَقْلِهَا، أَلَيْسَ إِذَا حَاضَتْ لَمْ تُصَلِّ وَلَمْ تَصُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْنَ بَلَى‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَذَلِكَ مِنْ نُقْصَانِ دِينِهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: "O women! Give alms, as I have seen that the majority of the dwellers of Hell-fire were you (women)." They asked, "Why is it so, O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) ?" He replied, "You curse frequently and are ungrateful to your husbands. I have not seen anyone more deficient in intelligence and religion than you. A cautious sensible man could be led astray by some of you." The women asked, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! What is deficient in our intelligence and religion?" He said, "Is not the evidence of two women equal to the witness of one man?" They replied in the affirmative. He said, "This is the deficiency in her intelligence. Isn't it true that a woman can neither pray nor fast during her menses?" The women replied in the affirmative. He said, "This is the deficiency in her religion

bukhari:304.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was either using rhetorical hyperbole to encourage charity on Eid or merely describing merciful ritual and legal exemptions—rather than innate inferiority—when calling women 'deficient in intelligence and religion' (*nāqiṣāt ʿaql wa-dīn*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that women comprise the majority of Hell's inhabitants (*akthara ahli al-nār*) and directly defines a woman's halved legal testimony as proof of her intellectual deficiency (*fa-dhālika min nuqṣāni ʿaqlihā*), reinforcing [Quran 2:282](quran://2/282)'s premise that women are inherently prone to err (*an taḍilla iḥdāhumā*). Furthermore, by declaring a God-ordained biological function (menstruation) to be a 'deficiency in her religion' (*nuqṣāni dīnihā*), the narration locks women into an inescapable ontological and legal subordination.

bukhari:508.note: Aisha objects to the prophetic ruling transmitted by other Companions (bukhari:511, muslim:1144) that a woman, a donkey, and a dog invalidate a man's prayer, asking, 'Do you make us (women) equal to dogs and donkeys?' Disputing that a woman's presence annuls prayer, she recounts that Muhammad used to pray facing the middle of the bed while she lay in front of him before she quietly slipped away from the foot of the bed.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَتْ أَعَدَلْتُمُونَا بِالْكَلْبِ وَالْحِمَارِ لَقَدْ رَأَيْتُنِي مُضْطَجِعَةً عَلَى السَّرِيرِ، فَيَجِيءُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَيَتَوَسَّطُ السَّرِيرَ فَيُصَلِّي، فَأَكْرَهُ أَنْ أُسَنِّحَهُ فَأَنْسَلُّ مِنْ قِبَلِ رِجْلَىِ السَّرِيرِ حَتَّى أَنْسَلَّ مِنْ لِحَافِي‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Do you make us (women) equal to dogs and donkeys? While I used to lie in my bed, the Prophet (ﷺ) would come and pray facing the middle of the bed. I used to consider it not good to stand in front of him in his prayers. So I used to slip away slowly and quietly from the foot of the bed till I got out of my guilt

bukhari:508.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that grouping women with dogs and donkeys is merely a legal categorization of potential distractions to a worshipper's focus (*khushūʿ*) rather than an equation of value, or claim that Aisha's objection disproves the ruling altogether. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states Aisha's own outrage at the Companions' direct equation (*a-ʿadaltumūnā bi-l-kalbi wa-l-ḥimāri*—'Have you made us equal to the dog and the donkey?'), proving that the earliest Muslim generation understood this teaching as a degrading comparison. Furthermore, parallel narrations in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* (1144) explicitly record Muhammad himself decreeing that 'prayer is severed by a woman, a donkey, and a dog' (*yaqṭaʿu aṣ-ṣalāta al-marʾatu wa-l-ḥimāru wa-l-kalbu*), and both Al-Nawawī and Ibn Hajar affirm that Aisha's experience of lying stationary (*muḍṭajiʿatan*) does not overturn the explicit Prophetic text regarding a woman passing in front of a praying man.

bukhari:5093.note: Narrated via Ibn Umar, Muhammad declares that evil omen (*al-shuʾm*) is in the woman, the house, and the horse. Parallel variants (bukhari:2858, bukhari:5094, bukhari:5772) similarly classify women alongside residential property and riding animals, framing these three either as an explicit exception to the general negation of superstitious omens (*tiyarah*) or as the sole locus of bad omen if it exists in anything.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ الشُّؤْمُ فِي الْمَرْأَةِ وَالدَّارِ وَالْفَرَسِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Evil omen is in the women, the house and the horse

bukhari:5093.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was merely quoting pre-Islamic superstitions—citing a report attributed to Aisha claiming Ibn Umar only heard the end of the remark—or appeal to Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī to reinterpret al-shuʾm (evil omen) as mere marital incompatibility. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states 'al-shuʾm fī al-marʾati wa-al-dāri wa-al-faras' ('evil omen is in the woman, the house, and the horse') as a direct Prophetic declaration, and independent Ṣaḥīḥ chains from Sahl ibn Saʿd (bukhari:5094, bukhari:5772) collapse the mishearing excuse by recording Muhammad first prohibiting general omens ('lā ṭiyarah') and then explicitly singling out women, houses, and beasts as the three genuine exceptions where bad omen resides.

bukhari:7099.note: Upon hearing that the Persians had appointed Khosrau's daughter as their ruler, Muhammad declares that a people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never succeed. Recalled by Abu Bakra during the Battle of the Camel in reference to Aisha's leadership (cf. bukhari:4425), this generalized principle serves in classical Sunni jurisprudence as the primary textual basis for barring women from supreme political rule.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَمَّا بَلَغَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّ فَارِسًا مَلَّكُوا ابْنَةَ كِسْرَى قَالَ ‏ "‏ لَنْ يُفْلِحَ قَوْمٌ وَلَّوْا أَمْرَهُمُ امْرَأَةً ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: When the Prophet heard the news that the people of the Persia had made the daughter of Khosrau their Queen (ruler), he said, "Never will succeed such a nation as makes a woman their ruler

bukhari:7099.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this statement was merely a specific political prediction regarding the crumbling Sasanian Persian Empire under Khosrau's daughter (Queen Boran in 630 AD), rather than a universal prohibition against female leadership. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "lan yufliḥa qawmun wallaw amrahum imraʾatan" ("Never will a people succeed who entrust their affairs to a woman"), pairing the emphatic particle of future negation (lan) with the indefinite nouns qawmun (any people) and imraʾatan (any woman)—a grammatical structure that classical jurists universally recognized as an unrestricted, binding rule (al-ʿibrah bi-ʿumūm al-lafẓ lā bi-khuṣūṣ al-sabab). Moreover, the Companion Abū Bakrah himself invoked this exact wording to condemn the leadership of the Prophet's own wife ʿĀʾishah at the Battle of the Camel (656 AD), and Ibn Hajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī 13/53) confirms unanimous Sunni consensus (ijmāʿ) barring women from heads-of-state and judicial office due to their divinely decreed deficiency in intellect (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 304).

muslim:7191.note: In an exhortation regarding women, Muhammad asks why a man flogs his wife like a slave or slave-girl (jald al-ʿabd / jald al-amah) when he may lie with her sexually (yuḍājiʿuhā, stated explicitly as sexual intercourse, yujāmiʿuhā, in bukhari:5204) at the end of his day. The published English translation obscures this clause with the euphemism 'and then comforts his bed with the help of that at the end of the day.'

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ النِّسَاءَ فَوَعَظَ فِيهِنَّ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ إِلاَمَ يَجْلِدُ أَحَدُكُمُ امْرَأَتَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فِي رِوَايَةِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ ‏"‏ جَلْدَ الأَمَةِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَفِي رِوَايَةِ أَبِي كُرَيْبٍ ‏"‏ جَلْدَ الْعَبْدِ وَلَعَلَّهُ يُضَاجِعُهَا مِنْ آخِرِ يَوْمِهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He then delivered instruction in regard to the women saying: There is amongst you who beats his woman, and in the narration on the authority of Abu Bakr, the words are: He flogs her like a slave-girl. And in the narration of Abu Kuraib (the words are): He flogs like a slave and then comforts his bed with the help of that at the end of the day

muslim:7191.literal_translation: Then he mentioned women and exhorted concerning them, then said: 'Why does one of you flog his wife'—in the narration of Abu Bakr: 'the flogging of a slave-girl,' and in the narration of Abu Kuraib: 'the flogging of a slave, when perhaps he will lie with her (sexually) at the end of his day?'

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَلَعَلَّهُ يُضَاجِعُهَا مِنْ آخِرِ يَوْمِهِ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and then comforts his bed with the help of that at the end of the day
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and perhaps he will lie with her (in bed / sexually) at the end of his day
translation_issue.explanation: The published translation renders 'wa-laʿallahu yuḍājiʿuhā' ('and perhaps he will lie with her [in bed / sexually]') as the euphemism 'and then comforts his bed with the help of that,' obscuring the direct contrast between flogging a wife like a slave and lying with her the same evening.

muslim:7191.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration shows Muhammad condemning domestic abuse and promoting marital compassion by reminding husbands of the intimacy they share with their wives. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states جَلْدَ الأَمَةِ ('the flogging of a slave-girl') and جَلْدَ الْعَبْدِ وَلَعَلَّهُ يُضَاجِعُهَا مِنْ آخِرِ يَوْمِهِ ('the flogging of a slave, when perhaps he will lie with her sexually at the end of his day'), which neither revokes the license to beat wives in [Quran 4:34](quran://4/34) nor objects to the flogging of slaves. Instead, the statement treats the whipping of enslaved people as an accepted baseline and moderates the beating of a wife on the practical ground that the husband may desire sexual intercourse with her that same evening (cf. bukhari:4942, bukhari:5204, bukhari:6042).

bukhari:511.note: When told that a dog, a donkey, and a woman sever prayer—a ruling explicitly attributed to Muhammad in other authentic reports (muslim:1137, muslim:1139)—Aisha protests, "You have made us dogs!" She counters this claim by recounting that Muhammad used to pray while she lay on the bed between him and the qibla, slipping away quietly whenever she had a need.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ذُكِرَ عِنْدَهَا مَا يَقْطَعُ الصَّلاَةَ فَقَالُوا يَقْطَعُهَا الْكَلْبُ وَالْحِمَارُ وَالْمَرْأَةُ‏.‏ قَالَتْ قَدْ جَعَلْتُمُونَا كِلاَبًا، لَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ ـ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ ـ يُصَلِّي، وَإِنِّي لَبَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْقِبْلَةِ، وَأَنَا مُضْطَجِعَةٌ عَلَى السَّرِيرِ، فَتَكُونُ لِي الْحَاجَةُ، فَأَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَسْتَقْبِلَهُ فَأَنْسَلُّ انْسِلاَلاً‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The things which annul the prayers were mentioned before me. They said, "Prayer is annulled by a dog, a donkey and a woman (if they pass in front of the praying people)." I said, "You have made us (i.e. women) dogs. I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) praying while I used to lie in my bed between him and the Qibla. Whenever I was in need of something, I would slip away. for I disliked to face him

bukhari:511.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Aisha's rebuttal disproves the equivalence of women with animals, or they cite Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* to claim that grouping them under *yaqṭaʿu al-ṣalāt* (يَقْطَعُ الصَّلاَةَ, severing prayer) merely addresses distraction of focus (*khushūʿ*) rather than shared degradation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states the ruling that "the dog, the donkey, and the woman sever it" (يَقْطَعُهَا الْكَلْبُ وَالْحِمَارُ وَالْمَرْأَةُ), which Aisha herself immediately recognized as demeaning when she protested, "You have made us dogs" (قَدْ جَعَلْتُمُونَا كِلاَبًا; cf. bukhari:514, أَعَدَلْتُمُونَا بِالْكَلْبِ وَالْحِمَارِ, "Have you equated us with the dog and the donkey?"). Moreover, Sahih Muslim (muslim:1137, muslim:1139) canonizes this exact tripartite decree directly from Muhammad's own mouth, and classical scholars neutralized Aisha's objection by ruling that her lying stationary on the bed (مُضْطَجِعَةٌ عَلَى السَّرِيرِ) did not overturn the prophetic verdict against a woman walking past.

bukhari:514.note: When the ruling that a dog, a donkey, and a woman annul prayer (transmitted from Muhammad by other companions, as in muslim:1137) is mentioned before Aisha, she objects, "You have compared us to donkeys and dogs." She swears that Muhammad used to pray while she lay on the bed between him and the Qibla, slipping away by his feet when needed.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ذُكِرَ عِنْدَهَا مَا يَقْطَعُ الصَّلاَةَ الْكَلْبُ وَالْحِمَارُ وَالْمَرْأَةُ فَقَالَتْ شَبَّهْتُمُونَا بِالْحُمُرِ وَالْكِلاَبِ، وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُصَلِّي، وَإِنِّي عَلَى السَّرِيرِ ـ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْقِبْلَةِ ـ مُضْطَجِعَةً فَتَبْدُو لِي الْحَاجَةُ، فَأَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَجْلِسَ فَأُوذِيَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَنْسَلُّ مِنْ عِنْدِ رِجْلَيْهِ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The things which annul prayer were mentioned before me (and those were): a dog, a donkey and a woman. I said, "You have compared us (women) to donkeys and dogs. By Allah! I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) praying while I used to lie in (my) bed between him and the Qibla. Whenever I was in need of something, I disliked to sit and trouble the Prophet. So, I would slip away by the side of his feet

bukhari:514.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration exonerates Islam by showing Aisha correcting a companion's private misconception, or claim—citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—that grouping women with dogs and donkeys only concerns distracting a worshipper's focus (*khushūʿ*) rather than equating their worth. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Aisha herself condemned the doctrine as a degrading equation (*shabbahtumūnā bi-l-ḥumuri wa-l-kilāb*, 'You have compared us to donkeys and dogs'), and the exact decree she protested against is canonized in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* (510a, 511a) as the direct, authentic words of Muhammad himself (*yaqṭaʿu al-ṣalāta al-marʾatu wa-l-ḥimāru wa-l-kalb*). Moreover, classical commentators like Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawī note that Aisha only lay stationary (*muḍṭajiʿatan*) and still had to 'slip away by the side of his feet' (*fa-ansallu min ʿindi rijlayhi*) to avoid passing in front of him, thereby preserving the prophetic ruling that a woman walking past a praying man annuls his prayer alongside donkeys and dogs.

bukhari:4942.note: In a sermon, Muhammad rebukes a husband for flogging his wife like the flogging of a slave (`جَلْدَ الْعَبْدِ`) on the stated rationale that he may lie with her at the end of the same day (bukhari:5204). Classical commentators harmonize this with the permission to strike wives in [Quran 4:34](quran://4/34) by restricting the rebuke to severe, slave-like whipping rather than prohibiting wife-beating altogether.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَذَكَرَ النِّسَاءَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَعْمِدُ أَحَدُكُمْ يَجْلِدُ امْرَأَتَهُ جَلْدَ الْعَبْدِ، فَلَعَلَّهُ يُضَاجِعُهَا مِنْ آخِرِ يَوْمِهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) then mentioned about the women (in his sermon). "It is not wise for anyone of you to lash his wife like a slave, for he might sleep with her the same evening."

bukhari:4942.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this sermon proves Muhammad condemned domestic violence and sought to protect women by appealing to marital intimacy, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* to claim that anything beyond a symbolic tap is prohibited. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that a man should not flog his wife *jald al-‘abd* ('like the flogging of a slave') solely because *la‘allahu yuḍāji‘uhā min ākhiri yawmihi* ('perhaps he will lie with her at the end of his day'), grounding the objection in the husband's sexual convenience rather than the wife's human dignity while normalizing the brutal whipping of slaves as an unquestioned baseline. Moreover, Ibn Hajar explicitly confirms in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* (on `bukhari:5204`) that this phrasing renders even severe, slave-like flogging merely disliked (*makrūh*) rather than forbidden (*ḥarām*), leaving a husband's legal right to beat his wife under Quran 4:34 fully intact.

muslim:2951.note: During his Farewell Sermon at Arafa in AD 632, Muhammad declares that men have taken women under Allah's security and made their private parts (furūjahunna) lawful by Allah's word. He commands husbands to beat (fa-ḍribūhunna ḍarban ghayra mubarriḥ, a non-severe beating) wives who allow anyone the husbands dislike onto their beds, while defining wives' rights over husbands as food and clothing provided in a fitting manner ([Quran 4:34](quran://4/34), [Ephesians 5:25](bible://eph/5/25)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ فِي النِّسَاءِ فَإِنَّكُمْ أَخَذْتُمُوهُنَّ بِأَمَانِ اللَّهِ وَاسْتَحْلَلْتُمْ فُرُوجَهُنَّ بِكَلِمَةِ اللَّهِ وَلَكُمْ عَلَيْهِنَّ أَنْ لاَ يُوطِئْنَ فُرُشَكُمْ أَحَدًا تَكْرَهُونَهُ ‏.‏ فَإِنْ فَعَلْنَ ذَلِكَ فَاضْرِبُوهُنَّ ضَرْبًا غَيْرَ مُبَرِّحٍ وَلَهُنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ رِزْقُهُنَّ وَكِسْوَتُهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Fear Allah concerning women! Verily you have taken them on the security of Allah, and intercourse with them has been made lawful unto you by words of Allah. You too have right over them, and that they should not allow anyone to sit on your bed whom you do not like. But if they do that, you can chastise them but not severely. Their rights upon you are that you should provide them with food and clothing in a fitting manner.

muslim:2951.literal_translation: Fear Allah concerning women! Verily you have taken them on the security of Allah, and you have made their private parts lawful for yourselves by the word of Allah. And your right over them is that they do not allow anyone whom you dislike to tread upon your beds. And if they do that, then beat them with a beating that is not severe. And their right upon you is their provision and their clothing in a fitting manner.

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَإِنْ فَعَلْنَ ذَلِكَ فَاضْرِبُوهُنَّ ضَرْبًا غَيْرَ مُبَرِّحٍ
translation_issue.published_rendering: But if they do that, you can chastise them but not severely.
translation_issue.literal_meaning: And if they do that, then beat/strike them with a beating that is not severe (or bone-breaking).
translation_issue.explanation: The translator softens the explicit imperative to physically beat wives ('fa-ḍribūhunna ḍarban' — 'beat them with a beating') into 'you can chastise them', and euphemizes 'istaḥlaltum furūjahunna' ('you have made their private parts/vaginas lawful for yourselves') as 'intercourse with them has been made lawful unto you'.

muslim:2951.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's Farewell Sermon in AD 632 was a revolutionary charter of women's rights, citing Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim to claim that the phrase ḍarban ghayra mubarriḥ ('a beating not severe') restricts discipline to a harmless, symbolic tap with a tooth-stick (siwāk). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states fa-ḍribūhunna ('then beat them'—reinforcing Quran 4:34) and reduces marriage to an asymmetric transaction in which husbands acquire lawful access to women's private parts (istaḥlaltum furūjahunna) in exchange for mere food and clothing (rizquhunna wa-kiswatuhunna), a subjugated status that parallel Farewell Sermon accounts explicitly equate to that of helpless captives ('awān, tirmidhi:1163). Furthermore, Al-Nawawī himself defines ghayra mubarriḥ merely as physical blows that stop short of breaking bones or disfiguring the body, and bukhari:5825 confirms that the Companions inflicted literal, skin-bruising beatings on their wives under Muhammad's direct oversight.

bukhari:3237.note: Muhammad declares that if a man calls his wife to his bed, she refuses, and he spends the night angry with her, the angels curse her until morning. Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi affirm that this establishes a binding obligation for a wife to comply with her husband's sexual summons whenever she has no physical or ritual incapacity.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا دَعَا الرَّجُلُ امْرَأَتَهُ إِلَى فِرَاشِهِ فَأَبَتْ، فَبَاتَ غَضْبَانَ عَلَيْهَا، لَعَنَتْهَا الْمَلاَئِكَةُ حَتَّى تُصْبِحَ
problematic_excerpt.english: If a husband calls his wife to his bed (i.e. to have sexual relation) and she refuses and causes him to sleep in anger, the angels will curse her till morning

bukhari:3237.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this warning only applies to a wife who maliciously weaponizes intimacy without a valid excuse like illness, claiming Islam enforces mutual marital rights.
