However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the angelic curse (لَعَنَتْهَا الْمَلاَئِكَةُ) is triggered simply because she refused (فَأَبَتْ) and he slept angry with her (فَبَاتَ غَضْبَانَ عَلَيْهَا), making her spiritual condemnation entirely dependent on his subjective sexual frustration with zero reciprocal curse in the Sunnah against a husband who refuses his wife. Moreover, in Fatḥ al-Bārī (on bukhari:5193) and Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (1436), Sunni authorities confirm that a wife's lack of desire is not a valid excuse, obligating her to submit whenever she is not menstruating or physically incapacitated.

bukhari:5193.note: Muhammad declares that if a man summons his wife to his bed and she refuses to come, the angels curse her until the morning. Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawi affirm that a wife's refusal of her husband's sexual summons without a recognized legal excuse (such as illness or obligatory fasting) incurs this angelic curse.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا دَعَا الرَّجُلُ امْرَأَتَهُ إِلَى فِرَاشِهِ فَأَبَتْ أَنْ تَجِيءَ لَعَنَتْهَا الْمَلاَئِكَةُ حَتَّى تُصْبِحَ
problematic_excerpt.english: If a man Invites his wife to sleep with him and she refuses to come to him, then the angels send their curses on her till morning

bukhari:5193.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this warning only applies when a wife maliciously withholds intimacy without a valid medical or religious excuse, and claim that treating refusal as a spiritual sin actually protects women from physical coercion. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a unilateral curse upon the wife simply for declining her husband's summons to bed (إِذَا دَعَا الرَّجُلُ امْرَأَتَهُ إِلَى فِرَاشِهِ فَأَبَتْ أَنْ تَجِيءَ لَعَنَتْهَا الْمَلاَئِكَةُ) with zero reciprocal penalty for an unwilling husband, while parallel Sahih narrations (muslim:3541) declare that God Himself remains wrathful with her until her husband is pleased with her (حَتَّى يَرْضَى عَنْهَا). Furthermore, classical commentators like Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) and Ibn Hajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) affirm that a woman's lack of desire is never a valid excuse to refuse intercourse, and Quran 4:34 compounds this spiritual coercion by authorizing husbands to physically strike (وَاضْرِبُوهُنَّ) wives who persist in such marital refusal (nushūz).

bukhari:5194.note: Muhammad declares that if a woman spends the night forsaking her husband's bed, the angels curse her until she returns.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا بَاتَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ مُهَاجِرَةً فِرَاشَ زَوْجِهَا لَعَنَتْهَا الْمَلاَئِكَةُ حَتَّى تَرْجِعَ
problematic_excerpt.english: If a woman spends the night deserting her husband's bed (does not sleep with him), then the angels send their curses on her till she comes back (to her husband)

bukhari:5194.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this warning only applies when a wife maliciously weaponizes intimacy without a valid legal excuse ('udhr shar'i), claiming that Islamic marriage enforces reciprocal conjugal rights for both spouses. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a unilateral spiritual threat against the woman (idha batat al-mar'atu muhajiratan firasha zawjiha la'anatha al-mala'ikatu hatta tarji'a), which parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:3237, bukhari:5193) trigger whenever a husband goes to sleep angry (ghadban) after she declines his summons. Moreover, classical commentators like Al-Nawawi (Sharh Sahih Muslim) and Ibn Hajar (Fath al-Bari) confirm that a wife's personal or emotional unwillingness never exempts her from these curses, whereas Quran 4:34 explicitly grants the husband the unilateral right to abandon his wife's bed (wahjuruhunna fi al-madaji') as a disciplinary measure without incurring any angelic wrath.

muslim:3527.note: When the thrice-divorced ex-wife of Rifa'a al-Qurazi complains that her second husband is impotent like the fringe of her garment, Muhammad smiles and laughs before ruling that she cannot return to her first husband until the second husband consummates the marriage with her ('tasted your sweetness and you have tasted his sweetness', [Quran 2:230](quran://2/230), cf. [Deuteronomy 24:1](bible://dt/24/1)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رِفَاعَةَ الْقُرَظِيَّ طَلَّقَ امْرَأَتَهُ فَبَتَّ طَلاَقَهَا فَتَزَوَّجَتْ بَعْدَهُ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ الزَّبِيرِ فَجَاءَتِ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ تَحْتَ رِفَاعَةَ فَطَلَّقَهَا آخِرَ ثَلاَثِ تَطْلِيقَاتٍ فَتَزَوَّجْتُ بَعْدَهُ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ الزَّبِيرِ وَإِنَّهُ وَاللَّهِ مَا مَعَهُ إِلاَّ مِثْلُ الْهُدْبَةِ وَأَخَذَتْ بِهُدْبَةٍ مِنْ جِلْبَابِهَا ‏.‏ قَالَ فَتَبَسَّمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ضَاحِكًا فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ لَعَلَّكِ تُرِيدِينَ أَنْ تَرْجِعِي إِلَى رِفَاعَةَ لاَ حَتَّى يَذُوقَ عُسَيْلَتَكِ وَتَذُوقِي عُسَيْلَتَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Rifa'a al-Quraid (Allah be pleased with him) divorced his wife, making her divorce irrevocable. Afterwards she married Abd at-Rahman b. al-Zubair (Allah be pleased with him), She came to Allah'sApostle (may peace be upon him and said to Allah's messenger (ﷺ) that she had been the wife of Rifa'a (Allah be pleased with him) and he had divorced her by three pronouncements and afterwards she married 'Abd al-Rahman b. al-Zubair. By Allah, all he possesses is like the fringe of a garment, and she took hold of the fringe of her garment. Thereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) laughed and said:Perhaps you wish to return to Rifa'a, (but you) cannot (do it) until he has tasted your sweetness and you have tasted his sweetness.

muslim:3527.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that the intervening marriage rule in Quran 2:230 protects women by deterring men from rash triple divorces, and that Muhammad only laughed because he discerned she was fabricating her second husband's impotence to engineer a sham return to Rifa'a. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *lā ḥattā yadhūqa ʿusaylataki wa-tadhūqī ʿusaylatahu* ('No, until he tastes your sweetness and you taste his sweetness')—which Al-Nawawī defines as mandatory vaginal penetration (*taghyīb al-ḥashafah fī al-farj*)—reducing the woman's body to a compulsory sexual instrument to expiate her first husband's reckless pronouncement. Furthermore, the parallel narration in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 5825 records that even when this second husband beat her until her skin was 'greener than her green garment' (*ashaddu khuḍratan min thawbihā*), Muhammad still refused to rescue her and enforced the exact same requirement of sexual consummation.

bukhari:4425.note: Explaining what kept him from joining and fighting alongside the Companions of the Camel, Abu Bakra reports that upon learning the Persians had crowned Khosrau's daughter as their ruler, Muhammad declared that a people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never prosper.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَمَّا بَلَغَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّ أَهْلَ فَارِسَ قَدْ مَلَّكُوا عَلَيْهِمْ بِنْتَ كِسْرَى قَالَ ‏ "‏ لَنْ يُفْلِحَ قَوْمٌ وَلَّوْا أَمْرَهُمُ امْرَأَةً ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was informed that the Persians had crowned the daughter of Khosrau as their ruler, he said, "Such people as ruled by a lady will never be successful

bukhari:4425.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was merely making a specific political prophecy about the collapsing Sassanian Persian Empire under Khosrau's daughter, rather than issuing a universal ban on female leadership. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "lan yufliḥa qawmun wallaw amrahum imraʾatan" ("never will a people prosper who entrust their affairs to a woman"), using indefinite nouns (qawmun and imraʾatan) in the context of an emphatic negation—a grammatical structure that classical jurists and Ibn Ḥajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī affirm is a universal prohibition establishing scholarly consensus (ijmāʿ) that women are permanently barred from supreme political and judicial authority. Furthermore, the framing of the Hadith itself refutes the Persia-only excuse, as the Companion Abū Bakrah explicitly applied Muhammad's decree against Muhammad's own wife ʿĀʾishah leading Muslim forces at the Battle of the Camel in 656 AD.

bukhari:402.note: Umar ibn al-Khattab states that his Lord agreed with him in three instances where Quranic verses were revealed in direct accordance with his prior suggestions and exact words ([Quran 2:125](quran://2/125), [Quran 33:53](quran://33/53), [Quran 66:5](quran://66/5)). Specifically, after Umar urged Muhammad to command his wives to veil themselves because both righteous and wicked men spoke to them, the verse of the Hijab ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53)) was revealed, and when he warned Muhammad's wives that Allah might replace them with better wives if divorced, his exact statement was revealed as [Quran 66:5](quran://66/5).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَافَقْتُ رَبِّي فِي ثَلاَثٍ، فَقُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوِ اتَّخَذْنَا مِنْ مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مُصَلًّى فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏وَاتَّخِذُوا مِنْ مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مُصَلًّى‏}‏ وَآيَةُ الْحِجَابِ قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، لَوْ أَمَرْتَ نِسَاءَكَ أَنْ يَحْتَجِبْنَ، فَإِنَّهُ يُكَلِّمُهُنَّ الْبَرُّ وَالْفَاجِرُ‏.‏ فَنَزَلَتْ آيَةُ الْحِجَابِ، وَاجْتَمَعَ نِسَاءُ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي الْغَيْرَةِ عَلَيْهِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُنَّ عَسَى رَبُّهُ إِنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ أَنْ يُبَدِّلَهُ أَزْوَاجًا خَيْرًا مِنْكُنَّ‏.‏ فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: My Lord agreed with me in three things: -1. I said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), I wish we took the station of Abraham as our praying place (for some of our prayers). So came the Divine Inspiration: And take you (people) the station of Abraham as a place of prayer (for some of your prayers e.g. two rak`at of Tawaf of Ka`ba)". (2.125) -2. And as regards the (verse of) the veiling of the women, I said, 'O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! I wish you ordered your wives to cover themselves from the men because good and bad ones talk to them.' So the verse of the veiling of the women was revealed. -3. Once the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) made a united front against the Prophet (ﷺ) and I said to them, 'It may be if he (the Prophet) divorced you, (all) that his Lord (Allah) will give him instead of you wives better than you.' So this verse (the same as I had said) was revealed

bukhari:402.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Umar's interventions—celebrated in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* as *Muwāfaqāt ʿUmar*—merely reflected divinely inspired intuition (*ilhām*) and protective honor (*ghayrah*) to dignify and shield the Prophet's wives rather than subjugate women or dictate scripture. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the mandate to veil and seclude women (`أَنْ يَحْتَجِبْنَ`) and the divine threat to divorce and replace Muhammad's wives (`عَسَى رَبُّهُ إِنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ أَنْ يُبَدِّلَهُ أَزْوَاجًا خَيْرًا مِنْكُنَّ` in Quran 66:5) were revealed as verbatim endorsements of Umar's prior demands, restricting women's freedom simply because 'wicked men' (`الْفَاجِرُ`) spoke to them. Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:146`, `bukhari:4790`) admit that when Muhammad initially resisted imposing the veil, Umar stalked the Prophet's wife Sawdah at night as she went out to relieve herself and publicly harassed her until the Hijab verse was revealed to satisfy him.

bukhari:4483.note: Umar ibn al-Khattab states that his Lord concurred with him in three matters (*Muwafaqat Umar*): taking the station of Abraham as a prayer site ([Quran 2:125](quran://2/125)), ordering Muhammad's wives to be veiled ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53)), and warning Muhammad's wives that Allah would replace them with better wives if they did not cease. After one of the wives objected to Umar admonishing them on Muhammad's behalf, [Quran 66:5](quran://66/5) was revealed repeating Umar's exact warning that Allah would replace them with better wives if Muhammad divorced them.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَافَقْتُ اللَّهَ فِي ثَلاَثٍ ـ أَوْ وَافَقَنِي رَبِّي فِي ثَلاَثٍ ـ قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، لَوِ اتَّخَذْتَ مَقَامَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مُصَلًّى وَقُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ يَدْخُلُ عَلَيْكَ الْبَرُّ وَالْفَاجِرُ، فَلَوْ أَمَرْتَ أُمَّهَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِالْحِجَابِ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ آيَةَ الْحِجَابِ قَالَ وَبَلَغَنِي مُعَاتَبَةُ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَعْضَ نِسَائِهِ، فَدَخَلْتُ عَلَيْهِنَّ قُلْتُ إِنِ انْتَهَيْتُنَّ أَوْ لَيُبَدِّلَنَّ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ صلى الله عليه وسلم خَيْرًا مِنْكُنَّ‏.‏ حَتَّى أَتَيْتُ إِحْدَى نِسَائِهِ، قَالَتْ يَا عُمَرُ، أَمَا فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَا يَعِظُ نِسَاءَهُ حَتَّى تَعِظَهُنَّ أَنْتَ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ ‏{‏عَسَى رَبُّهُ إِنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ أَنْ يُبَدِّلَهُ أَزْوَاجًا خَيْرًا مِنْكُنَّ مُسْلِمَاتٍ‏}‏ الآيَةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: I agreed with Allah in three things," or said, "My Lord agreed with me in three things. I said, 'O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Would that you took the station of Abraham as a place of prayer.' I also said, 'O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Good and bad persons visit you! Would that you ordered the Mothers of the believers to cover themselves with veils.' So the Divine Verses of Al-Hijab (i.e. veiling of the women) were revealed. I came to know that the Prophet (ﷺ) had blamed some of his wives so I entered upon them and said, 'You should either stop (troubling the Prophet (ﷺ) ) or else Allah will give His Apostle better wives than you.' When I came to one of his wives, she said to me, 'O `Umar! Does Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) haven't what he could advise his wives with, that you try to advise them?' " Thereupon Allah revealed:-- "It may be, if he divorced you (all) his Lord will give him instead of you, wives better than you Muslims (who submit to Allah)

bukhari:4483.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the "Concordances of Umar" (Muwāfaqāt ʿUmar) discussed in Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī merely demonstrate Umar's spiritual intuition (ilhām) and protective honor for the Prophet's household rather than patriarchal subjugation or human dictation of the Quran. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that when one of Muhammad's wives rebuked Umar for meddling in their domestic affairs ("ḥattā taʿiẓahunna anta"), Allah immediately revealed Quran 66:5 repeating Umar's exact threat word-for-word ("أَنْ يُبَدِّلَهُ أَزْوَاجًا خَيْرًا مِنْكُنَّ"), proving that "divine revelation" was deployed on demand to silence female pushback and enforce Umar's campaign of domestic seclusion (cf. bukhari:146, where Umar harassed Sawdah at night to force the revelation of the ḥijāb verse).

bukhari:5772.note: On the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, Muhammad negates general bird-omens (*lā ṭiyara*) only to carve out an explicit affirmative exception (*innamā al-shuʾmu fī thalāth*) declaring that evil omens reside solely in a horse, a woman, and a house. Multiple independent Companions—including Ibn ʿUmar, Sahl ibn Saʿd, and Jābir—corroborate this direct prophetic declaration across the *Ṣaḥīḥayn* (bukhari:2858, bukhari:5093, bukhari:5094, muslim:5804), precluding later attempts outside the *Ṣaḥīḥayn* to reframe the statement as a mere quotation of pre-Islamic beliefs.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّمَا الشُّؤْمُ فِي ثَلاَثٍ فِي الْفَرَسِ، وَالْمَرْأَةِ، وَالدَّارِ
problematic_excerpt.english: an evil omen is only in three: a horse, a woman and a house

bukhari:5772.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Ibn ʿUmar misheard Muhammad quoting a pre-Islamic superstition (citing a later report from ʿĀʾishah), or they appeal to Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* to claim that *shuʾm* merely refers to practical domestic incompatibility rather than literal bad omens. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *innamā al-shuʾm fī thalāth* ('evil omen is *only* in three'), using the restrictive particle *innamā* directly after negating general omens (*wa-lā ṭiyarah*) to carve out a literal prophetic exception for horses, women, and houses. Furthermore, this exact ruling is independently corroborated in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* by other Companions like Sahl ibn Saʿd (bukhari:2858, bukhari:5094–5095), compelling classical commentators to admit that multiple authentic chains confirm Muhammad spoke these words as his own normative doctrine.

bukhari:5772.note: Muhammad categorically declares that there is no contagious disease transmission (*lā ʿadwā*) alongside his denial of omens (*wa-lā ṭiyara*). Adjacent reports in the same chapter confirm a literal denial of horizontal contagion rather than an unstated theological qualification—dismissing a Bedouin's observation of mange spreading through a camel herd by asking "Then who infected the first?" (bukhari:5717, bukhari:5770) and prompting Abū Hurayra to retract his own narration of "no *ʿadwā*" when confronted with the contradictory quarantine command (bukhari:5771).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لاَ عَدْوَى، وَلاَ طِيَرَةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: there is neither 'Adwa nor Tiyara

bukhari:5772.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that *lā ʿadwā* ('no contagion') only negates the pagan belief that diseases transmit autonomously without Allah's will, pointing to the clause in bukhari:5707 ('flee from the leper') as proof that Islam affirms medical quarantine. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an unqualified categorical negation (*lā ʿadwā*), and in parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:5717, bukhari:5770), when a Bedouin empirically challenges Muhammad by noting that a single mangy camel infects a whole healthy herd, Muhammad refutes the physical transmission itself by retorting, *fa-man aʿdā al-awwal* ('Then who infected the first?'). Rather than saying Allah causes the first camel to infect the second, Muhammad's counter-argument treats the subsequent infections as independent divine acts, proving he rejected biological contagion as a superstitious illusionon par with bird-augury (*ṭiyarah*).

bukhari:5753.note: Narrated via Ibn Umar, Muhammad declares that while general bird-omens (*ṭiyarah*) are negated, evil omen (*al-shuʾm*) resides in three things: a woman, a house, and a riding animal. Although Aisha elsewhere argued that Ibn Umar misheard a reference to pre-Islamic beliefs, multiple authentic chains in Bukhari (bukhari:5093, bukhari:5094) record this as a direct prophetic exception.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لاَ عَدْوَى وَلاَ طِيَرَةَ، وَالشُّؤْمُ فِي ثَلاَثٍ فِي الْمَرْأَةِ، وَالدَّارِ، وَالدَّابَّةِ
problematic_excerpt.english: There is neither 'Adwa (no contagious disease is conveyed to others without Allah's permission) nor Tiyara, but an evil omen may be in three a woman, a house or an animal

bukhari:5753.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Ibn Umar misheard Muhammad quoting pre-Islamic superstitions, or claim via Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim that al-shu'm (evil omen) merely refers metaphorically to practical incompatibility or a wife's difficult temperament. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states wa-l-shu'mu fī thalāthin fī al-mar'ati wa-l-dāri wa-l-dābbati ('and evil omen is in three: in the woman, the house, and the beast'), carving out a literal exception immediately after negating general omens (lā ṭiyarata). Furthermore, this exact ruling is independently narrated across Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī (2858, 5093–5094) and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (2225) by Sahl ibn Sa'd, Jābir ibn 'Abdullāh, and Anas ibn Mālik, completely refuting the excuse that Ibn Umar alone misheard the statement.

bukhari:5753.note: Muhammad declares in the Arabic text that 'there is no contagion' (*lā ʿadwā*) while simultaneously affirming that evil omens reside in a woman, a house, and an animal. The English translator inserts an interpolated parenthetical caveat ('without Allah's permission') absent from the Arabic text to harmonize this denial of disease transmission with later medical understanding (cf. bukhari:5707, bukhari:5717).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لاَ عَدْوَى وَلاَ طِيَرَةَ، وَالشُّؤْمُ فِي ثَلاَثٍ فِي الْمَرْأَةِ، وَالدَّارِ، وَالدَّابَّةِ
problematic_excerpt.english: There is neither 'Adwa (no contagious disease is conveyed to others without Allah's permission) nor Tiyara, but an evil omen may be in three a woman, a house or an animal

bukhari:5753.literal_translation: There is no contagion and no evil bird-omens, and evil omen is in three: in the woman, the house, and the beast.

translation_issue.arabic_term: لاَ عَدْوَى
translation_issue.published_rendering: There is neither 'Adwa (no contagious disease is conveyed to others without Allah's permission)
translation_issue.literal_meaning: There is no contagion
translation_issue.explanation: The Arabic text states simply lā ʿadwā ('there is no contagion'). The translator leaves the term untranslated and interpolates the unattested parenthetical caveat '(no contagious disease is conveyed to others without Allah's permission)' to harmonize and soften Muhammad's categorical denial of contagious disease transmission.

bukhari:5753.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, that Muhammad only denied that diseases transmit autonomously apart from Allah's decree—an excuse modern translators insert into the English text via parenthetical glosses—while pointing to his command to flee from a leper (bukhari:5707). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states lā 'adwā ('There is no contagion') using the categorical particle of absolute negation (lā al-nāfiyah li-l-jins) with zero mention of divine permission. In parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:5717; muslim:5788), when a Bedouin empirically objects that a single mangy camel infects an entire healthy herd, Muhammad doubles down against physical host-to-host transmission by retorting, fa-man a'dā al-awwala ('Then who infected the first one?').

bukhari:1462.note: During an Eid sermon, Muhammad commands women to give alms because he saw that they form the majority of the inhabitants of Hell due to cursing frequently and showing ingratitude to their husbands. He further declares women to be deficient in intelligence and religion, which parallel reports (bukhari:304) define through a woman's legal testimony equaling half that of a man and her exemption from prayer and fasting during menstruation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَمَرَّ عَلَى النِّسَاءِ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا مَعْشَرَ النِّسَاءِ تَصَدَّقْنَ، فَإِنِّي رَأَيْتُكُنَّ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِ النَّارِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقُلْنَ وَبِمَ ذَلِكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ تُكْثِرْنَ اللَّعْنَ وَتَكْفُرْنَ الْعَشِيرَ، مَا رَأَيْتُ مِنْ نَاقِصَاتِ عَقْلٍ وَدِينٍ أَذْهَبَ لِلُبِّ الرَّجُلِ الْحَازِمِ مِنْ إِحْدَاكُنَّ يَا مَعْشَرَ النِّسَاءِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Then he went towards the women and said, "O women! Give alms, for I have seen that the majority of the dwellers of Hell-Fire were you (women)." The women asked, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! What is the reason for it?" He replied, "O women! You curse frequently, and are ungrateful to your husbands. I have not seen anyone more deficient in intelligence and religion than you. O women, some of you can lead a cautious wise man astray."

bukhari:1462.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that calling women 'deficient in intelligence and religion' (nāqiṣāt ʿaql wa-dīn) is not an ontological insult, claiming via Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim that it merely references benign legal exemptions during menstruation and reduced financial testimony burdens, or serves as playful hyperbole complimenting women's ability to charm 'a cautious wise man' (al-rajul al-ḥāzim). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad delivered this rebuke as a terrifying warning because he saw women forming the majority of Hellfire (akthara ahl al-nār), directly attributing their damnation to collective moral failings ('you curse frequently and are ungrateful to your husbands,' tukthirna al-laʿn wa-takfurna al-ʿashīr) and ordering them to give alms (taṣaddaqna) to escape punishment. Furthermore, the parallel narration in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 304 explicitly defines a woman's 'deficiency in intelligence' (nuqṣān ʿaqlihā) by equating her witness testimony to half that of a man's under Qur'an 2:282, proving that both her cognitive capacity and biological menstruation are codified as literal intellectual and spiritual defects.

bukhari:2658.note: Muhammad states that a woman's testimony is equal to half that of a man ([Quran 2:282](quran://2/282)) and declares that this stems from a deficiency in her intellect (nuqsan 'aqliha).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏"‏ أَلَيْسَ شَهَادَةُ الْمَرْأَةِ مِثْلَ نِصْفِ شَهَادَةِ الرَّجُلِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْنَا بَلَى‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَذَلِكَ مِنْ نُقْصَانِ عَقْلِهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Isn't the witness of a woman equal to half of that of a man?" The women said, "Yes." He said, "This is because of the deficiency of a woman's mind

bukhari:2658.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the two-for-one testimony rule in Quran 2:282 was merely a practical accommodation for 7th-century AD socio-economic norms where women were less involved in financial transactions, or that *nuqṣān ʿaqlihā* simply denotes a reduction in legal burden rather than cognitive inferiority. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `فَذَلِكَ مِنْ نُقْصَانِ عَقْلِهَا` (*fa-dhālika min nuqṣāni ʿaqlihā*—'that is from the deficiency of her mind'), establishing an innate mental deficit as the direct cause (`مِنْ`) of her halved legal standing rather than a temporary cultural circumstance. Furthermore, in the fuller parallel narrations (`bukhari:304`, `muslim:241`), Muhammad cites this exact intellectual deficiency alongside a religious deficiency caused by menstruation (`نُقْصَانِ دِينِهَا`) to explain why women form the majority of the inhabitants of Hellfire, proving he was asserting a permanent biological and spiritual inferiority rather than a benign commercial exemption.

bukhari:6240.note: Around AD 627, Umar ibn al-Khattab repeatedly urged Muhammad to veil and seclude his wives, and after Muhammad did not do so, Umar spotted the tall Sauda bint Zam'a from a gathering as the wives went out at night toward al-Manasi' (the open latrine fields, cf. bukhari:146) and called out that he recognized her out of an explicit desire for the Hijab to be revealed. Allah subsequently revealed the Hijab verse ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53); cf. [Quran 33:59](quran://33/59)), whereas the immediately preceding reports in the same chapter (bukhari:6238, bukhari:6239) attribute its revelation to wedding guests lingering at Muhammad's marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ يَقُولُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم احْجُبْ نِسَاءَكَ‏.‏ قَالَتْ فَلَمْ يَفْعَلْ، وَكَانَ أَزْوَاجُ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَخْرُجْنَ لَيْلاً إِلَى لَيْلٍ قِبَلَ الْمَنَاصِعِ، خَرَجَتْ سَوْدَةُ بِنْتُ زَمْعَةَ، وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَةً طَوِيلَةً فَرَآهَا عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ وَهْوَ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ فَقَالَ عَرَفْتُكِ يَا سَوْدَةُ‏.‏ حِرْصًا عَلَى أَنْ يُنْزَلَ الْحِجَابُ‏.‏ قَالَتْ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ آيَةَ الْحِجَابِ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: `Umar bin Al-Khattab used to say to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) "Let your wives be veiled" But he did not do so. The wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) used to go out to answer the call of nature at night only at Al-Manasi.' Once Sauda, the daughter of Zam`a went out and she was a tall woman. `Umar bin Al-Khattab saw her while he was in a gathering, and said, "I have recognized you, O Sauda!" He (`Umar) said so as he was anxious for some Divine orders regarding the veil (the veiling of women.) So Allah revealed the Verse of veiling. (Al-Hijab; a complete body cover excluding the eyes)

bukhari:6240.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this incident is a virtuous example of *Muwāfaqāt ʿUmar* (Allah's concurrences with Umar's pious intuition), claiming—as Ibn Hajar does in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that Umar acted out of protective honor (*ghayrah*) to shield the Prophet's wives from being harassed by Medinan hypocrites. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad repeatedly ignored Umar's command (`احْجُبْ نِسَاءَكَ ... فَلَمْ يَفْعَلْ`—'Veil your wives... yet he did not do so'), leading Umar to publicly call out Sauda from a men's gathering as she went to relieve herself at night (`عَرَفْتُكِ يَا سَوْدَةُ`) specifically 'out of an eager desire that the Hijab be revealed' (`حِرْصًا عَلَى أَنْ يُنْزَلَ الْحِجَابُ`). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:146, muslim:5668) record that Umar continued accosting Sauda in the dark even *after* the veil was mandated (`أَمَا وَاللَّهِ مَا تَخْفَيْنَ عَلَيْنَا`—'By Allah, you are not hidden from us'), proving that Umar himself was the intimidator and that the Quranic mandate ([Quran 33:53](quran://33/53), [Quran 33:59](quran://33/59)) capitulated to his coercion.

muslim:241.note: Muhammad tells women that they form the majority of the inhabitants of Hellfire because they curse frequently and are ungrateful to their husbands, and declares them 'deficient in intellect and religion' (*nāqiṣāt ʿaql wa-dīn*). When asked to explain, he defines their deficiency in intellect as the testimony of two women equaling that of one man ([Quran 2:282](quran://2/282)) and their deficiency in religion as spending nights without praying and breaking the fast in Ramadan during menstruation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: يَا مَعْشَرَ النِّسَاءِ تَصَدَّقْنَ وَأَكْثِرْنَ الاِسْتِغْفَارَ فَإِنِّي رَأَيْتُكُنَّ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِ النَّارِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَتِ امْرَأَةٌ مِنْهُنَّ جَزْلَةٌ وَمَا لَنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِ النَّارِ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ تُكْثِرْنَ اللَّعْنَ وَتَكْفُرْنَ الْعَشِيرَ وَمَا رَأَيْتُ مِنْ نَاقِصَاتِ عَقْلٍ وَدِينٍ أَغْلَبَ لِذِي لُبٍّ مِنْكُنَّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَمَا نُقْصَانُ الْعَقْلِ وَالدِّينِ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَمَّا نُقْصَانُ الْعَقْلِ فَشَهَادَةُ امْرَأَتَيْنِ تَعْدِلُ شَهَادَةَ رَجُلٍ فَهَذَا نُقْصَانُ الْعَقْلِ وَتَمْكُثُ اللَّيَالِيَ مَا تُصَلِّي وَتُفْطِرُ فِي رَمَضَانَ فَهَذَا نُقْصَانُ الدِّينِ
problematic_excerpt.english: O womenfolk, you should give charity and ask much forgiveness for I saw you in bulk amongst the dwellers of Hell. A wise lady among them said: Why is it, Messenger of Allah, that our folk is in bulk in Hell? Upon this the Prophet observed: You curse too much and are ungrateful to your spouses. I have seen none lacking in common sense and failing in religion but (at the same time) robbing the wisdom of the wise, besides you. Upon this the woman remarked: What is wrong with our common sense and with religion? He (the Holy Prophet) observed: Your lack of common sense (can be well judged from the fact) that the evidence of two women is equal to one man, that is a proof of the lack of common sense, and you spend some nights (and days) in which you do not offer prayer and in the month of Ramadan (during the days) you do not observe fast, that is a failing in religion

muslim:241.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that calling women 'deficient in intellect and religion' (*nāqiṣāt ʿaql wa dīn*) is merely a playful hyperbole or a neutral legal description of merciful exemptions from ritual worship and specialized financial testimony rules, rather than a literal condemnation of female intelligence or spiritual worth. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly delivers this diagnosis within a grave warning that women form the majority of the inhabitants of Hellfire (*akthara ahli al-nār*) and directly defines a woman's halved legal testimony as proof of her cognitive deficiency (*fa-hādhā nuqṣānu al-ʿaql*), which the parallel narration in bukhari:304 and [Quran 2:282](quran://2/282) ground in a woman's innate proneness to err (*an taḍilla iḥdāhumā*). Furthermore, by labeling mandatory menstrual abstention from prayer and fasting a 'deficiency in religion' (*nuqṣānu al-dīn*), the Hadith traps women in a theological double bind where a biological process created by Allah and enforced by Islamic law is simultaneously cited against them as an inherent spiritual defect.

muslim:3526.note: When Rifa'a's irrevocably divorced wife complained that her second husband was impotent ('like the fringe of a garment'), Muhammad smiled and ruled that she could not return to her first husband until she and her new husband consummated their marriage through actual sexual intercourse ('tasted each other's sweetness'; cf. [Quran 2:230](quran://2/230), [Deuteronomy 24:1](bible://dt/24/1)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: جَاءَتِ امْرَأَةُ رِفَاعَةَ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ كُنْتُ عِنْدَ رِفَاعَةَ فَطَلَّقَنِي فَبَتَّ طَلاَقِي فَتَزَوَّجْتُ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ الزَّبِيرِ وَإِنَّ مَا مَعَهُ مِثْلُ هُدْبَةِ الثَّوْبِ فَتَبَسَّمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ أَتُرِيدِينَ أَنْ تَرْجِعِي إِلَى رِفَاعَةَ لاَ حَتَّى تَذُوقِي عُسَيْلَتَهُ وَيَذُوقَ عُسَيْلَتَكِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: There came the wife of Rifa'a to Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) and said: I was married to Rifa'a but he divorced me, making may divorce irrevocable. Afterwards I married Abd al-Rahman b. al-Zubair, but all he possesses is like the fringe of a garment (i. e. he is sexually weak). Thereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) smiled, and said: Do you wish to return to Rifa'a. (You) cannot (do it) until you have tasted his sweetness and he ('Abd al-Rahman) has tasted your sweetness.

muslim:3526.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that requiring a thrice-divorced woman to marry another man before returning to her first husband (Quran 2:230) protects women by deterring husbands from recklessly pronouncing irrevocable divorce (*ṭalāq*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that when Rifa'a's ex-wife pleaded that her second husband was impotent (*mithlu hudbati al-thawb*)—and in parallel *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 5825 showed her green bruises from his beatings—Muhammad merely smiled (*fatabassama*) and ruled, *'lā, ḥattā tadhūqī ʿusaylatahū wa yadhūqa ʿusaylataki'* ('No, not until you taste his sweetness and he tastes your sweetness'). As Al-Nawawī confirms in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, this metaphor strictly mandates actual vaginal penetration (*al-jimāʿ*), punishing the woman for her first husband's rashness by forcing her to submit to unwanted sexual intercourse with another man before she can reunite with her spouse.

muslim:1143.note: When told of the ruling that a dog, a donkey, and a woman invalidate prayer, Aisha objects, "You likened us to the asses and the dogs," and recounts lying on a bed between Muhammad and the Qibla while he prayed. Although Aisha disputes this rule based on her own experience, the ruling that a woman, a donkey, and a dog cut off prayer is explicitly attributed to Muhammad in the immediately preceding reports (muslim:1137, muslim:1139).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَذُكِرَ، عِنْدَهَا مَا يَقْطَعُ الصَّلاَةَ الْكَلْبُ وَالْحِمَارُ وَالْمَرْأَةُ ‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ قَدْ شَبَّهْتُمُونَا بِالْحَمِيرِ وَالْكِلاَبِ ‏.‏ وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ رَأَيْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُصَلِّي وَإِنِّي عَلَى السَّرِيرِ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْقِبْلَةِ مُضْطَجِعَةً فَتَبْدُو لِي الْحَاجَةُ فَأَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَجْلِسَ فَأُوذِيَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأَنْسَلُّ مِنْ عِنْدِ رِجْلَيْهِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: It was mentioned before'A'isha that prayer is invalidated (in case of passing) of a dog, an ass and a woman (before the worshipper, when he is not screened). Upon this 'A'isha said: You likened us to the asses and the dogs. By Allah I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying prayer while I lay on the bedstead interposing between him and the Qibla. When I felt the need, I did not like to wit to front (of the Holy Prophet) and perturb the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and quietly moved out from under its (i. e. of the bedstead) legs

muslim:1143.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Aisha's objection disproves the ruling as a companion's misunderstanding, or—citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—claim that grouping women with animals merely denotes a shared legal effect (*ishtirāk fī al-ḥukm*) due to distraction (*fitnah*) rather than equal status, applying only to passing by rather than lying down. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states Aisha's own indignant rebuke—`قَدْ شَبَّهْتُمُونَا بِالْحَمِيرِ وَالْكِلاَبِ` (*'You have likened us to donkeys and dogs!'*)—proving that Muhammad's own wife recognized the unmistakable degradation of the prophetic decree (`يَقْطَعُ الصَّلاَةَ الْكَلْبُ وَالْحِمَارُ وَالْمَرْأَةُ`). Furthermore, multiple independent *Ṣaḥīḥ* narrations (`muslim:1137`, `muslim:1139`) confirm that Muhammad himself authored this exact triadic classification alongside demonic black dogs, and classical scholars like Al-Nawawī dismiss Aisha's counter-argument—in which she merely lay still (`مُضْطَجِعَةً`) and slunk away (`فَأَنْسَلُّ`) from Muhammad's feet—because explicit prophetic testimony overrides her personal objection.

muslim:1139.note: Muhammad states through Abu Huraira that a woman, a donkey, and a dog sever the prayer unless a barrier like the back of a saddle is placed in front of the worshiper ([Galatians 3:28](bible://gal/3/28)). In the immediately following narrations (muslim:1140-1143; bukhari:511), Aisha protests the companions equating women with donkeys and dogs, testifying that Muhammad prayed while she lay stretched out in front of him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ يَقْطَعُ الصَّلاَةَ الْمَرْأَةُ وَالْحِمَارُ وَالْكَلْبُ وَيَقِي ذَلِكَ مِثْلُ مُؤْخِرَةِ الرَّحْلِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: A woman, an ass and a dog disrupt the prayer, but something like the back of a saddle guards against that

muslim:1139.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that—as suggested in al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—'cutting off the prayer' (*yaqṭaʿu al-ṣalāta*) merely refers to diminishing a worshiper's mental focus (*khushūʿ*) through distraction, or they appeal to Aisha's objection in `bukhari:511` to dismiss the ruling. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *yaqṭaʿu al-ṣalāta al-marʾatu wa-l-ḥimāru wa-l-kalbu* ('a woman, a donkey, and a dog sever the prayer'), directly grouping women with beasts as ritual nullifiers—including the dog, which parallel narration `muslim:1137` defines as a 'devil' (*shayṭān*). Furthermore, Aisha's own outraged rebuke in `muslim:1143` and `bukhari:511` ('You have equated us with donkeys and dogs!') proves that the literal Arabic wording was recognized by the Companions themselves as a degrading ritual equation with animals rather than a benign comment on concentration.

muslim:1142.note: When told that a woman and a donkey sever prayer—a prophetic decree narrated from Muhammad by other Companions in the same chapter (muslim:1137, muslim:1139)—Aisha protests the ruling by exclaiming, "Indeed, the woman is then an evil beast!" (*dābbatu saw'in*), and recounts lying stretched out like a funeral bier in front of Muhammad while he prayed.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ مَا يَقْطَعُ الصَّلاَةَ قَالَ فَقُلْنَا الْمَرْأَةُ وَالْحِمَارُ ‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ إِنَّ الْمَرْأَةَ لَدَابَّةُ سَوْءٍ لَقَدْ رَأَيْتُنِي بَيْنَ يَدَىْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مُعْتَرِضَةً كَاعْتِرَاضِ الْجِنَازَةِ وَهُوَ يُصَلِّي ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: 'A'isha asked: What disrupts the prayer? We said: The woman and the ass. Upon this she remarked: Is the woman an ugly animal? I lay in front of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) like the bier of a corpse and he said prayer

muslim:1142.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration exonerates Islam because Aisha is correcting a mistaken male opinion, or they cite Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* to claim that a woman 'severing' (*yaqṭaʿu*) the prayer merely refers to distracting a man's concentration (*khushūʿ*) rather than equating her with impure animals. However, the primary Arabic text of the preceding chapters (`muslim:1137`, `muslim:1139`) explicitly states that Muhammad himself decreed that 'the woman, the donkey, and the dog' (*al-marʾatu wa-al-ḥimāru wa-al-kalbu*) sever a man's prayer, and Aisha's own outraged sarcasm—'Indeed, the woman is then an evil beast!' (*inna al-marʾata la-dābbatu sawʾin*)—proves that the earliest Muslims understood the prophetic ruling in its plain, degrading sense as classifying women alongside vile animals. Moreover, as classical commentators like Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar note, Sunni jurists Who upheld the ruling dismissed Aisha's counter-example by arguing that her lying stationary (*muʿtariḍatan*) in front of Muhammad did not abrogate his explicit statement regarding a woman passing (*murūr*) before a worshipper.

muslim:1137.note: Muhammad declares that if a worshipper prays without a barrier the height of the back of a saddle in front of him, his prayer is cut off (yaqta'u salatahu) by the passing of a donkey, a woman, or a black dog ([Galatians 3:28](bible://gal/3/28)). Whether interpreted by jurists as completely invalidating the prayer or diminishing its reward, the ruling groups women alongside donkeys and black dogs—an equivalence Aisha explicitly protested in parallel narrations (bukhari:511, muslim:1143).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِذَا قَامَ أَحَدُكُمْ يُصَلِّي فَإِنَّهُ يَسْتُرُهُ إِذَا كَانَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِثْلُ آخِرَةِ الرَّحْلِ فَإِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِثْلُ آخِرَةِ الرَّحْلِ فَإِنَّهُ يَقْطَعُ صَلاَتَهُ الْحِمَارُ وَالْمَرْأَةُ وَالْكَلْبُ الأَسْوَدُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Messenger of 'Allah (ﷺ) said: When any one of you stands for prayer and there is a thing before him equal to the back of the saddle that covers him and in case there is not before him (a thing) equal to the back of the saddle, his prayer would be cut off by (passing of an) ass, woman, and black Dog.

muslim:1137.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase 'cuts off his prayer' (yaqṭaʿu ṣalātahu) only refers to a loss of mental concentration (khushūʿ) due to distraction rather than literal ritual invalidation, citing Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and Aisha's protest in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 511 as proof that women are not equated with animals. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that 'the donkey, the woman, and the black dog cut off his prayer' (يَقْطَعُ صَلاَتَهُ الْحِمَارُ وَالْمَرْأَةُ وَالْكَلْبُ الأَسْوَدُ) under a single shared legal ruling, which is the exact reason Aisha herself protested in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 511, 'You have equated us with donkeys and dogs!' (شَبَّهْتُمُونَا بِالْحَمِيرِ وَالْكِلَابِ). Moreover, Aisha's personal defense that she lay motionless 'like a corpse' (كَالْجَنَازَةِ) in front of Muhammad fails to overturn the explicit prophetic decree reported independently by Abu Dharr, Abu Hurayrah (Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:1139), and Ibn Abbas regarding a woman actively passing in front of a praying man.

muslim:1137.note: When Abu Dharr asks Muhammad what distinguishes a black dog from a red or yellow dog in cutting off prayer, Muhammad states that "the black dog is a devil" (al-kalbu al-aswadu shaytan). Because this statement provides the explicit legal rationale for why only a black dog—rather than a red or yellow one—severs prayer, it functions in the ruling as a literal classification rather than a figure of speech.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قُلْتُ يَا أَبَا ذَرٍّ مَا بَالُ الْكَلْبِ الأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْكَلْبِ الأَحْمَرِ مِنَ الْكَلْبِ الأَصْفَرِ قَالَ يَا ابْنَ أَخِي سَأَلْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَمَا سَأَلْتَنِي فَقَالَ ‏"‏ الْكَلْبُ الأَسْوَدُ شَيْطَانٌ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I said: O Abu Dharr, what feature is there in a black dog which distinguish it from the red dog and the yellow dog? He said: O, son of my brother, I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as you are asking me, and he said: The black dog is a devil

muslim:1137.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing one of the alternative suggestions in Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, that calling the black dog a 'devil' (shayṭān) is merely an Arabic figure of speech (majāz) describing a particularly fierce, rebellious, or harmful animal rather than a literal supernatural demon. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states 'the black dog is a devil' (الْكَلْبُ الأَسْوَدُ شَيْطَانٌ) to explain why a black coat alone—as opposed to a red or yellow dog (الْكَلْبِ الأَحْمَرِ مِنَ الْكَلْبِ الأَصْفَرِ)—possesses the occult power to sever a believer's ritual prayer (يَقْطَعُ صَلاَتَهُ). Because behavioral aggression neither depends on fur pigment nor nullifies ritual worship, and parallel canonical commands in Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:4132 order the extermination of jet-black dogs specifically because they are devils, classical authorities like Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah affirmed that black dogs are literal demonic entities in canine form.

muslim:6937.note: Muhammad declares that when he stood at the door of Paradise, the majority of those entering it were the poor while the wealthy were detained, and when he stood at the door of the Fire, the majority of those entering it were women.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ قُمْتُ عَلَى بَابِ الْجَنَّةِ فَإِذَا عَامَّةُ مَنْ دَخَلَهَا الْمَسَاكِينُ وَإِذَا أَصْحَابُ الْجَدِّ مَحْبُوسُونَ إِلاَّ أَصْحَابَ النَّارِ فَقَدْ أُمِرَ بِهِمْ إِلَى النَّارِ وَقُمْتُ عَلَى بَابِ النَّارِ فَإِذَا عَامَّةُ مَنْ دَخَلَهَا النِّسَاءُ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: I stood at the door of Paradise and I found that the overwhelming majority of those who entered therein was that of poor persons and the wealthy persons were detained to get into that. The denizens of Hell were commanded to get into Hell, and I stood upon the door of Fire and the majority amongst them who entered there was that of women

muslim:6937.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that women form the majority in Hell solely because women outnumber men in the general population, or that their state is comparable to the temporary detention of the wealthy. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that while the wealthy (أَصْحَابُ الْجَدِّ, aṣḥāb al-jadd) are merely detained (مَحْبُوسُونَ, maḥbūsūna) outside Paradise, the denizens of the Fire were already commanded into Hell (أُمِرَ بِهِمْ إِلَى النَّارِ, umira bihim ilā al-nār), where the overwhelming majority of those entering were women (فَإِذَا عَامَّةُ مَنْ دَخَلَهَا النِّسَاءُ, fa-idhā ʿāmmatu man dakhalahā al-nisāʾ). If demographic size explained this disparity, women would likewise constitute the majority entering Paradise, yet the narration (paralleled in bukhari:5196, bukhari:6547, and muslim:6938) identifies the poor (الْمَسَاكِينُ, al-masākīn) at the door of Paradise while singling out women at the door of the Fire.

muslim:3538.note: Muhammad declares that when a woman spends the night forsaking her husband's bed, the angels curse her until morning ([1 Corinthians 7:3](bible://1cor/7/3), [Ephesians 5:25](bible://eph/5/25)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ إِذَا بَاتَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ هَاجِرَةً فِرَاشَ زَوْجِهَا لَعَنَتْهَا الْمَلاَئِكَةُ حَتَّى تُصْبِحَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira (Allah be pleased with him) reported that Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) said:When a woman spends the night away from the bed of her husband, the angels curse her until morning

muslim:3538.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this warning only applies to a wife who maliciously weaponizes sexual refusal without a valid excuse ('udhr shar'ī), claiming that marital intimacy in Islam is a reciprocal right. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a unilateral curse upon the woman (idhā bātat al-mar'atu hājiratan firāsha zawjihā la'anathā al-malā'ikatu ḥattā tuṣbiḥa), and the adjacent parallel in Sahih Muslim (muslim:3540) adds that 'He Who is in the heaven is displeased with her until her husband is pleased with her'—which Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) cites to affirm that a wife's compliance is strictly obligatory whenever her husband summons her. Moreover, this spiritual coercion is entirely one-sided: no canonical text ever curses a husband for denying his wife, whereas Quran 4:34 explicitly commands husbands to forsake their wives in bed (wahjurūhunna fī al-maḍāji') and strike them to enforce obedience.

bukhari:1052.note: Muhammad states that he was shown the Hellfire during the eclipse prayer and saw that women constitute the majority of its inhabitants. When asked if this is due to disbelief in Allah, he explains that it is because of their ingratitude toward their husbands and good treatment, stating that a wife who sees a single fault after a lifetime of kindness will claim her husband has never done her any good.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَأُرِيتُ النَّارَ، فَلَمْ أَرَ مَنْظَرًا كَالْيَوْمِ قَطُّ أَفْظَعَ، وَرَأَيْتُ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِهَا النِّسَاءَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالُوا بِمَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ بِكُفْرِهِنَّ ‏"‏‏.‏ قِيلَ يَكْفُرْنَ بِاللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ يَكْفُرْنَ الْعَشِيرَ، وَيَكْفُرْنَ الإِحْسَانَ، لَوْ أَحْسَنْتَ إِلَى إِحْدَاهُنَّ الدَّهْرَ كُلَّهُ، ثُمَّ رَأَتْ مِنْكَ شَيْئًا قَالَتْ مَا رَأَيْتُ مِنْكَ خَيْرًا قَطُّ
problematic_excerpt.english: I also saw the Hell-fire and I had never seen such a horrible sight. I saw that most of the inhabitants were women." The people asked, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Why is it so?" The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, "Because of their ungratefulness." It was asked whether they are ungrateful to Allah. The Prophet said, "They are ungrateful to their companions of life (husbands) and ungrateful to good deeds. If you are benevolent to one of them throughout the life and if she sees anything (undesirable) in you, she will say, 'I have never had any good from you

bukhari:1052.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that women constitute the majority of Hell simply because females outnumber males in the general population (citing discussions in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*), and that *kufr* here is merely a pedagogical warning against minor domestic ingratitude (*kufr dūna kufr*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that when asked *why* (`بِمَ`) women form the majority of Hell's inhabitants (`أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِهَا النِّسَاءَ`), Muhammad never invokes demographics, instead directly attributing their damnation in the Fire (`النَّارَ`) to ungratefulness toward their husbands (`يَكْفُرْنَ الْعَشِيرَ`). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:304`) explicitly tie women being the majority of Hell directly to their inherent 'deficiency in intelligence and religion' (`نَاقِصَاتِ عَقْلٍ وَدِينٍ`), proving that the text grounds their disproportionate damnation in essentialist female inferiority rather than population ratios.

bukhari:29.note: Muhammad declares that he was shown the Hellfire and observed that the majority of its inhabitants are women. When asked whether this is due to disbelief in Allah, he clarifies that it is because they are ungrateful to their husbands and deny the lifelong kindness shown to them.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أُرِيتُ النَّارَ فَإِذَا أَكْثَرُ أَهْلِهَا النِّسَاءُ يَكْفُرْنَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قِيلَ أَيَكْفُرْنَ بِاللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ يَكْفُرْنَ الْعَشِيرَ، وَيَكْفُرْنَ الإِحْسَانَ، لَوْ أَحْسَنْتَ إِلَى إِحْدَاهُنَّ الدَّهْرَ ثُمَّ رَأَتْ مِنْكَ شَيْئًا قَالَتْ مَا رَأَيْتُ مِنْكَ خَيْرًا قَطُّ
problematic_excerpt.english: I was shown the Hell-fire and that the majority of its dwellers were women who were ungrateful." It was asked, "Do they disbelieve in Allah?" (or are they ungrateful to Allah?) He replied, "They are ungrateful to their husbands and are ungrateful for the favors and the good (charitable deeds) done to them. If you have always been good (benevolent) to one of them and then she sees something in you (not of her liking), she will say, 'I have never received any good from you

bukhari:29.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Ḥajar’s *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Bukhari’s chapter title—that *yakfurna al-ʿashīr* (ingratitude toward the husband) denotes a lesser sin (*kufr dūna kufr*) meant as a moral warning rather than eternal damnation, or that women form the majority in Hell simply because they outnumber men in the general population. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that women comprise the majority of Hell's inhabitants (*aktharu ahlihā al-nisāʾ*) specifically because they are ungrateful to their husbands (*yakfurna al-ʿashīr*), directly tying their population of Hellfire to marital complaints rather than demographics. Furthermore, the parallel narration in `bukhari:304` (`muslim:241`) explicitly links this exact condemnation to Muhammad declaring women inherently 'deficient in intelligence and religion' (*nāqiṣāt ʿaqlin wa-dīn*)—citing their menstruation and their testimony being worth half a man's—proving the doctrine is rooted in systemic female inferiority.

bukhari:5197.note: Muhammad states that he saw the Hellfire and observed that women constitute the majority of its inhabitants. When asked if this is due to disbelief in Allah, he clarifies that it is because of their ingratitude toward their husbands (*yakfurna al-ʿashīr*) and for favors done to them, claiming never to have seen any good from a husband despite a lifetime of kindness if they observe a single fault.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَرَأَيْتُ النَّارَ فَلَمْ أَرَ كَالْيَوْمِ مَنْظَرًا قَطُّ وَرَأَيْتُ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِهَا النِّسَاءَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالُوا لِمَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ بِكُفْرِهِنَّ ‏"‏‏.‏ قِيلَ يَكْفُرْنَ بِاللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ يَكْفُرْنَ الْعَشِيرَ، وَيَكْفُرْنَ الإِحْسَانَ، وَلَوْ أَحْسَنْتَ إِلَى إِحْدَاهُنَّ الدَّهْرَ، ثُمَّ رَأَتْ مِنْكَ شَيْئًا قَالَتْ مَا رَأَيْتُ مِنْكَ خَيْرًا قَطُّ
problematic_excerpt.english: Then I saw the (Hell) Fire, and I have never before, seen such a horrible sight as that, and I saw that the majority of its dwellers were women." The people asked, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! What is the reason for that?" He replied, "Because of their ungratefulness." It was said. "Do they disbelieve in Allah (are they ungrateful to Allah)?" He replied, "They are not thankful to their husbands and are ungrateful for the favors done to them. Even if you do good to one of them all your life, when she seems some harshness from you, she will say, "I have never seen any good from you

bukhari:5197.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that women form the majority of Hell merely because females outnumber males in the general human population (citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*), and claim the term *kufr* here only denotes lesser domestic ingratitude (*kufr dūna kufr*) used as a rhetorical moral warning. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that their majority status in Hell is directly caused by their conduct toward their husbands (*bi-kufrihinna ... yakfurna al-ʿashīr*) rather than mere demographics, elevating a wife's frustrated complaint (*mā raʾaytu minka khayran qaṭṭ*) into a damnable offense warranting Hellfire. Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations completely dismantle the demographic excuse by stating that women are simultaneously the *minority* of Paradise's inhabitants (*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2738: *ʾinna ʾaqalla sākinī al-jannati al-nisāʾu*) and explicitly tying their damnation to an inherent female 'deficiency in intelligence and religion' (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 304: *nāqiṣāt ʿaql wa-dīn*).

bukhari:1951.note: Muhammad states that a woman's abstention from prayer and fasting during menstruation constitutes a deficiency in her religion (*nuqṣān dīnihā*). This report is an abbreviated legal excerpt from a fuller narration (bukhari:304, bukhari:1462) in which Muhammad cites this mandatory ritual suspension to explain why women are deficient in intelligence and religion when warning that they form the majority of Hell's inhabitants.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ أَلَيْسَ إِذَا حَاضَتْ لَمْ تُصَلِّ، وَلَمْ تَصُمْ فَذَلِكَ نُقْصَانُ دِينِهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Isn't it true that a woman does not pray and does not fast on menstruating? And that is the defect (a loss) in her religion

bukhari:1951.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists (citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*) typically argue that *nuqṣān dīnihā* ('deficiency in her religion') is merely a neutral, technical description of a merciful legal exemption (*rukhṣah*) from ritual obligations during menstruation rather than a mark of spiritual inferiority. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly labels this involuntary biological cycle a religious defect (*فَذَلِكَ نُقْصَانُ دِينِهَا*), and the full narration in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 304 and *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 241 pairs it directly with an inherent deficiency in intelligence (*نُقْصَانُ عَقْلِهَا*) while Muhammad warns women that they form the majority of the inhabitants of Hell (*أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِ النَّارِ*). Because Islamic law strictly forbids menstruating women from praying or fasting, this defense exposes a theological catch-22 in which women are legally barred from worship due to their God-given biology and then disparaged as 'deficient in intellect and religion' (*نَاقِصَاتِ عَقْلٍ وَدِينٍ*) for obeying that very prohibition.

muslim:2967.note: Abu Dharr states that the two forms of *mutʿah*—temporary marriage with women (*mutʿat al-nisāʾ*) and *tamattuʿ* in Hajj—were permissible exclusively as a special concession for Muhammad's Companions ([Quran 4:24](quran://4/24), [Matthew 19:4](bible://mt/19/4)). As classical commentators like al-Nawawi confirm, this refers to the prophetic dispensation allowing the Companions to contract temporary marriages during Muhammad's lifetime before Sunni jurisprudence held the practice to be subsequently abrogated (muslim:3419).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ أَبُو ذَرٍّ رضى الله عنه لاَ تَصْلُحُ الْمُتْعَتَانِ إِلاَّ لَنَا خَاصَّةً ‏.‏ يَعْنِي مُتْعَةَ النِّسَاءِ وَمُتْعَةَ الْحَجِّ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Dharr (Allah be pleased with him) said:Two are the Mut'as which were not permissible but only for us, i. e. temporary marriage with women and Tamattu' in Hajj

muslim:2967.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that temporary pleasure-marriage (*mutʿat al-nisāʾ*) was merely a brief wartime concession that Muhammad permanently abrogated, and that Abū Dharr was only forbidding later generations from practicing it. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that short-term pleasure-marriage with women was sanctioned as an exclusive privilege for Muhammad's Companions (*lā taṣluḥu al-mutʿatāni illā lanā khāṣṣatan*), which still indicts Islamic revelation for authorizing transactional sex-for-hire for its most revered generation. Furthermore, parallel narrations in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* (3416, 3417) refute the prophetic abrogation excuse by recording that the Companions continued contracting women for a mere "handful of dates or flour" (*bi-l-qabḍati mina al-tamri wa-l-daqīq*) throughout Muhammad's entire lifetime and Abū Bakr's caliphate until ʿUmar unilaterally banned it.

muslim:3428.note: Al-Rabīʿ b. Sabrah al-Juhanī reports from his father that Sabrah contracted a temporary marriage (*mutʿah al-nisāʾ*) with a woman in exchange for two red cloaks (*bi-burdayn aḥmarayn*) under Muhammad's prior authorization (muslim:3424, muslim:3425) before Muhammad forbade the practice at the Conquest of Mecca (AD 630). Although Sunni jurisprudence holds that Muhammad permanently abrogated *mutʿah* shortly thereafter (muslim:3430), his earlier prophetic sanction of short-term marriage for material goods contrasts with the biblical standard of lifelong covenant marriage ([Matthew 19:4-6](bible://mt/19/4), [Hebrews 13:4](bible://heb/13/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ الرَّبِيعِ بْنِ سَبْرَةَ الْجُهَنِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّهُ أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَهَى عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ زَمَانَ الْفَتْحِ مُتْعَةِ النِّسَاءِ وَأَنَّ أَبَاهُ كَانَ تَمَتَّعَ بِبُرْدَيْنِ أَحْمَرَيْنِ
problematic_excerpt.english: This hadith has been narrated on the authority of Rabi' b. Sabra that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) forbade to contract temporary marriage with women at the time of Victory, and that his father had contracted the marriage for two red cloaks

muslim:3428.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that this narration proves Islam's moral reform because Muhammad permanently prohibited temporary marriage at the Conquest of Mecca (*نَهَى عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ زَمَانَ الْفَتْحِ*) after only briefly tolerating it as a gradual legislative concession (*tadrīj*) for soldiers on campaign. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Sabra contracted and enjoyed the woman for two red cloaks (*كَانَ تَمَتَّعَ بِبُرْدَيْنِ أَحْمَرَيْنِ*), and the surrounding Sahih Muslim parallels (muslim:3419, muslim:3424, muslim:3425) record that Muhammad himself actively authorized this practice (*أَذِنَ لَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ*), proving that an allegedly final moral lawgiver explicitly sanctioned bartering clothing for short-term sexual access before reversing his own decree.

muslim:3429.note: 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubair condemns those who issue verdicts permitting temporary marriage (*mutʿah*) and threatens to stone the man (identified as Ibn 'Abbas) who defends and instructs an inquirer to practice it on the grounds that it was performed during Muhammad's lifetime. Ibn Abi 'Amrah counters that it was only an early concession for extreme necessity—like carrion, blood, and pork—before Allah prohibited it, and Sabrah recounts enjoying a woman of Banu 'Amir in temporary marriage for two red cloaks before Muhammad forbade it ([Quran 4:24](quran://4/24), [Matthew 19:4-6](bible://mt/19/4), [Hebrews 13:4](bible://heb/13/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ابْنُ شِهَابٍ فَأَخْبَرَنِي خَالِدُ بْنُ الْمُهَاجِرِ بْنِ سَيْفِ اللَّهِ أَنَّهُ بَيْنَا هُوَ جَالِسٌ عِنْدَ رَجُلٍ جَاءَهُ رَجُلٌ فَاسْتَفْتَاهُ فِي الْمُتْعَةِ فَأَمَرَهُ بِهَا فَقَالَ لَهُ ابْنُ أَبِي عَمْرَةَ الأَنْصَارِيُّ مَهْلاً ‏.‏ قَالَ مَا هِيَ وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ فُعِلَتْ فِي عَهْدِ إِمَامِ الْمُتَّقِينَ ‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي عَمْرَةَ إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ رُخْصَةً فِي أَوَّلِ الإِسْلاَمِ لِمَنِ اضْطُرَّ إِلَيْهَا كَالْمَيْتَةِ وَالدَّمِ وَلَحْمِ الْخِنْزِيرِ ثُمَّ أَحْكَمَ اللَّهُ الدِّينَ وَنَهَى عَنْهَا ‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ شِهَابٍ وَأَخْبَرَنِي رَبِيعُ بْنُ سَبْرَةَ الْجُهَنِيُّ أَنَّ أَبَاهُ قَالَ قَدْ كُنْتُ اسْتَمْتَعْتُ فِي عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم امْرَأَةً مِنْ بَنِي عَامِرٍ بِبُرْدَيْنِ أَحْمَرَيْنِ ثُمَّ نَهَانَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنِ الْمُتْعَةِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Ibn Shihab said. Khalid b. Muhajir b. Saifullah informed me: While I was sitting in the company of a person, a person came to him and he asked for a religious verdict about Mut'a and he permitted him to do it. Ibn Abu 'Amrah al-Ansari (Allah be pleased with him) said to him: Be gentle. It was permitted in- the early days of Islam, (for one) who was driven to it under the stress of necessity just as (the eating of) carrion and the blood and flesh of swine and then Allah intensified (the commands of) His religion and prohibited it (altogether). Ibn Shihab reported: Rabi' b. Sabra told me that his father (Sabra) said: I contracted temporary marriage with a woman of Banu 'Amir for two cloaks during the lifetime of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) ; then he forbade us to do Mut'a.

muslim:3429.literal_translation: Ibn Shihab said: Khalid b. al-Muhajir b. Saifullah informed me that while he was sitting with a man [Ibn 'Abbas], a man came to him and asked him for a legal verdict concerning Mut'ah, so he instructed him to do it. Ibn Abi 'Amrah al-Ansari said to him: 'Wait!' He [Ibn 'Abbas] said: 'What is wrong with it? By Allah, it was certainly practiced in the era of the Leader of the Pious [Muhammad]!' Ibn Abi 'Amrah said: 'It was a concession in the beginning of Islam for one who was driven by necessity to it, like carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine, then Allah perfected the religion and forbade it.' Ibn Shihab said: And Rabi' b. Sabrah al-Juhani informed me that his father said: 'I had enjoyed [in temporary marriage] a woman of Banu 'Amir for two red cloaks during the era of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) forbade us from Mut'ah.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: قَالَ مَا هِيَ وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ فُعِلَتْ فِي عَهْدِ إِمَامِ الْمُتَّقِينَ ‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي عَمْرَةَ
translation_issue.published_rendering: [omitted]
translation_issue.literal_meaning: He [Ibn 'Abbas] said: 'What is wrong with it? By Allah, it was certainly practiced in the era of the Leader of the Pious!' Ibn Abi 'Amrah said:
translation_issue.explanation: The published translation completely omits Ibn 'Abbas's second oath defending the lawfulness of temporary marriage on the basis of Muhammad's practice, while also softening 'fa-amarahu biha' ('he instructed/commanded him to do it') to 'he permitted him to do it'.

muslim:3429.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that *mutʿah* (temporary marriage) was merely a brief, gradualist concession (*rukhṣah*) for soldiers facing severe hardship on early military campaigns before being permanently abrogated, and that Ibn ʿAbbās only permitted it under extreme necessity. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Sabrah 'enjoyed a woman of Banū ʿĀmir for two red cloaks during the era of Allah's Messenger' (*istamtaʿtu fī ʿahdi rasūli llāhi ... imraʾatan min banī ʿāmirin bi-burdayni aḥmarayni*), while Ibn Abī ʿAmrah himself equated this Prophetic allowance to the impure desperation of consuming 'carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine' (*ka-l-maytati wa-l-dami wa-laḥmi l-khinzīr*). Furthermore, the Arabic records that Muhammad's own cousin Ibn ʿAbbās actively instructed a questioner to practice it (*fa-amarahu bihā*) and swore a second oath that it was done under the 'Leader of the Pious'—a clause entirely omitted from the published English translation—proving that Muhammad personally sanctioned transactional sexual exploitation whenever his men desired women.

bukhari:6042.note: Muhammad asks how a man can beat his wife like a stallion camel—or flog her like a slave—when he may subsequently embrace her. Rather than prohibiting disciplinary wife-beating ([Quran 4:34](quran://4/34)), this statement discourages only severe beatings on the grounds of subsequent marital intimacy.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَقَالَ ‏"‏ بِمَ يَضْرِبُ أَحَدُكُمُ امْرَأَتَهُ ضَرْبَ الْفَحْلِ، ثُمَّ لَعَلَّهُ يُعَانِقُهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ وَقَالَ الثَّوْرِيُّ وَوُهَيْبٌ وَأَبُو مُعَاوِيَةَ عَنْ هِشَامٍ ‏"‏ جَلْدَ الْعَبْدِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: and said, "How does anyone of you beat his wife as he beats the stallion camel and then he may embrace (sleep with) her?" And Hisham said, "As he beats his slave

bukhari:6042.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration proves Muhammad condemned domestic violence, or cite Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* to claim it mercifully restricts [Quran 4:34](quran://4/34) by prohibiting severe beatings. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad only discouraged beating a wife to the extreme degree of a stallion camel (`ضَرْبَ الْفَحْلِ`, *ḍarb al-faḥl*) or flogging a slave (`جَلْدَ الْعَبْدِ`, *jald al-ʿabd*), which Ibn Hajar himself notes merely regulates the *severity* of the beating rather than abolishing the Quranic command to strike wives (`وَاضْرِبُوهُنَّ`, *wa-ḍribūhunna*). Furthermore, the Prophet grounds this restraint not in a woman's inherent dignity, but in the pragmatic awkwardness of a husband brutally whipping his wife and then wanting to embrace her in bed (`ثُمَّ لَعَلَّهُ يُعَانِقُهَا`, *thumma laʿallahu yuʿāniquhā*)—while casually treating the flogging of slaves as an unobjectionable baseline.

muslim:2048.note: During an Eid sermon, Muhammad commands the assembled women to give alms because most of them are the firewood of Hell due to complaining frequently and showing ingratitude toward their husbands (*kufr al-ʿashīr*), prompting them to cast their earrings and rings into Bilāl's garment ([Galatians 3:28](bible://gal/3/28), [1 Peter 3:7](bible://1pt/3/7)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ مَضَى حَتَّى أَتَى النِّسَاءَ فَوَعَظَهُنَّ وَذَكَّرَهُنَّ فَقَالَ تَصَدَّقْنَ فَإِنَّ أَكْثَرَكُنَّ حَطَبُ جَهَنَّمَ فَقَامَتْ امْرَأَةٌ مِنْ سِطَةِ النِّسَاءِ سَفْعَاءُ الْخَدَّيْنِ فَقَالَتْ لِمَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ لِأَنَّكُنَّ تُكْثِرْنَ الشَّكَاةَ وَتَكْفُرْنَ الْعَشِيرَ قَالَ فَجَعَلْنَ يَتَصَدَّقْنَ مِنْ حُلِيِّهِنَّ يُلْقِينَ فِي ثَوْبِ بِلَالٍ مِنْ أَقْرِطَتِهِنَّ وَخَوَاتِمِهِنَّ
problematic_excerpt.english: He then walked on till he came to the women and preached to them and admonished them, and asked them to give alms, for most of them are the fuel for Hell. A woman having a dark spot on the cheek stood up and said: Why is it so, Messenger of Allah? He said: For you grumble often and show ingratitude to your spouse. And then they began to give alms out of their ornaments such as their earrings and rings which they threw on to the cloth of Bilal

muslim:2048.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this warning is merely a rhetorical exhortation to charity against general moral failings, or cite commentators like Ibn Ḥajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) to claim women form the majority of Hell simply because they outnumber men in the total human population. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "fa-inna aktharakunna ḥaṭabu jahannam" ("for indeed most of you women are the firewood of Hell") and directly attributes their damnation not to demographics, but specifically to domestic grievances—complaining often (tukthirna al-shakāh) and showing ingratitude to husbands (takfurna al-ʿashīr). Furthermore, the parallel Eid sermon narration in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 304 immediately pairs this threat with Muhammad declaring women inherently "deficient in intelligence and religion" (nāqiṣāt ʿaqlin wa-dīn), proving the text weaponizes eternal hellfire to enforce female subjugation to husbands.

muslim:2109.note: Following the solar eclipse prayer, Muhammad declares that he was shown Hellfire and observed that women constitute the majority of its inhabitants due to their ingratitude toward their husbands (kufr al-'ashir) and denial of lifelong kindness when displeased. Classical commentators such as al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar affirm this literal majority and classify a wife's ingratitude toward her husband as a major sin (kabirah) meriting punishment in the Fire ([Galatians 3:28](bible://gal/3/28), [1 Peter 3:7](bible://1pt/3/7)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَرَأَيْتُ النَّارَ فَلَمْ أَرَ كَالْيَوْمِ مَنْظَرًا قَطُّ وَرَأَيْتُ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِهَا النِّسَاءَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا بِمَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ بِكُفْرِهِنَّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قِيلَ أَيَكْفُرْنَ بِاللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ بِكُفْرِ الْعَشِيرِ وَبِكُفْرِ الإِحْسَانِ لَوْ أَحْسَنْتَ إِلَى إِحْدَاهُنَّ الدَّهْرَ ثُمَّ رَأَتْ مِنْكَ شَيْئًا قَالَتْ مَا رَأَيْتُ مِنْكَ خَيْرًا قَطُّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I saw Hell also. No such (abominable) sight have I ever seen as that which I saw today; and I observed that most of its inhabitants were women. They said: Messenger of Allah, on what account is it so? He said: For their ingratitude or disbelief (bi-kufraihinna). It was said: Do they disbelieve in Allah? He said: (Not for their disbelief in God) but for their ingratitude to their husbands and ingratitude to kindness. If you were to treat one of them kindly for ever, but if she later saw anything (displeasing) in you, she would say: I have never seen any good in you

muslim:2109.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that women form the majority in Hell simply because they outnumber men in the total human population, or that Muhammad was merely issuing a rhetorical warning against the general human flaw of ingratitude (*kufr dūna kufr*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that when asked why (*bima yā Rasūl Allāh*) women constitute the majority of Hell's inhabitants, Muhammad attributed it not to demographics, but directly to wives' ungratefulness toward their husbands (*bi-kufri al-ʿashīr wa-bi-kufri al-iḥsān*). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations completely dismantle the demographic excuse by tying this exact condemnation to women's alleged 'deficiency in intelligence and religion' (bukhari:304; muslim:241) and explicitly declaring that women are the smallest minority in Paradise (*inna aqalla sākinī al-jannati al-nisāʾ*, muslim:6942).

bukhari:6546.note: Muhammad declares that upon looking into Paradise he saw that most of its inhabitants were the poor, and upon looking into the Fire he saw that most of its inhabitants were women. In related Sahih al-Bukhari reports (bukhari:29, bukhari:304), he explains that women form the majority of Hell's inhabitants due to their ingratitude toward their husbands and their deficiency in intelligence and religion.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: اطَّلَعْتُ فِي الْجَنَّةِ فَرَأَيْتُ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِهَا الْفُقَرَاءَ وَاطَّلَعْتُ فِي النَّارِ فَرَأَيْتُ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِهَا النِّسَاءَ
problematic_excerpt.english: I looked into paradise and saw that the majority of its people were the poor, and I looked into the Fire and found that the majority of its people were women

bukhari:6546.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration merely reflects demographic reality—claiming women simply outnumber men in the total human population—or that it serves as a benign moral warning against marital ingratitude rather than an indictment of female nature (citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states without demographic qualification that the majority of Hell's dwellers are women (*akthara ahlihā al-nisā'*), and parallel *Ṣaḥīḥ* narrations (`bukhari:29`, `bukhari:304`) record Muhammad directly linking their consignment to the Fire both to ungratefulness toward husbands (*yakfurna al-'ashīr*) and to women's innate 'deficiency in intelligence and religion' (*nāqiṣāti 'aqlin wa-dīn*). This collapses the demographic excuse by rooting women's damnation directly in Islamic legal inferiority (Quran 2:282), female biology (menstruation), and domestic subordination.

bukhari:6547.note: Muhammad declares that when he stood at the gate of Paradise, the majority of those who had entered it were the poor while the wealthy were detained, and when he stood at the gate of the Fire, the majority of those who had entered it were women.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَقُمْتُ عَلَى باب النَّارِ فَإِذَا عَامَّةُ مَنْ دَخَلَهَا النِّسَاءُ
problematic_excerpt.english: And I stood at the gate of the Fire and found that the majority of the people entering it were women

bukhari:6547.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that women form the majority in Hell simply because women outnumber men in the total human population (a harmonization discussed in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*), or that the vision merely warns against specific behavioral sins rather than inherent female inferiority. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the overwhelming mass of those entering the Fire were women (*fa-idhā ʿāmmatu man dakhalahā al-nisāʾ*), while parallel Sahih narrations demolish the demographic excuse by stating that women are simultaneously the smallest minority of the inhabitants of Paradise (*inna aqalla sākinī al-jannati al-nisāʾ*, *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2738a). Furthermore, Muhammad directly links women's predominance in Hell to ungratefulness toward their husbands and an innate 'deficiency in intelligence and religion' (*nāqiṣāti ʿaqlin wa-dīn*, *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 29 and 304), grounding their condemnation in essentialized female deficiency.

muslim:3541.note: Muhammad declares that if a man invites his wife to his bed and she does not come to him, and he spends the night angry with her, the angels curse her until morning ([Quran 4:34](quran://4/34), [1 Corinthians 7:4](bible://1cor/7/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ إِذَا دَعَا الرَّجُلُ امْرَأَتَهُ إِلَى فِرَاشِهِ فَلَمْ تَأْتِهِ فَبَاتَ غَضْبَانَ عَلَيْهَا لَعَنَتْهَا الْمَلاَئِكَةُ حَتَّى تُصْبِحَ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: When a man invites his wife to his bed and she does not come, and he (the husband) spends the sight being angry with her, the angels curse her until morning

muslim:3541.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this warning only applies when a wife maliciously weaponizes sexual refusal without a valid medical or religious excuse (*ʿudhr sharʿī*), claiming that marital intimacy in Islam is a balanced, mutual obligation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the angelic curse (*laʿanathā al-malāʾikatu*) is triggered unilaterally by the husband's summons and anger (*idhā daʿā al-rajulu imraʾatahu ilā firāshihi fa-lam taʾtihi fa-bāta ghaḍbāna ʿalayhā*), whereas no Hadith ever curses a husband for refusing his wife—in fact, Quran 4:34 explicitly commands husbands to abandon their wives' beds (*wahjurūhunna fī al-maḍājiʿ*) as a disciplinary punishment. Furthermore, Imam al-Nawawī confirms in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* that outside of menstruation or physical illness, a wife is strictly forbidden from refusing her husband's demand regardless of her own lack of desire, codifying unilateral sexual compliance under threat of divine wrath.

muslim:3531.note: When asked whether a thrice-divorced woman who married and was divorced by a second man before consummation may remarry her first husband, Muhammad decrees that she cannot do so until the second husband has 'tasted her sweetness' (*'usaylah*) through actual sexual intercourse ([Quran 2:230](quran://2/230), bukhari:5260). Mandating sexual consummation with an intervening husband as a prerequisite for reconciling with the first husband directly inverts the law in [Deuteronomy 24:1](bible://dt/24/1), which forbids a man from remarrying a former wife after she has married another man.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: طَلَّقَ رَجُلٌ امْرَأَتَهُ ثَلاَثًا فَتَزَوَّجَهَا رَجُلٌ ثُمَّ طَلَّقَهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ بِهَا فَأَرَادَ زَوْجُهَا الأَوَّلُ أَنْ يَتَزَوَّجَهَا فَسُئِلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ لاَ حَتَّى يَذُوقَ الآخِرُ مِنْ عُسَيْلَتِهَا مَا ذَاقَ الأَوَّلُ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A person divorced his wife by three pronouncements; then another person married her and he also divorced her without having sexual intercourse with her. Then the first husband of her intended to remarry her. It was about such a case that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was asked, whereupon he said: No, until the second one has tasted her sweetness as the first one had tasted
