Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) called for them and divided them into three sections, cast lots amongst them, and set two free and kept four in slavery; and he (the Holy Prophet) spoke severely of him

muslim:4335.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islam prioritized the gradual abolition of slavery through voluntary emancipation, and that Muhammad only intervened here to protect the financial inheritance of the dying man's heirs since he owned no other property (لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ مَالٌ غَيْرُهُمْ). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that after the man emancipated his six slaves (أَعْتَقَ سِتَّةَ مَمْلُوكِينَ لَهُ), Muhammad summoned them, divided them into three sections (فَجَزَّأَهُمْ أَثْلاَثًا), cast lots among them (ثُمَّ أَقْرَعَ بَيْنَهُمْ), freed two, and actively returned four to slavery (فَأَعْتَقَ اثْنَيْنِ وَأَرَقَّ أَرْبَعَةً). Rather than praising the man for freeing his slaves, Muhammad spoke severely of him (وَقَالَ لَهُ قَوْلاً شَدِيدًا) and prioritized property claims (مَالٌ) over the freedom of four already-emancipated human beings.

muslim:4339.note: After a man from the Ansar who had no other property declared his slave free upon his death, Muhammad annulled the post-mortem manumission by selling the Coptic slave to Ibn al-Nahham, and he died in the first year of Ibn al-Zubair's rule.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: دَبَّرَ رَجُلٌ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ غُلاَمًا لَهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ مَالٌ غَيْرُهُ فَبَاعَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏ قَالَ جَابِرٌ فَاشْتَرَاهُ ابْنُ النَّحَّامِ عَبْدًا قِبْطِيًّا مَاتَ عَامَ أَوَّلَ فِي إِمَارَةِ ابْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Jabir is reported to have said:A person amongst the Ansar who had no other property declared a slave free after his death. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) sold him, and Ibn al-Nahham bought him and he was a Coptic slave (who) died in the first year of the Caliphate of Ibn Zubair

muslim:4339.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islam systematically encouraged manumission and only intervened here to protect the financial welfare of an impoverished owner who had no other property (*lam yakun lahu mālun ghayruhu*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that after the Ansari man declared his slave free upon his death (*dabbara rajulun min al-Anṣār ghulāman lahu*), Muhammad personally revoked that emancipation by selling him (*fa-bāʿahu Rasūl Allāh*) to Ibn al-Nahham. By prioritizing the master's estate over the freedom already pledged to the Coptic slave (*ʿabdan qibṭiyyan*), the ruling treated a human being strictly as liquidatable property and consigned him to remain a slave until he died during the rule of Ibn al-Zubair (*māta ʿāma awwala fī imārat Ibn al-Zubayr*), contrasting with the New Testament call to receive a bondservant no longer as a slave but as a beloved brother ([Philemon 1:16](bible://phlm/1/16)).

bukhari:6716.note: When an Ansari man who owned no other property declared that his Coptic slave would be freed upon his death (*mudabbar*), Muhammad overrode the promised manumission by offering the slave for sale and selling him to Nu'aym ibn al-Nahham for eight hundred dirhams, with Jabir noting that the enslaved man died that first year.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَجُلاً، مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ دَبَّرَ مَمْلُوكًا لَهُ، وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ مَالٌ غَيْرُهُ فَبَلَغَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ مَنْ يَشْتَرِيهِ مِنِّي ‏"‏‏.‏ فَاشْتَرَاهُ نُعَيْمُ بْنُ النَّحَّامِ بِثَمَانِمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ، فَسَمِعْتُ جَابِرَ بْنَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ يَقُولُ عَبْدًا قِبْطِيًّا مَاتَ عَامَ أَوَّلَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: An Ansari man made his slave a Mudabbar and he had no other property than him. When the Prophet (ﷺ) heard of that, he said (to his companions), "Who wants to buy him (i.e., the slave) for me?" Nu'aim bin An-Nahham bought him for eight hundred Dirhams. I heard Jabir saying, "That was a coptic slave who died in the same year

bukhari:6716.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islam systematically encouraged manumission to gradually abolish slavery, and that Muhammad only intervened here out of financial necessity because the impoverished owner had no other assets (*wa-lam yakun lahu mālun ghayruhu*) or needed to settle debts (as discussed by Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that after the owner voluntarily granted his Coptic slave post-mortem freedom (*dabbara mamlūkan lahu*), Muhammad personally revoked the emancipation and auctioned the man off as chattel (*man yashtarīhi minnī*—"Who will buy him from me?") for eight hundred dirhams. Rather than relieving the poor Ansari from the public treasury or asking wealthy companions to donate charity while preserving the slave's freedom, Muhammad treated a human being purely as liquidable property (*māl*), resulting in the Coptic slave dying in bondage that very year (*ʿabdan qibṭiyyan māta ʿāma awwala*).

muslim:2313.note: When a man from Banu 'Udhra with no other property arranged for his slave to be freed upon his death (*mudabbar*), Muhammad overturned the posthumous manumission, sold the enslaved man to Nu'aym ibn 'Abdullah al-'Adawi for 800 dirhams, and gave the proceeds to the master to spend on himself and his family first ([Exodus 21:16](bible://ex/21/16), [1 Timothy 1:10](bible://1tm/1/10)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَعْتَقَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ بَنِي عُذْرَةَ عَبْدًا لَهُ عَنْ دُبُرٍ، فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَلَكَ مَالٌ غَيْرُهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لاَ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَنْ يَشْتَرِيهِ مِنِّي ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَاشْتَرَاهُ نُعَيْمُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْعَدَوِيُّ بِثَمَانِمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ فَجَاءَ بِهَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَدَفَعَهَا إِلَيْهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ ابْدَأْ بِنَفْسِكَ فَتَصَدَّقْ عَلَيْهَا فَإِنْ فَضَلَ شَىْءٌ فَلأَهْلِكَ
problematic_excerpt.english: A person from the Banu 'Udhra set a slave free after his death. This news reached the Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon hhn). Upon this he said: Have you any property besides it? He said: No. Upon this he said: Who would buy (this slave) from me? Nulaim b. Abdullah bought it for eight hundred dirhams and (this amount was) brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who returned it to him (the owner), and then said: Start with your own self and spend it on yourself, and if anything is left, it should be spent on your family

muslim:2313.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islam systematically sought to phase out slavery by encouraging emancipation, claiming Muhammad merely prioritized financial responsibility toward one's dependents or, as some jurists cited in Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* suggested, sold only the slave's temporary labor rather than revoking his freedom. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad categorized the human being strictly as liquid property (*māl*—`أَلَكَ مَالٌ غَيْرُهُ`) and personally auctioned him off by asking, "Who will buy him from me?" (`مَنْ يَشْتَرِيهِ مِنِّي`), selling the man himself to Nu'aym ibn 'Abdullāh for 800 dirhams (`فَاشْتَرَاهُ... بِثَمَانِمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ`). As both Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) confirm, the full market price of 800 dirhams proves the slave's physical person (*raqabah*) was sold back into permanent chattel bondage, showing Muhammad actively nullified a voluntary manumission (`أَعْتَقَ... عَنْ دُبُرٍ`) so the master could spend the cash on himself first (`ابْدَأْ بِنَفْسِكَ`).

bukhari:6947.note: When an Ansari man with no other property promises his Coptic slave post-mortem emancipation (mudabbar), Muhammad overrides the arrangement to preserve the owner's financial solvency and personally sells the slave to Nu'aym ibn al-Nahham for 800 dirhams. Classical commentators like Ibn Hajar cite this transaction as the legal precedent permitting the sale of slaves promised freedom upon their master's death.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَجُلاً، مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ دَبَّرَ مَمْلُوكًا، وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ مَالٌ غَيْرُهُ، فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ مَنْ يَشْتَرِيهِ مِنِّي ‏"‏‏.‏ فَاشْتَرَاهُ نُعَيْمُ بْنُ النَّحَّامِ بِثَمَانِمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: A man from the Ansar made his slave, a Mudabbar. And apart from that slave he did not have any other property. This news reached Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and he said, "Who will buy that slave from me?" So Nu'aim bin An-Nahham bought him for 800 Dirham.

bukhari:6947.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islam sought to gradually abolish slavery and, citing Ibn Hajar’s Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī’s Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, claim Muhammad only intervened here out of financial prudence to prevent an indigent owner from falling into destitution or defaulting on debts. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the owner had already promised the slave post-mortem freedom (dabbara mamlūkan), yet Muhammad personally nullified this manumission and acted as a slave auctioneer—asking, 'Who will buy him from me?' (man yashtarīhi minnī)—resulting in the Coptic man being sold for 800 dirhams and dying in chattel bondage that very year (māta ʿāma awwala). Parallel Sahih narrations (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 2141; Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:2313) confirm that rather than using public funds to secure the man's liberty, Muhammad directly prioritized the master's financial liquidity over a human being's emancipation.

bukhari:7186.note: Upon learning that a companion with no other property had arranged to free his slave after his death (mudabbar), Muhammad revokes the promised post-mortem manumission, sells the slave for 800 dirhams, and sends the proceeds to the master (cf. bukhari:2141).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَجُلاً مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ أَعْتَقَ غُلاَمًا عَنْ دُبُرٍ، لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ مَالٌ غَيْرَهُ، فَبَاعَهُ بِثَمَانِمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: one of his companions had given the promise of freeing his slave after his death, but as he had no other property than that slave, the Prophet (ﷺ) sold that slave for 800 dirhams

bukhari:7186.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islam sought to phase out slavery by consistently prioritizing emancipation, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* to claim Muhammad only intervened here out of financial prudence because the impoverished owner had no other assets (*lam yakun lahu mālun ghayruhu*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that after the companion had already arranged the man's freedom upon death (*aʿtaqa ghulāman ʿan duburin*), Muhammad personally nullified that emancipation and sold the human being as liquid property for 800 dirhams (*fabāʿahu bithamānimiʾati dirhamin*). Instead of relieving the companion's poverty through communal charity while preserving the slave's promised liberty, Muhammad actively reversed a voluntary act of manumission and auctioned the man back into permanent chattel bondage (as further detailed in `bukhari:2141`).

muslim:2317.note: After Maimuna bint al-Harith emancipates a slave-girl (*walīdah*) and informs Muhammad, he tells her that giving the girl to her maternal uncles instead would have earned her a greater reward (cf. bukhari:2592, bukhari:2594). Classical commentators such as al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar explain from this report that gifting a slave to needy relatives to uphold kinship ties (*ṣilat al-raḥim*) carries a greater reward than manumission.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ مَيْمُونَةَ بِنْتِ الْحَارِثِ، أَنَّهَا أَعْتَقَتْ وَلِيدَةً فِي زَمَانِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَذَكَرَتْ ذَلِكَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ لَوْ أَعْطَيْتِهَا أَخْوَالَكِ كَانَ أَعْظَمَ لأَجْرِكِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Maimuna bint Harith reported that she set free a slave-girl during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and she made a mention of that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said:Had you gives her to your maternal uncles, you would have a greater reward

muslim:2317.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islam sought to gradually abolish slavery, citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim to claim that Maimuna's maternal uncles had a pressing need for a servant that made maintaining family ties (ṣilat al-raḥim) a higher priority in that specific instance. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that after Maimuna had already emancipated the slave-girl (aʿtaqat walīdatan), Muhammad corrected her by declaring, 'Had you given her to your maternal uncles, you would have had a greater reward' (law aʿṭaytihā akhwālaki kāna aʿẓama li-ajriki). By ruling that perpetuating a woman's chattel bondage as a family gift carries greater divine reward (aʿẓama li-ajriki) than setting her free, Muhammad directly inverted any abolitionist ethic and subordinated human liberty to the material convenience of extended relatives.

bukhari:2228.note: Anas ibn Malik reports that Safiyya bint Huyayy was among the war captives (saby) and first went to Dihya al-Kalbi before subsequently passing to Muhammad. Fuller parallel accounts (bukhari:371, bukhari:2235, muslim:3321) specify that after she was allotted to Dihya following the conquest of Khaybar in AD 628, Muhammad acquired her from him in exchange for other captives.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ فِي السَّبْىِ صَفِيَّةُ، فَصَارَتْ إِلَى دَحْيَةَ الْكَلْبِيِّ، ثُمَّ صَارَتْ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم
problematic_excerpt.english: Amongst the captives was Safiya. First she was given to Dihya Al-Kalbi and then to the Prophet

bukhari:2228.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that Muhammad rescued and honored Safiyya bint Huyayy by emancipating and marrying her as a noblewoman so she would not remain a subordinate captive under Dihya al-Kalbi. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that she was seized among the war captives (*fī al-sabyi*, فِي السَّبْىِ) and transferred as property from Dihya to Muhammad (فَصَارَتْ إِلَى دَحْيَةَ الْكَلْبِيِّ، ثُمَّ صَارَتْ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ), a transaction Al-Bukhari tellingly catalogs under the *Book of Sales and Trade* (*Kitāb al-Buyūʿ*). Parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:371, bukhari:2235) further confirm that Muhammad only requisitioned her after being informed of her beauty, purchasing her from Dihya in exchange for other captives and consummating the union after the Battle of Khaybar in AD 628 right after her husband and male relatives were killed.

bukhari:5085.note: When Muhammad consummated his union with Safiyya bint Huyayy between Khaybar and Medina, the Muslims questioned whether she was one of the Mothers of the Believers or a right-hand possession slave-concubine (*mā malakat yamīnuhu*), concluding that only the imposition of the veil (*ḥijāb*) would establish her as a wife rather than a concubine. Although he subsequently screened her with a veil upon departure, the immediately following narration (bukhari:5086) records that her prior captive status was resolved by counting her manumission itself as her marriage dowry.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَقَامَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَيْنَ خَيْبَرَ وَالْمَدِينَةِ ثَلاَثًا يُبْنَى عَلَيْهِ بِصَفِيَّةَ بِنْتِ حُيَىٍّ فَدَعَوْتُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ إِلَى وَلِيمَتِهِ فَمَا كَانَ فِيهَا مِنْ خُبْزٍ وَلاَ لَحْمٍ، أُمِرَ بِالأَنْطَاعِ فَأَلْقَى فِيهَا مِنَ التَّمْرِ وَالأَقِطِ وَالسَّمْنِ فَكَانَتْ وَلِيمَتَهُ، فَقَالَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ إِحْدَى أُمَّهَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَوْ مِمَّا مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُهُ، فَقَالُوا إِنْ حَجَبَهَا فَهْىَ مِنْ أُمَّهَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَحْجُبْهَا فَهْىَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُهُ، فَلَمَّا ارْتَحَلَ وَطَّى لَهَا خَلْفَهُ وَمَدَّ الْحِجَابَ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ النَّاسِ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) stayed for three days between Khaibar and Medina, and there he consummated his marriage to Safiyya bint Huyai. I invited the Muslims to the wedding banquet in which neither meat nor bread was offered. He ordered for leather dining-sheets to be spread, and dates, dried yoghurt and butter were laid on it, and that was the Prophet's wedding banquet. The Muslims wondered, "Is she (Saffiyya) considered as his wife or his slave girl?" Then they said, "If he orders her to veil herself, she will be one of the mothers of the Believers; but if he does not order her to veil herself, she will be a slave girl. So when the Prophet (ﷺ) proceeded from there, he spared her a space behind him (on his she-camel) and put a screening veil between her and the people

bukhari:5085.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad honored Safiyya bint Huyayy by emancipating her and elevating her to a noble wife ('Mother of the Believers') rather than keeping her in bondage. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that even after consummation (*yubnā ʿalayhi bi-Ṣafiyyah*) on the road from Khaybar, his companions openly debated whether she was a wife or a right-hand possession concubine (*mimmā malakat yamīnuhu*) based solely on whether he imposed the veil (*in ḥajabahā*). This casual calculation—alongside parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:4211`–`4213`) showing she was seized as war booty immediately after her family's execution with her manumission merely serving as her technical dowry—proves that sexual access to unveiled female captives was routine prophetic practice.

bukhari:5159.note: After Muhammad consummated his union with Safiyya bint Huyayy between Khaybar and Medina, the Muslims questioned whether she was one of the Mothers of the Believers (a wife) or a slave concubine ("what his right hand possessed," *mimmā malakat yamīnuhu*). They determined that her status depended on whether he veiled her, and recognized her as a wife when he drew a screen (*ḥijāb*) between her and the people upon departing.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَقَامَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بَيْنَ خَيْبَرَ وَالْمَدِينَةِ ثَلاَثًا يُبْنَى عَلَيْهِ بِصَفِيَّةَ بِنْتِ حُيَىٍّ فَدَعَوْتُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ إِلَى وَلِيمَتِهِ، فَمَا كَانَ فِيهَا مِنْ خُبْزٍ وَلاَ لَحْمٍ، أَمَرَ بِالأَنْطَاعِ فَأُلْقِيَ فِيهَا مِنَ التَّمْرِ وَالأَقِطِ وَالسَّمْنِ فَكَانَتْ وَلِيمَتَهُ، فَقَالَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ إِحْدَى أُمَّهَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَوْ مِمَّا مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُهُ فَقَالُوا إِنْ حَجَبَهَا فَهْىَ مِنْ أُمَّهَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَحْجُبْهَا فَهْىَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُهُ فَلَمَّا ارْتَحَلَ وَطَّى لَهَا خَلْفَهُ وَمَدَّ الْحِجَابَ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ النَّاسِ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) stayed for three days at a place between Khaibar and Medina, and there he consummated his marriage with Safiyya bint Huyay. I invited the Muslims to a banquet which included neither meat nor bread. The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered for the leather dining sheets to be spread, and then dates, dried yogurt and butter were provided over it, and that was the Walima (banquet) of the Prophet. The Muslims asked whether Safiyya would be considered as his wife or as a slave girl of what his right hands possessed. Then they said, "If the Prophet (ﷺ) screens her from the people, then she Is the Prophet's wife but if he does not screen her, then she is a slave girl." So when the Prophet (ﷺ) proceeded, he made a place for her (on the camel) behind him and screened her from people

bukhari:5159.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and `bukhari:5085`—that Muhammad honored Safiyya bint Huyayy by emancipating her and elevating her to a Mother of the Believers (*Ummahāt al-Mu'minīn*) rather than keeping her in bondage. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that even after Muhammad consummated his relationship with her (*yubnā 'alayhi bi-Ṣafiyya*) on the march from Khaybar and held a banquet, his own companions still did not know whether she was a wife or a right-hand possession slave concubine (*mimmā malakat yamīnuhu*) until they watched to see if he would screen her (*in ḥajabahā*) upon departure. This confirms that sexual access to war captives was so normalized and indistinguishable from marriage in practice—with her emancipation itself serving as her dowry (`bukhari:5085`)—that no public marriage contract, witnesses, or free consent was required prior to consummation.

bukhari:4350.note: Sent to Khalid to collect the fifth (khumus) of the war spoils, Ali performed a post-intercourse ritual bath (ghusl—after selecting a female captive from the khumus for himself, as stated verbatim in the fuller parallel report in bukhari:4346). When Buraida complained of this to Muhammad, Muhammad told him not to hate Ali and declared that Ali was entitled to even more than that from the khumus.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: بَعَثَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَلِيًّا إِلَى خَالِدٍ لِيَقْبِضَ الْخُمُسَ وَكُنْتُ أُبْغِضُ عَلِيًّا، وَقَدِ اغْتَسَلَ، فَقُلْتُ لِخَالِدٍ أَلاَ تَرَى إِلَى هَذَا فَلَمَّا قَدِمْنَا عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لَهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا بُرَيْدَةُ أَتُبْغِضُ عَلِيًّا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ تُبْغِضْهُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ فِي الْخُمُسِ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent `Ali to Khalid to bring the Khumus (of the booty) and I hated `Ali, and `Ali had taken a bath (after a sexual act with a slave-girl from the Khumus). I said to Khalid, "Don't you see this (i.e. `Ali)?" When we reached the Prophet (ﷺ) I mentioned that to him. He said, "O Buraida! Do you hate `Ali?" I said, "Yes." He said, "Do you hate him, for he deserves more than that from the Khumlus

bukhari:4350.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the Companions' objection was merely a procedural dispute over whether Ali had the authority to take from the unapportioned fifth (al-khumus) or whether he observed the waiting period (istibrā'), with Ibn Hajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī speculating that the captive was a virgin whom Ali lawfully claimed as the Prophet's deputy. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Ali had already performed the post-coital ritual bath (وَقَدِ اغْتَسَلَ) right on the expedition, and Muhammad's dismissal of the complaint—"Do not hate him, for he deserves more than that from the fifth" (فَإِنَّ لَهُ فِي الْخُمُسِ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ)—treats a newly captured woman strictly as a quantifiable unit of war booty for immediate sexual consumption.

bukhari:4802.note: At sunset, Muhammad asks Abu Dharr where the sun sets and declares that it travels until it prostrates beneath Allah's Throne, citing [Quran 36:38](quran://36/38) as the explanation of its course.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنْتُ مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي الْمَسْجِدِ عِنْدَ غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا أَبَا ذَرٍّ أَتَدْرِي أَيْنَ تَغْرُبُ الشَّمْسُ ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْتُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِنَّهَا تَذْهَبُ حَتَّى تَسْجُدَ تَحْتَ الْعَرْشِ، فَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى ‏{‏وَالشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَهَا ذَلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ‏}‏‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Once I was with the Prophet (ﷺ) in the mosque at the time of sunset. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "O Abu Dharr! Do you know where the sun sets?" I replied, "Allah and His Apostle know best." He said, "It goes and prostrates underneath (Allah's) Throne; and that is Allah's Statement:-- 'And the sun runs on its fixed course for a term (decreed). And that is the decree of All-Mighty, the All-Knowing

bukhari:4802.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the sun's prostration (*sujūd*) is merely a metaphor for its submission to cosmic laws, or that its 'running to a resting place' (*tajrī li-mustaqarrin lahā* in Quran 36:38) miraculously describes the modern astronomical concept of the solar apex. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that this occurs specifically at sunset (*ʿinda ghurūbi al-shams*) in direct answer to 'where does the sun set?' (*ayna taghrubu al-shams*), declaring that 'it goes until it prostrates beneath the Throne' (*tadhhabu ḥattā tasjuda taḥta al-ʿarsh*). Furthermore, the parallel narration in bukhari:3199 confirms this is a literal, daily geocentric transit in which the sun must ask permission after setting to rise again until it is eventually ordered to 'return whence you came' to rise from the west—a real, physical prostration (*sujūd ḥaqīqī*) explicitly affirmed against allegorical reinterpretation by both Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) and Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*).

bukhari:3938.note: Answering 'Abdullāh ibn Salām's test of prophethood with information he states Gabriel just revealed to him, Muhammad declares that a child resembles the father if the man's fluid precedes the woman's fluid, and resembles the mother if the woman's fluid precedes the man's.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَأَمَّا الْوَلَدُ، فَإِذَا سَبَقَ مَاءُ الرَّجُلِ مَاءَ الْمَرْأَةِ نَزَعَ الْوَلَدَ، وَإِذَا سَبَقَ مَاءُ الْمَرْأَةِ مَاءَ الرَّجُلِ نَزَعَتِ الْوَلَدَ
problematic_excerpt.english: As for the child, if the man's discharge proceeds the woman's discharge, the child attracts the similarity to the man, and if the woman's discharge proceeds the man's, then the child attracts the similarity to the woman.

bukhari:3938.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that mā' al-mar'ah ('the woman's fluid') refers to the female ovum and that sabaqa ('precedes')—alongside 'alā ('prevails') in parallel narrations—miraculously describes dominant and recessive genetic alleles, while classical commentators like Ibn Hajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī attempt to harmonize the texts by claiming resemblance depends on which partner's fluid is discharged first or in greater volume. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states idhā sabaqa mā'u al-rajuli mā'a al-mar'ati naza'a al-walada ('if the man's fluid precedes the woman's fluid, he draws the child in resemblance'), making inherited physical traits strictly contingent on which partner climaxes first during intercourse. Parallel Sahih narrations (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 130, Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:710–muslim:315) confirm that mā' al-mar'ah is a visible 'thin, yellow fluid' (raqīqun aṣfar) discharged during female orgasm or nocturnal emission (iḥtilām), proving that what Muhammad explicitly claimed Gabriel had just revealed to him (akhbaranī bihi Jibrīlu ānifan) is merely 2nd-century AD Galenic two-seed superstition rather than genetics.

bukhari:5717.note: Muhammad declares that there is no disease contagion (*lā 'adwā*) and counters a Bedouin's observation of mange spreading among camels by asking who infected the first camel. Elsewhere, he commands quarantining sick camels and fleeing from lepers (bukhari:5707, bukhari:5771), a discrepancy over which Abu Huraira's listeners later confronted him (bukhari:5771).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ عَدْوَى وَلاَ صَفَرَ وَلاَ هَامَةَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ أَعْرَابِيٌّ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَمَا بَالُ إِبِلِي تَكُونُ فِي الرَّمْلِ كَأَنَّهَا الظِّبَاءُ فَيَأْتِي الْبَعِيرُ الأَجْرَبُ فَيَدْخُلُ بَيْنَهَا فَيُجْرِبُهَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ فَمَنْ أَعْدَى الأَوَّلَ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, 'There is no 'Adwa (no disease is conveyed from the sick to the healthy without Allah's permission), nor Safar, nor Hama." A bedouin stood up and said, "Then what about my camels? They are like deer on the sand, but when a mangy camel comes and mixes with them, they all get infected with mangy." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Then who conveyed the (mange) disease to the first one?

bukhari:5717.literal_translation: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, 'There is no contagion, nor Safar, nor Hama.' A bedouin stood up and said, 'Then what about my camels? They are like deer on the sand, but when a mangy camel comes and mixes with them, they all get infected with mange.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'Then who infected the first one?'

translation_issue.arabic_term: لاَ عَدْوَى
translation_issue.published_rendering: There is no 'Adwa (no disease is conveyed from the sick to the healthy without Allah's permission)
translation_issue.literal_meaning: There is no contagion
translation_issue.explanation: The translator interpolates a theological qualification ('without Allah's permission') to soften Muhammad's categorical denial of contagious disease transmission.

bukhari:5717.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as claimed in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, Muhammad was merely refuting the pre-Islamic belief that diseases transmit autonomously without Allah's permission, citing quarantine commands in `bukhari:5707` and `bukhari:5771` to claim he affirmed biological infection. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *lā 'adwā* ("there is no contagion") as an unqualified categorical negation, and when the Bedouin points to empirical mange transmission (*fayujribuhā*), Muhammad dismisses physical transmission altogether by asking, *faman a'dā al-awwal* ("Then who infected the first one?"). Furthermore, `bukhari:5771` records that the contradiction between *lā 'adwā* and Muhammad's quarantine orders was so glaring that Abu Huraira later denied ever narrating the former, proving the earliest companions understood the statement as a literal denial of contagion rather than a theological qualification.

muslim:6723.note: Muhammad declares that a human embryo is collected in the womb for 40 days, becomes a blood clot (*'alaqah*) for a like period of 40 days, and then becomes a chewed lump of flesh (*mudghah*) for another 40 days before an angel breathes the spirit into it at day 120 ([Quran 22:5](quran://22/5), [Quran 23:14](quran://23/14); cf. bukhari:3332, bukhari:7454), whereas muslim:6725 places the angel's arrival at 40 or 45 nights. In reality, a human embryo never develops from a blood clot and completes organogenesis by day 56 rather than remaining a clot and an undifferentiated lump of flesh through day 120.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُوَ الصَّادِقُ الْمَصْدُوقُ ‏ "‏ إِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ يُجْمَعُ خَلْقُهُ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا ثُمَّ يَكُونُ فِي ذَلِكَ عَلَقَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ ثُمَّ يَكُونُ فِي ذَلِكَ مُضْغَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ ثُمَّ يُرْسَلُ الْمَلَكُ فَيَنْفُخُ فِيهِ الرُّوحَ وَيُؤْمَرُ بِأَرْبَعِ كَلِمَاتٍ بِكَتْبِ رِزْقِهِ وَأَجَلِهِ وَعَمَلِهِ وَشَقِيٌّ أَوْ سَعِيدٌ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) who is the most truthful (of the human beings) and his being truthful (is a fact) said:Verily your creation is on this wise. The constituents of one of you are collected for forty days in his mother's womb in the form of blood, after which it becomes a clot of blood in another period of forty days. Then it becomes a lump of flesh and forty days later Allah sends His angel to it with instructions concerning four things, so the angel writes down his livelihood, his death, his deeds, his fortune and misfortune.

muslim:6723.literal_translation: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he is the truthful, the believed, told us: 'Verily the creation of one of you is brought together in his mother's belly for forty days, then in that period he becomes a blood clot for a like period [forty days], then in that period he becomes a chewed lump of flesh for a like period [forty days]; then the angel is sent and breathes the spirit into him, and is commanded with four words: to write down his provision, his lifespan, his deeds, and whether he is wretched [damned] or blessed [saved].'

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَيَنْفُخُ فِيهِ الرُّوحَ
translation_issue.published_rendering: [omitted]
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and he breathes the spirit/soul into it
translation_issue.explanation: The published English translation completely omits the clause stating that the angel breathes the spirit/soul into the fetus after the third forty-day period (day 120).

muslim:6723.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that all three embryonic stages occur within a single forty-day period rather than totaling 120 days, and redefine *'alaqah* as a clinging substance rather than a blood clot. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *thumma yakūnu fī dhālika 'alaqatan mithla dhālika thumma yakūnu fī dhālika muḍghatan mithla dhālika* ('then in that [belly] he becomes a blood clot for a like period, then in that he becomes a chewed lump of flesh for a like period'), using the sequential conjunction *thumma* ('then') and the repeated phrase *mithla dhālika* ('like that [forty-day period]') to establish three consecutive forty-day stages before the angel breathes the spirit into the fetus (*fayanfukhu fīhi al-rūḥ*). Furthermore, the published English translation's complete omission of *fayanfukhu fīhi al-rūḥ* ('and breathes the spirit into it') confirms that the text places ensoulment after the third forty-day interval at day 120, matching the parallel narrations in `bukhari:3208`, `bukhari:6594`, and `bukhari:7454`.

muslim:6723.note: Muhammad declares that an angel is commanded in the womb to write down a fetus's provision, lifespan, deeds, and whether he is wretched (damned, *shaqī*) or blessed (saved, *sa'īd*) (cf. bukhari:3208, bukhari:6594, muslim:6725). Consequently, a person may perform the deeds of the people of Paradise until only a cubit remains between him and it, at which point the pre-written decree (*al-kitāb*) overtakes him so that he performs the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ يُرْسَلُ الْمَلَكُ فَيَنْفُخُ فِيهِ الرُّوحَ وَيُؤْمَرُ بِأَرْبَعِ كَلِمَاتٍ بِكَتْبِ رِزْقِهِ وَأَجَلِهِ وَعَمَلِهِ وَشَقِيٌّ أَوْ سَعِيدٌ فَوَالَّذِي لاَ إِلَهَ غَيْرُهُ إِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ لَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ حَتَّى مَا يَكُونَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهَا إِلاَّ ذِرَاعٌ فَيَسْبِقُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ فَيَدْخُلُهَا وَإِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ لَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ حَتَّى مَا يَكُونَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهَا إِلاَّ ذِرَاعٌ فَيَسْبِقُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ فَيَدْخُلُهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Then it becomes a lump of flesh and forty days later Allah sends His angel to it with instructions concerning four things, so the angel writes down his livelihood, his death, his deeds, his fortune and misfortune. By Him, besides Whom there is no god, that one amongst you acts like the people deserving Paradise until between him and Paradise there remains but the distance of a cubit, when suddenly the writing of destiny overcomes him and he begins to act like the denizens of Hell and thus enters Hell, and another one acts in the way of the denizens of Hell, until there remains between him and Hell a distance of a cubit that the writing of destiny overcomes him and then he begins to act like the people of Paradise and enters Paradise

muslim:6723.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the angel's recording in the womb merely reflects divine foreknowledge of free human choices, and that the person who turns to evil at the end of life was only outwardly pretending to be righteous before people. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *fayasbiqu 'alayhi al-kitābu faya'malu bi-'amali ahli al-nāri fayadkhuluhā* ('then the writing [decree] overtakes him, so he performs the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it'), making the pre-written decree (*al-kitāb*) the active subject that overtakes the individual and causes his final actions via the resultative particle *fa-* ('so'). Furthermore, this narration makes no mention of hypocrisy or mere outward appearance, stating unconditionally that the angel is commanded in the womb to write the fetus's deeds and whether he is damned or saved (*wa-'amalihi wa-shaqīyun aw sa'īd*), as paralleled in `bukhari:3208`, `bukhari:6594`, and `muslim:6725`.

muslim:7149.note: Muhammad declares that the inhabitants of Paradise will share the physical stature of their father Adam at sixty cubits (approximately 90 feet) tall into the sky (bukhari:3326, bukhari:6227). This asserted human stature contradicts both biomechanical scaling limits and the paleoanthropological record.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّ أَوَّلَ زُمْرَةٍ يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ عَلَى صُورَةِ الْقَمَرِ لَيْلَةَ الْبَدْرِ وَالَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ عَلَى أَشَدِّ كَوْكَبٍ دُرِّيٍّ فِي السَّمَاءِ إِضَاءَةً لاَ يَبُولُونَ وَلاَ يَتَغَوَّطُونَ وَلاَ يَمْتَخِطُونَ وَلاَ يَتْفُلُونَ أَمْشَاطُهُمُ الذَّهَبُ وَرَشْحُهُمُ الْمِسْكُ وَمَجَامِرُهُمُ الأَلُوَّةُ وَأَزْوَاجُهُمُ الْحُورُ الْعِينُ أَخْلاَقُهُمْ عَلَى خُلُقِ رَجُلٍ وَاحِدٍ عَلَى صُورَةِ أَبِيهِمْ آدَمَ سِتُّونَ ذِرَاعًا فِي السَّمَاءِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said:The (members of the) first group which would get into Paradise will have their faces as bright as stars in the sky. They would neither pass water, nor void excrement, nor will they suffer from catarrh, nor will they spit, and their combs would be made of gold, and their sweat will be musk, the fuel of their brazier will be aloes, and their wives will be large-eyed maidens and their form would be alike as one single person after the form of their father (Adam) sixty cubits tall

muslim:7149.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the measurement of sixty cubits applies only to the resurrected bodies of believers in the hereafter, or that Adam possessed this stature solely while in a celestial realm prior to his earthly existence. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the inhabitants of Paradise are modeled "upon the form of their father Adam, sixty cubits into the sky" (*ʿalā ṣūrati abīhim Ādama sittūna dhirāʿan fī al-samāʾ*), which directly identifies sixty cubits as the defining physical stature of Adam himself alongside parallel narrations in `bukhari:3326` and `bukhari:6227`.

muslim:7149.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
muslim:7149.note: Muhammad declares that the first group to enter Paradise will shine like the full moon, neither urinate, defecate, blow their noses, nor spit, and possess golden combs, musk sweat, aloes-wood braziers, and large-eyed celestial maidens (*al-ḥūr al-ʿīn*) as wives ([Quran 44:54](quran://44/54)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّ أَوَّلَ زُمْرَةٍ يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ عَلَى صُورَةِ الْقَمَرِ لَيْلَةَ الْبَدْرِ وَالَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ عَلَى أَشَدِّ كَوْكَبٍ دُرِّيٍّ فِي السَّمَاءِ إِضَاءَةً لاَ يَبُولُونَ وَلاَ يَتَغَوَّطُونَ وَلاَ يَمْتَخِطُونَ وَلاَ يَتْفُلُونَ أَمْشَاطُهُمُ الذَّهَبُ وَرَشْحُهُمُ الْمِسْكُ وَمَجَامِرُهُمُ الأَلُوَّةُ وَأَزْوَاجُهُمُ الْحُورُ الْعِينُ أَخْلاَقُهُمْ عَلَى خُلُقِ رَجُلٍ وَاحِدٍ عَلَى صُورَةِ أَبِيهِمْ آدَمَ سِتُّونَ ذِرَاعًا فِي السَّمَاءِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said:The (members of the) first group which would get into Paradise will have their faces as bright as stars in the sky. They would neither pass water, nor void excrement, nor will they suffer from catarrh, nor will they spit, and their combs would be made of gold, and their sweat will be musk, the fuel of their brazier will be aloes, and their wives will be large-eyed maidens and their form would be alike as one single person after the form of their father (Adam) sixty cubits tall

muslim:7149.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that these descriptions of Paradise are symbolic metaphors for spiritual bliss, or that the negation of bodily waste (*lā yabūlūna wa-lā yataghawwaṭūna*) proves the state is non-carnal. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that inhabitants have physical sweat of musk (*wa-rashḥuhum al-misk*), golden combs (*amshāṭuhum al-dhahab*), aloes-wood braziers (*majāmiruhum al-aluwwah*), and large-eyed wives (*wa-azwājuhum al-ḥūr al-ʿīn*), establishing across this narration, `bukhari:3254`, and `muslim:7150` a literal, material, and marital afterlife that stands in direct opposition to [Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30).

bukhari:3887.note: During his ascent past the seventh heaven to Sidrat al-Muntaha (the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary), Muhammad reports seeing four rivers and states that Gabriel identified the two visible ones as the Nile and the Euphrates (cf. bukhari:3207, muslim:416). While commentators such as al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar interpret this metaphorically to signify the rivers' blessing or the spread of Islam into their regions, the text itself describes Muhammad directly observing the four rivers at the celestial tree.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ رُفِعَتْ لِي سِدْرَةُ الْمُنْتَهَى، فَإِذَا نَبِقُهَا مِثْلُ قِلاَلِ هَجَرَ، وَإِذَا وَرَقُهَا مِثْلُ آذَانِ الْفِيَلَةِ قَالَ هَذِهِ سِدْرَةُ الْمُنْتَهَى، وَإِذَا أَرْبَعَةُ أَنْهَارٍ نَهْرَانِ بَاطِنَانِ، وَنَهْرَانِ ظَاهِرَانِ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ مَا هَذَانِ يَا جِبْرِيلُ قَالَ أَمَّا الْبَاطِنَانِ، فَنَهَرَانِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ، وَأَمَّا الظَّاهِرَانِ فَالنِّيلُ وَالْفُرَاتُ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Then I was made to ascend to Sidrat-ul-Muntaha (i.e. the Lote Tree of the utmost boundary) Behold! Its fruits were like the jars of Hajr (i.e. a place near Medina) and its leaves were as big as the ears of elephants. Gabriel said, 'This is the Lote Tree of the utmost boundary) . Behold ! There ran four rivers, two were hidden and two were visible, I asked, 'What are these two kinds of rivers, O Gabriel?' He replied,' As for the hidden rivers, they are two rivers in Paradise and the visible rivers are the Nile and the Euphrates.'

bukhari:3887.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that linking the Nile and Euphrates to the seventh heaven is merely a metaphor for their blessedness and sweet water, or that angels originally brought their waters down to earthly mountains. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly contrasts the two hidden rivers of Paradise (*al-bāṭinān*) with the two physically visible earthly rivers (*al-ẓāhirān*), while parallel narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3207; *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 164) state that all four literally gush forth from the physical base (*yakhruju min aṣlihā*) of the celestial Lote Tree (*Sidrat al-Muntahā*). Even Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* concedes that the text's apparent meaning (*al-ẓāhir*) is that these rivers physically originate in Paradise before emerging on earth—a hydrological impossibility given their actual geographical sources in East Africa and the Turkish highlands.

bukhari:4814.note: Abu Huraira transmits the prophetic declaration (explicitly attributed to Muhammad in bukhari:4935) that every part of the human body decays except the coccyx ('ajb adh-dhanab), from which creation will be reconstructed at the resurrection. Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawi affirm that this refers to a literal physical bone ('aẓm wāḥid) that resists decomposition in the earth, rather than microscopic cells or an embryonic structure.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَيَبْلَى كُلُّ شَىْءٍ مِنَ الإِنْسَانِ إِلاَّ عَجْبَ ذَنَبِهِ، فِيهِ يُرَكَّبُ الْخَلْقُ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Everything of the human body will decay except the coccyx bone (of the tail) and from that bone Allah will reconstruct the whole body

bukhari:4814.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that `'ajb adh-dhanab` refers either to an invisible, microscopic particle (*dharrah*) preserved supernaturally—as proposed by Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—or to embryonic 'primitive streak' stem cells that supposedly survive cremation and decay. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *'wa yablā kullu shayʾin mina al-insāni illā ʿajba dhanabihi'* ('everything of the human decays except his coccyx bone'), using the literal anatomical term for the physical tailbone, while parallel Sahih narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4935; *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2955a) specify that the physical earth consumes the entire body except this bone (*'yaʾkuluhu at-turābu illā ʿajba adh-dhanab'*). Because forensic taphonomy and cremation empirically prove that the coccyx and all its cellular tissues completely disintegrate just like the rest of the skeleton, reducing a macroscopic bone to an undetectable metaphysical atom directly contradicts the explicit physical contrast in the text.

bukhari:4921.note: In explaining the occasion of revelation for [Quran 72:1](quran://72/1), Ibn Abbas states that shooting stars and meteors (*al-shuhub*) were sent against devils (*al-shayatin*) to block them from intercepting the news of heaven ([Quran 72:8-9](quran://72/8)), prompting them to search the earth until they encountered Muhammad reciting the Quran at Nakhla.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَقَدْ حِيلَ بَيْنَ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَبَيْنَ خَبَرِ السَّمَاءِ، وَأُرْسِلَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الشُّهُبُ فَرَجَعَتِ الشَّيَاطِينُ فَقَالُوا مَا لَكُمْ فَقَالُوا حِيلَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ خَبَرِ السَّمَاءِ وَأُرْسِلَتْ عَلَيْنَا الشُّهُبُ‏.‏ قَالَ مَا حَالَ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَ خَبَرِ السَّمَاءِ إِلاَّ مَا حَدَثَ
problematic_excerpt.english: At that time something intervened between the devils and the news of the Heaven, and flames were sent down upon them, so the devils returned. Their fellow-devils said, "What is wrong with you? " They said, "Something has intervened between us and the news of the Heaven, and fires (flames) have been shot at us." Their fellow-devils said, "Nothing has intervened between you and the news of the Heaven, but an important event has happened.

bukhari:4921.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *al-shuhub* refers to unseen metaphysical energy in the spiritual realm (*al-ghayb*) rather than physical meteors, or follow Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* in claiming that ordinary astronomical phenomena were merely weaponized at the onset of Muhammad's mission. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that shooting stars were sent upon them (`وَأُرْسِلَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الشُّهُبُ`) as the specific physical event that alarmed the devils, and [Quran 67:5](quran://67/5) explicitly identifies the visible lamps adorning the lowest sky (*al-sama' al-dunya*) as the exact missiles (*rujuman*) thrown at them. Furthermore, in muslim:5819, Muhammad points directly to a visible meteor streaking across the night sky (`رُمِيَ بِنَجْمٍ فَاسْتَنَارَ`) before his companions and declares it was just hurled at an eavesdropping devil, proving the text refers to ordinary atmospheric meteors.

bukhari:3399.note: Muhammad declares that meat would never decay were it not for the Children of Israel, and that no woman would ever betray her husband were it not for Eve (bukhari:3330). Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawi explain this as a literal claim that meat never spoiled before the Israelites hoarded food in the wilderness.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَوْلاَ بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ لَمْ يَخْنَزِ اللَّحْمُ، وَلَوْلاَ حَوَّاءُ لَمْ تَخُنْ أُنْثَى زَوْجَهَا الدَّهْرَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Were it not for Bani Israel, meat would not decay; and were it not for Eve, no woman would ever betray her husband

bukhari:3399.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this statement is merely a figurative moral analogy—citing a secondary view mentioned in Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—meaning only that the Israelites in the wilderness were the first people to hoard meat long enough for it to spoil, rather than claiming meat never biologically decomposed before Moses. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *'lawlā Banū Isrāʾīl lam yakhnaz al-laḥm'* ('Were it not for the Children of Israel, meat would not putrefy'), using the absolute counterfactual *lawlā* with the universal definite noun *al-laḥm* ('meat') to assert that the physical phenomenon of putrefaction (*khanz*) itself is a direct consequence of Israelite hoarding. As Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 10/59) and the majority of classical scholars confirm, the Hadith literally teaches that meat never rotted prior to the Exodus in the 2nd millennium BC—a folk etiology borrowed from misremembered Exodus 16:20 traditions that contradicts the biological reality of organic decomposition.

muslim:1401.note: Muhammad declares that the most intense summer heat (*al-ḥarr*) and winter cold (*al-zamharīr*) experienced on earth are the direct result of Hellfire (*al-nār*) complaining to its Lord that its parts were consuming one another and receiving permission to take two exhalations (*nafasayn*)—one in winter and one in summer (cf. bukhari:536, bukhari:3260). Classical commentators including al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) affirm that the orthodox Sunni majority interprets this report literally (*'alā ẓāhirihi*), maintaining that Hellfire possesses actual speech and physically exhales twice a year.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: اشْتَكَتِ النَّارُ إِلَى رَبِّهَا فَقَالَتْ يَا رَبِّ أَكَلَ بَعْضِي بَعْضًا ‏.‏ فَأَذِنَ لَهَا بِنَفَسَيْنِ نَفَسٍ فِي الشِّتَاءِ وَنَفَسٍ فِي الصَّيْفِ فَهُوَ أَشَدُّ مَا تَجِدُونَ مِنَ الْحَرِّ وَأَشَدُّ مَا تَجِدُونَ مِنَ الزَّمْهَرِيرِ
problematic_excerpt.english: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: The Fire made a complaint before the Lord saying." O Lord, some parts of mine have consumed the others." So it was allowed to take two exhalations, one exhalation in winter and the other exhalation in summer. That is why you find extreme heat (in summer) and extreme cold (in winter)

muslim:1401.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Hellfire's complaint and two exhalations are either metaphorical expressions (*majāz*) or unseen metaphysical realities (*al-ghayb*) operating behind ordinary astronomical seasons. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Hell's breath (*nafas*) is the direct physical cause of earthly temperature extremes—"it is the most extreme heat you experience and the most extreme freezing cold (*al-zamharīr*) you experience" (`فَهُوَ أَشَدُّ مَا تَجِدُونَ مِنَ الْحَرِّ وَأَشَدُّ مَا تَجِدُونَ مِنَ الزَّمْهَرِيرِ`). Furthermore, both Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) affirm that mainstream Sunni orthodoxy takes this narration literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*), which is reinforced by parallel narrations (`bukhari:536`, `muslim:1403`) where Muhammad alters legal prayer times specifically because midday summer heat is from the physical "boiling of Hell" (`فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ`).

muslim:1161.note: Muhammad states that Al-Masjid al-Haram in Mecca was the first mosque established on earth and that Al-Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem was established forty years later. Because Islamic scripture credits Abraham with raising the foundations of the Ka'bah ([Quran 2:127](quran://2/127)) whereas Solomon built the Jerusalem Temple ([1 Kings 6:1](bible://1kgs/6/1)) roughly a millennium later, classical commentators such as Al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar propose that Adam or angels originally founded both sanctuaries forty years apart and that Abraham and Solomon later rebuilt them.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَىُّ مَسْجِدٍ وُضِعَ فِي الأَرْضِ أَوَّلُ قَالَ ‏"‏ الْمَسْجِدُ الْحَرَامُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ ثُمَّ أَىٌّ قَالَ ‏"‏ الْمَسْجِدُ الأَقْصَى ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ كَمْ بَيْنَهُمَا قَالَ ‏"‏ أَرْبَعُونَ سَنَةً وَأَيْنَمَا أَدْرَكَتْكَ الصَّلاَةُ فَصَلِّ فَهُوَ مَسْجِدٌ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I said: Messenger of Allah, which mosque was set up first on the earth? He said: Al-Masjid al-Haram (the sacred). I (again) said: Then which next? He said: It was the Masjid Aqsa. I (again) said: How long the space of time (between their setting up)? He (the Holy Prophet) said: It was forty years.

muslim:1161.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the forty-year interval is not a chronological error because Adam (or Abraham and Jacob) allegedly laid the original foundations (waḍʿ) of both sanctuaries, while Abraham and Solomon merely renovated them centuries later (as proposed in Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in the Quran that Allah first designated the site of the Ka'bah for Abraham (wa-idh bawwaʾnā li-Ibrāhīma makāna al-bayti, [Quran 22:26](quran://22/26)) who raised its foundations (al-qawāʿid, [Quran 2:127](quran://2/127)), while authentic Hadith credit Solomon with the construction of the Jerusalem sanctuary (bināʾ Bayt al-Maqdis, nasai:693). Because neither the Quran nor any authentic prophetic narration ever attributes the founding of either mosque to Adam or Jacob, this "prior foundation" excuse is an uncorroborated, ad-hoc invention designed to mask a 1,000-year historical anachronism between Abraham (~2000 BC) and Solomon (~960 BC).

bukhari:3305.note: Muhammad states that he considers a lost group of Israelites to have become rats, citing as proof that a rat drinks sheep's milk but refuses she-camel's milk, and Abu Huraira confirms to Ka'b that he heard this directly from the Prophet rather than the Torah. Classical commentators explain the lineage claim as Muhammad's personal conjecture prior to stating that transmuted creatures leave no offspring (muslim:7496), though his empirical assertion that rats refuse camel's milk is stated unconditionally.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فُقِدَتْ أُمَّةٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ لاَ يُدْرَى مَا فَعَلَتْ، وَإِنِّي لاَ أُرَاهَا إِلاَّ الْفَارَ إِذَا وُضِعَ لَهَا أَلْبَانُ الإِبِلِ لَمْ تَشْرَبْ، وَإِذَا وُضِعَ لَهَا أَلْبَانُ الشَّاءِ شَرِبَتْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَحَدَّثْتُ كَعْبًا فَقَالَ أَنْتَ سَمِعْتَ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُهُ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ لِي مِرَارًا‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ أَفَأَقْرَأُ التَّوْرَاةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "A group of Israelites were lost. Nobody knows what they did. But I do not see them except that they were cursed and changed into rats, for if you put the milk of a she-camel in front of a rat, it will not drink it, but if the milk of a sheep is put in front of it, it will drink it." I told this to Ka`b who asked me, "Did you hear it from the Prophet (ﷺ) ?" I said, "Yes." Ka`b asked me the same question several times.; I said to Ka`b. "Do I read the Torah? (i.e. I tell you this from the Prophet)

bukhari:3305.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as explained by Ibn Hajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī in Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, Muhammad's phrase 'I do not see them except as rats' (lā urāhā illā al-fār) was merely personal conjecture (ẓann) spoken prior to receiving corrective revelation in Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:6771 that transformed humans (maskh) leave no offspring, or that the report originated from Jewish folklore (Isrā'īliyyāt). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad grounded his deduction in a demonstrably false empirical claim—asserting that a rat refuses she-camel's milk (albān al-ibil lam tashrab) while drinking sheep's milk (albān al-shā' sharibat) in observance of Mosaic kosher law—and Abu Huraira directly refutes the Isrā'īliyyāt excuse by asking the incredulous Jewish convert Ka'b al-Ahbar, 'Do I read the Torah?' (a-fa-aqra'u al-Tawrāh?). Consequently, even the classical 'uninspired conjecture' defense forces apologists to concede that their prophet asserted a false zoological fact from his own imagination to validate a superstitious myth.

bukhari:4803.note: Muhammad explains [Quran 36:38](quran://36/38) by declaring that the sun's resting place (*mustaqarr*) is beneath Allah's Throne, where it travels at sunset to prostrate and seek permission to rise again (bukhari:4802). The parenthetical disclaimer in the English translation redefining this prostration as "obedience" is a translator interpolation absent from the Arabic text.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَأَلْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنْ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى ‏{‏وَالشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَهَا‏}‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ مُسْتَقَرُّهَا تَحْتَ الْعَرْشِ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the Statement of Allah:-- 'And the sun runs on fixed course for a term (decreed), ' (36.38) He said, "Its course is underneath "Allah's Throne."

bukhari:4803.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *mustaqarr* ('resting place') refers either to a temporal limit on the Day of Judgment or to the sun's continuous orbit within a cosmos entirely situated beneath Allah's Throne—with translator Muhsin Khan even mistranslating *mustaqarruhā* as 'its course' and inserting an unauthenticated parenthetical gloss claiming the sun's prostration is merely metaphorical obedience. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *mustaqarruhā taḥta al-ʿarsh* ('its resting place is beneath the Throne'), using the noun of place (*ism makān*) from *istaqarra* (to settle or come to rest) to designate a specific spatial destination. Furthermore, the complete versions of this exact Abu Dharr narration in Sahih al-Bukhari (3199 and 4802) explicitly specify that this occurs daily 'when the sun sets' (*ḥīna taghrubu*), where it goes to physically prostrate (*tasjudu*) beneath the Throne and ask permission to rise again until the day it is ordered to 'return from whence you came' and rise from the west, confirming a literal, daily geocentric stop rather than continuous orbital motion.

bukhari:5770.note: Muhammad declares that there is no disease contagion (*lā ʿadwā*), and when a Bedouin objects that a mangy camel infects a healthy herd, he responds by asking who infected the first camel. In the immediately following report (bukhari:5771), Abu Huraira narrates the opposite command not to mix diseased cattle with healthy ones and, when confronted with the contradiction, denies having ever narrated 'there is no contagion.'

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لاَ عَدْوَى، وَلاَ صَفَرَ، وَلاَ هَامَةَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ أَعْرَابِيٌّ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَمَا بَالُ الإِبِلِ تَكُونُ فِي الرَّمْلِ كَأَنَّهَا الظِّبَاءُ، فَيُخَالِطُهَا الْبَعِيرُ الأَجْرَبُ فَيُجْرِبُهَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَمَنْ أَعْدَى الأَوَّلَ
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'No 'Adwa (i.e. no contagious disease is conveyed to others without Allah's permission); nor (any evil omen in the month of) Safar; nor Hama" A bedouin said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! What about the camels which, when on the sand (desert) look like deers, but when a mangy camel mixes with them they all get infected with mange?" On that Allah's Apostle said, "Then who conveyed the (mange) disease to the first (mangy) camel?

bukhari:5770.literal_translation: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'There is no contagion, nor Safar, nor Hama.' A bedouin said, 'O Messenger of Allah! What about camels that are like gazelles in the sand, but when a mangy camel mixes with them, it infects them with mange?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, 'Then who infected the first one?'

translation_issue.arabic_term: لاَ عَدْوَى
translation_issue.published_rendering: No 'Adwa (i.e. no contagious disease is conveyed to others without Allah's permission)
translation_issue.literal_meaning: There is no contagion
translation_issue.explanation: The translator inserted the theological caveat '(i.e. no contagious disease is conveyed to others without Allah's permission)' to soften Muhammad's explicit denial of disease contagion and harmonize it with medical reality.

bukhari:5770.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was not denying biological contagion itself, but merely refuting the pre-Islamic belief that diseases transmit autonomously apart from Allah's decree, pointing to adjacent narrations advising quarantine (`bukhari:5707` and `bukhari:5771`). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *lā ʿadwā* (لاَ عَدْوَى—an absolute categorical negation meaning 'there is no contagion' with zero mention of Allah's permission), and when the Bedouin points to the empirical reality of a mangy camel infecting a healthy herd (*fayukhāliṭuhā al-baʿīr al-ajrab fayujribuhā*), Muhammad rejects the transmission mechanism outright by asking, 'Then who infected the first one?' (*faman aʿdā al-awwal*). Moreover, `bukhari:5717` records that the contradiction between denying contagion and ordering quarantine was so irreconcilable that Abū Hurayrah later tried to deny he ever narrated the quarantine command when confronted about the inconsistency.

bukhari:5773.note: Muhammad declares that there is no contagious disease (*lā ʿadwā*) and counters a Bedouin's observation that a mangy camel infects healthy camels by asking who infected the first camel. Although the same report also prohibits bringing diseased livestock among healthy livestock, his rebuttal to the Bedouin directly argues against horizontal transmission from one animal to another.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ عَدْوَى ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَامَ أَعْرَابِيٌّ فَقَالَ أَرَأَيْتَ الإِبِلَ تَكُونُ فِي الرِّمَالِ أَمْثَالَ الظِّبَاءِ فَيَأْتِيهِ الْبَعِيرُ الأَجْرَبُ فَتَجْرَبُ‏.‏ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَمَنْ أَعْدَى الأَوَّلَ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira also said: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "No 'Adwa." A bedouin got up and said, "Don't you see how camels on the sand look like deer but when a mangy camel mixes with them, they all get infected with mange?" On that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Then who conveyed the (mange) disease to the first camel?

bukhari:5773.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, that Muhammad was not denying biological contagion itself, but merely refuting the pre-Islamic pagan belief that diseases transmit by their own autonomous nature (bi-ṭabʿihā) independent of Allah's decree. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an absolute categorical negation (lā ʿadwā, "there is no contagion"), and when a Bedouin challenges him with the empirical observation of a mangy camel (al-baʿīr al-ajrab) infecting a healthy herd (fa-tajrabu), Muhammad does not qualify contagion as a secondary cause under divine will, but dismisses physical transmission altogether by retorting, "Then who infected the first?" (fa-man aʿdā al-awwal?).

bukhari:5773.note: Abu Huraira narrates from Muhammad both that there is no contagious disease (*lā ʿadwā*) and that diseased livestock must not be brought among healthy livestock. In the parallel report (bukhari:5771), when Abu Salama confronts Abu Huraira over narrating both opposing statements, Abu Huraira denies having previously transmitted 'no contagion' and speaks in Ethiopic.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ عَدْوَى ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو سَلَمَةَ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ تُورِدُوا الْمُمْرِضَ عَلَى الْمُصِحِّ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "No 'Adwa." Abu Huraira also said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The cattle suffering from a disease should not be mixed up with healthy cattle (or said "Do not put a patient with a healthy person as a precaution.")

bukhari:5773.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, following al-Bāqillānī and Ibn Ḥajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī, that these two commands are harmonious because the ban on mixing sick and healthy cattle (lā tūridū al-mumriḍ ʿalā al-muṣiḥḥ) was merely meant to prevent weak-faithed owners from falling into polytheism (shirk) by blaming the diseased camel if healthy ones fell ill by coincidence. However, the primary Arabic text juxtaposes two mutually exclusive rulings—an absolute denial of contagion (lā ʿadwā) and a strict quarantine mandate—and the immediately adjacent narration in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī (bukhari:5771) proves the early Muslims themselves recognized this as an irreconcilable contradiction, recording that Abū Hurayrah eventually suppressed and angrily denied ever narrating "No ʿAdwā" when confronted with his own conflicting report.

bukhari:4480.note: Answering 'Abdullah ibn Salam's test of prophethood, Muhammad states that Gabriel just informed him that a child resembles the father if the man's fluid (mā') precedes (sabaqa) the woman's fluid, and resembles the mother if the woman's fluid precedes the man's. Parallel reports alternate between one fluid 'preceding' (sabaqa) and 'prevailing over' ('alā) the other (bukhari:3329, bukhari:3938).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَإِذَا سَبَقَ مَاءُ الرَّجُلِ مَاءَ الْمَرْأَةِ نَزَعَ الْوَلَدَ، وَإِذَا سَبَقَ مَاءُ الْمَرْأَةِ نَزَعَتْ
problematic_excerpt.english: And if a man's discharge preceded that of the woman, then the child resembles the father, and if the woman's discharge preceded that of the man, then the child resembles the mother.

bukhari:4480.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that 'fluid' (mā') and 'preceded' (sabaqa) are metaphors for dominant and recessive genes—appealing to Ibn Hajar's attempt in Fatḥ al-Bārī to harmonize 'preceded' with parallel wordings meaning 'prevailed' (ʿalā)—or claim Muhammad was merely citing Jewish folklore to pass Abdullah ibn Salam's test. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states 'أَخْبَرَنِي بِهِنَّ جِبْرِيلُ آنِفًا' ('Gabriel has informed me about them just now'), locking the claim into direct divine revelation, and uses 'سَبَقَ مَاءُ الرَّجُلِ مَاءَ الْمَرْأَةِ' to describe the chronological order of male and female sexual discharge during intercourse. Parallel Sahih narrations (such as bukhari:130, 3329, and muslim:710–muslim:315) confirm that 'mā'' refers literally to physical orgasmic fluid experienced in nocturnal emissions—repeating erroneous 7th-century AD Galenic two-seed embryology—whereas biology proves that hereditary resemblance is fixed by DNA at fertilization regardless of who climaxes first or whether a woman orgasms at all.

bukhari:5756.note: Muhammad declares that there is no contagious disease transmission (*lā ʿadwā*) and no evil bird-omens (*lā ṭiyarah*), while expressing approval for good omens (*al-faʾl al-ṣāliḥ*). Although the English translator and classical commentators interpolate an unattested theological caveat ('without Allah's permission') to reconcile this denial with conflicting quarantine commands (bukhari:5707, bukhari:5770), the primary Arabic text states the negation without qualification.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لاَ عَدْوَى وَلاَ طِيَرَةَ، وَيُعْجِبُنِي الْفَأْلُ الصَّالِحُ، الْكَلِمَةُ الْحَسَنَةُ
problematic_excerpt.english: No 'Adwa (no contagious disease is conveyed to others without Allah's permission), nor Tiyara, but I like the good Fal, i.e., the good word

bukhari:5756.literal_translation: There is no contagion and no evil bird-omens, but the good omen pleases me: the good word.

translation_issue.arabic_term: لاَ عَدْوَى
translation_issue.published_rendering: No 'Adwa (no contagious disease is conveyed to others without Allah's permission)
translation_issue.literal_meaning: There is no contagion
translation_issue.explanation: The translator inserted the parenthetical theological caveat '(no contagious disease is conveyed to others without Allah's permission)' to mask Muhammad's categorical denial of disease transmission.

bukhari:5756.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *lā ʿadwā* merely negates the pre-Islamic belief that diseases transmit autonomously by their own nature apart from Allah's decree—an excuse drawn from Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and inserted directly into Muhsin Khan's parenthetical translation—while citing 'flee from the leper' (bukhari:5707) as proof of medical foresight. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *lā ʿadwā wa-lā ṭiyarah* ('there is no contagion and no evil bird-omen'), using an unconditional categorical negation that places biological disease transmission on the exact same footing as imaginary pagan superstitions. Furthermore, when a Bedouin empirically challenged this claim by observing that a mangy camel infects a healthy herd, Muhammad doubled down by asking, 'Then who infected the first one?' (*fa-man aʿdā al-awwal*, bukhari:5717, 5770), proving he denied the physical mechanism of host-to-host transmission itself and exposing an irreconcilable contradiction with his own command to flee lepers.

bukhari:5610.note: Muhammad states that when he was raised to the celestial Lote Tree (al-Sidrah), he saw four rivers: two hidden (batinan) rivers in Paradise and two apparent (zahiran) rivers that he identifies as the Nile and the Euphrates (cf. bukhari:3207, bukhari:3887).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: رُفِعْتُ إِلَى السِّدْرَةِ فَإِذَا أَرْبَعَةُ أَنْهَارٍ، نَهَرَانِ ظَاهِرَانِ، وَنَهَرَانِ بَاطِنَانِ، فَأَمَّا الظَّاهِرَانِ النِّيلُ وَالْفُرَاتُ، وَأَمَّا الْبَاطِنَانِ فَنَهَرَانِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ
problematic_excerpt.english: I was raised to the Lote Tree and saw four rivers, two of which were coming out and two going in. Those which were coming out were the Nile and the Euphrates, and those which were going in were two rivers in paradise.

bukhari:5610.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration—citing metaphorical interpretations discussed by Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar—merely signifies the spiritual blessing (barakah) and sweetness of the Nile and Euphrates or foretells the spread of Islam to their fertile valleys rather than describing their physical geographical source. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad saw four rivers at the Lote Tree in the seventh heaven (رُفِعْتُ إِلَى السِّدْرَةِ فَإِذَا أَرْبَعَةُ أَنْهَارٍ), directly pairing two 'hidden/interior' rivers in Paradise (الْبَاطِنَانِ فَنَهَرَانِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ) with two 'visible/exterior' rivers identified as the earthly Nile and Euphrates (الظَّاهِرَانِ النِّيلُ وَالْفُرَاتُ). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:3887, muslim:416) specify that all four rivers physically gush forth from the tree's base (يَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَصْلِهَا), confirming that the plain literal text (ẓāhir) posits a celestial origin for two terrestrial rivers whose earthly headwaters in East Africa and Anatolia are well-mapped.

muslim:7150.note: Muhammad declares that the inhabitants of Paradise will possess the physical stature of their father Adam at sixty cubits tall (عَلَى طُولِ أَبِيهِمْ آدَمَ سِتُّونَ ذِرَاعًا). Together with parallel reports (bukhari:3326, bukhari:3254, muslim:7149) stating that human height has decreased since Adam's creation, this attributes a literal sixty-cubit stature to the first human that is contradicted by the anatomical and archaeological record.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ أَوَّلُ زُمْرَةٍ تَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ مِنْ أُمَّتِي عَلَى صُورَةِ الْقَمَرِ لَيْلَةَ الْبَدْرِ ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ عَلَى أَشَدِّ نَجْمٍ فِي السَّمَاءِ إِضَاءَةً ثُمَّ هُمْ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ مَنَازِلُ لاَ يَتَغَوَّطُونَ وَلاَ يَبُولُونَ وَلاَ يَمْتَخِطُونَ وَلاَ يَبْزُقُونَ أَمْشَاطُهُمُ الذَّهَبُ وَمَجَامِرُهُمُ الأَلُوَّةُ وَرَشْحُهُمُ الْمِسْكُ أَخْلاَقُهُمْ عَلَى خُلُقِ رَجُلٍ وَاحِدٍ عَلَى طُولِ أَبِيهِمْ آدَمَ سِتُّونَ ذِرَاعًا ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:The first group of my Ummah to get into Paradise would be like a full moon in the night. Then those who would be next to them; they would be like the most significantly glittering stars in regard to brightness, then after them (others) in ranks. They would neither void excrement, nor pass water, nor suffer from catarrh, nor would they spit. And their combs would be made of gold, and the fuel of their braziers would be aloes and their sweat would be musk and their form would be the form of one single person according to the length of their father sixty cubits tall.

muslim:7150.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the sixty-cubit stature describes only a metaphysical body unique to the afterlife, or that the measurement is a figurative expression of honor rather than the literal anatomical height of Adam. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the inhabitants of Paradise are formed `عَلَى طُولِ أَبِيهِمْ آدَمَ سِتُّونَ ذِرَاعًا` ('according to the length of their father Adam, sixty cubits tall') and `عَلَى خَلْقِ رَجُلٍ` ('in the physical creation of a single man'), directly anchoring their future height to Adam's original bodily dimensions. Parallel narrations in `bukhari:3326` and `muslim:7149` likewise anchor this sixty-cubit measurement to Adam's original creation rather than treating it as an exclusively eschatological metaphor.

bukhari:318.note: Muhammad declares that an angel appointed over every womb reports the embryo's progression through a drop (*nuṭfah*), a clot (*'alaqah*), and a lump of flesh (*muḍghah*) ([Quran 22:5](quran://22/5)), and only after the lump-of-flesh stage asks Allah whether the child will be male or female and wretched or blessed (bukhari:3333, bukhari:6595). This sequence places the determination of biological sex after the *muḍghah* stage rather than at fertilization.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏ "‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ ـ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ـ وَكَّلَ بِالرَّحِمِ مَلَكًا يَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ نُطْفَةٌ، يَا رَبِّ عَلَقَةٌ، يَا رَبِّ مُضْغَةٌ‏.‏ فَإِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَقْضِيَ خَلْقَهُ قَالَ أَذَكَرٌ أَمْ أُنْثَى شَقِيٌّ أَمْ سَعِيدٌ فَمَا الرِّزْقُ وَالأَجَلُ فَيُكْتَبُ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "At every womb Allah appoints an angel who says, 'O Lord! A drop of semen, O Lord! A clot. O Lord! A little lump of flesh." Then if Allah wishes (to complete) its creation, the angel asks, (O Lord!) Will it be a male or female, a wretched or a blessed, and how much will his provision be? And what will his age be?' So all that is written while the child is still in the mother's womb

bukhari:318.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that 'ʿalaqah' means a microscopic 'clinging leech-like structure' rather than a blood clot, and cite Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī to claim that the angel asking about the fetus's sex after the 'muḍghah' stage merely makes known to the angel what Allah had eternally decreed. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the embryo transitions sequentially from a drop of fluid (nuṭfah) to a blood clot (ʿalaqah, defined by Ibn Hajar and classical Arabic lexicographers as 'dam jāmid', thick congealed blood) to a lump of flesh (muḍghah), and that only after reaching this lump stage (fa-idhā arāda an yaqḍiya khalqahu) is whether it will be male or female (a-dhakarun am unthā) determined and written. Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (such as bukhari:3208, bukhari:6595, and muslim:6726) lock these stages into literal forty-day intervals—asserting that a fetus remains a drop of semen and a blood clot for eighty days before its biological sex is decided—which echoes 2nd-century AD Galenic myths and contradicts modern embryology, where chromosomal sex is fixed at fertilization.

bukhari:3208.note: Muhammad states that a human's creation is gathered in the mother's womb for forty days, then becomes a clot (`'alaqah`) for an equal forty-day period, and then becomes a lump of flesh (`mudghah`) for a third forty-day period—totaling 120 sequential days before an angel is sent and the soul is breathed into the fetus ([Quran 22:5](quran://22/5)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ يُجْمَعُ خَلْقُهُ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ عَلَقَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ مُضْغَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ مَلَكًا، فَيُؤْمَرُ بِأَرْبَعِ كَلِمَاتٍ، وَيُقَالُ لَهُ اكْتُبْ عَمَلَهُ وَرِزْقَهُ وَأَجَلَهُ وَشَقِيٌّ أَوْ سَعِيدٌ‏.‏ ثُمَّ يُنْفَخُ فِيهِ الرُّوحُ
problematic_excerpt.english: (The matter of the Creation of) a human being is put together in the womb of the mother in forty days, and then he becomes a clot of thick blood for a similar period, and then a piece of flesh for a similar period. Then Allah sends an angel who is ordered to write four things. He is ordered to write down his (i.e. the new creature's) deeds, his livelihood, his (date of) death, and whether he will be blessed or wretched (in religion). Then the soul is breathed into him.

bukhari:3208.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—appealing to a late reinterpretation mentioned in Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and the forty-two-night report in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2645a—that all three embryonic stages occur within a single forty-day period rather than totaling 120 days, since modern embryology proves organs and limbs develop by day 56. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *"arbaʿīna yawman, thumma yakūnu ʿalaqatan mithla dhālika, thumma yakūnu muḍghatan mithla dhālika"* ("forty days, then he becomes a clot for a similar period, then he becomes a lump of flesh for a similar period"), where the sequential conjunction *thumma* ("then") and the temporal phrase *mithla dhālika* ("for a like duration") grammatically lock in three consecutive forty-day intervals. Both Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 16/190) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī* 11/479) affirm the classical Sunni consensus that the embryo remains a blood clot from day 40 to day 80 and a chewed lump until day 120 before ensoulment.

bukhari:3208.note: Muhammad declares that an angel records in the womb a person's deeds, livelihood, lifespan, and whether they will be wretched or blessed, stating that a man may act until only a cubit remains between him and Paradise—or Hellfire—before that pre-written decree overtakes him (`fayasbiqu 'alayhi kitabuhu`) so that he performs the deeds of the opposite destination ([Ezekiel 18:20](bible://ez/18/20); [Romans 2:6](bible://rom/2/6)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَإِنَّ الرَّجُلَ مِنْكُمْ لَيَعْمَلُ حَتَّى مَا يَكُونُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْجَنَّةِ إِلاَّ ذِرَاعٌ، فَيَسْبِقُ عَلَيْهِ كِتَابُهُ، فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ، وَيَعْمَلُ حَتَّى مَا يَكُونُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ النَّارِ إِلاَّ ذِرَاعٌ، فَيَسْبِقُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ، فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ
problematic_excerpt.english: So, a man amongst you may do (good deeds till there is only a cubit between him and Paradise and then what has been written for him decides his behavior and he starts doing (evil) deeds characteristic of the people of the (Hell) Fire. And similarly a man amongst you may do (evil) deeds till there is only a cubit between him and the (Hell) Fire, and then what has been written for him decides his behavior, and he starts doing deeds characteristic of the people of Paradise

bukhari:3208.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Ḥajar's commentary and parallel narrations such as *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 2898 ("in what appears to people")—that the angel's record represents passive divine foreknowledge rather than coercive fatalism, claiming the person who turns to evil at the end was secretly a lifelong hypocrite. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *"fa-yasbiqu ʿalayhi kitābuhu fa-yaʿmalu bi-ʿamali ahli al-nār"* ("then his written decree overtakes him, so he does the deeds of the people of the Fire"), using the verb *yasbiqu ʿalayhi* ("overtakes/prevails over him") and the causal particle *fa-* ("so/consequently") to show that the womb-inscribed decree actively forces his final actions. Moreover, the symmetrical reverse case in the exact same sentence—where a lifelong evildoer is overtaken by *al-kitāb* at the last cubit and enters Paradise—collapses the "secret hypocrisy" excuse and confirms that salvation is dictated by a pre-written script (*Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2643a).
