bukhari:3332.note: Muhammad declares that human development in the womb proceeds through three sequential forty-day stages—being gathered for forty days, becoming a clot (*'alaqah*) for an equal period (*mithla dhalika*), and becoming a lump of flesh (*mudghah*) for another equal period—totaling 120 days before an angel breathes the soul into the body ([Quran 22:5](quran://22/5); bukhari:3208, bukhari:6594).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ يُجْمَعُ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ عَلَقَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ مُضْغَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكًا بِأَرْبَعِ كَلِمَاتٍ، فَيُكْتَبُ عَمَلُهُ وَأَجَلُهُ وَرِزْقُهُ وَشَقِيٌّ أَوْ سَعِيدٌ، ثُمَّ يُنْفَخُ فِيهِ الرُّوحُ
problematic_excerpt.english: every one of you is collected in the womb of his mother for the first forty days, and then he becomes a clot for another forty days, and then a piece of flesh for another forty days. Then Allah sends an angel to write four items: He writes his deeds, time of his death, means of his livelihood, and whether he will be wretched or blessed (in religion). Then the soul is breathed into his body.

bukhari:3332.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the three embryonic stages occur simultaneously within a single forty-day window rather than consecutively, appealing to muslim:6726 to harmonize the Hadith with modern embryology where organogenesis concludes by day 56. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that each phase follows the previous one using the sequential particle *thumma* (ثُمَّ, 'then/thereafter') coupled with *mithla dhālika* (مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ, 'for a period like that')—أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ عَلَقَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ مُضْغَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ—which parallel narrations (muslim:6724) and classical commentators like Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) and Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) unanimously calculate as three successive forty-day periods totaling 120 days before ensoulment. This locks Muhammad into the fatal scientific error that a human fetus remains an unformed blood clot (*ʿalaqah*) from day 40 to day 80 and a lump of flesh (*muḍghah*) until day 120, long after all major organs and a beating heart are already formed.

bukhari:3332.note: Muhammad states that an angel is sent to the womb to pre-write four decrees for every person: their deeds, time of death, livelihood, and whether they will be wretched or blessed. Consequently, a man may perform the deeds of the people of Paradise until only a cubit remains between him and it, when the pre-written decree (*al-kitab*) overtakes him so that he performs the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it ([Ezekiel 18:20](bible://ez/18/20); [Romans 2:6](bible://rom/2/6)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَإِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ حَتَّى مَا يَكُونُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهَا إِلاَّ ذِرَاعٌ، فَيَسْبِقُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ، فَيَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ، وَإِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ، حَتَّى مَا يَكُونُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهَا إِلاَّ ذِرَاعٌ فَيَسْبِقُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ، فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ فَيَدْخُلُ النَّارَ
problematic_excerpt.english: So a man may do deeds characteristic of the people of the (Hell) Fire, so much so that there is only the distance of a cubit between him and it, and then what has been written (by the angel) surpasses, and so he starts doing deeds characteristic of the people of Paradise and enters Paradise. Similarly, a person may do deeds characteristic of the people of Paradise, so much so that there is only the distance of a cubit between him and it, and then what has been written (by the angel) surpasses, and he starts doing deeds of the people of the (Hell) Fire and enters the (Hell) Fire

bukhari:3332.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and parallel variants adding *fīmā yabdū lil-nās* ('in what appears to people', e.g., bukhari:2898)—that the person performing righteous deeds was secretly a hypocrite and that the angel's record in the womb reflects passive divine foreknowledge rather than coercive predestination. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states فَيَسْبِقُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ، فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ فَيَدْخُلُ النَّارَ ('then the [decreed] Book overtakes him, and so he does the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters the Fire'), using the causal conjunction *fa-* (فَـ, 'so/consequently') to establish that the pre-natal decree (شَقِيٌّ أَوْ سَعِيدٌ, 'wretched or blessed') actively overrides the man's conduct and forces his apostasy. Parallel Sahih narrations—such as muslim:6769, where Allah creates souls specifically for Hellfire while still in their fathers' loins, and bukhari:6614, where Adam absolves himself of guilt because Allah decreed his sin forty years before his creation—confirm that this decree is deterministic compulsion that nullifies human moral agency.

bukhari:3333.note: Muhammad declares that an angel in the womb reports the successive embryonic stages of a drop (*nuṭfah*), a clot (*ʿalaqah*), and a lump of flesh (*muḍghah*), and only afterward—when Allah wills to complete its creation—asks whether the fetus will be male or female and wretched (*shaqī*) or blessed (*saʿīd*) (cf. [Quran 23:14](quran://23/14), bukhari:3332). The angel then writes down the child's biological sex, livelihood, lifespan, and predestined fate while still in the mother's womb.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ وَكَّلَ فِي الرَّحِمِ مَلَكًا فَيَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ نُطْفَةٌ، يَا رَبِّ عَلَقَةٌ، يَا رَبِّ مُضْغَةٌ، فَإِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَهَا قَالَ يَا رَبِّ، أَذَكَرٌ أَمْ يَا رَبِّ أُنْثَى يَا رَبِّ شَقِيٌّ أَمْ سَعِيدٌ فَمَا الرِّزْقُ فَمَا الأَجَلُ فَيُكْتَبُ كَذَلِكَ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah has appointed an angel in the womb, and the angel says, 'O Lord! A drop of discharge (i.e. of semen), O Lord! a clot, O Lord! a piece of flesh.' And then, if Allah wishes to complete the child's creation, the angel will say. 'O Lord! A male or a female? O Lord! wretched or blessed (in religion)? What will his livelihood be? What will his age be?' The angel writes all this while the child is in the womb of its mother

bukhari:3333.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *ʿalaqah* means a "leech-like clinging embryo" rather than a blood clot, and claim (citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*) that the angel asking about the fetus's sex after the *muḍghah* stage merely describes the outward anatomical differentiation of the genitalia rather than when biological sex is determined. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly places the decree of biological sex *after* the *nuṭfah*, *ʿalaqah*, and *muḍghah* stages (`فَإِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَهَا قَالَ يَا رَبِّ، أَذَكَرٌ أَمْ يَا رَبِّ أُنْثَى`), which parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:3208, muslim:6726) date to 42 or 120 days—contradicting the biological reality that sex is fixed at fertilization and that human embryos never form out of a congealed blood clot (*ʿalaqah*) or unformed lump of flesh (*muḍghah*). Furthermore, because the angel asks in the exact same breath whether the child will be eternally damned or saved (`شَقِيٌّ أَمْ سَعِيدٌ`), the text undeniably describes a literal, post-conception divine decision rather than physical organ development.

bukhari:5757.note: Muhammad declares that there is no infectious contagion (*lā ʿadwā*, left untranslated in the English rendering), grouping disease transmission alongside pre-Islamic superstitions such as evil bird-omens (*ṭiyarah*) and owl-spirits (*hāmah*). Although commentators interpolate "without Allah's permission" to harmonize this negation with his command to flee from a leper (bukhari:5707), parallel reports confirm a literal denial of transmission when he dismisses a Bedouin's observation that a mangy camel infects a healthy herd by asking, "Then who infected the first one?" (bukhari:5717, muslim:5788).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لاَ عَدْوَى، وَلاَ طِيَرَةَ، وَلاَ هَامَةَ، وَلاَ صَفَرَ
problematic_excerpt.english: There is no 'Adwa, nor Tiyara, nor Hama, nor Safar

bukhari:5757.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—that *lā ʿadwā* ('there is no contagion') merely negates the pre-Islamic belief that diseases transmit autonomously apart from Allah's will, appealing to commands like 'flee from the leper' (bukhari:5707) as proof of quarantine. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly uses the absolute categorical negation *lā nāfiyah lil-jins* ('there is no contagion whatsoever') to classify contagion alongside purely imaginary superstitions (*ṭiyarah* bird-omens and *hāmah* owl-spirits), and in bukhari:5717, when a Bedouin objects that one mangy camel visibly infects a healthy herd, Muhammad rejects biological transmission by asking, 'Then who infected the first one?' (*fa-man aʿdā al-awwal?*). Indeed, this contradiction between denying contagion and fearing lepers was so irreconcilable that Abu Hurayrah later tried to deny ever narrating *lā ʿadwā* until his peers publicly confronted him for changing his story (bukhari:5771, 5774).

muslim:7163.note: Muhammad declares that Allah created Adam sixty cubits tall and that everyone who enters Paradise will enter in Adam's sixty-cubit form. The Arabic text further states that human stature has continuously diminished after him down to the present day (fa-lam yazal al-khalqu yanquṣu baʿdahu ḥattā al-ān), precluding claims that the reduction occurred only once upon leaving Paradise.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ آدَمَ عَلَى صُورَتِهِ طُولُهُ سِتُّونَ ذِرَاعًا فَلَمَّا خَلَقَهُ قَالَ اذْهَبْ فَسَلِّمْ عَلَى أُولَئِكَ النَّفَرِ وَهُمْ نَفَرٌ مِنَ الْمَلاَئِكَةِ جُلُوسٌ فَاسْتَمِعْ مَا يُجِيبُونَكَ فَإِنَّهَا تَحِيَّتُكَ وَتَحِيَّةُ ذُرِّيَّتِكَ قَالَ فَذَهَبَ فَقَالَ السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ فَقَالُوا السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ - قَالَ - فَزَادُوهُ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ - قَالَ - فَكُلُّ مَنْ يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ عَلَى صُورَةِ آدَمَ وَطُولُهُ سِتُّونَ ذِرَاعًا فَلَمْ يَزَلِ الْخَلْقُ يَنْقُصُ بَعْدَهُ حَتَّى الآنَ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, created Adam in His image with His length of sixty cubits, and as He created him He told him to greet that group, and that was a party of angels sitting there, and listen to the response that they give him, for it would form his greeting and that of his offspring. He then went away and said: Peace be upon you! They (the angels) said: May there be peace upon you and the Mercy of Allah, and they made an addition of" Mercy of Allah". So he who would get into Paradise would get in the form of Adam, his length being sixty cubits, then the people who followed him continued to diminish in size up to this day

muslim:7163.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Adam's sixty-cubit stature applied only to his existence in Paradise before descending to earth, or that humanity's height was reduced all at once rather than gradually over history. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *falam yazal al-khalqu yanquṣu baʿdahu ḥattā al-ān* ('then the people who followed him continued to diminish in size up to this day'), where the construction *lam yazal* with the imperfect verb *yanquṣu* denotes an unbroken, continuous diminution across earthly generations down to the speaker's own time. Parallel narrations in bukhari:3326 and bukhari:6227 confirm this literal sixty-cubit measurement and ongoing physical decrease.

muslim:7163.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:7163.subcategory: Divine Immanence, Entering Creation & Visible Form (Incarnation Precedents)
muslim:7163.note: Muhammad declares that Allah created Adam 'in His image' (ʿalā ṣūratihi) with a length of sixty cubits, conceding the Christian doctrine that man was created in the image of God. Because Allah is the sole preceding referent and grammatical subject of the clause (khalaqa Allāhu ʿazza wa-jalla Ādama ʿalā ṣūratihi), the possessive pronoun in 'His image' refers to Allah rather than back to Adam.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ آدَمَ عَلَى صُورَتِهِ طُولُهُ سِتُّونَ ذِرَاعًا
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, created Adam in His image with His length of sixty cubits

muslim:7163.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the possessive pronoun in *ʿalā ṣūratihi* ('in his image') refers back to Adam rather than to Allah, claiming it merely means Adam was created directly in his own full-grown, sixty-cubit form without passing through childhood. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *khalaqa Allāhu ʿazza wa-jalla Ādama ʿalā ṣūratihi* ('Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, created Adam in His image') and then later specifies that everyone who enters Paradise will enter *ʿalā ṣūrati Ādama* ('in the form of Adam'). This shift from the pronoun in *ʿalā ṣūratihi* (referring to the grammatical subject, Allah) to the explicit noun phrase *ʿalā ṣūrati Ādama* later in the same narration—paralleled in bukhari:6227—refutes the claim that the opening pronoun meant Adam's own form.

muslim:7414.note: Muhammad declares that every part of the human body decays (*yablā*) except a single bone (*ʿaẓman wāḥidan*)—the tailbone (*ʿajb al-dhanab*)—from which resurrected bodies are reconstituted and sprout like vegetables (*al-baql*) when water descends from the sky (bukhari:4814, bukhari:4935, muslim:7415). This explicit claim regarding the physical preservation of a specific bone is an empirical anatomical error, as the human coccyx decomposes and disintegrates just like the rest of the skeleton.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ‏"‏ ثُمَّ يُنْزِلُ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَيَنْبُتُونَ كَمَا يَنْبُتُ الْبَقْلُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ وَلَيْسَ مِنَ الإِنْسَانِ شَىْءٌ إِلاَّ يَبْلَى إِلاَّ عَظْمًا وَاحِدًا وَهُوَ عَجْبُ الذَّنَبِ وَمِنْهُ يُرَكَّبُ الْخَلْقُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Then Allah would cause the water to, descend from the sky and they (people) will sprout like vegetable. The only thing in a man which would not decay would be one bone (the tailbone) from which the whole frame would be reconstituted on the Day of Resurrection

muslim:7414.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *ʿajb al-dhanab* does not refer to the macroscopic anatomical tailbone, but rather to an invisible microscopic particle, embryonic stem cell, or metaphysical seed that survives physical destruction. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `إِلاَّ عَظْمًا وَاحِدًا وَهُوَ عَجْبُ الذَّنَبِ` ("except one bone, and it is the tailbone"), using the literal anatomical noun *ʿaẓman* ("a bone") and asserting that every part of a human decays (`يَبْلَى`) except this single bone. By tying bodily reconstitution (`وَمِنْهُ يُرَكَّبُ الْخَلْقُ`) and sprouting like vegetables (`فَيَنْبُتُونَ كَمَا يَنْبُتُ الْبَقْلُ`) directly to the physical survival of a bone that empirically decomposes and burns to ash, the text rules out any non-skeletal reinterpretation.

muslim:7415.note: Muhammad declares that the earth consumes every part of the human body except the tailbone (*ʿajb al-dhanab*), from which man was originally created (*minhu khuliqa*) and from which he will be reassembled (*wa-fīhi yurakkabu*). This statement contains two anatomical and embryological errors, as the human coccyx decomposes like other bones and is not the initial structure from which the human body develops.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ كُلُّ ابْنِ آدَمَ يَأْكُلُهُ التُّرَابُ إِلاَّ عَجْبَ الذَّنَبِ مِنْهُ خُلِقَ وَفِيهِ يُرَكَّبُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:The earth would consume all of the son of Adam except his tailbone. From it he was created, and from it he will be recreated (on the Day of Resurrection)

muslim:7415.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *ʿajb al-dhanab* refers to a microscopic, unobservable cellular remnant or the embryonic primitive streak rather than the macroscopic coccyx bone itself. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *"kullu ibni Ādama yaʾkuluhu al-turābu illā ʿajba al-dhanabi minhu khuliqa wa-fīhi yurakkabu"* ("The earth would consume all of the son of Adam except his tailbone. From it he was created, and from it he will be recreated"), naming the anatomical tailbone in the soil (*al-turāb*) as the physical structure exempt from decay and the original source of human creation (*minhu khuliqa*). In reality, the physical coccyx decomposes and disintegrates like all other skeletal bones, and the human embryo develops from a fertilized cell long before any tailbone is formed.

bukhari:4935.note: Muhammad declares that every part of the human body decays except a single bone—the coccyx ('ajb adh-dhanab)—from which human bodies will sprout like vegetation when Allah sends rain on the Day of Resurrection (cf. bukhari:4814). Classical commentators such as Ibn Ḥajar and al-Nawawī affirm this as a literal Prophetic teaching on the physical imperishability of the coccyx, even though the human tailbone decomposes and incinerates like any other bone.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ يُنْزِلُ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً‏.‏ فَيَنْبُتُونَ كَمَا يَنْبُتُ الْبَقْلُ لَيْسَ مِنَ الإِنْسَانِ شَىْءٌ إِلاَّ يَبْلَى إِلاَّ عَظْمًا وَاحِدًا وَهْوَ عَجْبُ الذَّنَبِ، وَمِنْهُ يُرَكَّبُ الْخَلْقُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
problematic_excerpt.english: "Then (after this period) Allah will send water from the sky and then the dead bodies will grow like vegetation grows, There is nothing of the human body that does not decay except one bone; that is the little bone at the end of the coccyx of which the human body will be recreated on the Day of Resurrection."

bukhari:4935.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that 'ajb adh-dhanab refers either to the embryonic 'primitive streak' or to an invisible, microscopic particle within the tailbone that miraculously survives cremation and decomposition (as suggested by modern scientific-miracle apologists and Ibn Hajar's Fath al-Bari). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that what never decays (yabla) is 'one bone, and it is the coccyx' (إِلَّا عَظْمًا وَاحِدًا وَهْوَ عَجْبُ الذَّنَبِ), identifying a literal anatomical bone rather than a subatomic particle or a transient embryonic feature that vanishes before birth. Because the physical coccyx completely disintegrates through cremation, acid, or prolonged burial, the narration merely repeats the 5th-century AD rabbinic folk myth of the indestructible luz bone at the base of the spine (Genesis Rabbah 28:3; Ecclesiastes Rabbah 12:5) from which heavenly moisture sprouts the resurrected body.

muslim:716.note: Answering a Jewish rabbi, Muhammad declares that a man's fluid (*māʾ*) is white and a woman's fluid is yellow, and that when they meet, a child is male if the man's semen (*maniyy*) rises above the woman's semen and female if the woman's semen rises above the man's (cf. muslim:717, bukhari:3329). After the rabbi departs, Muhammad states that he had no prior knowledge of any of these matters until Allah revealed them to him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ جِئْتُ أَسْأَلُكَ عَنِ الْوَلَدِ قَالَ ‏"‏ مَاءُ الرَّجُلِ أَبْيَضُ وَمَاءُ الْمَرْأَةِ أَصْفَرُ فَإِذَا اجْتَمَعَا فَعَلاَ مَنِيُّ الرَّجُلِ مَنِيَّ الْمَرْأَةِ أَذْكَرَا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَإِذَا عَلاَ مَنِيُّ الْمَرْأَةِ مَنِيَّ الرَّجُلِ آنَثَا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ الْيَهُودِيُّ لَقَدْ صَدَقْتَ وَإِنَّكَ لَنَبِيٌّ ثُمَّ انْصَرَفَ فَذَهَبَ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لَقَدْ سَأَلَنِي هَذَا عَنِ الَّذِي سَأَلَنِي عَنْهُ وَمَا لِي عِلْمٌ بِشَىْءٍ مِنْهُ حَتَّى أَتَانِيَ اللَّهُ بِهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He then said: I have come to ask you about the child. He (the Holy Prophet) said: The reproductive substance of man is white and that of woman (i. e. ovum central portion) yellow, and when they have sexual intercourse and the male's substance (chromosomes and genes) prevails upon the female's substance (chromosomes and genes), it is the male child that is created by Allah's Decree, and when the substance of the female prevails upon the substance contributed by the male, a female child is formed by the Decree of Allah. The Jew said: What you have said is true; verily you are an Apostle. He then returned and went away. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: He asked me about such and such things of which I have had no knowledge till Allah gave me that

muslim:716.literal_translation: He said: 'I have come to ask you about the child.' He said: 'The fluid of the man is white and the fluid of the woman is yellow. When they meet and the man's semen rises above the woman's semen, they produce a male by Allah's permission; and when the woman's semen rises above the man's semen, they produce a female by Allah's permission.' The Jew said: 'You have spoken the truth, and indeed you are a prophet.' Then he turned and went away. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'This man asked me about what he asked me, and I had no knowledge of any of it until Allah brought it to me.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: مَاءُ الرَّجُلِ أَبْيَضُ وَمَاءُ الْمَرْأَةِ أَصْفَرُ فَإِذَا اجْتَمَعَا فَعَلاَ مَنِيُّ الرَّجُلِ مَنِيَّ الْمَرْأَةِ أَذْكَرَا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ
translation_issue.published_rendering: The reproductive substance of man is white and that of woman (i. e. ovum central portion) yellow, and when they have sexual intercourse and the male's substance (chromosomes and genes) prevails upon the female's substance (chromosomes and genes), it is the male child that is created by Allah's Decree
translation_issue.literal_meaning: The fluid of the man is white and the fluid of the woman is yellow; when they meet and the man's semen rises above the woman's semen, they produce a male by Allah's permission
translation_issue.explanation: The translator replaces 'māʾ' (fluid/water) and 'maniyy' (semen/ejaculate) with 'reproductive substance' and interpolates modern scientific terms ('ovum central portion', 'chromosomes and genes') to disguise the ancient Galenic two-semen error.

muslim:716.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the woman's 'yellow fluid' (māʾ al-marʾah aṣfar) refers to the ovum or yellow follicular fluid and that one substance 'prevailing' (ʿalā) describes chromosomes and genes—as interpolated directly into Abdul Hamid Siddiqui's English translation—or else claim Muhammad was merely echoing 7th-century AD medical custom rather than speaking by revelation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the woman discharges actual semen (maniyy al-marʾah, مَنِيُّ الْمَرْأَةِ)—which parallel narrations (Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:710 and Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3329) define as a visible orgasmic fluid requiring ritual bathing (ghusl)—and asserts that a female child is formed when the woman's semen rises above the man's (wa-idhā ʿalā maniyyu al-marʾati maniyya al-rajuli ānathā), whereas biological sex is determined exclusively by the father's X or Y sperm chromosome. Furthermore, Muhammad himself forecloses any 'cultural opinion' excuse in the final sentence by declaring, 'I had no knowledge of any of it until Allah brought it to me' (wa-mā lī ʿilmun bi-shayʾin minhu ḥattā atāniya Allāhu bihi), directly attributing this 2nd-century AD Galenic and Talmudic (Niddah 31a) two-semen error to divine revelation.

bukhari:3199.note: At sunset, Muhammad asks Abu Dharr where the sun goes and explains that it travels until it prostrates beneath the Throne and asks permission to rise again, citing this as the meaning of [Quran 36:38](quran://36/38). He adds that a time will come when its prostration and request for permission are rejected, and it will be ordered to return from where it came and rise from the west.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لأَبِي ذَرٍّ حِينَ غَرَبَتِ الشَّمْسُ ‏"‏ تَدْرِي أَيْنَ تَذْهَبُ ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْتُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِنَّهَا تَذْهَبُ حَتَّى تَسْجُدَ تَحْتَ الْعَرْشِ، فَتَسْتَأْذِنَ فَيُؤْذَنَ لَهَا، وَيُوشِكُ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ فَلاَ يُقْبَلَ مِنْهَا، وَتَسْتَأْذِنَ فَلاَ يُؤْذَنَ لَهَا، يُقَالُ لَهَا ارْجِعِي مِنْ حَيْثُ جِئْتِ‏.‏ فَتَطْلُعُ مِنْ مَغْرِبِهَا، فَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى ‏{‏وَالشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَهَا ذَلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ ‏}‏‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) asked me at sunset, "Do you know where the sun goes (at the time of sunset)?" I replied, "Allah and His Apostle know better." He said, "It goes (i.e. travels) till it prostrates Itself underneath the Throne and takes the permission to rise again, and it is permitted and then (a time will come when) it will be about to prostrate itself but its prostration will not be accepted, and it will ask permission to go on its course but it will not be permitted, but it will be ordered to return whence it has come and so it will rise in the west. And that is the interpretation of the Statement of Allah: "And the sun Runs its fixed course For a term (decreed). that is The Decree of (Allah) The Exalted in Might, The All- Knowing

bukhari:3199.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the sun's prostration (sujūd) is merely a metaphor for its submission to natural law, or that because Allah's Throne (al-'Arsh) encompasses the entire cosmos, the sun remains perpetually beneath it during a continuous orbit without ever stopping at night. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that at the specific moment of earthly sunset (ḥīna gharabati al-shamsu), the sun travels until it prostrates beneath the Throne (fa-innahā tadhhabu ḥattā tasjuda taḥta al-'arshi) and awaits permission to rise again, before one day being ordered to physically reverse its course and rise from the west (irji'ī min ḥaythu ji'ti fa-taṭlu'u min maghribihā). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:4802, 7424; muslim:399) explicitly define the sun's Quranic 'resting place' (mustaqarr in Quran 36:38) as this nightly station beneath the Throne, and classical commentators like Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) and Ibn Hajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) affirm that the sun's prostration and speech are literal (ḥaqīqah), exposing a geocentric cosmology in which the sun physically departs from a stationary earth after sunset.

muslim:6725.note: Muhammad states that an angel enters upon the conceptus while it is still a drop of fluid (*nutfah*) after 40 or 45 nights in the womb and asks Allah whether it will be male or female, at which point its sex is decreed and written (muslim:6723, muslim:6726, bukhari:318). In human biology, genetic sex is determined at fertilization rather than six weeks into gestation, when the conceptus is no longer a drop of fluid.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏ "‏ يَدْخُلُ الْمَلَكُ عَلَى النُّطْفَةِ بَعْدَ مَا تَسْتَقِرُّ فِي الرَّحِمِ بِأَرْبَعِينَ أَوْ خَمْسَةٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً فَيَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ أَشَقِيٌّ أَوْ سَعِيدٌ فَيُكْتَبَانِ فَيَقُولُ أَىْ رَبِّ أَذَكَرٌ أَوْ أُنْثَى فَيُكْتَبَانِ وَيُكْتَبُ عَمَلُهُ وَأَثَرُهُ وَأَجَلُهُ وَرِزْقُهُ ثُمَّ تُطْوَى الصُّحُفُ فَلاَ يُزَادُ فِيهَا وَلاَ يُنْقَصُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When the drop of (semen) remains in the womb for forty or forty five nights, the angel comes and says: My Lord, will he be good or evil? And both these things would be written. Then the angel says: My Lord, would he be male or female? And both these things are written. And his deeds and actions, his death, his livelihood; these are also recorded. Then his document of destiny is rolled and there is no addition to nor subtraction from it

muslim:6725.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the forty-to-forty-five-night mark refers to the physical differentiation of gonads rather than genetic sex determination at fertilization, and that nuṭfah is used broadly for the early conceptus. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the angel enters upon the drop of fluid (yadkhulu al-malaku 'alā al-nuṭfah) after it has settled in the womb for forty or forty-five nights and asks Allah whether it will be male or female (a-dhakarun aw unthā), whereupon the decree is written (fa-yuktabān). By calling the six-week embryo a nuṭfah and depicting the angel as asking Allah to decide its sex only after forty nights, the narration places both the fluid stage and sex determination weeks after fertilization.

muslim:6725.note: Muhammad states through Hudhayfah ibn Usayd that the angel enters upon the drop of fluid (*nutfah*) after 40 or 45 nights to record its deeds, lifespan, provision, and whether it is wretched or blessed, after which the scrolls are rolled up with nothing added or subtracted. This timeline conflicts with the reports in muslim:6723, bukhari:3208, and bukhari:6594, which state that the angel is sent to write these four decrees only after three sequential 40-day stages of drop, clot, and lump totaling 120 days.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏ "‏ يَدْخُلُ الْمَلَكُ عَلَى النُّطْفَةِ بَعْدَ مَا تَسْتَقِرُّ فِي الرَّحِمِ بِأَرْبَعِينَ أَوْ خَمْسَةٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً فَيَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ أَشَقِيٌّ أَوْ سَعِيدٌ فَيُكْتَبَانِ فَيَقُولُ أَىْ رَبِّ أَذَكَرٌ أَوْ أُنْثَى فَيُكْتَبَانِ وَيُكْتَبُ عَمَلُهُ وَأَثَرُهُ وَأَجَلُهُ وَرِزْقُهُ ثُمَّ تُطْوَى الصُّحُفُ فَلاَ يُزَادُ فِيهَا وَلاَ يُنْقَصُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When the drop of (semen) remains in the womb for forty or forty five nights, the angel comes and says: My Lord, will he be good or evil? And both these things would be written. Then the angel says: My Lord, would he be male or female? And both these things are written. And his deeds and actions, his death, his livelihood; these are also recorded. Then his document of destiny is rolled and there is no addition to nor subtraction from it

muslim:6725.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the drop, clot, and lump stages all occur within a single forty-day period, or that the angel writes the decree once at forty nights and again after 120 days. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the angel enters upon the embryo while it is still a drop of fluid (yadkhulu al-malaku 'alā al-nuṭfah) after forty or forty-five nights (bi-arba'īna aw khamsatin wa-arba'īna laylah), and that once its fate, sex, deeds, lifespan, and provision are written, the scrolls are rolled up with nothing added or subtracted (thumma tuṭwā al-ṣuḥufu fa-lā yuzādu fīhā wa-lā yunqaṣu). This completed recording during the forty-night nuṭfah stage directly conflicts with muslim:6723 and bukhari:3208, which state that the angel is sent to write these same four decrees only after three sequential forty-day stages totaling 120 days.

muslim:6725.note: Muhammad states that after 40 or 45 nights in the womb, an angel asks Allah whether the fetus will be wretched (*shaqī*, damned) or blessed (*sa'īd*, saved) and writes all of its future deeds, traces, lifespan, and provision on scrolls that are then rolled up so nothing can ever be added or subtracted ([Quran 11:105](quran://11/105), muslim:6723, muslim:6726, bukhari:6594).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏ "‏ يَدْخُلُ الْمَلَكُ عَلَى النُّطْفَةِ بَعْدَ مَا تَسْتَقِرُّ فِي الرَّحِمِ بِأَرْبَعِينَ أَوْ خَمْسَةٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً فَيَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ أَشَقِيٌّ أَوْ سَعِيدٌ فَيُكْتَبَانِ فَيَقُولُ أَىْ رَبِّ أَذَكَرٌ أَوْ أُنْثَى فَيُكْتَبَانِ وَيُكْتَبُ عَمَلُهُ وَأَثَرُهُ وَأَجَلُهُ وَرِزْقُهُ ثُمَّ تُطْوَى الصُّحُفُ فَلاَ يُزَادُ فِيهَا وَلاَ يُنْقَصُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When the drop of (semen) remains in the womb for forty or forty five nights, the angel comes and says: My Lord, will he be good or evil? And both these things would be written. Then the angel says: My Lord, would he be male or female? And both these things are written. And his deeds and actions, his death, his livelihood; these are also recorded. Then his document of destiny is rolled and there is no addition to nor subtraction from it

muslim:6725.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the angel's recording of the child's fate and actions in the womb merely reflects divine foreknowledge of future human choices rather than coercive predetermination. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that while the embryo is still a drop of fluid (nuṭfah), the angel asks whether it is wretched or blessed (a-shaqiyyun aw sa'īd)—the exact eschatological terms for the damned and saved in [Quran 11:105](quran://11/105)—and writes its deeds and traces (wa-yuktabu 'amaluhu wa-atharuhu). Furthermore, the narration concludes that the scrolls are immediately rolled up so that nothing is added to or subtracted from them (thumma tuṭwā al-ṣuḥufu fa-lā yuzādu fīhā wa-lā yunqaṣu), establishing a fixed decree of every action and eternal fate before birth, as also recorded in muslim:6723 and bukhari:6594.

muslim:6726.note: Muhammad states that when 42 nights pass over the drop of semen (*nuṭfah*) in the womb, Allah sends an angel to shape it and create its hearing, sight, skin, flesh, and bones, after which the angel asks whether it will be male or female and Allah decrees and records its sex—whereas biological sex is fixed at fertilization.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا مَرَّ بِالنُّطْفَةِ ثِنْتَانِ وَأَرْبَعُونَ لَيْلَةً بَعَثَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهَا مَلَكًا فَصَوَّرَهَا وَخَلَقَ سَمْعَهَا وَبَصَرَهَا وَجِلْدَهَا وَلَحْمَهَا وَعِظَامَهَا ثُمَّ ‏.‏ قَالَ يَا رَبِّ أَذَكَرٌ أَمْ أُنْثَى فَيَقْضِي رَبُّكَ مَا شَاءَ وَيَكْتُبُ الْمَلَكُ
problematic_excerpt.english: When forty-two nights pass after the semen gets into the womb, Allah sends the angel and gives him shape. Then he creates his sense of hearing, sense of sight, his skin, his flesh, his bones, and then says: My Lord, would he be male or female? And your Lord decides as He desires and the angel then puts down that also

muslim:6726.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the forty-two-night mark accurately describes the sixth week of gestation when gonadal differentiation begins, claiming the angel's question refers only to the physical manifestation of sex rather than its initial genetic determination. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the embryo remains a drop of fluid (*bi-al-nuṭfah*) until forty-two nights pass, at which point Allah sends an angel who fashions its hearing, sight, skin, flesh, and bones (*fa-ṣawwarahā wa-khalaqa samʿahā wa-baṣarahā wa-jildahā wa-laḥmahā wa-ʿiẓāmahā*) and only afterward (*thumma*) asks whether it will be male or female, whereupon Allah decrees what He wills (*fa-yaqḍī rabbuka mā shāʾa*)—placing both full organ formation and the decree of biological sex after the forty-second night (`muslim:6725`, `muslim:6728`, `muslim:6729`).

muslim:6726.note: After Abdullah b. Mas'ud declares that the evil/wretched one (*al-shaqī*) is he who is wretched in his mother's womb, Hudhaifa b. Usaid al-Ghifari answers the question of how a man can be wretched without committing any deed (*bi-ghayri ʿamal*) by quoting Muhammad's teaching that at 42 nights an angel writes Allah's decrees for the fetus on a scroll of destiny from which nothing is added or subtracted.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: الشَّقِيُّ مَنْ شَقِيَ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ وَالسَّعِيدُ مَنْ وُعِظَ بِغَيْرِهِ ‏.‏ فَأَتَى رَجُلاً مِنْ أَصْحَابِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُقَالُ لَهُ حُذَيْفَةُ بْنُ أَسِيدٍ الْغِفَارِيُّ فَحَدَّثَهُ بِذَلِكَ مِنْ قَوْلِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ فَقَالَ وَكَيْفَ يَشْقَى رَجُلٌ بِغَيْرِ عَمَلٍ فَقَالَ لَهُ الرَّجُلُ أَتَعْجَبُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ إِذَا مَرَّ بِالنُّطْفَةِ ثِنْتَانِ وَأَرْبَعُونَ لَيْلَةً بَعَثَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهَا مَلَكًا فَصَوَّرَهَا وَخَلَقَ سَمْعَهَا وَبَصَرَهَا وَجِلْدَهَا وَلَحْمَهَا وَعِظَامَهَا ثُمَّ ‏.‏ قَالَ يَا رَبِّ أَذَكَرٌ أَمْ أُنْثَى فَيَقْضِي رَبُّكَ مَا شَاءَ وَيَكْتُبُ الْمَلَكُ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ أَجَلُهُ ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُ رَبُّكَ مَا شَاءَ وَيَكْتُبُ الْمَلَكُ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ رِزْقُهُ ‏.‏ فَيَقْضِي رَبُّكَ مَا شَاءَ وَيَكْتُبُ الْمَلَكُ ثُمَّ يَخْرُجُ الْمَلَكُ بِالصَّحِيفَةِ فِي يَدِهِ فَلاَ يَزِيدُ عَلَى مَا أُمِرَ وَلاَ يَنْقُصُ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Evil one is he who is evil in the womb of his mother and the good one is he who takes a lesson from the (fate of) others. The narrator came to a person from amongst the Companions of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) who was called Hudhaifa b. Usaid Ghifari and said: How can a person be an evil one without (committing an evil) deed? Thereupon the person said to him: You are surprised at this, whereas I have heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying: When forty-two nights pass after the semen gets into the womb, Allah sends the angel and gives him shape. Then he creates his sense of hearing, sense of sight, his skin, his flesh, his bones, and then says: My Lord, would he be male or female? And your Lord decides as He desires and the angel then puts down that also and then says: My Lord, what about his age? And your Lord decides as He likes it and the angel puts it down. Then he says: My Lord, what about his livelihood? And then the Lord decides as He likes and the angel writes it down, and then the angel gets out with his scroll of destiny in his hand and nothing is added to it and nothing is subtracted from it

muslim:6726.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the angel's writing in the womb merely records Allah's passive foreknowledge of a person's future free choices rather than an unalterable decree that condemns someone prior to any moral action. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Hudhaifa b. Usaid cited this prophetic report specifically to silence the question of how a man can be wretched without any deed (*wa-kayfa yashqā rajulun bi-ghayri ʿamal*), demonstrating that the statement 'the wretched one is he who is wretched in the belly of his mother' (*al-shaqī man shaqiya fī baṭni ummihi*) rests on Allah actively deciding what He wills (*fa-yaqḍī rabbuka mā shāʾa*) and sealing a scroll (*bi-al-ṣaḥīfah*) to which nothing commanded is ever added or subtracted (*fa-lā yazīdu ʿalā mā umira wa-lā yanquṣu*), as paralleled in `bukhari:3208`, `muslim:6723`, and `muslim:6725`.

muslim:6728.note: Muhammad states that a drop of semen (*nuṭfah*) remains in the womb for forty nights before an angel gives it shape and asks Allah whether it will be male or female and whether it will be sound (*sawiyy*) or imperfect (*ghayr sawiyy*), at which point Allah makes it male or female and sound or imperfect.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ النُّطْفَةَ تَقَعُ فِي الرَّحِمِ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً ثُمَّ يَتَصَوَّرُ عَلَيْهَا الْمَلَكُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ زُهَيْرٌ حَسِبْتُهُ قَالَ الَّذِي يَخْلُقُهَا ‏"‏ فَيَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ أَذَكَرٌ أَوْ أُنْثَى فَيَجْعَلُهُ اللَّهُ ذَكَرًا أَوْ أُنْثَى ثُمَّ يَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ أَسَوِيٌّ أَوْ غَيْرُ سَوِيٍّ فَيَجْعَلُهُ اللَّهُ سَوِيًّا أَوْ غَيْرَ سَوِيٍّ
problematic_excerpt.english: The semen stays in the womb for forty nights, then the angel, gives it a shape. Zubair said: I think that he said: One who fashions that and decides whether he would be male or female. Then he (the angel) says: Would his limbs be full or imperfect? And then the Lord makes thein full and perfect or otherwise as He desires.

muslim:6728.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration refers to the phenotypic differentiation of the gonads around the sixth week of gestation rather than chromosomal sex determination, or that the angel is merely asking to record what was already set at fertilization. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the semen drop (*al-nuṭfah*) remains in the womb for forty nights and only "then" (*thumma*) does the angel fashion it and ask, "O Lord, male or female?" after which "Allah makes it male or female" (*fayajʿaluhu Allāhu dhakaran aw unthā*). The sequential conjunctions *thumma* ("then") and *fa-* ("so/and then") coupled with the causative verb *yajʿaluhu* ("He makes it") place both embryonic shaping and the determination of biological sex strictly after the forty-night period.

muslim:6728.note: Muhammad declares that after forty nights in the womb, the angel asks Allah about the fetus's livelihood (*rizquhu*), lifespan (*ajaluhu*), and moral disposition (*khuluquhu*), whereafter Allah makes the individual wretched (*shaqiyyan*) or blessed (*saʿīdan*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ يَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ مَا رِزْقُهُ مَا أَجَلُهُ مَا خُلُقُهُ ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ اللَّهُ شَقِيًّا أَوْ سَعِيدًا
problematic_excerpt.english: Then he says: My Lord, what about his livelihood, and his death and what about his disposition? And then the Lord decides about his misfortune and fortune

muslim:6728.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the decree in the womb merely reflects Allah's passive foreknowledge of the moral choices the individual will freely make in life, rather than coercive predestination of their character and eternal destiny. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that after the angel asks, "What is his moral disposition (*mā khuluquhu*)?", "then Allah makes him wretched or blessed" (*thumma yajʿaluhu Allāhu shaqiyyan aw saʿīdan*), employing the active causative verb *yajʿaluhu* ("He makes him") rather than a verb of mere knowing. By placing moral disposition (*khuluquhu*) and eternal fate under the exact same causative decree as biological sex, physical completeness (*asawiyyun aw ghayru sawiyyin*), livelihood (*rizquhu*), and lifespan (*ajaluhu*), the text treats human morality and salvation as pre-natal assignments fixed before birth.

muslim:6730.note: Muhammad states that an angel appointed over the womb reports the embryo progressing from a drop of semen (*nuṭfah*) into a blood clot (*ʿalaqah*) and then a lump of flesh (*muḍghah*), and only when Allah wills to complete its creation after the *muḍghah* stage does the angel ask whether it will be male or female—whereas human embryos never develop from a blood clot and biological sex is determined at fertilization.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ قَدْ وَكَّلَ بِالرَّحِمِ مَلَكًا فَيَقُولُ أَىْ رَبِّ نُطْفَةٌ أَىْ رَبِّ عَلَقَةٌ أَىْ رَبِّ مُضْغَةٌ ‏.‏ فَإِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَقْضِيَ خَلْقًا - قَالَ - قَالَ الْمَلَكُ أَىْ رَبِّ ذَكَرٌ أَوْ أُنْثَى شَقِيٌّ أَوْ سَعِيدٌ فَمَا الرِّزْقُ فَمَا الأَجَلُ فَيُكْتَبُ كَذَلِكَ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah, the Exlated and Glorious, has appointed an angel as the caretaker of the womb, and he would say: My Lord, it is now a drop of semen; my Lord, It is now a clot of blood; my Lord, it has now become a lump of flesh, and when Allah decides to give it a final shape, the angel says: My Lord, would it be male or female or would he be an evil or a good person? What about his livelihood and his age? And it is all written as he is in the womb of his mother

muslim:6730.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *ʿalaqah* denotes a clinging substance rather than a blood clot, and that the angel asking whether the fetus is male or female after the *muḍghah* stage merely describes the angel learning and recording a sex already fixed at conception. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that only after the embryo sequentially becomes a *nuṭfah* (drop of semen), *ʿalaqah* (clot of blood), and *muḍghah* (lump of flesh) does the conditional clause *fa-idhā arāda Allāhu an yaqḍiya khalqan* ('and when Allah decides to decree its creation') take effect, prompting the angel to ask, *ay rabbi dhakarun aw unthā* ('My Lord, male or female?'). By grouping biological sex alongside unfixed decrees such as livelihood (*al-rizq*) and lifespan (*al-ajal*) after the *muḍghah* stage (as also recorded in bukhari:318 and bukhari:6595), the text presents sex determination itself as a post-*muḍghah* divine decree rather than a genetic reality fixed at fertilization.

muslim:6730.note: Muhammad declares that when Allah wills to complete the creation of a fetus, the angel of the womb asks whether the child will be wretched (*shaqī*) or blessed (*saʿīd*), and its status, provision, and lifespan are decreed and written while it is still in its mother's womb.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَإِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَقْضِيَ خَلْقًا - قَالَ - قَالَ الْمَلَكُ أَىْ رَبِّ ذَكَرٌ أَوْ أُنْثَى شَقِيٌّ أَوْ سَعِيدٌ فَمَا الرِّزْقُ فَمَا الأَجَلُ فَيُكْتَبُ كَذَلِكَ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: and when Allah decides to give it a final shape, the angel says: My Lord, would it be male or female or would he be an evil or a good person? What about his livelihood and his age? And it is all written as he is in the womb of his mother

muslim:6730.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that writing whether a fetus will be *shaqī* (wretched/evil) or *saʿīd* (blessed/good) in the womb merely reflects Allah's passive foreknowledge of future free choices rather than deterministic compulsion. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that this inscription occurs under the governing clause *fa-idhā arāda Allāhu an yaqḍiya khalqan* ('and when Allah decides to decree its creation'), framing the moral outcome as an active divine decree (*yaqḍiya*) rather than passive observation. Furthermore, the angel groups *shaqiyyun aw saʿīd* ('wretched or blessed') directly alongside involuntary, unchosen parameters—biological sex (*dhakarun aw unthā*), livelihood (*al-rizq*), and lifespan (*al-ajal*)—all of which are identically decreed and written in the mother's womb (*fa-yuktabu kadhālika fī baṭni ummihi*, cf. bukhari:6595 and muslim:6723) prior to birth or moral agency.

bukhari:7424.note: Muhammad states that when the sun sets, it goes to ask permission to prostrate before being permitted to continue, and that one day it will be ordered to return and rise from the west. While this specific narration does not state the location of the prostration, parallel reports (bukhari:3199, bukhari:4802) explicitly specify that it prostrates beneath the Throne of Allah.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: يَا أَبَا ذَرٍّ هَلْ تَدْرِي أَيْنَ تَذْهَبُ هَذِهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِنَّهَا تَذْهَبُ تَسْتَأْذِنُ فِي السُّجُودِ فَيُؤْذَنُ لَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: "O Abu Dharr! Do you know where this (sun) goes?" I said, "Allah and His Apostle know best." He said, "It goes and asks permission to prostrate, and it is allowed

bukhari:7424.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the sun's prostration is either a metaphorical expression of its submission to natural laws or an unseen metaphysical reality (*al-ghayb*) cited by Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar that does not contradict a heliocentric solar system. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that this journey happens specifically after sunset (*falammā gharabat al-shams*) and directly governs the physical direction of sunrise, stating that when ordered *"irji'ī min ḥaythu ji'ti"* ("return from where you came"), *"fataṭlu'u min maghribihā"* ("it will rise from its place of setting"). Parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:3199, muslim:399) further confirm a literal geocentric cosmology in which the sun physically travels beneath Allah's Throne every night and must receive permission before rising in the east each morning.

bukhari:7424.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:7424.note: The Arabic text records a variant reading of [Quran 36:38](quran://36/38) attributed to the recitation of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ("That is a resting place for it"), which diverges from the standardized Uthmanic consonantal text. The published English translation omits this variant wording and substitutes the standard Uthmanic verse in its place.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ قَرَأَ ‏{‏ذَلِكَ مُسْتَقَرٌّ لَهَا‏}‏ فِي قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
problematic_excerpt.english:
Then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited, "That: "And the sun runs on its fixed course (for a term decreed)," (36.38) as it is recited by `Abdullah

[omitted from the english translation: {That is a resting place for it}]

bukhari:7424.literal_translation: Then he recited '{That is a resting place for it}' in the recitation of Abdullah.

translation_issue.arabic_term: ذَلِكَ مُسْتَقَرٌّ لَهَا
translation_issue.published_rendering: "That: "And the sun runs on its fixed course (for a term decreed)," (36.38)
translation_issue.literal_meaning: That is a resting place for it
translation_issue.explanation: The translator omitted the non-standard wording attributed to the recitation of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (leaving only the stray word 'That:') and substituted the standard Uthmanic text of Quran 36:38 to conceal the textual discrepancy.

bukhari:7424.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that Abdullah ibn Mas'ud's reading was merely a non-canonical explanatory gloss (*qirā'ah tafsīriyyah*) or an abrogated dialect (*ḥarf*) that does not challenge the word-for-word preservation of the standard Uthmanic text of Quran 36:38 (*dhālika taqdīru al-'azīzi al-'alīm*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *"thumma qara'a: {dhālika mustaqarrun lahā} fī qirā'ati 'Abdillāh"* ("then he recited: {That is a resting place for it} in the recitation of Abdullah"), attributing this variant wording directly to Muhammad's own formal Quranic recitation (*qara'a*) rather than a Companion's commentary. Moreover, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:4802, muslim:399) record Ibn Mas'ud reciting another conflicting variant (*lā mustaqarra lahā* — "there is no resting place for it"), proving that divergent, non-Uthmanic wordings of Quran 36:38 were taught as scripture before Uthman burned competing codices.

bukhari:130.note: Muhammad rules that a woman must perform ritual bathing after a wet dream if she visibly sees her fluid discharge (al-ma'), and declares to Umm Salamah that this female fluid is what causes a child to resemble its mother.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: جَاءَتْ أُمُّ سُلَيْمٍ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يَسْتَحْيِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ، فَهَلْ عَلَى الْمَرْأَةِ مِنْ غُسْلٍ إِذَا احْتَلَمَتْ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِذَا رَأَتِ الْمَاءَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَغَطَّتْ أُمُّ سَلَمَةَ ـ تَعْنِي وَجْهَهَا ـ وَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَتَحْتَلِمُ الْمَرْأَةُ قَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ تَرِبَتْ يَمِينُكِ فَبِمَ يُشْبِهُهَا وَلَدُهَا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Um-Sulaim came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said, "Verily, Allah is not shy of (telling you) the truth. Is it necessary for a woman to take a bath after she has a wet dream (nocturnal sexual discharge?) The Prophet replied, "Yes, if she notices a discharge." Um Salama, then covered her face and asked, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Does a woman get a discharge?" He replied, "Yes, let your right hand be in dust (An Arabic expression you say to a person when you contradict his statement meaning "you will not achieve goodness"), and that is why the son resembles his mother

bukhari:130.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the female "water" (al-mā') mentioned here is a miraculous 7th-century AD reference to the microscopic ovum or follicular fluid carrying maternal DNA. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that this fluid is a visible nocturnal discharge noticed upon waking from a wet dream (idhā iḥtalamat... idhā ra'at al-mā'), and parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:3328, muslim:712) further describe it as a "thin, yellow fluid" (raqīq aṣfar) that determines the child's resemblance based on which parent climaxes first. Because a microscopic ovum is neither a visible yellow fluid nor emitted during an erotic dream, the narration clearly reflects ancient Hippocratic and Galenic two-seed embryology rather than modern genetics.

muslim:399.note: Muhammad declares that the sun travels to its resting place (*mustaqarr*) beneath Allah's Throne, where it falls prostrate and remains until it is commanded to return and rise in the morning from its rising place, until the day when it will be ordered to rise from its setting place. Parallel reports explicitly state that this daily journey occurs when the sun sets and cite [Quran 36:38](quran://36/38) as its scriptural basis (bukhari:3199, bukhari:4802, muslim:401).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ يَوْمًا ‏"‏ أَتَدْرُونَ أَيْنَ تَذْهَبُ هَذِهِ الشَّمْسُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ هَذِهِ تَجْرِي حَتَّى تَنْتَهِيَ إِلَى مُسْتَقَرِّهَا تَحْتَ الْعَرْشِ فَتَخِرُّ سَاجِدَةً وَلاَ تَزَالُ كَذَلِكَ حَتَّى يُقَالَ لَهَا ارْتَفِعِي ارْجِعِي مِنْ حَيْثُ جِئْتِ فَتَرْجِعُ فَتُصْبِحُ طَالِعَةً مِنْ مَطْلِعِهَا ثُمَّ تَجْرِي حَتَّى تَنْتَهِيَ إِلَى مُسْتَقَرِّهَا تَحْتَ الْعَرْشِ فَتَخِرُّ سَاجِدَةً وَلاَ تَزَالُ كَذَلِكَ حَتَّى يُقَالَ لَهَا ارْتَفِعِي ارْجِعِي مِنْ حَيْثُ جِئْتِ فَتَرْجِعُ فَتُصْبِحُ طَالِعَةً مِنْ مَطْلِعِهَا ثُمَّ تَجْرِي لاَ يَسْتَنْكِرُ النَّاسُ مِنْهَا شَيْئًا حَتَّى تَنْتَهِيَ إِلَى مُسْتَقَرِّهَا ذَاكَ تَحْتَ الْعَرْشِ فَيُقَالُ لَهَا ارْتَفِعِي أَصْبِحِي طَالِعَةً مِنْ مَغْرِبِكِ فَتُصْبِحُ طَالِعَةً مِنْ مَغْرِبِهَا ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Do you know where the sun goes? They replied: Allah and His Apostle know best. He (the Holy Prophet) observed: Verily it (the sun) glides till it reaches its resting place under the Throne. Then it falls prostrate and remains there until it is asked: Rise up and go to the place whence you came, and it goes back and continues emerging out from its rising place and then glides till it reaches its place of rest under the Throne and falls prostrate and remains in that state until it is asked: Rise up and return to the place whence you came, and it returns and emerges out from it rising place and the it glides (in such a normal way) that the people do not discern anything ( unusual in it) till it reaches its resting place under the Throne. Then it would be said to it: Rise up and emerge out from the place of your setting, and it will rise from the place of its setting.

muslim:399.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the sun's prostration under the Throne is merely a metaphorical description of its continuous submission to natural law—since the entire cosmos is perpetually beneath Allah's Throne—or that its 'resting place' (*mustaqarr*) in Quran 36:38 refers to the modern astronomical concept of the solar apex. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a sequential, nightly physical journey in which the sun travels until it reaches a specific destination (`حَتَّى تَنْتَهِيَ إِلَى مُسْتَقَرِّهَا تَحْتَ الْعَرْشِ`), remains halted there in prostration (`وَلاَ تَزَالُ كَذَلِكَ حَتَّى يُقَالَ لَهَا`), and is then ordered to 'return from where you came' (`ارْجِعِي مِنْ حَيْثُ جِئْتِ`) to rise at dawn (`فَتُصْبِحُ طَالِعَةً مِنْ مَطْلِعِهَا`). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:3199; muslim:400) record Muhammad asking this question specifically at sunset (`حِينَ غَرَبَتِ الشَّمْسُ`) and explicitly defining Quran 36:38 as this nightly halt beneath the Throne, leading Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) to affirm that the sun's prostration is literal (*ʿalā ẓāhirihi*).

muslim:401.note: After sunset, Muhammad asks Abu Dharr where the sun goes and declares that it travels to seek permission to prostrate, is granted permission, and will eventually be commanded to return from where it came and rise from its setting place ([Quran 36:38](quran://36/38); cf. bukhari:3199, muslim:399).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا غَابَتِ الشَّمْسُ قَالَ ‏"‏ يَا أَبَا ذَرٍّ هَلْ تَدْرِي أَيْنَ تَذْهَبُ هَذِهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِنَّهَا تَذْهَبُ فَتَسْتَأْذِنُ فِي السُّجُودِ فَيُؤْذَنُ لَهَا وَكَأَنَّهَا قَدْ قِيلَ لَهَا ارْجِعِي مِنْ حَيْثُ جِئْتِ فَتَطْلُعُ مِنْ مَغْرِبِهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ فِي قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَذَلِكَ مُسْتَقَرٌّ لَهَا ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When the sun disappeared (from the sight) he said: O Abu Dharr! Do you know where it goes? He (the narrator) said: Allah and His Apostle know best. He (the Holy Prophet) said. Verily it goes and begs permission, for prostration (to Allah) and the permission is granted to it. Once it would be said: Return to the place whence you came, and then it would rise from its setting place. Then he, after the recitation of 'Abdullah recited it: And that is its appointed term

muslim:401.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the sun's prostration (*sujūd*) is merely a metaphor for its continuous submission to cosmic laws or refers to its solar orbit through the galaxy rather than a daily spatial departure after earthly sunset. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly anchors this event to the moment the sun disappears from sight (*fa-lammā ghābati al-shamsu*), asking where it physically goes (*ayna tadhhabu hādhihi*) and stating that it travels away to beg permission to prostrate before eventually being ordered to reverse its spatial trajectory (*irjiʿī min ḥaythu jiʾti fa-taṭluʿu min maghribihā*). Furthermore, both Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) reject the metaphorical excuse, affirming that the sun performs a literal, physical prostration beneath Allah's Throne after setting.

muslim:401.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:401.note: The narration concludes with the recitation of [Quran 36:38](quran://36/38) according to the reading of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (*fī qirāʾati ʿAbdillāh*: *wa-dhālika mustaqarrun lahā*, 'And that is its resting place'), a non-Uthmanic consonantal wording—classified in Sunni scholarship as an irregular (*shādhdh*) or abrogated variant—that differs from the standardized Uthmanic text (*li-mustaqarrin lahā*; cf. bukhari:4803).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِنَّهَا تَذْهَبُ فَتَسْتَأْذِنُ فِي السُّجُودِ فَيُؤْذَنُ لَهَا وَكَأَنَّهَا قَدْ قِيلَ لَهَا ارْجِعِي مِنْ حَيْثُ جِئْتِ فَتَطْلُعُ مِنْ مَغْرِبِهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ فِي قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَذَلِكَ مُسْتَقَرٌّ لَهَا ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He (the Holy Prophet) said. Verily it goes and begs permission, for prostration (to Allah) and the permission is granted to it. Once it would be said: Return to the place whence you came, and then it would rise from its setting place. Then he, after the recitation of 'Abdullah recited it: And that is its appointed term

muslim:401.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the variant phrase *wa-dhālika mustaqarrun lahā* ('And that is its resting place') was merely an explanatory gloss (*qirāʾah tafsīriyyah*) or an abrogated solitary (*shādhdh*) reading that does not compromise the standardized Uthmanic text of Quran 36:38 (*dhālika taqdīru al-ʿazīzi al-ʿalīm*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly identifies this wording as the formal Quranic recitation of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (*thumma qaraʾa fī qirāʾati ʿAbdillāh: wa-dhālika mustaqarrun lahā*), and parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:4803`, `muslim:399`) record Muhammad himself reciting it verbatim to prove the sun stops beneath the Throne. The fact that Ibn Masʿūd—whom Muhammad personally endorsed as the foremost teacher of the Quran (`bukhari:4999`)—preserved a completely different Arabic clause for Quran 36:38 proves that prophetic Quranic readings were excluded from the Uthmanic codex.

muslim:1402.note: Muhammad commands delaying the noon prayer until it cools down during hot weather, declaring that intense heat originates from the exhalation (*fayḥ*) of Hellfire after it complained to its Lord and was permitted two breaths (*nafasayn*) each year—one in winter and one in summer. Classical Sunni commentators such as al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar affirm that the orthodox position takes Hellfire's complaint and two annual exhalations literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*) as the actual physical cause of extreme seasonal heat and cold.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا كَانَ الْحَرُّ فَأَبْرِدُوا عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ فَإِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَذَكَرَ ‏"‏ أَنَّ النَّارَ اشْتَكَتْ إِلَى رَبِّهَا فَأَذِنَ لَهَا فِي كُلِّ عَامٍ بِنَفَسَيْنِ نَفَسٍ فِي الشِّتَاءِ وَنَفَسٍ فِي الصَّيْفِ
problematic_excerpt.english: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: When it is hot, make delay (in the noon prayer) till it cools down, for the intensity of beat is from the Exhalation of Hell; and he also mentioned that Hellfire complained to the Lord (about the congested atmosphere) and so it was permitted to take two exhalations during the whole year, one exhalation during the winter and one exhalation during the summer

muslim:1402.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that describing seasonal temperature extremes as the 'exhalation of Hell' (*fayḥ Jahannam*) is merely a metaphor (*majāz*) meant to remind believers of the Hereafter when experiencing worldly heat and cold. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a literal causal narrative in which the Fire complained to its Lord (`أَنَّ النَّارَ اشْتَكَتْ إِلَى رَبِّهَا`) because its parts were consuming one another (cf. `bukhari:3260`), prompting Allah to grant it two annual breaths (`بِنَفَسَيْنِ نَفَسٍ فِي الشِّتَاءِ وَنَفَسٍ فِي الصَّيْفِ`) as the direct physical reason for delaying the noon prayer. Furthermore, both Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) explicitly refute the metaphorical excuse, affirming that Sunni orthodoxy requires taking this report literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*) as actual heat and bitter frost (*zamharīr*) physically venting from Hell onto the earth.

muslim:1403.note: Muhammad states that after the Fire complained to its Lord that its parts were consuming one another, Allah granted it two annual exhalations—one in winter and one in summer—declaring that whatever cold or bitter cold (*zamharīr*) and heat or scorching heat (*ḥarūr*) people experience originate from the breath of Gehenna. Classical commentators including Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar affirm that the orthodox Sunni majority (*al-jumhūr*) interprets this report literally (*'alā ḥaqīqatihi*) rather than metaphorically.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَتِ النَّارُ رَبِّ أَكَلَ بَعْضِي بَعْضًا فَأْذَنْ لِي أَتَنَفَّسْ ‏.‏ فَأَذِنَ لَهَا بِنَفَسَيْنِ نَفَسٍ فِي الشِّتَاءِ وَنَفَسٍ فِي الصَّيْفِ فَمَا وَجَدْتُمْ مِنْ بَرْدٍ أَوْ زَمْهَرِيرٍ فَمِنْ نَفَسِ جَهَنَّمَ وَمَا وَجَدْتُمْ مِنْ حَرٍّ أَوْ حَرُورٍ فَمِنْ نَفَسِ جَهَنَّمَ
problematic_excerpt.english: The Fire said to the Lord: O Lord! some parts of mine have consumed the others, so allow me to exhale (in order to find some relief from this congestion). It was granted permission to take two exhalations, one exhalation during the winter and the other exhalation during the summer So whatever you perceive in the form of intense cold or hurting cold is from the exhalation of Hell. And whatever you perceive in the form of extreme heat or intense beat is from the exhalation of Hell

muslim:1403.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration is a metaphorical reminder (*majāz*) comparing earthly weather extremes to the afterlife, or that it refers to an unseen metaphysical cause operating behind natural solar seasons. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the actual physical cold and scorching heat humans perceive on earth come directly from Hell venting its congestion ("famā wajadtum min bardin aw zamharīrin famin nafasi jahannama wa mā wajadtum min ḥarrin aw ḥarūrin famin nafasi jahannama"), a causal claim so tangible that Muhammad ordered delaying the noon prayer (muslim:1401) until the exhalation cooled. Furthermore, classical Sunni authorities including Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) explicitly reject metaphorical reinterpretations of this Hadith, affirming that orthodox consensus (*al-jumhūr*) requires taking Hell's speech and its two annual exhalations onto the earth literally (*ʿalā ẓāhirihi*).

bukhari:3328.note: When Umm Salama asks in surprise whether a woman experiences nocturnal emission and discharges fluid (ma'), Muhammad replies by asking how else a child would resemble its mother, directly attributing a child's maternal resemblance to female sexual discharge.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَهَلْ عَلَى الْمَرْأَةِ الْغُسْلُ إِذَا احْتَلَمَتْ قَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ، إِذَا رَأَتِ الْمَاءَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَضَحِكَتْ أُمُّ سَلَمَةَ، فَقَالَتْ تَحْتَلِمُ الْمَرْأَةُ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَبِمَا يُشْبِهُ الْوَلَدُ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Is it obligatory for a woman to take a bath after she gets nocturnal discharge?' He said, 'Yes, if she notices the water (i.e. discharge).' Um Salama smiled and said, 'Does a woman get discharge?' Allah's Apostle said. 'Then why does a child resemble (its mother)?

bukhari:3328.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the 'woman's water' (al-māʾ) mentioned here is a miraculous reference to the female ovum or follicular fluid carrying maternal genetic material, rather than non-reproductive vaginal lubrication. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that ritual bathing after a nocturnal emission (idhā iḥtalamat) is required 'if she visibly sees the fluid' (idhā raʾat al-māʾ), proving it refers to macroscopic external discharge emitted during sexual climax rather than a microscopic, internally ovulated egg. Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3327 and Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:710) confirm that Muhammad was repeating the ancient Greek 'two-seed' theory popularized by Galen in the 2nd century AD, describing this female fluid as 'thin and yellow' (raqīqun aṣfaru) and claiming that a child's resemblance depends on which parent's discharge precedes or overpowers the other.

bukhari:3329.note: Answering `Abdullah bin Salam's test of prophethood and attributing the answer directly to immediate revelation from the angel Gabriel, Muhammad declares that a child resembles the father if the man's fluid precedes the woman's during intercourse, and resembles the mother if her fluid precedes his.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَأَمَّا الشَّبَهُ فِي الْوَلَدِ فَإِنَّ الرَّجُلَ إِذَا غَشِيَ الْمَرْأَةَ فَسَبَقَهَا مَاؤُهُ كَانَ الشَّبَهُ لَهُ، وَإِذَا سَبَقَ مَاؤُهَا كَانَ الشَّبَهُ لَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: As for the resemblance of the child to its parents: If a man has sexual intercourse with his wife and gets discharge first, the child will resemble the father, and if the woman gets discharge first, the child will resemble her.

bukhari:3329.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that 'her fluid' (māʾuhā) refers to the female ovum and that its 'preceding' (sabaqa) or 'prevailing' (ʿalā in bukhari:3938 and Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī) is a metaphor for dominant and recessive genetic alleles. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states 'fa-inna al-rajula idhā ghashiya al-marʾata fa-sabaqahā māʾuhu' ('when a man has intercourse with a woman and his fluid precedes hers'), tying a child's physical resemblance directly to the chronological timing of fluid discharge during the act of coitus rather than pre-existing DNA. Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:130, muslim:710) explicitly define māʾu al-marʾati as the yellow, thin fluid a woman discharges during an erotic wet dream (iḥtilām), proving that Muhammad—despite claiming instantaneous revelation from Gabriel ('khabbaranī bihinna ānifan Jibrīl')—was merely repeating the debunked ancient 'two-seed' theory of reproduction.

muslim:3651.note: Muhammad declares that had it not been for the Children of Israel, food would never spoil and meat would never rot, and that had it not been for Eve, no woman would ever betray her husband. Classical commentators such as Al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar affirm this literally, explaining that meat never decayed prior to the Israelites hoarding quail in the wilderness.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ لَوْلاَ بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ لَمْ يَخْبُثِ الطَّعَامُ وَلَمْ يَخْنَزِ اللَّحْمُ وَلَوْلاَ حَوَّاءُ لَمْ تَخُنْ أُنْثَى زَوْجَهَا الدَّهْرَ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Had it not been for Bani Isra'il, food would not have become stale, and meal would not have gone bad; and had it not been for Eve, a woman would never have acted unfaithfully toward her husband

muslim:3651.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this statement is merely figurative, claiming Muhammad only meant that the Israelites initiated the human habit of hoarding meat long enough for it to spoil rather than asserting that biological putrefaction began with them. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an unconditional physical counterfactual (lawlā Banū Isrāʾīl lam yakhbuth al-ṭaʿām wa-lam yakhnaz al-laḥm—'Had it not been for the Children of Israel, food would not go bad and meat would not rot'), directly attributing the natural phenomenon of food spoilage itself to a 2nd-millennium BC nation. Furthermore, both Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) and Ibn Ḥajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī on bukhari:3330) confirm the literal meaning that Allah caused meat to decay for the very first time in history after the Israelites stored quail in the wilderness, flatly contradicting the biological reality that microbial decomposition existed hundreds of millions of years before humanity.

bukhari:6227.note: Muhammad declares that Allah created Adam sixty cubits (approx. 90 feet / 30 meters) tall and that human stature has continuously diminished from that height down to the present day (bukhari:3326). This claim conflicts with human skeletal biomechanics and the archaeological record—a discrepancy Ibn Hajar acknowledged in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, noting that the ancient rock-hewn dwellings of Thamud prove human height has not continuously shrunk and confessing that he had found no resolution to the problem.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: خَلَقَ اللَّهُ آدَمَ عَلَى صُورَتِهِ، طُولُهُ سِتُّونَ ذِرَاعًا، فَلَمَّا خَلَقَهُ قَالَ اذْهَبْ فَسَلِّمْ عَلَى أُولَئِكَ النَّفَرِ مِنَ الْمَلاَئِكَةِ جُلُوسٌ، فَاسْتَمِعْ مَا يُحَيُّونَكَ، فَإِنَّهَا تَحِيَّتُكَ وَتَحِيَّةُ ذُرِّيَّتِكَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ‏.‏ فَقَالُوا السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ‏.‏ فَزَادُوهُ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ، فَكُلُّ مَنْ يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ عَلَى صُورَةِ آدَمَ، فَلَمْ يَزَلِ الْخَلْقُ يَنْقُصُ بَعْدُ حَتَّى الآنَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah created Adam in His picture, sixty cubits (about 30 meters) in height. When He created him, He said (to him), "Go and greet that group of angels sitting there, and listen what they will say in reply to you, for that will be your greeting and the greeting of your offspring." Adam (went and) said, 'As-Salamu alaikum (Peace be upon you).' They replied, 'AsSalamu-'Alaika wa Rahmatullah (Peace and Allah's Mercy be on you) So they increased 'Wa Rahmatullah' The Prophet (ﷺ) added 'So whoever will enter Paradise, will be of the shape and picture of Adam Since then the creation of Adam's (offspring) (i.e. stature of human beings is being diminished continuously) to the present time

bukhari:6227.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Adam was only sixty cubits tall while in Paradise and was immediately reduced to normal human proportions upon descending to Earth. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "fa-lam yazal al-khalqu yanquṣu baʿdu ḥattā al-ān" ("and creation has continued to diminish ever since until now"), mandating a continuous, gradual shrinkage across earthly generations right up to the seventh century AD. Even Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī admitted in Fatḥ al-Bārī (on bukhari:3326) that this wording creates an unresolved problem because the ancient rock-hewn dwellings of Thamūd prove that bygone generations were not giants.

bukhari:6227.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
bukhari:6227.subcategory: Divine Immanence, Entering Creation & Visible Form (Incarnation Precedents)
bukhari:6227.note: Muhammad declares that 'Allah created Adam in His image (*ʿalā ṣūratihi*),' affirming the exact formula of [Genesis 1:26](bible://gn/1/26) that Muslim polemicists reject as anthropomorphism. While Ashʿarī commentators like al-Nawawī attempt to redirect the pronoun 'His' back to Adam (claiming it merely means Adam was created directly in his own sixty-cubit adult form), Ibn Hajar documented in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* that explicit variant narrations state 'Allah created Adam in the image of the Most Merciful (*ʿalā ṣūrat al-Raḥmān*).'

problematic_excerpt.arabic: خَلَقَ اللَّهُ آدَمَ عَلَى صُورَتِهِ، طُولُهُ سِتُّونَ ذِرَاعًا، فَلَمَّا خَلَقَهُ قَالَ اذْهَبْ فَسَلِّمْ عَلَى أُولَئِكَ النَّفَرِ مِنَ الْمَلاَئِكَةِ جُلُوسٌ، فَاسْتَمِعْ مَا يُحَيُّونَكَ، فَإِنَّهَا تَحِيَّتُكَ وَتَحِيَّةُ ذُرِّيَّتِكَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ‏.‏ فَقَالُوا السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ‏.‏ فَزَادُوهُ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ، فَكُلُّ مَنْ يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ عَلَى صُورَةِ آدَمَ، فَلَمْ يَزَلِ الْخَلْقُ يَنْقُصُ بَعْدُ حَتَّى الآنَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah created Adam in His picture, sixty cubits (about 30 meters) in height. When He created him, He said (to him), "Go and greet that group of angels sitting there, and listen what they will say in reply to you, for that will be your greeting and the greeting of your offspring." Adam (went and) said, 'As-Salamu alaikum (Peace be upon you).' They replied, 'AsSalamu-'Alaika wa Rahmatullah (Peace and Allah's Mercy be on you) So they increased 'Wa Rahmatullah' The Prophet (ﷺ) added 'So whoever will enter Paradise, will be of the shape and picture of Adam Since then the creation of Adam's (offspring) (i.e. stature of human beings is being diminished continuously) to the present time

bukhari:6227.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—following Ashʿarī commentators like al-Nawawī—that the possessive pronoun in ʿalā ṣūratihi ("in his image") refers back to Adam rather than Allah, meaning Allah created Adam directly in his own full-grown human form without developmental stages. However, the primary Arabic text in parallel narrations such as Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:6655 forbids striking the human face "fa-inna Allāha khalaqa Ādama ʿalā ṣūratihi" ("for indeed Allah created Adam in His image"), a rationale that collapses if Adam merely looked like himself, and the explicit prophetic variant cited by Ibn Ḥajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī states verbatim "ʿalā ṣūrati al-Raḥmān" ("in the image of the Most Merciful"), eliminating any pronoun ambiguity.

muslim:1162.note: Muhammad states that Al-Masjid al-Haram in Mecca was the first mosque established on earth and that Al-Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem was built forty years later (bukhari:3366), despite the roughly thousand-year chronological gap between Abraham's raising of the Kaaba ([Quran 2:127](quran://2/127)) and Solomon's construction of the Jerusalem Temple ([1 Kings 6:1](bible://1kgs/6/1)). To reconcile this timeline, classical commentators such as al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar posit that Abraham and Solomon merely reconstructed older sanctuaries originally founded forty years apart by Adam or Jacob.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَأَلْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنْ أَوَّلِ مَسْجِدٍ وُضِعَ فِي الأَرْضِ قَالَ ‏"‏ الْمَسْجِدُ الْحَرَامُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ ثُمَّ أَىٌّ قَالَ ‏"‏ الْمَسْجِدُ الأَقْصَى ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ كَمْ بَيْنَهُمَا قَالَ ‏"‏ أَرْبَعُونَ عَامًا ثُمَّ الأَرْضُ لَكَ مَسْجِدٌ فَحَيْثُمَا أَدْرَكَتْكَ الصَّلاَةُ فَصَلِّ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the mosque that was first set up on the earth. He said: Masjid Harim. I said: Then which next? He said: The Masjid al-Aqsa. I said: How long is the space of time between the two? He said: Forty years.

muslim:1162.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, following Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that Abraham and Solomon merely renovated preexisting sanctuaries whose original foundations were laid forty years apart by Adam or by Jacob after Abraham. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the question concerns the very first mosque placed on earth (`أَوَّلِ مَسْجِدٍ وُضِعَ فِي الأَرْضِ`), while [Quran 2:127](quran://2/127) and bukhari:3364 confirm that Abraham and Ishmael laid the Kaaba's foundations (`الْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ`) in a barren, previously structureless valley roughly a millennium before Solomon built the Jerusalem Temple around 960 BC. Inventing an unrecorded sanctuary built by Adam or Jacob has zero basis in the Quran, authentic ḥadīth, or Levantine archaeology, leaving Muhammad's forty-year gap (`أَرْبَعُونَ عَامًا`) as an irreconcilable chronological error.

bukhari:3326.note: Muhammad declares that Allah created Adam 60 cubits (approximately 90 feet) tall and that humanity has been continuously decreasing in stature up to the present day. This assertion contradicts human skeletal biomechanics and the archaeological record—a discrepancy that classical commentator Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani acknowledged in *Fath al-Bari*, noting that the surviving dwellings of ancient peoples like Thamud show no such continuous shrinkage and admitting he could not resolve the problem.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: خَلَقَ اللَّهُ آدَمَ وَطُولُهُ سِتُّونَ ذِرَاعًا، ثُمَّ قَالَ اذْهَبْ فَسَلِّمْ عَلَى أُولَئِكَ مِنَ الْمَلاَئِكَةِ، فَاسْتَمِعْ مَا يُحَيُّونَكَ، تَحِيَّتُكَ وَتَحِيَّةُ ذُرِّيَّتِكَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ‏.‏ فَقَالُوا السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ‏.‏ فَزَادُوهُ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ‏.‏ فَكُلُّ مَنْ يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ عَلَى صُورَةِ آدَمَ، فَلَمْ يَزَلِ الْخَلْقُ يَنْقُصُ حَتَّى الآنَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah created Adam, making him 60 cubits tall. When He created him, He said to him, "Go and greet that group of angels, and listen to their reply, for it will be your greeting (salutation) and the greeting (salutations of your offspring." So, Adam said (to the angels), As-Salamu Alaikum (i.e. Peace be upon you). The angels said, "As-salamu Alaika wa Rahmatu-l-lahi" (i.e. Peace and Allah's Mercy be upon you). Thus the angels added to Adam's salutation the expression, 'Wa Rahmatu-l-lahi,' Any person who will enter Paradise will resemble Adam (in appearance and figure). People have been decreasing in stature since Adam's creation

bukhari:3326.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Adam was only sixty cubits tall while in Paradise and was immediately reduced to normal human height upon descending to Earth, or that the decrease refers to lifespan and spiritual status rather than physical stature. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states fa-lam yazal al-khalqu yanquṣu ḥattā al-ān ('creation has not ceased decreasing until now'), using a continuous verb construction directly tied to ṭūluhu sittūna dhirāʿan ('his height of sixty cubits') to assert a gradual, ongoing physical shrinkage across earthly generations up to Muhammad's own time.
