Even Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī in Fatḥ al-Bārī conceded that this narration is empirically problematic (yushkilu ʿalā hādhā), admitting that the extant rock-cut dwellings of ancient nations like Thamūd show normal-sized doorways and prove that human stature had not been progressively shrinking.

bukhari:6594.note: Muhammad declares that an embryo is gathered in the mother's womb for forty days, becomes a clot ('alaqah) for forty days, and then becomes a lump of flesh (mudghah) for an equal period of forty days—a literal 120-day sequence affirmed by classical commentators—before an angel is sent to record its provision, lifespan, and whether it will be wretched or blessed ([Quran 22:5](quran://22/5)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ يُجْمَعُ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا، ثُمَّ عَلَقَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ مُضْغَةً مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، ثُمَّ يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ مَلَكًا فَيُؤْمَرُ بِأَرْبَعٍ بِرِزْقِهِ، وَأَجَلِهِ، وَشَقِيٌّ، أَوْ سَعِيدٌ
problematic_excerpt.english: Each one of you collected in the womb of his mother for forty days, and then turns into a clot for an equal period (of forty days) and turns into a piece of flesh for a similar period (of forty days) and then Allah sends an angel and orders him to write four things, i.e., his provision, his age, and whether he will be of the wretched or the blessed (in the Hereafter).

bukhari:6594.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase 'like that' (mithla dhālika) refers to the developmental manner rather than the time period, claiming all three stages—drop, clot, and lump of flesh—occur within a single forty-day window to harmonize this text with muslim:6726 and modern embryology. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states 'arbaʿīna yawman, thumma ʿalaqatan mithla dhālika, thumma yakūnu muḍghatan mithla dhālika' ('forty days, then a clot for a period like that, then a lump of flesh for a period like that'), where the sequential particle thumma ('then/subsequently') paired with mithla dhālika grammatically mandates three consecutive forty-day intervals totaling 120 days. Classical authorities including Ibn Ḥajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī in Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim unanimously affirmed this 120-day timeline, which absurdly leaves the fetus as an unformed 'lump of flesh' (muḍghah) at seventeen weeks of gestation—over two months after all human organs and limbs have already developed.

bukhari:6594.note: Muhammad swears by Allah that a person may perform the deeds of the people of Paradise until only a cubit or two remains between him and it, at which point the pre-written decree overtakes him (fayasbiqu 'alayhi al-kitab) so that he performs the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it, and vice versa ([Ezekiel 18:20](bible://ez/18/20); [Romans 2:6](bible://rom/2/6)). While auxiliary narrations add the qualifier 'in what appears to people' (bukhari:2898), this text directly attributes the reversal of a person's final deeds and eternal destination to the prior written decree overtaking him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَوَاللَّهِ إِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ ـ أَوِ الرَّجُلَ ـ يَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ، حَتَّى مَا يَكُونُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهَا غَيْرُ بَاعٍ أَوْ ذِرَاعٍ، فَيَسْبِقُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ، فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ، فَيَدْخُلُهَا، وَإِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ، حَتَّى مَا يَكُونُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَهَا غَيْرُ ذِرَاعٍ أَوْ ذِرَاعَيْنِ، فَيَسْبِقُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ، فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ، فَيَدْخُلُهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: And by Allah, a person among you (or a man) may do deeds of the people of the Fire till there is only a cubit or an arm-breadth distance between him and the Fire, but then that writing (which Allah has ordered the angel to write) precedes, and he does the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it; and a man may do the deeds of the people of Paradise till there is only a cubit or two between him and Paradise, and then that writing precedes and he does the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it

bukhari:6594.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and variant narrations like bukhari:2898, that the preordained decree merely reflects divine foreknowledge rather than coercion, claiming the person who turns to evil at the end was a secret hypocrite who only did righteous deeds 'in what appears to people' (fīmā yabdū lil-nās). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states 'fayasbiqu ʿalayhi al-kitābu fayaʿmalu bi-ʿamali ahli al-nāri' ('then the writing overtakes him, so he does the deeds of the people of the Fire'), using the causal conjunction fa- ('so/consequently') to establish that the angel's womb-writing (shaqiyyun aw saʿīd, 'wretched or blessed') actively overtakes the person and causes his final deeds. This fatalistic causation is reinforced across the Sahih corpus, where Allah creates souls specifically for Hellfire while they are still in their fathers' loins (muslim:6769) and Adam is exonerated from blame because Allah predestined his transgression forty years before creating him (bukhari:6614).

bukhari:7454.note: Muhammad declares that human gestation proceeds in three consecutive 40-day stages—first collected in the womb for 40 days and nights, then a blood clot ('alaqah) for 40 days, and then a lump of flesh (mudghah) for 40 days—totaling 120 days before an angel breathes in the soul, whereas human organogenesis and limb formation are completed by day 56 without a blood-clot stage.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ خَلْقَ أَحَدِكُمْ يُجْمَعُ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا وَأَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ عَلَقَةً مِثْلَهُ، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ مُضْغَةً مِثْلَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: The creation of everyone of you starts with the process of collecting the material for his body within forty days and forty nights in the womb of his mother. Then he becomes a clot of thick blood for a similar period (40 days) and then he becomes like a piece of flesh for a similar period.

bukhari:7454.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that all three embryonic stages—drop, clot, and lump of flesh—occur within a single 40-day window rather than 120 days, appealing to muslim:6726 to rescue the narration from modern embryology. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "thumma yakūnu ʿalaqatan mithlahu, thumma yakūnu muḍghatan mithlahu" ("then he becomes a clot for a similar period, then he becomes a piece of flesh for a similar period"), where the sequential particle thumma ("then/subsequently") paired with mithlahu ("like it," referring directly to the forty days and nights) grammatically mandates three consecutive 40-day periods. Furthermore, both Ibn Hajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī in Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim explicitly affirm that the fetus remains unensouled for 120 full days—the exact basis for classical Sunni jurisprudence on abortion—rendering a 40-day clot and 40-day lump stage an undeniable anatomical falsehood.

bukhari:7454.note: Muhammad states that an angel is ordered to write a fetus's livelihood, lifespan, deeds, and whether they will be wretched or blessed before breathing the soul into them. He adds that a person may perform the deeds of the people of Paradise until only a cubit remains between them and it, at which point the pre-written decree overtakes them (fayasbiqu 'alayhi al-kitab), causing them to perform the deeds of the people of the Fire and enter it.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَيَكْتُبُ رِزْقَهُ وَأَجَلَهُ وَعَمَلَهُ وَشَقِيٌّ أَمْ سَعِيدٌ ثُمَّ يَنْفُخُ فِيهِ الرُّوحَ، فَإِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ لَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ، حَتَّى لاَ يَكُونُ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُ إِلاَّ ذِرَاعٌ، فَيَسْبِقُ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابُ، فَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ النَّارِ فَيَدْخُلُ النَّارَ
problematic_excerpt.english: and the angel is allowed (ordered) to write four things; his livelihood, his (date of) death, his deeds, and whether he will be a wretched one or a blessed one (in the Hereafter) and then the soul is breathed into him. So one of you may do (good) deeds characteristic of the people of Paradise so much that there is nothing except a cubit between him and Paradise but then what has been written for him decides his behavior and he starts doing (evil) deeds characteristic of the people of Hell (Fire) and (ultimately) enters Hell (Fire)

bukhari:7454.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and parallel narrations like bukhari:2898, that the angel's inscription merely reflects Allah's passive foreknowledge rather than coercive fatalism, and that the doomed person only appeared righteous to others while harboring secret hypocrisy. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "fa-yasbiqu ʿalayhi al-kitābu fa-yaʿmalu bi-ʿamali ahli al-nāri" ("then the Book overtakes him, so he does the deeds of the people of the Fire"), using the causal conjunction fa- ("so/consequently") to establish that the pre-written decree (al-kitāb) actively forces the behavioral reversal rather than merely recording it. This deterministic causation is further cemented by bukhari:6614, where Muhammad vindicates Adam against Moses by declaring that Adam could not be blamed for sinning because Allah had already written that fate upon him forty years before creating him.

muslim:715.note: When asked about the visible fluid (*al-mā'*) a woman discharges during a wet dream, Muhammad states that a child's resemblance to its maternal or paternal uncles comes from that fluid, depending on whether the woman's fluid (*mā'uhā*) or the man's fluid (*mā' al-rajul*) rises above (*ʿalā*) the other. While the published English translation renders *mā'* ('water/fluid') as 'genes,' the Arabic text explicitly identifies the fluid governing hereditary resemblance as the visible sexual discharge that obligates ritual bathing (*ghusl*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ امْرَأَةً، قَالَتْ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم هَلْ تَغْتَسِلُ الْمَرْأَةُ إِذَا احْتَلَمَتْ وَأَبْصَرَتِ الْمَاءَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ لَهَا عَائِشَةُ تَرِبَتْ يَدَاكِ وَأُلَّتْ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ دَعِيهَا وَهَلْ يَكُونُ الشَّبَهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ قِبَلِ ذَلِكِ إِذَا عَلاَ مَاؤُهَا مَاءَ الرَّجُلِ أَشْبَهَ الْوَلَدُ أَخْوَالَهُ وَإِذَا عَلاَ مَاءُ الرَّجُلِ مَاءَهَا أَشْبَهَ أَعْمَامَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Should a woman wash herself when she sees a sexual dream and sees (the marks) of liquid? He (the Holy Prophet) said: Yes. 'A'isha said to her: May your hand be covered with dust and injured. She narrated: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Leave her alone. In what way does the child resemble her but for the fact that when the genes contributed by woman prevail upon those of man, the child resembles the maternal family, and when the genes of man prevail upon those of woman the child resembles the paternal family

muslim:715.literal_translation: Should a woman wash herself when she has a wet dream and sees the fluid? He said: 'Yes.' Aisha said to her: 'May your hands be covered with dust and wounded!' She narrated: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Leave her alone. Is resemblance from anything other than that? When her fluid rises above the man's fluid, the child resembles his maternal uncles, and when the man's fluid rises above her fluid, he resembles his paternal uncles.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: إِذَا عَلاَ مَاؤُهَا مَاءَ الرَّجُلِ أَشْبَهَ الْوَلَدُ أَخْوَالَهُ وَإِذَا عَلاَ مَاءُ الرَّجُلِ مَاءَهَا أَشْبَهَ أَعْمَامَهُ
translation_issue.published_rendering: when the genes contributed by woman prevail upon those of man, the child resembles the maternal family, and when the genes of man prevail upon those of woman the child resembles the paternal family
translation_issue.literal_meaning: when her fluid (water) rises above the man's fluid (water), the child resembles his maternal uncles, and when the man's fluid rises above her fluid, he resembles his paternal uncles
translation_issue.explanation: The translator anachronistically replaces 'mā'uhā' ('her fluid/water', referring to vaginal wet-dream discharge) and 'mā' al-rajul' ('the man's fluid') with 'the genes contributed by woman' and 'the genes of man' to disguise an ancient Galenic reproductive fluid error as modern genetics.

muslim:715.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that 'her fluid' (*mā'uhā*) and 'rises above' (*ʿalā*) metaphorically describe the female ovum and dominant genetic chromosomes prevailing over recessive traits—an excuse so prevalent that translator Abdul Hamid Siddiqi anachronistically rendered *mā'* ('water/fluid') directly as 'genes.' However, the primary Arabic text explicitly defines this *mā'* as the macroscopic vaginal discharge a woman physically sees with her eyes after a wet dream (*iḥtalamat wa-abṣarati al-mā'*), which parallel narrations (such as *Sahih Muslim* 311) further describe as 'thin and yellow' (*raqīq aṣfar*). Far from anticipating modern genetics, Muhammad is repeating 2nd-century AD Galenic two-seed embryology by claiming that female orgasmic secretion and male ejaculate physically compete in volume or sequence (*sabaqa* in *Sahih al-Bukhari* 3329) to determine a child's familial resemblance.

muslim:710.note: When Umm Sulaim asks whether women experience nocturnal emissions, Muhammad replies that a child's parental resemblance depends on this discharge, declaring that a man's fluid is thick and white while a woman's fluid is thin and yellow, and whichever of the two fluids rises above or precedes the other (`'ala aw sabaqa`) determines who the child resembles.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَأَلَتْ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنِ الْمَرْأَةِ تَرَى فِي مَنَامِهَا مَا يَرَى الرَّجُلُ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِذَا رَأَتْ ذَلِكِ الْمَرْأَةُ فَلْتَغْتَسِلْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ أُمُّ سُلَيْمٍ وَاسْتَحْيَيْتُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ قَالَتْ وَهَلْ يَكُونُ هَذَا فَقَالَ نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ نَعَمْ فَمِنْ أَيْنَ يَكُونُ الشَّبَهُ إِنَّ مَاءَ الرَّجُلِ غَلِيظٌ أَبْيَضُ وَمَاءَ الْمَرْأَةِ رَقِيقٌ أَصْفَرُ فَمِنْ أَيِّهِمَا عَلاَ أَوْ سَبَقَ يَكُونُ مِنْهُ الشَّبَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: she asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about a woman who sees in a dream what a man sees (sexual dream). The Messenger of Allah (may peace be upon bi m) said:In case a woman sees that, she must take a bath. Umm Sulaim said: I was bashful on account of that and said: Does it happen? Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Yes (it does happen), otherwise how can (a child) resemble her? Man's discharge (i. e. sperm) is thick and white and the discharge of woman is thin and yellow; so the resemblance comes from the one whose genes prevail or dominate

muslim:710.literal_translation: She asked the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) about a woman who sees in her sleep what a man sees. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'When a woman sees that, let her perform ritual washing (ghusl).' Umm Sulaim said: 'I felt shy because of that,' and she said: 'And does this happen?' The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Yes, then from where does resemblance come? Indeed, the fluid of a man is thick and white, and the fluid of a woman is thin and yellow; so from whichever of the two [fluids] rises above (or overcomes) or precedes [the other], the resemblance comes from it.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَمِنْ أَيِّهِمَا عَلاَ أَوْ سَبَقَ يَكُونُ مِنْهُ الشَّبَهُ
translation_issue.published_rendering: so the resemblance comes from the one whose genes prevail or dominate
translation_issue.literal_meaning: so from whichever of the two [fluids] rises above (or overcomes) or precedes [the other], the resemblance comes from it
translation_issue.explanation: The translator anachronistically inserts the modern biological word 'genes'—which has no basis in the Arabic text—and replaces 'aw sabaqa' ('or precedes / discharges first') with 'or dominate' to conceal the ancient humorist physiology in which hereditary resemblance is determined by whether the thick white male fluid or the thin yellow female orgasmic fluid precedes or tops the other.

muslim:710.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the woman's 'thin, yellow fluid' (mā’u al-mar’ati raqīqun aṣfar) and the verb 'rises above' (‘alā) miraculously refer to yellowish ovarian follicular fluid and genetic dominance, as interpolated in the published English translation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that this fluid is the external orgasmic discharge emitted during a sexual dream (tarā fī manāmihā mā yarā al-rajul) that obligates ritual bathing (ghusl), asserting that a child's resemblance comes from whichever partner's fluid physically 'rises above or precedes [discharges first]' (‘alā aw sabaqa). As Al-Nawawī confirms in Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and parallel narrations (bukhari:3329) clarify, Muhammad was repeating the ancient Greco-Roman two-seed myth that female climax emits reproductive seed, whereas human ovulation and DNA inheritance occur entirely independently of orgasmic discharge.

bukhari:3366.note: Muhammad declares that the first sanctuary placed on earth was al-Masjid al-Haram in Mecca and the second was al-Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem, stating that forty years separated their construction. Because the Quran attributes the building of the Kaaba to Abraham ([Quran 2:127](quran://2/127), c. 2000 BC) while Solomon built the Jerusalem Temple over a millennium later in c. 960 BC ([1 Kings 6:1](bible://1kgs/6/1))—a chronological difficulty (*ishkāl*) acknowledged by Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—classical commentators propose that Adam or Jacob originally founded both sites and that Abraham and Solomon merely rebuilt them.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَىُّ مَسْجِدٍ وُضِعَ فِي الأَرْضِ أَوَّلُ قَالَ ‏"‏ الْمَسْجِدُ الْحَرَامُ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ ثُمَّ أَىٌّ قَالَ ‏"‏ الْمَسْجِدُ الأَقْصَى ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْتُ كَمْ كَانَ بَيْنَهُمَا قَالَ ‏"‏ أَرْبَعُونَ سَنَةً، ثُمَّ أَيْنَمَا أَدْرَكَتْكَ الصَّلاَةُ بَعْدُ فَصَلِّهْ، فَإِنَّ الْفَضْلَ فِيهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Which mosque was first built on the surface of the earth?" He said, "Al-Masjid-ul-Haram (in Mecca)." I said, "Which was built next?" He replied, "The mosque of Al-Aqsa (in Jerusalem) ." I said, "What was the period of construction between the two?" He said, "Forty years." He added, "Wherever (you may be, and) the prayer time becomes due, perform the prayer there, for the best thing is to do so (i.e. to offer the prayers in time)

bukhari:3366.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the passive verb *wuḍiʿa* (وُضِعَ, 'was laid/established')—as proposed in Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—refers to Adam or Jacob originally laying the foundations of both sanctuaries forty years apart, claiming that Abraham (c. 2000 BC) and Solomon (c. 960 BC) merely renovated pre-existing structures. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *ayyu masjidin wuḍiʿa fī al-arḍi awwalu* (أَيُّ مَسْجِدٍ وُضِعَ فِي الأَرْضِ أَوَّلُ, 'which mosque was first established on the earth'), and the foundational Islamic sources themselves identify Abraham and Solomon as the original builders: [Quran 2:127](quran://2/127) and `bukhari:3364` depict Abraham raising the Kaaba's foundations in a barren, structureless valley, while `nasai:693` and `ibnmajah:1408` explicitly credit Solomon with constructing the Jerusalem Temple (*bināʾi Bayt al-Maqdis*). Because not a single authentic (*ṣaḥīḥ*) prophetic narration in the entire Hadith corpus mentions Adam or Jacob building Al-Aqsa, this 'renovation' excuse is an unsubstantiated *ad hoc* conjecture invented solely to salvage Muhammad's 1,000-year chronological blunder.

bukhari:7433.note: When asked by Abu Dharr to explain Qur'an 36:38 ("And the sun runs to a resting place for it"), Muhammad declares that the sun's resting place (*mustaqarr*) is beneath Allah's Throne. As detailed in the fuller narration of this report (bukhari:3199), where the sun travels beneath the Throne at sunset to prostrate and seek permission to rise, Muhammad's own exegesis directly precludes modern apologetic reinterpretations of the verse as the solar apex.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ سَأَلْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنْ قَوْلِهِ ‏{‏وَالشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَهَا‏}‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ مُسْتَقَرُّهَا تَحْتَ الْعَرْشِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding the Verse:--'And the sun runs on its fixed course for a term decreed for it.' (36.28) He said, "Its fixed course is underneath Allah's Throne

bukhari:7433.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that 'beneath the Throne' (taḥta al-ʿarsh) is merely a metaphorical expression of divine sovereignty or that the entire physical cosmos exists beneath Allah's encompassing Throne while the sun travels along its modern galactic orbit. However, the primary Arabic text of the fuller narration transmitted through this exact same chain (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199 and 4802) explicitly states that Muhammad was answering where the sun goes 'when it sets' (ḥīna gharabat al-shams), explaining that it travels to prostrate beneath the Throne and asks permission to rise again until the day it is commanded, 'Return from where you came' (irjiʿī min ḥaythu jiʾti), causing it to rise from the west. This locks mustaqarruhā ('its resting place/fixed course') into a literal, geocentric nightly destination after sunset rather than a continuous galactic orbit or abstract metaphor.

bukhari:536.note: Muhammad declares that seasonal temperature extremes—the severest heat of summer and the severest cold (*zamharīr*) of winter—are caused by two annual breaths (*nafasayn*) granted to Hellfire after it complained to Allah that its parts were consuming one another. Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi affirm that the Sunni majority understands this report literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*) rather than metaphorically.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: اشْتَكَتِ النَّارُ إِلَى رَبِّهَا فَقَالَتْ يَا رَبِّ أَكَلَ بَعْضِي بَعْضًا‏.‏ فَأَذِنَ لَهَا بِنَفَسَيْنِ نَفَسٍ فِي الشِّتَاءِ، وَنَفَسٍ فِي الصَّيْفِ، فَهُوَ أَشَدُّ مَا تَجِدُونَ مِنَ الْحَرِّ، وَأَشَدُّ مَا تَجِدُونَ مِنَ الزَّمْهَرِيرِ
problematic_excerpt.english: The Hell-fire of Hell complained to its Lord saying: O Lord! My parts are eating (destroying) one another. So Allah allowed it to take two breaths, one in the winter and the other in the summer. The breath in the summer is at the time when you feel the severest heat and the breath in the winter is at the time when you feel the severest cold

bukhari:536.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the 'two breaths' (*nafasayn*) of Hellfire are merely a figurative metaphor (*majāz*) meant to remind believers of the hereafter, or an unseen metaphysical reality (*ghayb*) that operates alongside physical seasons. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a direct physical causation and identity—declaring that midday heat is literally 'from the raging of Gehenna' (*min fayḥi jahannam*) and that its breath '*is* the severest heat you feel and the severest bitter cold (*al-zamharīr*) you feel' (*fa-huwa ashaddu mā tajidūna*)—which is why both Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) explicitly reject the metaphorical excuse and insist the narration must be taken literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatih*). Furthermore, claiming that Allah grants Hellfire one breath in summer and one in winter presupposes a localized, pre-scientific cosmology, entirely unaware that summer and winter occur simultaneously in opposite hemispheres due to Earth's axial tilt.

bukhari:537.note: Muhammad states that the severest summer heat and winter cold (*zamharīr*) are caused by Allah granting Hellfire two annual breaths (*nafasayn*)—one in summer and one in winter—after it complained that its parts were consuming one another. Classical commentators such as al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar affirm that the orthodox Sunni majority understands Hellfire's complaint and two seasonal exhalations literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatih*) rather than metaphorically.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: اشْتَكَتِ النَّارُ إِلَى رَبِّهَا فَقَالَتْ يَا رَبِّ أَكَلَ بَعْضِي بَعْضًا‏.‏ فَأَذِنَ لَهَا بِنَفَسَيْنِ نَفَسٍ فِي الشِّتَاءِ، وَنَفَسٍ فِي الصَّيْفِ، فَهُوَ أَشَدُّ مَا تَجِدُونَ مِنَ الْحَرِّ، وَأَشَدُّ مَا تَجِدُونَ مِنَ الزَّمْهَرِيرِ
problematic_excerpt.english: The Hell-fire of Hell complained to its Lord saying: O Lord! My parts are eating (destroying) one another. So Allah allowed it to take two breaths, one in the winter and the other in the summer. The breath in the summer is at the time when you feel the severest heat and the breath in the winter is at the time when you feel the severest cold

bukhari:537.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the 'two breaths' (*nafasayn*) and complaint of Hellfire are merely figurative (*majāz*) reminders of the hereafter, or unseen metaphysical realities (*ghayb*) operating behind natural seasonal causes. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that midday heat is directly 'from the raging of Jahannam' (*min fayḥi Jahannam*) and identifies its exhalation as 'the severest heat... and bitter cold that you feel' (*fa-huwa ashaddu mā tajidūna min al-ḥarri... wa-al-zamharīr*), making this physical causation the concrete legal basis for delaying the noon prayer. Furthermore, both Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) explicitly reject the metaphorical evasion by affirming that Sunni orthodoxy takes Hell's complaint and physical exhalations literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatih*), exposing a pre-scientific meteorology that cannot account for why the Northern and Southern Hemispheres experience opposite seasons simultaneously.

bukhari:3260.note: Muhammad states that after the Hellfire complained to its Lord that its parts were consuming one another, it was granted two breaths (*nafasayn*)—one in winter and one in summer—which cause the severest seasonal cold (*zamharīr*) and heat experienced on earth. Classical commentators such as al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar affirm that the orthodox majority (*jumhūr*) interprets this report literally (*ʿalā ẓāhirihi*) as an actual physical cause of seasonal temperature extremes.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: اشْتَكَتِ النَّارُ إِلَى رَبِّهَا، فَقَالَتْ رَبِّ أَكَلَ بَعْضِي بَعْضًا، فَأَذِنَ لَهَا بِنَفَسَيْنِ نَفَسٍ فِي الشِّتَاءِ وَنَفَسٍ فِي الصَّيْفِ، فَأَشَدُّ مَا تَجِدُونَ فِي الْحَرِّ، وَأَشَدُّ مَا تَجِدُونَ مِنَ الزَّمْهَرِيرِ
problematic_excerpt.english: The (Hell) Fire complained to its Lord saying, 'O my Lord! My different parts eat up each other.' So, He allowed it to take two breaths, one in the winter and the other in summer, and this is the reason for the severe heat and the bitter cold you find (in weather)

bukhari:3260.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Hell's complaint and its 'two breaths' (*nafasayn*) are merely metaphorical (*majāz*) reminders of the afterlife, or refer to an unseen metaphysical realm (*ghayb*) that does not negate normal meteorological causes. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a direct physical causation—that the severest heat and bitter cold (*al-zamharīr*) humans physically experience on earth (*mā tajidūna*) are the actual exhalations of Hell, a causal link reinforced in the parallel narration `bukhari:536` which states that extreme weather comes directly 'from the raging of Hell' (*min fayḥi jahannam*). Furthermore, leading Sunni authorities including Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) explicitly refute the metaphorical excuse and insist the Hadith must be taken literally (*ʿalā ẓāhirihi*), exposing a 7th-century AD cosmology unaware that summer and winter occur simultaneously in opposite hemispheres due to Earth's axial tilt.

muslim:402.note: Asked by Abu Dharr to explain [Quran 36:38](quran://36/38) ("And the sun runs to a resting place for it"), Muhammad declares that the sun's resting place (*mustaqarruhā*) is beneath the Throne (*taḥta al-'arsh*). In fuller parallel reports of this exchange (muslim:399, bukhari:3199, bukhari:4802), he states that the sun travels there after sunset to prostrate and ask permission to rise again—an account that classical commentators such as al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar affirm according to its apparent meaning (*'alā ẓāhirihi*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ سَأَلْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنْ قَوْلِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى ‏{‏ وَالشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَهَا‏}‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ مُسْتَقَرُّهَا تَحْتَ الْعَرْشِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the (implication of the) words of Allah, the Exalted: The sun glides to its appointed resting place. He replied: Its appointed resting place is under the Throne

muslim:402.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *mustaqarr* in [Quran 36:38](quran://36/38) refers to the modern astronomical concept of the solar apex or, following Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar, that being "under the Throne" merely denotes the sun's continuous metaphorical submission within the cosmos without halting its orbit. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that "under the Throne" (*taḥta al-ʿarsh*) is the specific resting place (*mustaqarruhā*) to which the sun travels, which the fuller parallel narrations of Abū Dharr's report (bukhari:3199, muslim:399) identify as a literal nightly destination after sunset (*ḥīna taghrubu*) where the sun goes, prostrates (*tasjudu*), and awaits permission to rise again until the day it is ordered to return and rise from the west.

muslim:712.note: Muhammad declares that a woman must perform ritual bathing (*ghusl*) if she sees discharged fluid (*al-mā'*) after a nocturnal emission, asserting that this visible secretion is what causes a child to resemble its mother.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: جَاءَتْ أُمُّ سُلَيْمٍ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يَسْتَحْيِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ فَهَلْ عَلَى الْمَرْأَةِ مِنْ غُسْلٍ إِذَا احْتَلَمَتْ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ نَعَمْ إِذَا رَأَتِ الْمَاءَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَتْ أُمُّ سَلَمَةَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَتَحْتَلِمُ الْمَرْأَةُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ تَرِبَتْ يَدَاكِ فَبِمَ يُشْبِهُهَا وَلَدُهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Umm Sulaim went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: Apostle of Allah, Allah is not ashamed of the truth. Is bathing necessary for a woman when she has a sexual dream? Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Yes, when she sees the liquid (vaginal secretion). Umm Salama said: Messenger of Allah, does a woman have sexual dream? He (the Holy Prophet) said: Let your hand be covered with dust, in what way does her child resemble her?

muslim:712.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the "water" (*al-mā'*) mentioned by Muhammad refers to the microscopic female ovum or follicular fluid carrying maternal genetics. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that this fluid is an external orgasmic secretion visibly seen by a woman after a nocturnal wet dream (*idhā iḥtalamat... idhā ra'at al-mā'*), which Muhammad directly credits with causing a child's hereditary resemblance (*fa-bima yushbihuhā waladuhā*). Furthermore, parallel narrations (`muslim:715`, `bukhari:3328`) describe the woman's fluid as "yellow and thin" (*aṣfar raqīq*) that determines resemblance whenever it "prevails over or precedes" (*'alā aw sabaqa*) the man's fluid, proving Muhammad was repeating ancient Galenic "two-seed" embryology rather than describing ovulation.

muslim:5819.note: When a star (*najm*, rendered as 'meteor') is thrown and flashes at night, Muhammad states that stars are not hurled for anyone's birth or death, but are thrown to pelt jinn who snatch overheard angelic reports of Allah's decrees in the lowest heaven and cast them to their allies.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: بَيْنَمَا هُمْ جُلُوسٌ لَيْلَةً مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم رُمِيَ بِنَجْمٍ فَاسْتَنَارَ فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ مَاذَا كُنْتُمْ تَقُولُونَ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ إِذَا رُمِيَ بِمِثْلِ هَذَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ كُنَّا نَقُولُ وُلِدَ اللَّيْلَةَ رَجُلٌ عَظِيمٌ وَمَاتَ رَجُلٌ عَظِيمٌ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَإِنَّهَا لاَ يُرْمَى بِهَا لِمَوْتِ أَحَدٍ وَلاَ لِحَيَاتِهِ وَلَكِنْ رَبُّنَا تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى اسْمُهُ إِذَا قَضَى أَمْرًا سَبَّحَ حَمَلَةُ الْعَرْشِ ثُمَّ سَبَّحَ أَهْلُ السَّمَاءِ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ التَّسْبِيحُ أَهْلَ هَذِهِ السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا ثُمَّ قَالَ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَ حَمَلَةَ الْعَرْشِ لِحَمَلَةِ الْعَرْشِ مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ فَيُخْبِرُونَهُمْ مَاذَا قَالَ - قَالَ - فَيَسْتَخْبِرُ بَعْضُ أَهْلِ السَّمَوَاتِ بَعْضًا حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْخَبَرُ هَذِهِ السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا فَتَخْطَفُ الْجِنُّ السَّمْعَ فَيَقْذِفُونَ إِلَى أَوْلِيَائِهِمْ وَيُرْمَوْنَ بِهِ فَمَا جَاءُوا بِهِ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ فَهُوَ حَقٌّ وَلَكِنَّهُمْ يَقْرِفُونَ فِيهِ وَيَزِيدُونَ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: As we were sitting during the night with Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), a meteor shot gave a dazzling light. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: What did you say in the pre-Islamic days when there was such a shot (of meteor)? They said: Allah and His Messenger know best (the actual position), but we, however, used to say that that very night a great man had been born and a great man had died, whereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: (These meteors) are shot neither at the death of anyone nor on the birth of anyone. Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, issues Command when He decides to do a thing. Then (the Angels) supporting the Throne sing His glory, then sing the dwellers of heaven who are near to them until this glory of God reaches them who are in the heaven of this world. Then those who are near the supporters of the Throne ask these supporters of the Throne: What your Lord has said? And they accordingly inform them what He says. Then the dwellers of heaven seek information from them until this information reaches the heaven of the world. In this process of transmission (the jinn snatches) what he manages to overhear and he carries it to his friends. And when the Angels see the jinn they attack them with meteors. If they narrate only which they manage to snatch that is correct but they alloy it with lies and make additions to it

muslim:5819.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the word *najm* here merely denotes a meteoroid rather than a star, or that the pelting of jinn is an unseen spiritual event unrelated to the physical streaks of light observed in the night sky. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad gave this explanation immediately after he and his companions physically witnessed a star being thrown that flashed with light (`رُمِيَ بِنَجْمٍ فَاسْتَنَارَ`), asking what they used to say in pre-Islamic times when the like of this was thrown (`إِذَا رُمِيَ بِمِثْلِ هَذَا`). Muhammad directly identifies that visible celestial event as the mechanism by which eavesdropping jinn in the lowest heaven (`هَذِهِ السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا`) are pelted (`وَيُرْمَوْنَ بِهِ`) when they snatch overheard angelic reports to cast to their allies, matching the cosmology of [Quran 15:16](quran://15/16), [Quran 37:6](quran://37/6), and [Quran 67:5](quran://67/5) (see also `bukhari:3210`, `bukhari:4701`, `bukhari:4800`).

muslim:7416.note: Muhammad states that the human tailbone (*ʿajb al-dhanab*, coccyx) is never consumed by the earth and that human bodies will be reassembled from it on the Day of Resurrection.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ فِي الإِنْسَانِ عَظْمًا لاَ تَأْكُلُهُ الأَرْضُ أَبَدًا فِيهِ يُرَكَّبُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا أَىُّ عَظْمٍ هُوَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ عَجْبُ الذَّنَبِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: There is a bone in the human being which the earth would never consume and it is from this that new bodies would be reconstituted (on the Day of Resurrection). They said: Allah's Messenger, which bone is that? Thereupon he said: It is the spinal bone

muslim:7416.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration refers metaphorically to an unseen genetic blueprint or microscopic cellular remnant rather than a literal anatomical bone that resists decay. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that there is an actual bone (*ʿaẓman*) in the human being that the earth never consumes (*lā taʾkuluhu al-arḍu abadan*), and when asked which bone (*ayyu ʿaẓmin*) it is, Muhammad names the physical tailbone (*ʿajb al-dhanab*). Confirmed across parallel reports (muslim:7414, muslim:7415, and bukhari:4935), the text makes a literal anatomical claim about an indestructible bone that is falsified by the complete physical decomposition and destruction of the human coccyx.

bukhari:6091.note: Muhammad rules that a woman must perform ritual bathing after a wet dream if she sees emitted fluid (al-ma'), and when Umm Salamah asks whether women experience nocturnal emissions, he attributes a child's resemblance to its mother to this discharge.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَتْ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يَسْتَحِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ، هَلْ عَلَى الْمَرْأَةِ غُسْلٌ إِذَا احْتَلَمَتْ قَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ إِذَا رَأَتِ الْمَاءَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَضَحِكَتْ أُمُّ سَلَمَةَ فَقَالَتْ أَتَحْتَلِمُ الْمَرْأَةُ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَبِمَ شَبَهُ الْوَلَدِ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Um Sulaim said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Verily Allah is not shy of (telling you) the truth. Is it essential for a woman to take a bath after she had a wet dream (nocturnal sexual discharge)?" He said, "Yes, if she notices discharge. On that Um Salama laughed and said, "Does a woman get a (nocturnal sexual) discharge?" He said, "How then does (her) son resemble her (his mother)?

bukhari:6091.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the woman's 'water' (al-mā') metaphorically refers to the microscopic female ovum or follicular fluid carrying maternal chromosomes, claiming the Hadith miraculously anticipates modern genetics. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that this fluid is a visible discharge noticed after a nocturnal wet dream (idhā iḥtalamat... idhā ra'at al-mā', 'when she has a wet dream... if she sees the water') that obligates ritual bathing (ghusl). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3328; Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:710) describe this reproductive fluid as a 'thin, yellow' liquid whose climax timing or dominance over the male's semen dictates the child's resemblance—directly repeating 2nd-century AD Galenic 'two-seed' embryology rather than describing ovulation, which occurs independently of sexual climax.

bukhari:6595.note: Muhammad states that an angel assigned to the womb reports sequential stages of a drop (`nutfah`), a clot (`'alaqah`), and a lump of flesh (`mudghah`) ([Quran 22:5](quran://22/5)), and only after the `mudghah` stage asks Allah whether the fetus will be male or female—whereas biological sex is genetically fixed at fertilization. At this same post-`mudghah` stage (cf. the 40-day intervals in bukhari:6594), the angel simultaneously writes whether the child is predestined to be wretched (`shaqiyy`) or blessed (`sa'id`), along with its provisions and lifespan.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَكَّلَ اللَّهُ بِالرَّحِمِ مَلَكًا فَيَقُولُ أَىْ رَبِّ نُطْفَةٌ، أَىْ رَبِّ عَلَقَةٌ، أَىْ رَبِّ مُضْغَةٌ‏.‏ فَإِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَقْضِيَ خَلْقَهَا قَالَ أَىْ رَبِّ ذَكَرٌ أَمْ أُنْثَى أَشَقِيٌّ أَمْ سَعِيدٌ فَمَا الرِّزْقُ فَمَا الأَجَلُ فَيُكْتَبُ كَذَلِكَ فِي بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah puts an angel in charge of the uterus and the angel says, 'O Lord, (it is) semen! O Lord, (it is now ) a clot! O Lord, (it is now) a piece of flesh.' And then, if Allah wishes to complete its creation, the angel asks, 'O Lord, (will it be) a male or a female? A wretched (an evil doer) or a blessed (doer of good)? How much will his provisions be? What will his age be?' So all that is written while the creature is still in the mother's womb

bukhari:6595.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *ʿalaqah* (*عَلَقَةٌ*) metaphorically means a 'leech-like clinging embryo' rather than a literal blood clot, and that the angel asking whether the fetus is male or female after the *muḍghah* (*مُضْغَةٌ*) stage merely reflects the angel recording Allah's prior knowledge rather than sex being determined late in gestation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that only after the *nuṭfah*, *ʿalaqah*, and *muḍghah* stages—which parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:3208, bukhari:6594) fix at forty days each—does Allah 'decree its creation' (*أَنْ يَقْضِيَ خَلْقَهَا*) as 'male or female' (*ذَكَرٌ أَمْ أُنْثَى*). This uncritically reproduces 2nd-century AD Galenic embryology, directly contradicting the biological reality that chromosomal sex is fixed at fertilization and that a human embryo never remains a drop of semen for forty days or a clot of congealed blood for another forty days.

muslim:1395.note: Muhammad instructs his followers to delay the noon prayer until extreme heat subsides, declaring that severe heat originates from the exhalation of Hellfire (*fayḥ jahannam*). Classical commentators such as al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar confirm that the orthodox Sunni majority interprets this literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*) as actual heat escaping from Hell rather than a metaphor, reinforced by parallel reports detailing Hell's two seasonal breaths (bukhari:536).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا اشْتَدَّ الْحَرُّ فَأَبْرِدُوا بِالصَّلاَةِ فَإِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ
problematic_excerpt.english: When it is very hot, say (the noon prayer) when the extreme heat passes away, for intensity of heat is from the exhalation of Hell

muslim:1395.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase 'from the exhalation of Hell' (*min fayḥ jahannam*) is merely a metaphorical figure of speech (*majāz*) comparing intense summer heat to the punishment of the hereafter. However, the primary Arabic text and its immediate sequel in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* (537) explicitly establish a literal, physical etiology in which Hellfire complained to Allah that its parts were consuming one another (*akalat baʿḍī baʿḍan*), prompting Him to grant it two physical breaths (*nafasayn*) each year that directly cause the earth's fiercest summer heat and winter frost (*zamharīr*). Consequently, authoritative Sunni commentators including Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) explicitly reject the metaphorical excuse and rule that this phenomenon must be taken literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*).

muslim:1397.note: Muhammad commands delaying the prayer on hot days until the temperature cools, declaring that extreme heat is caused by the exhalation of Hellfire (*fayḥ jahannam*). Classical commentators including al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar affirm that mainstream Sunni scholarship interprets this causal statement literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*) rather than metaphorically.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا كَانَ الْيَوْمُ الْحَارُّ فَأَبْرِدُوا بِالصَّلاَةِ فَإِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ
problematic_excerpt.english: When it is a hot day, (delay) the prayer till the extreme heat passes away, for the intensity of heat is from the exhalation of Hell.

muslim:1397.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that attributing extreme midday heat to the exhalation of Hell (*fayḥ jahannam*) is merely a metaphorical figure of speech meant to remind believers of the hereafter. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a direct causal link (*fa-inna shiddata al-ḥarri min fayḥi jahannam*), which parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:537; muslim:1402) expand into a literal cosmology where Hellfire complained to Allah of consuming itself and was granted two physical breaths (*nafasayn*) per year to produce summer's fiercest heat and winter's bitterest cold (*zamharīr*). Consequently, classical authorities including Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) explicitly reject the metaphorical deflection, ruling that orthodox Sunni scholarship affirms this phenomenon in its literal, physical reality (*ʿalā ẓāhirihi wa-ḥaqīqatihi*).

bukhari:3330.note: Muhammad declares that meat would never decay were it not for the Children of Israel, and that no woman would ever betray her husband were it not for Eve. Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi affirm this as a literal etiology, explaining that meat first began to spoil when the Israelites hoarded food in the wilderness.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَوْلاَ بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ لَمْ يَخْنَزِ اللَّحْمُ، وَلَوْلاَ حَوَّاءُ لَمْ تَخُنْ أُنْثَى زَوْجَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: But for the Israelis, meat would not decay and but for Eve, wives would never betray their husbands

bukhari:3330.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this statement is merely a figure of speech warning against hoarding food, or that it only means stored meat would not spoil had the Israelites not been the first to store it. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an absolute, universal counterfactual—`لَوْلاَ بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ لَمْ يَخْنَزِ اللَّحْمُ` ('Were it not for the Children of Israel, meat would not decay')—directly paired with an etiologic claim tracing all female marital betrayal back to Eve (`وَلَوْلاَ حَوَّاءُ`). Moreover, classical commentators like Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1470) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī* 3399) confirm from this wording that meat literally did not putrefy until the Israelites hoarded quail during the Exodus in the second millennium BC, committing Muhammad to the scientific absurdity that organic tissue never decomposed before the time of Moses.

bukhari:7059.note: Muhammad wakes from sleep and declares that a gap has been opened that very day in the barrier (*radm*) of Gog and Magog, warning the Arabs of an approaching destruction if evil increases. Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar affirm this refers to the physical iron-and-copper wall built by Dhul-Qarnayn in [Surah 18:94-98](quran://18/94), despite the absence of any such barrier or trapped population on Earth.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: اسْتَيْقَظَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنَ النَّوْمِ مُحْمَرًّا وَجْهُهُ يَقُولُ ‏"‏ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ، وَيْلٌ لِلْعَرَبِ مِنْ شَرٍّ قَدِ اقْتَرَبَ، فُتِحَ الْيَوْمَ مِنْ رَدْمِ يَاجُوجَ وَمَاجُوجَ مِثْلُ هَذِهِ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) got up from his sleep with a flushed red face and said, "None has the right to be worshipped but Allah. Woe to the Arabs, from the Great evil that is nearly approaching them. Today a gap has been made in the wall of Gog and Magog like this."

bukhari:7059.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the breach in the barrier is merely a metaphorical warning (*majāz*) for approaching political tribulations, or that the wall is concealed in an unseen dimension (*al-ghayb*) beyond terrestrial detection. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `فُتِحَ الْيَوْمَ مِنْ رَدْمِ يَاجُوجَ وَمَاجُوجَ مِثْلُ هَذِهِ` ('Today a gap has been made in the wall of Gog and Magog like this'), pairing the statement with a physical finger-circle measurement (`تِسْعِينَ أَوْ مِائَةً`) that led Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* to affirm its literal physical reality (*ʿalā al-ḥaqīqah*). Furthermore, [Surah 18:96-98](quran://18/96) defines this *radm* as a tangible earthly structure forged from iron blocks (`زُبَرَ الْحَدِيدِ`) and molten copper (`قِطْرًا`) between two physical mountain peaks (`بَيْنَ الصَّدَفَيْنِ`) that holds back the tribes until the end times, refuting both metaphorical and unseen-realm deflections.

bukhari:535.note: Muhammad instructs his caller to delay the midday (*Ẓuhr*) prayer until the weather cools, declaring that the severity of heat comes from the raging breath of Hellfire (*fayḥ jahannam*). Classical commentators such as Ibn Ḥajar and al-Nawawī affirm that the majority of Sunni scholars interpret this statement according to its literal reality (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*) rather than as a metaphor.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: شِدَّةُ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ، فَإِذَا اشْتَدَّ الْحَرُّ فَأَبْرِدُوا عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ
problematic_excerpt.english: the severity of heat is from the raging of the Hell-fire. In severe hot weather, pray when it becomes (a bit) cooler

bukhari:535.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that attributing severe summer heat to the 'raging of the Hell-fire' (*fayḥ jahannam*) is merely a metaphorical expression (*majāz*) comparing oppressive midday weather to the torment of Hell. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a direct causal origin (`شِدَّةُ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ`, 'the severity of heat is from the boiling exhalation of Hell'), which accompanying Sahih narrations (`bukhari:537`, `muslim:1400`) expand into a literal cosmological account where Hell complained to Allah of consuming itself and was granted two physical breaths (*nafasayn*) each year to generate summer's extreme heat and winter's bitter cold (*al-zamharīr*). Consequently, classical Sunni authorities like Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* explicitly reject metaphorical reinterpretations and insist that the narration must be affirmed according to its literal, physical reality (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi wa-ẓāhirihi*).

bukhari:538.note: Muhammad instructs his followers to delay the midday (*Ẓuhr*) prayer until the weather cools, declaring that intense heat originates from the raging exhalation of Hellfire (*fayḥ jahannam*). Classical commentators such as al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar affirm that the majority of orthodox scholars interpret this statement literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*) rather than metaphorically, consistent with neighboring reports (bukhari:536, bukhari:537) attributing extreme summer heat and winter cold to the two breaths of Hell.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَبْرِدُوا بِالظُّهْرِ، فَإِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Pray Zuhr prayer when it becomes (a bit) cooler as the severity of heat is from the raging of the Hell-fire

bukhari:538.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase 'from the raging of the Hell-fire' (*min fayḥ jahannam*) is merely a metaphor (*majāz*) comparing intense midday heat to the torment of Hell, or referring to an unseen metaphysical reality behind ordinary solar radiation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a direct causal origin (فَإِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ), and immediate parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:536, bukhari:537, muslim:1395) detail the literal mechanism: Hell complained to Allah that its parts were consuming one another (أَكَلَ بَعْضِي بَعْضًا), so He granted it two physical exhalations (نَفَسَيْنِ) that directly cause the earth's peak summer heat and bitter winter frost (الزَّمْهَرِيرِ). Consequently, both Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* explicitly refute the metaphorical excuse, affirming that the hadith must be taken according to its literal, physical reality (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi* and *ʿalā ẓāhirihi*).

bukhari:539.note: Muhammad commands delaying the midday prayer during intense heat, declaring that severe heat originates from the raging of Hellfire (*fayḥ jahannam*). Classical commentators such as Ibn Ḥajar and Al-Nawawī affirm that the dominant orthodox position interprets this causal link literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*), as reinforced by the narration attributing seasonal extremes to the two breaths of Hellfire (bukhari:536).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ، فَإِذَا اشْتَدَّ الْحَرُّ فَأَبْرِدُوا بِالصَّلاَةِ
problematic_excerpt.english: The severity of heat is from the raging of the Hell-fire, and in very hot weather pray (Zuhr) when it becomes cooler

bukhari:539.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that attributing scorching weather to the raging of Hellfire (*fayḥ jahannam*) is merely a figurative metaphor (*majāz*) meant to remind believers of the hereafter rather than a literal meteorological claim. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that severe heat originates directly 'from the exhalation and boiling of Hell' (*min fayḥ jahannam*), which parallel Sahih narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 537 and 3260) cement as a literal physical etiology by explaining that Allah granted Hell two actual breaths (*nafasayn*) each year—causing the peak heat of summer and the bitter frost (*al-zamharīr*) of winter. Consequently, premier Sunni commentators including Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* explicitly refute the metaphorical evasion and affirm that the statement must be taken according to its literal reality (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatih*).

bukhari:3258.note: Muhammad commands delaying the midday prayer until the weather cools, declaring that severe earthly heat originates from the boiling exhalation of Hellfire (*fayḥ jahannam*). Classical commentators such as Ibn Ḥajar and al-Nawawī affirm that the majority of Sunni scholars understand this literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*), as confirmed by parallel narrations (bukhari:3260) attributing extreme summer heat and winter cold to Hell's two physical breaths.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَبْرِدُوا بِالصَّلاَةِ، فَإِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Delay the (Zuhr) Prayer till it gets cooler, for the severity of heat is from the increase in heat of Hell (fire)

bukhari:3258.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase 'from the raging breath of Hell' (*min fayḥ jahannam*) is merely a figurative metaphor (*majāz*) meant to remind believers of the hereafter, or an unseen metaphysical reality compatible with modern meteorology. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a direct causal link (*fa-inna shiddata al-ḥarri min fayḥi jahannam*), and parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:537, bukhari:3260) foreclose any metaphorical reading by explaining that Hellfire complained to Allah of consuming itself and was granted two literal breaths (*nafasayn*) each year—generating both the scorching heat of summer and the bitter frost (*zamharīr*) of winter. Furthermore, both Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* explicitly reject the allegorical excuse, affirming that mainstream Sunni orthodoxy holds that these seasonal extremes literally issue from the physical substance of Hell (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi wa ẓāhirihi*).

bukhari:3425.note: Muhammad declares that the Jerusalem sanctuary (al-Masjid al-Aqsa) was built forty years after the Kaaba (al-Masjid al-Haram), a report Bukhari places directly within his chapter on Solomon despite the Quran attributing the Kaaba's foundations to Abraham ([Quran 2:127](quran://2/127)) roughly a millennium before Solomon built the Jerusalem Temple c. 960 BC ([1 Kings 6:1](bible://1kgs/6/1)). Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar in *Fath al-Bari* acknowledge this thousand-year gap between Abraham and Solomon as a chronological problem (*ishkal*), attempting to resolve it by positing earlier, unrecorded foundations of both sanctuaries by Adam or Jacob.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ‏.‏ أَىُّ مَسْجِدٍ وُضِعَ أَوَّلُ قَالَ ‏"‏ الْمَسْجِدُ الْحَرَامُ ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْتُ ثُمَّ أَىٌّ قَالَ ‏"‏ ثُمَّ الْمَسْجِدُ الأَقْصَى ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْتُ كَمْ كَانَ بَيْنَهُمَا قَالَ ‏"‏ أَرْبَعُونَ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Which mosque was built first?" He replied, "Al-Masjid-ul-Haram." I asked, "Which (was built) next?" He replied, "Al-Masjid-ul-Aqsa (i.e. Jerusalem)." I asked, "What was the period in between them?" He replied, "Forty (years)."

bukhari:3425.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—that Abraham (c. 2000 BC) and Solomon (c. 960 BC) were merely later renovators (*mujaddidān*), claiming the original foundations (*wuḍiʿa*) of both sanctuaries were laid forty years apart by Adam or by Abraham and his grandson Jacob. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in the immediately adjacent narration (bukhari:3364–bukhari:3365) that when Abraham arrived in Mecca there was no building at all—only a barren red hillock (*rabwah ḥamrāʾ*) upon which he and Ishmael built the Kaaba from scratch—while Quran 2:127 and 3:96–97 directly tie the very first house established (*أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ*) for mankind to Abraham's construction (*مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ*). Because neither the Quran nor any authentic Hadith ever credits Adam or Jacob with building *al-Masjid al-Aqṣā* (whereas Sunan al-Nasa'i 693 and 1 Kings 6:1 attribute the Jerusalem Temple's construction to Solomon), the 'prior foundation' claim collapses as an uncorroborated *ad hoc* invention designed to salvage a thousand-year chronological error.

muslim:416.note: Muhammad states that during his ascension to the seventh heaven he saw four rivers issuing from "its root" (min aṣlihā—referring to Sidrat al-Muntahā, the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary explicitly named in the unabridged parallel reports muslim:411 and bukhari:3887): two hidden rivers and two manifest rivers. When he asks Gabriel to identify them, Gabriel declares that the two hidden rivers are in Paradise while the two manifest rivers are the Nile and the Euphrates.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَحَدَّثَ نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ رَأَى أَرْبَعَةَ أَنْهَارٍ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَصْلِهَا نَهْرَانِ ظَاهِرَانِ وَنَهْرَانِ بَاطِنَانِ ‏"‏ فَقُلْتُ يَا جِبْرِيلُ مَا هَذِهِ الأَنْهَارُ قَالَ أَمَّا النَّهْرَانِ الْبَاطِنَانِ فَنَهْرَانِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ وَأَمَّا الظَّاهِرَانِ فَالنِّيلُ وَالْفُرَاتُ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He (the narrator) narrat- ed in this hadith that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) told that he saw four rivers which flowed from (the root of the lote-tree of the farthest limits): two manifest rivers and two hidden rivers. I said: ' Gabriel! what are these rivers? He replied: The two hidden rivers are the rivers of Paradise, and as regards the two manifest ones, they are the Nile and the Euphrates.

muslim:416.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that describing the Nile and Euphrates as originating in the seventh heaven is merely a metaphor for their immense blessing (*barakah*) and fertility, citing secondary allegorical opinions recorded in Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad saw the four rivers literally "exiting from its root" (*yakhruju min aṣlihā* / يَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَصْلِهَا) at the heavenly Lote-tree, directly contrasting the two "hidden" (*bāṭinān*) rivers of Paradise with the two "manifest" (*ẓāhirān*) physical rivers on earth (وَأَمَّا الظَّاهِرَانِ فَالنِّيلُ وَالْفُرَاتُ). Moreover, both Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar affirm that the authoritative Sunni position (*al-aṣaḥḥ*) is the literal reading (*al-ẓāhir*)—that the physical waters of the Nile and Euphrates actually originate in Paradise before descending into the earth—locking the Hadith into an ancient Near Eastern cosmological myth falsified by modern geography and the hydrological cycle.

muslim:1398.note: Muhammad declares that this heat comes from the exhalation of Hellfire (*fayḥ jahannam*) and commands delaying the prayer until it cools. Classical commentators such as al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar affirm that mainstream orthodoxy interprets this literally (*ḥaqīqatan*), reinforced by parallel reports (bukhari:536) attributing summer heat and winter cold to two breaths of Hell.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ هَذَا الْحَرَّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ فَأَبْرِدُوا بِالصَّلاَةِ
problematic_excerpt.english: This heat is from the exhalation of Hell-fire, so delay the prayer till it is cool

muslim:1398.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that describing summer heat as the 'exhalation of Hell-fire' (*fayḥ jahannam*) is merely a poetic metaphor meant to remind believers of the hereafter rather than a literal meteorological claim. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a direct causal origin (*inna hādhā al-ḥarra min fayḥi jahannam*), and parallel Sahih narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 537; *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 1399) detail that Hell complained to Allah of overcrowding and was granted two physical breaths (*nafasān*) per year, which directly cause the earth's severest summer heat and winter frost (*zamharīr*). Consequently, classical Sunni authorities like Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) explicitly reject the metaphorical excuse and insist the narration must be taken according to its literal, physical reality (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi wa-ẓāhirihi*).

muslim:1399.note: Muhammad commands delaying prayer until the midday heat subsides, declaring that intense heat comes from the exhalation and boiling over of Hellfire (*fayḥ jahannam*). Classical commentators such as al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar affirm that the majority of Sunni scholars interpret this literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*) rather than metaphorically, as reinforced by adjacent reports (muslim:1401) stating that Hellfire was granted two yearly breaths that cause extreme summer heat and winter cold.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَبْرِدُوا عَنِ الْحَرِّ فِي الصَّلاَةِ فَإِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Let the heat become less severe before prayer, for the intensity of heat is from the exhalation of Hell

muslim:1399.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase *min fayḥ jahannam* ('from the exhalation of Hell') is merely a figurative metaphor (*majāz*) comparing scorching summer weather to the torment of the hereafter, or an unseen metaphysical connection (*ghayb*) that does not contradict solar meteorology. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a direct causal explanation (*fa-inna shiddata al-ḥarri min fayḥi jahannam*), which parallel *Ṣaḥīḥ* narrations (`muslim:1395`, `bukhari:538`) cement as a physical etiology by detailing how Hell complained to Allah of consuming itself and was granted two literal breaths (*nafasāni*) per year that directly produce the earth's severest summer heat and bitterest winter frost (*al-zamharīr*). Consequently, classical authorities including Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) explicitly reject the metaphorical deflection and rule that the majority of Sunni scholars take this narration in its strict literal sense (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi wa-ẓāhirihi*).

muslim:1400.note: Muhammad commands that the noon prayer be delayed until the weather cools, declaring that intense heat comes from the exhalation of Hellfire (*fayḥ jahannam*). Classical commentators such as al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar note that the majority of Sunni scholars (*al-jumhūr*) interpret this literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*) as the actual cause of extreme heat rather than a metaphor.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِالظُّهْرِ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَبْرِدْ أَبْرِدْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ أَوْ قَالَ ‏"‏ انْتَظِرِ انْتَظِرْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ فَإِذَا اشْتَدَّ الْحَرُّ فَأَبْرِدُوا عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: The Mu'adhdbin (the announcer of the hour of prayer) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called for the noon prayer. Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Let it cool down, let it cool down, or he said: Wait, wait for the intensity of heat is from the exhalation of Hell. When the heat is intense, delay the prayer till it becomes cooler.

muslim:1400.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that describing midday heat as 'the exhalation of Hell' (*fayḥ jahannam*) is merely a figurative metaphor (*majāz*) meant to remind believers of the Hereafter rather than a literal meteorological claim. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states this as a direct causal fact (*inna shiddata al-ḥarri min fayḥi jahannam*), and parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:539) detail the physical mechanism: Hellfire complained to Allah of consuming itself, so He granted it two annual breaths (*nafasayn*) that directly cause Earth's severest summer heat and winter cold (*al-zamharīr*). Consequently, classical Sunni authorities like Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) explicitly reject the metaphorical excuse and insist that this thermal venting must be affirmed as a literal physical reality (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*).

bukhari:533.note: Muhammad instructs his followers to delay the midday prayer until the temperature cools down, declaring that the severity of atmospheric heat originates from the raging exhalation of Hellfire (*fayḥ jahannam*). Classical commentators such as Ibn Ḥajar and al-Nawawī affirm that this causal statement is taken upon its literal reality (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*), reinforced by parallel reports (bukhari:537) stating that Hell was permitted to exhale two breaths driving the extreme heat of summer and bitter cold of winter.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا اشْتَدَّ الْحَرُّ فَأَبْرِدُوا عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ، فَإِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ
problematic_excerpt.english: If it is very hot, then pray the Zuhr prayer when it becomes (a bit) cooler, as the severity of the heat is from the raging of the Hell-fire

bukhari:533.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase 'from the raging of Hellfire' (*min fayḥ jahannam*) is merely a figurative metaphor (*majāz*) intended to remind believers that intense summer heat resembles the torment of Hell. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a direct causal origin (*fa-inna shiddata al-ḥarri min fayḥi jahannam*), which Muhammad himself defines literally in the immediate companion narration (bukhari:536) by claiming that Hellfire complained of consuming itself (*akala baʿḍī baʿḍan*) and was granted two physical breaths (*nafasayn*) that directly cause the earth's extreme summer heat and winter frost (*al-zamharīr*). Furthermore, both Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* explicitly reject the metaphorical deflection, affirming that orthodox Sunni scholarship holds this meteorological claim to be strictly literal (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*).

bukhari:534.note: Muhammad instructs delaying the midday prayer during intense heat, declaring that severe heat originates from the raging of Hellfire (*fayḥ jahannam*). The immediate chapter context (bukhari:536) and classical commentators like Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi affirm this literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihā*), explaining that Hell was granted two breaths that cause extreme summer heat and winter cold.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا اشْتَدَّ الْحَرُّ فَأَبْرِدُوا عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ، فَإِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ
problematic_excerpt.english: If it is very hot, then pray the Zuhr prayer when it becomes (a bit) cooler, as the severity of the heat is from the raging of the Hell-fire

bukhari:534.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that attributing severe midday heat to the 'raging of Hellfire' (*fayḥ jahannam*) is merely a poetic metaphor meant to remind believers of the Hereafter. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a direct causal link (*fa-inna shiddat al-ḥarri min fayḥ jahannam*), which immediate parallel narrations (`bukhari:536`, `bukhari:537`, `bukhari:3260`) expand into a literal meteorological etiology where Hellfire complained to Allah that its parts were consuming each other (*akala baʿḍī baʿḍan*) and was granted two physical exhalations (*nafasayn*) per year that directly produce earthly summer heat and winter frost. Consequently, both Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* explicitly reject the metaphorical excuse and affirm that orthodox Sunni scholarship takes this overflow of Hellfire onto the earth according to its literal, physical reality (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi wa-ẓāhirihi*).

bukhari:629.note: After repeatedly instructing the caller to delay the midday prayer call until the weather cooled, Muhammad declares that the severity of midday heat originates from the raging exhalation of Hellfire (*fayḥ jahannam*). Classical commentators such as Ibn Ḥajar and al-Nawawī affirm that orthodox scholarship takes this statement literally, consistent with parallel reports attributing extreme summer heat and winter cold to two breaths exhaled by Hell (bukhari:536).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُنَّا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي سَفَرٍ فَأَرَادَ الْمُؤَذِّنُ أَنْ يُؤَذِّنَ فَقَالَ لَهُ ‏"‏ أَبْرِدْ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُؤَذِّنَ فَقَالَ لَهُ ‏"‏ أَبْرِدْ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُؤَذِّنَ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُ ‏"‏ أَبْرِدْ ‏"‏‏.‏ حَتَّى سَاوَى الظِّلُّ التُّلُولَ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏{‏إِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ‏}‏
problematic_excerpt.english: We were in the company of the Prophet (ﷺ) on a journey and the Mu'adh-dhin wanted to pronounce the Adhan for the (Zuhr) prayer. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him, "Let it become cooler." Then he again wanted to pronounce the Adhan but the Prophet; said to him, "Let it become cooler." The Mu'adh-dhin again wanted to pronounce the Adhan for the prayer but the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Let it become cooler," till the shadows of the hillocks become equal to their sizes. The Prophet (ﷺ) added, "The severity of the heat is from the raging of Hell

bukhari:629.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase *fayḥ jahannam* ('the raging of Hell') is merely a figurative metaphor meant to remind believers of the Hereafter during scorching desert afternoons. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a direct causal origin (*inna shiddata al-ḥarri min fayḥi jahannam*), which parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:536`, `bukhari:3260`) expand into a literal meteorological mechanism where Hell complained to Allah and was granted two physical 'breaths' (*nafasayn*) per year that directly produce the earth's severest summer heat and winter cold (*zamharīr*). Consequently, classical Sunni authorities like Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* explicitly reject metaphorical reinterpretations and insist that Hell's exhalation into the earthly atmosphere must be taken upon its literal reality (*ʿalā ẓāhirihi*).

bukhari:3259.note: Muhammad commands delaying the prayer until the weather cools, declaring that intense atmospheric heat originates from the raging heat and exhalation of Hellfire (*fayḥ jahannam*). Both Ibn Ḥajar and Al-Nawawī affirm that the majority of Sunni scholars hold this statement to its literal reality (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi wa-ẓāhirihi*), reinforced by the adjacent report (bukhari:3260) stating that Allah granted Hellfire two breaths that cause the extreme heat of summer and bitter cold of winter.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَبْرِدُوا بِالصَّلاَةِ فَإِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Delay the (Zuhr) Prayer till it gets cooler, for the severity of heat is from the increase in the heat of Hell (fire)

bukhari:3259.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase 'from the raging of Hell' (*min fayḥ jahannam*) is merely a figurative metaphor (*majāz*) comparing intense midday heat to Hellfire as a spiritual reminder rather than making a literal meteorological claim. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that severe heat originates directly from the boiling exhalation of Hell (فَإِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحَرِّ مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ), and the immediately following narration (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3260; cf. 537) refutes any metaphorical reading by detailing the physical mechanism: Hellfire complained to Allah that its parts were consuming one another, so He permitted it to take two literal breaths (*nafasayn*) each year—one in summer causing extreme heat and one in winter causing extreme frost (*zamharīr*). Consequently, both Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* affirm that mainstream Sunni orthodoxy requires taking this report according to its literal, physical reality (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*).

bukhari:7517.note: During his ascension into the lowest heaven, Muhammad sees two flowing rivers that Gabriel identifies as the origin ('unsuruhuma) of the Nile and Euphrates rivers. Although this narration via Sharik bin 'Abdullah concludes with Muhammad waking up in the Sacred Mosque, parallel accounts of the ascension (bukhari:3207, muslim:164) likewise state that the Nile and Euphrates originate from the Lote Tree in heaven.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ مَا هَذَانِ النَّهَرَانِ يَا جِبْرِيلُ قَالَ هَذَا النِّيلُ وَالْفُرَاتُ عُنْصُرُهُمَا
problematic_excerpt.english: He asked, "What are these two rivers, O Gabriel?" Gabriel said, "These are the sources of the Nile and the Euphrates."

bukhari:7517.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this description is merely a metaphor for the spiritual blessing (*barakah*) and sweetness of the Nile and Euphrates, or they attempt to dismiss the wording by claiming the transmitter Sharīk ibn ʿAbdillāh confused details of the Night Journey. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *hādhā al-Nīlu wa-l-Furātu ʿunṣuruhumā* (هَذَا النِّيلُ وَالْفُرَاتُ عُنْصُرُهُمَا—'these are the origin/source of the Nile and the Euphrates') regarding two literally flowing rivers (*naharayni yaṭṭaridāni*), and this exact cosmological claim is corroborated across independent chains free of Sharīk—such as *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3207 and *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 164—which state that two 'manifest/visible rivers' (*naharāni ẓāhirāni*) spring directly from the base of the Lote Tree (*Sidrat al-Muntahā*) as the earthly Nile and Euphrates. Consequently, classical scholars like Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* explicitly affirmed that the primary outward meaning (*ẓāhir*) of the text is that these rivers literally originate in the heavenly realm before descending to earth.

muslim:7054.note: Taking hold of Abu Hurayrah's hand, Muhammad declares that Allah created the soil on Saturday, mountains on Sunday, and trees on Monday, yet did not create light until Wednesday. This chronology places the formation of the earth, its mountains, and its trees days before the existence of light.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَخَذَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِيَدِي فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ التُّرْبَةَ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ وَخَلَقَ فِيهَا الْجِبَالَ يَوْمَ الأَحَدِ وَخَلَقَ الشَّجَرَ يَوْمَ الاِثْنَيْنِ وَخَلَقَ الْمَكْرُوهَ يَوْمَ الثُّلاَثَاءِ وَخَلَقَ النُّورَ يَوْمَ الأَرْبِعَاءِ وَبَثَّ فِيهَا الدَّوَابَّ يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ وَخَلَقَ آدَمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ بَعْدَ الْعَصْرِ مِنْ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ فِي آخِرِ الْخَلْقِ وَفِي آخِرِ سَاعَةٍ مِنْ سَاعَاتِ الْجُمُعَةِ فِيمَا بَيْنَ الْعَصْرِ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) took hold of my hands and said:Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, created the clay on Saturday and He created the mountains on Sunday and He created the trees on Monday and He created the things entailing labour on Tuesday and created light on Wednesday and He caused the animals to spread on Thursday and created Adam (peace be upon him) after 'Asr on Friday; the last creation at the last hour of the hours of Friday, i. e. between afternoon and night.

muslim:7054.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this report is either an unprophetic statement mistakenly attributed to Muhammad by a transmitter or a non-chronological description of earthly provisions after the cosmos already existed. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Messenger of Allah took Abu Huraira by the hand (أَخَذَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِيَدِي فَقَالَ) and declared in sequence that Allah created the soil (التُّرْبَةَ) on Saturday, the mountains (الْجِبَالَ) on Sunday, the trees (الشَّجَرَ) on Monday, and light (النُّورَ) on Wednesday. By recording this step-by-step daily timeline as Muhammad's direct teaching in muslim:7054, the narration places the creation of botanical tree life two days before the creation of light ([Genesis 1:3](bible://gn/1/3), [Genesis 1:11](bible://gn/1/11)).

muslim:7054.note: Muhammad enumerates seven consecutive days of creation from Saturday through Friday afternoon—assigning soil to Saturday, mountains to Sunday, trees to Monday, hated things to Tuesday, light to Wednesday, animals to Thursday, and Adam to Friday. This seven-day schedule contradicts the Quranic declaration that Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days ([Quran 7:54](quran://7/54), [Quran 41:9](quran://41/9), [Quran 50:38](quran://50/38)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَخَذَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِيَدِي فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ التُّرْبَةَ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ وَخَلَقَ فِيهَا الْجِبَالَ يَوْمَ الأَحَدِ وَخَلَقَ الشَّجَرَ يَوْمَ الاِثْنَيْنِ وَخَلَقَ الْمَكْرُوهَ يَوْمَ الثُّلاَثَاءِ وَخَلَقَ النُّورَ يَوْمَ الأَرْبِعَاءِ وَبَثَّ فِيهَا الدَّوَابَّ يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ وَخَلَقَ آدَمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ بَعْدَ الْعَصْرِ مِنْ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ فِي آخِرِ الْخَلْقِ وَفِي آخِرِ سَاعَةٍ مِنْ سَاعَاتِ الْجُمُعَةِ فِيمَا بَيْنَ الْعَصْرِ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) took hold of my hands and said:Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, created the clay on Saturday and He created the mountains on Sunday and He created the trees on Monday and He created the things entailing labour on Tuesday and created light on Wednesday and He caused the animals to spread on Thursday and created Adam (peace be upon him) after 'Asr on Friday; the last creation at the last hour of the hours of Friday, i. e. between afternoon and night.

muslim:7054.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration either suffers from a transmitter defect in the chain from Abu Huraira or refers only to the furnishing of the earth so that Friday is excluded from the Quranic six-day total. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states through an authenticated chain in muslim:7054 that Allah performed specific acts of creation (خَلَقَ) on all seven named days of the week, beginning with the soil on Saturday (يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ) and concluding with the creation of Adam after 'Asr on Friday as the last of creation (فِي آخِرِ الْخَلْقِ). Counting Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday yields seven distinct days of divine creation, contradicting the six-day creation total stated in [Quran 7:54](quran://7/54), [Quran 41:9](quran://41/9), and [Quran 50:38](quran://50/38).

muslim:411.note: Muhammad states that he rode al-Buraq—a white beast larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule whose stride reaches the horizon—to the Jerusalem Temple (*Bayt al-Maqdis*), tethered it to the ring used by the prophets, and entered (*dakhaltu*), prayed two rak'ahs inside (*fihi*), and exited (*thumma kharajtu*) the mosque (*al-masjid*) ([Quran 17:1](quran://17/1)). This account describes entering and exiting a standing structure in Jerusalem despite the Romans having destroyed the Second Temple in AD 70 and no mosque building existing on the Temple Mount during Muhammad's lifetime.
