problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ أَبُو سَلَمَةَ كَانَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ يُحَدِّثُهُمَا كِلْتَيْهِمَا عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ثُمَّ صَمَتَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ عَنْ قَوْلِهِ ‏"‏ لاَ عَدْوَى ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَأَقَامَ عَلَى ‏"‏ أَنْ لاَ يُورِدُ مُمْرِضٌ عَلَى مُصِحٍّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَالَ الْحَارِثُ بْنُ أَبِي ذُبَابٍ - وَهُوَ ابْنُ عَمِّ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ - قَدْ كُنْتُ أَسْمَعُكَ يَا أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ تُحَدِّثَنَا مَعَ هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ حَدِيثًا آخَرَ قَدْ سَكَتَّ عَنْهُ كُنْتَ تَقُولُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لاَ عَدْوَى ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَأَبَى أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ أَنْ يَعْرِفَ ذَلِكَ وَقَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ يُورِدُ مُمْرِضٌ عَلَى مُصِحٍّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَمَا رَآهُ الْحَارِثُ فِي ذَلِكَ حَتَّى غَضِبَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ فَرَطَنَ بِالْحَبَشِيَّةِ فَقَالَ لِلْحَارِثِ أَتَدْرِي مَاذَا قُلْتُ قَالَ لاَ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ أَبَيْتُ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو سَلَمَةَ وَلَعَمْرِي لَقَدْ كَانَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ يُحَدِّثُنَا أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ عَدْوَى ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَنَسِيَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ أَوْ نَسَخَ أَحَدُ الْقَوْلَيْنِ الآخَرَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Salama said that Abu Huraira used to narrate these two (different ahadith) from Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), but afterwards Abu Huraira became silent on these words:" There is no transitive disease," but he stuck to this that the sick person should not be taken to one who is healthy. Harith b. Abu Dhubab (and he was the first cousin of Abu Huraira) said: Abu Huraira, I used to hear from you that you narrated to us along with this hadith and the other one also (there is no transitive disease), but now you observe silence about it. You used to say that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: There is no transitive disease. Abu Huraira denied having any knowledge of that, but he said that the sick camel should not be taken to the healthy one. Harith, however, did not agree with him, which irritated Abu Huraira and he said to him some words in the Abyssinian language. He said to Harith: Do you know what I said to you? He said: No. Abu Huraira said: I simply denied having said it. Abu Salama sad: By my life, Abu Huraira in fact used to report Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) having said: There is no transitive disease. I do not know whether Abu Huraira has forgotten it or he deemed it an abrogated statement in the light of the other one

muslim:5791.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Abu Huraira possessed unfailing memory and integrity in transmitting prophetic traditions, and that he merely withheld the first narration out of caution so listeners would not neglect practical quarantine measures. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that when his cousin Harith b. Abu Dhubab reminded him of what he used to narrate, 'فَأَبَى أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ أَنْ يَعْرِفَ ذَلِكَ' ('Abu Huraira denied having any knowledge of that'), grew angry ('غَضِبَ'), spoke in the Abyssinian language ('فَرَطَنَ بِالْحَبَشِيَّةِ'), and declared 'قُلْتُ أَبَيْتُ' ('I simply denied having said it'). Instead of offering a harmonizing explanation, Abu Huraira repudiated a statement that Abu Salama swore ('وَلَعَمْرِي', 'By my life') he had previously narrated from Muhammad, leaving Abu Salama unable to tell whether Abu Huraira had forgotten his own narration ('أَنَسِيَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ') or dropped it due to abrogation.

bukhari:5782.note: Muhammad commands that if a fly falls into a person's vessel, they must submerge it completely before discarding it, declaring that one of its wings contains healing and the other contains a disease.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا وَقَعَ الذُّبَابُ فِي إِنَاءِ أَحَدِكُمْ، فَلْيَغْمِسْهُ كُلَّهُ، ثُمَّ لْيَطْرَحْهُ، فَإِنَّ فِي أَحَدِ جَنَاحَيْهِ شِفَاءً وَفِي الآخَرِ دَاءً
problematic_excerpt.english: If a fly falls in the vessel of any of you, let him dip all of it (into the vessel) and then throw it away, for in one of its wings there is a disease and in the other there is healing (antidote for it) i e. the treatment for that disease

bukhari:5782.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this command is a 'scientific miracle' anticipating modern microbiology by claiming that flies carry bacteriophages or antibiotic-producing microbes on their exoskeletons, while citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* (and Abu Dawud 3844) to claim the fly instinctively dips its pathogenic wing first. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that 'in one of its two wings is a cure and in the other is a disease' (فِي أَحَدِ جَنَاحَيْهِ شِفَاءً وَفِي الآخَرِ دَاءً), asserting a literal, asymmetrical anatomical division between a toxic wing and a curative wing rather than general surface microbiota. Furthermore, the imperative to submerge the entire fly (فَلْيَغْمِسْهُ كُلَّهُ) forces its feces-contaminated legs, proboscis, and gut pathogens directly into the human beverage, increasing rather than neutralizing microbial contamination.

muslim:5788.note: Muhammad declares that there is no disease contagion (*lā ʿadwā*) and counters a Bedouin's observation that a mangy camel infects an entire herd of healthy camels by asking who infected the first camel. This denial of physical animal-to-animal transmission stands in tension with parallel reports prescribing plague quarantine (muslim:5787) and commanding people to flee from a leper (bukhari:5707).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ أَبِي، هُرَيْرَةَ حِينَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لاَ عَدْوَى وَلاَ صَفَرَ وَلاَ هَامَةَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ أَعْرَابِيٌّ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَمَا بَالُ الإِبِلِ تَكُونُ فِي الرَّمْلِ كَأَنَّهَا الظِّبَاءُ فَيَجِيءُ الْبَعِيرُ الأَجْرَبُ فَيَدْخُلُ فِيهَا فَيُجْرِبُهَا كُلَّهَا قَالَ ‏"‏ فَمَنْ أَعْدَى الأَوَّلَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:There is no infection, no safar, no hama. A desert Arab said: Allah's Messenger, how is it that when the camel is in the sand it is like a deer-then a camel afflicted with scab mixes with it and it is affected by sub? He (the Holy Prophet) said: Who infected the first one? Note: The majority of scholars interpret this to mean that these things in and of themselves do not transmit or cause harm through supernatural or hidden means but that Allah is ultimately in control and any fearful superstition around these is false

muslim:5788.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was not denying physical disease transmission, but merely teaching that diseases do not transmit harm in and of themselves through supernatural means apart from Allah's control. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *lā ʿadwā* ("there is no contagion"), prompting a Bedouin to counter with the physical observation of a mangy camel (*al-baʿīr al-ajrab*) mixing with healthy camels and infecting all of them (*fa-yujribuhā kullahā*). Rather than affirming physical contagion as a secondary biological cause under divine decree, Muhammad dismisses the transmission of disease from one animal to another by asking, "Then who infected the first one?" (*fa-man aʿdā al-awwal*).

muslim:5792.note: Abu Huraira reports Muhammad declaring that there is no transitive disease (*la 'adwa*) while simultaneously instructing that the ill should not be brought to the healthy. In the immediate parallel report (muslim:5791; cf. bukhari:5771), Abu Huraira later ceased narrating the first clause denying contagion due to the contradiction between the two statements.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَخْبَرَنِي أَبُو سَلَمَةَ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، يُحَدِّثُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ عَدْوَى ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَيُحَدِّثُ مَعَ ذَلِكَ ‏"‏ لاَ يُورِدُ الْمُمْرِضُ عَلَى الْمُصِحِّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ بِمِثْلِ حَدِيثِ يُونُسَ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:There is no transitive disease and he also reported along with it: The ill should not be taken to the healthy

muslim:5792.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the denial of contagion only means diseases do not transmit independently of divine decree, claiming the instruction to keep the sick away from the healthy proves quarantine. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "لاَ عَدْوَى" ('There is no transitive disease') as an unqualified negation containing no mention of independent causation or divine permission. Reporting this categorical denial alongside the rule "لاَ يُورِدُ الْمُمْرِضُ عَلَى الْمُصِحِّ" ('The ill should not be taken to the healthy', cf. bukhari:5771 and muslim:5791) leaves a direct contradiction within the report itself.

muslim:5794.note: Muhammad declares that 'there is no transitive disease' (la 'adwa), grouping biological contagion alongside pre-Islamic superstitions about bird omens (hamah), rain-stars (naw'), and the month of Safar. This denial conflicts with his command that 'the ill should not be taken to the healthy' (muslim:5792), a discrepancy that led the narrator Abu Huraira to cease transmitting the 'no contagion' report (muslim:5791).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ لاَ عَدْوَى وَلاَ هَامَةَ وَلاَ نَوْءَ وَلاَ صَفَرَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:There is no transitive disease, no huma, no star promising rain, no safar

muslim:5794.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the denial of contagion means only that diseases do not transmit independently of Allah's decree, rather than denying biological transmission itself. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states 'there is no transitive disease' (lā ʿadwā) as a categorical negation and places it in an identical grammatical series with non-existent pre-Islamic superstitions: 'no huma, no star promising rain, no safar' (wa-lā hāmata wa-lā nawʾa wa-lā ṣafara). Grouping contagion directly alongside fictitious omens of owls, rain-stars, and the month of Safar treats disease transmission itself as a false superstition rather than a real physical cause.

muslim:5795.note: Muhammad declares that infectious contagion ('There is no contagion') does not exist, negating disease transmission in the exact same grammatical structure as evil omens and desert ghouls. In parallel reports, Abu Huraira stopped narrating 'There is no contagion' when confronted with its contradiction against quarantine orders (muslim:5791).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ جَابِرٍ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ لاَ عَدْوَى وَلاَ طِيَرَةَ وَلاَ غُولَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Jabir reported Allal's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:There is no transitive disease, no ill omen, no ghoul. Note: The majority of scholars interpret this to mean that these things in and of themselves do not transmit or cause harm through supernatural or hidden means but that Allah is ultimately in control and any fearful superstition around these is false

muslim:5795.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was not denying the medical reality of infectious disease, but merely teaching that contagion does not transmit or cause harm in and of itself apart from Allah's control. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "لاَ عَدْوَى وَلاَ طِيَرَةَ وَلاَ غُولَ" ("There is no contagion, no evil omen, and no ghoul"), containing none of the apologetic qualifiers appended as an explanatory note in the published English rendering. Because the categorical negation "لاَ" ("there is no") governs all three nouns identically, supplying "in and of itself" to rescue contagion would grammatically require that evil omens and ghouls also exist and cause harm by Allah's permission (cf. bukhari:5757, muslim:5791, muslim:5794).

muslim:5796.note: Muhammad issues an unqualified negation of contagious or transitive disease (*lā ʿadwā*), grouping disease transmission alongside ghouls (*ghūl*) and *ṣafar* with no textual restriction limiting the denial to autonomous causation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ جَابِرٍ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ لاَ عَدْوَى وَلاَ غُولَ وَلاَ صَفَرَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Jabir reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:There is no transitive disease, no ghoul, no safar

muslim:5796.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase *lā ʿadwā* only negates the pre-Islamic belief that disease spreads independently of Allah's decree rather than denying physical contagion itself. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *lā ʿadwā wa-lā ghūla wa-lā ṣafara* ("There is no transitive disease, no ghoul, no safar"), issuing an unqualified categorical negation with no mention of secondary causation. By placing transitive disease (*ʿadwā*) in the exact same grammatical construction as fictitious ghouls (*ghūl*) and the *ṣafar* superstition, the declaration treats biological contagion itself as a non-existent myth (`bukhari:5707`, `muslim:5791`, `muslim:5797`).

bukhari:5768.note: Muhammad declares that anyone who eats 'Ajwa dates (specified as seven dates in a variant transmission) in the morning will not be harmed by poison or magic until nightfall. Notably, other authentic traditions record that Muhammad himself was bewitched (bukhari:5766) and later died from the lingering effects of poison (bukhari:4428).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: مَنِ اصْطَبَحَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ تَمَرَاتٍ عَجْوَةً، لَمْ يَضُرُّهُ سَمٌّ وَلاَ سِحْرٌ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ
problematic_excerpt.english: If somebody takes some `Ajwa dates every morning, he will not be affected by poison or magic on that day till night.

bukhari:5768.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim—that this protection stems from a spiritual blessing (barakah) exclusive to Medina's 'Ajwa dates or merely refers to general nutritional resistance against mild toxins. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an unconditional, universal guarantee—«لَمْ يَضُرُّهُ سَمٌّ وَلاَ سِحْرٌ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ» ('neither poison nor magic will harm him that day until night')—where the indefinite nouns sammun (poison) and siḥrun (magic) in a negative clause (nakirah fī siyāq al-nafy) grammatically mandate absolute immunity against all poisons and sorcery. Furthermore, this remedy failed Muhammad himself while living in Medina, as he was both bewitched by Labīd ibn al-A'ṣam (bukhari:5763) and ultimately killed by the Khaybar poison, which he confessed on his deathbed had severed his aorta (bukhari:4428).

bukhari:5769.note: Muhammad declares that anyone who eats seven 'Ajwa dates in the morning will not be harmed by poison or magic on that day (`لَمْ يَضُرُّهُ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ سَمٌّ وَلاَ سِحْرٌ`). Classical commentators such as al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar address this unqualified promise of physical immunity by proposing that the effect is restricted to dates grown in Medina or exclusively to Muhammad's era.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: مَنْ تَصَبَّحَ سَبْعَ تَمَرَاتٍ عَجْوَةً، لَمْ يَضُرُّهُ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ سَمٌّ وَلاَ سِحْرٌ
problematic_excerpt.english: If Somebody takes seven 'Ajwa dates in the morning, neither magic nor poison will hurt him that day

bukhari:5769.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—that this protection applies exclusively to the `'Ajwah` dates of Medina through special prophetic *barakah*, or that "poison" (*samm*) merely refers to mild bodily toxins rather than lethal substances. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an unconditional, universal rule (`مَنْ تَصَبَّحَ... لَمْ يَضُرُّهُ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ سَمٌّ وَلاَ سِحْرٌ`), where the indefinite nouns `سَمٌّ` (poison) and `سِحْرٌ` (magic) fall under the negation `لَمْ يَضُرُّهُ` ("will not harm him"), grammatically mandating total immunity against any literal poison or sorcery. Moreover, *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* itself refutes the Medina defense by recording that Muhammad—while residing in Medina—fell victim to the magic of Labīd ibn al-A'ṣam (`bukhari:5765`) and died proclaiming that the literal poison he ingested at Khaybar had severed his aorta (`bukhari:4428`).

bukhari:5779.note: Muhammad declares without qualification that anyone who eats seven 'Ajwa dates in the morning will not be harmed by either poison or magic for the rest of that day. While classical commentators attempt to reconcile this medical claim by restricting its efficacy exclusively to dates grown in Medina's 'Aliyah district or to Muhammad's own era, the text here states the immunity as a general rule.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: مَنِ اصْطَبَحَ بِسَبْعِ تَمَرَاتٍ عَجْوَةٍ لَمْ يَضُرَّهُ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ سَمٌّ وَلاَ سِحْرٌ
problematic_excerpt.english: Whoever takes seven 'Ajwa dates in the morning will not be effected by magic or poison on that day

bukhari:5779.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this promise merely describes general nutritional detoxifying properties, or—citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—claim the protection is restricted to specific Medinan dates (*'Ajwat al-'Āliyah*) and requires the eater's unwavering spiritual conviction (*yaqīn*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *lam yaḍurrahu dhālika al-yawma sammun wa-lā siḥrun* (لَمْ يَضُرَّهُ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ سَمٌّ وَلاَ سِحْرٌ), using indefinite nouns in a negative clause (*nakirah fī siyāq al-nafy*) to guarantee absolute, universal immunity against any poison or witchcraft whatsoever on that day. Furthermore, the appeal to Medinan provenance and spiritual conviction collapses under bukhari:5763 and 4428, which record that Muhammad himself—while residing in Medina—was successfully bewitched by Labīd ibn al-A'ṣam and ultimately died from the lingering effects of the poison he ingested at Khaybar.

bukhari:3262.note: Muhammad declares that human fever originates from the boiling heat of Hellfire (*fawr jahannam*) and commands sufferers to cool it with water. Bukhari classifies this report in the Book of the Beginning of Creation under the attributes of Hell, and classical commentators like Ibn Ḥajar and al-Nawawī affirm that the primary Sunni position takes the statement literally (*ʿalā ẓāhirihi*) as an actual manifestation of Hellfire's heat in this world.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: الْحُمَّى مِنْ فَوْرِ جَهَنَّمَ، فَأَبْرِدُوهَا عَنْكُمْ بِالْمَاءِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Fever is from the heat of the (Hell) Fire; so cool it with water

bukhari:3262.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that describing fever as coming from Hellfire is merely a metaphorical simile (*majāz*) meant to remind sick believers of the hereafter while offering the practical medical advice of cooling a fever with water. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that fever originates from the literal boiling eruption of Gehenna (*min fawr jahannam*, الْحُمَّى مِنْ فَوْرِ جَهَنَّمَ), using the partitive preposition *min* to denote physical origin rather than poetic comparison. Both Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* confirm that the normative Sunni position takes this literally (*ʿalā ẓāhirihi*) as an actual physical manifestation of Hell, which is reinforced by the preceding narration in the same chapter (`bukhari:3260`) teaching that earthly summer heat and winter cold are literal breaths exhaled by the Fire.

bukhari:3263.note: Muhammad declares that bodily fever originates from the boiling exhalation (*fayḥ*) of Hellfire and instructs cooling it with water. Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawi affirm that taking this statement literally—as an actual physical heat emanating from Hell—is the primary orthodox view, alongside secondary metaphorical readings.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: الْحُمَّى مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ، فَأَبْرِدُوهَا بِالْمَاءِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Fever is from the heat of the (Hell) Fire, so cool it with water

bukhari:3263.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that describing fever as coming from Hellfire is merely a figurative metaphor (*majāz*) comparing the burning sensation of a high temperature to the torment of the hereafter, while praising the instruction to cool it with water as ahead-of-its-time medical wisdom. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that fever originates *min fayḥ jahannam* ("from the raging exhalation of Hell"), a literal etiology reinforced by the immediately preceding narration in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* (3260) where Muhammad claims that earthly summer heat and winter cold are caused by Hellfire physically breathing twice a year. Furthermore, classical commentators like Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* affirm that the primary orthodox position takes this *ʿalā ẓāhirihi* (literally) as an actual physical portion of heat released from Gehenna.

bukhari:5723.note: Muhammad states that fever comes from the raging heat of Hell (*fayḥ jahannam*) and commands extinguishing it with water, an etiology the narrator Ibn Umar understood literally by praying for relief from divine punishment (*al-rijz*) when feverish.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ الْحُمَّى مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ فَأَطْفِئُوهَا بِالْمَاءِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ نَافِعٌ وَكَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ يَقُولُ اكْشِفْ عَنَّا الرِّجْزَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'Fever is from the heat of Hell, so put it out (cool it) with water.' " Nafi` added: `Abdullah used to say, "O Allah! Relieve us from the punishment,"

bukhari:5723.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that describing fever as originating from the 'heat of Hell' (*fayḥ jahannam*) is merely a metaphorical comparison (*majāz*) to remind believers of the hereafter, while citing the command to cool it with water as prophetic medical foresight. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the narrator, ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar, understood the etiology literally as an outbreak of hellish torment, praying during fevers, 'Relieve us from the punishment (*ikshif ʿannā al-rijz*).' Furthermore, Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* affirms that the literal meaning (*al-ḥaqīqah*) is the default, a pre-scientific cosmology confirmed by parallel narrations (e.g., *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 536 and 3260) where Muhammad equally attributes earthly summer heat and winter cold to the literal breathing (*nafasān*) of Hellfire.

bukhari:5725.note: Narrated by Aisha, Muhammad declares that fever originates from the raging heat of Hell (*fayḥ jahannam*) and commands cooling it with water. Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawi affirm that this statement is to be understood literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*) as a physical emanation from Hellfire rather than a metaphor.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ الْحُمَّى مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ فَابْرُدُوهَا بِالْمَاءِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Fever is from the heat of Hell, so abate fever with water

bukhari:5725.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that describing fever as coming from the heat of Hell is merely a metaphorical expression (*majāz*) comparing the severity of a fever to Hellfire, while praising the instruction to cool the body with water as prescient medical advice. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that fever is `مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ` (*min fayḥ jahannam*—literally originating 'from the raging exhalation of Hell') using a partitive/causal preposition rather than a simile, which is why Al-Bukhari cataloged the parallel narration (bukhari:3263) in the *Book of the Beginning of Creation* as proof of Hell's current physical existence. Furthermore, both Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* affirm that the default orthodox position takes this literally (*ʿalā ẓāhirihi*) as a physical emanation from Hell—matching Muhammad's literal claim in bukhari:3260 that summer heat and winter cold are caused by Hell's breathing.

bukhari:5726.note: Muhammad declares that human fever originates from the boiling breath of Hell (*fawḥ jahannam*) and commands cooling it with water. Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi affirm that this statement applies in its apparent literal sense (*ʿalā ẓāhirihi*) as an actual emanation from Hellfire rather than a metaphor.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ الْحُمَّى مِنْ فَوْحِ جَهَنَّمَ، فَابْرُدُوهَا بِالْمَاءِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "Fever is from the heat of Hell, so abate fever with water

bukhari:5726.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that describing fever as coming from Hell is merely a figurative metaphor (*majāz*) meant to remind believers of the hereafter, while praising the command to cool fever with water as miraculous medical foresight. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that fever originates *min fawḥ jahannam* (مِنْ فَوْحِ جَهَنَّمَ, literally 'from the boiling exhalation of Hell'), a literal etiology corroborated by parallel Sahih narrations (such as bukhari:3260 and 3262) in which Hellfire physically exhales onto Earth to cause terrestrial heat and fever. Furthermore, classical Sunni authorities like Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* confirm that the primary orthodox position takes this phrasing according to its literal outward reality (*ʿalā ẓāhirihi*) as an actual physical emanation from Hell rather than a figure of speech.

bukhari:3264.note: Muhammad declares that fever (*al-ḥummā*) comes from the boiling heat of Hellfire (*min fayḥ jahannam*) and commands cooling it with water, an etiology that classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar affirm as a literal physical origin from Hellfire.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: الْحُمَّى مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ فَأَبْرِدُوهَا بِالْمَاءِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Fever is from the heat of the (Hell) Fire; so abate fever with water

bukhari:3264.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that describing fever as coming from Hellfire is merely a figurative metaphor (*majāz*) comparing the intensity of illness to the hereafter while prescribing the practical medical remedy of cooling the body with water. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *al-ḥummā min fayḥ jahannam* ("fever is from the raging boil of Hell") as a direct causal origin, which both Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* insist is to be taken in its literal reality (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*) as an actual portion of Hell's heat emerging on earth. Moreover, Bukhari places this narration in the exact same chapter as `bukhari:3260`, which uses the identical term (*fayḥ*) to claim that summer heat waves are caused by Hell literally exhaling, proving Muhammad was teaching a literal cosmological superstition rather than a poetic simile.

muslim:5752.note: Reported through Ibn Umar, Muhammad declares that the severity of fever (*shiddata al-ḥummā*) comes from the boiling heat of Hellfire (*fayḥi jahannam*) and commands that it be cooled with water.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ إِنَّ شِدَّةَ الْحُمَّى مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ فَابْرُدُوهَا بِالْمَاءِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Ibn Umar reported Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) as saying:Fever is due to vehemence of the heat of Hell, so cool it with water

muslim:5752.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that describing fever as coming from Hellfire is merely a figurative metaphor for intense bodily heat, emphasizing instead the practical instruction to cool the body with water. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *inna shiddat al-ḥummā min fayḥi jahannam* ("indeed, the severity of fever is from the boiling heat of Hell"), using the preposition *min* ("from") to assert a direct physical origin rather than a simile, and grounds the command (*fa-brudūhā bi-l-mā'*, "so cool it with water") in that literal etiology across `muslim:5752`, `bukhari:3264`, `muslim:5751`, and `muslim:5753`.

muslim:5753.note: Muhammad declares that fever originates from the raging heat of Hellfire (*fayḥi jahannam*) and commands that it be extinguished with water.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ الْحُمَّى مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ فَأَطْفِئُوهَا بِالْمَاءِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Ibn Umar reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:Fever is from the vehement raging of the fire of Hell, so extinguish it with water

muslim:5753.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this statement is merely a metaphor comparing the intense heat of a fever to Hellfire while prescribing practical cooling with water. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that fever originates from the raging of Hell (*min fayḥi jahannam*) using the preposition *min* (from), and commands followers to extinguish it with water (*fa-aṭfiʾūhā bi-l-māʾ*). This literal causal claim is repeated in parallel narrations such as bukhari:3264, bukhari:5725, and muslim:5751, presenting bodily fever as a direct emission from Hellfire rather than a figure of speech.

muslim:5754.note: Muhammad declares that bodily fever originates from the raging heat of Hellfire (*fayḥi jahannam*) and commands that it be extinguished (*fa-aṭfiʾūhā*) with water.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ الْحُمَّى مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ فَأَطْفِئُوهَا بِالْمَاءِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Ibn 'Umar reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:Fever is from the vehement Paging of the Hell-fire, so cool it with water

muslim:5754.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that attributing fever to Hellfire is merely a figurative metaphor describing the intensity of bodily heat rather than a literal statement of its origin. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that fever is from the boiling heat of Hellfire (*al-ḥummā min fayḥi jahannam*) as a direct causal declaration and immediately pairs it with the physical command to extinguish it with water (*fa-aṭfi'ūhā bi-l-mā'*), a literal etiology confirmed across `bukhari:3264`, `muslim:5751`, and `muslim:5753`.

muslim:5755.note: Aisha reports Muhammad declaring that fever (*al-ḥummā*) is from the raging heat of Hellfire (*fayḥi jahannam*) and instructing that it be cooled with water.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ الْحُمَّى مِنْ فَيْحِ جَهَنَّمَ فَابْرُدُوهَا بِالْمَاءِ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha reported Allah's messenger (ﷺ) as saying:Fever is from the vehement raging of the Hell-fire, so cool it with water

muslim:5755.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that describing fever (*al-ḥummā*) as coming from the raging heat of Hellfire is merely a figurative metaphor comparing a high bodily temperature to the heat of Hell, while presenting the instruction to cool the patient with water as practical medical guidance. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that fever is *min fayḥi jahannam* ('from the vehement raging of the Hell-fire'), using the preposition *min* ('from') to assert a direct causal origin rather than a poetic simile, and directly premises the physical remedy (*fa-abrudūhā bi-l-mā'*, 'so cool it with water') on counteracting that literal infernal heat. This literal diagnosis is reinforced across parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:3263`, `bukhari:5726`, `muslim:5751`), leaving no grammatical basis in the text for reinterpreting the statement as a figure of speech.

muslim:5759.note: Muhammad declares that fever (*al-humma*) is a boiling eruption of heat from Hellfire (*fawrun min Jahannam*) and commands that it be cooled with water.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: رَافِعِ بْنِ خَدِيجٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ إِنَّ الْحُمَّى فَوْرٌ مِنْ جَهَنَّمَ فَابْرُدُوهَا بِالْمَاءِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Rafi' b. Khadij reported:I heard Allah's messenger (ﷺ) as saying: The fever is due to the intense heat of the Hell, so cool it with water

muslim:5759.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that describing fever as originating from Hell is a metaphor for intense bodily heat, and that cooling a fever with water is practical medical advice. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that fever is a boiling eruption from Hellfire (*inna al-ḥummā fawrun min Jahannam*), presenting a literal origin in Jahannam as the direct premise for the command to cool it with water (*fa-abrudūhā bi-l-mā'*), as repeated in bukhari:3264, muslim:5757, and muslim:5760.

muslim:5760.note: As reported by Rafi' ibn Khadij, Muhammad declares that bodily fever originates from the boiling heat of Hell (*min fawri Jahannam*) and instructs his listeners to cool it off themselves with water.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: حَدَّثَنِي رَافِعُ بْنُ خَدِيجٍ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏"‏ الْحُمَّى مِنْ فَوْرِ جَهَنَّمَ فَابْرُدُوهَا عَنْكُمْ بِالْمَاءِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Rafi' b. Khadij reported:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying: The fever is due to the intense heat of Hell, so cool it down in your (bodies) with water.

muslim:5760.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that describing fever as originating from Hell is merely a figurative reminder of the afterlife's torment paired with a practical instruction to reduce body temperature using cold water. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that fever is *min fawri Jahannam* (from the boiling heat of Hell), using the preposition *min* (from) to assert a direct causal origin rather than a metaphor, as repeated across `bukhari:3264`, `muslim:5757`, and `muslim:5759`. By linking this supernatural origin directly to the physical remedy *fabrudūhā 'ankum bil-mā'* (so cool it down from you with water), the statement presents fever as actual heat emanating from Hell rather than a physiological response to illness.

muslim:5801.note: Muhammad declares that there is no contagious or transitive disease (lā ʿadwā) and no divination, while stating that he is pleased by a good omen defined as a good word. While English translations of parallel reports (bukhari:5756, muslim:5800) add parenthetical qualifiers suggesting disease does not transmit by its own nature without Allah's permission, the Arabic text states an unqualified negation (lā ʿadwā).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ عَدْوَى وَلاَ طِيَرَةَ وَيُعْجِبُنِي الْفَأْلُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ قِيلَ وَمَا الْفَأْلُ قَالَ ‏"‏ الْكَلِمَةُ الطَّيِّبَةُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Anas b. Malik reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:There is no transitive disease, no divination, but good omen pleases me. It was said: What is good omen? He said: Sacred words

muslim:5801.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was only denying the pre-Islamic belief that diseases transmit by their own independent power apart from Allah's decree, rather than denying physical contagion itself. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an unqualified categorical negation (*lā ʿadwā*, 'there is no transitive disease') and pairs it directly with the rejection of superstitious omens (*wa lā ṭiyarah*, 'and no divination'). Because the statement in `muslim:5801` and its parallels (`bukhari:5756`, `bukhari:5776`, `muslim:5800`) contains no qualification about divine causation, it treats physical disease transmission as just as imaginary as bad omens.

bukhari:5766.note: Aisha narrates that Labid bin al-A'sam, a Jewish man from Banu Zuraiq, bewitched Muhammad using a comb, hair combings, and a male date-palm pollen sheath placed in the well of Dharwan, causing Muhammad to imagine he had done things that he had not actually done. Classical commentators affirm the literal occurrence of this bewitchment while arguing that its effects were restricted to Muhammad's worldly affairs rather than his prophetic revelation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سُحِرَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى إِنَّهُ لَيُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ يَفْعَلُ الشَّىْءَ وَمَا فَعَلَهُ، حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ وَهْوَ عِنْدِي دَعَا اللَّهَ وَدَعَاهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَشَعَرْتِ يَا عَائِشَةُ أَنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَفْتَانِي فِيمَا اسْتَفْتَيْتُهُ فِيهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْتُ وَمَا ذَاكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ جَاءَنِي رَجُلاَنِ، فَجَلَسَ أَحَدُهُمَا عِنْدَ رَأْسِي وَالآخَرُ عِنْدَ رِجْلَىَّ، ثُمَّ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا لِصَاحِبِهِ مَا وَجَعُ الرَّجُلِ قَالَ مَطْبُوبٌ‏.‏ قَالَ وَمَنْ طَبَّهُ قَالَ لَبِيدُ بْنُ الأَعْصَمِ، الْيَهُودِيُّ مِنْ بَنِي زُرَيْقٍ‏.‏ قَالَ فِيمَا ذَا قَالَ فِي مُشْطٍ وَمُشَاطَةٍ، وَجُفِّ طَلْعَةٍ ذَكَرٍ‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَيْنَ هُوَ قَالَ فِي بِئْرِ ذِي أَرْوَانَ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Magic was worked on Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) so that he began to imagine that he had done something although he had not. One day while he was with me, he invoked Allah and invoked for a long period and then said, "O `Aisha! Do you know that Allah has instructed me regarding the matter I asked Him about?" I asked, "What is that, O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)?" He said, "Two men came to me; one of them sat near my head and the other sat near my feet. One of them asked his companion, 'What is the disease of this man?' The other replied, 'He is under the effect of magic.' The first one asked, 'Who has worked magic on him?" The other replied, 'Labid bin A'sam, a Jew from the tribe of Bani Zuraiq.' The (first one asked), 'With what has it been done?' The other replied, 'With a a comb and the hair stuck to it and a skin of the pollen of a male datepalm tree.' The first one asked, 'Where is it?' The other replied, 'In the well of Dharwan.'

bukhari:5766.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as explained by Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ and Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, Labīd ibn al-Aʿṣam's spell only affected Muhammad's physical body and worldly marital relations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 5765) without compromising his intellect or prophetic infallibility (*ʿiṣmah*) in delivering revelation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that he was bewitched (`سُحِرَ النَّبِيُّ`) to the point of cognitive delusion where 'he imagined that he was doing a thing when he had not done it' (`لَيُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ يَفْعَلُ الشَّىْءَ وَمَا فَعَلَهُ`), proving that his mental perception and memory of reality were directly hijacked by occult magic. Furthermore, conceding that Muhammad became *masḥūr* (bewitched) and suffered from false memories directly vindicates the exact charge of his Meccan critics recorded in the Qur'an (Sūrah 17:47 and 25:8)—that he was 'a bewitched man' (`رَجُلًا مَّسْحُورًا`)—pitting *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* directly against the Qur'an's own defense of his prophethood.

bukhari:3346.note: Muhammad entered upon Zaynab bint Jahsh in a state of alarm and warned of approaching destruction for the Arabs, declaring that an opening the size of a circle formed by his thumb and index finger had been made that day in the barrier of Gog and Magog. While classical commentators debated whether the breach was literal or figurative for impending tribulations, both readings presuppose the physical existence of Dhul-Qarnayn's iron-and-copper wall holding back those tribes ([Quran 18:96](quran://18/96)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا فَزِعًا يَقُولُ ‏"‏ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ، وَيْلٌ لِلْعَرَبِ مِنْ شَرٍّ قَدِ اقْتَرَبَ فُتِحَ الْيَوْمَ مِنْ رَدْمِ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ مِثْلُ هَذِهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ وَحَلَّقَ بِإِصْبَعِهِ الإِبْهَامِ وَالَّتِي تَلِيهَا‏.‏ قَالَتْ زَيْنَبُ ابْنَةُ جَحْشٍ فَقُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَنَهْلِكُ وَفِينَا الصَّالِحُونَ قَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ، إِذَا كَثُرَ الْخُبْثُ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: That the Prophet (ﷺ) once came to her in a state of fear and said, "None has the right to be worshipped but Allah. Woe unto the Arabs from a danger that has come near. An opening has been made in the wall of Gog and Magog like this," making a circle with his thumb and index finger. Zainab bint Jahsh said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Shall we be destroyed even though there are pious persons among us?" He said, "Yes, when the evil persons will increase

bukhari:3346.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's warning was merely a figurative metaphor (*majāz*) for approaching political tribulations (*fitan*), or that the barrier is supernaturally concealed from modern satellite detection. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *"futiḥa al-yawma min radmi Ya'jūja wa Ma'jūja mithlu hādhihi"* ("an opening has been made today in the barrier of Gog and Magog like this") while Muhammad physically measured the breach with his thumb and index finger (*wa ḥallaqa bi-iṣba'ihi al-ibhāmi wa-allatī talīhā*), directly referencing the tangible iron-and-copper mountain dam of [Quran 18:96](quran://18/96). Furthermore, Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* affirms that the literal physical meaning (*al-ḥaml 'alā al-ḥaqīqah*) is the baseline orthodox reading, leaving Sunni tradition bound to a 7th-century AD geographical fable that complete terrestrial and satellite mapping has decisively falsified.

muslim:6149.note: Muhammad states that the Angel of Death came to Moses and commanded him, "Respond to your Lord," whereupon Moses struck the angel's eye and gouged it out. After the angel returned to Allah complaining that Moses did not want to die and had knocked out his eye, Allah restored the eye and sent the angel back to offer Moses an extra year of life for every hair covered by his hand on the back of an ox (cf. bukhari:1339, bukhari:3407, muslim:6148).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: جَاءَ مَلَكُ الْمَوْتِ إِلَى مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَجِبْ رَبَّكَ - قَالَ - فَلَطَمَ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَيْنَ مَلَكِ الْمَوْتِ فَفَقَأَهَا - قَالَ - فَرَجَعَ الْمَلَكُ إِلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى فَقَالَ إِنَّكَ أَرْسَلْتَنِي إِلَى عَبْدٍ لَكَ لاَ يُرِيدُ الْمَوْتَ وَقَدْ فَقَأَ عَيْنِي - قَالَ - فَرَدَّ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ عَيْنَهُ وَقَالَ ارْجِعْ إِلَى عَبْدِي فَقُلِ الْحَيَاةَ تُرِيدُ فَإِنْ كُنْتَ تُرِيدُ الْحَيَاةَ فَضَعْ يَدَكَ عَلَى مَتْنِ ثَوْرٍ فَمَا تَوَارَتْ يَدُكَ مِنْ شَعْرَةٍ فَإِنَّكَ تَعِيشُ بِهَا سَنَةً قَالَ ثُمَّ مَهْ قَالَ ثُمَّ تَمُوتُ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) having said that the Angel of Death came to Moses and said:Respond (to the call) of Allah (i. e. be prepared for death). Moses (peace be upon him) gave a blow at the eye of the Angel of Death and knocked it out. The Angel went back to Allah (the Exalted) and said: You sent me to your servant who does not like to die and he knocked out my eye. Allah restored his eye to its proper place (and revived his eyesight) and said: Go to My servant and say: Do you want life? And in case you want life, keep your hand on the body of the ox and you would live such number of years as the (number of) hair your hand covers. He (Moses) said: What, then? He said: Then you would die

muslim:6149.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the Angel of Death approached Moses disguised as an unrecognized human intruder entering his home without permission, or that knocking out the angel's eye is a metaphor for Moses winning an argument. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the angel opened with the divine summons 'Respond to your Lord' (ajib rabbaka), after which Moses physically slapped his eye and gouged it out (fa-latama Musa 'ayna malaki al-mawti fa-faqa'aha) until Allah restored his eye to him (fa-radda Allahu ilayhi 'aynahu). Furthermore, the angel reported to Allah that Moses 'does not want death' (la yuridu al-mawt), and Allah responded by offering Moses an extension of one year of life for every hair covered by his hand on the back of an ox ('ala matni thawrin), confirming a literal physical resistance to dying rather than a case of mistaken identity.

muslim:6146.note: Muhammad states that when the Israelites accused Moses of bathing alone due to a scrotal hernia, a stone fled with Moses's garment so he chased it naked until the Israelites looked at his private parts, after which the stone stopped and Moses struck it repeatedly. Abu Huraira swears by Allah that Moses's blows left six or seven scars on the stone, and the immediately following report (muslim:6147) identifies this incident as the occasion of revelation for [Quran 33:69](quran://33/69).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَتْ بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ يَغْتَسِلُونَ عُرَاةً يَنْظُرُ بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَى سَوْأَةِ بَعْضٍ وَكَانَ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَغْتَسِلُ وَحْدَهُ فَقَالُوا وَاللَّهِ مَا يَمْنَعُ مُوسَى أَنْ يَغْتَسِلَ مَعَنَا إِلاَّ أَنَّهُ آدَرُ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَذَهَبَ مَرَّةً يَغْتَسِلُ فَوَضَعَ ثَوْبَهُ عَلَى حَجَرٍ فَفَرَّ الْحَجَرُ بِثَوْبِهِ - قَالَ - فَجَمَحَ مُوسَى بِأَثَرِهِ يَقُولُ ثَوْبِي حَجَرُ ثَوْبِي حَجَرُ ‏.‏ حَتَّى نَظَرَتْ بَنُو إِسْرَائِيلَ إِلَى سَوْأَةِ مُوسَى فَقَالُوا وَاللَّهِ مَا بِمُوسَى مِنْ بَأْسٍ ‏.‏ فَقَامَ الْحَجَرُ بَعْدُ حَتَّى نُظِرَ إِلَيْهِ - قَالَ - فَأَخَذَ ثَوْبَهُ فَطَفِقَ بِالْحَجَرِ ضَرْبًا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ بِالْحَجَرِ نَدَبٌ سِتَّةٌ أَوْ سَبْعَةٌ ضَرْبُ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ بِالْحَجَرِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Banu Isra'il used to take bath (together) naked and thus saw private parts of one another, but Moses (peace be upon him) used to take bath alone (in privacy), and they said: By Allah, nothing prevents Moses to take bath along with us; but scrotal hernia. One day when he (Moses) was taking bath (alone) he placed his clothes upon a stone, but the stone began to move along with his clothes. Moses raced after it saying: My garment, stone; until (some of the people) of Banu Isra'il looked at the private parts of Moses, and they said: By Allah, there is no trouble with Moses. The stone stopped after he (Moses) had been seen. He took hold of his garments and struck the stone. Abu Huraira said: I swear by Allah that there were six or seven scars on the stone because of the striking of stone by Moses (peace be upon him)

muslim:6146.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this incident was a divine miracle ordained to exonerate Moses from the Israelites' slander ([Quran 33:69](quran://33/69)), that Moses struck the rock only to leave a lasting sign, or that his garment was merely carried off by natural forces. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the stone itself fled with his garment (*fa-farra al-ḥajaru bi-thawbihi*), that Moses shouted directly at the rock (*thawbī ḥajaru*, "My garment, stone!"), and that the stone halted only after the Israelites looked at Moses's private parts (*ḥattā naẓarat Banū Isrā'īla ilā saw'ati Mūsā*) to confirm he did not have a scrotal hernia (*ādar*). Rather than preserving the modesty for which Moses bathed alone (*yaghtasilu waḥdahu*), the narrative resolves a rumor about his anatomy by forcing him to chase a moving rock naked in public view before beating six or seven scars (*nadabun sittatun aw sab'atun*) into the stone (`bukhari:278`, `bukhari:3404`, `muslim:6147`).

muslim:7496.note: Muhammad states that a lost nation of the Children of Israel (*ummah min Banī Isrā'īl*) is, in his view, none other than rats (*wa-lā urāhā illā al-fa'r*), offering as proof that when camel's milk (*albān al-ibil*) is placed before them they do not drink it, whereas when sheep's or goat's milk (*albān al-shā'*) is placed before them they drink it. When Abu Huraira narrates this report to Ka'b and Ka'b repeatedly asks whether he heard it directly from Allah's Messenger, Abu Huraira affirms that he did and asks in reply whether he reads the Torah (*a-aqra'u al-Tawrāh*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فُقِدَتْ أُمَّةٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ لاَ يُدْرَى مَا فَعَلَتْ وَلاَ أُرَاهَا إِلاَّ الْفَأْرَ أَلاَ تَرَوْنَهَا إِذَا وُضِعَ لَهَا أَلْبَانُ الإِبِلِ لَمْ تَشْرَبْهُ وَإِذَا وُضِعَ لَهَا أَلْبَانُ الشَّاءِ شَرِبَتْهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ فَحَدَّثْتُ هَذَا الْحَدِيثَ كَعْبًا فَقَالَ آنْتَ سَمِعْتَهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قُلْتُ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ ذَلِكَ مِرَارًا ‏.‏ قُلْتُ أَأَقْرَأُ التَّوْرَاةَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said:A group of Bani Isra'il was lost. I do not know what happened to it, but I think (that it 'underwent a process of metamorphosis) and assumed the shape of rats. Don't you see when the milk of the camel is placed before them, these do not drink and when the milk of goat is placed before them, these do drink. Abu Huraira said: I narrated this very hadith to Ka'b and he said: Did you hear this from Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)? I (Abu Huraira) said: Yes. He said this again and again, and I said: Have I read Torah?

muslim:7496.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was merely voicing a tentative personal conjecture (*lā urāhā illā al-fa'r*) rather than making a factual biological claim, or that this report was Jewish folklore (*Isrā'īliyyāt*) from Ka'b that Abu Huraira mistakenly attributed to Muhammad. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad substantiated his claim that the lost Israelite nation (`أُمَّةٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ`) is contemporary rats (`وَلاَ أُرَاهَا إِلاَّ الْفَأْرَ`) by appealing to their observable behavior as empirical proof: "Don't you see when the milk of the camel is placed before them, these do not drink and when the milk of goat is placed before them, these do drink" (`أَلاَ تَرَوْنَهَا إِذَا وُضِعَ لَهَا أَلْبَانُ الإِبِلِ لَمْ تَشْرَبْهُ وَإِذَا وُضِعَ لَهَا أَلْبَانُ الشَّاءِ شَرِبَتْهُ`). Furthermore, the narration directly refutes the *Isrā'īliyyāt* excuse, recording that when Ka'b repeatedly asked (`قَالَ ذَلِكَ مِرَارًا`), "Did you hear this from Allah's Messenger?" (`آنْتَ سَمِعْتَهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ`), Abu Huraira confirmed (`قُلْتُ نَعَمْ`) and retorted, "Have I read Torah?" (`أَأَقْرَأُ التَّوْرَاةَ`), proving the teaching originated from Muhammad himself (see also `bukhari:3305` and `muslim:7497`).

bukhari:4701.note: Commenting on [Quran 34:23](quran://34/23), Muhammad states that when Allah decrees a matter in heaven, angels beat their wings with a sound like a chain on a rock while eavesdroppers (devils) stack one atop another to overhear the decree and pass it down to earth. He states that a shooting star or flame (shihab) sometimes overtakes and burns the listener before he can relay the word to the one below him, and sometimes does not overtake him before it is cast onto the tongue of a sorcerer or soothsayer who adds a hundred lies to it ([Quran 15:17-18](quran://15/17); [Quran 37:6-10](quran://37/6); [Quran 72:8-9](quran://72/8)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا قَضَى اللَّهُ الأَمْرَ فِي السَّمَاءِ ضَرَبَتِ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ بِأَجْنِحَتِهَا خُضْعَانًا لِقَوْلِهِ كَالسِّلْسِلَةِ عَلَى صَفْوَانٍ ـ قَالَ عَلِيٌّ وَقَالَ غَيْرُهُ صَفْوَانٍ ـ يَنْفُذُهُمْ ذَلِكَ فَإِذَا فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ قَالُوا مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ، قَالُوا لِلَّذِي قَالَ الْحَقَّ وَهْوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ، فَيَسْمَعُهَا مُسْتَرِقُو السَّمْعِ، وَمُسْتَرِقُو السَّمْعِ هَكَذَا وَاحِدٌ فَوْقَ آخَرَ ـ وَوَصَفَ سُفْيَانُ بِيَدِهِ، وَفَرَّجَ بَيْنَ أَصَابِعِ يَدِهِ الْيُمْنَى، نَصَبَهَا بَعْضَهَا فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ ـ فَرُبَّمَا أَدْرَكَ الشِّهَابُ الْمُسْتَمِعَ، قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْمِيَ بِهَا إِلَى صَاحِبِهِ، فَيُحْرِقَهُ وَرُبَّمَا لَمْ يُدْرِكْهُ حَتَّى يَرْمِيَ بِهَا إِلَى الَّذِي يَلِيهِ إِلَى الَّذِي هُوَ أَسْفَلُ مِنْهُ حَتَّى يُلْقُوهَا إِلَى الأَرْضِ ـ وَرُبَّمَا قَالَ سُفْيَانُ حَتَّى تَنْتَهِيَ إِلَى الأَرْضِ ـ فَتُلْقَى عَلَى فَمِ السَّاحِرِ، فَيَكْذِبُ مَعَهَا مِائَةَ كَذْبَةٍ فَيَصْدُقُ، فَيَقُولُونَ أَلَمْ يُخْبِرْنَا يَوْمَ كَذَا وَكَذَا يَكُونُ كَذَا وَكَذَا، فَوَجَدْنَاهُ حَقًّا لِلْكَلِمَةِ الَّتِي سُمِعَتْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ
problematic_excerpt.english: When Allah has ordained some affair in the Heaven, the angels beat with their wings in obedience to His statement, which sounds like a chain dragged over a rock." (`Ali and other sub-narrators said, "The sound reaches them.") "Until when fear is banished from their (angels) hearts, they (angels) say, 'What was it that your Lord said? They say, 'The truth; And He is the Most High, the Most Great.' (34.23) Then those who gain a hearing by stealing (i.e. devils) will hear Allah's Statement:-- 'Those who gain a hearing by stealing, (stand one over the other like this). (Sufyan, to illustrate this, spread the fingers of his right hand and placed them one over the other horizontally.) A flame may overtake and burn the eavesdropper before conveying the news to the one below him; or it may not overtake him till he has conveyed it to the one below him, who in his turn, conveys it to the one below him, and so on till they convey the news to the earth. (Or probably Sufyan said, "Till the news reaches the earth.") Then the news is inspired to a sorcerer who would add a hundred lies to it. His prophecy will prove true (as far as the heavenly news is concerned). The people will say. 'Didn't he tell us that on such-and-such a day, such-and-such a thing will happen? We have found that is true because of the true news heard from heaven."

bukhari:4701.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the pelting of eavesdropping devils belongs entirely to the unseen realm (*al-ghayb*), claiming—often by appealing to discussions in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that the stacking of jinn and the *shihāb* (flame) describe non-physical or metaphorical phenomena rather than literal meteorology. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly depicts a physical spatial chain extending down 'to the earth' (`إِلَى الأَرْضِ`), with devils stationed 'one atop another' (`وَاحِدٌ فَوْقَ آخَرَ`, physically demonstrated by Sufyan stacking his fingers `بَعْضَهَا فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ`) racing to toss down overheard words before a shooting star (`الشِّهَابُ`) overtakes and burns the listener (`فَيُحْرِقَهُ`). Moreover, both [Quran 67:5](quran://67/5) and parallel narration muslim:5819 explicitly identify the visible lamps adorning the lowest heaven—and the physical meteors witnessed streaking across the night sky—as the very missiles (*rujūman lil-shayāṭīn*) launched at these demons.

muslim:5513.note: When Gabriel fails to appear for a promised nighttime visit, Muhammad has a puppy removed from beneath their cot and sprinkles water on the spot. That evening, Gabriel explains that they do not enter a house containing a dog or a picture, and the next morning Muhammad orders the killing of dogs—including those guarding small orchards—while sparing those guarding large orchards.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّ جِبْرِيلَ كَانَ وَعَدَنِي أَنْ يَلْقَانِي اللَّيْلَةَ فَلَمْ يَلْقَنِي أَمَ وَاللَّهِ مَا أَخْلَفَنِي ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَظَلَّ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَوْمَهُ ذَلِكَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ ثُمَّ وَقَعَ فِي نَفْسِهِ جِرْوُ كَلْبٍ تَحْتَ فُسْطَاطٍ لَنَا فَأَمَرَ بِهِ فَأُخْرِجَ ثُمَّ أَخَذَ بِيَدِهِ مَاءً فَنَضَحَ مَكَانَهُ فَلَمَّا أَمْسَى لَقِيَهُ جِبْرِيلُ فَقَالَ لَهُ ‏"‏ قَدْ كُنْتَ وَعَدْتَنِي أَنْ تَلْقَانِي الْبَارِحَةَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَجَلْ وَلَكِنَّا لاَ نَدْخُلُ بَيْتًا فِيهِ كَلْبٌ وَلاَ صُورَةٌ ‏.‏ فَأَصْبَحَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَوْمَئِذٍ فَأَمَرَ بِقَتْلِ الْكِلاَبِ حَتَّى إِنَّهُ يَأْمُرُ بِقَتْلِ كَلْبِ الْحَائِطِ الصَّغِيرِ وَيَتْرُكُ كَلْبَ الْحَائِطِ الْكَبِيرِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Gabriel had promised me that he would meet me tonight, but he did not meet me. By Allah, he never broke his promises, and Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) spent the day in this sad (mood). Then it occurred to him that there had been a puppy under their cot. He commanded and it was turned out. He then took some water in his hand and sprinkled it at that place. When it was evening Gabriel met him and he said to him: you promised me that you would meet me the previous night. He said: Yes, but we do not enter a house in which there is a dog or a picture. Then on that very morning he commanded the killing of the dogs until he announced that the dog kept for the orchards should also be killed, but he spared the dog meant for the protection of extensive fields (or big gardens)

muslim:5513.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the command to kill dogs was a public-health measure targeting dangerous strays and that Gabriel merely avoided ritual impurity out of respect for revelation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that a puppy (جِرْوُ كَلْبٍ) under a cot prevented Gabriel from fulfilling his promised night visit because angels declare, 'we do not enter a house in which there is a dog or a picture' (لاَ نَدْخُلُ بَيْتًا فِيهِ كَلْبٌ وَلاَ صُورَةٌ). Furthermore, the narration directly links Gabriel's refusal to enter—after Muhammad sprinkled water on the puppy's spot (فَنَضَحَ مَكَانَهُ)—to his order the very next morning to kill dogs (فَأَمَرَ بِقَتْلِ الْكِلاَبِ), including dogs kept for small orchards (كَلْبِ الْحَائِطِ الصَّغِيرِ).

bukhari:3286.note: Muhammad declares that Satan stabs every newborn descendant of Adam in both sides with his finger at birth, except Jesus, the son of Mary, whom Satan attempted to stab but struck the placental membrane (al-hijab) instead. Classical Sunni commentators such as Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi affirm the literal physical reality of this pricking at birth against allegorical reinterpretations (cf. bukhari:3431, muslim:6133).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُلُّ بَنِي آدَمَ يَطْعُنُ الشَّيْطَانُ فِي جَنْبَيْهِ بِإِصْبَعِهِ حِينَ يُولَدُ، غَيْرَ عِيسَى بْنِ مَرْيَمَ، ذَهَبَ يَطْعُنُ فَطَعَنَ فِي الْحِجَابِ
problematic_excerpt.english: When any human being is born. Satan touches him at both sides of the body with his two fingers, except Jesus, the son of Mary, whom Satan tried to touch but failed, for he touched the placenta-cover instead

bukhari:3286.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Satan's 'touch' at birth is merely a figurative metaphor (*majāz*) for humanity's lifelong susceptibility to demonic temptation (*waswasa*) rather than a literal biological event. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly describes a physical, anatomical assault at the exact moment of delivery (*ḥīna yūladu*), stating that Satan stabs the infant 'in both his sides with his finger' (*yaṭʿunu al-shayṭānu fī janbayhi bi-iṣbaʿihi*) and physically missed Jesus by 'stabbing into the placenta-membrane instead' (*fa-ṭaʿana fī al-ḥijābi*). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:3431, 4548) identify this physical jab as the literal cause of why newborns scream at birth (*fa-yastahillu ṣārikhan*), compelling classical Sunni authorities like Al-Nawawī and Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ to affirm that the demonic stabbing occurs according to its literal reality (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*).

bukhari:3286.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
bukhari:3286.subcategory: Uncreated Divine Word, Original Sin & Sacramental Relics (Trinitarian & Soteriological Precedents)
bukhari:3286.note: While Islamic theology denies Original Sin ([Psalm 51:5](bible://ps/51/5), [Romans 5:12](bible://rom/5/12)) and claims all prophets share equal sinlessness, Muhammad states that Satan stabs every newborn child of Adam at birth except Jesus, the son of Mary ([Luke 1:35](bible://lk/1/35), [Hebrews 4:15](bible://heb/4/15)). Parallel narrations in (bukhari:3431) and (bukhari:4548) state the exception as 'Mary and her son' in direct connection with [Quran 3:36](quran://3/36) (cf. [Ibn Kathir 3:36](ibnkathir://3/36)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُلُّ بَنِي آدَمَ يَطْعُنُ الشَّيْطَانُ فِي جَنْبَيْهِ بِإِصْبَعِهِ حِينَ يُولَدُ، غَيْرَ عِيسَى بْنِ مَرْيَمَ، ذَهَبَ يَطْعُنُ فَطَعَنَ فِي الْحِجَابِ
problematic_excerpt.english: When any human being is born. Satan touches him at both sides of the body with his two fingers, except Jesus, the son of Mary, whom Satan tried to touch but failed, for he touched the placenta-cover instead

bukhari:3286.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists (citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*) typically argue that 'every child of Adam' (*kullu banī Ādama*) is a general statement with unstated exceptions (*ʿāmm makhṣūṣ*), claiming that Muhammad and all other prophets shared in Jesus's immunity from Satan at birth. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly pairs the universal quantifier *kullu banī Ādama* ('every single child of Adam') with the restrictive exception *ghayra ʿĪsā ibni Maryama* ('except Jesus the son of Mary'—and 'except Mary and her son' in bukhari:3431 and 4548), which grammatically excludes Muhammad and every other prophet from this birth immunity. Indeed, Sahih Muslim (413) confirms that Muhammad himself possessed a 'portion of Satan' (*ḥaẓẓu al-shayṭāni*) that angels had to physically wash out of his chest, leaving Jesus alone in Islamic primary sources as uniquely untouchable by Satan from conception and birth.

muslim:1930.note: Muhammad instructs 'Amr ibn 'Abasah to refrain from praying at sunrise, midday, and sunset, declaring that the sun rises and sets between the two horns of a devil (*bayna qarnay shayṭān*) when unbelievers prostrate to it, and that Hellfire is stoked (*tusjaru jahannam*) at solar noon. Classical commentators such as al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar affirm that the primary Sunni position takes these statements according to their apparent literal meaning (*'alā ẓāhirihi*), holding that a devil physically positions his head at the horizon as the sun rises and sets.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: صَلِّ صَلاَةَ الصُّبْحِ ثُمَّ أَقْصِرْ عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ حَتَّى تَرْتَفِعَ فَإِنَّهَا تَطْلُعُ حِينَ تَطْلُعُ بَيْنَ قَرْنَىْ شَيْطَانٍ وَحِينَئِذٍ يَسْجُدُ لَهَا الْكُفَّارُ ثُمَّ صَلِّ فَإِنَّ الصَّلاَةَ مَشْهُودَةٌ مَحْضُورَةٌ حَتَّى يَسْتَقِلَّ الظِّلُّ بِالرُّمْحِ ثُمَّ أَقْصِرْ عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ فَإِنَّ حِينَئِذٍ تُسْجَرُ جَهَنَّمُ فَإِذَا أَقْبَلَ الْفَىْءُ فَصَلِّ فَإِنَّ الصَّلاَةَ مَشْهُودَةٌ مَحْضُورَةٌ حَتَّى تُصَلِّيَ الْعَصْرَ ثُمَّ أَقْصِرْ عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ حَتَّى تَغْرُبَ الشَّمْسُ فَإِنَّهَا تَغْرُبُ بَيْنَ قَرْنَىْ شَيْطَانٍ وَحِينَئِذٍ يَسْجُدُ لَهَا الْكُفَّارُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Observe the dawn prayer, then stop praying when the sun is rising till it is fully up, for when it rises it comes up between the horns of Satan, and the unbelievers prostrate themselves to it at that time. Then pray, for the prayer is witnessed and attended (by angels) till the shadow becomes about the length of a lance; then cease prayer, for at that time Hell is heated up. Then when the shadow moves forward, pray, for the prayer is witnessed and attended by angels, till you pray the afternoon prayer, then cease prayer till the sun sets, for it sets between the horns of devil, and at that time the unbelievers prostrate themselves before it.

muslim:1930.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that 'the two horns of Satan' (*qarnay shayṭān*) is merely a figurative metaphor for Satanic influence during pagan sun-worship, claiming the prohibition is solely to prevent outward resemblance (*tashabbuh*) to idolaters. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states as a causal reality that the sun rises and sets 'between the two horns of a devil' (*bayna qarnay shayṭān*) and that at local midday 'Hell is kindled' (*fa-inna ḥīna'idhin tusjaru jahannam*)—a literal physical reality affirmed by both Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*), who explain that Satan literally positions his head before the solar disc so sun-worshippers prostrate to him. Furthermore, tethering cosmic events like the stoking of Hellfire and Satan's physical alignment to local sunrise, zenith, and sunset presupposes a flat-earth cosmology, oblivious to the fact that on a spherical earth the sun is simultaneously rising, peaking at midday, and setting at every moment around the globe.

muslim:7386.note: Muhammad convenes the mosque congregation to affirm Tamim al-Dari's account of thirty sailors who were driven onto an island after a month at sea and met a talking, hair-covered beast (*al-Jassasa*) whose front could not be distinguished from its rear. The beast directed the sailors to a monastery where the Dajjal (Antichrist) was physically bound in iron shackles from his knees to his ankles with his hands tied to his neck, an account Muhammad endorses from the pulpit as corroborating his own prior teachings.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنِّي وَاللَّهِ مَا جَمَعْتُكُمْ لِرَغْبَةٍ وَلاَ لِرَهْبَةٍ وَلَكِنْ جَمَعْتُكُمْ لأَنَّ تَمِيمًا الدَّارِيَّ كَانَ رَجُلاً نَصْرَانِيًّا فَجَاءَ فَبَايَعَ وَأَسْلَمَ وَحَدَّثَنِي حَدِيثًا وَافَقَ الَّذِي كُنْتُ أُحَدِّثُكُمْ عَنْ مَسِيحِ الدَّجَّالِ حَدَّثَنِي أَنَّهُ رَكِبَ فِي سَفِينَةٍ بَحْرِيَّةٍ مَعَ ثَلاَثِينَ رَجُلاً مِنْ لَخْمٍ وَجُذَامَ فَلَعِبَ بِهِمُ الْمَوْجُ شَهْرًا فِي الْبَحْرِ ثُمَّ أَرْفَئُوا إِلَى جَزِيرَةٍ فِي الْبَحْرِ حَتَّى مَغْرِبِ الشَّمْسِ فَجَلَسُوا فِي أَقْرُبِ السَّفِينَةِ فَدَخَلُوا الْجَزِيرَةَ فَلَقِيَتْهُمْ دَابَّةٌ أَهْلَبُ كَثِيرُ الشَّعَرِ لاَ يَدْرُونَ مَا قُبُلُهُ مِنْ دُبُرِهِ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ الشَّعَرِ فَقَالُوا وَيْلَكِ مَا أَنْتِ فَقَالَتْ أَنَا الْجَسَّاسَةُ ‏.‏ قَالُوا وَمَا الْجَسَّاسَةُ قَالَتْ أَيُّهَا الْقَوْمُ انْطَلِقُوا إِلَى هَذَا الرَّجُلِ فِي الدَّيْرِ فَإِنَّهُ إِلَى خَبَرِكُمْ بِالأَشْوَاقِ ‏.‏ قَالَ لَمَّا سَمَّتْ لَنَا رَجُلاً فَرِقْنَا مِنْهَا أَنْ تَكُونَ شَيْطَانَةً - قَالَ - فَانْطَلَقْنَا سِرَاعًا حَتَّى دَخَلْنَا الدَّيْرَ فَإِذَا فِيهِ أَعْظَمُ إِنْسَانٍ رَأَيْنَاهُ قَطُّ خَلْقًا وَأَشَدُّهُ وِثَاقًا مَجْمُوعَةٌ يَدَاهُ إِلَى عُنُقِهِ مَا بَيْنَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ إِلَى كَعْبَيْهِ بِالْحَدِيدِ
problematic_excerpt.english: He said: By Allah. I have not made you assemble for exhortation or for a warning, but I have detained you here, for Tamim Dari, a Christian, who came and accepted Islam, told me something, which agrees with what I was telling, you about the Dajjal. He narrated to me that he had sailed in a ship along with thirty men of Bani Lakhm and Bani Judham and had been tossed by waves in the ocean for a month. Then these (waves) took them (near) the land within the ocean (island) at the time of sunset. They sat in a small side-boat and entered that island. There was a beast with long thick hair (and because of these) they could not distinguish his face from his back. They said: Woe to you, who can you be? Thereupon it said: I am al-Jassasa. They said: What is al-Jassasa? And it said: O people, go to this person in the monastery as he is very much eager to know about you. He (the narrator) said: When it named a person for us we were afraid of it lest it should be a devil. Then we hurriedly went on till we came to that monastery and found a well-built person there with his hands tied to his neck and having iron shackles between his two legs up to the ankles.

muslim:7386.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Tamim al-Dari's account was merely a dream, an allegorical vision, or an unverified Christian sailor's tale that Muhammad relayed without endorsing as literal physical history, or that *al-Jassasa* was simply a human spy rather than a talking beast. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Tamim sailed on a sea vessel with thirty men from Lakhm and Judham (`رَكِبَ فِي سَفِينَةٍ بَحْرِيَّةٍ مَعَ ثَلاَثِينَ رَجُلاً مِنْ لَخْمٍ وَجُذَامَ`), met a physical hair-covered creature (`دَابَّةٌ أَهْلَبُ كَثِيرُ الشَّعَرِ لاَ يَدْرُونَ مَا قُبُلُهُ مِنْ دُبُرِهِ`), and found a giant man bound in iron shackles from his knees to his ankles (`مَا بَيْنَ رُكْبَتَيْهِ إِلَى كَعْبَيْهِ بِالْحَدِيدِ`). Furthermore, Muhammad swore by Allah (`إِنِّي وَاللَّهِ`) before the assembled mosque congregation that he detained them specifically because Tamim's report matched what he himself had already been teaching them about the Dajjal (`وَافَقَ الَّذِي كُنْتُ أُحَدِّثُكُمْ عَنْ مَسِيحِ الدَّجَّالِ`), binding his own prophetic authority to the literal truth of the island encounter.

muslim:7386.note: Upon learning from the sailors that Muhammad has migrated from Mecca to Yathrib (Medina) and overcome the neighboring Arabs, the chained Dajjal declares that the date-palms of Baisan will soon cease bearing fruit, the Lake of Tabariyya will soon dry up, and he will soon be permitted to emerge. At the close of his sermon endorsing this report, Muhammad states that the Dajjal is in the Syrian Sea or the Yemen Sea before immediately retracting both locations on the pulpit and declaring that he is in the east.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ أَخْبِرُونِي عَنْ بُحَيْرَةِ الطَّبَرِيَّةِ ‏.‏ قُلْنَا عَنْ أَىِّ شَأْنِهَا تَسْتَخْبِرُ قَالَ هَلْ فِيهَا مَاءٌ قَالُوا هِيَ كَثِيرَةُ الْمَاءِ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَمَا إِنَّ مَاءَهَا يُوشِكُ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَخْبِرُونِي عَنْ عَيْنِ زُغَرَ ‏.‏ قَالُوا عَنْ أَىِّ شَأْنِهَا تَسْتَخْبِرُ قَالَ هَلْ فِي الْعَيْنِ مَاءٌ وَهَلْ يَزْرَعُ أَهْلُهَا بِمَاءِ الْعَيْنِ قُلْنَا لَهُ نَعَمْ هِيَ كَثِيرَةُ الْمَاءِ وَأَهْلُهَا يَزْرَعُونَ مِنْ مَائِهَا ‏.‏ قَالَ أَخْبِرُونِي عَنْ نَبِيِّ الأُمِّيِّينَ مَا فَعَلَ قَالُوا قَدْ خَرَجَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ وَنَزَلَ يَثْرِبَ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَقَاتَلَهُ الْعَرَبُ قُلْنَا نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ كَيْفَ صَنَعَ بِهِمْ فَأَخْبَرْنَاهُ أَنَّهُ قَدْ ظَهَرَ عَلَى مَنْ يَلِيهِ مِنَ الْعَرَبِ وَأَطَاعُوهُ قَالَ لَهُمْ قَدْ كَانَ ذَلِكَ قُلْنَا نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَمَا إِنَّ ذَاكَ خَيْرٌ لَهُمْ أَنْ يُطِيعُوهُ وَإِنِّي مُخْبِرُكُمْ عَنِّي إِنِّي أَنَا الْمَسِيحُ وَإِنِّي أُوشِكُ أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لِي فِي الْخُرُوجِ فَأَخْرُجَ فَأَسِيرَ فِي الأَرْضِ فَلاَ أَدَعَ قَرْيَةً إِلاَّ هَبَطْتُهَا فِي أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً غَيْرَ مَكَّةَ وَطَيْبَةَ فَهُمَا مُحَرَّمَتَانِ عَلَىَّ كِلْتَاهُمَا كُلَّمَا أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَدْخُلَ وَاحِدَةً أَوْ وَاحِدًا مِنْهُمَا اسْتَقْبَلَنِي مَلَكٌ بِيَدِهِ السَّيْفُ صَلْتًا يَصُدُّنِي عَنْهَا وَإِنَّ عَلَى كُلِّ نَقْبٍ مِنْهَا مَلاَئِكَةً يَحْرُسُونَهَا قَالَتْ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَطَعَنَ بِمِخْصَرَتِهِ فِي الْمِنْبَرِ ‏"‏ هَذِهِ طَيْبَةُ هَذِهِ طَيْبَةُ هَذِهِ طَيْبَةُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ يَعْنِي الْمَدِينَةَ ‏"‏ أَلاَ هَلْ كُنْتُ حَدَّثْتُكُمْ ذَلِكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّاسُ نَعَمْ ‏"‏ فَإِنَّهُ أَعْجَبَنِي حَدِيثُ تَمِيمٍ أَنَّهُ وَافَقَ الَّذِي كُنْتُ أُحَدِّثُكُمْ عَنْهُ وَعَنِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَمَكَّةَ أَلاَ إِنَّهُ فِي بَحْرِ الشَّامِ أَوْ بَحْرِ الْيَمَنِ لاَ بَلْ مِنْ قِبَلِ الْمَشْرِقِ ما هُوَ مِنْ قِبَلِ الْمَشْرِقِ مَا هُوَ مِنْ قِبَلِ الْمَشْرِقِ مَا هُوَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَأَوْمَأَ بِيَدِهِ إِلَى الْمَشْرِقِ ‏.
problematic_excerpt.english: He said: Inform me about the lake of Tabariyya? We said: Which aspect of it do you want to know? He said: Is there water in it? They said: There is abundance of water in it. Thereupon he said: I think it would soon become dry. He again said: Inform me about the spring of Zughar. They said: Which aspect of it you want to know? He (the chained person) said: Is there water in it and does it irrigate (the land)? We said to him: Yes, there is abundance of water in it and the inhabitants (of Medina) irrigate (land) with the help of it, He said: Inform me about the unlettered Prophet; what has he done? We said: He has come out from Mecca and has settled In Yathrib (Medina). He said: Do the Arabs fight against him? We said: Yes. He said: How did he deal with them? We informed him that he had overcome those in his neighbourhood and they had submitted themselves before him. Thereupon he said to us: Has it actually happened? We said: Yes. Thereupon he said: If it is so that is better for them that they should show obedience to him. I am going to tell you about myself and I am Dajjal and would be soon permitted to get out and so I shall get out and travel in the land, and will not spare any town where I would not stay for forty nights except Mecca and Medina as these two (places) are prohibited (areas) for me and I would not make an attempt to enter any one of these two. An angel with a sword in his hand would confront me and would bar my way and there would be angels to guard every passage leading to it; then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) striking the pulpit with the help of the end of his staff said: This implies Taiba meaning Medina. Have I not, told you an account (of the Dajjal) like this? 'The people said: Yes, and this account narrated by Tamim Dari was liked by me for it corroborates the account which I gave to you in regard to him (Dajjal) at Medina and Mecca. Behold he (Dajjal) is in the Syrian sea (Mediterranean) or the Yemen sea (Arabian sea). Nay, on the contrary, he is in the east, he is in the east, he is in the east, and he pointed with his hand towards the east.

muslim:7386.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the verb *yūshiku* ("soon" or "about to") denotes relative nearness in eschatological time rather than seventh-century AD imminence, and that Muhammad's shift from the Syrian or Yemen sea to the east merely distinguished where the Dajjal was chained from where he would later emerge while treating Ibn Sayyad as a separate lesser impostor. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the chained figure linked his imminent release (`إِنِّي أُوشِكُ أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لِي فِي الْخُرُوجِ`), the drying of the Lake of Tabariyya (`إِنَّ مَاءَهَا يُوشِكُ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ`), and the failure of the date-palms of Baisan directly to contemporaneous seventh-century AD events—namely Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Yathrib and victory over the surrounding Arabs (`قَدْ خَرَجَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ وَنَزَلَ يَثْرِبَ`). Moreover, Muhammad explicitly negates his own initial geographical guess on the pulpit using the corrective phrase *lā bal* ("Nay, on the contrary, he is in the east": `لاَ بَلْ مِنْ قِبَلِ الْمَشْرِقِ`), while parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:1354`, `muslim:7346`, `muslim:7373`) show Muhammad hiding behind palm trees to test whether the Medinan youth Ibn Sayyad was the Dajjal, which is irreconcilable with already knowing the Dajjal to be a giant chained in an eastern island monastery.

muslim:6762.note: Muhammad declares that Satan strikes every newborn human infant in both of its flanks (*yalkuzuhu al-shayṭānu fī ḥiḍnayhi*) at birth, with the sole exception of Mary and her son Jesus ([Quran 3:36](quran://3/36)). The published English translation obscures the literal physical phrase *fī ḥiḍnayhi* ("in his two sides") by rendering it as the parenthetical gloss "(has two aspects of his life)."

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُلُّ إِنْسَانٍ تَلِدُهُ أُمُّهُ عَلَى الْفِطْرَةِ وَأَبَوَاهُ بَعْدُ يُهَوِّدَانِهِ وَيُنَصِّرَانِهِ وَيُمَجِّسَانِهِ فَإِنْ كَانَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ فَمُسْلِمٌ كُلُّ إِنْسَانٍ تَلِدُهُ أُمُّهُ يَلْكُزُهُ الشَّيْطَانُ فِي حِضْنَيْهِ إِلاَّ مَرْيَمَ وَابْنَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: The mother of every person gives him birth according to his true nature. It is subsequently his parents who make him a Jew or a Christian or a Magian. Had his parents been Muslim he would have also remained a Muslim. Every person to whom his mother gives birth (has two aspects of his life) ; when his mother gives birth Satan strikes him but it was not the case with Mary and her son (Jesus Christ)

muslim:6762.literal_translation: Every human being is born of his mother upon the natural disposition (fiṭrah), and his parents afterward make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian; if they are Muslims, then he is a Muslim. Every human being whom his mother gives birth to, Satan punches him in his two sides (flanks), except Mary and her son.

translation_issue.arabic_term: يَلْكُزُهُ الشَّيْطَانُ فِي حِضْنَيْهِ
translation_issue.published_rendering: (has two aspects of his life) ; when his mother gives birth Satan strikes him
translation_issue.literal_meaning: Satan punches him in his two sides (flanks)
translation_issue.explanation: The translator omits the physical phrase 'fī ḥiḍnayhi' ('in his two sides/flanks'), which specifies where Satan punches ('yalkuzuhu') the newborn's body, while inserting the unattested parenthetical gloss '(has two aspects of his life)'.

muslim:6762.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Satan's strike at birth is merely a figurative metaphor for the onset of spiritual temptation in the world, or that the phrase refers abstractly to two aspects of human life as rendered in the English translation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *yalkuzuhu al-shayṭānu fī ḥiḍnayhi* ("Satan punches him in his two sides"), pairing a concrete verb of physical striking with the dual anatomical noun for bodily flanks (*ḥiḍnayhi*). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:3286`, `bukhari:3431`, `muslim:6133`, `muslim:6135`) confirm this is a literal physical contact that directly causes the newborn infant to cry out at the moment of delivery.

muslim:6762.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:6762.subcategory: Uncreated Divine Word, Original Sin & Sacramental Relics (Trinitarian & Soteriological Precedents)
muslim:6762.note: Immediately after stating that every child is born upon the innate *fiṭrah*—a clause cited in polemics against Original Sin ([Psalm 51:5](bible://ps/51/5), [Romans 5:12](bible://rom/5/12))—Muhammad declares in the very same narration that Satan strikes every newborn human being in both flanks at birth except Mary and her son Jesus ([Quran 3:36](quran://3/36), [Ibn Kathir 3:36](ibnkathir://3/36)). By explicitly restricting this exemption to Mary and Jesus (*illā Maryama wa-bnahā*), the text affirms Christ's unique immunity from Satan's natal strike ([Luke 1:35](bible://lk/1/35), [Hebrews 4:15](bible://heb/4/15)) without extending that exception to any other prophet.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُلُّ إِنْسَانٍ تَلِدُهُ أُمُّهُ عَلَى الْفِطْرَةِ وَأَبَوَاهُ بَعْدُ يُهَوِّدَانِهِ وَيُنَصِّرَانِهِ وَيُمَجِّسَانِهِ فَإِنْ كَانَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ فَمُسْلِمٌ كُلُّ إِنْسَانٍ تَلِدُهُ أُمُّهُ يَلْكُزُهُ الشَّيْطَانُ فِي حِضْنَيْهِ إِلاَّ مَرْيَمَ وَابْنَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: The mother of every person gives him birth according to his true nature. It is subsequently his parents who make him a Jew or a Christian or a Magian. Had his parents been Muslim he would have also remained a Muslim. Every person to whom his mother gives birth (has two aspects of his life) ; when his mother gives birth Satan strikes him but it was not the case with Mary and her son (Jesus Christ)

muslim:6762.literal_translation: Every human being is born of his mother upon the natural disposition (fiṭrah), and his parents afterward make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian; if they are Muslims, then he is a Muslim. Every human being whom his mother gives birth to, Satan punches him in his two sides (flanks), except Mary and her son.

translation_issue.arabic_term: يَلْكُزُهُ الشَّيْطَانُ فِي حِضْنَيْهِ
translation_issue.published_rendering: (has two aspects of his life) ; when his mother gives birth Satan strikes him
translation_issue.literal_meaning: Satan punches him in his two sides (flanks)
translation_issue.explanation: The translator omits the physical phrase 'fī ḥiḍnayhi' ('in his two sides/flanks'), which specifies where Satan punches ('yalkuzuhu') the newborn's body, while inserting the unattested parenthetical gloss '(has two aspects of his life)'.
