Classical commentators including Al-Qurtubi, Al-Nawawi, and Ibn Hajar affirm that taking this urination literally ('ala haqiqatihi) is a primary orthodox Sunni position, as there is no impossibility in Satan eating, drinking, and excreting.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ذُكِرَ عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَجُلٌ فَقِيلَ مَا زَالَ نَائِمًا حَتَّى أَصْبَحَ مَا قَامَ إِلَى الصَّلاَةِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ بَالَ الشَّيْطَانُ فِي أُذُنِهِ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: A person was mentioned before the Prophet (ﷺ) and he was told that he had kept on sleeping till morning and had not got up for the prayer. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Satan urinated in his ears

bukhari:1144.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that 'Satan urinated in his ears' is merely an Arabic metaphor (majāz) for Satan's contempt or spiritually dulling a sleeper's hearing against the call to prayer. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states as an unqualified factual assertion, 'Satan urinated in his ear' (bāla al-shayṭānu fī udhunihi) without any particle of simile, leading authoritative commentators like Al-Qurtubi, Al-Nawawi (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim), and Ibn Hajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) to rule that literal physical urination (ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi) is the soundest interpretation since Satan literally eats and drinks in Islamic theology. Moreover, a literal reading is demanded by Muhammad's broader physical demonology across the Ṣaḥīḥayn, where Satan physically lodges overnight inside a human's nostrils (bukhari:3295) and flees the call to prayer while noisily passing wind (bukhari:608).

muslim:856.note: Muhammad states that whenever Satan hears the call to prayer (Adhan), he turns and flees while audibly passing wind (*ḍurāṭ*) so as not to hear its sound, returning once it ends to whisper distractions to worshippers, and repeats this flight and return during the *iqāmah*. Classical commentators such as al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar affirm that *ḍurāṭ* carries its literal meaning of Satan physically passing loud wind to drown out the call.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ إِذَا سَمِعَ النِّدَاءَ بِالصَّلاَةِ أَحَالَ لَهُ ضُرَاطٌ حَتَّى لاَ يَسْمَعَ صَوْتَهُ فَإِذَا سَكَتَ رَجَعَ فَوَسْوَسَ فَإِذَا سَمِعَ الإِقَامَةَ ذَهَبَ حَتَّى لاَ يَسْمَعَ صَوْتَهُ فَإِذَا سَكَتَ رَجَعَ فَوَسْوَسَ
problematic_excerpt.english: When Satan hears the call to prayer, he turns back and breaks the wind so as not to hear the call being made, but when the call is finished he turns round and distracts (the minds of those who pray), and when he hears the Iqama, he again runs away so as not to hear its voice and when it subsides, he comes back and distracts (the minds of those who stand for prayer)

muslim:856.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Satan's loud flatulence (*ḍurāṭ*) is merely an Arabic metaphor for extreme panic, humiliation, and frantic flight rather than a literal bodily function. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a literal acoustic purpose—that he emits loud wind specifically 'so that he does not hear its sound' (*ḥattā lā yasmaʿa ṣawtahu*)—and classical commentators like Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* affirm that taking the narration literally (*ʿalā ẓāhirihi*) as an actual sound emitted from his body is the primary, sound interpretation. Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (`muslim:857`, `bukhari:608`) pair this act with an exact geographical distance for his flight ('as far as Rawḥāʾ,' thirty-six miles from Medina), proving Muhammad was describing a literal, physical action rather than speaking in poetic figure.

muslim:7491.note: Muhammad commands anyone who yawns to hold his hand over his mouth because Satan enters through it.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ إِذَا تَثَاوَبَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيُمْسِكْ بِيَدِهِ عَلَى فِيهِ فَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَدْخُلُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said:When one of you yawns, he should keep his mouth shut with the help of his hand, for it is the devil that enters therein

muslim:7491.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the devil's entry is a metaphor for spiritual laziness or an instruction on polite etiquette when yawning. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *fa-inna al-shayṭāna yadkhulu* ("for the devil enters") as the direct causal reason one must physically hold a hand over the mouth (*falyumsik bi-yadihi ʿalā fīhi*). Commanding a physical barrier with the hand to block entry treats the devil's passage through an open mouth as a literal spatial intrusion rather than a figure of speech for fatigue.

bukhari:3270.note: When told of a man who slept through the night until morning, Muhammad declares that Satan urinated in his ears (or ear). While some commentators interpret the statement figuratively, classical authorities such as Al-Qurṭubī, Al-Nawawī, and Ibn Ḥajar affirm that taking Satan's urination as a literal act ('alā al-ḥaqīqah) is an established orthodox position.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ذُكِرَ عِنْدَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم رَجُلٌ نَامَ لَيْلَهُ حَتَّى أَصْبَحَ، قَالَ ‏ "‏ ذَاكَ رَجُلٌ بَالَ الشَّيْطَانُ فِي أُذُنَيْهِ ـ أَوْ قَالَ ـ فِي أُذُنِهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: It was mentioned before the Prophet (ﷺ) that there was a man who slept the night till morning (after sunrise). The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "He is a man in whose ears (or ear) Satan had urinated

bukhari:3270.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Satan urinating in a sleeper's ears is merely an Arabic metaphor (*kināyah*) signifying spiritual heedlessness and demonic contempt rather than a literal bodily function. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *bāla al-shayṭānu fī udhunayhi — aw qāla — fī udhunihi* ('Satan urinated in both his ears—or he said—in his ear'), where the narrator's scrupulous precision over whether the urine entered one ear or two proves the Companions understood it as a literal physical act. Furthermore, classical authorities including Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* on `muslim:1817`) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī* on `bukhari:1144`) explicitly affirm that taking this urination literally (*ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi*) is fully sound because orthodox Sunni theology maintains that devils literally eat, drink, and excrete.

muslim:859.note: Muhammad states that when the call to prayer (*adhān*) is proclaimed, Satan flees while audibly breaking wind (*ḍurāṭ*) so that he cannot hear the call, and after the second call (*iqāmah*) finishes, he returns to whisper distractions until the worshipper no longer knows how much he has prayed.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلاَةِ أَدْبَرَ الشَّيْطَانُ لَهُ ضُرَاطٌ حَتَّى لاَ يَسْمَعَ التَّأْذِينَ فَإِذَا قُضِيَ التَّأْذِينُ أَقْبَلَ حَتَّى إِذَا ثُوِّبَ بِالصَّلاَةِ أَدْبَرَ حَتَّى إِذَا قُضِيَ التَّثْوِيبُ أَقْبَلَ حَتَّى يَخْطِرَ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَنَفْسِهِ يَقُولُ لَهُ اذْكُرْ كَذَا وَاذْكُرْ كَذَا لِمَا لَمْ يَكُنْ يَذْكُرُ مِنْ قَبْلُ حَتَّى يَظَلَّ الرَّجُلُ مَا يَدْرِي كَمْ صَلَّى
problematic_excerpt.english: When the call to prayer is made, Satan runs back and breaks wind so as not to hear the call being made, and when the call is finished. he turns round. When Iqama is proclaimed he turns his back, and when it is finished he turns round to distract a man, saying: Re- member such and such; remember such and such, referring to something the man did not have in his mind, with the result that he does not know how much he has prayed

muslim:859.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase *lahu ḍurāṭ* ('breaking wind') is merely an Arabic idiom or metaphor for fleeing in extreme terror rather than a literal bodily sound. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states the acoustic purpose of the flatulence—*ḥattā lā yasmaʿa al-taʾdhīn* ('so as not to hear the call to prayer')—leading both Imām al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) to affirm that its literal meaning (*ʿalā ẓāhirihi*) is an actual loud noise emitted by Satan to drown out the Adhan. Furthermore, the narration exposes the theological irony that while the mere announcement of prayer sends Satan fleeing in flatulent panic, the sacred act of prayer itself cannot prevent him from returning moments later to hijack the worshipper's mind.

muslim:7492.note: Muhammad instructs his followers that when any of them yawns, he should restrain it with his hand because Satan enters.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ إِذَا تَثَاوَبَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيُمْسِكْ بِيَدِهِ فَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَدْخُلُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said:When one of you yawns, he should try to restrain it with cue help of his hand since it is the Satan that enters therein

muslim:7492.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this instruction is merely a rule of social etiquette and hygiene, claiming that Satan's entry is a metaphor for laziness or heedlessness rather than a physical event. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "falyumsik bi-yadihi fa-inna al-shayṭāna yadkhulu" ("he should restrain it with his hand, for indeed the Satan enters"), directly linking the physical act of blocking the mouth to preventing a literal entry. Using a hand as a physical barrier over an open mouth during an involuntary yawn only functions if the entry being blocked is spatial and literal, as repeated across parallel narrations (muslim:7491, muslim:7493, bukhari:6226).

bukhari:608.note: Muhammad states that when the call to prayer (Adhan) is pronounced, Satan flees while audibly passing wind (durat) so as not to hear the call, and returns after the Adhan and Iqama are completed to whisper distractions into the worshipper's mind until he forgets how much he has prayed.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلاَةِ أَدْبَرَ الشَّيْطَانُ وَلَهُ ضُرَاطٌ حَتَّى لاَ يَسْمَعَ التَّأْذِينَ، فَإِذَا قَضَى النِّدَاءَ أَقْبَلَ، حَتَّى إِذَا ثُوِّبَ بِالصَّلاَةِ أَدْبَرَ، حَتَّى إِذَا قَضَى التَّثْوِيبَ أَقْبَلَ حَتَّى يَخْطُرَ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَنَفْسِهِ، يَقُولُ اذْكُرْ كَذَا، اذْكُرْ كَذَا‏.‏ لِمَا لَمْ يَكُنْ يَذْكُرُ، حَتَّى يَظَلَّ الرَّجُلُ لاَ يَدْرِي كَمْ صَلَّى
problematic_excerpt.english: When the Adhan is pronounced Satan takes to his heels and passes wind with noise during his flight in order not to hear the Adhan. When the Adhan is completed he comes back and again takes to his heels when the Iqama is pronounced and after its completion he returns again till he whispers into the heart of the person (to divert his attention from his prayer) and makes him remember things which he does not recall to his mind before the prayer and that causes him to forget how much he has prayed

bukhari:608.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Satan's noisy passing of wind (ḍurāṭ) is merely an Arabic idiom or metaphor (majāz) expressing extreme panic and humiliation rather than a literal bodily function. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states a literal acoustic purpose—'وَلَهُ ضُرَاطٌ حَتَّى لاَ يَسْمَعَ التَّأْذِينَ' ('and he emits noisy flatulence so that he does not hear the Adhan')—proving that the physical noise itself is what drowns out the call to prayer in his ears. Furthermore, both Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) and Ibn Ḥajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) confirm that taking this flatulence literally (ʿalā ẓāhirihi) as an actual sound emitted from Satan's body is the primary, established Sunni position, consistent with other Sahih narrations where Satan physically eats, sleeps, and urinates.

muslim:532.note: Muhammad declares that 999 out of every 1,000 descendants of Adam are consigned to Hellfire, reassuring his companions that this quota is filled because there are a thousand people from the tribes of Gog and Magog (*Ya'juj wa-Ma'juj*)—whom [Quran 18:94-98](quran://18/94-98) places behind an earthly barrier of iron and copper—for every one person from among them (cf. bukhari:3348, bukhari:4741, bukhari:6530). Classical commentators including Al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar affirm this literal demographic ratio to explain how 999 out of every 1,000 humans enter Hell while Muslims still constitute up to half the inhabitants of Paradise.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَيُّنَا ذَلِكَ الرَّجُلُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَبْشِرُوا فَإِنَّ مِنْ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ أَلْفًا وَمِنْكُمْ رَجُلٌ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: they said: Messenger of Allah, who amongst us would be (that unfortunate) person (who would be doomed to Hell)? He said: Good tidings for you, Yajuj Majuj would be those thousands (who would be the denizens of Hell) and a person (selected for Paradise) would be amongst you.

muslim:532.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the 999-to-1 ratio is merely Arabic hyperbole (*mubālaghah*) to emphasize the vastness of creation, or that *Ya'jūj wa-Ma'jūj* refers to non-human unseen beings or historical Eurasian nomads rather than a literal population outnumbering humanity. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah commands Adam (`يَا آدَمُ`) to extract this exact proportion from his own human offspring (`مِنْ كُلِّ أَلْفٍ تِسْعَمِائَةٍ وَتِسْعَةً وَتِسْعِينَ`), and Muhammad resolves his Companions' literal mathematical dread (`أَيُّنَا ذَلِكَ الرَّجُلُ`) by directly offsetting their numbers against Gog and Magog (`فَإِنَّ مِنْ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ أَلْفًا وَمِنْكُمْ رَجُلٌ`). Both Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī* on `bukhari:3348`) confirm that this is a literal demographic census of Adam's physical descendants trapped behind Dhū al-Qarnayn's iron-and-copper wall ([Quran 18:94-98](quran://18/94-98)), leaving no room for metaphorical deflection.

muslim:7493.note: Muhammad instructs that if anyone yawns during prayer, he must restrain it as much as possible because Satan enters.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ إِذَا تَثَاوَبَ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي الصَّلاَةِ فَلْيَكْظِمْ مَا اسْتَطَاعَ فَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَدْخُلُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said. When one of you yawns while engaged in prayer, he should try to restrain so far as it lies in his power, since it is the Satan that enter therein

muslim:7493.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the reference to Satan entering during a yawn is merely a metaphor for spiritual laziness, distraction in prayer, or basic polite etiquette rather than a literal physical event. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the worshipper must physically restrain the yawn as much as possible (falyakzim ma istata'a) specifically because Satan enters (fa-inna al-shaytana yadkhulu). Grounding a physical action to close or restrain the mouth directly on the causal statement that Satan enters treats the demon's entry through the yawning mouth as a literal reality, as corroborated in muslim:7491, muslim:7492, and bukhari:3289.

bukhari:1222.note: Muhammad states that when the call to prayer (adhān) is pronounced, Satan flees while audibly passing wind (ḍurāṭ) so he cannot hear it, retreats again during the iqāmah, and returns afterward to distract the worshipper until he forgets how much he has prayed. Classical Sunni commentators (including al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar) note that while some suggested this phrasing is a metaphor for intense terror, the primary position takes Satan's flatulence literally as an actual sound emitted to drown out the call.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا أُذِّنَ بِالصَّلاَةِ أَدْبَرَ الشَّيْطَانُ لَهُ ضُرَاطٌ حَتَّى لاَ يَسْمَعَ التَّأْذِينَ، فَإِذَا سَكَتَ الْمُؤَذِّنُ أَقْبَلَ، فَإِذَا ثُوِّبَ أَدْبَرَ فَإِذَا سَكَتَ أَقْبَلَ، فَلاَ يَزَالُ بِالْمَرْءِ يَقُولُ لَهُ اذْكُرْ مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ يَذْكُرُ حَتَّى لاَ يَدْرِي كَمْ صَلَّى
problematic_excerpt.english: When the Adhan for the prayer is pronounced, then Satan takes to his heels passing wind so that he may not hear the Adhan and when the Mu'adh-dhin finishes, he comes back; and when the Iqama is pronounced he again takes to his heels and when it is finished, he again comes back and continues reminding the praying person of things that he used not to remember when not in prayer till he forgets how much he has prayed.

bukhari:1222.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase 'passing wind' (lahu ḍurāṭ) is merely a figurative Arabic idiom (majāz) expressing Satan's extreme panic and hasty flight from the call to prayer rather than literal flatulence. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states 'lahu ḍurāṭun ḥattā lā yasmaʿa al-taʾdhīn' ('he passes wind loudly so that he may not hear the Adhan'), assigning a direct acoustic purpose—drowning out the sound of the call—which compelled classical Sunni authorities like Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) and Ibn Ḥajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī) to affirm that Satan's flatulence is literal physical reality (ʿalā ḥaqīqatihi), matching parallel Sahih narrations where Satan physically urinates in a sleeper's ears (bukhari:1144) and lodges inside human nostrils (bukhari:3295).

bukhari:5242.note: Muhammad narrates that Solomon had sexual relations with one hundred women in a single night so each would bear a son to fight in Allah's cause, but because he forgot to say "if Allah wills" when prompted by an angel, only one woman gave birth to a "half-person" (niṣf insān), whereas saying it would have kept his oath from failing. Parallel narrations in Sahih al-Bukhari report the number of women variously as sixty (bukhari:7469), seventy (bukhari:2819), ninety (bukhari:3424), ninety-nine (bukhari:6720), and one hundred (bukhari:6639), while classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar affirm the literal prophetic attribution of the account.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ ـ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلاَمُ ـ لأَطُوفَنَّ اللَّيْلَةَ بِمِائَةِ امْرَأَةٍ، تَلِدُ كُلُّ امْرَأَةٍ غُلاَمًا، يُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَلَكُ قُلْ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ‏.‏ فَلَمْ يَقُلْ وَنَسِيَ، فَأَطَافَ بِهِنَّ، وَلَمْ تَلِدْ مِنْهُنَّ إِلاَّ امْرَأَةٌ نِصْفَ إِنْسَانٍ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لَوْ قَالَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَمْ يَحْنَثْ، وَكَانَ أَرْجَى لِحَاجَتِهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: (The Prophet) Solomon son of (the Prophet) David said, "Tonight I will go round (i.e. have sexual relations with) one hundred women (my wives) everyone of whom will deliver a male child who will fight in Allah's Cause." On that an Angel said to him, "Say: 'If Allah will.' " But Solomon did not say it and forgot to say it. Then he had sexual relations with them but none of them delivered any child except one who delivered a half person. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "If Solomon had said: 'If Allah will,' Allah would have fulfilled his (above) desire and that saying would have made him more hopeful

bukhari:5242.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Solomon was divinely granted miraculous physical stamina, that the conflicting totals across Sahih narrations (60, 70, 90, or 100 women) merely reflect rounding or a distinction between free wives and concubines (as claimed in Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī), and that the offspring was simply a premature miscarriage explaining Solomon's trial in Qur'an 38:34. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Solomon had sexual relations with all one hundred women in a single night (lā'aṭūfanna al-laylata bi-mi'ati imra'atin ... fa-aṭāfa bihinna) and that one delivered a literal 'half-human' (niṣfa insānin—described in parallel Sahih narrations like bukhari:3424 as a split 'half-man,' shiqqa rajulin), which classical exegetes directly identify as the lifeless body (jasad) cast upon his throne. Furthermore, Muhammad's own concluding guarantee (law qāla in shā'a Allāhu lam yaḥnath) insists that merely uttering the verbal formula in shā' Allāh would have caused all one hundred women (contradictorily reported as seventy in bukhari:2819 and ninety in bukhari:3424) to simultaneously conceive and birth male warriors from one night, reducing human biology to a magical incantation while exposing irreconcilable numerical contradictions in Muhammad's own words.

bukhari:1231.note: Muhammad states that when the call to prayer (Adhan) is made, Satan flees while audibly passing wind (durat) so as not to hear it, then returns after the second call (Iqama) to whisper distractions until a worshipper forgets how many prayer units (rak'at) he has performed. To remedy this Satan-induced forgetfulness, Muhammad prescribes two sitting prostrations (sujud al-sahu)—the exact procedure he himself performs after forgetting his own prayer count in the immediately preceding chapter reports (bukhari:1229, bukhari:1230).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا نُودِيَ بِالصَّلاَةِ أَدْبَرَ الشَّيْطَانُ وَلَهُ ضُرَاطٌ حَتَّى لاَ يَسْمَعَ الأَذَانَ، فَإِذَا قُضِيَ الأَذَانُ أَقْبَلَ، فَإِذَا ثُوِّبَ بِهَا أَدْبَرَ فَإِذَا قُضِيَ التَّثْوِيبُ أَقْبَلَ حَتَّى يَخْطِرَ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَنَفْسِهِ يَقُولُ اذْكُرْ كَذَا وَكَذَا مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ يَذْكُرُ حَتَّى يَظَلَّ الرَّجُلُ إِنْ يَدْرِي كَمْ صَلَّى
problematic_excerpt.english: When the call for prayer is made, Satan takes to his heels passing wind so that he may not hear the Adhan and when the call is finished he comes back, and when the Iqama is pronounced, Satan again takes to his heels, and when the Iqama is finished he comes back again and tries to interfere with the person and his thoughts and say, "Remember this and that (which he has not thought of before the prayer)", till the praying person forgets how much he has prayed.

bukhari:1231.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the phrase 'passing wind' (wa-lahu ḍurāṭ) is merely an Arabic idiom or metaphor (majāz) illustrating Satan's intense panic and hasty flight from the call to prayer. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that he emits loud flatulence for a literal acoustic purpose—'so that he may not hear the Adhan' (ḥattā lā yasmaʿa al-adhān)—and parallel Sahih narrations (muslim:856) even measure his physical flight to the town of al-Rawḥāʾ, thirty-six miles from Medina. Consequently, classical authorities like Al-Nawawī (Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:856) and Ibn Ḥajar (Fatḥ al-Bārī 608) affirm that this flatulence must be taken literally (ʿalā ẓāhirihi), since Islamic orthodoxy teaches that Satan has a physical body that literally eats, drinks, and expels gas to drown out the call.

muslim:6771.note: When monkeys and swine resulting from metamorphosis (*maskh*) are mentioned before him, Muhammad declares that Allah did not grant offspring or posterity to any metamorphosed creature and states that monkeys and swine already existed before that transformation ([Quran 2:65](quran://2/65), [Quran 5:60](quran://5/60), [Quran 7:166](quran://7/166)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ وَذُكِرَتْ عِنْدَهُ الْقِرَدَةُ قَالَ مِسْعَرٌ وَأُرَاهُ قَالَ وَالْخَنَازِيرُ مِنْ مَسْخٍ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمْ يَجْعَلْ لِمَسْخٍ نَسْلاً وَلاَ عَقِبًا وَقَدْ كَانَتِ الْقِرَدَةُ وَالْخَنَازِيرُ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He (the narrator) further said: Mention was made before him about monkeys, and Mis'ar (one of the narrators) said: I think that (the narrator) also (made a mention) of the swine, which had suffered metamorphosis. Thereupon he (the Holy Prophet) said: Verily, Allah did not cause the race of those which suffered metamorphosis to grow or they were not survived by young ones. Monkeys and swine had been in existence even before (the metamorphosis of the human beings)

muslim:6771.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the transformation into monkeys and pigs in [Quran 2:65](quran://2/65), [Quran 5:60](quran://5/60), and [Quran 7:166](quran://7/166) was merely a metaphorical description of moral degradation, or that this Hadith refutes superstition by denying that modern animals descend from humans. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah gave the metamorphosed beings (*maskh*) neither biological offspring nor descendants (*lam yaj'al li-maskhin naslan wa-la 'aqiban*) and notes that monkeys and pigs already existed before that event (*wa-qad kanat al-qiradatu wa-al-khanaziru qabla dhalika*). By addressing their reproductive sterility and distinguishing them from pre-existing animal species (see also `muslim:6773` and `bukhari:3305`), Muhammad affirms the physical metamorphosis of human beings into animals as a literal biological event rather than a figure of speech.

bukhari:3285.note: Muhammad states that when the call to prayer is pronounced, Satan turns and flees while loudly passing wind (durat), returning when it finishes, fleeing again at the second call (iqama), and then returning to intrude between a person and his heart until the worshipper forgets whether he has prayed three or four units (rak'at).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا نُودِيَ بِالصَّلاَةِ أَدْبَرَ الشَّيْطَانُ وَلَهُ ضُرَاطٌ، فَإِذَا قُضِيَ أَقْبَلَ، فَإِذَا ثُوِّبَ بِهَا أَدْبَرَ، فَإِذَا قُضِيَ أَقْبَلَ، حَتَّى يَخْطِرَ بَيْنَ الإِنْسَانِ وَقَلْبِهِ، فَيَقُولُ اذْكُرْ كَذَا وَكَذَا‏.‏ حَتَّى لاَ يَدْرِي أَثَلاَثًا صَلَّى أَمْ أَرْبَعًا
problematic_excerpt.english: When the call for the prayer is pronounced, Satan takes to his heels, passing wind with noise, When the call for the prayer is finished, he comes back. And when the Iqama is pronounced, he again takes to his heels, and after its completion, he returns again to interfere between the (praying) person and his heart, saying to him. 'Remember this or that thing.' till the person forgets whether he has offered three or four rak`at

bukhari:3285.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Satan's 'passing wind with noise' is merely a figurative Arabic idiom for extreme terror and hasty flight rather than literal bodily flatulence. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states 'wa-lahu ḍurāṭ' (وَلَهُ ضُرَاطٌ)—using the unambiguous anatomical noun for audible rectal flatulence—and parallel narrations (such as bukhari:608 and 1222) specify that he does this physically 'so that he will not hear the call to prayer' (حَتَّى لاَ يَسْمَعَ التَّأْذِينَ). Consequently, leading Sunni commentators like Al-Nawawī and Ibn Hajar affirm that the description is strictly literal ('alā ẓāhirihi), maintaining that Satan is a corporeal being who eats and emits loud gas to drown out the Adhan in his own ears.

bukhari:6639.note: Muhammad swears an oath that Solomon had sexual intercourse with ninety women in a single night to sire ninety horsemen to fight in Allah's cause, but because he omitted "if Allah wills" (in sha'a Allah), only one woman conceived and delivered a half-man (shiqqa rajul), whom classical exegetes identify as the lifeless body placed on Solomon's throne in [Quran 38:34](quran://38/34). Parallel reports from Abu Huraira in Sahih al-Bukhari give conflicting numbers of women: sixty (bukhari:7469), seventy (bukhari:3424), ninety (bukhari:2819), and one hundred (bukhari:5242).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ سُلَيْمَانُ لأَطُوفَنَّ اللَّيْلَةَ عَلَى تِسْعِينَ امْرَأَةً، كُلُّهُنَّ تَأْتِي بِفَارِسٍ يُجَاهِدُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُ صَاحِبُهُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ‏.‏ فَلَمْ يَقُلْ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ‏.‏ فَطَافَ عَلَيْهِنَّ جَمِيعًا، فَلَمْ تَحْمِلْ مِنْهُنَّ إِلاَّ امْرَأَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ، جَاءَتْ بِشِقِّ رَجُلٍ، وَايْمُ الَّذِي نَفْسُ مُحَمَّدٍ بِيَدِهِ لَوْ قَالَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ‏.‏ لَجَاهَدُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فُرْسَانًا أَجْمَعُونَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Solomon once said, 'Tonight I will sleep with ninety women, each of whom will bring forth a (would-be) cavalier who will fight in Allah's Cause." On this, his companion said to him, "Say: Allah willing!" But he did not say Allah willing. Solomon then slept with all the women, but none of them became pregnant but one woman who later delivered a halfman. By Him in Whose Hand Muhammad's soul is, if he (Solomon) had said, 'Allah willing' (all his wives would have brought forth boys) and they would have fought in Allah's Cause as cavaliers

bukhari:6639.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Prophets were divinely granted superhuman sexual stamina—as claimed by Ibn Hajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī—and that the resulting birth was merely a malformed stillborn infant serving as the trial of Quran 38:34 to teach the necessity of saying in shāʾ Allāh. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Solomon had intercourse with all ninety women in a single literal night (لأَطُوفَنَّ اللَّيْلَةَ ... فَطَافَ عَلَيْهِنَّ جَمِيعًا) and that one delivered a literal 'half-man' (شِقِّ رَجُلٍ), a biologically absurd fable that Muhammad swears by Allah's name would have yielded ninety jihadist cavaliers had Solomon merely uttered a verbal formula. Worse still for claims of pristine oral preservation, the Ṣaḥīḥ narrations from Abu Huraira wildly contradict one another on the number of women, fluctuating between 60 (Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:4285), 70 (Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:4286), 90 (bukhari:6639), 99 (bukhari:5242), and 100 (bukhari:3424).

muslim:6773.note: When asked whether apes and swine are the descendants of people who underwent metamorphosis (*maskh*), Muhammad affirms the physical transformation of ancient humans into apes and pigs as a historical punishment ([Quran 2:65](quran://2/65), [Quran 5:60](quran://5/60)), clarifying only that those transformed people produced no biological offspring and that apes and swine already existed before that event (muslim:6771, bukhari:3305).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ الْقِرَدَةُ وَالْخَنَازِيرُ هِيَ مِمَّا مُسِخَ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ لَمْ يُهْلِكْ قَوْمًا أَوْ يُعَذِّبْ قَوْمًا فَيَجْعَلَ لَهُمْ نَسْلاً وَإِنَّ الْقِرَدَةَ وَالْخَنَازِيرَ كَانُوا قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A person said: Allah's Messenger, what about those apes and swine which suffered metamorphosis? Thereupon Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) said: Verily, Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, did not destroy a people or did not torment a people, and let their race grow. Apes and swine had been even before that (when the deniers of truth were tormented and suffered metamorphosis).

muslim:6773.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the transformation of ancient humans into apes and swine in [Quran 2:65](quran://2/65) and [Quran 5:60](quran://5/60) was a metaphorical change in moral character rather than a literal physical metamorphosis. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah did not grant biological descendants (`فَيَجْعَلَ لَهُمْ نَسْلاً`) to those who suffered metamorphosis (`مِمَّا مُسِخَ`) and that apes and swine already existed before that punishment (`وَإِنَّ الْقِرَدَةَ وَالْخَنَازِيرَ كَانُوا قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ`). By distinguishing modern animals from those metamorphosed people solely on the basis of reproduction (`نَسْلاً`) and prior existence (`قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ`), Muhammad treats the physical transformation of humans into literal apes and pigs as historical reality.

muslim:6773.note: In response to Umm Habiba's prayer for her family, Muhammad declares that fixed lifespans and apportioned sustenance are never hastened before their due time or deferred beyond it, conflicting with his statement in bukhari:2067 that upholding kinship ties increases sustenance and extends one's lifespan. Furthermore, his categorical rule that Allah never grants offspring to a tormented, metamorphosed people (*maskh*) (muslim:6771) contradicts bukhari:3305, where he identifies contemporary living rats as a lost Israelite tribe that underwent metamorphosis.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ لَهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّكِ سَأَلْتِ اللَّهَ لآجَالٍ مَضْرُوبَةٍ وَآثَارٍ مَوْطُوءَةٍ وَأَرْزَاقٍ مَقْسُومَةٍ لاَ يُعَجِّلُ شَيْئًا مِنْهَا قَبْلَ حِلِّهِ وَلاَ يُؤَخِّرُ مِنْهَا شَيْئًا بَعْدَ حِلِّهِ وَلَوْ سَأَلْتِ اللَّهَ أَنْ يُعَافِيَكِ مِنْ عَذَابٍ فِي النَّارِ وَعَذَابٍ فِي الْقَبْرِ لَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَكِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ الْقِرَدَةُ وَالْخَنَازِيرُ هِيَ مِمَّا مُسِخَ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ لَمْ يُهْلِكْ قَوْمًا أَوْ يُعَذِّبْ قَوْمًا فَيَجْعَلَ لَهُمْ نَسْلاً وَإِنَّ الْقِرَدَةَ وَالْخَنَازِيرَ كَانُوا قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said to her: Verily, you have asked Allah about the durations of life already set, and the steps which you would take, and the sustenances the share of which is fixed. Nothing would take place earlier than its due time, and nothing would be deferred beyond that when it is due. So, if you were to ask Allah about your safety from the torment of Hell-Fire and from the torment of the grave, it would have been better for you. A person said: Allah's Messenger, what about those apes and swine which suffered metamorphosis? Thereupon Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) said: Verily, Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, did not destroy a people or did not torment a people, and let their race grow. Apes and swine had been even before that (when the deniers of truth were tormented and suffered metamorphosis).

muslim:6773.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's teaching in `bukhari:3305` and `muslim:2997` that living rats are a lost Israelite tribe was spoken before he learned that metamorphosed people leave no offspring, and that extending life and sustenance through kinship ties in `bukhari:2067` and `muslim:2557` refers only to metaphorical blessing. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that lifespans are already set (`لآجَالٍ مَضْرُوبَةٍ`) and sustenances are already divided (`وَأَرْزَاقٍ مَقْسُومَةٍ`) such that nothing is hastened before its time or deferred beyond it (`لاَ يُعَجِّلُ شَيْئًا مِنْهَا قَبْلَ حِلِّهِ وَلاَ يُؤَخِّرُ مِنْهَا شَيْئًا بَعْدَ حِلِّهِ`), which Muhammad uses to rebuke Umm Habiba's literal prayer for her husband, her father Abu Sufyan, and her brother Mu'awiya. Furthermore, his unqualified rule that Allah never grants descendants to a tormented people (`لَمْ يُهْلِكْ قَوْمًا أَوْ يُعَذِّبْ قَوْمًا فَيَجْعَلَ لَهُمْ نَسْلاً`) includes no claim of abrogating a prior statement, leaving a direct contradiction with his identification of living rodents as a metamorphosed Israelite tribe in `bukhari:3305` and `muslim:2997`.

muslim:4289.note: Muhammad states that Solomon went round to all ninety of his wives in a single night without saying 'Insha' Allah,' resulting in only one wife conceiving and giving birth to 'half of a man' (*bi-shiqqi rajul*, rendered in the English translation as 'a premature child'). Muhammad then swears by Him in Whose hand is his soul that had Solomon said 'Insha' Allah,' all of them would have fought in the cause of Allah as horsemen.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ لأَطُوفَنَّ اللَّيْلَةَ عَلَى تِسْعِينَ امْرَأَةً كُلُّهَا تَأْتِي بِفَارِسٍ يُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُ صَاحِبُهُ قُلْ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ ‏.‏ فَلَمْ يَقُلْ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ ‏.‏ فَطَافَ عَلَيْهِنَّ جَمِيعًا فَلَمْ تَحْمِلْ مِنْهُنَّ إِلاَّ امْرَأَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَجَاءَتْ بِشِقِّ رَجُلٍ وَايْمُ الَّذِي نَفْسُ مُحَمَّدٍ بِيَدِهِ لَوْ قَالَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ ‏.‏ لَجَاهَدُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فُرْسَانًا أَجْمَعُونَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Sulaiman b. Dawud (once) said:I will go round in the night to my ninety wives, and every one of them will give birth to a child (who will grow up) as a horseman and fight in the cause of Allah His companions said to him: Say" Insha' Allah." but he did not say Inshii' Allah. He went round all of them but none of them became pregnant but one, and she gave birth to a premature child. And by Him in Whose hand is the life of Muhammad, if he had said, Insha' Allah (his wives would have given birth to the children who would all have grown up into horsemen and fought in the way of Allah)

muslim:4289.literal_translation: Sulaiman b. Dawud said: 'I will certainly go round tonight to ninety wives, each of whom will bring forth a horseman who will fight in the cause of Allah.' His companion said to him: 'Say: Insha' Allah,' but he did not say Insha' Allah. He went round all of them, and none of them became pregnant except one woman, who gave birth to half of a man. And by Him in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, had he said Insha' Allah, they would all have fought in the cause of Allah as horsemen.

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَلَمْ تَحْمِلْ مِنْهُنَّ إِلاَّ امْرَأَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَجَاءَتْ بِشِقِّ رَجُلٍ
translation_issue.published_rendering: none of them became pregnant but one, and she gave birth to a premature child.
translation_issue.literal_meaning: none of them became pregnant except one woman, and she brought forth half of a man (bi-shiqqi rajul).
translation_issue.explanation: The published translation renders 'bi-shiqqi rajul' ('half of a man' or 'one side of a man') as 'a premature child', replacing the literal anatomical term with a naturalized medical expression.

muslim:4289.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Solomon was granted miraculous prophetic strength, or that the outcome was simply a routine miscarriage as suggested by the English rendering 'a premature child.' However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Solomon went round to all ninety wives in a single night (*fa-ṭāfa 'alayhinna jamī'an*) so that each would conceive a horseman, and that the lone pregnant wife literally brought forth 'half of a man' (*fa-jā'at bi-shiqqi rajul*). Furthermore, Muhammad swears a solemn oath by Allah (*wa-aymu alladhī nafsu Muḥammadin bi-yadihi*) that all ninety women would have conceived and borne fighting horsemen from that single night had Solomon merely uttered the verbal formula *Insha' Allah* (cf. `muslim:4286`, `bukhari:3424`, `bukhari:6639`, [Quran 38:34](quran://38/34)).

bukhari:3295.note: Muhammad instructs anyone performing ablution upon waking from sleep to sniff water into the nostrils and blow it out three times, declaring that Satan spends the night in the upper nasal passage (khayshum). Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi affirm that this statement is taken literally ('ala zahirihi), noting that the prescription of physical water to flush the nose precludes a purely metaphorical reading.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا اسْتَيْقَظَ ـ أُرَاهُ ـ أَحَدُكُمْ مِنْ مَنَامِهِ فَتَوَضَّأَ فَلْيَسْتَنْثِرْ ثَلاَثًا، فَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَبِيتُ عَلَى خَيْشُومِهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: If anyone of you rouses from sleep and performs the ablution, he should wash his nose by putting water in it and then blowing it out thrice, because Satan has stayed in the upper part of his nose all the night

bukhari:3295.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Satan lodging in the nose is merely a figurative metaphor (*majāz*) for morning sluggishness or the hygienic need to clear dust, mucus, and microscopic germs accumulated during sleep. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `فَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ يَبِيتُ عَلَى خَيْشُومِهِ` ("for indeed Satan spends the night on his upper nasal cavity") as the direct causal reason for physically flushing and blowing out the nostrils three times (`فَلْيَسْتَنْثِرْ ثَلاَثًا`). Furthermore, both Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) affirm that the primary Sunni position takes this literally (*ʿalā ẓāhirihi*) as an actual devil occupying the unsealed nasal passage overnight—matching parallel Sahih narrations where Satan physically urinates in a sleeper's ears (bukhari:1144) and ties knots on the back of his head (bukhari:1142).

muslim:4286.note: Muhammad recounts that Solomon vowed to have intercourse with seventy wives in a single night so each would bear a son to fight in Allah's cause, but because he forgot to say *Insha' Allah*, none of his wives gave birth except one who delivered "half of a boy" (*bi-shiqqi ghulām*, rendered in the English translation as "a premature child"). Muhammad declares that had Solomon said *Insha' Allah*, he would not have failed his oath and would have attained his desire.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ لأَطُوفَنَّ اللَّيْلَةَ عَلَى سَبْعِينَ امْرَأَةً كُلُّهُنَّ تَأْتِي بِغُلاَمٍ يُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُ صَاحِبُهُ أَوِ الْمَلَكُ قُلْ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ ‏.‏ فَلَمْ يَقُلْ وَنَسِيَ ‏.‏ فَلَمْ تَأْتِ وَاحِدَةٌ مِنْ نِسَائِهِ إِلاَّ وَاحِدَةٌ جَاءَتْ بِشِقِّ غُلاَمٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ وَلَوْ قَالَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ ‏.‏ لَمْ يَحْنَثْ وَكَانَ دَرَكًا لَهُ فِي حَاجَتِهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Sulaiman b. Dawud, the Messenger of Allah, observed:I will have an intercourse with seventy wives during the night; all of them will give birth to a male child who will fight in the cause of Allah. His companion or the ang I said to him: Say," If God wills." But he (Hadrat Sulaimin) did not say so, and he forgot it. And none of his wives gave birth to a child, but one who gave birth to a premature child. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Had he said Insha' Allah (if God so will). he would not have failed and his desire would have been materialised

muslim:4286.literal_translation: Sulaiman b. Dawud, the Prophet of Allah, said: 'I will certainly go round tonight to seventy wives, each of whom will give birth to a boy who will fight in the cause of Allah.' His companion or the angel said to him: 'Say: If Allah wills.' But he did not say it and forgot. And none of his wives gave birth except one, who gave birth to half of a boy. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Had he said Insha' Allah, he would not have broken his oath and would have attained his need.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَلَمْ تَأْتِ وَاحِدَةٌ مِنْ نِسَائِهِ إِلاَّ وَاحِدَةٌ جَاءَتْ بِشِقِّ غُلاَمٍ
translation_issue.published_rendering: And none of his wives gave birth to a child, but one who gave birth to a premature child.
translation_issue.literal_meaning: And none of his wives gave birth except one, who brought forth half of a boy (bi-shiqqi ghulām).
translation_issue.explanation: The translator renders 'bi-shiqqi ghulām' ('half of a boy', from shiqq meaning 'half' or 'one side') as 'a premature child' to rationalize the delivery of a half-formed boy into a standard premature birth.

muslim:4286.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that prophets were granted supernatural physical strength, that the phrase rendered as 'a premature child' merely describes a routine miscarriage or congenital birth defect, and that the narrative simply teaches the spiritual humility of saying *Insha' Allah*. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Solomon vowed to go round to seventy wives in a single night (لأَطُوفَنَّ اللَّيْلَةَ عَلَى سَبْعِينَ امْرَأَةً) and that the lone conceiving wife delivered a literal 'half of a boy' (بِشِقِّ غُلاَمٍ), a folkloric detail that the English translator obscures behind a clinical euphemism. Furthermore, Muhammad's declaration that merely pronouncing *Insha' Allah* (وَلَوْ قَالَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ) would have prevented the broken oath and fulfilled his desire for seventy male fighters (لَمْ يَحْنَثْ وَكَانَ دَرَكًا لَهُ فِي حَاجَتِهِ) treats a verbal formula as an automatic guarantee of biological conception (cf. bukhari:5242, muslim:4288, [Quran 38:34](quran://38/34)).

bukhari:3424.note: Muhammad declares that Solomon vowed to have intercourse with seventy (or ninety) women in a single night so each would conceive a horseman to fight in Allah's cause, but because he failed to say "if Allah wills" when prompted by his companion, none conceived except one who delivered half a child. Muhammad adds that had Solomon uttered the phrase, they all would have borne warriors who fought in Allah's cause—a literal account that classical commentators connect to the body (jasad) placed on Solomon's throne in [Quran 38:34](quran://38/34).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ لأَطُوفَنَّ اللَّيْلَةَ عَلَى سَبْعِينَ امْرَأَةً تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ امْرَأَةٍ فَارِسًا يُجَاهِدُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ صَاحِبُهُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ‏.‏ فَلَمْ يَقُلْ، وَلَمْ تَحْمِلْ شَيْئًا إِلاَّ وَاحِدًا سَاقِطًا إِحْدَى شِقَّيْهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لَوْ قَالَهَا لَجَاهَدُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ شُعَيْبٌ وَابْنُ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ ‏"‏ تِسْعِينَ ‏"‏‏.‏ وَهْوَ أَصَحُّ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Solomon (the son of) David said, 'Tonight I will sleep with seventy ladies each of whom will conceive a child who will be a knight fighting for "Allah's Cause.' His companion said, 'If Allah will.' But Solomon did not say so; therefore none of those women got pregnant except one who gave birth to a half child." The Prophet (ﷺ) further said, "If the Prophet Solomon (ﷺ) had said it (i.e. 'If Allah will') he would have begotten children who would have fought in Allah's Cause." Shuaib and Ibn Abi Az-Zinad said, "Ninety (women) is more correct (than seventy)

bukhari:3424.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that prophets possessed miraculous physical stamina granted by Allah—citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—or claim this narration is merely a symbolic moral lesson on saying *in shāʾ Allāh* rather than a literal folkloric myth. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Solomon physically went to seventy or ninety women in a single night for conception (`لأَطُوفَنَّ اللَّيْلَةَ عَلَى سَبْعِينَ امْرَأَةً تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ امْرَأَةٍ فَارِسًا`) and that one woman literally birthed a half-child (`وَاحِدًا سَاقِطًا إِحْدَى شِقَّيْهِ`, rendered `شِقَّ إِنْسَانٍ` in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 5242). Moreover, the transmitters openly contradict one another on whether the number of women was seventy, ninety (`تِسْعِينَ وَهْوَ أَصَحُّ`), or one hundred (Bukhārī 5242), while classical exegetes like al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr identify this grotesque half-infant as the literal lifeless body (*jasadan*) cast onto Solomon's throne in Qur'an 38:34.

muslim:4288.note: Abu Huraira reports that Solomon vowed to have intercourse with seventy wives in a single night so each would bear a son to fight in Allah's cause, yet after failing to say 'Insha' Allah,' only one wife gave birth—delivering 'half a human being' (*niṣfa insān*), which the English translation softens to 'an incomplete person.' Muhammad explicitly affirms this account and its outcome, stating that had Solomon said 'Insha' Allah,' he would not have broken his oath and his desire would have been fulfilled.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ لأُطِيفَنَّ اللَّيْلَةَ عَلَى سَبْعِينَ امْرَأَةً تَلِدُ كُلُّ امْرَأَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ غُلاَمًا يُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ‏.‏ فَقِيلَ لَهُ قُلْ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ ‏.‏ فَلَمْ يَقُلْ ‏.‏ فَأَطَافَ بِهِنَّ فَلَمْ تَلِدْ مِنْهُنَّ إِلاَّ امْرَأَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ نِصْفَ إِنْسَانٍ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ لَوْ قَالَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ ‏.‏ لَمْ يَحْنَثْ وَكَانَ دَرَكًا لِحَاجَتِهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Sulaiman b. Dawud said:I will certainly have intercourse with seventy wives during the night, and every wife amongst them will give birth to a child, who will fight in the cause of Allah. It was said to him: Say:" Insha' Allah" (God willing), but he did not say so and forgot it. He went round them but none of them give birth to a child except one woman and that too was an incomplete person. Upon this Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: If he had said" Insha' Allah." he would not have failed, and his desire must have been fulfilled

muslim:4288.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the account uses figurative hyperbole or describes miraculous prophetic vigor, and that the resulting birth was simply a premature miscarriage or a congenitally malformed infant. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states as literal fact that Solomon physically went round to seventy wives in a single night (la-uṭīfanna al-laylata ʿalā sabʿīna imraʾatan... fa-aṭāfa bihinna) and that one wife delivered a literal 'half a human being' (niṣfa insān). Furthermore, Muhammad affirms the event's literal cause-and-effect in this report and its Sahih parallels (bukhari:6720, muslim:4286, muslim:4289) linked to [Quran 38:34](quran://38/34), stating that had Solomon merely spoken the formula in shāʾa Allāh, his desire for all seventy wives to bear warrior sons from that single night would have been fulfilled (wa-kāna darakan li-ḥājatihi).

bukhari:3860.note: Muhammad forbade using bones or animal dung to clean his private parts after relieving himself, instructing Abu Huraira to bring him stones instead. He explained that bones and animal dung are the food of the jinn, stating that after a delegation of jinn from Nasibin asked him for provisions, he prayed to Allah that they would never pass by a bone or piece of dung without finding food on it.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ ‏"‏ ابْغِنِي أَحْجَارًا أَسْتَنْفِضْ بِهَا، وَلاَ تَأْتِنِي بِعَظْمٍ وَلاَ بِرَوْثَةٍ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَأَتَيْتُهُ بِأَحْجَارٍ أَحْمِلُهَا فِي طَرَفِ ثَوْبِي حَتَّى وَضَعْتُ إِلَى جَنْبِهِ ثُمَّ انْصَرَفْتُ، حَتَّى إِذَا فَرَغَ مَشَيْتُ، فَقُلْتُ مَا بَالُ الْعَظْمِ وَالرَّوْثَةِ قَالَ ‏"‏ هُمَا مِنْ طَعَامِ الْجِنِّ، وَإِنَّهُ أَتَانِي وَفْدُ جِنِّ نَصِيبِينَ وَنِعْمَ الْجِنُّ، فَسَأَلُونِي الزَّادَ، فَدَعَوْتُ اللَّهَ لَهُمْ أَنْ لاَ يَمُرُّوا بِعَظْمٍ وَلاَ بِرَوْثَةٍ إِلاَّ وَجَدُوا عَلَيْهَا طَعَامًا ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Bring me stones in order to clean my private parts, and do not bring any bones or animal dung." Abu Huraira went on narrating: So I brought some stones, carrying them in the corner of my robe till I put them by his side and went away. When he finished, I walked with him and asked, "What about the bone and the animal dung?" He said, "They are of the food of Jinns. The delegate of Jinns of (the city of) Nasibin came to me--and how nice those Jinns were--and asked me for the remains of the human food. I invoked Allah for them that they would never pass by a bone or animal dung but find food on them

bukhari:3860.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that prohibiting bones and animal dung for anal cleansing (*istinjā'*) was a prescient hygienic rule to prevent infection, or that 'jinn' in this context is a prophetic metaphor for microscopic bacteria feeding on decomposing waste. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the prohibition is unrelated to human sanitation, as Muhammad explains, 'They are of the food of the jinn; a delegation of the jinn of Nasibin came to me—and how excellent those jinn were—and asked me for provisions' (*humā min ṭa‘āmi al-jinn, wa-innahu atānī wafdu jinni Naṣībīn... fa-sa’alūnī al-zād*). Furthermore, the parallel narration in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* (`muslim:1007`) specifies that every bone becomes miraculously reclothed with meat for these Muslim jinn to eat while every piece of dung turns into fodder (*‘alaf*) for their riding beasts (*dawābb*), confirming literal seventh-century AD folklore about invisible tribes and their livestock rather than microbiology.

bukhari:3289.note: Muhammad declares that the physiological reflex of yawning comes from Satan and commands his followers to suppress it as much as possible, stating that if a person makes a 'Ha' sound while yawning, Satan laughs at him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: التَّثَاؤُبُ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ، فَإِذَا تَثَاءَبَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَرُدَّهُ مَا اسْتَطَاعَ، فَإِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ إِذَا قَالَ هَا‏.‏ ضَحِكَ الشَّيْطَانُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Yawning is from Satan and if anyone of you yawns, he should check his yawning as much as possible, for if anyone of you (during the act of yawning) should say: 'Ha', Satan will laugh at him

bukhari:3289.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that attributing yawning to Satan is merely a metaphor (citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*) meaning that Satan encourages gluttony and laziness which induce sluggishness, and that the command simply teaches polite etiquette. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that yawning itself is from Satan (*al-tathā'ubu min al-shayṭān*) and that making the sound 'Hā' causes Satan to laugh (*ḍaḥika al-shayṭān*), while parallel Sahih narrations (`muslim:2995`) command holding the mouth shut because otherwise 'Satan enters' (*fa-inna al-shayṭāna yadkhulu*). Ibn Hajar himself acknowledged that this refers to literal physical entry (*al-dukhūl ḥaqīqatan*) into the mouth, confirming a superstitious demonology that mistakes an involuntary autonomic reflex—present even in unborn fetuses—for demonic interference.

bukhari:4987.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:4987.note: Uthman instructs the three Quraishi scribes to write the Quran in the dialect of Quraish whenever they disagree with Zaid bin Thabit, sends a transcribed copy to every Muslim province, and orders that all other Quranic manuscripts and complete codices be burned.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَأَمَرَ بِمَا سِوَاهُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ فِي كُلِّ صَحِيفَةٍ أَوْ مُصْحَفٍ أَنْ يُحْرَقَ
problematic_excerpt.english: and ordered that all the other Qur'anic materials, whether written in fragmentary manuscripts or whole copies, be burnt

bukhari:4987.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī, that Uthman only burned unverified private notebooks containing personal tafsir notes or abrogated readings while preserving the authentic Quran through unanimous companion consensus (ijmāʿ). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Uthman ordered the burning of "whatever else was of the Qur'an in every fragment or complete codex" (bi-mā siwāhu min al-Qurʾān fī kulli ṣaḥīfah aw muṣḥaf an yuḥraqa) only after instructing his own committee how to settle their internal disputes over the Quranic text (idhā ikhtalaftum antum wa-Zayd ibn Thābit fī shayʾin min al-Qurʾān). This destroys the myth of a single preserved text or unanimous consensus, as confirmed in the immediately following narrations (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4988 and 5000; Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:6332) where Zayd had to hunt for missing verses from lone witnesses and Muhammad's premier reciter, ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, fiercely denounced Uthman's standardization and refused to surrender his codex to the flames.

bukhari:4987.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:4987.note: Alarmed by differences in Quranic recitation between the Muslim armies of Sham and Iraq during the conquest of Armenia and Azerbaijan, Hudhaifa bin al-Yaman urges Caliph Uthman to intervene before the nation differs over the Book as the Jews and Christians did.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَفْزَعَ حُذَيْفَةَ اخْتِلاَفُهُمْ فِي الْقِرَاءَةِ فَقَالَ حُذَيْفَةُ لِعُثْمَانَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَدْرِكْ هَذِهِ الأُمَّةَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْتَلِفُوا فِي الْكِتَابِ اخْتِلاَفَ الْيَهُودِ وَالنَّصَارَى
problematic_excerpt.english: Hudhaifa was afraid of their (the people of Sham and Iraq) differences in the recitation of the Qur'an, so he said to `Uthman, "O chief of the Believers! Save this nation before they differ about the Book (Qur'an) as Jews and the Christians did before."

bukhari:4987.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the differences between the armies of Sham and Iraq were merely benign, divinely revealed dialectical pronunciations (al-aḥruf al-sabʿah) that never threatened the integrity of the Quranic text. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that these recitational clashes terrified Hudhayfah (fa-afzaʿa Ḥudhayfah ikhtilāfuhum fī al-qirāʾah) to the point of comparing them directly to the scriptural corruption and schisms of the Jews and Christians (ikhtilāf al-Yahūd wa-al-Naṣārā). Furthermore, Ibn Hajar admits in Fatḥ al-Bārī that the Syrian and Iraqi troops—reciting the competing codices of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and Ibn Masʿūd, which differed in whole chapters, verse lengths, and wording—were actively accusing one another of disbelief (takfīr), proving that human political intervention (adrik hādhihi al-ummah) was required to rescue the text from fracturing.

muslim:3597.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:3597.note: Aisha states that what was revealed of the Quran included a stipulation that ten known sucklings make marriage unlawful, which was then abrogated by five known sucklings. She testifies that the five-sucklings verse was still being recited as part of the Quran when Muhammad died, though neither verse exists in the modern Quran ([Quran 15:9](quran://15/9)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ كَانَ فِيمَا أُنْزِلَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ عَشْرُ رَضَعَاتٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ يُحَرِّمْنَ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ نُسِخْنَ بِخَمْسٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ فَتُوُفِّيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُنَّ فِيمَا يُقْرَأُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha (Allah be pleased with, her) reported that it had been revealed in the Holy Qur'an that ten clear sucklings make the marriage unlawful, then it was abrogated (and substituted) by five sucklings and Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) died and it was before that time (found) in the Holy Qur'an (and recited by the Muslims)

muslim:3597.literal_translation: Aisha reported that she said: Among what was revealed of the Quran was that ten known sucklings make marriage unlawful; then they were abrogated by five known sucklings, and the Messenger of Allah died while they were still among what was being recited of the Quran.

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَتُوُفِّيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُنَّ فِيمَا يُقْرَأُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) died and it was before that time (found) in the Holy Qur'an (and recited by the Muslims)
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and the Messenger of Allah died while they were still among what was being recited of the Quran
translation_issue.explanation: The translator inserts the unattested phrase 'before that time' to invert the Arabic circumstantial clause (wāw al-ḥāl), obscuring that the verse was still recited when Muhammad died.

muslim:3597.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the recitation of the five-sucklings verse was abrogated shortly before Muhammad's death, or rely on the English translator's unbracketed addition 'before that time' to claim it was no longer recited when he died. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states فَتُوُفِّيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُنَّ فِيمَا يُقْرَأُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ ('and the Messenger of Allah died while they were still among what was being recited of the Quran'), using a circumstantial clause (wāw al-ḥāl) to establish that the five-sucklings verse remained part of the recited Quran at the moment of his death. Since revelation and abrogation ended with Muhammad's death, the subsequent disappearance of a verse that was still being recited when he died contradicts the claim of complete Quranic preservation in [Quran 15:9](quran://15/9).

muslim:2419.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:2419.note: Addressing three hundred Quran reciters of Basra, the Companion Abu Musa al-Ash'ari states that they used to recite two surahs—one comparable in length and severity to Surah Bara'ah ([Quran 9:1](quran://9/1)) and another resembling the *Musabbihat*—before he forgot or was caused to forget them (*fa-unsītuhā*), retaining only the 'two valleys of wealth' verse from the first and an uncanonical continuation to [Quran 61:2](quran://61/2) ('so it is written as a testimony around your necks...') from the second. While classical commentators reconcile the absence of these passages from the canonical text ([Quran 15:9](quran://15/9)) through the doctrine of abrogation of recitation (*naskh al-tilāwah*), parallel reports record other Companions like Ibn Abbas expressing uncertainty over whether the 'two valleys' saying was originally part of the Quran or prophetic speech (muslim:2418, bukhari:6440).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَإِنَّا كُنَّا نَقْرَأُ سُورَةً كُنَّا نُشَبِّهُهَا فِي الطُّولِ وَالشِّدَّةِ بِبَرَاءَةَ فَأُنْسِيتُهَا غَيْرَ أَنِّي قَدْ حَفِظْتُ مِنْهَا لَوْ كَانَ لاِبْنِ آدَمَ وَادِيَانِ مِنْ مَالٍ لاَبْتَغَى وَادِيًا ثَالِثًا وَلاَ يَمْلأُ جَوْفَ ابْنِ آدَمَ إِلاَّ التُّرَابُ ‏.‏ وَكُنَّا نَقْرَأُ سُورَةً كُنَّا نُشَبِّهُهَا بِإِحْدَى الْمُسَبِّحَاتِ فَأُنْسِيتُهَا غَيْرَ أَنِّي حَفِظْتُ مِنْهَا ‏{‏ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِمَ تَقُولُونَ مَا لاَ تَفْعَلُونَ‏}‏ فَتُكْتَبُ شَهَادَةً فِي أَعْنَاقِكُمْ فَتُسْأَلُونَ عَنْهَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: We used to recite a surah which resembled in length and severity to (Surah) Bara'at. I have, however, forgotten it with the exception of this which I remember out of it:" If there were two valleys full of riches, for the son of Adam, he would long for a third valley, and nothing would fill the stomach of the son of Adam but dust." And we used so recite a surah which resembled one of the surahs of Musabbihat, and I have forgotten it, but remember (this much) out of it:" Oh people who believe, why do you say that which you do not practise" (lxi 2.) and" that is recorded in your necks as a witness (against you) and you would be asked about it on the Day of Resurrection" (xvii)

muslim:2419.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that these two entire surahs were not lost through human memory failure, but were divinely abrogated in their recitation (*naskh al-tilāwah*) by Allah during Muhammad's lifetime in accordance with Quran 2:106. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Abu Musa still retained specific verses from both forgotten surahs in his personal memory (*ghayra annī qad ḥafiẓtu minhā* — 'except that I have memorized from it') right after warning the Basran reciters not to let time pass and neglect the Quran, refuting the claim of a uniform supernatural erasure. Furthermore, parallel narrations (`bukhari:6440`, `muslim:2416`) record that senior Companions like Ibn 'Abbas openly admitted they did not know whether the 'two valleys' passage was Quranic revelation or merely a prophetic statement, proving genuine textual confusion and memory loss rather than an official prophetic abrogation.

muslim:1837.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:1837.note: Upon hearing a man reciting the Quran at night, Muhammad declares that the reciter reminded him of multiple verses (*kadhā wa-kadhā āyatan*) that he had dropped (*asqaṭtuhā*) from certain surahs ([Quran 15:9](quran://15/9), [Quran 87:6](quran://87/6); cf. muslim:1838). Classical commentators such as al-Nawawī maintain that Muhammad had already conveyed these verses to his companions and only forgot them during a subsequent recitation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم سَمِعَ رَجُلاً يَقْرَأُ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ يَرْحَمُهُ اللَّهُ لَقَدْ أَذْكَرَنِي كَذَا وَكَذَا آيَةً كُنْتُ أَسْقَطْتُهَا مِنْ سُورَةِ كَذَا وَكَذَا ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard a person reciting the Qur'an at night. Upon this he said:May Allah show mercy to him; he has reminded me of such and such a verse which I had missed in such and such a surah

muslim:1837.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar, that Muhammad only forgot these verses after he had already conveyed (*tablīgh*) them to his Companions, claiming this temporary lapse merely fulfills the exception in [Quran 87:7](quran://87/7) ('except what Allah wills') without threatening the Quran's preservation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *kadhā wa-kadhā āyatan kuntu asqaṭtuhā min sūrati kadhā wa-kadhā* ('such-and-such verses which I had dropped from such-and-such surah')—alongside *kuntu unsītuhā* ('I had been made to forget them') in `muslim:1838`—directly contradicting the divine guarantee in [Quran 87:6](quran://87/6) (*sa-nuqriʾuka fa-lā tansā*, 'We will make you recite, so you will not forget'). If the supreme prophet and final arbiter of the revelation could unwittingly omit multiple verses from multiple surahs until he happened to overhear a reciter at night, the foundational claim of an infallible, divinely safeguarded oral transmission collapses.

bukhari:4977.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:4977.note: Zirr bin Hubaish questions Ubayy bin Ka'b regarding Abdullah ibn Mas'ud's statement (abbreviated in the Arabic text as *kadha wa-kadha*, referring in Bukhari's chapters on *al-Mu'awwidhatayn* and bukhari:4976 to his exclusion of [Surah 113](quran://113/1) and [Surah 114](quran://114/1) from his *mushaf*), to which Ubayy replies that Muhammad told him, "It was said to me, so I said it," and thus Ubayy recites them accordingly. In *Fath al-Bari*, Ibn Hajar affirms the authenticity of the reports that Ibn Mas'ud—whom Muhammad designated as one of the four primary teachers of the Quran (bukhari:4999)—omitted both chapters from his codex, explaining that Ibn Mas'ud considered them revealed protective supplications rather than part of the canonical Quran.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَأَلْتُ أُبَىَّ بْنَ كَعْبٍ قُلْتُ يَا أَبَا الْمُنْذِرِ إِنَّ أَخَاكَ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ يَقُولُ كَذَا وَكَذَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ أُبَىٌّ سَأَلْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ لِي قِيلَ لِي‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ، قَالَ فَنَحْنُ نَقُولُ كَمَا قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I asked Ubai bin Ka`b, "O Abu AlMundhir! Your brother, Ibn Mas`ud said so-and-so (i.e., the two Mu'awwidh-at do not belong to the Qur'an)." Ubai said, "I asked Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) about them, and he said, 'They have been revealed to me, and I have recited them (as a part of the Qur'an)," So Ubai added, "So we say as Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) has said"

bukhari:4977.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—following Ibn Hazm's outright denial or Ibn Hajar's defense in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that reports of Ibn Mas'ud rejecting Surahs 113 and 114 (*al-Mu'awwidhatayn*) are either fabricated or reflect a benign personal opinion (*ijtihād*) that they were merely prophetic supplications (*ta'wīdh*) overruled by Companion consensus (*ijmā'*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Zirr confronted Ubayy bin Ka'b because Ibn Mas'ud was actively teaching this exclusion (`إِنَّ أَخَاكَ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ يَقُولُ كَذَا وَكَذَا`), which Ibn Hajar himself concedes in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* is established via *ṣaḥīḥ* chains in *Musnad Aḥmad* where Ibn Mas'ud physically scraped (*yaḥukku*) both chapters out of his codex (*muṣḥaf*) and declared, 'They are not from the Book of Allah.' This shatters the claim of unbroken *mutawātir* preservation, proving that the foremost Quranic teacher whom Muhammad personally commanded the Ummah to learn the Quran from first (`bukhari:4999`) rejected two entire chapters of the canonical Quran.

muslim:6332.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:6332.note: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud quotes [Quran 3:161](quran://3/161) regarding bringing what one conceals on the Day of Judgment (glossed in the English translation as instructing his companions to conceal their copies of the Quran) and asks by whose mode of recitation he is being commanded to read, stating that he recited over seventy chapters directly to Muhammad and that the Companions know he is the most knowledgeable among them in the Book of Allah. Shaqiq adds that when he sat in the circles of Muhammad's Companions, none of them rejected or found fault with Ibn Mas'ud's statement ([Quran 15:9](quran://15/9)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ ‏{‏ وَمَنْ يَغْلُلْ يَأْتِ بِمَا غَلَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ‏}‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ مَنْ تَأْمُرُونِي أَنْ أَقْرَأَ فَلَقَدْ قَرَأْتُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِضْعًا وَسَبْعِينَ سُورَةً وَلَقَدْ عَلِمَ أَصْحَابُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنِّي أَعْلَمُهُمْ بِكِتَابِ اللَّهِ وَلَوْ أَعْلَمُ أَنَّ أَحَدًا أَعْلَمُ مِنِّي لَرَحَلْتُ إِلَيْهِ ‏.‏ قَالَ شَقِيقٌ فَجَلَسْتُ فِي حَلَقِ أَصْحَابِ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَمَا سَمِعْتُ أَحَدًا يَرُدُّ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِ وَلاَ يَعِيبُهُ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abdullah (b. Mas'ud) reported that he (said to his companions to conceal their copies of the Qur'an) and further said:He who conceals anything he shall have to bring that which he had concealed on the Day of judgment, and then said: After whose mode of recitation you command me to recite? I in fact recited before AIlah's Messenger (ﷺ) more than seventy chapters of the Qur'an and the Companions of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) know it that I have better understanding of the Book of Allah (than they do), and if I were to know that someone had better understanding than I, I would have gone to him. Shaqiq said: I sat in the company of the Companions of Mubkmmad (ﷺ) but I did not hear anyone having rejected that (that is, his recitation) or finding fault with it

muslim:6332.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the standardization of the Quran enjoyed the unanimous consensus of Muhammad's Companions and that Abdullah ibn Mas'ud's protest was merely a temporary hesitation over parting with his personal copy. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Ibn Mas'ud invoked [Quran 3:161](quran://3/161) (`وَمَنْ يَغْلُلْ يَأْتِ بِمَا غَلَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ`) to urge his companions to conceal their copies for the Day of Judgment while challenging the command to abandon a recitation of over seventy chapters learned directly from Muhammad (`عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ مَنْ تَأْمُرُونِي أَنْ أَقْرَأَ فَلَقَدْ قَرَأْتُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِضْعًا وَسَبْعِينَ سُورَةً`). Moreover, Shaqiq testifies that across the circles of Muhammad's Companions, no one rejected or found fault with Ibn Mas'ud's recitation (`فَمَا سَمِعْتُ أَحَدًا يَرُدُّ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِ وَلاَ يَعِيبُهُ`), confirming that a premier authority on the Book of Allah openly defied the order to adopt another man's mode of reading (`bukhari:5000`, `muslim:6333`).

bukhari:4679.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:4679.note: Following heavy casualties at the Battle of Yamama, Umar warns Abu Bakr that much of the Quran will be lost if reciters die on future battlefields, persuading him and Zaid ibn Thabit to undertake a compilation that the Prophet had never done. Zaid collects the Quran from parchments, shoulder blades, date-palm stalks, and men's memories, finding the final two verses of Surah At-Tawbah ([Quran 9:128-129](quran://9/128-129)) with Khuza'ima (or Abu Khuza'ima) al-Ansari and with no one else.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ عُمَرَ أَتَانِي فَقَالَ إِنَّ الْقَتْلَ قَدِ اسْتَحَرَّ يَوْمَ الْيَمَامَةِ بِالنَّاسِ، وَإِنِّي أَخْشَى أَنْ يَسْتَحِرَّ الْقَتْلُ بِالْقُرَّاءِ فِي الْمَوَاطِنِ فَيَذْهَبَ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ، إِلاَّ أَنْ تَجْمَعُوهُ، وَإِنِّي لأَرَى أَنْ تَجْمَعَ الْقُرْآنَ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ قُلْتُ لِعُمَرَ كَيْفَ أَفْعَلُ شَيْئًا لَمْ يَفْعَلْهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ عُمَرُ هُوَ وَاللَّهِ خَيْرٌ‏.‏ فَلَمْ يَزَلْ عُمَرُ يُرَاجِعُنِي فِيهِ حَتَّى شَرَحَ اللَّهُ لِذَلِكَ صَدْرِي، وَرَأَيْتُ الَّذِي رَأَى عُمَرُ‏.‏ قَالَ زَيْدُ بْنُ ثَابِتٍ وَعُمَرُ عِنْدَهُ جَالِسٌ لاَ يَتَكَلَّمُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ إِنَّكَ رَجُلٌ شَابٌّ عَاقِلٌ وَلاَ نَتَّهِمُكَ، كُنْتَ تَكْتُبُ الْوَحْىَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَتَتَبَّعِ الْقُرْآنَ فَاجْمَعْهُ‏.‏ فَوَاللَّهِ لَوْ كَلَّفَنِي نَقْلَ جَبَلٍ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ مَا كَانَ أَثْقَلَ عَلَىَّ مِمَّا أَمَرَنِي بِهِ مِنْ جَمْعِ الْقُرْآنِ قُلْتُ كَيْفَ تَفْعَلاَنِ شَيْئًا لَمْ يَفْعَلْهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ هُوَ وَاللَّهِ خَيْرٌ، فَلَمْ أَزَلْ أُرَاجِعُهُ حَتَّى شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرِي لِلَّذِي شَرَحَ اللَّهُ لَهُ صَدْرَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ وَعُمَرَ، فَقُمْتُ فَتَتَبَّعْتُ الْقُرْآنَ أَجْمَعُهُ مِنَ الرِّقَاعِ وَالأَكْتَافِ وَالْعُسُبِ وَصُدُورِ الرِّجَالِ، حَتَّى وَجَدْتُ مِنْ سُورَةِ التَّوْبَةِ آيَتَيْنِ مَعَ خُزَيْمَةَ الأَنْصَارِيِّ، لَمْ أَجِدْهُمَا مَعَ أَحَدٍ غَيْرِهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: `Umar has come to me and said, The people have suffered heavy casualties on the day of (the battle of) Yamama, and I am afraid that there will be more casualties among the Qurra' (those who know the Qur'an by heart) at other battle-fields, whereby a large part of the Qur'an may be lost, unless you collect it. And I am of the opinion that you should collect the Qur'an." Abu Bakr added, "I said to `Umar, 'How can I do something which Allah's Apostle has not done?' `Umar said (to me), 'By Allah, it is (really) a good thing.' So `Umar kept on pressing, trying to persuade me to accept his proposal, till Allah opened my bosom for it and I had the same opinion as `Umar." (Zaid bin Thabit added:) `Umar was sitting with him (Abu Bakr) and was not speaking to me. "You are a wise young man and we do not suspect you (of telling lies or of forgetfulness): and you used to write the Divine Inspiration for Allah's Messenger (ﷺ). Therefore, look for the Qur'an and collect it (in one manuscript). " By Allah, if he (Abu Bakr) had ordered me to shift one of the mountains (from its place) it would not have been harder for me than what he had ordered me concerning the collection of the Qur'an. I said to both of them, "How dare you do a thing which the Prophet has not done?" Abu Bakr said, "By Allah, it is (really) a good thing. So I kept on arguing with him about it till Allah opened my bosom for that which He had opened the bosoms of Abu Bakr and `Umar. So I started locating Qur'anic material and collecting it from parchments, scapula, leaf-stalks of date palms and from the memories of men (who knew it by heart). I found with Khuza`ima two Verses of Surat-at-Tauba which I had not found with anybody else

bukhari:4679.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that the Quran was already universally memorized (*mutawātir*) and that Zayd ibn Thabit merely meant he did not find the final two verses of Surah At-Tawbah (9:128–129) in *written* form with anyone other than Khuzaymah. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Zayd searched both physical fragments and 'the memories of men' (*wa-ṣudūri al-rijāl*) before declaring unconditionally, 'I did not find them with anyone other than him' (*lam ajidhumā ma'a aḥadin ghayrihi*), with zero restriction to written manuscripts. Moreover, Umar's emergency appeal after the 632 AD Battle of Yamama was driven by his explicit warning that as memorizers (*al-qurrā'*) were killed, 'much of the Quran would be lost' (*fa-yadh-haba kathīrun mina al-Qur'ān*), refuting the claim of independent oral preservation while the Hadith's own transmitters cannot even agree whether the sole witness was Khuzaymah or Abu Khuzaymah.

bukhari:4944.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:4944.note: After Alqamah confirms that Abdullah ibn Mas'ud recited Surat al-Layl as "and by the male and the female" (*wadh-dhakari wal-unthā*), Abu al-Darda testifies that he heard Muhammad recite it the exact same way and swears by Allah that he will not follow those pressing him to recite "and by Him Who created the male and the female" (*wa mā khalaqa adh-dhakara wal-unthā*), the reading now preserved in [Quran 92:3](quran://92/3). Although classical commentators attribute this discrepancy to abrogated recitation (*naskh al-tilāwah*) or the final prophetic review (*al-'arḍah al-akhīrah*), both Ibn Mas'ud and Abu al-Darda maintained the shorter reading after Muhammad's death and explicitly refused to adopt the longer phrasing (cf. bukhari:3742, bukhari:4943).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ أَيُّكُمْ يَقْرَأُ عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ كُلُّنَا‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَيُّكُمْ يَحْفَظُ وَأَشَارُوا إِلَى عَلْقَمَةَ‏.‏ قَالَ كَيْفَ سَمِعْتَهُ يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ عَلْقَمَةُ ‏{‏وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَشْهَدُ أَنِّي سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ هَكَذَا، وَهَؤُلاَءِ يُرِيدُونِي عَلَى أَنْ أَقْرَأَ ‏{‏وَمَا خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أُتَابِعُهُمْ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Then he asked them,: 'Who among you can recite (Qur'an) as `Abdullah recites it?" They replied, "All of us." He asked, "Who among you knows it by heart?" They pointed at 'Alqama. Then he asked Alqama. "How did you hear `Abdullah bin Mas`ud reciting Surat Al-Lail (The Night)?" Alqama recited: 'By the male and the female.' Abu Ad-Darda said, "I testify that I heard me Prophet reciting it likewise, but these people want me to recite it:-- 'And by Him Who created male and female.' but by Allah, I will not follow them

bukhari:4944.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Ibn Mas'ud and Abu al-Darda's shorter recitation of Quran 92:3 (`وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى`, *wadh-dhakari wal-unthā*) was either a permitted dialectal mode (*ḥarf*) or an early reading whose wording was abrogated (*mansūkh al-tilāwah*) during Muhammad's final review with Gabriel (*al-'arḍah al-akhīrah*) before news of the abrogation reached them (as claimed by Ibn Hajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Abu al-Darda—one of the four premier authorities who collected the entire Quran during Muhammad's lifetime (bukhari:5003), confirming Ibn Mas'ud's master recitation (bukhari:3758)—testified (`أَشْهَدُ أَنِّي سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ ... يَقْرَأُ هَكَذَا`) that Muhammad recited the verse without `وَمَا خَلَقَ` (*wa mā khalaqa*), and swore by Allah (`وَاللَّهِ لاَ أُتَابِعُهُمْ`) that he would never follow those pressuring him to adopt the wording now standardized in the Uthmanic Quran. Had both readings been valid *aḥruf* or had the Uthmanic addition been a known prophetic revision, the Prophet's own foremost Quranic teachers in Kufa and Syria would not have independently rejected the today-canonical text of Quran 92:3 and sworn under oath never to recite it.

muslim:1904.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:1904.note: After Ubayy ibn Ka'b heard two men recite the Quran in different ways and Muhammad approved both recitations, Ubayy experienced a sense of denial (*al-takdhīb*) in his soul greater than anything he had felt during the pre-Islamic period of ignorance (*al-Jāhiliyyah*). Seeing his state, Muhammad struck Ubayy's chest—causing him to break out in sweat as though looking at Allah in fear—and explained that he had repeatedly requested leniency for his nation until the Quran's recitation was expanded from one mode (*ḥarf*) to seven ([Quran 15:9](quran://15/9), [Quran 85:21-22](quran://85/21-22)).
