problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ أُبَىِّ بْنِ كَعْبٍ، قَالَ كُنْتُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ فَدَخَلَ رَجُلٌ يُصَلِّي فَقَرَأَ قِرَاءَةً أَنْكَرْتُهَا عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ دَخَلَ آخَرُ فَقَرَأَ قِرَاءَةً سِوَى قِرَاءَةِ صَاحِبِهِ فَلَمَّا قَضَيْنَا الصَّلاَةَ دَخَلْنَا جَمِيعًا عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقُلْتُ إِنَّ هَذَا قَرَأَ قِرَاءَةً أَنْكَرْتُهَا عَلَيْهِ وَدَخَلَ آخَرُ فَقَرَأَ سِوَى قِرَاءَةِ صَاحِبِهِ فَأَمَرَهُمَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَرَءَا فَحَسَّنَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم شَأْنَهُمَا فَسُقِطَ فِي نَفْسِي مِنَ التَّكْذِيبِ وَلاَ إِذْ كُنْتُ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ فَلَمَّا رَأَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مَا قَدْ غَشِيَنِي ضَرَبَ فِي صَدْرِي فَفِضْتُ عَرَقًا وَكَأَنَّمَا أَنْظُرُ إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فَرَقًا فَقَالَ لِي ‏"‏ يَا أُبَىُّ أُرْسِلَ إِلَىَّ أَنِ اقْرَإِ الْقُرْآنَ عَلَى حَرْفٍ فَرَدَدْتُ إِلَيْهِ أَنْ هَوِّنْ عَلَى أُمَّتِي ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Ubayy b. Ka'b reported:I was in the mosque when a man entered and prayed and recited (the Qur'in) in a style to which I objected. Then another man entered (the mosque) and recited in a style different from that of his companion. When we had finished the prayer, we all went to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said to him: This man recited in a style to which I objected, and the other entered and recited in a style different from that of his companion. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked them to recite and so they recited, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) expressed approval of their affairs (their modes of recitation). and there occurred In my mind a sort of denial which did not occur even during the Days of Ignorance. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw how I was affected (by a wrong idea), he struck my chest, whereupon I broke into sweating and felt as though I were looking at Allah with fear. He (the Holy Prophet) said to me: Ubayy. a message was sent to me to recite the Qur'an in one dialect, and I replied: Make (things) easy for my people. It was conveyed to me for the second time that it should be recited in two dialects. I again replied to him: Make affairs easy for my people. It was again conveyed to me for the third time to recite in seven dialects

muslim:1904.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that the seven *aḥruf* (modes) were a divinely revealed concession to accommodate diverse Arab tribal dialects, and that Ubayy bin Ka'b's doubt was merely a fleeting Satanic whisper before he learned of this dispensation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad's foremost Quranic reciter was plunged into a crisis of suspecting falsehood (*suqiṭa fī nafsī min al-takdhīb*) deeper than in his pre-Islamic pagan days (*al-jāhiliyyah*) upon hearing Muhammad validate mutually conflicting recitations (*qirāʾatan siwā qirāʾati ṣāḥibihi*), and rather than demonstrating textual harmony, Muhammad physically struck his chest (*ḍaraba fī ṣadrī*) and claimed he bargained the revelation from one mode into seven. Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:4992) prove these textual clashes occurred between men of the exact same Qurayshi tribe rather than different dialects, and Caliph Uthman later burned the competing codices (bukhari:4987), permanently destroying the very modes Muhammad claimed to have negotiated.

bukhari:4992.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:4992.note: Umar ibn al-Khattab seizes his fellow Qurayshi companion Hisham ibn Hakim by his garment and drags him to Muhammad for reciting Surah Al-Furqan in ways Muhammad had not taught Umar. Muhammad validates both divergent recitations as revealed and declares that the Quran was sent down in seven modes (ahruf), despite both men sharing the same Qurayshi dialect and classical scholars remaining divided over the meaning and survival of these modes after Uthman's standardization.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقُلْتُ إِنِّي سَمِعْتُ هَذَا يَقْرَأُ بِسُورَةِ الْفُرْقَانِ عَلَى حُرُوفٍ لَمْ تُقْرِئْنِيهَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ أَرْسِلْهُ اقْرَأْ يَا هِشَامُ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَرَأَ عَلَيْهِ الْقِرَاءَةَ الَّتِي سَمِعْتُهُ يَقْرَأُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ كَذَلِكَ أُنْزِلَتْ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ اقْرَأْ يَا عُمَرُ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَرَأْتُ الْقِرَاءَةَ الَّتِي أَقْرَأَنِي، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ كَذَلِكَ أُنْزِلَتْ، إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ أُنْزِلَ عَلَى سَبْعَةِ أَحْرُفٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: I heard this person reciting Surat Al-Furqan in a way which you haven't taught me!" On that Allah's Apostle said, "Release him, (O `Umar!) Recite, O Hisham!" Then he recited in the same way as I heard him reciting. Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "It was revealed in this way," and added, "Recite, O `Umar!" I recited it as he had taught me. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) then said, "It was revealed in this way. This Qur'an has been revealed to be recited in seven different ways

bukhari:4992.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the 'seven aḥruf' (sabʿati aḥruf) were merely minor tribal dialects or pronunciation variants granted to accommodate diverse Arab tribes without altering the text, and that they remain preserved in today's canonical qirāʾāt. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Hishām recited 'in many different ways' (ʿalā ḥurūfin kathīratin) completely different from what ʿUmar was taught (ʿalā ghayri mā qaraʾta)—even though, as Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī notes in Fatḥ al-Bārī, both men belonged to the exact same Meccan tribe of Quraysh, proving these were substantive wording divergences rather than tribal accents. Furthermore, because Caliph ʿUthmān later eradicated competing codices by fire (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4987), six of the seven forms Muhammad declared 'revealed in this way' (kadhālika unzilat) were permanently lost, leaving classical scholars with over thirty-five conflicting opinions on what the seven aḥruf even were.

bukhari:5005.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:5005.note: 'Umar states that although Ubayy ibn Ka'b—one of the four primary Quranic teachers endorsed by Muhammad (bukhari:5003)—is the best reciter among the Companions, they still abandon parts of his recitation even though Ubayy insists he learned them directly from Muhammad's mouth and refuses to give them up. 'Umar then cites [Quran 2:106](quran://2/106) to justify omitting those verses on the grounds that they had been abrogated or caused to be forgotten.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ عُمَرُ أُبَىٌّ أَقْرَؤُنَا وَإِنَّا لَنَدَعُ مِنْ لَحَنِ أُبَىٍّ، وَأُبَىٌّ يَقُولُ أَخَذْتُهُ مِنْ فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلاَ أَتْرُكُهُ لِشَىْءٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: `Umar said, Ubai was the best of us in the recitation (of the Qur'an) yet we leave some of what he recites.' Ubai says, 'PI have taken it from the mouth of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and will not leave for anything whatever."

bukhari:5005.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that the passages Ubayy ibn Ka'b insisted on reciting had simply been abrogated in recitation (*mansūkh al-tilāwah*) during Muhammad's final review with Jibril without Ubayy's knowledge, or that `لَحَنِ أُبَىٍّ` (*laḥn Ubayy*) refers merely to dialectical pronunciation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that despite acknowledging Ubayy as the community's foremost Quranic master (`أُبَىٌّ أَقْرَؤُنَا`—whom Muhammad himself commanded Muslims to learn the Quran from in *Sahih al-Bukhari* 4999), 'Umar admits they deliberately discarded parts of his recitation (`وَإِنَّا لَنَدَعُ مِنْ لَحَنِ أُبَىٍّ`, rendered explicitly as `مِنْ قَوْلِ أُبَىٍّ`, "from the words of Ubayy," in parallel narration *Sahih al-Bukhari* 4481). Furthermore, Ubayy flatly rejected 'Umar's appeal to abrogation by testifying, "I took it directly from the mouth of the Messenger of Allah and will not abandon it for anything" (`أَخَذْتُهُ مِنْ فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلاَ أَتْرُكُهُ لِشَىْءٍ`), proving that Muhammad's chief reciter knew of no such cancellation and exposing how the Companions used *naskh* (Surah 2:106) to justify excising prophetic transmissions.

bukhari:5042.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:5042.note: Aisha reports that upon overhearing a man reciting the Quran in the mosque at night, Muhammad declared that the reciter had reminded him of specific verses he had dropped (*asqattuha*) from certain surahs (cf. bukhari:5038). Addressing the tension with [Surah 87:6](quran://87/6), classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar argue that such lapses in memory occurred only after Muhammad had initially conveyed the verses to his companions.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَمِعَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَارِئًا يَقْرَأُ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ يَرْحَمُهُ اللَّهُ لَقَدْ أَذْكَرَنِي كَذَا وَكَذَا آيَةً، أَسْقَطْتُهَا مِنْ سُورَةِ كَذَا وَكَذَا ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) heard a reciter reciting, the Qur'an in the mosque at night. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "May Allah bestow His Mercy on him, as he has remind ed me of such-and-such Verses of such and-such Suras, which I missed

bukhari:5042.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ—that this lapse occurred only after the verses had already been taught to the companions, or that Allah caused a temporary slip merely to legislate the sunnah regarding forgetfulness while Surah 87:6 guaranteed permanent preservation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad confessed, 'أَسْقَطْتُهَا مِنْ سُورَةِ كَذَا وَكَذَا' ('I dropped them from such-and-such Sura')—and in the parallel bukhari:5038, 'أُنْسِيتُهَا' ('I was made to forget them')—proving he had omitted multiple verses across multiple surahs until he happened to overhear a reciter by chance at night. If the primary vessel of revelation could drop verses without realizing it until an accidental reminder, Quranic claims of a supernaturally guarded prophetic memory (Surah 75:17, 87:6) collapse, leaving no guarantee that every other verse Muhammad dropped was fortunate enough to be overheard and restored.

bukhari:7191.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:7191.note: Following the deaths of many Quran reciters at the Battle of al-Yamama, Umar warns that "a large part of the Quran may be lost" (فَيَذْهَبَ قُرْآنٌ كَثِيرٌ), prompting Abu Bakr—after both he and Zaid ibn Thabit initially object that Muhammad never did so—to commission Zaid to gather the Quran from palm stalks, leather, stones, and men's memories. During this compilation, Zaid locates the final verses of [Surah at-Tawbah (9:128–129)](quran://9/128-129) with Khuza'ima or Abu Khuza'ima alone (cf. bukhari:4986); while commentators argue this meant only the written copy was unique to him, the narration's stated premise is that the deaths of memorizers threatened the permanent loss of the Quran.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ عُمَرَ أَتَانِي فَقَالَ إِنَّ الْقَتْلَ قَدِ اسْتَحَرَّ يَوْمَ الْيَمَامَةِ بِقُرَّاءِ الْقُرْآنِ، وَإِنِّي أَخْشَى أَنْ يَسْتَحِرَّ الْقَتْلُ بِقُرَّاءِ الْقُرْآنِ فِي الْمَوَاطِنِ كُلِّهَا، فَيَذْهَبَ قُرْآنٌ كَثِيرٌ، وَإِنِّي أَرَى أَنْ تَأْمُرَ بِجَمْعِ الْقُرْآنِ‏.‏ قُلْتُ كَيْفَ أَفْعَلُ شَيْئًا لَمْ يَفْعَلْهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ عُمَرُ هُوَ وَاللَّهِ خَيْرٌ‏.‏ فَلَمْ يَزَلْ عُمَرُ يُرَاجِعُنِي فِي ذَلِكَ حَتَّى شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرِي لِلَّذِي شَرَحَ لَهُ صَدْرَ عُمَرَ، وَرَأَيْتُ فِي ذَلِكَ الَّذِي رَأَى عُمَرُ‏.‏ قَالَ زَيْدٌ قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ وَإِنَّكَ رَجُلٌ شَابٌّ عَاقِلٌ لاَ نَتَّهِمُكَ، قَدْ كُنْتَ تَكْتُبُ الْوَحْىَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَتَتَبَّعِ الْقُرْآنَ فَاجْمَعْهُ‏.‏ قَالَ زَيْدٌ فَوَاللَّهِ لَوْ كَلَّفَنِي نَقْلَ جَبَلٍ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ مَا كَانَ بِأَثْقَلَ عَلَىَّ مِمَّا كَلَّفَنِي مِنْ جَمْعِ الْقُرْآنِ‏.‏ قُلْتُ كَيْفَ تَفْعَلاَنِ شَيْئًا لَمْ يَفْعَلْهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ هُوَ وَاللَّهِ خَيْرٌ‏.‏ فَلَمْ يَزَلْ يَحُثُّ مُرَاجَعَتِي حَتَّى شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرِي لِلَّذِي شَرَحَ اللَّهُ لَهُ صَدْرَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ وَعُمَرَ، وَرَأَيْتُ فِي ذَلِكَ الَّذِي رَأَيَا، فَتَتَبَّعْتُ الْقُرْآنَ أَجْمَعُهُ مِنَ الْعُسُبِ وَالرِّقَاعِ وَاللِّخَافِ وَصُدُورِ الرِّجَالِ، فَوَجَدْتُ آخِرَ سُورَةِ التَّوْبَةِ ‏{‏لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ‏}‏ إِلَى آخِرِهَا مَعَ خُزَيْمَةَ أَوْ أَبِي خُزَيْمَةَ فَأَلْحَقْتُهَا فِي سُورَتِهَا،
problematic_excerpt.english: `Umar has come to my and said, 'A great number of Qaris of the Holy Qur'an were killed on the day of the battle of Al-Yamama, and I am afraid that the casualties among the Qaris of the Qur'an may increase on other battle-fields whereby a large part of the Qur'an may be lost. Therefore I consider it advisable that you (Abu Bakr) should have the Qur'an collected.' I said, 'How dare I do something which Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) did not do?' `Umar said, By Allah, it is something beneficial.' `Umar kept on pressing me for that till Allah opened my chest for that for which He had opened the chest of `Umar and I had in that matter, the same opinion as `Umar had." Abu Bakr then said to me (Zaid), "You are a wise young man and we do not have any suspicion about you, and you used to write the Divine Inspiration for Allah's Messenger (ﷺ). So you should search for the fragmentary scripts of the Qur'an and collect it (in one Book)." Zaid further said: By Allah, if Abu Bakr had ordered me to shift a mountain among the mountains from one place to another it would not have been heavier for me than this ordering me to collect the Qur'an. Then I said (to `Umar and Abu Bakr), "How can you do something which Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) did not do?" Abu Bakr said, "By Allah, it is something beneficial." Zaid added: So he (Abu Bakr) kept on pressing me for that until Allah opened my chest for that for which He had opened the chests of Abu Bakr and `Umar, and I had in that matter, the same opinion as theirs. So I started compiling the Qur'an by collecting it from the leafless stalks of the date-palm tree and from the pieces of leather and hides and from the stones, and from the chests of men (who had memorized the Qur'an). I found the last verses of Surat-at-Tauba: ("Verily there has come unto you an Apostle (Muhammad) from amongst yourselves--' (9.128-129) ) from Khuza`ima or Abi Khuza`ima and I added to it the rest of the Sura.

bukhari:7191.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that the Quran was already universally memorized (*mutawātir*) and that Zayd ibn Thābit merely lacked a written manuscript for Sūrah al-Tawbah (9:128–129) until finding it with Abū Khuzaymah. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that ʿUmar feared the death of reciters would cause "much of the Quran to be lost" (*fa-yadh-haba qurʾānun kathīrun*) and that Zayd was already collecting from both written scraps and "the chests [memories] of men" (*wa-ṣudūri al-rijāli*) when he located those final verses with a single man—whom the parallel narration (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4986) confirms he "did not find with anyone other than him" (*lam ajidhā maʿa aḥadin ghayrihi*). Furthermore, the narration cannot even definitively identify this sole source—wavering between "Khuzaymah or Abū Khuzaymah" (*maʿa Khuzaymata aw Abī Khuzaymata*)—which proves these verses hung on a single uncertain individual (*khabar al-wāḥid*) rather than mass uninterrupted transmission.

muslim:1916.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:1916.note: Alqama testifies that Abdullah ibn Mas'ud recited [Quran 92:1](quran://92/1) and [Quran 92:3](quran://92/3) as 'By the night when it covers, and the male and the female,' and Abu al-Darda' swears by Allah that he heard Muhammad recite it the exact same way while refusing the Syrian demand to include the phrase 'and what He created' (*wa mā khalaqa*). Despite classical appeals to the seven *ahruf* or abrogation, both Companions maintained this non-Uthmanic wording as the prophetic recitation and rejected the *wa mā khalaqa* reading now standardized in the canonical text ([Quran 92:3](quran://92/3); cf. [Quran 15:9](quran://15/9)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ فَكَيْفَ سَمِعْتَ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ يَقْرَأُ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ وَأَنَا وَاللَّهِ هَكَذَا سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَؤُهَا وَلَكِنْ هَؤُلاَءِ يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ وَمَا خَلَقَ ‏.‏ فَلاَ أُتَابِعُهُمْ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He again said: How did you hear 'Abdullah reciting this verse: (wa'l-lail-i-idha yaghsha = when the night covers)? He ('Alqama) said: I heard him reciting it (like this) (wa'l-lail-i-idha yaghsha) wa-dhakar wal untha = when the night covers and the males and the females). Upon this he said: By Allah, I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting in this way, but they (the Muslims of Syria) desire us to recite: (wa ma khalaqa), but I do not yield to their desire

muslim:1916.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the omission of *wa mā khalaqa* ('and He who created') in Quran 92:3 was merely an earlier variant mode (*ḥarf*) abrogated during Muhammad's final review with Gabriel (*al-'arḍah al-akhīrah*), claiming alongside Al-Nawawī and Ibn Hajar that Ibn Mas'ud and Abu al-Darda' were simply unaware of its abrogation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Abu al-Darda' swore by Allah (*wa-Allāhi hākadhā sami'tu Rasūla Allāhi*) that he heard the Prophet recite the verse without *wa mā khalaqa* and adamantly refused to follow (*fa-lā utābi'uhum*) those pressuring him to add those words. This collapses the abrogation defense, because neither the Syrian Muslims nor any Companion ever cited a final prophetic review to override him, proving that Muhammad's own premier Quran teachers held irreconcilable versions of the text and rejected the standard Uthmanic reading.

bukhari:4988.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:4988.note: Zayd ibn Thabit reports that while copying the Mushaf during Uthman's standardization (bukhari:4987), he discovered that [Quran 33:23](quran://33/23) was missing from the earlier compilation, so the scribes searched for it, found it with a single companion—Khuzaymah ibn Thabit al-Ansari—and appended it to Surah Al-Ahzab in the codex. Although commentators argue that only a written manuscript was missing rather than oral memorization, the report explicitly records that the verse's inclusion in the official text depended on locating it with one individual whose lone testimony Muhammad had declared equal to that of two men (bukhari:2807).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ فَقَدْتُ آيَةً مِنَ الأَحْزَابِ حِينَ نَسَخْنَا الْمُصْحَفَ قَدْ كُنْتُ أَسْمَعُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ بِهَا فَالْتَمَسْنَاهَا فَوَجَدْنَاهَا مَعَ خُزَيْمَةَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ الأَنْصَارِيِّ
problematic_excerpt.english: A verse from Surat Ahzab was missed by me when we copied the Qur'an and I used to hear Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) reciting it. So we searched for it and found it with Khuza`ima bin Thabit Al-Ansari.

bukhari:4988.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the Quran was preserved through unbroken mass-transmitted (*mutawātir*) memorization and, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, claim Zayd ibn Thābit was merely seeking a written parchment to corroborate what he already knew by heart, accepting Khuzaymah's sole copy because Muhammad had declared his testimony equal to two men (*Sahih al-Bukhari* 2807). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *faqadtu āyatan min al-Aḥzāb ḥīna nasakhnā al-muṣḥaf* ("I lost a verse from Al-Ahzab when we copied the *Muṣḥaf*"), proving that this verse had been omitted from Abu Bakr's initial compilation and was only noticed missing decades later during Uthman's recension (c. 650 AD). Because the entire Uthmanic committee had to search for the missing text and found it with only one person (*fa-ltamasnāhā fa-wajadnāhā ma'a Khuzaymah*), the canonical inclusion of Surah Al-Ahzab 33:23 demonstrably rests on a solitary (*āḥād*) report rather than unbroken *mutawātir* preservation.

muslim:1427.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:1427.note: While having Abu Yunus transcribe a personal codex (*muṣḥaf*) of the Quran for her, Aisha dictated [Quran 2:238](quran://2/238) with the additional phrase 'and the afternoon prayer' (*wa-ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr*)—words absent from the standard Uthmanic text that commentators attribute to an abrogation of recitation (*naskh al-tilāwah*)—testifying that she heard the verse recited this way directly from Muhammad ([Quran 15:9](quran://15/9)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَمَرَتْنِي عَائِشَةُ أَنْ أَكْتُبَ لَهَا مُصْحَفًا وَقَالَتْ إِذَا بَلَغْتَ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ فَآذِنِّي ‏{‏ حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَالصَّلاَةِ الْوُسْطَى‏}‏ فَلَمَّا بَلَغْتُهَا آذَنْتُهَا فَأَمْلَتْ عَلَىَّ حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَالصَّلاَةِ الْوُسْطَى وَصَلاَةِ الْعَصْرِ ‏.‏ وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَانِتِينَ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ سَمِعْتُهَا مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Yunus, the freed slave of 'A'isha said:'A'isha ordered me to transcribe a copy of the Qur'an for her and said: When you reach this verse:" Guard the prayers and the middle prayer" (ii. 238), inform me; so when I reached it, I informed her and she gave me dictation (like this): Guard the prayers and the middle prayer and the afternoon prayer, and stand up truly obedient to Allah. 'A'isha said: This is how I have heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)

muslim:1427.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists, citing Al-Nawawi's *Sharh Sahih Muslim*, typically argue that the phrase 'and the afternoon prayer' (*wa-salat al-'asr*) was merely an explanatory gloss (*qira'ah tafsiriyyah*) or an abrogated recitation (*mansukh al-tilawah*) that was cancelled during Muhammad's lifetime. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that long after Muhammad's death, Aisha ordered a formal Quranic codex to be transcribed (*an aktuba laha mushafan*) and dictated those exact words directly into the middle of the verse (*fa-amlat 'alayya... wa-salati l-'asri wa-qumu lillahi qanitina*) on the authority that she 'heard it from the Messenger of Allah' (*sami'tuha min rasuli llah*). Furthermore, the conjunctive 'and' (*waw al-'atf*) in *wa-salati l-'asr* grammatically embeds the phrase as part of the recited scripture rather than a marginal comment, proving that Muhammad's own wife rejected its alleged abrogation and preserved a Quranic reading missing from today's Uthmanic text.

bukhari:4943.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:4943.note: Alqama and Abu al-Darda attest that both Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Muhammad recited [Quran 92:3](quran://92/3) as 'and by the male and the female' (*wa-dh-dhakari wal-unthā*), omitting the phrase 'and by Him Who created' (*wa mā khalaqa*) present in the standardized Uthmanic text (cf. bukhari:4944). Although the English translation interpolates '(Him Who created)' in brackets, the Arabic text omits those words, leading classical commentators to classify this authenticated prophetic reading as abrogated in recitation (*mansūkh al-tilāwah*) or non-canonical (*shādhdh*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَرَأْتُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَنْتَ سَمِعْتَهَا مِنْ فِي صَاحِبِكَ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ وَأَنَا سَمِعْتُهَا مِنْ فِي النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهَؤُلاَءِ يَأْبَوْنَ عَلَيْنَا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: so I recited the verse:-- 'By the night as it envelops 'By the day as it appears in brightness; By (Him Who created) male and the female.' (92.1-3) Abu Ad-Darda' then said to me, "Did you hear it (like this) from the mouth of your friend (`Abdullah bin Mas`ud)?" I said, "Yes." He said, "I too, heard it (like this) from the mouth of the Prophet, but these people do not consider this recitation as the correct one

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
translation_issue.published_rendering: By (Him Who created) male and the female.
translation_issue.literal_meaning: And by the male and the female.
translation_issue.explanation: The Arabic text explicitly records the variant recitation 'wa-dh-dhakari wal-unthā' ('And by the male and the female'), which lacks the Uthmanic phrase 'wa mā khalaqa' ('and Him Who created'). The translator interpolates '(Him Who created)' in parentheses from the standard Uthmanic text of Quran 92:3 directly into the variant, obscuring the exact textual discrepancy that the hadith was narrated to highlight.

bukhari:4943.literal_translation: So I recited: 'By the night when it covers, and by the day when it shines in brightness, and by the male and the female.' He said: 'Did you hear it from the mouth of your companion?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And I too heard it from the mouth of the Prophet (peace be upon him), yet these people refuse us [this recitation].'
bukhari:4943.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue (citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*) that the omission of *wa mā khalaqa* ('and by Him Who created') in Quran 92:3 was merely an abrogated reading (*mansūkh al-tilāwah*) cancelled during the Prophet's final review (*al-'arḍah al-akhīrah*), or an isolated (*shādhdh*) variant superseded by the Uthmanic codex. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that two of Muhammad's foremost Quranic authorities—Ibn Mas'ud and Abu al-Darda—both testified long after Muhammad's death, 'I heard it like this from the mouth of the Prophet' (*sami'tuhā min fī al-nabī*), with Abu al-Darda lamenting that the Syrians 'refuse to accept it from us' (*wa-hā'ulā'i ya'bawna 'alaynā*) and nearly coerced him into abandoning what he heard directly from Muhammad (`bukhari:3742`, `bukhari:4944`). This proves that the Uthmanic standardization forcibly suppressed authentic, non-abrogated Prophetic recitations preserved by the very companions from whom Muhammad commanded Muslims to learn the Quran (`bukhari:4999`).

bukhari:7462.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:7462.note: Ibn Mas'ud transmits [Quran 17:85](quran://17/85) with the non-Uthmanic consonantal variant *wa-mā ūtū* ("and they were not given [of knowledge]") instead of the standardized Uthmanic reading *wa-mā ūtītum* ("and you were not given"), with the Kufan narrator al-A'mash explicitly stating, "Thus it is in our recitation." The published English translation alters the pronoun to conform to the standard Uthmanic text and omits al-A'mash's testimony regarding the variant reading.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ ‏{‏وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الرُّوحِ قُلِ الرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي وَمَا أُوتُوا مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ الأَعْمَشُ هَكَذَا فِي قِرِاءَتِنَا
problematic_excerpt.english: Then he said: "They ask you concerning the Spirit, Say: The Spirit; its knowledge is with my Lord. And of knowledge you (mankind) have been given only a little" [omitted from the original translation: Al-A'mash said: "Thus it is in our reading."]

bukhari:7462.literal_translation: Then he said: {They ask you concerning the Spirit, Say: The Spirit is from the command of my Lord, and they have not been given of knowledge except a little}. Al-A'mash said: 'Thus it is in our recitation.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَمَا أُوتُوا مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً. قَالَ الأَعْمَشُ هَكَذَا فِي قِرِاءَتِنَا
translation_issue.published_rendering: And of knowledge you (mankind) have been given only a little
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and they have not been given of knowledge except a little. Al-A'mash said: 'Thus it is in our recitation.'
translation_issue.explanation: The translator conformed the verse to the standard Uthmanic text ('you' instead of 'they') and omitted the narrator's explicit admission of a variant reading to conceal early Quranic textual variants.

bukhari:7462.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Ibn Mas'ud's reading of Quran 17:85 was merely a personal explanatory gloss (qira'ah tafsiriyyah) or one of the seven ahruf (modes) lawfully superseded by Uthman's standardized codex. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states وَمَا أُوتُوا مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً ('and they have not been given of knowledge except a little')—directly contradicting the consonantal skeleton (rasm) of the Uthmanic Quran (وَمَا أُوتِيتُمْ, 'and you have not been given')—followed by the Kufan transmitter Al-A'mash affirming هَكَذَا فِي قِرِاءَتِنَا ('thus it is in our recitation'). This proves that generations after Uthman burned competing manuscripts, Kufan scholars still actively recited a variant Quranic text with different consonants and theological scope, an admission so damaging that the English translator silently overwrote the text with the modern reading and deleted Al-A'mash's statement entirely.

muslim:2418.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:2418.note: After transmitting Muhammad's statement about the son of Adam longing for a second valley of riches, Ibn Abbas states that he does not know whether the passage is from the Quran or not, with Zuhair's variant recording the same uncertainty without explicitly naming Ibn Abbas as its speaker (cf. [Quran 15:9](quran://15/9)). Because parallel reports (such as muslim:2419 and bukhari:6438) identify this text as formerly recited revelation, classical commentators explain the uncertainty by classifying it as a verse whose Quranic recitation was abrogated (naskh al-tilawah).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ لَوْ أَنَّ لاِبْنِ آدَمَ مِلْءَ وَادٍ مَالاً لأَحَبَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ إِلَيْهِ مِثْلُهُ وَلاَ يَمْلأُ نَفْسَ ابْنِ آدَمَ إِلاَّ التُّرَابُ وَاللَّهُ يَتُوبُ عَلَى مَنْ تَابَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَمِنَ الْقُرْآنِ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ ‏.‏ وَفِي رِوَايَةِ زُهَيْرٍ قَالَ فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَمِنَ الْقُرْآنِ ‏.‏ لَمْ يَذْكُرِ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Ibn Abbas reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:If there were for the son of Adam a valley full of riches, he would long to possess another one like it. and Ibn Adam does not feel satiated but with dust. And Allah returns to him who returns (to Him). Ibn Abbas said: I do not know whether it is from the Qur'an or not; and in the narration transmitted by Zuhair it was said: I do not know whether it is from the Qur'an, and he made no mention of Ibn Abbas

muslim:2418.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar—that this passage was a revelation whose recitation was later abrogated (*naskh al-tilāwah*), claiming that Ibn ʿAbbās simply had not yet been informed of its abrogation when he made this remark. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Ibn ʿAbbās—universally revered in Sunni Islam as the premier interpreter of the Quran (*Turjumān al-Qur'ān*)—flatly confessed, "I do not know whether it is from the Qur'an or not" (`فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَمِنَ الْقُرْآنِ هُوَ أَمْ لاَ`). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (muslim:2416, muslim:2419, bukhari:6438) confirm that other senior Quranic authorities like Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī continued to treat it as part of the Quran after Muhammad's death, proving that the Prophet's own inner circle could not even agree on which texts belonged in the Quran.

muslim:508.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:508.note: Ibn Abbas and al-A'mash recite two revealed Quranic readings absent from the standardized Uthmanic text: the additional clause *wa-rahṭaka minhum al-mukhlaṣīn* ('and your group of sincere ones among them') in [Quran 26:214](quran://26/214) and the variant *wa-qad tabb* ('and he has indeed perished', rather than *wa-tabb*) in [Quran 111:1](quran://111/1) ([Quran 15:9](quran://15/9)). Classical commentators such as al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar identify both variants as readings from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud's codex, reconciling their absence from the canonical text as abrogated recitation (*naskh al-tilāwah*) or anomalous (*shādhdh*) Companion readings.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَمَّا نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ ‏{‏ وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الأَقْرَبِينَ‏}‏ وَرَهْطَكَ مِنْهُمُ الْمُخْلَصِينَ ‏.‏ خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى صَعِدَ الصَّفَا فَهَتَفَ ‏"‏ يَا صَبَاحَاهْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالُوا مَنْ هَذَا الَّذِي يَهْتِفُ قَالُوا مُحَمَّدٌ ‏.‏ فَاجْتَمَعُوا إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا بَنِي فُلاَنٍ يَا بَنِي فُلاَنٍ يَا بَنِي فُلاَنٍ يَا بَنِي عَبْدِ مَنَافٍ يَا بَنِي عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ ‏"‏ فَاجْتَمَعُوا إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ لَوْ أَخْبَرْتُكُمْ أَنَّ خَيْلاً تَخْرُجُ بِسَفْحِ هَذَا الْجَبَلِ أَكُنْتُمْ مُصَدِّقِيَّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا مَا جَرَّبْنَا عَلَيْكَ كَذِبًا ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِنِّي نَذِيرٌ لَكُمْ بَيْنَ يَدَىْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَالَ أَبُو لَهَبٍ تَبًّا لَكَ أَمَا جَمَعْتَنَا إِلاَّ لِهَذَا ثُمَّ قَامَ فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ السُّورَةُ تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَقَدْ تَبَّ ‏.‏ كَذَا قَرَأَ الأَعْمَشُ إِلَى آخِرِ السُّورَةِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: when this verse was revealed:" And warn thy nearest kindred" (and thy group of selected people among them) the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set off till he climbed Safa' and called loudly: Be on your guard! They said: Who is it calling aloud? They said: Muhammad. They gathered round him, and he said: O sons of so and so, O sons of so and so, O sons of 'Abd Manaf, O sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib, and they gathered around him. He (the Apostle) said: If I were to inform you that there were horsemen emerging out of the foot of this mountain, would you believe me? They said: We have not experienced any lie from you. He said: Well, I am a warner to you before a severe torment. He (the narrator) said that Abu Lahab then said: Destruction to you! Is it for this you have gathered us? He (the Holy Prophet) then stood up, and this verse was revealed:" Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and he indeed perished" (cxi. 1). A'mash recited this to the end of the Sura

muslim:508.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that the extra clause in Quran 26:214 and the wording variant in Quran 111:1 were merely explanatory glosses (*qirāʾah tafsīriyyah*) or readings whose recitation was abrogated (*mansūkh al-tilāwah*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the additional clause came down as part of the revealed verse itself (*lammā nazalat hādhihi al-āyah: wa-andhir ʿashīrataka al-aqrabīn wa-rahṭaka minhum al-mukhlaṣīn*) and records that the Kufan master al-Aʿmash actively recited *wa-qad tabb* as part of the Surah (*kadhā qaraʾa al-Aʿmash ilā ākhir al-sūrah*). Because Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, and their Kufan successors continued reciting these non-Uthmanic readings as binding scripture generations after Muhammad's death, this narration proves that early prophetic codices preserved divergent Quranic wording rather than mere commentary or abrogated drafts.

muslim:1838.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:1838.note: After listening to a man reciting the Quran in the mosque, Muhammad states that the reciter reminded him of a verse he had been made to forget (*unsītuhā*), which parallel accounts report he had dropped (*asqaṭtuhā*) from a surah (bukhari:5038, muslim:1837; cf. [Quran 15:9](quran://15/9), [Quran 87:6](quran://87/6)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَتْ كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَسْتَمِعُ قِرَاءَةَ رَجُلٍ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ لَقَدْ أَذْكَرَنِي آيَةً كُنْتُ أُنْسِيتُهَا ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) listened to the recitation of the Qur'an by a man in the mosque. Thereupon he said:May Allah have mercy upon him; be reminded me of the verse which I had been made to forget

muslim:1838.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Quran 87:6–7 ('We will make you recite, so you will not forget, except what Allah wills')—as explained in Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—permits either the purposeful abrogation of verses or a momentary human lapse after the revelation had already been safely memorized by the Companions. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *kuntu unsītuhā* ('I had been made to forget it'), and its immediate parallel narration (`muslim:1837`, cf. `bukhari:5038`) adds *asqaṭtuhā min sūrati kadhā wa-kadhā* ('which I had dropped from such-and-such Surah'). This proves the verse was neither abrogated nor securely retained by the Prophet, who inadvertently omitted active scripture from a Surah and only recovered it by chance upon overhearing an ordinary worshipper in the mosque.

bukhari:7550.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:7550.note: After Umar ibn al-Khattab drags his fellow Qurayshi tribesman Hisham ibn Hakim by his cloak to Muhammad over numerous differing readings (huruf) in his recitation of Surah al-Furqan, Muhammad validates both conflicting recitations and declares that the Quran was revealed in seven modes (sab'atu ahruf). Because both men belonged to the same Quraysh tribe, their textual divergences were not merely regional tribal dialects, and Uthman later burned all competing codices to enforce a single standardized text (bukhari:4987).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنِّي سَمِعْتُ هَذَا يَقْرَأُ سُورَةَ الْفُرْقَانِ عَلَى حُرُوفٍ لَمْ تُقْرِئْنِيهَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَرْسِلْهُ، اقْرَأْ يَا هِشَامُ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَرَأَ الْقِرَاءَةَ الَّتِي سَمِعْتُهُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ كَذَلِكَ أُنْزِلَتْ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ اقْرَأْ يَا عُمَرُ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَرَأْتُ الَّتِي أَقْرَأَنِي فَقَالَ ‏"‏ كَذَلِكَ أُنْزِلَتْ، إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ أُنْزِلَ عَلَى سَبْعَةِ أَحْرُفٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: I have heard this man reciting Surat-al- Furqan in a way that you have not taught me." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "(O `Umar) release him! Recite, O Hisham." Hisham recited in the way I heard him reciting. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "It was revealed like this." Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Recite, O `Umar!" I recited in the way he had taught me, whereupon he said, "It was revealed like this," and added, "The Qur'an has been revealed to be recited in seven different ways

bukhari:7550.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the 'seven aḥruf' (sabʿatu aḥruf) merely represent seven regional Arab dialects or minor phonetic pronunciations authorized to ease recitation for diverse tribes without altering the actual words. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Hishām recited 'upon many readings' (ʿalā ḥurūfin kathīratin) so substantially different that ʿUmar accused him of lying (kadhabta) and dragged him by his cloak, even though both men belonged to the exact same Meccan tribe of Quraysh and spoke the identical dialect—a fact Ibn Ḥajar highlights in Fatḥ al-Bārī to refute the dialect excuse. Furthermore, Ibn Ḥajar admits that Sunni scholars fractured into roughly thirty-five conflicting guesses over what the seven aḥruf even meant, and because Caliph ʿUthmān later burned all competing codices (Bukhārī 4987), six of these seven divinely revealed forms of the Quran were permanently lost.

muslim:1545.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:1545.note: Anas ibn Malik states that Allah revealed a Quranic verse regarding the Companions killed at Bi'r Ma'una—'Convey to our people the tidings that we have met our Lord, and He was pleased with us and we were pleased with Him'—which the Muslims recited as part of the Quran until its wording was later abrogated (*naskh al-tilawah*) and omitted from the canonical text (cf. [Quran 2:106](quran://2/106), [Quran 15:9](quran://15/9)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ أَنَسٌ أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِي الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا بِبِئْرِ مَعُونَةَ قُرْآنًا قَرَأْنَاهُ حَتَّى نُسِخَ بَعْدُ أَنْ بَلِّغُوا قَوْمَنَا أَنْ قَدْ لَقِينَا رَبَّنَا فَرَضِيَ عَنَّا وَرَضِينَا عَنْهُ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Anas said:Allah the Exalted and Great revealed (a verse) regarding those who were killed at Bi'r Ma'una, and we recited it, till it was abrogated later on (and the verse was like this):, convey to it our people the tidings that we have met our Lord, and He was pleased with us and we were pleased with Him

muslim:1545.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*), that this passage was either a non-canonical *ḥadīth qudsī* or an intentional case of 'abrogation of recitation' (*naskh al-tilāwah*) enacted by divine decree during Muhammad's lifetime rather than textual loss. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah revealed 'a Quran that we recited until it was abrogated later' (*qur'ānan qara'nāhu ḥattā nusikha ba'du*)—categorically refuting the *ḥadīth qudsī* deflection—and because the verse is a purely historical announcement containing no legal ruling (*ḥukm*) to supersede, invoking *naskh al-tilāwah* exposes recitation-abrogation as an ad-hoc theological device invented to rationalize missing scripture in direct tension with the doctrine of an eternally preserved tablet ([Quran 15:9](quran://15/9), [85:21-22](quran://85/21-22)).

bukhari:3742.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:3742.note: After Alqama recites Abdullah ibn Mas'ud's reading of Surah al-Layl as 'and by the male and the female'—omitting the phrase 'and He who created' (*wa ma khalaqa*) present in the canonical Uthmanic text ([Quran 92:3](quran://92/3))—Abu al-Darda swears by Allah that Muhammad taught him to recite it that exact way 'from his mouth to my mouth.' Although classical commentators attribute this consonantal variant to abrogated *ahruf* from the final review (*al-'ardah al-akhirah*), both senior Quranic companions continued to uphold this reading after Muhammad's death on the basis of direct oral instruction from the Prophet (bukhari:3743, bukhari:4944).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ قَالَ كَيْفَ يَقْرَأُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏، فَقَرَأْتُ عَلَيْهِ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ أَقْرَأَنِيهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ فِيهِ إِلَى فِيَّ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Darda further asked, "How does `Abdullah (bin Mas`ud) recite the Sura starting with, 'By the Night as it conceals (the light)." (92.1) Then I recited before him: 'By the Night as it envelops: And by the Day as it appears in brightness; And by male and female.' (91.1-3) On this Abu Ad-Darda' said, "By Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) made me recite the Sura in this way while I was listening to him (reciting it)" [omitted from the original translation: from his mouth to my mouth]

bukhari:3742.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that omitting *wa mā khalaqa* in Surah 92:3—as explained in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's commentary—was either a temporary *aḥruf* dialectal allowance or an abrogated recitation (*mansūkh al-tilāwah*) superseded in Muhammad's final review with Gabriel, rendering Ibn Mas'ūd and Abū al-Dardā's reading anomalous (*shādhdh*) against the *mutawātir* Uthmanic consensus. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Abū al-Dardā' swore by Allah (*wa-Allāhi laqad aqrā'anīhā Rasūlu Allāhi... min fīhi ilā fiyya*) long after Muhammad's death that the Prophet personally taught him this exact wording "from his mouth to my mouth," while parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:4944) record him actively resisting the Syrians' attempts to make him adopt the canonical wording. When two of the four master reciters from whom Muhammad explicitly commanded Muslims to learn the Quran (bukhari:3808) knew nothing of any abrogation and testified under oath that the standardized text altered what came directly from the Prophet's mouth, the claim of unbroken Quranic preservation collapses.

bukhari:3743.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:3743.note: Upon confirming with Alqama that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited [Quran 92:1-3](quran://92/1-3) as 'And by the male and the female' (*wa al-dhakari wa al-untha*), Abu al-Darda states that the people of Sham nearly succeeded in pressuring him to abandon this reading, which he had heard directly from Muhammad. Although classical commentators attribute the absence of 'And by He who created' (*wa ma khalaqa*) found in the canonical Uthmanic text ([Quran 92:3](quran://92/3)) to the seven *ahruf* or abrogated recitation (*naskh al-tilawah*), both senior Companions upheld the shorter wording as the authentic prophetic transmission (bukhari:4944).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى‏}‏ قُلْتُ ‏{‏وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ مَا زَالَ بِي هَؤُلاَءِ حَتَّى كَادُوا يَسْتَنْزِلُونِي عَنْ شَىْءٍ سَمِعْتُهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Then Abu Ad-Darda asked, "How (Abdullah bin Masud) used to recite the Sura starting with: "By the night as it envelopes; By the day as it appears in brightness?" (92.1-2). Alqama said "And by male and female." Abu Ad-Darda then said, "These people (of Sham) tried hard to make me accept something other than what I had heard from the Prophet [omitted from the original translation: (ﷺ).]"

bukhari:3743.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) and Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) claim, omitting *wa mā khalaqa* ('and He Who created') in Quran 92:3 was merely an irregular (*shādhdh*) recitation from one of the seven *aḥruf* that was abrogated during the Prophet's final review (*al-'Arḍah al-Akhīrah*) prior to the Uthmanic standardization. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Abu al-Darda—one of the elite Companions who compiled the Quran during Muhammad's lifetime (`bukhari:5003`)—testified long after the Prophet's death that `{وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى}` was the exact wording he heard directly from the Prophet's mouth (*شَىْءٍ سَمِعْتُهُ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ*), and in the parallel narration (`bukhari:4944`) he flatly refuses to adopt the Uthmanic addition of *wa mā khalaqa*. That two of Islam's foremost Quranic masters in Kufa (Ibn Mas'ud) and Damascus (Abu al-Darda) independently rejected the canonical wording as a deviation from prophetic teaching collapses the claim of an unbroken, *mutawātir* consensus behind today's Uthmanic text.

bukhari:3761.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:3761.note: Abu al-Darda testifies that Muhammad personally taught him to recite [Quran 92:3](quran://92/3) mouth-to-mouth as 'and by male and female' (*wa adh-dhakari wal-unthā*), matching the reading of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud while omitting the phrase *wa mā khalaqa* ('and He who created') found in the standardized Uthmanic text, despite the people of Sham pressuring him to abandon it. Classical commentators classify this prophetically taught recitation as abrogated or non-canonical (*shadhdh*) because it diverges from the Uthmanic codex.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَيْفَ قَرَأَ ابْنُ أُمِّ عَبْدٍ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ‏}‏ فَقَرَأْتُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَقْرَأَنِيهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَاهُ إِلَى فِيَّ، فَمَا زَالَ هَؤُلاَءِ حَتَّى كَادُوا يَرُدُّونِي‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: How did Ibn Um `Abd (i.e. `Abdullah bin Mas`ud) use to recite Surat-al-lail (the Night:92)?" I recited:-- "By the Night as it envelops By the Day as it appears in brightness. And by male and female." (92.1- 3) On that, Abu Darda said, "By Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) made me read the Verse in this way after listening to him, but these people (of Sham) tried their best to let me say something different

bukhari:3761.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Ibn Mas'ud and Abu al-Darda's reading (*wa adh-dhakari wal-unthā*) was one of the Seven *Aḥruf* whose recitation was abrogated during the Prophet's final review with Gabriel (*al-'arḍah al-akhīrah*), leaving their variant as a non-canonical (*shādhdh*) reading superseded by the standardized Uthmanic consensus. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Prophet taught this exact wording directly to Abu al-Darda "mouth to mouth" (*fāhu ilā fiyya*, فَاهُ إِلَى فِيَّ), and that both he and Ibn Mas'ud—whom Muhammad personally designated as one of the four premier masters from whom to learn the Quran—fiercely defended it as the authentic prophetic text against the people of Sham who pressured him to abandon it (*ḥattā kādū yaruddūnī*, حَتَّى كَادُوا يَرُدُّونِي) long after the Prophet's death. Claiming that Muhammad's foremost Quranic authorities were ignorant of the final text and spent decades reciting an abrogated verse proves that the Uthmanic standardization suppressed direct prophetic transmission rather than preserving an unbroken, unanimous revelation.

bukhari:6278.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:6278.note: In Syria, 'Alqama confirms to Abu al-Darda that 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud recited Surah al-Layl as "wadh-dhakari wal-unthā" ("and by the male and the female"), prompting Abu al-Darda to state that the locals persisted in arguing with him over this reading until they nearly made him doubt even though he heard it directly from Muhammad. Both senior Companions thus attest that Muhammad recited the verse without the words "wa-mā khalaqa" ("and that which created") present in the standardized Uthmanic text of [Quran 92:3](quran://92/3) (cf. bukhari:4944).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَيْفَ كَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ ‏{‏وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ مَا زَالَ هَؤُلاَءِ حَتَّى كَادُوا يُشَكِّكُونِي، وَقَدْ سَمِعْتُهَا مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: How did Ibn Mas`ud use to recite 'By the night as it conceals (the light)?" (Sura 92). 'Alqama said, "Wadhdhakari Wal Untha' (And by male and female.") Abu Ad-Darda added. 'These people continued to argue with me regarding it till they were about to cause me to have doubts although I heard it from Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)

bukhari:6278.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that the shorter reading *'wadh-dhakari wal-unthā'* (omitting *'wa mā khalaqa'*) was either an explanatory gloss (*qirā'ah tafsīriyyah*) or a reading from the Seven *Aḥruf* that was abrogated during the Prophet's final review (*al-'arḍah al-akhīrah*) without Ibn Mas'ud or Abu al-Darda knowing. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Abu al-Darda recited it as the verbatim Quranic text he heard directly from the Prophet's own mouth (`وَقَدْ سَمِعْتُهَا مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ`) and steadfastly resisted the Syrians who pressured him to accept the Uthmanic wording (`مَا زَالَ هَؤُلاَءِ حَتَّى كَادُوا يُشَكِّكُونِي`). Since Muhammad explicitly commanded Muslims to learn the Quran from both Ibn Mas'ud and Abu al-Darda's circle (`bukhari:4999`), the excuse that the Prophet's premier Quranic masters in Kufa and Damascus were both ignorant of the final Quranic text exposes the Uthmanic standardization as a post-prophetic textual revision rather than unbroken preservation.

bukhari:2807.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:2807.note: While copying the written sheets into the Quranic codices, Zaid bin Thabit reports that he was missing [Surah Al-Ahzab 33:23](quran://33/23), which he used to hear Muhammad recite. He could not find the verse with anyone except a single man, Khuzaymah bin Thabit al-Ansari, whose testimony Muhammad had declared equal to that of two men (cf. bukhari:4784, bukhari:4986).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَفَقَدْتُ آيَةً مِنْ سُورَةِ الأَحْزَابِ، كُنْتُ أَسْمَعُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ بِهَا، فَلَمْ أَجِدْهَا إِلاَّ مَعَ خُزَيْمَةَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ الأَنْصَارِيِّ
problematic_excerpt.english: one of the Verses of Surat Al-Ahzab was missing which I used to hear Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) reciting. I could not find it except with Khuza`ima bin Thabit Al-Ansari

bukhari:2807.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as Ibn Hajar claims in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, the Quran was infallibly preserved through mass oral memorization (*tawātur*) and Zayd ibn Thābit merely lacked a written manuscript for Surah Al-Ahzab 33:23 to satisfy a procedural two-witness rule. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Zayd discovered the missing verse only when copying the earlier manuscripts into the Uthmanic codices (*nasakhtu al-ṣuḥufa fī al-maṣāḥif fa-faqadtu āyatan*), proving that the initial official compilation (*ṣuḥuf*) under Abu Bakr omitted this verse for years. Furthermore, Zayd's admission that he found it solely with one man (*fa-lam ajidhā illā maʿa Khuzaymah*) and had to invoke a legal exception equating Khuzaymah's lone testimony to two men (*shahādatahu shahādata rajulayn*) collapses the doctrine of unbroken *mutawātir* transmission by reducing a canonical Quranic verse to a solitary report (*āḥād*).

bukhari:4049.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:4049.note: Chief compiler Zaid ibn Thabit states that while copying the Quranic codex (*mushaf*), he missed [Surah 33:23](quran://33/23)—a verse he used to hear Muhammad recite—and after searching, found it only with Khuzaymah ibn Thabit al-Ansari before appending it to its chapter. Even when classical commentators interpret "missing" as referring strictly to written parchments, the report establishes that the initial compilation lacked the verse and that its canonical inclusion relied on a single individual's testimony rather than uninterrupted mass transmission (*mutawatir*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَدْتُ آيَةً مِنَ الأَحْزَابِ حِينَ نَسَخْنَا الْمُصْحَفَ، كُنْتُ أَسْمَعُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ بِهَا، فَالْتَمَسْنَاهَا فَوَجَدْنَاهَا مَعَ خُزَيْمَةَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ الأَنْصَارِيِّ
problematic_excerpt.english: When we wrote the Holy Qur'an, I missed one of the Verses of Surat-al-Ahzab which I used to hear Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) reciting. Then we searched for it and found it with Khuza`ima bin Thabit Al-Ansari.

bukhari:4049.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that Zaid bin Thabit and the Companions already had Surah Al-Ahzab 33:23 memorized, and that "missing" it merely meant he was looking for a written parchment to satisfy a procedural two-witness rule. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `فَقَدْتُ آيَةً مِنَ الأَحْزَابِ حِينَ نَسَخْنَا الْمُصْحَفَ... فَالْتَمَسْنَاهَا فَوَجَدْنَاهَا مَعَ خُزَيْمَةَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ` ("I lost a verse from Al-Ahzab when we copied the Mushaf... so we searched for it and found it with Khuza'ima bin Thabit"), while parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:4986`–`4987`) confirm that Zaid searched both written fragments and "the memories of men" (`وَصُدُورِ الرِّجَالِ`) yet found missing verses with no one else (`لَمْ أَجِدْهَا مَعَ أَحَدٍ غَيْرِهِ`). Furthermore, because this occurred during Uthman's later copying of the codices, it proves that Abu Bakr's original Mushaf omitted Q 33:23 for years and that the Quranic text relied on single-person (*āḥād*) recovery rather than universal (*mutawātir*) transmission.

bukhari:4784.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:4784.note: Zaid ibn Thabit reports that while copying the compiled Quranic sheets (suhuf) into the official codices (masahif), he was missing [Surah al-Ahzab 33:23](quran://33/23) and could not find it with anyone except a single Companion, Khuza'ima al-Ansari. To validate the verse's inclusion, Zaid relied on Muhammad's prior ruling that Khuza'ima's solitary testimony equaled that of two men (see also bukhari:2807, bukhari:4986).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لَمَّا نَسَخْنَا الصُّحُفَ فِي الْمَصَاحِفِ فَقَدْتُ آيَةً مِنْ سُورَةِ الأَحْزَابِ، كُنْتُ أَسْمَعُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَؤُهَا، لَمْ أَجِدْهَا مَعَ أَحَدٍ إِلاَّ مَعَ خُزَيْمَةَ الأَنْصَارِيِّ
problematic_excerpt.english: When we collected the fragmentary manuscripts of the Qur'an into copies, I missed one of the Verses of Surat al-Ahzab which I used to hear Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) reading. Finally I did not find it with anybody except Khuza`ima Al-Ansari

bukhari:4784.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as claimed in Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī, Surah 33:23 was already widely memorized by the masses (mutawātir) and Zaid ibn Thabit merely lacked a written copy to satisfy a strict two-witness procedural rule. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Zaid lost the verse (faqadtu āyatan) while copying Abu Bakr's compilation into Uthman's codices (lammā nasakhnā al-ṣuḥuf fī al-maṣāḥif) and 'did not find it with anyone except Khuzaymah al-Ansari' (lam ajidhā ma'a aḥadin illā ma'a Khuzaymata al-Anṣārī), proving the verse was completely missing from the first official Quranic codex for nearly two decades. Moreover, Zaid had to rely on Muhammad's legal decree equating Khuzaymah's lone testimony to that of two men (shahādatahu shahādata rajulayn) just to authenticate the text—an evidentiary exception that collapses the myth of unbroken, mass-memorized preservation.

bukhari:4986.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:4986.note: After heavy casualties among Quran memorizers at the Battle of Yamama prompt Umar to warn that much of the Quran could be lost, Abu Bakr and Zayd ibn Thabit initially object to compiling it because Muhammad never did so. Once persuaded, Zayd gathers the Quran from palm stalks, thin white stones, and the memories ('chests') of men, reporting that he found the final verses of Surah at-Tawbah ([Quran 9:128-129](quran://9/128-129)) with Abu Khuzaima al-Ansari and with no one else.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَتَتَبَّعْتُ الْقُرْآنَ أَجْمَعُهُ مِنَ الْعُسُبِ وَاللِّخَافِ وَصُدُورِ الرِّجَالِ حَتَّى وَجَدْتُ آخِرَ سُورَةِ التَّوْبَةِ مَعَ أَبِي خُزَيْمَةَ الأَنْصَارِيِّ لَمْ أَجِدْهَا مَعَ أَحَدٍ غَيْرَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: So I started looking for the Qur'an and collecting it from (what was written on) palme stalks, thin white stones and also from the men who knew it by heart, till I found the last Verse of Surat at-Tauba (Repentance) with Abi Khuzaima Al-Ansari, and I did not find it with anybody other than him.

bukhari:4986.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar’s *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that the Quran was already preserved through unbroken mass memorization (*tawātur*), claiming Zaid’s statement merely meant he did not find the final verses of Surah At-Tauba *in writing* with anyone else. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Umar initiated the compilation precisely because the memorizers (*qurrā'*) were dying at Yamama and he feared "a large part of the Quran may be lost" (`فَيَذْهَبَ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ`), and Zaid explicitly searched both written materials and "the chests [memories] of men" (`وَصُدُورِ الرِّجَالِ`) before declaring unconditionally, "I did not find it with anybody other than him" (`لَمْ أَجِدْهَا مَعَ أَحَدٍ غَيْرَهُ`). Worse still, relying on a single individual (*khabar al-wāḥid*) shatters the Islamic theological requirement of *mutawātir* transmission, while parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:4986` vs. `bukhari:4679` and `bukhari:4987`) even contradict each other over whether this sole witness was Abu Khuzaima al-Ansari or Khuzaima ibn Thabit.

bukhari:4989.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:4989.note: Commissioned by Abu Bakr to search for and compile the Quran, Zaid bin Thabit states that he found the final two verses of Surah At-Tawbah ([Quran 9:128-129](quran://9/128-129)) solely with Abu Khuza'ima al-Ansari and with no one else. Even under the classical commentary qualification that Zaid meant he found them in written form (*maktuban*) with no other companion, the report establishes that the written preservation of these verses during the official compilation rested on a single individual's copy.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَتَتَبَّعْتُ حَتَّى وَجَدْتُ آخِرَ سُورَةِ التَّوْبَةِ آيَتَيْنِ مَعَ أَبِي خُزَيْمَةَ الأَنْصَارِيِّ لَمْ أَجِدْهُمَا مَعَ أَحَدٍ غَيْرَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: I started searching for the Qur'an till I found the last two Verses of Surat at-Tauba with Abi Khuza`ima Al-Ansari and I could not find these Verses with anybody other than him.

bukhari:4989.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Zayd ibn Thābit and the Companions already had Surah At-Tawbah 9:128–129 memorized via mass transmission (*tawātur*), claiming (via Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*) that Zayd only lacked a second written manuscript and accepted a single copy because Muhammad had declared Khuzayma's testimony equal to two men. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states with an unqualified negation that Zayd—the Prophet's own chief scribe—had to hunt for the text (`فَتَتَبَّعْتُ`) and found these two verses exclusively with Abū Khuzayma (`لَمْ أَجِدْهُمَا مَعَ أَحَدٍ غَيْرَهُ`, 'I did not find them with anyone other than him'), proving their survival rested on a single isolated individual (*khabar al-wāḥid*) rather than universal preservation. Worse still, the 'two-witness privilege' defense collapses under Sahih al-Bukhari's own parallel narrations, which reveal that the Companion whose testimony equaled two men was **Khuzayma ibn Thābit** (the sole source for Surah 33:23 in `bukhari:4784` and `bukhari:4987`), whereas the man here is a completely different individual (**Abū Khuzayma al-Anṣārī**), exposing both a single-source bottleneck and contradictory confusion at the heart of the Quran's canonization.

bukhari:5037.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:5037.note: Muhammad states that hearing a man reciting the Quran in the mosque reminded him of specific verses from a surah, which its appended Hishām chain and parallel transmission (bukhari:5038) specify he had actively dropped (`asqaṭtuhunna`, "I dropped them") or been caused to forget (`kuntu unsītuhā`). Classical commentators like Ibn Hajar affirm that Muhammad forgot these verses, reconciling the report with [Quran 87:6](quran://87/6) by arguing that the memory lapse occurred after the verses had already been conveyed to his companions.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: يَرْحَمُهُ اللَّهُ لَقَدْ أَذْكَرَنِي كَذَا وَكَذَا آيَةً مِنْ سُورَةِ كَذَا
problematic_excerpt.english: May Allah bestow His Mercy on him, as he has reminded me of such-and-such Verses of such a Surah

bukhari:5037.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this momentary lapse falls under the divine exception of Surah 87:6–7 ("except what Allah wills") and occurred only after Muhammad had already infallibly conveyed the verses to the community, as argued in Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and evidenced by the Companion already reciting them in the mosque. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states laqad adhkaranī kadhā wa-kadhā āyatan ("he has reminded me of such-and-such verses"), while its immediate parallel in bukhari:5038 adds kuntu unsītuhā ("I had been made to forget them") and asqaṭtuhunna ("I had dropped/omitted them"), proving that Muhammad actively omitted un-abrogated Quranic revelation until a chance encounter restored his memory. This admission collapses the preservation guarantee of Surah 75:16–17, as it leaves zero assurance that every other verse Muhammad forgot was fortuitously overheard again before his death in 632 AD.

bukhari:5038.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:5038.note: Upon hearing a man reciting a surah at night, Muhammad states that the reciter reminded him of specific Quranic verses that he had been caused to forget (`kuntu unsītuhā`), standing in tension with [Quran 87:6](quran://87/6). In the adjacent parallel report (bukhari:5037), Muhammad adds that he had dropped (`asqaṭtuhunna`) those verses from the surahs.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: يَرْحَمُهُ اللَّهُ لَقَدْ أَذْكَرَنِي كَذَا وَكَذَا آيَةً كُنْتُ أُنْسِيتُهَا مِنْ سُورَةِ كَذَا وَكَذَا
problematic_excerpt.english: May Allah bestow His Mercy on him, as he has reminded me of such-and-such Verses of such-and-such Suras, which I was caused to forget

bukhari:5038.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Hajar's Fath al-Bari and Al-Nawawi—that this was either deliberate divine abrogation (Surah 2:106) or a temporary pedagogical lapse demonstrating that the Companions' collective memory safeguarded the revelation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad praised the man for reminding him of verses he was caused to forget (لَقَدْ أَذْكَرَنِي كَذَا وَكَذَا آيَةً كُنْتُ أُنْسِيتُهَا), while the parallel narration in bukhari:5037 admits he had outright dropped them (أَسْقَطْتُهُنَّ) from the surahs. Because divinely abrogated verses would not remain valid for a companion to recite or for the Prophet to reclaim upon overhearing a chance nighttime prayer, this proves that active Quranic revelation was vulnerable to Muhammad's own memory loss, directly contradicting Surah 87:6.

bukhari:5041.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:5041.note: Umar ibn al-Khattab seized fellow Qurayshi Companion Hisham ibn Hakim by the collar and accused him of lying after hearing him recite Surah al-Furqan ([Surah 25](quran://25/1)) in numerous ways (huruf) that Muhammad had not taught Umar. When brought to judge between them, Muhammad validated both divergent recitations as divinely revealed and declared that the Quran was revealed in seven modes (sab'at ahruf), six of which were later eliminated during Uthman's standardization and burning of variant codices (bukhari:4987).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَمِعْتُ هِشَامَ بْنَ حَكِيمِ بْنِ حِزَامٍ، يَقْرَأُ سُورَةَ الْفُرْقَانِ فِي حَيَاةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَاسْتَمَعْتُ لِقِرَاءَتِهِ فَإِذَا هُوَ يَقْرَؤُهَا عَلَى حُرُوفٍ كَثِيرَةٍ لَمْ يُقْرِئْنِيهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَكِدْتُ أُسَاوِرُهُ فِي الصَّلاَةِ فَانْتَظَرْتُهُ حَتَّى سَلَّمَ فَلَبَبْتُهُ فَقُلْتُ مَنْ أَقْرَأَكَ هَذِهِ السُّورَةَ الَّتِي سَمِعْتُكَ تَقْرَأُ قَالَ أَقْرَأَنِيهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ كَذَبْتَ فَوَاللَّهِ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَهُوَ أَقْرَأَنِي هَذِهِ السُّورَةَ الَّتِي سَمِعْتُكَ، فَانْطَلَقْتُ بِهِ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَقُودُهُ فَقُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي سَمِعْتُ هَذَا يَقْرَأُ سُورَةَ الْفُرْقَانِ عَلَى حُرُوفٍ لَمْ تُقْرِئْنِيهَا وَإِنَّكَ أَقْرَأْتَنِي سُورَةَ الْفُرْقَانِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا هِشَامُ اقْرَأْهَا ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَرَأَهَا الْقِرَاءَةَ الَّتِي سَمِعْتُهُ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ هَكَذَا أُنْزِلَتْ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ اقْرَأْ يَا عُمَرُ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَرَأْتُهَا الَّتِي أَقْرَأَنِيهَا، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ هَكَذَا أُنْزِلَتْ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّ الْقُرْآنَ أُنْزِلَ عَلَى سَبْعَةِ أَحْرُفٍ فَاقْرَءُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I heard Hisham bin Hakim bin Hizam reciting Surat-al-Furqan during the lifetime of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), and I listened to his recitation and noticed that he recited it in several ways which Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) had not taught me. So I was on the point of attacking him in the prayer, but I waited till he finished his prayer, and then I seized him by the collar and said, "Who taught you this Surah which I have heard you reciting?" He replied, "Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) taught it to me." I said, "You are telling a lie; By Allah! Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) taught me (in a different way) this very Surah which I have heard you reciting." So I took him, leading him to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! I heard this person reciting Surat-al-Furqan in a way that you did not teach me, and you have taught me Surat-al-Furqan." The Prophet said, "O Hisham, recite!" So he recited in the same way as I heard him recite it before. On that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "It was revealed to be recited in this way." Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Recite, O `Umar!" So I recited it as he had taught me. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) then said, "It was revealed to be recited in this way." Allah" Apostle added, "The Qur'an has been revealed to be recited in several different ways, so recite of it that which is easier for you

bukhari:5041.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the 'seven modes' (*sab'atu aḥruf*) were merely minor dialectical pronunciations granted to accommodate different Arab tribes, which Caliph Uthman later standardized without losing any divinely revealed text. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Hisham recited *Surah al-Furqan* in 'many modes' (*'alā ḥurūfin kathīratin*) so radically different in wording that Umar accused him of lying (*kadhabta*) and seized him by the collar (*falababtuhu*)—despite both men belonging to the exact same Quraysh tribe and sharing the same dialect. Moreover, because Muhammad confirmed each divergent reading by declaring, 'Thus it was revealed' (*hākadhā unzilat*), Caliph Uthman's subsequent burning of all variant codices (bukhari:4987) permanently eradicated six of the seven divinely revealed *aḥruf*.

bukhari:7425.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:7425.note: Zaid ibn Thabit reports that during Abu Bakr's compilation of the Quran, he found the final verses of Surat at-Tawbah ([Quran 9:128-129](quran://9/128-129)) solely with a single individual, Abu Khuzaima al-Ansari, and with no one else. In the fuller parallel account of this compilation (bukhari:4986), Zaid specifies that he was collecting the Quran from both written fragments and the memories ('chests') of men when he found these verses exclusively with Abu Khuzaima.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَتَتَبَّعْتُ الْقُرْآنَ حَتَّى وَجَدْتُ آخِرَ سُورَةِ التَّوْبَةِ مَعَ أَبِي خُزَيْمَةَ الأَنْصَارِيِّ لَمْ أَجِدْهَا مَعَ أَحَدٍ غَيْرِهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: I collected the Qur'an till I found the last part of Surat-at-Tauba with Abi Khuza`ima Al-Ansari and did not find it with anybody else.

bukhari:7425.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that Zayd ibn Thābit and the Companions already had Quran 9:128–129 memorized, and that Zayd only meant he did not find these verses *in written form* (*maktūban*) with anyone other than Abū Khuzayma al-Anṣārī. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *lam ajidhā maʿa aḥadin ghayrihi* ('I did not find it with anybody else') without any qualification restricting the search to written copies, and in the fuller parallel narration (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4986) Zayd explicitly states he was tracking down the Quran from both written materials and 'the breasts/memories of men' (*wa-ṣudūri al-rijāl*) before concluding that he found the end of Sūrat al-Tawba exclusively with Abū Khuzayma. This collapses the orthodox claim of continuous mass transmission (*tawātur*) by proving that parts of the Quranic canon hung on a solitary informant (*khabar al-wāḥid*)—a textual bottleneck further compounded by rival *Ṣaḥīḥ* narrations (*Bukhārī* 4987) that contradictorily identify the lone possessor of these verses as Khuzayma ibn Thābit rather than Abū Khuzayma.

muslim:1918.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:1918.note: Alqama recites [Quran 92:1-3](quran://92/1-3) according to the reading of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud as 'and the male and the female' (*wa al-dhakari wa al-unthā*), omitting the standard Uthmanic phrase 'and He who created' (*wa mā khalaqa* in [Quran 92:3](quran://92/3)), and Abu al-Darda' testifies that he heard Muhammad himself recite the verse in this manner ([Quran 15:9](quran://15/9); cf. bukhari:4944). Although the published English translation interpolates 'and the creating of' where it is absent from the Arabic text, classical commentators acknowledge the variant reading and attribute its exclusion from the Uthmanic codex to abrogation during Gabriel's final review (*al-'ardah al-akhirah*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ هَلْ تَقْرَأُ عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ قَالَ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَاقْرَأْ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏ قَالَ فَقَرَأْتُ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَضَحِكَ ثُمَّ قَالَ هَكَذَا سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَؤُهَا ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He again said: Do you recite according to the recitation of 'Abdullah b. Mas'ud? I said: Yes. He said: Recite this verse (By the night when it covers) So I recited it: (By the night when it covers, and the day when it shines, and the creating of the male and the female). He laughed and said: I have heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting like this

muslim:1918.literal_translation: He said: 'Do you recite according to the recitation of Abdullah b. Mas'ud?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then recite: {By the night when it covers}.' So I recited: '{By the night when it covers, and the day when it shines, and the male and the female}.' He laughed and then said: 'Thus did I hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏
translation_issue.published_rendering: (By the night when it covers, and the day when it shines, and the creating of the male and the female)
translation_issue.literal_meaning: By the night when it covers, and the day when it shines, and the male and the female
translation_issue.explanation: The translator interpolates 'and the creating of' (from the Uthmanic 'wa mā khalaqa') into the English translation despite its absence in the Arabic text, concealing the textual discrepancy between the recitation attributed to Muhammad and the standard Uthmanic Quran.

muslim:1918.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that omitting *wa mā khalaqa* ('and He who created') in Quran 92:3 was either a valid variant among the seven *aḥruf* or an early reading whose recitation was abrogated (*mansūkh al-tilāwah*) during Muhammad's final review with Gabriel, citing Al-Nawawī and Ibn Hajar to dismiss this reading as anomalous (*shādhdh*) against the Uthmanic consensus. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states the verse as *wa al-dhakari wa al-unthā* ('and the male and the female'—a discrepancy the English translator deceptively masks by interpolating 'and the creating of') and records Abu al-Darda's direct testimony: *hākadhā samiʿtu Rasūla Allāhi (ﷺ) yaqraʾuhā* ('Thus did I hear the Messenger of Allah recite it'). Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (muslim:1916; bukhari:4944) prove that both Ibn Mas'ud and Abu al-Darda'—two of the four master reciters from whom Muhammad commanded Muslims to learn the Quran—actively rejected the Uthmanic addition long after the Prophet's death, collapsing the claim of final prophetic abrogation.

muslim:3598.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
muslim:3598.note: Aisha states that verses stipulating ten known breastfeedings and then five known breastfeedings were revealed in the Quran regarding fosterage that makes marriage unlawful. In the immediately preceding narration (muslim:3597), she specifies that the ten were abrogated by the five, which were still being recited as part of the Quran when Muhammad died, though neither verse exists in the canonical Quran today ([Quran 15:9](quran://15/9)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ عَمْرَةَ، أَنَّهَا سَمِعَتْ عَائِشَةَ، تَقُولُ - وَهْىَ تَذْكُرُ الَّذِي يُحَرِّمُ مِنَ الرَّضَاعَةِ - قَالَتْ عَمْرَةُ فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ نَزَلَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ عَشْرُ رَضَعَاتٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ ثُمَّ نَزَلَ أَيْضًا خَمْسٌ مَعْلُومَاتٌ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Amra reported that she heard 'A'isha (Allah he pleased with her) discussing fosterage which (makes marriage) unlawful; and she ('A'isha) said:There was revealed in the Holy Qur'an ten clear sucklings, and then five clear (sucklings)

muslim:3598.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the verses stipulating ten and five breastfeedings underwent abrogation of recitation (`naskh al-tilāwah`), meaning Allah intentionally removed their wording from the Quran while leaving the legal ruling intact. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Aisha cited these revelations while defining the active law of fosterage that makes marriage unlawful (`وَهْىَ تَذْكُرُ الَّذِي يُحَرِّمُ مِنَ الرَّضَاعَةِ`), testifying that ten and then five known sucklings were revealed in the Quran (`نَزَلَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ عَشْرُ رَضَعَاتٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ ثُمَّ نَزَلَ أَيْضًا خَمْسٌ مَعْلُومَاتٌ`). Because neither verse exists in the canonical text today across this report and its parallels (`muslim:3597`, `muslim:3599`), invoking unwritten recitation-abrogation is a circular admission that revealed Quranic verses disappeared from the text ([Quran 15:9](quran://15/9)).

bukhari:7323.subcategory: Quranic Loss, Forgotten Verses & Uthmanic Burning
bukhari:7323.note: Upon returning to Medina from his final Hajj, Caliph Umar publicly declares to the Muhajirun and Ansar that the Verse of Stoning (Āyat al-Rajm) was revealed to Muhammad as part of the Book (cf. bukhari:6830). Because this verse is absent from the standardized Uthmanic codex, classical Sunni jurisprudence accounts for its omission through the doctrine of abrogated recitation with an enduring legal ruling (naskh al-tilāwah dūna al-ḥukm).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بَعَثَ مُحَمَّدًا صلى الله عليه وسلم بِالْحَقِّ وَأَنْزَلَ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابَ، فَكَانَ فِيمَا أُنْزِلَ آيَةُ الرَّجْمِ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: 'Umar (in a Friday Khutba-sermon) said, "No doubt, Allah sent Muhammad with the Truth and revealed to him the Book (Quran), and among what was revealed, was the Verse of Ar-Rajm (stoning adulterers to death).'"

bukhari:7323.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the stoning verse (āyat al-rajm) is an instance of 'abrogation of recitation while the legal ruling remains' (naskh al-tilāwah dūna al-ḥukm), citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī to claim Allah intentionally withdrew its wording from the Quran. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the verse was revealed as part of the Book (wa-anzala 'alayhi al-kitāba fa-kāna fīmā unzila āyatu al-rajm), and in the full parallel narration (bukhari:6830), Umar confesses he would have written it into the physical muṣḥaf himself if not for fear that people would accuse him of adding to Allah's Book (lawlā an yaqūla al-nāsu... la-katabtuhā).
