Ibn Saiyad stopped his murmuring. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "If his mother had kept quiet, then I would have learnt more about him."

bukhari:6173.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as suggested by Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, Muhammad merely tested Ibn Ṣayyād as a lesser soothsayer or only suspected him prior to learning via Tamīm al-Dārī that the Greater Dajjāl was chained on an island. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Muhammad crept behind palm trunks to eavesdrop on the boy (`يَتَّقِي بِجُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ، وَهْوَ يَخْتِلُ`), lamented that the boy's mother prevented him from discovering the truth (`لَوْ تَرَكَتْهُ بَيَّنَ`), and warned ʿUmar regarding the singular Antichrist, 'If he is him, you cannot overpower him' (`إِنْ يَكُنْ هُوَ لاَ تُسَلَّطُ عَلَيْهِ`). Furthermore, senior companions like ʿUmar, Jābir, and Ibn ʿUmar continued swearing by Allah long after Muhammad's death that Ibn Ṣayyād was the literal Dajjāl (bukhari:7355; muslim:7353), proving Muhammad died without ever resolving the contradiction between this Medinan youth and the chained island monster of muslim:7386.

bukhari:6618.note: Muhammad tests Ibn Sayyad with a hidden word and stops Umar from decapitating him by expressing uncertainty over whether the youth is the Dajjal ("if he is he, you will not be able to overcome him, and if he is not, there is no good for you in killing him"). This uncertainty over whether a Medinan youth is the Dajjal contradicts the canonical Tamim al-Dari report (muslim:7386), in which Muhammad affirms that the Dajjal is already chained in a monastery on a remote island.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لاِبْنِ صَيَّادٍ ‏"‏ خَبَأْتُ لَكَ خَبِيئًا ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ الدُّخُّ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ اخْسَأْ فَلَنْ تَعْدُوَ قَدْرَكَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ عُمَرُ ائْذَنْ لِي فَأَضْرِبَ عُنُقَهُ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ دَعْهُ، إِنْ يَكُنْ هُوَ فَلاَ تُطِيقُهُ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ هُوَ فَلاَ خَيْرَ لَكَ فِي قَتْلِهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Ibn Saiyad, "I have kept for you a secret." Ibn Saiyad said, "Ad-Dukh." The Prophet said, "Keep quiet, for you cannot go beyond your limits (or you cannot exceed what has been foreordained for you)." On that, `Umar said (to the Prophet (ﷺ) ), "Allow me to chop off his neck!" The Prophet said, "Leave him, for if he is he (i.e., Ad-Dajjal), then you will not be able to overcome him, and if he is not, then you gain no good by killing him

bukhari:6618.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as suggested in Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī, Muhammad had not yet received definitive revelation regarding the Dajjal's identity when testing Ibn Ṣayyād, or that the boy was merely a lesser impostor before Tamīm al-Dārī's island narrative (muslim:7386) settled the matter. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states "in yakun huwa falā tuṭīquhu" (إِنْ يَكُنْ هُوَ فَلاَ تُطِيقُهُ — "if he is he, you will not be able to overcome him"), proving Muhammad genuinely thought a local Medinan youth could be the invincible eschatological Antichrist rather than an ancient prisoner chained on a remote island. Furthermore, senior companions like Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh and ʿUmar continued swearing by Allah that Ibn Ṣayyād was the actual Dajjal (bukhari:7355), refuting the claim that subsequent revelation ever resolved this contradiction.

muslim:2143.note: Umar and Ibn Umar's narration that Muhammad declared the dead are punished in the grave for being wailed over is directly refuted by Aisha in the same chapter (muslim:2149, muslim:2150, bukhari:1288). In those reports, Aisha swears that Muhammad never made this general statement, charges Umar and Ibn Umar with misremembering a remark made about a specific unbeliever, and cites [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164) against their transmission.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ عُمَرَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ الْمَيِّتُ يُعَذَّبُ فِي قَبْرِهِ بِمَا نِيحَ عَلَيْهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Umar reported Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) as saying:The dead is punished in the grave because of wailing on it

muslim:2143.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that there is no real contradiction in the *Ṣaḥīḥayn* because ʿUmar and Ibn ʿUmar preserved a genuine prophetic teaching that ʿĀʾishah simply had not heard, and that the affirmative testimony of multiple Companions overrides her denial. However, the primary Arabic text of the parallel narrations (`bukhari:1288`, `muslim:2149`, `muslim:2150`) explicitly states that ʿĀʾishah swore by Allah that Muhammad never said this, declared that "hearing makes mistakes" (*walākinna al-samʿa yukhṭiʾu*), and explained the exact incident ʿUmar mangled: Muhammad had merely passed by a deceased Jewish woman whose family was weeping while she was being tormented for her own unbelief. This leaves Sunni Islam with an inescapable dilemma at the highest tier of *Ṣaḥīḥ* transmission: either Caliph ʿUmar and his son distorted a specific remark into a false universal doctrine contradicting [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164), or ʿĀʾishah falsely swore by Allah to repudiate an authentic prophetic command.

muslim:2143.note: Umar and Ibn Umar report an unqualified statement from Muhammad declaring that a dead person is tormented in the grave because of the wailing performed over him by the living. Because punishing the deceased for the actions of others conflicts with [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164) and [Ezekiel 18:20](bible://ez/18/20), classical commentators had to interpolate unstated conditions—such as the deceased having commanded the wailing before death—or redefine torment as mere grief.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ عُمَرَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ الْمَيِّتُ يُعَذَّبُ فِي قَبْرِهِ بِمَا نِيحَ عَلَيْهِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Umar reported Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) as saying:The dead is punished in the grave because of wailing on it

muslim:2143.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, following Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar, that this punishment only applies if the deceased explicitly commanded their family to wail over them before dying, or that "punished" (*yuʿadhdhabu*) merely means the soul feels emotional grief upon hearing its family weep. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states as an unqualified universal rule that "the dead is tormented in his grave because of the wailing over him" (*al-mayyitu yuʿadhdhabu fī qabrihi bimā nīḥa ʿalayhi*) with zero mention of a prior bequest. Furthermore, parallel narrations (`muslim:2142`, `muslim:2149`) show ʿUmar violently beating weeping women out of fear it would bring torment upon the deceased and ʿĀʾishah condemning the report as a violation of [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164)—proving the Companions themselves understood the statement as literal, vicarious punishment.

muslim:6483.note: Jabir b. 'Abdullah reports that one month before his death, Muhammad declared that no breathing soul alive 'today' (al-yawma) would still be living in one hundred years—a clause omitted with ellipses in the published English translation—which 'Abd al-Rahman interpreted to mean a shortening of human lifespans (naqs al-'umur). This transmission differs from Jabir's adjacent reports in muslim:6481 and muslim:6485, which give the 100-year pronouncement in response to questions about the Last Hour, omit the qualifier 'today' (muslim:6481), and date the statement to the return from Tabuk rather than a month before Muhammad's death (muslim:6485).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ قَالَ ذَلِكَ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ بِشَهْرٍ أَوْ نَحْوِ ذَلِكَ ‏ "‏ مَا مِنْ نَفْسٍ مَنْفُوسَةٍ الْيَوْمَ تَأْتِي عَلَيْهَا مِائَةُ سَنَةٍ وَهْىَ حَيَّةٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَعَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، صَاحِبِ السِّقَايَةِ عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِمِثْلِ ذَلِكَ وَفَسَّرَهَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ قَالَ نَقْصُ الْعُمُرِ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Jabir b. 'Abdullah reported Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) as saying one mouth before his death (or something like it):None amongst the created beings who had been living by that time (during the lifetime of Allah's Apostle).... 'Abd al-Rahman has interpreted these words of Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) as: The ages (of the people) would be diminished

muslim:6483.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the word 'today' (`al-yawma`) restricts Muhammad's statement solely to the individuals alive at the time of his speech, or that the report merely describes a gradual shortening of human lifespans. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the narrator 'Abd al-Rahman appended his own interpretation (`wa-fassarahā 'Abd al-Raḥmān qāla naqṣ al-ʿumur`) that lifespans would be diminished, which directly conflicts with Ibn Umar's explanation in `muslim:6479` that the pronouncement meant the passing of that generation. Furthermore, the parallel narration in `muslim:6481` lacks the qualifier 'today,' demonstrating that transmitters relied on diverging wording and competing explanations to account for the declaration that no breathing soul would remain alive after one hundred years (`taʾtī ʿalayhā miʾatu sanatin wa-hiya ḥayyatun yawmaʾidhin`).

muslim:6485.note: Abu Sa'id reports that when Muhammad returned from Tabuk, his Companions asked him about the Last Hour and he replied that one hundred years would not pass with any breathing soul alive that day remaining on earth. Parallel narrations instead place this statement one month before Muhammad's death and reinterpret the one-hundred-year limit as the passing of that generation rather than the arrival of the Last Hour (muslim:6481, muslim:6483).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ، قَالَ لَمَا رَجَعَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ تَبُوكَ سَأَلُوهُ عَنِ السَّاعَةِ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ لاَ تَأْتِي مِائَةُ سَنَةٍ وَعَلَى الأَرْضِ نَفْسٌ مَنْفُوسَةٌ الْيَوْمَ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Sa'id reported that when Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) came back from Tabuk they (his Companions) asked about the Last Hour. Thereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said:There would be none amongst the created beings living on the earth (who would survive this century)

muslim:6485.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad only meant that the generation alive on that day (`الْيَوْمَ`) would die within a century rather than predicting the Last Hour, and that he repeated the saying on separate occasions to harmonize the return from Tabuk (late AD 630) with Jabir's account one month before his death in AD 632 (`muslim:6481`, `muslim:6483`). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Companions asked him about the Last Hour (`سَأَلُوهُ عَنِ السَّاعَةِ`), and his immediate reply was that one hundred years would not come (`لاَ تَأْتِي مِائَةُ سَنَةٍ`) with any breathing soul remaining on the earth (`وَعَلَى الأَرْضِ نَفْسٌ مَنْفُوسَةٌ الْيَوْمَ`). Positing that Muhammad pronounced the exact same one-hundred-year (`مِائَةُ سَنَةٍ`) limit in both late AD 630 and AD 632 (`muslim:6481`, `muslim:6483`, `bukhari:601`) produces two different expiration dates and severs his answer from the Companions' question about the Last Hour (`السَّاعَةِ`).

bukhari:1597.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
bukhari:1597.note: `Umar ibn al-Khattab kisses the Black Stone while declaring that it is merely a stone that can neither harm nor benefit anyone—the exact description the Quran applies to powerless idols ([Quran 10:18](quran://10/18); [Quran 21:66](quran://21/66))—and states that he would not have kissed it had he not seen Muhammad doing so. Classical commentators such as Ibn Hajar and al-Nawawi explain that this ritual is maintained strictly as unquestioning ritual compliance (ta'abbud) and imitation (ittiba') of Muhammad's practice ([Exodus 20:4-5](bible://ex/20/4)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّهُ جَاءَ إِلَى الْحَجَرِ الأَسْوَدِ فَقَبَّلَهُ، فَقَالَ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ حَجَرٌ لاَ تَضُرُّ وَلاَ تَنْفَعُ، وَلَوْلاَ أَنِّي رَأَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُقَبِّلُكَ مَا قَبَّلْتُكَ
problematic_excerpt.english: `Umar came near the Black Stone and kissed it and said "No doubt, I know that you are a stone and can neither benefit anyone nor harm anyone. Had I not seen Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) kissing you I would not have kissed you

bukhari:1597.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that ʿUmar's declaration, as explained by Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, proves pure monotheism (*tawḥīd*) by teaching recent converts from paganism that kissing the Black Stone is merely ritual obedience (*ittibāʿ*) to Muhammad rather than stone veneration. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that ʿUmar confessed the stone 'neither harms nor benefits' (*lā taḍurru wa-lā tanfaʿu* — لاَ تَضُرُّ وَلاَ تَنْفَعُ), echoing the exact Quranic formula Abraham used to condemn lifeless pagan idols (Quran 21:66; 26:72–73) and proving that ʿUmar's own conscience recognized kissing a rock (*faqabbalahu*) as indistinguishable from pre-Islamic Arab litholatry (*Bukhārī* 4376). Furthermore, authenticated Sunni traditions record Muhammad teaching that touching the Black Stone expiates sins and that Allah will resurrect it with 'two eyes by which it sees and a tongue by which it speaks' to testify for its venerators (*Tirmidhī* 959, 961), directly refuting ʿUmar's rationalist disclaimer by attributing animistic agency and spiritual benefit to the stone itself.

bukhari:7384.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
bukhari:7384.note: Muhammad states that people will continue to be thrown into Hell while it asks for more until the Lord of the worlds places His foot (qadamahu) in it (fīhā, softened to 'over it' in the English translation), causing its sides to contract together and cry, 'Enough, enough!' (cf. bukhari:6661). Classical commentators divide between affirming Allah's foot placed in Hellfire literally without specifying how (bilā kayf) and metaphorically reinterpreting (ta'wīl) 'foot' to mean a group of creation sent ahead.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لاَ يَزَالُ يُلْقَى فِيهَا وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِنْ مَزِيدٍ‏.‏ حَتَّى يَضَعَ فِيهَا رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ قَدَمَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: (The people will be thrown into Hell ( Fire) and it will keep on saying, 'Is there any more?' till the Lord of the worlds puts His Foot over it

bukhari:7384.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ash'ari commentators like Ibn Hajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī in Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim—that qadam ('foot') is either a metaphor for Allah's subjugating power or refers to a group of people sent ahead (qaddama) into the Fire, while Athari apologists invoke bilā kayf ('without asking how') to deny creaturely physicality. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Lord of the worlds places His foot directly in the Fire (يَضَعَ فِيهَا رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ قَدَمَهُ), and parallel Sahih narrations (such as bukhari:4848, 6661 and muslim:7177) interchange qadamahu with the unmistakable anatomical noun rijlahu (رِجْلَهُ, 'His leg/foot'), which physically compresses Hell's walls together. This explicit anatomical substitution demolishes the figurative 'people sent ahead' evasion and locks orthodox Sunni theology into depicting God Almighty stepping bodily into Hellfire.

bukhari:4919.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
bukhari:4919.note: Explaining [Quran 68:42](quran://68/42), Muhammad declares that on the Day of Judgment our Lord will uncover His Shin (*yakshifu Rabbunā ʿan sāqihi*), causing all believers to prostrate before Him while those who prostrated for show have their backs stiffen into a single bone. By explicitly attaching the possessive pronoun to Allah ('His Shin') as a visible sign (cf. bukhari:7439), the primary text precludes metaphorical attempts to interpret the indefinite *sāq* of [Quran 68:42](quran://68/42) as a mere idiom for severity.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: يَكْشِفُ رَبُّنَا عَنْ سَاقِهِ فَيَسْجُدُ لَهُ كُلُّ مُؤْمِنٍ وَمُؤْمِنَةٍ، وَيَبْقَى مَنْ كَانَ يَسْجُدُ فِي الدُّنْيَا رِئَاءً وَسُمْعَةً، فَيَذْهَبُ لِيَسْجُدَ فَيَعُودُ ظَهْرُهُ طَبَقًا وَاحِدًا
problematic_excerpt.english: Our Lord Allah will lay bare His Shin, and then all the Believers, men and women, will prostrate themselves before Him, but there will remain those who used to prostrate in the world for showing off and for gaining good reputation. Such people will try to prostrate (on the Day of Judgment) but their back swill be as stiff as if it is one bone (a single vertebra)

bukhari:4919.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ash'arite commentators recorded in Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī—that 'uncovering the shin' (kashf al-sāq) in Quran 68:42 is merely a figurative Arabic idiom for the severity and hardship of Judgment Day rather than a literal anatomical limb. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states يَكْشِفُ رَبُّنَا عَنْ سَاقِهِ (yakshifu Rabbunā 'an sāqihi, 'Our Lord will lay bare His shin'), attaching a personal possessive pronoun directly to Allah that grammatically refutes an impersonal idiom of calamity. Furthermore, the parallel narration in bukhari:7439 specifies that when believers fail to recognize Allah's initial form and are asked if there is a visible sign by which they know Him (آيَةٌ تَعْرِفُونَهُ), they answer 'the Shin' (السَّاقُ)—whereupon Allah exposes His shin as a physical identifying mark so they can visually recognize Him.

bukhari:7437.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
bukhari:7437.note: Muhammad states that on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will come to the believers and declare Himself their Lord, yet they will refuse to follow Him until He returns in 'His form (surah) which they know.' Parallel accounts further specify that Allah initially appears in a form other than His own before transforming into His recognizable form and uncovering His shin (bukhari:6573; bukhari:7439).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَيَأْتِيهِمُ اللَّهُ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُونَ هَذَا مَكَانُنَا حَتَّى يَأْتِيَنَا رَبُّنَا فَإِذَا جَاءَنَا رَبُّنَا عَرَفْنَاهُ فَيَأْتِيهِمُ اللَّهُ فِي صُورَتِهِ الَّتِي يَعْرِفُونَ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah will come to them and say, 'I am your Lord.' They will (deny Him and) say, 'We will stay here till our Lord comes, for when our Lord comes, we will recognize Him.' So Allah will come to them in His appearance which they know, and will say, 'I am your Lord.'

bukhari:7437.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that—as claimed in Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim—the term ṣūrah ('form/appearance') is merely a metaphorical attribute or a subjective perceptual test created in the minds of the beholders rather than a literal physical change in Allah's essence. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah Himself comes to the believers 'in His form which they recognize' (fī ṣūratihi allatī yaʿrifūna) only after they visually reject His initial appearance. Furthermore, the immediate parallel narration in bukhari:7439 (and muslim:454) states that Allah first arrives 'in a form other than that which they know' (fī ghayri al-ṣūrah), literally 'transforms Himself' (fayataḥawwalu), and physically 'uncovers His shin' (fayakshifu ʿan sāqihi) as an identifying bodily mark, demolishing any metaphorical reinterpretation.

muslim:1776.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
muslim:1776.note: Muhammad declares that once the first third of the night passes, Allah descends (*nazala*) to the lowest heaven and calls out for supplicants, penitents, and petitioners until daybreak (cf. [Psalm 139:7](bible://ps/139/7)). This nightly schedule presupposes a single-timezone Earth and divides classical commentators between Athari literalism—affirming Allah's actual descent into the created lowest heaven—and Ash'ari figurative reinterpretation claiming only an angel or command descends, which conflicts with parallel reports where the speaker declares, 'I am the King' (muslim:1773).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُمْهِلُ حَتَّى إِذَا ذَهَبَ ثُلُثُ اللَّيْلِ الأَوَّلُ نَزَلَ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا فَيَقُولُ هَلْ مِنْ مُسْتَغْفِرٍ هَلْ مِنْ تَائِبٍ هَلْ مِنْ سَائِلٍ هَلْ مِنْ دَاعٍ حَتَّى يَنْفَجِرَ الْفَجْرُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah waits till when one-third of the first part of the night is over; He descends to the lowest heaven and says: It there any supplicator of forgiveness? Is there any penitant? Is there any petitioner (for mercy and favour)? Is there any solicitor? -till it is daybreak

muslim:1776.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Allah's nightly descent is either a metaphor for the descent of His mercy or an angel (as proposed by Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*), or a transcendent descent 'befitting His majesty' (*bilā kayf*) that operates outside earthly time zones. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah Himself descends (*nazala ilā al-samāʾ al-dunyā*) within a strictly bounded terrestrial timeframe—from after the first third of the night until daybreak (*ḥattā yanfajira al-fajr*)—and immediate parallel narrations (Ṣaḥīḥ muslim:1772; Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 1145) record the descending speaker proclaiming in the first person, 'I am the King (*anā al-Malik*)! Who is calling upon Me that I may answer him?' This first-person declaration refutes any angelic or metaphorical substitute, while the continuous rotation of a spherical Earth means night and dawn occur simultaneously around the globe, which would trap Allah permanently in the lowest heaven and exposes the Hadith's presupposition of a flat, single-timezone world.

muslim:7147.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
muslim:7147.note: In response to a debate over whether men or women are more numerous in Paradise, Abu Huraira cites Muhammad's declaration that no one in Paradise is unmarried and that every man possesses two wives whose leg bone marrow is visible beneath their flesh.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِمَّا تَفَاخَرُوا وَإِمَّا تَذَاكَرُوا الرِّجَالُ فِي الْجَنَّةِ أَكْثَرُ أَمِ النِّسَاءُ فَقَالَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ أَوَلَمْ يَقُلْ أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ إِنَّ أَوَّلَ زُمْرَةٍ تَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ عَلَى صُورَةِ الْقَمَرِ لَيْلَةَ الْبَدْرِ وَالَّتِي تَلِيهَا عَلَى أَضْوَإِ كَوْكَبٍ دُرِّيٍّ فِي السَّمَاءِ لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ زَوْجَتَانِ اثْنَتَانِ يُرَى مُخُّ سُوقِهِمَا مِنْ وَرَاءِ اللَّحْمِ وَمَا فِي الْجَنَّةِ أَعْزَبُ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Muhammad reported that some (persons) stated with a sense of pride and some discussed whether there would be more men in Paradise or more women. It was upon this that Abu Huraira reported that Abu'l Qasim (the Holy Prophet) (ﷺ) said:The (members) of the first group to get into Paradise would have their faces as bright as full moon during the night, and the next to this group would have their faces as bright as the shining stars in the sky, and every person would have two wives and the marrow of their shanks would glimmer beneath the flesh and there would be none without a wife in Paradise

muslim:7147.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that descriptions of heavenly spouses and their physical features are metaphorical expressions of spiritual purity and companionship rather than literal bodily gratification. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that this report resolves a numerical dispute over whether men or women are more numerous in Paradise (الرِّجَالُ فِي الْجَنَّةِ أَكْثَرُ أَمِ النِّسَاءُ) by affirming that every man possesses two wives (لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ زَوْجَتَانِ اثْنَتَانِ), that the marrow of their shanks is visible beneath the flesh (يُرَى مُخُّ سُوقِهِمَا مِنْ وَرَاءِ اللَّحْمِ), and that no one in Paradise is unmarried (وَمَا فِي الْجَنَّةِ أَعْزَبُ). Such anatomical and numerical specificity—reinforced in parallel reports (bukhari:3245, bukhari:3246, muslim:7151)—precludes an allegorical reading and stands in direct opposition to Jesus's teaching that in the resurrection people neither marry nor are given in marriage ([Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30)).

muslim:7158.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
muslim:7158.note: Muhammad states that a believer in Paradise will have a tent made of a single hollowed pearl sixty miles long housing multiple wives or families (*ahlūn*) whom the believer visits in turn without them seeing one another ([Quran 55:72](quran://55/72); cf. bukhari:3243, bukhari:4879, muslim:7159). The published English translation renders the Arabic clause *li-l-muʾmini fīhā ahlūna yaṭūfu ʿalayhimu al-muʾminu* ("for the believer in it are wives whom the believer goes around to visit") as "the believers would go around it."

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ فِي الْجَنَّةِ لَخَيْمَةً مِنْ لُؤْلُؤَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ مُجَوَّفَةٍ طُولُهَا سِتُّونَ مِيلاً لِلْمُؤْمِنِ فِيهَا أَهْلُونَ يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْمُؤْمِنُ فَلاَ يَرَى بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا
problematic_excerpt.english: in Paradise there would be for a believer a tent of a single hollowed pearl the breadth of which would be sixty miles. It would be meant for a believer and the believers would go around it and none would be able to see the others

muslim:7158.literal_translation: Indeed, for the believer in Paradise there is a tent of a single hollowed pearl, its length is sixty miles; in it the believer has wives whom the believer goes around to visit, and they do not see one another.

translation_issue.arabic_term: لِلْمُؤْمِنِ فِيهَا أَهْلُونَ يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْمُؤْمِنُ فَلاَ يَرَى بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا
translation_issue.published_rendering: It would be meant for a believer and the believers would go around it and none would be able to see the others
translation_issue.literal_meaning: For the believer in it are wives whom the believer goes around to visit, and they do not see one another
translation_issue.explanation: The published rendering omits 'ahlūn' (wives/spouses) altogether and alters the singular 'yaṭūfu ʿalayhim al-muʾminu' (the believer goes around to visit them) into 'the believers would go around it', obscuring the multiple wives inside the tent.

muslim:7158.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that descriptions of physical pleasures in Paradise are symbolic metaphors for spiritual bliss, or rely on the English rendering that "the believers would go around" a shared tent. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the sixty-mile hollowed pearl tent holds multiple wives (*ahlūn*) whom the believer visits in turn (*yaṭūfu ʿalayhim al-muʾmin*) while they remain hidden from one another (*falā yarā baʿḍuhum baʿḍan*), echoing the secluded companions in tents of [Quran 55:72](quran://55/72) and parallels in bukhari:3243, bukhari:4879, and muslim:7159. This concrete depiction of a polygamous afterlife stands in direct opposition to Jesus's teaching in [Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30) that in the resurrection people neither marry nor are given in marriage.

bukhari:111.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
bukhari:111.note: Ali states that his written scroll (*ṣaḥīfah*) contains rulings on blood money (*al-ʿaql*), the ransoming of captives, and the law that a Muslim shall not be put to death for killing a disbeliever (*lā yuqtalu muslimun bi-kāfirin*). As documented in Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, the majority of Sunni legal schools (Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and Aḥmad, against the Ḥanafī restriction to hostile combatants) uphold the literal generality of this exemption even when the victim is a protected non-Muslim subject (*dhimmī*), directly contrasting with the biblical mandate of a single capital standard for native and foreigner alike ([Leviticus 24:21-22](bible://lv/24/21-22)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قُلْتُ لِعَلِيٍّ هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ كِتَابٌ قَالَ لاَ، إِلاَّ كِتَابُ اللَّهِ، أَوْ فَهْمٌ أُعْطِيَهُ رَجُلٌ مُسْلِمٌ، أَوْ مَا فِي هَذِهِ الصَّحِيفَةِ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ فَمَا فِي هَذِهِ الصَّحِيفَةِ قَالَ الْعَقْلُ، وَفَكَاكُ الأَسِيرِ، وَلاَ يُقْتَلُ مُسْلِمٌ بِكَافِرٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Juhaifa said, "I asked `Ali, 'Have you got any book (which has been revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) apart from the Qur'an)?' `Ali replied, 'No, except Allah's Book or the power of understanding which has been bestowed (by Allah) upon a Muslim or what is (written) in this sheet of paper (with me).' Abu Juhaifa said, "I asked, 'What is (written) in this sheet of paper?' `Ali replied, it deals with The Diyya (compensation (blood money) paid by the killer to the relatives of the victim), the ransom for the releasing of the captives from the hands of the enemies, and the law that no Muslim should be killed in Qisas (equality in punishment) for the killing of (a disbeliever)

bukhari:111.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the term *kāfir* in this decree refers solely to a hostile enemy combatant (*ḥarbī*) rather than a peaceful non-Muslim citizen (*dhimmī*), often appealing to the minority Hanafi opinion to claim equal judicial protection. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in unrestricted terms, *wa-lā yuqtalu muslimun bi-kāfirin* ('and no Muslim is killed for a disbeliever'), employing an indefinite noun in a negative clause (*nakirah fī siyāq al-nafy*) that grammatically encompasses every non-Muslim without exception. Consequently, as Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani confirms in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* alongside the parallel narration in `bukhari:6915`, Caliph Ali himself and the majority of Sunni orthodoxy (the Shafi'i, Maliki, and Hanbali schools) enforced this exact prophetic scroll to exempt Muslims from capital retaliation (*qiṣāṣ*) even for murdering an innocent, tax-paying *dhimmī*.

muslim:451.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
muslim:451.note: Muhammad states that on the Day of Resurrection Allah will come to the Muslims in a form (*ṣūrah*) other than the form they recognize and declare, 'I am your Lord,' prompting them to seek refuge with Allah from Him until He returns in the form they recognize ([Numbers 23:19](bible://nm/23/19), [James 1:17](bible://jas/1/17)). Later in the same narration, Allah takes covenants and agreements from the last man entering Paradise not to ask for more, calls him treacherous when he repeatedly breaks them, and laughs at him before admitting him to Paradise.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَتَبْقَى هَذِهِ الأُمَّةُ فِيهَا مُنَافِقُوهَا فَيَأْتِيهِمُ اللَّهُ - تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى - فِي صُورَةٍ غَيْرِ صُورَتِهِ الَّتِي يَعْرِفُونَ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُونَ نَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْكَ هَذَا مَكَانُنَا حَتَّى يَأْتِيَنَا رَبُّنَا فَإِذَا جَاءَ رَبُّنَا عَرَفْنَاهُ ‏.‏ فَيَأْتِيهِمُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى فِي صُورَتِهِ الَّتِي يَعْرِفُونَ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُونَ أَنْتَ رَبُّنَا ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: This Ummah (of Islam) alone would be left behind and there would be hypocrites too amongst it. Allah would then come to them in a form other than His own Form, recognisable to them, and would say: I am your Lord. They would say: We take refuge with Allah from thee. We will stay here till our Lord comes to us. and when our Lord would come we would recognise Him. Subsequently Allah would come to them in His own Form, recognisable to them, and say: I am your Lord. They would say: Thou art our Lord.

muslim:451.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that *ṣūrah* (form) merely means an abstract attribute (*ṣifah*) or an angel sent to test the hypocrites, and that Allah's laughter (*ḍaḥik*) is only a metaphor for divine pleasure (*riḍā*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah Himself comes to them in a form other than His own recognizable form (*fī ṣūratin ghayri ṣūratihi allatī ya'rifūna*) and personally declares, 'I am your Lord' (*Anā Rabbukum*)—a divine claim no angel could make—before transforming (*yataḥawwalu* in muslim:454) into His recognizable form and laughing (*yaḍḥaku*) at a man who repeatedly breaks his solemn oaths (*mā aghdaraka*).

muslim:451.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:451.subcategory: Divine Immanence, Entering Creation & Visible Form (Incarnation Precedents)
muslim:451.note: Muhammad states that on the Day of Resurrection Allah Himself will come to the believers first in a form (*ṣūrah*) other than the one they know and say, 'I am your Lord,' before returning to them in the recognizable form (*ṣūrah*) they know ([John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14), [Colossians 1:15](bible://col/1/15)). Parallel narrations of this account add that Allah then uncovers His shin as the sign by which the believers recognize Him (muslim:454, bukhari:7439; cf. [Quran 68:42](quran://68/42), [Ibn Kathir 68:42](ibnkathir://68/42)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَتَبْقَى هَذِهِ الأُمَّةُ فِيهَا مُنَافِقُوهَا فَيَأْتِيهِمُ اللَّهُ - تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى - فِي صُورَةٍ غَيْرِ صُورَتِهِ الَّتِي يَعْرِفُونَ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُونَ نَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْكَ هَذَا مَكَانُنَا حَتَّى يَأْتِيَنَا رَبُّنَا فَإِذَا جَاءَ رَبُّنَا عَرَفْنَاهُ ‏.‏ فَيَأْتِيهِمُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى فِي صُورَتِهِ الَّتِي يَعْرِفُونَ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُونَ أَنْتَ رَبُّنَا ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: This Ummah (of Islam) alone would be left behind and there would be hypocrites too amongst it. Allah would then come to them in a form other than His own Form, recognisable to them, and would say: I am your Lord. They would say: We take refuge with Allah from thee. We will stay here till our Lord comes to us. and when our Lord would come we would recognise Him. Subsequently Allah would come to them in His own Form, recognisable to them, and say: I am your Lord. They would say: Thou art our Lord.

muslim:451.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Allah's appearance in the Hereafter involves no real assumption of form or change in God, insisting that the laws of the afterlife are completely incomparable to the Christian Incarnation on earth. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah comes to His creatures in two distinct, visible forms (*fī ṣūratin ghayri ṣūratihi* and *fī ṣūratihi allatī ya'rifūna*) and even transforms Himself (*yataḥawwalu*) while uncovering His shin (*yakshifu 'an sāqihi* in bukhari:7439) so believers can physically see Him just as they see the sun and full moon. Since Sunni orthodoxy concedes that the infinite Creator can assume visible forms to reveal Himself to finite creatures without ceasing to be God, their core philosophical objection against the Incarnation collapses.

bukhari:1605.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
bukhari:1605.note: Umar ibn al-Khattab declares that the Black Stone is a stone that neither harms nor benefits and states that the original reason for *ramal* (trotting during *tawaf* to display strength before the Meccan polytheists) has passed since Allah destroyed them, yet he touches the stone (*istalama*, and kisses it in bukhari:1597) and maintains *ramal* solely because Muhammad did so. Classical commentators (Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawi) confirm that both pre-Islamic ritual forms are retained strictly as acts of devotional imitation (*ta'abbud*) after their original rationale expired, contrasting with biblical prohibitions against setting up or venerating sacred stones ([Leviticus 26:1](bible://lv/26/1)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ لِلرُّكْنِ أَمَا وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لأَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ حَجَرٌ لاَ تَضُرُّ وَلاَ تَنْفَعُ، وَلَوْلاَ أَنِّي رَأَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم اسْتَلَمَكَ مَا اسْتَلَمْتُكَ‏.‏ فَاسْتَلَمَهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ فَمَا لَنَا وَلِلرَّمَلِ إِنَّمَا كُنَّا رَاءَيْنَا بِهِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ، وَقَدْ أَهْلَكَهُمُ اللَّهُ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ شَىْءٌ صَنَعَهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلاَ نُحِبُّ أَنْ نَتْرُكَهُ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: `Umar bin Al-Khattab addressed the Corner (Black Stone) saying, 'By Allah! I know that you are a stone and can neither benefit nor harm. Had I not seen the Prophet (ﷺ) touching (and kissing) you, I would never have touched (and kissed) you.' Then he kissed it and said, 'There is no reason for us to do Ramal (in Tawaf) except that we wanted to show off before the pagans, and now Allah has destroyed them.' `Umar added, '(Nevertheless), the Prophet (ﷺ) did that and we do not want to leave it (i.e. Ramal)

bukhari:1605.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Umar's declaration (as explained by Ibn Hajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī in Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim) exemplifies pure monotheism (tawḥīd) and ritual submission (taʿabbud), claiming he spoke aloud only to teach recent converts that stones hold no independent power. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Umar himself recognized the stone as completely inert (ḥajar lā taḍurru wa-lā tanfaʿu) and the brisk walk of ramal as an obsolete display for pagans (rāʾaynā bihi al-mushrikīn), yet felt compelled to perpetuate both pre-Islamic litholatric customs solely out of blind imitation of Muhammad (shayʾun ṣanaʿahu al-nabiyyu fa-lā nuḥibbu an natrukahu).

bukhari:1605.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
bukhari:1605.subcategory: Uncreated Divine Word, Original Sin & Sacramental Relics (Trinitarian & Soteriological Precedents)
bukhari:1605.note: Umar addresses the Black Stone using the Quranic anti-idolatry formula—'I know that you are a stone that neither harms nor benefits' (cf. [Quran 20:89](quran://20/89), [Quran 21:66](quran://21/66))—before touching it (*istalama*, and kissing it in bukhari:1597) solely because he saw Muhammad do so. To reconcile this act with strict monotheism, classical commentators (Al-Tabari, Al-Nawawi, and Ibn Hajar) distinguish between worshipping an object for intrinsic power and venerating a physical symbol out of obedience to God—the same theological distinction Christians make regarding crosses, icons, and relics.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ لِلرُّكْنِ أَمَا وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لأَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ حَجَرٌ لاَ تَضُرُّ وَلاَ تَنْفَعُ، وَلَوْلاَ أَنِّي رَأَيْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم اسْتَلَمَكَ مَا اسْتَلَمْتُكَ‏.‏ فَاسْتَلَمَهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ فَمَا لَنَا وَلِلرَّمَلِ إِنَّمَا كُنَّا رَاءَيْنَا بِهِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ، وَقَدْ أَهْلَكَهُمُ اللَّهُ‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَالَ شَىْءٌ صَنَعَهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلاَ نُحِبُّ أَنْ نَتْرُكَهُ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: `Umar bin Al-Khattab addressed the Corner (Black Stone) saying, 'By Allah! I know that you are a stone and can neither benefit nor harm. Had I not seen the Prophet (ﷺ) touching (and kissing) you, I would never have touched (and kissed) you.' Then he kissed it and said, 'There is no reason for us to do Ramal (in Tawaf) except that we wanted to show off before the pagans, and now Allah has destroyed them.' `Umar added, '(Nevertheless), the Prophet (ﷺ) did that and we do not want to leave it (i.e. Ramal)

bukhari:1605.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that kissing the Black Stone is purely an act of prophetic obedience (ittibāʿ) devoid of any belief in the stone's efficacy, whereas Christian veneration of crosses, icons, and relics constitutes polytheistic idolatry (shirk). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Umar physically kissed and honored an inanimate object while confessing it neither harms nor benefits (lā taḍurru wa-lā tanfaʿu) solely out of love and imitation of Muhammad (lawlā annī raʾaytu al-nabiyya صلى الله عليه وسلم istalamaka mā istalamtuka), conceding the exact theological distinction between relative honor toward a sacred symbol and worship of God that Christians maintain.

muslim:7151.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
muslim:7151.note: Via Abu Hurayrah, Muhammad states that the first group to enter Paradise will have forms like the full moon, will neither spit, blow their noses, nor defecate, and will possess gold and silver vessels and combs, aloeswood braziers, and sweat of musk. Each of them will have two spouses whose leg bone marrow is visible from behind their flesh due to their beauty (cf. bukhari:3245, bukhari:3254, muslim:7152).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ أَوَّلُ زُمْرَةٍ تَلِجُ الْجَنَّةَ صُوَرُهُمْ عَلَى صُورَةِ الْقَمَرِ لَيْلَةَ الْبَدْرِ لاَ يَبْصُقُونَ فِيهَا وَلاَ يَمْتَخِطُونَ وَلاَ يَتَغَوَّطُونَ فِيهَا آنِيَتُهُمْ وَأَمْشَاطُهُمْ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ وَمَجَامِرُهُمْ مِنَ الأَلُوَّةِ وَرَشْحُهُمُ الْمِسْكُ وَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمْ زَوْجَتَانِ يُرَى مُخُّ سَاقِهِمَا مِنْ وَرَاءِ اللَّحْمِ مِنَ الْحُسْنِ
problematic_excerpt.english: The (members of the) first group that would be admitted to Paradise would have their faces as bright as full moon during the night. They would neither spit nor suffer catarrh, nor void excrement. They would have their utensils and their combs made of gold and silver and the fuel of their braziers would be aloes and their sweat would be musk and every one of them would have two spouses (so beautiful) that the marrow of their shanks would be visible through the flesh.

muslim:7151.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islamic descriptions of Paradise are metaphorical illustrations of spiritual bliss, pointing to the closing clause where the inhabitants glorify Allah morning and evening with united hearts (`قُلُوبُهُمْ قَلْبٌ وَاحِدٌ يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّهَ بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا`). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states concrete anatomical and material realities—specifying that inhabitants neither spit, blow their noses, nor defecate (`لاَ يَبْصُقُونَ فِيهَا وَلاَ يَمْتَخِطُونَ وَلاَ يَتَغَوَّطُونَ`), sweat musk (`وَرَشْحُهُمُ الْمِسْكُ`), use gold and silver utensils and combs (`آنِيَتُهُمْ وَأَمْشَاطُهُمْ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ`), and each receive two wives whose shank marrow is visible through their flesh (`وَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمْ زَوْجَتَانِ يُرَى مُخُّ سَاقِهِمَا مِنْ وَرَاءِ اللَّحْمِ`). This physical and marital depiction of heaven stands in direct contrast to the biblical teaching that in the resurrection people neither marry nor are given in marriage ([Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30)) and that the Kingdom of God consists of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit ([Romans 14:17](bible://rom/14/17)).

muslim:7173.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
muslim:7173.note: Muhammad states that after Paradise and Hell dispute with one another, Allah declares that each will receive its fill, yet Hell will not be filled until He places His foot (*qadamahu*) upon it, causing it to cry out 'Enough, enough!' as its parts contract together ([Quran 50:30](quran://50/30), bukhari:4848, bukhari:4850, muslim:7175).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ اللَّهُ لِلْجَنَّةِ أَنْتِ رَحْمَتِي أَرْحَمُ بِكِ مَنْ أَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِي ‏.‏ وَقَالَ لِلنَّارِ أَنْتِ عَذَابِي أُعَذِّبُ بِكِ مَنْ أَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِي وَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْكُمْ مِلْؤُهَا فَأَمَّا النَّارُ فَلاَ تَمْتَلِئُ ‏.‏ فَيَضَعُ قَدَمَهُ عَلَيْهَا فَتَقُولُ قَطْ قَطْ ‏.‏ فَهُنَالِكَ تَمْتَلِئُ وَيُزْوَى بَعْضُهَا إِلَى بَعْضٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: Thereupon Allah said to the Paradise: You are (the means) of My Mercy whereby I show mercy to those of My servants whom 1 wish, and He said to the Hell: You are (the means) of punishment whereby 1 punish those of My servants whoml wish. Both of you will be full. The Hell will riot be filled up until Allah puts down His foot in it. The Hell would say: Enough, enough, enough, and at that time it will be filled up, all its parts integrated together

muslim:7173.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *qadamahu* ('His foot') is either a metaphor for those sent ahead into the Fire or an attribute affirmed without physical modality (*bilā kayf*) to express divine power. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that after Allah promises both Paradise and Hell their fill (*milʾuhā*), Hell remains unfilled until He places His foot upon it (*fayaḍaʿu qadamahu ʿalayhā*), which causes it to cry out 'Enough, enough!' (*qaṭ qaṭ*) as its parts contract into one another (*wayuzwā baʿḍuhā ilā baʿḍin*). Depicting Allah's foot as the volume that fills and compresses the space of Hell reduces God to a localized body, contradicting the biblical teaching that God is spirit ([John 4:24](bible://jn/4/24)).

muslim:7175.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
muslim:7175.note: Muhammad declares that after Paradise and Hell dispute over their inhabitants, Allah promises to fill both: Hell will not be filled until Allah places His leg or foot (*rijlahu*) into it, causing it to cry 'Enough, enough, enough!' and draw together, whereas Allah creates a new creation to fill Paradise ([Quran 50:30](quran://50/30)). Parallel accounts in muslim:7173, muslim:7177, and bukhari:4848 corroborate this report using the explicit term *qadamahu* (His foot) for what Allah places into Hell.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ اللَّهُ لِلْجَنَّةِ إِنَّمَا أَنْتِ رَحْمَتِي أَرْحَمُ بِكِ مَنْ أَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِي ‏.‏ وَقَالَ لِلنَّارِ إِنَّمَا أَنْتِ عَذَابِي أُعَذِّبُ بِكِ مَنْ أَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِي ‏.‏ وَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْكُمَا مِلْؤُهَا فَأَمَّا النَّارُ فَلاَ تَمْتَلِئُ حَتَّى يَضَعَ اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى رِجْلَهُ تَقُولُ قَطْ قَطْ قَطْ ‏.‏ فَهُنَالِكَ تَمْتَلِئُ وَيُزْوَى بَعْضُهَا إِلَى بَعْضٍ وَلاَ يَظْلِمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ أَحَدًا وَأَمَّا الْجَنَّةُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُنْشِئُ لَهَا خَلْقًا
problematic_excerpt.english: Thereupon Allah said to Paradise: You are a (means) of My Mercy. 1 shall show mercy through you to one whom I will from amongst My servants. And lie said to the Hell: You are a (sign) of My chastisement and I shall chastise through you anyone whom I will from amongst My servants and both of you, would be full. And as regards the Hell it would not be full until Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, places His foot therein, and it would say: Enough, enough, enough, and it would be then full and the one part would draw very close to the other one and Allah would not treat unjustly anyone amongst His creation and He would create another creation for the Paradise (to accommodate it)

muslim:7175.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the Arabic word *rijlahu* ('His foot') is either a figure of speech for divine subjugation or denotes a 'group' of sinners whom Allah casts into Hell to fill it. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah places His own foot (*yaḍaʿa Allāhu tabāraka wa-taʿālā rijlahu*) into the Fire specifically because 'Allah would not treat unjustly anyone amongst His creation' (*wa-lā yaẓlimu Allāhu min khalqihi aḥadan*) by creating new souls merely to burn, contrasting Hell directly with Paradise, for which alone 'Allah creates a creation' (*fa-inna Allāha yunshiʾu lahā khalqan*). Furthermore, the narration details a physical action in which the parts of Hell 'draw very close to one another' (*yuzwā baʿḍuhā ilā baʿḍin*) beneath His foot until the Fire cries out, 'Enough, enough, enough!' (*qaṭ qaṭ qaṭ*), a bodily placement reinforced across parallel Sahih reports (bukhari:4848, bukhari:7449, muslim:7173).

muslim:7177.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
muslim:7177.note: Muhammad states that Hell will continue asking, 'Is there anything more?' ([Quran 50:30](quran://50/30)) until the Lord of Honor places His foot (*qadamahu*) into it, causing its parts to draw close together as it cries, 'Enough, enough, by Your Honor!' Parallel narrations (muslim:7176, muslim:7179) explain that Allah fulfills His prior oath to fill Hell by placing His own foot inside it.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لاَ تَزَالُ جَهَنَّمُ تَقُولُ هَلْ مِنْ مَزِيدٍ ‏.‏ حَتَّى يَضَعَ فِيهَا رَبُّ الْعِزَّةِ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى قَدَمَهُ فَتَقُولُ قَطْ قَطْ وَعِزَّتِكَ ‏.‏ وَيُزْوَى بَعْضُهَا إِلَى بَعْضٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: Anas b. Malik reported that Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) said that the Hell would continue to say:Is there anything more, until Allah, the Exalted and High, would place His foot therein and that would say: Enough, enough, by Your Honour, and some parts of it would draw close to the other

muslim:7177.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *qadamahu* ('His foot') is either a linguistic metaphor for a group of people sent ahead into Hell or a figurative expression of divine power subduing the Fire without bodily contact. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that 'the Lord of Might, Blessed and Exalted, would place His foot therein' (*ḥattā yaḍaʿa fīhā rabbu l-ʿizzati tabāraka wa-taʿālā qadamahu*), which directly causes the parts of Hell to contract and draw close to one another (*wa-yuzwā baʿḍuhā ilā baʿḍin*) until it cries out, 'Enough, enough, by Your Honour!' (*qaṭ qaṭ wa-ʿizzatika*). This direct action of Allah placing (*yaḍaʿa*) His own foot inside (*fīhā*) to compress Hell after it asks 'Is there anything more?' ([Quran 50:30](quran://50/30)) refutes attempts to reduce the term to human inhabitants or abstract authority (cf. `bukhari:4848`, `bukhari:6661`, `muslim:7179`).

muslim:7179.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
muslim:7179.note: Commenting on [Quran 50:30](quran://50/30), Muhammad states via Anas ibn Malik that sinners will continue to be thrown into Hell while it asks for more until the Lord of Might (*Rabb al-'Izzah*) places His foot (*qadamahu*) into it, causing its parts to draw together and cry, 'Enough, enough, by Your Might and Generosity!'

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لاَ تَزَالُ جَهَنَّمُ يُلْقَى فِيهَا وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِنْ مَزِيدٍ حَتَّى يَضَعَ رَبُّ الْعِزَّةِ فِيهَا قَدَمَهُ فَيَنْزَوِي بَعْضُهَا إِلَى بَعْضٍ وَتَقُولُ قَطْ قَطْ بِعِزَّتِكَ وَكَرَمِكَ
problematic_excerpt.english: (The sinners) would be thrown therein and it would continue to say: Is there anything more, until Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, would keep His foot there- in and some of its part would draw close to the other and it would say: Enough, enough, by Thy Honour and by Thy Dignity

muslim:7179.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that *qadamahu* ('His foot') is either a metaphor for a group of sinners sent ahead into Hell or a non-spatial attribute that does not occupy physical space. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that 'the Lord of Honor places His foot into it' (*ḥattā yaḍaʿa rabbu al-ʿizzati fīhā qadamahu*), which physically compresses Hell so that 'some of its parts draw close to the others' (*fayanzawī baʿḍuhā ilā baʿḍin*) until it cries out, 'Enough, enough!' Furthermore, the narration directly contrasts Allah filling Hell with His own foot against how He fills the remaining space in Paradise by creating 'a new creation' (*yunshiʾa Allāhu lahā khalqan*) to inhabit it, refuting the claim that 'His foot' refers to a created group of people.

bukhari:7449.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
bukhari:7449.note: Muhammad states that Hellfire will continue asking for more until Allah places His foot in it (*yada'a fiha qadamahu*), causing its parts to compress together until it cries, 'Enough!' (contrasting with [John 4:24](bible://jn/4/24)). While some commentators attempt to allegorize *qadamahu* as 'those sent ahead,' parallel narrations (such as bukhari:4848) explicitly use the anatomical term *rijlahu* (His leg/foot), leading Athari scholars to affirm a literal divine foot placed into the Fire.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِنْ مَزِيدٍ‏.‏ ثَلاَثًا، حَتَّى يَضَعَ فِيهَا قَدَمَهُ فَتَمْتَلِئُ وَيُرَدُّ بَعْضُهَا إِلَى بَعْضٍ وَتَقُولُ قَطْ قَطْ قَطْ
problematic_excerpt.english: and it will say thrice, 'Is there any more, till Allah (will put) His Foot over it and it will become full and its sides will come close to each other and it will say, 'Qat! Qat! Qat! (Enough! Enough! Enough)

bukhari:7449.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—following Ash'ari commentators cited by Al-Nawawī and Ibn Hajar—that `قَدَمَهُ` (*qadamahu*) is a figurative idiom for sinners whom Allah 'sent forth' (*qaddama*) into Hell, or they invoke *bilā kayf* ('without asking how') to deny that Allah physically steps into His own creation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `حَتَّى يَضَعَ فِيهَا قَدَمَهُ فَتَمْتَلِئُ وَيُرَدُّ بَعْضُهَا إِلَى بَعْضٍ` ('until He places His foot *in it*, so it becomes full and its parts are compressed into one another'), describing a spatial, physical compression of the Fire that English translators dishonestly soften to 'over it.' Moreover, the parallel narration in bukhari:4848 replaces `قَدَمَهُ` with the unmistakable anatomical noun `رِجْلَهُ` (*rijlahu*, 'His leg/foot'), which cannot lexically mean 'those sent ahead' and locks Sunni orthodoxy into a crudely corporeal deity.

bukhari:7449.note: Muhammad declares that Allah originates for Hellfire whomever He wills and casts them into it so that it may be filled, contrasting with [1 Timothy 2:4](bible://1tm/2/4). Because parallel narrations (such as bukhari:4848) state that Allah originates this new creation for Paradise rather than Hell, classical commentators like Ibn Hajar either affirm that Allah creates people specifically for Hellfire ([Quran 7:179](quran://7/179)) or concede that a narrator inverted (*qalb*) the text in Sahih al-Bukhari.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَإِنَّهُ يُنْشِئُ لِلنَّارِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ فَيُلْقَوْنَ فِيهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: He creates for Hell (Fire) whomever He will, and they will be thrown into it

bukhari:7449.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this passage merely reflects Allah's passive foreknowledge of human free will, or they cite Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* to claim the narrator accidentally inverted the wording (*maqlūb*) and meant to say Allah creates extra people for Paradise rather than Hell. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `وَإِنَّهُ يُنْشِئُ لِلنَّارِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ فَيُلْقَوْنَ فِيهَا` ('and indeed He originates for the Fire whomever He wills, and they are thrown into it'), directly contrasting Paradise with Allah's arbitrary decree to populate Hell (`أُصِيبُ بِكِ مَنْ أَشَاءُ`). Furthermore, this fatalistic creation for damnation is corroborated verbatim by Quran 7:179 (`وَلَقَدْ ذَرَأْنَا لِجَهَنَّمَ كَثِيرًا`, 'We have certainly created for Hell many') and muslim:6769, whereas pleading narrator corruption in Bukhari's *Ṣaḥīḥ* only undermines the collection's claimed reliability.

bukhari:7494.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
bukhari:7494.note: Muhammad declares that Allah descends to the lowest heaven (al-sama' al-dunya) during the last third of every night and asks in the first person who is invoking Him or seeking His forgiveness (bukhari:1145). While Ash'ari commentators reinterpret this as the descent of an angel or mercy despite the explicit first-person speech ("Who invokes Me"), literalist Sunni affirmation that Allah Himself enters a created heaven during a fixed nocturnal window both presupposes a single local night and affirms that God can enter creation without compromising His divinity.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: يَتَنَزَّلُ رَبُّنَا تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا حِينَ يَبْقَى ثُلُثُ اللَّيْلِ الآخِرُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Every night when it is the last third of the night, our Lord, the Superior, the Blessed, descends to the nearest heaven

bukhari:7494.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ash'arī commentators like al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar—that this descent is merely a metaphor (ta'wīl) for the descent of Allah's mercy or an appointed angel, or else invoke the Atharī formula of bilā kayf ('without asking how') to evade the spatial and geographical absurdities. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that 'our Lord' Himself descends (yatanazzalu Rabbunā) and speaks in the exclusive first-person singular—'Who invokes Me that I may respond to him?... Who asks forgiveness of Me that I may forgive him?' (man yad'ūnī fa-astajība lahu... man yastaghfirunī fa-aghfira lahu)—divine prerogatives that neither a created angel nor an abstract attribute could ever utter. Moreover, by locking Allah's movement to the temporal window 'when the last third of the night remains' (ḥīna yabqā thuluthu al-layli al-ākhiru), the narration betrays a flat-Earth presupposition of a single universal night, whereas on a spherical globe the last third of the night occurs continuously across rotating time zones, trapping Allah in the lowest heaven permanently.

muslim:464.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
muslim:464.note: Muhammad declares that the lowest-ranking man in Paradise will be granted everything he wishes for plus ten times its like, and will then enter his house where his two wives from among the houris (*zawjatāhu mina al-ḥūri al-ʿīn*) will greet him by praising Allah for bringing him to life for them and them to life for him. This promise of marital consorts in Paradise contrasts directly with Jesus's teaching that those in the resurrection neither marry nor are given in marriage ([Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَيُذَكِّرُهُ اللَّهُ سَلْ كَذَا وَكَذَا فَإِذَا انْقَطَعَتْ بِهِ الأَمَانِيُّ قَالَ اللَّهُ هُوَ لَكَ وَعَشَرَةُ أَمْثَالِهِ - قَالَ - ثُمَّ يَدْخُلُ بَيْتَهُ فَتَدْخُلُ عَلَيْهِ زَوْجَتَاهُ مِنَ الْحُورِ الْعِينِ فَتَقُولاَنِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَاكَ لَنَا وَأَحْيَانَا لَكَ - قَالَ - فَيَقُولُ مَا أُعْطِيَ أَحَدٌ مِثْلَ مَا أُعْطِيتُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah will remind him: Ask such and such, and when his expectations would be realised, Allah would say: That is for you, and ten times as much. He said that he would then enter his house and his two wives with large and dark eyes would enter after him. They will say: Praise be to Allah, Who has created you for us and us for you. He will say: No one has been given the like of what I have been given

muslim:464.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that descriptions of the *ḥūr al-ʿīn* are either metaphorical accommodations for human comprehension—invoking the maxim that Paradise shares only names with worldly things—or represent purified, holistic companionship rather than carnal indulgence. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that two consorts from among the houris (*zawjatāhu mina al-ḥūri al-ʿīn*) physically enter upon the man in his house and declare that Allah brought them to life exclusively for him (*aḥyāka lanā wa-aḥyānā laka*), a literal reality the English translator masks by euphemistically rendering the technical term as 'two wives with large and dark eyes.' Moreover, Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and parallel Sahih narrations (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 3254; *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2834a) confirm that these two wives are literal, specially created celestial females whose hyper-physical anatomy—down to the marrow of their shins visible through their flesh—is designed for bodily pleasure.

muslim:469.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
muslim:469.note: In Jabir ibn 'Abdullah's account of the Day of Resurrection (explicitly traced to Muhammad in muslim:470), when Allah comes to the community and declares, 'I am your Lord,' they reply, '[Wait] until we look at You,' whereupon He manifests Himself to them laughing (*yaḍḥaku*, softened to 'smilingly' in the English translation) and leads them forward ([John 4:24](bible://jn/4/24)). Every believer and hypocrite is then given a light to follow Him toward the hooked and spiked bridge of Hell, where the hypocrites' light is extinguished while the believers are saved ([1 John 1:5](bible://1jn/1/5)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: ثُمَّ يَأْتِينَا رَبُّنَا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَيَقُولُ مَنْ تَنْظُرُونَ فَيَقُولُونَ نَنْظُرُ رَبَّنَا ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُونَ حَتَّى نَنْظُرَ إِلَيْكَ ‏.‏ فَيَتَجَلَّى لَهُمْ يَضْحَكُ - قَالَ - فَيَنْطَلِقُ بِهِمْ وَيَتَّبِعُونَهُ وَيُعْطَى كُلُّ إِنْسَانٍ مِنْهُمْ - مُنَافِقٍ أَوْ مُؤْمِنٍ - نُورًا ثُمَّ يَتَّبِعُونَهُ وَعَلَى جِسْرِ جَهَنَّمَ كَلاَلِيبُ وَحَسَكٌ تَأْخُذُ مَنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ يَطْفَأُ نُورُ الْمُنَافِقِينَ
problematic_excerpt.english: Then our Lord would come to us and say: Whom are you waiting for? They would say: We are waiting for our Lord. He would say: I am your Lord. They would say: (We are not sure) till we gaze at Thee, and He would manifest Himself to them smilingly, and would go along with them and they would follow Him; and every person, whether a hypocrite or a believer, would be endowed with a light, and there would be spikes and hooks on the bridge of the Hell, which would catch hold of those whom Allah willed. Then the light of the hypocrites would be extinguished

muslim:469.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, following Ash'ari commentators like Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that Allah's laughing (*yaḍḥaku*) is merely a metaphor for divine pleasure (*riḍā*) and that the unrecognized figure testing the believers is a created image or angel rather than Allah Himself. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Lord Himself approaches (*ya'tīnā Rabbunā*), declares 'I am your Lord' (*anā Rabbukum*), and visually manifests Himself laughing (*fayatajallā lahum yaḍḥaku*) before physically walking ahead of the crowd (*fayanṭaliqu bihim wayattabi'ūnahu*). Parallel Sahih accounts (bukhari:7439, muslim:454) cement this literal anthropomorphism by specifying that Allah initially appears in an altered form (*fī ṣūratin ghayri ṣūratihi*) and must bare His physical shin (*sāq*) to prove His identity, right before baiting hypocrites onto the hooked bridge of Hell with a temporary light only to extinguish it (*yuṭfa'u nūru al-munāfiqīn*).

bukhari:7438.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
bukhari:7438.note: Muhammad declares that on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will first come to the Muslim community in an unrecognized appearance, be denied by them, and then return 'in His form (ṣūratihi) which they know' so that they recognize and follow Him.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَيَأْتِيهِمُ اللَّهُ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُونَ هَذَا مَكَانُنَا حَتَّى يَأْتِيَنَا رَبُّنَا فَإِذَا جَاءَنَا رَبُّنَا عَرَفْنَاهُ فَيَأْتِيهِمُ اللَّهُ فِي صُورَتِهِ الَّتِي يَعْرِفُونَ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah will come to them and say, 'I am your Lord.' They will (deny Him and) say, 'We will stay here till our Lord comes, for when our Lord comes, we will recognize Him.' So Allah will come to them in His appearance which they know, and will say, 'I am your Lord.'

bukhari:7438.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the word ṣūrah ('form') in this narration—as rationalized by Al-Nawawī in Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and Ibn Ḥajar in Fatḥ al-Bārī—merely denotes a metaphorical attribute (ṣifah) or a perceptual test in the eyes of the beholders rather than Allah physically changing shape. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states fa-ya'tīhimu Allāhu fī ṣūratihi allatī ya'rifūna ('So Allah will come to them in His form which they know'), while immediate parallel narrations (bukhari:7439; muslim:451) specify that Allah initially arrives in an unrecognizable form, declares Anā Rabbukum ('I am your Lord'), and then transforms (fa-yataḥawwalu) and uncovers His shin (sāq) so the believers can visually verify Him. This traps Sunni theology in an inescapable dilemma: either Allah possesses a mutable, anatomical body that shifts shapes, or He actively deceives His own followers on Judgment Day in direct contradiction to the Quranic claim of absolute transcendence (Q. 42:11).

muslim:7159.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
muslim:7159.note: Muhammad states that a believer in Paradise will have a sixty-mile-wide hollowed pearl tent with wives (*ahl*) stationed in every corner whom he visits in turn (*yaṭūfu ʿalayhim*) out of sight of one another ([Quran 55:72](quran://55/72), bukhari:4879).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فِي الْجَنَّةِ خَيْمَةٌ مِنْ لُؤْلُؤَةٍ مُجَوَّفَةٍ عَرْضُهَا سِتُّونَ مِيلاً فِي كُلِّ زَاوِيَةٍ مِنْهَا أَهْلٌ مَا يَرَوْنَ الآخَرِينَ يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْمُؤْمِنُ
problematic_excerpt.english: in Paradise there would be a tent made of a single hollowed pearl, the breadth of which would be sixty miles from all sides and there would live a family in each corner and the other would not be able to see the believer who goes around them

muslim:7159.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the term *ahl* merely denotes general family companionship and privacy in a symbolic description of Paradise rather than a physical harem. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the believer 'makes rounds upon them' (*yaṭūfu ʿalayhim*) across the corners of a sixty-mile hollowed pearl tent so they do not see one another, which is the standard Classical Arabic idiom for visiting multiple wives in turn for conjugal relations (`bukhari:3243`, `bukhari:4879`, `muslim:7158`). This depiction of carnal polygyny with consorts secluded in pavilions ([Quran 55:72](quran://55/72)) directly contradicts the Biblical teaching that in the resurrection people neither marry nor are given in marriage ([Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30)).

muslim:7160.subcategory: Crude Anthropomorphism, Carnal Paradise & Pagan Vestiges
muslim:7160.note: Muhammad declares that the believer's tent in Paradise is a pearl extending sixty miles into the sky, housing wives (*ahl*) for the believer in every corner out of sight of the others ([Quran 55:72](quran://55/72)). Parallel narrations add that the believer makes the rounds (*yatufu 'alayhim*) visiting the wives in each corner (bukhari:4879, muslim:7158, muslim:7159).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: الْخَيْمَةُ دُرَّةٌ طُولُهَا فِي السَّمَاءِ سِتُّونَ مِيلاً فِي كُلِّ زَاوِيَةٍ مِنْهَا أَهْلٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ لاَ يَرَاهُمُ الآخَرُونَ
problematic_excerpt.english: there would be a tent made of a pearl whose height towards the sky would be sixty miles. In each corner, there would be a family of the believer, out of sight for the others

muslim:7160.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the term *ahl* refers simply to a general family household in Paradise and that the description of the pearl pavilion is metaphorical rather than a literal arrangement of multiple wives. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that inside a pearl tent extending sixty miles into the sky (*al-khaymah durrah ṭūluhā fī al-samāʾ sittūna mīlan*), the believer has *ahl* (wives) stationed in every corner who are kept out of sight of the others (*fī kulli zāwiyah minhā ahlun lil-muʾmin lā yarāhum al-ākharūn*), matching [Quran 55:72](quran://55/72) and the parallel reports in `bukhari:4879`, `muslim:7158`, and `muslim:7159`. This depiction of separate wives partitioned across the corners of a physical tent stands in direct contrast to Jesus's teaching that in the resurrection people neither marry nor are given in marriage ([Matthew 22:30](bible://mt/22/30)).

muslim:7014.note: Muhammad declares that people among the Muslims will come on the Day of Resurrection with sins like mountains (*bi-dhunūbin amthāli al-jibāl*), and Allah will forgive those sins for them and place them upon the Jews and the Christians (*wa-yaḍaʿuhā ʿalā al-yahūdi wa-al-naṣārā*). Because the feminine object pronoun (*-hā*) in *wa-yaḍaʿuhā* refers grammatically to the Muslims' own sins (*dhunūb*) rather than merely inheriting spaces in Hellfire (cf. muslim:7012), the statement contradicts the principle in [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164) that no soul bears the burden of another.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ يَجِيءُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ نَاسٌ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ بِذُنُوبٍ أَمْثَالِ الْجِبَالِ فَيَغْفِرُهَا اللَّهُ لَهُمْ وَيَضَعُهَا عَلَى الْيَهُودِ وَالنَّصَارَى ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Burda reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:There would come people amongst the Muslims on the Day of Resurrection with as heavy sins as a mountain, and Allah would forgive them and He would place in their stead the Jews and the Christians.

muslim:7014.literal_translation: From the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'People from among the Muslims will come on the Day of Resurrection with sins like mountains, and Allah will forgive them for them and will place them (those sins) upon the Jews and the Christians.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَيَغْفِرُهَا اللَّهُ لَهُمْ وَيَضَعُهَا عَلَى الْيَهُودِ وَالنَّصَارَى
translation_issue.published_rendering: and Allah would forgive them and He would place in their stead the Jews and the Christians
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and Allah will forgive them (the sins) for them and place them (the sins) upon the Jews and the Christians
translation_issue.explanation: The feminine singular object pronoun '-hā' in both 'yaghfiruhā' and 'yaḍa'uhā' refers grammatically to the broken plural 'dhunūb' (sins), meaning Allah places the Muslims' sins upon the Jews and Christians, which the translator alters to 'place in their stead' to conceal explicit sin-transfer.

muslim:7014.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration is merely a figurative expression meaning Jews and Christians will occupy the places in Hellfire that Muslims would have filled, or that the sub-narrator Abu Rawh's remark indicates uncertainty in the transmission, so as to avoid contradicting [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *fayaghfiruhā Allāhu lahum wa-yaḍaʿuhā ʿalā al-yahūdi wa-al-naṣārā* ("and Allah will forgive them for them and will place them upon the Jews and the Christians"), where the feminine object pronoun *-hā* in both verbs refers grammatically to the Muslims' mountain-sized sins (*dhunūb*). Furthermore, Abu Burda immediately confirms the narration's chain with 'Umar b. 'Abd al-'Aziz as coming directly from his father from the Prophet, and parallel narrations (muslim:7011, muslim:7012) independently establish that Allah ransoms Muslims from Hellfire using Jews and Christians.

muslim:7014.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:7014.subcategory: Vicarious Ransom, Sin-Transfer & Intercessory Salvation (Atonement Precedents)
muslim:7014.note: Muhammad states that on the Day of Resurrection Allah will forgive Muslims' mountain-sized sins (*dhunūb*) and place them upon the Jews and the Christians (*wa-yaḍaʿuhā ʿalā al-yahūdi wa-al-naṣārā*), a report that ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz explicitly confirmed with the narrator Abū Burda. Alongside the parallel report designating Jews and Christians as a Muslim's ransom from the Fire (*fakākuka min al-nār* in muslim:7011), this grammatical transfer of sins (*-hā*) onto others concedes the mechanism of vicarious sin-transfer and substitutionary atonement ([Isaiah 53:6](bible://is/53/6), [2 Corinthians 5:21](bible://2cor/5/21)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ يَجِيءُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ نَاسٌ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ بِذُنُوبٍ أَمْثَالِ الْجِبَالِ فَيَغْفِرُهَا اللَّهُ لَهُمْ وَيَضَعُهَا عَلَى الْيَهُودِ وَالنَّصَارَى ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Burda reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying:There would come people amongst the Muslims on the Day of Resurrection with as heavy sins as a mountain, and Allah would forgive them and He would place in their stead the Jews and the Christians.

muslim:7014.literal_translation: From the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'People from among the Muslims will come on the Day of Resurrection with sins like mountains, and Allah will forgive them for them and will place them (those sins) upon the Jews and the Christians.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَيَغْفِرُهَا اللَّهُ لَهُمْ وَيَضَعُهَا عَلَى الْيَهُودِ وَالنَّصَارَى
translation_issue.published_rendering: and Allah would forgive them and He would place in their stead the Jews and the Christians
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and Allah will forgive them (the sins) for them and place them (the sins) upon the Jews and the Christians
translation_issue.explanation: The feminine singular object pronoun '-hā' in both 'yaghfiruhā' and 'yaḍa'uhā' refers grammatically to the broken plural 'dhunūb' (sins), meaning Allah places the Muslims' sins upon the Jews and Christians, which the translator alters to 'place in their stead' to conceal explicit sin-transfer.

muslim:7014.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islam rejects all forms of vicarious sin-transfer as unjust, claiming via the softened English rendering ("place in their stead") that Jews and Christians merely enter Hell for their own disbelief or only bear the guilt of those they personally misled. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *bi-dhunūbin amthāli al-jibāli fayaghfiruhā Allāhu lahum wa-yaḍaʿuhā ʿalā al-yahūdi wa-al-naṣārā*, using the exact same feminine object pronoun (*-hā*) for the mountain-sized sins (*dhunūb*) that Allah forgives for the Muslims and then places (*yaḍaʿuhā*) directly onto the Jews and Christians without any qualification that those non-Muslims caused them. While this narration alongside muslim:7011 and muslim:7012 concedes the mechanism of substitutionary sin-transfer by forcing unwilling Jews and Christians to bear Muslim guilt, the Biblical atonement in [Isaiah 53:6](bible://is/53/6) and [2 Corinthians 5:21](bible://2cor/5/21) is the voluntary, sinless self-sacrifice of Christ for all humanity.

bukhari:3409.note: Muhammad declares twice that Adam defeated Moses in argument when Moses rebuked him for the sin (khaṭī'atuka) that expelled him from Paradise, as Adam countered that he should not be blamed for a matter Allah had already decreed upon him before he was created.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: احْتَجَّ آدَمُ وَمُوسَى فَقَالَ لَهُ مُوسَى أَنْتَ آدَمُ الَّذِي أَخْرَجَتْكَ خَطِيئَتُكَ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُ آدَمُ أَنْتَ مُوسَى الَّذِي اصْطَفَاكَ اللَّهُ بِرِسَالاَتِهِ وَبِكَلاَمِهِ، ثُمَّ تَلُومُنِي عَلَى أَمْرٍ قُدِّرَ عَلَىَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ أُخْلَقَ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى ‏"‏ مَرَّتَيْنِ
problematic_excerpt.english: Adam and Moses argued with each other. Moses said to Adam. 'You are Adam whose mistake expelled you from Paradise.' Adam said to him, 'You are Moses whom Allah selected as His Messenger and as the one to whom He spoke directly; yet you blame me for a thing which had already been written in my fate before my creation?"' Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said twice, "So, Adam overpowered Moses

bukhari:3409.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that Adam did not use predestination to excuse his sin, claiming Moses only lamented the earthly calamity of leaving Paradise rather than the disobedience itself, or that Adam was only immune from blame because he had already repented. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Moses indicted Adam directly for his moral fault (*أَخْرَجَتْكَ خَطِيئَتُكَ*, 'your sin expelled you'), and parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:6614`, `muslim:6742`) confirm that Adam defended the act of eating from the tree itself as decreed forty years before his creation. Crucially, Adam never mentions repentance (*tawbah*) in his defense, appealing exclusively to pre-creation fatalism (*أَمْرٍ قُدِّرَ عَلَيَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ أُخْلَقَ*), which Muhammad twice endorses as a decisive refutation (*فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى*).

muslim:6401.note: When Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah is caught sending a letter to the polytheists of Mecca informing them of Muhammad's affairs and Umar asks permission to behead him as a hypocrite, Muhammad pardons him because he participated in Badr, stating that Allah looked upon the people of Badr and declared, 'Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you' ([Quran 60:1](quran://60/1); bukhari:3007, bukhari:4890). This exemption for veterans of Badr is reaffirmed when Hatib's slave complains against him and Muhammad replies that Hatib cannot enter Hell because he witnessed Badr and Hudaybiyyah (muslim:6403).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ عُمَرُ دَعْنِي يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَضْرِبْ عُنُقَ هَذَا الْمُنَافِقِ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّهُ قَدْ شَهِدَ بَدْرًا وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ اطَّلَعَ عَلَى أَهْلِ بَدْرٍ فَقَالَ اعْمَلُوا مَا شِئْتُمْ فَقَدْ غَفَرْتُ لَكُمْ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: 'Umar said: Allah's Messenger, permit me to strike the neck of this hypocrite. But he (the Holy Prophet) said: He was a participant in Badr and you little know that Allah revealed about the people of Badr: Do what you like for there is forgiveness for you.

muslim:6401.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the declaration to the veterans of Badr is merely rhetorical praise or reflects Allah's foreknowledge of their future righteousness, rather than a license to commit sin with impunity. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `إِنَّهُ قَدْ شَهِدَ بَدْرًا ... اعْمَلُوا مَا شِئْتُمْ فَقَدْ غَفَرْتُ لَكُمْ` ('He was a participant in Badr ... Do what you like, for I have forgiven you'), applying this blanket pardon as the direct legal ruling to stop Umar from beheading Hatib (`أَضْرِبْ عُنُقَ هَذَا الْمُنَافِقِ`) after he was caught sending intelligence to the polytheists of Mecca (`الْمُشْرِكِينَ مِنْ أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ`). The accompanying citation of [Quran 60:1](quran://60/1) (`لاَ تَتَّخِذُوا عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمْ أَوْلِيَاءَ`) confirms that Hatib committed an active offense that was exempted from punishment solely because of his past military service at Badr (`bukhari:3007`, `bukhari:4890`, `muslim:6403`), contrasting with the New Testament teaching that forgiveness never licenses transgression ([Romans 6:1](bible://rom/6/1)).

bukhari:7487.note: Muhammad reports that Gabriel brought him glad tidings that anyone who dies without associating partners with Allah will enter Paradise, explicitly confirming that this guarantee holds even if the person commits theft and adultery (contrast with [1 Corinthians 6:9-10](bible://1cor/6/9)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَتَانِي جِبْرِيلُ فَبَشَّرَنِي أَنَّهُ مَنْ مَاتَ لاَ يُشْرِكُ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قُلْتُ وَإِنْ سَرَقَ وَإِنْ زَنَى قَالَ ‏"‏ وَإِنْ سَرَقَ وَإِنْ زَنَى
problematic_excerpt.english: anyone who died without worshipping anything besides Allah, would enter Paradise. I asked (Gabriel), 'Even if he committed theft, and even if he committed illegal sexual intercourse?' He said, '(Yes), even if he committed theft, and even if he Committed illegal sexual intercourse

bukhari:7487.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration does not grant moral license, claiming via Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* that unrepentant thieves and adulterers must either repent before death or suffer temporary punishment in Hellfire before eventually entering Paradise.
