However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states without qualification that anyone who dies avoiding *shirk* enters Paradise (`مَنْ مَاتَ لاَ يُشْرِكُ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ`) 'even if he committed theft and even if he committed adultery' (`وَإِنْ سَرَقَ وَإِنْ زَنَى`), containing zero mention of repentance (*tawbah*) or purgatorial torment. Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:5827; muslim:272) record that when Abu Dharr repeatedly objected in shock at this unconditional guarantee, Muhammad silenced him by declaring 'even in spite of Abu Dharr's defiance' (`وَإِنْ رَغِمَ أَنْفُ أَبِي ذَرٍّ`), confirming that Islamic soteriology reduces divine justice to ritual monotheism where grave moral depravity is arbitrarily excused (cf. [Quran 4:48](quran://4/48)).

bukhari:4850.note: Muhammad declares that Hellfire will not be filled until Allah places His foot (*rijlahu*) over it, causing its parts to draw together and cry out, 'Enough, enough, enough!' while Allah creates a new creation to fill Paradise ([Quran 50:30](quran://50/30)). This explicit attribution of a divine foot entering Hellfire sparked classical Sunni disputes between literalist affirmation and Ash'ari metaphorical reinterpretation (*ta'wil*), and directly contradicts Islamic polemics claiming God cannot enter created space.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَمَّا النَّارُ فَلاَ تَمْتَلِئُ حَتَّى يَضَعَ رِجْلَهُ فَتَقُولُ قَطٍ قَطٍ قَطٍ‏.‏ فَهُنَالِكَ تَمْتَلِئُ وَيُزْوَى بَعْضُهَا إِلَى بَعْضٍ، وَلاَ يَظْلِمُ اللَّهُ ـ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ـ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ أَحَدًا، وَأَمَّا الْجَنَّةُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ يُنْشِئُ لَهَا خَلْقًا
problematic_excerpt.english: As for the Fire (Hell), it will not be filled till Allah puts His Foot over it whereupon it will say, 'Qati! Qati!' At that time it will be filled, and its different parts will come closer to each other; and Allah will not wrong any of His created beings. As regards Paradise, Allah will create a new creation to fill it with

bukhari:4850.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that 'His foot' (rijlahu) is either a figurative expression for a 'multitude of people' sent into Hell (citing Ibn Hajar and Al-Nawawī's lexical appeal to rijl meaning a swarm) or a non-spatial divine attribute affirmed 'without modality' (bi-lā kayf). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah places His foot (ḥattā yaḍa'a rijlahu) into the Fire so that its parts physically contract and compress into one another (wa-yuzwā ba'ḍuhā ilā ba'ḍin) until it cries 'Enough!' (qaṭin qaṭin), and parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:4848, bukhari:4849) substitute the unambiguous anatomical noun qadamahu ('His foot'), which never means a group of people in Classical Arabic and proves a literal, spatial insertion of Allah's limb to fill Hell's volume.

bukhari:5076.note: When Abu Huraira repeatedly asked how to avoid sexual sin (al-'anat) because he could not afford marriage, Muhammad remained silent three times before declaring that the pen has dried regarding what he will encounter, telling him to either castrate himself on that basis or leave it. Although neighboring reports (bukhari:5074, bukhari:5075) prohibit castration—leading commentators like Ibn Hajar to interpret the imperative as an expression of rhetorical futility rather than legal permission—the reply explicitly predicates moral outcomes on an unalterable, pre-written decree.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي رَجُلٌ شَابٌّ وَأَنَا أَخَافُ عَلَى نَفْسِي الْعَنَتَ وَلاَ أَجِدُ مَا أَتَزَوَّجُ بِهِ النِّسَاءَ، فَسَكَتَ عَنِّي، ثُمَّ قُلْتُ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، فَسَكَتَ عَنِّي ثُمَّ قُلْتُ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، فَسَكَتَ عَنِّي ثُمَّ قُلْتُ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ يَا أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ جَفَّ الْقَلَمُ بِمَا أَنْتَ لاَقٍ، فَاخْتَصِ عَلَى ذَلِكَ أَوْ ذَرْ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: I said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! I am a young man and I am afraid that I may commit illegal sexual intercourse and I cannot afford to marry." He kept silent, and then repeated my question once again, but he kept silent. I said the same (for the third time) and he remained silent. Then repeated my question (for the fourth time), and only then the Prophet said, "O Abu Huraira! The pen has dried after writing what you are going to confront. So (it does not matter whether you) get yourself castrated or not

bukhari:5076.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's reply is merely a rhetorical rebuke (*tahdīd*) against self-mutilation and an affirmation of divine foreknowledge rather than moral fatalism, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and noting that fasting is prescribed elsewhere to curb desire. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `جَفَّ الْقَلَمُ بِمَا أَنْتَ لاَقٍ، فَاخْتَصِ عَلَى ذَلِكَ أَوْ ذَرْ` ('The pen has dried with what you are going to confront, so castrate yourself upon that or leave it'), answering a young man's desperate plea to avoid sexual sin (`الْعَنَتَ`) after three cold silences by declaring that human preventative effort is futile against pre-written fate. This hard determinism is confirmed by Abu Huraira's parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:6612`, `muslim:6735`), where Muhammad declares that Allah has already written upon every person an inescapable share of fornication that he will inevitably commit (`كَتَبَ اللَّهُ عَلَى ابْنِ آدَمَ نَصِيبَهُ مِنَ الزِّنَا، فَهْوَ مُدْرِكٌ ذَلِكَ لاَ مَحَالَةَ`).

bukhari:3047.note: Ali ibn Abi Talib states that his written scroll (sahifa) of prophetic rulings decrees that a Muslim shall not be executed for killing a disbeliever (la yuqtalu muslimun bi-kafir). Majority Sunni jurisprudence (the Shafi'i, Maliki, and Hanbali schools) upholds this ruling to exempt Muslims from capital retaliation (qisas) for killing non-Muslims, contrasting with the equal standard of capital justice in [Exodus 20:13](bible://ex/20/13) and [Leviticus 24:21-22](bible://lv/24/21).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قُلْتُ وَمَا فِي الصَّحِيفَةِ قَالَ الْعَقْلُ وَفَكَاكُ الأَسِيرِ، وَأَنْ لاَ يُقْتَلَ مُسْلِمٌ بِكَافِرٍ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I asked, "What is written in this paper?" He replied, "(The regulations of) blood-money, the freeing of captives, and the judgment that no Muslim should be killed for killing an infidel

bukhari:3047.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the term *kāfir* (unbeliever) here refers strictly to a hostile enemy combatant (*ḥarbī*) rather than a peaceful non-Muslim subject (*dhimmī*), citing minority Ḥanafī jurisprudence to claim judicial equality. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *lā yuqtala muslimun bi-kāfirin* (لاَ يُقْتَلَ مُسْلِمٌ بِكَافِرٍ, 'no Muslim shall be killed for an unbeliever'), employing an indefinite noun under negation (*nakirah fī siyāq al-nafy*) that grammatically encompasses every non-Muslim without exception. As Ibn Ḥajar explains in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* (on bukhari:6915), because a hostile combatant's blood is already unprotected in Islamic law, restricting this decree to combatants would render the prophetic ruling redundant—which is why the majority of Sunni orthodoxy (the Mālikī, Shāfiʿī, and Ḥanbalī schools) ruled that a Muslim cannot be executed even for murdering an innocent *dhimmī*.

bukhari:806.note: Muhammad states that on the Day of Resurrection, believers will see Allah as clearly as the cloudless sun and full moon, and that when Allah first comes to them declaring, 'I am your Lord,' they will not recognize Him until He comes to them a second time (cf. bukhari:6573, bukhari:7437). The narration further states that Allah laughs at the last man brought out of Hell after the man repeatedly breaks his covenants not to ask for more, before granting him entrance to Paradise.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَيَأْتِيهِمُ اللَّهُ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ فَيَقُولُونَ هَذَا مَكَانُنَا حَتَّى يَأْتِيَنَا رَبُّنَا، فَإِذَا جَاءَ رَبُّنَا عَرَفْنَاهُ‏.‏ فَيَأْتِيهِمُ اللَّهُ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُونَ أَنْتَ رَبُّنَا‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah will come to them and say, 'I am Your Lord.' They will say, 'We shall stay in this place till our Lord comes to us and when our Lord will come, we will recognize Him. Then Allah will come to them again and say, 'I am your Lord.' They will say, 'You are our Lord.'

bukhari:806.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that Allah does not literally alter His form or physically laugh, claiming instead that an angel appears first as a test, that the change occurs only in the beholders' perception, and that Allah's laughing (*yaḍḥaku*) is merely a metaphor for divine pleasure (*riḍā*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `فَيَأْتِيهِمُ اللَّهُ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ` ('Allah will come to them and say: I am your Lord') in both instances, and its direct parallels in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 6573 and 7437 specify that Allah Himself comes `فِي غَيْرِ الصُّورَةِ الَّتِي يَعْرِفُونَهُ فِيهَا` ('in a form other than the form in which they know Him') before returning `فِي صُورَتِهِ الَّتِي يَعْرِفُونَ` ('in His form which they know'). By depicting Allah as shifting between distinct visual forms (*ṣūrah*) to test His followers and laughing (`فَيَضْحَكُ اللَّهُ`) at a bargaining man, the narration locks Sunni theology into overt anthropomorphism (*tashbīh*) that directly contradicts Surah 42:11 (`لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ`, 'There is nothing like unto Him').

bukhari:1291.note: Prefacing his testimony with Muhammad's warning of Hellfire for false attribution, Al-Mughira reports Muhammad's unqualified declaration that a deceased person is tormented (*yu'adhdhabu*) for the wailing performed over them by others, contradicting the biblical principle that a soul bears only its own guilt ([Ezekiel 18:20](bible://ez/18/20); [Deuteronomy 24:16](bible://dt/24/16)). Although Aisha rejected this report from Umar and Ibn Umar as contradicting [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164) (bukhari:1288) and commentators attempt to supply unstated conditions or redefine the punishment as grief, Al-Mughira's independent attestation and parallel reports specifying torment on the Day of Judgment (muslim:5641) establish the unconditional statement.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏"‏ مَنْ نِيحَ عَلَيْهِ يُعَذَّبُ بِمَا نِيحَ عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) saying, "The deceased who is wailed over is tortured for that wailing

bukhari:1291.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this torment applies only if the deceased explicitly instructed their family to wail over them before dying (citing Al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar), or they invoke Aisha's objection (`bukhari:1288`) that Umar and Ibn Umar misheard the Prophet in light of Quran 6:164 ('no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another'). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an unqualified, universal decree—`مَنْ نِيحَ عَلَيْهِ يُعَذَّبُ بِمَا نِيحَ عَلَيْهِ` ('Whoever is wailed over is tortured for that wailing')—with zero mention of a prior bequest, and Al-Mughira deliberately prefaces it with Muhammad's warning against lying about him (`مَنْ كَذَبَ عَلَىَّ مُتَعَمِّدًا`) to certify its verbatim accuracy. Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:1292`, `muslim:2143`) show Umar and Ibn Umar applying this literal punishment to pious Muslims, proving that Aisha's appeal to Quranic justice was directly contradicted by multiple eyewitness companions.

bukhari:4948.note: Muhammad declares that every created soul's place in Paradise or Hell—and whether it is blessed or miserable—has already been written. When asked whether people should therefore rely on their written fate and abandon deeds, he states that those written among the blessed are facilitated (`yuyassaruna`) to do the deeds of the blessed while those written among the miserable are facilitated to do the deeds of the miserable, reciting [Quran 92:5-10](quran://92/5).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: مَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ وَمَا مِنْ نَفْسٍ مَنْفُوسَةٍ إِلاَّ كُتِبَ مَكَانُهَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ وَالنَّارِ، وَإِلاَّ قَدْ كُتِبَتْ شَقِيَّةً أَوْ سَعِيدَةً ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ رَجُلٌ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَفَلاَ نَتَّكِلُ عَلَى كِتَابِنَا وَنَدَعُ الْعَمَلَ فَمَنْ كَانَ مِنَّا مِنْ أَهْلِ السَّعَادَةِ فَسَيَصِيرُ إِلَى أَهْلِ السَّعَادَةِ، وَمَنْ كَانَ مِنَّا مِنْ أَهْلِ الشَّقَاءِ فَسَيَصِيرُ إِلَى عَمَلِ أَهْلِ الشَّقَاوَةِ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَمَّا أَهْلُ السَّعَادَةِ فَيُيَسَّرُونَ لِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ السَّعَادَةِ وَأَمَّا أَهْلُ الشَّقَاوَةِ فَيُيَسَّرُونَ لِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الشَّقَاءِ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ ‏{‏فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَى وَاتَّقَى * وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَى‏}‏ الآيَةَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: There is none among you, and no created soul but has his place written for him either in Paradise or in the Hell-Fire, and also has his happy or miserable fate (in the Hereafter) written for him." A man said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Shall we depend upon what is written for us and give up doing (good) deeds? For whoever among us is destined to be fortunate (in the Hereafter), will join the fortunate peoples and whoever among us is destined to be miserable will do such deeds as are characteristic of the people who are destined to misery." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Those who are destined to be happy (in the Hereafter) will find it easy and pleasant to do the deeds characteristic of those destined to happiness, while those who are to be among the miserable (in the Hereafter), will find it easy to do the deeds characteristic of those destined to misery." Then he recited: 'As for him who gives (in charity) and keeps his duty to Allah and believes in the Best reward from Allah

bukhari:4948.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this Hadith merely describes Allah's omniscient foreknowledge rather than coercive fatalism (*jabr*), citing Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) to claim that Muhammad's quoting of Quran 92:5–10 proves human free will and moral acquisition (*kasb*) precede divine facilitation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states in the passive voice that every soul's fate is already decreed before action (*qad kutibat shaqiyyatan aw saʿīdatan*—"it has already been written as miserable or happy") and that the damned are passively steered toward evil (*fayuyassarūna li-ʿamali ahli al-shaqāʾ*—"they are made to find easy the deeds of the people of misery"). Furthermore, when a companion asks if they should abandon deeds since their fate is sealed, Muhammad never denies that their actions are predetermined, which is confirmed by parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:3208`, `muslim:6731`) stating that the angel writes a fetus's deeds and eternal destination in the womb so inexorably that a man may do the deeds of the people of Paradise until he is an arm's length away, only for "what was written to overtake him" (*fayasbiqu ʿalayhi al-kitāb*) and force him into the deeds of Hell.

bukhari:7018.note: At the death of Uthman bin Maz'un, Muhammad questions a companion's testimony that Allah had honored the deceased and swears by Allah that, despite being Allah's Messenger, he does not know what will be done with himself or his followers ([Quran 46:9](quran://46/9)). While commentators such as Ibn Hajar argue this statement was later superseded by [Quran 48:2](quran://48/2) or cite a variant pronoun in bukhari:1243, the first-person declaration ("what will be done with me") is preserved in bukhari:3929, bukhari:7003, and bukhari:7018, contrasting with the Biblical assurance of salvation ([1 John 5:13](bible://1jn/5/13)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَاللَّهِ مَا أَدْرِي وَأَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلاَ بِكُمْ
problematic_excerpt.english: By Allah, though I am Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), I neither know what will happen to me, nor to you.

bukhari:7018.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was merely referring to worldly trials prior to the revelation of Surah Al-Fath (48:2), or they cite Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī to claim that narrators mistakenly altered the pronoun from 'what will happen to him' (mā yuf'alu bihi) to 'what will happen to me' (mā yuf'alu bī). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states under a solemn prophetic oath, 'wa-Allāhi mā adrī wa-anā Rasūlu Allāhi mā yuf'alu bī wa-lā bikum' ('By Allah, though I am Allah's Messenger, I neither know what will happen to me, nor to you'), which verbatim matches the unalterable Quranic confession in Surah Al-Ahqaf (46:9). Because Muhammad uttered this rebuke over the corpse of 'Uthman bin Maz'un after death (al-yaqīn) had already arrived to challenge the claim that Allah had honored him in the hereafter (laqad akramaka Allāh), his admitted ignorance undeniably governs eternal salvation rather than earthly events.

muslim:6744.note: Muhammad states that when Moses blamed Adam for bringing humanity down from Paradise through his sin (bi-khaṭīʾatika), Adam defeated Moses in argument by citing that Allah wrote the Torah forty years before creating him with the words 'And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray' ([Quran 20:121](quran://20/121)). Adam concludes that Moses cannot blame him for committing a deed (ʿamalan) that Allah had written upon him to do forty years before his creation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: احْتَجَّ آدَمُ وَمُوسَى عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلاَمُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمَا فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى قَالَ مُوسَى أَنْتَ آدَمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ اللَّهُ بِيَدِهِ وَنَفَخَ فِيكَ مِنْ رُوحِهِ وَأَسْجَدَ لَكَ مَلاَئِكَتَهُ وَأَسْكَنَكَ فِي جَنَّتِهِ ثُمَّ أَهْبَطْتَ النَّاسَ بِخَطِيئَتِكَ إِلَى الأَرْضِ فَقَالَ آدَمُ أَنْتَ مُوسَى الَّذِي اصْطَفَاكَ اللَّهُ بِرِسَالَتِهِ وَبِكَلاَمِهِ وَأَعْطَاكَ الأَلْوَاحَ فِيهَا تِبْيَانُ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ وَقَرَّبَكَ نَجِيًّا فَبِكَمْ وَجَدْتَ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ التَّوْرَاةَ قَبْلَ أَنْ أُخْلَقَ قَالَ مُوسَى بِأَرْبَعِينَ عَامًا ‏.‏ قَالَ آدَمُ فَهَلْ وَجَدْتَ فِيهَا ‏{‏ وَعَصَى آدَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوَى‏}‏ قَالَ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَفَتَلُومُنِي عَلَى أَنْ عَمِلْتُ عَمَلاً كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَىَّ أَنْ أَعْمَلَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَنِي بِأَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: There was an argument between Adam and Moses (peace be upon both of them) in the presence of their Lord. Adam came the better of Moses. Moses said: Are you that Adam whom Allah created with His Hand and breathed into himHis sprit, and commanded angels to fall in prostration before him and He made you live in Paradise with comfort and ease. Then you caused the people to get down to the earth because of your lapse. Adam said: Are you that Moses whom Allah selected for His Messengership and for His conversation with him and conferred upon you the tablets, in which everything was clearly explained and granted you the audience in order to have confidential talk with you. What is your opinion, how long Torah would haye been written before I was created? Moses said: Forty years before. Adam said: Did you not see these words: Adam committed an error and he was enticed to (do so). He (Moses) said: Yes. Whereupon, he (Adam) said: Do you then blame me for an act which Allah had ordained for me forty years before He created me? Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: This is how Adam came the better of Moses

muslim:6744.literal_translation: Adam and Moses (peace be upon both of them) argued in the presence of their Lord, and Adam defeated Moses in argument. Moses said: 'You are Adam whom Allah created with His Hand, breathed into you of His spirit, made His angels prostrate to you, and settled you in His Paradise; then you brought humanity down to the earth because of your sin.' Adam said: 'You are Moses whom Allah chose for His Messengership and His speech, gave you the tablets in which is the explanation of everything, and brought you near as a confidant; so by how long did you find that Allah wrote the Torah before I was created?' Moses said: 'By forty years.' Adam said: 'Did you find in it: "And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray"?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you then blame me for doing a deed which Allah wrote upon me to do forty years before He created me?' Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: 'Thus Adam defeated Moses in argument.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: بِخَطِيئَتِكَ ... وَعَصَى آدَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوَى
translation_issue.published_rendering: because of your lapse ... Adam committed an error and he was enticed to (do so)
translation_issue.literal_meaning: because of your sin ... And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray
translation_issue.explanation: The translator softens 'bi-khaṭīʾatika' ('because of your sin') to 'because of your lapse' and alters the active Quranic clause 'wa-ʿaṣā Ādamu Rabbahu fa-ghawā' ('And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray') into 'Adam committed an error and he was enticed to (do so),' omitting 'his Lord' and shifting the active verb 'fa-ghawā' ('went astray') into a passive construction.

muslim:6744.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Adam did not invoke predestination to excuse his sin, claiming he only deflected blame for the earthly calamity that followed after his repentance and that the pre-existent Torah merely reflects divine foreknowledge. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Adam cited the exact words of his rebellion (`وَعَصَى آدَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوَى` — 'And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray,' attributing the Arabic wording of [Quran 20:121](quran://20/121) to the Torah, `التَّوْرَاةَ`) and excused the act itself by asking, 'Do you then blame me for doing a deed which Allah wrote upon me to do forty years before He created me?' (`عَمِلْتُ عَمَلاً كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَىَّ أَنْ أَعْمَلَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَنِي بِأَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً`). Muhammad twice validates this fatalistic plea by declaring `فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى` ('Adam defeated Moses in argument'), shifting moral responsibility for human sin (`بِخَطِيئَتِكَ`) onto Allah's decree in contradiction to [James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13).

bukhari:6243.note: Muhammad declares that Allah has written (`kataba`) for every human being a share of adultery (`zina`) that they will inevitably (`la mahala`) commit. Cited by Ibn Abbas to define minor sins (`lamam`), the report specifies that the adultery of the eyes is looking, the adultery of the tongue is speaking, the soul wishes and desires, and the private parts confirm or deny it—explicitly attributing each person's inevitable share of these sins to Allah's decree (cf. bukhari:6612; [James 1:13-14](bible://jas/1/13); [1 Corinthians 10:13](bible://1cor/10/13)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ عَلَى ابْنِ آدَمَ حَظَّهُ مِنَ الزِّنَا، أَدْرَكَ ذَلِكَ لاَ مَحَالَةَ، فَزِنَا الْعَيْنِ النَّظَرُ، وَزِنَا اللِّسَانِ الْمَنْطِقُ، وَالنَّفْسُ تَمَنَّى وَتَشْتَهِي، وَالْفَرْجُ يُصَدِّقُ ذَلِكَ كُلَّهُ وَيُكَذِّبُهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: "Allah has written for Adam's son his share of adultery which he commits inevitably. The adultery of the eyes is the sight (to gaze at a forbidden thing), the adultery of the tongue is the talk, and the inner self wishes and desires and the private parts testify all this or deny it

bukhari:6243.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration merely describes God's passive foreknowledge of minor human temptations (*lamam*) and figurative lapses of the senses rather than fatalistic compulsion to sin. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah has decreed this share *upon* man (`كَتَبَ عَلَى ابْنِ آدَمَ`) and that he will overtake it with absolute inevitability (`أَدْرَكَ ذَلِكَ لاَ مَحَالَةَ`, 'with no escape'). Furthermore, both Al-Bukhari (*Sahih al-Bukhari* 6612) and Muslim (*Sahih Muslim* 2657a) categorize this narration under *Kitāb al-Qadar* (The Book of Divine Preordainment), confirming that classical Sunni orthodoxy treats these sins as inescapable divine decrees.

muslim:6754.note: Muhammad declares that Allah has written upon every human being a share of adultery (*zinā*) that he will inevitably commit—defining the adultery of the eyes as looking and of the tongue as speaking, while the soul craves and the genitals either confirm or belie it—which Ibn Abbas cites in the Arabic text as the closest example of minor sins (*al-lamam*).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ مَا رَأَيْتُ شَيْئًا أَشْبَهَ بِاللَّمَمِ مِمَّا قَالَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ عَلَى ابْنِ آدَمَ حَظَّهُ مِنَ الزِّنَى أَدْرَكَ ذَلِكَ لاَ مَحَالَةَ فَزِنَى الْعَيْنَيْنِ النَّظَرُ وَزِنَى اللِّسَانِ النُّطْقُ وَالنَّفْسُ تَمَنَّى وَتَشْتَهِي وَالْفَرْجُ يُصَدِّقُ ذَلِكَ أَوْ يُكَذِّبُهُ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) as saying:Verily Allah has fixed the very portion of adultery which a man will indulge in, and which he of necessity must commit. The adultery of the eye is the lustful look, and the adultery of the tongue is the licentious speech, the heart desires and yearns, which the parts may or may not put into effect

muslim:6754.literal_translation: From Ibn Abbas, who said: I have not seen anything more closely resembling minor sins (al-lamam) than what Abu Huraira narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Verily, Allah has written upon the son of Adam his share of adultery, which he will inevitably commit: the adultery of the eyes is looking, the adultery of the tongue is speaking, the soul wishes and craves, and the genitals confirm that or belie it.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: قَالَ مَا رَأَيْتُ شَيْئًا أَشْبَهَ بِاللَّمَمِ مِمَّا قَالَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ
translation_issue.published_rendering: Abu Huraira reported
translation_issue.literal_meaning: [Ibn Abbas] said: I have not seen anything more closely resembling minor sins (al-lamam) than what Abu Huraira said
translation_issue.explanation: The published English translation completely omits Ibn Abbas's opening statement classifying these predestined acts of adultery of the eyes, tongue, and heart as minor faults ('al-lamam').

muslim:6754.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Allah's writing (*kataba*) denotes mere foreknowledge rather than compulsion, and that calling lustful looks and speech 'adultery' (*zinā*) is a figurative warning where moral culpability depends on whether a person chooses to consummate the act. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah has written upon the son of Adam his fixed share of adultery (`كَتَبَ عَلَى ابْنِ آدَمَ حَظَّهُ مِنَ الزِّنَى`) which he must inevitably commit without escape (`أَدْرَكَ ذَلِكَ لاَ مَحَالَةَ`), making divine decree the source of unavoidable sin (see also `bukhari:6243`, `bukhari:6612`, and `muslim:6755`). Furthermore, the untranslated Arabic preface records Ibn Abbas classifying these lustful looks, speech, and cravings (`تَمَنَّى وَتَشْتَهِي`) as mere minor faults (`بِاللَّمَمِ`) under [Quran 53:32](quran://53/32) unless confirmed by the genitals (`وَالْفَرْجُ يُصَدِّقُ ذَلِكَ`), standing in direct contrast to [James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13) and [Matthew 5:28](bible://mt/5/28).

bukhari:6614.note: Muhammad declares three times that Adam defeated Moses in argument when Moses rebuked him for causing humanity's expulsion from Paradise, with Adam asking how Moses could blame him for a matter Allah had decreed upon him forty years before creating him. Although classical commentators attempt to restrict Adam's defense to post-repentance blame or mere calamity rather than sin, the text and its parallel (bukhari:3409, which specifies expulsion 'by your sin') ground Adam's rebuttal solely in Allah's pre-creational decree rather than repentance (cf. [Ezekiel 18:20](bible://ez/18/20); [James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: احْتَجَّ آدَمُ وَمُوسَى، فَقَالَ لَهُ مُوسَى يَا آدَمُ أَنْتَ أَبُونَا خَيَّبْتَنَا وَأَخْرَجْتَنَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ‏.‏ قَالَ لَهُ آدَمُ يَا مُوسَى اصْطَفَاكَ اللَّهُ بِكَلاَمِهِ، وَخَطَّ لَكَ بِيَدِهِ، أَتَلُومُنِي عَلَى أَمْرٍ قَدَّرَ اللَّهُ عَلَىَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَنِي بِأَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً‏.‏ فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى، فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى
problematic_excerpt.english: "Adam and Moses argued with each other. Moses said to Adam. 'O Adam! You are our father who disappointed us and turned us out of Paradise.' Then Adam said to him, 'O Moses! Allah favored you with His talk (talked to you directly) and He wrote (the Torah) for you with His Own Hand. Do you blame me for action which Allah had written in my fate forty years before my creation?' So Adam confuted Moses, Adam confuted Moses," the Prophet (ﷺ) added, repeating the Statement three times

bukhari:6614.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, Al-Nawawī, and Ibn Taymiyyah—that Adam did not invoke predestination (*qadar*) to excuse his sin, but merely to explain the resulting calamity (*muṣībah*) of leaving Paradise after he had already repented. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Adam deflected blame for the preordained matter itself (*أَتَلُومُنِي عَلَى أَمْرٍ قَدَّرَ اللَّهُ عَلَىَّ*—'Do you blame me for a matter Allah decreed upon me?'), which parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:3409) specify was the very act of transgression (*عَلَى أَنْ عَمِلْتُ عَمَلاً كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَىَّ أَنْ أَعْمَلَهُ*—'for doing a deed Allah wrote upon me to do'). With zero mention of repentance in the narration, Muhammad thrice ratifies Adam's fatalistic appeal (*فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى*—'So Adam defeated Moses in argument'), confirming that Allah's prior decree alone won the debate.

muslim:6769.note: At the funeral of a child of the Ansar, Aisha remarks that the child is a bird of Paradise because he neither committed sin nor reached the age of accountability, but Muhammad replies that it may be otherwise because Allah created people for Paradise and people for Hellfire while they were still in their fathers' loins (cf. muslim:6768).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَتْ دُعِيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِلَى جَنَازَةِ صَبِيٍّ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ فَقُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ طُوبَى لِهَذَا عُصْفُورٌ مِنْ عَصَافِيرِ الْجَنَّةِ لَمْ يَعْمَلِ السُّوءَ وَلَمْ يُدْرِكْهُ قَالَ ‏ "‏ أَوَغَيْرَ ذَلِكَ يَا عَائِشَةُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ لِلْجَنَّةِ أَهْلاً خَلَقَهُمْ لَهَا وَهُمْ فِي أَصْلاَبِ آبَائِهِمْ وَخَلَقَ لِلنَّارِ أَهْلاً خَلَقَهُمْ لَهَا وَهُمْ فِي أَصْلاَبِ آبَائِهِمْ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha, the mother of the believers, said that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was called to lead the funeral prayer of a child of the Ansar. I said:Allah's Messenger, there is happiness for this child who is a bird from the birds of Paradise for it committed no sin nor has he reached the age when one can commit sin. He said: 'A'isha, per adventure, it may be otherwise, because God created for Paradise those who are fit for it while they were yet in their father's loins and created for Hell those who are to go to Hell. He created them for Hell while they were yet in their father's loins

muslim:6769.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was merely cautioning Aisha against declaring a specific person's unseen fate without revelation, or that predestination here refers only to divine foreknowledge of future adult deeds. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the deceased was a child of the Ansar (`صَبِيٍّ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ`) who died having neither committed evil nor reached the age of sin (`لَمْ يَعْمَلِ السُّوءَ وَلَمْ يُدْرِكْهُ`). Muhammad directly counters Aisha's reasoning (`أَوَغَيْرَ ذَلِكَ يَا عَائِشَةُ`) by stating that Allah created inhabitants for the Fire while they were still in their fathers' loins (`وَخَلَقَ لِلنَّارِ أَهْلاً خَلَقَهُمْ لَهَا وَهُمْ فِي أَصْلاَبِ آبَائِهِمْ`), matching [Quran 7:179](quran://7/179).

muslim:6735.note: When Suraqa bin Malik asks whether present human deeds pertain to an open future or to that upon which the pens have already dried and the decrees of destiny have operated, Muhammad replies that deeds occur in that upon which the pens have dried and the decrees have operated, instructing his followers to act because everyone is facilitated. While the published English translation appends the unattested phrase 'what he intends to do,' parallel reports (muslim:6731, muslim:6733, muslim:6736, muslim:6737, bukhari:6605) complete the Arabic phrase 'kullun muyassar' as 'everyone is facilitated for that for which he was created.'

problematic_excerpt.arabic: جَاءَ سُرَاقَةُ بْنُ مَالِكِ بْنِ جُعْشُمٍ قَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ بَيِّنْ لَنَا دِينَنَا كَأَنَّا خُلِقْنَا الآنَ فِيمَا الْعَمَلُ الْيَوْمَ أَفِيمَا جَفَّتْ بِهِ الأَقْلاَمُ وَجَرَتْ بِهِ الْمَقَادِيرُ أَمْ فِيمَا نَسْتَقْبِلُ قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ ‏.‏ بَلْ فِيمَا جَفَّتْ بِهِ الأَقْلاَمُ وَجَرَتْ بِهِ الْمَقَادِيرُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَفِيمَ الْعَمَلُ قَالَ زُهَيْرٌ ثُمَّ تَكَلَّمَ أَبُو الزُّبَيْرِ بِشَىْءٍ لَمْ أَفْهَمْهُ فَسَأَلْتُ مَا قَالَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ اعْمَلُوا فَكُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Jabir reported that Suriqa b. Malik b. Ju'shuin came and said:Allah's Messenger, explain our religion to us (in a way) as if we have been created just now. Whosoever deeds we do today, is it because of the fact that-the pens have dried (after recording them) and the destitiles have began to operate or these have effects in future? Thereupon he said: The pens have dried tmd destinies have begun to operate. (Suraqa b. Malik) said: If it Is so, then what is the use of doing good deeds? Zuhair said: Then Abu Zubair said something but I could not understand that and I said. What did he say? Thereupon he said: Act, for everyone is facilitated what he intends to do

muslim:6735.literal_translation: Suraqa bin Malik bin Ju'shum came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, explain our religion to us as though we were created just now: regarding what do we act today? Is it in that upon which the pens have dried and the decrees of destiny have operated, or in what we face in the future?' He said: 'No, rather in that upon which the pens have dried and the decrees of destiny have operated.' He said: 'Then what is the point of acting?' Zuhair said: Then Abu al-Zubair spoke something that I did not understand, so I asked: 'What did he say?' He said: 'Act, for everyone is facilitated.'

translation_issue.arabic_term: اعْمَلُوا فَكُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ
translation_issue.published_rendering: Act, for everyone is facilitated what he intends to do
translation_issue.literal_meaning: Act, for everyone is facilitated
translation_issue.explanation: The translator appends the unattested English clause 'what he intends to do' without brackets to the passive Arabic phrase 'kullun muyassar' ('everyone is facilitated'), reframing pre-ordained divine facilitation as human intention.

muslim:6735.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the dried pens merely record divine foreknowledge of free human choices, relying on the English rendering that 'everyone is facilitated what he intends to do' to preserve human moral agency. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *la, bal fima jaffat bihi al-aqlam wa jarat bihi al-maqadir* ('No, rather in that upon which the pens have dried and the decrees of destiny have operated'), directly rejecting Suraqa's alternative that today's deeds are open matters we face in the future (*am fima nastaqbilu*). Furthermore, the closing Arabic clause reads only *i'malu fa-kullun muyassar* ('Act, for everyone is facilitated')—lacking any Arabic words for 'what he intends to do'—and instead denotes being facilitated toward the destiny for which one was created (`muslim:6731`, `muslim:6736`, `bukhari:6605`).

muslim:7374.note: When Gog and Magog declare that they have killed those on the earth and shoot their arrows toward the sky to 'kill those who are in the sky,' the Arabic text states that Allah Himself returns their arrows to them dyed with blood (`fa-yaruddu Allāhu ʿalayhim nushshābahum makhḍūbatan daman`; cf. [Quran 3:54](quran://3/54)). Although `Allāhu` is the explicit grammatical subject of `fa-yaruddu`, the published English translation omits Allah's agency and renders the clause intransitively ('and the arrows would return to them besmeared with blood').

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَيَقُولُونَ لَقَدْ قَتَلْنَا مَنْ فِي الأَرْضِ هَلُمَّ فَلْنَقْتُلْ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاءِ ‏.‏ فَيَرْمُونَ بِنُشَّابِهِمْ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فَيَرُدُّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ نُشَّابَهُمْ مَخْضُوبَةً دَمًا
problematic_excerpt.english: and they would say:We have killed those who are upon the earth. Let us now kill those who are In the sky and they would throw their arrows towards the sky and the arrows would return to them besmeared with blood.

muslim:7374.literal_translation: And they will say: 'We have killed those who are upon the earth; come, let us kill those who are in the sky!' So they will shoot their arrows towards the sky, and Allah will return their arrows to them dyed with blood.

translation_issue.arabic_term: فَيَرُدُّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ نُشَّابَهُمْ مَخْضُوبَةً دَمًا
translation_issue.published_rendering: and the arrows would return to them besmeared with blood
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and Allah will return their arrows to them dyed with blood
translation_issue.explanation: The published English translation omits 'Allāh' as the agent who returns the blood-stained arrows, concealing that Allah actively participates in deceiving Gog and Magog.

muslim:7374.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the blood-stained arrows are merely a test for rebellious disbelievers, or rely on the published English rendering ('the arrows would return to them') to distance Allah from the act. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `فَيَرُدُّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ نُشَّابَهُمْ مَخْضُوبَةً دَمًا` (`fa-yaruddu Allāhu ʿalayhim nushshābahum makhḍūbatan daman`—'and Allah will return their arrows to them dyed with blood'), naming Allah as the direct grammatical subject who returns bloodied arrows in response to their boast of killing those in the sky. Instead of the Biblical God in whom there is no darkness at all ([1 John 1:5](bible://1jn/1/5)), this narration portrays Allah actively staging a physical deception in keeping with [Quran 3:54](quran://3/54).

bukhari:2692.note: Muhammad declares that one who conveys or fabricates favorable statements (*yanmī khayran*) to reconcile people is not counted as a liar. Alongside fuller parallels permitting falsehood in war, reconciliation, and between spouses (muslim:6633, muslim:6634), classical Sunni commentators confirm this establishes a legal dispensation (*rukhṣah*) for beneficial deception or equivocation, contrasting with the biblical prohibition against falsehood ([Exodus 20:16](bible://ex/20/16), [Proverbs 12:22](bible://prv/12/22), [Ephesians 4:25](bible://eph/4/25)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ لَيْسَ الْكَذَّابُ الَّذِي يُصْلِحُ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ، فَيَنْمِي خَيْرًا، أَوْ يَقُولُ خَيْرًا
problematic_excerpt.english: saying, "He who makes peace between the people by inventing good information or saying good things, is not a liar

bukhari:2692.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration only permits *tawriyah* (ambiguous double-entendres, a view of Al-Ṭabarī cited in Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*) rather than outright fabrication, or that it is a harmless exception restricted strictly to peacemaking. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the reconciler 'conveys/invents good (*yanmī khayran*),' and the fuller parallel in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* (muslim:6633–6634) records Umm Kulthūm stating that Muhammad granted a formal dispensation (*yurakhkhaṣu*) in 'what people call lying (*mimmā yaqūlu al-nāsu kadhib*)' across three broad arenas: war, peacemaking, and a husband and wife speaking to one another. As Al-Nawawī confirms in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, the majority of Sunni scholars hold that this authorizes literal, outright falsehood (*al-kadhib al-ṣarīḥ*)—fabricating statements that were never spoken—whenever a person deems the outcome beneficial.

bukhari:6661.note: Muhammad declares that Hellfire will continue asking for more inhabitants ([Quran 50:30](quran://50/30)) until the Lord of Honor places His foot directly inside it (*fīhā qadamahu*—softened to 'over it' in the English translation), causing its sides to contract together and cry out that it has had enough. This depiction of Allah placing His foot (and leg, *rijlahu*, in bukhari:4848) directly into the created abode of Hellfire undercuts Islamic polemics claiming a transcendent God cannot enter created space.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: لاَ تَزَالُ جَهَنَّمُ تَقُولُ هَلْ مِنْ مَزِيدٍ حَتَّى يَضَعَ رَبُّ الْعِزَّةِ فِيهَا قَدَمَهُ فَتَقُولُ قَطْ قَطْ وَعِزَّتِكَ‏.‏ وَيُزْوَى بَعْضُهَا إِلَى بَعْضٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: "The Hell Fire will keep on saying: 'Are there anymore (people to come)?' Till the Lord of Power and Honor will put His Foot over it and then it will say, 'Qat! Qat! (sufficient! sufficient!) by Your Power and Honor. And its various sides will come close to each other (i.e., it will contract)

bukhari:6661.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the word *qadam* ('foot') is either a non-physical attribute affirmed 'without modality' (*bilā kayf*) or, as Ash'arī commentators cited in Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* claim, an Arabic idiom for sinners whom Allah 'sends forth' (*qaddama*) into the Fire. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *yaḍaʿa Rabbu al-ʿizzati fīhā qadamahu* ('the Lord of Honor puts His foot *into it*'), causing Hell's walls to physically compress and contract together (*yuzwā baʿḍuhā ilā baʿḍin*). Moreover, parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:4848`, `bukhari:4849`) substitute *qadam* with the anatomical noun *rijlahu* ('His leg/foot')—which lexicographically cannot mean 'people sent forth'—and explicitly contrast Allah creating extra humans to fill Paradise with Allah filling Hell by inserting His own limb.

muslim:7011.note: Muhammad declares that on the Day of Resurrection Allah will hand a Jew or a Christian over to every Muslim and state, 'This is your ransom (*fakāk*) from the Fire.' This substitution of a Jew or a Christian into Hellfire to redeem a Muslim—reinforced in muslim:7014 where Allah places Muslims' mountain-sized sins onto them—contradicts the declaration in [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164) that no soul bears the burden of another.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ إِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ دَفَعَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ يَهُودِيًّا أَوْ نَصْرَانِيًّا فَيَقُولُ هَذَا فَكَاكُكَ مِنَ النَّارِ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Musa' reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said:When it will be the Day of Resurrection Allah would deliver to every Muslim a Jew or a Christian and say: That is your rescue from Hell-Fire

muslim:7011.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration is metaphorical, claiming that Jews and Christians merely occupy the places in Hellfire that Muslims would have entered had they disbelieved, rather than serving as substitutes in violation of [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah hands over to every Muslim a Jew or a Christian (dafa'a Allāhu 'azza wa-jalla ilā kulli muslimin yahūdiyyan aw naṣrāniyyan) and declares, 'This is your ransom from the Fire' (hādhā fakākuka mina al-nār). The noun fakāk denotes an actual ransom or redemption price paid to release a captive, which alongside parallel reports (muslim:7012, muslim:7014) establishes literal human substitution rather than a mere reassignment of space.

muslim:7011.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:7011.subcategory: Vicarious Ransom, Sin-Transfer & Intercessory Salvation (Atonement Precedents)
muslim:7011.note: Although Muslim polemicists reject Christian substitutionary atonement ([Isaiah 53:5](bible://is/53/5), [Mark 10:45](bible://mk/10/45)) by citing [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164), Muhammad affirms vicarious human ransom (*fakāk*) on the Day of Resurrection by stating that Allah will give every Muslim a Jew or a Christian as their ransom from the Fire. Together with muslim:7014, where Allah transfers Muslims' sins onto Jews and Christians, this establishes substitutionary ransom and sin-transfer within Sahih Muslim.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ إِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ دَفَعَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ يَهُودِيًّا أَوْ نَصْرَانِيًّا فَيَقُولُ هَذَا فَكَاكُكَ مِنَ النَّارِ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Musa' reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said:When it will be the Day of Resurrection Allah would deliver to every Muslim a Jew or a Christian and say: That is your rescue from Hell-Fire

muslim:7011.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islam categorically rejects vicarious atonement on the basis of [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164) and that muslim:7011 only describes non-Muslims entering Hellfire for their own disbelief while Muslims are saved by Allah's mercy. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah delivers a Jew or a Christian to every Muslim and proclaims, 'This is your ransom from the Fire' (hādhā fakākuka mina al-nār), employing the direct terminology of substitutionary redemption (fakāk) as corroborated in muslim:7012 and muslim:7014. Whereas the New Testament teaches that a sinless Savior voluntarily gave His own life as a ransom for many ([Mark 10:45](bible://mk/10/45)), Muhammad's Hadith concedes the principle of vicarious ransom by having Allah involuntarily trade Jews and Christians into Hellfire to redeem Muslims.

bukhari:3147.note: After receiving the war spoils (*fay'*) of the Hawazin tribe in AD 630, Muhammad distributed one hundred camels each to men of Quraish while leaving out the Ansar whose swords were still dripping with blood. When younger men among the Ansar objected, Muhammad gathered the Ansar privately and explained that he was giving this wealth to men who had only recently left unbelief (*ḥadīthun 'ahduhum bi-kufr*) to reconcile their hearts and secure their allegiance to Islam ([Quran 8:41](quran://8/41), [Quran 9:60](quran://9/60)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: حِينَ أَفَاءَ اللَّهُ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ أَمْوَالِ هَوَازِنَ مَا أَفَاءَ، فَطَفِقَ يُعْطِي رِجَالاً مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ الْمِائَةَ مِنَ الإِبِلِ فَقَالُوا يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُعْطِي قُرَيْشًا وَيَدَعُنَا، وَسُيُوفُنَا تَقْطُرُ مِنْ دِمَائِهِمْ قَالَ أَنَسٌ فَحُدِّثَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ بِمَقَالَتِهِمْ، فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَى الأَنْصَارِ، فَجَمَعَهُمْ فِي قُبَّةٍ مِنْ أَدَمٍ، وَلَمْ يَدْعُ مَعَهُمْ أَحَدًا غَيْرَهُمْ، فَلَمَّا اجْتَمَعُوا جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَا كَانَ حَدِيثٌ بَلَغَنِي عَنْكُمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ لَهُ فُقَهَاؤُهُمْ أَمَّا ذَوُو آرَائِنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَلَمْ يَقُولُوا شَيْئًا، وَأَمَّا أُنَاسٌ مِنَّا حَدِيثَةٌ أَسْنَانُهُمْ فَقَالُوا يَغْفِرُ اللَّهُ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُعْطِي قُرَيْشًا وَيَتْرُكُ الأَنْصَارَ، وَسُيُوفُنَا تَقْطُرُ مِنْ دِمَائِهِمْ‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنِّي أُعْطِي رِجَالاً حَدِيثٌ عَهْدُهُمْ بِكُفْرٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: When Allah favored His Apostle with the properties of Hawazin tribe as Fai (booty), he started giving to some Quraishi men even up to one-hundred camels each, whereupon some Ansari men said about Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), "May Allah forgive His Apostle! He is giving to (men of) Quraish and leaves us, in spite of the fact that our swords are still dropping blood (of the infidels)" When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was informed of what they had said, he called the Ansar and gathered them in a leather tent and did not call anybody else along, with them. When they gathered, Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) came to them and said, "What is the statement which, I have been informed, and that which you have said?" The learned ones among them replied," O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! The wise ones amongst us did not say anything, but the youngsters amongst us said, 'May Allah forgive His Apostle; he gives the Quraish and leaves the Ansar, in spite of the fact that our swords are still dribbling (wet) with the blood of the infidels.' " Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) replied, I give to such people as are still close to the period of Infidelity

bukhari:3147.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that distributing the Hawazin spoils to the *Mu'allafatu Qulūbuhum* ('those whose hearts are to be reconciled' under Quran 9:60) was a benevolent act of statesmanship from Muhammad's legitimate fifth (*khums*) to foster unity rather than purchasing allegiance with war plunder. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that while the Ansar's swords were still 'dripping with their blood' (*wa-suyūfunā taqṭuru min dimā'ihim*), Muhammad handed out massive fortunes of 'a hundred camels' (*al-mi'ata min al-ibil*) apiece to wealthy Quraishi elites solely because they were 'recent in their covenant with unbelief' (*ḥadīthun 'ahduhum bi-kufrin*). Parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:4331, muslim:2436) further confirm that Muhammad openly admitted he used expropriated livestock to 'conciliate them' (*ata'allafuhum*) while leaving his devoted followers empty-handed, proving that early Islamic loyalty was overtly bought through blood-soaked material inducements.

muslim:2142.note: When Hafsa wept over her father Umar, he told her to refrain by citing Muhammad's declaration that a deceased person is punished because of his family's weeping over him ([Quran 6:164](quran://6/164), [Ezekiel 18:20](bible://ez/18/20)). Although Aisha rejected Umar and Ibn Umar's reports for violating [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164) (muslim:2149, muslim:2150) and later commentators attempted to restrict the punishment to those who explicitly willed their families to wail, Umar applied the warning directly to his own daughter without qualification.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ حَفْصَةَ، بَكَتْ عَلَى عُمَرَ فَقَالَ مَهْلاً يَا بُنَيَّةُ أَلَمْ تَعْلَمِي أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ إِنَّ الْمَيِّتَ يُعَذَّبُ بِبُكَاءِ أَهْلِهِ عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abdullah b. 'Umar reported that Hafsa wept for 'Umar (when he was about to die). He ('Umar) said:Be quiet, my daughter. Don't you know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said:" The deceased is punished because of his family's weeping over the death"?

muslim:2142.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Aisha's objection in parallel narrations (muslim:2145) and Al-Nawawī's Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim—that Umar and Ibn Umar misremembered the context, or that يُعَذَّبُ (yu'adhdhabu, 'is tormented') only applies when the deceased had pre-instructed their family to wail. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Umar cited Muhammad's unrestricted rule (إِنَّ الْمَيِّتَ يُعَذَّبُ بِبُكَاءِ أَهْلِهِ عَلَيْهِ) while rebuking his daughter Hafsa to stop weeping (مَهْلاً يَا بُنَيَّةُ), proving that the punishment was understood to fall upon the dead even when they actively forbade the weeping. Furthermore, the clash between Umar, Ibn Umar, and Hafsa (herself a wife of Muhammad) affirming this doctrine and Aisha rejecting it as a violation of Quran 6:164 exposes an irreconcilable contradiction within the Sahih corpus itself.

muslim:7012.note: Confirmed by a triple oath by Allah that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz required of Abu Burda, Muhammad declares that no Muslim man dies without Allah admitting a Jew or a Christian into Hellfire in his place (*makānahu*). Adjacent chapter narrations specify that the Jew or Christian is given as the Muslim's ransom from the Fire (muslim:7011) and has the Muslims' mountain-sized sins placed upon him (muslim:7014), contradicting [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ لاَ يَمُوتُ رَجُلٌ مُسْلِمٌ إِلاَّ أَدْخَلَ اللَّهُ مَكَانَهُ النَّارَ يَهُودِيًّا أَوْ نَصْرَانِيًّا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَاسْتَحْلَفَهُ عُمَرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ بِاللَّهِ الَّذِي لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ أَنَّ أَبَاهُ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ فَحَلَفَ لَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Burda reported on the authority of his father that Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) said:No Muslim would die but Allah would admit in his stead a Jew or a Christian in Hell-Fire. 'Umar b. Abd al-'Aziz took an oath: By One besides Whom there is no god but He, thrice that his father had narrated that to him from Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)

muslim:7012.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration must be harmonized with [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164) by interpreting the phrase 'in his stead' (*makānahu*) as a figurative reference to a Jew or a Christian occupying a spatial spot in Hellfire that a Muslim would have filled had he disbelieved, rather than one person taking another's place in punishment. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states as a universal rule that no Muslim man dies without Allah admitting a Jew or a Christian into the Fire in his place (*lā yamūtu rajulun muslimun illā adkhala Allāhu makānahu al-nāra yahūdiyyan aw naṣrāniyyan*), tying the non-Muslim's admission into Hellfire directly to the Muslim's death. Furthermore, the text records that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz compelled Abu Burda to swear three times by Allah (*bi-Allāhi alladhī lā ilāha illā huwa thalātha marrātin*) that his father heard this from Muhammad, demonstrating that early Muslims recognized the gravity of its literal substitutionary meaning (reinforced by `muslim:7011` and `muslim:7014`) rather than treating it as a figurative expression.

muslim:7012.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:7012.subcategory: Vicarious Ransom, Sin-Transfer & Intercessory Salvation (Atonement Precedents)
muslim:7012.note: While Islamic polemics reject the Christian doctrine of substitutionary atonement ([2 Corinthians 5:21](bible://2cor/5/21), [1 Peter 3:18](bible://1pt/3/18)) on the grounds that one person cannot bear another's punishment, Muhammad declares—in a report verified by a triple oath before Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz—that no Muslim man dies without Allah admitting a Jew or a Christian into Hellfire in his place (*makānahu*). Neighboring narrations in the same chapter reinforce this vicarious substitution by stating that the Jew or Christian serves as the Muslim's ransom (*fakāk*) from the Fire (muslim:7011) and has the Muslims' mountain-sized sins transferred onto him (muslim:7014).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ لاَ يَمُوتُ رَجُلٌ مُسْلِمٌ إِلاَّ أَدْخَلَ اللَّهُ مَكَانَهُ النَّارَ يَهُودِيًّا أَوْ نَصْرَانِيًّا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَاسْتَحْلَفَهُ عُمَرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ بِاللَّهِ الَّذِي لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ أَنَّ أَبَاهُ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ فَحَلَفَ لَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Burda reported on the authority of his father that Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) said:No Muslim would die but Allah would admit in his stead a Jew or a Christian in Hell-Fire. 'Umar b. Abd al-'Aziz took an oath: By One besides Whom there is no god but He, thrice that his father had narrated that to him from Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)

muslim:7012.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Islam rejects all forms of vicarious punishment, claiming that the word *makānahu* ('in his stead') merely signifies a non-Muslim inheriting a vacated allotment in Hellfire for his own unbelief rather than serving as a penal substitute for a Muslim. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that whenever a Muslim man dies, Allah admits a Jew or a Christian into Hellfire in his place (*إِلاَّ أَدْخَلَ اللَّهُ مَكَانَهُ النَّارَ يَهُودِيًّا أَوْ نَصْرَانِيًّا*), establishing a direct one-for-one substitutionary exchange confirmed across parallel narrations (`muslim:7011`, `muslim:7014`) and verified under a triple oath before Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz. This removes the foundational Islamic objection to the substitutionary atonement of Christ ([2 Corinthians 5:21](bible://2cor/5/21), [1 Peter 3:18](bible://1pt/3/18)), since this Hadith concedes the mechanism of penal substitution while replacing a sinless Savior who voluntarily bears the sins of the guilty with Allah consigning Jews and Christians to Hellfire in the place of deceased Muslims.

muslim:6745.note: Muhammad declares that when Moses confronted Adam over the sin (khaṭīʾatuka) that expelled him from Paradise, Adam defeated Moses in argument by objecting that he could not be blamed for an affair Allah had predestined upon him before he was created.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: احْتَجَّ آدَمُ وَمُوسَى فَقَالَ لَهُ مُوسَى أَنْتَ آدَمُ الَّذِي أَخْرَجَتْكَ خَطِيئَتُكَ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ فَقَالَ لَهُ آدَمُ أَنْتَ مُوسَى الَّذِي اصْطَفَاكَ اللَّهُ بِرِسَالَتِهِ وَبِكَلاَمِهِ ثُمَّ تَلُومُنِي عَلَى أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِّرَ عَلَىَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ أُخْلَقَ فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى
problematic_excerpt.english: There was an argument between Adam and Moses. Moses said: Are you that Adam whose lapse caused you to get out of Paradise? Adam said to him: Are you that Moses whom Allah selected for His Messengership, for His conversation and you blame me for an affair which had been ordained for me before I was created? This is how Adam came the better of Moses

muslim:6745.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Moses was only blaming Adam for the resulting earthly hardship of leaving Paradise rather than his sin, or that Adam was exempt from blame only because he had previously repented. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Moses cited Adam's sin (khaṭīʾatuka, خَطِيئَتُكَ, softened to 'lapse' in the English translation) as what expelled him from Paradise (أَخْرَجَتْكَ خَطِيئَتُكَ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ), and Adam defeated Moses in argument (فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى) solely by appealing to pre-creation predestination (تَلُومُنِي عَلَى أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِّرَ عَلَىَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ أُخْلَقَ) with no mention of repentance. By validating Adam's appeal to prior divine decree (قَدْ قُدِّرَ عَلَىَّ) to deflect blame (تَلُومُنِي) for his sin, the narration grounds moral immunity in fatalism against the biblical teaching that God never tempts or predestines anyone to sin ([James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13)).

muslim:500.note: Muhammad tells a questioner that both the man's deceased father and Muhammad's own father ('Abdullah, who died before Muhammad's birth) are in Hellfire. As al-Nawawi confirms, this consigns those who died during the unwarned pre-Islamic interval to the Fire—despite later apologetic attempts to reinterpret 'father' as his uncle Abu Talib—conflicting with the declaration that no people are punished before a messenger is sent to warn them ([Quran 17:15](quran://17/15), [Quran 36:6](quran://36/6); cf. [Romans 2:12](bible://rom/2/12)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَجُلاً، قَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَيْنَ أَبِي قَالَ ‏"‏ فِي النَّارِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَلَمَّا قَفَّى دَعَاهُ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ أَبِي وَأَبَاكَ فِي النَّارِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Verily, a person said: Messenger of Allah, where is my father? He said: (He) is in the Fire. When he turned away, he (the Holy Prophet) called him and said: Verily my father and your father are in the Fire

muslim:500.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that 'my father' (*abī*) figuratively refers to Muhammad's uncle Abū Ṭālib, or they cite Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* to claim that pre-Islamic Arabs were still accountable because remnants of Abraham's monotheism had reached them. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *'inna abī wa-abāka fī al-nār'* ('Verily, my father and your father are in the Fire'), directly pairing the questioner's literal father with Muhammad's biological father 'Abdullāh—just as *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 976b confirms Allah forbade Muhammad from seeking forgiveness for his mother Āminah—while [Quran 32:3](quran://32/3), [34:44](quran://34/44), and [36:6](quran://36/6) explicitly testify that no warner had come to their forefathers, collapsing the excuse and exposing a direct contradiction with [Quran 17:15](quran://17/15).

muslim:6742.note: Muhammad declares twice that Adam defeated Moses in argument after Moses blamed him for disappointing humanity and causing their expulsion from Paradise, to which Adam replied by asking how Moses—whom Allah chose for His speech and for whom He wrote the Torah with His own Hand—could blame him for a matter that Allah had predestined upon him forty years before creating him. In parallel reports (bukhari:3409, muslim:6744), Moses specifies that it was Adam's sin (khati'atika) that expelled humanity from Paradise, and Adam gives the same rebuttal that Allah had decreed the act before his creation.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: احْتَجَّ آدَمُ وَمُوسَى فَقَالَ مُوسَى يَا آدَمُ أَنْتَ أَبُونَا خَيَّبْتَنَا وَأَخْرَجْتَنَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ فَقَالَ لَهُ آدَمُ أَنْتَ مُوسَى اصْطَفَاكَ اللَّهُ بِكَلاَمِهِ وَخَطَّ لَكَ بِيَدِهِ أَتَلُومُنِي عَلَى أَمْرٍ قَدَّرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَىَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَنِي بِأَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: There was argument between Adam and Moses. Moses said to Adam: You are our father. You did us harm and caused us to get out of Paradise. Adam said to him: You are Moses. Allah selected you (for direct conversation with you) and wrote with His own Hand the Book (Torah) for you. Despite this you blame me for an act which Allah had ordained for me forty years before He created me. Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) said:. This is how Adam came the better of Moses and Adam came the better of Moses

muslim:6742.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Moses only blamed Adam for the earthly calamity of leaving Paradise rather than his transgression, or that Adam could invoke divine decree only because he had already been forgiven. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Adam rejected blame solely because the act was ordained for him by Allah forty years before his creation (أَتَلُومُنِي عَلَى أَمْرٍ قَدَّرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَىَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَنِي بِأَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً), making no mention of repentance. By affirming twice that Adam defeated Moses with this deterministic plea (فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى), Muhammad validates blaming Allah's decree for human wrongdoing, contradicting the biblical teaching that God tempts no one and holds individuals accountable for their sin ([Genesis 3:11](bible://gn/3/11), [James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13)).

bukhari:6573.note: Muhammad states that on the Day of Resurrection, Allah will come to the believers in an unfamiliar form (*ṣūrah*)—prompting them to seek refuge from Him—before returning in a recognizable form (*ṣūrah*), and later laughs (*yaḍḥaku*) and admits the last man into Paradise after the man thrice breaks his sworn covenants not to ask for more (bukhari:806, bukhari:7437). Although later Ash'arī commentators attempt metaphorical reinterpretations (*ta'wīl*) of this passage, the explicit Arabic text affirms that God can manifest in a visible, recognizable form, directly undercutting the Islamic polemic that God cannot take on a form in biblical theophanies or the Incarnation ([John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14); [John 14:9](bible://jn/14/9)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَيَأْتِيهِمُ اللَّهُ فِي غَيْرِ الصُّورَةِ الَّتِي يَعْرِفُونَ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُونَ نَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْكَ، هَذَا مَكَانُنَا حَتَّى يَأْتِيَنَا رَبُّنَا، فَإِذَا أَتَانَا رَبُّنَا عَرَفْنَاهُ فَيَأْتِيهِمُ اللَّهُ فِي الصُّورَةِ الَّتِي يَعْرِفُونَ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُونَ أَنْتَ رَبُّنَا، فَيَتْبَعُونَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah will come to them in a shape other than they know and will say, 'I am your Lord.' They will say, 'We seek refuge with Allah from you. This is our place; (we will not follow you) till our Lord comes to us, and when our Lord comes to us, we will recognize Him. Then Allah will come to then in a shape they know and will say, "I am your Lord.' They will say, '(No doubt) You are our Lord,' and they will follow Him.

bukhari:6573.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—following Ash'arī commentators like Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—that *ṣūrah* (shape/form) merely denotes a metaphorical attribute (*ṣifah*) or a perceptual test in the beholders' eyes, and that Allah's laughing (*yaḍḥaku*) is purely a figure of speech for divine pleasure (*riḍā*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah Himself comes to them in an unfamiliar form (`فَيَأْتِيهِمُ اللَّهُ فِي غَيْرِ الصُّورَةِ الَّتِي يَعْرِفُونَ`) and declares, 'I am your Lord' (`أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ`)—a claim no created angel or apparition could utter—before returning in a form they recognize (`فِي الصُّورَةِ الَّتِي يَعْرِفُونَ`). Parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:7439`; `muslim:454`) confirm this literal mutability by stating that Allah 'transformed Himself' (`تَحَوَّلَ`) and uncovered His physical shin (`يَكْشِفُ عَنْ سَاقِهِ`), exposing a fatal contradiction whenever Muslim polemicists attack the Christian Incarnation as incompatible with divine immutability.

bukhari:6321.note: Muhammad declares that Allah descends (*yatanazzalu*) every night into the lowest heaven (*al-samāʾ al-dunyā*) during the final third of the night, calling out in the first person to ask who is invoking Him, petitioning Him, or seeking His forgiveness. Although later commentators attempt to reinterpret this metaphorically as the descent of an angel or abstract mercy, Allah's explicit first-person speech ('Who invokes Me so that I may respond to him?') affirms His own entry into created space during a nightly window that occurs continuously around a spherical Earth.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ يَتَنَزَّلُ رَبُّنَا تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا حِينَ يَبْقَى ثُلُثُ اللَّيْلِ الآخِرُ يَقُولُ مَنْ يَدْعُونِي فَأَسْتَجِيبَ لَهُ، مَنْ يَسْأَلُنِي فَأُعْطِيَهُ، وَمَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُنِي فَأَغْفِرَ لَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "When it is the last third of the night, our Lord, the Blessed, the Superior, descends every night to the heaven of the world and says, 'Is there anyone who invokes Me (demand anything from Me), that I may respond to his invocation; Is there anyone who asks Me for something that I may give (it to) him; Is there anyone who asks My forgiveness that I may forgive him?

bukhari:6321.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—that Allah's nightly descent is merely a metaphor for the descent of His mercy or a designated angel, or they invoke *bilā kayf* ('without modality') to deny spatial movement even while attacking the Christian Incarnation on the grounds that God cannot enter His creation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that 'our Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, descends' (*yatanazzalu Rabbunā tabāraka wa-ta'ālā*) and speaks exclusively in the divine first person ('Who asks My forgiveness that I may forgive him?' — *wa-man yastaghfirunī fa-aghfira lahu*), while the parallel in `muslim:1772` adds His declaration, 'I am the King!' (*anā al-Malik*), which completely refutes the excuse that an angel or abstract attribute is descending. Furthermore, because the 'last third of the night' (*thuluthu al-layli al-ākhir*) rotates continuously around a spherical earth, this narration either traps Allah permanently inside the lowest heaven (*al-samā' al-dunyā*) or betrays a flat-earth cosmology where night falls everywhere simultaneously.

muslim:6743.note: Muhammad states that when Moses rebuked Adam for misleading people and causing their expulsion from Paradise (and for his sin in muslim:6745), Adam defeated Moses in the argument solely by asking how Moses could blame him for an affair that had been ordained for him before he was created.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: تَحَاجَّ آدَمُ وَمُوسَى فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى فَقَالَ لَهُ مُوسَى أَنْتَ آدَمُ الَّذِي أَغْوَيْتَ النَّاسَ وَأَخْرَجْتَهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ فَقَالَ آدَمُ أَنْتَ الَّذِي أَعْطَاهُ اللَّهُ عِلْمَ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ وَاصْطَفَاهُ عَلَى النَّاسِ بِرِسَالَتِهِ قَالَ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَتَلُومُنِي عَلَى أَمْرٍ قُدِّرَ عَلَىَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ أُخْلَقَ
problematic_excerpt.english: There was argument between Adam and Moses, and Adam came the better of Moses. Moses said to him: You are the same Adam who misled people, and caused them to get out of Paradise. Adam said: You are the same (Moses) whom Allah endowed the knowledge of everything and selected him amongst the people as His Messenger. He said: Yes. Adam then again said: Even then you blame me for an affair which had been ordained for me before I was created

muslim:6743.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Adam was not using predestination to excuse his sin, claiming that Moses only blamed him for the earthly consequence of leaving Paradise rather than his act of disobedience. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Moses indicted Adam both for misleading humanity and for expelling them from Paradise (`أَغْوَيْتَ النَّاسَ وَأَخْرَجْتَهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ`), and that Adam defeated Moses (`فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى`) solely by protesting that the affair had been ordained upon him before he was created (`فَتَلُومُنِي عَلَى أَمْرٍ قُدِّرَ عَلَىَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ أُخْلَقَ`). By endorsing Adam's appeal to pre-creation decree as a victorious defense against blame, the narration shifts moral responsibility for human transgression onto Allah, contradicting [James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13).

bukhari:6596.note: When asked whether the inhabitants of Paradise are already distinguished from those of Hellfire and why people still perform deeds, Muhammad affirms that they are already known and declares that every person acts for that for which they were created, or that which has been made easy for them ([Deuteronomy 30:19](bible://dt/30/19); [Romans 2:6](bible://rom/2/6)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ رَجُلٌ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَيُعْرَفُ أَهْلُ الْجَنَّةِ مِنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ قَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ فَلِمَ يَعْمَلُ الْعَامِلُونَ قَالَ ‏"‏كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ لِمَا خُلِقَ لَهُ ـ أَوْ لِمَا يُسِّرَ لَهُ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A man said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Can the people of Paradise be known (differentiated) from the people of the Fire; The Prophet (ﷺ) replied, "Yes." The man said, "Why do people (try to) do (good) deeds?" The Prophet said, "Everyone will do the deeds for which he has been created to do or he will do those deeds which will be made easy for him to do."

bukhari:6596.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as explained in Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's commentary on *qadar*, this narration refers merely to Allah's passive foreknowledge (*'ilm*) of human free-will choices and that deeds serve only as outward signs (*'alāmāt*) rather than predetermined compulsion. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that every individual acts strictly toward the destiny for which they were created and divinely steered (*kullun ya'malu limā khuliqa lahu aw limā yussira lahu*), employing the passive verbs *khuliqa* (was created for) and *yussira* (was facilitated toward) to establish active divine causation rather than passive observation. This fatalistic mechanism is further confirmed by parallel Sahih narrations (`bukhari:1362`, `bukhari:4949`) and Quran 7:179, which explicitly state that Allah created multitudes specifically for Hellfire and actively facilitates the deeds of the damned to seal their pre-ordained decree.

bukhari:4736.note: Muhammad declares that Adam defeated Moses's rebuke over humanity's expulsion from Paradise (`فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى`) by arguing that Allah had already written the decree upon him (`كُتِبَ عَلَىَّ`) prior to his creation. While classical commentators claim Moses only blamed Adam for the calamity of expulsion rather than the sin itself, parallel narrations (bukhari:3409, bukhari:4738) explicitly cite Adam's sin and mistake (`بِذَنْبِكَ` / `خَطِيئَتُكَ`) as the action excused by pre-creation decree ([Deuteronomy 30:19](bible://dt/30/19); [James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: الْتَقَى آدَمُ وَمُوسَى، فَقَالَ مُوسَى لآدَمَ أَنْتَ الَّذِي أَشْقَيْتَ النَّاسَ وَأَخْرَجْتَهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ قَالَ لَهُ آدَمُ أَنْتَ الَّذِي اصْطَفَاكَ اللَّهُ بِرِسَالَتِهِ، وَاصْطَفَاكَ لِنَفْسِهِ وَأَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكَ التَّوْرَاةَ قَالَ نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ فَوَجَدْتَهَا كُتِبَ عَلَىَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَنِي قَالَ نَعَمْ‏.‏ فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى
problematic_excerpt.english: Adam and Moses met, and Moses said to Adam "You are the one who made people miserable and turned them out of Paradise." Adam said to him, "You are the one whom Allah selected for His message and whom He selected for Himself and upon whom He revealed the Torah." Moses said, 'Yes.' Adam said, "Did you find that written in my fate before my creation?' Moses said, 'Yes.' So Adam overcame Moses with this argument

bukhari:4736.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, per Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, Adam was not using divine predestination (*qadar*) to excuse his sin, but merely objecting to Moses blaming him for the calamity of expulsion after Allah had already accepted his repentance. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Adam's victorious rebuttal (*fa-ḥajja Ādamu Mūsā*) rested entirely on the plea that the matter was decreed against him before his creation (*kutiba 'alayya qabla an yakhluqanī*), making zero mention of repentance. Furthermore, parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:6614; muslim:6742) confirm that Moses indicted Adam's transgression itself (*bi-khaṭī'atika*—'by your sin') and that Adam defeated the moral charge solely by asking how he could be blamed for an act Allah had predestined for him before creating him (*atalūmunī 'alā amrin qaddarahu Allāhu 'alayya qabla an yakhluqanī*).

bukhari:4738.note: When Moses blames Adam for expelling humanity from Paradise specifically 'by your sin' (bi-dhanbika), Adam refutes the blame by appealing to what Allah wrote and decreed (qaddarahu) upon him before his creation. Muhammad rules that Adam defeated Moses with this argument, establishing that pre-creational divine decree nullifies blame for sin ([Ezekiel 18:20](bible://ez/18/20); [James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: حَاجَّ مُوسَى آدَمَ، فَقَالَ لَهُ أَنْتَ الَّذِي أَخْرَجْتَ النَّاسَ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ بِذَنْبِكَ وَأَشْقَيْتَهُمْ‏.‏ قَالَ قَالَ آدَمُ يَا مُوسَى أَنْتَ الَّذِي اصْطَفَاكَ اللَّهُ بِرِسَالَتِهِ وَبِكَلاَمِهِ أَتَلُومُنِي عَلَى أَمْرٍ كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَىَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَنِي أَوْ قَدَّرَهُ عَلَىَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَنِي ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى
problematic_excerpt.english: Moses argued with Adam and said to him (Adam), 'You are the one who got the people out of Paradise by your sin, and thus made them miserable." Adam replied, 'O Moses! You are the one whom Allah selected for His Message and for His direct talk. Yet you blame me for a thing which Allah had ordained for me before He created me?." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) further said, "So Adam overcame Moses by this Argument

bukhari:4738.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that—following Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn Ḥajar in *Fatḥ al-Bārī*—Adam did not invoke predestination (*qadar*) to excuse sin, claiming Moses only lamented the earthly calamity (*muṣībah*) of expulsion after Adam had already repented. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Moses indicted Adam specifically "by your sin" (*bi-dhanbika*, بِذَنْبِكَ), and in the parallel narration of `bukhari:3409`, Adam replies, "Do you blame me for doing a deed (*ʿamalan*) which Allah wrote upon me to do before He created me?" Rather than appealing to repentance, Adam cites only Allah's pre-creation decree (*katabahu Allāhu ʿalayya*) to absolve himself of culpability for his disobedience, and Muhammad ratifies this fatalistic plea by declaring, "So Adam overcame Moses" (*fa-ḥajja Ādamu Mūsā*).

bukhari:1292.note: Reported via Umar and Ibn Umar, Muhammad declares that a deceased person is tormented in the grave on account of the wailing and weeping of the living over him, directly conflicting with individual moral accountability ([Quran 6:164](quran://6/164); [Ezekiel 18:20](bible://ez/18/20); [Deuteronomy 24:16](bible://dt/24/16)). Although later commentators attempt to restrict this torment to cases where the deceased had instructed his family to wail, Umar applied the rule literally to spontaneous weeping on his deathbed (bukhari:1290), and Aisha explicitly rejected Umar and Ibn Umar's narration as incompatible with [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164) (bukhari:1288, bukhari:3978).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ الْمَيِّتُ يُعَذَّبُ فِي قَبْرِهِ بِمَا نِيحَ عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏‏.‏ تَابَعَهُ عَبْدُ الأَعْلَى حَدَّثَنَا يَزِيدُ بْنُ زُرَيْعٍ حَدَّثَنَا سَعِيدٌ حَدَّثَنَا قَتَادَةُ‏.‏ وَقَالَ آدَمُ عَنْ شُعْبَةَ ‏"‏ الْمَيِّتُ يُعَذَّبُ بِبُكَاءِ الْحَىِّ عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The deceased is tortured in his grave for the wailing done over him." Narrated Shu'ba: The deceased is tortured for the wailing of the living ones over him

bukhari:1292.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Aisha's objection in parallel narrations or commentaries like Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—that Umar misremembered the saying, that `yu'adhdhabu` merely means emotional distress, or that the torment only applies if the deceased explicitly instructed his family to wail before dying. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an unqualified universal rule (`الْمَيِّتُ يُعَذَّبُ بِبُكَاءِ الْحَىِّ عَلَيْهِ` — 'the deceased is tortured by the weeping of the living over him') with zero stipulation of a prior will, and in parallel Sahih accounts (`bukhari:1290`, `muslim:2143`), a dying Umar strictly forbade Suhaib from weeping over him to avoid this exact punishment—proving the Caliph himself knew it applied even to a righteous believer who opposed wailing. Consequently, apologists are trapped in a fatal dilemma: either affirm vicarious grave-torture in direct contradiction to [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164), or admit that the highest-ranking Companions and *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* transmitted corrupted, contradictory theology.

bukhari:1362.note: Muhammad declares that every created soul has already had its place in Paradise or Hell and its status as blessed or wretched written for it. When asked whether people should therefore rely on what is written and abandon deeds, he replies that the blessed are facilitated to do the deeds of the blessed and the wretched are facilitated to do the deeds of the wretched, citing [Quran 92:5-10](quran://92/5).
