problematic_excerpt.arabic: مَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ، مَا مِنْ نَفْسٍ مَنْفُوسَةٍ إِلاَّ كُتِبَ مَكَانُهَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ وَالنَّارِ، وَإِلاَّ قَدْ كُتِبَ شَقِيَّةً أَوْ سَعِيدَةً ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَفَلاَ نَتَّكِلُ عَلَى كِتَابِنَا وَنَدَعُ الْعَمَلَ، فَمَنْ كَانَ مِنَّا مِنْ أَهْلِ السَّعَادَةِ فَسَيَصِيرُ إِلَى عَمَلِ أَهْلِ السَّعَادَةِ، وَأَمَّا مَنْ كَانَ مِنَّا مِنْ أَهْلِ الشَّقَاوَةِ فَسَيَصِيرُ إِلَى عَمَلِ أَهْلِ الشَّقَاوَةِ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَمَّا أَهْلُ السَّعَادَةِ فَيُيَسَّرُونَ لِعَمَلِ السَّعَادَةِ، وَأَمَّا أَهْلُ الشَّقَاوَةِ فَيُيَسَّرُونَ لِعَمَلِ الشَّقَاوَةِ
problematic_excerpt.english: There is none among you, and not a created soul, but has place either in Paradise or in Hell assigned for him and it is also determined for him whether he will be among the blessed or wretched." A man said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Should we not depend on what has been written for us and leave the deeds as whoever amongst us is blessed will do the deeds of a blessed person and whoever amongst us will be wretched, will do the deeds of a wretched person?" The Prophet said, "The good deeds are made easy for the blessed, and bad deeds are made easy for the wretched.

bukhari:1362.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, following Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī, that this decree (*kitābah*) merely reflects Allah's non-coercive foreknowledge (*ʿilm*) of free human choices, claiming Muhammad's citation of Quran 92:5–10 affirms moral agency (*kasb*) rather than fatalism (*jabr*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that every soul is already inscribed as wretched or blessed (`قَدْ كُتِبَ شَقِيَّةً أَوْ سَعِيدَةً`), and when a companion concludes that their preordained category dictates their future conduct, Muhammad validates that deterministic premise by declaring in the passive voice that the wretched 'are facilitated toward the deeds of wretchedness' (`أَمَّا أَهْلُ الشَّقَاوَةِ فَيُيَسَّرُونَ لِعَمَلِ الشَّقَاوَةِ`). Thus, the Arabic syntax makes one's pre-assigned identity as 'wretched' the prior cause that channels a person into evil deeds, matching Sahih parallels (`bukhari:3208`, `bukhari:6605`) where the written decree (`الْكِتَابُ`) overtakes a person at the end of life to compel the deeds of Hell.

bukhari:4946.note: While at a funeral, Muhammad scrapes the ground with a stick and declares that every person's seat in either the Fire or Paradise has already been written. When his companions ask whether they should simply rely on this decree, he instructs them to continue working because everyone is facilitated toward what was decreed for them, reciting [Quran 92:5-6](quran://92/5-6) (cf. bukhari:1362; [Ezekiel 18:20](bible://ez/18/20); [James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَأَخَذَ عُودًا يَنْكُتُ فِي الأَرْضِ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلاَّ وَقَدْ كُتِبَ مَقْعَدُهُ مِنَ النَّارِ أَوْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَفَلاَ نَتَّكِلُ قَالَ ‏"‏ اعْمَلُوا فَكُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ ‏{‏فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَى وَاتَّقَى * وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَى‏}‏ الآيَةَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: he took a small stick and started scraping the earth with it and said, "There is none among you but has his place written for him, either in the Hell Fire or in Paradise." They (the people) said, "Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Shall we depend on this (and leave work)?" He replied. "Carry on doing (good deeds), for everybody will find easy (to do) such deeds as will lead him to his destined place." The Prophet (ﷺ) then recited:-- 'As for him who gives (in charity) and keeps his duty to Allah, and believes in the Best Reward

bukhari:4946.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, that the decree of a person's place in Hell or Paradise reflects mere descriptive foreknowledge (*ʿilm sābiq*) rather than coercive compulsion (*jabr*), claiming Muhammad's command to 'work' (*iʿmalū*) and citation of Quran 92:5 preserve genuine moral agency. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that every soul's seat in the Fire or Paradise has already been written (*wa-qad kutiba maqʿaduhu min al-nār aw min al-jannah*) and that everyone is passively facilitated (*fa-kullun muyassarun*)—explicitly defined in the immediate parallel narration (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4945) as `مُيَسَّرٌ لِمَا خُلِقَ لَهُ` ('facilitated toward that for which he was created'). Rather than rescuing free will, Muhammad's answer confirms that human deeds are merely the pre-engineered conduit through which Allah steers individuals into the eternal fate He already created and scripted for them.

bukhari:4947.note: Muhammad declares that every person's seat in Paradise or Hellfire has already been written, and when his companions ask whether they should simply rely on this decree, he instructs them to continue performing deeds because each person is facilitated toward their pre-written fate, reciting [Quran 92:5](quran://92/5)-[10](quran://92/10) ([Deuteronomy 30:19](bible://dt/30/19); [Romans 2:6](bible://rom/2/6)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلاَّ وَقَدْ كُتِبَ مَقْعَدُهُ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ وَمَقْعَدُهُ مِنَ النَّارِ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقُلْنَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَفَلاَ نَتَّكِلُ قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ، اعْمَلُوا فَكُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ ‏{‏فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَى وَاتَّقَى * وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَى * فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَى‏}‏ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ ‏{‏فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَى‏}‏
problematic_excerpt.english: he said, "There is none among you but has his place written for him, either in Paradise or in the Hell-Fire." We said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Shall we depend (on this fact and give up work)?" He replied, "No! Carry on doing good deeds, for everybody will find easy (to do) such deeds as will lead him to his destined place." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: 'As for him who gives (in charity) and keeps his duty to Allah, and believes in the Best reward. We will make smooth for him the path of ease....the path for evil

bukhari:4947.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad's command to 'work' (*i'malū*) and his citation of Quran 92:5–10 affirm human moral agency, claiming the written decree (*kutiba*) merely reflects Allah's passive foreknowledge of what individuals will freely choose. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *'wa-qad kutiba maq'aduhu'* ('his place has already been written') and *'fa-kullun muyassar'* ('for everybody is facilitated/steered'), which the immediate parallel narration (`bukhari:4949`) completes as *'limā khuliqa lahu'* ('toward that for which he was created')—proving that a person's pre-assigned creation for Hellfire or Paradise causally dictates which deeds are made easy for them. In fact, both Ibn Hajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) and Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) weaponize this exact Hadith to refute the *Qadariyyah* (proponents of free will), confirming that in classical Sunni orthodoxy human actions are merely outward signs (*'alāmāt*) engineered by Allah to fulfill His prior decree.

bukhari:4949.note: Muhammad declares that every person's seat in the Hellfire or Paradise has already been written, instructing his companions to continue working because everyone is facilitated to perform the deeds of the blessed or the wretched for which they were created ([Quran 92:5-10](quran://92/5)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: مَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلاَّ وَقَدْ كُتِبَ مَقْعَدُهُ مِنَ النَّارِ وَمَقْعَدُهُ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَفَلاَ نَتَّكِلُ عَلَى كِتَابِنَا وَنَدَعُ الْعَمَلَ قَالَ ‏"‏ اعْمَلُوا فَكُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ لِمَا خُلِقَ لَهُ، أَمَّا مَنْ كَانَ مِنْ أَهْلِ السَّعَادَةِ فَيُيَسَّرُ لِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ السَّعَادَةِ، وَأَمَّا مَنْ كَانَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الشَّقَاءِ فَيُيَسَّرُ لِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الشَّقَاوَةِ ‏"‏‏.‏ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ ‏{‏فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَى وَاتَّقَى * وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَى‏}‏ الآيَةَ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: There is none among you but has his place written for him either in the Hell Fire or in Paradise." They said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Shall we not depend upon what has been written for us and give up deeds? He said, "Carry on doing (good) deeds, for everybody will find easy to do such deeds as will lead him to his destined place for which he has been created. So he who is destined to be among the happy (in the Hereafter), will find it easy to do the deeds characteristic of such people, while he who is destined to be among the miserable ones, will find it easy to do the deeds characteristic of such people." Then he recited: 'As for him who gives (in charity) and fears Allah, and believes in the best

bukhari:4949.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this pre-inscription (*al-kitābah*) merely reflects divine foreknowledge (*'ilm*) of free human choices, pointing to Muhammad's command to 'work' (*i'malū*) and his citation of [Quran 92:5-10](quran://92/5) as proof of moral agency rather than compulsion (*jabr*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that 'everyone is facilitated toward that for which he was created' (*kullun muyassarun limā khuliqa lahu* — كُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ لِمَا خُلِقَ لَهُ), establishing that a person's prior designation among 'the people of misery' (*ahl al-shaqā'*) is what passively channels (*fayuyassaru*) them into performing the deeds of the damned. This teleological fatalism is further cemented by [Quran 7:179](quran://7/179) and parallel Sahih traditions (bukhari:3208, muslim:6769), which confirm that Allah creates specific souls expressly for Hellfire while they are still in the womb or their fathers' loins.

muslim:272.note: Muhammad declares to Abu Dharr on the authority of Gabriel that anyone in his community who dies without associating partners with Allah will enter Paradise, explicitly confirming this applies even if he committed adultery and theft (contrast with [1 Corinthians 6:9](bible://1cor/6/9), [Revelation 21:8](bible://rv/21/8)). Classical Sunni commentators such as al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar affirm this narration as foundational orthodoxy, holding that any Muslim free of polytheism is guaranteed eventual entry into Paradise even if he dies unrepentant of major sins.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَتَانِي جِبْرِيلُ - عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ - فَبَشَّرَنِي أَنَّهُ مَنْ مَاتَ مِنْ أُمَّتِكَ لاَ يُشْرِكُ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ وَإِنْ زَنَى وَإِنْ سَرَقَ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ وَإِنْ زَنَى وَإِنْ سَرَقَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Gabriel came to me and gave me the tidings: Verily he who died amongst your Ummah without associating anything with Allah would enter Paradise. I (the narrator) said: Even if he committed adultery and theft. He (the Holy Prophet) said: (Yes), even if he committed adultery and theft

muslim:272.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, according to Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, this guarantee either presumes repentance before death or means the grave sinner may first be temporarily punished in Hellfire before eventually entering Paradise under Allah's arbitrary will (*mashīʾah*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states an unconditional *مَنْ مَاتَ مِنْ أُمَّتِكَ لَا يُشْرِكُ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ ... وَإِنْ زَنَى وَإِنْ سَرَقَ* ('whoever dies amongst your Ummah without associating anything with Allah would enter Paradise... even if he committed adultery and theft') with zero requirement of repentance, while parallel narrations (`muslim:273`, `bukhari:1237`) add *عَلَى رَغْمِ أَنْفِ أَبِي ذَرٍّ* ('in spite of Abu Dharr's defiance') specifically to silence Abu Dharr's moral objection. Even granting the commentators' interpolation of temporary purgation, Sunni soteriology still guarantees eternal Paradise to unrepentant adulterers and thieves solely for avoiding *shirk*, divorcing final salvation from divine holiness and moral regeneration.

muslim:273.note: Muhammad declares that anyone who professes 'there is no god but Allah' and dies in that state will enter Paradise, affirming three times to Abu Dharr's repeated questioning that this holds even if the person commits adultery and theft, before adding on the fourth time, 'in defiance of Abu Dharr' (contrast with [1 Corinthians 6:9](bible://1cor/6/9), [Galatians 5:19](bible://gal/5/19)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: مَا مِنْ عَبْدٍ قَالَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ مَاتَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ إِلاَّ دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ وَإِنْ زَنَى وَإِنْ سَرَقَ قَالَ ‏"‏ وَإِنْ زَنَى وَإِنْ سَرَقَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قُلْتُ وَإِنْ زَنَى وَإِنْ سَرَقَ قَالَ ‏"‏ وَإِنْ زَنَى وَإِنْ سَرَقَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ ثَلاَثًا ثُمَّ قَالَ فِي الرَّابِعَةِ ‏"‏ عَلَى رَغْمِ أَنْفِ أَبِي ذَرٍّ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: There is none among the bondsmen who affirmed his faith in La illaha ill-Allah there is no God but Allah) and died in this state and did not enter Paradise. I (Abu Dharr) said: Even if he committed adultery and theft? He (the Holy Prophet) replied: (Yes) even though he committed adultery and theft. I (again said): Even if he committed adultery and theft? He replied: (Yes) even though he committed adultery and theft. (Th Holy Prophet repeated it three times) and said for the fourth time: In defiance of Abu Dharr.

muslim:273.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that, as Al-Nawawī (1233–1277 AD) and Ibn Ḥajar (1372–1449 AD) claim, this narration either predated the revelation of Islamic legal commandments or merely means that a sinning monotheist will eventually enter Paradise after temporary punishment in Hell or arbitrary divine pardon. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states without qualification that anyone who dies professing the creed enters Paradise "even if he committed adultery and even if he stole" (وَإِنْ زَنَى وَإِنْ سَرَقَ), a guarantee Muhammad repeats three times before silencing Abu Dharr's moral outrage with "in defiance of Abu Dharr" (عَلَى رَغْمِ أَنْفِ أَبِي ذَرٍّ). Furthermore, even the commentators' fallback—that unrepentant adulterers and thieves are guaranteed eventual Paradise solely for reciting a formula while upright non-Muslims burn eternally—only confirms that Islamic soteriology substitutes creedal tribalism for genuine moral regeneration.

muslim:2150.note: Umar and Ibn Umar narrate from Muhammad that the deceased is punished for the weeping of his family, a statement Umar applies directly to Suhaib's weeping over him after he is wounded. Although Aisha rejects the punishment of a believer by citing [Quran 6:164](quran://6/164), she swears that Muhammad declared Allah increases the punishment of the unbeliever because of his family's weeping over him ([Deuteronomy 24:16](bible://dt/24/16); [Ezekiel 18:20](bible://ez/18/20)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَلَمَّا أَنْ أُصِيبَ عُمَرُ دَخَلَ صُهَيْبٌ يَبْكِي يَقُولُ وَاأَخَاهْ وَاصَاحِبَاهْ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ عُمَرُ يَا صُهَيْبُ أَتَبْكِي عَلَىَّ وَقَدْ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّ الْمَيِّتَ يُعَذَّبُ بِبَعْضِ بُكَاءِ أَهْلِهِ عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ فَلَمَّا مَاتَ عُمَرُ ذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِعَائِشَةَ فَقَالَتْ يَرْحَمُ اللَّهُ عُمَرَ لاَ وَاللَّهِ مَا حَدَّثَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُعَذِّبُ الْمُؤْمِنَ بِبُكَاءِ أَحَدٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَلَكِنْ قَالَ ‏"‏ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَزِيدُ الْكَافِرَ عَذَابًا بِبُكَاءِ أَهْلِهِ عَلَيْهِ ‏"‏ قَالَ وَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ حَسْبُكُمُ الْقُرْآنُ ‏{‏ وَلاَ تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَى‏}‏
problematic_excerpt.english: When 'Umar was wounded, Suhaib came walling: Alas, for the brother! alas for the companion! 'Umar said: O Suhaib, do you wail for me, whereas the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:" The dead would be punished on account of the lamentation of the (members of his family)"? Ibn 'Abbas said: When 'Umar died I made a mention of it to 'A'isha. She said: May Allah have mercy upon 'Umar! I swear by Allah that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) never said that Allah would punish the believer because of the weeping (of any one of the members of his family), but he said that Allah would increase the punishment of the unbeliever because of the weeping of his family over him. 'A'isha said: The Qur'an is enough for you (when it states):" No bearer of burden will bear another's burden" (vi. 164).

muslim:2150.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*), that the deceased is only punished if he previously commanded his family to wail, that 'punished' (*yuʿadhdhabu*) merely denotes emotional distress, or that ʿĀʾishah's correction invoking Qurʾān 6:164 resolves the moral dilemma. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states without qualification that the dead is tormented by his family's weeping (*yuʿadhdhabu bi-bukāʾi ahlihi ʿalayhi*)—which is why ʿUmar feared punishment when Ṣuhayb wept unprompted—and ʿĀʾishah's own counter-narration explicitly states that Allah increases the unbeliever's torment because of his family's tears (*inna Allāha yazīdu al-kāfira ʿadhāban bi-bukāʾi ahlihi ʿalayhi*). Thus, even ʿĀʾishah's revision still depicts Allah violating the very verse she cites (Qurʾān 6:164, *wa-lā taziru wāziratun wizra ukhrā*) by inflicting extra torment on the dead for the independent actions of the living, while exposing an irreconcilable contradiction among Islam's foremost Companions (ʿUmar and Ibn ʿUmar versus ʿĀʾishah) over what Muhammad actually said.

muslim:2305.note: Muhammad tells Abu Dharr that Gabriel appeared to him by the stony ground and instructed him to give glad tidings to his nation (`ummah`) that anyone who dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise, affirming three times that this holds true even if the person committed theft, committed fornication, and drank wine ([1 Corinthians 6:9](bible://1cor/6/9), [Revelation 21:8](bible://rv/21/8)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏"‏ ذَاكَ جِبْرِيلُ عَرَضَ لِي فِي جَانِبِ الْحَرَّةِ فَقَالَ بَشِّرْ أُمَّتَكَ أَنَّهُ مَنْ مَاتَ لاَ يُشْرِكُ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ يَا جِبْرِيلُ وَإِنْ سَرَقَ وَإِنْ زَنَى قَالَ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ وَإِنْ سَرَقَ وَإِنْ زَنَى قَالَ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ وَإِنْ سَرَقَ وَإِنْ زَنَى قَالَ نَعَمْ وَإِنْ شَرِبَ الْخَمْرَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: He (the Holy Prophet) said: It was Gabriel who met me by the side of the stony ground and said: Give glad tidings to your Ummah that he who died without associating ought with Allah would go into Paradise. I said: Gabriel, even if he committed theft and fornication? He said: Yes. I said: Even it he committed theft and fornication? He said: Yes, I again said: Even if he committed theft and fornication? He said: Yes, even if he drank wine

muslim:2305.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that this Hadith does not grant moral immunity for major sins (*kabā'ir*), claiming the sinner must either repent before death or first endure temporary punishment in Hellfire before eventually entering Paradise. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Gabriel commanded Muhammad to proclaim unconditional glad tidings (`بَشِّرْ أُمَّتَكَ`) that anyone who dies without *shirk* enters Paradise (`مَنْ مَاتَ لاَ يُشْرِكُ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ`), answering Muhammad's thrice-repeated shock—"even if he committed theft and even if he committed fornication?" (`وَإِنْ سَرَقَ وَإِنْ زَنَى`)—with an unqualified "Yes, even if he drank wine" (`نَعَمْ وَإِنْ شَرِبَ الْخَمْرَ`) and zero mention of repentance or purgatorial fire. Indeed, if this promise merely meant that repentant sinners are forgiven, neither Muhammad nor Abu Dharr—whom Muhammad rebukes in the parallel *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 5827 with "even in spite of Abu Dharr's nose!" (`وَإِنْ رَغِمَ أَنْفُ أَبِي ذَرٍّ`)—would have been scandalized by the statement, proving that Islamic soteriology guarantees Paradise to unrepentant thieves and adulterers based purely on ritual monotheism.

bukhari:6612.note: Citing Abu Hurayrah's report as the closest illustration of minor faults (*al-lamam*), Ibn Abbas relays Muhammad's declaration that Allah has decreed upon the son of Adam his share of adultery (*zina*), which he will inevitably attain (*adraka dhalika la mahalah*). Muhammad defines this decreed share as the adultery of the eye in looking, the adultery of the tongue in speaking, and the soul's wishing and desiring, which the private parts then either confirm or deny ([James 1:13-14](bible://jas/1/13); [1 Corinthians 10:13](bible://1cor/10/13)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَتَبَ عَلَى ابْنِ آدَمَ حَظَّهُ مِنَ الزِّنَا، أَدْرَكَ ذَلِكَ لاَ مَحَالَةَ، فَزِنَا الْعَيْنِ النَّظَرُ، وَزِنَا اللِّسَانِ الْمَنْطِقُ، وَالنَّفْسُ تَمَنَّى وَتَشْتَهِي، وَالْفَرْجُ يُصَدِّقُ ذَلِكَ، وَيُكَذِّبُهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: "Allah has written for the son of Adam his inevitable share of adultery whether he is aware of it or not: The adultery of the eye is the looking (at something which is sinful to look at), and the adultery of the tongue is to utter (what it is unlawful to utter), and the innerself wishes and longs for (adultery) and the private parts turn that into reality or refrain from submitting to the temptation

bukhari:6612.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration merely reflects God's non-coercive foreknowledge of minor, metaphorical slips (*al-lamam*), claiming that the concluding clause proves humans retain free will to refrain from actual physical fornication. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah bindingly decreed upon (`كَتَبَ عَلَى`, *kataba ʿalā*) the son of Adam his allotted share of adultery, which he will "inevitably attain without escape" (`أَدْرَكَ ذَلِكَ لاَ مَحَالَةَ`, *adraka dhālika lā maḥālata*—a fatalistic clause the translator obscures as "whether he is aware of it or not"). Furthermore, al-Bukhārī places this narration directly in the Book of Divine Predestination (*Kitāb al-Qadar*), proving that whether the sin is unlawful lustful looking, speaking, or physical consummation (`وَالْفَرْجُ يُصَدِّقُ ذَلِكَ`), Islamic orthodoxy views the human commission of impurity as inescapably preordained by Allah.

bukhari:7003.note: At the funeral of the emigrant companion Uthman bin Maz'un in Medina, Muhammad questions a woman's testimony that Allah has honored the deceased and swears by Allah that, despite being Allah's Messenger, he does not know what will be done with him (matching [Quran 46:9](quran://46/9)). Although a variant wording in bukhari:7004 reads 'what will be done with him' and Sunni commentators often argue this statement preceded the assurance of forgiveness in [Quran 48:2](quran://48/2), this canonical transmission explicitly records Muhammad disclaiming knowledge of his own posthumous fate.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَوَاللَّهِ مَا أَدْرِي وَأَنَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ مَاذَا يُفْعَلُ بِي
problematic_excerpt.english: By Allah, in spite of the fact that I am Allah's Messenger (ﷺ), I do not know what Allah will do to me.

bukhari:7003.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Hajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī, that Muhammad's uncertainty referred merely to worldly trials, was later abrogated by Surah 48:2, or resulted from a transmitter slip for 'what will be done with him' (bihi). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states 'wa-wallāhi mā adrī wa-anā rasūlu Allāhi mādhā yufʿalu bī' ('By Allah, I do not know—while I am the Messenger of Allah—what will be done with me'), where the circumstantial clause appealing to his own prophetic office grammatically requires the first-person bī ('with me') and verbatim echoes Quran 46:9 ('wa-mā adrī mā yufʿalu bī wa-lā bikum'). Furthermore, because Muhammad swore this oath specifically to rebuke Umm al-ʿAlāʾ for declaring that Allah had honored the newly deceased ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn in the hereafter ('laqad akramaka Allāh'), the context is strictly eschatological and proves that even Islam's prophet lacked assurance of salvation.

bukhari:7515.note: Muhammad declares that Adam defeated Moses in a debate after Moses blamed him for causing his offspring's expulsion from Paradise, with Adam objecting that the matter had been divinely ordained for him before his creation. Although commentators like al-Nawawī and Ibn Ḥajar argue that Moses only reproached a repentant Adam for the resulting earthly calamity rather than the sin itself, the text explicitly validates appealing to pre-eternal divine decree to deflect blame, contradicting the Biblical teaching that human beings bear personal moral responsibility for their transgressions rather than attributing them to God ([James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ آدَمُ أَنْتَ مُوسَى الَّذِي اصْطَفَاكَ اللَّهُ بِرِسَالاَتِهِ وَكَلاَمِهِ، ثُمَّ تَلُومُنِي عَلَى أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِّرَ عَلَىَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ أُخْلَقَ‏.‏ فَحَجَّ آدَمُ مُوسَى
problematic_excerpt.english: Adam said, "You are Moses whom Allah chose for His Message and for His direct talk, yet you blame me for a matter which had been ordained for me even before my creation?' Thus Adam overcame Moses

bukhari:7515.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, following Ibn Taymiyyah and Al-Nawawī, that Moses only blamed Adam for the earthly calamity (*al-muṣībah*) of leaving Paradise rather than his already-forgiven sin, claiming divine decree (*qadar*) may be cited to accept calamities but never to excuse sins. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Adam deflected blame for his own action by declaring it was "a matter which had been ordained for me even before my creation" (*amrin qad quddira ʿalayya qabla an ukhlaq*), while parallel Sahih narrations (such as bukhari:6614 and 3409) explicitly record Moses condemning Adam's "sin" (*khaṭīʾatuka*) and Adam excusing the specific deed Allah wrote for him to commit. By concluding "Thus Adam overcame Moses" (*fa-ḥajja Ādamu Mūsā*), Muhammad directly ratifies divine pre-ordination as a victorious defense to absolve human moral culpability.

bukhari:7551.note: When asked by Imran why people strive to perform deeds, Muhammad declares that every person is facilitated to do that for which they were created, a foundational statement of divine predestination (qadar) affirming that individuals are eased toward the deeds leading to their predetermined final abode.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قُلْتُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فِيمَا يَعْمَلُ الْعَامِلُونَ قَالَ ‏ "‏ كُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ لِمَا خُلِقَ لَهُ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: I said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Why should a doer (people) try to do good deeds?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Everybody will find easy to do such deeds as will lead him to his destined place for which he has been created

bukhari:7551.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that divine decree (*qadar*) merely reflects Allah's passive foreknowledge of free human choices rather than coercive compulsion (*jabr*), appealing to Ash'ari *kasb* (acquisition) theory to claim humans retain moral agency. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *kullun muyassaru limā khuliqa lahu* ('everyone is facilitated for that for which he was created'), using the purposive preposition *limā* ('for that which') with the passive verb *khuliqa* ('he was created') to establish predetermined purpose rather than passive foreknowledge. As the fuller parallel narrations in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4949 and *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* 2649 confirm, `Imran asked this question precisely because Muhammad had just declared that the inhabitants of Paradise and Hellfire are already distinguished and written, proving that Allah creates individuals specifically for Hell (Quran 7:179) and actively facilitates their deeds to seal that fate.

bukhari:7552.note: Muhammad declares that every person's seat in either the Fire or Paradise has already been written, and when asked whether people should simply rely on that decree, he instructs them to work because everyone is facilitated toward their outcome, reciting [Quran 92:5](quran://92/5). Although the English translation supplies 'for which he has been created' in this entry, the Arabic text here ends at 'everyone is facilitated' (fa-kullun muyassar), with the full clause 'for that for which he was created' (lima khuliqa lahu) appearing explicitly in the immediately preceding narration (bukhari:7551).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: مَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلاَّ كُتِبَ مَقْعَدُهُ مِنَ النَّارِ أَوْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالُوا أَلاَ نَتَّكِلُ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ اعْمَلُوا فَكُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ
problematic_excerpt.english: "There is none of you but has his place assigned either in Hell or in Paradise." They (the people) said, "Shall we not depend upon that (and give up doing any deeds)?' He said, " Carry on doing (good deeds) for everybody will find it easy to do such deeds as will lead him to his destined place for which he has been created ."

bukhari:7552.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Ibn Ḥajar's Fatḥ al-Bārī and Al-Nawawī, that Allah's decree here merely reflects passive divine foreknowledge of human choices, claiming the imperative اعْمَلُوا ("do deeds") affirms genuine free will and moral responsibility. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states كُتِبَ مَقْعَدُهُ مِنَ النَّارِ أَوْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ ("his seat in the Fire or in Paradise has already been written") and فَكُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ ("for everyone is facilitated/steered"), which parallel Sahih narrations of this exact speech (bukhari:4949; muslim:6731) complete as فَكُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ لِمَا خُلِقَ لَهُ ("for everyone is steered toward that for which he was created"). Rather than mere foreknowledge, Allah pre-assigns each person's eternal destination and actively channels their deeds toward the end for which He created them—a fatalism reinforced in muslim:6769, where Muhammad states that Allah created specific people for Hellfire while they were still in their fathers' loins.

muslim:6755.note: Muhammad declares that a share of adultery (*zinā*) has been written upon every son of Adam, which he will inevitably commit without escape through the eyes looking, the ears listening, the tongue speaking, the hand seizing, the foot walking, the heart lusting and wishing, and the genitals confirming or belying it.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ كُتِبَ عَلَى ابْنِ آدَمَ نَصِيبُهُ مِنَ الزِّنَى مُدْرِكٌ ذَلِكَ لاَ مَحَالَةَ فَالْعَيْنَانِ زِنَاهُمَا النَّظَرُ وَالأُذُنَانِ زِنَاهُمَا الاِسْتِمَاعُ وَاللِّسَانُ زِنَاهُ الْكَلاَمُ وَالْيَدُ زِنَاهَا الْبَطْشُ وَالرِّجْلُ زِنَاهَا الْخُطَا وَالْقَلْبُ يَهْوَى وَيَتَمَنَّى وَيُصَدِّقُ ذَلِكَ الْفَرْجُ وَيُكَذِّبُهُ ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying. Allah fixed the very portion of adultery which a man will indulge in. There would be no escape from it. The adultery of the eye is the lustful look and the adultery of the ears is listening to voluptuous (song or talk) and the adultery of the tongue is licentious speech and the adultery of the hand is the lustful grip (embrace) and the adultery of the feet is to walk (to the place) where he intends to commit adultery and the heart yearns and desires which he may or may not put into effect

muslim:6755.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this narration merely warns against metaphorical temptations of the senses and reflects divine foreknowledge rather than predestined sin, since a person can still refrain from consummating the act. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *kutiba 'alā ibn Ādam naṣībuhu min al-zinā mudrikun dhālika lā maḥālata* ('written upon the son of Adam is his share of adultery, which he will inevitably commit without escape'), which the published translation renders as 'Allah fixed the very portion of adultery which a man will indulge in. There would be no escape from it.' Even if the genitals belie the desire rather than confirm it (*wa-yuṣaddiqu dhālika al-farju wa-yukadhhibuhu*), the text still declares that Allah has fixed an inescapable share of *zinā* upon every person's eyes, ears, tongue, hands, feet, and lusting heart (`bukhari:6243`, `bukhari:6612`, `muslim:6754`), contrasting with [James 1:13](bible://jas/1/13).

muslim:6768.note: When Aisha remarks that a deceased child is blessed as a bird of Paradise, Muhammad responds by asking whether she does not know that Allah created both Paradise and Hell and created inhabitants for each ([Quran 7:179](quran://7/179)). The immediate parallel report (muslim:6769) specifies that this was an Ansari child who died before reaching the age of sin, and that Allah created the inhabitants of Hell while they were still in their fathers' loins.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَتْ تُوُفِّيَ صَبِيٌّ فَقُلْتُ طُوبَى لَهُ عُصْفُورٌ مِنْ عَصَافِيرِ الْجَنَّةِ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ أَوَلاَ تَدْرِينَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ الْجَنَّةَ وَخَلَقَ النَّارَ فَخَلَقَ لِهَذِهِ أَهْلاً وَلِهَذِهِ أَهْلاً ‏"‏
problematic_excerpt.english: A'isha, the mother of the believers, reported that a child died and I said:There is happiness for this child who is a bird from amongst the birds of Paradise. Thereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Don't you know that Allah created the Paradise and He created the Hell and He created the dwellers for this (Paradise) and the denizens for this (Hell)?

muslim:6768.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Muhammad was merely instructing Aisha not to pronounce definitive judgment on any specific individual's afterlife without revelation, or that Allah's decree reflects passive foreknowledge rather than the arbitrary predestination of children. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that when a young child died (*tuwuffiya ṣabiyyun*) and Aisha called him a bird of Paradise (*ʿuṣfūrun min ʿaṣāfīri al-jannah*), Muhammad countered her by declaring that Allah created both Paradise and the Fire and "created inhabitants for this and inhabitants for this" (*fa-khalaqa li-hādhihi ahlan wa-li-hādhihi ahlan*). Instead of assuring the salvation of a child who died prior to moral accountability (contrast [Matthew 19:14](bible://mt/19/14)), Muhammad's response subjects even deceased children to a fatalistic decree in which Allah creates inhabitants specifically for Hell ([Quran 7:179](quran://7/179), muslim:6769).

muslim:6739.note: When asked whether people's deeds are already decreed upon them from a prior decree or determined going forward by what their Prophet brought them, Muhammad replies that they are already decreed and executed among them because Allah inspires every soul with its wickedness and its piety ([Quran 91:7](quran://91/7), [Quran 91:8](quran://91/8)). Addressing whether this preordination constitutes injustice, Imran b. al-Husayn approves Abu al-Aswad's answer that everything is Allah's creation and possession and that He cannot be questioned about what He does while they will be questioned ([Quran 21:23](quran://21/23)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ لِي عِمْرَانُ بْنُ الْحُصَيْنِ أَرَأَيْتَ مَا يَعْمَلُ النَّاسُ الْيَوْمَ وَيَكْدَحُونَ فِيهِ أَشَىْءٌ قُضِيَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَضَى عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ قَدَرِ مَا سَبَقَ أَوْ فِيمَا يُسْتَقْبَلُونَ بِهِ مِمَّا أَتَاهُمْ بِهِ نَبِيُّهُمْ وَثَبَتَتِ الْحُجَّةُ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقُلْتُ بَلْ شَىْءٌ قُضِيَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَضَى عَلَيْهِمْ قَالَ فَقَالَ أَفَلاَ يَكُونُ ظُلْمًا قَالَ فَفَزِعْتُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَزَعًا شَدِيدًا وَقُلْتُ كُلُّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقُ اللَّهِ وَمِلْكُ يَدِهِ فَلاَ يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لِي يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ إِنِّي لَمْ أُرِدْ بِمَا سَأَلْتُكَ إِلاَّ لأَحْزُرَ عَقْلَكَ إِنَّ رَجُلَيْنِ مِنْ مُزَيْنَةَ أَتَيَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالاَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَرَأَيْتَ مَا يَعْمَلُ النَّاسُ الْيَوْمَ وَيَكْدَحُونَ فِيهِ أَشَىْءٌ قُضِيَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَضَى فِيهِمْ مِنْ قَدَرٍ قَدْ سَبَقَ أَوْ فِيمَا يُسْتَقْبَلُونَ بِهِ مِمَّا أَتَاهُمْ بِهِ نَبِيُّهُمْ وَثَبَتَتِ الْحُجَّةُ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ بَلْ شَىْءٌ قُضِيَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَضَى فِيهِمْ وَتَصْدِيقُ ذَلِكَ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ‏{‏ وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّاهَا * فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا‏}‏ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Abu al-Aswad reported that 'Imran b Husain asked him:What is your view, what the people do today in the world, and strive for, is it something decreed for them or preordained for them or will their fate in the Hereafter be deterrained by the fact that their Prophets brought them teaching which they did not act upon? I said: Of course, it is something which is predetermined for them and preordained for them. He (further) said: Then, would it not be an injustice (to punish them)? I felt greatly disturbed because of that, and said: Everything is created by Allah and lies in His Power. He would not be questioned as to what He does, but they would be questioned; thereupon he said to me: May Allah have mercy upon you, I did not mean to ask you but for testing your intelligence. Two men of the tribe of Muzaina came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said: Allah's Messenger, what is your opinion that the people do in the world and strive for, is something decreed for them; something preordained for them and will their fate in the Hereafter be determined by the fact that their Prophets brought them teachings which they did not act upon. and thus they became deserving of punishment? Thereupon, he said: Of course, it happens as it is decreed by Destiny and preordained for them, and this view is confirmed by this verse of the Book of Allah, the Exalted and Glorious:" Consider the soul and Him Who made it perfect, then breathed into it its sin and its piety" (xci)

muslim:6739.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that divine decree in this narration refers merely to Allah's passive foreknowledge and that `فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا` ([Quran 91:8](quran://91/8)) only means Allah made known to the soul the difference between sin and piety while leaving humans free to choose how they respond to prophetic teaching. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states the opposite: when asked whether human deeds are already settled by a prior decree or determined going forward by how people respond to what their Prophet brought them (`أَوْ فِيمَا يُسْتَقْبَلُونَ بِهِ مِمَّا أَتَاهُمْ بِهِ نَبِيُّهُمْ`), Muhammad rejects the second option with `لاَ بَلْ شَىْءٌ قُضِيَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَضَى فِيهِمْ` ('No! Rather, it is something already decreed upon them and executed among them'). Furthermore, when asked whether punishing people for preordained actions is injustice (`أَفَلاَ يَكُونُ ظُلْمًا`), the narration resolves the objection not by appealing to human free will, but by declaring that everything is Allah's possession and `فَلاَ يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ` ('He cannot be questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned,' [Quran 21:23](quran://21/23)).

muslim:6731.note: Muhammad declares that Allah has already written every born soul's place in Paradise or the Fire as blessed or wretched (damned), and when asked whether people should therefore rely on what is written and abandon deeds, he replies that everyone will end up doing and being facilitated toward the deeds of the class to which they belong ([Quran 92:5](quran://92/5)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قَالَ ‏"‏ مَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ مَا مِنْ نَفْسٍ مَنْفُوسَةٍ إِلاَّ وَقَدْ كَتَبَ اللَّهُ مَكَانَهَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ وَالنَّارِ وَإِلاَّ وَقَدْ كُتِبَتْ شَقِيَّةً أَوْ سَعِيدَةً ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَفَلاَ نَمْكُثُ عَلَى كِتَابِنَا وَنَدَعُ الْعَمَلَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَنْ كَانَ مِنْ أَهْلِ السَّعَادَةِ فَسَيَصِيرُ إِلَى عَمَلِ أَهْلِ السَّعَادَةِ وَمَنْ كَانَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الشَّقَاوَةِ فَسَيَصِيرُ إِلَى عَمَلِ أَهْلِ الشَّقَاوَةِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ اعْمَلُوا فَكُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ أَمَّا أَهْلُ السَّعَادَةِ فَيُيَسَّرُونَ لِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ السَّعَادَةِ وَأَمَّا أَهْلُ الشَّقَاوَةِ فَيُيَسَّرُونَ لِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الشَّقَاوَةِ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: There is not one amongst you whom a seat in Paradise or Hell has not been allotted and about whom it has not been written down whether he would be an evil person or a blessed person. A person said: Allah's Messenger, should we not then depend upon our destiny and abandon our deeds? Thereupon he said: Acts of everyone will be facilitated in that which has been created for him so that whoever belongs to the company of the blessed will have good works made easier for him and whoever belongs to the unfortunate ones will have evil acts made easier for him.

muslim:6731.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that divine decree merely reflects foreknowledge of free human choices, pointing to Muhammad's command to act (*i'malu*) and his recitation of [Quran 92:5](quran://92/5) to claim that individuals earn their own facilitation toward good or evil. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah has already written every soul's place in Paradise or the Fire (*kataba Allahu makanaha min al-jannati wa al-nar*) as wretched or blessed, and adds—in a clause omitted from the English translation—that 'whoever belongs to the people of wretchedness will inevitably end up doing the deeds of the people of wretchedness' (*man kana min ahli al-shaqawati fasayasiru ila 'amali ahli al-shaqawati*). Rather than deeds determining one's destiny, the Arabic text makes pre-written membership among the damned (*ahl al-shaqawah*) the prior condition for why they 'are facilitated toward the deeds of the people of wretchedness' (*yuyassaruna li-'amali ahli al-shaqawati*), as paralleled in `bukhari:1362`, `bukhari:4949`, and `bukhari:6605`.

muslim:6737.note: After affirming that the people of Paradise are already known and distinguished from the people of Hellfire, Muhammad answers the question of why people perform deeds by stating that everyone is facilitated toward that for which he was created ([Quran 7:179](quran://7/179), bukhari:4949, muslim:6736).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: قِيلَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَعُلِمَ أَهْلُ الْجَنَّةِ مِنْ أَهْلِ النَّارِ قَالَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ نَعَمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ قِيلَ فَفِيمَ يَعْمَلُ الْعَامِلُونَ قَالَ ‏"‏ كُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ لِمَا خُلِقَ لَهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: Imran b. Husain repotted that it was said to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ):Has there been drawn a distinction between the people of Paradise and the denizens of hell? He said: Yes. It was again said: (If it is so), then What is the use of doing good deeds? Thereupon he said: Everyone is facilitated in what has been created for him

muslim:6737.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that divine decree merely reflects foreknowledge of human choices and that individuals freely perform their own deeds without compulsion. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states كُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ لِمَا خُلِقَ لَهُ (kullun muyassarun limā khuliqa lahu, 'Everyone is facilitated toward that for which he was created'), directly answering the question فَفِيمَ يَعْمَلُ الْعَامِلُونَ ('Then for what do the doers of deeds work?') by affirming that people are created for either Paradise or Hellfire and steered toward that predetermined end ([Quran 7:179](quran://7/179), muslim:6736, bukhari:4949).

muslim:6733.note: Muhammad declares that every soul's abode in Paradise or Hell is already known and allotted, and when asked why people should perform deeds rather than rely on their destiny, he replies that everyone is facilitated toward that for which they were created, reciting [Quran 92:5](quran://92/5) through [Quran 92:10](quran://92/10).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَقَالَ ‏"‏ مَا مِنْكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ إِلاَّ وَقَدْ عُلِمَ مَنْزِلُهَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ وَالنَّارِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ فَلِمَ نَعْمَلُ أَفَلاَ نَتَّكِلُ قَالَ ‏"‏ لاَ ‏.‏ اعْمَلُوا فَكُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ لِمَا خُلِقَ لَهُ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: He raised his head and said:There is not one amongst you who has not been allotted his seat in Paradise or Hell. They said: Allah's Messenger. then, why should we perform good deeds, why not depend upon our destiny? Thereupon he said. No, do perform good deeds, for everyone is facilitated in that for which he has been created

muslim:6733.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that `عُلِمَ مَنْزِلُهَا` ('its place is known') refers only to passive divine foreknowledge rather than predestination, citing Muhammad's command to perform deeds (`اعْمَلُوا`) and his quotation of [Quran 92:5](quran://92/5) as proof of independent human choice. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `فَكُلٌّ مُيَسَّرٌ لِمَا خُلِقَ لَهُ` ('for everyone is facilitated in that for which he has been created'), directly tying human actions to the specific abode in Paradise or Hell (`الْجَنَّةِ وَالنَّارِ`) for which each soul was created. Rather than resolving the companions' objection about why they should act (`فَلِمَ نَعْمَلُ أَفَلاَ نَتَّكِلُ`), Muhammad's closing recitation of `{ فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَى}` ('We shall facilitate him toward the difficult end') confirms that individuals are steered toward their pre-allotted destiny.

bukhari:1145.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
bukhari:1145.subcategory: Divine Immanence, Entering Creation & Visible Form (Incarnation Precedents)
bukhari:1145.note: Muhammad declares that Allah Himself (*Rabbunā*) descends (*yanzilu*) every night during the final third of the night into the lowest heaven (*al-samāʾ al-dunyā*)—which in Islamic cosmology is part of the created physical universe ([Quran 41:12](quran://41/12), [Quran 67:5](quran://67/5))—to answer prayers and grant forgiveness. While Ashʿarī commentators reinterpret this phrasing metaphorically (*taʾwīl*) as the descent of an angel or divine mercy, Atharī scholars affirm literal divine descent into created space, conceding the theological premise underlying the Christian Incarnation ([John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: يَنْزِلُ رَبُّنَا تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا حِينَ يَبْقَى ثُلُثُ اللَّيْلِ الآخِرُ يَقُولُ مَنْ يَدْعُونِي فَأَسْتَجِيبَ لَهُ مَنْ يَسْأَلُنِي فَأُعْطِيَهُ مَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُنِي فَأَغْفِرَ لَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Our Lord, the Blessed, the Superior, comes every night down on the nearest Heaven to us when the last third of the night remains, saying: "Is there anyone to invoke Me, so that I may respond to invocation? Is there anyone to ask Me, so that I may grant him his request? Is there anyone seeking My forgiveness, so that I may forgive him?

bukhari:1145.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Ashʿarī commentators like Al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*) and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*)—that 'our Lord descends' (*yanzilu rabbunā*) is merely a metaphor for the descent of Allah's mercy, command, or an angel, or else claim (*bilā kayf*) that He descends without entering created space. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the One who descends to the created lowest heaven (*ilā al-samāʾ al-dunyā*, cf. [Quran 41:12](quran://41/12)) speaks in the exclusive divine first-person—'Who calls upon Me that I may answer him... Who seeks My forgiveness that I may forgive him?' (*man yadʿūnī fa-astajība lahu... man yastaghfirunī fa-aghfira lahu*)—words no angel or impersonal attribute could ever utter. Consequently, Sunni Islam's own Atharī authorities (such as Ibn Taymiyyah in *Sharḥ Ḥadīth al-Nuzūl*) rejected the metaphorical excuse and affirmed that Allah Himself genuinely descends (*ḥaqīqatan*), conceding that God can enter a created realm without compromising His divine majesty.

muslim:6655.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:6655.subcategory: Divine Immanence, Entering Creation & Visible Form (Incarnation Precedents)
muslim:6655.note: Muhammad commands anyone fighting his brother to avoid the face because Allah created Adam in His own image (ʿalā ṣūratihi), conceding the Biblical doctrine of the Imago Dei ([Genesis 1:26](bible://gn/1/26), [Genesis 1:27](bible://gn/1/27)) that Muslim polemicists reject on the basis of [Quran 42:11](quran://42/11). Attempts to redirect the pronoun in ʿalā ṣūratihi to the person being struck are precluded by the parallel narration in bukhari:6227, which states that Allah created Adam in His image where no struck person is mentioned.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَفِي حَدِيثِ ابْنِ حَاتِمٍ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ إِذَا قَاتَلَ أَحَدُكُمْ أَخَاهُ فَلْيَجْتَنِبِ الْوَجْهَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ آدَمَ عَلَى صُورَتِهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏
problematic_excerpt.english: in the hadith transmitted on the authority of Ibn Hatim Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) is reported to have said:When any one of you fights with his brother, he should avoid his face for Allah created Adam in His own image

muslim:6655.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the possessive pronoun `-hi` in `ʿalā ṣūratihi` ("in his image") refers back to Adam or to the brother being struck rather than to Allah, claiming it merely means Adam was created in his own human form. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states `فَلْيَجْتَنِبِ الْوَجْهَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ خَلَقَ آدَمَ عَلَى صُورَتِهِ` ("he should avoid his face for Allah created Adam in His own image"), giving Adam's creation in Allah's image as the causal reason (`fa-inna`) why the human face must not be struck. Reading the pronoun as referring to Adam reduces the clause to a tautology that Adam was created in Adam's own image, which fails to explain why the face is uniquely protected and contradicts the standard rendering of `muslim:6655` and its parallels (`bukhari:6227`, `muslim:6651`) as "in His own image."

muslim:1773.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:1773.subcategory: Divine Immanence, Entering Creation & Visible Form (Incarnation Precedents)
muslim:1773.note: Muhammad declares that after the first third of every night passes, Allah descends (*yanzilu*) to the lowest heaven (*al-samāʾ al-dunyā*) and calls out, 'I am the King,' offering to answer supplications and forgive sins until dawn breaks. Because the lowest heaven is a created realm adorned with lamps ([Quran 41:12](quran://41/12), [Quran 67:5](quran://67/5)), this report affirms that God enters created space, countering polemics against the Christian Incarnation ([John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: يَنْزِلُ اللَّهُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ حِينَ يَمْضِي ثُلُثُ اللَّيْلِ الأَوَّلُ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَا الْمَلِكُ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَدْعُونِي فَأَسْتَجِيبَ لَهُ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَسْأَلُنِي فَأُعْطِيَهُ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَسْتَغْفِرُنِي فَأَغْفِرَ لَهُ فَلاَ يَزَالُ كَذَلِكَ حَتَّى يُضِيءَ الْفَجْرُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah descends every night to the lowest heaven when one-third of the first part of the night is over and says: I am the Lord; I am the Lord: who is there to supplicate Me so that I answer him? Who is there to beg of Me so that I grant him? Who is there to beg forgiveness from Me so that I forgive him? He continues like this till the day breaks

muslim:1773.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that following Ashʿarī commentators like al-Nawawī (*Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*), the phrase 'Allah descends' (*yanzilu Allāhu*) is merely a metaphor meaning that Allah's command, mercy, or an angel descends, or else claim via Atharī theology that He descends without entering creation (*bilā kayf*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the One who descends into the created lowest heaven (*إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا*, *ilā al-samāʾ al-dunyā*) proclaims in the first person, 'I am the King! I am the King! Who is there to supplicate Me so that I answer him... and beg forgiveness from Me so that I forgive him?' (*أَنَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَا الْمَلِكُ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَدْعُونِي فَأَسْتَجِيبَ لَهُ*), which makes the 'angel or mercy' metaphor blasphemous—since no angel or abstract attribute can claim to be the Divine King who forgives sins—and directly places Allah's personal presence inside a temporally and spatially bounded tier of creation until dawn breaks (*حَتَّى يُضِيءَ الْفَجْرُ*).

muslim:1775.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:1775.subcategory: Divine Immanence, Entering Creation & Visible Form (Incarnation Precedents)
muslim:1775.note: Muhammad declares that Allah descends in the lowest heaven (*yanzilu Allāhu fī al-samāʾi al-dunyā*) at the half or final third of the night and stretches out His two hands (*yabsuṭu yadayhi*) while calling for petitioners. Because the lowest heaven is part of the created physical universe ([Quran 41:12](quran://41/12), [Quran 67:5](quran://67/5)), this narration concedes that God enters created space, challenging the common philosophical objection against the Christian Incarnation ([John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: يَنْزِلُ اللَّهُ فِي السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا لِشَطْرِ اللَّيْلِ أَوْ لِثُلُثِ اللَّيْلِ الآخِرِ فَيَقُولُ مَنْ يَدْعُونِي فَأَسْتَجِيبَ لَهُ أَوْ يَسْأَلُنِي فَأُعْطِيَهُ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ مَنْ يُقْرِضُ غَيْرَ عَدِيمٍ وَلاَ ظَلُومٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ مُسْلِمٌ ابْنُ مَرْجَانَةَ هُوَ سَعِيدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَمَرْجَانَةُ أُمُّهُ ‏.‏ حَدَّثَنَا هَارُونُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ الأَيْلِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ وَهْبٍ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ بِلاَلٍ، عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، بِهَذَا الإِسْنَادِ وَزَادَ ‏"‏ ثُمَّ يَبْسُطُ يَدَيْهِ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى يَقُولُ مَنْ يُقْرِضُ غَيْرَ عَدُومٍ وَلاَ ظَلُومٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: Allah descends to the lowest heaven at half of the night or at one-third of the latter part and says: Who is there to supplicate Me so that I answer him? Who is there to ask Me so that I grant him? And then says: Who will lend to One Who is neither indigent nor tyrant? (This hadith has been narrated by Sa'd b. Sa'id with the same chain of transmitters with this addition:" Then the Blessed and the Exalted (Lord) stretches His Hands and says: Who will lend to One Who is neither indigent nor tyrant?

muslim:1775.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*—either that this descent is a metaphor (*majāz*) meaning only Allah's mercy or an angel descends, or that Allah descends in a transcendent manner (*bilā kayf*) without entering physical creation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *yanzilu Allāhu fī al-samāʾ al-dunyā* ('Allah descends in the lowest heaven') and immediately adds *thumma yabsuṭu yadayhi tabāraka wa-taʿālā* ('Then He, Blessed and Exalted, stretches out His Hands') while asking in the first person, *'Who is there to supplicate Me (yadʿūnī) so that I answer him?'* Because no created angel or impersonal mercy can be called 'Blessed and Exalted' or answer prayer as God, and because the 'lowest heaven' (*al-samāʾ al-dunyā*) is explicitly a created physical sphere adorned with stars (Quran 41:12, 67:5), the Hadith indisputably places Allah Himself inside His own creation.

bukhari:4581.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
bukhari:4581.subcategory: Divine Immanence, Entering Creation & Visible Form (Incarnation Precedents)
bukhari:4581.note: Muhammad declares that on the Day of Resurrection, believers will see Allah as clearly as the unclouded sun or full moon, and that the Lord of the Worlds will come to them in a visible form (*ṣūrah*)—relevant to discussions of whether God can manifest in a visible form ([John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14), [Colossians 1:15](bible://col/1/15)). While this abridged narration ends as the believers initially refuse to recognize Him in that form, fuller parallel transmissions (bukhari:4919, bukhari:7439) record that He subsequently returns in the form they first saw and uncovers His shin ([Quran 68:42](quran://68/42), [Ibn Kathir 68:42](ibnkathir://68/42)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: أَتَاهُمْ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ فِي أَدْنَى صُورَةٍ مِنَ الَّتِي رَأَوْهُ فِيهَا، فَيُقَالُ مَاذَا تَنْتَظِرُونَ تَتْبَعُ كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ مَا كَانَتْ تَعْبُدُ‏.‏ قَالُوا فَارَقْنَا النَّاسَ فِي الدُّنْيَا عَلَى أَفْقَرِ مَا كُنَّا إِلَيْهِمْ، وَلَمْ نُصَاحِبْهُمْ، وَنَحْنُ نَنْتَظِرُ رَبَّنَا الَّذِي كُنَّا نَعْبُدُ‏.‏ فَيَقُولُ أَنَا رَبُّكُمْ، فَيَقُولُونَ لاَ نُشْرِكُ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا‏.‏ مَرَّتَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلاَثًا
problematic_excerpt.english: Then (Allah) the Lord of the worlds will come to them in a shape nearest to the picture they had in their minds about Him. It will be said, 'What are you waiting for?' Every nation has followed what they used to worship.' They will reply, 'We left the people in the world when we were in great need of them and we did not take them as friends. Now we are waiting for our Lord Whom we used to worship.' Allah will say, 'I am your Lord.' They will say twice or thrice, 'We do not worship any besides Allah

bukhari:4581.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue—following Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, or relying on Muhsin Khan's interpolated translation ('the picture they had in their minds')—that Allah does not actually assume a visible form, claiming the *ṣūrah* ('form') is merely a subjective mental perception or a newly created image used to test the gathering. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the Lord of the Worlds Himself comes to them in a form (*atāhum Rabbu al-ʿālamīn fī adnā ṣūrah*) and personally declares, 'I am your Lord' (*anā Rabbukum*), while parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:6573, bukhari:7439) confirm that Allah appears in a form other than His original form (*fī ṣūratin ghayri ṣūratihi*), transforms (*yataḥawwalu*) back into His recognizable form, and uncovers His shin (*sāq*) to prove His identity. Once Sunni orthodoxy concedes that Allah can manifest in and transform between distinct visible forms (*ṣuwar*) before His creatures without ceasing to be God, their foundational philosophical objection against God assuming a visible form in the Incarnation collapses.

muslim:1772.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:1772.subcategory: Divine Immanence, Entering Creation & Visible Form (Incarnation Precedents)
muslim:1772.note: Muhammad declares through Abu Huraira that Allah descends (*yanzilu*) every night during the final third of the night into the lowest heaven (*al-samāʾ al-dunyā*)—a created sphere adorned with stars ([Quran 41:12](quran://41/12), [Quran 67:5](quran://67/5))—to answer and forgive those who call upon Him. Although Muslim polemicists reject the Christian Incarnation ([John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14)) on the premise that God cannot enter created space, traditional Sunni theology affirms Allah's nightly descent into the lowest heaven as a real divine action rather than a metaphor.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: يَنْزِلُ رَبُّنَا تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا حِينَ يَبْقَى ثُلُثُ اللَّيْلِ الآخِرُ فَيَقُولُ مَنْ يَدْعُونِي فَأَسْتَجِيبَ لَهُ وَمَنْ يَسْأَلُنِي فَأُعْطِيَهُ وَمَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُنِي فَأَغْفِرَ لَهُ
problematic_excerpt.english: Our Lord, the Blessed and the Exalted, descends every night to the lowest heaven when one-third of the latter part of the night is left, and says: Who supplicates Me so that I may answer him? Who asks Me so that I may give to him? Who asks Me forgiveness so that I may forgive him?

muslim:1772.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that this descent is merely metaphorical (*taʾwīl*)—claiming via Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* that only Allah's mercy (*raḥmatuhu*), command, or an angel descends—or else insist (*bilā kayf*) that Allah descends without entering created space. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that the subject who descends (*yanzilu*) into the lowest heaven (*al-samāʾ al-dunyā*) is *Rabbunā tabāraka wa-taʿālā* ('Our Lord, the Blessed and the Exalted'), who immediately speaks in the first-person divine voice: *'Man yadʿūnī fa-astajība lahu... wa-man yastaghfirunī fa-aghfira lahu'* ('Who supplicates Me so that I may answer him... and who asks Me forgiveness so that I may forgive him?'). Since no angel or abstract attribute can claim to answer prayers and forgive sins as 'Me,' and since the Quran defines *al-samāʾ al-dunyā* as the created physical sky adorned with stars (Quran 41:12, 67:5), the narration irrefutably depicts Allah Himself entering created space.

muslim:1774.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:1774.subcategory: Divine Immanence, Entering Creation & Visible Form (Incarnation Precedents)
muslim:1774.note: Muhammad declares that after half or two-thirds of the night has passed, Allah descends (*yanzilu Allāhu*) to the lowest heaven (*al-samāʾ al-dunyā*) and calls out until daybreak for anyone asking, supplicating, or seeking forgiveness. While Muslim polemicists reject the Incarnation ([John 1:14](bible://jn/1/14)) by arguing God cannot enter created space, the lowest heaven is explicitly part of the created physical universe ([Quran 41:12](quran://41/12), [Quran 67:5](quran://67/5)), and parallel reports (bukhari:1145) record Allah speaking there in the first person, precluding later Ash'ari attempts to substitute an angel for Allah.

problematic_excerpt.arabic: إِذَا مَضَى شَطْرُ اللَّيْلِ أَوْ ثُلُثَاهُ يَنْزِلُ اللَّهُ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى إِلَى السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا فَيَقُولُ هَلْ مِنْ سَائِلٍ يُعْطَى هَلْ مِنْ دَاعٍ يُسْتَجَابُ لَهُ هَلْ مِنْ مُسْتَغْفِرٍ يُغْفَرُ لَهُ حَتَّى يَنْفَجِرَ الصُّبْحُ
problematic_excerpt.english: When half of the night or two-third of it is over. Allah, the Blessed and the Exalted, descends to the lowest heaven and says: Is there any beggar, so that he be given? Is there any supplicator so that he be answered? Is there any beggar of forgiveness so that he be forgiven? (And Allah continues it saying) till it is daybreak

muslim:1774.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Allah's descent is either a metaphor for the descent of His mercy or an angel (as claimed by Ashʿarī commentators like al-Nawawī in *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*), or a mysterious descent 'without how' (*bilā kayf*) that somehow avoids entering creation. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Allah Himself descends (*yanzilu Allāhu tabāraka wa-taʿālā*) into *al-samāʾ al-dunyā*—the physical, created lowest heaven adorned with stars ([Quran 67:5](quran://67/5))—and parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:1145) quote Him speaking in the first person ('Who is calling upon Me that I may answer him?'), which no angel could ever claim. Thus, whether taken literally or via *bilā kayf*, Sunni orthodoxy concedes that God can enter a created realm to draw near to humanity without ceasing to be God, demolishing their core philosophical objection to the Christian Incarnation.

bukhari:7440.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
bukhari:7440.subcategory: Uncreated Divine Word, Original Sin & Sacramental Relics (Trinitarian & Soteriological Precedents)
bukhari:7440.note: In this intercession account, the Arabic text titles Jesus "the Spirit of Allah and His Word" (*wa Ruhallahi wa Kalimatahu*, cf. [John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1); [Quran 4:171](quran://4/171))—which the English translation alters to "a soul created by Him and His Word. (Be: And it was.)." Furthermore, while Adam, Noah, Abraham, and Moses each cite their own sins and Jesus describes Muhammad as a servant "whose past and future sins Allah has forgiven," Jesus is the sole prophet in the narrative to whom no sin is attributed (cf. [1 Peter 2:22](bible://1pt/2/22); bukhari:4712).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: وَلَكِنِ ائْتُوا عِيسَى عَبْدَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولَهُ وَرُوحَ اللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتَهُ‏.‏ قَالَ فَيَأْتُونَ عِيسَى فَيَقُولُ لَسْتُ هُنَاكُمْ وَلَكِنِ ائْتُوا مُحَمَّدًا صلى الله عليه وسلم عَبْدًا غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ‏.‏ فَيَأْتُونِي فَأَسْتَأْذِنُ عَلَى رَبِّي فِي دَارِهِ فَيُؤْذَنُ لِي عَلَيْهِ،
problematic_excerpt.english: 'Go to Jesus, Allah's slave and His Apostle, and a soul created by Him and His Word.' (Be: And it was.) They will go to Jesus who will say, 'I am not fit for this undertaking but you'd better go to Muhammad the slave whose past and future sins have been forgiven by Allah.' So they will come to me, and I will ask my Lord's permission to enter His House and then I will be permitted.

translation_issue.arabic_term: وَرُوحَ اللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتَهُ
translation_issue.published_rendering: and a soul created by Him and His Word.' (Be: And it was.)
translation_issue.literal_meaning: and the Spirit of Allah and His Word.
translation_issue.explanation: The Arabic phrase 'wa-rūḥa llāhi wa-kalimatah' is a direct genitive construction (iḍāfah) meaning 'and the Spirit of Allah and His Word.' The published translation inserts the unattested words 'created by' directly into the text without brackets—changing 'the Spirit of Allah' into 'a soul created by Him'—and appends the parenthetical gloss '(Be: And it was.)' to polemically preempt the Christian doctrine of the uncreated Logos and Spirit.

bukhari:7440.literal_translation: Rather, go to Jesus, the servant of Allah and His Messenger, and the Spirit of Allah and His Word. So they will come to Jesus, and he will say: 'I am not in a position for that, but go to Muhammad (ﷺ), a servant whose past and future sins Allah has forgiven.' So they will come to me, and I will ask permission to enter upon my Lord in His abode, and permission will be granted to me.
bukhari:7440.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that calling Jesus 'the Spirit of Allah and His Word' (*rūḥu llāhi wa-kalimatuhu*) is merely a genitive of honor (*iḍāfat tashrīf*) referring to the created command 'Be!' (*Kun*), and that all prophets share equal infallibility (*ʿiṣmah*) while the faults mentioned on Judgment Day are merely minor lapses in judgment (*tark al-awlā*). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly labels the acts of Adam, Noah, and Moses as actual sin (*khaṭīʾatahu*), charges Abraham with three lies (*kadhaba-hunna*), and identifies Muhammad as a servant needing forgiveness for his past and future sins (*mā taqaddama min dhanbihi wa-mā taʾakhkhara*), whereas parallel Sahih narrations (bukhari:4712; muslim:480) state of Jesus alone: *fa-lā yadhkuru dhanban* ('he does not mention any sin'). Moreover, in *Kitāb al-Tawḥīd* (bukhari:7410), al-Bukhārī himself cites Jesus's title as Allah's *Kalimah* to prove that Allah's Word is uncreated, leaving Jesus uniquely sinless and ontologically distinct from every other prophet.

muslim:6878.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:6878.subcategory: Uncreated Divine Word, Original Sin & Sacramental Relics (Trinitarian & Soteriological Precedents)
muslim:6878.note: Muhammad declares through Khawlah bint Hakim that whoever stops at a place and says, "I seek refuge in the Perfect Words of Allah (*kalimāti Allāhi al-tāmmāt*) from the evil of what He has created (*mā khalaqa*)," will not be harmed by anything until departing from that place. By directing believers to seek refuge in Allah's Words against created things, the supplication distinguishes an uncreated Divine Word from creation while Islamic texts simultaneously title Jesus the Word of Allah ([Quran 4:171](quran://4/171), [Ibn Kathir 4:171](ibnkathir://4/171), [John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: سَمِعْتُ خَوْلَةَ بِنْتَ حَكِيمٍ السُّلَمِيَّةَ، تَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏ "‏ مَنْ نَزَلَ مَنْزِلاً ثُمَّ قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ‏.‏ لَمْ يَضُرُّهُ شَىْءٌ حَتَّى يَرْتَحِلَ مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ ذَلِكَ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Khaula bint Hakim Sulamiyya reported:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying: When anyone lands at a place, and then says:" I seek refuge in the Perfect Word of Allah from the evil of what He has created," nothing would harm him until he marches from that stopping place

muslim:6878.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that seeking refuge in the Words of Allah is merely an idiomatic plea for protection through His decrees rather than an invocation of a distinct eternal attribute, and that titling Jesus a Word in [Quran 4:171](quran://4/171) only means he was brought into existence by a created command. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *a'ūdhu bi-kalimāti Allāhi al-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaqa* ("I seek refuge in the Perfect Words of Allah from the evil of what He has created"), directly contrasting the Words of Allah against *mā khalaqa* ("what He has created") and placing the Divine Word outside the category of creation (`muslim:6878`, `bukhari:3371`). Because seeking refuge (*isti'ādha*) in anything created is forbidden in Islam as polytheism (*shirk*), Muhammad's command to seek refuge directly in the Words of Allah concedes an uncreated Divine Word distinguishable from creation, paralleling [John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1).

bukhari:4712.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
bukhari:4712.subcategory: Uncreated Divine Word, Original Sin & Sacramental Relics (Trinitarian & Soteriological Precedents)
bukhari:4712.note: In this Hadith of Intercession, humanity addresses Jesus as Allah's Messenger, 'His Word (*Kalimatuhu*) which He cast to Mary, and a Spirit from Him (*Rūḥun minhu*)' ([Quran 4:171](quran://4/171), [Ibn Kathir 4:171](ibnkathir://4/171); cf. [John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1)). While Adam, Noah, Abraham, and Moses each cite a specific transgression or invocation and Muhammad is addressed as having his past and future sins (*dhanb*) forgiven, Muhammad explicitly states that Jesus alone mentions no sin (*wa-lam yadhkur dhanban*; cf. [1 Peter 2:22](bible://1pt/2/22)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَيَأْتُونَ عِيسَى فَيَقُولُونَ يَا عِيسَى أَنْتَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُ أَلْقَاهَا إِلَى مَرْيَمَ وَرُوحٌ مِنْهُ، وَكَلَّمْتَ النَّاسَ فِي الْمَهْدِ صَبِيًّا اشْفَعْ لَنَا أَلاَ تَرَى إِلَى مَا نَحْنُ فِيهِ فَيَقُولُ عِيسَى إِنَّ رَبِّي قَدْ غَضِبَ الْيَوْمَ غَضَبًا لَمْ يَغْضَبْ قَبْلَهُ مِثْلَهُ، وَلَنْ يَغْضَبَ بَعْدَهُ مِثْلَهُ ـ وَلَمْ يَذْكُرْ ذَنْبًا ـ نَفْسِي نَفْسِي نَفْسِي، اذْهَبُوا إِلَى غَيْرِي اذْهَبُوا إِلَى مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم
problematic_excerpt.english: So they will go to Jesus and say, 'O Jesus! You are Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and His Word which He sent to Mary, and a superior soul created by Him, and you talked to the people while still young in the cradle. Please intercede for us with your Lord. Don't you see in what state we are?' Jesus will say, 'My Lord has today become angry as He has never become before nor will ever become thereafter. Jesus will not mention any sin, but will say, 'Myself! Myself! Myself! Go to someone else; go to Muhammad.'

bukhari:4712.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that calling Jesus 'His Word and a Spirit from Him' (citing Ibn Hajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī* and Al-Nawawī) merely denotes a created soul formed by the command 'Be' (*Kun*), and that all prophets are equally sinless (*maʿṣūm*) while only mentioning minor slips out of humility. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Jesus is *'Kalimatuhu alqāhā ilā Maryam wa rūḥun minhu'* (كَلِمَتُهُ أَلْقَاهَا إِلَى مَرْيَمَ وَرُوحٌ مِنْهُ) with zero mention of being 'created'—a theological gloss interpolated by the English translator—and Al-Bukhārī himself invokes this exact title in *Kitāb al-Tawḥīd* (`bukhari:7410`) when treating Allah's uncreated Speech. Furthermore, the narration explicitly isolates Jesus as the sole figure who 'did not mention any sin' (*wa lam yadhkur dhanban*, وَلَمْ يَذْكُرْ ذَنْبًا), directly contrasting his unique sinlessness against both the patriarchs' confessed transgressions and Muhammad's own 'past and future sins' (*dhanbika*, ذَنْبِكَ).

bukhari:3371.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
bukhari:3371.subcategory: Uncreated Divine Word, Original Sin & Sacramental Relics (Trinitarian & Soteriological Precedents)
bukhari:3371.note: Muhammad recites over al-Hasan and al-Husain the prayer, 'I seek refuge with the Perfect Words of Allah' (أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ), declaring that Abraham used the same invocation for Ishmael and Isaac. Classical Sunni authorities (including Ahmad ibn Hanbal, al-Bukhari in Khalq Af'al al-'Ibad, and Ibn Hajar in Fath al-Bari) cite this formula as proof that Allah's Word is uncreated—since seeking refuge in any created thing is polytheism (shirk)—thereby conceding the coherence of an uncreated Word subsisting in God ([John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُعَوِّذُ الْحَسَنَ وَالْحُسَيْنَ وَيَقُولُ ‏ "‏ إِنَّ أَبَاكُمَا كَانَ يُعَوِّذُ بِهَا إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ، أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ، وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لاَمَّةٍ
problematic_excerpt.english: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek Refuge with Allah for Al-Hasan and Al-Husain and say: "Your forefather (i.e. Abraham) used to seek Refuge with Allah for Ishmael and Isaac by reciting the following: 'O Allah! I seek Refuge with Your Perfect Words from every devil and from poisonous pests and from every evil, harmful, envious eye

bukhari:3371.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that 'the Perfect Words of Allah' refers merely to an impersonal attribute of speech (*ṣifat al-kalām*) or figuratively to the 'Lord of the Words,' rather than a distinct divine hypostasis like the Christian *Logos*. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *'aʿūdhu bi-kalimāti Allāhi al-tāmmah'* ('I seek refuge directly *with* the Perfect Words of Allah'), which compelled Sunni authorities like Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal and Ibn Ḥajar (*Fatḥ al-Bārī*) to rule that Allah's Word must be an uncreated, eternal reality (*ghayr makhlūq*) because seeking refuge in anything created is polytheism (*shirk*). Since the Quran explicitly titles Jesus himself *'His Word'* (*kalimatuhu*, Q 4:171), Sunni theology concedes the exact metaphysical premise of an uncreated, prayer-receiving Divine Word subsisting in God while condemning Christians for the very same doctrine.

muslim:475.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:475.subcategory: Uncreated Divine Word, Original Sin & Sacramental Relics (Trinitarian & Soteriological Precedents)
muslim:475.note: In this narration of the Day of Resurrection, Adam, Noah, Abraham, and Moses each decline to intercede after recalling a personal fault (*khaṭīʾatuhu*), and Muhammad is described as a servant whose former and later sins (*dhanbihi*) have been forgiven. By contrast, Jesus—titled 'the Spirit of Allah and His Word (*rūḥa Allāhi wa-kalimatuhu*)' (cf. muslim:480, [Quran 4:171](quran://4/171), [Ibn Kathir 4:171](ibnkathir://4/171), [John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1))—is the only figure in the sequence to whom no sin or fault is attributed ([1 Peter 2:22](bible://1pt/2/22)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَيَأْتُونَ مُوسَى - عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ - فَيَقُولُ لَسْتُ هُنَاكُمْ - وَيَذْكُرُ خَطِيئَتَهُ الَّتِي أَصَابَ فَيَسْتَحْيِي رَبَّهُ مِنْهَا - وَلَكِنِ ائْتُوا عِيسَى رُوحَ اللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتَهُ ‏.‏ فَيَأْتُونَ عِيسَى رُوحَ اللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتَهُ فَيَقُولُ لَسْتُ هُنَاكُمْ ‏.‏ وَلَكِنِ ائْتُوا مُحَمَّدًا صلى الله عليه وسلم عَبْدًا قَدْ غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ فَيَأْتُونِي فَأَسْتَأْذِنُ عَلَى رَبِّي فَيُؤْذَنُ لِي
problematic_excerpt.english: So they would come to Moses (peace be upon him) He would say: I am not in a position to do that for you, and would recall his fault that he had committed and would fight shy of his Lord on account of that (and would say): You better go to Jesus, the Spirit of Allah and His word He would say: I am not in a position to do that for you; you better go to Muhammad (ﷺ), a servant whose former and later sins have been forgiven. He (the narrator) said: The Messenger or Allah (ﷺ) observed: So they would come to me and I would ask the permission of my Lord and it would be granted to me

muslim:475.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that calling Jesus 'the Spirit of Allah and His Word' (citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*) is merely an honorific attribution (*iḍāfat tashrīf*) referring to his creation by the command 'Be!' (*Kun*), and that all prophets are equally sinless (*maʿṣūm*), with the earlier prophets only recalling minor suboptimal choices (*khilāf al-awlā*) out of humility to defer intercession to Muhammad. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states that Adam, Noah, Abraham, and Moses each recalled 'his sin which he had committed and felt ashamed before his Lord because of it' (*khaṭīʾatahu allatī aṣāba fa-yastaḥyī rabbahu minhā*) and identifies Muhammad as a servant whose 'former and later sins' (*mā taqaddama min dhanbihi wa-mā taʾakhkhara*) required forgiveness, while uniquely attributing zero sin to Jesus—a distinction underscored in the parallel narration of bukhari:4712, which explicitly adds *wa-lam yadhkur dhanban* ('and he did not mention any sin'). Furthermore, the 'Kun' ('Be!') deflection collapses because Adam and all creation were also brought into existence by Allah's command 'Be!' (Quran 3:59), yet Jesus alone is ontologically titled 'the Spirit of Allah and His Word' (*rūḥa Allāhi wa-kalimatahu*).

muslim:6880.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:6880.subcategory: Uncreated Divine Word, Original Sin & Sacramental Relics (Trinitarian & Soteriological Precedents)
muslim:6880.note: Muhammad instructs anyone staying at a place—including a man stung at night by a scorpion—to seek refuge in the "Perfect Words of Allah" (*kalimāti Allāhi al-tāmmāt*) from the evil of what He created so that nothing will harm him. Seeking refuge directly in Allah's Words against created things distinguishes the uncreated Divine Word from creation, while Islamic scripture identifies Jesus as Allah's Word ([Quran 4:171](quran://4/171), [Ibn Kathir 4:171](ibnkathir://4/171), [John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ خَوْلَةَ بِنْتِ حَكِيمٍ السُّلَمِيَّةِ، أَنَّهَا سَمِعَتْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏"‏ إِذَا نَزَلَ أَحَدُكُمْ مَنْزِلاً فَلْيَقُلْ أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ‏.‏ فَإِنَّهُ لاَ يَضُرُّهُ شَىْءٌ حَتَّى يَرْتَحِلَ مِنْهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ يَعْقُوبُ وَقَالَ الْقَعْقَاعُ بْنُ حَكِيمٍ عَنْ ذَكْوَانَ أَبِي صَالِحٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ مَا لَقِيتُ مِنْ عَقْرَبٍ لَدَغَتْنِي الْبَارِحَةَ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَمَا لَوْ قُلْتَ حِينَ أَمْسَيْتَ أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ لَمْ تَضُرُّكَ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Khaula bint Hakim Sulamiyya reported:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying: When any one of you stays at a place, he should say:" I seek refuge in the Perfect Word of Allah from the evil of that He created." Nothing would then do him any harm until he moves from that place. Abu Huraira reported that a person came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said:" Allah's Messenger, I was stung by a scorpion during the night.
