Thereupon he said: Had you recited these words in the evening:" I seek refuge in the Perfect Word of Allah from the evil of what He created," it would not have done any harm to you

muslim:6880.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that the "Perfect Words of Allah" refers merely to recited Quranic verses or an abstract attribute of divine speech, and that calling Jesus "His Word" in [Quran 4:171](quran://4/171) only means he was brought into existence by the command "Be" ([Ibn Kathir 4:171](ibnkathir://4/171)). However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *aʿūdhu bi-kalimāti Allāhi al-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaqa* ("I seek refuge in the Perfect Words of Allah from the evil of what He created"), which directly separates Allah's Words from the entirety of creation (*mā khalaqa*) and commands seeking refuge in them—an act of reliance reserved exclusively for the uncreated Creator. By proving across this narration and its parallels (`bukhari:3371`, `muslim:6878`, `muslim:6879`) that Allah's Word is uncreated while [Quran 4:171](quran://4/171) applies the title "His Word" (*kalimatuhu*) directly to the person of Jesus, Islamic primary sources concede the theological framework of [John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1) that an eternal, uncreated Word of God is compatible with strict monotheism.

muslim:479.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:479.subcategory: Uncreated Divine Word, Original Sin & Sacramental Relics (Trinitarian & Soteriological Precedents)
muslim:479.note: In this abridged narration of the Day of Resurrection, Moses directs humanity to Jesus by declaring that he is 'the Spirit of Allah and His Word' (*Ruhullah wa Kalimatuhu*), echoing [Quran 4:171](quran://4/171) and paralleling the Christian doctrine of the Divine Word ([John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1)). While commentators like Al-Nawawi and Ibn Hajar gloss these titles as a created spirit or the creative fiat (*Kun*) ([Ibn Kathir 4:171](ibnkathir://4/171)), the prophetic text uniquely assigns them to Jesus, and fuller parallel narrations (muslim:473, muslim:480, bukhari:4712) add 'cast to Mary' while recording the other prophets citing their personal sins yet attributing none to him ([1 Peter 2:22](bible://1pt/2/22)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: فَيُؤْتَى مُوسَى فَيَقُولُ لَسْتُ لَهَا وَلَكِنْ عَلَيْكُمْ بِعِيسَى - عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ - فَإِنَّهُ رُوحُ اللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُ ‏.‏ فَيُؤْتَى عِيسَى فَيَقُولُ لَسْتُ لَهَا وَلَكِنْ عَلَيْكُمْ بِمُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَأُوتَى فَأَقُولُ أَنَا لَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: They would come to Moses, but he would say: I am not fit to do this, but you should go to Jesus, for he is the Spirit of Allah and His word. They would come to Jesus, and he would say, I am not fit to do this; you better go to Muhammad (ﷺ). They would come to me, and I would say: I am in a position to do that

muslim:479.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue, citing Al-Nawawī's *Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim* and Ibn Ḥajar's *Fatḥ al-Bārī*, that calling Jesus 'the Spirit of Allah and His Word' is merely a metaphorical honorific (*iḍāfat tashrīf*) for being created by the command 'Be' (*Kun*), and that his deferral of intercession (*lastu lahā*) proves Muhammad's superiority. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly singles out Jesus alone with the ontological titles `رُوحُ اللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُ` (*Rūḥullāhi wa Kalimatuhu* — the Spirit of Allah and His Word), even though Adam and the entire universe were also created by 'Be' without ever receiving such divine designations. Furthermore, in the expanded Sahih parallels of this exact intercession account (*Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* 4712 and 7410), every other prophet confesses a disqualifying personal sin (*dhanb*) whereas the text explicitly states that Jesus 'did not mention any sin' (`وَلَمْ يَذْكُرْ ذَنْبًا`), contrasting his absolute sinlessness with the Quran's repeated commands for Muhammad to seek forgiveness for his own sins (Quran 40:55, 47:19).

muslim:6135.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:6135.subcategory: Uncreated Divine Word, Original Sin & Sacramental Relics (Trinitarian & Soteriological Precedents)
muslim:6135.note: While Islamic theology rejects Original Sin ([Psalm 51:5](bible://ps/51/5), [Romans 5:12](bible://rom/5/12)) and equates the sinlessness of all prophets, Muhammad declares using the universal quantifier 'every son of Adam' (كُلُّ بَنِي آدَمَ) that Satan touches every human at birth with the sole exception of Mary and her son Jesus ([Quran 3:36](quran://3/36), [Ibn Kathir 3:36](ibnkathir://3/36), [Luke 1:35](bible://lk/1/35), [Hebrews 4:15](bible://heb/4/15)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: كُلُّ بَنِي آدَمَ يَمَسُّهُ الشَّيْطَانُ يَوْمَ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ إِلاَّ مَرْيَمَ وَابْنَهَا
problematic_excerpt.english: The satan touches every son of Adam on the day when his mother gives birth to him with the exception of Mary and her son

muslim:6135.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that Satan's touch at birth is merely a harmless physical contact rather than a spiritual vulnerability, and that other prophets like Muhammad are also implicitly excluded from this rule. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states kullu banī Ādam yamassuhu al-shayṭān yawma waladathu ummuhu illā Maryam wa-ibnahā ("The satan touches every son of Adam on the day when his mother gives birth to him with the exception of Mary and her son"), using the universal quantifier kullu ("every") paired with the restrictive exception illā ("except") to grant sole immunity from Satan's touch at birth to Mary and Jesus (bukhari:3286, muslim:6133, [Ibn Kathir 3:36](ibnkathir://3/36)).

muslim:6879.category: Christian Doctrines Muslims Attack That Are Conceded in Hadith
muslim:6879.subcategory: Uncreated Divine Word, Original Sin & Sacramental Relics (Trinitarian & Soteriological Precedents)
muslim:6879.note: Muhammad commands believers to seek refuge directly in the "Perfect Words of Allah" (*kalimāti Allāhi al-tāmmāt*) from "the evil of what He created" (*min sharri mā khalaqa*), distinguishing Allah's uncreated Word—invoked for protection—from all created things while Islamic scripture identifies Jesus as Allah's Word ([Quran 4:171](quran://4/171), [Ibn Kathir 4:171](ibnkathir://4/171), [John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1)).

problematic_excerpt.arabic: عَنْ خَوْلَةَ بِنْتِ حَكِيمٍ السُّلَمِيَّةِ، أَنَّهَا سَمِعَتْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏"‏ إِذَا نَزَلَ أَحَدُكُمْ مَنْزِلاً فَلْيَقُلْ أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ‏.‏ فَإِنَّهُ لاَ يَضُرُّهُ شَىْءٌ حَتَّى يَرْتَحِلَ مِنْهُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ يَعْقُوبُ وَقَالَ الْقَعْقَاعُ بْنُ حَكِيمٍ عَنْ ذَكْوَانَ أَبِي صَالِحٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ مَا لَقِيتُ مِنْ عَقْرَبٍ لَدَغَتْنِي الْبَارِحَةَ قَالَ ‏"‏ أَمَا لَوْ قُلْتَ حِينَ أَمْسَيْتَ أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ لَمْ تَضُرُّكَ ‏"
problematic_excerpt.english: Khaula bint Hakim Sulamiyya reported:I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying: When any one of you stays at a place, he should say:" I seek refuge in the Perfect Word of Allah from the evil of that He created." Nothing would then do him any harm until he moves from that place. Abu Huraira reported that a person came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said:" Allah's Messenger, I was stung by a scorpion during the night. Thereupon he said: Had you recited these words in the evening:" I seek refuge in the Perfect Word of Allah from the evil of what He created," it would not have done any harm to you

muslim:6879.anticipated_defense: Muslim apologists typically argue that seeking refuge in the Words of Allah merely refers to reciting scripture as an appeal to Allah's decree rather than invoking a distinct, uncreated divine reality. However, the primary Arabic text explicitly states *a'ūdhu bi-kalimāti Allāhi al-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq* ("I seek refuge in the Perfect Words of Allah from the evil of what He created"), directly contrasting Allah's Words with the entirety of creation (*mā khalaq*) and making the Words themselves the object of protection (`bukhari:3371`, `muslim:6878`, `muslim:6880`). Because seeking refuge in any created thing is forbidden in Sunni theology, this formula concedes that Allah's Word is uncreated and eternal, affirming the theological category of the eternal Word in [John 1:1](bible://jn/1/1) while [Quran 4:171](quran://4/171) ([Ibn Kathir 4:171](ibnkathir://4/171)) explicitly identifies Jesus as the Word of Allah.
